children.text:
tatra bhavatā
annambhaṭṭena viracitaḥ tarkasaṃgrahaḥ tatkṛtadīpikākhyavyākhyānasahitaḥ
nyāyaśāstramadhijigāṃsamānaiḥ sarvairapi ādau paṭhyata iti
viśvaprasiddham/ tarkasaṃgrahasya dīpikāvyatiriktāni padakṛtyam,
nyāyabodhinī, vākyavṛttiḥ, niruktiḥ, paṭṭābhirāmaṭippaṇī
ityādīni bahūni vyākhyānāni mudritānyamudritāni ca upalabhyante/
tathā dīpikāyāḥ rāmarudrī, nīlakaṇṭhakṛtā prakāśikā,
nṛsiṃhaśāstrikṛtā prakāśikā, paṭṭābhirāmakṛtā prakāśikā,
ityādayaḥ anekā vyākhyāḥ mudritā amudritāśca vartante/
tarkasaṃgrahavyākhyāsu nyāyabodhinyāḥ dīpikāvyakhyāsu
nīlakaṇṭhīyaprakāśikāyāśca paṭhanapāṭhanapracāro 'sti/ saṃkṣiptaśailyā
apekṣitasakalārthapratipādakatvarūpo viśeṣa eva
paṭhanapāṭhanagocaratāyāṃ mukhyo hetuḥ/ tatrāpi nīlakaṇṭhaprakāśikā
laghugādādharīti vyapadeśayogyā chātrāṇāṃ viduṣāṃ ca
cittarañjakatamā cakāsti/ yeṣāṃ gādādharyādiṣu grantheṣu gāḍhaḥ
paricayo vartate ta eva prakāśikāyāḥ tātparyaṃ rasaṃ ca
jñātumanubhavituṃ ca śaknuvanti/
children.translated_text: It is universally well-known that the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of Reasoning) composed by the revered <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, together with his own commentary called <s>Dīpikā</s> (Lamp), is first studied by all who desire to learn <s>Nyāya-śāstra</s> (the science of logic). Apart from the <s>Dīpikā</s>, many commentaries on the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> are available, both printed and unprinted, such as the <s>Padakṛtya</s>, <s>Nyāyabodhinī</s>, <s>Vākyavṛtti</s>, <s>Nirukti</s>, <s>Paṭṭābhirāma-ṭippaṇī</s>, and others. Likewise, there exist many commentaries on the <s>Dīpikā</s>, both printed and unprinted, such as the <s>Rāmarudrī</s>, the <s>Prakāśikā</s> by <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, the <s>Prakāśikā</s> by <s>Nṛsiṃha Śāstrī</s>, the <s>Prakāśikā</s> by <s>Paṭṭābhirāma</s>, and others. Among the commentaries on the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>, the <s>Nyāyabodhinī</s>, and among the commentaries on the <s>Dīpikā</s>, the <s>Nīlakaṇṭhīya Prakāśikā</s>, are widely studied and taught. Their special quality of presenting all required meanings in a concise style is the chief reason for their being objects of study and teaching. Among these, the <s>Nīlakaṇṭha Prakāśikā</s> shines forth as most delightful to the minds of students and scholars alike, worthy of being called a brief <s>Gadādharī</s>. Only those who have deep acquaintance with works such as the <s>Gadādharī</s> and others can know and experience the purport and essence of the <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text:
tasyāḥ
nīlakaṇṭhaprakāśikāyāḥ prativākyaṃ bhāvārthaspaṣṭīkaraṇacaṇā kācana
vyākhyā cirāt nāvatīrṇā/ yadyapi nīlakaṇṭhaputreṇa kṛtā
bhāskārodayanāmnī vyākhyā bahoḥ kālāt pūrvaṃ
nirṇayasāgarayantrālayena mudrāpitā upalabhyate, tathāpi apekṣitasthale
samucitarītyā avyākhyānāta anapekṣitavistarakaraṇācca
bālatārkikāṇāṃ nopakāriṇī sā/ pratyuta bahuṣu sthaleṣu
prakāśikāyāḥ hṛdayamanavagacchantī viparītatayā vyākhyāntī
vyāmohameva janayati/ iyaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaputreṇa na kṛtā syādityapi
tādṛśasthalānāṃ darśanena matiḥ samupajāyate/ ata eva mādṛśānāṃ
bālatārkikāṇāṃ viduṣāṃ copakārāya samīcīnā kācana vyākhyā
kartavyeti bahoḥ kālāt pūrvaṃ nāvalpākābhijanān paṇḍitapravarān
en. es. rāmānujatātācāryān prārthayam/ teṣāṃ savidhe
nyāyaśāstraṃ mayādhītamitīmaṃ sambandhaṃ puraskṛtya prārthanāmakaravam/
te 'pi sadyaḥ prārthanāṃ svīkṛtya ekavarṣābhyantare bālapriyānāmnīṃ
prakāśikāyāḥ vyākhyāṃ nirmāya aduḥ/ tasyāḥ prakāśanasamayo 'dhunā
samupanata iti nitarāṃ momudyate cetaḥ/ anayā vyākhyayā
bālatārkikāḥ sarve 'pi mahāntamupakāraṃ prāpyasyantīti niścapracam/
children.translated_text: For a long time, no commentary devoted to clarifying the intended meaning of each sentence of that <s>Nīlakaṇṭha Prakāśikā</s> had appeared. Although a commentary named <s>Bhāskarodaya</s> (Sunrise of Illumination) composed by the son of <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> had been printed long ago by the Nirṇaya Sāgar Press, it is nevertheless not helpful to beginning logicians, since it fails to explain adequately at required places and expands unnecessarily at others. Indeed, in many places, failing to grasp the heart of the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, it explains in a contrary manner and only generates confusion. Seeing such passages, the thought arises that this may not have been composed by <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>'s son at all. Therefore, having long ago requested the eminent scholar <s>En. Es. Rāmānuja Tātācārya</s> of the <s>Nāvalpākka</s> lineage to compose a proper commentary for the benefit of beginning logicians like myself and of scholars, making my request on the basis of the connection that I had studied <s>Nyāya-śāstra</s> under him, he graciously accepted the request and within one year composed the commentary on the <s>Prakāśikā</s> named <s>Bālapriyā</s> and gave it to me. Now that the time for its publication has arrived, my heart rejoices greatly. I am certain that all beginning logicians will derive great benefit from this commentary.

children.text: atha
bhāskarodayāyāṃ
children.translated_text: in the <s>Bhāskarodaya</s>,

children.text:
vidyamānānyasāṃgatyāni
sthālīpulākanyāyena pradarśayāmaḥ---
children.translated_text: we shall demonstrate the inconsistencies present therein by the method of <s>sthālīpulāka-nyāya</s> (testing by a sample grain from the pot)—
Now,

children.text: prakāśikāyāṃ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>,

children.text:
'tarkasyāpādakābhāvasādhakaviparyayapratiyogyāpādyakatvarūpaviparyaye
tatkoṭiparyavasāyitvaṃ darśayati - darśanābhāvānnāstīti' iti
paṅktiḥ (pṛ. 142) dṛśyate/ asyāḥ paṅktervāstavārthaḥ ayam - 'yadyatra
ghaṭaḥ syāttarhi bhūtalamiva ghaṭo 'drakṣyata' ityākārake tarke āpādako
ghaṭaḥ tasyābhāvaḥ ghaṭābhāvastasya sādhako viparyayadarśanābhāvaḥ tasya
pratiyogi darśanameva āpādyamiti āpādakābhāvaḥ
sādhakaviparyayapratiyogyāpādyakatvaṃ tarkasyeti/
children.translated_text: the passage is seen (p. 142): 'It shows that <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) has the character of terminating in that limb, in the form of the reversal of the nature whereby what is to be established is the counterpositive of the absence of the producer, which establishes the contrary'—that is, 'because of the absence of perception, it is not.' The actual meaning of this passage is: In <s>tarka</s> of the form 'if a pot were here, it would be perceived like the ground,' the producer is the pot; its absence is the absence of the pot; the establisher of that is the absence of contrary perception; the counterpositive of that is perception itself, which is what is to be established. Thus, <s>tarka</s> has the nature whereby what is to be established is the counterpositive of the contrary whose establisher is the absence of the producer.

children.text: bhāskarodayākārastu
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Bhāskarodaya</s>, however,

children.text:
imamāśayamagṛhītvā kimapi likhati/
tathā hi
children.translated_text: not having grasped this meaning, writes something else. Namely,

children.text: bhāskārodayā
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhāskarodaya</s>

children.text:
paṅktiḥ- 'āpādakasya
darśanāpattisaṃpādakaghaṭāstitvasya abhāvasādhako darśanābhāvo
nāstīti yo viparyayaḥ
tatpratiyogidarśanābhāvarūpaviparyayapratiyogi yaddarśanaṃ
tasyāpādyatvarūpaṃ viparyaye darśanābhāvānnāstīti vyatyāsarūpe
tatkoṭiparyavasāyitvaṃ nāstītyabhāvakoṭiparyavasāyitvaṃ tarkasya
darśayatīti samuditārthaḥ" (pṛ. 80) iti/
children.translated_text: passage reads (p. 80): 'The absence that establishes the absence of the producer—namely the existence of the pot which produces the occurrence of perception—the contrary which is "it is not" being the absence of perception, the counterpositive of the contrary in the form of the absence of perception—namely that perception—whose nature of being that which is to be established, the termination in that limb in the form of the reversal "it is not because of the absence of perception," shows the termination of <s>tarka</s> in the limb of absence—this is the combined meaning.'

children.text:
'tarkitā āpāditā
pratiyogino ghaṭādeḥ sattvasya sattvaprasakteḥ' iti
prakāśikā
children.translated_text: the <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: (pṛ.142)/ atra tarkitā
children.translated_text: (p. 142). Here, the meaning of 'tarkitā' (established by reasoning) is
'The counterpositive, namely the pot and so on, whose existence is being established by <s>tarka</s>'—thus

children.text:
ityasya
āpādanaviṣayabhūtetyarthaḥ/ āpādanāśrayabhūteti bhāskarodayā (pṛ.80)/
children.translated_text: 'that which is the object of the establishment'—this is the meaning. The <s>Bhāskarodaya</s> (p. 80) says 'that which is the locus of the establishment.'

children.text: satpratipakṣaprakaraṇe
prakāśikāyāṃ
children.translated_text: in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>,

children.text:
'yatsaṃbandhi yat sādhyaṃ
tadabhāvavyāpyahetvantarasya jñānaṃ pakṣe 'sti sa satpratipakṣa ityarthaḥ'
iti paṅktirdṛśyate (pṛ. 203)/ tasyā ayamarthaḥ- yatsaṃbandhītyasya
yaddhetusaṃbandhītyarthaḥ/ tathā ca yaddhetusaṃbandhi yat sādhyaṃ
tadabhāvavyāpyahetvantarasya jñānaṃ tatpakṣe 'sti sa satpratipakṣaḥ/ sa
satpratipakṣa ityatra
children.translated_text: the passage is seen (p. 203): 'That which is related to which, and that which is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum)—when the cognition of another <s>hetu</s> (reason) pervaded by the absence of that exists in the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject), that is <s>satpratipakṣa</s>—this is the meaning.' The meaning of this is: 'that which is related to' means 'that which is related to the <s>hetu</s>.' And thus, that <s>sādhya</s> which is related to that <s>hetu</s>, when the cognition of another <s>hetu</s> pervaded by the absence of that <s>sādhya</s> exists in that <s>pakṣa</s>, that is <s>satpratipakṣa</s>. In 'sa satpratipakṣa,' the word 'tat'
In the section on <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (genuine counter-argument),

children.text:
tatpadena
yatsaṃbandhītyatra yatpadena gṛhīto heturgrāhya iti/
bhāskārodayāyāṃ tu - 'yatpadena prakṛtābhipretapakṣaparigrahaḥ/
pakṣetyatra tadityādiḥ/ tathā ca yatpakṣakaṃ yatsādhyaṃ
tadabhāvavyāpyahetvantarasya jñānaṃ tatpakṣe sa ityanvayaḥ' iti
vyākhyānaṃ dṛśyate (pṛ. 116)/ atrānanvayādikaṃ viduṣāṃ spaṣṭam/
children.translated_text: should be understood as referring to the <s>hetu</s> indicated by the word 'yat' in 'yatsaṃbandhī.' In the <s>Bhāskarodaya</s>, however, the commentary reads (p. 116): 'By the word "yat" the intended <s>pakṣa</s> in question is taken; "in the pakṣa" corresponds to "tat" and so on. Thus the construal is: that which has a certain <s>pakṣa</s>, that which is the <s>sādhya</s>, when the cognition of another <s>hetu</s> pervaded by the absence of that exists in that <s>pakṣa</s>.' The lack of proper syntactic connection here and other defects are clear to scholars.

children.text: prāmāṇyavāde
prakāśikāyāṃ
children.translated_text: in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>,

children.text:
- 'bhaṭṭamate tu jñānasyātīndriyatayā
jñātatāliṅgakānumitereva prāthamikajñānagraharūpatayā tayā prāmāṇyaṃ
gṛhyate' iti paṅktirdṛśyate (pṛ. 239)/ atra jñānasya grahaḥ jñānagrahaḥ
prāthamikaścāsau jñānagrahaśceti karmadhārayaḥ/ tena prāthamikatvaṃ
jñānagrahaviśeṣaṇam/ jñānagrahe prāthamikatvaviśeṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: the passage is seen (p. 239): 'In the view of <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>, since cognition is supersensible, <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity) is apprehended by the <s>anumiti</s> (inference) based on the indicator of being-cognized, which has the nature of being the first apprehension of cognition.' Here, 'apprehension of cognition' is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound meaning 'that which is both first and an apprehension of cognition.' Thus, 'firstness' qualifies the apprehension of cognition. By the qualification of firstness in the apprehension of cognition,
In the discussion of <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity of cognition),

children.text:
naiyāyikasaṃmatapravṛttyādiliṅgakānumityātmakaḥ dvitīyo
jñānagrahaḥ vyavacchidyata iti prakāśikāśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: the second apprehension of cognition, which consists in inference based on indicators such as successful activity accepted by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, is excluded—this is the intent of the <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text: bhāskārodayāyāṃ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bhāskarodaya</s>, however,

children.text:
tu etattattvājñānāt 'prathame bhavaṃ prāthamikaṃ
tacca jñānaṃ vyavasāyātmakaṃ, tasya graharūpatayā
tadgrāhakānumityātmakajñānasvarūpatayeti yāvat' iti yatkimapi
vyākhyātam (pṛ. 137)/
children.translated_text: due to ignorance of this true meaning, something else entirely is explained (p. 137): '<s>Prāthamika</s> means occurring in the first; and that cognition is of the nature of <s>vyavasāya</s> (determinate cognition); by virtue of being the apprehension of that—meaning, by virtue of being the cognition that apprehends that, which is of the nature of inference.'

children.text: tathā
tatraiva
children.translated_text: in the same place,

children.text:
- 'anumānaprayogastu idaṃ jñānamapramā
visaṃvādipravṛttijanakatvāt yannaivaṃ tannaivam' iti dṛśyate (pṛ.288)/ atra visaṃvādipravṛttītyatra visaṃvādinī yā pravṛttiḥ
tajjanakatvādityarthaḥ/ visaṃvādinītyasya viphaletyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the passage reads (p. 288): 'The inferential formulation is: this cognition is not <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), because it generates <s>visaṃvādi-pravṛtti</s> (discordant activity); whatever is not so is not so.' Here, in 'visaṃvādi-pravṛtti,' the meaning is: activity that is discordant—because it generates that. The meaning of 'visaṃvādinī' is 'fruitless.'

children.text: bhāskārodayāyāṃ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bhāskarodaya</s>, however,

children.text:
tu 'viparītajñāna
vatpravṛttijanakatvādityarthaḥ' ityuktam/ anena visaṃvādinaḥ
pravṛttiriti vigraho 'bhipretaḥ/ atrānaucityaṃ spaṣṭameva/
children.translated_text: it is said: 'the meaning is: because it generates activity like erroneous cognition.' By this, the intended analysis is 'the activity of the discordant one.' The impropriety here is quite evident.
Similarly,

children.text:
udāharaṇārthaṃ
kānicit sthalāni pradarśitāni/ etādṛśasthaleṣu
bālapriyāyāṃ
children.translated_text: in the <s>Bālapriyā</s>,

children.text: prāmāṇikarītyā vyākhyānaṃ kṛtam/
children.translated_text: the explanation has been given in an authoritative manner.
A few passages have been shown as examples. At such places,

children.text:
athaitanmudraṇasamāptisamaye tiruppukkulisvāmīti vikhyātaiḥ
sārdhaśatasaṃvatsarebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ kāñcīmadhyuṣitavadbhiḥ
catustantraniṣṇātaiviracitānekanyāyagranthakroḍapatraiḥ
śrīkṛṣṇatātācāryaiḥ kṛtāyāḥ prasāraṇāḥ khyāyāḥ prakāśikāvyākhyāyāḥ
ekā tālapatramayī granthalipimātṛkā saṃprati kāñcīmadhivasatāṃ
villiyaṃpākkaṃ śrīsampatkumāratātācāryāṇāṃ sakāśāt labdhā/
vyākhyeyaṃ śrīkṛṣṇatātācāryaiṃḥ mātṛkārūpeṇa vilikhiteti
tālapatrāgranthapuṣpikātaḥ avagamyate/ api cātratyapramā tvānugamaḥ
tathaiva

nyāyasiddhāñjanavyākhyāyāṃ
ratnapeṭikāyāṃ
children.translated_text: is likewise seen in the <s>Ratna-peṭikā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Nyāya-siddhāñjana</s>.

children.text:
dṛśyata/ kiṃ ca
tadīyagranthāntaraśailīmanukarotīyaṃ prasāraṇā/ ato vyākhyeyaṃ
śrīkṛṣṇatātācāryaiḥ kṛtetyatra na ko 'pi saṃdehaḥ/ asyāṃ prasāraṇāyāṃ
prāyaḥ sarveṣāṃ lakṣaṇānāmanugamāḥ vartante/ tasmādiyaṃ vyākhyā
anugamamārgajijñāsūnāṃ mahate upakārāya kalpeteti matvā asyā api
prakāśanaṃ yuktarūpaṃ manvānena mayā anubandharūpeṇa vyākhyeyaṃ
mudrāpitā/ yadi pūrvameveyaṃ samupalabdhā abhaviṣyat tadā iyamapi
tattatsthalasyādhasyāt bālapriyayā sākaṃ mudrāpitā abhaviṣyat/ athāpi
anubandharūpeṇa vā mudraṇārthamiyaṃ labdheti alabhyalābheneva
saṃtuṣyatyantaraṅgam/
children.translated_text: Furthermore, this <s>Prasāraṇā</s> follows the style of his other works. Therefore, there is no doubt that this commentary was composed by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Tātācārya</s>. In this <s>Prasāraṇā</s>, validations of nearly all definitions are present. Considering that this commentary would be of great benefit to those desirous of learning the method of validation, and deeming its publication appropriate, I have printed it as an appendix. Had this been obtained earlier, it too would have been printed together with the <s>Bālapriyā</s> beneath the relevant passages. Nevertheless, having obtained it for printing even as an appendix, my heart is as satisfied as if having gained the ungainable.

Now, at the time of completion of this printing, a palm-leaf manuscript of the commentary on the <s>Prakāśikā</s> called <s>Prasāraṇā</s>, composed by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Tātācārya</s>—known as the <s>Tiruppukkuli Svāmī</s>, who lived in <s>Kāñcī</s> more than one hundred and fifty years ago, who was expert in the four <s>tantras</s> and authored numerous <s>Nyāya</s> treatise-annotations—was obtained from <s>Villiyaṃpākkaṃ Śrī Sampatkumāra Tātācārya</s>, who currently resides in <s>Kāñcī</s>. It is understood from the colophon of the palm-leaf manuscript that this commentary was written by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Tātācārya</s> himself in manuscript form. Moreover, the method of establishing validity found herein

children.text:
granthasyāsya
tarkasaṃṅgraha-dīpikā-prakāśikā-bālapriyā-prasāraṇā-guñjarūpasya
prakāśanam -
children.translated_text: The publication of this work in its five-fold form—<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>, <s>Dīpikā</s>, <s>Prakāśikā</s>, <s>Bālapriyā</s>, and <s>Prasāraṇā</s>—

children.text:

children.translated_text: Discussion on <s>Maṅgala</s> (Auspicious Invocation)

children.text:
iha khalu prāyaḥ
sarve 'pi ganthakārāḥ granthārambhasamaye maṅgalamācarantīti

prayojanamiti maṅgalavāde nirūpyate/ nyāyabhāṣyakāraḥ

vārtikakāraḥ kuto vā granthārambhe maṅgalaṃ nācacāretyāśaṅkya
iṣṭadevatānamaskārarūpaṃ maṅgalaṃ kṛtavāneva/ athāpi granthe tanna
nyaveśayat/ na hi maṅgalakaraṃ yadyatkriyate tatsarvaṃ granthe
niveśanīyamiti nirbandho 'stīti samādhānaṃ provāca ṭīkākāraḥ/
tatsandarbhe ---
children.translated_text: It is universally accepted that here nearly all authors perform an auspicious invocation at the commencement of their works. In the discussion on <s>maṅgala</s> (auspicious invocation), it is examined: what is the authority for performing the auspicious invocation? And what is its purpose? The author of the <s>Nyāya-bhāṣya</s> did not say anything regarding auspicious invocation. The author of the <s>Nyāya-vārtika</s> also began his treatise without any auspicious invocation. However, the commentator <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s> began his <s>ṭīkā</s> (sub-commentary) only after performing an auspicious invocation. There, raising the doubt as to why even the supremely learned author of the <s>Vārtika</s> did not perform an auspicious invocation at the beginning of his work, the commentator explained that he did indeed perform the auspicious invocation in the form of obeisance to his chosen deity, but did not include it in the text. For there is no compulsion that everything auspicious that one does must be included in the text—thus the commentator provided the resolution. In that context—

children.text: 'avigītaśiṣṭācāraparamparāprāpto vārtikakāreṇa
children.translated_text: 'The obeisance to the chosen deity, received through the tradition of uncontested conduct of the learned,

children.text:
paramaśiṣṭena
kṛto 'pīṣṭadevatānamaskāro na śāstre
children.translated_text: though performed by the supremely learned author of the <s>Vārtika</s>,

children.text: niveśetiḥ'1
children.translated_text: was not included in the treatise.'

children.text:
iti vadan
maṅgalācaraṇe śiṣṭācāraḥ pramāṇamiti sūcayati/
tātparyaṭīkāpariśuddhau udayanācāryāḥ- kāryārambhe
children.translated_text: Thus speaking, he indicates that the conduct of the learned is the authority for auspicious invocation. In the <s>Tātparya-ṭīkā-pariśuddhi</s>, <s>Udayanācārya</s> says: At the commencement of any undertaking,

children.text:
prārabdhasyāntarāyaviraheṇa parisamāptiṃ kāmayamānāḥ
abhīṣṭadevatānamaskārapūrvakaṃ prekṣāvantaḥ pravartante/ paraṃ tu dṛśyate
tatra tatra bahuśo vyabhicāraḥ, kṛtanamaskārasyāpi samīhitāsiddheḥ,
akṛtanamaskārasyāpi samīhitasiddheśca/ na cātra 'vṛṣṭikāmaḥ kārīrīṃ
nirvapet' itivat 'prārabdhaparisamāptikāmo devatāṃ
namaskuryāt' iti śrutirasti yena vyabhicāre 'pi
karmakartṛsādhanavaiguṇyaṃ kalpayāmaḥ/ tasmāt 'arthakāma iha vaṭe
prativasantaṃ vakṣaṃ pūjayet' itivat
children.translated_text: those who are discerning proceed with obeisance to the chosen deity first, desiring the completion of what has been commenced without obstacles. However, deviation is seen here and there in many cases, since even one who has made obeisance may not achieve his desired goal, and even one who has not made obeisance may achieve his desired goal. And there is no Vedic injunction here such as 'one who desires completion of what has been commenced should make obeisance to the deity,' like the injunction 'one who desires rain should perform the <s>kārīrī</s> rite,' by which we could attribute the failure to a deficiency in the ritual, the performer, or the means. Therefore, like the popular belief that 'one who desires wealth should worship the <s>yakṣa</s> residing in a banyan tree,'

children.text:
aprāmāṇikaprasiddhivijṛmbhitametanmaṅgalācaraṇamityabhisandhāya
kimu vārtikakṛtā maṅgalaṃ na kṛtam? ityākāṅkṣāsamādhānārthaṃḥ
pūrvoktaṭīkāgantha ityavatārikāṃ kṛtvā, pratyakṣamiva
avigītaśiṣṭācāro 'pi śrutisadbhāve pramāṇameva, nirmūlasya
śiṣṭācārasyāsaṃbhavāt/ tathā ca kvacinmaṅgale samāptyabhāvaḥ
karmakartṛsādhanavaiguṇyaprayuktaḥ/ iha janmani asatyapi maṅgale
samāptistu janmāntarīyamaṅgalādhīneti samavarṇayan/ etena
śiṣṭācārānumitā śrutiḥ granthārambhe maṅgalakartavyatāyāṃ
pramāṇamiti udayanācāryāśayo 'vagamyate, maṅgalaṃ samāptiphalakamiti
ca/
children.translated_text: suspecting that this practice of auspicious invocation is a display of unauthoritative popular belief, and in order to resolve the question of why the author of the <s>Vārtika</s> did not perform the auspicious invocation, he composed the above-quoted passage from the <s>ṭīkā</s> as an introduction, explaining that the uncontested conduct of the learned, like direct perception, is indeed authoritative when a Vedic text exists, since rootless learned conduct is impossible. And thus, the absence of completion in some cases despite performing the auspicious invocation is due to deficiency in the ritual, the performer, or the means. And completion even without performing the invocation in this life is dependent on auspicious invocations performed in previous lives—thus he explained. By this, it is understood that <s>Udayanācārya</s>'s intent is that the Vedic text inferred from the conduct of the learned is the authority for the obligation to perform auspicious invocation at the commencement of a work, and that the auspicious invocation has completion as its fruit.

children.text: tatna bhūṣaṇakārāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Therein, the view of the author of the <s>Nyāya-bhūṣaṇa</s>:

children.text:
nyāyabhūṣaṇakārāḥ -
praṇāmakṛtena hi maṅlenaṃ adharmapratibandhakena adharmaṃmūlā
vighnavināyakāḥ protsāryante/ tataḥ śāstraparisamāptirityarthavān
praṇāmaḥ/ yatra tu na samāptistatra praṇāmasyāsamyakatvamanumeyaṃ
karturadharmabāhulyaṃ vā/ yatrāpyantareṇa praṇāmaṃ
śāstraparisamāptirdṛśyate, tatrāpi mānasaḥ kāyiko vā
praṇāmo 'numeyaḥ, sādhanāntarasādhyo vā dharmaḥ/ vācikapraṇāme
tvanyeṣāmapyupadeśasiddhiriti viśeṣaḥ/ yasya tu vighnaheturadharma eva
nāsti, tenāpi tadāśaṅkyā kartavya eva praṇāmaḥ/ śatrvādyāśaṅkyā
astrādisaṃgrahavaditi nirūpayantaḥ maṅgalasyāvaśyakartavyatāṃ
bodhayanti/ maṅgalakartavyatāyāṃ pramāṇaṃ tu te na pratyapādayan/
maṅgalasya samāptiphalakatvameva bhāsarvañjñābhimatam/
children.translated_text: The authors of the <s>Nyāya-bhūṣaṇa</s> state: By the auspicious invocation in the form of obeisance, which counteracts <s>adharma</s> (demerit), the obstacles rooted in <s>adharma</s> are driven away. Thence follows the completion of the treatise—thus obeisance is purposeful. Where there is no completion, one should infer either the incompleteness of the obeisance or the abundance of <s>adharma</s> in the performer. Even where completion of a treatise is seen without obeisance, one should infer a mental or physical obeisance, or else <s>dharma</s> (merit) accomplished by other means. The distinction regarding verbal obeisance is that it also accomplishes instruction for others. Even one who has no <s>adharma</s> that could cause obstacles should still perform obeisance, apprehending it might arise, just as one keeps weapons apprehending enemies—thus they demonstrate the obligatory nature of the auspicious invocation. However, they did not establish the authority for the obligation of the auspicious invocation. That the auspicious invocation has completion as its fruit is also the view accepted by <s>Bhāsarvajña</s>.

children.translated_text: The method of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system

children.text: ḥ

vaiśeṣikadarśane
'athāto dharmaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ' iti prathamasūtre ādau athaśabdaṃ
prayuñjānaḥ kaṇādo maṅgalamācarati smeti upaskārakāro vyācaṣṭe/
bhāṣyakāraḥ praśastapādācāryaḥ 'praṇamya hetumīśvaram'
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system, the author of the <s>Upaskāra</s> commentary explains that <s>Kaṇāda</s>, by employing the word 'atha' (now) at the beginning of the first <s>sūtra</s> 'athāto dharmaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ' (Now, therefore, we shall explain <s>dharma</s>), performed the auspicious invocation. The <s>bhāṣya</s> author, <s>Praśastapāda Ācārya</s>, with 'praṇamya hetum īśvaram' (having bowed to <s>Īśvara</s>, the cause),

children.text:
itīśvarapraṇāmātmakaṃ
maṅgalamanvatiṣṭhat/ tatra kiraṇāvalyām1 - kṛtamaṅgalena cārabdhaṃ
karma parisamāpyate pracīyate ca/ (pracayo nāma prāripsitasya granthasya
gurūṇā śiṣyāya dānasyāvicchedaḥ/) na cānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ
vyabhicārāt maṅgalasya nirvighnaparisamāptihetutvaṃ na bhavatīti
vācyam/ āgamamūlakasya kāryakāraṇabhāvasyābādhyatvāt/ satyapi
maṅgale samāptyabhāvastu karmakartṛsādhanavaiguṇyāditi pratyapādi/
children.translated_text: followed the auspicious invocation in the form of obeisance to <s>Īśvara</s>. There, in the <s>Kiraṇāvalī</s>: a task commenced with the auspicious invocation is brought to completion and is propagated. (Propagation means the unbroken transmission of the text from teacher to student.) Nor should one say that because of deviation in both positive and negative concomitance, the auspicious invocation is not the cause of unobstructed completion—for the causal relation based on scripture is not sublatable. The absence of completion despite the auspicious invocation was explained as due to deficiency in the ritual, the performer, or the means.

utānyasmādapi/ na tāvannamaskārādevetyasti niyamaḥ/ asatyapi

cet - kartuḥ śiṣṭatayaiva/ mleccho 'pi tāvat gurvārambhe karmaṇi na
pravartate yāvadiṣṭān na namasyati/ tathā ca paramāstikau
vātsyāyanaśabarasvāminau maṅgalaṃ
nānvatiṣṭhatāmityetadasaṃbhāvitam
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Nyāya-kandalī</s> also, while commenting on the verse 'praṇamya hetum īśvaram,' says: At the commencement of an undertaking, deity and teacher are saluted—this is the conduct of the learned. And the fruit of obeisance is the destruction of obstacles. Now, does the cessation of obstacles come from obeisance alone or from other means as well? There is indeed no rule that it comes from obeisance alone, since the <s>Nyāya</s> and <s>Mīmāṃsā Bhāṣyas</s> were completed even without obeisance. And if it can come from other means as well, then the mandatory performance of auspicious invocation would be purposeless. To this he replies: the cessation of obstacles comes from obeisance alone, because the learned invariably perform it at the commencement of works. Nor is it the case that the authors of the <s>Nyāya</s> and <s>Mīmāṃsā Bhāṣyas</s> did not perform obeisance—rather, having performed it, they simply did not include it in the text. How is this known? By the very fact that the authors were learned. Even a barbarian does not commence an important undertaking without first paying obeisance to his chosen ones. Therefore, it is inconceivable that <s>Vātsyāyana</s> and <s>Śabara Svāmin</s>, who were supremely devout, did not perform the auspicious invocation.

children.text: maṅgalācāre smṛtisaṃmatiḥ
children.translated_text: The support of <s>Smṛti</s> (traditional law) for auspicious conduct

children.text:
maṅgalācāre
smṛtirapi pramāṇam/ tathā hi manuḥ3---
children.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> is also an authority for auspicious conduct. For <s>Manu</s> says:

children.text:
"maṅgalācārayuktaḥ syāt prayatātmā
jitendriya/
children.translated_text: "One should be endowed with auspicious conduct, self-controlled, with senses subdued;

children.text:
japecca juhuyāccaiva
nityamagnimatandritaḥ//
children.translated_text: and one should always recite prayers and offer oblations into the fire, without laziness.

children.text:
maṅgalācārayuktānāṃ
nityaṃ ca prayatātmanām/
children.translated_text: For those endowed with auspicious conduct, always self-controlled,

children.text:
japatāṃ juhvatāṃ caiva
vinipāto na vidyate //"
children.translated_text: who recite prayers and offer oblations, there is no calamity."

children.text:
iti/ vinipāta
ityasya vighna ityarthaḥ/ atra dvitīyaślokaḥ maṇikāraiḥ
maṅgalavādānte pramāṇatayā udāhṛtaḥ/
children.translated_text: Here, the meaning of 'vinipāta' is 'obstacle.' The second verse here was cited by the <s>Maṇikāras</s> (authors of the <s>Maṇi</s> commentary) as an authority at the end of the discussion on <s>maṅgala</s>.

children.text: tatra itihāsasaṃmatiḥ
children.translated_text: Therein, the support of <s>Itihāsa</s> (epic literature):

children.text:
itihāsaśreṣṭhe
mahābhārate1 vyāsasaṃhitāṃ śrotumicchadbhiḥ maharṣibhiḥ prārthitaḥ
sautiḥ paurāṇikaḥ kathārambhāt prāk---
children.translated_text: In the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, the foremost among <s>itihāsas</s>, <s>Sauti</s> the reciter of <s>Purāṇas</s>, having been requested by the great sages who wished to hear the compilation of <s>Vyāsa</s>, before commencing the narration—

children.text: "ādyaṃ puruṣamīśānaṃ puruhūtaṃ puruṣṭutam/
children.translated_text: "The primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Lord, much invoked, much praised,

children.text:
ṛtamekākṣaraṃ brahma
vyaktāvyaktaṃ sanātanam//
children.translated_text: the Truth, the single-syllabled <s>Brahman</s>, manifest and unmanifest, eternal,

children.text:
asacca sadasaccaiva
yadviśvaṃ sadasatparam/
children.translated_text: both non-being and being, the universe that transcends being and non-being,

children.text:
parāvarāṇāṃ sraṣṭāraṃ
purāṇaṃ paramavyayam//
children.translated_text: the creator of the higher and the lower, ancient, supremely imperishable,

children.text:
maṅgalyaṃ maṅgalaṃ
viṣṇuṃ vareṇyamanaghaṃ śucim/
children.translated_text: the auspicious, the auspice itself, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the most excellent, the sinless, the pure—

children.text:
namaskṛtya hṛṣīkeśaṃ
carācaraguruṃ harim//
children.translated_text: having bowed to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the guru of all that moves and does not move, <s>Hari</s>,

children.text:
maharṣeḥ pūjitasyeha
sarvalokairmahātmanaḥ/
children.translated_text: of the great-souled sage worshipped here by all the worlds,

children.text:
pravakṣyāmi mataṃ puṇyaṃ
vyāsasyādbhutakarmaṇaḥ//"
children.translated_text: I shall narrate the sacred teaching of <s>Vyāsa</s>, of wondrous deeds."

children.text:
itīṣṭadevatānamaskārapūrvakaṃ kathāmārabhamāṇaḥ granthārambhe
maṅgalācaraṇasyāvaśyakartavyatāṃ nivedayati/ evaṃ viṣṇupurāṇe 'pi
parāśara2ḥ---
children.translated_text: Thus, commencing the narration with obeisance to his chosen deity, he demonstrates the obligatory nature of auspicious invocation at the beginning of a work. Similarly, in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>—

children.text:
"viṣṇuṃ grasiṣṇuṃ viśvasya sthitau sarge tathā
prabhum/
children.translated_text: "<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the devourer, the lord in preservation and creation of the universe,

children.text:
praṇamya
jagatāmīśamajamakṣayamavyayam//
children.translated_text: having bowed to the lord of the worlds, the unborn, the imperishable, the immutable,

children.text:
kathayāmi
yathāpūrvam.......'
children.translated_text: I shall narrate as it was before...'

children.text:
iti
viṣṇunamaskārapūrvakaṃ granthamārabhate sma/
children.translated_text: thus commenced his work with obeisance to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: maṇikṛnmatam
children.translated_text: The view of the <s>Maṇikāras</s>:

children.text:
maṇikārāḥ ādau
saṃpradāyamatamanusṛtya vistareṇa maṅgalasya samāptiphalakatvaṃ
sādhayāmāsuḥ/ śiṣṭācārānumitaśrutireva maṅgalakartavyatāyāṃ
pramāṇamityapi nyarūpayan/ tato maṅgalasya vighnadhvaṃsaḥ phalamiti
svasiddhāntaṃ vistareṇa samavarṇayan/
children.translated_text: The <s>Maṇikāras</s> first, following the traditional view, established at length that the auspicious invocation has completion as its fruit. They also determined that the Vedic text inferred from the conduct of the learned is indeed the authority for the obligation of the auspicious invocation. Then they expounded at length their own doctrine that the destruction of obstacles is the fruit of the auspicious invocation.

children.text: annambhaṭṭasyāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The intent of <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>:

children.text:
dīpikākārā
annambhaṭṭāḥ śiṣṭācāreṇānumitā 'samāptikāmo maṅgalamācaret'
iti śrutiḥ granthārambhe maṅgalakartavyatāyāṃ pramāṇam/ maṅgalasya
samāptiḥ phalam/ vighnadhvaṃso dvāram/ vighnasamasaṃkhyākasya maṅgalasya
kāraṇatvāt nānvayavyabhicāraḥ/ janmāntarīyamaṅgalamādāya na
vyatirekavyabhicāra iti nirūpayanti/ prakāśikāyām maṅgalasya
vighnadhvaṃsaḥ phalamiti maṇikṛnmatamapi saṃgṛhītam/ na kevalaṃ śrutiḥ
maṅgalakartavyatāyāṃ pramāṇam, api tu
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Dīpikā</s>, <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, determines: The Vedic text 'one who desires completion should perform the auspicious invocation,' inferred from the conduct of the learned, is the authority for the obligation of the auspicious invocation at the commencement of a work. Completion is the fruit of the auspicious invocation. The destruction of obstacles is the means. Since the auspicious invocation is the cause of obstacles equal in number to the invocations, there is no deviation in positive concomitance. Taking into account the auspicious invocations of previous lives, there is no deviation in negative concomitance either. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, the view of the <s>Maṇikāras</s> that the destruction of obstacles is the fruit of the auspicious invocation is also incorporated. Not only is the Vedic text the authority for the obligation of the auspicious invocation, but also

children.text:
'maṅgalaṃ kartavyaṃ
samāptiphalakatvāt' ityanumānamapi tatra pramāṇamiti
pratipādayāmbabhūvuḥ prakāśikākṛtaḥ/
children.translated_text: the inference 'the auspicious invocation ought to be performed, because it has completion as its fruit' is also an authority for it—thus the authors of the <s>Prakāśikā</s> taught.

children.text: tamovādaḥ
children.translated_text: Discussion on <s>Tamas</s> (Darkness)

children.text:
navaiva dravyāṇīti
dravyavibhajanamasaṃgatam/ pṛthivyādinavadravyavyatiriktasya
tamonāmakasya dravyasya sadbhāvāditi mīmāṃsakamatarītyā ākṣipya
tamasaḥ tejo 'bhāve 'ntarbhāvāt na tadatiriktaṃ dravyamiti dravyamiti
dīpikāyāṃ nyarūpyata/ tatra mīmāṃsakānāmayamāśayaḥ- tamaso dravyatvaṃ
tāvadavaśyamaṅgīkaraṇīyam/ 'nīlaṃ tamaḥ' iti pratītyā rūpavattvasya
'calati tamaḥ' iti pratītyā kriyāvattvasya cāvagamena
rūpavattvakriyāvattvābhyāṃ dravyatvavyāpyābhyāṃ dravyatvasiddheḥ/ tathā ca
tamo dravyaṃ nīlādiprakārakābādhitapratītiviṣayatvāt ghaṭavat
ityanumānaṃ tamaso dravyatve pramāṇam/ na ca yatra yatrālokābhāvaḥ
tatra
children.translated_text: The division of <s>dravya</s> (substance) into only nine is questioned as inconsistent, since there exists a substance called <s>tamas</s> (darkness) distinct from the nine substances beginning with <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth)—thus the objection is raised following the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> position, and in the <s>Dīpikā</s> it is determined that <s>tamas</s> is subsumed under the absence of <s>tejas</s> (light) and is therefore not a separate substance. There, the intent of the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> is as follows: The substantiality of <s>tamas</s> must certainly be accepted, since from the cognition 'darkness is blue,' possession of color is understood, and from the cognition 'darkness moves,' possession of action is understood; and since possession of color and possession of action are pervaded by substantiality, substantiality is established. Thus, the inference 'darkness is a substance, because it is the object of uncontradicted cognition qualifying it with blue and such properties, like a pot' is the authority for the substantiality of <s>tamas</s>. Nor should one say that wherever there is absence of light, there

children.text:
cākṣuṣapramāviṣayatvābhāvaḥ iti vā yatra
yatrālokābhāvavadviṣayakajñānatvaṃ tatra cākṣuṣapramātvābhāva iti vā
vyāptisattvāt 'nīlaṃ tamaḥ' iti pratyayasya pramātvāsaṃbhavāt
uktahetuḥ svarūpāsiddha iti vācyam/ ālokādyātmake tejasi
saṃyogasaṃbandhāvacchinnālokābhāvasattvena tatra
cākṣaṣupramāviṣayatvasyaiva sattvena vyabhicārāt uktavyāpterasaṃbhavāt/
na ca tejobhinnatvaṃ niveśya vyāptirvaktavyā/ tathā ca yatra yatra
tejobhinnatve sati ālokābhāvaḥ tatra tatra cākṣuṣapramāviṣayatvābhāva
iti vyāpterna vyabhicāra iti vācyam/ tathāpi tamastvena
bhavadabhimate ālokābhāve ālokasaṃyogarūpakāraṇābhāve 'pi
cākṣuṣapramāviṣayatvasyaiva sattvena vyabhicārasya durvāratvāt/ evaṃ
ālokābhāvaḥ tamaḥ, rūpapratītyabhāvaḥ tamaḥ, viyadvyāptaṃ
pārthivaparamāṇugatanailyameva tama iti pakṣāḥ na saṃgacchante/
vidhirūpeṇa nañullekharahitatayā pratīyamānasya tamasaḥ
abhāvarūpatvāsaṃbhavāt/ nailyāśrayatayā pratīyamānasya tamasaḥ
nailyarūpatvāsaṃbhavācca/ na ca vidhirūpeṇa pratīyamānatvasya
bhāvatvasādhakatve pralayavināśādipadollikhitapratītiviṣayasya
pradhvaṃsasyābhāvatvānupapattiriti vācyam/
nailyacalanādiguṇakriyāśrayasya itaraviviktasya vastunaḥ
sphuṭopalambhavat bhūtale ghaṭapralaya ityādau viviktatayā
bhāvarūpavastvantarānupalambhāt pralayasyābhāvarūpatvāt/ api ca ghaṭasya
pralayaḥ ghaṭasya vināśa ityevaṃ sapratiyogikatayā upalambhāt
pralayasyābhāvarūpatvam/ tamasastu niṣpratiyogikatayā upalambhāt
nābhāvarūpatvam/ na
children.translated_text: Or, the absence of being an object of visual <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is such that wherever there is cognition having as its object something possessing absence of light, there is absence of visual <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) — since such <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) holds. And since the cognition 'darkness is blue' cannot be a <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), the stated <s>hetu</s> (reason) is unestablished in its own nature — so it might be said. But in <s>tejas</s> (fire/light) which has the nature of light and such, since there exists absence of light delimited by the relation of contact, and since there exists the property of being an object of visual <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) in that very case, there is deviation, and hence the stated <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is impossible. Nor should one say that the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is to be stated by incorporating the qualifier 'being other than <s>tejas</s> (fire),' such that wherever there is absence of light in something other than <s>tejas</s>, there is absence of being an object of visual <s>pramā</s> — and there is no deviation. Even so, since in the absence of light as maintained by your position to be darkness, even when there is absence of the cause in the form of contact with light, the property of being an object of visual <s>pramā</s> actually obtains, the deviation is unavoidable. Thus the positions that darkness is absence of light, that darkness is absence of perception of color, and that darkness is merely the blue color residing in earthy atoms pervading space — none of these are tenable. Since darkness, which is cognized as having a positive nature without any negative particle being indicated, cannot have the nature of absence; and since darkness, which is cognized as having blue color as its substrate, cannot have the nature of mere blue color. Nor should one say that the capacity of being cognized in a positive manner to establish the nature of a positive entity leads to the impossibility of <s>pradhvaṃsa</s> (posterior absence) — the object of cognitions expressed by words like 'destruction' and 'annihilation' — being an absence. For just as a substance distinct from others possessing qualities like blue color and actions like movement is clearly apprehended, so in cases like 'the destruction of the pot on the ground,' since no other positive entity is distinctly apprehended, destruction has the nature of absence. Moreover, since destruction is apprehended as having a counter-positive — as in 'the destruction of the pot,' 'the annihilation of the pot' — destruction has the nature of absence. But since darkness is apprehended without a counter-positive, it does not have the nature of absence. Nor

children.text:
codbhūtayapavatpārthivasyodbhūtasparśavattvaniyamāt tamasaḥ
pārthivatve tatra sparśopalambhaprasaṅgaṃ iti vācyam/
indranīlamaṇyālokādīnāṃ nīlarūpavattayā pārthivatvāvaśyaṃbhāvāt
tatra vyabhicāreṇa uktaniyamāsaṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: should one say that since earthy substances with manifest form necessarily have manifest touch, if darkness were earthy there would follow the apprehension of touch in it. For since indranīla gems, light, and such things, being possessed of blue color, must necessarily be earthy, there is deviation in those cases, and the stated rule is impossible.

children.text:
nanu 'tamo na dravyam,
ālokābhāvavatve sati cākṣuṣapratyakṣaviṣayatvāt ālokābhāvavat'
ityanumānena tamaso dravyatvābhāvasiddheḥ kathaṃ tasya dravyatvam/
ghaṭādau vyabhicāravāraṇāya ālokābhāvavattve satīti viśeṣaṇamiti
cet - kimidamanumānaṃ prābhākaraiḥ prayujyate, uta naitāyikaiḥ,
āhosvit rūpamātraṃ tama iti vādibhiḥ/ nādyaḥ, tanmate
atiriktābhāvānaṅgīkāreṇa ālokābhāvarūpadṛṣṭāntasya
tadghaṭitahetoścāsiddheḥ/ na dvitīyaḥ, naiyāyikamate
ālokābhāvasyaiva tamastvāt pakṣadṛṣṭāntabhedābhāvāt/ tathā ca
ālokābhāva eva dravyabhedasādhanamiti paryavasānāt siddhasādhanaṃ
doṣaḥ iti/ na tṛtīyaḥ/
divābhītādidṛśyamānairdravyairvyabhicārāt/
mānuṣacākṣuṣaviṣayatvādityuktāvapi
yogidṛśyamānairdravyairvyabhicārāt/
children.translated_text: Now, if it is argued that through the inference 'darkness is not a <s>dravya</s> (substance), because it is an object of visual <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) while possessing absence of light, like the absence of light itself,' the absence of <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood) of darkness is established — how then can it have <s>dravyatva</s>? The qualifier 'while possessing absence of light' is added to exclude deviation in cases like pots and such — if so, then: Is this inference employed by the <s>Prābhākara</s> school, or by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, or by those who hold that darkness is merely color? Not the first, because in their view, since they do not accept additional absences, the example in the form of absence of light and the <s>hetu</s> (reason) constituted by it are unestablished. Not the second, because in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, since absence of light itself is darkness, there is no difference between <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example). And since it ultimately amounts to saying that absence of light alone establishes a distinct <s>dravya</s> (substance), the defect of <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already established) arises. Not the third either, because there is deviation through substances seen in daylight and by the fearful and such. Even if one says 'because it is an object of human visual perception,' there is deviation through substances perceived by <s>yogins</s>.

children.text:
tathā ca tamaso
dravyatve siddhe gandhaśūnyatvāt pṛthivītvābhāve nīlarūpavattvāt
jalāditvābhāve ca siddhe atiriktadravyatvaṃ sidhyatīti/
children.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood) of darkness is established, since it is devoid of smell and hence the absence of <s>pṛthivītva</s> (earthiness) is established, and since it possesses blue color and hence the absence of being water and such is established, its nature as a distinct <s>dravya</s> (substance) is proven.

children.text: naiyāyikamatam
children.translated_text: The <s>Naiyāyika</s> view:

children.text:
prauḍhaṃ prakāśakaṃ ca
yattejaḥ tatsāmānyābhāvastama ityetāvataivopapattau
atiriktadravyatvakalpane pramāṇābhāvaḥ/ tamo na dravyaṃ
ālokāsahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyatvāt ālokābhāvavat ityanumānaṃ
tamaso dravyatvābhāve pramāṇam/ tejassāmānyābhāvarūpaṃ tamaḥ pakṣa.,
tejoviśeṣābhāvo dṛṣṭānta iti pakṣadṛṣṭāntabhedābhāva iti
dūṣaṇasya nāvakāśaḥ/ atha vā tamaśśabdavācyaṃ pakṣaḥ ālokābhāvo
dṛṣṭānta iti na doṣaḥ/ 'nīlaṃ tamaḥ' 'calati tamaḥ' iti
pratītyorbhramatvāt na tābhyāṃ rūpavattvaṃ kriyāvattvaṃ vā tamasaḥ
sidhyatīti naiyāyikamatam/
children.translated_text: When the matter is fully explained by saying that darkness is the general absence of that <s>tejas</s> (fire/light) which is luminous and illuminating, there is no evidence for postulating a separate <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood). The inference 'darkness is not a <s>dravya</s> (substance), because it is grasped by the eye without the aid of light, like the absence of light' is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) for the absence of <s>dravyatva</s> in darkness. Darkness being the general absence of <s>tejas</s> is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus), and the absence of a particular <s>tejas</s> is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) — so the objection of no difference between <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> has no scope. Alternatively, that which is denoted by the word 'darkness' is the <s>pakṣa</s>, and absence of light is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> — so there is no defect. Since the cognitions 'darkness is blue' and 'darkness moves' are erroneous, neither <s>rūpavattva</s> (possession of color) nor <s>kriyāvattva</s> (possession of action) of darkness is established through them — this is the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view.

children.text:
atrāhuḥ -
rūpādimattāpratīterbhramatvaṃ na vaktuṃ śakyam/ 'nīlaṃ tamaḥ' 'calati
tamaḥ' iti pratītyanantaraṃ 'nedaṃ tamo nīlam' 'nedaṃ tamaścalati'
iti bādhakapratītyanudayena tasyāḥ bhramatvāyogāt/ kiṃ ca
tamasastejobhāvarūpatve kiñjinniṣṭhanīlarūpāropeṇa nīlaṃ tama iti
pratītirūpapādanīyā/ tathā sati kiñcinniṣṭhapītarūpāropeṇa kadācit
pītaṃ tama iti pratītirapi syāt/
maṇimayameruśikharādirūpādyāropeṇa nīlaṃ nabhaḥ pītaṃ nabhaḥ
ityādipratītivat/ tasmādanyadīyanīlarūpādarāropāsambhavena
rūpavattāpratīterbhramatvāyogena pramātvasyaivāvaśyakatayā
nīlarūpavattvādinā
children.translated_text: To this they reply: The erroneousness of the cognition of possession of color and such cannot be maintained. After the cognitions 'darkness is blue' and 'darkness moves,' since there does not arise a sublating cognition such as 'this darkness is not blue' or 'this darkness does not move,' the erroneousness of that cognition is untenable. Moreover, if darkness has the nature of absence of <s>tejas</s> (fire/light), then the cognition 'darkness is blue' must be explained through the superimposition of blue color belonging to something else. In that case, sometimes the cognition 'darkness is yellow' should also arise through the superimposition of yellow color belonging to something else — just as the cognitions 'the sky is blue' and 'the sky is yellow' arise through the superimposition of color from jewel-crested mountain peaks and such. Therefore, since superimposition of blue color belonging to another is impossible, and since the erroneousness of the cognition of possession of color is untenable, and since its being a <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is necessary, through the possession of blue color and such

children.text:
tamaso 'tiriktadravyatvaṃ
siddhameva/
children.translated_text: the nature of darkness as a distinct <s>dravya</s> (substance) is indeed established.

children.text:
nanu
niruktayuktibhistamaso 'tiriktarūpavaddravyatvāṅgīkāre ālo
kasahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyatvaṃ syāt/ dravyavṛttilaukikaviṣayatāsaṃbandhena
cākṣuṣatvāvacchinnaṃ prati ālokasahakṛtacakṣuṣaḥ kāraṇatvāvaśyaṃbhāvāt
tamoviṣayakacākṣuṣasya ālokavirahe 'pi jāyamānatvānna
tamaso 'tiriktadravyatvasiddhiḥ/ na ca tamobhinnadravyacākṣuṣatvāvacchinnaṃ
pratyevālokasya kāraṇatvāṅgīkārāt nānupapattiriti vācyam/
kāryatāvacchedake tamobhinnatvaniveśena gauravāpatteriti cet - na/
bhavanmate 'pi tejoviṣayaka pratyakṣe tejo 'ntarasaṃnikarṣānapekṣaṇena
ālokasahakṛtacakṣuṣaḥ kāraṇatve alokātmakadravyacākṣuṣānupapattyā
children.translated_text: Now, if the nature of darkness as a distinct color-possessing <s>dravya</s> (substance) is accepted through the aforementioned reasoning, it should be graspable by the eye aided by light. Since for visual cognition delimited by the relation of inherence-based objecthood residing in <s>dravya</s> (substance), the eye aided by light is necessarily a cause, and since visual cognition of darkness arises even without light, the establishment of darkness as a distinct <s>dravya</s> is not achieved. Nor should one say there is no difficulty because the causality of light is accepted only for visual cognition delimited by the qualifier 'pertaining to substances other than darkness.' If it is objected that incorporating 'being other than darkness' in the delimitor of the effect-relation leads to the fault of complexity — no, this is not valid. In your view too, regarding the perception of <s>tejas</s> (fire/light), since another <s>tejas</s> as contact is not required, due to the impossibility of the eye aided by light being a cause for visual cognition of light-constituted <s>dravya</s>,

children.text:
tejobhinnadravyacākṣuṣatvāvacchinnaṃ pratyeva
ālokasahakṛtacakṣuṣaḥ kāraṇatvaṃ vācyam/ tathā ca
tejoviṣayakacākṣuṣaṃ prati ālokasahakṛtacakṣuṣaḥ kāraṇatvābhāvena
andhakāre sūvarṇātmakatejaścākṣuṣāpattyā tadvāraṇāya suvarṇabhinnaṃ
yattejaḥ tadbhinnadravyacākṣuṣaṃ prati ālokasahakṛtacakṣuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: the causality of the eye aided by light must be stated only for visual cognition delimited by 'pertaining to substances other than <s>tejas</s>.' And thus, since the eye aided by light is not a cause for visual cognition of <s>tejas</s>, to avoid the consequence that golden <s>tejas</s> would be visually perceived in darkness, and to prevent that, one must say that the eye aided by light is a cause for visual cognition of substances other than gold which are other than <s>tejas</s>;

children.text:
kāraṇatvaṃ vācyamiti
kāryatāvacchedakagauravasya duṣpariharatvāt/ ataḥ tamobhinnaṃ
suvarṇabhinnatejobhinnaṃ ca yaddravyaṃ tadviṣayakacākṣuṣaṃ pratyeva
ālokasahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyatvābhāve 'pi kṣativirahāt
tamaso 'tiriktadravyatvasiddhirniṣpratyūhaiveti/
children.translated_text: thus the complexity in the delimitor of the effect-relation is difficult to avoid. Therefore, even if there is no absence of being graspable by the eye aided by light for visual cognition of <s>dravya</s> (substance) that is other than darkness, other than gold, and other than <s>tejas</s>, there is no harm, and the establishment of darkness as a distinct <s>dravya</s> is entirely unobstructed.

children.text: suvarṇavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Investigation regarding gold

children.text:
tatra
prācīnamatam
children.translated_text: Here, the ancient view:

children.text:
nyāyasūtratadbhāṣyavaiśeṣikasūtreṣu suvarṇasya
taijasatvaprastāvo na dṛśyate/ paraṃ tu
'trapusīsaloharajatasuvarṇānāmagnisaṃyogāddravatvamadbhiḥ
sāmānyam' (vai. sū. 2-1-7) iti sūtraṃ suvarṇasya naimittikadravatvaṃ
bodhayati/ tatra sūtre 'taijasānām' iti padamadhikamāsīditi
jñāyate/ yato vedāntadeśikaiḥ sarvārthaṃsiddhau1 --
'trapusīsalohasuvarṇānāṃ taijasānāmagnisaṃyogāt dravatvamadbhiḥ
sāmānyam' iti
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyasūtras</s>, their <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary), and the <s>Vaiśeṣikasūtras</s>, no discussion of the fiery nature of gold is found. However, the <s>sūtra</s> 'tin, lead, iron, silver, and gold have fluidity from contact with fire, which is common with water' (<s>Vaiśeṣikasūtra</s> 2-1-7) indicates the adventitious fluidity of gold. In that <s>sūtra</s>, the word 'of fiery substances' was additionally present, as is known. For <s>Vedāntadeśika</s> in the <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> has quoted

children.text:
vaiśeṣikasūtramuddhṛtamasti/ tena ca suvarṇasya taijasatvaṃ
kaṇādasyāpi saṃmatamiti jñāyate/ praśastapādabhāṣye1
children.translated_text: the <s>Vaiśeṣikasūtra</s> as 'tin, lead, iron, and gold, being fiery, have fluidity from contact with fire, which is common with water.' From this it is known that the fiery nature of gold was accepted by <s>Kaṇāda</s> as well. In <s>Praśastapāda's</s> <s>Bhāṣya</s>,

children.text:
tejonirūpaṇaprakaraṇe
viṣayarūpaṃ tejaḥ bhaumadivyodaryākarajabhedāt caturdhā vibhajya
'ākarajaṃ suvarṇādi' ityetāvanmātramuktam/ tatra kandalīkāraḥ2 --
'ākaraḥ sthānaviśeṣaḥ/ tasmin suvarṇarajatādi taijasaṃ dravyaṃ jāyate/
suvarṇādīnāṃ taijasatve tāvadāgamaḥ pramāṇam/ nyāyaścābhihitaḥ/
bhogināmadṛṣṭavaśena bhūyasāṃ pārthivāvayavānāmupaṣṭambhāt
anudbhūtarūpasparśaṃ piṇḍībhāvayogyaṃ suvarṇādikamārabhyate/ tatra
pārthivadravyasamavetā rasādaya upalabhyante' ityāha/ atra āgamapadena
'agnerapatyaṃ prathamaṃ hiraṇyam' iti śrutivākyaṃ vivakṣitam/
children.translated_text: in the section on the examination of <s>tejas</s> (fire), having divided perceptible <s>tejas</s> into four kinds — terrestrial, celestial, intestinal, and mineral — only this much was stated: 'mineral is gold and such.' There the <s>Kandalī</s> commentator states: 'A mine is a particular location. In it, golden, silver, and other fiery substances are produced. As for the fiery nature of gold and such, scripture is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (authority). And reasoning has also been stated. Through the support of predominantly earthy atoms due to the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) of beings who are to enjoy them, gold and such, having unmanifest color and touch, capable of forming aggregates, are produced. In those, taste and other qualities inherent in earthy substances are perceived.' Here, by the word 'scripture' the Vedic statement 'gold is the first offspring of fire' is intended.

children.text: 'kṣititejasornaimittikadravatvayogaḥ'3
children.translated_text: 'Earth and fire have adventitious fluidity' —

children.text:
iti
bhāṣyavyākhyāvasare kandalyāṃ suvarṇasya taijasatvasādhako
nyāyo 'bhihitaḥ/ sa ca - sūvarṇe dravatvaṃ nāsti/ gurutvamiva
pṛthivyāmeva vidyamānaṃ dravatvaṃ dahyamāneṣu suvarṇeṣu
saṃyuktasamavāyāt pratīyata iti cet - na/
pārthivadravatvasyātyantāgnisaṃyogena bhasmībhāvadarśanāt
suvarṇadravatvasya cātyantāgnisaṃyoge 'pi bhasmībhāvavirahāt suvarṇaṃ
na pārthivam iti/
children.translated_text: during the occasion of commenting on this <s>bhāṣya</s> passage, in the <s>Kandalī</s>, a reasoning establishing the fiery nature of gold was stated. It is as follows: fluidity does not exist in gold. If it is said that fluidity, which exists only in earth like heaviness, is perceived in gold being heated through the relation of conjunction with what is conjoined — no. Because earthy fluidity is observed to result in reduction to ashes through extreme contact with fire, and because gold's fluidity does not result in reduction to ashes even through extreme contact with fire, gold is not earthy.

children.text:
kiraṇāvalyāmapi4 --
'suvarṇādikaṃ na pārthivam
atyanatānalasaṃyoge 'pyaparāvartamānarūpavattvāt jalavat'
ityanumānena suvarṇasya pṛthivībhinnatvaṃ prasādhya
sāṃsiddhikadravatvaśaityayorabhāvāt
snehāvinābhūtadravyāntarasaṃgrahānupalambhācca jalabhinnatvaṃ saṃsādhya,
rūpavattvāt vāyuprabhṛtyanyatvaṃ sādhayitvā pariśeṣāt taijasatvaṃ
prasādhitam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kiraṇāvalī</s> as well — through the inference 'gold and such are not earthy, because they possess color that does not reverse even through extreme contact with fire, like water,' the otherness of gold from earth was established; and having established its otherness from water due to the absence of natural fluidity and coldness and the non-observation of inclusion in another substance inseparable from unctuousness; and having established its otherness from wind and such because of possessing color — by elimination, its fiery nature was established.

children.text: maṇikārāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The view of <s>Maṇikāra</s> (<s>Maṇikaṇṭha</s>):

children.text:
maṇikārā api
kandalīkiraṇāvalyādṛtaṃ panthānamevānusṛtyānumānena suvarṇasya
taijasatvaṃ sādhitavantaḥ/ tatrānuktāni anyānyapi kānicidanumānāni
maṇau pradarśitānīti viśeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇikāra</s> also, following the very path traced by the <s>Kandalī</s> and <s>Kiraṇāvalī</s>, established the fiery nature of gold through inference. The distinction is that certain additional inferences not stated there were presented in the <s>Maṇi</s>.

children.text: tāni yathā ---
children.translated_text: They are as follows:

children.text:
( 1 )
atyantāgnisaṃyogi pītarūpavaddravyaṃ
vijātīyarūpapratibandhakadravardravyasaṃyuktam, naktandivamagnisaṃyoge 'pi
children.translated_text: (1) A substance possessing yellow color that is in extreme contact with fire is conjoined with a fluid substance that obstructs color of a different kind; even when in contact with fire day and night,

children.text:
pītarūpātiriktarūpānāśrayatvāt,
tāvatparyantamagnisaṃyuktajalamadhyasthapītaṭavat/
children.translated_text: it does not become the substrate of any color other than yellow — like a yellow lump situated in water that is in contact with fire for that duration.

children.text:
( 2 )
atyantāgnisaṃyogenānucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇaṃ taijasam
jalapṛthivībhyāmanyatve sati rūpavattvāt
children.translated_text: (2) That whose substrate of fluidity is not destroyed by extreme contact with fire is fiery, because it possesses color while being other than water and earth —

children.text: vahnivat/
children.translated_text: like fire.

children.text:
( 3 ) pītaṃ
dravatvādhikaraṇaṃ dravatvocchedapratibandhakadravadravyasaṃyuktam
children.translated_text: (3) That which is yellow and a substrate of fluidity is conjoined with a fluid substance that obstructs the destruction of fluidity;

children.text:
atyantāgnisaṃyoge 'pyanucchidyamānadravatvādhārapārthivatvāt
kvathyamānajalamadhyasthitaghṛtavat/
children.translated_text: because its substrate of earthy fluidity is not destroyed even by extreme contact with fire — like ghee situated in water being boiled.

children.text:
( 4 ) vivādādhyāsitaṃ
dravatvādhikaraṇaṃ taijasaṃ asati dravadravyasaṃyoge
children.translated_text: (4) The substrate of fluidity that is under dispute is fiery; in the absence of conjunction with a fluid substance,

children.text:
atyantāgnisaṃyoge 'pyanucchidyamānadravatvādhāratvāt yannaivaṃ
tannaivaṃ yathā jalaṃ ghṛtaṃ vā/
children.translated_text: because it is a substrate of fluidity not destroyed even by extreme contact with fire — whatever is not thus is not thus, just as water or ghee.

children.text:
( 5 ) tejastvaṃ
nādravarūpavanmātravṛtti rūpavadvṛttidravyatvasākṣādvyāpyajātitvāt
pṛthivītvavat/
children.translated_text: (5) <s>Tejastva</s> (the universal 'fire-ness') does not reside only in what possesses non-fluid form, because it is a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that directly pervades <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood) residing in what possesses form — like <s>pṛthivītva</s> (the universal 'earthiness').

children.text: yadvā
children.translated_text: Or alternatively:

children.text:
tejastvaṃ drutavṛtti
rūpavadvṛttidravyatvasākṣādvyāpyajātitvāt jalatvavat/
children.translated_text: <s>Tejastva</s> (fire-ness) resides in what is fluid, because it is a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that directly pervades <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood) residing in what possesses form — like <s>jalatva</s> (the universal 'water-ness').

children.text:
( 6 ) suvarṇārambhakāḥ
paramāṇavaḥ na pārthivāḥ
atyantāgnisaṃyogenānucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇatvāt
children.translated_text: (6) The <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms) that constitute gold are not earthy, because they are substrates of fluidity not destroyed by extreme contact with fire —

children.text:
jalaparamāṇuvat/
taijasā vā tata eva, yannaivaṃ tannaivaṃ yathā ghṛtaparamāṇuḥ/
children.translated_text: like water <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms). Or they are fiery, for the same reason — whatever is not thus is not thus, just as a ghee <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom).

children.text:
( 7 ) pārthivārabdhaṃ
taijasārabdhaṃ vā suvarṇamapārthivaṃ taijasaṃ vā
children.translated_text: (7) Gold, whether produced from earthy or from fiery constituents, is non-earthy or fiery,

children.text:
atyantāgnisaṃyoge 'pyanucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇaparamāṇvārabdhatvāt
iti vā/
children.translated_text: because it is produced from <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms) that are substrates of fluidity not destroyed even by extreme contact with fire.

children.text:
dīpikāyāmapyannambhaṭṭaḥ imāmeva rītimavalambya suvarṇasya
taijasatvaṃ sādhayati/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> also, <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s> establishes the fiery nature of gold following this very method.

children.text:
ekadeśimatena suvarṇasya
pārthivatvam
children.translated_text: According to the <s>ekadeśī</s> (partial) view, gold is earthy (<s>pārthiva</s>).

children.text:
muktāvalīvyākhyāne
dinakarīye1 --- 'navīnāstu' ityādinā suvarṇasya pārthivatvasādhakaṃ
matāntaramupanyastam/ teṣāmāśayastu 'pītaṃ suvarṇaṃ drutam' iti
pratītyā pītarūpavati suvarṇe ata eva pārthive dravatvavattvamavagamyate/
tathā pratīyamānasya pārthivadravatvasya atitāpe 'pyanucchedāt tatra
vyabhicāro durvāraḥ/ na ca tādṛśapratītirbhramarūpeti vācyam/
bādhakābhāvāt/ na ca tasya pārthivatve agnisaṃyogāttadīyarūpanāśaḥ
kuto na bhavatīti vācyam/ anubhavabalena rūpanāśaṃ prati tādātmyena
suvarṇasya pratibandhakatvāṅgīkārāditi/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Muktāvalī</s> commentary called <s>Dinakarī</s> — by the passage beginning 'the moderns however,' an alternative view establishing the earthy nature of gold is presented. Their intent is as follows: from the cognition 'gold is yellow and fluid,' fluidity is apprehended in gold which possesses yellow color and is therefore earthy. Since the earthy fluidity thus cognized is not destroyed even by extreme heat, the counter-example (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) there is irrefutable. Nor should it be said that such a cognition is erroneous, because there is no sublating cognition. Nor should it be said: if gold is earthy, why does its color not get destroyed by contact with fire? — because, by the force of experience, the obstructive nature of gold through identity with respect to the destruction of color is accepted.

children.text:
atredaṃ vicāraṇīyam
--- pratibandhakābhāvaviśiṣṭaḥ atyantāgnisaṃyogaḥ pārthivadravatvanāśaṃ
prati heturiti
children.translated_text: Here the following is to be examined — extreme contact with fire, qualified by the absence of an obstructor, is the cause of the destruction of earthy fluidity;

children.text:
kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ
āvaśyakaḥ/ tatra suvarṇasthapārthivabhāgamatadravatvanāśarūpakāryasya abhāvaḥ
pratibandhakābhāvaviśiṣṭātyantāgnisaṃyogarūpakāraṇābhāvaprayuktaḥ
iti nirvivādam/ tatra tādṛśaviśiṣṭābhāvarūpaḥ kāraṇābhāvaḥ na
viśeṣyābhāvāt, atyantāgnisaṃyogarūpasya viśeṣyasya yatra sattvāt/
kiṃ tu pratibandhakābhāvarūpasya viśeṣaṇasyā bhāvādeva vaktavya iti
pratibandhaka kiñcit dravadravyāntaraṃ tatrāstīti vaktavyam/ tasyāpi
pṛthivītve taddravatvanāśapratibandhakaṃ dravyāntaraṃ tasyāpi
tathetyanavasthā syāt/ ataḥ pratibandhakāntaraṃ vinā
avinaśyaddravatvādeva tanna pṛthivī iti/
children.translated_text: the causal relation is necessary. There, the absence of the effect in the form of non-destruction of the fluidity of the earthy component in gold is due to the absence of the cause in the form of extreme contact with fire qualified by the absence of an obstructor — this is undisputed. There, the absence of the cause in the form of the absence of such a qualified [entity] is not due to the absence of the qualificand, since the qualificand in the form of extreme contact with fire is present there. Rather, it must be stated that it is due to the absence of the qualifier in the form of the absence of an obstructor — hence some other fluid substance serving as an obstructor must be posited there. If that too is earthy, then another substance obstructing the destruction of its fluidity [must be posited], and of that too likewise — leading to infinite regress. Therefore, since it has a fluidity that does not perish without [positing] another obstructor, that [gold] is not earth.

children.text:
dīpikākārāḥ
pārthivabhāgasyāpi dravatvaṃ tejobhāgasyāpi dravatvamaṅgīkurvanti/
'pītadravyadravatvanāśa' 'dravadravyāntara' iti padayoḥ svārasyāt/
muktāvalyāṃ tu 'jalamadhyasthamaṣīkṣodavattasyādrutatvāt' iti granthena
pārthivabhāgasya dravatvābhāva eva pratipāditaḥ/ ata eva tadanusāreṇa
suvarṇasya taijasatvasādhakamanumānāntaraṃ muktāvalyāmupanyastamiti
children.translated_text: The authors of the <s>Dīpikā</s> accept fluidity of both the earthy component and the fiery component. This is evident from the natural meaning of the terms 'destruction of fluidity of the yellow substance' and 'another fluid substance.' But in the <s>Muktāvalī</s>, by the passage 'like ink-powder in the midst of water, since it is not fluid,' the absence of fluidity in the earthy component is established. Accordingly,

children.text:
bālapriyākārāḥ
vistareṇa nirūpayanti/
children.translated_text: the authors of the <s>Bālapriyā</s> explain at length that another inference establishing the fiery nature of gold is presented in the <s>Muktāvalī</s>.

children.text: vāyupratyakṣavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Investigation of the perceptibility of wind (<s>vāyu</s>)

children.text:
dīpikākārāḥ
sparśānumeyo vāyurityādinā sparśaliṅgakānumānavedyatvaṃ vāyoḥ
prasādhya rūparahitatvāt vāyuḥ na pratyakṣavedya iti nyarūpayan/
etattattvamadhunā parīkṣyate/
children.translated_text: The authors of the <s>Dīpikā</s>, having established through the passage beginning 'wind is inferred through touch' that wind is knowable through inference based on the mark of touch, demonstrated that wind is not an object of perception because it is devoid of color. The truth of this is now examined.

children.text:
bahidindriyajanyadravyapratyakṣasāmānyaṃ prati udbhūtarūpaṃ
kāraṇam/ tathā ca vāyorudbhūtarūpavirahāt na pratyakṣagocaratvam,
kiṃ tvanumānaikavedyatā/ tathā ca vaiśeṣikaṃ sūtram --- 'sparśaśca
vāyoḥ' [vai. sū. 2-1-9] iti/ caśabdena śabdadhṛtikampā gṛhyanta/
ataḥ sparśādibhirvāyuranumeyaḥ, na tu pratyakṣa iti sūtrārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: A manifest color (<s>udbhūtarūpa</s>) is the cause of substance-perception generated by external sense organs in general. Accordingly, since wind lacks manifest color, it is not an object of perception, but is knowable only through inference. And thus the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> <s>sūtra</s> — 'And touch [is the mark] of wind' (<s>Vaiśeṣikasūtra</s> 2.1.9). By the word 'and,' sound, support, and movement are included. Therefore, wind is inferable through touch and the rest, but not perceptible — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text:
tathā ca
praśastapādabhāṣyam1 ---
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Praśastapāda-bhāṣya</s> —

children.text: 'viṣayastūpalabhyamānasparśādhiṣṭhānabhūtaḥ
children.translated_text: 'The object [wind] is the substratum of apprehended touch,

children.text: sparśaṃśabdadhṛtikampaliṅgaḥ'
children.translated_text: and is indicated by the marks of touch, sound, support, and movement.'

children.text:
iti/ tatra
kandalīkāraḥ2 --- na tāvadvāyorastitve pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam,
sparśādanyasya tvacā agrahaṇāt/ na ca vāyurvātīti jñānāt vāyuḥ
pratyakṣa iti vācyam/ tasya jñānasya sparśaliṅgakānumitirūpatvāt/
yatra yatra spārśanapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ tatra tatra cākṣuṣapratyakṣaviṣayatvamiti
vyāpteḥ ghaṭādau darśanāt rūpābhāvena vāyau cākṣaṣatvarūpasya
vyāpakasya
children.translated_text: Thus. There the author of the <s>Kandalī</s> [says] — perception is not a valid means of knowledge for the existence of wind, because nothing other than touch is grasped by the skin. Nor should it be said that wind is perceptible from the cognition 'the wind blows,' because that cognition is in the nature of inference based on the mark of touch. Wherever there is the character of being an object of tactile perception, there is also the character of being an object of visual perception — this is the invariable concomitance, observed in cases like a pot. Due to the absence of color in wind, when the pervader in the form of visual perceptibility

children.text:
nivṛttau tadvyāpyaṃ
spārśanatvamapi nivartate/ ato vāyurna pratyakṣaviṣayaḥ, api tvanumeya
iti nyarūpayat/
children.translated_text: ceases, its pervasion — the character of being a tactile object — also ceases. Therefore wind is not an object of perception, but is rather inferable — thus he demonstrated.

children.text: maṇikāramatam
children.translated_text: The view of <s>Maṇikāra</s> (the author of <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s>)

children.text:
dravyaviṣayakaspārśanaṃ prati nodbhūtasparśamātraṃ prayojakam/
tathā sati udbhūtasparśāśrayasya nidāghoṣmaṇaḥ pratyakṣatayā
tadvṛttisaṃkhyāderapi pratyakṣatā syāt/ yogyavyaktivṛtteḥ saṃkhyāyāḥ
yogyatvamiti niyamāt/ na khalūṣmaṇi kareṇa parāmṛṣṭe 'pi
tadgatāṃ saṃkhyāṃ ko 'pyadhyakṣayati/ nāpi dravyapratyakṣaṃ prati
udbhūtarūpamātraṃ prayojakam, tathā sati
children.translated_text: Mere manifest touch is not the operative cause for tactile perception of substances. For if it were, then since summer heat possessing manifest touch is perceptible, the number and other properties residing in it would also be perceptible. Because number, which resides in a suitable universal-instance, has [such] suitability as a rule. But surely, even when one touches heat with the hand, no one perceives the number residing in it. Nor is mere manifest color the operative cause for substance-perception, for if it were,

children.text:
udbhūtarūpavataḥ
candrādyudyotasyāpi pratyakṣatayā tadgatasaṃkhyāyā api pratyakṣatā
prasajyeta/ na hi nipuṇamavalokayannapi candraprabhādigataṃ saṃkhyādikaṃ
kaścit paśyati/ ataḥ pratyekaṃ vyabhicārāt udbhūtasparśaḥ
udbhūtarūpaṃ cetyubhayamapi dravyapratyakṣatve prayojakamiti vaktavyam/
candrādyālokaḥ udbhūtarūpavānapi udbhūtasparśavānna bhavati/
nidāghoṣmā udbhūtasparśavānapi nodbhūtarūpavān/
atastayorapratyakṣatvāt tadgatasaṃkhyāyāḥ pratyakṣatā āpādayituṃ na
śakyate/ tathā ca vāyurudbhūtasparśavānapi nodbhūtarūpavāniti na
pratyakṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: since moonlight and other luminosities possessing manifest color would also be perceptible, the number residing in them would also have to be perceptible. But no one perceives the number and such properties residing in moonlight, even when observing it carefully. Therefore, since there is deviation in each case separately, it must be said that both manifest touch and manifest color together are the operative causes for substance-perceptibility. Moonlight possesses manifest color but not manifest touch. Summer heat possesses manifest touch but not manifest color. Therefore, since both are imperceptible, the perceptibility of the number residing in them cannot be established. And thus, wind too, though possessing manifest touch, lacks manifest color, and therefore is not perceptible.

children.text:
api ca dravyapratyakṣaṃ
prati nodbhūtasparśaḥ kāraṇam/ tathā sati pakṣikāṇḍe calati
pūrvadeśavibhāgottaradeśasaṃyogayoḥ pratyakṣatā na syāt/
prabhāmaṇḍalātmakayoḥ pūrvottaradeśayoḥ udbhūtasparśaśūnyatvāt/ ata
udbhūtarūpameva dravyapratyakṣatāyāṃ tantramiti saṃpradāyavidaḥ/
tanmate 'pi udbhūtarūpaśūnyo vāyurapratyakṣa eveti maṇikārāḥ
pratyapīpadan/
children.translated_text: Moreover, manifest touch is not a cause for substance-perception. For if it were, when a bird's feather moves, the perception of the contact with the subsequent location and separation from the prior location would not be possible — since the prior and subsequent locations consisting of the luminous aura are devoid of manifest touch. Therefore, manifest color alone is the governing factor for substance-perceptibility — so say those who know the tradition. Even on that view, wind, being devoid of manifest color, is imperceptible — thus the authors of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Tattvacintāmaṇi) have established.

children.text:
evaṃ ca
bahirindriyajanyadravyapratyakṣaṃ prati udbhūtarūpasya kāraṇatve niścite
'vāyuḥ bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayaḥ pratyakṣasparśāśrayatvā'
dityanumāne
pakṣadharmadravyatvāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakamudabhūtarūpavattvamupādhiḥ/ tathā ca
vāyuḥ bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣāviṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, when it is determined that manifest color is the cause for substance-perception generated by external sense organs, in the inference 'wind is an object of perception generated by external sense organs, because it is the substratum of perceptible touch,' the property of possessing manifest color, which pervades the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) delimited by substance-hood, is the imposed condition (<s>upādhi</s>). And thus, wind is not an object of perception generated by external sense organs —

children.text:
rūpaśūnyadravyatvāt
ākāśavadityanumānena vāyorapratyakṣatvaṃ sidhyatīti
maṇikāranirūpaṇasya sārāṃśaḥ/ dīpikākāro 'pyamumeva
panthānamavalalambe/
children.translated_text: this is established by the inference 'because it is a substance devoid of color, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space).' This is the essence of the demonstration by the <s>Maṇikāra</s>. The author of the <s>Dīpikā</s> also followed this very path.

children.text:
muktāvalyāṃ vāyoḥ
pratyakṣatvopapādanam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Muktāvalī</s>, the establishment of the perceptibility of wind.

children.text:
muktāvalyāṃ1navīnāstu ityādinā vāyoḥ pratyakṣattvaṃ
vyavāsthāpi/ tathā hi - bahirindriyajanyadravyapratyakṣatvāvacchinnaṃ prati na
rūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ, pramāṇābhāvāt/ api tu cākṣuṣapratyakṣe rūpaṃ,
children.translated_text: In the <s>Muktāvalī</s>, by the passage beginning 'the moderns however,' the perceptibility of wind is established. Thus — color is not the cause of substance-perception delimited by external-sense-organ-generated perceptibility, because there is no valid proof. Rather, in visual perception, color [is the cause],

children.text:
spārśanapratyakṣe sparśaḥ
kāraṇam/ tathā ca sparśāśrayasya vāyoḥ tvācapratyakṣaviṣayatve na
kimapi bādhakam/ yathā hi udbhūtasparśaśūnyāyā api prabhāyāḥ 'prabhāṃ
paśyāmi' ityanubhavabalāt cākṣuṣapratyakṣaviṣayatvamupeyate, tathā
'vāyuṃ spṛśāmi' ityanubhavāt udbhūtarūpaśūnyasyāpi vāyoḥ
spārśanapratyakṣaviṣayatve ko virodhaḥ? tarhi yogyavāyuvṛttiḥ
saṃkhyāpi gṛhyeteti maṇyuktadoṣasya kaḥ parihāra iti cet - ayam/
sajātīyasaṃvalanarūpāddoṣāt kvacit vāyoḥ saṃkhyā na gṛhyate/
doṣābhāve tu saṃkhyāgrahaṇamiṣṭameveti/
children.translated_text: and in tactile perception, touch is the cause. Accordingly, there is no obstacle to wind, the substratum of touch, being an object of tactile perception. Just as luminous radiance (<s>prabhā</s>), though devoid of manifest touch, is accepted as an object of visual perception by the force of the experience 'I see the radiance,' similarly, what objection is there to wind, though devoid of manifest color, being an object of tactile perception, given the experience 'I touch the wind'? If [one objects:] then the number residing in wind, being suitable, would also be grasped — what is the answer to the defect raised by the <s>Maṇi</s>? The answer is this: due to the defect in the form of proximity to similar entities (<s>sajātīya-saṃvalana</s>), in some cases the number of wind is not grasped. But in the absence of such a defect, the grasping of number is quite acceptable.

children.text:
vastutastu pakṣikāṇḍe
gacchati pūrvottarasaṃyogavibhāgau pratyakṣau/ tatrāśrayasya
prabhātmakadeśasyāpratyakṣatve tadāśrita saṃyogavibhāgayorapratyakṣatā
syāditi yuktyā prabhāyāḥ pratyakṣatve 'pi vāyorna tathātvamiti
maṇikārairuktatvāt prabhādṛṣṭāntena vāyoḥ pratyakṣatā sādhayituṃ na
śakyate/ vāyau tu naitādṛśī yuktirasti/ ato vāyurapratyakṣa eveti
dinakaryādau2 spaṣṭam/
children.translated_text: But in truth, when a bird's feather moves, the contact and separation with the prior and subsequent locations are perceptible. If the substratum in the form of the luminous location were imperceptible, the contact and separation residing in it would be imperceptible — on this reasoning, even if the perceptibility of radiance is [granted], wind is not similarly [perceptible] — since this was stated by the authors of the <s>Maṇi</s>, the perceptibility of wind cannot be established through the example of radiance. But in the case of wind, no such reasoning exists. Therefore, wind is indeed imperceptible — this is clear in the <s>Dinakarī</s> and other [commentaries].

children.text:
cintāmaṇiprakāśakāraḥ
rucidattamiśraḥ vāyoḥ pratyakṣatvameva samarthaṃyate/ udbhūtarūpasparśavati
sauratejasi pratyakṣe 'pi saṃkhyādikaṃ na pratyakṣam/ tathā vāyāvapyastu/
yadi ca sauratejasi saṃkhyādikaṃ pratyakṣamevetyaṅgīkriyate, tathā
vāyāvapi
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Cintāmaṇiprakāśa</s>, <s>Rucidattamiśra</s>, supports the perceptibility of wind. Even though solar fire (<s>sauratejasa</s>) possesses manifest color and touch and is perceptible, its number and other properties are not perceptible. Similarly, let it be in the case of wind.

children.text:
svīkriyatām/ yadvā
saṃkhyāpratyakṣaṃ prati āśraye udbhūtasparśavattve sati
udbhūtarūpavattvameva prayojakam/
children.translated_text: And if it is accepted that the number and other properties of solar fire are indeed perceptible, let the same be accepted for wind. Alternatively, the operative cause for the perception of number is the possession of manifest color in a substratum that possesses manifest touch.

children.text:
ato vāyau saṃkhyā na
gṛhyate/ tathāpi vāyoḥ spārśanatve udbhūtasparśamātraṃ prayojakamiti
vāyoḥ spārśaṃnatvaṃ nirābādhamiti tena nyarūpi/
children.translated_text: Therefore, the number in wind is not grasped. Still, for the tactile perceptibility of wind, mere manifest touch is the operative cause — thus the tactile perceptibility of wind is unobstructed — so he demonstrated.

children.text: pramālakṣaṇavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Investigation of the definition of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>)

children.text:
dīpikāyāṃ 'tadvati
tatprakārako 'nubhavo yathārthaḥ', 'tadabhāvavati
tatprakārako 'nubhavo 'yathārthaḥ' iti maṇikāraniṣkṛṣṭaṃ
panthānamavalambya pramāyāḥ apramāyāśca lakṣaṇe abhihite/ atra viṣaye
prāktanānāmāśayaṃ nūtanalakṣaṇābhidhāne kāraṇaṃ ca vimṛśāmaḥ/
'tattvajñānānniḥ- śreyasādhigamaḥ' (nyā. sū. 1-1-1) iti prathamasūtre
tattvajñānasyāpavargopāyatvamuktvā tatprakārapratipādanapare 'duḥkhajanma'
ityādidvitīyasūtre tattvajñānaṃ mithyājñānasya nivartakamityavadat/
tena tattvajñānaṃ prameti sūtrakāro manyate/ pramāyā eva
bhramarūpamithyājñānanivartakatvāt/ tasya bhāvaḥ tattvaṃ -
viśeṣyavṛttidharmaḥ tasya jñānaṃ tattvajñānam/ viśeṣyavṛttidharmaprakārakaṃ
jñānaṃ tattvajñānamiti yāvat/ anena viśeṣyavṛttidharmaprakārakajñānatvaṃ
pramāyāḥ lakṣaṇamiti paryavasyati/ atra pakṣe yathārthasmṛtāvativyāptiḥ
prasajati, tasyā api viśeṣyavṛttidharmaprakārakajñānatvāt/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, the definitions of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) and invalid cognition (<s>apramā</s>) were stated following the method refined by the <s>Maṇikāra</s>: 'An experience having the qualifier-mode of that [property] in what possesses that [property] is veridical,' and 'An experience having the qualifier-mode of that [property] in what lacks that [property] is non-veridical.' Here we examine the intent of the earlier thinkers and the reason for formulating the new definition.
