In the first <s>sūtra</s>, 'From the knowledge of reality, the attainment of the highest good' (<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.1), having stated that knowledge of reality is the means to liberation, in the second <s>sūtra</s> beginning 'suffering, birth [etc.],' which aims to explain its nature, he said that knowledge of reality is the remover of erroneous cognition. Thus the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> considers that knowledge of reality is <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), since only valid cognition removes erroneous cognition in the form of error. Its nature (<s>tattva</s>) is — a property that resides in the qualificand; knowledge of that is knowledge of reality. That is, cognition whose qualifier-mode is a property residing in the qualificand is knowledge of reality. From this, it follows that the definition of <s>pramā</s> is: being a cognition whose qualifier-mode is a property residing in the qualificand. In this view, the defect of over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) to veridical memory arises, since it too is a cognition whose qualifier-mode is a property residing in the qualificand.

children.text:
tṛtīyasūtre bhāṣye1
--- 'upalabdhisādhanāni pramāṇānīti samākhyānirvacanasāmarthyāt
boddhavyamiti vadan bhāṣyakāraḥ 'upalabdhi pramā' iti sūcayati/
'buddhirūpalabdhirjñānamityanarthāntaram' iti (nyā. sū. 1-1-15)
sūtrānusāreṇa upalabdhipadasya jñānam ityathaḥ/
nirviṣayakajñānasyāsaṃbhavāt arthaṃviṣayakajñānatvaṃ pramātvamiti labhyate/
ata eva 'yattat arthavijñānaṃ sā pramitiḥ' iti prathamasūtre bhāṣyam/
paraṃ tvatra lakṣaṇe smṛtau bhrame cātivyāptiḥ, tayorapi
arthaviṣayakatvāt jñānatvācca/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the third <s>sūtra</s> — 'The instruments of apprehension are the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge)' — saying this, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, by the force of etymological derivation, indicates that 'apprehension is <s>pramā</s>.' In accordance with the <s>sūtra</s> 'Intellect, apprehension, and knowledge are synonymous' (<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.15), the word 'apprehension' means knowledge. Since cognition without an object is impossible, the definition of <s>pramā</s> is: being a cognition having an object as its content. Accordingly, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the first <s>sūtra</s>: 'That which is the cognition of an object is <s>pramiti</s> (valid cognition).' However, in this definition there is over-extension to memory and error, since both of them too have an object as content and are cognitions.

children.text: uktānupapattimālocyaiva ṭīkākārāḥ vācaspatimiśrāḥ1 --
children.translated_text: Having considered the stated difficulties, the <s>Ṭīkā</s> authors, <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s> —

children.text:
'lokādhīnāvadhāraṇo
hi śabdārthasaṃbandhaḥ/ lokaśca
children.translated_text: 'The relation between word and meaning is indeed determined by common usage. And common usage

children.text: smṛteranyāmupalabdhimarthāvyabhicāriṇīṃ pramāmācaṣṭe'
children.translated_text: calls <s>pramā</s> an apprehension other than memory that does not deviate from the object.'

children.text:
ityāhuḥ/
arthāvyabhicāri smṛtibhinnaṃ jñānaṃ prameti tadarthaḥ/
jñānasyārthāvyabhicaritatvaṃ yathāvasthitārthaviṣayakatvam/ atra pakṣe 'pi
yathārthasmṛtāvativyāptidoṣo vartate/
children.translated_text: Thus they state. The meaning is: <s>pramā</s> is a cognition different from memory that does not deviate from the object. The non-deviation of cognition from the object means having as its content the object as it actually is. Even in this view, the defect of over-extension to veridical memory persists.

children.text:
ata eva nyāyasāre2
jñānapadasya sthāne anubhavapadaṃ niveśya 'samyaganubhavaḥ pramā' iti
pramāyāḥ lakṣaṇamuktam/ anubhave samyaktvaṃ ca
tathābhūtārthaniścayasvabhāvatvamiti nyāyabhūṣaṇe3/
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in the <s>Nyāyasāra</s>, having placed the term 'experience' (<s>anubhava</s>) in place of the term 'knowledge,' the definition of <s>pramā</s> is stated as 'correct experience is <s>pramā</s>.' And correctness in experience is having the nature of ascertainment of the object as it truly is — so it is stated in the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s>.

children.text:
sūtrasthasya tattvajñānasya
pramāttve smṛtāvativyāptiriti paryālocyaiva 'tattvānubhūtiḥ pramā'
iti lakṣaṇāvalyāmudamanācāryaiḥ saptapadārthyāṃ
śivādityamiśraiścābhyadhāyi/ idaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bahudhā vikalpya khaṇḍana
khaṇḍakhādye
children.translated_text: Having considered that if the <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality) stated in the <s>sūtra</s> were to be the definition of <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), there would be over-extension to <s>smṛti</s> (memory), the definition '<s>tattvānubhūtiḥ pramā</s>' (valid cognition is the experience of reality) was propounded by <s>Udayanācārya</s> in the <s>Lakṣaṇāvalī</s> and by <s>Śivādityamiśra</s> in the <s>Saptapadārthī</s>. This definition was examined in various ways and refuted in the <s>Khaṇḍanakhaṇḍakhādya</s>

children.text: adūṣyata/
children.translated_text: by <s>Śrīharṣa</s>.

children.text:
nyāyakusumāñjalau
udayanācāryāḥ---
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyakusumāñjali</s>, <s>Udayanācārya</s> stated:

children.text:
'yathārthānubhavo
mānamanapekṣatayeṣyate'4
children.translated_text: 'Valid cognition is held to be veridical experience, by virtue of its independence' —

children.text:
iti kārikābhāgena
yathārthānubhavatvaṃ pramāyāḥ lakṣaṇamiti avadan/ anubhavapadasaṃyojanena
smṛtāvativyāptirnirākṛtā bhavati/ anubhave yathārthatvaṃ yatra yadasti
tatra tadviṣayakatvameva/ tathā hi bhrāntinirvacanāvasare kusumāñjalau5
children.translated_text: through this portion of the verse, he declared that the definition of <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is the nature of veridical experience. By the inclusion of the word 'experience' (<s>anubhava</s>), the over-extension to <s>smṛti</s> (memory) is precluded. Veridicality in experience means that where something exists, the cognition has that very thing as its object. Thus, on the occasion of defining error in the <s>Kusumāñjali</s>,

children.text:
'yannāsti tatra
tasyāvagatiriti bhrāntyarthatvāt' ityabhāṇi/
children.translated_text: it was stated: 'The cognition of that which does not exist there — this is the meaning of error.'

children.text:
tadvyākhyāne prakāśe
vardhamānopādhyāyaiḥ6---
children.translated_text: In the commentary on that called the <s>Prakāśa</s>, <s>Vardhamānopādhyāya</s> stated:

children.text:
'etena yad yatrāsti
tatra tajjñānaṃ prametyapi nirūktam'
children.translated_text: 'By this, it is also explained that cognition of a thing where that thing exists is <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition).'

children.text:
ityavādi/ evaṃ ca
tadvati tatprakārakānubhavatvaṃ pramātvamiti udayanācāryāṇāṃ niṣkṛṣṭaṃ
pramālakṣaṇam/ maṇikārairapyetallakṣaṇaṃ siddhāntatvena svīkṛtamiti
dīpikākāro 'pi tadeva lakṣaṇaṃ provāca/
children.translated_text: Thus, the refined definition of <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) according to <s>Udayanācārya</s> is: <s>pramātva</s> (the nature of valid cognition) is being an experience whose qualifier belongs to what is qualified by it. Since <s>Maṇikāra</s> also accepted this definition as established doctrine, the author of the <s>Dīpikā</s> also proclaimed that very definition.

children.text: smṛtisādhāraṇaṃ pramātvam
children.translated_text: <s>Pramātva</s> (valid cognition) as common to <s>smṛti</s> (memory):

children.text: viśvanāthapañcānanena kārikāvalyāṃ pramāyāḥ lakṣaṇadvayamuktam
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvanātha Pañcānana</s> stated two definitions of <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) in the <s>Kārikāvalī</s>:

children.text:
'bhramabhinnaṃ tu
jñānamatrocyate pramā' (kārikā. 134)
children.translated_text: 'Cognition that is different from error is here called <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition)' (<s>Kārikā</s> 134).

children.text:
'athavā tatprakāraṃ
yajjñānaṃ tadviśeṣyakam/ tatpramā'
children.translated_text: 'Or alternatively, that cognition which has as its qualifier what qualifies its qualificand — that is <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition)'

children.text: (kārikā 135)
children.translated_text: (<s>Kārikā</s> 135).

children.text:
iti/ tatra prathamaṃ
lakṣaṇaṃ bhramabhinnatve sati jñānatvamiti/ atra lakṣaṇe śuktirajatayoḥ 'hame
rajate' iti jñānaṃ rajate rajataviṣayakatvāṃśe pramā itīṣyate/
tatra bhramabhinnatvaṃ nāstīti avyāptiṃ paryālocya dvitīyaṃ
lakṣaṇamanusṛtam/ tacca tadvadviśeṣyakatve sati tatprakārakaṃ jñānaṃ
prameti/
children.translated_text: Of these, the first definition is: being cognition that is different from error. In this definition, regarding silver-nacre, the cognition 'this is silver' in the silver, insofar as it has silver as its object, is accepted as <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition). Since in that case the property of being different from error does not obtain, the second definition was adopted upon considering the under-extension. That second definition is: cognition that has as its qualifier what qualifies its qualificand, where that qualificand possesses that qualifier, is <s>pramā</s>.

children.text:
atra lakṣaṇadvaye 'pi
anubhavapadamaniveśva jñānapadasyaiva niveśāt smṛtāvativyāptiḥ
pramālakṣaṇasyeti śaṅkāyāḥ itthaṃ samādhānamuktaṃ muktāvalyām -
smṛteḥ pramātvamiṣyata eva/ atastasyā api
pramālakṣaṇalakṣyatvānnātivyāptiḥ/ yadi smṛteḥ pramātvamabhyupagamyate
tarhitatkāraṇasya pañcamapramāṇatvamāpadyata iti cet - maivam/
pramāṇalakṣaṇasyānubhavaghaṭitatvāt/ yathārthānubhavakaraṇaṃ pramāṇamiti
pramāṇalakṣaṇam/ smṛtikaraṇasyānubhavakaraṇatve nāsti,
smṛteranubhavatvābhāvāt iti na pramāṇatvaprasaktiḥ iti/
children.translated_text: In both these definitions, since the word 'cognition' (<s>jñāna</s>) is used rather than 'experience' (<s>anubhava</s>), there arises the doubt of over-extension of the definition of <s>pramā</s> to <s>smṛti</s> (memory). The resolution of this doubt is stated thus in the <s>Muktāvalī</s>: the <s>pramātva</s> (validity) of <s>smṛti</s> (memory) is indeed accepted; therefore, since memory too is a proper instance of the definition of <s>pramā</s>, there is no over-extension. If it is objected that upon accepting the <s>pramātva</s> of <s>smṛti</s>, its cause would attain the status of a fifth <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) — not so, because the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> includes the component 'experience.' The definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> is: the instrument of veridical experience. Since the instrument of memory does not have the nature of an instrument of experience — because <s>smṛti</s> is not <s>anubhava</s> (experience) — there is no consequence of <s>pramāṇatva</s> (being a means of valid knowledge).

children.text:
viśvanāthasyedamupapādanaṃ yuktarūpaṃ pratibhāti/
nyāyasūtrakāreṇa mithyājñānavirodhini pramājñāne 'tattvajñānam'
iti smṛtisādhāraṇajñānapadasyaiva prayogāt smṛterapi pramātvaṃ
tadabhimatam/ tenaiva 'pratyakṣānumānopamānaśabdāḥ pramāṇāni' (nyā.
sū. 1-1-3) iti sūtre smṛtikaraṇasya pramāṇamadhye 'parigaṇanāt
anubhavaghaṭitameva pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ kartavyamiti sūcitamiti/
children.translated_text: This explanation by <s>Viśvanātha</s> appears well-reasoned. Since the author of the <s>Nyāyasūtras</s> himself used the word 'cognition' (<s>jñāna</s>), which is common to <s>smṛti</s> (memory), in defining <s>pramā</s>-cognition as '<s>tattvajñāna</s>' (knowledge of reality) which opposes false knowledge, the <s>pramātva</s> of <s>smṛti</s> was intended by him as well. By the very same author, in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>pratyakṣa</s>, <s>anumāna</s>, <s>upamāna</s>, and <s>śabda</s> are the <s>pramāṇas</s>' (<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1-1-3), since the instrument of memory was not enumerated among the <s>pramāṇas</s>, it was indicated that the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> must include the component 'experience.'

children.text: prakāśikākāraniṣkarṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The conclusion of the author of the <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
'tadvati
tatprakārakānubhavo yathārthaḥ' ityuktāvapi raṅgarajatayoḥ 'ime
rajataraṅge' iti bhrame 'tivyāptiḥ/ tasyāpi
rajatatvavadrajataviśeṣyakatve sati rajatatvaprakārakatvāt
raṅgatvavadraṅgaviśeṣyakatve sati raṅgatvaprakārakatvācca/ ato
viśeṣyatāprakāratayornirūpyanirūpakabhāvaṃ niveśya
tadvanniṣṭhāviśeṣyatānirūpitatanniṣṭhaprakāratāśālyanubhavatvaṃ
pramālakṣaṇaṃ vācyamiti prakāśikāyāṃ niṣkarṣaḥ kṛtaḥ/
children.translated_text: Even when it is stated that 'an experience whose qualifier belongs to the qualificand is veridical,' there is over-extension in the case of stage-silver, where the erroneous cognition 'these are silver ornaments on stage' — because that too has silver as qualificand qualified by silverness while being a qualifier of silverness, and has stage-prop as qualificand qualified by stage-prop-ness while being a qualifier of stage-prop-ness. Therefore, by incorporating the relation of determinant and determinable between the qualificand-ness and qualifier-ness, the definition of <s>pramā</s> should be stated as: being an experience possessing qualifier-ness that determines the qualificand-ness residing in what possesses that qualifier. This is the conclusion reached in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text:
ayamatrānugamaḥ ---
prakāratāviśiṣṭaviśeṣyatānirūpakānubhavaḥ pramā/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchedakasambandhena svāśrayavanniṣṭhatvasavanirūpitatvobhayasambandhena/
yadvā prakāritāviśiṣṭaviśeṣyitāvadanubhavaḥ pramā/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchinnatvasvanirūpitaprakāratāviśiṣṭaviśeṣyatānirūpitatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
prakāratāvaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca svāvacchedakasambandhena
svāśrayavanniṣṭhatvasambandheneti/ adhikaṃ prasāraṇākhyavyākhyāyāṃ
draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: The elucidation here is as follows: <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is an experience whose qualificand-ness is distinguished by qualifier-ness. The distinction is through the dual relation of: residing in what possesses the delimiting relation of itself, and being determined by what has the same substrate. Or alternatively, <s>pramā</s> is an experience that possesses qualificand-ness distinguished by qualifier-ness. The distinction is through the dual relation of: being delimited by itself and being determined by the qualificand-ness distinguished by the qualifier-ness delimited by itself. The distinction in qualifier-ness is through the relation of its own delimiting relation and the relation of residing in what possesses its own substrate. Further details should be consulted in the commentary called <s>Prasāraṇa</s>.

children.text:
paraṃ tvevaṃ
niṣkṛṣṭalakṣaṇasyāpi nirvikalpakāvyāptiḥ/ niṣprakārake
nirvikalpakapadābhidheyajñāne tatprakārakatvaghaṭitapramālakṣaṇavirahāt/
ataḥ tadabhāvavati tatprakārakānubhavaḥ apramā, tadbhinno 'nubhavaḥ pramā
iti lakṣaṇaṃ vācyam/ muktāvalīkṛtastu nirvikalpakaṃ
bhramapramābahirbhūntamiti manyante/
children.translated_text: However, even this refined definition has under-extension with respect to <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate cognition). In <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition, which is without qualifiers and is denoted by the word '<s>nirvikalpaka</s>,' the definition of <s>pramā</s> constituted by having-a-qualifier is absent. Therefore, the definition should be stated as: an experience that has a qualifier belonging to what possesses it is <s>apramā</s> (non-valid cognition) when the qualifier is absent in it, and an experience different from that is <s>pramā</s>. But the author of the <s>Muktāvalī</s> considers <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition to be outside both error and valid cognition.

children.text: kāraṇatraividhyavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Investigation of the threefold nature of causes

children.text:
tarkasaṃgraha-dīpikā-kārikāvalī-muktāvalīprabhṛtiṣu
nyāyavaiśeṣikānusāriṣu prakaraṇagrantheṣu samavāyikāraṇam
asamavāyikāraṇaṃ nimittakāraṇaṃ ceti kāraṇaṃ tredhā vibhajya tasya
pratyekaṃ lakṣaṇamapi niṣkṛṣya pratipāditamasti/ paraṃ
tvādhunikavimarśakāḥ kecana itthaṃ kāraṇasya tredhā vibhāgaḥ na
sūtrādiṣu prācīneṣu grantheṣūllikhitaḥ kevalaṃ navīnanaiyāyikaiḥ
pratipādita iti manyante/ etattattvamadhunā paryālocyate/
children.translated_text: In primer texts following the <s>Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika</s> system such as the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>, <s>Dīpikā</s>, <s>Kārikāvalī</s>, and <s>Muktāvalī</s>, <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause) is divided threefold as <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause), <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause), and <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause), and the definition of each has been refined and presented. However, certain modern critics hold that this threefold division of cause is not found in ancient texts like the <s>sūtras</s> and was propounded only by the later <s>Naiyāyikas</s>. The truth of this matter is now examined.

children.text:
'kriyāguṇavat
samavāyikāraṇamiti dravyalakṣaṇam' (vai.sū. 1-1-15), ' kāraṇaṃ
tvasamavāyino guṇāḥ' (vai.sū.5-2-24) 'kāraṇena kālaḥ' (vai.sū.5-2-26)
ityādivaiśeṣikasūtrāṇāmavalokanena kāraṇatrayamapi
sūtrākārasaṃmatamiti jñāyate/ praśastapādabhāṣye 'pi kāraṇatrayaṃ
svīkṛtam/ 'yugapat trayāṇāṃ samavāyyasamavāyinimittakāraṇānāṃ
vināśāt paratvasya vināśaḥ' ityādayo bhāṣyagranthāḥ draṣṭavyāḥ/
children.translated_text: By examining <s>Vaiśeṣikasūtras</s> such as 'that which possesses action and quality through inherence is the definition of <s>dravya</s> (substance) as inherent cause' (<s>Vaiśeṣikasūtra</s> 1-1-15), '<s>guṇas</s> (qualities) are non-inherent causes' (<s>Vaiśeṣikasūtra</s> 5-2-24), and 'time is a cause' (<s>Vaiśeṣikasūtra</s> 5-2-26), it is known that the threefold causation was accepted by the author of the <s>sūtras</s>. In <s>Praśastapāda's</s> <s>Bhāṣya</s> too, the threefold causation is accepted. Passages in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> such as 'from the simultaneous destruction of the three — the inherent, non-inherent, and efficient causes — the destruction of the posterior follows' should be consulted.

children.text:
yadyapi nyāsasūtreṣu
kāraṇatrayaprastāvo na dṛśyate, tathāpi vātsyāyanabhāṣye tatsūcanaṃ
vartate/ tathā hi nyāyadarśaṃne caturthādhyāne prathamāhnike aṣṭādaśaṃ
sūtram --- 'kramanirdeśādapratiṣedhaḥ' iti/ sūtramidaṃ śūnyameva
jagadupādānakāraṇamiti matanirākaraṇasaṃdarbhe/ vidyate/ tatra ca
bhāṣyam ---
children.translated_text: Although in the <s>Nyāyasūtras</s> there is no discussion of the threefold causation, nevertheless an indication of it is present in <s>Vātsyāyana's</s> <s>Bhāṣya</s>. Thus, in the <s>Nyāyadarśana</s>, in the first section of the fourth chapter, the eighteenth <s>sūtra</s> is: 'there is no prohibition because of the sequential instruction.' This <s>sūtra</s> occurs in the context of refuting the view that the world has void as its material cause. There the <s>bhāṣya</s> states:

children.text:
'bījāvayavāḥ
kutaścinnimittāt prādurbhūtakriyāḥ
children.translated_text: 'The parts of the seed, having their activity manifested by some efficient cause,

children.text:
pūrvavyūhaṃ jahati
vyūhāntaraṃ cāpadyante/
children.translated_text: abandon the previous arrangement and assume another arrangement.

children.text:
vyūhāntarāt aṅkura
utpadyate/ dṛśyante
children.translated_text: From the other arrangement, a sprout is produced. Indeed,

children.text:
khalvavayavāḥ
tatsaṃyogāśca aṅkurotpattihetavaḥ'
children.translated_text: the parts and their conjunctions are seen to be the causes of the production of the sprout.'

children.text:
iti/ atra
'kutaścinnimittāt' ityanena adṛṣṭādirūpaṃ nimittakāraṇaṃ
sūcitam/ 'avayavāstatsaṃyogāścāṅkurotpattihetavaḥ' ityanena
avayavarūpaṃ samavāyikāraṇam avayavasaṃyogarūpamasamavāyikāraṇaṃ ca
sūcitam/ nyāyavārtikakāro 'pi trīṇi kāraṇāni tatra tatra kaṇṭharaveṇa
nirdiśati/ 'tatkāritatvādahetuḥ' (nyā.sū.4-1-21) iti sūtrasthaṃ
'tatkāritatvādityevaṃ bruvatā nimittakāraṇamīśvaraḥ ityupagataṃ
bhavati/ yacca nimittaṃ tat itarayoḥ
samavāyikāraṇāsamavāyikāraṇayoranugrāhakaṃ yathā turyādi tantūnāṃ
tatsaṃyogānāṃ ca' iti vārtikam,
'ghrāṇarasanacakṣustvakśrotrāṇīndriyāṇi bhūtebhyaḥ' (nyā.sū. 1-1-12)
iti sūtrasthaṃ 'na kiñcidapyekakāraṇakaṃ kāryaṃ dṛṣṭam/ sarvaṃ hi kāryaṃ
prādurbhavat samavāyyasamavāyinimittakāraṇebhyo bhavati' iti
vārtikaṃ cātrānusandhānamarhataḥ/ tathā
children.translated_text: Here, by the phrase 'from some efficient cause,' the <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause) in the form of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) and such is indicated. By the phrase 'the parts and their conjunctions are causes of the production of the sprout,' the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause) in the form of parts and the <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause) in the form of conjunction of parts are indicated. The author of the <s>Nyāyavārtika</s> also explicitly mentions the three causes here and there. The <s>vārtika</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> 'it is not a non-cause because of being effected by that' (<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4-1-21) states: 'By saying "because of being effected by that," it is implied that <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is the <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause). And that which is the efficient cause supports the other two — the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause) and the <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause) — just as the loom and such support the threads and their conjunctions.' The <s>vārtika</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> 'the sense organs — smell, taste, sight, touch, and hearing — arise from the elements' (<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1-1-12) states: 'No effect whatsoever is seen to have a single cause. For every effect that comes into being arises from the inherent, non-inherent, and efficient causes.' This too deserves consideration here. Thus,

children.text:
ca
samavāyikāraṇāsamavāyikāraṇanimittakāraṇarūpeṇa kāraṇaṃ
trividhamiti vibhāgaḥ prācīnagranthārūḍha iti siddham/ navyagrantheṣu
teṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ lakṣaṇānyeva pariṣkṛtya pratipāditāni/
children.translated_text: the division that <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause) is threefold in the form of <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause), <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause), and <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause) is established as found in ancient texts. In the later texts, only the definitions of those causes were refined and presented.

children.text: kāraṇatrayasvīkāre upapattayaḥ
children.translated_text: Justifications for accepting the threefold causation:

children.text:
atra kācidāśaṅkā
--- yathā vedāntiprabhṛtayaḥ upādānakāraṇaṃ nimittakāraṇaṃ ceti
kāraṇaṃ dvividhamaṅgīkurvanti, tathā kuto naiyāyikā
nāṅgīkurvantīti/ tatrocyate/ naiyāyikā avayavātiriktamavayavinaṃ
svīkurvanti/ vedāntinastu tantūnāṃ saṃyogaviśeṣa eva paṭo na
tadatirikta iti prāhuḥ/ vedāntināṃ mate tantuseyāṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: Here a doubt arises: just as <s>Vedāntins</s> and others accept cause as twofold — <s>upādānakāraṇa</s> (material cause) and <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause) — why do the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> not accept the same? To this it is replied: The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> accept the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) as distinct from the parts (<s>avayava</s>). The <s>Vedāntins</s>, however, say that the cloth is nothing but a particular conjunction of threads, and not something additional. In the <s>Vedānta</s> view, the conjunction of threads

children.text:
kāryakoṭau
niviśate/ naiyāyikānāṃ mate tu paṭanāmako 'vayavī kāryabhūtaḥ/ sa
ca tantusaṃyogaviśeṣādutpadyate/ atastantusaṃyogo 'pi kāraṇamiti
svīkartavyam/ tasya samavāyikāraṇatvāsaṃbhavena asamavāyikāraṇatvaṃ
pratipāditamiti/
children.translated_text: falls within the category of effects. But in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, the whole called 'cloth' is the effect. And it arises from a particular conjunction of threads. Therefore, the conjunction of threads too must be accepted as a cause. Since it cannot be an inherent cause, its status as <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause) has been established.

children.text:
tarhi samavāyikāraṇaṃ
nimittakāraṇaṃ ceti dvedhā vibhāgo 'stu, tantusaṃyogasyāpi
nimittakāraṇatvamevāstu iti cet --- atrocyate/
nimittakāraṇabhūtatantuvāyanāśe 'pi paṭarūpaṃ kāryaṃ tiṣṭhati/
tantusaṃyoganāśe tu na paṭastiṣṭhati, api tu naśyati/ ato
nimittakāraṇasya vaidharmyāt samavāyikāraṇavaidharmyācca tantusaṃyogaḥ
asamavāyikāraṇatvena svīkṛta iti/
children.translated_text: If it is then suggested that there should be only a twofold division into <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause) and <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause), and the conjunction of threads should simply be an efficient cause — to this it is replied: even when the weaving that is the <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause) is destroyed, the effect in the form of cloth continues to exist. But when the conjunction of threads is destroyed, the cloth does not persist — rather, it perishes. Therefore, because of the dissimilarity from <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> and the dissimilarity from <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>, the conjunction of threads is accepted as <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause).

children.text:
kiṃ
cāsamavāyikāraṇānabhyupagame dravyanāśaṃ prati kiṃ kāraṇamiti
vaktavyam/ na tāvannimittakāraṇanāśaḥ, kulālādisadbhāve 'pi
ghaṭanāśadarśanāt kulālādināśe 'pi ghaṭasadbhāvadarśanācca/ nāpi
samavāyikāraṇanāśaḥ kāraṇam/ dvyaṇukanāśānupapatteḥ/ dvyaṇukasya
hi paramāṇuḥ samavāyikāraṇam/ na hi tasya nāśaḥ saṃbhavati,
nityatvāt/ ato dvyaṇukasya samavāyikāraṇanāśānnāśo na
saṃbhavatīti asamavāyikāraṇabhūtasya paramāṇudvayasaṃyogasya nāśādeva
nāśo vaktavyaḥ/ tathā ca dvyaṇukanāśasya asamavāyikāraṇanāśo
hetuḥ, itarakāryadravyanāśasya samavāyikāraṇanāśo heturiti
kalpanāmapekṣyānugatatayā kāryadravyasāmānyanāśaṃ prati
asamavāyikāraṇasvīkāra āvaśyakaḥ/
children.translated_text: Moreover, if <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause) is not accepted, one must explain what is the cause for the destruction of a <s>dravya</s> (substance). It is not the destruction of the <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause), since the destruction of a pot is observed even when the potter and such exist, and the pot is observed to exist even when the potter has perished. Nor is the destruction of the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause) the cause, due to the impossibility of explaining the destruction of a <s>dvyaṇuka</s> (dyad). For the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> of a <s>dvyaṇuka</s> is the <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom), and its destruction is not possible since it is eternal. Therefore, the destruction of a <s>dvyaṇuka</s> cannot be explained by the destruction of its <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>, and must be explained by the destruction of the conjunction of the two <s>paramāṇus</s> that constitutes the <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>. Thus, the destruction of a <s>dvyaṇuka</s> is caused by the destruction of the <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>, while the destruction of other effect-substances is caused by the destruction of the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> — considering the need for a uniform account in preference to this bifurcation, the acceptance of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> for the destruction of effect-substances in general is necessary.

children.text:
tarhi samavāyikāraṇaṃ
asamavāyikāraṇaṃ ceti dvedhā vibhāgo 'stu, nimittakāraṇaṃ māstu
iti ceta - na/ yadi samavāyikāraṇabhinnaṃ sarvaṃ
kāraṇamasamavāyikāraṇamiti varge 'ntarbhāvyate, tarhi
asamavāyikāraṇanāśasya pūrvoktarītyā dravyanāśahetutvāt
kulālādināśe 'pi ghaṭanāśāpattiḥ syāt/ ato
nimittakāraṇamatiriktatayā svīkaraṇīyamiti/ tathā ca yuktiyuktatvāt
kāraṇatrayamapi svīkaraṇīyamiti tredhā kāraṇavibhāgaḥ
prācīnagranthārūḍhaśceti siddham/
children.translated_text: If it is then suggested that there should be only a twofold division into <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause) and <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause), and there need be no <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause) — no. If all causes other than the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> are subsumed under the category of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>, then since the destruction of the <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> is the cause of the destruction of a <s>dravya</s> (substance) as stated before, the destruction of the potter and such would also entail the destruction of the pot. Therefore, <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause) must be accepted as a distinct category. Thus, since it is well-reasoned, all three types of causes should be accepted, and the threefold division of causes is established as found in ancient texts.

children.text: ( 7 ) nirvikalpakasavikalpakavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: (7) Investigation of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate) and <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate) cognition:

children.text:
pratyakṣaṃ dvividhaṃ
nirvikalpakaṃ savikalpakam ca/
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is of two kinds: <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate) and <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate).

children.text:
niṣprakārakaṃ jñānaṃ
nirvikalpakam, saprakārakaṃ jñānaṃ savikalpakam iti tarkasaṃgrahe
uktam/ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṃbandhānavagāhi jñānaṃ nirvikalpakam,
nāmajātyādiviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṃbandhāvagāhi jñānaṃ savikalpakam
iti dīpikāyām/ viśeṣyatāśūnyatvaṃ prakāratāśūnyatvaṃ
saṃsargatāśūnyatve ca nirvikalpakatvam, viśeṣyatānirūpakatvaṃ
prakāratānirūpakatvaṃ saṃsargatānirūpakatvam ca savikalpakatvamiti
prakāśikāyām/ etattattvamidārnīṃ prāktanagranthāloḍanapūrvakaṃ
vicāryate/
children.translated_text: Knowledge without qualificatory mode is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate cognition), and knowledge with qualificatory mode is <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate cognition) — thus it is stated in the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>. Knowledge that does not apprehend the relation of qualifier and qualificand is <s>nirvikalpaka</s>, and knowledge that apprehends the relation of name, universal, and other qualifiers with the qualificand is <s>savikalpaka</s> — thus in the <s>Dīpikā</s>. The absence of qualificand-ness, the absence of qualifier-mode, and the absence of relational-mode constitute <s>nirvikalpakatva</s>; while that which is determined by qualificand-ness, determined by qualifier-mode, and determined by relational-mode constitutes <s>savikalpakatva</s> — thus in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>. The truth of this matter is now examined through a survey of earlier texts.

children.text:
nyāyasetre na kvāpi
nirvikalpakasavikalpakaśabdābhyāṃ pratyakṣavibhāgaḥ kṛtaḥ/
'indriyārthasaṃnikarṣotpannam' iti
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>, nowhere is a division of perception made using the terms <s>nirvikalpaka</s> and <s>savikalpaka</s>. 'Arising from the contact of sense-organ and object' — thus

children.text:
pratyakṣalakṣaṇapratipādakasūtrasthābhyāṃ 'avyapadeśyam'
'vyavasāyātmakam' iti padābhyāṃ nirvikalpakasavikalpake vivakṣite
iti tātparyaṭīkākārāḥ nirūpayanti/ paraṃ tu bhāṣye vārtike vā
naivaṃvidhaṃ nirūpaṇamupalabhāmahe/
children.translated_text: the authors of the <s>Tātparyaṭīkā</s> explain that by the two terms 'avyapadeśya' (non-verbal) and 'vyavasāyātmaka' (of the nature of determination), occurring in the <s>sūtra</s> that sets forth the definition of perception, <s>nirvikalpaka</s> and <s>savikalpaka</s> are intended. However, we do not find such an explanation in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> or the <s>Vārtika</s>.

children.text:
nyāyamañjaryāṃ
nyāyasāre ca nirvikalpakaṃ savikalpakaṃ ceti pratyakṣadvayaṃ yadyapi
sayuktikaṃ prasādhitam, tathāpi sūtrāt tādṛśavibhāgasya
lābhaprakārastatra na pradarśitaḥ/ nyāyabhūṣaṇe tu avyapadeśyapadena
nirvikalpakasya vyavasāyātmakapadena savikalpakasya grahaṇamiti
sayuktikaṃ pratyapādi/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyamañjarī</s> and the <s>Nyāyasāra</s>, although the twofold nature of perception as <s>nirvikalpaka</s> and <s>savikalpaka</s> has been established with reasoning, nevertheless the method of deriving such a division from the <s>sūtra</s> has not been shown there. In the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s>, however, it was established with reasoning that by the term 'avyapadeśya' <s>nirvikalpaka</s> is grasped and by the term 'vyavasāyātmaka' <s>savikalpaka</s> is grasped.

children.text: praśastapādabhāṣye1 ---
children.translated_text: In the <s>Praśastapādabhāṣya</s> —

children.text:
'dravye tāvadvividhe
mahatyanekadravyavattvodbhūtarūpaprakāśa --
children.translated_text: 'In the case of a substance that is twofold — a great [substance] possessing many substances, with manifested color and light —

children.text:
catuṣṭayasaṃnikarṣāt
dharmādisāmagrye ca svarūpālocanamātram'
children.translated_text: from the contact of the four [sense-faculties], and in the aggregate of <s>dharma</s> and the rest, there is mere apprehension of the intrinsic nature.'

children.text:
iti granthena
nirvikalpakapratyakṣaṃ pradarśitam/ svarūpālocanamātramityasya
svarūpamātrasya grahaṇamityarthaḥ/ mātrapadena
jātyādisaṃbandhaviṣayakatvavyavacchedaḥ/ tataḥ ---
children.translated_text: By this passage, <s>nirvikalpaka pratyakṣa</s> (indeterminate perception) has been demonstrated. The meaning of 'mere apprehension of the intrinsic nature' is 'the grasping of the intrinsic nature alone.' By the word 'mere,' the exclusion of having universals and the like as objects of relation [is indicated]. Then —

children.text: 'sāmānyaviśeṣadravyaguṇakarmaviśeṣaṇāpekṣāt ātmamanaḥ -
children.translated_text: 'From the expectation of the qualifiers — universal, particular, substance, quality, and action — and from the contact of self and mind,

children.text:
saṃnikarṣāt
pratyakṣamutpadyate sat dravyaṃ pṛthivī viṣāṇī
children.translated_text: perception arises: 'It exists,' 'It is a substance,' 'It is earth,' 'It has horns,'

children.text: śuklo gaurgacchati'
children.translated_text: 'It is white,' 'It is a cow,' 'It moves.''

children.text:
iti granthena
savikalpakapratyakṣaṃ sodāharaṇamupadarśitam/ paraṃ tu
nirvikalpakasavikalpakaśabdau na prayuktau/ kumārilabhaṭṭa api1 ---
children.translated_text: By this passage, <s>savikalpaka pratyakṣa</s> (determinate perception) has been shown with examples. However, the terms <s>nirvikalpaka</s> and <s>savikalpaka</s> were not used [explicitly]. <s>Kumārilabhaṭṭa</s> also —

children.text:
'asti hyālocanājñānaṃ
prathamaṃ nirvikalpakam/
children.translated_text: 'There is indeed an apprehensive cognition, the first, which is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate),

children.text: bālamūkādivijñānasadṛśaṃ śuddhavastujam//'
children.translated_text: resembling the cognition of infants and mutes, born of pure objects.'

children.text:
iti ślokena
nirvikalpakaṃ,
children.translated_text: By this verse, <s>nirvikalpaka</s> [was defined],

children.text:
'tataḥ paraṃ ca tadvastu
dharmairjātyādibhiryathā/
children.translated_text: 'And thereafter, that very object, by its properties such as universals and the like,

children.text:
buddhyāvasīyate
sāpi pratyakṣatvena saṃmatā//'
children.translated_text: is determined by the intellect — that too is regarded as perception.'

children.text:
iti ślokena
savikalpakaṃ ca lakṣayāṃbabhūvuḥ/ prakaraṇapañcikāyāṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: By this verse, <s>savikalpaka</s> was also defined. And in the <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> —

children.text:
'savikalpāvikalpā ca
dvividhā buddhiriṣyate/
children.translated_text: 'Determinate and indeterminate — the intellect is considered to be twofold.

children.text:
ādyā viśiṣṭaviṣayā
svarūpaviṣayetarā//'
children.translated_text: The first has a qualified object; the other has the intrinsic form as its object.'

children.text:
iti pratyakṣasya
nirvikalpakasavikalpakabhedena dvaividhyaṃ prādarśayan/
children.translated_text: Thus, the twofold nature of perception as <s>nirvikalpaka</s> and <s>savikalpaka</s> was demonstrated.

children.text:
tattvacintāmaṇau2 ---
'nāmajātyādiyojanārahitaṃ vaiśiṣṭyānavagāhi niṣprakārakaṃ
nirvikalpakam' iti nirvikalpakalakṣaṇaṃ prādarśi/
vaiśiṣṭyānavagāhītyasyaiva vivaraṇaṃ niṣprakārakamiti/ nirvikalpake
prakāratākhyaviṣayatāśūnyatvamiva viśeṣyatākhyaviṣayatāśūnyatvamapi
vartate/ tathā ca nirviśeṣyakaṃ jñānaṃ nirvikalpakamityapi śakyate
vaktum/ tathā anuktvā niṣprakārakamiti vadatāṃ
maṇikārāṇāmayamāśayaḥ--- yathā savikalpakasya viśiṣṭajñānatvāt tataḥ
pūrvaṃ viśeṣaṇajñānaṃ kalpyate, tathā nirvikalpakahetutayā jñānāntaraṃ
nāpekṣitamiti/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s> — 'That which is devoid of the association of name, universal, and the like, which does not apprehend distinction, and is without qualificatory mode — that is <s>nirvikalpaka</s>' — thus the definition of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> was presented. 'Without qualificatory mode' is itself an elaboration of 'not apprehending distinction.' In <s>nirvikalpaka</s>, just as there is absence of object-ness called qualifier-mode, so too there is absence of object-ness called qualificand-ness. Accordingly, one could also say that cognition without a qualificand is <s>nirvikalpaka</s>. The intention of the <s>Maṇikāras</s> (authors of the <s>Maṇi</s>) in saying 'without qualificatory mode' rather than stating it thus is: just as, because <s>savikalpaka</s> is a qualified cognition, a prior cognition of the qualifier is postulated, so too no additional cognition is required as a cause of <s>nirvikalpaka</s>.

children.text:
etādṛśanirvikalpakasadbhāve pramāṇaṃ tu - etajjanmani prāthamikaṃ
gauriti pratyakṣaṃ janyaviśeṣaṇajñānajanyaṃ janyaviśiṣṭajñānatvāt
anumitivat ityanumānam/ yathā 'parvato vahnimān'
ityanumitiḥ vahniviśiṣṭaparvataviṣiyaṇī
children.translated_text: The proof for the existence of such <s>nirvikalpaka</s> is this inference: the first cognition in this life, 'This is a cow,' is produced by a cognition of the qualifier that is itself produced — because it is a qualified cognition, like an inference. Just as the inference 'The mountain possesses fire'

children.text:
vahnarūpaviśeṣaṇajñānātmakasādhyaprasiddhijanyā tathā prāthamikaṃ
gauriti viśiṣṭapratyakṣamapi gotvātmakaviśeṣaṇajñānādevodetīti
vaktavyam/ tadeva vaiśiṣṭyāviṣayakaṃ nirvikalpakam/
children.translated_text: is produced by the cognition of the established probandum in the form of fire as qualifier — so too the first determinate perception 'This is a cow' must arise from a cognition of the qualifier in the form of cow-ness. That [prior cognition], which does not have distinction as its object, is <s>nirvikalpaka</s>.

children.text:
na ca tatra
prāthamikaviśiṣṭapratyakṣaṃ prati gotvarūpaviśeṣaṇasmaraṇameva hetuḥ,
tathā ca na nirvikalpakapratyakṣaṃ sidhyatīti vācyam/ etajjanmani pūrvaṃ
gotvasyānanubhavena tatsmaraṇāsaṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that the cause of the first determinate perception of cow-ness as qualifier is merely the remembrance of cow-ness, and therefore <s>nirvikalpaka</s> perception is not established — because, prior to this life's [first] experience of cow-ness, remembrance of it is impossible since it has not been previously experienced.

children.text:
na ca
gotvarūpaviśeṣaṇānubhavaḥ savikalpaka eva san 'ayaṃ gauḥ' iti
viśiṣṭapratyakṣaṃ janayatu/ tathā ca gataṃ nirvikalpakeneti vācyam/
tathātve tasyāpi viśiṣṭajñānatvena viśeṣaṇajñānajanyatvaṃ tasyāpi
tathetyanavasthāprasaṅgāt/ tathā ca gotvaviṣayakaṃ
nirvikalpakamarthātsidhyati/
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said: let the experience of the qualifier in the form of cow-ness, being itself <s>savikalpaka</s>, generate the qualified perception 'This is a cow,' and thus <s>nirvikalpaka</s> is dispensed with. For in that case, since that [experience] too would be a qualified cognition and hence produced by a cognition of a qualifier, and that too likewise — an infinite regress would follow. Therefore, a <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition having cow-ness as its object is established by implication.

children.text:
atredamāśaṅkyate -
yaduktaṃ viśiṣṭabuddherviśeṣaṇajñānapūrvakatvānnirvikalpakaṃ sidhyatīti/
tanna/ gauriti viśiṣṭajñānaṃ viśeṣaṇajñānajanyaṃ viśiṣṭajñānatvāt
ityanumāne bhinnasāmagrīvedyaviṣayakatvasyopādhitvāt/ yatra
viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyaṃ ca bhinnasāmagrīvedyaṃ tatraiva viśiṣṭajñānaṃ
viśeṣaṇajñānapūrvakaṃ dṛṣṭam, yathā sūrabhi candanamiti
viśiṣṭapratyakṣam/ tatra hi viśeṣaṇaṃ saurabhaṃ ghrāṇendriyavedyaṃ viśeṣyaṃ
candanaṃ cakṣurvedyamiti bhinnasāmāgrīvedyaviṣayakatvāt viśiṣṭapratyakṣasya
ādau saurabharūpaviśeṣaṇajñānaṃ, tena surabhi candanamiti
viśiṣṭapratyakṣaṃ bhavati/ ekendriyavedyayorgotvayorekakāla
viśiṣṭajñānasaṃbhavāt gotvajñānaṃ tato gotvaviśiṣṭagojñānamiti
kalpanaṃ na yujyate/
children.translated_text: Here one objects: it was said that because qualified cognition is preceded by cognition of the qualifier, <s>nirvikalpaka</s> is established — but this is wrong. In the inference 'The qualified cognition "cow" is produced by a cognition of the qualifier, because it is a qualified cognition, like the cognition "a man with a staff"' — having objects cognizable by different causal aggregates is an interfering condition (<s>upādhi</s>). Only where the qualifier and the qualificand are cognizable by different causal aggregates has a qualified cognition been observed to be preceded by a cognition of the qualifier — as in the case of the qualified perception 'fragrant sandalwood.' For there the qualifier, fragrance, is cognizable by the olfactory sense, and the qualificand, sandalwood, is cognizable by the visual sense; because the qualified perception has objects cognizable by different aggregates, first the cognition of the qualifier in the form of fragrance arises, and then the qualified perception 'fragrant sandalwood' occurs. Since cow-ness and cow-individual, both cognizable by a single sense, can be known simultaneously, the postulation that first there is cow-ness cognition and then a cow-ness-qualified cow-cognition is not justified.

children.text:
nanu
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoḥ gotvagovyaktyoḥ ekendriyayogyatvena
ekajñānaviṣayatve 'pi tayoḥ saṃbandhasyātathātvāt
children.translated_text: But even though the qualifier and qualificand — cow-ness and cow-individual — being fit for a single sense, may be objects of a single cognition, because their relation is not of that nature,

children.text:
prathamajñāne tayoḥ
saṃbandho na bhāsate/ tadeva nirvikalpakam/
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṃbandhānavagāhijñānasyaivāsmābhirnivikalpakaśabdavācyatvāṅgīkārāditi
cet-na/ saṃbandhapadena kiṃ svarūpaṃ vivakṣitam? ata samavāyaḥ? ādye
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasvarūpagrahaṇe saṃbandho 'pi gṛhīta eveti kva
nirvikalpakam/ dvitīye cakṣuṣā saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatākhyasaṃnikarṣeṇa
samavāyo gṛhyata iti bhavatsiddhāntāt
gogotvasamavāyānāmekendriyayogyatvāt ekakāla eva trayāṇāṃ
grahaṇaṃ bhaviturmahati/ anyathā yogyasyāpi samavāyasya prathamamagrahaṇe
paścādapi grahaṇaṃ na syāt/ tathā ca saṃsargānavagāhi nirvikalpakajñānaṃ
na yuktisahamiti/
children.translated_text: in the first cognition their relation does not appear. That itself is <s>nirvikalpaka</s>. If it be said that we accept only cognition that does not apprehend the relation of qualifier and qualificand as denoted by the word <s>nirvikalpaka</s> — [we reply:] no. By the word 'relation,' is the intrinsic nature intended, or <s>samavāya</s> (inherence)? In the first case, when the intrinsic natures of qualifier and qualificand are grasped, the relation too is already grasped — so where is <s>nirvikalpaka</s>? In the second case, since according to your own doctrine <s>samavāya</s> is grasped by the visual sense through the sense-contact called 'qualified-qualifier-contact,' and since the cow, cow-ness, and their <s>samavāya</s> are all fit for a single sense, the grasping of all three at one time is quite possible. Otherwise, if <s>samavāya</s>, though fit [to be perceived], is not grasped initially, it would never be grasped subsequently either. Therefore, a <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition that does not apprehend relation is not sustainable by reasoning.

children.text:
atretthaṃ samādhīyate ---
nirvikalpakajñāne jātyādirūpaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ vyaktirūpaṃ viśeṣyaṃ ca
bhāsate/ saṃbandhastu na bhāsate/ saṃbandhajñānaṃ prati saṃbandhijñānasya
kāraṇatayā pūrvaṃ tadabhāvāt/ tathā ca pūrvaṃ
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyarūpasaṃbandhinorjñānaṃ nirvikalpātmakaṃ jāyate,
tatastayoḥ saṃbandhāvagāhi savikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ jāyate/
taduktamudayanācāryaiḥ --- 'sahakārivaikalyāttu nirvikalpake
samavāyāgrahaṇam' iti/ sahakārivaikalyādityasya
saṃbandhijñānavirahādityarthaḥ/ tathā ca saṃbandho 'pi kuto nirvikalpake
na bhāsata iti codyasya nāvasaraḥ/
children.translated_text: Here the resolution is as follows: In <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition, the qualifier in the form of universal and the like, and the qualificand in the form of the individual, do appear. But the relation does not appear — because, since cognition of the relata is a cause of cognition of the relation, and that [cognition of relata] is initially absent, [the relation cannot appear]. Thus, first a <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition arises having the relata — qualifier and qualificand — as its content, and then from that arises a <s>savikalpaka</s> cognition apprehending their relation. As stated by <s>Udayanācārya</s>: 'Due to the deficiency of an auxiliary cause, <s>samavāya</s> is not grasped in <s>nirvikalpaka</s>.' The meaning of 'due to the deficiency of an auxiliary cause' is 'due to the absence of cognition of the relata.' Accordingly, the objection 'why does the relation too not appear in <s>nirvikalpaka</s>?' has no occasion [to arise].

children.text:
yadapi
bhinnasāmagrīvedyaviṣayakatvamupādhiriti - tatradaṃ vaktavyam/
anumitiśābdādau sādhyaprasiddhyādeḥ kāraṇatayā yadviśeṣayoriti
nyāyena viśiṣṭajñānatvāvacchinnaṃ prati viśeṣaṇajñānatvāvacchinnaṃ
kāraṇamiti sāmānyakāryaṅkāraṇabhāvasya siddhau ekasāmagrīvedyeṣvapi
viśeṣaṇajñānakalpanena tajjanyaiva viśiṣṭabuddhiḥ/ tathā ca
bhinnasāmagrīvedyaviṣayakatvasya sādhyavyāpakatvabhaṅgāt upādhitvaṃ na
saṃbhavatīti/
children.translated_text: As for the claim that having objects cognizable by different causal aggregates is an interfering condition — to that, the following must be said. In the case of inference, verbal cognition, and the like, since the establishment of the probandum and the like serve as causes, by the principle 'because that which [is related] to the two qualifiers,' the general causal relation is established that what is delimited by qualifier-cognition-ness is a cause of what is delimited by qualified-cognition-ness. Even in cases where [the objects are] cognizable by a single aggregate, the qualified cognition arises from the cognition of the qualifier by postulating [such cognition]. Therefore, since the pervading character of the <s>sādhya</s> by 'having objects cognizable by different aggregates' is broken, its status as an interfering condition is not possible.

children.text:
sarvamidaṃ
manasikṛtyaiva dīpikāyāmuktam ---
children.translated_text: Having considered all this, it is stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s> —

children.text:
'nanu nirvikalpake kiṃ
pramāṇamiti cet-na/ gauḥ iti
children.translated_text: 'If it be asked: what is the proof for <s>nirvikalpaka</s>? — [we reply:] no [difficulty]. The cognition 'cow'

children.text:
viśiṣṭajñānaṃ
viśeṣaṇajñānajanyaṃ viśiṣṭajñānatvāt daṇḍīti
children.translated_text: — a qualified cognition — is produced by a cognition of the qualifier, because it is a qualified cognition, like the cognition

children.text:
jñānavat
ityanumānasya pramāṇatvāt/ viśeṣaṇajñānasyāpi
children.translated_text: 'a man with a staff' — this inference serves as the proof. And since if the cognition of the qualifier too

children.text:
savikalpakatve
anavasthāprasaṅgāt nirvikalpakasiddhiḥ'
children.translated_text: were <s>savikalpaka</s>, an infinite regress would follow, <s>nirvikalpaka</s> is established'

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: — thus.

children.text: saṃnikarṣavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃnikarṣa</s>-vicāra (Investigation of Sense-Object Contact)

children.text:
tarkasaṃgrahe
dīpikāyāṃ ca pratyakṣahetuḥ saṃnikarṣaḥ saṃyogādibhedena ṣaḍvidha
iti sodāharaṇaṃ pradarśitam/ prakāśikāyāṃ pratyakṣaṃ dvividhaṃ
laukikam alaukikaṃ ceti/ laukikapratyakṣahetuḥ saṃnikarṣaḥ
saṃyogādibhedena ṣaṅvidhaḥ/ alaukikapratyakṣahetuḥ saṃnikarṣaḥ
sāmānyalakṣaṇaḥ jñānalakṣaṇaḥ yogajadharma iti trividha iti
pratyapādi/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> and the <s>Dīpikā</s>, <s>saṃnikarṣa</s> (sense-object contact), the cause of perception, has been shown with examples as sixfold, beginning with conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and the rest. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, it was established that perception is twofold — ordinary (<s>laukika</s>) and extraordinary (<s>alaukika</s>). The cause of ordinary perception, <s>saṃnikarṣa</s>, is sixfold beginning with conjunction. The cause of extraordinary perception, <s>saṃnikarṣa</s>, is threefold: <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s> (perception through universals), <s>jñānalakṣaṇa</s> (perception through prior knowledge), and <s>yogaja</s> (born of yogic power).

children.text:
ṣoḍhā saṃnikarṣastu
nyāyavārtike prastutaḥ, sūtre bhāṣye vā na dṛśyate kvāpi/ etaṃ
viṣayamadhikṛtya nyāyabhūṣaṇakārāḥ1 itthaṃ kiñcidvicārayanti ---
ācāryādhyayanapādanāmā nyāyasūtrabhāṣyakāraḥ nikarṣaśabdenaiva saṃbandha
ityarthe labdhe 'sam' ityupasargabalāt saṃbhavī saṃbandhaḥ
saṃnikarṣaśabdenocyate/ saṃbhavī ca saṃbandhaḥ ṣaḍvidha eveti
pratyapādayat/ tanna/ tathā sati 'ni' ityupasargasya vyarthatvāt/
karṣaśabdenaiva dhātūnāmanekārthatvāt saṃbandha ityarthe labdhe 'saṃ'
śabdamahimnā ṣaḍvidhatvalābhe niśabdo vyartha iti/ karṣaśabdasya
saṃbandhārthakatvena lokaprasiddhirnāstīti cet nikaṣaśabdasya
saṃbandhavācakatvena kutra prasiddhiriti bhavatā vaktavyam/
nikṛṣṭatvavācakatayā hi nikarṣaśabdo loke prasiddho na
sambandhavācakatayā/ tasmāt 'sam' 'ni' ityupasargadvayayukta eva
kṛṣadhātuḥ saṃbandhamabhidhatte yathā 'sam' 'ava' ityupasargadvayapūrvakaḥ
iṇdhātuḥ samavāyam/ tasmāt kṛṣadhātoḥ sambandhārthakatvadyotakatayā
sārthakaḥ 'sam' śabdaḥ ṣaṅvidhatvapratipādanāya nālamiti 'sam'
śabdamahimnā ṣaḍvidhatvalābha iti vyākhyānaṃ na samīcīnam/
tasmādyathā ālokādayaḥ sūtrānuktā api anvayavyatirekabalāt
pratyakṣahetutayā anumanyante tathā ṣaḍvidhānāṃ saṃnikarṣāṇāmapi
pratyakṣaṃ pratyanvayavyatirekabalāddhetutvaṃ sidhyati/ nyāyasiddho 'yamartho
yataḥ sūtrakārairna nirākṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The sixfold <s>saṃnikarṣa</s> is discussed in the <s>Nyāyavārtika</s>, but is not found anywhere in the <s>sūtra</s> or the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. Regarding this topic, the author of the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> deliberates somewhat as follows: The teacher <s>Adhyayanapāda</s>, the author of the <s>Nyāyasūtrabhāṣya</s>, [held that] since the word 'nikarṣa' alone yields the meaning 'relation,' by the force of the prefix 'sam,' a possible relation is denoted by the word <s>saṃnikarṣa</s>. And the possible relation is precisely sixfold — thus he established. [The author responds:] that is not so. In that case, the prefix 'ni' would be purposeless. Since by the word 'karṣa' alone, due to the multiple meanings of verbal roots, the meaning 'relation' is obtained, and since the sixfold nature is obtained by the force of 'saṃ,' the syllable 'ni' would be purposeless. If it be said that the word 'karṣa' is not well-known in the world as meaning 'relation,' then you too must answer where the word 'nikarṣa' is well-known as meaning 'relation.' For the word 'nikarṣa' is well-known in the world as meaning 'inferiority,' not as meaning 'relation.' Therefore, it is only the root 'kṛṣ' combined with both prefixes 'sam' and 'ni' that denotes relation — just as the root 'iṇ' preceded by both prefixes 'sam' and 'ava' [denotes] <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). Therefore, since the syllable 'sam' serves to indicate the relational meaning of the root 'kṛṣ,' it is insufficient for establishing the sixfold nature — thus the explanation that 'the sixfold nature is obtained by the force of the word sam' is not correct. Therefore, just as the causes of perception such as light and the like, though not mentioned in the <s>sūtra</s>, are accepted as causes of perception by the force of co-presence and co-absence, so too the six types of <s>saṃnikarṣa</s> are established as causes of perception by the force of co-presence and co-absence with respect to perception. This matter being established by reasoning,

children.text:
atastatsaṃmata
ityunnīyate/ 'paramatamapratiṣiddhamanumatamiti hi tantrayuktiḥ' iti
nyāyāt iti/
children.translated_text: since the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> has not refuted it, it is inferred to be accepted by him. For there is the methodological principle: 'An opposing view not refuted is [considered] accepted' — thus.

children.text:
vaiśeṣikadarśane tu
saṃnikarṣaprabhedaviṣaye nyāyasūtrāpekṣayā kiñcit spaṣṭatayā
sūcanamasti/ tathā hi ---
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system, however, regarding the varieties of perceptual contact (<s>saṃnikarṣa</s>), there is a somewhat clearer indication compared to the <s>Nyāyasūtras</s>. Thus —

children.text:
'ātmamanasoḥ
saṃyogādātmapratyakṣam' (vai.sū.9-1-11) iti sūtreṇa
ātmaviṣayakapratyakṣaṃ prati manassaṃyogaḥ kāraṇamityuktam/ tena
dravyaviṣayakapratyakṣaṃ prati indriyasaṃyogaḥ kāraṇamiti sūcitam/
tataḥ-- 'ātmasamavāyādātmaguṇeṣu' (vai.sū.9-1-15) iti sūtreṇa
ātmasamavetajñānādiguṇaviṣayakapratyakṣe manassaṃyuktasamavāyaḥ
kāraṇamiti spaṣṭīkṛtam/ tathā --
children.translated_text: By the <s>sūtra</s> 'From the conjunction of the self and mind, perception of the self [arises]' (Vai.Sū. 9-1-11), it is stated that the conjunction with mind (<s>manassaṃyoga</s>) is the cause of perception pertaining to the self. Thereby it is indicated that conjunction with the sense-organ (<s>indriyasaṃyoga</s>) is the cause of perception pertaining to substances (<s>dravya</s>). Then, by the <s>sūtra</s> 'From inherence in the self, [perception arises] regarding the qualities of the self' (Vai.Sū. 9-1-15), it is made clear that <s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s> (inherence in what is conjoined [with mind]) is the cause in the perception of qualities like knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) etc. inhering in the self. Likewise —

children.text:
'anekadravyasamavāyādrūpaviśeṣācca rūpopalabdhiḥ' (vai.sū.4.1.7)
'saṃkhyāḥ parimāṇaṃ karma ca rūpidravyasamavāyāccākṣuṣāṇi'
(vai.sū.4-1-11) iti sūtrābhyāṃ dravyagataguṇakriyāviṣayakapratyakṣe
cakṣussaṃyuktasamavāyaḥ kāraṇamiti spaṣṭamuktam/
children.translated_text: By the <s>sūtras</s> 'From inherence in multiple substances and from the specific [nature] of color, there is apprehension of color' (Vai.Sū. 4.1.7) and 'Number, dimension, and action are perceived by the eye from inherence in a substance possessing color' (Vai.Sū. 4-1-11), it is clearly stated that <s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s> (inherence in what is conjoined [with the sense-organ]) is the cause in perception pertaining to qualities and actions residing in substances.

children.text:
'etena guṇatve bhāve
ca sarvendriyaṃ jñānaṃ vyākhyātam' (vai.sū.4.1.13) iti sūtreṇa yathā
guṇapratyakṣe dravyasamavāyo hetustathā guṇagatajātipratyakṣe 'pi
saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyo heturiti vyañjitam/ tathā-
children.translated_text: By the <s>sūtra</s> 'By this, knowledge through all sense-organs regarding quality-hood and being [i.e. universals] is explained' (Vai.Sū. 4.1.13), it is implied that just as inherence in the substance is the cause of perception of a quality, so too <s>saṃyuktasamavetasamavāya</s> (inherence in what inheres in what is conjoined) is the cause of perception of the universal (<s>jāti</s>) residing in a quality. Likewise —

children.text:
'śrotragrahaṇo yor'thaḥ
sa śabdaḥ' (vai.sū.2-2-21) iti sūtreṇa śabdasya
śrotrajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ lakṣaṇamuktvā,
children.translated_text: By the <s>sūtra</s> 'That object which is grasped by the ear is sound' (Vai.Sū. 2-2-21), having stated as the definition of sound that it is the object of perception born from the ear,

children.text:
'ekadravyatvānna dravyam'
(vai.sū.2-2-23) iti sūtreṇa śabdasyādravyatve
ākāśātmakaikadravyasamavāyasyaṃ het karaṇāt,
children.translated_text: by the <s>sūtra</s> 'It is not a substance, because of being [inherent] in a single substance' (Vai.Sū. 2-2-23), since [this sūtra] establishes that sound is not a substance by adducing its inherence in a single substance, namely <s>ākāśa</s> (space),

children.text:
'bhūyasttvāt
gandhavattvācca pṛthivī gandhajñāne prakṛtiḥ'
children.translated_text: 'Because of preponderance [of earth], and because of possessing smell, earth is the material cause in the cognition of smell'

children.text:
'tathāpastejo vāyuśca
rasarūpasparśāviśeṣāt' (vai.sū.8-2-6) ityāṣṭamikasūtrābhyāṃ
ghrāṇarasanacakṣusttvacāṃ caturṇāmindriyāṇāṃ
bhūtaprakṛtikatvamupanyasyatā śrotrasya prakṛtiviśeṣānirdeśena
nityatvasūcanadvārā ākāśasya śrotratvasūcanācca śrotrasamavāyaḥ
śabdapratyakṣe heturiti dhvanitam/
children.translated_text: by the eighth-chapter <s>sūtras</s> — 'And likewise water, fire, and air, because of the non-distinction of taste, color, and touch [respectively]' (Vai.Sū. 8-2-6) — while presenting the elemental material nature of the four sense-organs (smell, taste, sight, and touch), by not specifying a particular material nature for the ear, through the indication of the ear's eternality, and through the indication that <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is the [substance of the] ear, it is implied that <s>śrotrasamavāya</s> (inherence in the ear) is the cause in the perception of sound.

children.text:
'etena guṇatve bhāve
ca' (vai.sū.4-1-13)
children.translated_text: 'By this, regarding quality-hood and being' (Vai.Sū. 4-1-13) —

children.text:
iti sūtroktanyāyena
śabdatvapratyakṣe samavetasamavāyākhyaḥ saṃnikarṣo 'pi sūcita eva/ tathā
children.translated_text: by the principle stated in this <s>sūtra</s>, the perceptual contact called <s>samavetasamavāya</s> (inherence in what inheres) is also indicated for the perception of soundness (<s>śabdatva</s>). Likewise —

children.text:
'asaditi
bhūtapratyakṣābhāvāt bhūtasmṛtervirodhipratyakṣavat'
children.translated_text: '[That it] is non-existent — [this is known] from the absence of perception of what has existed, and from the memory of what has existed, like the perception of an opposite'

children.text:
iti sūtraṃ dṛśyate/
tasyāyamarthaḥ --- asan ghaṭa ityadyākārakamabhāvapratyakṣaṃ
virodhipratyakṣavat pratiyogighaṭapratyakṣatulyam/ pratiyogino
ghaṭasya pratyakṣaṃ yathānubhavasiddhaṃ laukikasaṃnikarṣajanyaṃ ca tathā
abhāvapratyakṣamapi nāpalāpārhaṃ saṃnikarṣajanyaṃ cetyarthaḥ/ abhāvapratyakṣe
tu pratiyogino yogyānupalabdhiḥ smaraṇaṃ ceti
sahakārikāriṇadvayamapekṣitamiti vaśeṣaḥ/ tadāha ---
bhūtapratyakṣābhāvāt bhūtasmṛteriti/ bhūtasya utpadya vinaṣṭasya ghaṭādeḥ
pratiyoginaḥ upalabdhyabhāvāt smaraṇāccetyarthaḥ/ evaṃ cābhāvapratyakṣasya
saṃnikarṣajanyatvaṃ sūcayan sūtrakāraḥ saṃyogasamavāyādyasaṃbhavāt
viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvātmakaṃ saṃnikarṣamapi samasūcayat/ tathā ca
ṣaḍvidha iti śabdena avibhakto 'pi ṣaṭsaṃkhyākaḥ saṃnikarṣaḥ
vaiśeṣikatantrasūcita iti niścinumahe/ praśastapādabhāṣye
pratyakṣanirūpaṇāvasare viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaṃ vinā anye pañca
saṃnikarṣāḥ nirdiṣṭāḥ/ abhāvapadārthamadhikṛtya praśastapādabhāṣye yato
nirūpaṇaṃ nāsti ato viśeṣaṇatākhyasaṃnikarṣasya tatra prastāvo na
vidyate/ kandalīkārāstu ṣaḍvidhamapi saṃnikarṣaṃ sodāharaṇaṃ
pradarśayāmāsa/
children.translated_text: — this <s>sūtra</s> is seen. Its meaning is as follows: The perception of absence (<s>abhāva</s>), of the form 'the pot is non-existent,' is like the perception of an opposite — i.e., it is equivalent to the perception of the counter-positive (<s>pratiyogin</s>), the pot. Just as the perception of the counter-positive pot is established by experience and is born from ordinary perceptual contact (<s>laukikasaṃnikarṣa</s>), so too the perception of absence is not to be denied and is also born from perceptual contact — this is the meaning. However, in the perception of absence, two auxiliary conditions are required: the qualified non-apprehension (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>) of the counter-positive and its memory (<s>smaraṇa</s>) — this is the distinction. This is what is meant by 'from the absence of perception of what has existed, and from the memory of what has existed' — i.e., from the absence of apprehension and from the memory of the counter-positive, namely the pot etc. that has arisen and perished. Thus, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (the author of the sūtras), while indicating that the perception of absence is born from perceptual contact, since conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), etc. are impossible [in the case of absence], also thereby indicated a perceptual contact of the nature of the qualifier-qualified relation (<s>viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāva</s>). And thus we conclude that a sixfold perceptual contact, though not explicitly divided by the word 'sixfold,' is indicated in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system. In the <s>Praśastapādabhāṣya</s>, in the course of examining perception, the five perceptual contacts other than the qualifier-qualified relation are specified. Since there is no examination of the category of absence (<s>abhāva</s>) in the <s>Praśastapādabhāṣya</s>, the perceptual contact called qualifier-hood (<s>viśeṣaṇatā</s>) has no occasion there. But the <s>Kandalī</s> commentators have demonstrated all six types of perceptual contact with examples.

children.text:
pratyakṣasūtre
nyāyavārtikakārāḥ1 'saṃnikarṣaḥ punaḥ ṣoḍhā bhidyate, ityādinā
granthena pūrvoktān ṣaḍvidhān saṃnikarṣān sodāharaṇaṃ
prādarśayan/ sūtrādayaṃ vibhāgaḥ kathaṃ labhya iti śaṅkāyām ---
children.translated_text: In [commenting on] the <s>sūtra</s> on perception, the author of the <s>Nyāyavārtika</s> demonstrated the aforementioned six types of perceptual contact with examples through the passage beginning 'Perceptual contact is divided in six ways.' When the doubt [arose] as to how this division can be derived from the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.text:
'so 'yaṃ
saṃnikarṣaśabdaḥ saṃyogasamavāya-
children.translated_text: 'This very word <s>saṃnikarṣa</s> (perceptual contact), being a pervader of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>),

children.text: viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvavyāpakatvādupāttaḥ'
children.translated_text: and the qualifier-qualified relation (<s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s>), is employed [by the sūtrakāra]'

children.text:
iti granthena2
saṃyogasamavāyādisādhāraṇaṃ saṃnikarṣaśabdaṃ prayuktavatā sūtrakāreṇa
saṃbhāvitāḥ saṃnikarṣā grahītavyā iti sūcitamiti samāhitam/
children.translated_text: — by this passage, it is settled that the <s>sūtrakāra</s>, having used the word <s>saṃnikarṣa</s> as a common [term] for conjunction, inherence, etc., indicated that the [various] possible perceptual contacts should be understood.

children.text: viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: The qualifier-qualified relation (<s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s>)

children.text:
nyāyavārtike
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ saṃnikarṣaḥ proktaḥ/ sa ca
samavāyaviṣayakapratyakṣaṃ prati
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyavārtika</s>, the qualifier-qualified relation is stated as the sixth perceptual contact. And it is established as the cause

children.text:
abhāvaviṣayakapratyakṣaṃ
prati ca heturiti prasādhitam/ tatra ṭīkāyām3 --
children.translated_text: of perception pertaining to inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) and of perception pertaining to absence (<s>abhāva</s>). In the <s>Ṭīkā</s> (sub-commentary) on that —

children.text:
'viśeṣaṇabhāvena
saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇaṃ samavetaviśeṣaṇaṃ ca saṃgṛhītam' iti vyākhyānaṃ
dṛśyate/ tasyāyamāśayaḥ/ bhūtalādiviśeṣyakābhāvapratyakṣaṃ prati
saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ saṃnikarṣaṃḥ/ akāre 'nudāttasvaro
nāstītyādiśabdaviśeṣyakābhāvapratyakṣaṃ prati samavetaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ
saṃnikarṣa iti/ nyāyasāre4 tu ---
children.translated_text: 'By the mode of qualifier, [the terms] <s>saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier of what is conjoined) and <s>samavetaviśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier of what inheres) are included' — this explanation is seen. Its purport is as follows: For the perception of absence whose qualificand is the ground (<s>bhūtala</s>) etc., <s>saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being the qualifier of what is conjoined) is the perceptual contact. For the perception of absence whose qualificand is a particular sound, such as 'there is no <s>udātta</s> accent in the syllable <s>a</s>,' <s>samavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being the qualifier of what inheres) is the perceptual contact. But in the <s>Nyāyasāra</s> —

children.text: 'etapañcavidhasambandhasaṃbaddhaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvāt
children.translated_text: 'From the qualifier-qualified relation connected by these five kinds of relation,

children.text: dṛśyābhāvasamavāyayorgrahaṇam'
children.translated_text: there is apprehension of visible absence and inherence'

children.text:
ityabhihitam/
viśeṣaṇatvaṃ pañcavidhaṃ saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatvam,
saṃyuktasamavetaviśeṣaṇatvam, saṃyuktasamavetasamavetaviśeṣaṇatvam,
samavetaviśeṣaṇatvam, samavetasamavetaviśeṣaṇatvam ceti tadāśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: — this is stated. The purport is that qualifier-hood (<s>viśeṣaṇatva</s>) is fivefold: (1) <s>saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being the qualifier of what is conjoined), (2) <s>saṃyuktasamavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being the qualifier of what inheres in what is conjoined), (3) <s>saṃyuktasamavetasamavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being the qualifier of what inheres in what inheres in what is conjoined), (4) <s>samavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being the qualifier of what inheres), and (5) <s>samavetasamavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being the qualifier of what inheres in what inheres).

children.text:
dīpikāyāṃ
prakāśikāyāṃ ca viśeṣaṇatvaviśeṣyatvayorubhayorapi saṃnikarṣatvam
sayuktikaṃ pratyapādi/ tadvistaro bālapriyāyāṃ draṣṭavyaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> and the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, both qualifier-hood and qualificand-hood are rationally established as [valid forms of] perceptual contact. The details of this should be seen in the <s>Bālapriyā</s>.

children.text:
trividhaḥ
alaukikasaṃnikarṣastu prācīnagrantheṣu na dṛśyate/ maṇikāraistatra tatra
vyavahṛtaḥ muktāvalīkārādibhiḥ prapañcitaḥ/ anumānakhaṇḍe maṇau
sāmānyalakṣaṇā pratyāsattiḥ paraṃ vistareṇa sthāpitetyāstāmiyatā/
children.translated_text: The threefold extraordinary perceptual contact (<s>alaukikasaṃnikarṣa</s>) is not found in the ancient texts. It was employed here and there by <s>Maṇikāra</s> (the author of the <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s>) and elaborated by the author of the <s>Muktāvalī</s> and others. In the section on inference in the <s>Maṇi</s>, <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā pratyāsatti</s> (the extraordinary perceptual contact through a universal) alone has been established at length — let this much suffice.

children.text: ( 9 ) anupalabdhivicāraḥ
children.translated_text: (9) Investigation of Non-apprehension (<s>Anupalabdhi</s>)

children.text:
anupalabdhisahakṛtendriyeṇaivābhāvajñānopapattau anupalabdhiḥ na
pramāṇāntaram/ adhikaraṇajñānārthamapekṣitasyendriyasyaiva
karaṇatvopapattau anupalabdheḥ karaṇatvāyogāditi dīpikākārāḥ/
etattattvamidānīṃ vicārya nirdhāryate/
children.translated_text: Since cognition of absence can be accounted for by the sense-organ itself assisted by non-apprehension, non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) is not a separate means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Since the sense-organ itself, which is required for the cognition of the substratum, can be established as the instrument, non-apprehension cannot serve as the instrument — so say the authors of the <s>Dīpikā</s>. The truth of this matter is now examined and determined.

children.text:
nyāyadarśane --- 'na
catuṣṭvamaittihyārthāpattisaṃbhavābhāvaprāmāṇyāt' (nyā. sū. 2-2-1)
iti sūtreṇa catvāryeva pramāṇānītyetanna saṃgacchate/ aitihyam
arthāpattiḥ saṃbhavaḥ abhāvaśceti caturṇāṃ pramāṇānāṃ saṃbhavāt
ityāśaṅkya, 'śabde aitihyānarthāntarabhāvāt
anumāner'thāpattisaṃbhavābhāvānāmanarthāntarabhāvāccāpratiṣedhaḥ' (nyā.
sū. 2-2-2) iti sūtreṇa aitihyasya śabde arthāpattisaṃbhavābhāvānāṃ
trayāṇāmanumāne 'ntarbhāvāt catvāryeva pramāṇānīti siddhāntitam/
tatrābhāvapadena kiṃ vivakṣitam? tasya kathamanumāne 'ntarbhāvaḥ? iti
viṣaye nyāyasūtrataḥ kimapi nāvagamyate/ nyāyabhāṣyakāraḥ
tatsūtravyākhyānāvasare ---
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāya</s> system — by the <s>sūtra</s> 'There are not [only] four [means of knowledge], because of the validity of tradition (<s>aitihya</s>), presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), probability (<s>saṃbhava</s>), and non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>)' (Nyā.Sū. 2-2-1), [the objection is raised that] it is not consistent [to say] there are only four <s>pramāṇas</s>, because four [additional] <s>pramāṇas</s> — tradition, presumption, probability, and non-existence — exist. Anticipating this [objection], by the <s>sūtra</s> 'Because tradition is not different from verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), and because presumption, probability, and non-existence are not different from inference (<s>anumāna</s>), there is no prohibition' (Nyā.Sū. 2-2-2), it is concluded that there are indeed only four <s>pramāṇas</s>, since tradition is subsumed under verbal testimony, and the three — presumption, probability, and non-existence — are subsumed under inference. What is intended by the word <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence/absence) there? How is it subsumed under inference? — regarding this, nothing [definitive] is understood from the <s>Nyāyasūtras</s>. The author of the <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s>, in the course of commenting on that <s>sūtra</s> —

children.text:
'abhāvo virodhī
abhūtaṃ bhūtasayaḥ avidyamānaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Absence is [that which is] contrary [to presence]; what has not [yet] come into being [is known] from what has come into being; what is non-existent —

children.text:
varṣakarma vidyamānasya
vāyvabhrasaṃyogasya pratipādakama/
children.translated_text: [namely] the action of raining — is the indicator of the existing conjunction of wind and clouds.

children.text:
vidhārake hi
vāyvabhrasaṃyoge gurutvādapāṃ patanakama
children.translated_text: For when the conjunction of wind and clouds, which sustains [the rain], exists, the falling of waters due to gravity

children.text: na bhavati'
children.translated_text: does not occur'

children.text:
iti abhāṣata/
tasyāyamāśayaḥ - abhāvo 'pi kasyacidarthasya pramiti-he turbhavati, yathā
toyapātarūpavṛṣṭyabhāvaḥ vāyumeghasaṃyogasya/ ataḥ
abhāvenāpyarthāntarapramityutpattyā abhāvo 'pi pramāṇamiti pūrvapakṣaḥ/
siddhāntastu - satyamabhāvaḥ pramāṇam, na tvatiriktaṃ pramāṇam/ abhāvasya
liṅgavidhayā arthāntarapramitijanakatvenānumāne 'ntarbhāvāt iti/
vārtikatātparyaṭīkayorapyevamevopapāditam/ paraṃ tveteṣu
mūlagrantheṣu mīmāṃsakaiḥ abhāvaśabdena vyavahniyamāṇaṃ yat
atupalabdhyākhyaṃ pramāṇaṃ tasya prastāva eva nāsti/
yadyapyanupalabdherapyupalabdhyabhāvarūpatayā tasyāpi
ghaṭābhāvādipratyāyakasya pramāṇatvaśaṅkā tasyānumāne 'ntarbhāvaśca
pūrvottarapakṣasūtrābhyāṃ sūcyata ityasti saṃbhāvayitumavakāśaḥ tathapi
bhāṣyavārtikādito 'syāśayasya sūcakaṃ kimapi nopalabhyate/
children.translated_text: — thus he spoke. His purport is this: Absence too serves as the means of ascertaining some object; for example, the absence of rainfall (in the form of the falling of water) [serves as the means of knowing] the conjunction of wind and clouds. Therefore, [the objection is:] since through absence too, cognition of another object is produced, absence too is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) — this is the prima facie position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). But the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is: True, absence is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, but it is not an additional <s>pramāṇa</s> — because absence, functioning as a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>), generates cognition of another object and is therefore subsumed under inference. This is established in the same way in the <s>Vārtika</s> and the <s>Tātparyaṭīkā</s> as well. However, in these foundational texts, there is no occasion at all for the <s>pramāṇa</s> called <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), which is what the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> denote by the word <s>abhāva</s>. Although there is room to conjecture that the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> and <s>siddhānta</s> sūtras also hint at the doubt about the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood of non-apprehension — since non-apprehension too, being of the nature of absence of apprehension, produces awareness of pot-absence etc. — and its subsumption under inference, nevertheless no indication of this purport is found from the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, <s>Vārtika</s>, etc.

children.text:
kaṇādamuniḥ
abhāvapramāṇamadhikṛtya viśiṣya na kiñcidabhyadhāt/ tathāpi 'asaditi
bhūtapratyakṣābhāvāt
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Kaṇāda</s> did not specifically state anything regarding the <s>pramāṇa</s> of absence. Nevertheless, by the <s>sūtra</s> 'That it is non-existent — from the absence of perception of what has existed,

children.text:
bhūtasmṛteḥ' [vai.sū.9-1-6] iti sūtreṇa abhāvapratyakṣaṃ
pratiyogyupalambhābhāvajanyamiti kathanena
pratiyogyupalambhābhāvasahakṛtamindriyamabhāvapratyakṣaheturiti
sūcitavāt/ kandalīkāraḥ1 ----
children.translated_text: and from the memory of what has existed' (Vai.Sū. 9-1-6), by stating that the perception of absence is born from the non-apprehension of the counter-positive, he indicated that the sense-organ assisted by the non-apprehension of the counter-positive is the cause of the perception of absence. The <s>Kandalī</s> commentator —

children.text:
'api
cendriyārthasaṃnikarṣādupalabhyamāne bhūtale
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, when the ground is apprehended through the contact of the sense-organ and the object,

children.text:
abhāvajñānamapi bhavati
aghaṭaṃ bhūtalamiti /
children.translated_text: the cognition of absence also arises — [namely] 'the ground without a pot';

children.text:
tatra
bhūtalasyevābhāvasyāpi pratyakṣatā kiṃ neṣyate'
children.translated_text: therein, why should the perceptual status of absence not be accepted, just as [it is accepted] for the ground?'

children.text:
iti granthena
abhāvabuddhiḥ pratyakṣepyantarbhāvayituṃ śakyate, ato na tatsādhanaṃ
pramāṇāntaramanveṣṭavyamiti pratyapādayat/
children.translated_text: — by this passage, he established that the cognition of absence can be subsumed under perception itself, and therefore no separate <s>pramāṇa</s> need be sought as its means.

children.text:
śabarasvāminaḥ
abhāvākhyapramāṇamadhikṛtya2 ---
children.translated_text: Regarding the <s>pramāṇa</s> called absence, <s>Śabarasvāmin</s> —

children.text:
'abhāvo 'pi
pramāṇābhāvaḥ nāstītyasyārthasyāsaṃnikṛṣṭasya'
children.translated_text: 'Absence too is a <s>pramāṇa</s> — [it is] the absence of [other] <s>pramāṇas</s>, [operative] for the meaning "it does not exist," which is not in contact [with the senses]'

children.text:
ityabhāṣanta/ 'bhūtale
ghaṭo nāsti' ityevaṃ pratīyamāno yo nañartho 'bhāvaḥ
indriyāsaṃnikṛṣṭaḥ tasya bodhakaṃ pramāṇam abhāva ityucyate/
abhāvo nāma pramāṇābhāvaḥ, pratyakṣādipramāṇapañcakābhāva ityarthaḥ/
ayamevānupalabdhipadena paścātkālikairvyavahriyate/
children.translated_text: — thus he spoke. The meaning of the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) that is cognized in such [judgments] as 'there is no pot on the ground' — [this] absence, which is not in contact with the sense-organs — the <s>pramāṇa</s> that generates awareness of it is called <s>abhāva</s> (absence). Absence [as a pramāṇa] means the absence of [the other five] <s>pramāṇas</s> — namely, the absence of the five <s>pramāṇas</s> beginning with perception — this is the meaning. This is what later authors refer to by the term <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension).

children.text:
udayanācāryāḥ1
anupalabdheḥ pratyakṣānumānayorantarbhāvaṃ sādhayanti sma/ tathā hi -
anupalabdhiḥ kadācit jñāyamānā abhāvapramāṃ prati kāraṇam,
kadāciccājñāyamānā/ tatra jñātānupalabdheḥ anumāne, ajñātānupalabdheḥ
pratyakṣe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/ jñātakāraṇasya parokṣajñānajanakatāyāḥ ajñātakāraṇasya
pratyakṣajñānajanakatāyāśca liṅgendriyādau darśanāt/
jñātānupalabdherudāharaṇaṃ yathā - mandirāccaitramānetumājñaptaḥ preṣyaḥ
svāminaṃ kathayati - 'nipuṇataramanviṣṭo mayā mandire caitraḥ, evamapi
nopalabdhaḥ' iti/ asmācca mandire caitrasya yogyānupalabdhiṃ jñātvā
svāmī anuminoti 'preṣyapraveśasamaye caitro mandire
children.translated_text: The master <s>Udayana</s> established the subsumption of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) under perception and inference. Thus: Non-apprehension, when it is itself cognized, is the cause of the <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) regarding absence; and sometimes it is not cognized [as such]. Of these, the known non-apprehension is subsumed under inference, and the unknown non-apprehension under perception — because a known cause is seen to generate indirect knowledge (as in inference through a mark), and an unknown cause [is seen to generate] direct knowledge (as in perception through a sense-organ). An example of known non-apprehension: A servant commanded to bring <s>Caitra</s> from the mansion tells his master: 'I searched the mansion most carefully for <s>Caitra</s>, but even so did not find him.' From this, knowing the qualified non-apprehension of <s>Caitra</s> in the mansion, the master infers: 'At the time of the servant's entry, <s>Caitra</s> was not in the mansion'

children.text:
nāsīt' iti/ atra
parakīyānupalabdhiḥ śabdato jñāyamānā anumityātmakaṃ parokṣajñānaṃ
janayatīti/ evameva prātaḥkālikābhāvapratītirapi vyākhyātavyā/ tathā
hi caitro mandire prātarāsīt kim? iti madhyāhne kenacit
pṛṣṭe kaścidevaṃ manyate - nipuṇataraṃ prātaścaitrānveṣaṇāya mandiraṃ
praviṣṭavatāpi mayā yasmāccaitro nopalabdhaḥ, tasmāttadā sa tatra
nāsīditi/ atra svayameva svakīyānupalabdhiṃ kālāntare jñātvā
abhāvamanuminoti/ tasmātprātaḥkālikasyābhāvasya pratītirmadhyāhne
jñāyamānā jñātānupalabdhijanyatvādanumitirūpeti/
children.translated_text: was not [present]' — thus. Here, the non-apprehension belonging to another person, being known through verbal testimony, generates indirect knowledge (parokṣajñāna) in the form of inference (anumiti). In the same way, the cognition of absence at a morning time is also to be explained. For instance, when someone asks at noon 'Was Caitra in the temple in the morning?', someone reasons thus: 'Since even by me, who entered the temple in the morning for a most careful search for Caitra, Caitra was not apprehended, therefore he was not there at that time.' Here, one recalls one's own non-apprehension at a different time and infers the absence. Therefore, the cognition of the morning-time absence, being known at noon, is inferential in nature because it arises from a known non-apprehension.

children.text:
ajñātānupalabdhijanyaṃ
tu jñānaṃ pratyakṣam/ tatra catvāro hetava upanyastāḥ---
children.translated_text: But the cognition arising from an unknown non-apprehension is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Therein, four reasons have been presented —

children.text: 'pratipatterapārokṣyādindriyasyānupakṣayāt/
children.translated_text: 'Because of the non-mediated character of the cognition, because of the non-impairment of the sense organ,

children.text:
ajñātakāraṇatvācca
bhāvāveśācca cetasaḥ//' iti/
children.translated_text: because of the unknown-ness of the cause, and because of the mind's absorption in a positive entity' — thus.

children.text:
indriyabhūtalasaṃyogānantarabhavā 'aghaṭaṃ bhūtalaṃ'
ityabhāvapratītiḥ indriyakaraṇikā aparokṣarūpatvāt
kāryāntarānupakṣīṇendriyasāpekṣatvāt ajñāyamānakaraṇakatvāt
manaso bhāvarūpaṃ kāraṇāntaramapekṣyaiva
bāhyānubhavajanakatvaniyamasiddhāt
manassahakāribhāvabhūtakaraṇasāpekṣatvācceti uktaślokasyārthaḥ/ ete ca
hetavaḥ kusumāñjalau tattvacintāmaṇau savistaramupapāditāstatraiva
draṣṭavyāḥ/
children.translated_text: The cognition of absence 'the ground is without a pot' (<s>aghaṭaṃ bhūtalam</s>), which arises immediately after the contact of the sense organ with the ground, has the sense organ as its instrument, because it is of the nature of immediate apprehension, because it requires a sense organ not impaired by another operation, because its instrument is unknown [to the cognizer], and because of the established principle that in generating external experience [the mind] necessarily depends on an additional cause of the nature of a positive entity — that is, it depends on a cooperating cause in the form of a positive entity [conjoined with] the mind. This is the meaning of the cited verse. And these reasons have been established in detail in the <s>Kusumāñjali</s> and the <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s>, and should be examined there.

children.text:
api ca prācīneṣu
sarveṣu grantheṣu yogyasyānupalabdhiḥ iti ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣamabhipretya
yogyapratiyogiprakārakayogyādhikaraṇaviśeṣyakopalambhābhāvo
yogyānupalabdhiriti vyavahriyate sma/
yogyapratiyogiprakārakatvaviśeṣaṇāt stambhe piśācābhāvasya na
pratyakṣatā/ yogyādhikaraṇaviśeṣyakatvaniveśāt jalaparamāṇau
