And accordingly, because in what possesses the absence of <s>maṅgala</s> there exists <s>samāpti</s> in the form of the absence of the absence of <s>samāpti</s>, the counter-positive-ness of the absence of <s>samāpti</s> — that is, the pervasion by the absence of <s>maṅgala</s> in the form of not being the counter-positive of absolute absence residing in what possesses the absence of <s>maṅgala</s> — does not belong to the absence of <s>samāpti</s>. This is the purport.

children.text:
vighnanāśakatvamiṣyate/
vighnānyenasaṅkhyākasyetyuktau tatsaṅgraho na syādityālocyoktam
-
balavattarasya ve
children.translated_text: or [a <s>maṅgala</s>] that is more powerful —

children.text:
ti/ nanu kādambaryādau nāstikakṛte
granthe maṅgalābhāve 'pi samāptidarśanāt vyatirekavyabhicāra iti
śaṅkāyāḥ parihārārthaṃ hi 'kādambaryādau granthādbahireva maṅgalaṃ
kṛtamato na vyabhicāraḥ' iti dīpikāgranthaḥ pravṛttaḥ/ tena ca
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Dīpikā</s> text was introduced to resolve the doubt that 'in the <s>Kādambarī</s> and other works composed by atheists, even in the absence of <s>maṅgala</s>, <s>samāpti</s> is observed, hence there is a deviation in negative concomitance,' stating 'In the <s>Kādambarī</s> and other works, <s>maṅgala</s> was indeed performed outside the text, hence there is no deviation.' And by that —

children.text: bahireva
children.translated_text: 'outside' —

children.text:
granthārambhe maṅgalanibandhanamakṛtvā, maṅgalaṃ kṛtam,
maṅgalanibandhanamave na kṛtam, maṅgalaṃ tu kṛtemevetyartho
labhyate/ sa tu na yuktaḥ; nāstikena kādambaryādigranthapraṇetrā
īśvaranamaskārādirūpamaṅgalakaraṇāsambhavādityāśaṅkya
vyācaṣṭe-
children.translated_text: Without making the <s>maṅgala</s> a subject-matter at the commencement of the work, the <s>maṅgala</s> was performed; the <s>maṅgala</s> subject-matter was simply not composed, but the <s>maṅgala</s> was certainly performed — this meaning is obtained. But that is not appropriate, since it is impossible for the atheist author of the <s>Kādambarī</s> and other works to perform <s>maṅgala</s> in the form of salutation to God (<s>Īśvara</s>) and the like. Anticipating this objection, he explains —

children.text: bahireve
children.translated_text: 'outside' —

children.text: ti/
children.translated_text: means:

children.text: janmāntaraṃ evetyartha
children.translated_text: 'in a previous birth' — this is the meaning.

children.text:
iti/ tathā ca tādṛśagranthakartuḥ etajjnamani nāstikatve 'pi
janmāntare āstikatvāt tadānīṃ kṛtāt maṅgalāt asmin janmani
samāptiḥ/ ataḥ kāraṇābhāve 'pi kāryarūpaḥ vyatirekavyabhicāro
durvaca ityāśayaḥ/ nanu janmāntarīyamaṅgalasya tadānīmeva
naṣṭatvāt etajjanmīyasamāptyavyavahitapūrvamasatastasya 1kathaṃ
kāraṇatvaṃ, kathaṃ vā vyatirekavyabhicāraparihāra ityāśaṅkya
svajanyavighnadhvaṃsavattvasambandhena maṅgalasya kāraṇatvāt
maṅgalābhāve1pi tajjanyavighnadhvaṃsarūpadvārasattvāt
kāraṇatvamupapadyate, yathā yāgasya nāśe 'pi tajjanyāpūrvarūpadvārasya
svargāvyavahitapūrvaṃ sattvāt yāgasya svargakāraṇatvaṃ tadvadityāśayena
samādhatte---
children.translated_text: And accordingly, even though the author of such a work may be an atheist in this birth, due to being a theist in a previous birth, from the <s>maṅgala</s> performed at that time, <s>samāpti</s> [occurs] in this birth. Therefore, even in the absence of the cause, a deviation in negative concomitance in the form of the effect is difficult to assert — this is the intent. Now, since the <s>maṅgala</s> of a previous birth has been destroyed at that very time, and since that [<s>maṅgala</s>], being non-existent immediately prior to the <s>samāpti</s> of this birth, how can it have causality? And how can the deviation in negative concomitance be resolved? — anticipating this doubt, since <s>maṅgala</s> has causality through the relation of possessing the destruction of obstacles produced by it, even in the absence of <s>maṅgala</s>, due to the existence of the intermediary in the form of the destruction of obstacles produced by it, causality is established — just as even after the destruction of the <s>yāga</s> (sacrifice), due to the existence of <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen merit produced by it) immediately prior to heaven, the <s>yāga</s> has causality for heaven — with this intent, he resolves —

children.text:
tādṛśamaṅgalasya
vighnadhvaṃsadvāre
children.translated_text: Through the medium of the destruction of obstacles by such a <s>maṅgala</s> —

children.text: ti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: evaṃ ca kāraṇatvaṃ sidhyatīti
children.translated_text: And thus causality is established —

children.text:
/ pūrvoktarītyā
anvayavyatirekavyabhicārayoḥ parihṛtatvāt
anvayavyatirekavyabhicāraniścayarūpapratibandhakābhāvāt
niyatānvayavyatirekasahacāraniścayarūpakāraṇasattvāt maṅgalasya
samāptikāraṇatvaniścayo bhavatītyarthaḥ/ athavā evaṃ ca -
janmāntarīyamaṅgalasya vighnadhvaṃsadvārā sattvāt
children.translated_text: The meaning is: since by the method stated earlier the deviations in both positive and negative concomitance have been resolved, and since the hindrances in the form of the determination of deviations in positive and negative concomitance are absent, and since the cause in the form of the determination of invariable positive and negative concomitance exists, the determination of the causality of <s>maṅgala</s> for <s>samāpti</s> is established. Alternatively: 'and thus' — since the <s>maṅgala</s> of a previous birth exists through the medium of the destruction of obstacles,
capacity to destroy obstacles is accepted. If it had been said 'whose number is fewer than the obstacles,' then such [cases] would not be included — considering this, it was said —

children.text:
janmāntarīyamaṅgalasya
2samāptayavyavahitapūrvavūttitvarūpaṃ kāraṇatvaṃ sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: the causality of the <s>maṅgala</s> of a previous birth in the form of being present immediately prior to <s>samāpti</s> is established — this is the purport.

children.text:
1. kathaṃ kāraṇatvamiti/
kāryāvyavahitaprākkṣaṇavṛttitvasyaiva kāraṇatvapadārthatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'How can there be causality?' — The purport is: because the meaning of the term 'causality' is precisely the property of being present at the moment immediately prior to the effect.

children.text:
2.
samāptyavyavahitetyādi/ tathā ca sākṣātsambandhena samavāyena samāpteḥ
pūrvaṃ maṅgalasyābhāve 'pi svajanyavighnadhvaṃsavattvasambandhena sattvāt
samāptyavyavahitapūrvakṣaṇavṛttitvamastīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Immediately prior to <s>samāpti</s>' etc. — And accordingly, even though <s>maṅgala</s> is absent prior to <s>samāpti</s> through the direct relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), because it exists through the relation of possessing the destruction of obstacles produced by it, the property of being present at the moment immediately prior to <s>samāpti</s> obtains — this is the purport.

children.text: uktahetudvayādi
children.translated_text: By the two reasons stated above and so forth —

children.text:
ti - 'kiraṇāvalyādau
vighnabāhulyāt samāptyabhāvaḥ, kādambaryādau granthāt bahireva
maṅgalaṃ kṛtam' iti pūrvagranthoktahetudvayādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: by the two reasons stated in the preceding text, namely 'In the <s>Kiraṇāvalī</s> and other works, there is absence of <s>samāpti</s> due to the abundance of obstacles' and 'In the <s>Kādambarī</s> and other works, <s>maṅgala</s> was performed outside the text.'

children.text: svasāmagrīvaśād
children.translated_text: Through the force of its own aggregate [of causes] —

children.text:
iti/ svasyāḥ- samāpteḥ sāmagrī -
buddhipratibhādikāraṇakalāpāḥ tadvaśāt-tadadhīnatayetyarthaḥ/ satyapi
maṅgale buddhipratibhādikāraṇakalāpābhāve granthasamāpterasambhavāt
buddhipratibhādikameva samāptiṃ prati kāraṇam/ maṅgalaṃ tu
samāptipratibandhakavighnotsāraṇe kāraṇam iti maṇikārāśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: 'its own' means 'of <s>samāpti</s>'; 'aggregate' means the collection of causes such as intellect, creative inspiration (<s>pratibhā</s>), and the like; 'through its force' means 'depending on that.' Even when <s>maṅgala</s> is present, if the collection of causes such as intellect, creative inspiration, and the like is absent, the completion of the work is impossible; therefore intellect, creative inspiration, and the like alone are the cause with respect to <s>samāpti</s>. But <s>maṅgala</s> is the cause in removing obstacles that hinder <s>samāpti</s> — this is the intent of the author of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Tattvacintāmaṇi).

children.text:
maṅgalaṃ kartavyamiti
jñānamantarā maṅgalaṃ na ko 'pi kuryāt/ 1tadviṣayakakṛtiṃ prati
tadviśeṣyakakṛtisādhyatājñānasya kāraṇatvāt/ kartavyatvaṃ ca
kṛtisādhyatvam/ maṅgalaṃ kartavyamiti jñānaṃ ca śiṣṭānāṃ granthārambhe
maṅgalānuṣṭhānarūpeṇa ācāreṇa anumitā yā 'samāptikāmo
maṅgalamācareta' iti śrutiḥ tayā bhavati ityāśayena pūrvaṃ
'śiṣṭācārānumitaśrutibodhitakartavyatākamiṣṭadevatānamaskārātmakaṃ
maṅgalam' iti
dīpikāyāmu
children.translated_text: the <s>Dīpikā</s> —

children.text:
ktam/ tena
maṅgalasya kartavyatve śiṣṭācārānumitā śrutiḥ pramāṇamiti labhyate/
tadave śrutipramāṇakakartaṃvyatākatvaṃ maṅgalasya śaṅkāsamādhānarūpeṇa
sthāpayati 'nanu maṅgalasya kartavyatve kiṃ pramāṇam' ityādinā
dīpikāgranthena/ tadetadāha
children.translated_text: '<s>Maṅgala</s> consists of salutation to one's chosen deity, whose oughtness is known from <s>śruti</s> inferred through the conduct of the learned.' From this, it is obtained that the <s>śruti</s> inferred through the conduct of the learned is the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for the oughtness of <s>maṅgala</s>. That very point — that <s>maṅgala</s> has oughtness established by <s>śruti</s>-based valid knowledge — is established through the <s>Dīpikā</s> text in the form of raising and resolving the doubt 'Now, what is the means of valid knowledge for the oughtness of <s>maṅgala</s>?' and so forth. This is what he states —

children.text:
prakāśikāyāṃ---maṅgalasya śrutibodhitakartavyatākatvaṃ
vyavasthāpayitum
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'to establish that <s>maṅgala</s> has oughtness taught by <s>śruti</s>' —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

Without the knowledge '<s>maṅgala</s> ought to be performed,' no one would perform <s>maṅgala</s>. Because the cognition of the form 'the object of my effort is achievable through effort,' having the same qualificand as that [<s>maṅgala</s>], is a cause for the effort directed toward that [<s>maṅgala</s>]. And 'oughtness' (<s>kartavyatā</s>) is achievability through effort (<s>kṛtisādhyatva</s>). And the knowledge '<s>maṅgala</s> ought to be performed' arises from the <s>śruti</s> (scriptural text) 'One who desires completion should perform <s>maṅgala</s>' — which is inferred through the conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) of the learned, namely their practice of performing <s>maṅgala</s> at the commencement of works. With this intent, it was earlier stated in

children.text:
nanu maṅgalasya
kartavyatve 'samāptikāmo maṅgalamācareta' iti śrutirna
pramāṇam/ tādṛśaśruteḥ paṭhyamānavede kutrāpyadarśanāt
ityāśaṅkāyāṃ śiṣṭācārānumiteti śruterviśeṣaṇamupāttaṃ
dīpikāyām/
children.translated_text: in the <s>Dīpikā</s>.

children.text:
yadyapi śrutiḥ na pratyakṣā tathāpi ācāreṇa
liṅgena tādṛśī śrutiranumīyate/ tathā ca ācārānumitā śrutiḥ
maṅgalakartavyatve pramāṇamiti
children.translated_text: Even though the <s>śruti</s> is not directly perceptible, still through conduct as the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), such a <s>śruti</s> is inferred. And accordingly, the <s>śruti</s> inferred through conduct is the means of valid knowledge for the oughtness of <s>maṅgala</s> —

Now, for the oughtness of <s>maṅgala</s>, the <s>śruti</s> 'One who desires completion should perform <s>maṅgala</s>' is not a valid means of knowledge, since such a <s>śruti</s> is not found anywhere in the <s>Vedas</s> that are currently recited — in response to this doubt, the qualifier 'inferred through the conduct of the learned' was attached to <s>śruti</s>

children.text:
1. tadviṣayakakṛti
pratīti/ yathā yāgaviṣayakaprayatnaṃ prati 'yāgaḥ matkṛtisādhyaḥ'
ityākārakaṃ yāgaviśeṣyakaṃ kṛtisādhyatvaprakārakaṃ jñānaṃ
kāraṇamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The effort directed toward that object' — Just as the cognition having <s>yāga</s> (sacrifice) as qualificand and the property 'achievable through my effort' as qualifier-mode is a cause for the effort directed toward that <s>yāga</s> — this is the purport.

children.text:
tadāśayaḥ/
anumānaprakāraśca 'maṅgalaṃ vedabodhitakartavyatākam'
ityādigranthena pradarśitaḥ/ tasmin anumāne
vedabodhitakartavyatākatvaṃ hi sādhyam, na tu vedaḥ/ yat
anumānasādhyaṃ - anumitividheyaṃ tadevānumintamityucyate/ tathā
children.translated_text: This is the intent. And the mode of inference is shown by the text '<s>maṅgala</s> has oughtness taught by the <s>Vedas</s>' and so forth. In that inference, the property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) is 'having oughtness taught by the <s>Vedas</s>,' not the <s>Vedas</s> themselves. That which is the provable of an inference — the predicate of the inferential cognition — is called the 'inferred' (<s>anuminata</s>). Accordingly,

children.text:
ca
vedabodhitakartavyatākatvaṃ śiṣṭācārānumitaṃ na tu veda iti
kathaṃ śruteḥ śiṣṭācārānumitatvamupapadyate?
anumitividheyatāvacchedakasyāpi anumitiviṣayatvamātreṇa
anumitividheyatvamaṅgīkṛtyānumitamiti vyavahāropapādane
vahnitvamanumitamityapi vyavahārāpatterityāśaṅkāyām
āśayamāviṣkaroti--
atrāyamāśaya
children.translated_text: Here is the intent —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

the property of having oughtness taught by the <s>Vedas</s> is what is inferred through the conduct of the learned, not the <s>Vedas</s> themselves — so how is the being-inferred-through-conduct-of-the-learned applicable to the <s>śruti</s>? If one accepts that merely by being an object of the inferential cognition, even the delimitor of the predicate-hood has predicate-hood, and on that basis one justifies the usage 'inferred' — then even the usage 'fire-hood is inferred' [from smoke] would follow. In response to this doubt, he reveals the intent —

children.text: vedavodhite
children.translated_text: 'Taught by the <s>Vedas</s>' —

children.text:
tyādi/ vedabodhitakartavyatākatvarūpaṃ
yat vakṣyamāṇaṃ vidheyaṃ sādhyaṃ tatkoṭipraviṣṭatve 'pi
tadavacchedakatve 'pītyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: and so forth. Even though the property of having oughtness taught by the <s>Vedas</s>, which is the predicate (<s>sādhya</s>) to be stated, falls within the scope [of the inference], and even though it is the delimitor [of predicate-hood] — this is the meaning.

children.text: apinā
children.translated_text: 'Even' (<s>api</s>) —

children.text:
vidheyatāvacchedakasya
vidheyatvāsambhavarūpo virodho dyotyate/
children.translated_text: indicates the contradiction in the form of the impossibility of the delimitor of predicate-hood itself having predicate-hood.

children.text: tadantarbhāveṇa
children.translated_text: 'Through the inclusion of that' —

children.text: --vidheyatāvacchedakāntarbhāveṇa/
children.translated_text: means: through the inclusion within the delimitor of predicate-hood.

children.text: tacchruteḥ
children.translated_text: 'Of that <s>śruti</s>' —

children.text:
---
'sāmāptikāmo maṅgalamācareta' iti śruteḥ/
children.translated_text: means: of the <s>śruti</s> 'One who desires completion should perform <s>maṅgala</s>.'

children.text: anumiteḥ
children.translated_text: 'Of inference' —

children.text: pūrvamasiddhatvāditi/
children.translated_text: means: because [the <s>śruti</s>] is not established prior to inference.

children.text:
tathā ca anumiteḥ
pūrvamasiddhatvameva anumitividheyatāyāṃ prayojakam/ maṅgalasya
kartavyatā anumiteḥ pūrvamasiddhete tatra yathā anumitividheyatā
asti, tathā anumiteḥ pūrvamasiddhatvāta vidheyatāvacchedakabhūtāyāṃ
children.translated_text: And accordingly, the very fact of not being established prior to inference is what is operative in [determining] predicate-hood of inference. The oughtness of <s>maṅgala</s> is not established prior to inference — just as predicate-hood of inference obtains there,

children.text:
śrutāvapi
vidheyatākhyaviṣayatā aṅgīkriyate/ tataśca
śruteranumitividheyatvāt anumitatvamupapadyata iti
śrutiśśiṣṭācārānumitā iti vyavahāre na kimapi bādhakamiti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: so also, because of not being established prior to inference, predicate-hood — that is, the status of being an object [of inference] — is accepted even for <s>śruti</s>, which is the delimitor of predicate-hood. And consequently, since <s>śruti</s> has predicate-hood of inference, the status of being inferred is established — and thus there is no obstacle whatsoever to the usage '<s>śruti</s> is inferred through the conduct of the learned.' This is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
anumitividheyatāvacchedakasyāpyanumitividheyatvāṅgīkāre
'parvato vahnimān' iti anumitividheyatāvacchedakasya
vahnitvasyāpi tādṛśānumitividheyatvaṃ syāt/ tathā ca
vahnirdhūmānuminta iti
children.translated_text: Now, if one accepts that even the delimitor of the predicate-hood of inference has predicate-hood of inference, then in the inference 'The mountain has fire,' fire-hood (<s>vahnitva</s>), which is the delimitor of the predicate-hood of that inference, would also have such predicate-hood of inference. And accordingly,

children.text:
vyavahāravat vahnitvaṃ
dhūmānumitamiti vyavahāro 'pi prāmāṇikaḥ syāt ityāśaṅkāṃ
samādhatte-
etene
children.translated_text: 'By this' —

children.text:
ti/ anuminteḥ pūrvamasiddhasyaiva
vidheyatāvacchedakasya anumitividheyatvāṅgīkāreṇetyarthaḥ/ tathā ca
vahnitvasyānamiteḥ pūrvaṃ siddhatayā nānumitividheyatvaprasaṅga
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: by the acceptance of predicate-hood of inference only for that delimitor of predicate-hood which is not established prior to inference. And accordingly, since fire-hood is established prior to inference, there is no unwanted consequence of its having predicate-hood of inference — this is the purport.

children.text: anumitiviṣayatām
children.translated_text: 'The status of being an object of inference' —

children.text:
iti/
vidheyatāvacchedakatārūpāṃ viṣayatāmityarthaḥ/ viśeṣyatayā
viśeṣaṇatayā vā anumitiviṣayatvameva anumitatvavyavahāre
prayojakamiti svīkāreṇetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the status of being an object [of inference] in the form of being the delimitor of predicate-hood. The meaning is: by accepting that merely being an object of inference — whether as qualificand or as qualifier — is what warrants the usage 'inferred.'

children.text: śrutau
children.translated_text: 'In <s>śruti</s>' —

children.text: vidheyatvābhyupagamene
children.translated_text: 'the acceptance of predicate-hood' —

children.text: ti/ anumiteḥ pūrvamasiddhatvāditi śeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: with the remainder being: 'because of not being established prior to inference.'

children.text: tādṛśavyavahāra
children.translated_text: 'Such a usage' —

children.text:
iti/ śrutiḥ anumitā iti vyavahāra
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the usage '<s>śruti</s> is inferred.'

children.text: bādhakābhāvād
children.translated_text: 'Due to the absence of an invalidating cognition' —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.
just as there is the usage 'fire is inferred from smoke,' the usage 'fire-hood is inferred from smoke' would also be warranted — he resolves this doubt —

children.text:
anumitamiti
vyavahāre anumiteḥ pūrvaṃ siddhatvaṃ bādhakam, tadabhāvāt ityarthaḥ/
nanu 'śrutereva pramāṇatvāt' ityatra evakārasya
anyayogavyavacchedārthakatayā śrutyatiriktasya pramāṇatvaṃ vyavacchidyata
iti pratīyate/ tanna saṅgacchate, maṅgalakartavyatāyāṃ 'maṅgalaṃ
kartavyam samāptiphalakatvāt' ityanumānasyāpi
pramāṇatvādityāśaṅkāyāmāha--
evakāro 'pyarthaka
children.translated_text: The particle 'alone' (<s>eva</s>) is also meaningful —

children.text:
iti/
aperartho yasya saḥ apyarthakaḥ, apyarthasuccayārthaka ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca
śruterevetyasya śruterapītyarthaḥ/ apinā anumānasya pramāṇatvaṃ
samuccīyate/ ato nāsaṅgatiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. That which has the meaning of 'also' (<s>api</s>) is <s>apyarthaka</s>; the meaning is that the particle <s>api</s> has the sense of aggregation (<s>samuccaya</s>). And accordingly, 'from <s>śruti</s> alone' means 'from <s>śruti</s> also.' By the particle <s>api</s>, the status of inference as a means of valid knowledge is aggregated. Therefore there is no incoherence — this is the purport.

The meaning is: in the usage 'inferred,' being established prior to inference is the invalidating factor, and due to the absence of that [invalidating factor]. Now, in the passage 'because <s>śruti</s> alone is the means of valid knowledge,' the word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>), having the function of excluding what is not otherwise connected, seems to exclude the status of being a means of valid knowledge for anything other than <s>śruti</s>. That does not fit, since even inference such as '<s>maṅgala</s> ought to be performed because it has the fruit of completion' is also a means of valid knowledge for the oughtness of <s>maṅgala</s> — anticipating this doubt, he says —

children.text:
śruteranumitatvaṃ
anumitividheyatāvacchedake 'pi pūrvamasiddhe vidheyatvāṅgīkāreṇa
upapāditaṃ prakāśikākāraiḥ/ etaṃ kleśaṃ śruteranumitatvam
upapādayatāṃ matamāha-
anye tvi
children.translated_text: 'Others however'

children.text:
ti/ 'maṅgalaṃ
vedabodhitakartavyatākam' iti pratijñāyāḥ maṅgalaṃ
svabodhitakartavyatākatvasambandhena vedaviśiṣṭam ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca
tādṛśānumitau veda eva vidheya iti
vedasyānumitatvamanāyāsenopapadyata iti bhāvaḥ/
īdṛśaparamparāyāḥ sādhyatāvacchedakasambandhatve mānābhāvaḥ,
yathāśrutamūlārthatyāgaścāsvarasaḥ
children.translated_text: thus. The proposition '<s>maṅgala</s> has oughtness taught by the <s>Vedas</s>' means: <s>maṅgala</s> is qualified by the <s>Vedas</s> through the relation of possessing oughtness taught by itself. And accordingly, in such an inference, the <s>Vedas</s> alone are the predicate — thus the being-inferred of the <s>Vedas</s> is effortlessly established — this is the purport. The absence of proof for such a chain being the delimiting relation of the property to be proved, and the unsavoriness of abandoning the literal meaning —

children.text: āhu
children.translated_text: 'they say'

children.text: rityanena sūcitaḥ/
children.translated_text: — is indicated by this [expression].

The being-inferred of <s>śruti</s> has been justified by the authors of the <s>Prakāśikā</s> by accepting predicate-hood even for the delimitor of predicate-hood of the inferential cognition, which was not previously established. He states the view of those who undergo this effort of justifying the being-inferred of <s>śruti</s> —

children.text: dīpikāyām
alaukikāvigītaśiṣṭācāraviṣayatvād
children.translated_text: 'Because it has as its object the conduct of the learned that is extra-ordinary and uncontested' —

children.text:
iti/ śiṣṭānāmācāraḥ śiṣṭācāraḥ
śiṣṭācārasya viṣayaḥ śiṣṭācāraviṣayaḥ, avigītaścāsau
śiṣṭācāraviṣayaśca avigītaśiṣṭācāraviṣayaḥ, alaukikaścāsau
avigītaśiṣṭācāraviṣayaśca alaukikāvigīntaśiṣṭācāraviṣayaḥ tasya
bhāvastattvam/ alaukikatve sati avigītatve sati śiṣṭācāraviṣayatvaṃ
heturiti phalitam/ laukikatvaṃ vidhyatiriktapramāṇagamyatvam,
tadbhinnatvamalaiṅkikatvam/ hetau
children.translated_text: thus. The conduct of the learned is <s>śiṣṭācāra</s>; the object of <s>śiṣṭācāra</s> is <s>śiṣṭācāraviṣaya</s>; that which is uncontested and is the object of the conduct of the learned is <s>avigītaśiṣṭācāraviṣaya</s>; that which is extra-ordinary and is the uncontested object of the conduct of the learned is <s>alaukikāvigītaśiṣṭācāraviṣaya</s>; its nature is the abstract property thereof. The resultant meaning is: the inferential reason (<s>hetu</s>) is — having as its object the conduct of the learned, provided it is extra-ordinary and uncontested. 'Ordinary' (<s>laukika</s>) means cognizable by a means of valid knowledge other than injunction (<s>vidhi</s>); 'extra-ordinary' (<s>alaukika</s>) means being different from that. In the inferential reason,
In the <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
alaukikatvānupādāne
rāgaprāpte bhojanādau vedabodhitakartavyatākatvarūpasādhyābhāvavati
avigītaśiṣṭācāraviṣayatvarūpahetusattvāt vyabhicāraḥ syāt/
tadvāraṇāya alaiṅkikatvamupāttam/ avigītatvaṃ dharmaśāstrāniṣiddhatvam/
tadanupādāne vedabodhitakartavyatākatvarūpasādhyābhāvavati
rātriśrāddhādau 1alaiṅkikaśiṣṭācāraviṣayatvarūpahetusattvāt
vyabhicāraḥ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya avigītatvamupāttam/ rātriśrāddhādeḥ
'rātrau śrāddhaṃ na kurvīta' iti dharmaśāstraniṣiddhatvāt na tatra
vyabhicāraḥ/
children.translated_text: if the qualification of being extra-ordinary is not included, then in the case of eating and the like, which are prompted by desire, since the reason in the form of being the object of uncontested conduct of the learned is present in what lacks the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) in the form of having oughtness taught by the <s>Vedas</s>, there would be a deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). To prevent that, extra-ordinariness is included. 'Uncontestedeness' means not being prohibited by <s>dharmaśāstra</s>. If that is not included, since the reason in the form of being the object of extra-ordinary conduct of the learned is present in the performance of <s>śrāddha</s> at night and the like, which lack the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of having oughtness taught by the <s>Vedas</s>, there would be deviation. To prevent that, uncontestedeness is included. Since nighttime <s>śrāddha</s> is prohibited by the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> text 'One should not perform <s>śrāddha</s> at night,' there is no deviation there.

children.text: prakāśikāyāṃ
vidhimantare
children.translated_text: 'In another injunction' —

children.text:
ti/ liṅloṭtavyapratyayaghaṭitaṃ
vedavākyaṃ vidhiḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. A Vedic sentence composed with the suffixes <s>liṅ</s>, <s>loṭ</s>, or <s>tavya</s> is an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>).

children.text: vedoktatattvajñānene
children.translated_text: 'By knowledge of reality taught by the <s>Vedas</s>' —

children.text:
ti/
tṛtīyāyāḥ janyatvamarthaḥ karmakārītyatra kṛdhātvarthakṛtyanvayi/
vedoktaṃ yattattvaṃ tadviṣayakajñānajanyā yā
vedavihitakarmaviṣayakakṛtiḥ tadāśrayaḥ śiṣṭa ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. The meaning of the third case-ending is 'produced by' — it connects with the agent-noun <s>karmakārī</s> (one who performs actions) through the meaning of the affix <s>kṛtya</s> derived from the root <s>kṛ</s>. The meaning is: a learned person (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) is one who is the locus of effort (<s>kṛti</s>) directed toward actions enjoined by the <s>Vedas</s>, [that effort] being produced by knowledge whose object is reality as taught by the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: vedotthatattvajñānene
children.translated_text: 'By knowledge of reality arising from the <s>Vedas</s>' —

children.text:
ti kvacitpāṭhaḥ/ vedajanyaṃ yattattvajñānaṃ
tenetyarthaḥ/ sa eva pāṭhaśroyān/ vedavihitakarmakartā śiṣṭaḥ
ityetāvanmātroktau vedavihitāhiṃsādikarmakartuḥ bauddhasyāpi
śiṣṭatvāpattiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
children.translated_text: is a variant reading found in some [manuscripts]. The meaning is: by that knowledge of reality which is produced by the <s>Vedas</s>. That reading is indeed preferable. If only so much were stated — that a <s>śiṣṭa</s> is one who performs actions enjoined by the <s>Vedas</s> — then even a Buddhist, who performs <s>Veda</s>-enjoined actions such as non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), would have the unwanted consequence of being a <s>śiṣṭa</s>. To prevent that,

children.text: vedotthatattvajñānene
children.translated_text: 'by knowledge of reality arising from the <s>Vedas</s>' —

children.text:
ti/ bauddhasya yat ahiṃsāditattvajñānaṃ na tat vedajanyamiti
nātivyāptiḥ/ yadvā
children.translated_text: thus. Since the knowledge of reality regarding non-violence and the like that a Buddhist possesses is not produced by the <s>Vedas</s>, there is no over-extension. Alternatively,

children.text: vedoktattvajñānene
children.translated_text: 'by knowledge that this is taught by the <s>Vedas</s>' —

children.text:
ti
pāṭhaḥ 2sādhīyān/ idaṃ vedoktamiti jñānapūrvakaṃ yaḥ vedavihitaṃ
karma karoti sa śiṣṭaḥ/ bauddhastu vedavihitamahiṃsādikaṃ karma
kurvannapi idaṃ vedoktamiti buddhyā na karoti, tena
vedaprāmāṇyānabhyupagamāditi na tasya śiṣṭatvāpattiḥ/
children.translated_text: this reading is most preferable. One who performs actions enjoined by the <s>Vedas</s> with the prior knowledge 'this is taught by the <s>Vedas</s>' is a <s>śiṣṭa</s>. But a Buddhist, even while performing <s>Veda</s>-enjoined actions such as non-violence, does not perform them with the understanding 'this is taught by the <s>Vedas</s>' — because he does not accept the authority of the <s>Vedas</s>. Therefore, the unwanted consequence of his being a <s>śiṣṭa</s> does not arise.
In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
nanu śiṣṭācārasyaiva
hetutvamastu, kimācāraviṣayatvaparyantasya hetutvānudhāvanena/ na ca
ācāraḥ kṛtiḥ, tasyā
children.translated_text: Now, let the conduct of the learned itself be the reason — what is the point of pursuing causality through the object-of-conduct? Nor is conduct the same as effort (<s>kṛti</s>), because of its [i.e., effort's]

children.text:
1. alaukiketi/
rātriśrāddhasya 'śrāddhaṃ kurvīta' iti vidhinaivāvagamāt
vidhyatiriktapramāṇānavagamyatvarūpamalaukikatvamastīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Extra-ordinary' — The purport is: since nighttime <s>śrāddha</s> is known solely through the injunction 'One should perform <s>śrāddha</s>,' it has the quality of extra-ordinariness in the form of not being cognizable by a means of valid knowledge other than injunction.

children.text:
2. sādhīyāniti/ tathā
ca vedoktatvaprakārakajñānajanyayāgādikarmānukūlakṛtimattvaṃ
śiṣṭatvamiti labhyate/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Is most preferable' — And accordingly, the definition of <s>śiṣṭa</s>-hood obtained is: possessing effort favorable to actions such as sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and the like, produced by cognition whose qualifier-mode is being-taught-by-the-<s>Vedas</s>.

children.text:
ātmaniṣṭhatvena
maṅgalarūpa pakṣaniṣṭhatvābhāvāt kathaṃ hetutvamiti vācyam/
kṛterviṃṣayatāsambandhena hetutvasambhavāt, samavāyena ātmaniṣṭhāyāḥ
kṛteḥ viṣayatāsambandhena maṅgalaniṣṭhatayā
hetutvasambhavādityāśaṅkyāha
ācāraḥ
children.translated_text: 'Conduct' —

Since effort resides in the self and <s>maṅgala</s>, which is the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject), does not possess it [through inherence], how can [the conduct of the learned] serve as a reason? — this should not be objected, because causality is possible through the object-relation (<s>viṣayatā</s>) of effort. Since effort, which resides in the self through inherence, is possible as a reason through the object-relation by which it pertains to <s>maṅgala</s> — anticipating this doubt, he says —

children.text: kṛtiri
children.translated_text: 'is effort' —

children.text:
tyādinā/ vṛttiḥ ādheyatā tanniyāmakaḥ
sambandhaḥ vṛttiniyāmakaḥ sambandhaḥ saṃyogasamavāyādiḥ/ viṣayatā tu na
vṛttiniyāmakasambandhaḥ/ viṣayatāsambandhena kṛtiḥ maṅgalavṛttiriti
pratītyabhāvāt/ vṛttiniyāmakasambandha eva ca hetutāvacdedakasambandhaḥ
na tu vṛttyaniyāmako viṣayatādiḥ/ tathā ca kṛteḥ
viṣayatāsambandhāvacchinnahetutvāsambhavāt ācāraviṣayatvasya
hetutvānudhāvanam/ viṣayatvaṃ tu svarūpasambandhena hetuḥ,
svarūpasambandhastu vṛttiniyāmaka iti tena sambandhena
ācāraviṣayatvasya hetutvaṃ sambhavatītyāśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: and so forth. Residence (<s>vṛtti</s>) means being contained; the relation that determines it is the residence-determining relation, such as contact (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and the like. But object-relation (<s>viṣayatā</s>) is not a residence-determining relation — because there is no cognition of the form 'effort resides in <s>maṅgala</s> through object-relation.' And only a residence-determining relation is the delimiting relation of the reason-hood, not a non-residence-determining [relation] such as object-relation. And accordingly, since causality delimited by the object-relation is impossible for effort, there is pursuit of the object-of-conduct as the reason. Object-hood, however, is a reason through the self-linking relation (<s>svarūpasambandha</s>), and the self-linking relation is a residence-determining [relation] — through that relation, the causality of 'being the object of conduct' is possible — this is the intent.

children.text:
ācāraviṣayatvapadasya
prayojanaṃ mūle 'nuktamiti svayaṃ tatprayojanaṃ kathayati---
svargādiphala
children.translated_text: 'The fruit such as heaven' —

children.text:
iti/ tathā ca hetau
ācāraviṣayatvapadānupādāne alaukikatve sati avigītatvaṃ hetuḥ
syāt/ svargādirūpe phale 'pi tatsattvāt
vedabodhitakartavyatākatvarūpasādhyābhāvāt vyabhicāraḥ syāditi
tadvāraṇāya
children.translated_text: thus. And accordingly, if the term 'object of conduct' is not included in the reason, then being extra-ordinary and uncontested would be the reason. Since that [reason] is present even in fruits such as heaven and the like, there would be deviation due to the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of having oughtness taught by the <s>Vedas</s>. To prevent that,

children.text: ācāraviṣayatvāt
children.translated_text: 'because it is the object of conduct' —

children.text:
ityupāttam/ svargādestu
kṛtiviṣayatvaṃ nāstīti na vyabhicāra iti bhāvaḥ/ nanu kṛteḥ
uddeśyaṃ vidheyam upādānamiti viṣayatrayamasti/ yāgaḥ vidheyaḥ svarga
uddeśyaḥ prayājādyaṅgajātamupādānam/ svarge
kṛtinirūpitoddeśyatākhyaviṣayatāyāḥ sattvāt
kṛtiviṣayatvopādāne 'pi vyabhicāra ityāśaṅkyāha---
children.translated_text: is included. Since heaven and the like do not have the property of being objects of effort (<s>kṛtivisayatva</s>), there is no deviation — this is the purport. Now, effort has three objects: the end (<s>uddeśya</s>), the means (<s>vidheya</s>), and the subsidiary (<s>upādāna</s>). Sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) is the means, heaven is the end, and the collection of subsidiaries such as <s>prayāja</s> and the like is the subsidiary. Since heaven possesses the object-relation called 'end-ness' (<s>uddeśyatā</s>) as determined by effort, even with the inclusion of 'being the object of effort,' there would be deviation — anticipating this doubt, he says —

children.text: vidheyatayā ācāraviṣayatvārthakami
children.translated_text: 'The meaning of "object of conduct" is in the sense of predicate (<s>vidheya</s>)' —

children.text:
ti/ tṛtīyāyā abhedor'thaḥ/
ācāranirūpitavidheyatvābhinnaviṣayatvaṃ hetuḥ/ svargādaiṃ
kṛtinirūpitavidheyatākhyaviṣayatvābhāvāt na vyabhicāra iti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. The meaning of the third case-ending is non-difference. The reason is: object-hood that is non-different from predicate-hood as determined by conduct. Since heaven and the like lack the object-hood called 'predicate-hood' as determined by effort, there is no deviation — this is the purport.
The purpose of the term 'object of conduct' was not stated in the root text; he himself explains its purpose —

children.text:
nanu vyāpyāropeṇa
vyāpakāropastarkaḥ/ tathā ca tarkasaṅgraha ityasya
vyāpyāropajanyavyāpakāropātmakatarkapratipādakagrantha ityartho
bhavati/ sa na yujyate, tarkasaṅgrahagranthena
āropamātrasyāpratipādanāt, itarapadārthānāmapi
pratipādanādityāśaṅkya tarkaśabdena yathā granthapratipādyasakalapadārthaḥ/
pratipādyeta tathā tarkaśabdo vyutpādyate dīpikāyāmityāha--
tarkapadasye
children.translated_text: 'Of the term <s>tarka</s>' —

children.text: tyādinā/
children.translated_text: and so forth.

children.text: āropārthakatvabhramamiṃ
children.translated_text: 'The error that it means supposition' —

children.text:
ti/ vyāpyāropeṇa vyāpakāropārthakatvabhramamityarthaḥ/
saṅgrahaśabdasyopādānamityapyartho 'sti/ so 'tra na sambhavati;
1guṇādipadārthānāṃ, dravyeṣvapi ākāśādināmupādānasyāsambhavāt/
upādānaṃ hi hastakaraṇakavyāpāraviśeṣaḥ/ tasmāt
saṅgrahapadasyasaṅkṣepeṇa svarūpakathanamityartho mūle varṇita
ityāha
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the error that it means the supposition of the pervader through the supposition of the pervaded. The word <s>saṃgraha</s> also has the meaning of 'collection' (<s>upādāna</s>). That meaning is not possible here, since the collection [in the physical sense] of categories such as qualities and the like, and even among substances, of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the like, is impossible. For collection is a specific type of activity performed by the hands. Therefore, the meaning of the word <s>saṃgraha</s> is 'a brief statement of the essential nature' — this was explained in the root text. He says —

children.text: upādānarūpe
children.translated_text: 'In the sense of collection' —

children.text:
ti/ nanu svarūpakathanamityatra
kathanaśabdasyoccāraṇamarthaḥ/ uccāraṇaṃ nāma
tālvoṣṭhapuṭasaṃyogānukūlavyāpāraḥ/ tasya śabdamātraviṣayakasya
dravyādipadārthasvarūpaviṣayakatvāsambhavāt svarūpakathanamiti śabdaḥ katha
sādhurityāśaṅkyāha-
children.translated_text: thus. Now, in 'a statement of the essential nature,' the word 'statement' (<s>kathana</s>) means utterance. Utterance is a specific activity involving the contact of the palate, lips, and mouth. Since that, being directed only at words, cannot be directed at the essential nature of categories such as substance and the like, the expression 'statement of the essential nature' — anticipating the doubt that the word <s>kathana</s> is difficult to construe, he says —

children.text:
svarūpakathanaṃ
svarūpajñajñanānukūlaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Statement of the essential nature' means [a verbal expression] conducive to knowledge of the essential nature —

children.text: śabda
children.translated_text: 'verbal expression' (<s>śabda</s>) —

children.text:
iti/ tathā ca prakṛte kathanaśabdasya noccāraṇamarthaḥ, kintu
jñānānukūlaḥ śabdor'thaḥ/ jñāne svarūpaviṣayakatvānvayāt
padārthaṃsvarūpaviṣayakajñānānukūlaśabdaḥ svarūpakathanaśabdārtha iti
nānupapattiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. And accordingly, in this context the word 'statement' (<s>kathana</s>) does not mean utterance, but rather 'verbal expression conducive to knowledge' is its meaning. Since the qualifier 'having the essential nature as its object' connects with knowledge, a verbal expression conducive to knowledge whose object is the essential nature of the categories — this is the meaning of the term 'statement of the essential nature.' Thus there is no difficulty — this is the purport.

Now, <s>tarka</s> (suppositional reasoning) is the supposition of the pervader through the supposition of the pervaded. And accordingly, the meaning of '<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>' would be: a treatise that expounds suppositional reasoning in the form of the supposition of the pervader generated by the supposition of the pervaded. That is not fitting, since the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> treatise does not expound mere supposition, and also expounds other categories as well — anticipating this doubt, the word <s>tarka</s> is etymologically derived in the <s>Dīpikā</s> so as to include all the categories expounded in the treatise. He says —

children.text:
prekṣāvatāṃ
buddhipūrvakāriṇāṃ yā granthādhyayane pravṛttiḥ tatra
anubandhacatuṣṭayamaṅgam/ viṣayaprayojanasambandhādhikāriṇaḥ
catvāro 'nubandhāḥ/ anubadhnanti puruṣaṃ granthādhyayane
prerayantītyanubandhāḥ granthapratipādyo viṣayaḥ, granthādhyayanasya
prayojanam, granthasya viṣayasya ca sambandhaḥ, ganthādhyayane 'dhikārī
ityeteṣāṃ caturṇāṃ jñānaṃ vinā na ko 'pi granthādhyayane pravarteta/
tathā cāvaśyavaktavyasyānubandhacatuṣṭayasyākathanāt mūlasya
nyūnatāmāśaṅkya taccatuṣṭayaṃ kaṇṭharaveṇānuktamapi lena
sūcitamevetyāha -
etāvate
children.translated_text: 'By this much' —

children.text:
ti/ tarkasaṃṅgrahapadasya
vyākhyānenetyarthaḥ/ sukhabodhāya ityatra sukhasya bodha iti
ṣaṣṭhītatpuraṃṣāṅgīkāre sukhaviṣayakabodhaḥ asya granthasya
prayojanamiti labhyeta/ tathā sati nikhilapadārthabodhakatvaṃ
tarkasaṃṅgrahapadavyākhyānena sūcitaṃ virudhyeta/ ataḥ sukhena
children.translated_text: The meaning is: by the explanation of the term <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>. Regarding 'for easy understanding' (<s>sukhabodhāya</s>) — if the compound is taken as a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> meaning 'understanding of ease,' then one would obtain that 'knowledge having ease as its object is the purpose of this treatise.' In that case, it would contradict the indication through the explanation of the term <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> that the treatise teaches knowledge of all categories. Therefore,

The four preliminary topics (<s>anubandha-catuṣṭaya</s>) are the limbs for the engagement of discerning persons — those who act with deliberation — in the study of a treatise. The four <s>anubandhas</s> are: subject matter (<s>viṣaya</s>), purpose (<s>prayojana</s>), connection (<s>sambandha</s>), and qualified student (<s>adhikārin</s>). They are called <s>anubandhas</s> because they bind — that is, impel — a person to study the treatise. The subject matter is what the treatise expounds; the purpose is the goal of studying the treatise; the connection is between the treatise and its subject matter; the qualified student is the one entitled to study the treatise. Without the knowledge of these four, no one would engage in studying the treatise. And accordingly, since these four preliminary topics, which must necessarily be stated, were not explicitly stated in the root text, anticipating the charge of incompleteness, he says that these four, though not explicitly stated in words, are indicated [implicitly] —

By the etymology '<s>padārtha</s> is the meaning (<s>artha</s>) of a word (<s>pada</s>),' being an object of denotation (<s>abhidheyatva</s>) is the general definition of <s>padārtha</s>. Now, since the number seven is already established from the division itself, the use of the word 'seven' is redundant — if this is objected — no, because it serves to exclude any additional number. Now, is an additional category cognized by a valid means of knowledge or not? Not the first, because what is cognized by valid means cannot be negated. Not the second, because negation is impossible without the cognition of the counter-positive — if this is objected — no, because category-hood is pervaded by being one among the seven such as substance and the like. [The word 'seven'] serves exclusion. Now, 'being one among the seven' means 'being different from what is different from the seven.' Since what is different from the seven is not established, how can the invariable concomitance with 'being one among the seven' be ascertained? — if this is objected — no, because 'being one among the seven such as substance and the like' means 'possessing the absence of the seven differences from substance and the like.' Therefore there is no defect.

And accordingly, since the words <s>dravya</s> and the rest have as their purport the properties <s>dravyatva</s> and the rest that have become qualifier-modes of their own referents, they are designations where the abstract property is primary.

children.translated_text: that is to say, a verbal expression. Such a division in the form of a verbal expression — the question 'How many kinds does a category have?' — can only be undertaken when the student has the desire for cognition qualified by specific properties. Otherwise, there would be the defect of stating what is not desired to be known, i.e. irrelevance. The cognition qualified by a general property is the cause for the desire to know specifics. Alternatively, the cognition having as its qualifier-mode the property of being a means to the desired end, with the specific-property-qualified cognition as its property-locus — i.e. a cognition of the form 'cognition qualified by the specific property is a means to my desired end' — is a cause for the desire, through the relation of having as its qualifier-mode, for the cognition qualified by the specific property. For such a cognition of being a means to the desired end, the cognition having as its qualifier-mode the specific property that is the delimitor of the property-locus is a cause. viṃśeṣadharmaprakārakajñāne ca sāmānyadharmajñānaṃ kāraṇamiti paramparayā
sāmānyadharmajñānasya viśeṣadharmajijñāsāyāṃ hetutvamiti
children.translated_text: as it has been established. And the cognition of the general property is a cause for the cognition having the specific property as its qualifier-mode — thus, indirectly, the cognition of the general property has causality for the desire to know the specific property.

children.text: gadādharā
children.translated_text: This is the intent of <s>Gadādhara</s> —

children.text:
śayaḥ/ tathā ca sāmānyadharmajñānaṃ vinā viśeṣajijñāsā
notpattumarhatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: And accordingly, without the cognition of the general property, the desire to know specifics cannot arise — this is the purport.

children.text: sāmānyalakṣaṇakathanānantaram
children.translated_text: After the statement of the general definition —

children.text:
iti/ padārthānāṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇe kathite
tādṛśalakṣaṇātmakasāmānyadharmajñānāt padārthaḥ katividha iti
viśeṣadharmajijñāsā bhavitumarhatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: The purport is: when the general definition of the categories has been stated, from the cognition of the general property in the form of such a definition, the desire to know the specific property — 'how many kinds does a category have?' — can arise.

children.text: nyūnatām
children.translated_text: deficiency —

children.text:
iti/
avaśyavaktavyārthākathanaṃ labhyate/ katham abhidheyatvaṃ labhyata iti
mūloktaṃ saṅgacchata ityāśaṅkyāha -
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the non-statement of what necessarily needs to be stated. How is the property of being expressible (<s>abhidheyatva</s>) obtained? — anticipating the doubt of how the statement in the root text is consistent, he says —

children.text: padasyārthe 'bhidheya
children.translated_text: 'the meaning of a word is the expressible' —

children.text:
iti/ yadyapi śabdataḥ padasambandhyabhidhāviṣayatvaṃ labhyate,
tathāpi samagraṃ na lakṣaṇam, abhidhāviṣayatvasyaiva
padārthasāmānyalakṣaṇatvasambhavena padasambandhitvāṃśsya vyarthatvāt/
children.translated_text: Even though from the words [of the text] literally, the property of being the object of designation (<s>abhidhā</s>) related to a word is obtained, still that is not the complete definition, because the component 'related to a word' is superfluous since the property of being the object of designation alone can serve as the general definition of <s>padārtha</s>.

children.text:
1. svaṃ viśeṣadharmaḥ
dravyatvaguṇatvādiḥ tatprakārakatvasambandhena dravyatvādiviśiṣṭaṃ yat
jñānaṃ tadviṣayakecchā 'dravyatvādiprakārakajñānaṃ mama bhavatu'
ityākārikā tāṃ prati 'dravyatvādiprakārakajñānaṃ madiṣṭasādhanam'
ityākāraka jñānaṃ kāraṇam/ tādṛśajñānaṃ prati dharmitāvacchedakānāṃ
dravyatvādīnāṃ jñānaṃ kāraṇam/ dravyatvādijñāne
padārthatvarūpasāmānyadharmajñānaṃ kāraṇamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Its own' means the specific properties such as <s>dravyatva</s>, <s>guṇatva</s>, and the rest; 'through the relation of having that as qualifier-mode' — the cognition qualified by <s>dravyatva</s> and the rest — the desire for that, i.e. the desire of the form 'may cognition having <s>dravyatva</s> and the rest as qualifier-mode arise in me' — for that, the cognition of the form 'cognition having <s>dravyatva</s> and the rest as qualifier-mode is a means to my desired end' is a cause. For such a cognition, the cognition of <s>dravyatva</s> and the rest, which are the delimitors of the property-locus, is a cause. And for the cognition of <s>dravyatva</s> and the rest, the cognition of the general property in the form of <s>padārthatva</s> is a cause — this is the meaning.

children.text:
2. vyutpattivāde
prathamākārake rājapuruṣavākyārthavicārāvasare 'rājasvatvābhāvavān
puruṣaḥ sundaraḥ' ityākārake rājasvatvābhāvaviśiṣṭe puruṣe
sundaratvavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhijñāne 'rājasvatvābhāvavān puruṣaḥ'
ityākārakaṃ viśeṣyatāvacchedakībhūtarājasvatvābhāvaprakārakaṃ jñānaṃ
kāraṇamiti nirūpitam/ tadatra anusaṃhitam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] In the <s>vyutpattivāda</s>, during the first type of discussion of the meaning of the sentence about the king's man (<s>rājapuruṣa</s>), in the cognition apprehending the qualification of beauty in the man qualified by the absence of belonging to the king — i.e. in the cognition of the form 'the man not belonging to the king is beautiful' — the cognition having as its qualifier-mode the absence of belonging to the king, which is the delimitor of qualificand-hood, has been established as a cause. That is applied here.

children.text:
ataḥ
padārthaśabdalabhyārthaikadeśabhūtaṃ abhidheyatvameva lakṣaṇatvena
vivakṣitamityāśayaḥ/
avyāvartakatvād
children.translated_text: because it is non-differentiating —

children.text:
iti/
avyāptyativyāptyādivāraṇarūpaprayojanaśūnyatvādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because it is devoid of the purpose of preventing [defects] such as under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) and over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>).
Therefore, the intent is that <s>abhidheyatva</s> (expressibility), which is a part of the meaning obtained from the word <s>padārtha</s>, alone is intended as the definition.

children.text:
atredaṃ cintyam -
dīpikoktaḥ vibhāgavākyaghaṭakapadārthapadena sāmānyalakṣaṇalābhaprakāraḥ
na śobhate/
children.translated_text: Here is something to be considered: the method of obtaining the general definition from the word <s>padārtha</s> which is a component of the division-sentence, as stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, is not satisfactory.

children.text:
sāmānyalakṣaṇakathanānantaraṃ tataḥ śiṣyasya sāmānyadharmajñānena
padārthaḥ katividha iti viśeṣajijñāsāyāṃ vibhāgavākyasya pravṛtteḥ
vibhāgavākyāghaṭakapadena sāmānyadharmasūcanasyaivocitatvāt
vibhāgavākyaghaṭakena padena
vibhāgavākyaprayojakaviśeṣajijñāsājanakasāmānyadharmajñānotpādane 'nyonyaśrayādidoṣeṇaucityavirahāt/
tasmāt maṅgalaślokasthatarkapadena jñeyatvarūpaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ
sūcitam/ tato viśaiṣajijñāsāyāṃ
dravyaguṇetyādivibhāgavākyamavatīrṇamiti kathanameva yuktam/ tathaiva
nirvyūḍhaṃ ca
niruktyādigrantha
children.translated_text: the <s>Nirukti</s> and other texts —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

Since the division-sentence is employed only after the statement of the general definition, when the student's desire to know specifics has arisen through the cognition of the general property, it is appropriate that only the general property be indicated by a word that is a component of the division-sentence. [But] the generation of the cognition of the general property — which is the cause of the desire to know specifics, which in turn is the occasion for the division-sentence — by a word that is itself a component of the division-sentence, involves the defect of mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>) and hence is inappropriate. Therefore, it is proper to say that the general definition in the form of <s>jñeyatva</s> (knowability) is indicated by the word <s>tarka</s> occurring in the opening benedictory verse, and from that the desire to know specifics arises, and then the division-sentence beginning with '<s>dravya</s>, <s>guṇa</s>' and so forth is introduced. And indeed this has been elaborated in

children.text:
padārthatvāvāntaradharmapuraskāreṇa
dharmipratipādanādeve
children.translated_text: precisely because [the division-sentence] teaches the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) by foregrounding a sub-property of <s>padārthatva</s> —

children.text: ti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text:
padārthatvavyāpyadravyatvādidharmaṃviśiṣṭadravyādidharmipratipādakadravyādiśabdādityarthaḥ/
nanu dravyaguṇetyādiśabdamātrāt dravyatvādiviśiṣṭadravyādīnāṃ
bodhe 'pi teṣu saptatvasaṅkhyāyāḥ kathaṃ bodha iti cet - atrāhuḥ/
vibhāgādeveti mūlasya
dravyaguṇetyādidvandvasamabhivyāhṛtabahuvacanādevetyarthaḥ/ tathā
ca dvandvasamabhivyāhṛbahuvacanasya
dvandvapratipādyatāvadarthaparyāptasaṅkhyāvācakatvaniyamaḥ
avaśyamaṅgīkaraṇīyaḥ/ anyathā rāmalakṣmaṇabharataśatrughnā ityatra
bahuvacanena tritvādibodhāpattyā anubhavavirodhāpatteḥ/ evaṃ ca
prakṛte
dvandvapratipādyadravyādyabhāvāntasamudāyaparyāptasaṅkhyāvācakatāyāḥ
tādṛśadvandvasamabhivyāhṛtabahuvacanasyāvaśyaṃ svīkaraṇīyatayā
tādṛśasaṅkhyā saptatvasaṅkhyaṃveti bahuvacanena tatsiddhiriti/
nīlakaṇṭhaprakāśikāyā
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nīlakaṇṭha Prakāśikā</s> also —

children.text: api kathañcidatraiva tātparyaṃ bodhyam/
children.translated_text: the purport should be understood as somehow settling here alone.

The meaning is: from the words <s>dravya</s> and the rest, which teach the property-possessors such as <s>dravya</s> qualified by properties such as <s>dravyatva</s> that pervade <s>padārthatva</s>. Now, even if from the mere words '<s>dravya</s>, <s>guṇa</s>' and so forth there arises the cognition of <s>dravya</s> and the rest qualified by <s>dravyatva</s> and the rest, how does the number seven become known among them? — to this they reply: 'From the division alone' means: from the <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) and the plural ending co-occurring in '<s>dravya</s>, <s>guṇa</s>' and so forth in the root text — this is the meaning. And accordingly, the rule that a plural ending co-occurring with a <s>dvandva</s> compound denotes only the number sufficient for the items conveyed by the <s>dvandva</s> must necessarily be accepted. Otherwise, in '<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Bharata</s>, and <s>Śatrughna</s>' the plural would give rise to the cognition of three-ness and the like, leading to a contradiction with experience. And accordingly, in the present context, since the denotation of a number sufficient for the aggregate of <s>dravya</s> and the rest up to <s>abhāva</s> conveyed by the <s>dvandva</s> must necessarily be accepted for such a <s>dvandva</s>-co-occurring plural, that number is the number seven — hence its establishment through the plural.

children.text:
mūle
adhikasaṅkhyāvyavacchedārthakatvād
children.translated_text: In the root text, 'because [the word] has the purpose of excluding a greater number' —

children.text:
iti/ adhikasaṅkhyāyāḥ saptatvādhikāṣṭatvasaṅkhyāyāḥ vyavacchedaḥ
niṣedhanirṇayaḥ arthaḥ prayojanaṃ yasya tattvādityarthaḥ/ tadāha -
children.translated_text: The meaning is: 'greater number' means the number eight, which is greater than seven; 'exclusion' means the determination of negation; 'that is its purpose' means that is its function. He states this —

children.text: tādṛśasaṅkhye
children.translated_text: of such a number —

children.text:
ti/ evaṃ ca saptapadena
aṣṭamapadārthanāstitvaṃ bodhyata iti phalitam/ aṣṭamapadārthasya
bhrāntisiddhatve tasya niṣedhasambhavena niṣedhāyogāditi
children.translated_text: And thus the result is that through the word 'seven,' the non-existence of an eighth category is conveyed. If the eighth category were established through error, then since its negation would be possible, the objection that negation is impossible

children.text:
khaṇḍanaṃ na yujyata
ityāśayena jñāta ityanuktvā pramita iti mūle uktam/ pramita
ityasya pramāviṣaya ityarthaḥ/ pramāviṣayasya sattāniyamena
niṣedhāyogāt iti vaktu śakyata iti bhāvaḥ/
tatraiva pratiyogipramiti vine
children.translated_text: In that very [context], without the valid cognition of the counter-positive —

children.text:
ti/ yadyapyabhāvabuddhau pratiyogijñānameva
kāraṇam na tu pratiyogipramā, gaganādyabhāvabuddhau
pratiyogigaganādiprakārakapramāyāḥ kāraṇatvāsambhavāt,
gaganāderavṛttitayā tatprakārikāyāḥ 'idaṃ gaganavat'
ityākārakapramāyāḥ asambhavāt/ tathāpi prakṛte
pratiyogipramāpadena na pratiyogiprakārakapramā vivakṣitā api tu
pratiyogitāvacchedakaprakārakapratiyogiviśeṣyakapramaiva 1vivakṣitā/
'idaṃ gaganam' ityākārikā
gaganatvaprakārakagaganaviśeṣyakapramāprasiddhaiveti tadbalāt
gaganābhāvabuddhiḥ sambhavati/ prakṛte saptapadārthātiriktapadārthaṃsya pramā
nāstīti tanniṣedho nopapadyata iti
children.translated_text: thus. Although in the cognition of absence, it is only the cognition of the counter-positive that is the cause and not the valid cognition of the counter-positive — since a valid cognition having the counter-positive such as the sky as its qualifier-mode is not possible as a cause in the cognition of the absence of the sky and the like, because the sky has no occurrence [in a locus] and therefore a valid cognition of the form 'this possesses the sky' is impossible — nevertheless, in the present context, by the expression 'valid cognition of the counter-positive,' what is intended is not a valid cognition having the counter-positive as its qualifier-mode, but rather a valid cognition having the delimitor of counter-positive-ness as its qualifier-mode and the counter-positive as its qualificand. The valid cognition of the form 'this is the sky,' having sky-ness as qualifier-mode and the sky as qualificand, is well-established, and on its basis the cognition of the absence of the sky is possible. In the present case, since there is no valid cognition of a category beyond the seven categories, its negation is not tenable — this is the

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>'s

children.text: śayaḥ/
children.translated_text: intent.

— this refutation would not be proper. With this intent, the root text uses the word 'validly known' (<s>pramita</s>) rather than 'known' (<s>jñāta</s>). The meaning of <s>pramita</s> is 'object of valid cognition' (<s>pramāviṣaya</s>). Since the object of valid cognition is necessarily existent, one can say that negation is impossible — this is the purport.

children.text:
dravyaguṇetyādivākyena padārthānuddiśya
dravyādisaptānyatamatvaṃ vidhīyate/ uddeśyavidheyabhāvasthale ca
uddeśyatāvacchedake vidheyavyāpyatvaṃ bhāsata iti sāmānyaniyamaḥ/
yathā dhanavān sukhītyatra dhanavanvamuddiśya sukhasya vidhāne
uddeśyatāvacchedake dhane sukhavyāpyatvaṃ bhāsate yatra yatra dhanaṃ tatra
sukhamiti, tathā prakṛte 'pi uddeśyatāvacchedake padārthantve
dravyādisaptānyatamatvavyāpyatvaṃ bhāsate yatra yatra padārthatvaṃ tatra tatra
dravyādisaptānyatamatvamiti/ tathā ca siddhyasiddhibhyāṃ vyāghāto
netyarthaḥ/ tadetadāha -
uddeśyavidheyabhāvasthala
children.translated_text: In the context of the subject-predicate relation

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: autsargikami
children.translated_text: By default (<s>autsargika</s>)

children.text:
ti/ sāmānyanyāyasiddhamityarthaḥ/
'adhikasaṅkhyāvyavacchedārthakatvāt' iti pūrvatanamūlagranthe
vyavacchedaśabdasya yathā niṣedhor'thaḥ tathā 'saptānyatamatvavyāpyamiti
vyavacchedārthakatvāt' iti
children.translated_text: thus. The meaning is: established by the general rule. In the earlier root text, just as the word '<s>vyavaccheda</s>' (exclusion) has the meaning of negation in 'because it serves to exclude the higher number,' so too in 'because it serves to exclude what is pervaded by the property of being one of the seven'

By the sentence 'substance, quality' and so forth, having indicated the categories, the property of being one of the seven such as substance and the rest is predicated. And in a context where there is a subject-predicate relation, the general rule is that what is predicated appears as pervaded by the delimitor of subject-hood. Just as in 'The wealthy person is happy,' when happiness is predicated of the wealthy person, the pervasion of happiness by wealth, which is the delimitor of subject-hood, appears — wherever there is wealth, there is happiness — so too in the present case, the pervasion of the property of being one of the seven such as substance and the rest by category-hood, which is the delimitor of subject-hood, appears — wherever there is category-hood, there is the property of being one of the seven such as substance and the rest. And accordingly, there is no contradiction from either establishment or non-establishment — this is the meaning. He states this very point —

children.text:
1. tathā ca 'abhāvabuddhau
pratiyogijñānaṃ kāraṇam' iti pravādasyāpi pratiyogitā
vacchedakaprakārakapratiyogiviśeṣyakajñānaṃ kāraṇamityevārthaḥ/ na tu
pratiyogiprakārakajñānamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. And accordingly, even the doctrine 'In the cognition of absence, the cognition of the counter-positive is the cause' means that the cognition having the delimitor of counter-positive-ness as its qualifier-mode and the counter-positive as its qualificand is the cause — not a cognition having the counter-positive as its qualifier-mode. This is the purport.

children.text:
prakṛttamūlasthavyavacchedapadasyāpi niṣedhor'tha iti na
bhramitavyamiti bodhayituṃ vyācaṣṭe -
etadrūpa
children.translated_text: Of this form

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: tadarthakatvād
children.translated_text: Because it has that meaning

children.text: iti/ saptagrahaṇasyeti śeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. The remainder is: 'of the mention of seven.'
the word '<s>vyavaccheda</s>' in the present root text also has the meaning of negation — to convey that one should not be confused about this, he explains —

children.text:
nanu saptānyatamatvaṃ
nāma saptabhinnabhinnatvam/ saptapadārthabhinnasyāprasiddhyā
tadbhinnatvarūpamanyatamatvamaprasiddhamiti tannirūpitavyāpyatvaṃ padārthe na
niścetuṃ śakyata iti tādṛśaniścayaphalakatvaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, the property of being one of the seven (<s>saptānyatamatva</s>) means being different from what is different from the seven. Since what is different from the seven categories is not established, the property of being different from that, which constitutes the 'one-of-ness,' is also not established — and therefore the pervasion delimited by that cannot be ascertained with respect to the categories. Hence the purpose of the mention of seven for producing such ascertainment

children.text:
saptagrahaṇasya na yujyata
ityāśaṅkitaṃ 'nanu saptānyatamatvam' ityādinā
dīpikāyām
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>.

children.text:
/ tatrāprasiddhiśaṅkāna na yujyate, ye
dravyādayaḥ saptapadārthāḥ pratyekaṃ tadbhinnabhinnatvasya pratyekaṃ sattvāt/
dravyabhinnaguṇādibhinnatvasya dravye, guṇabhinnadravyādibhinnatvasya guṇe
satatvamiti rītyā saptasvapi padārtheṣu tadbhinnabhinnatvasya
sattvādityāśaṅkya vyācaṣṭe -
children.translated_text: There, the doubt of non-establishment is not justified, because for each of the seven categories such as substance and the rest, the property of being different from what is different from each of them individually obtains. In substance, there is the property of being different from quality and the rest which are different from substance; in quality, there is the property of being different from substance and the rest which are different from quality — in this manner, in all seven categories the property of being different from what is different from them obtains. Anticipating this, he explains —

children.text: dravyādayo ye sapte
children.translated_text: Substance and the rest, which are seven,

children.text:
ti/
evaṃ ca dravyādayo ye sapta padārthāḥ tadbhedakūṭaviśiṣṭaṃ -
tadbhedasaptakaviśiṣṭaṃ yat tadbhinnatvaṃ saptānyatamatvam/
children.translated_text: thus. And accordingly, those seven categories which are substance and the rest — the property of being qualified by the aggregate of their differences, i.e. being different from what is qualified by the sevenfold collection of differences from them, is <s>saptānyatamatva</s> (the property of being one of the seven).

children.text: tatra
children.translated_text: There,

children.text:
bhedasaptakaviśiṣṭamaprasiddham, dravye
guṇādipratiyogikabhedaṣaṭkasya sattve 'pi dravyabhedasyāsattvena
tadghaṭitasaptabhedasamudāyasyāsambhavāt, evaṃ guṇādāvapi/ tathā ca
bhedasaptakaviśiṣṭātmakasya saptabhinnasyāprasiddhatayā tadbhinnatvarūpaṃ
saptabhinnabhinnatvamaprasiddhamiti śaṅkiturāśaya iti bhāvaḥ/ dravye
guṇabhedaḥ guṇe dravyabheda ityevaṃ pratyekaṃ prasiddhā ye bhedāḥ sapta
tatsamudāyatvāvacchinnābhāvo 'tra saptānyatamatvam/ padārthatvaṃ yatra
children.translated_text: that which is qualified by the sevenfold collection of differences is not established. In substance, although there is the sixfold collection of differences having quality and the rest as counter-positives, since the difference from substance itself does not exist [in substance], the aggregate of seven differences constituted by that is not possible — and similarly in quality and the rest. And accordingly, since what is different from the seven, being constituted by the sevenfold collection of differences, is not established, the property of being different from that, namely the property of being different from what is different from the seven, is not established — this is the intent of the objector. This is the purport. The differences that are individually established — such as the difference from quality in substance, the difference from substance in quality — these seven differences taken as an aggregate qualified by the absence delimited by the aggregate-hood of those: that is <s>saptānyatamatva</s> here. Wherever category-hood exists,
is not justified — this was raised as a doubt in the <s>Dīpikā</s> with 'Now, the property of being one of the seven' and so forth.

children.text:
yatrāsti tatra
tādṛśasamudāyatvāvacchinnābhāvo 'sti ataḥ vyāptiniścayaḥ sukara
ityāśayamāha -
dravyādibhedānām
children.translated_text: Of the differences from substance and the rest

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.
there the absence delimited by such aggregate-hood exists; therefore the ascertainment of pervasion is easy — he states this intent —

children.text:
bahuṣu grantheṣu
saptānyatametvamaprasiddhamiti śaṅkātatsamādhānaparo grantho na
dṛśyate/ ataḥ padārthatvaṃ dravyādisaptānyatamatvavyāpyamiti dīpikāyāḥ
yādṛśārthavarṇane 'prasiddhiśaṅkā nodiyāt tādṛśamarthaṃ kathayati -
vastutastv
children.translated_text: In reality, however,

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

In many texts, the property of being one of the seven is [treated as] not established, and no text addressing this doubt and its resolution is found. Therefore, the <s>Dīpikā</s>'s exposition of the meaning such that the doubt of non-establishment would not arise regarding the pervasion 'category-hood is pervaded by the property of being one of the seven such as substance and the rest' — he explains the true meaning —

children.text:
yatra yatra padārthatvaṃ

vyāptiḥ prakṛte vivakṣitā/ padārthatvaṃ dravye 'sti, tatra
dravyatvādisaptānyatamabhūtadravyatvavattvamastīti/ dravyādau vyāptiḥ
sugrahā/ anyatamatvaṃ ca tadbhinnabhinnatvameva/ dravyatvādayaḥ ye sapta
dharmāḥ tadbhinnāḥ ghaṭatvādayaḥ tadbhinnatvaṃ dravyatvādiṣvastīti
nāprasiddhiśaṅkāvakāśa iti bhāvaḥ/ evaṃ rītyeti/ dravyatvaṃ
pṛthivyādyanyatamatvavyāpyamiti nirṇayārthaṃ navagrahaṇamiti
rītyetyarthaḥ//
children.translated_text: The pervasion intended in the present context is: wherever there is category-hood, there is the property of possessing one of the seven attributes such as substance-hood and the rest. In substance there is category-hood, and there substance-hood, which is one of the seven attributes beginning with substance-hood, is present — thus the pervasion is easily grasped in substance and the rest. And 'one-of-ness' (<s>anyatamatva</s>) is indeed being different from what is different from them. The seven attributes which are substance-hood and the rest — what is different from them, such as pot-hood and the like — the property of being different from those exists in substance-hood and the rest — so there is no room for the doubt of non-establishment. This is the purport. 'In this manner' — means in the manner that the mention of nine serves to determine that substance-hood is pervaded by the property of being one of [the nine] such as earth-hood and the rest — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: text which is problematic. For: the singular number following the word 'substance' has the meaning of oneness. Its connection is with substance, which is the meaning of the stem. The connection of that [oneness] with the meaning of the accusative case as a qualificand is through the relation of superstratum-hood. The connection of qualificand-ness is through the delimiting relation with a part of the meaning of the verbal root, namely knowledge. The meaning of the verbal root with the prefix <s>vi</s>- and the root <s>bhaj</s> is: a word that generates knowledge in the form of valid cognition having as its qualifier-modes various mutually contradictory attributes pervaded by substance-hood. The connection of that with the verbal action (<s>kṛti</s>) denoted by the verbal ending is through the relation of favorability, and the connection of that [action] with <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s> is through the relation of locus-hood. Thus,
Now, the <s>Dīpikā</s> passage 'He divides substance — there'

children.text:

iti 'dravyaṃ vibhajata' iti vākyāt bodhaḥ/ tatra ekadravyaviśeṣyakaṃ
dravyatvavyāpyapṛthivītvādinānādharmaviśeṣaṇakaṃ pramātmakaṃ jñānaṃ na
sambhavati/ pṛthivyādi rūpaikadravyaviśe 'tiriktatve
anantāvayavatatprāgabhāvādikalpanāgauravam ata
āvaśyakatejo 'bhāvarūpatvaṃ sidhyatītyapi bodhyam//
children.translated_text: the verbal understanding from the sentence 'He divides substance' is: <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s> is the locus of the action favorable to a word that generates knowledge in the form of valid cognition having a single substance as qualificand and various attributes pervaded by substance-hood as qualifier-modes. But there, a knowledge in the form of valid cognition having a single substance as qualificand and various specific attributes such as earth-hood and the rest pervaded by substance-hood as qualifier-modes is not possible. If one posits that earth and the like are a single substance over and above individual substances, the unwanted consequence of postulating infinite parts and prior absences thereof would follow. From this it is also to be understood that the nature of fire-absence is necessarily established.

dravyatvarūpaviśeṣyāsiddhiparihārāya 'tamaḥ dravyam, rūpavattvāt

children.translated_text: The inference 'Darkness is a tenth substance, because it possesses substance-hood while not being included among the established substances' was intended to prove that darkness is a tenth substance through the method of elimination (<s>pariśeṣa</s>). There, to resolve the non-establishment of the qualificand in the reason, namely substance-hood, the inference 'Darkness is a substance, because it possesses color and because it possesses motion'

children.text:

'nīlaṃ tamaḥ,' 'calati tamaḥ' ityākārikayā abādhitayā pratyakṣarūpayā

children.translated_text: 'By the force of cognition'

children.text:
iti
1pañcamyantasya rūpādhāratve kriyādhāratve cānvayaḥ/

jñānasāmānyavācakapratītiśabdaḥ prakṛte pratyakṣātmakajñānaparaḥ,
prathamopasthitaparityāge mānābhāvāt/ pratyakṣāsambhavasthala
evānumānaparatvāt jñānasāmānyavācakapadasyetyāśayenāha -
children.translated_text: thus. The fifth-case ending [in '<s>pratītibalāt</s>'] connects with both being the substratum of color and being the substratum of motion. Since a contradicted cognition cannot establish its object, the word 'uncontradicted' was used. The word '<s>pratīti</s>' (cognition), which generally denotes cognition in general, in the present context refers to perceptual cognition, since there is no ground for abandoning the first [i.e. most immediate] referent. And since [the general word for cognition] refers to inference only when direct perception is impossible — with this intent he says —

children.text:
prakāśikāyāṃ
prātyakṣikapratītibalād
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'by the force of perceptual cognition'

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

should be employed to establish the substance-hood of darkness. Even there, the doubt of the non-establishment of the reason should not be raised; because by the uncontradicted perceptual cognition of the form 'Darkness is dark-colored' and 'Darkness moves,' the possession of color and the possession of motion by darkness are established. This is stated

children.text:
nanu 'tamo dravyam, nīlarūpādhāratvāt

sattvādityāśaṅkyāha -
samavāyena
children.translated_text: 'Through inherence (<s>samavāya</s>)'

children.text: nīlarūpavatteyetyartha
children.translated_text: meaning: possessing dark color [through inherence] —

children.text:
iti/ tathā ca
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnanīlarūpaniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitādhāratvaṃ
tādṛśakriyāniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitādhikaraṇatvaṃ ca prakṛte hetutayā
vivakṣitam/ janyaguṇādau kālikasambandhāvacchinna
children.translated_text: thus. And accordingly, what is intended as the reason in the present context is: the substratum-hood delimited by the superstratum-hood residing in dark color qualified by the relation of inherence, and the locus-hood delimited by the superstratum-hood residing in such motion qualified by the relation of inherence. In produced qualities and the like, [color and motion exist only] through a temporal relation —

Now, the inference 'Darkness is a substance because it is the substratum of dark color and because it is the substratum of motion' is deviant (<s>vyabhicārin</s>), since even in a produced quality and the like which lack substance-hood, the property of being a substratum of color and of motion exists through the temporal relation — anticipating this doubt, he says —

children.text:
1. pratītibalāditi
pañcamyantasya 'tamaso dravyatvaṃ siddham' ityanenānvaya iti
bhramavāraṇāya rūpādhāratve kriyādhāratve cānvaya ityuktam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'By the force of cognition' — the fifth-case ending connects with 'the substance-hood of darkness is established'; to prevent the misconception [that it connects otherwise], it was said that it connects with being the substratum of color and being the substratum of motion.

children.text:
2. nityapadārtheṣu
kālikasambandhena kimapi nāsti, nityeṣu kālikāyogāditi
siddhāntāt/ tathā ca nityaguṇādeḥ kālikasambandhena rūpādhāratvaṃ na
sambhavatītyamipretya janyaguṇādāvityuktam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 2. In eternal entities, nothing exists through a temporal relation, since temporal relation is impossible in eternal things — this is the established doctrine. And accordingly, since the substratum-hood of color through a temporal relation is not possible for eternal qualities and the like — with this in mind, it was said 'in produced qualities and the like.'

children.text:
1rūpakriyāniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitādhāratvamevāstīti na
vyabhicāra iti bhāvaḥ/
kālikasambandhena tasye
children.translated_text: 'Through temporal relation, of that'

children.text: ti/ kālikasambandhāvacchinnarūpakriyādhāratvasyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. The meaning is: of the substratum-hood of color and motion delimited by a temporal relation.

children.text: atiprasaktatve 'pi

children.text: - dravyātiriktavṛttitve 'pi/
children.translated_text: — even if it occurs in what is other than substance,

children.translated_text: — there is no deviation.

children.text: evamagre 'pi bodhyam
children.translated_text: 'This should be understood further ahead as well'

iti/'tamaso nākāśādipañcake 'ntarbhāvaḥ
rūpavattvāt' ityatrāpi rūpavattvādityasya samavāyena
rūpavattvādityartho bodhya iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. In 'Darkness is not included among the five such as space and the rest, because it possesses color,' there too the meaning to be understood is: 'because it possesses color through inherence.' This is the purport.
only the substratum-hood delimited by the superstratum-hood of color and motion exists [through temporal relation] — hence there is no deviation. This is the purport.

children.text:

daśamadravyam, kḷptadravyānantarbhūtatve sati dravyatvāt' iti

kḷptadravyānantarbhūtatvaṃ sādhyate
dīpikāyām tatra tamasa
children.translated_text: in the <s>Dīpikā</s> with 'There, of darkness'
