ityādinā/ nanu rūpavattvahetunaiva tamasaḥ vāyāvanantarbhāve
siddhe punaḥ tatsādhakatayā sparśābhāvasyopanyāso vyartha
ityāśaṅkyāha -
children.translated_text: and so forth. Now, since the non-inclusion of darkness in air is already established by the reason of possessing color alone, the additional mention of the absence of touch as an establishing factor is redundant — anticipating this doubt, he says —

children.text: sambandhabhedābhiprāyeṇe
children.translated_text: 'With the intention of a difference in relation'

children.text:
ti/rūpavattvaṃ samavāyasambandhena hetuḥ/
sparśābhāvastu svarūpasambandhena hetuḥ/ samavāyasambandhena hetumuktvā
svarūpasambandhena hetumāhetyarthaḥ/ yadi tamo vāyāvantarbhavet
rūpavat na syāt sparśaśūnyaṃ ca na syāt/ yataḥ tamaḥ rūpavat
sparśaśūnyaṃ ca ato vāyau nāntarbhavatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. Possession of color is a reason through the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). But absence of touch is a reason through the self-linking relation (<s>svarūpa-sambandha</s>). Having stated the reason through the relation of inherence, he states the reason through the self-linking relation — this is the meaning. If darkness were included in air, it would not possess color and would not be devoid of touch. Since darkness does possess color and is devoid of touch, therefore it is not included in air — this is the purport.

By this much, in the inference by elimination 'Darkness is a tenth substance, because it possesses substance-hood while not being included among the established substances,' the substance-hood that is a component of the reason has been established. Now the other component of the reason, namely the non-inclusion among the established substances, is established

children.text:
nanu 'tamaḥ
vāyubhinnam, sparśābhāvāt' ityanumānaṃ phalitam/ tatra
vāyubhedarūpasādhyābhāvavati vāyau
sparśaniṣṭhasaṃyogasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvarūpasya
sparśābhāvasya sattvāt vyabhicāraḥ/ na ca
sparśaniṣṭhasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvo hetutvena
vivakṣitaḥ/ sa ca na vāyāvasti, tatra samavāyena sparśasya sattvāt
tadabhāvāsambhavāditi vācyam/
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnasparśaniṣṭhapratiyogitākābhāvasya
kālikasambandhena vāyau sattvāt vyabhicāratādavasthyāt/ na ca
samavāyāvacchinnasparśābhāvasya svarūpasambandhena hetutāyāḥ
vivakṣitatvāt na vyabhicāra iti vācyam/ evamapi
utpattikālāvacchinnavāyau 'utpannaṃ dravyaṃ kṣaṇamaguṇamakriyaṃ ca tiṣṭhati'
iti nyāyena sparśasyābhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, the inference 'Darkness is different from air, because of the absence of touch' is resultant. There, in air, which possesses the absence of the probandum in the form of difference from air, since the absence of touch in the form of an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of conjunction inhering in touch exists, there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). Nor should it be said that what is intended as the probans is the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of inherence inhering in touch, and that this does not exist in air because touch exists there through inherence and hence its absence is impossible — for since the absence whose counter-positiveness inhering in touch is delimited by the relation of inherence exists in air through temporal relation, the deviation remains as before. Nor should it be said that since the absence of touch delimited by inherence is intended as having causality through the self-linking relation (<s>svarūpasaṃbandha</s>), there is no deviation — for even so, in air at the moment of origination, by the principle that 'a produced substance remains for a moment without qualities and without actions,' the absence of touch

children.text:
1. rūpaniṣṭhā
kriyāniṣṭhā ca yā ādheyatā tannirūpitādhāratvamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. The meaning is: that substratum-hood which is determined by the container-hood inhering in form and inhering in action.

children.text:
svarūpasambandhenāstīti
vyabhicārasya durvāratvādityāśaṅkyāha
idaṃ ca dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvādhikaraṇa
children.translated_text: This is the locus of destruction and prior absence —

children.text:
iti/ tathā ca sparśaprāgabhāvavati
utpattikṣaṇāvacchinnavāyau sparśātyantābhāvo nāstīti hetoḥ
prācīnamate na vyabhicāra iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. And accordingly, in air at the moment of origination, which possesses the prior absence of touch, the absolute absence of touch does not exist — hence on the ancient view there is no deviation. This is the purport.

children.text: anyathe
children.translated_text: Otherwise —

children.text:
ti/
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvādhikaraṇe 'tyantābhāvo 'ṅgīkriyata iti navīnamata
ityarthaḥ/ navyamate 'pi vyabhicāraṃ vārayitumāha -
children.translated_text: thus. The meaning is: 'on the new view,' i.e., the view that accepts absolute absence even in the locus of destruction and prior absence. Even on the new view, to ward off deviation, he says —

children.text: vastutastu
children.translated_text: In reality, however —

children.text:
iti/ tathā ca vāyau sparśātyantābhāvaḥ
utpattikālāvacchinnadaiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhenaiva
children.translated_text: thus. And accordingly, the absolute absence of touch in air exists only through the relation of spatial qualification delimited by the time of origination,
exists through the self-linking relation — and so the deviation is unavoidable. Anticipating this objection, he says —

children.text:
vartate, na tu
niravacchinnadaiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandheneti na vyabhicāra iti bhāvaḥ/
daiśikaviśeṣaṇatāpadena svarūpasambandhaḥ kālikaviśeṣaṇatāpadena
kālikasambandhaśca navyanyāyagrantheṣu vyavahriyate/
children.translated_text: and not through the relation of undelimited spatial qualification — hence there is no deviation. This is the purport. In the <s>Navya-Nyāya</s> texts, the term 'spatial qualification' (<s>daiśikaviśeṣaṇatā</s>) is used for the self-linking relation, and the term 'temporal qualification' (<s>kālikaviśeṣaṇatā</s>) for the temporal relation.

children.text: viṣamavyāptahetum
children.translated_text: A probans with asymmetric pervasion (<s>viṣamavyāpta</s>) —

children.text:
iti/ sādhyamātranirūpitavyāptimān hetuḥ
viṣamavyāpta iti,
hetunirūpitavyāptimatsādhyanirūpitavyāptimān hetuḥ samavyāpta
iti cocyate/ 'tamaḥ vāyubhinnam, rūpavattvāt'
ityanumānaprayoge yatra yatra rūpavattvaṃ tatra vāyubheda iti
vāyubhedanirūpitā vyāptiḥ hetau rūpavattve 'sti/ yatra yatra vāyubhedaḥ
tatra tatra rūpavattvamiti rūpavattvanirūpitā vyāptistu vāyubhede na
sambhavati, vāyubhedavatyākāśādau rūpavattvābhāvena vyabhicārāt/
ato rūpavattvaṃ viṣamavyāpto hetuḥ/ evaṃ sparśābhāvo 'pi/ yatra yatra
sparśābhāvaḥ tatra tatra vāyubheda iti vyāptisattve 'pi yatra yatra
vāyubhedaḥ tatra tatra sparśābhāva iti vyāptyabhāvāt vāyubhedavati
ghaṭādau sparśasyaiva sattvāt/ 'tamaḥ vāyubhinnam,
sadāgatimattvābhāvāt' ityatra sadāgatimattvābhāvastu samavyāpto
hetuḥ/ yatra yatra vāyubhedaḥ tatra tatra sadāgatimattvābhāva iti
sadāgatimattvābhāvanirūpitavyāpteḥ vāyubhede, yatra yatra
sadāgagimattvābhāvaḥ tatra tatra vāyubheda iti
vāyubhedanirūpitavyāpteḥ sadāgatimattvābhāve ca sattvāditi/
children.translated_text: thus. A probans that possesses pervasion determined only by the probandum is called 'asymmetrically pervaded' (<s>viṣamavyāpta</s>), and a probans that possesses pervasion determined by the probandum as well as pervasion determined by the probans is called 'symmetrically pervaded' (<s>samavyāpta</s>). In the inferential application 'Darkness is different from air, because of possessing form (<s>rūpavatva</s>)' — the pervasion determined by difference-from-air exists in the probans 'possessing form': wherever there is form-possession, there is difference from air. But the pervasion determined by form-possession does not obtain in difference-from-air: wherever there is difference from air, there is form-possession — this does not hold, because of deviation in space (<s>ākāśa</s>) etc. which possess difference from air but lack form. Therefore, form-possession is an asymmetrically pervaded probans. Similarly for the absence of touch: even though the pervasion 'wherever there is absence of touch, there is difference from air' holds, the pervasion 'wherever there is difference from air, there is absence of touch' does not hold, because in pots etc. which possess difference from air, touch itself exists. In 'Darkness is different from air, because of the absence of perpetual motion (<s>sadāgatimattvābhāva</s>),' the absence of perpetual motion is a symmetrically pervaded probans — because both the pervasion determined by the absence of perpetual motion in difference-from-air and the pervasion determined by difference-from-air in the absence of perpetual motion obtain.

children.text: vijātīyakriye
children.translated_text: A motion of a different kind (<s>vijātīyakriyā</s>) —

children.text: ti/ vāyumātravṛttirvilakṣaṇakriyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: a distinctive motion that occurs only in air.

children.text: dīpikāyāṃ nāpi tejasī
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'Nor is [darkness] included in fire (<s>tejas</s>)' —

children.text:
ti/ 'tamaḥ tejasi nāntarbhavati
(tejobhinnam), bhāsvararūpābhāvāt uṣṇasparśābhāvācca'
ityanumānam/ tatra bhāsvararūpābhāvaḥ viṣamavyāptaḥ, uṣṇasparśābhāvaḥ
samavyāptaḥ/ evaṃ 'tamaḥ jalabhinnam śītasparśābhāvāt nīlarūpavattvācca'
ityanumāne śītasparśābhāvaḥ samavyāptaḥ, nīlarūpavattvaṃ
viṣamavyāptam/ 'tamḥ pṛthivībhinnam, gandhābhāvāt
sparśarahitatvācca' ityatra gandhābhāvaḥ samavyāptaḥ, sparśarahitatvaṃ
viṣamavyāptamiti ūhyam/
children.translated_text: thus. The inference is: 'Darkness is not included in fire (is different from fire), because of the absence of luminous form and because of the absence of hot touch.' There, the absence of luminous form is asymmetrically pervaded; the absence of hot touch is symmetrically pervaded. Similarly, in the inference 'Darkness is different from water, because of the absence of cold touch and because of possessing blue form,' the absence of cold touch is symmetrically pervaded, and possessing blue form is asymmetrically pervaded. In 'Darkness is different from earth, because of the absence of smell and because of being devoid of touch,' the absence of smell is symmetrically pervaded, and being devoid of touch is asymmetrically pervaded — this should be understood.

children.text:
tamasaḥ dravyatvameva
nāsti, kuto daśamadravyatvam/ tamastvabhāvākhye
saptamapadārtheṃ'ntarbhūtamiti matvā
tamasastejo 'bhāvarūpatvāt
children.translated_text: because darkness has the nature of the absence of fire (<s>tejas</s>) —

children.text: ityuktaṃ
children.translated_text: this was stated

children.text: dīpikāyām
children.translated_text: in the <s>Dīpikā</s>.

children.text:
/ tatra tejo 'bhāvapadena
tejaḥpratiyogikābhāvavivakṣāyāṃ sūryāditejasvatyapi deśe
tejo 'ntarapratiṃyogikābhāvasattvena tama iti pratītiprasaṅgaḥ/
tejastvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvavivakṣāyāṃ tamasvatyapi deśe
tejaḥparamāṇvādisattvena tejassāmānyābhāvasyāsattvena tama iti
pratītyanupapattiḥ/ prakāśakaṃ yattejaḥ
tattvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvavivakṣaṇena tejaḥparamāṇvādīnāṃ
prakāśakatvābhāvāt pūrvoktadoṣavāraṇe 'pi
prakāśakatejastryaṇukakhadyotādimati pradeśe tamaḥpratītyanupapattiḥ/ ataḥ
prauḍhaṃ prākaśakaṃ ca yattejaḥ tattvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvo
vivakṣaṇīyaḥ/ prauḍhatvaṃ ca prakṛṣṭamahatvavattvam/
tryaṇukādetādṛśaprauḍhatvābhāvāt tatsattve 'pi
tamaḥpratīternānupapattiḥ/ tadetatsarvaṃ manasikṛtyāha -
children.translated_text: There, if by the term 'absence of fire' one intends an absence having fire as its counter-positive, then even in a place possessing sunlight and other forms of fire, since an absence having some other fire as its counter-positive exists, there would be the unwanted consequence of the cognition 'there is darkness.' If one intends an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by fire-ness, then even in a place possessing darkness, since atoms of fire and the like exist there, the universal absence of fire-ness does not obtain, and the cognition 'there is darkness' would be unjustified. By intending an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the property of being illuminating fire — since atoms of fire and the like lack the property of being illuminating — even though the previously stated defect is averted, in a place possessing illuminating fire in the form of three-atom aggregates, fireflies, and the like, the cognition of darkness would be unjustified. Therefore, one should intend an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the property of being mature and illuminating fire. And maturity means possessing extensive magnitude. Since three-atom aggregates and the like lack such maturity, even when they are present, there is no impossibility of the cognition of darkness. Having considered all this, he says —

children.text: prauḍhaprakāśake
children.translated_text: Mature illuminating [fire] —

children.text: ti/ prakāśakapadaprayojanamāha -
children.translated_text: thus. He states the purpose of the word 'illuminating' —

children.text: ata
children.translated_text: Therefore —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.
Darkness is not a substance at all — how then could it be a tenth substance? Considering that darkness is included in the seventh category called absence (<s>abhāva</s>),

children.text:
prauḍhaprakāśakatejastvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvastama
ityuktau prakāśakapadaṃ vayartham/ tejaḥparamāṇūnāṃ
prakṛṣṭamahattvarūpaprauḍhatvābhāvādeva vāraṇasambhavāt/ ataḥ
hiraṇyāditejovāraṇāya prakāśakapadamiti vaktavyam/ evamapi
children.translated_text: If darkness were stated as the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the property of being mature illuminating fire, the word 'illuminating' would be redundant — because atoms of fire can be excluded by the very absence of the maturity in the form of extensive magnitude. Therefore, the word 'illuminating' is to be stated for the purpose of excluding fire such as gold and the like. Even so,

children.text:
cakṣurāditejasvati
pradeśe tamaḥpratītyanupapattiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya udbhūtarūpavattvamapi tejasi
viśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ tathā ca
prakṛṣṭamahattvavatprakāśakodbhūtarūpavattejastvāvacchinnapratiyogi tākābhāvastamaḥ/
atha vā pauḍhatvaṃ mahāprabhāvattvam/ tenaiva paramāṇūnāṃ hiraṇyādeśca
vāraṇasambhavāt prakāśakapadamanupādeyam/
mahāprabhāvattvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvastama iti phalitam/
tadetadabhisandhāyāha -
digi
children.translated_text: In [all] directions —

children.text: ti/
children.translated_text: thus.

in a place possessing fire in the form of the eye and similar [sense organs], the cognition of darkness would be unjustified. To avert this, the qualification 'possessing manifest form' (<s>udbhūtarūpavatva</s>) should also be added to fire. And accordingly, darkness is the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the property of being fire that possesses extensive magnitude, is illuminating, and possesses manifest form. Alternatively, maturity means having great radiance (<s>mahāprabhāvatva</s>). By that alone, the exclusion of atoms and of gold and the like is possible, so the word 'illuminating' need not be included. The result is that darkness is the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the property of having great radiance. With this intent, he says —

children.text:
nanu tamaso
rūpavattvena dravyatvasya pūrvaṃ prasādhitatvāt
kathamabhāvarūpatvamityāśaṅkya
dīpikāyāṃ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> —

children.text:
'tamaḥ na
rūpidravyam' ityādyuktam/ atra tamaso rūpavattvābhāvaḥ dravyatvābhāvaśca
siṣādhayiṣitaḥ/ tamo yadi rūpavat dravyaṃ vā bhavet, tadā
ālokasahakṛtenaiva cakṣuṣā gṛhyeta, yataḥ ālokāsāhakṛtena cakṣuṣā
gṛhyate ataḥ tamo na rūpavat na vā dravyamiti/ yatra yatra
ālokāsahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyatvaṃ tatra tatra rūpavadbhinnatvaṃ dravyabhinnatvaṃ ca
yathā ālokābhāve iti vyāptisadbhāvāt/ hetau
ālokāsahakṛteti viśeṣaṇānupādāne sādhyābhāvavati rūpavaddravye
ghaṭādaucakṣurgrāhyatvarūpahetusattvāt vyabhicāraḥ syāditi
tadupādānam/ ghaṭādirālokasahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyaḥ na
tadasahakṛtacakṣurgrāhya iti na vyabhicāraḥ/ tadāha -
children.translated_text: 'Darkness is not a substance possessing form' and so forth was stated. Here, the absence of form-possession and the absence of substance-hood in darkness is what is sought to be proved. If darkness were a substance possessing form, then it would be apprehended only by the eye assisted by light; since it is apprehended by the eye without the assistance of light, therefore darkness neither possesses form nor is a substance. Because the pervasion holds: wherever there is apprehensibility by the eye without the assistance of light, there is difference from form-possessing [entities] and difference from substance — as in the case of the absence of light. The qualifier 'without the assistance of light' in the probans is included because: without that qualifier, since the probans in the form of 'apprehensibility by the eye' exists in form-possessing substances like pots and the like which possess the absence of the probandum, there would be deviation. Pots and the like are apprehensible by the eye assisted by light, not by the eye unassisted by light — hence there is no deviation. He states this —

children.text: ghaṭādāv
children.translated_text: In pots and the like —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.
Now, since the form-possessing nature of darkness, and hence its substance-hood, was previously established, how can it have the nature of absence? Anticipating this doubt —

children.text:
nanu cakṣurgrāhyatvaṃ nāma
cakṣurjanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvam/
ālokāsahakṛtacakṣurjanyatamoviṣayakapratyakṣe yatra
children.translated_text: Now, 'apprehensibility by the eye' means being the object of a perception generated by the eye. In a perception generated by the eye without the assistance of light, whose object is darkness, where

children.text:
jñānalakṣaṇapratyāsattyā
ghaṭo 'pi bhātaḥ, tatpratyakṣaviṣaye ghaṭādau vyabhicāra iti
śaṅkāyāmāha

- cakṣurgrāhyatvaṃ
cakṣurjanyajñānīyalaukikaviṣayatvam
children.translated_text: apprehensibility by the eye means being a worldly (<s>laukika</s>) object of a cognition generated by the eye —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: tamasaścākṣuṣa
children.translated_text: The visual [perception] of darkness —

children.text:
iti/ tamoviṣayake cakṣurjanyapratyakṣa
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: a perception generated by the eye whose object is darkness.

children.text: upanayamaryādaye
children.translated_text: Through the principle of application (<s>upanaya</s>) —

children.text:
ti/ jñānalakṣaṇapratyāsattyetyarthaḥ/
keṣucit kośeṣu"tena tamasaścākṣuṣe tamovān ghaṭa iti
ghaṭādināmupanayamaryādayā bhāne 'pi na kṣatiḥ"iti
pāṭho dṛśyate/ tatra 'tamovān ghaṭa iti' iti bhāgaḥ aprāmāṇikaḥ,
upanītaṃ viśeṣaṇatayaiva bhāsate na tu viśeṣyatayeti
siddhāntavirodhāt/ atastadbhāgarahitaḥ pāṭhaḥ eva kvacit dṛśyamānaḥ
sādhuḥ/ atha vā 'ghaṭavattamaḥ iti' iti śodhayitvā paṭhanīyam/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: through <s>jñānalakṣaṇapratyāsatti</s> (extraordinary perceptual contact through cognition). In some manuscripts, the reading 'therefore, in the visual [perception] of darkness, [the pot appearing as] a pot possessing darkness — even though pots and the like appear through the principle of application, there is no harm' is found. There, the portion 'a pot possessing darkness' is inauthentic, because what is presented through extraordinary contact appears only as a qualifier, not as a qualificand — which contradicts the established doctrine. Therefore, the reading without that portion, which is seen in some [manuscripts], is correct. Alternatively, it should be emended and read as 'darkness possessing a pot.'

a pot too appears through <s>jñānalakṣaṇapratyāsatti</s> (extraordinary perceptual contact through cognition) — if a doubt arises regarding deviation in pots and the like which are objects of that perception, he says —

children.text:
nanu
tejassāmānyābhāvasya pakṣatayā tadantargatasya ālokābhāvasya
dṛṣṭāntatvakathanaṃ na yuktam, pakṣātiriktasyaiva dṛṣṭāntatvāt ityata
āha -
viśeṣābhāvam
children.translated_text: A particular absence —

children.text:
iti/
sāmānyadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ pakṣaḥ, tadatiriktaḥ
viśeṣadharmāvacchinnābhāvo dṛṣṭāntaḥ/ ato nānupapattiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. The absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a general property is the thesis; distinct from that, the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a particular property is the example. Therefore there is no difficulty — this is the purport.

Now, since the absence of fire in general is the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), stating the absence of light, which is included within it, as the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is not proper, because only something other than the thesis can be the example. To this he says —

children.text:
nanu
ālokāsahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyatvarūpaheturastu rūpavaddravyabhedarūpasādhyaṃ
māstu ityaprayojakaśaṅkāyāmuktaṃ
dīpikāyām - rūpidravyacākṣuṣapramāyāmityā
children.translated_text: in the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'In the valid cognition of a form-possessing substance through the eye' and so forth.

children.text:
di/ yadi rūpidravyabhedo na syāt tarhi
ālokāsahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyaṃ na syāt/ arthāt yadi rūpidravyaṃ syāt
tarhi ālokasahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyaṃ syāditi tarkaḥ
aprayojakaśaṅkānivārakaḥ vaktavyaḥ/ sa ca tarkaḥ
rūpavattvaprakārakadravyaviśeṣyakacakṣurjanyapramātmakapratyakṣe ālokaḥ
kāraṇamiti kāryakāraṇabhāve sati syādityāśayena kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ
pradarśitaḥ/ tatra pramāpadasya prayojanamāha -
children.translated_text: If there were no difference from form-possessing substance, then there would be no apprehensibility by the eye without the assistance of light. In other words, if it were a form-possessing substance, then it would be apprehensible by the eye assisted by light — this <s>tarka</s> (counterfactual reasoning) is to be stated as averting the purposeless objection. And that <s>tarka</s> is presented through the causal relation, with the intent that light is a cause in the perception that has form-possession as qualifier-mode and substance as qualificand and is a valid cognition generated by the eye. There, he states the purpose of the word 'valid cognition' (<s>pramā</s>) —

children.text: ālokaṃ vine
children.translated_text: Without light —

children.text:
ti/ tathā
ca pramāpadānupādāne ālokābhāve 'pi
rūpavattvaprakārakatamoviśeṣyakabhramātmakapratyakṣotpattyā
vyatirekavyabhicāraḥ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya pramāpadamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. And accordingly, without the inclusion of the word 'valid cognition,' even in the absence of light, since a perception in the form of an erroneous cognition having form-possession as qualifier-mode and darkness as qualificand arises, there would be deviation in the negative concomitance (<s>vyatirekavyabhicāra</s>). To avert that, the word 'valid cognition' is included — this is the purport.

children.text: anyathe
children.translated_text: Otherwise —

children.text: ti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: rū
children.translated_text: Of form- —

children.text:
pidravyacākṣuṣapramāyāmālokasya
kāraṇatvābhāve ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: possessing substance through the eye — the meaning is: if light lacked causality in the valid visual cognition of a form-possessing substance.

Now, let the probans in the form of 'apprehensibility by the eye without the assistance of light' exist — let the probandum in the form of 'difference from form-possessing substance' not [be established]. In response to this purposeless objection, it was stated

children.text:
nanu
rūpidravyaviṣayakacākṣuṣapramāyāmālokasya kāraṇatvaṃ na sambhavati,
ālokaṃ vināpi rūpavatastejodravyasya
children.translated_text: Now, the causality of light in the valid visual cognition of a form-possessing substance is impossible, because of deviation in the negative concomitance — since even without light, valid visual cognition of fire-substance, which possesses form, arises.

children.text:
cākṣuṣapramāyāḥ utpattyā
vyatirekavyabhiñcārāt/ na ca tejobhinnaṃ yat rūpidravyaṃ
tadviṣayakacākṣuṣapramāyāmevālokasya kāraṇatvam, ato na
vyatirekavyabhicāra iti vācyam/ tejobhinnatvavat
tamobhinnatvamityapi viśeṣaṇaṃ dattvā tamobhinnaṃ tejobhinnaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that light has causality only in the valid visual cognition of a form-possessing substance that is different from fire, and hence there is no deviation in the negative concomitance — for by adding the qualification 'different from darkness' just as 'different from fire' [was added], since one could accept that light is a cause only in the valid visual cognition of a substance that is different from both fire and darkness,

children.text:
dravyaṃ
tadviṣayakacākṣuṣapramāyāmeva ālokaḥ kāraṇamiti svīkāreṇa ālokaṃ
vināpi tamasaścākṣuṣatvasambhavāt/ tathā ca
ālokāsahakṛtacakṣurgrāṃhyatve 'pi kṣatyabhāvāt tamaso 'tiriktadravyatvaṃ
niṣpratyūhamevetyata āha-digiti/ sarvāṃnūbhūyamānoṣṇasparśāśrayatayā
tejodravyasyāvaśyaṃ svīkāryatayā tatpratyakṣanirvāhāya
kāryatāvacchedakakoṭau tejobhinnatvaniveśe 'pi
tamaso 'bhāvarūpatve 'pi kṣatyabhāvāt tadbhinnatvaniveśo 'nucitaḥ/
tathā ca
children.translated_text: the visual apprehensibility of darkness even without light would be possible. And accordingly, even with apprehensibility by the eye without the assistance of light, since there would be no harm, the extra-categorical substance-hood of darkness would be unimpeded. To this he says — 'in [all] directions.' Since fire-substance must necessarily be accepted as the substratum of hot touch that is universally experienced, and since for establishing the perception of that [fire], even when the qualification 'different from fire' is included in the delimitor of the effect-hood, even if darkness has the nature of absence, there is no harm — the inclusion of 'different from darkness' is unjustified. And accordingly,

children.text:
tamaso dravyatve
ālokāsahakṛtacakṣurgrāhyatvānupapattyā tamo na rūpidravyamiti
suṣṭhūktamiti bhāvaḥ//
children.translated_text: if darkness were a substance, the impossibility of its apprehensibility by the eye without the assistance of light [would follow]; therefore the statement 'darkness is not a form-possessing substance' is well-stated — this is the purport.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: dravyalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: The definition of substance (<s>dravya</s>)

children.text: dravyatvajātimattvaṃ guṇavattvaṃ vā dravyasāmānyalakṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: Possessing the universal <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood), or possessing qualities (<s>guṇavattva</s>), is the general definition of substance (<s>dravya</s>).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
muktisādhanībhūtapadārthatattvajñānaṃ lakṣaṇajñānaṃ vinā nopapadyata
ityata āha -
dravyatve
children.translated_text: '<s>Dravyatva</s>' (substance-hood) —

children.text:
ti/ saṃyogajanakatāvacchedakatayā
dravyatvajātisiddhiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. The purport is: the universal <s>dravyatva</s> is established through its being the delimiting property of the capacity to produce conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>).
Since knowledge of the true nature of the categories, which is the means to liberation (<s>mukti</s>), is not possible without knowledge of their definitions, he says —

children.text:
nanu
lakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchedakayorabheda ityata āha -
guṇavattvam
children.translated_text: 'Possessing qualities (<s>guṇavattva</s>)' —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: dravyasāmānyalakṣaṇami
children.translated_text: 'is the general definition of substance' —

children.text:
ti/ evaṃ ca sāmānyadharmākathanena na
nyūnateti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. And accordingly, the purport is that there is no deficiency in not stating the common properties.
Now, since the definition and the delimiting property of the definiendum are identical — anticipating this [objection], he says —

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
mūle
dravyatvajātimattvaṃ dravyasya lakṣaṇamuktam/ tatra dravyatvajātau kiṃ
mānamityāśaṅkyāha -
saṃyogajanakatāvacchedakataye
children.translated_text: 'Through being the delimiting property of the capacity to produce conjunction' —

children.text:
ti/ anena dravyatvajātau anumānaṃ pramāṇamuktaṃ bhavati/ tathā hi
- dravyayoreva saṃyoga iti saṃyogaṃ prati dravyaṃ samavāyikāraṇam/
samavāyasambandhena saṃyogaṃ prati tādātmyasambandhena dravyaṃ kāraṇam/
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnasaṃyoganiṣṭhakāryatānirupitatādātmyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatā
dravye vartate/ tāṃ kāraṇatāṃ pakṣīkṛtya tatra kiñciddharmāvacchinnatvaṃ
kāraṇatātvena hetunā sādhanīyam/
children.translated_text: thus. By this, inference is stated as the means of valid knowledge for the universal <s>dravyatva</s>. For indeed — since conjunction is only between two substances, substance is the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) of conjunction. Through the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), substance is a cause of conjunction; through the relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), substance is a cause. The causality delimited by the identity relation, which determines the effect-hood residing in conjunction and delimited by the inherence relation, resides in substance. Taking that causality as the subject and establishing through the reason 'because it is causality' that it is delimited by some property —

In the root text, possessing the universal <s>dravyatva</s> was stated as the definition of substance. Therein, anticipating the question 'what is the means of valid knowledge for the universal <s>dravyatva</s>?', he says —

children.text:
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnasaṃyoganiṣṭhakāryatānirūpitādātmyasambandhāvacchinnadravyaniṣṭhakāraṇatā
kiñciddharmāvacchinnā kāraṇatātvāt, yā yā kāraṇatā sā sā kāraṇatā
kiñciddharmāvacchinnā yathā ghaṭaniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitadaṇḍaniṣṭhakāraṇatā
daṇḍatvāvacchinnā tadvat ityanumānena dravyaniṣṭhoktakāraṇatāyāṃ
dravyatvarūpakiñciddharmāṃvacchinnatvasiddhau sidhyato dharmasya jātitve
lāghavamiti lāghavajñānasahakāreṇa dravyatvākhyajātisiddhiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: the causality residing in substance, delimited by the identity relation, which determines the effect-hood residing in conjunction delimited by the inherence relation, is delimited by some property, because it is causality. Whatever is causality is delimited by some property — just as the causality residing in the stick, which determines the effect-hood residing in the pot, is delimited by stick-hood. Similarly, through this inference, when the delimitation of the said causality residing in substance by some property in the form of <s>dravyatva</s> is established, the purport is that the universal-hood of the established property follows from the principle of parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>); thus, assisted by the knowledge of parsimony, the universal called <s>dravyatva</s> is established.

children.text:
dravyasya guṇavattvaṃ
lakṣaṇāntaramuktaṃ mūle/ tatkathate bījamāha -
lakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchedakayorabhe
children.translated_text: 'Of the definition and the delimiting property of the definiendum, the identity' —

children.text:
da iti/ dravyasya dravyatvaṃ lakṣaṇamitmukte lakṣyaṃ dravyam
lakṣyatāvacchedakaṃ dravyatvam, lakṣaṇamapi dravyatvameveti
lakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchedakayorabhedaḥ syāt/ nanvastu nāma tayorabhedaḥ,
tāvatā ko doṣa iti cet - śrūyatām/ lakṣaṇasya hi lakṣye
itarabhedānumitiḥ prayojanam/ lakṣaṇaṃ
lakṣyoddeśyaketarabhedavidheyakānumitijanakamiti yāvat/ yathā goḥ
sāsnāvattvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cet 'gauḥ svetarabhinnā, sāsnāvattvāt'
ityanumānena goḥ itarabhinnatvaṃ sidhyati/ tathā prakṛte 'pi
dravyasya yadi dravyatvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tadā 'dravyam itarabhinnam, dravyatvāt'
ityanumānaṃ prayoktavyam/ tatra 'dravyam itarabhinnam'
children.translated_text: thus. If the definition of substance is said to be <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood), the definiendum is substance, the delimiting property of the definiendum is <s>dravyatva</s>, and the definition is also <s>dravyatva</s> itself — thus there would be identity of the definition and the delimiting property of the definiendum. Now, even if there is identity between them, what defect does that cause? — if asked, listen. The purpose of a definition is to generate an inference of the difference of the definiendum from other things. That is, the definition is such that it generates an inference whose subject is the definiendum and whose predicate is difference from others. For example, if 'possessing a dewlap' (<s>sāsnāvattva</s>) is the definition of a cow, then through the inference 'a cow is different from other things, because of possessing a dewlap,' the difference of a cow from others is established. Similarly in the present case, if <s>dravyatva</s> is the definition of substance, then the inference 'substance is different from others, because of <s>dravyatva</s>' must be employed. There, 'substance is different from others'
In the root text, possessing qualities (<s>guṇavattva</s>) was stated as an alternative definition of substance. He states the seed [reason] for that —

children.text:
ityanumitiḥ/
tāṃ prati itarabhedavyāpyadravyatvavat dravyamiti parāmarśaṃḥ kāraṇam/
vyāptiśca hetuvyāpakasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyarūpā/ tathā ca
dravyatvavyāpaketarabhedasamānādhikaraṇadravyatvavat dravyamiti
parāmarśasya ākāraḥ sampannaḥ/ tatra dravyatve
itarabhedasāmānādhikaraṇye bhāsamāne tulyavittivedyatayā
itarabhede dravyatvasāmānādhikaraṇyamapi bhāsate/ tulyavittivedyatā
nāma ekajñānaviṣayatvam/ anumittau ca pakṣavṛttitvātmakaṃ
pakṣatāvacchedakasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ sādhye bhāsate/ evaṃ ca
anumitiviṣayasya itarabhededravyavṛttitvasya parāmarśena
viṣayīkṛtatayā parāmarśasiddhasyaiva viṣayasya anumityā sādhanāt
siddhasādhanākhyo doṣaḥ prasajati/ anumiteḥ pūrvaṃ pakṣe
sādhyaniścayasattve siddhasādhanadoṣaḥ bhavati/ ato dravyasya yadi
dravyatvajātimattvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tadā siddhasādhanākhyadoṣaḥ prasajatīti
paryālocya lakṣaṇāntarānudhāvanaṃ kṛtamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: is the conclusion to be inferred. The inferential cognition (<s>parāmarśa</s>) that serves as its cause is: 'substance possesses <s>dravyatva</s> which pervades difference from others.' The pervasion has the form of co-location of the <s>sādhya</s> with the pervader of the reason. And accordingly, the form of the inferential cognition is established as: 'substance possesses <s>dravyatva</s> co-located with difference from others, which pervades <s>dravyatva</s>.' There, when the co-location of difference-from-others with <s>dravyatva</s> is cognized, since they are cognized as objects of a single cognition, the co-location of <s>dravyatva</s> with difference-from-others also shines forth. Co-location means being the object of one cognition. And in the inference, the co-location of the <s>sādhya</s> with the delimiting property of the subject-hood — in the form of residing in the subject — shines forth. And thus, since the content of the inferential cognition — the residing of difference-from-others in substance — being already cognized through the inferential cognition, is the very content already established in the inferential cognition, the defect called <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already proven) arises. The defect of <s>siddhasādhana</s> occurs when there is certainty of the <s>sādhya</s> in the subject prior to the inference. Therefore, reflecting that if possessing <s>dravyatva</s> is the definition of substance, the defect of <s>siddhasādhana</s> would arise, the pursuit of an alternative definition was undertaken — this is the purport.

Since without knowledge of general properties, the desire to know specific properties does not arise, and hence division would be inappropriate — to remove this doubt, he says that the general definition of substance was stated in the root text —

children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: avyāptyādilakṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>avyāpti</s> (under-pervasion) and the like.

children.text:
1lakṣaṇasya trīṇi
dūṣaṇāni/ lakṣyaikadeśāvṛttitvamavyāptiḥ/ yathā goḥ kapilatvam/
alakṣye lakṣaṇasya vartanamativyāptiḥ/ yathā goḥ śṛṅgitvam/
lakṣyamātrāvṛttitvamasambhavaḥ/ yathā gorekaśaphavattvam/
children.translated_text: A definition has three defects. Non-pervasion of a part of the definiendum is <s>avyāpti</s> (under-pervasion) — for example, tawny color (<s>kapilatva</s>) [as a definition] of a cow. The presence of the definition in a non-definiendum is <s>ativyāpti</s> (over-pervasion) — for example, having horns (<s>śṛṅgitva</s>) [as a definition] of a cow. Non-presence in any definiendum at all is <s>asambhava</s> (impossibility) — for example, having a single hoof (<s>ekaśaphavatva</s>) [as a definition] of a cow.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:

children.translated_text: thus. The meaning is: non-pervasion of some definiendum through the relation intended as the delimiting relation of definition-hood.

iti/ na cātra
alakṣyavṛttitvarūpātivyāpterapi sattvāt saṅkara iti vācyam/

children.translated_text: thus. And here, it should not be objected that there is confusion (<s>saṅkara</s>) because the defect of over-pervasion — in the form of residing in a non-definiendum — is also present; because of the maxim 'even in a defective confusion, there is no confusion of defects.'

Since only a property free from the three defects is to be stated [below] as having the status of a definition, the knowledge of that is not possible without knowledge of its being free from the three defects as a qualifier. And the knowledge of being free from the three defects depends on the specific knowledge of the three defects [themselves]. Since in the cognition of an absence, the knowledge of the counter-positive qualified by its delimiting property is necessary — with this intent, he presents the three defects —

To satisfy that, the definition of a definition must be stated. Prior to that, the statement of <s>avyāpti</s> and the like would be disconnected — anticipating this [objection], he says —

And accordingly, the final import is that the definition of a definition is: being a property qualified by the absence of three defects. Therein, since in a qualified cognition, the knowledge of the qualifier is a cause, the knowledge of the qualifier in the form of the absence of three defects is a cause. And such knowledge of the qualifier is not possible without the knowledge of the three defects, because in the cognition of absence, the knowledge of the counter-positive is a cause. Therefore the three defects

asambhavatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāva - etattrayaviśiṣṭo dharmo
children.translated_text: thus. Here the intent is as follows — being free from three defects does not mean the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by 'being one of the three defects.' For if it were so, in a property like tawny color (<s>kapilatva</s>) etc., which has one of the defects such as <s>avyāpti</s> and the like, by the maxim 'even when one [of the three] exists, the three do not exist,' since the absence of the three [as a group] would obtain, the property <s>kapilatva</s> etc. possessing that [absence] would undesirably become a definition. Rather, it must be said that being free from three defects means: taking the defects — <s>avyāpti</s>, <s>ativyāpti</s>, and <s>asambhava</s> — specifically qualified by <s>avyāptitva</s> (under-pervasion-hood) and the like, the three absences whose counter-positive-hoods are delimited by these [respectively] constitute being free from three defects. And accordingly, the final import is: a property qualified by (1) the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by <s>avyāptitva</s>, (2) the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by <s>ativyāptitva</s>, and (3) the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by <s>asambhavatva</s>

When tawny color (<s>kapilatva</s>) is said to be the definition of a cow, the definiendum

tṛtīyārthaḥ/ tathā ca lakṣyatāvacchedakādhikaraṇanirūpita

And accordingly, the definition of <s>avyāpti</s> — the nature of <s>avyāpti</s> — is: the absence of the property of residing, delimited by the relation intended as the delimiting relation of definition-hood, as determined by a locus of the delimiting property of the definiendum. Tawny color exists in a tawny cow through inherence (<s>samavāya</s>); so inherence is the relation intended as the delimiting relation of definition-hood.

is a cow, the delimiting property of the definiendum is cow-hood (<s>gotva</s>); a locus of cow-hood is, for example, a white cow; the absence of the property of residing as determined by that [white cow] is present in tawny color — thus the definition of <s>avyāpti</s> applies to the defective property. Now, since tawny color is present in a white cow through a temporal relation (<s>kālikasambandha</s>), the absence of the property of residing as determined by a locus of the delimiting property of the definiendum does not exist [in tawny color] — and thus the definition of <s>avyāpti</s> would be inapplicable to a defective property — anticipating this doubt, he says —

sambandhena lakṣye vartate sa sambandhaḥ lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] The relation through which the definition resides in the definiendum — that relation is the delimiting relation of definition-hood.

kapilatve sattve 'pi tannirūpitasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnavṛttitvābhāvāt
kapilatve lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ lakṣyatāvacchedakādhikaraṇatvaṃ ca
lakṣyatāvacchedakaniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitādhiṅkaraṇatvam, tatrādheyatāyāṃ
1lakṣyatāvacchedakatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśanīyam/ anyathā
sallakṣaṇe sāsnāvattvādau kālikasambandhena
lakṣyatāvacchedakagotvādhikaraṇaṃ yat mahiṣādi tadvṛttitvābhāvasattvena
avyāptalakṣaṇasyātivyāpteḥ/ evaṃ lakṣyatāvacchedakasamānādhikaraṇatve
satītyapi avyāptalakṣaṇe viśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ anyathā asambhavagraste
ekaśaphavattvādau avyāptalakṣaṇasyātivyāpteḥ/,
gotvādhikaraṇanirūpitavṛttitvābhāvasya tatrāpi sattvāt/ tasmin
viśeṣaṇe datte tu ekaśaphavattvādau nātivyāptiḥ, tasya
gotvādhikaraṇavṛttitvābhāvāt/
children.translated_text: Even though the property of residing, delimited by the temporal relation and determined by a white cow that is a locus of cow-hood, is present in tawny color, since the absence of the property of residing delimited by the inherence relation and determined by that [white cow] exists in tawny color, the definition of <s>avyāpti</s> applies. And the 'locus of the delimiting property of the definiendum' means: being a locus of the superstratum-hood determined by the delimiting property of the definiendum; therein, the superstratum-hood must be qualified by being delimited by the relation that delimits the delimiting property of the definiendum. Otherwise, in a valid definition like 'possessing a dewlap' (<s>sāsnāvattva</s>) and the like, since a buffalo etc. would be a locus of the delimiting property cow-hood through the temporal relation, the absence of residing therein being present would cause over-pervasion of the definition of <s>avyāpti</s>. Similarly, 'while being co-located with the delimiting property of the definiendum' should also be given as a qualifier in the definition of <s>avyāpti</s>. Otherwise, in a [property] swallowed by <s>asambhava</s> (impossibility), such as having a single hoof (<s>ekaśaphavatva</s>) and the like, there would be over-pervasion of the definition of <s>avyāpti</s> — because the absence of the property of residing determined by a locus of cow-hood is present there too. But when that qualifier is given, there is no over-pervasion in having a single hoof and the like, because it lacks the property of residing in a locus of cow-hood.
