children.translated_text: And co-location with the delimitor of the definiendum-hood (<s>lakṣyatāvacchedakasamānādhikaraṇatva</s>) is: possessing residence determined by the substratum-hood that determines the superstratum-hood residing in the delimitor of definiendum-hood. There, in the superstratum-hood residing in the delimitor of definiendum-hood, the delimitation by the relation that delimits the delimitor-hood of definiendum-hood must be included. Otherwise, since the delimitor of definiendum-hood, namely cow-hood, resides in a horse through temporal relation, and since the property of having a single hoof is present there, there would be over-extension of the definition of under-extended to something afflicted with impossibility. But when that [qualification] is included, the substratum of cow-hood through the relation of inherence is only a cow; since the property of having a single hoof does not have residence determined by such [a cow], there is no over-extension. Similarly, in the property of residence [of the definition], the delimitation by the relation that delimits the definition-hood must be included. Otherwise, since the property of having a single hoof resides in a cow through temporal relation, the aforementioned defect would arise. And thus,

children.text:
dakasambandhāvacchinnavṛttitve sati
lakṣyatāvacchedakatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnalakṣyatāvacchedakaniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitā-
children.translated_text: the definition of under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) in its resultant form is: the absence of residence delimited by the relation that delimits the definition-hood, determined by the substratum-hood that determines the superstratum-hood residing in the delimitor of definiendum-hood delimited by the relation that delimits the delimitor-hood of definiendum-hood, when there is

children.text:
dhikaraṇatāvanniyapitalakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnavṛttitvābhāvaḥ
avyāptasya lakṣaṇamiti phalitam/ adhikaṃ
children.translated_text: residence delimited by the relation that delimits the definition-hood, determined by the substratum-hood that determines the superstratum-hood residing in the delimitor of definiendum-hood delimited by the relation that delimits the delimitor-hood of definiendum-hood — this is the resultant definition of under-extension. More

children.text: paṭṭābhirāmaṭippaṇyā
children.translated_text: [is to be seen] in the <s>Paṭṭābhirāma</s> commentary

children.text: dau draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: and other works.

children.text:
1.
lakṣyatāvacchedakadharmaḥ yena sambandhena lakṣye vartate sa sambandhaḥ
lakṣyatāvacchedakatāvacchedakasambandhaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] The relation through which the property that delimits definiendum-hood resides in the definiendum — that relation is the relation that delimits the delimitor-hood of definiendum-hood.

children.text:
dīpikāyām - alakṣye lakṣaṇasya
vartanamativyāptir
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'The occurrence of the definition in what is not the definiendum is over-extension' —

children.text:
iti/
alakṣyamityasya lakṣyaniṣṭhapratiyogitākabhedavadityarthaḥ/ saptamyāḥ
nirūpitatatvamarthaḥ/ tasya vartanaśabdārthe ādheyatve 'nvayaḥ/
lakṣyaniṣṭhapratiyogitākabhedavannirūpitavṛttitvamativyāptirityuktaṃ
bhavatiṃ/ yathā goḥ śṛṅgitvaṃ lakṣaṇamuktaṃ cet idaṃ
lakṣaṇamativyāptiduṣṭaṃ bhavati, lakṣyā gauḥ
tanniṣṭhapratiyogitānirūpakabhedavati mahiṣādau śṛṅgitvasya
vartanāt/ atra lakṣyaniṣṭhapratiyogitāyāṃ lakṣyatāvacchedakāvacchinnatvaṃ
niveśanīyam/ anyathā goniṣṭhapratiyogitākabheda ityanena
śvetagobhedasyāpi grahītuṃ śakyatayā tadvati kapilagavi kapilatvasya
vartamānatayā avyāptadharme ativyāptalakṣaṇasyātivyāpteḥ/ tanniveśe tu
lakṣyā gauḥ, lakṣyatāvacchedakaṃ gotvaṃ,
tadavacchinnagoniṣṭhapratiyogitākabhedaḥ 'gaurna' iti pratītisiddhaḥ
gosāmānyabhedaḥ tadvān kapilagaurna bhavati, kiṃ tu mahiṣādikameva
tadvṛttitvaṃ kapilatve nāstīti nātivyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: thus. The meaning of 'in what is not the definiendum' is: in what possesses a difference whose counter-positive-hood resides in the definiendum. The meaning of the seventh case-ending is 'as determined by.' Its syntactic connection is with the sense of 'residence' (<s>ādheyatā</s>) conveyed by the word 'occurrence.' Thus what is stated is: over-extension is the property of residing as determined by what possesses a difference whose counter-positive-hood resides in the definiendum. For example, if 'possessing horns' (<s>śṛṅgitva</s>) is stated as the definition of a cow, this definition is vitiated by over-extension, because the property of possessing horns occurs in a buffalo and the like, which possess a difference whose counter-positive-hood resides in the definiendum, namely a cow. Here, in the counter-positive-hood residing in the definiendum, the delimitation by the delimitor of definiendum-hood must be included. Otherwise, since a difference whose counter-positive-hood resides in a cow would also include the difference from a white cow, in what possesses that — namely a tawny cow — since tawny-color is present, there would be over-extension of the definition that is over-extended to a property afflicted with under-extension. But when that [qualification] is included, the definiendum is a cow, the delimitor of definiendum-hood is cow-hood, and the difference whose counter-positive-hood delimited by cow-hood resides in a cow — this is the universal difference from cow, established by the cognition 'it is not a cow' — a tawny cow does not possess that, but only a buffalo and the like does. The property of residing in such [a buffalo] is absent in tawny-color — hence there is no over-extension.

children.text:
evaṃ vṛttitāyāṃ
lakṣṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśanīyam/ anyathā gobhinne
mahiṣādāvapi kālikasambandhena kapilatvasya vartamānatayā
pūrvoktadoṣāpatteḥ/ tanniveśe tu lakṣaṇaṃ yena sambandhena lakṣye
vartate se eva sambandhaḥ lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandha iti prakṛte
samavāyasyaiva tādṛśatayā
mahiśādinirūpitasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnavṛttitvasya
kapilatve 'bhāvāt na tatrātivyāptiḥ/ evamapi asambhavagraste
ekaśaphavattvādau lakṣyagobhinnāśvavṛttitvasattvāt
ativyāptalakṣṇasyātivyāptiriti tadvāraṇāya
lakṣyatāvacchedakasamānādhikaraṇatve satīti viśeṣaṇamatrāpi deyam/
ekaśaphavattvasya lakṣyatāvacchedakagotvādhikaraṇavṛttitvābhāvānna doṣaḥ/
tathā ca
lakṣyatāvacchedakatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnalakṣyatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnalakṣyatāvacchedakaniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitā-
dhikaraṇatāvannirūpitalakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnavṛttitve sati
lakṣyatāvacchedakāvacchinnalakṣyaniṣṭhapratiyogitānirūpakabhedavannirūpitalakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnavṛttitvam
ativyāptasya
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the property of residence, the delimitation by the relation that delimits the definition-hood must be included. Otherwise, since tawny-color is present even in a buffalo and the like, which are different from a cow, through temporal relation, the aforementioned defect would arise. But when that [qualification] is included, since the relation through which the definition resides in the definiendum — that very relation is the relation delimiting definition-hood — in the present case, only inherence has that status; since the property of residence through the relation of inherence as determined by a buffalo and the like is absent in tawny-color, there is no over-extension there. Even so, in the case of the property of having a single hoof and the like, which are afflicted with impossibility, since the property of residing in a horse — which is different from the definiendum cow — is present, there would be over-extension of the definition of over-extension. To prevent that, the qualification 'when there is co-location with the delimitor of definiendum-hood' must be given here as well. Since the property of having a single hoof does not reside in a substratum of cow-hood (the delimitor of definiendum-hood), there is no defect. And thus the resultant definition of over-extension is: the property of residing, delimited by the relation delimiting definition-hood, as determined by what possesses a difference whose counter-positive-hood, delimited by the delimitor of definiendum-hood, resides in the definiendum — determined by the substratum-hood that determines the superstratum-hood residing in the delimitor of definiendum-hood delimited by the relation that delimits the delimitor-hood of definiendum-hood — when there is co-location with the delimitor of definiendum-hood.

children.text: lakṣaṇamiti phalitam/
children.translated_text: This is the resultant definition.

children.text: lakṣyamātrāvṛttitvamasambhava
children.translated_text: 'Non-occurrence in any definiendum whatsoever is impossibility' —

children.text:
iti/ sarvatra lakṣye avartanamasambhavaḥ/
kvacillakṣye avartanamavyāptadharme 'pyastīti sarvatretyuktam/ goḥ
ekaśaphavattvam lakṣaṇamuktaṃ cet tatsarvāsu govyaktiṣu nāstīti
asambhavadoṣadūṣitaṃ bhavati/
lakṣyanirūpitavṛttitvatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvo 'tra vivakṣitaḥ, na
tu lakṣyavṛttitvapratiyogiko 'bhāvaḥ/ kapilatvādyavyāpyadharme 'pi
yatkiñcillakṣyaśvetagovṛttitvābhāvasya lakṣyavṛttitvapratiyogikasya
sattvenātivyāptyāpatteḥ/ tadvivakṣaṇe tu govṛttitvaṃ nāstīti
pratītisiddhasya govṛttitvasāmānyābhāvasyaiva
lakṣyanirūpitavṛttitvatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākatayā tasya kapilatve
kapilagovṛttau virahāt nātivyāptiriti sūcanāya kṛtsnārthakaṃ
mātrapadam/ evaṃ lakṣyanirūpitavṛttitve
lakṣṇatāvacchedakasambanghāvacchinnatvamapi niveśanīyam/ anyathā
ekaśaphavattvāderapi kālikasambandhena govṛttitvena
tadvṛttitvābhāvavirahāt asambhavalakṣaṇe asambhavadoṣaḥ syāditi/ tathā
ca
lakṣyanirūpitalakṣṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnavṛttitvatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ
asambhava iti phalitam/ sarvamidamabhisandhāyāha
children.translated_text: thus. Impossibility is non-occurrence in all definienda. Since non-occurrence in some definiendum is present even in a property afflicted with under-extension, the word 'all' is used. If 'possessing a single hoof' is stated as the definition of a cow, it is not present in any individual cow — hence it is vitiated by the defect of impossibility. The absence intended here is one whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the property of residing as determined by the definiendum, and not an absence whose counter-positive is the property of residing in the definiendum. Because in a property afflicted with under-extension, such as tawny-color, since the absence of the property of residing in some definiendum — namely a white cow — is present as an absence whose counter-positive is the property of residing in the definiendum, over-extension would result. But when the intended [reading] is adopted, the absence of cow-residence in the universal sense — established by the cognition 'it does not reside in a cow' — whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the property of residence-in-cow in the universal sense, since that [universal absence] is absent in tawny-color due to tawny-color's residing in tawny cows, there is no over-extension. This is indicated by the word <s>mātra</s> (only/all) having the sense of entirety. Similarly, in the property of residing as determined by the definiendum, the delimitation by the relation delimiting the definition-hood must also be included. Otherwise, since even the property of having a single hoof and the like resides in a cow through temporal relation, the defect of impossibility would arise for the definition of impossibility — since the absence of such residence would be absent. And thus the resultant definition of impossibility is: the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the property of residing, delimited by the relation delimiting definition-hood, as determined by the definiendum. Having intended all this, he says —

children.text:
prakāśikāyām mātrapadaṃ
kṛtsnārthakam
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'The word <s>mātra</s> has the sense of entirety' —

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: sambandhaviśeṣa
children.translated_text: 'A specific relation' —

children.text: ti/ lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the relation delimiting the definition-hood.

children.text: lakṣyavṛttitvasāmānyābhāve
children.translated_text: 'The absence of the universal property of residing in the definiendum' —

children.text:
ti/
lakṣyavṛttitvatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the property of residing-in-the-definiendum in the universal sense.

children.text:
nanu asambhavagraste
ekaśaphavattve alakṣyāśvṛttitvasattvena ativyāptyākhyadoṣasyāpi sattvāt
ekatra anekadoṣasāṅkaryaṃ prasajatīti śaṅkate -
na cātretyādi
children.translated_text: 'Nor here' and so forth —

children.text:
nā/ śaṅkeyaṃ
yathāśrutātivyāptilakṣaṇābhiprāyeṇa/
lakṣyatāvacchedakasamānādhikaraṇatve satīti viśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭasya
pūrvoktapariṣkṛtātivyāptisvarūpasya ekaśaphavattve virahāt/
doṣabhedāt/ duṣṭasyāpi bhedena bhavitavyamiti śaṅkiturbhāvaḥ/
samādhatte -
children.translated_text: [resolves the doubt.] The doubt is not [valid] — because it is intended according to the definition of over-extension as literally understood. Since the refined definition of over-extension stated above, which includes the qualification 'when there is co-location with the delimitor of definiendum-hood,' is absent in the property of having a single hoof, [there is no over-extension there.] The doubter's intent is: since [the defects] are different as defects, even what is defective should be distinguished accordingly.

children.text: duṣṭasaṅkare 'pī
children.translated_text: 'Even in the conflation of the defective' —

children.text:
ti/ duṣṭasyaikatve 'pi doṣasya ekatvaṃ
netyarthaḥ/ ekasmin anekadoṣāṇāṃ samāveśasambhavena doṣabhedāt
children.translated_text: The meaning is: even when the defective entity is one, the defect need not be one. Since it is possible for multiple defects to coexist in a single entity, the difference among defects

Now, in the property of having a single hoof, which is afflicted with impossibility, since the property of residing in a horse — which is not a definiendum — is also present, and thus the defect called over-extension is also present, the objection that there would be a conflation of multiple defects in a single case is raised —

children.text:
tadāśrayaduṣṭabhedāpattirneti samādhāturāśayaḥ/
'upadheyasaṅkare 'pyupādherasaṅkaraḥ' iti
maṇikāravacanasyāpyayamevārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: does not entail a difference in the defective entity that is their locus — this is the intent of the resolution. The statement of the <s>Maṇikāra</s> — 'Even when there is conflation of the qualified entities, there is no conflation of the qualifying conditions' — has this very meaning.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: lakṣaṇalakṣaṇavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Investigation of the definition of a definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>)

children.text:
etaddūṣaṇatrayarahitadharmo lakṣaṇam/ yathā goḥ sāsnādimattvam/
sa evāsādhāraṇadharma ityucyate/
lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvamasādhāraṇatvam/ vyāvartakasyaiva lakṣaṇatve
vyāvṛttāvabhidheyatvādau cātivyāptiḥ ataḥ tadvāraṇāya tadbhinnatvaṃ
dharmaviśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ vyavahārasyāpi lakṣaṇaprayojanatve tu tat na
deyam/ vyāvṛtterapi vyavahārasādhanatvāt/
children.translated_text: A property free from these three defects is a definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). For example, cow-hood's possession of a dewlap and the like (<s>sāsnādimatva</s>). That alone is called an uncommon property (<s>asādhāraṇadharma</s>). Being co-extensive with the delimitor of definiendum-hood is uncommonness (<s>asādhāraṇatva</s>). If only the property of being differentiating were the definition of a definition, there would be over-extension to differentiation (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), expressibility (<s>abhidheyatva</s>), and the like. Therefore, to prevent that, the qualification 'different from that' must be added to the property [in the definition]. But in the view that practical usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>) is also the purpose of a definition, that [qualification] need not be added — because differentiation too serves practical usage.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text: etaddūṣaṇatrayarahita
children.translated_text: 'Free from these three defects' —

children.text:
iti/ uktadūṣaṇābhāvatrayaviśiṣṭa
ityarthaḥ/ nanvasādhāraṇadharmo lakṣaṇamiti hi siddhāntaḥ/ tasmāt
kāraṇāt kathaṃ dūṣaṇatrayarahito dharmo lakṣaṇamityata āha -
children.translated_text: The meaning is: qualified by the three absences of the stated defects. Now, the established doctrine is that an uncommon property is a definition. For that reason, how can a property free from the three defects be a definition? — to this he says —

children.text: sa eve
children.translated_text: 'That alone' —

children.text: ti/
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: ityucyata
children.translated_text: 'is called' —

children.text:
iti/ abhiyuktairiti śeṣaḥ/ nanu
sādhāraṇyasya lakṣyālakṣyavṛttitvarūpatayā
tadabhāvarūpāsādhāraṇyasyāvyāptyādidoṣagrastadharme 'pi sattvāt kathaṃ
doṣatrayarahita evāsādhāraṇadharma ityāśaṅkāṃ parijihīrṣuḥ
asādhāraṇatvamanyādṛśaṃ nirvakti -
children.translated_text: The remainder is: 'by the learned.' Now, since commonness (<s>sādhāraṇya</s>) has the nature of occurring in both the definiendum and what is not the definiendum, and since uncommonness — the absence of that — is present even in a property afflicted with under-extension and the like, how can it be that only a property free from the three defects is an uncommon property? — wishing to resolve this doubt, he explains uncommonness in a different way —

children.text: lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvam
children.translated_text: 'Being co-extensive with the delimitor of definiendum-hood' —

children.text:
iti/ lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatve sati
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvamityarthaḥ/ avyāptyasambhavagrastayorvāraṇāya
satyantam/ ativyāptasya vāraṇāya viśeṣyam/ dharmapadaṃ
lakṣaṇatāghaṭakasambandhena vyāpakatvāditātparyagrāhakamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: being pervaded by the delimitor of definiendum-hood while also pervading the delimitor of definiendum-hood. The word <s>sati</s> ('when there is') is for preventing [the inclusion of properties afflicted with] under-extension and impossibility. The qualifying term is for preventing [the inclusion of properties afflicted with] over-extension. The word 'property' (<s>dharma</s>) indicates that the pervader-hood and the rest are through the relation that constitutes the definition-hood — this is the purport.

children.text:
atredaṃ bodhyam -
etaddoṣā asādhāraṇatvasya vighaṭakāḥ/ ativyāptau
vyāpyatvasyetarayośca vyāpakatvasya bhaṅgāt/ eteṣāṃ dūṣakatābījaṃ
lakṣaṇena lakṣaṇena itarabhedasādhane 'tivyāptau vyabhicāraḥ,
itarayośca bhāgāsiddhisvarūpāsiddhī iti/ nanu
lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvasya lakṣaṇalakṣaṇatve lakṣaṇasya vyāvṛttireva
prayojanamiti mate vyāvartakasyaiva lakṣaṇalakṣaṇalakṣyatayā
vyāvṛttyādāvativyaptirityāśaṅkāṃ tanmatānusāreṇa nirākaroti -
vyāvartakasyaive
children.translated_text: 'Of the differentiator alone' —

children.text:
ti/ itarabhedānumitijanakasyaivetyarthaṃḥ/
itarabhedavidheyakānumitijanaka
tāvacchedakaviṣayatāviśeṣāśrayasyaivetiyāvat/ etena
vyāvahārikavyavacchedaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: of only that which generates the inference of difference from others. That is: of only that which is the locus of the specific object-relation that is the delimitor of the predicate-hood of the inference having the predicate of difference from others. By this, the conventional [usage of differentiation] is excluded.

children.text: lakṣaṇatve
children.translated_text: 'Being a definition' —

children.text: gavādilakṣaṇatve uktalakṣaṇalakṣaṇalakṣyatva iti yāvat/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: being the definiendum of the stated definition-of-a-definition, i.e. being a definition of cow and the like.

children.text: lakṣyatva
children.translated_text: 'Definiendum-hood' —

children.text: iti pāṭhe 'pyayamevārtho bodhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: Even in this reading, the same meaning should be understood.

children.text: vyāvṛttāv
children.translated_text: 'In differentiation' —

children.text:
iti/
gavādītarabhede gotvādirūpalakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvasya
abhidheyatvaprameyatvādau padārthatvasamaniyatatvasya ca
sattvenātivyāptivāraṇāya vyāvṛttibhinnatvamabhidheyatvādibhinnatvaṃ ca
lakṣaṇalakṣaṇe niveśanīyamityarthaḥ/ yadyapi vyāvṛtterapi
vyāvahārikatvasya vakṣyamāṇatayā tenaiva rūpeṇa vyāvahārikatvena
sarveṣāṃ saṅgrahasambhavāt pṛthagabhidhānamanucitam, tathāpi
hetusādhyayoraikye hetumattāniścayakāle sādhyasaṃśayarūpapakṣatāyā
asattvena
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the qualification 'different from differentiation' and 'different from expressibility and the like' must be included in the definition-of-a-definition, because in the difference from others such as non-cows, co-extensiveness with the delimitor of definiendum-hood in the form of cow-hood is present, and in expressibility (<s>abhidheyatva</s>), knowability (<s>prameyatva</s>), and the like, co-extensiveness with <s>padārthatva</s> (category-hood) is present, and therefore [the qualification is needed] to prevent over-extension. Although, since differentiation too has conventionality as will be stated, and since through that very form of conventionality all [such cases] can be included, a separate mention is inappropriate, nevertheless,

Here is something to be understood: these defects are destructors of uncommonness. Because in the case of over-extension, the pervaded-hood [is destroyed], and in the case of the other two, the pervader-hood [is destroyed]. The basis for the vitiating capacity of these is: in establishing the difference from others by means of the definition, over-extension constitutes deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>), while the other two constitute partial unestablishedness (<s>bhāgāsiddhi</s>) and essential unestablishedness (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>) respectively. Now, if co-extensiveness with the delimitor of definiendum-hood is the definition of a definition, then in the view that the purpose of a definition is solely differentiation (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), since differentiation itself — being the differentiator — would be a definiendum of the definition-of-a-definition, there would be over-extension to differentiation, expressibility, and the like — he resolves this doubt according to that view —

children.text:
tānumitiriti
prācīnamate itarabhedasya vyāvartakatvābhāvena tatrātivyāptiḥ/
siṣādhayiṣāvirahaviśiṣṭasiddhyabhāvaḥ pakṣatā iti siddhāntimate
tu vyāvṛtterapi vyāvartakatvena lakṣyatayā tatra
lakṣaṇasaṅgamanasyeṣṭatvena nātivyāptirityāvedayituṃ
pṛthakkathanamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: since in the old view where there is no differentiating capacity of difference from others — because when the reason and the probandum are identical, the doubt-form of the subject-hood (<s>pakṣatā</s>) is absent at the time of ascertaining the reasoned entity — the inference [of difference] does not occur, and hence there is over-extension there [to differentiation]. But in the established view where the subject-hood is the absence of establishment qualified by the absence of the desire to establish, since even differentiation has differentiating capacity and hence definiendum-hood, the co-occurrence of the definition there is desirable and hence there is no over-extension — it should be noted that the separate mention is for conveying this point.

children.text:
nanu kimidaṃ nāma
lakṣaṇalakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchedakaṃ vyāvartakatvam/ na tāvat sāmānyato
bhedānumāpakatvam/ vyāvṛttyabhidheyatvāderapi
yatkiñcidubhayatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedānumāpakatayā
tatrātivyāptikathanāsaṅgateḥ/ sarveṣāmapi vyatirekadharmāṇāṃ
yatkiñcidvyāvartakatayā
asādhāraṇyādighaṭakavyāpakatvādivairthyāpātācca/ nāpi viśiṣya
tattaddharmāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakatvam/ tathā sati
gotvāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakasya sāsnādimattvasya
gotvasamaniyatatvaṃ lakṣaṇam ityevaṃ rītyā viśiṣya tattallakṣaṇasya
vaktavyatayā gotvādirūpalakṣyatāvacchedakatattaddharmasamanaiyatyasya
gotvāvacchinnetarabhedādirūpavyāvṛttau sattvenātivyāpteḥ
sambhave 'pyabhidhayatvādāvativyāptyalagnakatāpatteḥ duvaritvāt
gotvādisamanaiyatyasya tatrāsattvāditi cet -
children.translated_text: Now, what is this differentiating capacity (<s>vyāvartakatva</s>) that is the delimitor of defined-ness (<s>lakṣyatāvacchedaka</s>) in the definition of a definition? It is not, first of all, the capacity to infer difference in general (<s>sāmānyato bhedānumāpakatva</s>). For since <s>vyāvṛttyabhidheyatva</s> (expressibility of exclusion) and the like also have the capacity to infer difference delimited by some-or-other duality, stating over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) there would be incoherent. Moreover, since all properties that differentiate have some-or-other differentiating capacity, properties such as <s>asādhāraṇya</s> (uncommon-ness) and the constituent pervading properties would become purposeless. Nor is it the capacity to specifically infer difference delimited by each particular property from the others. For if that were so, the property of possessing a dewlap and the like (<s>sāsnādimatva</s>), which infers difference delimited by cow-hood (<s>gotva</s>) from others, would be co-extensive with cow-hood and thus a definition [of cow] — and in this manner, each particular definition would need to be stated specifically. [In that case,] the co-extensiveness of each such particular property with the respective delimitor of defined-ness, such as cow-hood, even though it obtains in the differentiation in the form of difference delimited by cow-hood from others, would have over-extension; and even if it obtains, the over-extension with respect to <s>abhidheyatva</s> and the like would be difficult to avoid, since such co-extensiveness does not obtain there, as cow-hood-co-extensiveness does not exist there. If this is objected —

children.text:
maivam - yataḥ
sāsnādimattvaṃ pakṣīkṛtya gotvāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakatve sādhye
viśeṣavyāptau anvayadṛṣṭāntālābhena yadyaddharmasamaniyataṃ
tattandavacchinnavyāvartakamiti rītyā sāmānyamukhena
vyāpterabhyupagantavyatayā tatra
siddhasādhanāprasiddhibhyāmavyāvartaṅkayorvyāvṛttyabhidheyatvayoḥ
tattaddharmasamanaiyatyarūpaprakṛtahetostattulyasya vā hetoḥ sattvena
prakṛtasādhyasya tattulyasya vā sādhyasyāsattvena vyabhicāraḥ syāt/
atastaddoṣavāraṇāya
children.translated_text: Not so — because when <s>sāsnādimatva</s> (possessing a dewlap etc.) is taken as the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) and the capacity to infer difference delimited by cow-hood from others is the property to be proved, since a corroborating example (<s>anvayadṛṣṭānta</s>) cannot be found in the specific pervasion, the pervasion must be accepted through a general route, in the manner 'whatever is co-extensive with a given property, that is a differentiator delimited by that property.' And in that [general formulation], with respect to <s>vyāvṛttyabhidheyatva</s> (expressibility of exclusion) and the like, which are non-differentiators, since the reason in question — namely co-extensiveness with each respective property — or a reason equivalent to it, is present, while the property to be proved in question or one equivalent to it is absent, there would be deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). Therefore, to prevent that defect,

children.text:
tattaddharmāvacchinnetarabhedarūpavyāvṛttibhinnatvamabhidheyatvādibhinnatvaṃ
ca tādṛśalakṣaṇe niveśanīyamityabhiprāyako 'yaṃ grantha iti na
pūrvoktadoṣāvasaraḥ/ adhikavicārastu anyatrānusandheyaḥ/
children.translated_text: the conditions 'being different from the differentiation in the form of difference delimited by each respective property from others' and 'being different from <s>abhidheyatva</s> and the like' must be incorporated into such a definition — this is the intent of this text. Thus there is no occasion for the previously stated defect. Further investigation should be pursued elsewhere.

children.text:
nanu lakṣaṇasya
vyavahāro 'pi prayojanam/ tena rūpeṇa vyavahartavyajñānaṃ vinā
tadrūpāvacchinnabodhakaśabdarūpavyavahārāsambhavāt/ evaṃ ca
vyāvahārikalakṣaṇasyāpi lakṣyatvāt tadbhinnatvaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ na
deyamityāha - vyavahārasyāpīti/ nanu vyāvṛttāvativyāptivāraṇāya
tadbhinnatvamāvaśyakam/ vyāvṛttervyāvahārikatvābhāvāditi bhramaṃ
vārayati - vyāvṛtterapīti/ apinā abhidheyatvādiparigraho
dṛṣṭāntalābhāya/
children.translated_text: Now, conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>) is also a purpose of a definition. For without the knowledge in that form [i.e. the definition], the conventional usage in the form of a word that conveys [the meaning] delimited by that form is impossible. And accordingly, since even the conventional definition (<s>vyāvahārikalakṣaṇa</s>) is a defined item, the qualifier 'different from that' should not be given — he says: 'of conventional usage also.' Now, to prevent over-extension in differentiation, [the qualifier] 'different from that' is necessary — he dispels the confusion that differentiation is not conventional — saying: 'of differentiation also.' The word 'also' (<s>api</s>) includes <s>abhidheyatva</s> and the like, for the purpose of obtaining a corroborating example.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanvetaddūṣaṇatrayarahitadharmo lakṣaṇam ityasya
avyāptyativyāptyasambhavarūpadoṣatrayābhāvaviśiṣṭo dharmo
lakṣaṇamityarthaḥ/ tathā ca 1ekadoṣavatyapi kapilatvādau doṣatrayaṃ
nāstīti 2lakṣaṇatvāpattirityāśaṅkya vyācakṣṭe -
uktadūṣaṇābhāvatrayaviśiṣṭa iti/ pratiyogini tritvaṃ na vivakṣitam,
kiṃ tu abhāve iti bhāvaḥ/ ekadoṣavati
itaradoṣābhāvadvayasattve 'pi doṣābhāvatrayaṃ nāstīti na
3pūrvoktāpattiriti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: Now, 'a definition is a property free from the three defects' — this means: a property qualified by the absence of the three defects in the form of <s>avyāpti</s> (under-extension), <s>ativyāpti</s> (over-extension), and <s>asambhava</s> (impossibility). And accordingly, even in <s>kapilatva</s> (tawny-color-ness) and the like, which possess [only] one defect, the three defects are absent — hence the unwanted consequence of its being a definition would arise. Anticipating this doubt, he explains: 'qualified by the absence of each of the stated defects.' The three-ness is not intended in the counter-positive, but rather in the absence — this is the purport. Even when a single-defect-possessing [property] has the two absences of the other defects, the three absences of defects are not present — hence the previously stated unwanted consequence does not arise. This should be noted.

children.text:
1. ekadoṣavatyapīti/
avyāptirūpakaidoṣaviśiṣṭe 'pītyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Even in one possessing a single defect' — the meaning is: even in one possessing the single defect of under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>).

children.text:
2. lakṣaṇatvāpattiriti/
golakṣaṇatvaprasaṅgaḥ ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The unwanted consequence of being a definition' — the meaning is: the unwanted consequence of being a definition of cow.

children.text:
3. pūrvoktāpattiriti/
kapiṃlatvādergolakṣaṇatvāpattirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The previously stated unwanted consequence' — the meaning is: the unwanted consequence that <s>kapilatva</s> (tawny-color-ness) and the like would be definitions of cow.

children.text:
nanu na sādhāraṇaḥ
asādhāraṇa iti karmadhārayasamāsāt asādhāraṇa ityasya
sādhāraṇabhinna ityarthaḥ/ sādhāraṇa ityasya ca lakṣyavṛttitve sati
alakṣyavṛttirityarthaḥ/ lakṣyavṛttitvaviśiṣṭālakṣyavṛttitvavāniti
yāvat/ asādhāraṇa ityasya ca
lakṣyavṛttitvaviśiṣṭālakṣyavṛttitvābhāvavānityarthaḥ/ avyāptigraste
kapilatvādau alakṣyavṛttitvarūpaviśeṣyābhāvāt viśiṣṭābhāvo 'sti/
asambhavagrastaḥ ekaśaphavattvādiḥ lakṣyavṛttitvarūpaviśeṣaṇābhāvāt
viśiṣṭābhāvavān/ tatathā ca ubhayoḥ asādhāraṇatayā lakṣaṇatvāpattiḥ,
doṣavato 'pi asādhāraṇatayā doṣatrayarahita evāsādhāraṇa
ityasaṅgatiśca ityāśaṅkya asādhāraṇaśabdārthaḥ
prakārāntareṇocyate dīpikāyāmityāha - nanu sādhāraṇyasyeti/
anyādṛśamiti/ lakṣyavṛttitvaviśiṣṭālakṣyavṛttitvābhāvāt
anyavidhamityarthaḥ/ lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatve satīti/ lakṣyatāvacchadakaṃ
yatra yatra vartate tatra sarvatra vartamānatvaṃ lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatvam/
lakṣyatāvacchedakaṃ yatra nāsti tatrāvartamānatvaṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvam/ lakṣyā gauḥ, lakṣyatāvacchedakaṃ gotvam,
tatra yatra yatra govyaktau vartate tatra sarvatra sāsnādimattvamasti, gotvaṃ
yatra nāsti mahiṣādau tatra sāsnādimattvaṃ nāstīti
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatve sati
children.translated_text: Now, from the <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound 'not common' (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), the meaning of <s>asādhāraṇa</s> is 'different from the common' (<s>sādhāraṇabhinna</s>). And 'common' (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) means: 'occurring in what is not the defined item while also occurring in the defined item.' That is: possessing the absence of non-occurrence-in-what-is-not-the-defined-item qualified by occurrence-in-the-defined-item. And 'not common' (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) means: possessing the absence of [the property of] occurrence-in-the-defined-item qualified by non-occurrence-in-what-is-not-the-defined-item. In <s>kapilatva</s> (tawny-color-ness), which is afflicted with under-extension, since the qualificand in the form of 'non-occurrence-in-what-is-not-the-defined-item' is absent, the qualified absence obtains. <s>Ekaśaphavatva</s> (single-hoofedness) and the like, afflicted with impossibility, since the qualifier in the form of 'occurrence-in-the-defined-item' is absent, possess the qualified absence. And accordingly, since both are uncommon, the unwanted consequence of their being definitions arises, and also the incoherence that even what is defective is uncommon while [the text says] 'only what is uncommon and free from the three defects is a definition.' Anticipating this doubt, the meaning of the word <s>asādhāraṇa</s> is stated in another manner in the <s>Dīpikā</s> — he says: 'Now, of <s>sādhāraṇya</s> (commonness).' 'Of another kind' — the meaning is: of a kind different from [the property of] occurrence-in-the-defined-item qualified by non-occurrence-in-what-is-not-the-defined-item. 'While pervading the delimitor of defined-ness' — wherever the delimitor of defined-ness exists, the property of existing there in all cases is the property of pervading the delimitor of defined-ness. The property of not existing where the delimitor of defined-ness does not exist is the property of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness. The defined item is a cow; the delimitor of defined-ness is cow-hood; <s>sāsnādimatva</s> (possessing a dewlap etc.) exists wherever each cow-individual exists; and where cow-hood does not exist, such as in a buffalo, <s>sāsnādimatva</s> does not exist — thus, while pervading the delimitor of defined-ness,

children.text:
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvāt sāsnādimattvaṃ asādhāraṇadharmoṃ
bhavati, atastat goḥ lakṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/ tathā ca
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatve sati lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvaṃ lakṣaṇasya
lakṣaṇamityuktaṃ bhavati/ satyantasya prayojanamāha -
avyāptyasambhavagrastayorvāraṇāyeti/ avyāptigraste kapilatve
lakṣaṇabhinne lakṣyatāvacchedakagotvaśūnyamahiṣādyavṛttitvarūpaṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvamastīti tatra lakṣaṇalakṣaṇasyātivyāptiḥ,
tadvāraṇāya lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatve satītyuktam/ gotvavati
śvetagavikapilatvābhāvāt lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatvaṃ tatra nāstīti
nātivyāptiḥ/ nanu uktarītyā
avyāptigraste 'tivyāptivāraṇarūpaprayojanasambhave 'pi asambhavagraste
tadvāraṇarūpaṃ prayojanaṃ na sambhavati/ asambhavagrastasya ekaśaphavattvādeḥ
lakṣyatāvacchedakagotvaśūnyāśvavṛttitayā
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvasyābhāvāt ativyāptyaprasakteriti cet -
atrāhuḥ/ atrāsambhavagrastapadaṃ gaganarūpasyāsambhavagrastasya tātparyeṇa
bodhakam/ goḥ gaganaṃ lakṣaṇamuktaṃ cet tadasambhavi/ gaganasya
avṛttipadārthatayā kutrāpi gavi asattvāt/ tathā cāsambhavagraste gagane
avṛttipadārthatvādeva
lakṣyatāvacchedakagotvaśūnyamahiṣādyavṛttitvamapyastīti
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvamātroktau tatrātivyāptiḥ syāditi
tadvāraṇāya lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatve satītyuktamiti/ ativyāptasya
vāraṇāya viśeṣyamiti/ lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvarūpaviśeṣyadalābhāve
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatvaṃ lakṣaṇalakṣaṇaṃ syāt/ tathā sati
children.translated_text: because it is pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness, <s>sāsnādimatva</s> is an uncommon property, and therefore it is the definition of cow — this is the purport. And accordingly, it has been stated that the property of pervading the delimitor of defined-ness while being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness is the definition of a definition. He states the purpose of the [qualifying phrase] 'while' (<s>sati</s>): 'for the exclusion of what is afflicted with under-extension and impossibility.' In <s>kapilatva</s> (tawny-color-ness), which is afflicted with under-extension and different from [being] a definition, there exists the property of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness (cow-hood) in the form of non-occurrence in buffalo etc. which lack the delimitor of defined-ness (cow-hood) — hence the definition of a definition would over-extend to it. To prevent that, the [qualifying phrase] 'while pervading the delimitor of defined-ness' was stated. Since <s>kapilatva</s> does not exist in [all] white cows etc. that possess cow-hood, the property of pervading the delimitor of defined-ness does not obtain there — hence there is no over-extension. Now, even if the purpose of preventing over-extension in what is afflicted with under-extension is achieved in the stated manner, the purpose of preventing [over-extension] in what is afflicted with impossibility is not achieved. For <s>ekaśaphavatva</s> (single-hoofedness), which is afflicted with impossibility, since it occurs in horses which lack the delimitor of defined-ness (cow-hood), the property of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness does not obtain — hence the threat of over-extension does not arise. If so — here they reply: the term 'afflicted with impossibility' (<s>asambhavagrasta</s>) here is intended to primarily convey what is afflicted with impossibility in the form of sky-ness (<s>gaganarūpa</s>). If sky were stated as a definition of cow, that would be afflicted with impossibility. Since sky is a non-occurring entity, it is absent in any cow. And accordingly, in sky, which is afflicted with impossibility, since it is a non-occurring entity, the property of non-occurrence in buffalo etc. which lack the delimitor of defined-ness (cow-hood) also obtains — hence if only being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness were stated, there would be over-extension to it. To prevent that, the [qualifying phrase] 'while pervading the delimitor of defined-ness' was stated. 'The qualificand for the exclusion of what is over-extended' — without the qualificand-component of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness, the pervading of the delimitor of defined-ness alone would be the definition of a definition. In that case,

children.text:
ativyāptiduṣṭasya
śṛṅgitvasya gotvavyāpakatvamastīti tatrātivyāptiḥ syāt/
tadvāraṇāya lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvopādānam/ śṛṅgitvasya
gotvaśūnyamahiṣādivrṛttitayā lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvaṃ nāstīti
nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>śṛṅgitva</s> (horn-possessing-ness), which is afflicted with over-extension, since it pervades cow-hood, would have over-extension there. To prevent that, the inclusion of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness [is needed]. Since <s>śṛṅgitva</s> occurs in buffalo etc. which lack cow-hood, the property of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness does not obtain — hence there is no over-extension. This is the purport.

children.text:
atredaṃ bodhyam --
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatvaṃ nāma
lakṣyatāvacchedakaniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitādhikaraṇatāvanniṣṭhātyantābhāvāprat iyogitvam/
tatrādheyatāyāṃ lakṣyatāvacchedakatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ
niveśyam/ anyathā gotvasya kālikasambandhena adhikaraṇe mahiṣādau
vartamānasya sāsnādimattvābhāvasya pratiyogyeva sāsnādimattvamiti
lakṣaṇe sāsnādimattvādau asambhavāpatteḥ/ evaṃ pratiyogitāyāṃ
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśanīyam/ anyathā samavāyena
gotvavati gavi yaḥ saṃyogasambandhāvacchinnasāsnādimattvābhāvaḥ
tatpratiyogitvasyaiva sāsnādimattve sattvena asaṃbhavāpatteḥ/ evaṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvaṃ na lakṣyatāvacchedakābhāvavadavṛttitvam,
padārthasya abhidheyatvaṃ lakṣaṇamityādau
lakṣyatāvacchedakapadārthatvābhāvavato 'prasiddhyā abhidheyatvādirūpe
lakṣaṇe avyāptyāpatteḥ/ kiṃ tu svavyāpakatatkatvam/ svaṃ - lakṣaṇam,
tat - lakṣyatāvacchedakam/ lakṣyatāvacchedakasya padārthatvasya
lakṣaṇībhūtābhidheyatvavyāpakatvamastīti na pūrvoktadoṣaḥ/
anayorvyāpakatvavyāpyatvayordvidhā niveśe gauravāt sakṛnniveśya
svavyāpakalakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatvaṃ lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvamiti
pariṣkāro yuktaḥ/ svavyāpakatvaṃ ca
svaniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitādhikaraṇatāvanniṣṭhātyantābhāvāpratiyogitvam/
tatrādheyatāyāṃ lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśanīyam/
anyathā sāsnādimattvasya kālikasambandhenādhikaraṇe mahiṣādau vartate
yo 'tyantābhāvaḥ gotvābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvasyaiva gotve sattvena
asambhavāpatteḥ/ evaṃ pratiyogitāyāṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśanīyam/ anyathā
samavāyena sāsnādimati gavi yaḥ saṃyogasambandhāvacchinnagotvābhāvaḥ
tatpratiyogitvasyaiva gotve sattvena pūrvoktadoṣāpatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Here the following should be understood — the property of pervading the delimitor of defined-ness (<s>lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatva</s>) is: not being the counter-positive of an absolute absence residing in what possesses the substratum-hood (<s>adhikaraṇatā</s>) determined by the superstratum-hood (<s>ādheyatā</s>) residing in the delimitor of defined-ness. In that [formulation], the superstratum-hood must be delimited by the relation that is the delimitor of the delimitor-of-defined-ness-hood. Otherwise, since <s>sāsnādimatva</s>, which exists in buffalo etc. through the temporal relation, would be the counter-positive of the absence of cow-hood, <s>sāsnādimatva</s> and the like would face the unwanted consequence of impossibility as definitions. Similarly, in the counter-positive-ness, the delimitation by the relation that is the delimitor of definition-hood must be incorporated. Otherwise, the absence of <s>sāsnādimatva</s> delimited by the relation of conjunction in a cow that possesses cow-hood through inherence — the counter-positive-ness of that [absence] would obtain in <s>sāsnādimatva</s> itself, leading to the unwanted consequence of impossibility. Similarly, the property of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-ness is not [simply] non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the delimitor of defined-ness. For in cases like '<s>abhidheyatva</s> (expressibility) is the definition of <s>padārtha</s> (category),' since there is no established entity that possesses the absence of the delimitor of defined-ness, namely <s>padārthatva</s>, there would be the unwanted consequence of under-extension in definitions such as <s>abhidheyatva</s>. Rather, [it means]: having one's pervader as that [delimitor of defined-ness]. 'One's own' means the definition; 'that' means the delimitor of defined-ness. Since the delimitor of defined-ness, <s>padārthatva</s>, pervades the definition-constituting <s>abhidheyatva</s>, the previously stated defect does not arise. Since incorporating these two — pervading and being pervaded — in two places involves prolixity, incorporating them once and refining [the formulation] as 'co-extensiveness with the delimitor of defined-ness, which is a pervader of oneself' (<s>svavyāpakalakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatva</s>) is appropriate. And 'pervading of oneself' (<s>svavyāpakatva</s>) is: not being the counter-positive of an absolute absence residing in what possesses the substratum-hood determined by the superstratum-hood residing in oneself. In that [formulation], the superstratum-hood must be delimited by the relation that is the delimitor of definition-hood. Otherwise, since there exists in buffalo etc., through the temporal relation, an absolute absence that is the absence of cow-hood, and the counter-positive-ness of that [absence] obtains in cow-hood itself, the unwanted consequence of impossibility would arise. Similarly, in the counter-positive-ness, the delimitation by the relation that is the delimitor of the delimitor-of-defined-ness-hood must be incorporated. Otherwise, the absence of cow-hood delimited by the relation of conjunction in a cow that possesses <s>sāsnādimatva</s> through inherence — the counter-positive-ness of that [absence] would obtain in cow-hood itself, leading to the previously stated defect.

dūṣaṇatrayarahitadharma
evāsādhāraṇadharma ityucyata iti kathanāt anyatamadoṣavān dharmaḥ

ativyāptyādidoṣāṇāmasādhāraṇyābhāvaprayojakatvaṃ labhyate/

children.translated_text: Since it was said that only a property free from the three defects is called an exclusive property (<s>asādhāraṇa dharma</s>), it follows that a property possessing any one of the defects is not exclusive. From this, the capacity of defects such as over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) and the like to destroy exclusiveness is obtained. He establishes that very point — with 'Here this should be understood' and so forth. 'These defects' means non-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>), over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>), and impossibility (<s>asambhava</s>). 'Destroyers of exclusiveness' means causes of the absence of exclusiveness. The remainder is: 'when over-extension obtains.' And the remainder for the other two is: 'when they obtain.' And accordingly, when the defect in the form of over-extension obtains, there is no pervasion by the delimitor of definiendum-ness; when the defect in the form of non-extension or the defect in the form of impossibility obtains, there is no pervading of the delimitor of definiendum-ness —

children.text:

children.translated_text: in this manner, the defects destroy exclusiveness — this is the purport. The defects corrupt the definition. How? To that he says — 'The seed of their corrupting capacity is this.' Here the intent is as follows: a definition, in the manner of an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), generates with respect to the definiendum an inference whose predicate is difference from others. For example: 'A cow is different from others, because of possessing dewlap and the like.' The inferential mark requires two aspects: pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) and residence in the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>). If a certain definition has the defect of over-extension, then by that definition, difference from others cannot be inferred — because of the breach of pervasion due to the defect of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). For consider: the inference 'A cow is different from others, because of possessing horns' is to be applied. When it is known that horn-possession is over-extended, occurring in what is different from a cow, the knowledge of deviation necessarily arises — namely that horn-possession occurs in what possesses the absence of the probandum in the form of difference from cows' others. By this, the pervasion-knowledge 'horn-possession does not occur in what possesses the absence of difference from cows' others' is obstructed, and thereby inference is obstructed. And accordingly, through producing deviation that contradicts pervasion, over-extension corrupts the definition.

And accordingly, 'occurring in what possesses the absence of difference from cows' others' simply means 'occurring in what possesses the property of being other than a cow, i.e. occurring in what is different from a cow.' And thus the knowledge of over-extension has the form of the knowledge of deviation —

When the defect of impossibility in the form of non-occurrence in all definienda obtains, the defect of essential non-establishment (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>), in the form of non-occurrence in the entire subject, applies. And by both of these, the residence-in-the-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) of the probans is breached. And accordingly,

vyāvartakaṃ lakṣyaṃ bhavati/ vyāvartakabhinnā vyāvṛttiḥ abhidheyatvādikaṃ
cālakṣyaṃ bhavati/ tatrāpi lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvasattvāt
lakṣaṇalakṣaṇasyātivyāptirdeṣaḥ/ tadvāraṇāya lakṣaṇalakṣaṇe
vyāvṛttibhinnatvaṃ abhidheyatvādibhinnatvaṃ ca viśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ kathaṃ
vyāvṛttau abhidheyatvādau ca lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvamastīti
cet - śrū yatām - vyāvṛttirnāma itarabhedaḥ, prakṛte
gavetarabhedaḥ/ saḥ lakṣyatāvacchedakagotvavyāpakaḥ gotvavatīṣu
sarvāsu goṣu gavetarāpekṣayā bhedasya sattvāt/ evaṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyaśca; gotvaśūnyeṣu mahiṣādiṣu gavetareṣu
gavetarabhedasyāvṛtteḥ/ evaṃ abhidheyatvādikaṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakapadārthatvavyāpakam, padārthatvavatsu sarveṣu padārtheṣu
abhidheyatvādeḥ sattvāt/ evaṃ padārthatvavyāpyaṃ ca/ yadyapi
tacchūnyāvṛttitvarūpaṃ padārthatvavyāpyatvaṃ na sambhavati,
padārthatvaśūnyasyāprasiddheḥ/ tathāpi svavyāpakatatkatvarūpaṃ vyāpyatvaṃ
sambhavati/ svam - abhidheyatvam, tadvyāpakaṃ - padārthatvaṃ
tatkatvasyābhidheyatve sadbhāvāt/ evaṃ ca yadi vyāvartakameva
lakṣaṇalakṣaṇalakṣyaṃ syāt tadā alakṣyeṣu vyāvṛttāvabhidheyatvādiṣu
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'If only the differentiator (<s>vyāvartaka</s>) is the definition' and so forth. That which causes an inference of difference from others with respect to the definiendum is called a 'differentiator' — and that alone is the definition, according to some. That which is not a differentiator but is merely the ground for verbal usage in the form of word-application is also a definition, according to others. In the view that only the differentiator is the definition, the previously stated definition of definition — namely being co-extensive with the delimitor of definiendum-ness — has the differentiator as its definiendum. Differentiation (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), which is other than the differentiator, and expressibility (<s>abhidheyatva</s>) and the like become non-definienda. In those too, since the co-extensiveness with the delimitor of definiendum-ness obtains, there is the defect of over-extension in the definition of definition. To avert that, in the definition of definition, the qualifiers 'being different from differentiation' and 'being different from expressibility and the like' should be added. How does co-extensiveness with the delimitor of definiendum-ness exist in differentiation and in expressibility and the like? Listen — differentiation means difference from others, here difference from cows' others. That is pervading the delimitor of definiendum-ness, namely cow-ness, because in all cows that possess cow-ness, difference with respect to others-than-cows exists. Similarly, it is also pervaded by the delimitor of definiendum-ness; because in buffaloes and the like that lack cow-ness, being others-than-cows, difference from cows' others does not occur [in them as definienda]. Similarly, expressibility and the like are pervading category-hood, which is the delimitor of definiendum-ness, because in all categories that possess category-hood, expressibility and the like exist. Similarly, [expressibility] is also pervaded by category-hood. Although pervasion in the form of non-occurrence in what lacks it is not possible — since nothing lacking category-hood is established — nevertheless, pervasion in the form of 'what pervades oneself is a property of that' is possible. 'Oneself' is expressibility; 'its pervader' is category-hood; 'being a property of that' exists in expressibility. And thus, if only the differentiator were the definiendum of the definition of definition, then in the non-definienda such as differentiation and expressibility and the like,

children.text:
ca
lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvasattvādativyāptiriti tadvāraṇāya
tattadbhinnatvaṃ lakṣaṇe niveśanīyamiti dīpikāgranthasya bhāvaḥ/
vyāvartakasyetyasya sāmānyataḥ itarabhedajñānajanakasyetyartho yadi
syāt tadā jñānapadena pratyakṣasya vā śābdabodhasya vā vivakṣāyāṃ
tajjanakatvaṃ viṣayādividhayā vyāvṛtterapyastīti tasyāḥ alakṣyatvaṃ na
syāditi paryālocya prakāśikāyām
itarabhedānamitijanakasyetyartha uktaḥ/ siddhasādhanadoṣeṇa vyāvṛtteḥ
itarabhedānumitijanakatvaṃ nāstīti paścādupapādayiṣyati/
children.translated_text: since co-extensiveness with the delimitor of definiendum-ness obtains, there is over-extension — and to avert that, the respective qualities of being different from each must be incorporated into the definition. This is the purport of the <s>Dīpikā</s> text. If the meaning of 'of the differentiator' were 'of what generates knowledge of difference from others in general,' then, since the generation of knowledge — in the mode of being an object and so forth — also belongs to differentiation, its status as a non-definiendum would not hold. Having reflected on this, in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> the meaning 'of what generates an inference having difference from others as its predicate' was stated. He will later establish that differentiation lacks the capacity to generate an inference of difference from others, due to the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).

children.text:
nanu
vyāvartakasyetyasya itarabhedānumitijanakasyetyartho na saṅcchete,
liṅgajñānamevānumitijanakam, na tu liṅgam iti mate
lakṣaṇarūpasya hetoḥ anamitijanakatvābhāvāt/ na ca vyāvartakasyetyasya
itarabhedavidheyakānumitijanakajñānaviṣayasyetyarthaḥ, tathā ca
noktadoṣa iti vācyam/ anumitijanake 1samūhālambanaparāmarśe
ghaṭādīnāmapi viṣayatayā teṣāmapi vyāvartaṅkatvāpatteḥ/ na
cetarabhedavidheyakānumitijanakatāvacchedakaviṣayatāśrayasyetyarthaḥ,
gavetarabhedavyāpyasāsnādimān ghaṭaśceti samūhālambanaparāmarśe
ghaṭādeḥ viṣayatve 'pi ghaṭādiniṣṭhaviṣayatāyā na
2janakatāvacchedakatvamiti vācyam/
children.translated_text: Now, the meaning 'of what generates an inference having difference from others as its predicate' does not fit the expression 'of the differentiator,' because in the view that inferential knowledge alone generates inference, not the inferential mark itself, the reason in the form of a definition does not have the property of generating inference. Nor should it be said that the meaning of 'of the differentiator' is 'of what is the object of the knowledge that generates an inference whose predicate is difference from others,' and hence the stated defect does not arise — because in the aggregate-apprehending <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective judgment) that generates inference, since pots and the like are also objects, they too would have the unwanted consequence of being differentiators. Nor should it be said that the meaning is 'of what is the locus of the object-hood that delimits the generation-capacity of the inference whose predicate is difference from others' — [for even if] in the aggregate-apprehending <s>parāmarśa</s> of the form 'A cow possesses what is pervaded by difference from cows' others, and a pot [also appears],' though a pot has object-hood, the object-hood residing in the pot does not delimit the generation-capacity, so [this interpretation could work] — one should not say so.

children.text: itarabhedaniṣṭhaviṣayatānirūpitavyāptiniṣṭhaviṣayatānirūpitasāsnādihetun iṣṭhaviṣayatānirūpitagavādipakṣaniṣṭhaviṣaya-
children.translated_text: Because the generation-capacity [of the <s>parāmarśa</s>] operates through the property of being a cognition possessing: the object-hood residing in the subject such as the cow, which delimits the object-hood residing in the probans such as possessing dewlap and the like, which delimits the object-hood residing in the pervasion, which delimits the object-hood residing in difference from others —

children.text:
tāśālijñānatvena
parāmarśasya janakatayā itarabhedaniṣṭhaviṣayatāyā api
janakatāvacchedakatayā tadāśrayasyetarabhedasyāpi vyāvartakatvāpatteḥ/
evaṃ pakṣādīnāmapi vyāvartakatvāpatteśca/ ato niṣkṛṣya vyācaṣṭe -
itarabhedavidheyaketi/ viṣayatāviśeṣapadena hetuniṣṭhaviṣayataiva
gṛhyate, tadāśrayatvaṃ ca sādhyapakṣādernāstīti na teṣāṃ
vyāvartakatvāpattiriti hṛdayam/

children.translated_text: Now, a definition is indeed twofold: differentiating (<s>vyāvartaka</s>) and conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>). In the view that only the differentiating definition is the definiendum, there is over-extension in the non-definiendum that is the conventional [definition] — and to avert that, the qualification 'being different from the conventional' should be incorporated — let this be what is said. Since the term 'conventional' itself covers both differentiation and expressibility and the like, the separate mention of each is redundant — he raises this doubt with 'Even though.' 'As will be stated' — the remainder is: by the passage 'because differentiation too has the capacity to establish usage.' 'Because of the possibility of inclusion' — the meaning is: because of the possibility of being conveyed by a single word. 'Separate mention' means indication by distinct words. He resolves this — with 'Nevertheless.' Here the intent is as follows: the capacity of differentiation, which has the form of difference from others of the definiendum, to generate an inference whose predicate is difference from others is not possible in the old view that <s>pakṣatā</s> (thesis-hood) is doubt about the probandum (<s>sādhyasaṃśaya</s>). For consider: if it is said 'difference from others generates an inference of difference from others,' there is identity between the probandum and the probans, since the inference would have to be applied as 'A cow is different from others, because of difference from others.' And in that case, the <s>parāmarśa</s> 'A cow possesses what is pervaded by difference from cows' others, namely difference from others' — this <s>parāmarśa</s>, apprehending difference from others in the cow, would have the form of an ascertainment of the probandum with the cow as qualificand. And at that time, the <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of the doubt 'Does the cow possess difference from others or not?' cannot exist, because of the ascertainment of the probandum being

children.translated_text: Now, what is this? and so forth. Here is the gist of the passage: since it was previously stated that the definition of a definition is 'being co-extensive with the delimitor of definiandum-hood,' and that differentiating power is the delimitor of definiandum-hood of the definition-of-a-definition, it follows [that we must ask]: what exactly is differentiating power? It is certainly not the capacity to generate inference having some difference or other as its predicate in the general form of difference-ness — because then, since even predicate-hood (<s>abhidheyatva</s>) of exclusion and the like would have differentiating power through generating inference of some difference, there would be the undesirable consequence of their being definianda, and hence the statement of over-pervasion with respect to them would be incoherent. [For instance:] 'A cow is different from both a cow and a pot, because of difference-from-non-cows,' 'An entity is different from both pot and cloth, because of predicate-hood' — thus, since the capacity to generate inference having any arbitrary pair-wise difference as its predicate, which falls under difference-ness, exists even in predicate-hood of exclusion and the like. children.translated_text: The <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), however, is as follows: by the definition, in the definiandum, just as difference-from-others is inferred, so too the delimitor of definiandum-hood is inferred. For instance, in 'a pot is earth, because of possessing smell,' the delimitor of definiandum-hood, namely earth-ness (<s>pṛthivītva</s>), is inferred in the pot by the definition of possessing smell. In the present case, dewlap-possession etc. is the definiandum; co-extensiveness with cow-ness is the definition; differentiating power in the form of generating inference of cow-ness-delimited difference-from-others is the delimitor of definiandum-hood — because it is in precisely that form that dewlap-possession etc. is a definiandum of the definition-of-a-definition. And thus, making dewlap-possession etc. the thesis, the cow-ness-delimited-difference-from-others-inference-generating power is to be proved there through co-extensiveness with cow-ness —

gavetarabhedānumitijanakatvaṃ nāsti, sādhyahetvoraikyena
pūrvoktarītyā siddhasādhanāt/ tathā ca
children.translated_text: 'Dewlap-possession etc. is capable of generating inference of difference from non-cows, because of co-extensiveness with cow-ness' — in that inference, the specific pervasion 'wherever there is co-extensiveness with cow-ness, there is the capacity to generate inference of difference from non-cows' cannot be stated, because both the probandum and the probans occur only in the thesis, and there is a dearth of an example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) beyond the thesis. Therefore, the pervasion must be stated in a general form: wherever there is co-extensiveness with such-and-such a property, there is the capacity to generate inference of difference-from-others delimited by that property. Smell-possession, which is co-extensive with earth-ness and generates inference of earth-ness-delimited difference-from-others, is the example. In a pervasion stated through such a general formulation, if the probans of the present case, or one similar to the present probans, is present, while the probandum of the present case, or one similar to the present probandum, is absent — that is the defect of deviation. And accordingly, in the exclusion in the form of difference-from-non-cows, the capacity to generate inference of cow-ness-delimited difference-from-others does not exist, because of the identity of the probandum and probans resulting in the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>), as stated earlier. And thus,

children.text:
gotvāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakatvarūpaṃ sādhyaṃ tatra nāsti/
gotvasamaniyatatvarūpaheturastīnti tatra vyabhicāraḥ syāt/
abhidheyatvādau prakṛtahetutulyaḥ padārthatvasamaniyatatvarūpo
heturasti, prakṛtasādhyatulyaṃ
children.translated_text: the probandum in the form of cow-ness-delimited-difference-from-others-inference-generating power does not exist there, but the probans in the form of co-extensiveness with cow-ness does exist — hence there would be deviation there. In predicate-hood and the like, a probans similar to the present probans, namely co-extensiveness with entity-ness (<s>padārthatva</s>), exists, but the probandum similar to the present probandum,

children.text:
1. tathā
lakṣyatāvacchedakamapyanumīyata iti/ prakāśikāyāṃ sāsnādimattvaṃ
pakṣīkṛtya gotvāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakatve sādhye iti kathaṃ
saṃgacchate? lakṣaṇena hītarabhedaḥ sādhyate na tvitarabhedānumāpakatvam
ityāśaṅkāṃ manasi nidhāyaivamuktam/ atha vā evaṃ tātparyaṃ
varṇanīyam lakṣaṇena lakṣye lakṣyatāvacchedakāvacchinnetarabhedaḥ kila
sādhanīyaḥ/ prakṛte gotvasamaniyatatvarūpasya lakṣaṇalakṣaṇasya
lakṣyatāvacchedakaṃ gotvāvacchinnaterabhedānumāpakatvam/
tadavacchinnetarabhedaḥ gotvasamaniyatatvena hetunā lakṣye
sāsnādimatve sādhanīyaḥ/ tadavacchinnetarabhedaśca
gavetarabhedānumāpakabhinnabhedaḥ gavetarabhedānumāpakatve
paryavasyanītyāśayena prakāśikāyāṃ
gotvāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakatve sādhye ityuktagiti/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'The delimitor of definiandum-hood too is inferred' — In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, how does it cohere that dewlap-possession etc. is made the thesis and the cow-ness-delimited-difference-from-others-inference-generating power is the probandum? For the definition proves difference-from-others, not the capacity to generate inference of difference-from-others — anticipating this doubt, this was stated. Alternatively, the purport should be explained thus: by the definition, in the definiandum, difference-from-others delimited by the delimitor of definiandum-hood is to be proved. In the present case, the delimitor of definiandum-hood of the definition-of-a-definition in the form of cow-ness-co-extensiveness is cow-ness-delimited-difference-from-others-inference-generating power. Difference-from-others delimited by that is to be proved in the definiandum, dewlap-possession etc., through the probans of cow-ness-co-extensiveness. And the difference-from-others delimited by that is difference other than that which is not capable of generating inference of difference from non-cows — which culminates in the capacity to generate inference of difference from non-cows. With this intent, in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> it was stated 'the probandum being cow-ness-delimited-difference-from-others-inference-generating power.'

children.text:
padārthatvāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakatvarūpaṃ sādhyaṃ nāsti
padārthetarasyāprasiddheriti vyabhicāraḥ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya
yaddharmasamaniyatatva rūpahetau vyāvṛttibhinnatve sati
abhidheyatvādibhinnatve sati iti viśeṣaṇaṃ dātavyam/ tena yatra
vyāvṛttibhinnatve sati abhidheyatvādibhinnatve sati yaddharmaṃsamaniyatatvaṃ
tatra taddharmāvacchinnetarabhedānumitijanakatvamiti sāmānyamukhī
vyāptiḥ paryavasyati tatra ca na ko 'pi doṣa ityabhiprāyo
dīpikāgranthasyeti/
children.translated_text: namely the entity-ness-delimited-difference-from-others-inference-generating power, does not exist — because 'non-entity' is not established — hence there would be deviation. To avert this, in the probans in the form of co-extensiveness with such-and-such a property, the qualifications 'being different from exclusion' and 'being different from predicate-hood and the like' must be added. Thereby, the general pervasion culminates in: wherever there is co-extensiveness with such-and-such a property, which is different from exclusion and different from predicate-hood and the like, there is the capacity to generate inference of difference-from-others delimited by that property. And therein there is no defect whatsoever — this is the intent of the <s>Dīpikā</s> text.

children.text:
atha kramaśaḥ
paṅktīnāmartha ucyate/ sāmānyato bhedānumāpakatvamiti/
pratiyogiviśeṣanirdeśamantarā bhedatvena bhedaṃ niveśya
kevalabhedavidheyakānumitijanakatvaṃ vyāvartakatvamiti vaktuṃ na
śakyata ityarthaḥ/ vyāvṛttyabhidheyatvāderapīti/ 'gauḥ
goghaṭobhayabhinna gavetarabhedāt', 'padārthaḥ ghaṭapaṭobhayabhinnaḥ
abhidheyatvāt' ityanumāne atra vivakṣite/
ativyāptikathanāsaṅgateriti/ lakṣye lakṣaṇasattvasyeṣṭatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
vyatirekidharmāṇāmiti/ kevalānvayidharmāṇāmabhidheyatvādīnāṃ
itarabhedānumāpakatvaṃ na sambhavati, abhidheyatvaśūnyasya
itarasyābhāvāt 'ghaṭaḥ itarabhinnaḥ abhidheyatvāt' ityapi
prayoktuṃ na śakyate, padārthetarasyaivāprasiddheriti bhāvaḥ/
asādhāraṇyaghaṭaketi/ lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvarūpāsādhāraṇyaghaṭakaṃ
yat vyāpakatvaṃ vyāpyatvaṃ ca tayorvaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt ityarthaḥ/
nāpi viśiṣyeti/ viśiṣyetyasya bhede 'nvayaḥ/ atra
lakṣyatāvacchedakagotvādyavacchinne ityadhyāhṛtya
gotvādyavacchinnoddeśyakagotvādyavacchinnetarabhedavidheyakānumitijanakatvamiti
vyākhyātavyam/ anyathā 'kapilagauḥ gavetarabhinnā kapilatvāt'
ityanumānasambhavena pūrvoktadoṣasattvenāsya pakṣāntaratvānupapatteḥ/
tādṛśalakṣaṇe niveśanīyamiti/ tādṛśalakṣaṇarūpe hetau
niveśanīyamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now the meaning of the lines is stated in order. 'Differentiating power in terms of difference in general' — the meaning is: it is not possible to state differentiating power as the capacity to generate inference having mere difference as predicate, by incorporating difference in the form of difference-ness without specifying the counter-positive. 'Even of predicate-hood of exclusion and the like' — this is said with reference to the intended inferences 'a cow is different from both cow and pot, because of difference-from-non-cows' and 'an entity is different from both pot and cloth, because of predicate-hood.' 'The statement of over-pervasion would be incoherent' — the purport is: because the presence of the definition in a definiandum is as desired. 'Of <s>vyatirekin</s> properties' — the capacity to generate inference of difference-from-others is not possible for purely positive (<s>kevalānvayin</s>) properties like predicate-hood, because the 'other' that lacks predicate-hood does not exist; nor can one even formulate 'a pot is different from others, because of predicate-hood,' since 'non-entity' is simply not established — this is the purport. 'The non-co-extensiveness-constituting [qualifier]' — the meaning is: the purposelessness of the pervasiveness and pervasion that constitute the non-co-extensiveness [component] of the delimitor-of-definiandum-hood-co-extensiveness as definition. 'Nor with specification' — the word 'with specification' connects with 'difference.' Here, one should supply 'delimited by the delimitor of definiandum-hood such as cow-ness etc.' and explain the differentiating power as the capacity to generate inference having cow-ness-etc.-delimited subject and cow-ness-etc.-delimited-difference-from-others as predicate. Otherwise, since the inference 'a tawny cow is different from non-cows, because of tawny-ness' would be possible, the previously stated defect would remain, and this could not stand as an alternative view.

children.text:
nanu lakṣaṇasya
vyavahāro 'pītyādi/ yathā lakṣaṇasya itarabhedānumitiḥ prayojanaṃ
tathā śabdaprayogarūpo vyavahāro 'pi prayojanam/ kathamiti cet-
ittham/ purovarti govyaktau 'iyaṃ gauḥ'
ityākārakagotvāvacchinnāvacakaśabdaprayogaṃ prati 'iyaṃ gauḥ'
ityākārakaṃ gotvaprakārakaṃ goviśeṣyakaṃ jñānaṃ kāraṇam/
taddharmāvacchinnabodhakaśabdaprayogarūpavyavahāraṃ prati
taddharmaprakārakavyavahartavyaviśeṣyakajñānasya kāraṇatvāt/ 'iyaṃ gauḥ'
ityākārakaṃ jñānaṃ ca gotvaparicāyakalakṣaṇajñānaṃ vinā na
sambhavatīti lakṣaṇasya svaviṣayakajñānajanyavyavahartavyaviṣayakajñānadvārā
vyavahāraḥ prayojanam/ tathā ca lakṣaṇaṃ vyāvahārikamapi bhavatīti
vyāvahārikalakṣaṇasyāpi lakṣyatāvacchedakasamaniyatatvaṃ lakṣaṇamiti
vyāvahārikamapi lakṣyamiti vyāvṛttyabhidheyatvāderapi lakṣyatvāt tatra
lakṣaṇasattvasyeṣṭatayā ativyāptyabhāvāt tadbhinnatvarūpaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ na
deyamiti bhāvaḥ/ tena rūpeṇa vyavahartavyajñānamiti/
taddharmaprakārakavyavahartavyaviśeṣyakajñānamityarthaḥ/
gotvādiprakārakagavādiviśeṣyakajñānamiti
children.translated_text: Now, practical usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>) is also [a purpose of] a definition — and so forth. Just as the inference of difference from others is the purpose of a definition, so too practical usage in the form of word-employment is also a purpose. How? — Thus: towards the employment of a word — delimited by cow-hood — denoting [the referent] in the form 'this is a cow' with respect to an individual cow present before one, the cognition having cow-hood as its qualifier-mode and the cow as its qualificand, of the form 'this is a cow,' is a cause. This is because knowledge having a certain property as its qualifier-mode and the object-to-be-dealt-with as its qualificand is a cause for practical usage in the form of employing a word that denotes [something] delimited by that property. And the cognition of the form 'this is a cow' is not possible without the knowledge of the definition that familiarizes one with cow-hood. Therefore, the purpose of a definition is practical usage, through the intermediary of knowledge having the definition's own object as its content, which generates knowledge of the object to be dealt with. And accordingly, a definition is also conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>). Since even a conventional definition is a definiendum — because differentiation (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), expressibility (<s>abhidheyatva</s>), and the like are also definienda, and since the presence of the definition in them is desired, there is no over-extension — the qualification 'different from that' need not be given; this is the purport. 'Knowledge of the object to be dealt with in that form' means knowledge having the object-to-be-dealt-with as qualificand with that property as qualifier-mode. That is, knowledge having the cow and the like as qualificand with cow-hood and the like as qualifier-mode —

children.text:
yāvat/
vyāvahārikalakṣaṇasyāpi -
vyavahāraprayojanakavyāvṛttyabhidheyatvādirūpalakṣaṇasyāpi/ lakṣyatvāt
-- lakṣaṇalakṣaṇalakṣyatvāt/ tadbhinnatvam --
vyāvṛttyabhidheyatvādibhinnatvam/ dṛṣṭāntalābhāyeti/ yathā
abhidheyatvādikaṃ vyavahārajanakaṃ tathā vyāvṛttirapi vyavahārajanikā
iti jñāpanāya iti bhāvaḥ//
children.translated_text: this much [is the meaning]. 'Even of a conventional definition' means: even of a definition in the form of differentiation, expressibility, and the like, which serves the purpose of practical usage. 'Because of being a definiendum' means: because of being a definiendum of the definition-of-a-definition. 'Different from that' means: different from differentiation, expressibility, and the like. 'For obtaining an example' — the purport is: to convey that just as expressibility and the like generate practical usage, so too differentiation generates practical usage.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
guṇavattvasya
dravyalakṣaṇatvasthāpanam
children.translated_text: Establishing <s>guṇavattva</s> (possessing qualities) as the definition of substance

children.text:
nanu guṇavattvaṃ na
dravyalakṣaṇam, ādyakṣaṇāvacchinnadravye utpannavinaṣṭadravye cāvyāpteriti
cet - na/ guṇasamānādhikaraṇasattābhinnajātimattvasya vivakṣitatvāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: <s>guṇavattva</s> (possessing qualities) is not the definition of substance, because of under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) in the case of a substance at the first moment of its existence, and in the case of a substance that is produced and destroyed [within a single moment]. Reply: No — because what is intended is possessing a universal (<s>jāti</s>) that is different from <s>sattā</s> (existence) and co-located with a quality (<s>guṇa</s>).

children.text:
nanvevamapi 'ekaṃ rūpaṃ
rasāt pṛthak' iti vyavahārāt rūpādāvativyāptiriti cet -
na/ ekārthasamavāyādeva tādṛśavyavahāropapattau guṇe
guṇānaṅgīkārāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, from the usage 'one color is separate from taste,' there is over-extension to color (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like. Reply: No — because since the said usage is explained by co-inherence in a single entity alone (<s>ekārthasamavāya</s>), a quality inhering in a quality is not accepted.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
nanu
ādyakṣaṇāvacchinne dravye guṇavattvasyāsattve 'pi kālāntarāvacchinne tatra
tatsattvamakṣatam/ evaṃ ca guṇāśrayatvalakṣaṇaṃ sādhvityata āha -
utpannavinaṣṭeti/ yādṛśadravyārambhakasaṃyogajanakakriyotpatteḥ
tṛtīyakṣaṇe 'vayavāntare tādṛśasaṃyoganāśikā kriyā jātā tādṛśadravya
ityarthaḥ/ navīnāḥ punaḥ asamavāyikāraṇasya kāryasahabhāvena
kāraṇatāmavalambyotpannavinaṣṭaṃ nāṅgīkurvanti/
guṇādāvativyāptivāraṇāya guṇasamānādhikaraṇeti jātiviśeṣaṇam/
sattāmādāyātivyāptivāraṇāya sattābhinneti/
dravyaguṇānyataratvamādāyātivyāpitavāraṇāya jātīti/ samavāyena
tādṛśadharmavattvatātparyagrāhakam/ ataḥ kālikādisambandhena
tadvattvamādāya nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, even though <s>guṇavattva</s> is absent in a substance at the first moment, it is unimpaired in that [substance] as delimited by a subsequent time. And thus the definition '<s>guṇāśrayatva</s>' (being a substratum of quality) is adequate — anticipating this [objection], he says — 'produced and destroyed' and so forth. The meaning is: a substance such that, at the third moment after the origination of the action that produces the conjunction that constitutes the cause for the origination of such a substance, an action destroying such conjunction has arisen — that is the meaning. The later scholars (<s>Navīnas</s>), however, by relying on the causality of the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) through co-existence with the effect, do not accept a 'produced and destroyed' [substance]. The qualifier 'co-located with a quality' in the term <s>guṇasamānādhikaraṇa</s> is to prevent over-extension to qualities and the like. 'Different from <s>sattā</s>' is to prevent over-extension by taking <s>sattā</s> [as the universal]. '<s>Jāti</s>' (universal) is to prevent over-extension by taking 'being either substance or quality' [as the property]. The word <s>jāti</s> conveys the purport that such property-possession is through the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). Therefore, there is no over-extension by taking such property-possession through the temporal relation and the like — this is the purport.

children.text:
evamapīti/ uktavivakṣayā
avyāptivāraṇe 'pi ekārthasamavāyādeveti/ ekasminnarthe samavāyena
sattvādevetyarthaḥ/ guṇānaṅgīkāraditi/ tathā ca kḷptena
samavāyaghaṭitasāmānādhirakaṇyenaiva guṇavattāvyavahāropapattau
tatrākḷptaguṇavattvakalpanaṃ na sambhavati gauravāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Even so' — even when under-extension is prevented by the stated intention — 'by co-inherence in a single entity alone' means: by existing through inherence in a single entity. 'A quality [inhering in a quality] is not accepted' — and accordingly, since the usage of possessing qualities can be explained by co-referentiality constituted by inherence, which is already established, the postulation of an unestablished quality-possession there is not possible due to the principle of ontological parsimony (<s>gaurava</s>) — this is the purport.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
dravyatvajātimattvaṃ
guṇavattvaṃ vā dravyalakṣaṇamiti pūrvamuktam/ tatra guṇavattvaṃ lakṣaṇam na
bhavitumarhati, utpattikṣaṇāvacchinne ghaṭe 'utpannaṃ dravyaṃ kṣaṇamaguṇaṃ
akriyaṃ ca tiṣṭhati' iti nyāyena guṇavattvābhāvena avyāptidoṣāt/
evaṃ yaḥ ghaṭaḥ prathamakṣaṇe utpannaḥ dvitīyakṣaṇe ca vinaṣṭaḥ, tatra prathamakṣaṇe
'utpannaṃ dravyaṃ kṣaṇamaguṇam' iti nyāyena guṇo nāsti, dvitīyakṣaṇe
ca guṇinaḥ ghaṭasyavināśāt na guṇaḥ iti
utpannavinaṣṭaghaṭe 'vyāpteśca ityāśaṅkitaṃ dīpikāyām - nanu
guṇavattvaṃ na dravyalakṣaṇamityādinā/ tatra dvitīyasthalānudhāvane
bījamāha - nanvādyakṣaṇāvacchinne dravya iti/ kālāntarāvacchinna iti/
dvitīyādikṣaṇavacchinna ityarthaḥ/ tatra tatsattvam - dravyaguṇasattvam/
guṇaśrayatvamiti/ guṇādhāratvamityarthaḥ/ samavāyena guṇaḥ
lakṣaṇamityukte yadyapyavyāptirasti, tathāpi guṇāśrayatvamityukte
nāvyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ yādṛśadravyārambhaketyādi/ kriyā, kriyāto
vibhāgaḥ, vibhāgāt pūrvadeśasaṃyoganāśaḥ, tataḥ uttradeśasaṃyogaḥ,
tataḥ dravyotpattiriti kramaḥ/ atra vibhāgaḥ saṃyogaśca avayavānāṃ
pūrvottaradeśānāṃ ca/ ghaṭotpādakaḥ yaḥ caturthakṣaṇotpannaḥ
uttaradeśasaṃyogaḥ tajjanikā kriyā prathamakṣaṇotpanna tasyāḥ tṛtīyakṣaṇaḥ
pūrvadeśasaṃyoganāśakṣaṇaḥ tadānīṃ ārambhakasaṃyoganāśajanakakriyā
jāyate cet utpattyanantarakṣaṇe dravyasya nāśo bhavati/ tathā cāyaṃ kramaḥ
- prathamakṣaṇe ghaṭotpādakakriyā, dvitīyakṣaṇe vibhāgaḥ, tṛtīyakṣaṇe
pūrvadeśāsaṃyoganāśaḥ uttaradeśasaṃyoganāśakakriyā ca, caturthakṣaṇe
uttaradeśasaṃyogaḥ vibhāgaśca, pañcamakṣaṇe ghaṭotpattiḥ
pūrvadeśaseyāṅganāśca, ṣaṣṭhakṣaṇe ghaṭanāśaḥ uttaradeśasaṃyogaśceti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: It was stated earlier that possessing the universal <s>dravyatva</s> or possessing qualities (<s>guṇavattva</s>) is the definition of substance. Therein, <s>guṇavattva</s> cannot be the definition, because by the maxim 'a produced substance remains for one moment without quality and without action,' <s>guṇavattva</s> is absent [at that moment], resulting in the defect of under-extension.
