Similarly, a pot that was produced at the first moment and destroyed at the second moment — there, at the first moment, by the maxim 'a produced substance remains for one moment without quality,' there is no quality; and at the second moment, the pot — the quality-bearer — has been destroyed, so there is no quality either. Thus there is under-extension in a produced-and-destroyed pot — this was objected to in the <s>Dīpikā</s> with 'Now, <s>guṇavattva</s> is not the definition of substance' and so forth. He states the seed for pursuing the second case — 'Now, at a substance delimited by the first moment' and so forth. 'Delimited by a subsequent time' means: delimited by the second and subsequent moments. 'The existence of that therein' means: the existence of quality in substance. '<s>Guṇāśrayatva</s>' means: being a receptacle of quality. The purport is: even though there is under-extension when 'quality through inherence' is stated as the definition, there is no under-extension when '<s>guṇāśrayatva</s>' (being a substratum of quality) is stated. 'Such a substance-producing' and so forth — the sequence is: action, from action vibration (separation), from separation the destruction of the conjunction with the previous location, from that the conjunction with the subsequent location, from that the origination of the substance. Here the separation and conjunction are of the parts and of the previous and subsequent locations. The conjunction with the subsequent location, produced at the fourth moment, which produces the pot — the action that generates it is produced at the first moment; its third moment is the moment of the destruction of the conjunction with the previous location. If at that time an action producing the destruction of the producing conjunction arises, then the substance is destroyed at the moment immediately after its origination. And thus the sequence is: at the first moment, the pot-producing action; at the second moment, separation; at the third moment, the destruction of the conjunction with the previous location and the action destroying the conjunction with the subsequent location; at the fourth moment, the conjunction with the subsequent location and separation; at the fifth moment, the origination of the pot and the destruction of the conjunction with the previous location; at the sixth moment, the destruction of the pot and the conjunction with the subsequent location — this is the purport.

children.text:
navīnāḥ punariti/
tathā ca etanmate caturthakṣaṇe eva ghaṭo 'pi uttaradeśasaṃyogātmakena
asamavāyikāraṇena saha utpadyate/ ghaṭanāśaśca tattṛtīyakṣaṇa eveti
ghaṭotpattidvitīyakṣaṇe ghaṭanāśābhāvāt utpannavinaṣṭaghaṭo 'prāmāṇika
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The later scholars, however' — and accordingly, on this view, at the fourth moment itself the pot too is produced together with the conjunction with the subsequent location, which is the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>). And the destruction of the pot occurs only at the third moment after that. Therefore, since at the second moment after the pot's origination there is no destruction of the pot, a 'produced and destroyed' pot is not established by valid evidence — this is the purport.

children.text:
dīpikāyām -
guṇasamānādhikaraṇeti/ guṇasamānādhikaraṇā guṇādhikaraṇavṛttiḥ yā
sattānyā jātiḥ tadvattvaṃ dravyasya lakṣaṇam/ bhavati hi dravyatvarūpā jātiḥ
guṇādhikaraṇapṛthivyādivṛttiḥ sattāto 'nyā ceti tadvattvamādāya dravye
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: '<s>guṇasamānādhikaraṇa</s>' — 'co-located with a quality' means: a universal (<s>jāti</s>) which resides in the substratum of quality, which is different from <s>sattā</s>, whose possession is the definition of substance. Indeed, the universal in the form of <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood) resides in earth and the like which are substrata of quality, and is different from <s>sattā</s>. Taking the possession of that, the definition applies to substance.

children.text:
lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/
ādyakṣaṇāvacchinnaghaṭe utpannavinaṣṭaghaṭe ca guṇābhāve 'pi
tatsamānādhikaraṇadravyatvajātisattvāt nāvyāptiḥ/ jātau
guṇasamānādhikaraṇeti viśeṣaṇānupādāne
sattābhinnaguṇatvajātimattvasya guṇe sattvāt tatrātivyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: In a pot at the first moment and in a produced-and-destroyed pot, even though quality is absent, since the universal <s>dravyatva</s> co-located with it is present, there is no under-extension. If the qualifier 'co-located with a quality' is not included in [the description of] the universal, then since the universal <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood), which is different from <s>sattā</s>, possesses the property of being a quality-co-located universal, there would be over-extension to quality.

children.text:
guṇasamānādhikaraṇeti
viśeṣaṇe upātte tu guṇe guṇānaṅgīkārāt guṇādhikaraṇaṃ na
guṇaḥ, kiṃ tu dravyameva tadvṛttitvaṃ guṇatve nāstīti jātipadena
guṇatvagrahaṇāsambhavāt nātivyāptiḥ/ guṇādhikaraṇadravyavṛttiḥ yā
sattājātiḥ tadvattvasya guṇe 'pi sattvādativyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya jātau
sattābhinneti viśeṣaṇam/ jātipadasthāne dharmapadaṃ
children.translated_text: But when the qualifier 'co-located with a quality' is included, since a quality [inhering in a] quality is not accepted [in Nyāya], the substratum of a quality is not a quality but only a substance; since the property of residing therein is absent in quality-hood, the universal <s>guṇatva</s> cannot be captured by the word <s>jāti</s> [in this definition], and hence there is no over-extension. Now, since <s>sattā</s> — the universal that resides in substance, which is the substratum of quality — also satisfies the conditions, there would be over-extension to quality as well. To prevent that, the qualifier 'different from <s>sattā</s>' is given for the universal. If in place of the word <s>jāti</s> (universal), the word <s>dharma</s> (property)

children.text:
nikṣipya
guṇasamānādhikaraṇasattābhinnadharmavattvaṃ dravyalakṣaṇamityukte
dravyaguṇānyataratvarūpo dharmo 'pi guṇādhikaraṇadravyavṛttiḥ
sattābhinnaśceti tadvattvasya guṇe 'pi sattvādativyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
jātītyuktam/ anyataratvaṃ tu na jātiḥ/ nanu jātipade upātte 'pi
kālikasambandhena tādṛśadravyatvarūpajātimattvasya guṇe 'pi
sattvādativyāptiḥ/ samavāyasambandhena tādṛśajātimattvavivakṣāyāṃ tu
jātipadaṃ vyartham/ samavāyasambandhena
guṇasamānādhikaraṇasattābhinnadharmavattvaṃ lakṣaṇamityuktyaiva
sāmañjasyāt/ dravyaguṇānyataratvarūpadharmasya svarūpameva sambandha iti
samavāyena tadvattvasya guṇe virahāditi cet - na/ samavāyasambandhena
tādṛśadharmavattvamatravivakṣitamiti dyotanāyaiva jātipadopādānāditi/
tadāha prakāśikāyām - guṇādāvativyāptivāraṇāyetyādinā/
children.translated_text: is substituted, and the definition is stated as 'possessing a property that is different from <s>sattā</s> and co-located with a quality' — then a property in the form of 'being either substance or quality' (<s>dravyaguṇānyataratva</s>) also resides in substance which is the substratum of quality, and is different from <s>sattā</s>; hence there would be over-extension to quality from possessing that. To prevent that, the word '<s>jāti</s>' was used. For '<s>anyataratva</s>' (being-either-of-two) is not a <s>jāti</s> (genuine universal). Now, even with the word <s>jāti</s> included, since the universal in the form of <s>dravyatva</s> can be present in quality through temporal relation, there would be over-extension. If the intention is that such universal-possession is through the relation of inherence, then the word <s>jāti</s> is redundant — since it would suffice to say 'possessing, through the relation of inherence, a property that is different from <s>sattā</s> and co-located with a quality.' For the property in the form of 'being either substance or quality' has self-linking relation (<s>svarūpa</s>) alone as its relation, and hence its possession through inherence is absent in quality — if this is objected — no, because the word <s>jāti</s> is included precisely to indicate that possession of such a property through the relation of inherence is what is intended here. This is stated in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> with 'to prevent over-extension to quality and the like' and so forth.

children.text:
dīpikāyām -
nanvevamapīti/"ekaṃ rūpam' iti vyavahārāt rūpe
ekatvasaṅkhyārūpo guṇo 'stītyavagamyate; 'rūpaṃ rasāt pṛthaka'
iti vyavahārāt rūpe pṛthaktvaguṇo 'stītyavagamyate/ tathā ca
guṇādhikaraṇaṃ rūpaṃ tadvṛttiryā sattābhinnā jātiḥ guṇatvaṃ tadvattvasya
guṇe sattvāt tatra dravyalakṣaṇasyātivyāptiriti śaṅkiturāśayaḥ/
samādhatte - ekārthasamavāyāditi/ ekasminnarthe samavāyādityarthaḥ/
ekatvarūpayoḥ pṛthaktvarūpayośca ekasminnarthe ghaṭādau samavāyāt 'ekaṃ
rūpam', 'rūpaṃ rasāt pṛthak' iti vyavahāra upapadyate/ 'ekaṃ rūpam'
ityasya svāśrayasamavāyasambandhena rūpam ekatvavat ityarthaḥ, na tu
samavāyasambandhena ekatvavat iti/ evaṃ ca uktaparamparāsambandhena rūpe
ekatvapṛthaktvaviṣayakatayaiva tādṛśavyavahārasyopapatteḥ guṇe
samavāyasambandhena guṇo nāṅgīkriyate/
guṇasamānādhikaraṇetyādilakṣaṇe ca guṇādhikaraṇatvaṃ
samavāyasambandhena vivakṣitam/ ato rūpādaiṃ nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'Even so' — from the usage 'one color (<s>rūpa</s>),' it is understood that in color there exists a quality in the form of the number oneness (<s>ekatva</s>); from the usage 'color is separate from taste,' it is understood that in color there exists the quality of separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>). And accordingly, color is the substratum of quality; the universal <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood), which resides therein and is a <s>jāti</s> different from <s>sattā</s> — since its possession obtains in quality, the definition of substance would be over-extended there — this is the intent of the objector. He resolves it: 'by co-inherence in a single entity' — the meaning is: by inherence in a single entity. Since the two — oneness and color, separateness and color — both inhere in a single entity such as a pot and the like, the usages 'one color' and 'color is separate from taste' are explained. The meaning of 'one color' is: color possesses oneness through the relation of co-inherence-in-its-own-substratum (<s>svāśrayasamavāya</s>), not through the relation of inherence. And thus, since such usage is explained by color and oneness being related merely as objects in the same substratum through the intermediary relation, a quality inhering in a quality through the relation of inherence is not accepted. And in the definition beginning with '<s>guṇasamānādhikaraṇa</s>' and the like, the substratum-hood of quality is intended through the relation of inherence. Therefore there is no over-extension to color and the like — this is the purport.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām -
samavāyaghaṭitasāmānādhikaraṇyeneti/ svāśrayasamavāyeneti yāvat/
svaniṣṭhasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnādheyatānirūpitādhikaraṇatānirūpitasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvaṃ
samavāyasambandhaghaṭitasāmānādhikaraṇyam/ tasya śodhane
svāśrayasamavāya ityeva paryavasyati/ akḷptaguṇavattvakalpanamiti/
akḷptasya samavāyasambandhena guṇavattvasya kalpanamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'by co-referentiality constituted by inherence' means: by co-inherence-in-its-own-substratum. The co-referentiality constituted by the inherence relation is: the property of being a superstratum whose superstratum-hood is determined by a substratum-hood determined by the inherence relation, which [superstratum-hood] is delimited by the inherence relation residing in oneself. Upon analysis, this simply amounts to co-inherence-in-one's-own-substratum. 'The postulation of an unestablished quality-possession' means: the postulation of quality-possession through the relation of inherence, which is unestablished.

children.text: tarkasaṃṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: guṇavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of Qualities

children.text: AnTs_4 rūparasagandhasparśasaṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvagurutvadravatvasnehaśabdabuddhisukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmādharmasaṃskārāś caturviṃśati guṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: Color (<s>rūpa</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), touch (<s>sparśa</s>), number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), magnitude (<s>parimāṇa</s>), separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>), conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>), remoteness (<s>paratva</s>), proximity (<s>aparatva</s>), heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>), fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>), viscidity (<s>sneha</s>), sound (<s>śabda</s>), cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), effort (<s>prayatna</s>), merit (<s>dharma</s>), demerit (<s>adharma</s>), and disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — these are the twenty-four qualities.

children.text:
rūpa-rasa-gandha-sparśa-saṅkhyā-parimāṇa-pṛthaktva-saṃyoga-vibhāga-paratva-aparatva-gurutva-dravatva-sneha-śabda-buddhi
-sukha - duḥkha - icchā-dveṣa - prayatna-dharma-adharma-saṃskārāḥ
caturviṃśatirguṇāḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpa</s> (color), <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>gandha</s> (smell), <s>sparśa</s> (touch), <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number), <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction), <s>paratva</s> (remoteness), <s>aparatva</s> (proximity), <s>gurutva</s> (heaviness), <s>dravatva</s> (fluidity), <s>sneha</s> (viscidity), <s>śabda</s> (sound), <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), <s>duḥkha</s> (pain), <s>icchā</s> (desire), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), <s>prayatna</s> (effort), <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>adharma</s> (demerit), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (disposition) — these are the twenty-four qualities.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
guṇān vibhajate -
rūpeti/ dravyakarmabhinnatve sati sāmānyavān guṇaḥ/
guṇatvajātimānvā/
children.translated_text: He divides the qualities — '<s>rūpa</s>' and so forth. A quality (<s>guṇa</s>) is that which possesses a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) while being different from substance (<s>dravya</s>) and action (<s>karma</s>). Or [alternatively], that which possesses the universal <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood).

children.text:
nanu
laghutva-kaṭhinatva-mṛdutvādīnāṃ vidyamānatvāt kathaṃ
catuviṃśatirguṃṇāḥ iti cet - na/ ladhutvasya gurutvābhāvarūpatvāt
mṛdutvakaṭhinatvayoḥ avayavasaṃyogaviśeṣarūpatvāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since lightness (<s>laghutva</s>), hardness (<s>kaṭhinatva</s>), softness (<s>mṛdutva</s>), and the like exist, how can there be [only] twenty-four qualities? Reply: No — because lightness is of the nature of the absence of heaviness, and hardness and softness are of the nature of specific types of conjunction of parts.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
sāmānyavāniti/
samavāyena sāmānyavattvaṃ bodhyam/ tena kālikādisambandhena tadvati
dhvaṃse nātivyāptiḥ/ guṇa iti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ/ lāghavādāha -
guṇatvajātimānveti/ yadyapi lakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchedakayorabhedaḥ tathāpi
lakṣaṇenetarabhede sādhye hetau sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaniśce 'pi
hetudharmitāvacchedakakasādhyaniścayasya aniyatatvābhiprayeṇedaṃ
lakṣaṇamiti saṅkṣepaḥ/ ekamagre 'pi bodhyam/ guṇatvajātisiddhistu
guṇapadaśakyatāvacchedakatayeti guṇadīdhitau bhaṭṭācāryāḥ/ na caivaṃ
vibhupadaśakyatāvacchedakatayā vibhutvajātiḥ
children.translated_text: 'possessing a universal' — the possession of a universal through inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) should be understood. Thereby, there is no over-extension to destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) residing in what possesses [a universal] through temporal and other relations. 'Quality' is the indication of the definiendum. For the sake of brevity, he says — 'possesses quality-hood as a universal.' Although the definition and the delimitor of definiendum-hood are non-different, nevertheless — when the definition is the reason for establishing difference from others as the probandum, even though the co-location of the probandum with the reason is ascertained, the ascertainment of the probandum with the delimitor of the reason-bearer-hood of the reason is not invariable — with this intent, this is the definition. This is the summary. The same should be understood in subsequent passages as well. As for the establishment of quality-hood as a universal (<s>jāti</s>), in the <s>Guṇadīdhiti</s>, <s>Bhaṭṭācārya</s> [states that it is established] by being the delimitor of the denotative capacity of the word 'quality.' Nor should it be said that similarly, by being the delimitor of the denotative capacity of the word 'all-pervading,' the universal of all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>)

children.text:
sidhyediti vācyam/
bhūtatvasaṅkarasya bādhakasya sattvena tasya jātitvāsambhavāt
jātitvābhimatasaṅkarasyaiva jātitvabādhakatvāt/ tathā coktam
dravyakiraṇāvalyām udayanācāryaiḥ-
children.translated_text: would be established — because since the impediment in the form of conflation (<s>saṅkara</s>) with element-hood (<s>bhūtatva</s>) exists, the universal-hood of that is impossible — because only conflation with what is considered a universal serves as an impediment to universal-hood. And thus <s>Udayanācārya</s> states in the <s>Dravyakiraṇāvalī</s> —

children.text:
"vyakterabhedastulyatvaṃ
saṅkāro 'thānavasthitiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Non-difference from the individual (<s>vyakti</s>), equality [of individuals],

children.text:
rūpahānirasambandho
jātibādhakasaṅgrahaḥ//"
children.translated_text: conflation (<s>saṅkara</s>), infinite regress (<s>anavasthiti</s>), loss of form (<s>rūpahāni</s>), and non-connection (<s>asambandha</s>) — this is the collection of impediments to universal-hood (<s>jātibādhaka</s>).'

children.text:
iti/ vyakterabhedaḥ
svāśrayavyakteraikyaṃ ākāśatvāderjātitve bādhakam/ vyaktestulyatvaṃ
anyūnānatiriktavyaktikatvaṃ
children.translated_text: Thus. Non-difference from the individual means identity with the individual that is its own substratum — this is an impediment to the universal-hood of space-hood (<s>ākāśatva</s>) and the like. Equality of individuals means having individuals that are neither fewer nor more —

children.text:
ghaṭatvakalaśatvādyorbhinnajātitve/ saṅkaraḥ
parasparātyantābhāvasamānādhikaraṇayordharmayorekatra samāveśaḥ
bhūtatvamūrtatvāderjātitve/ anavasthitiḥ- anāvasthā jāteḥ
jātimattve/ rūpahāniḥ svatāvyāvartakatvātmakarūpahāni viśeṣasya
jātimattve/ asambandha asamavetatvam abhāvāderjātimattve iti
saṃkṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: this is [an impediment] to the status of pot-hood (<s>ghaṭatva</s>) and jar-hood (<s>kalaśatva</s>) as distinct universals. Conflation (<s>saṅkara</s>) is the co-occurrence in a single locus of two properties that are co-located with their mutual absolute absences — this is [an impediment] to the universal-hood of element-hood (<s>bhūtatva</s>), corporeality (<s>mūrtatva</s>), and the like. Infinite regress (<s>anavasthiti</s>) means the absence of termination — an infinite regress in [attributing] universal-possession to a universal itself. Loss of form (<s>rūpahāni</s>) is the loss of the defining characteristic consisting of its own discriminative capacity — this is [an impediment] to the universal-possession of <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity). Non-connection (<s>asambandha</s>) means not being connected through inherence — this is [an impediment] to the universal-possession of absence (<s>abhāva</s>) and the like. This is the summary.

children.text:
laghutvādīnāṃ
prāmāṇikatve 'pi kḷpteṣvantarbhāvo nyāyya iti
samādhatte---laghutvasyeti/
children.translated_text: Even though properties such as lightness (<s>laghutva</s>) and the like are real, their subsumption under the established [universals] is proper — he resolves [the doubt] thus: 'of lightness' and so forth.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
tadvati dhvaṃsa
iti/ sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyānāṃ
prāgabhāvānyonyābhāvātyantābhāvānāṃ cājanyatvāt janyamātrasyaiva
children.translated_text: 'Destruction residing in what possesses [a universal]' — since universals (<s>sāmānya</s>), particularities (<s>viśeṣa</s>), and inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), as well as prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>), mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>), and absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>), are unoriginated, only what is originated

children.text:
kālopādhitayā teṣu
kālikasambandhena sāmānyavattvāsambhavāt ativyāptirna śakyate
vaktumityālocya dhvaṃse 'tivyāptiruktā/ yadyapi
lakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchedakayorabheda iti/ guṇasya guṇatvajātimattvaṃ yadi
lakṣaṇaṃ tadā guṇatvaṃ lakṣaṇam, lakṣyatāvacchedakamapi tadeveti
lakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchadakayorabhadaḥ syāt/ astu ko doṣa iti cet -
ucyate/ lakṣaṇaṃ hi vyāvartakam/
lakṣyaviśeṣyakalakṣyetarabhedavidheyakānumitijanakam/ tathā ca
guṇatvasya guṇalakṣaṇatve 'guṇaḥ itarabhinnaḥ guṇatvāt'
ityanumānaprayogaḥ kartavyaḥ/ tatra
guṇatvavyāpaketarabhedasamānādhikaraṇaguṇatvavān guṇa iti
parāmarśo vācyaḥ/ tatra guṇatve itarabhedasāmānādhikaraṇye
bhāsamāne 1tulyavittivedyatayā kadācit itarabhede
guṇatvasāmānādhikaraṇyamati bhāsitumarhati/ tathā ca
guṇatvarūpapakṣatāvacchedakasāmānādhikaraṇyasya itarabhedarūpasādhye
bhānāt anumitiviṣayasya sādhye pakṣatāvacchedakasāmānādhikaraṇyasya
parāmarśenaiva viṣayīkṛtatayā siddhasādhanaṃ doṣaḥ prasajatīti
śaṅkiturāśayaḥ/ samādhatte - tathāpīti/ hetau
sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇye bhāsamāne niyamena sādhye
hetusāmānādhikaraṇyabhānaṃ na sambhavati/ ato na siddhasādhnaprasaktiriti
guṇatvajātimattvaṃ guṇalakṣaṇaṃ bhavitumarhatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: — since time serves as a limiting condition for them, and since the possession of a universal through temporal relation is impossible in those [entities], the over-extension cannot be stated [there]. Therefore, the over-extension was stated with reference to destruction. 'Although the definition and the delimitor of definiendum-hood are non-different' — if the possession of quality-hood as a universal is the definition of quality, then quality-hood is the definition, and the delimitor of definiendum-hood is also the same — hence there would be non-difference between the definition and the delimitor of definiendum-hood. What is the defect in that? — it is answered: the definition is a differentiator — it generates an inference having the definiendum as qualificand and difference from others as predicate. And accordingly, when quality-hood is the definition of quality, the inferential application 'quality is different from others, because of quality-hood' must be performed. There, the apprehension (<s>parāmarśa</s>) must be stated as: quality possesses quality-hood co-located with difference-from-others pervaded by quality-hood. There, when quality-hood and co-location with difference-from-others are cognized, since they are cognized as having equal cognitive content, sometimes the co-location of quality-hood with difference-from-others may also be cognized. And accordingly, since the co-location of the delimitor of the subject-hood in the form of quality-hood with the probandum in the form of difference-from-others is cognized through the apprehension itself, as the content of inference is already cognized through the apprehension, the defect of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>) would arise — this is the doubter's intent. He resolves [the doubt] — 'Nevertheless' — even when the co-location of the probandum with the reason is cognized, the co-location of the reason with the probandum is not invariably cognized. Therefore, since the defect of proving what is already established does not arise, the possession of quality-hood as a universal can indeed be the definition of quality — this is the purport.

children.text:
guṇapadaśakyatāvacchedakatayeti/ 'guṇaniṣṭhā guṇapadaśakyatā
kiñciddharmāvacchinnā śakyatātvāt ghaṭaniṣṭhaghaṭapadaśakyatāvat'
ityanumānena guṇatvajātiḥ sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ/
bhūtatvasaṅkarasyeti/ bhūtatvena sākamekatra samāveśasyetyarthaḥ/ nanu
bhūtatvasyāpi jātitvābhāvāt katha tatsaṅkaraḥ vibhutvasya jātitve
bādhaka ityāśaṅkya na jātisaṅkaraḥjātitvabādhakaḥ, kiṃ tu
jātitvābhimatadharmasaṅkara eva tathā/ bhūtatvasya jātitvābhāve 'pi
jātitvābhimānaviṣayatvamastīti tatsaṅkaro jātitvabādhaka iti
samādhatte - jātitvābhimatasaṅkarasyaiveti/ vyakterabhedatulyatvaṃ
saṅkaraśca jātimattve bādhakāni/ anavasthā rūpahāniḥ asambandhaśca
jātitve bādhakāḥ/ jātibādhakasaṅgraha ityasya
jātitvajātimattvānyataraviṣayakajñānapratibandhakajñānaviṣayaviṣayakasaṅkṣiptaśabdaḥ
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'By being the delimitor of the denotative capacity of the word "quality"' — the purport is: by the inference 'the denotative capacity residing in quality for the word "quality" is delimited by some property, because it is a denotative capacity, like the denotative capacity of the word "pot" residing in a pot,' the universal quality-hood is established. 'The conflation with element-hood' — the meaning is: co-occurrence in a single locus together with element-hood. Now, since element-hood (<s>bhūtatva</s>) itself lacks universal-hood, how is its conflation an impediment to the universal-hood of all-pervasiveness? — anticipating this doubt — it is not conflation with a universal that is an impediment to universal-hood, but rather conflation with what is considered (<s>abhimata</s>) a universal is what serves as such. Even though element-hood lacks universal-hood, it is the object of the belief in universal-hood, and therefore its conflation is an impediment to universal-hood — he resolves: 'conflation with what is considered [a universal] alone.' Non-difference from the individual, equality, and conflation are impediments to universal-possession (<s>jātimattva</s>). Infinite regress, loss of form, and non-connection are impediments to universal-hood (<s>jātitva</s>). The meaning of 'collection of impediments to universals' is: a compressed expression for the objects of cognition that obstructs cognition concerning either universal-hood or universal-possession.

children.text:
vyakterabhedaḥ ityasya
svāśrayaikavyaktikatvamityarthaḥ/
svapratiyogivṛttitvasvānuyogivṛttitvobhayasambandhena
bhedaviśiṣṭānyatvamiti yāvat/ yasyāśrayabhūtā vyaktayaḥ anekāḥ sa
uktobhayasambandhena bhedaviśiṣṭo bhavati yathā ghaṭatnavaṃ
nīlaghaṭabhedaviśiṣṭam/ svaṃ nīlaghaṭabhedaḥ, svapratiyogī nīlaghaṭaḥ,
tadvṛttitvaṃ ghaṭatve, eva svaṃ nīlaghaṭabhedaḥ,
children.translated_text: The meaning of 'non-difference from the individual' is: having only one individual as substratum. That is: otherness qualified by a difference characterized by both relations — the property of residing in [the locus of] its own counter-positive and the property of residing in [the locus of] its own correlate. A [property] whose substrate-individuals are many possesses the said difference through both relations — like pot-hood, which is qualified by the difference from a blue pot. The 'own' [entity] is the difference from a blue pot; its counter-positive is the blue pot; the property of residing in that [counter-positive] is in pot-hood. Similarly, 'own' is the difference from a blue pot,

children.text:
1.
tulyavittivedyatayeti/ ekajñānaviṣayatayetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'As having equal cognitive content' — the meaning is: as being the content of a single cognition.

children.text:
tadanuyogī raktaghaṭaḥ
tadvṛttitvaṃ ca ghaṭatve iti ghaṭatvam uktobhayasambandhena
nīlaghaṭabhedaviśiṣṭam/ ākāśatvaṃ tu na tathā/ bhedapadena
ākāśabhedopādāne svapratiyogī ākāśaḥ, tadvṛttitvaṃ
yadyapyākāśe 'sti, tathāti ākāśabhedānuyogighaṭādivṛttitvaṃ nāsti/
ghaṭabhedopādāne svānuyogyākāśavṛttitvaṃ yadyapyakāśatve 'sti,
tathāpi spapratiyogighaṭavṛttitvaṃ nāstīti/ tathā ca
ākāśatvamuktobhayasambandhena bhedaviśiṣṭānyaditi tat
svāśrayaikavyaktikam, atastat na jātiḥ/ jātitvaṃ hi nityatve
satyanekasamavetatvam/ anekasamavetatvaṃ ca uktobhayasambandhena
bhedaviśiṣṭatvam/ atra ca ākāśatvaṃ jātiḥ (uktobhayasambandhena
bhedaviśiṣṭam) iti buddhiṃ prati ākāśatvaṃ svāśrayaikavyaktikam
(uktobhayasambandhena bhedaviśiṣṭānyat) iti jñānasya tadvattābuddhiṃ
prati tadabhāvavattājñānaṃ pratibandhakamiti rītyā pratibandhakatvāt
jātitvaviṣayakajñānapratibandhakajñānaviṣayatbasya vyakterabhede sattvāt
jātibādhakatvamityavadheyam/
children.translated_text: its correlate is the red pot, and the property of residing in that is also in pot-hood — thus pot-hood is qualified by the difference from a blue pot through both said relations. But space-hood (<s>ākāśatva</s>) is not so. If the difference referred to is the difference from space — its counter-positive is space, and the property of residing in that is indeed present in space-hood; however, the property of residing in something that is the correlate of the difference from space, such as a pot, is not [present in space-hood]. If the difference referred to is the difference from a pot — the property of the correlate, namely space, residing [as a locus of space-hood] is indeed present; however, the property of residing in the counter-positive, namely a pot, is not [present]. And accordingly, space-hood is other [than what is] qualified by difference through both said relations — hence it has only one individual as substratum, and therefore it is not a universal. For universal-hood is: while being eternal, residing in many through inherence. And residing in many is being qualified by difference through both said relations. And here, the cognition 'space-hood is a universal (qualified by difference through both said relations)' — against that cognition, the knowledge 'space-hood has only one individual as substratum (is other than what is qualified by difference through both said relations)' serves as obstructive in the manner of cognition whose content possesses the absence of that [property] obstructing the cognition whose content possesses that [property] — thus, since it has the quality of being the content of cognition that obstructs cognition concerning universal-hood, the status of non-difference from the individual as an impediment to universal-hood should be noted.

children.text:
vyaktestulyatvam
anyūnānatiriktavyaktikatvamiti/ anyūnānatiriktāśrayakatvamityarthaḥ/
ghaṭatvakalaśatvayorīdṛśatulyatvasattvāt tayorna bhinnajātitvam/
vastutastu
svabhinnajātyāśrayavyaktiniṣṭhasaṅkhyānyūnānatiriktasaṅkhyākavyaktikatvaṃ
svasamānādhikaraṇānyonyābhāvapratiyogitānavacchekadakasvabhinnajātisamānādhikaraṇanyonyābhāvapratiyogitānavaccheda-
children.translated_text: 'Equality of individuals means having individuals that are neither fewer nor more' — the meaning is: having substrata that are neither fewer nor more. Since pot-hood and jar-hood have such equality, they do not have distinct universal-hood. In truth, the equality in the form of having individuals of a number that is neither fewer nor more than the number of individuals residing in a substratum of a different universal from oneself — [more precisely,] in the form of

children.text:
katvarūpam
tulyatvamityarthaḥ/ idaṃ kambugrīvādimattvasya jātitve bādhakam/
svam - kambugrīvādimattvaṃ,
tatsamānādhikaraṇānyonyābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedikā svabhinnajātiḥ
ghaṭatvajātiḥ
tatsamānādhikaraṇānyonyābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakatvaṃ
kambugrīvādimattve asti/ yatraitādṛśaṃ tulyatvamasti 1tatra jātitvaṃ
nāsti/ evaṃ caitādṛśatulyatvajñānasya
jātitvābhāvavyāpyavattājñānavidhayā jātitvajñānapratibandhakatvam/
children.translated_text: not delimiting the counter-positive-hood of a mutual absence co-located with oneself [and] not delimiting the counter-positive-hood of a mutual absence co-located with a different universal from oneself that is co-located with oneself — this is equality in the intended sense. This is an impediment to the universal-hood of possessing a conch-shaped neck and the like (<s>kambugrīvādimatva</s>). The 'own' is possessing a conch-shaped neck and the like; the different universal co-located with it [whose mutual absence's counter-positive-hood] is not delimited [by it] is pot-hood as a universal; the non-delimitation of the counter-positive-hood of the mutual absence co-located with that is present in possessing a conch-shaped neck and the like. Wherever such equality is present, universal-hood is not present there. And accordingly, the cognition of such equality, being in the manner of cognition of what possesses the absence pervaded by the absence of universal-hood, obstructs the cognition of universal-hood.

children.text:
1. tatra jātitva
nāstīti/ yathā pṛthivyādimano 'ntānyatamatve/ svaṃ
pṛthivyādimanontānyatamatvaṃ, tadbhinnā jātiḥ dravyatvaṃ
tatsamaniyatatvaṃ pṛthivyādimanontānyatamatve 'stīti tanna jātiḥ/
tathā ca svabhinnajātisamaniyatatvaṃ tulyatvam/
svabhinnajātisamavaniyatatvaṃ ca
svasamānādhikaraṇānyonyābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakasvabhinnajātisamānā-
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Universal-hood is not present there' — as in the case of being-any-one-of-earth-up-to-mind. The 'own' is being-any-one-of-earth-up-to-mind; the different universal from it is substance-hood; co-extensiveness with that is present in being-any-one-of-earth-up-to-mind — therefore that is not a universal. And accordingly, equality is co-extensiveness with a different universal from oneself. And co-extensiveness with a different universal from oneself is

children.text: dhikaraṇānyonyābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakatvamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: not delimiting the counter-positive-hood of a mutual absence co-located with oneself [and] not delimiting the counter-positive-hood of a mutual absence co-located with a different universal from oneself that is co-located with oneself — this is the purport.

children.text:
saṅkaro nāma
parasparaṃ vihāya vartamānayordharmayorekatra vṛttiḥ/
parasparātyantābhāvasamānādhikaraṇayordharmayorekatra
children.translated_text: Conflation (<s>saṅkara</s>) is the co-occurrence in a single locus of two properties that exist excluding each other. That is: the co-occurrence in a single locus of two properties that are co-located with each other's absolute absence —

children.text:
vṛttiriti yāvat ayaṃ
bhūtatvamūrtatvayorjātitve bādhakaḥ, bhūtatvaṃ vihāya mūrtatvaṃ
manasi, mūrtatvaṃ vihāya bhūtatvaṃ ākāśe, ubhayoḥ
pṛthivyādicatuṣṭaye samāveśa iti dvayoḥ saṅkarāt na
jātitvam/ 1svādhikaraṇavṛttitva-svābhāvavadvṛttitva -
svādhikaraṇavṛttyatyantābhāvapratiyogitva-etattritayasambandhena
kiñciddharmaviśiṣṭatvaṃ saṅkara iti phalitam/ etādṛśasāṅkaryasya
kathaṃ jātitvabādhakatvamiti cet - ucyate/ liṅgavidhayaiva tasya
jātitvabādhakatvam/ tathā hi - bhūtatvaṃ na jātiḥ uktatritayasambandhena
mūrtatvavattvāt yat uktatritayasambandhena mūrtatvavat tanna jātiḥ yathā
2gaganamanassaṃyoga ityanumānāt bhūtatvasya jātitvābhāvasiddhau
bādhajñānavidhayā jātitvajñānapratibandhikā yā niruktānumitiḥ
tajjanakavyāptyādijñāne niruktasāṅkaryasya viṣayatvāt
sākṣātpratibandhakajñānaviṣayasyeva
children.translated_text: this is the meaning. This is an impediment to the universal-hood of element-hood (<s>bhūtatva</s>) and corporeality (<s>mūrtatva</s>): corporeality exists apart from element-hood in the mind; element-hood exists apart from corporeality in space (<s>ākāśa</s>); both co-occur in the four [elements] earth and the rest — since the two have conflation, they do not have universal-hood. The resultant meaning of conflation is: being qualified by some property through the three relations — (i) the property of residing in its own substratum, (ii) the property of residing in what possesses its own absence, and (iii) the counter-positive-hood of an absolute absence that resides in its own substratum. How is such conflation an impediment to universal-hood? — it is answered: it is an impediment by way of being an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Thus: 'Element-hood is not a universal, because it possesses corporeality through the said three relations; whatever possesses corporeality through the said three relations is not a universal — like the contact of space and mind' — through this inference, when the absence of universal-hood of element-hood is established, the said inference, which in the manner of a sublating cognition obstructs the cognition of universal-hood, [functions as the impediment]; and since the said conflation is the content of the cognition of invariable concomitance and the like that generates that inference, just as the content of the directly obstructing cognition [is an impediment],

children.text:
1. svādhikaraṇetyādi/
svaṃ bhūtatvaṃ svādhikaraṇaṃ pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayaṃ tadvṛttitvaṃ
mūrtatve 'sti/ evaṃ svaṃ bhūtatvaṃ svābhāvaḥ bhūtatvābhāvaḥ tadvat manaḥ
tadvṛttitvaṃ mūrtatve 'sti/ evaṃ svaṃ bhūtatvaṃ tadadhikaraṇamākāśaṃ
tadvṛttiryo 'tyantābhāvaḥ mūrtatvābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvaṃ mūrtatve 'sti/
evaṃ coktatritayasambandhena bhūtatvaviśiṣṭatvaṃ yat mūrtatvasya tadeva
saṃkara ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Its own substratum' and so forth — 'own' is element-hood; its own substratum is the four [elements] earth and the rest; the property of residing in that is present in corporeality. Similarly, 'own' is element-hood; its own absence is the absence of element-hood; what possesses that is the mind; the property of residing in that is present in corporeality. Similarly, 'own' is element-hood; its substratum is space; the absolute absence that resides in that is the absence of corporeality; the counter-positive-hood of that is present in corporeality. And accordingly, the qualification of element-hood by corporeality through the said three relations — that is conflation in the intended sense.

children.text:
2. gaganamanassaṃyoga
iti/ gaganamanassaṃyogasya mūrtatvādhikaraṇamanovṛttitvāt
mūrtatvābhāvādhikaraṇagaganavṛttitvāt
mūrtatvādhikaraṇapṛthivyādicatuṣṭayavṛttiḥ yaḥ
gaganamanassaṃyogābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvācca uktatritayasambandhena
mūrtatvavaiśiṣṭyamiti heturasti jātitvābhāvarūpasādhyaṃ cāstīti
gaganamanassaṃyogasya dṛṣṭāntatvam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The contact of space and mind' — since the contact of space and mind resides in the mind which is a substratum of corporeality, and resides in space which is a substratum of the absence of corporeality, and the absence of the contact of space and mind — whose counter-positive-hood is present — resides in the four [elements] earth and the rest which are substrata of corporeality, the qualification by corporeality through the said three relations is present as the reason, and the probandum in the form of absence of universal-hood is also present — thus the contact of space and mind serves as the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>).

children.text:
pratibandhakajñānajanakajñānaviṣayasyāpi jātibādhakapadārthatvena
1tasya sāṅkarye 'kṣatatvāt/ atha vā
2jātitvābhāvānumitijanakajātitvābhāvavyāpyaniruktatritayasambandhena
mūrtatvaparāmarśasya tadabhāvavyāpyavattāniścayatvena
jātitvaprakārakajñānapratibandhakatvāt niruktasāṅkaryasya tadviṣayatvena
sākṣājjātitvajñānapratibandhakajñānaviṣayatvamakṣatamityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: so too the content of the cognition that generates the obstructing cognition has the status of being an impediment to universals — because its [status as such] remains intact despite the conflation. Alternatively, the apprehension through the said three relations of corporeality that generates the inference of the absence of universal-hood — since that [apprehension] has the character of ascertaining what possesses the absence pervaded by the absence of universal-hood, it obstructs the cognition having universal-hood as its qualifier-mode; and since the said conflation is the content of that [obstructing apprehension], its direct status as the content of cognition that obstructs the cognition of universal-hood remains intact — so they say.

children.text:
anavasthā -
aprāmāṇikāttarottarakalpanāyāḥ viśrāntyabhāvaḥ/ iyaṃ jāteḥ
jātimattve bādhikā/ 3tarkavidhayā bādhakatvamasyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) is the absence of termination in an unwarranted successive postulation. This is an impediment to the universal-possession of a universal (<s>jāti</s>) itself. Its status as an impediment is by way of suppositional reasoning (<s>tarka</s>).

children.text:
rūpahāniḥ -
4svatovyāvartakatvarūpalakṣaṇasya bhaṅgaḥ/ iyaṃ viśeṣasya jātimattve
bādhikā/ viśeṣo hi svatovyāvartakatvena lakṣitaḥ/ viśeṣo yadi
jāmimān syāt tarhi jātereva
viśeṣasyetaravyāvṛttihetutvasambhavāt svatovyāvartakatvarūpaṃ
lakṣaṇaṃ bhagnaṃ syāt/ ato viśeṣo na jātimān/ evaṃ ca
rūpahānirapi tarkavidhayaiva
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpahāni</s> (loss of form) — means the breakdown of the definition in the form of self-differentiating capacity (<s>svatovyāvartakatva</s>). This is an invalidator of <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular) possessing a <s>jāti</s> (universal). For <s>viśeṣa</s> is defined by its self-differentiating capacity. If <s>viśeṣa</s> were to possess a <s>jāti</s>, then since the <s>jāti</s> itself could be the cause of the differentiation of <s>viśeṣa</s> from others, the definition in the form of self-differentiating capacity would be broken. Therefore, <s>viśeṣa</s> does not possess a <s>jāti</s>. And thus, <s>rūpahāni</s> too, in the manner of <s>tarka</s> (reductio), is

children.text: jātimattvabādhikā/
children.translated_text: an invalidator of <s>jāti</s>-possession.

children.text:
asambandhaḥ -
pratiyogitvānuyogitvānyatarasambandhena samavāyaśūnyatvam/ ayaṃ ca
samavāyābhāvayorjātimattve bādhakaḥ/ yatra yatra jātimattvaṃ vartate tatra
pratiyogitvānuyogitvānyatarasambandhena 5samavāyo 'sti/ samavāye
abhāve
children.translated_text: <s>Asambandha</s> (absence of relation) — means being devoid of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) through either the relation of counter-positive-ness or co-relatum-ness. This is an invalidator of <s>samavāya</s> and <s>abhāva</s> (absence) possessing a <s>jāti</s>. Wherever <s>jāti</s>-possession obtains, there <s>samavāya</s> exists through either the relation of counter-positive-ness or co-relatum-ness. In <s>samavāya</s> and <s>abhāva</s>,

children.text:
1. tasyeti/
pratibandhakajñānajanakajñānaviṣayatvasyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Of that' — the meaning is: of the property of being the object of the cognition that generates the obstructing cognition.

children.text:
2.
jātitvābhāvānumitīti/ bhūtatvaṃ na jātirityākārikā yā
jātitvābhāvānumitiḥ tajjanakaḥ ya parāmarśaḥ bhūtatvaṃ
jātitvābhāvavyāpyamūrtatvavat ityākārakaḥ tasyetyarthaḥ/ tathā
coktatritayasambandhena mūrtatvavattvarūpasya saṃkarasya
jātitvānumitipratibandhakaparāmarśaviṣayatayā
jātitvaviṣayakajñānapratibandhakajñānaviṣayatvarūpaṃ jātibādhakatvamiti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The inference of the absence of <s>jātitva</s> (universal-hood)' — the inference of the absence of <s>jātitva</s> which takes the form '<s>bhūtatva</s> (element-hood) is not a <s>jāti</s>'; the inferential cognition (<s>parāmarśa</s>) that generates it, which takes the form '<s>bhūtatva</s> is pervaded by the absence of <s>jātitva</s>, as it possesses <s>mūrtatvatva</s> (corporeality-possession)' — 'of that' means of that [inferential cognition]. And accordingly, through the stated threefold relation, since <s>saṃkara</s> (conflation) in the form of possessing <s>mūrtatvatva</s> is the object of the inferential cognition that obstructs the inference of <s>jātitva</s>, it has the property of being the object of a cognition that obstructs the cognition having <s>jātitva</s> as its content — and that constitutes being an invalidator of <s>jāti</s>. This is the purport.

children.text:
3. tarkavidhayeti/ yadi
jātirjātimatī syāt tarhi uttarottarajātikalpanāyāḥ viśrāntirna
syāditi tarko 'tra vivakṣitaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'In the manner of <s>tarka</s>' — the <s>tarka</s> (reductio) intended here is: if a <s>jāti</s> were to possess a <s>jāti</s>, then there would be no end to the postulation of successively higher <s>jātis</s>.

children.text:
4. svatovyāvartakatvaṃ
ca
svabhinnaliṅgakasvaviśeṣyakasvasajātīyetarabhedānumityaviṣayatvam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] Self-differentiating capacity (<s>svatovyāvartakatva</s>) is: not being the object of an inference of difference from a co-generic other, which has as its inferential mark something different from oneself and has oneself as its qualificand.

children.text:
5. samavāyo 'stīti/
yathā ghaṭe jātimatvamasti, tatra pratiyogitvasambandhena
ghaṭasamavāyo 'sti kapāle yo ghaṭasamavāyaḥ tatpratiyogitvāt
ghaṭasya, evam anuyogitāsambandhena ghaṭatvasamavāyo 'sti ghaṭe yo
ghaṭatvasamavāyaḥ tadanuyogitvāt ghaṭasyeti/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] '<s>Samavāya</s> exists' — for example, <s>jāti</s>-possession exists in a pot; there, through the relation of counter-positive-ness, the <s>samavāya</s> of the pot exists in the potsherd — because the pot is the counter-positive of the <s>samavāya</s> of the pot in the potsherd. Similarly, through the relation of co-relatum-ness, the <s>samavāya</s> of pot-hood exists in the pot — because the pot is the co-relatum of the <s>samavāya</s> of pot-hood.

children.text:
ca 1tadabhāvāt ta
jātimattvaṃ tayoḥ/ uktānyatarasambandhena samavāyābhāvaḥ
jātimattvābhāvavyāpyaḥ/ ataḥ asambandhajñānaṃ
tadabhāvavyāpyavattājñānavidhayā jātimattvajñānapratibandhakama
children.translated_text: and due to the absence of that [<s>samavāya</s>], <s>jāti</s>-possession does not belong to those two [<s>samavāya</s> and <s>abhāva</s>]. The absence of <s>samavāya</s> through the stated either-relation is pervaded by the absence of <s>jāti</s>-possession. Therefore, the cognition of absence-of-relation, in the manner of cognition of what possesses [a property] pervaded by that absence, is an obstructor of the cognition of <s>jāti</s>-possession.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: karmavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of <s>Karma</s> (Action)

children.text: AnTs_5 utkṣepaṇāvakṣepaṇākuñcanaprasāraṇagamanāni pañca karmāṇi //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 5:] Upward motion (<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>), downward motion (<s>avakṣepaṇa</s>), contraction (<s>ākuñcana</s>), expansion (<s>prasāraṇa</s>), and locomotion (<s>gamana</s>) — these are the five actions.

children.text:
utkṣepaṇa - apakṣepaṇa
- ākuñcana - prasāraṇa - gamanāni pañcakarmāṇi/
children.translated_text: Upward motion (<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>), downward motion (<s>apakṣepaṇa</s>), contraction (<s>ākuñcana</s>), expansion (<s>prasāraṇa</s>), and locomotion (<s>gamana</s>) — these are the five actions.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
karma vibhajate -
utkṣepaṇeti/ saṃyogabhinnatve sati saṃyogasamavāyikāraṇaṃ karma
karmatvajātimadvā/ nanu bhramaṇāderapyatiriktasya karmaṇaḥ sattvāt
pañcetyanupapannamiti cet - na/ bhramaṇādīnāmapigamane 'ntarbhāvāt na
pañcatvavirodhaḥ/
children.translated_text: He divides <s>karma</s> (action) — '<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>' etc. Action is [defined as]: while being different from <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), that which is the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) of <s>saṃyoga</s>; or [alternatively], what possesses the <s>jāti</s> of <s>karmatva</s> (action-hood). Now, since actions other than [the five listed], such as rotation (<s>bhramaṇa</s>) and the like, also exist, the statement 'five' is unjustified — if thus objected: no, because rotation and the like are subsumed under locomotion (<s>gamana</s>), hence there is no conflict with the five-ness.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
saṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇe saṃyoge 'tivyāptivāraṇāya
saṃyogabhinnatve satīti/ saṃyogasamavāyikāraṇa
dravye 'tivyāptivāraṇāya asamavāyīti/
children.translated_text: To prevent over-extension to <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), which is the non-inherent cause of [another] <s>saṃyoga</s>, [the qualification] 'while being different from <s>saṃyoga</s>' [is stated]. To prevent over-extension to <s>dravya</s> (substance), which is the non-inherent cause of <s>saṃyoga</s>, [the qualification] 'non-inherent' [is stated].

children.text:
bhramaṇādīnām
ityādinā recanasyandanordhvajvalanatiryaggamanānāṃ saṃgrahaḥ/
gamane 'ntarbhāvāditi/ na cotkṣepaṇādīnāmapi
gamane 'natarbhāvo 'stviti śaṅkyam/ svatantrecchasya
niyogaparyanuyogānarhasya munesaṃmatatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: By [the phrase] 'rotation and the like,' evacuation (<s>recana</s>), flowing (<s>syandana</s>), upward flaming (<s>ūrdhvajvalana</s>), and lateral movement (<s>tiryaggamana</s>) are included. 'Are subsumed under locomotion' — and one should not doubt that upward motion and the like too should be subsumed under locomotion; because it is universally accepted that the sage [<s>Kaṇāda</s>], being independently willing, is not subject to command or questioning — this is the purport.

children.text:
1. tadabhāvāditi/
samavāyo 'bhāvo vānyatra samavāyasambandhena nāsti, ataḥ
pratiyogitāsambandhena samavāyavattvaṃ samavāyābhāvayerna bhavati/ evaṃ
samavāye 'bhāve vā anyat kimapi samavāyasambandhena nāsti, ataḥ
anuyogitāsambandhena samavāyavattvaṃ tayorna bhavatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Due to the absence of that' — <s>samavāya</s> or <s>abhāva</s> does not exist in anything else through the relation of <s>samavāya</s>; therefore, through the relation of counter-positive-ness, the property of possessing <s>samavāya</s> does not belong to <s>samavāya</s> or <s>abhāva</s>. Similarly, in <s>samavāya</s> or <s>abhāva</s>, nothing else exists through the relation of <s>samavāya</s>; therefore, through the relation of co-relatum-ness, the property of possessing <s>samavāya</s> does not belong to those two — this is the purport.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
saṃyogabhinnatve
sati saṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇaṃ karmeti karmaṇo lakṣaṇamuktam/
saṃyogabhinnatve satītyanuktau saṃyogasya
saṃyogo 'pyasamavāyikāraṇam; kāyapustakasaṃyogaṃ prati
hastapusatakasaṃyogasyāsamavāyikāraṇatvāt; ataḥ
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>karma</s> (action) has been stated as: 'while being different from <s>saṃyoga</s>, that which is the non-inherent cause of <s>saṃyoga</s>.' If the phrase 'while being different from <s>saṃyoga</s>' were not stated, <s>saṃyoga</s> itself would also be a non-inherent cause of [another] <s>saṃyoga</s>; for instance, the <s>saṃyoga</s> of the hand and the book is the non-inherent cause of the <s>saṃyoga</s> of the body and the book. Therefore,

children.text:
saṃyoge 'tivyāptiḥ/
tadvāraṇāya saṃyogabhinnatve satītyuktam/
saṃyogakāraṇamityetāvanmātroktau saṃyogasamavāyikāraṇe
dravye 'tivyāptiḥ, tadvāraṇāya kāraṇe asamavāyīti viśeṣaṇam/
tadāhasaṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇa iti/
children.translated_text: there would be over-extension to <s>saṃyoga</s>. To prevent that, 'while being different from <s>saṃyoga</s>' was stated. If only 'cause of <s>saṃyoga</s>' were stated, there would be over-extension to <s>dravya</s> (substance), which is the inherent cause of <s>saṃyoga</s>. To prevent that, the qualifier 'non-inherent' is [added] to 'cause.' That is what is meant by 'the non-inherent cause of <s>saṃyoga</s>.'

children.text:
svatantrecchasyeti/
svatantreccho muniḥ niyogaparyanuyogānarha iti sarvasaṃmata
ityarthaḥ/ niyogaḥ - ājñā/ paryanuyogaḥ - praśnaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Of the independently willing [sage]' — the meaning is: the sage [<s>Kaṇāda</s>], who is independently willing, is universally accepted as not subject to command or questioning. 'Command' (<s>niyoga</s>) means order. 'Questioning' (<s>paryanuyoga</s>) means inquiry.

children.text: tarkasaṃṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: sāmānyavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of <s>Sāmānya</s> (Universal)

children.text: AnTs_6 param aparaṃ ceti dvividhaṃ sāmānyam //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 6:] <s>Sāmānya</s> (universal) is twofold: <s>para</s> (higher) and <s>apara</s> (lower).

children.text: sāmānyaṃ dvividham - param aparam ceti/
children.translated_text: <s>Sāmānya</s> is twofold — <s>para</s> (higher) and <s>apara</s> (lower).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
sāmānyaṃ vibhajate
- paramiti/ param - adhikadeśavṛtti/ aparam - nyūnadeśavṛtti/
sāmānyādicatuṣṭaye jātirnāsti/
children.translated_text: He divides <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) — '<s>para</s>' etc. <s>Para</s> (higher) means occurring in more loci. <s>Apara</s> (lower) means occurring in fewer loci. In the group of four beginning with <s>sāmānya</s> [i.e. <s>sāmānya</s>, <s>viśeṣa</s>, <s>samavāya</s>, <s>abhāva</s>], there is no <s>jāti</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
paramityādi/
sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ agre mūlakṛtaiva vakṣyata iti na nyūnateti dhyeyam/
sattāyā dravyatvādyapekṣayā adhikadeśavṛttitvena paratvameva/
ghaṭatvādīnāṃ nyūnadeśavṛttitvena aparatvameva/ dravyatvādīnāṃ
sattāto 'paratvam ghaṭatvāditaḥ paratvamiti vivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: '<s>Para</s>' and so forth. The definition of <s>sāmānya</s> will be stated later by the author of the root text himself — hence there is no deficiency. This should be noted. <s>Sattā</s> (existence), in comparison with <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood) and the like, has the status of <s>para</s> (higher) alone, due to occurring in more loci. <s>Ghaṭatva</s> (pot-hood) and the like have the status of <s>apara</s> (lower) alone, due to occurring in fewer loci. The distinction is: <s>dravyatva</s> and the like are <s>apara</s> relative to <s>sattā</s>, and <s>para</s> relative to <s>ghaṭatva</s> and the like.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: viśeṣavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of <s>Viśeṣa</s> (Particularity)

children.text: AnTs_7 nityadravyavṛttayo viśeṣās tv anantā eva //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 7:] <s>Viśeṣas</s> (particularities), which reside in eternal substances, are indeed infinite.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
viśeṣaṃ vibhajate -
nityeti/ pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayaparamāṇavaḥ ākāśādipañcakaṃ ca
nityadravyāṇi/
children.translated_text: He divides <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity) — '<s>nitya</s>' etc. The four ultimate atoms of earth and the rest, and the five [eternal substances] beginning with <s>ākāśa</s> (space) — these are the eternal substances.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: samavāyalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Samavāya</s> (Inherence)

children.text: AnTs_8 samavāyas tv eka eva //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 8:] <s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) is indeed one only.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
samavāyasya bhedo nāstītyāha -
samavāyastu iti/
children.translated_text: He states that there is no division of <s>samavāya</s> — '<s>samavāya</s> indeed' etc.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
samavāyasya bhedo
nāstīti/ na ca samavāyasyābhede sparśasamavāyavati vāyau
rūpavattāpratītiḥ syāditi śaṅkyam/ rūpasamavāyasattve 'pi rūpābhāvena
tathā pratīterabhāvāditi dik/
children.translated_text: That there is no division of <s>samavāya</s> — one should not doubt that if <s>samavāya</s> is non-different [i.e. one], then in wind (<s>vāyu</s>) which possesses the <s>samavāya</s> of touch, there should be a cognition of possessing color (<s>rūpa</s>). Because even when the <s>samavāya</s> of color exists [as non-different from samavāya in general], due to the absence of color [in wind], such a cognition does not arise — this is the indication.

children.text: bālapiyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
rūpavattāpratītiḥ syāditi/
sparśasamavāyasattvena tadabhinnasya rūpasamavāyasyāpi sattvāt
rūpasamavāyasyaiva rūpavattāpratītiniyāmakatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
rūpasamavāyo na rūpavattāpratītiniyāmakaḥ, api tu samavāyasambandhena
rūpam/
children.translated_text: 'There should be a cognition of possessing color' — because due to the existence of the <s>samavāya</s> of touch, the <s>samavāya</s> of color, being non-different from it, also exists; and since the <s>samavāya</s> of color alone is the determinant of the cognition of possessing color — this is the purport. The <s>samavāya</s> of color is not the determinant of the cognition of possessing color; rather, color through the relation of <s>samavāya</s> [is the determinant].

children.text:
vāyau tu na rūpamasti,
ato na rūpavattāpratītiprasaṅga ityāśayena samādhatte -
rūpasamavāyasattve 'pīti/ nanu vāyau rūpasamavāyasattve rūpaṃ nāstīti
vaktuṃ na śakyate sambandhasattāyāḥ sambandhisattāvyāpyatvādityāśaṅkyāha
- digiti/ ayamāśayaḥ - vāyvanuyogikatvaviśiṣṭaḥ
rūpapratiyogikatvaviśiṣṭaśca samavāyaḥ vāyau
rūpavattāpratītiniyāmakaḥ/ vāyvanuyogikatvaviśiṣṭasamavāye
rūpapratiyogikatvābhāvāt vāyū rūpavāniti pratītiḥ nāpādayituṃ
śakya iti/ adhikaṃ muktāvalīmañjūṣādau draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: But in wind, since color does not exist, the unwanted consequence of the cognition of possessing color does not arise — with this intent, he resolves: 'Even when the <s>samavāya</s> of color exists' etc. Now, if the <s>samavāya</s> of color exists in wind, one cannot say that color does not exist [there], since the existence of a relation is pervaded by the existence of the relata — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'this is the indication' (<s>dik</s>). The intent is: the <s>samavāya</s> qualified by having-wind-as-co-relatum and qualified by having-color-as-counter-positive is the determinant of the cognition 'wind possesses color.' Since in the <s>samavāya</s> qualified by having-wind-as-co-relatum, the qualification of having-color-as-counter-positive is absent, the cognition 'wind possesses color' cannot be produced. Further details should be consulted in the <s>Muktāvalīmañjūṣā</s> and other texts.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: abhāvavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of <s>Abhāva</s> (Absence)

children.text: AnTs_9 abhāvaś caturvidhaḥ / prāgabhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvo 'tyantābhāvo 'nyonyābhāvaś ceti //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 9:] <s>Abhāva</s> (absence) is fourfold: <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence), <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> (destructional absence), <s>atyantābhāva</s> (absolute absence), and <s>anyonyābhāva</s> (mutual absence).

children.text: abhāvaḥ caturvidhaḥ - prāgabhāvaḥ, pradhvaṃsābhāvaḥ, atyantābhāvaḥ, anyonyābhāvaśceti/
children.translated_text: <s>Abhāva</s> is fourfold: <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence), <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> (destructional absence), <s>atyantābhāva</s> (absolute absence), and <s>anyonyābhāva</s> (mutual absence).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
abhāvaṃ vibhajate -
abhāva iti/
children.translated_text: He divides <s>abhāva</s> (absence) — '<s>abhāva</s>' etc.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: pṛthivīnirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth)

children.text: AnTs_10[1] gandhavatī pṛthivī / sā dvividhā nityānityā ca / nityā paramāṇurūpā / anityā kāryarūpā / punas trividhā śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīram asmadādīnām / indriyaṃ gandhagrāhakaṃ ghrāṇaṃ nāsāgravarti / viṣayo mṛtpāṣāṇādiḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 10.1:] That which possesses smell (<s>gandha</s>) is earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>). It is twofold: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal [form] is in the form of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>). The non-eternal is in the form of products (<s>kārya</s>). [The non-eternal] is again threefold, due to the distinction of body (<s>śarīra</s>), sense-organ (<s>indriya</s>), and object (<s>viṣaya</s>). The body is [that] of ourselves and others. The sense-organ is the organ of smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), which grasps smell, situated at the tip of the nose. The object consists of clay, stone, and the like.

children.text: tatra gandhavatī pṛthivī/
children.translated_text: Among those [categories], earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is that which possesses smell (<s>gandha</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
tatroddeśakramānusārāt prathamaṃ pṛthivyāḥ lakṣaṇamāha - tatreti/
nāmnā padārthasaṅkīrtanamuddeśaḥ/ uddeśakrame ca sarvatra icchaiva
niyāmikā/
children.translated_text: Following the order of enumeration, he first states the definition of earth — 'among those.' Enumeration (<s>uddeśa</s>) is the mention of a category by name. And in the order of enumeration, desire alone is the determinant everywhere.

children.text:
nanu
surabhyasurabhyavayavārabdhe dravye parasparavirodhena
gandhānutpādādavyāptiḥ/ na ca tatra gandhapratītyanupapattiriti vācyam/
avayavagandhasyaiva tatra pratītisambhavena citragandhānaṅgīkārāt/ kiṃ
cotpannavinaṣṭaghaṭādāvavyāptiriti cet - na/
gandhasamānādhikaraṇadravyatvāparajātimattvasya vivakṣitatvāt/
children.translated_text: Now, in a substance produced from parts having pleasant and unpleasant [smells], since smell is not produced due to the mutual opposition [of those smells], there is under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>). Nor should it be said that the cognition of smell there is inexplicable — because since the smell of the parts alone can be cognized there, there is no need to accept composite smell (<s>citragandha</s>). Moreover, there is under-extension in a pot that has been produced and then destroyed — if thus objected: no, because what is intended is the possession of a lower <s>jāti</s> (<s>aparajātimatva</s>) that is co-located with the property <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood) that is co-located with smell.

children.text:
nanu jalādāvapi
gandhapratīterativyāptiriti cet - na/ anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ
pṛthivīgandhasyaiva tatra bhānāṅgīkārat/ nanu tathāpi kālasya
sarvādhāratayā sarveṣāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ kāle 'tivyāptiriti cet - na/
sarvādhāratāprayojakasambandhabhinnasambandhena lakṣaṇasya vivakṣitatvāt/
children.translated_text: Now, since smell is cognized even in water and the like, there is over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) — if thus objected: no, because through positive and negative concomitance, it is accepted that what is cognized there is only the smell of earth [transferred to water]. Now, even so, since time (<s>kāla</s>) is the substratum of everything, all definitions would over-extend to time — if thus objected: no, because the definition is intended with a relation different from the relation by which the property of being the substratum of everything is established.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
pṛthivīlakṣaṇasya
prāthamye bījamāha - tatreti/ pṛthivyādiṣu madhya ityarthaḥ/
gandhasamavāyikāraṇatāvacchedakatayā pṛthivītvajātisiddhiriti
bodhyam/ nāmneti/ tṛtīyārthaḥ abhedaḥ/ saṅkīrtanapadārthe
pratipādakaśabde 'nveti/ tathā ca vastupratipādakanāmamātramuddeśa
iti lakṣaṇaṃ paryavasyati/ atra ghaṭa iti pade 'tivyāptivāraṇāya
vastupadaṃ lakṣaṇīyavastuparam/ lakṣaṇīyasya pṛthivyādeḥ sāmānyataḥ
pratipādakaprameyapade 'tivyāpitavāraṇāya nāmapadaṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakāvacchinnaparam/ lakṣaṇavākye nāmasattvāt
ativyāptivāraṇāya mātrapadamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: He states the basis for the priority of the definition of earth — 'among those.' The meaning is: among earth and the rest. It should be understood that the <s>jāti</s> of <s>pṛthivītva</s> (earth-hood) is established through its being the delimitor of non-inherent-cause-hood of smell. 'By name' — the meaning of the instrumental case is identity. The word 'mention' (<s>saṅkīrtana</s>) applies to the designating word, which is the means of cognition. And accordingly, the definition resolves to: enumeration is merely the name that conveys the entity. To prevent over-extension in the word 'pot' [being considered an enumeration], the word 'entity' (<s>vastu</s>) refers to the entity that is to be defined. To prevent over-extension in the general cognitive term '<s>prameya</s>' (knowable), which conveys earth and the like in general, the word 'name' refers to what is delimited by the delimitor of defined-ness. To prevent over-extension, since names occur even in definition-sentences, the word 'merely' (<s>mātra</s>) [is added]. This should be noted.

children.text:
ārabdhe - janye/
parasparavirodheneti/ surabhigandhaṃ prati asurabhigandhasya
asurabhigandhaṃ prati surabhigandhasya pratibandhakatvenetyarthaḥ/
pratītyanupapattiriti/ ataścitragandha evāpratibadhyaḥ svīkārya iti
bhāvaḥ/ avayavagandhasyaiveti/ svāśrayasamavetatvasambandhenetyādiḥ/
tuṣyatu durjana iti nyāyenāṅgīkṛtyāha - kiṃ ceti/
jalatvādikamādāya ativyāptivāraṇāya gandhasamānādhikaraṇeti/
sattāvāraṇāya dravyatvāpareti dravyatvanyūnavṛttītyarthakam/ teda
dravyatvavyudāsaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Produced' (<s>ārabdha</s>) means 'originated' (<s>janya</s>). 'Due to mutual opposition' — the meaning is: because the pleasant smell is an obstructor of the unpleasant smell, and the unpleasant smell is an obstructor of the pleasant smell. 'Inexplicability of cognition' — hence composite smell, which is unobstructed, should be accepted. This is the purport. 'Of the smell of the parts alone' — [the cognition is] through the relation of being co-inhered with its own locus, and so forth. Accepting [the objection] in the manner of 'let the ill-intentioned be satisfied,' he says: 'Moreover.' Taking <s>jalatva</s> (water-hood) and the like [as counter-examples], to prevent over-extension [he adds] 'co-located with smell.' To exclude <s>sattā</s> (existence) [he adds] 'lower <s>jāti</s> co-located with <s>dravyatva</s>' — meaning: a <s>jāti</s> with narrower extension than <s>dravyatva</s>. By this, <s>dravyatva</s> is excluded.

children.text:
gandhapratīteriti/
surabhi jalamityādipratīterityarthaḥ/ pṛthivīgandhasyaiveti/
svāśrayasaṃyuktatvasambandhenetyādiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Cognition of smell' — the meaning is: the cognition such as 'the water is fragrant' and the like. 'Of the smell of earth alone' — [cognized] through the relation of being conjoined with its own locus, and so forth.

children.text:
tatra - jalādau/
yathāśrutagrāhī śaṅkate - nanviti/ anugatarūpeṇa
lakṣaṇatāghaṭakasambandhān niveśya kālādāvativyāptiṃ vārayati -
sarvādhāreti/ vassutastu samavāyādīnāṃ samavāyatvādinaiva
saṃsargatayā tenaiva rūpeṇa tattatsambandhasya tattallakṣaṇaghaṭakatvaṃ
bodhyam/
children.translated_text: 'There' means in water and the like. The literal-minded objector raises the doubt — 'Now.' Having incorporated the relation that constitutes the definition-hood in the form of a pervading character, he refutes the over-extension to time and the like — 'the substratum of everything.' In reality, since <s>samavāya</s> and the like have their relational character through <s>samavāyatva</s> (inherence-hood) itself, the constitution of each particular relation in each particular definition should be understood in that very form.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
gandhasamavāyikāraṇatāvacchedakatayeti/
'samavāyasambandhāvacchinnagandhatvāvacchinnagandhāniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitatādātmyasambandhāvacchinnapṛthivīniṣṭhakāraṇatā
kiṃyiddharmāvacchinnā kāraṇatātvāt kapālaniṣṭhaghaṭakāraṇatāvat'
ityanumānaprayogo 'tra vivakṣitaḥ/ nāmnā padārthasaṅkīrtanamuddeśa
iti mūlam/ padārthasya saṅkīrtanaṃ padārthasaṅkīrtanam/
saṅkīrtanaśabdasya pratipādakaśabda ityarthaḥ/
padārthaviṣayakajñānakaśabdaḥ padārthasaṅkīrtanamiti yāvat/
padārthaśabdo vastuparaḥ/ nāmneti tṛtīyārthasya abhedasya
śabde 'nvayāt nāmābhinnaḥ vastuviṣayakajñānajanakaśabdaḥ uddeśaḥ iti
phalati/ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśakāladigātmamanāṃsītyatra
pṛthivyādiśabdānāṃ pṛthivyādivastupratipādakatvāt nāmatvācca
uddeśalakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ ghaṭa iti padasyāpi vastupratipādakatvāt
nāmatvācca tatroddeśalakṣaṇasyātivyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: as the delimitor of the causality of smell through inherence — the inferential application intended here is: 'The causality residing in earth, delimited by the relation of identity, which determines the effect-hood residing in smell delimited by smell-ness and qualified by the relation of inherence, is delimited by some property — because it is a causality, like the causality residing in the potsherd for the pot.' The root text states: '<s>Uddeśa</s> (enumeration) is the designation of a category by name.' The designation of a category is the category-designation. The meaning of the word 'designation' (<s>saṅkīrtana</s>) is: a word that conveys [the category]. That is, a word that generates knowledge regarding a category is category-designation. The word 'category' (<s>padārtha</s>) here refers to an entity. Since the meaning of the instrumental case is identity, its connection with the word [gives]: an <s>uddeśa</s> is a word that is identical with a name and generates knowledge regarding an entity. In 'earth, water, fire, air, space, time, direction, self, mind,' since the words 'earth' and the like convey the entities earth and the like, and since they are names, the definition of <s>uddeśa</s> applies. But since the word 'pot' also conveys an entity and is a name, there is over-extension of the definition of <s>uddeśa</s> to it.

children.text:
tadvāraṇāya vastupadaṃ
lakṣaṇīyavastuparaṃ vaktavyam/ ghaṭādipadaṃ ca na tādaśamiti
nātivyāptiḥ/ prameyamiti padasyāpi
lakṣaṇīyapṛthivyādipratipādakatvāt tatrātivyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
vastupadaṃ lakṣyatāvacchedakāvacchinnavastuparaṃ vācyam/ prameyapadasya
prameyatvāvacchinnapṛthivyādibodhakatve 'pi
lakṣyatāvacchedakapṛthivītvādyavacchinnapṛthivyādibodhakatvābhāvānnātivyāptiḥ/
'tatra gandhavatī pṛthivī' ityādilakṣaṇavākyaghaṭakapṛthivīpadasyāpi
pṛthivītvāvacchinnabodhakatvāt nāmatvācca tasyoddeśatvāpattiḥ/
tadvāraṇāya nāmamātramityapi vaktavyam/ mātrapadena
lakṣaṇādivācakapadāsamabhivyāhṛtatvamucyate/ tathā ca
children.translated_text: To avert that, the word 'entity' (<s>vastu</s>) should be stated as referring to the entity that is the object of definition. And since the word 'pot' and the like are not such [definable entities], there is no over-extension. But since the word '<s>prameya</s>' (knowable) also conveys the definable entities earth and the like, there is over-extension to it. To avert that, the word 'entity' should be stated as referring to an entity delimited by the delimitor of definiendum-ness. Although the word '<s>prameya</s>' generates knowledge of earth and the like as delimited by <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability), since it does not generate knowledge of earth and the like as delimited by earth-ness etc. which is the delimitor of definiendum-ness, there is no over-extension. But since the word 'earth' (<s>pṛthivī</s>) in the definitional sentence 'There, earth possesses smell' also generates knowledge delimited by earth-ness and is a name, the unwanted consequence of its being an <s>uddeśa</s> arises. To avert that, [the qualification] 'mere name' should also be stated. By the word 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>), what is meant is: not being co-expressed with words denoting the definition and the like. And accordingly,

children.text:
lakṣyatāvacchedakaprakārakalakṣyaviśeṣyakajñānajanaka -
lakṣaṇādivācakapadāsamabhivyāhṛtanāmābhinnaḥ śabdaḥ uddeśaḥ iti
niṣkarṣaḥ/ tadāha - tṛtīyārtho 'bheda ityādinā/ saṅkīrtane
ityasya vivaraṇaṃ pratipādakaśabde iti/ sāmānyata iti/
prameyatvarūpasāmānyadharmeṇetyarthaḥ/ tṛtīyāyāḥ pratipattyanvayi
1prakāratvamarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the conclusion is: an <s>uddeśa</s> is a word identical with a name, not co-expressed with words denoting the definition and the like, that generates knowledge having the delimitor of definiendum-ness as qualifier-mode and the definiendum as qualificand. This is stated with 'The meaning of the instrumental is identity' and so forth. The explanation of 'designation' (<s>saṅkīrtana</s>) is 'a word that conveys.' 'In general' — the meaning is: through a general property in the form of <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability). The meaning of the instrumental case is qualifier-mode-hood in the cognition generated.

children.text:
gandhavattvasya
pṛthivīlakṣaṇatve
surabhigandhayuktāvayavāsurabhigandhayuktāvayavābhyāmutpanne dravye
kasyāpi gandhasyānutpādādavyāptiḥ/ na ca
avayavagatagandharūpasyāsamavāyikāraṇasya sattvāt kuto gandho
notpadyata iti śaṅkanīyam/ surabhigandhasya asurabhigandhaṃ prati
asurabhigandhasya surabhigandhaṃ prati pratibandhakatvena kasyāpi gandhasya
tatrotpattyasambhavāt/ na ca yadi tatra gandho notpadyate, tarhi kathaṃ tatra
gandhaḥ pratīyeta, atastatra parasparaṃ pratibandhāt
children.translated_text: If <s>gandhavatva</s> (smell-possession) were the definition of earth, there would be under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) in a substance produced from a component possessing fragrant smell and a component possessing non-fragrant smell, since no smell whatsoever arises in it. Nor should one object: since the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) in the form of smell residing in the component exists, why would smell not arise? — because, since fragrant smell obstructs non-fragrant smell and non-fragrant smell obstructs fragrant smell, the arising of any smell there is impossible. Nor [should one say]: if smell does not arise there, then how is smell cognized there? — therefore, since there is mutual obstruction,

children.text:
1. prakāratvamarya
iti/ tathā ca
prameyatvarūpasāmānyavarmaprakārakapṛthivyādiviśeṣyakajñānajanake
prameyapade ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Qualifier-mode-hood is the meaning' — and accordingly, in the word '<s>prameya</s>' which generates knowledge having the general property in the form of <s>prameyatva</s> as qualifier-mode and earth and the like as qualificand — this is the meaning.

children.text:
surabhigandhaḥ
asurabhigandho vā notpadyatām, citragandha utpadyatām, tena
gandhapratītirupadyate, gandhavattāsattvādavyāptiśca neti vācyam/
avayavagatagandhasyaiva svāśrayasamavetatvasambandhena avayavini
pratītisambhave citragandhasyānaṅgīkārāt/ tathā ca
tatrāvyāptitādavasthyam/ kiṃ ca yo ghaṭaḥ prathamakṣaṇe utpannaḥ atha
dvitīyakṣaṇe vinaṣṭaḥ tasmin ghaṭe avyāptiḥ, prathamakṣaṇe 'utpannaṃ dravyaṃ
kṣaṇamaguṇam' iti nyāyena gandhavirahāt/ dvitīyakṣaṇe dharmiṇa eva
nāśāt ityāśayena śaṅkate - dīpikāyām nanu
surabhyasurabhīti/
children.translated_text: let fragrant smell or non-fragrant smell not arise — let mixed smell (<s>citragandha</s>) arise, and by that the cognition of smell would arise and there would be no under-extension of smell-possession — this should not be said. Because when the cognition of the smell residing in the component is possible in the composite through the relation of being co-inherent with its substratum, mixed smell need not be accepted. And accordingly, the under-extension remains as before. Moreover, in a pot that was produced at the first moment and destroyed at the second moment, there is under-extension, since at the first moment it lacks smell by the principle 'A produced substance is quality-less for a moment,' and at the second moment the substrate itself is destroyed — with this intent, the doubt is raised in the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'Now, fragrant and non-fragrant' and so forth.

children.text:
gandhasamānādhikaraṇeti/ gandhādhikaraṇavṛttiḥ dravyatvavyāpyā ca
yā jātiḥ tadvattvaṃ pṛthivyāḥ lakṣaṇam/ gandhādhikaraṇaṃ puṣpāditadvṛttiḥ
dravyatvavyāpyā jātiḥ pṛthivītvajātiḥ tadvattvaṃ
surabhyasurabhyavayavārabdhe dravye utpannavinaṣṭaghaṭe cāstīti
nāvyāptiḥ/ dravyatvavyāpyajātimattvamātroktau dravyatvavyāpyā yā
jalatvajātiḥ tadvattvasya jale sattvāt tatrātivyāptiḥ/ ato
gandhasamānādhikaraṇeti/ jalatvasya gandhādhikaraṇavṛttitvābhāvāt na
doṣaḥ/ gandhasamānādhikaraṇajātimattvamātroktau
gandhādhikaraṇapṛthivīvṛttiḥ yā sattājātiḥ tadvattvasya jalādau sattvāt
ativyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya dravyatvavyāpyeti jātiviśeṣaṇam/ nanu
dravyatvavyāpyeti viśeṣaṇe datte 'pi
dravyatvajātimādāyajalādiṣvativyāptiḥ durvārā/ dravyatvasya
gandhādhikaraṇapṛthivīvṛttitvāt dravyatvaśūnyavṛttitvācceti cet -
na/ prakṛte dravyatvavyāpyatvaṃ na dravyatvaśūnayāvṛttitvam kiṃ tu
dravyatvanyūnavṛttitvarūpam/ dravyatvaṃ ca na dravyatvanyūnavṛtti
ityāśayāt/ dravyatvanyūnavṛttitvaṃ ca
1dravyatvasamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvam/ tadāha -
prakāśikāyām jalatvādikamādāyetyādi/
children.translated_text: 'Co-located with smell' (<s>gandhasamānādhikaraṇa</s>) — thus. The definition of earth is: possessing a universal that occurs in the substratum of smell and is pervaded by substance-hood. The substratum of smell is a flower and the like; a universal that occurs in it and is pervaded by substance-hood is the universal earth-ness (<s>pṛthivītva</s>); possessing that exists in substances produced from components with fragrant and non-fragrant smells, and also in a pot that was produced and destroyed — hence there is no under-extension. If only 'possessing a universal pervaded by substance-hood' were stated, since the universal water-ness (<s>jalatva</s>), which is pervaded by substance-hood, and possessing that exists in water, there would be over-extension there. Hence 'co-located with smell.' Since water-ness does not occur in the substratum of smell, there is no defect. If only 'possessing a universal co-located with smell' were stated, since the universal existence (<s>sattā</s>), which occurs in earth that is a substratum of smell, and possessing that exists in water and the like, there would be over-extension. To avert that, the qualifier 'pervaded by substance-hood' is added to the universal. Now, even with the qualifier 'pervaded by substance-hood,' the over-extension to water and the like by taking the universal substance-hood itself is unavoidable — since substance-hood occurs in earth which is the substratum of smell, and since substance-hood also occurs in what lacks substance-hood [i.e., this seems contradictory] — if one objects thus: no. In the present context, 'pervasion by substance-hood' (<s>dravyatvavyāpyatva</s>) does not mean non-occurrence in what lacks substance-hood, but rather has the form of occurrence no less extensive than substance-hood. And substance-hood itself does not have occurrence no less extensive than substance-hood — this is the intent. And 'occurrence no less extensive than substance-hood' means being the delimitor of the counter-positive-ness of a difference co-located with substance-hood. This is stated in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'By taking water-ness and the like' and so forth.

children.text:
1.
dravyatvasamānādhikaraṇeti/ dravyatvādhikaraṇaṃ jalaṃ tadvṛttiryo bheda
pṛthivībhedaḥ tatpratiyogitāvacchedakatvāt pṛthivītvasya
dravyatvanyūnavṛttitvam/ dravyatvaṃ tu na
dravyatvādhikaraṇavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakaṃ dravyabhedasya
dravyatvādhikaraṇāvṛttitvāditi dravyatvaṃ na dravyatvanyūnavṛttīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Co-located with substance-hood' — The substratum of substance-hood is water; a difference that occurs in it is the difference from earth; since earth-ness is the delimitor of the counter-positive-ness of that [difference], earth-ness has occurrence no less extensive than substance-hood. But substance-hood is not the delimitor of the counter-positive-ness of a difference occurring in the substratum of substance-hood — because the difference from substance does not occur in the substratum of substance-hood. Hence substance-hood does not have occurrence no less extensive than substance-hood — this is the purport.

children.text:
dīpikāyām nanu
jalādāvapi gandhapratīteriti/ tathā ca gandhavattvarūpasya pṛthivīlakṣaṇasya
jalādau ativyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ anvayavyatirekābhyāmiti/ jalādau
gandhavatpṛthivīsaṃyogasattve gandhapratītiḥ tadabhāve tadabhāva
ityanvayavyatirekābhyāmityarthaḥ/
