children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'Now, even in water and the like, the cognition of smell' — and accordingly, over-extension of the definition of earth in the form of smell-possession to water and the like — this is the purport. 'Through positive and negative concomitance' (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) — the meaning is: when the contact of earth possessing smell with water and the like is present, the cognition of smell is present; when it is absent, that [cognition] is absent — through such positive and negative concomitance.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām
svāśrayasaṃyuktatvasambandheneti/ svaṃ pṛthivīgandhaḥ, svāśrayaḥ pṛthivī,
tatsaṃyuktatvaṃ jalādau/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'Through the relation of being conjoined with its substratum' — 'its own' means the smell of earth; 'its substratum' is earth; 'being conjoined with that' exists in water and the like.

children.text:
yathāśrutagrāhī -
sambandhaviśeṣānavacchinnaṃ gandhavattvameva lakṣaṇamityabhimānavān/
anugatarūpeṇasarvādhāratāprayojakasambandhabhinnasambanghatvenetyarthaḥ/
kālikādisambandhaḥ sarvādhāratāprayojakaḥ tadbhinnasambandhatvaṃ
samavāyādau/ lakṣaṇatāghaṭakasambandhāt lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhān
samavāyādīn/ samavāyādīnāṃ samavāyatvādinaiva saṃsargatayeti/
spaṣṭaṃ cedam vyadhikaraṇagādādharyām/
children.translated_text: 'One who grasps the literal meaning' — means one who holds the view that smell-possession without qualification by a specific relation is itself the definition. 'Through a relation other than the relation that effects universality of substratum-hood' — this is the meaning. The temporal relation and the like effect universality of substratum-hood; a relation other than those — such as inherence and the like. [These are:] from the relation that constitutes the defining character, the relations that delimit the defining character, namely inherence and the like. Inherence and the like, through their inherence-ness and the like, function as the relational [qualifier] — this should be clearly understood from the <s>Vyadhikaraṇagādādharī</s>.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: pṛthivīvibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of Earth

children.text: AnTs_10[2] sā dvividhā nityānityā ca / nityā paramāṇurūpā / anityā kāryarūpā / punas trividhā śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīram asmadādīnām / indriyaṃ gandhagrāhakaṃ ghrāṇaṃ nāsāgravarti / viṣayo mṛtpāṣāṇādiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_10[2]: It (earth) is of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of products. [The non-eternal] is again threefold, due to the distinction of body, sense-organ, and object. The body is that of ourselves and others. The sense-organ is the nose (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), which grasps smell, situated at the tip of the nose. The object is clay, stone, and the like.

children.text:
sā dvividhā -
nityā anityā ceti/ nityā paramāṇurūpā/ anityā kāryarūpā/
punastrividhā - śarīra-indriya-viṣayabhedāt/ śarīraṃ
asmadādīnām/ indriyaṃ gandhagrāhakaṃ ghrāṇam/ tacca nāsāgravarti/
viṣayo mṛtpāṣāṇādiḥ/
children.translated_text: It is of two kinds — eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of products. Again threefold — due to the distinction of body, sense-organ, and object. The body is that of ourselves and others. The sense-organ is the nose (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), which grasps smell. And that is situated at the tip of the nose. The object is clay, stone, and the like.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
pṛthivīṃ vibhajate -
sā dvividheti/ nityatvaṃ dhvaṃsāpratiyogitvam/ anityatvam
dhvaṃsapratiyogitvam/ prakārāntareṇa vibhajate - punariti/ ātmano
bhogāyatanaṃ śarīram/ yadavacchinnātmani bhogo jāyate
tadbhogāyatanam/ sukhaduḥkhānyatarasākṣātkāro bhogaḥ/
śabdetarodbhūtaviśeṣaguṇānāśrayatve sati
jñānakāraṇamanassaṃyogāśrayatvaṃ indriyatvam/ śarīrendriyabhinno
viṣayaḥ/ evaṃ ca gandhavaccharīraṃ pārthivaśarīram, gandhavadindriyaṃ
pārthivendriyam, gandhavān viṣayaḥ pārthivaviṣaya iti tattallakṣaṇaṃ
bodhyam/ pārthivaśarīraṃ darśayati-śarīramiti/ pārthivendriyaṃ
darśayati - indriyamiti/ gandhagrāhakamiti prayojanakathanam/
ghrāṇamiti saṃjñā/ nāsogretyāśrayoktiḥ/ evamuttaratra jñeyam/
pārthivaviṣayaṃ darśayati - mṛtpāṣāṇādi iti/
children.translated_text: He divides earth — 'It is of two kinds' and so forth. Eternality (<s>nityatva</s>) is the non-counter-positive-ness of destruction. Non-eternality (<s>anityatva</s>) is the counter-positive-ness of destruction. He divides in another manner — with 'again.' The body is the locus of experience of the self. That in which experience arises in the self delimited [by that body] is the locus of experience. Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is the direct apprehension of either pleasure or pain. Sense-organ-hood (<s>indriyatva</s>) is: being the locus of the contact with mind (<s>manas</s>) that is a cause of cognition, while being the substratum of manifest particular qualities other than those produced by sound. What is different from body and sense-organ is the object. And accordingly, an earthen body is a body possessing smell; an earthen sense-organ is a sense-organ possessing smell; an earthen object is an object possessing smell — thus the respective definitions should be understood. He shows the earthen body — with 'body.' He shows the earthen sense-organ — with 'sense-organ.' 'That which grasps smell' — this is the statement of function. '<s>Ghrāṇa</s>' — this is the designation. 'At the tip of the nose' — this is the statement of locus. The same should be understood for what follows. He shows the earthen object — with 'clay, stone, and the like.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nityapṛthivītvādirūpalakṣaṇagataṃ nityatvādi darśayati -
nityatvamiti/ prakārāntareṇeti/ pṛthivīmityanuṣajyate/ atra
nityapṛthivyāḥ śarīrendriyabhinnatvarūpaviṣayalakṣaṇākrāntatvena
viṣayāntargatatvamiti pṛthivyāstrividhatvam/ ata eva mūle
punastrividhetyuktiḥ saṅgacchate iti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: He shows the eternality and the like contained in the definition of eternal earth and the like — with 'eternality.' 'In another manner' — the word 'earth' is to be supplied from the preceding context. Here, since eternal earth, through being characterized by the definition of object in the form of being different from body and sense-organ, is included within objects, the threefold division of earth [holds]. For this very reason, the statement in the root text 'again threefold' is coherent — this should be noted.

children.text:
kecittu -
anityapṛthivyā eva traividhyaṃ varṇayanti/ uddeśakramānusāreṇa prathamaṃ
śarīralakṣaṇamāha - ātmana iti/ āyatanaṃ avacchedakam/ tathā ca
militaṃ yādṛśaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ sampannaṃ tādṛśamāha - yadavacchinneti/
sukhaduḥkhānyatarasākṣātkārāvacchedakam iti yāvat/ atra
antyāvayavitve satīti viśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ tena pādādīnāṃ
avacchedakatve 'pi tatra na ativyāptiḥ/ yathā śarīratvaṃ na jātiḥ,
pṛthivītvādinā saṅkarāt tathā indriyatvaṃ na
jātirityāśayenāha - śabdetarodbhūteti/
ātmādāvativyāptivāraṇāya satyantam/ śrotre 'vyāptivāraṇāya
śabdetareti/ cakṣurādau viśeṣaguṇasyānudbhūtarūpādeḥ
sattvenāvyaptivāraṇāya udbhūteti/ udbhūtatvaṃ na jātiḥ
śuklatvādinā sāṃkaryāt/ na ca śuklatvādivyāpyaṃ
nānaivodbhūtatvamiti vācyam/ cākṣuṣādau udbhūtarūpatvādinā
kāraṇatvānupapatteḥ/ kiṃ tu śuklatvādivyāpyaṃ anudbhūtatvaṃ nānā
tadabhāvakūṭavattvamudbhūtatvam/ tacca saṃyogādāvapi/ tathā ca
śabdetarodbhūtaguṇaṃ saṃyogamādāya asambhavavāraṇāya viśeṣeti/
kālādāvativyāptivāraṇāya viśeṣyadalam; tatraiva
ativyāptivāraṇāya jñānakāraṇeti/ prācīnamate
viṣayāvayavendriyāvayavasaṃyogasya pratyakṣakāraṇatayā tadāśrayasya
indriyāvayavasya, navīnamate kālādau rūpābhāvapratyakṣe
sannikarṣaghaṭakatayā kāraṇībhūtacakṣussaṃyogāśrayasya kālādeśca
vāraṇāya manaḥ padam/ na ca ātmānyatve sati ityanenaiva ātmani
ativyāptivāraṇasambhave kiṃ
gurutaraśabdetarodbhūtetyādiviśeṣaṇeneti vācyam/ tathā sati
carmamanassaṃyogasya jñānamātraṃ prati hetutvamate
tatrātivyāpterityalaṃ vistareṇa/ evaṃ ceti/ tattadarthaṃsya
śarīrādisāmānyalakṣaṇatve cetyarthaḥ/ nanu gandhavattvapraveśenaiva
tallakṣaṇasya sāmañjasye gandhagrāhakatvaniveśanamanucitam/ evaṃ ca
indriyaṃ gandhagrāhakam iti mūlamanucitaṃ ityāśaṅkāṃ
parijihīrṣuḥ tanmūlaṃ tatprayojanakathanaparatayā
vyācaṣṭe-gandhagrāhakamiti/ uttaratra indriyaṃ rasagrāhakam ityādau/
children.translated_text: Some, however, describe the threefold division as pertaining only to non-eternal earth. Following the order of enumeration, he first states the definition of body — '<s>ātmanaḥ</s>' (of the self), etc. '<s>Āyatana</s>' means delimitor. And accordingly, he states the complete definition as it is — 'that which is delimited by' etc. It means: the delimitor of the direct realization of either pleasure or pain. Here, the qualification 'being a terminal part' should be added — thereby, even though hands, feet, and the like are delimitors, there is no over-pervasion in them. Just as body-ness is not a universal (<s>jāti</s>) because of intermixture with earth-ness and the like, so too sense-organ-ness is not a universal — with this intent he says: 'of a manifest [quality] other than sound,' etc. The word '<s>satya</s>' (lit. 'being') is [added] to avert over-pervasion in the self and the like. 'Other than sound' is to avert non-pervasion in the ear. 'Manifest' (<s>udbhūta</s>) is to avert non-pervasion in the eye and the like, where the specific quality such as non-manifest form exists. Manifest-ness (<s>udbhūtatva</s>) is not a universal, because of intermixture with white-ness and the like. Nor should it be said that manifest-ness pervaded by white-ness and the like is indeed manifold — because if so, causality through manifest form and the like in visual and other perception would be unjustified. Rather, non-manifest-ness pervaded by white-ness and the like is manifold, and manifest-ness is the possession of the aggregate of absences of non-manifest-ness. And that [manifest-ness] exists even in conjunction and the like. And accordingly, to avert the impossibility [in the definition], taking conjunction as a manifest quality other than sound, [he adds] 'specific' (<s>viśeṣa</s>). The qualificand component is to avert over-pervasion in time and the like; the [qualifier] 'cause of cognition' is also to avert over-pervasion in the same [time]. On the ancient view, since the conjunction of parts of the object with parts of the sense organ has the status of being a cause of perception, the word '<s>manas</s>' (mind) is [added] to exclude the part of the sense organ which is the substratum of that [conjunction]; on the new view, to exclude time and the like, which are the substrata of the contact with the eye that functions as a component of the extraordinary perceptual contact in the perception of the absence of form in time and the like, being causal [in that perception]. Nor should it be said: 'Since the qualification "being other than the self" alone would suffice to avert over-pervasion in the self, what is the need for the more cumbersome qualifications "manifest," "other than sound," etc.?' — for if so, on the view that the conjunction of skin with mind has causality with respect to cognition in general, there would be over-pervasion in that [skin]. Enough with elaboration. 'And thus' — the meaning is: if such-and-such a purpose [of each term] constitutes the general definition of body, sense organs, etc. Now, since the definition would already be adequate with the inclusion of smell-possession alone, the inclusion of smell-apprehending capacity is inappropriate. And accordingly, the root text 'the sense organ is smell-apprehending' would be inappropriate — wishing to address this doubt, he explains the purpose of that root text by commenting: 'smell-apprehending' etc. In the subsequent [discussion] 'the sense organ apprehends taste' and so forth.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu 'punaḥ
trividhā śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt' iti ganthena kiṃ
pṛthivīsāmānyasya tredhā vibhāga ucyate kiṃ vā anityapṛthivyāḥ/ nādyaḥ,
pṛthivīsāmānyasya yadyayaṃ vibhāgaḥ syāt tarhi nityapṛthivyā api
śarīrendriyaviṣayeṣu kvacidantarbhāvo vācyamaḥ/ sa ca na sambabhavati/
tathā hi - na tāvat nityapṛthivyāḥ śarīre 'ntarbhāvaḥ sambhavati, nāpi
children.translated_text: Now, by the text 'Again, it is threefold, due to the distinction of body, sense organ, and object,' is the threefold division stated of earth in general, or of non-eternal earth? Not the first — for if this were a division of earth in general, then eternal earth too would have to be included somewhere among body, sense organs, and objects. And that is not possible. For indeed, eternal earth

children.text:
indriye/
tayorubhayorapyanityatvāt/ nāpi viṣaye, mṛtpāṣāṇādirūpasya
viṣayasya nityatvābhāvāt/ na dvitīyaḥ, punastrividheti punaḥśabdena
pūrvaṃ vibhaktasyaiva vibhāgāntaraṃ kriyata iti sūcanāt
ityāśaṅkya āha-atra nityapṛthivyā ityādinā/ evaṃ ca
pṛthivīsāmānyasyaiva punastredhā vibhāgaḥ/ nityapṛthivyāḥ
śarīrendriyabhinnatvāt viṣaye antarbhāṃva iti nānupapattiriti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: is not [included] in sense organs — because both [body and sense organs] are non-eternal. Nor in objects — because objects in the form of clay, stones, and the like are not eternal. Not the second [interpretation] either, since the word 'punaḥ' (again) indicates that what was previously divided is being divided again — anticipating this objection, he says: 'here, of eternal earth' and so forth. And thus, the threefold division is indeed of earth in general again. The inclusion of eternal earth

children.text:
nanu kathañcidatra
nirvāhe 'pi tejaḥ prakaraṇe punastrividhamiti na saṅgacchate/
nityatejasaḥ paramāṇurūpasya bhaumadivyodaryākarajeṣu caturṣu
viṣayeṣvantarbhāvāsambhavāt/ janyatvaghaṭitabhaumatvādeḥ
nityayejasyasaṃbhavāt/ ataḥ anityapṛthivyā evāyaṃ vibhāgaḥ/
punaḥśabdaśca vākyālaṅkāra iti nānupapattirityāśayānānāṃ
matamāha - kecittu iti/ kecidityasvarasodbhāvanam/ tadbījaṃ
tu punaḥśabdāsvārasyāt nānityapṛthivyā ayaṃ vibhāgaḥ/ na ca sa
vākyālaṅkāra iti
children.translated_text: Now, even if this can somehow be reconciled here, in the section on fire, 'again threefold' does not work — because the eternal fire in the form of atoms cannot be included among the four types of objects: earthly, celestial, stomachic, and mineral. Since earthly-ness and the like, which involve the component of being produced, are impossible for eternal fire. Therefore, this division pertains only to non-eternal earth. And the word 'punaḥ' is merely a rhetorical ornament (<s>vākyālaṅkāra</s>) — this should not be said,

children.text:
vācyam/ vākyādau
prayuktasya punaḥśabdasya vākyālaṅkāratāyāḥ kutrāpyadṛṣṭacaratvāt/
yatkiñcitpadottaraṃ prayujyamānasyaiva punaḥśabdasya
vākyālaṅkāratāyāstatra tatra dṛṣṭatvāt/ kiṃ ca punaśśabdasya
prakārāntaraparatvameva annambhaṭṭasyāpi saṃmatam/ 'prakārāntareṇa
vibhajate - punastrividheti' ityavataraṇikādānāt/ na ca
pṛthivīsāmānyasyātra vibhāga iti kathañcit upapādane 'pi
tejaḥprakaraṇe 'nupapattiriti vācyam/ tatra bhaumādiśabdānāṃ
bhūmisambandhi ityādyevārthaḥ, na tu bhūmijanyamiti/ tathā ca
paramāṇurūpatejaso 'pi bhūmisambandhitvāderakṣatatayā
viṣayāntarbhāvo yujyata iti/
children.translated_text: because the use of the word 'punaḥ' at the beginning of a sentence as a mere rhetorical ornament is not attested anywhere. For it is only when 'punaḥ' is used after some other word that its function as a rhetorical ornament is observed in various places. Moreover, even <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s> himself accepts that 'punaḥ' means 'in another manner.' 'He divides in another manner — "again, threefold"' — this

children.text:
ātmano bhogāyatanaṃ
śarīramiti śarīralakṣaṇam/ ātmapadottaraṣaṣṭhyāḥ samavetatvamarthaḥ/
tasya bhoge 'nvayaḥ/ bhogo nāma sukhaduḥkhānyatarasākṣātkāraḥ/
āyatanamavacchedakam/ tathā ca
ātmasamavetasukhaduḥkhānyatarasākṣatkārāvacchedakaṃ śarīramityuktaṃ
bhavati/ idaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ hastapādādau śarīrāvayave 'tivyāptam/
hastapādādyavacchedenāpi ātmani
sukhaduḥkhānyatarasākṣātkārasyotpādāt/ ataḥ antyāvayavitve satīti
viśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ antyāvayavitvaṃ nāma dravyānārambhakatve sati
avayavitvam/ hastādeḥ śarīrārambhakatayā satyantābhāvāt
nātivyāptiḥ/ tadāha - sukhaduḥkhānyatarasākṣātkārāvacchedakamiti
yāvadityādinā pṛthivītvādinā saṅkarāditi/ śarīratvaṃ vihāya
pṛthivītvaṃ ghaṭādau, pṛthivītvaṃ vihāya śarīratvaṃ jalīyādiśarīre/
ubhayoḥ pārthivaśarīre samāveśāt saṅkara iti bhāvaḥ/ tathā
indriyatvaṃ na jātiriti/ pṛthivītvaṃ vihāya indriyatvaṃ
rasanādau / indriyatvaṃ vihāya pṛthivītvaṃ ghaṭādau, ubhayoḥ
samāveśaḥ ghrāṇendriyo ityevaṃ pṛthivītvādinā saṅkarāt
indriyatvaṃ na jātiriti bhāvaḥ/ ātmādāvativyāptivāraṇāya
satyantamiti/
jñānakāraṇamanassaṃyogāśrayatvamindriyatvamityetāvanmātroktau
jñānakāraṇībhūto yaḥ manassaṃyogaḥ ātmamanassaṃyogaḥ tadāśrayatvaṃ
ātmanyapyastīti tatrātivyāptiḥ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya satyantam/
tanniveśe ca śabdetaro yaḥ udbhūtaviśeṣaguṇaḥ jñānasukhādiḥ
tadāśrayatvasyaivātmani sattvāt nātivyāptiḥ ityarthaḥ/
udbhūtaviśaṣaguṇe śabdetara iti viśeṣaṇādāne śabdarūpaḥ yaḥ
udbhūtaviśeṣaguṇaḥ tadāśrayatvameva śrotrendriye 'sti na
tadanāśrayatvamityavyāptiḥ/ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya śabdetareti
viśeṣaṇam/ viśeṣaguṇe udbhūteti viśeṣaṇādāne cakṣurādau
śabdetaraḥ yaḥ viśeṣaguṇaḥ anudbhūtarūpādiḥ
tadāśrayatvamevāstītyavyāptiḥ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya udbhūteti
viśeṣaṇam/ viśeṣapadamanupādāya
śabdetarodbhūtaguṇānāśrayatvamityetāvanmātroktau śabdetaraḥ yaḥ
saṃyogākhyaḥ sāmānyaguṇaḥ tadāśrayatvasyaiva sattvāt
cakṣurādīndriyeṣvasabhbhavaḥ syāt; tadvāraṇāya viśeṣapadam/
children.translated_text: 'The body is the locus of the self's experience' — this is the definition of body. The genitive case after the word 'self' means 'inhering in.' Its connection is with 'experience.' Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) means the direct realization of either pleasure or pain. 'Locus' (<s>āyatana</s>) means delimitor. And accordingly, what is stated amounts to: the body is the delimitor of the direct realization of either pleasure or pain that inheres in the self. This definition, in hands, feet, and other parts of the body,

children.text:
nanu
viśeṣapadānupādāne 'pi saṃyogo nopādātu śakyate/
tasyodbhūtatvābhāvāt udbhūtapadenaiva tadvāraṇāt
ityāśaṅkyāha - udbhūtatvaṃ na jātirityādinā/ udbhūtatvaṃ
vihāya śuklatvaṃ anudbhūtaśukle, śuklatvaṃ vihāya udbhūtatvaṃ
udbhūtanīle, ubhayoḥ udbhūtatvaśuklatvayoḥ udbhūtaśukle samāveśa
iti sāṃkaryāt udbhūtatvaṃ na jātiḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, even without including the word 'specific' (<s>viśeṣa</s>), conjunction cannot be included [as a problematic case], because conjunction lacks manifest-ness, and the word 'manifest' (<s>udbhūta</s>) itself excludes it — anticipating this objection, he says: 'manifest-ness is not a universal,' etc. Setting aside manifest-ness, white-ness [is present] in a non-manifest white; setting aside white-ness, manifest-ness [is present] in a manifest blue; both manifest-ness and white-ness [are present] in a manifest white — since there is such mutual inclusion, there is intermixture (<s>sāṃkarya</s>);

children.text:
na ca śuklatvavyāpyam
udbhūtatvamanyat nīlatvavyāpyamudbhūtatvamānyat ityevaṃ
śuklatvādivyāpyaṃ udbhūtatvaṃ nānaiva/ tathā ca śuklatvaṃ vihāya
udbhūtatvaṃ nāstīti na saṃkara iti vācyam/ udbhūtatvasya
nānātve cākṣuṣādipratyakṣaṃ prati
children.translated_text: nor should it be said that manifest-ness pervaded by white-ness is one thing, manifest-ness pervaded by blue-ness is another, and thus manifest-ness pervaded by white-ness and the like is indeed manifold — and accordingly, since manifest-ness does not exist apart from white-ness, there is no intermixture. For if manifest-ness were manifold, visual and other perception being caused by

children.text:
udbhūtarūpaṃ
kāraṇamityevamanugatakāryakāraṇabhāvasya bhaṅgaprasaṅgāt/ ataḥ
śuklādibhedena tadvṛtti anudbhūtatvaṃ nānā/
anudbhūtatvābhāvakūṭavattvameva codbhūtatvam/ tadeva ca lakṣaṇe
niveśitam/ tacca sayoge 'pyasti/ saṃyogo hi nānudbhūta iti
anudbhūtatvābhāvakūṭavattvasya tatra sattvāt/ tathā ca
1niruktodbhūtatvāśrayasaṃyogāśrayatvamevendriyeṣvastītyasaṃbhavavāraṇāya
viśeṣapadamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: manifest form — such a uniform causal relation would be liable to break down. Therefore, non-manifest-ness is manifold according to the distinctions of white, etc. And manifest-ness is precisely the possession of the aggregate of absences of non-manifest-ness. And that alone is what is incorporated in the definition. And that exists even in conjunction — for conjunction is not non-manifest, and hence the possession of the aggregate of absences of non-manifest-ness obtains there. And accordingly,

children.text:
kālādāvativyāptivāraṇāya viśeṣyadalamiti/
jñānakāraṇamanassaṃyogāśrayatvamiti viśeṣyadalasyānupādāne kāle
kasyāpi viśeṣaguṇasyābhāvāt
śabdetarodbhūtaviśeṣaguṇānāśrayatvamastīti ativyāptiḥ syāt/
viśeṣyadale upātte tu jñānakāraṇībhūto yaḥ manassaṃyogaḥ
ātmamanassaṃyogaḥ manaindriyasaṃyogo vā tadāśrayatvaṃ kāle
nāstīti nātivyāptiḥ iti bhāvaḥ/ manassaṃyoge jñānakāraṇeti
viśeṣaṇasya prayojanamaha - tatraiveti/ kālasya vibhutayā vibhutvasya
sarvamūrtadravyasaṃyogitvarūpatayā manassaṃyogāśrayatvamastīti kāle
ativyāptivāraṇāya jñānakāraṇetyuktam/ kālānuyogikasya
manassaṃyogasya jñānakāraṇatvābhāvāt nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: the qualificand component is to avert over-pervasion in time and the like. If the qualificand component 'substratum of a mind-conjunction that is a cause of cognition' were not included, then since no specific quality exists in time, the property 'not being the substratum of a manifest specific quality other than sound' would obtain in time — and there would be over-pervasion. But when the qualificand component is included, the mind-conjunction that is a cause of cognition — either the self-mind conjunction or the mind-sense-organ conjunction — its substratum

children.text:
manaḥpadasya matabhedena
prayojanamāha - prācīnamata iti/ manaḥpadamanupādāya
jñānakāraṇasaṃyogāśrayatvamityetāvanmātroktau prācīnamate viṣayasya
indriyāvayavasya ca yaḥ saṃyogaḥ tasyāpi jñānakāraṇatayā
tadāśrayatvasya indriyāvayave sattvāt tatra ativyāptiḥ/ navīnamate
viṣayendriyasaṃyogasyaiva jñānakāraṇatvamiti yadyapi
indriyāvayave 'tivyāptiḥ na sambhavati/ tathāpi kāle rūpaṃ nāstīti
kālaviśeṣaṇakarūpābhāvaviśeṣyakapratyakṣe
cakṣussaṃyuktakālanirūpitaviśeṣyatāyāḥ saṃnikarṣavidhayā
children.translated_text: He states the purpose of the word 'mind' (<s>manas</s>) according to different views — 'on the ancient view,' etc. If, without including the word 'mind,' only 'substratum of a conjunction that is a cause of cognition' were stated, then on the ancient view, since the conjunction of the object with the part of the sense organ also has the status of being a cause of cognition, and the part of the sense organ possesses such substratum-hood, there would be over-pervasion in it. On the new view,

children.text:
kāraṇatvāt
tadghaṭakacakṣussaṃyogasyāpi kāraṇatvāt jñānakāraṇībhūto yaḥ
cakṣussaṃyogaḥ tadāśrayatvaṃ kāle 'stītyativyāptiḥ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya
manaḥpadam/ tathā sati viṣayendriyāvayavasaṃyogasya vā
kālacakṣussaṃyogasya vā manassaṃyogatvaṃ nāstīti na tāvādāya
pūrvoktātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ pūrvaṃ satyantānupādāne ātmani
ativyāptirityuktam/ sā ca
children.translated_text: since the object-sense-organ conjunction itself has causality, and since the eye-conjunction that is a component thereof also has causality, the substratum-hood of the eye-conjunction that is a cause of cognition would obtain in time — and there would be over-pervasion. To avert that, the word 'mind' is [added]. When that is so, since neither the conjunction of the object with the part of the sense organ nor the conjunction of time with the eye possesses the character of being a mind-conjunction, the previously stated over-pervasion does not arise based on those — this is the purport. Previously, 'being' (<s>satya</s>)

children.text:
1.
niruktodbhūtatveti/ anudbhūtatvābhāvakūṭavattvarūpaṃ yat
udbhūtatvaṃ tadāśrayetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Manifest-ness as explained' — the meaning is: the substratum of manifest-ness in the form of the possession of the aggregate of absences of non-manifest-ness.

children.text:
ativyāptiḥ
ātmānyatve satīti vaśeṣaṇadāne 'pi vārayituṃ śakyeti kimarthaṃ
śabdetaretyādigurutaraviśeṣaṇamiti śaṅkate - na ceti/ samādhatte -
tathā satīti/ ātmānyatve sati
jñānakāraṇamanassaṃyogāśrayatvamityuktau carmaṇaḥ ātmānyatvāt
jñānakāraṇībhūtaḥ yaḥ carmamanassaṃyogaḥ tadāśrayatvācca
carmaṇyativyāptiḥ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya śabdetaretyādigurutaraṃ
viśeṣaṇaṃ deyamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The over-extension can be prevented even by giving the qualifier 'being other than the self' — so why the heavier qualifier 'other than sound' and so forth? — he raises this doubt with 'Nor' and so forth. He resolves: 'that being so' — the meaning is: if it were said that the definition is 'being the locus of the conjunction of the mind that causes cognition, while being other than the self,' then since the skin is other than the self, and since the conjunction of skin and mind serves as a cause of cognition, and the skin is the locus of that, there would be over-extension to the skin. To prevent that, the heavier qualifier 'other than sound' and so forth must be given — this is the meaning.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: jalanirūpaṇama
children.translated_text: Determination of Water

children.text: AnTs_11 śitasparśavatya āpaḥ / tā dvividhāḥ nityā anityāś ca / ntyāḥ paramāṇurūpāḥ / anityāḥ kāryarūpāḥ. / punas trividhāḥ. śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīraṃ varuṇaloke / indriyaṃ rasagrāhakaṃ rasanaṃ jihvāgravarti / viṣayaḥ saritsamudrādiḥ //
children.translated_text: That which possesses cold touch is water (<s>āpas</s>). It is of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of effects. It is further of three kinds, due to the distinction of body, sense organ, and object. The body [of water] is in the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>. The sense organ is the organ of taste (<s>rasana</s>), which apprehends taste, located at the tip of the tongue. The object is rivers, oceans, and the like.

children.text:
śītasparśavatya
āpaḥ/ tāśca dvividhāḥ/ nityā anityāśceti/ nityāḥ paramāṇurūpāḥ/
anityāḥ kāryarūpāḥ/ punastrividhāḥ - śarīraindriya - viṣayabhedāt/
śarīraṃ varuṇaloke/ indriyaṃ rasagrāhakaṃ rasanam/ tacca
jihvāgravarti/ viṣayaḥ saritsamudrādiḥ/
children.translated_text: That which possesses cold touch is water (<s>āpas</s>). And it is of two kinds — eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of effects. It is further of three kinds — due to the distinction of body, sense organ, and object. The body [of water] is in the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>. The sense organ is the organ of taste (<s>rasana</s>), which apprehends taste. And that is located at the tip of the tongue. The object is rivers, oceans, and the like.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
apāṃ lakṣaṇamāha -
śīteti/ utpannavinaṣṭajale 'vyāptivāraṇāya
śītasparśasamānādhikaraṇadravyatvāparajātimattvaṃ vivakṣitam/ 'śītaṃ
śilātalam' ityādau jalasambandhādeva śītasparśabhānamiti
nātivyāptiḥ/ anyatsarvaṃ pūrvarītyā vyākhyeyam/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of water — 'cold (<s>śīta</s>)' and so forth. To prevent under-extension in water that is produced and destroyed [within a single moment], what is intended is: possessing a universal other than <s>sattā</s> (existence) that is co-located with cold touch and subordinate to <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood). In cases like 'the stone slab is cold,' the cognition of cold touch arises from the contact with water alone; therefore there is no over-extension. Everything else is to be explained in the same manner as before.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
śītasparśasamānādhikaraṇeti/ tatra viśeṣaṇaprayojanaṃ
pūrvoktarītyā ūhyam/ jalatvajātisiddhistu
snehajanakatāvacchedakatayeti dhyeyam/ anyatsarve pūrvarītyeti/
nityatvādikaṃ śarīrādilakṣaṇaṃ ca gandhavattvasthāne śītasparśavattvaṃ
niveśya pṛthivīnirūpaṇoktarītyerthaḥ/ evamagre 'pyūhyam/
children.translated_text: 'Co-located with cold touch' — the purpose of the qualifiers therein should be inferred in the manner stated earlier. The establishment of the universal <s>jalatva</s> (water-hood) is through being the delimiting property of the capacity to produce viscidity (<s>sneha</s>) — this should be noted. 'Everything else in the same manner as before' — the eternality and the like, and the definition of body and the rest, are to be understood by substituting 'possessing cold touch' in place of 'possessing smell,' following the manner stated in the determination of earth. The same should be inferred for what follows as well.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
pūrvoktarītyā
ūhyamiti/ dravyatvavyāpyajātimattvamātroktau
dravyatvavyāpyapṛthivītvajātimatyāṃ pṛthivyāmativyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
śītasparśasamānādhikaraṇeti jātiviśeṣaṇam/
śītasparśavajjalavṛttisattājatimādāya pṛthivyādāvativyāptivāraṇāya
dravyatvavyāpyeti/ dravyatvavyāpyatvaṃ ca dravyatvanyūnavṛttitvam na tu
tacchūnyāvṛttitvam/ ato dravyatvajātimādāya noktadoṣa iti
bhāvaḥ/ snehajanakatāvacchedakatayeti/
'samavāyasambandhāvacchinnasnehatvāvacchinnasnehaniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitatādātmyasambandhāvacchinnajalaniṣṭhakāraṇatā
kiñciddharmāvacchinnā kāraṇatātvāt' ityanumānena
jalatvajātisiddhirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Should be inferred in the manner stated earlier' — if only 'possessing a universal pervaded by <s>dravyatva</s>' were stated, there would be over-extension to earth, which possesses the universal <s>pṛthivītva</s> (earth-hood) pervaded by <s>dravyatva</s>. To prevent that, the qualifier 'co-located with cold touch' is given for the universal. To prevent over-extension to earth and the like by taking <s>sattā</s> — the universal of water that is co-located with cold touch — the qualifier 'pervaded by <s>dravyatva</s>' [is given]. And being pervaded by <s>dravyatva</s> means having a narrower occurrence than <s>dravyatva</s>, not occurring where <s>dravyatva</s> is absent. Therefore, there is no stated defect in taking the universal <s>dravyatva</s> — this is the purport. 'Through being the delimiting property of the capacity to produce viscidity' — the meaning is: the universal <s>jalatva</s> is established through the inference 'the causality residing in water, delimited by the identity relation, which determines the effect-hood residing in viscidity delimited by the inherence relation, is delimited by some property, because it is causality.'

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: tejonirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of Fire (<s>Tejas</s>)

children.text: AnTs_12 uṣṇasparśavat tejaḥ / tad dvividhaṃ nityam anityaṃ ca / niyyaṃ paramāṇurūpam / anityaṃ kāryarūpam / punas trividhaṃ śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīram ādityaloke / indriyaṃ rūpagrāhakaṃ cakṣuḥ kṛṣṇatārāgravarti / viṣayaś caturvidhaḥ / bhaumadivyaudaryākarajabhedāt / bhaumaṃ vahnyādikam / abindhanaṃ divyaṃ vidyudādi / bhuktasya pariṇāmahetur audaryam. ākarajaṃ suvarṇādi //
children.translated_text: That which possesses hot touch is fire (<s>tejas</s>). It is of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of effects. It is further of three kinds, due to the distinction of body, sense organ, and object. The body [of fire] is in the world of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). The sense organ is the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>), which apprehends color, located at the front of the black pupil. The object is of four kinds, due to the distinction of terrestrial, celestial, abdominal, and mineral. The terrestrial is fire and the like. The celestial, which is not kindled by water, is lightning and the like. The abdominal is that which causes the transformation of what has been eaten. The mineral is gold and the like.

children.text:
uṣṇasparśavat
tejaḥ/ tat dvividham - nityam anityam ceti/ nityaṃ
paramāṇurūpam/ anityaṃ kāryarūpam/ punastrividham - śarīraindriya
- viṣayabhedāt/ śarīramādityaloke/ indriyaṃ rūpagrāhakaṃ cakṣuḥ/
tacca kṛṣṇatārāgravarti/
children.translated_text: That which possesses hot touch is fire (<s>tejas</s>). It is of two kinds — eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of effects. It is further of three kinds — due to the distinction of body, sense organ, and object. The body is in the world of <s>Āditya</s>. The sense organ is the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>), which apprehends color. And that is located at the front of the black pupil.

children.text:
viṣayaścaturvidhaḥ -
bhauma-divya-udarya-ākaraja-bhedāt/ bhaumaṃ vahnyādi/ divyamabindhanaṃ
vidyudādi/ bhuktasya pariṇāmaheturudaryam/ ākarajaṃ suvarṇādi/
children.translated_text: The object is of four kinds — due to the distinction of terrestrial (<s>bhauma</s>), celestial (<s>divya</s>), abdominal (<s>udarya</s>), and mineral (<s>ākaraja</s>). The terrestrial is fire and the like. The celestial, which is not kindled by water, is lightning and the like. The abdominal is that which causes the transformation of what has been eaten. The mineral is gold and the like.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
tejaso lakṣaṇamāha - uṣṇasparśavaditi/
'uṣṇaṃ jalam' ityādipratīteḥ tejassaṃyogānuvidhāyitvāt
nātivyāptiḥ/ viṣayaṃ vibhajate - bhaumeti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of fire — 'possessing hot touch' and so forth. Since in the cognition 'the water is hot,' the appearance of hot touch follows from contact with fire, there is no over-extension. He divides the object — 'terrestrial' and so forth.

children.text: suvarṇataijasatvavādaḥ
children.translated_text: The doctrine that gold is fiery (<s>taijasa</s>)

children.text:
nanu suvarṇaṃ
pārthivaṃ pītatvāt gurutvāt haridrāvat iti cet - na/
atyantānalasaṃyoge sati ghṛtādau dravatvanāśadarśanena,
jalamadhyasthaghṛtādau tannāśādarśanena ca asati pratibandhake
pārthivadravatvanā śāgnisaṃyogayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvāvadhāraṇāt
suvarṇasya atyantānalasaṃyoge sati anucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇatvena
pārthivatvānupapatteḥ pītadravyadravatvanāśapratibandhakatayā
dravadravyāntarasiddhau naimittikadravatvādhikaraṇatayā jalatvānupapatteḥ
rūpavattayā vāyvādiṣu anantarbhāvāt taijasatvasiddhiḥ/
tasyoṣṇasparśabhāsvararūpayoḥ upaṣṭambhakapārthivarūpasparśābhyāṃ
pratibandhādanupalabdhiḥ/ tasmāt suvarṇaṃ taijasamiti siddham/
children.translated_text: Objection: Gold is earthy (<s>pārthiva</s>), because of its yellowness and heaviness, like turmeric. Reply: No — because by observing the destruction of fluidity in ghee and the like when there is extreme conjunction with fire, and by observing the non-destruction of that [fluidity] in ghee and the like placed within water, it is ascertained that the destruction of earthy fluidity and conjunction with fire have a cause-effect relationship in the absence of an impediment. Since gold, even in extreme conjunction with fire, is the substratum of fluidity that is not destroyed — its being earthy is not possible. Since, by establishing another fluid substance as the impediment to the destruction of the fluidity of yellow substances, and [gold] being the substratum of adventitious fluidity — its being water is not possible. Since it possesses color — it cannot be included among air and the like. Therefore, its being fiery is established. The non-apprehension of hot touch and luminous color in it is due to the obstruction by earthy color and touch that support it. Therefore, it is established that gold is fiery.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
mūle
abindhanamiti/ adbhiḥ indhanaṃ dīpanaṃ yasya tadityarthaḥ/ bhuktasyeti/
bhuktasyaudanādeḥ pariṇāmaḥ paripākaḥ, tatra heturityarthaḥ/
ākarajamiti/ ākaraḥ khaniḥ tatra jātamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the root text, '<s>abindhana</s>' — the meaning is: that whose kindling (<s>indhana</s>), i.e. igniting, is not by water (<s>adbhis</s>). '<s>Bhuktasya</s>' — the meaning is: of what has been eaten, such as cooked rice and the like, the transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) is the digestion; what causes that. '<s>Ākaraja</s>' — the meaning is: <s>ākara</s> is a mine; born in that.

children.text:
suvarṇasya taijasatvaṃ
vyavasthāpayituṃ śaṅkate - dīpikāyām nanviti/ pārthivatvasādhakaṃ
pītatvahetumuktvā taijasatvābhāvasādhakaṃ hetumāha - gurutvāditi/
etena suvarṇarūpatejasi vijātīyapītarūpaṃ svīkriyate/ 'pītaṃ
suvarṇaṃ' ityabādhitapratyakṣapratītibalāt/ evaṃ ca taijasatvasya
nirbādhatayā pṛthivītvaṃ na sidhyatīti kasyacit bhrāntirnirastā/
gurutvasyāpratyakṣatvena tathā vaktumaśakyatvāditi dik/ suvarṇasya
pītimagurutvāśrayato 'tiriktatvaṃ vyavasthāpayituṃ anumāne
aprayojakaśaṅkāvāraṇāya kāryakāraṇabhāvamanukūlatarkaṃ vyavasthāpayati
- atyantānaleti/ suvarṇasyetyādiḥ/ anumānaprayogastu
itthamavaseyaḥ - suvarṇaṃ apārthivam asati pratibandhake
atyantānalasaṃyoge sati anucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇatvāt yannaivaṃ
tannaivam/ yathā pṛthivī/ jalamadhyasthaghṛtādau vyabhicāravāraṇāya asati
pratibandhaka iti/ agnisaṃyogāsamānādhikaraṇadravatvavatighṛtādau
vyabhicāravāraṇāya atyantānalasaṃyoge sati iti/
dravadravyāntarasiddhāviti/ 'atyantānalasaṃyogī pītimāśrayaḥ
dravatvanāśapratibandhakadravadravyāntarasaṃyuktaḥ atyantānalasaṃyoge 'pi
anucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇatve sati gurutvāta
jalamadhyasthaghṛtādivat' ityanumānena tatsiddhirdraṣṭavyā/
jalādikamādāyānumānaparyavasānaṃ vārayati - naimittiketi/ nanu
uṣṇasparśabhāsvararūpayoḥ upalabdhyabhāvena suvarṇasya taijasatvaṃ
anupapannaṃ ityata āha - tasyeti/ pratibandhāditi/
doṣavidhayetyādiḥ/
children.translated_text: To establish that gold is fiery, he raises the objection — in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'Now' and so forth. Having stated the reason of yellowness as establishing earthiness, he states the reason establishing the absence of fieriness: 'because of heaviness' and so forth. By this, it is accepted that gold, being fire, has a heterogeneous yellow color. This is due to the force of the uncontradicted perceptual cognition 'gold is yellow.' And thus, since fieriness is uncontradicted, the error of some who think 'earthiness is established' is refuted. Because heaviness, being imperceptible, cannot be similarly claimed — this is the gist. To establish that gold is distinct from what possesses yellowness and heaviness, and to prevent an objection of irrelevant reason in the inference, he establishes the supporting suppositional reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) through the cause-effect relationship — 'extreme fire' and so forth. 'Of gold' and so forth. The inferential application is to be understood thus: Gold is non-earthy; because in the absence of an impediment, when there is extreme conjunction with fire, it is the substratum of fluidity that is not destroyed. Whatever is not so is not so — like earth. To prevent deviation in ghee and the like placed within water, 'in the absence of an impediment.' To prevent deviation in ghee and the like that possess fluidity not co-located with conjunction with fire, 'when there is extreme conjunction with fire.' 'When another fluid substance is established' — the inference for establishing that should be seen as: 'A substratum possessing yellowness, in extreme conjunction with fire, that is conjoined with another fluid substance that impedes the destruction of fluidity — because of being the substratum of fluidity that is not destroyed even in extreme conjunction with fire while possessing heaviness, like ghee placed within water.' To prevent the inference from concluding with water and the like, he says — 'adventitious' and so forth. Now, since the non-apprehension of hot touch and luminous color makes the fieriness of gold untenable — anticipating this, he says — 'of that' and so forth. 'Due to the obstruction' — defect-producing and so forth [is to be supplied].

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
suvarṇaṃ pārthivaṃ
pītatvāt gurutvāt haridrāvat iti mūle pītatvagurutvābhyāṃ
dvābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ suvarṇasya pārthivatvaṃ
children.translated_text: In the root text, 'Gold is earthy, because of yellowness and heaviness, like turmeric' — by the two reasons of yellowness and heaviness, the earthiness of gold

children.text:
pūrvapakṣiṇā
sādhitam/ tatra pītatvarūpeṇa aikena hetunaiva
pṛthivītvasādhanasambhavāt gurutvarūpadvitīyahetūpanyāso vyartha
ityāśaṅkyāha - pārthivatvasādhakamiti/ tathā ca pītatvaṃ
pārthivatvasādhakam/ gurutvaṃ tu tejobhinnatvasādhakam/ na ca
dvitīyānumānaṃ vyarthamiti vācyam/ paramatanirākaraṇapūrvakaṃ
svasiddhāntasya kathanīyatayā parābhimatataijasatvanirākaraṇāya
dvitīyānumānasya āvaśyakatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: was established by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (opponent). Therein, since establishing earthiness is possible by just one reason in the form of yellowness, the introduction of a second reason in the form of heaviness would be useless — anticipating this doubt, he says — 'establishing earthiness' and so forth. And accordingly, yellowness is the establisher of earthiness, while heaviness is the establisher of being different from fire. Nor should it be said that the second inference is useless — because since one's own doctrine must be stated after refuting the opponent's view, the second inference is necessary for refuting the fieriness held by the opponent — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu suvarṇasya
pārthivatvasādhananaiva arthāt taijasatvābhāvanirṇaye
anumānāntarapraṇayanavaiyarthyam/ ekenaiva pītatvahetunā
pārthivatvataijasabhinnatvayoḥ sādhanasambhavāditi cet - atrāhuḥ/
'suvarṇaṃ pārthivam' ityādyanumāne suvarṇatvaṃ na pakṣatāvacchedakam/
tathā sati rajatasya pakṣatāvacchedakānākrāntatayā tatra
pārthivatvāsiddhiprasaṅgāt/ tadarthamanumānāntarapraṇayane gauravācca/
nāpi rajatasādhāraṇaṃ hiraṇyatvaṃ pakṣatāvacchedakam/ tathā sati
pakṣatāvacchedakāśrayarajate pītatvarūpahetvabhāvena
bhāgāsiddhiprasaṅgāt/ tasmāt gurutvahetvanusaraṇam/ gurutvaṃ tu
rajate 'pyastīti na bhāgāsiddhiriti/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since by establishing the earthiness of gold, the absence of fieriness is thereby determined, the introduction of another inference is useless — since establishing both earthiness and difference-from-fire is possible by the single reason of yellowness. Reply: To this they say — in the inference 'gold is earthy' and the like, <s>suvarṇatva</s> (gold-hood) is not the delimiting property of subject-hood. For if it were, since silver would not be included in the delimiting property of subject-hood, the non-establishment of earthiness for silver would result. And introducing another inference for that purpose would involve ontological heaviness. Nor is <s>hiraṇyatva</s> (being [precious] metal), which is common to silver, the delimiting property of subject-hood. For if it were, since the reason of yellowness would be absent in silver — which is a locus of the delimiting property of subject-hood — partial unestablishedness would result. Therefore, the reason of heaviness must be pursued. For heaviness is present even in silver, and hence there is no partial unestablishedness.

children.text:
vastutastu atra
pūrvapakṣiṇaḥ suvarṇasya pārthivatvasādhane na nirbharaḥ/ suvarṇe
pārthivatvābhāvasya kenāpyanuktatayā tadabhāvarūpapṛthivītvamevāstu
iti pūrvapakṣasyāprasarāt/ 'ākarajaṃ suvarṇādi' iti granthakṛtā
pūrvasuvarṇasya tejastvakathanāt tadupari suvarṇaṃ tejo na bhavatīti
pūrvapakṣasyaiva yuktatvāt/ ata eva 'tasmāt suvarṇaṃ taijasam' iti
siddhānte upasaṃhāro 'pi saṅgacchate/ evaṃ ca suvarṇasya
tejobhinnatvamapyatra pūrvapakṣiṇā siṣādhayiṣitam/ suvarṇasya
tejobhinnatvaṃ tu pītatvena hetunā na sādhayituṃ śakyate 'suvarṇaṃ
pītam' ityākārakābādhitapratyakṣabalāt suvarṇasya tejastve 'pi
tatra pītatvasyopapatteḥ/ ato gurutvāditi dvitīyahetūpanyāsaḥ/
'suvarṇaṃ guru' iti pratyakṣābhāvena suvarṇasya tejastve 'pi
gurutvamupapadyata iti vaktumaśakyam/ ato gurutvaṃ
tejobhinnatvasādhane samarthamiti bhāvo 'tra pratīyate/ spaṣṭīkṛtaśca
ayaṃ bhāvaḥ 'etane' ityādigrantheneti/
children.translated_text: In truth, however, the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (opponent) is not insistent on establishing the earthiness of gold. Since the absence of earthiness in gold has not been stated by anyone, and since that absence — the earthiness itself — may simply be accepted, the opponent's position does not advance [as a serious argument]. Since the author of the treatise has earlier stated 'mineral [fire] is gold and the like,' thereby declaring the fieriness of gold, the opponent's position stating 'gold is not fire' is indeed appropriate [as an objection]. For precisely this reason, the conclusion 'therefore gold is fiery' in the <s>siddhānta</s> (established position) is also coherent. And thus, the fieriness-difference too was intended to be established by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>. But the difference-from-fire of gold cannot be established by the reason of yellowness — because of the force of the uncontradicted perceptual cognition 'gold is yellow,' the yellowness is tenable even if gold is fire. Therefore the second reason of heaviness is introduced. Since the perception 'gold is heavy' is absent, it cannot be said that heaviness is tenable even if gold is fire. Therefore heaviness is capable of establishing difference-from-fire — this is the purport that is understood here. And this purport has been made explicit by the passage beginning with 'by this' and so forth.

children.text:
dīpikāyām -
atyantānalasaṃyoge satītyādi/ ayamarthaḥ - ghṛtādipṛthivyāṃ yat
dravatvaṃ tasyātyantāgnisaṃyoge sati nāśo bhavati/ tena
pārthivagatadravatvanāśaṃ prati atyantāgnisaṃyogaḥ kāraṇamiti
kāryakāraṇabhāvo labhyate/ paraṃ tu tulamadhyasthaghṛtadravatvasya
atyantāgnisaṃyoge satyapi nāśo na
bhavatītyanvayavyabhicāraśaṅgāvāraṇāya uktakāryakāraṇabhāve 'asati
pratibandhake' iti viśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ tena
pratibandhakāsamavadhānakālīnaḥ atyantāgnisaṃyogaḥ pārthivadravatvanāśasya
hetuḥ iti kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ phalati/ jalamadhyasthaghṛte tu jalasya
pratibandhakatvāt na dravatvanāśaḥ/ tathā ca
pratibandhakāsamavahitāgnisaṃyogarūpakāraṇābhāvāt tatra
dravatvanāśarūpakāryābhāva iti na pūrvoktānvayavyabhicāraḥ/ suvarṇe
tu atyantāgnisaṃyoge satyapi tatra vidyamānapārthivabhāgasya yat
dravatvaṃ tannāśo na bhavati/ ataḥ taddravatvanāśapratibandhakaṃ kiñcit
dravyaṃ suvarṇe 'stīti vaktavyam/ tadeva tejaḥ/ tathā ca suvarṇe
pṛthivyasādhāraṇānubhūyamānapītarūpagurutvayorāśrayabhūtaḥ
pārthivabhāgaḥ tadgatadravatvapratibandhakatejobhāga iti
bhāgadvayamaṅgīkāryam/ tathā anaṅgīkāre suvarṇasya kṛtsnasyāpi
pārthivatve tadgatadravatvaṃ naśyet/ evaṃ ca atyantāgnisaṃyoge
pītimāśrayabhāgaḥ duvatvanāśapratibandhakadravadravyāntarasaṃyuktaḥ
atyantānalasaṃyoge satyapi avināśidravatvavattvāt
jalamadhyasthaghṛtavat ityanumānena pratibandhakadravadravyāntarasiddhau
'tat dravyam na pārthivam asati pratibandhake 'tyantāgnisaṃyoge sati
anucchidyamānadravatvavattvāt yannaivaṃ tannaivaṃ yathā pṛthivī'
ityanumānena tādṛśadravyāntarasya pṛthivībhinnatve siddhe tasya
'tādṛśadravyāntaraṃ na jalam taimitikadravatvavattvāt' ityanumānena
jalatvābhāve siddhe 'tādṛśadravyāntaraṃ na vāyvādikam rūpavattvāt'
ityanumānena vāyvāditvābhāve ca sati tādṛśadravyaṃ taijasaṃ
pṛthivyādyaṣṭakānyatve sati dravyatvāt iti pariśeṣānumānena tasya
taijasatvaṃ sidhyatīti/ na ca tādṛśadravyasya rūpavattvamasiddhamiti kathaṃ
tena hetunā vāyvādibhedaḥ sādhya iti vācyam/ tasya rūpaśūnyatve
vāyvādivat dravatvanāśapratibandhakatvānupapattyā rūpavattvasvīkārasya
āvaśyakatvāt ityāśayāt/ vastuto naimittikadravatvavattvenaiva
hetunā vāyvādibhedo 'pi śakyaḥ sādhayitum/ tathā ca tejastvena
nirṇītaṃ pratibandhakaṃ dravyameva suvarṇaṃ hiraṇyamityādibhiḥ
viśeṣaśabdaiḥ sāmānyaśabdaiśca vyavahriyata iti sidhyati/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> — 'When there is extreme contact with fire' and so forth. The meaning is as follows: the fluidity that exists in earthy substances such as ghee and the like is destroyed when there is extreme contact with fire. Thereby, the causal relation is obtained: extreme contact with fire is the cause of the destruction of earthy fluidity. However, since the fluidity of ghee placed in a balance pan is not destroyed even when there is extreme contact with fire, the qualification 'in the absence of an obstructor' must be given in the stated causal relation, to prevent the suspicion of deviation in positive concomitance. Thereby, the causal relation results as follows: extreme contact with fire occurring at a time when no obstructor is co-present is the cause of the destruction of earthy fluidity. In the case of ghee placed in water, since water serves as an obstructor, there is no destruction of fluidity. And accordingly, since the cause in the form of extreme fire-contact unaccompanied by an obstructor is absent there, the effect in the form of destruction of fluidity is absent — hence the aforementioned deviation in positive concomitance does not arise. But in the case of gold, even when there is extreme contact with fire, the fluidity of the earthy component present therein is not destroyed. Therefore, it must be said that some substance serving as an obstructor of the destruction of that fluidity exists in gold. That is fire (<s>tejas</s>) itself. And accordingly, two components must be accepted in gold: an earthy component that is the substratum of yellow color and heaviness — which are exclusively experienced in earth — and a fiery component that obstructs the destruction of the fluidity residing in that [earthy component]. Without accepting this, if the entirety of gold were earthy, its fluidity would be destroyed. And thus, through the inference — 'The component that is the substratum of yellow color, being conjoined with another fluid substance that obstructs the destruction of fluidity, has indestructible fluidity even when there is extreme contact with fire, like ghee placed in water' — when another fluid substance serving as an obstructor is established, through the inference — 'That substance is not earthy, because it has indestructible fluidity when there is extreme contact with fire in the absence of an obstructor; what is not so is not so, like earth' — when the non-earthy nature of such another substance is established, through the inference — 'Such another substance is not water, because it possesses heat-produced fluidity' — when its non-water nature is established, and through the inference — 'Such another substance is not wind and the like, because it possesses color' — when its non-wind nature and the like is established, then through the residual inference — 'Such a substance is fiery, because it is a substance while being different from the eightfold [category] of earth and the rest' — its fiery nature is established. Nor should it be said that such a substance's possession of color is unestablished, and therefore how can the difference from wind and the like be proved by that reason — because if it lacked color, like wind and the like, its obstructive power with respect to the destruction of fluidity would be inexplicable, and therefore accepting its possession of color is necessary. In reality, even the difference from wind and the like can be proved by the reason of possessing heat-produced fluidity alone. And accordingly, it is established that the obstructing substance determined as fiery is itself denoted by the specific terms 'gold' (<s>suvarṇa</s>), 'gold' (<s>hiraṇya</s>), and the like, as well as by general terms.

children.text:
atredaṃ tattvam -
pratibandhakābhāvaviśiṣṭaḥ atyantāgnisaṃyogaḥ pārthivadravatvanāśaṃ
iti heturiti
children.translated_text: Here is the truth of the matter: extreme contact with fire, qualified by the absence of an obstructor, is the cause of the destruction of earthy fluidity —

children.text:
kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ
āvaśyakaḥ/ tatra suvarṇasthapārthivabhāgagatadravatvanāśarūpakāryābhāvaḥ
pratibandhakābhāvaviśiṣṭātyantāgnisaṃyogarūpakāraṇābhāvaprayukta iti
nirvivādam/ tatra tādṛśaviśiṣṭābhāvarūpaḥ kāraṇābhāvaḥ na
viśeṣyābhāvāt, atyantāgnisaṃyogarūpasya viśeṣyasya tatra sattvāt/
kiṃ tu pratibandhakābhāvarūpasya viśeṣaṇasyābhāvādeva vaktavya iti
pratibandhakaṃ kiñcit dravadravyāntaraṃ tatrāstīti vaktavyam/ tasyāpi
pṛthivītve taddravatvanāśapratibandhakaṃ dravyāntaraṃ tasyāpi
tathetyanavasthā syāt/ ataḥ pratibandhakāntaraṃ vinā
avinaśyaddravatvādeva tanna pṛthivī iti/ ayaṃ dīpikāgranthaḥ
pārthivabhāgasyāpi dravatvaṃ tejobhāgasyāpi dravatvamityaṅgīkṛtya
pravṛtta iti pratīyate 'pītadravyadravatvanāśa' 'dravadravyāntara' iti
padayoḥ svārasyāt/ muktāvalyāṃ tu 'jalamadhyasthamaṣīkṣodavat
tasyādrutatvāta' iti granthena pārthivabhāgasya dravatvābhāva eva
pratipāditaḥ/ tanmate suvarṇasya taijasatvasādhakānumānamanyadeveti/
children.translated_text: this causal relation is necessary. There, the absence of the effect in the form of the non-destruction of the fluidity of the earthy component in gold is due to the absence of the cause in the form of extreme fire-contact qualified by the absence of an obstructor — this is undisputed. There, the absence of the cause in the form of the absence of such a qualified [entity] is not due to the absence of the qualificand, since the qualificand in the form of extreme fire-contact is present there. Rather, it must be stated that it is due to the absence of the qualifier in the form of the absence of an obstructor — hence some other fluid substance serving as an obstructor exists there. If that too were earthy, then another substance obstructing the destruction of its fluidity [must be posited], and of that too likewise — leading to infinite regress. Therefore, since it possesses fluidity that does not perish without [positing] another obstructor, that is not earth. This <s>Dīpikā</s> passage proceeds on the acceptance that both the earthy component has fluidity and the fiery component has fluidity — as is evident from the natural meaning of the terms 'destruction of fluidity of the yellow substance' and 'another fluid substance.' But in the <s>Muktāvalī</s>, by the passage 'like ink-powder placed in water, since it is not fluid,' the absence of fluidity in the earthy component alone is established. In that view, the inference establishing the fiery nature of gold is different.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām -
suvarṇasya pītimagurutvāśrayato 'tiriktatvamiti/ suvarṇaśabdavācyasya
bhāgaviśeṣasya pṛthivībhāgādatiriktatvamityarthaḥ/
anumāne 'prayojakaśaṅkāvāraṇāyeti/ suvarṇaśabdavācyasya
bhāgaviśeṣasya pṛthivyatiriktatvasādhake 'suvarṇam apārthivam
atyantāgnisaṃyoga sati anucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇatvāt'
ityanumāne atyantāgnisaṃyoge sati
anucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇatvarūpaheturastu apārthivatvarūpasādhyaṃ
māstu ityaprayojakaśaṅkāyāṃ tadvāraṇāya yadi suvarṇasya
pārthivatvaṃ syāt tarhi atyantāgnisaṃyoge sati
ucchidyamānadravatvādhikaraṇameva syāt; pārthivadravatvanāśaṃ prati
atyantāgnisaṃyogasya kāraṇatvāt
ityevaṃrūpamanukūlatarkamāhetyarthaḥ/ asati pratibandhake ityasya
pratibandhakābhāvaviśiṣṭamityarthaḥ/ tasya dravatve 'nvayaḥ/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
saṃyogasamavāyaghaṭita ekakālāvacchinnaikādhikaraṇavṛttitvarūpasāmānādhi karaṇyasambandhena/
atyantānalasaṃyoge sati ityasyāpi
samavāyaghaṭitoktasāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena
atyantāgnisaṃyogaviśiṣṭamityarthaḥ/ anvayaśca tasya dravatve eva/
jalamadhyasthaghṛtādau vyabhicāravāraṇāyeti/
apārthivatvarūpasādhyābhāvavati tatra
anucchidyamānadravatvarūpahetusattvāditi bhāvaḥ/
agnisaṃyogāsamānādhikaraṇadravatvavati ghṛtādāviti/
śikyasthaghṛtādau ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'Gold's being different from the substratum of yellow color and heaviness.' The meaning is: the distinctness of the specific component denoted by the word 'gold' from the earthy component. In the inference establishing the non-earthiness of the specific component denoted by the word 'gold' — 'Gold is non-earthy, because it is the substratum of non-destructible fluidity when there is extreme fire-contact' — to avert the doubt of irrelevance (<s>aprayojakaśaṅkā</s>): even if the reason in the form of being the substratum of non-destructible fluidity when there is extreme fire-contact is present, let the probandum in the form of non-earthiness not [follow] — to avert this doubt, he presented a supporting suppositional reasoning (<s>anukūlatarka</s>): 'If gold were earthy, then it would be a substratum of fluidity destructible when there is extreme fire-contact, because extreme fire-contact has causality for the destruction of earthy fluidity' — this is the meaning. The meaning of 'in the absence of an obstructor' is 'qualified by the absence of an obstructor.' Its syntactic connection is with fluidity. And the qualification is through the co-location relation constituted by co-temporal-co-substratal-occurrence through contact and inherence. The meaning of 'when there is extreme fire-contact' is also 'qualified by extreme fire-contact' through the co-location relation constituted by the stated inherence. And its syntactic connection is with fluidity alone. 'To avert the suspicion of deviation in the case of ghee placed in water' — the purport is: since the reason in the form of non-destructible fluidity is present in what lacks the probandum in the form of non-earthiness. 'In ghee not co-located with fire-contact' — the meaning is: in ghee placed in a basket and the like.

children.text:
atyantānalasaṃyogītyādi/ pītimāśrayatvamātrasya
pakṣatāvacchedakatve tadavacchedena ca anumiteruddeśyatve
agnisaṃyogarahitasyāpi pītimāśrayasya pakṣatāvacchedakākrāntatayā
tatrāgnisaṃyogaghaṭitasya hetorabhāvāt bhāgāsiddhiḥ syāt iti
tadvāraṇāya atyantānalasaṃyogīti pakṣaviśeṣaṇam/
atyantānalasaṃyoginaḥ taijasabhāgasya sādhyaśūnyatvāt bādhaḥ syāt
iti tadvāraṇāya pītimāśraya iti/ dravadravyāntarasya apratibandhakatve
tatkalpane 'pi prakṛte nopayoga iti sūcanāya
dravatvanāśapratibandhaketi sādhyaviśeṣaṇam/ jalamadhyasthaghṛtādau
pārthivadravatvanāśaṃ prati dravadravyasyaiva pratibandhakatvadarśanāt
prakṛte 'pi pratibandhakaṃ dravyaṃ dravameva syādityabhipretya draveti
viśeṣaṇam/ anumānaparyavasānamiti/
ajijñāsitārthaṃsiddhirūpamarthāntaraṃ vārayitumityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Having extreme fire-contact' and so forth. If mere being-a-substratum-of-yellow-color were the delimitor of the subject-hood, and if the inference had as its purpose only the subject delimited by that, then even a substratum of yellow color lacking fire-contact would be encompassed by the delimitor of subject-hood, and since the reason constituted by fire-contact would be absent there, the defect of partial unestablishedness (<s>bhāgāsiddhi</s>) would arise. To prevent that, 'having extreme fire-contact' is the qualifier of the subject. Since the fiery component of gold, being devoid of the probandum, would cause sublation (<s>bādha</s>), to prevent that, 'substratum of yellow color' [is added]. The qualifier 'obstructing the destruction of fluidity' in the probandum serves to indicate that if another fluid substance did not have obstructive power, positing it would be of no use in the present context. Since, from the observation that it is fluid substance alone that obstructs the destruction of earthy fluidity with respect to ghee placed in water and the like, the obstructing substance in the present context too would be fluid — with this intent, the qualifier 'fluid' [is added]. 'The conclusion of the inference' — the meaning is: to prevent the unintended consequence of establishing what is not desired to be known.

children.text:
nanu yadi suvarṇaṃ
taijasaṃ bhavet tarhi tejoguṇayoḥ uṣṇasparśabhāsvaraśuklarūpayoḥ
suvarṇe upalabdhiḥ syāt/ yataḥ na tayoḥ suvarṇe upalabdhiḥ ataḥ suvarṇaṃ
na taijasamiti śaṅkānirāsārthaḥ tasyeti grantha ityāha---nanu
uṣṇasparśeti/ vastutaḥ suvarṇe vidyamānayorapi uṣṇasparśaśuklarūpayoḥ
pratyakṣaṃ prati pārthivagatasparśarūpe pratibandhake iti
dīpikāyāmuktam/ tacca pratibandhakatvaṃ doṣavidhayā na tu tadvattābuddhiṃ
prati tadabhāvavattājñānavidhayetyabhipretyāha ---
children.translated_text: Now, if gold were fiery, then the qualities of fire — hot touch and bright white color — would be perceived in gold. Since these two are not perceived in gold, gold is not fiery — to refute this doubt, the passage beginning with 'of it' is [introduced]. He says: 'Now, hot touch' and so forth. In truth, even though hot touch and white color exist in gold, with respect to their perception, the touch and color residing in the earthy component serve as obstructors — this was stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s>. And that obstructive power is by way of being a defect (<s>doṣa</s>), not by way of cognition-of-possessing-the-absence [obstructing] cognition-of-possessing [the property] — with this intent he says:

children.text: doṣavidhayetyādiriti/
children.translated_text: 'By way of being a defect' and so forth.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: vāyunirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>)

children.text: AnTs_13 rūparahitasparśavān vāyuḥ / sa dvividho nityo 'nityaś ca / nityaḥ paramāṇurūpaḥ / anityaḥ kāryarūpaḥ / punas trividhaḥ śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīraṃ vāyuloke / indriyaṃ sparśagrāhakaṃ tvaksarvaśarīravarti / viṣayo vṛkṣādikampanahetuḥ // śarīrāntaḥsaṃcārī vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ / sa caiko 'py upādhibhedāt prāṇāpānādisaṃjñā labhate //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 13:] Wind (<s>vāyu</s>) possesses touch but is devoid of color (<s>rūpa</s>). It is twofold: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of products. [The non-eternal] is again threefold, due to the distinction of body, sense organ, and object. The body is in the world of wind. The sense organ is the skin (<s>tvak</s>), which grasps touch and pervades the entire body. The object is the cause of the trembling of trees and the like. The wind that moves within the body is <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). And that, though one, due to differences in limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>), receives the designations <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the rest.

children.text:
rūparahitasparśavān vāyuḥ/ saḥ dvividhaḥ/ nityaḥ anityaśca
iti/ nityaḥ paramāṇurūpaḥ/ anityaḥ kāryarūpaḥ/ punastrividhaḥ ---
śarīra - indriya - viṣayabhedāt/ śarīram vāyuloke/ indriyaṃ
sparśagrāhakaṃ tvak/ sarvaśarīravṛttiḥ/ viṣayo vṛkṣādikampanahetuḥ
vāyuḥ/ śarīrāntassañcārī vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ/ sa caiko 'pi upādhibhedāt
prāṇāpānādisaṃjñāṃ labhate/
children.translated_text: Wind possesses touch but is devoid of color. It is twofold: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of products. Again threefold — due to the distinction of body, sense organ, and object. The body is in the world of wind. The sense organ is the skin, which grasps touch. It pervades the entire body. The object is the wind that causes the trembling of trees and the like. The wind that moves within the body is <s>prāṇa</s>. And that, though one, due to differences in limiting conditions, receives the designations <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the rest.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
vāyuṃ lakṣayati -
rūparahiteti/ ākāśādau ativyāptivāraṇāya sparśavāniti/
pṛthivyādau ativyāptivāraṇāya rūparahiteti/ prāṇasya kutrāntarbhāva
ityata āha - śarīreti/ sa ceti/ eka eva prāṇaḥ sthānabhedāt
prāṇāpānādiśabdaiḥ vyavahriyata ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines wind — with 'devoid of color.' To avert over-extension to space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like, 'possessing touch' [is stated]. To avert over-extension to earth and the like, 'devoid of color' [is stated]. Where is <s>prāṇa</s> included? — to answer this, he says: 'the body' and so forth. 'And that' — the meaning is: the one and same <s>prāṇa</s> is designated by the terms <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the rest due to differences in location.

children.text:
sparśānumeyo vāyuḥ/
tathā hi - yo 'yaṃ vāyaiṃ vāti sati anuṣṇāśītasparśaṃ upalabhyate sa
kvacidāśritaḥ guṇatvāt rūpavat/ na cāsya āśrayaḥ pṛthivī,
udbhūtasparśaṃvatpārthivasya udbhūtarūpavattvaniyamāt/ na jalatejasī,
anuṣṇāśītasparśavattvāt/ na vibhucatuṣṭayam,
sarvatropalabdhiprasaṅgāt/ na manaḥ, paramāṇusparśasya atīndriyatvāt/
tasmāt ya. pratīyamānasparśāśrayaḥ sa vāyuḥ (eva)/
children.translated_text: Wind is inferred through touch. Thus: the neither-hot-nor-cold touch perceived when the wind blows must reside in some substratum, because it is a quality — like color. And its substratum is not earth, because an earthy substance possessing manifest touch must necessarily possess manifest color. Nor water or fire, because [their touch] is not neither-hot-nor-cold. Nor the four all-pervading [substances], because then it would be perceived everywhere. Nor mind, because the touch of an atom is super-sensory. Therefore, that which is the substratum of the perceived touch is wind (alone).

children.text:
nanu vāyuḥ pratyakṣaḥ
pratyakṣasparśāśrayatvāt ghaṭavat iti cet - na/
udbhūtarūpavattvasyopādhitvāt/ 'yatra dravyatve sati
bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣatvam, tatra udbhūtarūpavattvam' iti
sādhyavyāpakatvam/ pakṣe sādhanāvyāpakatvam/ na caivaṃ
taptavāristhatejaso 'pi apratyakṣatvāpattiḥ iṣṭatvāt/ tasmāt
rūparahitatvāt vāyuḥ apratyakṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, wind is perceptible, because it is the substratum of perceptible touch, like a pot — if thus objected: no, because possessing manifest color is an imposed condition (<s>upādhi</s>). 'Wherever there is substance-hood accompanied by perceptibility through external sense organs, there is possessing manifest color' — this is the pervader-hood of the probandum. [But] it does not pervade the reason in the subject. Nor is there the unwanted consequence that fire in heated water would also be imperceptible — because that is desired (<s>iṣṭa</s>). Therefore, due to being devoid of color, wind is imperceptible.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
śarīreti iti/
tathā ca prāṇasya viṣaye antarbhāva iti bhāvaḥ/ sthānabhedāditi/ 'hṛdi
prāṇa' ityādikośoktasthānabhedādityarthaḥ/ mukhanāsikābhyāṃ
niṣkramaṇapraveśanāt prāṇaḥ/ malādīnāmadhonayanāt apānaḥ/ āhāreṣu
pākārthaṃ vahneḥ samunnayanāt samānaḥ/ ūrdhvanayanāt udānaḥ/
nāḍīmukheṣu vitananāt vyānaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The body' and so forth — and accordingly, the purport is that <s>prāṇa</s> is included under the category of objects. 'Due to differences in location' — the meaning is: due to differences in location as stated in the lexicon (<s>kośa</s>) 'in the heart is <s>prāṇa</s>' and so forth. [It is called] <s>prāṇa</s> because of its going out and entering through the mouth and nostrils. [It is called] <s>apāna</s> because of its downward movement of waste and the like. [It is called] <s>samāna</s> because of its carrying fire upward for the purpose of digestion of food. [It is called] <s>udāna</s> because of its upward movement. [It is called] <s>vyāna</s> because of its spreading through the openings of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels).

children.text:
svamataṃ darśaṃyati - sparśānumeya iti/
asya - upalabhyamānasparśasya āśrayaḥ pṛthivī na ca ityanvayaḥ/
catuṣṭayamiti/ idaṃ ākāśādipratyekabhedasādhanābhiprāyeṇa/
sarvatropalabdhiprasaṅgāditi/ sparśasyetyādiḥ/ ākāśādīnāṃ
vibhutvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: He shows his own view — with 'inferred through touch.' 'Of this' — the syntactic connection is: the substratum of the perceived touch is not earth and the like. 'The four' — this is intended to establish the difference from each of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the rest individually. 'Because then it would be perceived everywhere' — the supplement is: 'of touch.' The purport is: because <s>ākāśa</s> and the rest are all-pervading.

children.text:
pratyakṣaḥ - bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayaḥ/
anudbhūtasparśāśraye tvagindriye vyabhicāravāraṇāya pratyakṣeti/
upādhitvāditi/ tathā ca hetau upādhivyabhicāreṇa
sādhyavyabhicāronnayanasambhavāt na pratyakṣatvasiddhiriti bhāvaḥ/ nanu
tādṛśapratyakṣatvasya guṇādāvapi sattvena tatrodbhūtarūpābhāvena
sādhyāvyāpakatvāt kathaṃ tasyopādhikatvamityata āha - yatreti/ tathā
ca pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpako 'yaṃ upādhiriti bhāvaḥ/
evaṃ-pratyakṣasparśāśrayasyāpi udbhetarūpābhāvena pratyakṣatvānaṅgīkāre '
apratyakṣatvāpattiriti/ udbhūtarūpābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Perceptible' (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) means the object of perception generated by an external sense-organ. The word 'perceptible' is [added] to prevent deviation in the tactile sense-organ (<s>tvagindriya</s>), which is the substratum of non-manifest touch. 'Because of being a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>)' — and accordingly, since deviation of the probandum can be demonstrated through the deviation of the limiting adjunct in the reason, the perceptibility is not established — this is the purport. Now, since such perceptibility exists even in qualities and the like, and since manifest form is absent there, [perceptibility] does not pervade the probandum — so how can it be a limiting adjunct? — to this he says: 'wherever' etc. And accordingly, this is a limiting adjunct that pervades the probandum as delimited by the property of the subject — this is the purport. Similarly, even for a substratum of perceptible touch, if perceptibility is not accepted due to the absence of manifest form, the unwanted consequence of non-perceptibility [would arise] — due to the absence of manifest form. This is the purport.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
na vibhucatuṣṭayam
ityasya vibhucatuṣṭayatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedavāniti nārthaḥ;
vibhāvapi pratyekaṃ taccatuṣṭayabhedasambhavenābhimatāsiddheḥ/ api tu
upalabhyamānasparśāśrayaḥ ākāśādyātmāntānyatamabhinna iti artho
vivakṣita ityāśayenāha -
idamākāśādipratyekabhedasādhanābhiprāyeṇeti/
children.translated_text: The meaning of 'not the four all-pervading [substances]' is not: 'possessing a difference whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by being-the-four-all-pervading-substances.' For even each all-pervading substance individually possesses a difference from each of those four — hence what is intended [by the opponent] would be unestablished. Rather, the meaning intended is: 'the perceivable substratum of touch is non-different from one of <s>ākāśa</s> (space), etc. up to <s>ātman</s> (self).' With this intent, he says: 'with the intention of proving individual difference from <s>ākāśa</s> and the rest.'

children.text:
tathā ca hetāviti/ 'pratyakṣasparśāśrayatvaṃ
pratyakṣatvavyabhicāri pratyakṣatvavyāpakodbhūtarūpavyabhicāritvāt;
yat yadvyāpakavyabhicāri tat tadvyabhicāri' iti prayogo 'tra
vivakṣitaḥ/ nanu 'vāyuḥ bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayaḥ
pratyakṣasparśāśrayatvāt' ityanumāne udbhūtarūpasya upādhitvaṃ na
sambhavati/ upādheḥ udbhūtarūpasya sādhyavyāpakatvābhāvāt
bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvavati guṇādau udbhūtarūpābhāvāt
ityāśaṅkate - nanu tādṛśapratyakṣatvasyetyādinā/
bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvasyetyarthaḥ/ tathā ceti/ pakṣaḥ vāyuḥ
tadgatadharmaḥ dravyatvam tadavacchinnaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena
tadviśiṣṭaṃ sādhyaṃ bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ tadvyāpaka
ityarthaḥ/ evaṃ ca dravyatvaviśiṣṭabahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ
guṇādau nāsti tatra dravyatvarūpaviśeṣaṇābhāvāt/ api tu dravye
ghaṭādāvevāsti/ tatra ca udbhūtarūpamastīti udbhūtarūpasya
pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakatvādupādhitvamupapadyata iti/ upādhirhi
kevalasādhyavyāpakaḥ, pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakaḥ,
sādhanāvacchinnasādhyavyāpaka iti trividhaḥ/ tatra
madhyamo 'yamupādhiriti bhāvaḥ/ evamiti vyākhyeyaṃ padam/ tasya
vyākhyānaṃ pratyakṣasparśāśrayasyāpyudbhūtarūpābhāvena
pratyakṣatvānaṅgīkāra iti/ udbhūtarūpasya sādhyavyāpakasya
vāyāvabhāvena vyāpakābhāvāt vyāpyābhāva iti rītyā
pratyakṣatvābhāvasya siddheriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'And accordingly, in the reason' — the inference intended here is: 'the perceptible substratum of touch deviates from perceptibility, because it deviates from manifest form (<s>udbhūtarūpa</s>), which pervades perceptibility; whatever deviates from a pervader deviates from the pervaded — this is [like the inference].' Now, in the inference 'Wind is the object of perception generated by an external sense-organ, because it is the perceptible substratum of touch,' manifest form cannot function as a limiting adjunct. Because the limiting adjunct, manifest form, does not pervade the probandum, since in qualities and the like where external-sense-generated perceptibility obtains, manifest form is absent — he raises the doubt with 'Now, of such perceptibility' etc. The meaning is: of external-sense-generated perceptibility. 'And accordingly' — the subject is wind; its property is substance-hood (<s>dravyatva</s>); the probandum, qualified by that through the relation of co-location, is external-sense-generated perceptibility; the pervader of that — this is the meaning. And accordingly, external-sense-generated perceptibility qualified by substance-hood does not exist in qualities and the like, since the qualifier in the form of substance-hood is absent there; but it exists only in substances such as pots and the like. And manifest form exists there [in pots etc.] — hence the status of manifest form as a limiting adjunct that pervades the probandum as delimited by the subject-property is established. The limiting adjunct is threefold: that which pervades the probandum simply, that which pervades the probandum as delimited by the subject-property, and that which pervades the probandum as delimited by the reason. Of these, this is the middle type of limiting adjunct — this is the purport. 'Similarly' — this is the word to be glossed. Its gloss is: 'even for a substratum of perceptible touch, non-acceptance of perceptibility due to the absence of manifest form.' Because of the absence of the pervader, namely manifest form, in wind, the absence of the pervaded — namely perceptibility — is established by the principle of pervader-absence-entailing-pervaded-absence — this is the purport.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: sṛṣṭisaṃhāraprakriyā
children.translated_text: The Process of Creation and Dissolution

children.text:
idānīṃ
kāryarūpapṛthivyādicatuṣṭayasya utpattivināśakramaḥ kathyate/ īśvarasya
cikīrṣāvaśāt paramāṇuṣu kriyā
children.translated_text: Now the order of origination and destruction of the fourfold product-form of earth and the like is described. By the force of the desire to create (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) of <s>Īśvara</s> (God), action arises in the atoms.

children.text:
jāyate/ tataḥ
paramāṇudvayasaṃyoge sati dvyaṇukamutpadyate/ tribhireva dvyaṇukaiḥ
tryaṇukaṃ utpadyate/ evaṃ caturaṇukādikrameṇa mahatī pṛthivī, mahatya
āpaḥ, mahattejaḥ, mahāvāyuḥ utpadyate/ evamutpannasya kāryadravyasya
saṃjihīrṣāvaśāt kriyayā paramāṇudvayavibhāge dvyaṇukanāśa
ityevaṃ pṛthivyādināśaḥ/ asamavāyikāraṇanāśāt dvyaṇukanāśaḥ/
samavāyikāraṇanāśāt tryaṇukānāśa iti saṃpradāyaḥ/
sarvatrāsamavāyikāraṇanāśāt dravyanāśa iti navīnāḥ/
children.translated_text: From that, when there is conjunction of two atoms, a dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) is produced. From exactly three dyads, a triad (<s>tryaṇuka</s>) is produced. Thus, through the progression of tetrads and so forth, the great earth, the great waters, the great fire, and the great wind are produced. Of the product-substance thus produced, by the force of the desire to dissolve (<s>saṃjihīrṣā</s>), through action, when the conjunction of two atoms is separated, the destruction of the dyad [occurs] — and thus the destruction of earth and the like. According to the traditional view (<s>saṃpradāya</s>): the destruction of the dyad is due to the destruction of its non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>); the destruction of the triad is due to the destruction of its inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>). According to the moderns (<s>navīnāḥ</s>): the destruction of any substance is due to the destruction of its non-inherent cause.

children.text:
kiṃ punaḥ
paramāṇusadbhāve pramāṇam? ucyate - jālasūryamarīcisthaṃ sarvataḥ
sūkṣmatamaṃ yat dravyaṃ upalabhyate tatsāvayavam cākṣuṣadravyatvāt
ghaṭavat/ tryaṇukāvayavo 'pi sāvayavaḥ mahadārambhakatvāt kapālavat/
yaḥ dvyaṇukāvayavaḥ sa eva paramāṇuḥ/ sa ca nityaḥ, tasyāpi kāryatve
anavasthāprasaṅgāt/ sṛṣṭipralayasadbhāve 'dhātā yathāpūrvaṃ
akalpayat' ityādi śrutireva pramāṇam/
'sarvakāryadravyadhvaṃso 'vāntarapralayaḥ, sarvabhāvakāryadhvaṃso
mahāpralayaḥ' iti vivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: What, then, is the means of valid knowledge for the existence of atoms? It is said: the finest substance that is observed in a sunbeam passing through a lattice-window — that is composite, because it is a visible substance, like a pot. Its component, the triad, is also composite, because it is the originator of a large [substance], like a potsherd. That which is the component of the dyad is the atom itself. And it is eternal, because if even that were a product, there would be an infinite regress. As for the existence of creation and dissolution, the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) 'The Creator fashioned [all things] as before' and the like is itself the means of valid knowledge. The distinction is: 'The destruction of all product-substances is a minor dissolution (<s>avāntarapralaya</s>); the destruction of all product-entities is the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>).'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanu paramāṇupuñjasyaiva ghaṭādirūpatvena
atiriktāvayavinaḥ asattvāt pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayasya
nityatvānityatvābhyāṃ vibhāgakathanamanupapannaṃ ityāśaṅkāṃ
vārayati -- idānīmiti/ pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayanirūpaṇānantaram
ityarthaḥ/ vdyaṇukanāśa ityasya paramāṇudvayasaṃyoganāśādityādiḥ/
sarvatreti/ janyadravyasāmānya ityarthaḥ/ sarvatra ekarītirevocitā
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, since the pot and the like are merely a mass of atoms, and since no composite whole (<s>avayavin</s>) distinct from atoms exists, the statement of the fourfold division of earth and the like through the division of eternal and non-eternal is unjustified — he prevents this doubt with: 'Now.' The meaning is: after the examination of the fourfold earth and the rest. 'Destruction of the dyad' — the supplement is: due to the destruction of the conjunction of two atoms. 'Everywhere' — the meaning is: in the generality of produced substances. The purport is: a single method is appropriate everywhere.

children.text:
cākṣuṣadravyatvāditi/
cākṣuṣatve sati dravyatvādityarthaḥ/ rūpādau ātmani ca
vyabhicāravāraṇāya viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇe/ na ca idaṃ aprayojakamiti
śaṅkyam/ cākṣuṣaṃ prati kāraṇasya mahattvasya truṭāvapekṣitatayā
sāvayavatvaṃ vinā avayavasaṅkhyājanyasya tasya svīkartumaśakyatvādinti
saṅkṣepaḥ/ yatkiciñjjanyadravyadhvaṃsasya idānīmapi sattvāt sarveti/
nityadravyāṇāṃ dhvaṃsāsambhavāt kāryeti/ paramāṇuniṣṭharūpādīnāṃ
tadānīmapi sattvāt dravyeti/ dhvaṃsānāṃ dhvaṃsāṃsaṃbhavena
mahāpralaye 'pi sattvāt bhāvetīti dik/
children.translated_text: 'Because it is a visible substance' (<s>cākṣuṣadravyatvāt</s>) — the meaning is: because it is substance-hood while being visible. The qualificand and qualifier [are stated] to prevent deviation in qualities and the like, and in the self.
