Nor should one doubt that this [inference] is pointless — because, in summary, since magnitude (<s>mahattva</s>), which is the cause of being visible, requires a minimum [size], it cannot be accepted without compositeness, because without compositeness the number-in-parts-generated [magnitude] cannot be accepted. 'All' — since the destruction of any produced substance exists even now. 'Product' — since the destruction of eternal substances is impossible. 'Substance' — since the qualities such as form residing in atoms exist even then. 'Entity' (<s>bhāva</s>) — since destructions, being impossible to be themselves destroyed, exist even during the great dissolution. This is the indication.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
paramāṇupuñjasyaiveti/ paramāṇusamūhasyaivetyarthaḥ/
atiriktāvayavina iti/ paramāṇubhinnasya avayavina ityarthaḥ/
vibhāgakathanamanupapannamiti/ anityasya pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayasyābhāvāt
iti bhāvaḥ/ mūle cikīrṣāvaśāditi/ sisṛkṣāvaśādityarthaḥ/
tribhireva vdyaṇukairiti/ dvābhyāṃ dvyaṇukābhyāṃ tryaṇukotpattiḥ na
bhavati/ tryaṇukamiti
1tritvasaṅkhyākāṇvavayavakatvapravṛttinimittakatryaṇukaśabdānupapatteriti
matvā evamuktam/ kāryadravyasya saṃjihīrṣāvaśāditi/
kāryandravyaviṣayakeśvarakartṛkasaṃhārecchāvaśādityarthaḥ/
asamavāyikāraṇanāśāditi/ dvyaṇukasya asamavāyikāraṇaṃ yaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Merely a mass of atoms' — the meaning is: merely an aggregate of atoms. 'A composite whole distinct from atoms' — the meaning is: a composite whole different from atoms. 'The statement of division is unjustified' — because the non-eternal fourfold earth and the like would be non-existent. This is the purport. In the root text, 'by the force of desire to create' — the meaning is: by the force of the desire to emit. 'From exactly three dyads' — a triad is not produced from two dyads. The word <s>tryaṇuka</s> (triad) is so called because its etymological derivation requires three-ness as a number, the component-hood of atomic [parts], and the occasion for applying [the term] — considering this, [the author] said thus. 'Of the product-substance, by the force of the desire to dissolve' — the meaning is: by the force of God's desire to dissolve, directed toward the product-substance. 'Due to the destruction of the non-inherent cause' — the non-inherent cause of the dyad is the

children.text:
paramāṇudvayasaṃyogaḥ
tasya nāśāt dvyaṇukasya nāśa ityarthaḥ/ samavāyikāraṇanāśāt
tryaṇukanāśa iti tryaṇukasya yat samavāyikāraṇaṃ dvyaṇukaṃ tasya
nāśāt tryaṇukanāśa ityarthaḥ/ dvyaṇukasya tu
samavāyikāraṇanāśāt nāśo na vaktuṃ śakyate/ samavāyikāraṇasya
paramāṇoḥ nāśāsambhavāditi bhāvaḥ/ jālasūryetyādi/ prathamānumānaṃ
dvyaṇukasādhakam, dvitīyānumānaṃ paramāṇusādhakamiti vivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: conjunction of two atoms; due to its destruction, the destruction of the dyad — this is the meaning. 'Due to the destruction of the inherent cause, the destruction of the triad' — the inherent cause of the triad is the dyad; due to its destruction, the destruction of the triad — this is the meaning. But the destruction of the dyad cannot be stated as due to the destruction of its inherent cause, because the destruction of the atom, which is its inherent cause, is impossible — this is the purport. 'In a sunbeam through a lattice-window' etc. — the first inference establishes the dyad; the second inference establishes the atom — this is the distinction.

children.text:
cākṣuṣadravyatvādityasya
cākṣuṣaṃ ca tat dravyatvaṃ ceti samāse ghaṭādau cākṣuṣaṃ yat dravyatvaṃ
tasyaiva ātmani sattvena sāvayavatvābhāvavati tatra hetoḥ vyabhicāraḥ
syāt/ ataḥ cākṣuṣaṃ ca tat dravyaṃ ca cākṣuṣadravyaṃ tasya bhāvaḥ iti
children.translated_text: 'Because it is a visible substance' (<s>cākṣuṣadravyatvāt</s>) — if the compound is analyzed as 'visible, and that is substance-hood,' then since substance-hood that is visible exists even in the self, and since compositeness is absent there, there would be deviation of the reason in the self. Therefore, the compound should be analyzed as 'visible, and that is a substance — the property of being such a visible substance' —

children.text:
1. tritvasaṃkhyāketi/
trīṇi aṇūni yasya tat tryaṇukamiti vigrahaḥ/ tathā ca
tritvaṃsaṃkhyāviśiṣṭāṇvavayavakatvaṃ tryaṇukaśabdasya pravṛttinimittam/
tatra tribhirdvyaṇukaiḥ tryaṇukotpattāveva saṃgacchata iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Three-ness as a number' — the etymological analysis is: <s>tryaṇuka</s> means that whose atoms are three. And accordingly, the occasion for applying the word <s>tryaṇuka</s> is: the component-hood of atoms qualified by the number three-ness. That is consistent only with the production of a triad from three dyads — this is the purport.

children.text:
cākṣuṣadravyaṃ tasya
bhāvaḥ iti samāso 'tra vivakṣitaḥ/ tena cākṣuṣatvaviśiṣṭadravyatvaṃ
heturiti phalati/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena/ ātmani
cākṣuṣatvarūpaviśeṣaṇābhāvāt viśiṣṭadravyatvarūpo hetuḥ nāstīti
na vyabhicāra
children.translated_text: 'A visible substance — the property of being such' — this compound analysis is intended here. And accordingly, the result is that the reason is substance-hood qualified by visibility. And the qualification is through the relation of co-location. Since the qualifier in the form of visibility is absent in the self, the reason in the form of qualified substance-hood does not exist there — hence there is no deviation.

children.text:
ityāśayenāha -
cākṣuṣatve sati dravyatvādityartha iti/ cākṣuṣatvamātroktau
sāvayavatvarūpasādhyābhāvavati rūpādau cākṣuṣatvasattvāt vyabhicāra
iti tadvāraṇāya dravyatvopādānam/ dravyatvamātroktau ātmani
vyabhicāra iti tadvāraṇāya dravyatvopādānam/ dravyatvamātroktau
ātmani vyabhicāra iti tadvāraṇāya
cakṣurindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvarūpacākṣuṣatvopādānam/
viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇe iti/ viśeṣyaṃ dravyatvam/ viśeṣaṇaṃ
cākṣuṣatvam/
children.translated_text: With this intent he says: 'The meaning is: substance-hood while being visible.' If only visibility were stated, since visibility exists in qualities like form, where the probandum of compositeness is absent, there would be deviation — to prevent that, substance-hood is included. If only substance-hood were stated, there would be deviation in the self — to prevent that, visibility in the form of being the object of perception generated by the visual sense-organ is included. 'Qualificand and qualifier' — the qualificand is substance-hood; the qualifier is visibility.

children.text:
na
cedamaprayojakamiti/ cākṣuṣadravyatvarūpaheturastu,
sāvayavatvarūpasādhyaṃ māstu ityāśaṅkāyāṃ
tadvārakatarkābhāvādityarthaḥ/ aprayojakam ityasya
vyabhicāraśaṅkānivartakatarkaṃśūnyamityarthaḥ/ tryaṇukarūpe pakṣe
sāvayavatvaṃ nāsti cet cākṣuṣadravyatvarūpaheturapi na syāt/
cākṣuṣapratyakṣaṃ prati mahattvasya kāraṇatayā tryaṇuke mahattvaṃ yadi syāt
tadaiva cākṣuṣatvaṃ tasya bhavet/ tryaṇuke mahattvaṃ tu
avayavagatabahutvasaṅkhyājanyamiti tryaṇukaṃ sāvayavamiti
aṅgīkāryam/ tathā ca sāvayavatvasya mahattvadvārā
tryaṇukacākṣuṣatvaprayojakatvāt sāvayavatvacākṣuṣatvayoḥ
children.translated_text: 'Nor is this pointless' — in response to the doubt: let the reason in the form of visible substance-hood exist, but let the probandum in the form of compositeness not exist — the meaning is: because there is no <s>tarka</s> (reductio) mediating that [connection]. The meaning of 'pointless' is: devoid of the <s>tarka</s> that removes the doubt of deviation. If compositeness does not exist in the subject, namely the triad, then even the reason in the form of visible substance-hood would not exist [there]. Since magnitude (<s>mahattva</s>), which is the cause of visibility for visual perception, requires [sufficient size], if a triad were to possess magnitude, only then would it be visible. But the magnitude in a triad is generated by the plurality-number residing in the parts — hence the triad must be accepted as composite. And accordingly, since compositeness is a cause of the triad's visibility through the medium of magnitude, between compositeness and visibility there exists

children.text:
prayojyaprayojakabhāvarūpānukūlatarkasadbhāvāt
nedamanumānaṃ aprayojakam ityāśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: a supporting <s>tarka</s> (reductio) in the form of the cause-effect relation — hence this inference is not pointless. This is the intent.

children.text:
nanu
tryaṇukagatamahattvasya nityatvasvīkāreṇa avayavasaṅkhyājanyatvasya
anāvaśyakatvāt sāvayavatvaṃ vināpi cākṣuṣatvopapatteḥ
aprayojakameva dvyaṇukasādhakatvenopanyastamanumānam
ityāśaṅkyāha - saṅkṣepa iti/
aṇuvyavahārasyāṇuparimāṇanibandhanatayā
tadāśrayadvyaṇukākhyāṇuvastunaḥ avaśyāṅgīkaraṇīyatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, if the magnitude residing in the triad is accepted as eternal, then since the production from part-number would be unnecessary, and since visibility would be possible even without compositeness, the inference presented to establish the dyad is simply pointless — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'in summary.' The purport is: since the usage '<s>aṇu</s>' (minute/atomic) is grounded in atomic dimension (<s>aṇuparimāṇa</s>), and since the minute entity called the dyad, which is the substratum of that [atomic dimension], must necessarily be accepted.

children.text:
sarvabhāvakāryadhvaṃsaḥ
mahāpralaya iti/ mahāpralayānantaraṃ punaḥ sṛṣṭyanabhyupagamenedam/
tadabhyupagame tu punaḥ sṛṣṭyupayogidharmādharmayorāvaśyakatvāt
sarvaṃbhāvakāryadhvaṃsarūpo mahāpralaya eva na syāt ityavadheyam/
'dhātā yathāpūrvamakalpayat' iti śrutistu
avāntarapralayānantarasṛṣṭiviṣayeti teṣāmāśayaḥ/ mahāpralaye 'pi
sattvāditi/ tathā ca sarvakāryāntargatadhvaṃsasya dhvaṃsābhāvāt
sarvakāryadhvaṃsarūpalakṣaṇāsambhavaḥ syāt iti tadvāraṇāya
bhāvapadamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The destruction of all product-entities is the great dissolution' — this is on the view that there is no further creation after the great dissolution. If further creation is accepted, then since <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), which are useful for further creation, would be necessary, the great dissolution in the form of the destruction of all product-entities would itself not occur — this should be noted. The <s>śruti</s> 'The Creator fashioned as before' is held by them to pertain to creation after a minor dissolution — this is their intent. 'Even during the great dissolution, because they exist' — and accordingly, since the destruction of a destruction is impossible, the destruction that is included among all products would exist — hence the definition in the form of 'destruction of all products' would face the defect of impossibility. To prevent that, the word 'entity' (<s>bhāva</s>) [is added] — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: ākāśanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Ākāśa</s> (Space/Ether)

children.text: AnTs_14 śabdaguṇam ākāśam / tac caikaṃ vibhu nityaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 14:] <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) has sound (<s>śabda</s>) as its quality. And it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: śabdaguṇakamākāśam/ tacca ekam, vibhu, nityam ca/
children.translated_text: <s>Ākāśa</s> has sound as its quality. And it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
ākāśaṃ lakṣayati -
śabdaguṇakamiti/ nanu ākāśamapi pṛthivyādivannānā kiṃ? netyāha -
taccaikamiti/ bhede pramāṇābhāvāt ityarthaḥ/ ekatvādeva sarvatra
śabdopalabdheḥ vibhutvaṃ aṅgīkartavyamityāha- vibhviti/
sarvamūrtadravyasaṃyogitvam vibhutvam/ mūrtatvam
paricchinnaparimāṇavattvaṃ, kriyāvattvam vā/ vibhutvādeva ātmavat
nityaṃ ityāha - nityaṃ ceti/
children.translated_text: He defines space (<s>ākāśa</s>) — 'having sound as its quality.' Now, is space also manifold like earth and the rest? No — he says: 'And that is one.' The meaning is: because there is no means of valid knowledge for [establishing] difference. Because of its oneness itself, since sound is apprehended everywhere, all-pervasiveness must be accepted — he says: 'all-pervading.' All-pervasiveness is conjunction with all corporeal substances. Corporeality (<s>mūrtatva</s>) is possessing a limited magnitude, or possessing motion. Because of all-pervasiveness itself, like the self, it is eternal — he says: 'and eternal.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
śabdaguṇakamityatra
śabdavaditi vaktavye tathākathanaṃ 'ākāśe śabda eva viśeṣaguṇa' iti
dyotanāya/ ghaṭākāśo maṭhākāśa ityādivyavahārasyopādhikṛtatvena
asādhakatvāt ākāśasya anekatve pramāṇaṃ netyāha - bheda iti/
ekatvāditi/
children.translated_text: In the root text, where it says 'having sound as its quality,' instead of saying 'possessing sound,' the purpose of stating it thus is to indicate that 'in space, sound alone is the specific quality.' Since the usages 'pot-space,' 'hall-space' and the like are caused by limiting adjuncts and hence do not prove [the plurality of space], there is no means of valid knowledge for the plurality of space — he says: 'difference.' 'Because of oneness' —

children.text:
ākāśasyetyādiḥ/
nanvekatve 'pi avibhutvaṃmastu ityata āha - sarvatreti/
sarvadigavacchedenetyarthaḥ/ paricchinnaparimāṇavattvamiti/ yadi
paricchinnasya apakarṣāśrayatvātmakatayā paramaṇoraṇutaratvena
dvyaṇukaparimāṇāpekṣayā paramāṇuparimāṇasya apakṛṣṭatvābhāvāt
paramāṇuṣu avyāptamidaṃ lakṣaṇamityucyate tadāpyāhakriyāvattvamiti/
vastutastu lāghavamevottarakalpānusaraṇe bījam iti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: [supply:] 'of space' and so forth. Now, even if space is one, let it not be all-pervading — to this he says: 'everywhere.' The meaning is: in the delimited portion of every direction. 'Possessing limited magnitude' — if it is objected that this definition has under-extension in atoms, since the atom's magnitude is not inferior compared to the magnitude of a dyad because, the atom being limited, its limitedness consists in being the locus of inferiority, and the atom's magnitude is not inferior [to anything] since it is the smallest — even so, he says: 'possessing motion.' In reality, however, it should be noted that parsimony alone is the basis for following the alternative formulation.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu ghaṭākāśaḥ
maṭhākāśa ityādivyavahārāt ākāśe 'pi bhedo 'stītyavagamyate/
tathā ca bhede pramāṇābhāvāditi dīpikoktiḥ na saṅgacchate/
uktavyavahārasyaiva ākāśasyānekatve pramāṇatvāt ityāśaṅkya
ghaṭamaṭhādirūpo ya ākāśasya avacchedakaḥ padārthaḥ tadgataṃ
bhedamāśritya ghaṭākāśo maṭhākāśa ityādivyavahāraḥ, na tu
ākāśagataṃ bhedam/ ataḥ sa na bhede pramāṇamiti samādhānaṃ abhiprayan
āha - ghaṭākāśa iti/ upādhikṛtatveneti/
children.translated_text: Now, from the usage 'pot-space,' 'hall-space' and the like, it is understood that there is difference even in space. And accordingly, the <s>Dīpikā</s>'s statement 'because there is no means of valid knowledge for difference' does not cohere — since the very stated usage itself is a means of valid knowledge for the plurality of space. Anticipating this doubt — the usage 'pot-space,' 'hall-space' and the like is based on the difference residing in the limiting entity (<s>avacchedaka</s>) such as the pot, hall, etc. of space, not on a difference residing in space itself. Therefore that [usage] is not a proof for difference [in space] — intending this resolution, he says: 'pot-space.' 'Because it is caused by limiting adjuncts' —

children.text:
ghaṭamaṭhajñadirūpāvacchedakagatabhedānimittakatvenetyarthaḥ/
asādhakatvāditi/ ākāśabhedāsādhakatvādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: because it is caused by the difference residing in the limiting entities such as pot, hall, etc. 'Because it does not prove' — the meaning is: because it does not prove difference in space.

children.text:
aṇutaratveneti/
utkarṣāśrayāṇuparimāṇavattvenetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'By being more minute' — the meaning is: by possessing an atomic magnitude that is the locus of superiority.

children.text:
nanu paricchinnatvaṃ
nāpakarṣāśrayatvam/ api tu paramamahatparimāṇabhinnatvam,
ākāśādicatuṣṭayānyatamāsamavetatvaṃ vā/ tathā ca
paramamahatparimāṇānyaparimāṇavattvaṃ
ākāśādicatuṣṭayānyatamāsamavetaparimāṇavattvaṃ vā mūrtatvam, tacca
paramāṇuṣvapi vartata iti na tatrāvyāptiḥ/ ato
dvitīyalakṣaṇānusaraṇe nāvyāptirheturityāśaṅkyāha - vastutasatu
iti/
children.translated_text: Now, limitedness (<s>paricchinnatva</s>) is not being the locus of inferiority, but rather being different from the maximally great magnitude, or being non-inherent in any of the four [all-pervading substances] such as space and the rest. And accordingly, corporeality is possessing a magnitude that is different from the maximally great magnitude, or possessing a magnitude not inhered in any of the four such as space and the rest — and that exists even in atoms. Hence there is no under-extension there. Therefore, the reason for following the second definition is not under-extension — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'In reality, however.'

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: kālanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Time

children.text: AnTs_15 atītādivyavahārahetuḥ kālaḥ / sa caiko vibhur nityaś ca //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_15: Time is the cause of the usages 'past' and the like. And it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: atītādivyavahārahetuḥ kālaḥ/ sa ca ekaḥ vibhuḥ nityaśca/
children.translated_text: Time is the cause of the usages 'past' and the like. And it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
kālaṃ lakṣayati -
atīteti/ sarvādhāraḥ kālaḥ sarvaṅkāryanimittakāraṇam/
children.translated_text: He defines time — 'past' and so forth. Time is the substratum of everything and the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>) of all products.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
atītādivyavahārahetuḥ kāla iti mūle ādinā
anāgatādiparigrahaḥ/ atītatvaṃ ca vartamānadhvaṃsapratiyogitvam/
children.translated_text: In the root text 'Time is the cause of the usages past and the like,' by the word 'and the like,' future and other [usages] are included. And 'past-ness' (<s>atītatva</s>) is being the counter-positive of the destruction of the present.

children.text:
varnamānatvam iha
śabdaprayogādhikaraṇakālavṛttivam/ bhaviṣyatvaṃ ca
vartamānaprāgabhāvapratiyogitvaṃ/ atra sarvatra kālasya ghaṭakatayā
śabdaprayogarūpātītādivyavahāre hetutvaṃ tasya iti dhyeyam/ na ca
tādṛśavyavahāraḥ sūryaparispandopādhimādāya sambhavatīti vācyam/
anugatasya vyavahārasya anugataviṣayaṃ vinā asambhavena
atiriktakālasvīkārāditi dik/ sarvādhāra iti/
kālikasambandhenetyādiḥ/ atra vibhinnakālikayoḥ
ādhārādheyabhāvavirahāt kriyādeḥ sarvādhāratvaśaṅkaiva
nāvataratīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Present-ness' (<s>vartamānatva</s>) here means occurring in the time that is the substratum of verbal usage. And 'future-ness' (<s>bhaviṣyattva</s>) is being the counter-positive of the prior absence of the present. In all these cases, it should be noted that time has causality in the usages 'past' and the like, which are in the form of verbal usage, through being a constituent [of those usages]. Nor should it be said that such usage is possible through the limiting adjunct of the revolution of the sun — because, since a uniform usage cannot exist without a uniform object, an extra-categorial time must be accepted. This is the indication. 'Substratum of everything' — [supply:] 'through the temporal relation' and so forth. Here, since between things at different times there is no container-contained relation, the doubt regarding the universality of substratum-hood of action and the like does not even arise — this is the purport.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu ghaṭaḥ atītaḥ
vartamānaḥ bhaviṣyan ityādiśabdaprayogaḥ kālasya yaḥ upādhiḥ
avacchedakaḥ sūryaparispandaḥ taddhetukaḥ/ tathā ca atīta ityasya
śabdaprayogādhikaraṇasūryaparispandavṛttidhvaṃsapratiyogītyarthaḥ/
vartamāna ityasya śabdaprayogādhikaraṇasūryaparispandavṛttirityarthaḥ/
bhaviṣyannityasya
śabdaprayogādhikaraṇasūryaparispandavṛttiprāgabhāvapratiyogītyarthaḥ/
tathā ca na kālaḥ sidhyati ityāśaṅkate - na ca tādṛśavyavahāra
iti/ samādhatte - anugatasyeti/ ekarūpaḥ atītaḥ ityādiḥ vyavahāraḥ
ekarūpaṃ viṣayaṃ vinā na sambhavati iti ekaḥ kālaḥ svīkaraṇīyaḥ/
sūryaparispandastu anekaḥ/ ataḥ kālaghaṭanayaiva atītatvādikaṃ
nirvācyaṃ iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, the verbal usage 'the pot is past, present, future' is caused by the revolution of the sun, which is the limiting adjunct of time. And accordingly, the meaning of 'past' is: being the counter-positive of the destruction that occurs in the revolution of the sun that is the substratum of verbal usage. The meaning of 'present' is: occurring in the revolution of the sun that is the substratum of verbal usage. The meaning of 'future' is: being the counter-positive of the prior absence of the occurrence in the revolution of the sun that is the substratum of verbal usage. And accordingly, time is not established — he raises this doubt with: 'Nor should it be said that such usage.' He resolves it with: 'Because a uniform [usage].' A uniform usage of the form 'past' etc. cannot exist without a uniform object — therefore a single time must be accepted. But the revolutions of the sun are many. Therefore, past-ness and the like should be explained only through the constitution of time — this is the purport.

children.text:
api ca sūryaparispandaḥ
atītādiviṣayeṣu sākṣātsambandhena nāsti/ ataḥ
1svāśrayatapanasaṃyogisaṃyogādirūpaparamparāsambandhenaiva
sūryaparispandavṛttitvaṃ ghaṭādervaktavyam/ tadapekṣatā lāghavāt
sākṣātsambandhaśālikālasvīkaraṇamevocitamityāśayenāha - digiti/
viṣayatāsambandhena sarvādhāratvaṃ jñānasyāpyasti ityāśaṅkya
kālikasambandhenetyādiriti kathitam/
sarvapadārthaniṣṭhakālikasambandhāvacchinnādheyatānirūpitādhikaraṇatvaṃ
sarvādhāratvamatra vivakṣitamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Moreover, the revolution of the sun does not exist in objects of past and the like through a direct relation. Therefore, the occurrence in the revolution of the sun for a pot and the like must be stated through a mediate relation in the form of conjunction with what is conjoined with the sun, which is the substratum of the [revolution], and so forth. Compared to that cumbersome [explanation], the acceptance of time having a direct relation is more appropriate — with this intent he says: 'This is the indication.' Since even cognition has universal substratum-hood through the relation of object-hood — anticipating this doubt, it was said 'through the temporal relation' and so forth. The meaning is: universal substratum-hood here means the substratum-hood that determines the superstratum-hood delimited by the temporal relation residing in all categories — this is the purport.

children.text:
1. svāśrayeti/ svaṃ
sūryaparispandaḥ tadāśrayaḥ sūryaḥ tatsaṃyogī kālaḥ tatsaṃyogī
ghaṭasya/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Its own substratum' — 'its own' means the revolution of the sun; 'its substratum' is the sun; 'conjoined with that' is time; 'conjoined with that' is [the relation] of the pot.

children.text:
nanu kriyāmātraṃ
kālopādhiriti siddhāntāt kriyāyāḥ kālikasambandhena
sarvādhāratvasattvāt tatrātivyāptirityata āha - atra
vibhinnakālikayoriti/ kriyāyāḥ
tatsamakālavartisakalapadārthādhāratve 'pi
tadasamakālavartipadārthādhāratvaṃ na saṃbhavati,
bhinnakālikayorādhārādheyabhāvavirahāt/ sarvādhāratvamityatra
sarvapadaṃ tu sakalakālavartisarvapadārthaparam, ato na
kriyāyāmativyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, since it is an established doctrine that mere motion is the limiting adjunct of time, and since the universal substratum-hood through the temporal relation exists in motion, there would be over-extension there — to this he says: 'here, between things at different times.' Although motion is the substratum of all categories existing at the same time as itself, it is not the substratum of categories not existing at the same time. [This is] because there is no container-contained relation between things at different times. And the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) in 'universal substratum-hood' refers to all categories existing at all times — therefore there is no over-extension in motion. This is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: diṅnirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Direction

children.text: AnTs_16 prācyādivyavahārahetur dik / sā caikā vibhvī nityā ca //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_16: Direction is the cause of the usages 'eastern' and the like. And it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: prācyādivyavahārahetuḥ dik/ sā ca ekā vibhvī nityā ca/
children.translated_text: Direction is the cause of the usages 'eastern' and the like. And it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
diśo lakṣaṇamāha -
prācīti/ digapi kāryamātranimittakāraṇam/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of direction — 'eastern' and so forth. Direction too is the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>) of all products.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
prācyādivyavahārahetuḥ iti mūle ādinā
pratīcyādiparigrahaḥ/ udayācalasannihitamūrtāvacchinnā dik prācī/
astācalasannihitamūrtāvacchinna dik pratīcī/
merusannihitamūrtāvacchinna dik udīcī/ tadvyavahitamūrtāvacchinnā
tu dakṣiṇā/
children.translated_text: In the root text 'Direction is the cause of the usages eastern and the like,' by the word 'and the like,' western and other [directions] are included. The direction delimited by a corporeal entity near the mountain of sunrise (<s>udayācala</s>) is eastern. The direction delimited by a corporeal entity near the mountain of sunset (<s>astācala</s>) is western. The direction delimited by a corporeal entity near [Mount] <s>Meru</s> is northern. And [the direction delimited by] a corporeal entity remote from that is southern.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: ātmanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of the Self

children.text: AnTs_17[1] jñānādhikaraṇam ātmā / sa dvividhaḥ paramātmā jīvātmā ca / tatreśvaraḥ sarvajñaḥ paramātmaika eva / jīvātmā pratiśarīraṃ bhinno vibhur nityaś ca //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_17[1]: The self (<s>ātman</s>) is the substratum of cognition. It is of two kinds: the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>) and the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>). Among these, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), the omniscient one, is the one and only supreme self. The individual self is distinct in each body, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: jñānādhikaraṇam ātmā/ saḥ dvividhaḥ jīvātmā paramātmā ceti/
children.translated_text: The self is the substratum of cognition. It is of two kinds: the individual self and the supreme self.

children.text: īśvarasādhanam
children.translated_text: Proof of the existence of God (<s>Īśvara</s>)

children.text:
tatreśvaraḥ sarvajñaḥ
paramātmā eka eva/
children.translated_text: Among these, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), the omniscient one, is the one and only supreme self.

children.text: jīvātmanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of the individual self

children.text:
jīvastu
pratiśarīraṃ bhinnaḥ/ vibhuḥ nityaśca/
children.translated_text: But the individual self (<s>jīva</s>) is distinct in each body, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
ātmano lakṣaṇamāha
- jñāneti/ ātmānaṃ vibhajate - sa dvividha iti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of the self — 'cognition' and so forth. He divides the self — 'It is of two kinds.'

children.text:
paramātmano lakṣaṇamāha
- tatreti/ nityajñānādhikaraṇatvam īśvaratvam/ nanu
īśvarasadbhāve kiṃ pramāṇam? na tāvat pratyakṣam/ taddhi bāhyaṃ
āntaraṃ vā/ nādyaḥ, arūpidravyatvāt/ na dvitīyaḥ,
ātmasukhaduḥkhādivyatiriktatvāt/ nāpyanumānam, liṅgābhāvāt/
nāpyāgamaḥ, tathāvidhāgamābhāvāt iti cet - na/ 'aṅkurādikaṃ
sakartṛkaṃ kāryatvāte ghaṭavat' ityanumānasyaiva pramāṇatvāt/
upādānagocarāparokṣajñānacikīrṣākṛtimattvaṃ kartṛtvam/ upādānaṃ
samavāyikāraṇam/ sakalaparamāṇvādisūkṣmadarśitvāt sarvajñatvam/ 'yaḥ
sarvajñaḥ sarvaṃvit' ityādyāgamo 'pi tatra pramāṇam/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of the supreme self — 'Among these.' Being the eternal substratum of cognition is Lordship (<s>īśvaratva</s>). Now, what is the means of valid knowledge for the existence of God? Not perception, first of all. For that is either external or internal. Not the first, because [God] is an incorporeal substance. Not the second, because [God] is different from the self, pleasure, pain, and the like [which are objects of internal perception]. Nor inference, because of the absence of an inferential mark. Nor scripture (<s>āgama</s>), because of the absence of such a scripture — if thus objected: no, because the inference 'Sprouts and the like have a maker, because they are products, like a pot' is itself the means of valid knowledge. Agent-hood (<s>kartṛtva</s>) is possessing immediate knowledge, desire to act (<s>cikīrṣā</s>), and effort (<s>kṛti</s>) regarding the material cause. The material cause is the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>). Because of seeing all subtle things such as all atoms and the rest, [God has] omniscience. The scripture '<s>yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvaṃvit</s>' ('He who is omniscient, who knows all') and the like is also a means of valid knowledge for that.

children.text:
jīvasya lakṣaṇamāha -
jīva iti/ sukhādyāśrayatvaṃ jīvalakṣaṇam/ nanu 'manuṣyo 'ham',
'brāhmaṇo 'ham' ityādau sarvatra ahaṃpratyaye śarīrasyaiva viṣayatvāt
śarīrameva ātmā iti cet - na/ śarīrasya ātmatve
karapādādināśe śarīranāśāt ātmano 'pi nāśaprasaṅgāt/ nāpi
indriyāṇāṃ ātmatvam 'yo 'haṃ ghaṭaṃ adrākṣam so 'haṃ idānīṃ
spṛśāmi' ityanusandhānābhāvaprasaṅgāt/ anyānubhūter'the
anyasyānusandhānāyogāt/ tasmāt dehendriyavyatiriktaḥ jīvaḥ
sukhaduḥkhādivaicitryāt pratiśarīraṃ bhinnaḥ/ sa ca na paramāṇuḥ/
sarvaśarīravyāpisukhādyanupalabdhiprasaṅgāt/ na madhyamaparimāṇavān/
tathā sati anityatvaprasaṅgena kṛtahāna - akṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgāt/
tasmāt nityaḥ vibhuḥ jīvaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of the individual self — '<s>jīva</s>' and so forth. Being the substratum of pleasure and the like is the definition of the individual self. Now, in the I-cognition everywhere — 'I am a human,' 'I am a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — since the body alone is the object [of that cognition], the body itself is the self — if thus objected: no, because if the body were the self, upon the destruction of hands, feet, and the like, since the body would be destroyed, there would be the unwanted consequence of the destruction of the self as well. Nor are the sense organs the self — because there would be the unwanted consequence of the absence of recognition (<s>anusandhāna</s>) such as 'I who saw the pot am now touching [it],' since it is impossible for one person to have recognition of another's experience. Therefore, the individual self is different from the body and sense organs. Due to the variety of pleasure, pain, and the like, it is distinct in each body. And it is not an atom — because there would be the unwanted consequence of not apprehending pleasure and the like pervading the entire body. Nor does it have medium magnitude — because in that case, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-eternality, and hence the unwanted consequence of the loss of what has been done and the attainment of what has not been done. Therefore the individual self is eternal and all-pervading.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mūle jñānādhikaraṇamiti/ samavāyena
jñānavadityarthaḥ/ tatra - tayormadhye/ dīpikāyām
nityajñānādhikaraṇatvamiti/ na ca '(nityaṃ) vijñānaṃ ānandaṃ brahma' iti
śrutvā virodha iti vācyam/ ānandapadasya ānandavadarthakatāyā
iva vijñānapadasyāpi
children.translated_text: In the root text 'the substratum of cognition' — the meaning is: possessing cognition through inherence. 'Among these' — among the two. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'being the eternal substratum of cognition.' Nor should it be said that there is a contradiction with the <s>śruti</s> '(<s>nityaṃ</s>) <s>vijñānaṃ ānandaṃ brahma</s>' (Brahman is eternal consciousness and bliss) — because, just as the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss) has the meaning of 'possessing bliss,' so too the word '<s>vijñāna</s>' (consciousness)

children.text:
vijñānavadarthakatāsvīkāreṇa avirodhāt/ na ca ānandapadasyaiva
tādṛśārthakatvamasiddhamiti vācyam/ arśa ādyajantatvāṅgīkāreṇa
tādṛśārthasiddheḥ/ anyathā napuṃsakatvānupapatteḥ/ atra ānandaḥ
'bhārāpagame sukhī saṃvṛtto 'ham' itivat duḥkhābhāve upacaryate/
navīnāstu nityasukhamīśvarasyāṅgīkurvanti ityalamadhikajalpanena/
arūpidravyatvāditi/ bāhyapratyakṣaṃ prati udbhūtarūpasya hetutvāditi
bhāvaḥ/ ātmasukhaduḥkhādīti/ vijātīyātmamanassaṃyogasya
mānasapratyakṣahetoḥ īśvare 'bhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/ pramāṇatvāditi/ na
cedaṃ aprayojakamiti śaṅyam/ aprayojakamiti śaṅkyam/
kāryatvāvacchinnaṃ prati kṛtitvāvacchinnasya hetutvena
children.translated_text: can be accepted as having the meaning of 'possessing consciousness,' and hence there is no contradiction. Nor should it be said that the meaning of the word '<s>ānanda</s>' as 'possessing bliss' is itself unestablished — because such a meaning is established by accepting that [the suffix] belongs to the '<s>arśa</s>' class of affixes. Otherwise, the neuter gender [of the word '<s>ānanda</s>'] would be unjustified. Here, '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss) is figuratively used for the absence of suffering, as in 'I have become happy upon the removal of the burden.' The moderns, however, accept eternal pleasure for God — but enough of excessive discussion. 'Because it is an incorporeal substance' — the purport is: because manifest form is a cause for external perception. 'The self, pleasure, pain, and the like' — the purport is: because the conjunction of the [individual] self with mind (<s>manas</s>), which is the cause of mental perception, does not obtain in God, since [what obtains in God would be] a conjunction of mind with a self of a different species. 'Because it is a means of valid knowledge' — nor should this be doubted as being a non-probative argument. Because the non-probativeness does not arise, since the probans delimited by product-hood has causality with respect to the probandum delimited by agent-hood —

children.text:
aprayojakatvābhāvāditi dik/ upādāneti/ yadyapi kartṛtvaṃ
kṛtimattvameva saṃbhavati tathāpi aparokṣajñānādeḥ cikīrṣādikaṃ prati
kāraṇatvapradarśanāya tathoktiriti dhyeyam/ sarvaviditi/
vidadhātvartho viśeṣarūpeṇa jñānam/
children.translated_text: this is the indication. 'Material cause' — although agent-hood can simply be possessing effort, nevertheless, the mention of immediate knowledge, desire to act, and the like is for the purpose of showing their causality with respect to desire to act and so forth — this should be noted. '<s>Sarvavit</s>' — the root '<s>vid</s>' means knowledge in a specific form.

children.text:
lakṣaṇamāheti/
svarūpamāhetyarthaḥ/ mūle pratiśarīraṃ bhinna iti/ na
cāvayavopacayābhyāṃ tattaccaitrādiśarīrāṇāṃ vibhinnatve 'pi
jīvabhedābhāvāt idamasaṅgatam/ evaṃ kāyavyūhasthale 'pīti
vācyam/ samānakālikāyogajadharmājanyaśarīrabhedena jīvabhedasyaiva
vivakṣitatayā adoṣāt/ evaṃ ca etaccharīrāvacchinnabhogavān
samānakālikayogajadharmājanyataccharīrāvacchinnabhogavadbhinna iti
rītyā pratiśarīraṃ jīvabhedaḥ sādhya ityalam/
children.translated_text: 'He states the definition' — the meaning is: he states the nature. In the root text: 'distinct in each body' — nor is this incoherent because, even though different bodies of different individuals such as <s>Caitra</s> and the like differ through increase and decrease of parts, the absence of difference in selves [does not follow]. Similarly, in the case of body-aggregation [i.e., multiple bodies for one self] too — this should not be said. Because no defect arises, since what is intended is the difference of selves through the difference of bodies that are not produced by merit (<s>dharma</s>) that is simultaneous [with those of another self]. And accordingly, the difference of selves to be proved for each body is in the following manner: the one who has experience delimited by this body is different from the one who has experience delimited by that body which is not produced by merit simultaneous [with the first]. Enough.

children.text:
śarīrasyaiveti/ anyathā
manuṣyatvādīnāṃ śarīradharmatvena tathā pratyayasyaiva
asaṅgatirityabhimānaḥ nāśaprasaṅgāditi/ samavāyikāraṇanāśasya
dravyanāśakatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ yo 'hamiti/ bhūtakālikadarśanavati
vartamānakālikaspārśanavattvaṃ pratyāyyate tacca bhavatāṃ mate na
sambhavati cākṣuṣaspārśanavatorbhedāditi bhāvaḥ/
anusandhānāyogāditi/ anyathā caitreṇānubhūtasya vastunaḥ maitreṇa
smaraṇāpatteriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Of the body alone' — otherwise, since human-ness and the like are properties of the body, such a cognition would be incoherent — this opinion [would follow] because of the consequence of destruction. The purport is: because the destruction of the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) brings about the destruction of the substance. 'I who [saw]' — it conveys that the one who possesses seeing at a past time possesses touching at the present time, and that is not possible on your view, because the one who sees and the one who touches are different. 'Because of the impossibility of recognition' (<s>anusandhānāyoga</s>) — the purport is: otherwise, what was experienced by <s>Caitra</s> could be remembered by <s>Maitra</s>.

children.text:
nanu
sarvaśarīrāvacchedena ātmani sukhādisākṣātkāropapattaye
sarvaśarīravyāpitvaṃ ātmano 'stu/ tathāpi vibhutvāṅgīkāre
prayojanābhāva ityata āha - na madhyameti/ anityatvaprasaṅgeneti/
yanmadhyamaparimāṇaṃ tadanityam iti vyāpteriti bhāvaḥ/ kṛteti/
kṛtasya yāgādinā sampāditasya dharmāderhānaṃ nāśaḥ,
akṛtasyābhyāgamaḥ prāptiḥ tatprasaṅgādityarthaḥ/ kartuḥ ātmana
uttarajanmani asattvāt, akartuśca sattvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, let the self pervade the entire body so that the direct realization of pleasure and the like can be justified in the self as delimited by the entire body. Even so, there is no purpose in accepting all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>). To this he says: 'not medium' etc. 'Because of the consequence of non-eternality' — the purport is: because of the pervasion that whatever has medium magnitude is non-eternal. 'Of what is performed' (<s>kṛta</s>) — the meaning is: the destruction, i.e. annihilation, of <s>dharma</s> and the like that have been accomplished through sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and the like, and the obtainment, i.e. acquisition, of what has not been performed — there would be the consequence of that. The purport is: because in the next birth, the doer (the self) would be absent, while the non-doer would be present.

children.text:
nanu jīvasya
aṇutvameva āstām, tāvatā noktadoṣaḥ/ sūkṣmadīpasya
sarvagṛhāvacchedeneva aṇurūpasyāpi jīvasya prabhāprasaraṇaṅgīkārāt
iti cet - na/ tathā sati kāyavyūhasthale
sukhādisākṣātkārānupapatteriti dik/
children.translated_text: Now, let the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) simply be atomic (<s>aṇu</s>) — there is no defect in what has been stated. For just as a small lamp illuminates an entire house, so too for the atomic soul, the spreading of radiance can be accepted. [Reply:] No — for if so, in the case of the <s>kāyavyūha</s> (multiple bodies [simultaneously animated by one soul]), the direct realization of pleasure and the like would be impossible — this is the indication.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
samavāyena
jñānavaditi/ kālikasambandhena jñānavati kāle 'tivyāptivāraṇāya
samavāyeneti/ sambandhaviśeṣāvacchinnādhāratāsūcanāyaiva
adhikaraṇapadam/ anyathā jñānavān ātmā ityeva vadet iti
bhāvaḥ/ dīpikāyām - bāhmam - bahirindriyajanyam/ āntaram -
manojanyam/ arūpidravyatvāditi/ rūpavato dravyasyaiva
bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
ātmasukhaduḥkhādivyatiriktatvāditi/ yasya jīvātmanaḥ svīyamanasā
saṃyogo 'sti sa tasyaiva jīvātmanaḥ tatsamavetasukhādervā
mānasapratyakṣaṃ janayet/ tajjīvātmatadīyasukhādivyatiriktaṃ
tadīyamanassaṃyogajanyapratyakṣaviṣayo na bhavati/ ataḥ īśvaraḥ
jīvātmatatsukhātiriktaḥ tadīyamānasapratyakṣaviṣayo na bhavatītyāśayaḥ
liṅgābhāvāditi/ īśvaravyāpyasya liṅgasyābhāvādīśvare
nānumānaṃ pramāṇamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Possessing knowledge through inherence' — to avert over-pervasion in time, which possesses knowledge through temporal relation, 'through inherence' is stated. The word 'substratum' (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) is used precisely to indicate the substratum-hood delimited by a specific relation; otherwise, he would simply say 'the self possessing knowledge' — this is the purport. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'external' means generated by external sense organs; 'internal' means generated by mind

children.text:
nanu '(nityaṃ)
vijñānamānandaṃ brahma' iti śrutyā ātmanaḥ jñānasvarūpatvamātrāvagamāt
jñānādhikaraṇatvaṃ na sambhavatīti śaṅkate - na ca nityamiti/ samādhatte
- ānandapadasyeti/ ānandārthakasya ānandaśabdasya
nityapuṃlliṅgatvāt ānandamiti napuṃsakatvānupapatteḥ
ānando 'syāstītyarthe ānandaśabdāt 'arśa ādibhyo 'c' ityacpratyaye
napuṃsaka ānandaśabdaḥ sampadyate/ tathā ca ānandamityasya ānandavadityartha
eva vaktavyaḥ/ tatsamabhivyāhṛtaḥ vijñānaśabdaḥ vijñānavadarthaka eva yuktaḥ/
tathā ca jñānādhikaraṇatvameva tayā śrutyā īśvarasya bodhyata
children.translated_text: Now, from the <s>śruti</s> '(Eternal) consciousness-bliss is <s>Brahman</s>,' since only the nature of the self as knowledge is cognized, the substratum-hood of knowledge is not possible — he raises the doubt: 'nor is [it] eternal' etc. He resolves it: 'of the word <s>ānanda</s>' — since the word <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) is permanently masculine, the neuter form '<s>ānandam</s>'

children.text:
iti bhāvaḥ/
upacaryate - lakṣaṇayā prayujyate/
children.translated_text: — this is the purport. 'Is used figuratively' — means: is employed through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).

children.text:
vijātīyātmamanassaṃyogasyeti/ parātmavyāvṛttasya
svātmamātravṛtteḥ manassaṃyogasyetyarthaḥ/ na cedamaprayojakamiti/
kāryatvamastu kartṛjanyatvaṃ māstu iti śaṅkāyāḥ nivartakastarko
nāstīti bhāvaḥ/ na cedamaprayojakamiti/ kāryatvarūpaheturastu
sakartṛkatvarūpasādhyaṃ māstu iti śaṅkāyā nivārako yastarkaḥ
tacchūnyamityarthaḥ/ kāryatvāvacchinnaṃ pratīti/ nanu sakartṛkatvaṃ hi
kartṛjanyatvam/ pakṣe tadabhāvo 'stu iti śaṅkāyāṃ yadi
kartṛjanyatvaṃ na syāt tarhi kāryatvamapi na syāt, kāryasāmānyaṃ
prati
children.translated_text: 'Of a mind-conjunction of a different kind' (<s>vijātīyātmamanassaṃyoga</s>) — the meaning is: a mind-conjunction that is distinguished from [that of] other selves and occurs only in one's own self. 'Nor is this a purposeless objection' — the purport is: there is no <s>tarka</s> (counterfactual reasoning) to avert the doubt 'let there be effect-hood, but let there not be the property of being produced by an agent.' 'Nor is this a purposeless objection' — let the probans in the form of effect-hood exist, but let agent-produced-ness not

children.text:
kartuḥ
kāraṇatvādityevaṃ kāryatvāvacchinnaṃ prati kartā kāraṇamiti
kāryakāraṇabhāvākhyo 'nukūlatarka eva vaktavyaḥ na tu kāryatvāvacchinnasya
kṛtitvāvacchinnaṃ kāraṇaṃ ityetādṛśa iti kathametaditi cet -
na/ sādhyaṃ sakartṛkatvaṃ na kartṛjayatvarūpam/ tathā sati kartṛtvasyaiva
janakatāvacchedakatvaṃ syāt/ kartṛtvaṃ ca kṛtimattvarūpaṃ
kṛtyātmakamiti anantānāṃ kṛtīnāṃ kāraṇatāvacchedakatve gauravaṃ
syāt/ ataḥ kṛtijanyatvameva sakartṛkatvam/ kṛtitvameva
janakatāvacchedakam kṛtitvaṃ tu jātirūpatayā ekamityāśayena
kāryatvāvacchinne kṛtitvāvacchinnaṃ kāraṇam
ityetādṛśakāryakāraṇabhāvāśyatarkābhidhānāt/
children.translated_text: [exist] — because the agent is a cause. Thus, the supportive <s>tarka</s> called the causal relation must be stated as: 'the agent is a cause with respect to what is delimited by effect-hood' — and not as 'what is delimited by effect-hood has as its cause what is delimited by effort-hood' in this manner. If [one asks] how this is so — [the reply is:] No, the probandum 'having-an-agent-ness' (<s>sakartṛkatva</s>) is not of the form of agent-produced-ness.

children.text:
nanu ghaṭatvāvacchinnaṃ
prati kulālakṛtitvāvacchinnā hetuḥ iti viśiṣyaiva
kāryakāraṇabhāvādetādṛśasāmānyakāryakāraṇabhāve pramāṇābhāve
ityatrāha - digiti/
ghaṭatvapaṭatvādibhedenānantakāryakāraṇabhāvakalpanāpekṣayā
kāryatvāvacchinnaṃ prati kṛtitvena ekahetuhetumadbhāvakalpanameva
ucitamiti bhāvaḥ/ dīpikāyām upādānagocareti/ upādānaṃ
samavāyikāraṇaṃ kapālādi tadviṣayakaṃ yat aparokṣajñānaṃ, evaṃ
samavāyikāraṇaviṣayiṇī yā cikīrṣā kapālena ghaṭaṃ kuryām
ityākārikā icchā, evaṃ samavāyikāraṇaviṣayiṇī yā kṛtiḥ
tadvattvaṃ kartṛtvamityarthaḥ/ upādānagocaretyasya triṣvapyanvayāt/
yadyapītyādi/ 'jānāti', 'icchati', 'yatate', 'karoti' iti
kramāt kāryasāmānyaṃ prati yatnaḥ kāraṇam, yatne cikīrṣā kāraṇam,
cikīrṣāṃ prati jñānaṃ kāraṇamiti jñāpanāya dīpikāyāṃ tritayamuktam/
sādhyaṃ tu kṛtijanyatvameveti bhāvaḥ/ nanu 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit'
iti śrutau sarvajñaśabdasamānārthakatvāt sarvavitpadasya
punaruktirityāśaṅkyāha - vidadhātvartha iti/ tathā ca sarvajñaśabdena
sāmānyataḥ prameyatvādinā sarvaviṣayakajñānamucyate/ sarvavitpadena
ghaṭatvapaṭatvādinā viśeṣarūpeṇa sarvaviṣayakajñānamucyate/ ato na
punaruktiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, since the causal relation is specifically that the potter's effort delimited by potter-ness is the cause with respect to what is delimited by pot-ness, and since there is no evidence for such a general causal relation — to this he says: 'the indication is.' Compared to postulating infinite causal relations differentiated by pot-ness, cloth-ness, and the like, [accepting] a general causal relation where effort-hood

children.text:
nanu jīvastu
'pratiśarīraṃ bhinna' iti mūle jīvasya pratiśarīraṃ bheda evocyate na
lakṣaṇam/ tathā ca tasya mlasya 'jīvasya lakṣaṇamāha' ityavataraṇaṃ na
yuktam ityata āha - svarūpamāhetyartha iti/ śaṅkate - na ceti/
caitraśarīrasya avayavopacayābhyāṃ bhedasyāvaśyakatayā
caitrīyabālaśarīrāpekṣayā tadīyayuvaśarīravṛddhaśarīrādīnāṃ bhedo
vaktavyaḥ/ tathā ca bālayuvādiśarīrabhede satyapi tadavacchinna ātmā eka
eva/ evaṃ saubhariprabhṛtīnāṃ ātmana ekatve 'pi
śarīrāsamūhāṅgīkārāt pratiśarīraṃ jīvabhedābhāvāt pratiśarīraṃ
jīvo bhinna iti kathaṃ saṅgacchata iti śaṅkāgranthasyārthaḥ/
kāyavyūhasthala iti/ ekena jīvena anekaśarīrādhiṣṭhānasthala
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) — the root text states 'is distinct for each body,' i.e., only the distinctness of the <s>jīva</s> for each body is stated, not its definition. And accordingly, the introductory statement 'he states the definition of <s>jīva</s>' is not appropriate for that root text — to this he says: 'the meaning is: [he states] the nature.' He raises the doubt: 'nor [is it the case]' etc. By the accretion of parts in <s>Caitra</s>'s body,

children.text:
samādhatte -
samānakāliketi/ samānakālikānāṃ yogajadharmājanyānāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ
bhedo yatra tatra jīvabheda ityeva mūle vivakṣitam/
caitrīyabālayuvādiśarīrāṇāṃ samānakālikatvābhāvāt
saubhariprabhṛtibhiḥ ekakāle adhiṣṭhitānāṃ
children.translated_text: He resolves: 'contemporaneous' etc. The root text intends precisely this: where there is difference of bodies that are contemporaneous and not produced by yoga-born <s>dharma</s>, there is difference of <s>jīvas</s>. Since <s>Caitra</s>'s bodies at the child stage, youth stage, etc. are not contemporaneous, [this does not apply to them]. And since the bodies simultaneously occupied by <s>Saubhari</s> and others

children.text:
śarīrāṇāṃ
yogajadharmajanyatvena tadajanyatvābhāvāt tādṛśaśarīrāṇāṃ bhedaḥ
nātmabhedavyāpyatayā mūlābhipreta iti nānupapattiḥ/ tathā ca
samānakālikayogajadharmājanyaśarīrabhedavyāpakabhedapratiyogī jīva
iti 'jīvastu pratiśarīraṃ bhinnaḥ' iti mūlārthaḥ/ tādṛśaḥ
śarīrabhedaḥ caitramaitrādiśarīreṣu tatrātmabhedo 'stīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: are produced by yoga-born <s>dharma</s> and hence do not lack such production, the difference of such bodies is not intended by the root text as being pervaded by difference of selves — hence there is no difficulty. And accordingly, the <s>jīva</s> is the counter-positive of a difference that pervades the difference of bodies that are contemporaneous, not produced by yoga-born <s>dharma</s> — this is the meaning of the root text 'the <s>jīva</s> is distinct for each body.'

children.text:
evaṃ cetyādi/
avacchedyatāsambandhena taccharīrabhinnaśarīravattvāditi hetuḥ pūraṇīyaḥ/
anyathetyādi/ 'ahaṃ manuṣya' ityādipratītyā ahamarthe ātmani
munaṣyatvādidharmāḥ prakāratayā bhāsante/ śarīra eva manuṣyatvādayaḥ
bhavanti/ tasmāt
ahamarthātmaviśeṣyakamanuṣyatvādidehadharmaprakārakapratītiriyaṃ
śarīramevātmā ityavagamayati/ yadi tu śarīrātiriktaḥ ātmā tarhi
manuṣyatvādirahite ātmani manuṣyatvādiprakārikā iyaṃ pratītiḥ
bhramarūpā syāt na pramātmiketi bhāvaḥ/ anyathā -
śarīrātiriktasyātmanaḥ ahamarthatve/ pratyayasyaivāsaṅgatiriti/ tathā
pratīteḥ pramātvānupapattirityarthaḥ/ manuṣyaśabdasya
manuṣyaśarīrāvacchinna ityarthāt 'ahaṃ manuṣya' iti pratītiḥ
ahamarthe manuṣyaśarīrāvacchinnatvamavagāhate/ ataḥ śarīrātmatvasādhikā
iyaṃ pratītirna bhavatīti siddhāntaṃ manasikṛtya 'ityabhimāna'
ityuktam/
children.translated_text: 'And thus' etc. The probans should be completed as: because [that self] possesses a body different from that body, through the relation of being delimited. 'Otherwise' etc. By the cognition 'I am a human,' in the referent of 'I,' namely the self, properties like human-ness and the like appear as qualifier-modes. Human-ness and the like exist only in the body. Therefore, in the self which is the referent of 'I,'

children.text:
bhūtakāliketi/
'yo 'hamadrākṣaṃ so 'hamidānīṃ spṛśāmi' iti pratītyā
bhūtakālikacākṣuṣapratyakṣāśrayavartamānakālikaspārśanapratyakṣāśrayayoraikyamavagamyate/
indriyātmavāde cākṣuṣapratyakṣāśrayaḥ cakṣuḥ spārśanapratyakṣāśrayaḥ tvak
iti tayorbhedāt tayoraikyāvagāhinī pratyabhijñāpratitirna ghaṭata
iti bhāvaḥ/ dīpikāyām anyānubhūta iti/ nanu
cakṣustvacorbhedāt tayorabhedāvagāhī pratyabhijñāpratyayo nopapadyata
ityeva vaktavyam/ na tvevamiti kathameṣa grantho yojanīya iti
cet - śrūyatām/ uktapratyabhijñā yathā vā
cākṣuṣaspārśanapratyakṣāśrayayoraikyamavagāhate tathā
cākṣuṣapratyakṣaviṣayasyaiva spārśanapratyakṣaviṣayatvamapyavagāhate/ tatra
cakṣuḥkartṛkacākṣuṣapratyakṣaviṣayasya ghaṭasya
tvakkartṛkasmaraṇaviṣayatvāsambhavāt tatsmaraṇapūrvakaṃ tatra
spārśanapratyakṣaviṣayatvāvagāhinītvakkartṛkapratyabhijñā na syāt/ ata
children.translated_text: 'Of past time' etc. From the cognition 'I who saw then am the one who now touches,' the identity of the substratum of visual perception at a past time and the substratum of tactile perception at the present time is comprehended. On the view that the self is [identical with] the sense organs, the substratum of visual perception is the eye and the substratum of tactile perception is the skin — since these two are different,

children.text:
indriyātiriktaḥ
cākṣuṣaspārśanapratyakṣayorāśrayaḥ eko 'ṅgīkāryaḥ/ sa ca svātmanaḥ
abheda svānubhūtamarthaṃ ca anusandhātumarhatītyāśayena dīpikāyāḥ
pravṛtteriti/ prakāśikāyāṃ hānaṃ nāśa iti/ kṛtsa karmaṇo nāśo
nāma niṣphalatvam/ karmakartuḥ phalānubhavaṃ vinaiva nāśāt/
children.translated_text: a single entity beyond the sense organs must be accepted as the substratum of both visual and tactile perception. And that [entity] is capable of being identical with itself and of recognizing an object previously experienced — with this intent, the <s>Dīpikā</s> proceeds. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'destruction' (<s>hāna</s>) means loss — the destruction of what is performed (<s>kṛta</s>) means the fruitlessness of action; for the doer of the action, the experience of the fruit

children.text:
akṛtasya karmaṇaḥ -
karmaṇyakṛta'pi abhyāgamaḥ - phalaprāptiḥ/ phalānubhavitā karmakarturanya
eveti tasya karmānuṣṭhānaṃ vinaiva tatphaprāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ tadāha -
kartuḥā mana iti/ prabhāprasaraṇāṅgīkārāditi/ jñānarūpaprabhāyāḥ
sarvaśarīravyāptyaṅgīkārāt ityarthaḥ/ kāyavyūhasthale iti/
ekena jīvena yugapadadhiṣṭhitāneka śarīsthale yasmin
śarīre 'ṇurjīvaḥ vartate taccharīre jīvaprabhāyāḥ jñānasya prasare 'pi
śarīrāntareṣu tataprasarābhāvāt tadavacchedyasukhādyanusandhānamātmano
na syāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Of action not performed' — the attainment (<s>abhyāgama</s>), i.e. obtaining of the result, even of action not performed. The purport is: since the experiencer of the result is someone other than the performer of the action, that person would obtain the result without performing the action. He says this with 'of the performer' and so forth. 'Because of accepting the spreading of radiance' — the meaning is: because of accepting that the radiance in the form of cognition pervades the entire body. 'In the case of a body-complex (<s>kāyavyūha</s>)' — in the case where one soul simultaneously presides over multiple bodies, even though the radiance of the soul — cognition — spreads in the body where the atomic soul resides, because of the absence of its spreading in the other bodies, the introspection of pleasure and the like delimited by those [other bodies] would not be possible for the self — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
kāyavyūhasthale 'pi yāvanti śarīrāṇi jīvenādhiṣṭhitāni tāvatsu
tatprabhāprasaro 'ṅgīkriyate/ ato nāktānupapatti
rityaśaṅkyāhadigiti/ yathā ekagṛhāntarāropitadīpasya prabhā
gṛhāntare na prasarati, tathā ekaśarīrāntaḥsthajīvasya prabhā śarīrāntare
na prasarediti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, even in the case of a body-complex, the spreading of its radiance is accepted in as many bodies as are presided over by the soul; therefore there is no impossibility — anticipating this doubt, he says 'like' and so forth. Just as the radiance of a lamp placed inside one house does not spread to another house, similarly the radiance of a soul situated within one body would not spread to another body — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: manonirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of Mind (<s>Manas</s>)

children.text: AnTs_18 sukhādyupalabdhisādhanam indriyaṃ manaḥ / tac ca pratyātmaniyatatvād anantaṃ paramāṇurūpaṃ nityaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: The sense organ that is the instrument for the apprehension of pleasure and the like is the mind (<s>manas</s>). And since it is specific to each self, it is infinite [in number], atomic in form, and eternal.

children.text:
sukhādyupalabdhisādhanam indriyaṃ manaḥ/ tacca
pratyātmaniyatatvāt anantaṃ paramāṇurūpaṃ nityaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: The sense organ that is the instrument for the apprehension of pleasure and the like is the mind (<s>manas</s>). And since it is specific to each self, it is infinite [in number], atomic in form, and eternal.

children.text: dipikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
manaso lakṣaṇamāha -
sukheti/ sparśarahitatve sati kriyāyattvaṃ manaso lakṣaṇam/ tadvibhajate
- tacceti/ ekaikasyātmana ekaikaṃ mana āvaśyakam ityātmanāṃ
anekatvāt manaso 'pyanekatvamityarthaḥ/ paramāṇurūpamiti/
madhyamaparimāṇavattve anityatvaprasaṅgādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of the mind — 'pleasure' and so forth. The definition of mind is: possessing activity while being devoid of touch. He divides it — 'and that' and so forth. Each self requires one mind each; since selves are many, the minds too are many — this is the meaning. 'Atomic in form' — the meaning is: because if it had medium magnitude, non-eternality would result.

children.text:
nanu 'mano vibhu
sparśarahitatve sati dravyatvāt, ākāśādivat' iti cet - na/
manaso vibhutve ātmamanassaṃyogasya asamavāyikāraṇasya abhāvāt
jñānānutpattiprasaṅgaḥ/ na ca vibhudvayasaṃyogaḥ asttviti vācyam/
tatsaṃyogasya nityatvena suṣuptyabhāvaprasaṅgāt,
purītadvyatiriktasthale ātmamanassaṃyogasya sarvadā vidyamānatvāt/
aṇutve tu yadā manaḥ purītati praviśati tadā suṣuptiḥ, yadā
nissarati tadā jñānotpattirityaṇutvasiddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'The mind is all-pervading, because of being a substance while being devoid of touch, like space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like.' Reply: No — if the mind were all-pervading, since the conjunction of the self and mind — the non-inherent cause — would be absent, the non-origination of cognition would result. Nor should it be said that the conjunction of two all-pervading [entities] exists — because since such conjunction would be eternal, the absence of deep sleep would result, since the conjunction of self and mind would always exist in locations other than the nerve (<s>purītat</s>). But if [the mind] is atomic, when the mind enters the <s>purītat</s>, there is deep sleep; when it exits, cognition arises — thus the atomicity of mind is established.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
manassaṃyogādyativyāptivārakendriyatvaghaṭitamūloktalakṣaṇāpekṣayā
laghulakṣaṇamāha - sparśarahitatve satīti/ ekaikaṃ mana iti/
sarvātmanāṃ ekasya manasaḥ svīkāre ekasya jñānadaśāyāṃ aparasya
tadanupapattiḥ, tasyāṇutvena sakalendriyairekadā saṃyogābhāvāditi
bhāvaḥ/ vibhviti/ tathā ca tasya paramamahatparimāṇavattvena
pūrvoktadoṣānavakāśa iti bhāvaḥ/ abhāvāditi/
vibhudvayasaṃyogānabhyupagamāditi bhāvaḥ/ vibhviti/ tathā ca tasya
paramamahatparimāṇavattvena pūrvoktadoṣānavakāśa iti bhāvaḥ/
abhāvāditi/ vibhudvayasaṃyogānabhyupagamāditi bhāvaḥ/
jñānānutpattīti/ bhāvakāryasyāsamavāyikāraṇajanyatvaniyamāditi
bhāvaḥ/ vibhudvayasaṃyogo 'stviti/ tasya nityatvena
asamavāyikāraṇakriyādyasattve 'pi na kṣatiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In contrast to the heavier definition in the root text, which incorporates sense-organ-hood (<s>indriyatva</s>) as a component to prevent over-extension to the conjunction with the mind and the like, he states a lighter definition: 'while being devoid of touch' and so forth. 'One mind each' — if a single mind were accepted for all selves, when one [self] is in the state of cognition, another would be unable to have it, because of the mind's atomicity preventing simultaneous conjunction with all sense organs — this is the purport. 'All-pervading' — and accordingly, since it would possess the largest magnitude, there would be no scope for the previously stated defect — this is the purport. 'Because of absence' — the purport is: because the conjunction of two all-pervading entities is not accepted. 'Non-origination of cognition' — the purport is: because a positive effect is necessarily produced from a non-inherent cause. 'Let the conjunction of two all-pervading [entities] exist' — the purport is: since its being eternal means that even in the absence of action and the like as non-inherent causes, there is no damage.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
tarkasaṅgrahoktaṃ
manolakṣaṇa parityajya dīpikāyāṃ anyasya manolakṣaṇasya kathane
bījamāha - manassaṃyogādīti/ 'sukhādisākṣātkārasādhanatvaṃ manaso
lakṣaṇam' ityetāvanmātroktau ātmamanassaṃyoge 'tivyāptiḥ,
tasyāpi sukhādisākṣātkārasādhanatvāt/ tadvāraṇāya indriyatvaṃ
niveśitam/ indriyatvaṃ va 'śabdetare' tyādirūpamiti tadghaṭitaṃ
manolakṣaṇaṃ atiguru iti paryālocya laghulakṣaṇaṃ dīpikāyāṃ
uktamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the seed for stating a different definition of mind in the <s>Dīpikā</s> while setting aside the definition stated in the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>: 'conjunction with the mind and the like' and so forth. If only 'being the instrument for the direct perception of pleasure and the like is the definition of mind' were stated, there would be over-extension to the conjunction of the self and mind, since that too is an instrument for the direct perception of pleasure and the like. To prevent that, sense-organ-hood (<s>indriyatva</s>) is included. But sense-organ-hood has the form of 'other than sound' and so forth [a complex definition]; reflecting that a definition incorporating that would be excessively heavy, a lighter definition was stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s> — this is the purport.

children.text:
"sādhanamityasya karaṇamityarthaḥ/
etallābhāyaiva indriyapadamupāttam, na tu tena rūpeṇa praveśaḥ
gauravāt"iti tu nṛsiṃhaśāstriṇaḥ prāhuḥ/ teṣāṃ
pakṣe sabhbhavato lakṣaṇāntarasyākathane nyūnatā syāditi tadvāraṇāyaiva
dīpikāyāṃ lakṣaṇāntarakaraṇam/ uktaṃ ca taireva -"nyūnatāparihārāya svayaṃ manolakṣaṇamāha"iti/ nanu vibhadvayasaṃyogaḥ katha bhavet? saṃyogaṃ prati
kriyāyāḥ saṃyogasya ca hetutvāt/ vibhunośca kriyāśūnyatvāt
kriyājanyaḥ saṃyogo na sambhavati/ avayavaśūnyatvāt
hastapusatakasāṃyogāt kāyapustakasaṃyogavat
saṃyogajasaṃyogo 'pi na saṃbhavatītyatrāha - tasya nityatvenati/
kriyādītyatra ādiśabdena saṃyogo gṛhyate/ tathā ca janyasaṃyogaṃ
pratyeva kriyādeḥ hetutvaṃ na tvasaṃyoge ajatvavirodhāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The meaning of "instrument" is "instrument in the technical sense (<s>karaṇa</s>)"' — the word <s>indriya</s> is included for obtaining this meaning, not as entering [the definition] in its own form, due to heaviness — thus say the <s>Nṛsiṃhaśāstrins</s>. On their view, the other definition that is available was not stated, resulting in deficiency; to prevent that very deficiency, the alternative definition was given in the <s>Dīpikā</s>. And they themselves state: 'To prevent deficiency, he himself states the definition of mind.' Now, how can there be a conjunction of two all-pervading entities? Since both action and conjunction are causes of conjunction, and since all-pervading entities are devoid of action, conjunction born of action is impossible. Since they are devoid of parts, conjunction born from conjunction — as the conjunction of a book with a hand produces the conjunction of the book with the body — is also impossible. To this he says: 'because of its being eternal' and so forth. The word 'and so forth' after 'action' refers to conjunction. And accordingly, action and the like serve as causes only for produced conjunction, not for eternal [conjunction] — because there is a contradiction with non-produced-ness — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: rūpanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of Color (<s>Rūpa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_19 cakṣurmātragrāhyo guṇo rūpam / tac ca śuklanīlapītaraktaharitakapiśacitrabhedāt saptavidhaṃ pṛthivījalatejovṛtti / tatra pṛthivyāṃ saptavidham / abhāsvaraśuklaṃ jale / bhāsvaraśuklaṃ tejasi //
children.translated_text: Color (<s>rūpa</s>) is the quality apprehended by the eye alone. It is of seven kinds, due to the distinction of white, blue, yellow, red, green, tawny, and variegated. It resides in earth, water, and fire. In earth, it is of all seven kinds. In water, it is non-luminous white. In fire, it is luminous white.

children.text:
cakṣurmātragrāhyo
guṇo rūpam/ tacca śukla - nīla-pīta - raktahirata - kapiśa -
citrabhedāt saptavidham/ pṛthivījalatejāvṛtti/ tatra pṛthivyāṃ
saptavidham/ abhāsvaraśuklaṃ jale/ bhāsvaraśuklaṃ tejasi/
children.translated_text: Color (<s>rūpa</s>) is the quality apprehended by the eye alone. It is of seven kinds, due to the distinction of white, blue, yellow, red, green, tawny, and variegated. It resides in earth, water, and fire. In earth, it is of all seven kinds. In water, it is non-luminous white. In fire, it is luminous white.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
rūpaṃ lakṣayati -
cakṣuriti/ saṅkhyādāvativyāptivāraṇāya mātrapadam/ rūpatve
ativyāptivāraṇāya guṇapadam/ rūpaṃ vibhajate - tacceti/
children.translated_text: He defines color — 'eye' and so forth. The word 'alone' (<s>mātra</s>) is to prevent over-extension to number and the like. The word 'quality' (<s>guṇa</s>) is to prevent over-extension to color-hood (<s>rūpatva</s>). He divides color — 'it' and so forth.

children.text:
nanu
avyāpyavṛttinīlādisamudāya eva citrarūpam iti cet - na/ rūpasya
vyāpyavṛttitvaniyamāt/ nanu citrapaṭe avayavarūpasyaiva
pratītirastviti cet - na/ rūparahitatvena
paṭasyāpratyakṣatvaprasaṅgāt/ na ca rūpavatsamavetatvaṃ
pratyakṣatvaprayojakam, gauravāt/ tasmāt paṭasya pratyakṣatvānupapattyā
citrarūpasiddhiḥ/ rūpasyāśrayamāha - pṛthivīti/ āśrayaṃ vibhajya darśayati
- tatreti/
children.translated_text: Objection: Variegated color is nothing but a collection of [multiple] partially pervading colors such as blue and the like. Reply: No — because color necessarily has fully pervading occurrence. Objection: Let the perception be of the colors of the parts only in a variegated cloth. Reply: No — because the cloth, being devoid of color, would then be imperceptible. Nor should it be said that being inherent in what possesses color makes [the cloth] perceptible — due to ontological heaviness. Therefore, from the impossibility of the cloth's being perceptible [otherwise], variegated color is established. He states the substratum of color: 'earth' and so forth. He shows the substratum by dividing: 'therein' and so forth.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
mātrapadamiti/
yadyapi cakṣurmātragrāhyatvaṃ cakṣuritarāgrāhyatve sati cakṣurgrāhyatvam, tacca
na rūpe saṃbhavati; tathāpi tvagindriyāgrāhyatve sati cakṣurgrāhyatvaṃ
taditi dhyeyam/ guṇapadamiti/ na caivamapi
prabhābhittisaṃyoge 'tivyāptiriti vācyam,
tvagagrāhyacakṣurgrāhyaguṇavibhājakadharmavattve paryavasānena adoṣāt/ ata
eva paramāṇurūpādau nāvayāptiriti bodhyam/ samudāya eveti/
evakāreṇātiriktacitrarūpavyavacchedaḥ/ vyāpyavṛttiveti/
daiśikavyāpyavṛttitvetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The word "alone"' — although 'apprehensible by the eye alone' (<s>cakṣurmātragrāhyatva</s>) [technically means] apprehensibility by the eye while not being apprehensible by anything other than the eye, and that is not possible in color [since the mind also cognizes it]; nevertheless, what is to be understood is: apprehensibility by the eye while not being apprehensible by the tactile sense organ. 'The word "quality"' — nor should it be objected that even so there is over-extension to the conjunction of radiance and a wall; because there is no defect, since it amounts to possessing the property that distinguishes the quality that is apprehensible by the eye and not apprehensible by the tactile organ. Precisely from this, it should be understood that there is no under-extension in atomic color and the like. 'Is nothing but a collection' — the word 'nothing but' (<s>eva</s>) excludes a distinct variegated color. 'Fully pervading occurrence' — the meaning is: spatially fully pervading occurrence.

children.text:
idamupalakṣaṇam -
ekaikacitrarūpasthale anekarūpāṇāṃ ekaikatattatprāgabhāvādisthale ca
anekaprāgabhāvādīnāṃ kalpanena anekarūpeṣu citraḥ
ityākārakapratītiviṣayatvakalpanena ca gauravamiti/
rūparahitatveneti/ samavāyenetyādiḥ/ prasaṅgāditi/ dravyacākṣuṣaṃ
prati samavāyena rūpasya kāraṇatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ rūpavatsamavetatvamiti/
spāśrayasamavetatvasambandhena rūpam/ pratyakṣatvaprayojakamiti/
pratyakṣaviṣayatvaprayojakamastu ityarthaḥ/ gauravāditi/
sākṣātsambandhena kāraṇatvāpekṣayā gauravādityarthaḥ/
citrāvayavakāvayavakapālaiḥ ārabdhapaṭasya cākṣuṣatvānurodhena
svasamavāyisamavetasamavetasamavetatvasambandhena rūpasya
tatprayojakatvamaṅgīkartavyam/ evaṃ ca truṭeḥ cākṣuṣatvānupapattirapi
draṣṭavyā/ pratyakṣatvānupapattyeti/ etena citrarūpavat citraraso 'pi
sidhyediti śaṅkānirastār/ davayalaukikarāsanasya aprasiddhyā
tadanupapattyabhāvena na citrarasāṅgīkāra iti saṅkṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: This is an indication [of the following]: in each case of variegated color, the postulation of many colors, and in the locus of each prior absence and the like of each such [color], the postulation of many prior absences and the like, and the postulation of being the object of cognition of the form 'variegated among many colors' — this involves ontological heaviness. 'Being devoid of color' — 'through inherence' and so forth [is to be supplied]. 'Would result' — the purport is: because color through inherence is a cause of the visual perception of substance. 'Being inherent in what possesses color' — color through the relation of being inherent in one's own substratum. 'Makes [the cloth] perceptible' — the meaning is: let it be the cause of being the object of perception. 'Due to heaviness' — the meaning is: due to the heaviness relative to the causality through the direct relation [of inherence]. Since the cloth produced from parts that are variegated must be visual, by accepting color through the relation of being inherent in what is inherent in what is inherent [in it], its causality for visual perception must be accepted. And thus the impossibility of the visual perception of an atom should also be noted. 'From the impossibility of perceptibility' — by this, the doubt that just as variegated color is established, so too variegated taste should be established, is also refuted. Since a special taste-organ for variegated taste is not established, there is no such impossibility [to require a distinct variegated taste]; hence variegated taste is not accepted — this is the summary.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
nanu
cakṣurmātragrāhyatvaṃ rūpe asambhavi/ cakṣuritarāgrāhyatve sati cakṣurgrāhyatvaṃ
hi cakṣurmātragrāhyatvam/ jñānasāmānye manasaḥ kāraṇatvāt
cakṣuritaramanojanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvasyaiva rūpe sattvena
cakṣuritarāgrāhyatvasya rūpe abhāvāditi śaṅkate - yadyapīti/
cakṣuritarāgrāhyatvaṃ cakṣuritarajanyapratyakṣāviṣayatvam/ cakṣurgrāhyatvaṃ
cakṣurindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvam/ samādhatte - tathāpīti/
cakṣuritarapadena tvagindriyaṃ vivakṣitam/ tathā ca
tvagindriyajanyapratyakṣāviṣayatve sati cakṣurindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ
cakṣurmātragrāhyatvam/ asti cedaṃ rūpe iti nāsambhava iti bhāvaḥ/
satyantānupādāne ekatvādisaṅkhyāyāmativyāptiḥ, tasyā api
cakṣurindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvāt/ tadupādāne tu saṅkhyāyāḥ
tvagindriyoṇāpi grāhyatayā tvagindriyajanyapratyakṣāviṣayatvaṃ nāstīti
nātivyāptiḥ/ atīndriye dharmādāvativyāptivāraṇāya viśeṣyam/ na
caivamapīti/ prabhābhittisaṃyogasya tvagindriyāgrāhyatvāt
cakṣurgrāhyatvācceti bhāvaḥ/ tvagagrāhyeti/ tvagindriyajanyapratyakṣāviṣayaḥ
cakṣurindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayaśca yaḥ guṇavibhājakadharmaḥ tadvattvaṃ rūpasya
lakṣaṇam/ guṇavibhājakadharmaḥ rūpatvajātiḥ/ sā ca tvagagrāhyā cakṣurgrāhyā
ca, yo guṇaḥ yadindriyagrāhyaḥ tanniṣṭhā jātiḥ tadabhāvaśca
tadindriyagrāhyau iti nyāyāt/ rūpatvavattvaṃ ca rūpe astīti
lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ prabhābhittisaṃyoge vighamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, 'apprehensible by the eye alone' is impossible in color. For 'apprehensible by the eye alone' means apprehensibility by the eye while not being apprehensible by anything other than the eye. Since the mind is a cause of cognition in general, and since color does possess the property of being the object of perception produced by a non-eye [organ], namely the mind, the property of not being apprehensible by anything other than the eye is absent in color — he raises this doubt: 'although' and so forth. 'Not apprehensible by other than the eye' means not being the object of perception produced by anything other than the eye. 'Apprehensible by the eye' means being the object of perception produced by the eye as sense organ. He resolves: 'nevertheless' and so forth. What is intended by 'other than the eye' is the tactile sense organ. And accordingly, 'apprehensible by the eye alone' means: being the object of perception produced by the eye as sense organ while not being the object of perception produced by the tactile sense organ. This is indeed present in color; hence there is no impossibility — this is the purport. Without that qualifier, there would be over-extension to the number 'oneness' and the like, since that too is the object of perception produced by the eye as sense organ. But with that qualifier, since number is apprehensible even by the tactile organ, the property of not being the object of perception produced by the tactile organ is absent — hence there is no over-extension. The qualificand is to prevent over-extension to imperceptible [qualities] like <s>dharma</s> and the like. 'Nor even so' — the purport is: because the conjunction of radiance and a wall is not apprehensible by the tactile organ and is apprehensible by the eye. 'Not apprehensible by the tactile organ' — the definition of color is: possessing the property that distinguishes a quality that is not the object of perception produced by the tactile organ and is the object of perception produced by the eye. The property that distinguishes a quality is the universal color-hood (<s>rūpatvajāti</s>). And that is not apprehensible by the tactile organ and is apprehensible by the eye — by the maxim that the universal residing in a quality and the absence of that [quality] are apprehensible by the same sense organ that apprehends that quality. And the possession of color-hood is present in color — thus the definition applies. The property that distinguishes the quality present in the conjunction of radiance and a wall

children.text:
guṇavibhājakadharmaḥ
saṃyogatvam/ sa ca na tvagagrāhyo bhavati ghaṭapaṭasaṃyogādau
saṃyogatvasya tvagindriyeṇa grahaṇāt iti
children.translated_text: is conjunction-hood (<s>saṃyogatva</s>). And that is not 'not apprehensible by the tactile organ,' because conjunction-hood in the conjunction of a pot and a cloth and the like is apprehended by the tactile organ. Therefore

children.text:
prabhābhittisaṃyoge
nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ etādṛśajātighaṭitalakṣaṇakaraṇe
prabhābhittisaṃyoge ativyāpitavāraṇavat
paramāṇurūpe 'vyāptivāraṇamiti prayojanamitsayāha - ata eveti/
paramāṇugatarūpasya atīndriyatayā tatra cakṣūrgrāhyatvābhāvāt/
children.translated_text: there is no over-extension in the conjunction of radiance and a wall — this is the purport. The same purpose of creating a definition incorporating such a universal also serves to prevent under-extension in atomic color, in the same way as it prevents over-extension in the conjunction of radiance and a wall — intending this, he says — 'precisely from this' and so forth. Since atomic color, being supersensory, lacks apprehensibility by the eye in that [atomic form].

children.text:
yathāśrutalakṣaṇe
avyāptiḥ/ yathoktajātighaṭitalakṣaṇe tu paramāṇurūpe vidyamānaḥ
guṇavibhājakadharmaḥ rūpatvam/ sa tu ghaṭarūpe cakṣurgrāhya eva/ tathā ca
cakṣargrāhyarūpatvavattayā paramāṇurūpe lakṣaṇasamanvayāt nāvyāptiriti
bhāvaḥ/ nanu utpattikṣaṇe ghaṭādau rūpābhāvena rūpasya
kālikāvyāpyavṛttitayā 'rūpasya vyāpyavṛttitvaniyamāt'
ityasaṅgatamityata āha - daiśikavyāpyavṛttitveti/
children.translated_text: In the definition as literally understood, there is under-extension. But in the definition incorporating the said universal, the property that distinguishes the quality present in atomic color is color-hood (<s>rūpatva</s>). And that is apprehensible by the eye in the color of a pot. And accordingly, since the possession of color-hood that is apprehensible by the eye is present in atomic color, there is no under-extension — this is the purport. Now, since at the moment of origination, color is absent in a pot and the like, color has temporally partial pervading occurrence; therefore the statement 'color necessarily has fully pervading occurrence' is incongruous — anticipating this, he says — 'spatially fully pervading' and so forth.

children.text:
nanu
svāśrayasamavetatvasambandhena paṭe tantugatarūpāṇāṃ sattvāt
rūparahitatvena ityasaṅgatam ityata āha - samavāyenetayāditi/
viṣayatāsambandhena pratyakṣaṃ prati samavāyasambandhena rūpasya kāraṇatvāt
paṭe samavāyena rūpaṃ nāsti cet paṭasya pratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ na syāditi
bhāvaḥ/ nanu pratyakṣatvaṃ pratyakṣajñānavṛtti/ pratyakṣajñāne ca
rūpavatsamavetatvābhāvāt 'rūpavatsamavetatvaṃ pratyakṣatvaprayojakam'
iti granthaḥ asaṅgata ityāśaṅkyāha -
pratyakṣaviṣayatvaprayojakamiti/ pratyakṣatvapadamatra
pratyakṣaviṣayatvārthakamiti bhāvaḥ/ viṣayatāsambandhena dravyapratyakṣaṃ prati
svāśrayasamavetatvasambandhena rūpaṃ kāraṇam/ paṭe samavāyena
rūpābhāve 'pi 1svāśrayasamavetatvasambandhena tanturūpaṃ tatra vartate/ ataḥ
tasya pratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ bhavati/ tasmāt citrarūpaṃ māstu ityāśayaḥ/
svasamavāyisamavetasamevatasamavatatvasambandheneti/ svaṃ citrarūpam/
svasamavāyinaḥ ye avayavāḥ kapālāvayavāvayavāḥ, tatra samavetāḥ
kapālāvayavāḥ, tatsamavetatvaṃ kapāle tatsamavetatvaṃ ghaṭe/ truṭeḥ
cākṣuṣatvānupapattiriti/ paramāṇugatarūpasya tryaṇuke
svasamavāyiparamāṇusamavetadvyaṇukasamavetatvasambandhena sattve 'pi
svasamavāyisamavetasamavetasamavetatvasambandhena asattvāt,
paramāṇoravayave satyeva tadrūpasya uktasambandhena tryaṇuke sambhavāt/
tathā coktasambandhena tryaṇuke rūpābhāvena tryaṇukasya
cākṣuṣapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ na syāditi bhāvaḥ/ nanu citro rasa iti
pratītyā atiriktacitrarasiddhirityata āha - saṅkṣepa iti/
tādṛśapratīteḥ avayavagatanānāsairupapatteḥ
atiriktacitrarasatatprāgabhāvadhvaṃsādikalpane gauravāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, since in cloth, the forms belonging to threads exist through the relation of inhering-in-what-inheres-in-itself (<s>svāśrayasamavetatva</s>), [to say it is] devoid of form is incoherent — to this he says: 'through inherence,' etc. Since form is a cause of perception through the relation of inherence qua object-hood relation, if there is no form in cloth through inherence, then the cloth would not be an object of perception — this is the purport. Now, perceptibility (<s>pratyakṣatva</s>) occurs in perceptual cognition; and since in perceptual cognition the relation of inhering-in-what-possesses-form is absent, the text 'inhering-in-what-possesses-form is the ground of perceptibility' is incoherent — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'the ground of being an object of perception.' The word 'perceptibility' here means 'being an object of perception' — this is the purport. Form is a cause of the perception of substance qua object-hood relation, through the relation of inhering-in-what-inheres-in-itself. Even though form is absent in cloth through inherence, the form of the thread exists there through the relation of inhering-in-what-inheres-in-itself. Therefore, it is an object of perception. Hence, let there be no composite form (<s>citrarūpa</s>) — this is the intent. 'Through the relation of inhering-in-what-inheres-in-what-inheres-in-what-is-self-inherent' — 'self' refers to composite form. The parts that are self-inherent are the parts of the pot-sherds; what inheres in them are the pot-sherds; its inherence-in-the-pot-sherd is in the pot-sherd, and its inherence is in the pot. 'The impossibility of visual perception of a <s>truṭi</s> (three-atom aggregate)' — even though the form belonging to an atom exists in a three-atom aggregate through the relation of inhering-in-the-dyad-inhering-in-the-atom-which-is-self-inherent, since it does not exist through the relation of inhering-in-what-inheres-in-what-inheres-in-what-is-self-inherent — because only when the atom has parts would the form exist in the three-atom aggregate through the stated relation.
