And accordingly, due to the absence of form in the three-atom aggregate through the stated relation, the three-atom aggregate would not be an object of visual perception — this is the purport. Now, from the cognition 'composite taste,' an additional composite taste is established — to this he says: 'in brief,' etc. Since such a cognition can be explained by the manifold [tastes] residing in the parts, postulating an additional composite taste, its prior absence, destruction, and the like would be cumbersome — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: rasanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of Taste (<s>Rasa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_20 rasanagrāhyo guṇo rasaḥ / sa ca madhurāmlalavaṇakaṭukaṣāyatiktabhedāt ṣaḍvidhaḥ / pṛthivyāṃ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / jale madhura eva //
children.translated_text: [<s>AnTs</s> 20] Taste is the quality apprehended by the tongue. It is sixfold, due to the distinction of sweet, sour, salty, pungent, astringent, and bitter. In earth, it is sixfold. In water, it is sweet alone.

children.text:
rasanagrāhyo guṇo
rasaḥ/ sa ca madhura - amla - lavaṇa - kaṭu - kaṣāya - tiktabhedāt
ṣaḍvidhaḥ/ pṛthivījalavṛttiḥ/ tatra pṛthivyāṃ ṣaḍvidhaḥ/ jale madhura
eva/
children.translated_text: Taste is the quality apprehended by the tongue. It is sixfold — due to the distinction of sweet, sour, salty, pungent, astringent, and bitter. It occurs in earth and water. In earth, it is sixfold. In water, it is sweet alone.

children.text:
1. svāśrayeti/ svaṃ
tanturūpaṃ tasyāśrayaḥ tantuḥ tatsamavetatvaṃ paṭasya/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Self-inherent' — 'self' is the thread's form; its substratum is the thread; its inherence is in the cloth.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
rasaṃ lakṣayati -
rasaneti/ rasatve 'tivyāptivāraṇāya guṇapadam/ rasasyāśrayamāha
pṛthivīti/ āśrayaṃ vibhajya darśayati - tatreti/
children.translated_text: He defines taste — 'by the tongue' etc. The word 'quality' is to avert over-pervasion in taste-ness (<s>rasatva</s>). He states the substratum of taste — 'in earth' etc. He shows the substratum by dividing it — 'therein' etc.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
rasatva iti/
rasanagrāhyaguṇavibhājakopādhimattve tātparyam/ evaṃ gandhalakṣaṇe 'pi/
children.translated_text: 'Taste-ness' etc. — the resultant meaning is: the possession of a distinguishing limiting property that is a quality apprehensible by the tongue. The same applies in the definition of smell.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
nanu rasanāgrāhyatve
sati guṇatvaṃ rasasya lakṣaṇam ityuktāvapi paramāṇurase avyāptiḥ,
tasya rasanendriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvābhāvāt ityāśaṅkyāha -
rasanagrāhyeti/ rasanendriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayo yaḥ guṇavibhājako dharmaḥ
tadvattvaṃ rasalakṣaṇam/ phalādirase rasatvajātiḥ 'yo guṇaḥ'
ityādinyāyena rasanendriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayo bhavati
tādṛśarasatvajātimattvasya paramāṇurase 'pi sattvāt nāvyāptiriti
bhāvaḥ/ evaṃ gandhalakṣaṇe 'pīti/ ghrāṇagrāhyaguṇavibhājakopādhimattvaṃ
gandhalakṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, even when it is stated that the definition of taste is quality-hood conjoined with apprehensibility by the tongue, there is non-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) in the taste of atoms, because atoms, being supersensuous, lack apprehensibility by the tongue-organ — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'apprehensible by the tongue' etc. [The meaning is:] that which is an object of perception generated by the tongue-organ,

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: gandhanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of Smell (<s>Gandha</s>)

children.text: AnTs_21 ghrāṇagrāhyo guṇo gandhaḥ / sa ca dvividhaḥ surabhirasurabhiś ca / pṛthivīmātravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>AnTs</s> 21] Smell is the quality apprehended by the nose. It is twofold: fragrant and non-fragrant. It occurs only in earth.

children.text:
ghrāṇagrāhyo guṇo
gandhaḥ/ sa dvividhaḥ - surabhiḥ asurabhiśceti/ pṛthivīmātravṛtti/
children.translated_text: Smell is the quality apprehended by the nose. It is twofold — fragrant and non-fragrant. It occurs only in earth.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
gandhaṃ lakṣayati -
ghrāṇeti/ gandhatve ativyāptivāraṇāya guṇapadam/
children.translated_text: He defines smell — 'by the nose' etc. The word 'quality' is to avert over-pervasion in smell-ness (<s>gandhatva</s>).

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: sparśanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of Touch (<s>Sparśa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_22 tvagindriyamātragrāhyo guṇo saparśaḥ / sa ca trividhaḥ śitoṣṇānuṣṇāśītabhedāt / pṛthivyaptejovāyuvṛttiḥ / tatra śīto jale / uṣṇas tejasi / anuṣṇāśītaḥ pṛthivīvāyvoḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>AnTs</s> 22] Touch is the quality apprehended only by the skin-organ. It is threefold, due to the distinction of cold, hot, and neither-cold-nor-hot. It occurs in earth, water, fire, and air. Therein, cold is in water; hot is in fire; neither-cold-nor-hot is in earth and air.

children.text:
tvagindriyamātragrāhyo guṇaḥ sparśaḥ/ saḥ trividhaḥ -
śīta-uṣṇa-anuṣṇāśītabhedāt/ pṛthivyaptejovāyuvṛttiḥ/ tatra śītalaṃ
jale/ uṣṇaḥ tejasi/ anuṣṇāśītaḥ pṛthivīvāyyoḥ/
children.translated_text: Touch is the quality apprehended only by the skin-organ. It is threefold — due to the distinction of cold, hot, and neither-cold-nor-hot. It occurs in earth, water, fire, and air. Therein, cold is in water; hot is in fire; neither-cold-nor-hot is in earth and air.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
sparśaṃ lakṣayati -
tvagiti/ sparśatve ativyāptivāraṇāya guṇapadam/
saṃyogādāvativyāptivāraṇāya mātrapadam/
children.translated_text: He defines touch — 'by the skin' etc. The word 'quality' is to avert over-pervasion in touch-ness (<s>sparśatva</s>). The word 'only' (<s>mātra</s>) is to avert over-pervasion in conjunction and the like.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
mātrapadamiti/
cakṣuragrāhyatvagindriyagrāhyaguṇavibhājakopādhimattvamiti phalitor'thaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The word "only"' etc. — the resultant meaning is: the possession of a distinguishing limiting property that is a quality apprehensible by the skin-organ and not apprehensible by the eye.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
nanu
tvagindriyamātragrāhyatve sati guṇatvaṃ sparśasya lakṣaṇamityuktāvapi
paramāṇugatasparśe 'vyāptiḥ/ tasyātīndriyatayā
tvagindriyagrāhyatvābhāvādityāśaṅkyāha - cakṣuragrāhyeti/
cakṣurindriyajanyapratyakṣāviṣayaḥ tvagindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayaśca yo
guṇavibhājako dharmaḥ tadvattvaṃ sparśasya lakṣaṇam/ ghaṭādisparśeṣu
sparśatvajātiḥ cakṣuragrāhyā tvaggrāhya ca bhavati tadvattvaṃ
paramāṇugatasparśe 'pyastīti samanvayaḥ/ tvagindriyagrāhyaṃ
saṅkhyātvamādāya saṅkhyāyāṃ ativyāptivāraṇāya cakṣuragrāhyetyuktam/
cakṣuragrāhyaṃ atīndriyaṃ dharmatvādharmatvādikamādāya
dharmādharmādiṣvativyāptivāraṇāya tvagindriyagrāhyetyuktam/
sparśaniṣṭhatayā gṛhyamāṇaṃ guṇatvaṃ cakṣuragrāhyaṃ tvaggrahyaṃ ca bhavatīti
tadbattvamādāya saḍkhyādau ativyāptivāraṇāya
guṇavibhājaketyupādhiviśeṣaṇam/ guṇatvaṃ tu na guṇavibhājakamiti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, even when it is stated that the definition of touch is quality-hood conjoined with apprehensibility only by the skin-organ, there is non-pervasion in the touch of atoms, because atoms, being supersensuous, lack apprehensibility by the skin-organ — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'not apprehensible by the eye,' etc. [The meaning is:] that which is an object of perception generated by the eye-organ,

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: pākaprakriyānirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of the Process of Transformation by Heat (<s>Pākaprakriyā</s>)

children.text: AnTs_23 rūpādicatuṣṭayaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pākajam anityaṃ ca / anyatrāpākajaṃ nityam antyaṃ ca / nityagataṃ nityam / anityagatam anityam //
children.translated_text: [<s>AnTs</s> 23] The tetrad of form and the like in earth is produced by heating (<s>pākaja</s>) and is non-eternal. In other [substances], it is not produced by heating, and is eternal or non-eternal: what belongs to an eternal [substance] is eternal; what belongs to a non-eternal [substance] is non-eternal.

children.text:
rūpādicatuṣṭayaṃ
pṛthivyāṃ pākajaṃ anityam/ anyatra apākajaṃ nityamanityaṃ ca/
nityagataṃ nityam/ anityagatamanityam/
children.translated_text: The tetrad of form and the like in earth is produced by heating and is non-eternal. In other [substances], it is not produced by heating, and is eternal or non-eternal: what belongs to an eternal [substance] is eternal; what belongs to a non-eternal [substance] is non-eternal.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
pākajamiti/ pākaḥ
tejassaṃyogaḥ/ tena pūrvayapaṃ naśyati rūpāntaramutpadyata ityarthaḥ/
tatra paramāṇuṣveva pākaḥ na dvyaṇukādau/ āmanikṣipte dhaṭe
paramāṇuṣu rūpāntarotpattau śyāmaghaṭanāśe punaḥ dvyaṇukādikrameṇa
raktaghaṭotpattiḥ/ tatra paramāṇavaḥ samavāyikāraṇam/ tejassaṃyogaḥ
asamavāyikāraṇam/ adṛṣṭādikaṃ nimittakāraṇam/ dvyaṇukādirūpe
children.translated_text: 'Produced by heating' — heating (<s>pāka</s>) is the conjunction with fire. By that, the previous form is destroyed and a different form is produced — this is the meaning. There, the heating occurs only in atoms, not in dyads and the like. When a raw pot is placed [in the kiln], upon the production of a different form in the atoms, [there follows] the destruction of the dark pot, and then again, dyad

children.text:
kāraṇarūpaṃ
asamavāyikāraṇamiti pīlupākavādino vaiśeṣikāḥ/ pūrvaghaṭasya
nāśaṃ vinaiva avayavini avayaveṣu ca paramāṇuparyanteṣu yugapat
rūpāntarotpattiḥ iti piṭharapākavādino naiyāyikāḥ/ ata eva
pārthivaparamāṇurūpādikaṃ anityamityarthaḥ/ anyatreti/ jalādāvityarthaḥ/
nityagatamiti/ paramāṇugatamityarthaḥ/ anityagatamiti/
dvyaṇukādigatamityarthaḥ/ rūpādicatuṣṭayaṃ udbhūtaṃ pratyakṣam/
anudbhūtamapratyakṣam/ udbhūtatvaṃ pratyakṣatvaprayojako dharmaḥ/
tadabhāvaḥ anudbhūtatvam/
children.translated_text: 'The form of the cause is the non-inherent cause' — thus [say] the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> who hold the <s>pīlupāka</s> (atom-heating) view. 'Without the destruction of the previous pot, a different form is simultaneously produced in both the whole and the parts down to the atoms' — thus [say] the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> who hold the <s>piṭharapāka</s> (pot-heating) view. And therefore,

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
paramāṇuṣveva pāka
iti/ paramāṇuṣveva pūrvarūpaparāvṛttyādijanakatejassaṃyoga
ityarthaḥ/ evakāravyavacchedyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Heating only in atoms' — the meaning is: the conjunction with fire that generates the displacement of the previous form and the like, [occurs] only in atoms. What is excluded by the word 'only'

children.text:
spaṣṭayati - na
vdyaṇukādāviti/ āmanikṣipte ghaṭa iti/ ghaṭe āmanikṣipte sati
śyāmaghaṭanāśe paramāṇuṣu rūpāntarotpattāvityanvayaḥ/ tatra
paramāṇurūpe/ avayavinipākānaṅgīkārādāha - kāraṇarūpamiti/
paramāṇuṣveva pākaṃ vadatāṃ vaiśeṣikāṇāmayamāśayaḥ -
vegātiśayavatā tejasā paramāṇūnāmabhighātasaṃyoge sati avaśyaṃ
teṣu kriyā jāyate/ tatayo vibhāgaḥ, tata ārambhakasaṃyoganāśe sati
avaśyaṃ yāvadavayavināśaḥ tataḥ svatantreṣu paramāṇuṣu
rūpāntarotpattau
children.translated_text: he clarifies: 'not in dyads and the like.' 'When a raw pot is placed' — when the pot is placed raw, upon the destruction of the dark pot and the production of a different form in the atoms — this is the construal. 'Therein' refers to the form of the atom. Since the heating of the whole is not accepted, he says: 'the form of the cause,' etc.

children.text:
punaradṛṣṭādidhaṭitasāmagrīvaśāt paramāṇuṣu
kriyāvibhāgādikrameṇa yathāsthitaṃ aparāvayaviparyantamutpattiriti/
children.translated_text: Then, by the force of the aggregate including unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) and the like, in the atoms, through the sequence of action, disjunction, and so forth, production [occurs] up to the ultimate whole, just as before.

children.text:
avayavinyapi pākaṃ
vadatāṃ naiyāyikānāṃ tu avamāśayaḥ - tejasā
paramāṇūnāmabhighātasaṃyoge 'pi tasya niyamata
ārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvivibhāgajanakakriyājanakatve mānābhāvena
avayavinyapi pākasvīkāra ucitaḥ/ ata eva 'so 'yaṃ ghaṭaḥ' iti
pratyābhijñāpi saṅgacchate/ anantāvayavināśādyakalpanena lāghavaṃ ceti/
na cāvayavirūpaṃ prati avayavarūpasya, tannāśaṃ prati āśrayanāśasya ca
hetutāyāṃ vyabhicāra iti vācyam/ kāryatāvacchedakakoṭau
vaijātyaniveśanena vyabhicāravāraṇasambhavāt/ anyatreti -
jalādāvityartha iti/ yadyapi rūpādicatuṣṭayaṃ jalādau bādhitam,
tathāpi yathāyogyamanvaye tātparyam/ udbhūtatvamiti/ udbhūtatvaṃ
jātiḥ/ na ca śuklatvādinā sāṅkaryam/ guṇasāṅkaryaṃ na doṣa
iti navīnamatābhiprāyako 'yaṃ grantha iti na doṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: The intent of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, who also accept heating in the whole, is: even when there is an impacting conjunction of fire with the atoms, since there is no evidence for its necessarily generating the action that produces the disjunction opposed to the originating conjunction, the acceptance of heating even in the whole

children.text:
kecittu -
śuklatvādivyāpyamanudbhūtatvaṃ nānā/ tadabhāvakūṭavattvameva
udbhūtatvamityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: Some, however, [say]: non-manifest-ness (<s>anudbhūtatva</s>) pervaded by white-ness and the like is manifold. And manifest-ness is precisely the possession of the aggregate of absences of [such multiple] non-manifest-nesses — thus they say.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
pūrvarūpaparāvṛttyādīti/ parāvṛttiḥ - nāśaḥ/ ādipadena
rūpāntarotpattiḥ gṛhyate/ tatreti vyākhyeyaṃ padam/ tasya vyākhyānaṃ
paramāṇurūpa iti/ paramāṇugate rūpe ityarthaḥ/ nanu
dvyaṇukādigatarūpe vijātīyatejassaṃyogātmakapākasyaiva
asamavāyikāraṇatvasambhavāt kāraṇarūpaṃ
asamavāyikāraṇamityasaṅgatamityāśaṅkyāha - avayavini
pākānaṅgīkārāditi/ pīlupākavādivaiśeṣikamate avayavini
pākavaśāt pūrvarūpādiparāvṛttiyapāntarotpattyoḥ anaṅgīkārāt
tatra rūpāntaraṃ prati pākasyāsamavāyikāraṇatvaṃ na sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/
yāvadavayavināśa iti/ antyāvayaviparyantaṃ nāśa ityarthaḥ/
ārambhakasaṃyogetyādi/ dvyaṇukādyārambhako yaḥ paramāṇusaṃyogaḥ
tatpratidvandvī tasya saṃyogasya vināśako yo vibhāgaḥ tajjanikā yā
kriyā tajjanakatva ityarthaḥ/ vaijātyaniveśaneneti/
pākajanyarūpatadvināśayoravṛtti yadvaijātyaṃ tadavacchinnaṃ prati
avayavarūpaṃ āśrayanāśaśca heturiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The displacement of the previous form and the like' — displacement means destruction; by the word 'and the like,' the production of a different form is understood. 'Therein' is the word to be explained; its explanation is 'the form of the atom' — meaning: the form residing in the atom. Now, in the form residing in dyads and the like, of a different kind

children.text:
'anyatra apākajaṃ
nityamanityaṃ ca' iti paramamūlam/ anyatra ityasya
jalādāvityarthaḥ/ pūrvavākyāt rūpādicatuṣṭayamityanuvartane/ tathā
ca jalādau vidyamānaṃ rūpādicatuṣṭayaṃ apākajamityartho labhyate/
tadetadasaṅgatam/ jalādau rūpādicatuṣṭayābhāvāt/ jale
gandharahitasya rūpāditrayasyaiva, tejasi gandharasarahitasya
rūpasparśadvikasyaiva vāyau sparśasyaiva sattvāt ityata āha -
yadyapītyādinā/ yathāyogyamanvaya iti/ rūpādicatuṣṭayamityasya
rūpādicatuṣṭayaghaṭakamityarthaḥ/ tadghaṭakaṃ ca trikaṃ dvayaṃ ekaṃ ca
bhavatīti nānupapattiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Elsewhere, [the fourfold group] is non-heat-produced, eternal, and non-eternal' — this is the primary root text. The meaning of 'elsewhere' is: in water and the like. From the preceding sentence, the continuation 'the fourfold [group] of color and the rest' [is understood]. And accordingly, the meaning obtained is that the fourfold [group] of color and the rest existing in water and the like is non-heat-produced. But this is inconsistent, since the complete fourfold [group] of color and the rest is absent in water and the like — in water, only the threefold [group] of color and the rest excluding smell exists; in fire, only the twofold [group] of color and touch excluding smell and taste; in wind, only touch exists. To this he says, with 'although' and so forth. 'The connection is as appropriate' — the meaning of 'the fourfold [group] of color and the rest' is: a constituent of the fourfold [group] of color and the rest. And since such a constituent can be three, two, or one, there is no difficulty — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: saṅkhyānirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Number (<s>Saṃkhyā</s>)

children.text: AnTs_24 ekatvādivyavahārahetuḥ saṃkhyā / navadravyavṛttir ekatvādiparārdhaparyantā / ekatvaṃ nityam anityaṃ ca / nityagataṃ nityam anityagatam anityam / dvitvādikaṃ tu sarvatrānityam eva //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 24:] Number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>) is the cause of the usage of oneness and the rest. It resides in the nine substances. It ranges from oneness up to <s>parārdha</s> (the highest number). Oneness is both eternal and non-eternal. [Oneness] in eternal [substances] is eternal; [oneness] in non-eternal [substances] is non-eternal. But two-ness and the rest are always non-eternal everywhere.

children.text:
ekatvādivyavahārahetuḥ saṅkhyā/ navadravyavṛttiḥ/
ekatvādiparārdhaparyantā/ ekatvaṃ nityagataṃ nityam/
anityagatamanityam/ dvitvādikaṃ tu sarvatrānityameva/
children.translated_text: Number is the cause of the usage of oneness and the rest. It resides in the nine substances. It ranges from oneness up to <s>parārdha</s>. Oneness in eternal [substances] is eternal. In non-eternal [substances] it is non-eternal. But two-ness and the rest are always non-eternal everywhere.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
saṅkhyāṃ lakṣayati -
eketi/
children.translated_text: He defines number — with 'oneness' and so forth.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mūle dvitvādikaṃ
tu sarvatrānityameveti/ hetubhūtāpekṣābuddhināśena
dvitvādināśāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the root text, 'But two-ness and the rest are always non-eternal everywhere' — the purport is: because two-ness and the rest are destroyed by the destruction of the comparative cognition (<s>apekṣābuddhi</s>) which is their cause.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: parimāṇanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Magnitude (<s>Parimāṇa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_25 mānavyavahārakāraṇaṃ parimāṇaṃ / navadravyavṛtti / tac caturvidham / aṇu mahad dīrghaṃ hrasvaṃ ceti //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 25:] Magnitude (<s>parimāṇa</s>) is the cause of the usage of measurement. It resides in the nine substances. It is fourfold: minute (<s>aṇu</s>), large (<s>mahat</s>), long (<s>dīrgha</s>), and short (<s>hrasva</s>).

children.text:
mānavyavahārāsādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ parimāṇam/ navadravyavṛtti/
taccaturvidham - aṇu-mahat-dīrghaṃ-hrasvaṃ ceti/
children.translated_text: Magnitude is the uncommon cause of the usage of measurement. It resides in the nine substances. It is fourfold: minute, large, long, and short.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
parimāṇaṃ lakṣayati
- māneti/ parimāṇaṃ vibhajate - tacceti/ bhāvapradhāno nirdeśaḥ/
aṇutvaṃ mahatvaṃ dīrghatvaṃ hrasvatvaṃ cetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines magnitude — with 'measurement' and so forth. He divides magnitude — with 'it' and so forth. The designation is property-predominant. The meaning is: minuteness (<s>aṇutva</s>), largeness (<s>mahattva</s>), longness (<s>dīrghatva</s>), and shortness (<s>hrasvatva</s>).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
parimāṇasya guṇibodhakaśabdaiḥ
vibhajanamasaṅgatam/ ataḥ dīpikāyām bhāvapradhāna iti/
children.translated_text: The division of magnitude by words denoting the qualified [substance] is inconsistent. Therefore, in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'the designation is property-predominant.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu parimāṇasya
guṇatvāt tadvibhāgo 'pi guṇabodhakaiḥ aṇutvamahatvādiśabdaireva
kartavyaḥ, na tu parimāṇaviśeṣarūpaguṇaviśiṣṭavācakaiḥ
aṇumahadādiśabdaiḥ iti śaṅkāyāṃ samādhānaṃ uktam - dīpikāyāṃ
bhāvapradhāno nirdeśa iti/ aṇumahadādayaḥ śabdāḥ mūle
dharmapradhānakāḥ/ tathā ca teṣāṃ śabdānāṃ aṇutvaṃ
mahattvamityādiparimāṇarūpaguṇā evārtha iti nānupapattiḥ/ tadāha -
parimāṇasyeti/
children.translated_text: Now, since magnitude is a quality, its division too should be made by words denoting qualities, such as minuteness (<s>aṇutva</s>), largeness (<s>mahattva</s>), and the like, and not by words denoting the qualified substance possessing those particular qualities. The resolution of this doubt is stated — in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'the designation is property-predominant.' The words 'minute,' 'large,' and the rest in the root text are property-predominant. And accordingly, the meanings of those words are the qualities in the form of magnitude, such as minuteness, largeness, and the like — hence there is no difficulty. He states this — with 'of magnitude' and so forth.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: pṛthaktvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Separateness (<s>Pṛthaktva</s>)

children.text: AnTs_26 pṛthagvyavahārakāraṇaṃ pṛthagtvaṃ / sarvadravyavṛtti //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 26:] Separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) is the cause of the usage of separation. It resides in all substances.

children.text: pṛthagvyavahārāsādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ pṛthaktvam/ sarvadravyavṛtti/
children.translated_text: Separateness is the uncommon cause of the usage of separation. It resides in all substances.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
pṛthaktvaṃ lakṣayati -
pṛthagiti/ 'idaṃ asmāt pṛthak' iti vyavahārakāraṇaṃ
pṛthaktvamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines separateness — with 'separation' and so forth. The meaning is: separateness is the cause of the usage 'this is separate from that.'

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: saṃyoganirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Conjunction (<s>Saṃyoga</s>)

children.text: AnTs_27 saṃyuktavyavahārahetuḥ saṃyogaḥ / sarvadravyavṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 27:] Conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is the cause of the usage 'conjoined.' It resides in all substances.

children.text: saṃyuktavyavahārahetuḥ saṃyogaḥ/ sarvadravyavṛttiḥ/
children.translated_text: Conjunction is the cause of the usage 'conjoined.' It resides in all substances.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
saṃyogaṃ lakṣayati -
saṃyukteti/ 'imau saṃyuktau' iti vyavahāraheturityarthaḥ/
saṅkhyādilakṣaṇe sarvatra/ dikkālādau ativyāptivāraṇāya
asādhāraṇeti viśeṣaṇīyam/
children.translated_text: He defines conjunction — with 'conjoined' and so forth. The meaning is: it is the cause of the usage 'these two are conjoined.' In all definitions such as that of number and the rest, the qualifier 'uncommon' (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) should be added to prevent over-extension to direction (<s>dik</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), and the like.

children.text:
saṃyogo dvividhaḥ -
karmajaḥ saṃyogajaśceti/ ādyo hastakriyayā hastapustakasaṃyogaḥ/
dvitīyo hastapustaka saṃyogāt kāyapusatakasaṃyogaḥ/ avyāpyavṛttiḥ
saṃyogaḥ/ svātyantābhāvasamānādhikaraṇatvaṃ avyāpyavṛttitvam/
children.translated_text: Conjunction is twofold: action-produced (<s>karmaja</s>) and conjunction-produced (<s>saṃyogaja</s>). The first is, for example, the conjunction of the hand and the book produced by the action of the hand. The second is, for example, the conjunction of the body and the book [arising] from the conjunction of the hand and the book. Conjunction has non-pervading occurrence (<s>avyāpyavṛtti</s>). Non-pervading occurrence means being co-located with one's own absolute absence.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
asādhāraṇetīti/
kālādeḥ sādhāraṇakāraṇatvena tatra nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
svātyantābhāveti/ svapratiyogitva -
svasāmānādhikaraṇyobhayasambandhena abhāvavattvamiti niṣkarṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Uncommon' — the purport is: since time and the like are common causes, there is no over-extension to them. 'Co-located with one's own absolute absence' — the conclusion is: possessing absence through both relations — the counter-positive-hood of oneself and the co-location of oneself.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
svapratiyogitveti/ svaṃ kapisaṃyogābhāvaḥ, tatpratiyogitvaṃ
kapisaṃyoge, tathā svaṃ kapisaṃyogābhāvaḥ, tadadhikaraṇavṛkṣavṛttitvaṃ
ca kapisaṃyoge/ tathā ca
svapratiyogitvasvādhikaraṇavṛttitvobhayasambandhena
kapisaṃyogābhāvaviśiṣṭatvaṃ kapisaṃyoge astīti
tasyāvyāpyavṛttitvam/ svapratiyogitvasambandhena ghaṭābhāvaviśiṣṭasya
ghaṭasyāvyāpyavṛttitvavāraṇāya svasāmānādhikaraṇyaniveśaḥ/ ghaṭasya
ghaṭātyantābhāva sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ nāstīti na doṣaḥ/
svādhikaraṇavṛttitvasambandhena ghaṭātyantābhāvaviśiṣṭasya
paṭasyāvyāpyavṛttitvavāraṇāya svapratiyogitvaniveśaḥ/ paṭasya
ghaṭābhāvapratiyogitvāt na doṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The counter-positive-hood of oneself' — 'own' is the absence of the monkey's conjunction; the counter-positive-hood of that is in the monkey's conjunction. Similarly, 'own' is the absence of the monkey's conjunction; the property of residing in the tree, which is its substratum, is also in the monkey's conjunction. And accordingly, the monkey's conjunction possesses the qualification by the absence of the monkey's conjunction through both relations — the counter-positive-hood of oneself and the property of residing in one's own substratum — hence it has non-pervading occurrence. To prevent [the definition from applying to] a pot, which possesses qualification by the absence of a pot through the counter-positive-hood relation, the 'co-location of oneself' is included. Since the pot does not have co-location with the absolute absence of a pot, there is no defect. To prevent [the definition from applying to] a cloth, which possesses qualification by the absolute absence of a pot through the residence-in-one's-own-substratum relation, the 'counter-positive-hood of oneself' is included. Since a cloth does not have the counter-positive-hood of the absence of a pot, there is no defect.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: vibhāganirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Disjunction (<s>Vibhāga</s>)

children.text: AnTs_28 saṃyoganāśako guṇo vibhāgaḥ / sarvadravyavṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 28:] Disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>) is a quality that destroys conjunction. It resides in all substances.

children.text:
saṃyoganāśako
guṇaḥ vibhāgaḥ/ sarvadravyavṛttiḥ/
children.translated_text: Disjunction is a quality that destroys conjunction. It resides in all substances.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
vibhāgaṃ lakṣayati -
saṃyogeti/ kālādau ativyāptivāraṇāya guṇa iti/ rūpādau
ativyāptivāraṇāya saṃyoganāśaka iti/
children.translated_text: He defines disjunction — with 'conjunction' and so forth. To prevent over-extension to time and the like, the word 'quality' [is stated]. To prevent over-extension to color and the like, 'conjunction-destroying' [is stated].

children.text:
vibhāgo 'ti dvividhaḥ -
karmajaḥ, vibhāgajaśceti/ ādyaḥ hastakriyatā hastapustakāvibhāgaḥ/
dvitīyaḥ hastapusatakavibhāgāt kāyapustakavibhagāḥ/
children.translated_text: Disjunction too is twofold: action-produced and disjunction-produced. The first is, for example, the disjunction of the hand and the book produced by the action of the hand. The second is, for example, the disjunction of the body and the book [arising] from the disjunction of the hand and the book.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
saṃyoganāśaka
itīti/ na ca tathāpi saṃyoge ativyāptiḥ/ tasya pratiyogividhayā
nāśaṃ prati kāraṇatvāditi vācyam/
pratiyogitāsambandhānavacchinnanāśaniṣṭhajanyatānirūpitajanakatvavivakṣaṇenādoṣāditi
kecit/
children.translated_text: 'Conjunction-destroying' — nor should it be said that even so there is over-extension to conjunction, since conjunction has causality for its own destruction by way of being the counter-positive. Some [resolve this as follows]: because the intended meaning is: the producer-hood that determines the produced-ness residing in the destruction of conjunction not delimited by the counter-positive-hood relation — hence there is no defect.

children.text:
pare tu
saṃyoganāśatvāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatvam
iti niṣkarṣaḥ/ etattatparyagrāhakaṃ guṇapadamityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: Others, however, [say that] the conclusion is: causality delimited by the inherence relation that determines the effect-hood delimited by the property of being the destruction of conjunction. They say that the word 'quality' is indicative of this purport.

children.text:
vibhāga iti/
ayamapyavyāpyavṛttiriti bodhyam/ ādyeti/ ādyatvamiha
svasamānādhikaraṇapatanapratiyogikadhvaṃsāsamānakālikatvam/
dvitīyapatanādīnāṃ prāthamikapatanadhvaṃsasamānakālikatvāt
children.translated_text: 'Disjunction' — it should be understood that this too has non-pervading occurrence. 'The first' — here, 'first-ness' means being different from what is contemporaneous with the destruction of a falling co-located with oneself. Since the second falling and the rest are contemporaneous with the destruction of the initial falling,

children.text: nirāsa iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: they are excluded — this is the purport.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
na ca tathāpi
saṃyāga iti/ saṃyoganāśakatvaṃ hi saṃyoganāśajanakatvam/ dhvaṃsaṃ
prati pratiyoginaḥ kāraṇatvāt saṃyoganāśaṃ prati saṃyogo 'pi
kāraṇam/ tathā ca saṃyoganāśajanakatvaṃ saṃyoge 'stīti
ativyāptirityarthaḥ/ pratiyogividhayeti/ pratiyogitvenetyarthaḥ/
pratiyogitāsambandhānavacchinneti/ pratiyogitāsambandhena nāśaṃ prati
tādātmyasambandhena pratiyogī kāraṇamiti kāryakāraṇabhāvāt
saṃyoganāśaniṣṭhā yā pratiyogitāsambandhāvacchinna kāryatā
tannirūpitatādātmyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatāyāḥ saṃyoge sattve 'pi
pratiyogitāsambandhānavacchinnasaṃyoganāśaniṣṭhajanyatānirūpitajanakatā
nāstīti na saṃyoge 'tivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Nor should it be said that even so, in conjunction' — conjunction-destroying-ness is indeed the property of generating the destruction of conjunction. Since the counter-positive has causality for its own destruction, conjunction too is a cause of the destruction of conjunction. And accordingly, the property of generating the destruction of conjunction exists in conjunction — hence over-extension. This is the meaning. 'By way of the counter-positive' — the meaning is: by being the counter-positive. 'Not delimited by the counter-positive-hood relation' — since, through the counter-positive-hood relation, the counter-positive is a cause of destruction through the identity relation, the effect-hood residing in the destruction of conjunction — the causality delimited by the identity relation that determines the effect-hood delimited by the counter-positive-hood relation — although that exists in conjunction, the producer-hood that determines the produced-ness residing in the destruction of conjunction not delimited by the counter-positive-hood relation is absent in conjunction — hence there is no over-extension in conjunction. This is the purport.

children.text:
pare tviti/
svarūpasambandhena saṃyoganāśaṃ prati samavāyasambandhena vibhāgaḥ
kāraṇamiti kāryakāraṇabhāvāt tadanusādeṇa svarūpasambandhāvacchinna -
saṃyoganāśatvāvacchinna -
kāryatānirūpitasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatvaṃ vibhāgalakṣaṇaṃ atra
vivakṣitam/ saṃyoge tu
saṃyoganāśaniṣṭhapratiyogitāsambandhāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitatādātmyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatāyāḥ
sattve 'pi uktavidhakāraṇatvābhāvāt nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
etattātparyagrāhakamiti/
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatātātparyadyotakamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Others, however' — conjunction is a cause of the destruction of conjunction through the inherence relation by the self-linking relation. And accordingly, following that [analysis], the causality delimited by the inherence relation that determines the effect-hood delimited by the property of being the destruction of conjunction delimited by the self-linking relation — this is the intended definition of disjunction here. In conjunction, although the causality delimited by the identity relation that determines the effect-hood delimited by the counter-positive-hood relation of the destruction of conjunction exists, since the said form of causality is absent, there is no over-extension — this is the purport. 'Indicative of this purport' — the meaning is: indicative of the purport that the causality is delimited by the inherence relation.

children.text:
ādyatvamiheti/
svasamānādhikaraṇapatanapratiyogikadhvaṃsasamānakālikaṃ yat yat
tadbhinnatvaṃ ādyatvamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'First-ness here' — the meaning is: first-ness is being different from whatever is contemporaneous with the destruction of a falling co-located with oneself.

children.text:
svaṃ dvitīyapatanādi
tatsamānādhikaraṇaṃ yat ādyapatanaṃ taddhvaṃsasamānakālikameva
dvitīyapatanādi tadbhinnatvaṃ cādyapatane astīti lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Own' is the second falling and the rest; the initial falling is co-located with that; [the second falling etc.] is contemporaneous precisely with its destruction; first-ness, i.e. being different from that, is present in the initial falling — this is the alignment of the definition.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: paratvāparatvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Remoteness and Proximity (<s>Paratva</s> and <s>Aparatva</s>)

children.text: AnTs_29 parāparavyavahārāsādhāraṇakāraṇe paratvāparatve / pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayamanovṛttīti / te dvividhe dikkṛte kālakṛte ca / dūrasthe dikkṛtaṃ paratvam / samīpasthe dikkṛtam aparatvam / jyeṣṭhe kālakṛthaṃ paratvam / kaniṣṭhe kālakṛtam aparatvam //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 29:] Remoteness (<s>paratva</s>) and proximity (<s>aparatva</s>) are the uncommon causes of the usage of 'far' and 'near.' They reside in the four [elements] earth and the rest and in mind. They are twofold: produced by direction (<s>dik</s>) and produced by time (<s>kāla</s>). Remoteness produced by direction is in what is distant. Proximity produced by direction is in what is near. Remoteness produced by time is in what is elder. Proximity produced by time is in what is younger.

children.text:
parāparavyavahārāsādhāraṇakāraṇe paratvāparatve/ te dvividhe -
dikkṛte kālakṛte ceti/ dūrasthe dikkṛtaṃ paratvam/ samīpasthe
dikkṛtaṃ aparatvam/ jyeṣṭhe kālakṛtaṃ paratvam/ kaniṣṭhe kālakṛtaṃ
aparatvam/
children.translated_text: Remoteness and proximity are the uncommon causes of the usage of 'far' and 'near.' They are twofold: produced by direction and produced by time. Remoteness produced by direction is in what is distant. Proximity produced by direction is in what is near. Remoteness produced by time is in what is elder. Proximity produced by time is in what is younger.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
paratvāparatvayoḥ
lakṣaṇamāha - parāpareti/ paravyavahārāsādhāraṇakāraṇaṃ paratvam/
aparavyavahārāsādhāraṇakāraṇaṃ apanaratvam ityarthaḥ/ te vibhajate -
te dvividhe iti/ dikkṛtayorudāharaṇamāha - dūrastha iti/
kālakṛte udāharati - jyeṣṭha iti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of remoteness and proximity — with 'far and near' and so forth. Remoteness is the uncommon cause of the usage 'far.' Proximity is the uncommon cause of the usage 'near.' — this is the meaning. He divides them — with 'they are twofold.' He gives examples of those produced by direction — with 'in what is distant.' He gives examples of those produced by time — with 'in what is elder.'

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: gurutvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Heaviness (<s>Gurutva</s>)

children.text: AnTs_30 ādyapatanāsamavāyikāraṇaṃ gurutvaṃ / pṛthivījalavṛtti //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 30:] Heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) is the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) of the initial falling. It resides in earth and water.

children.text: ādyapatanāsamavāyikāraṇaṃ gurutvam/ pṛthivījalavṛtti/
children.translated_text: Heaviness is the non-inherent cause of the initial falling. It resides in earth and water.

children.text: dravatvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Fluidity (<s>Dravatva</s>)

children.text: AnTs_31 ādyasyandanāsamavāyikāraṇaṃ dravatvaṃ pṛthivyaptejovṛtti / tad dvividhaṃ sāṃsiddhikaṃ naimittikaṃ ca / sāṃsiddhikaṃ jale naimittikaṃ pṛthivītejasoḥ / pṛthivyāṃ ghṛtādāvagnisaṃyogajanyaṃ daravatvam / tejasi suvarṇādau //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 31:] Fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>) is the non-inherent cause of the initial flowing. It resides in earth, water, and fire. It is twofold: natural (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>) and incidental (<s>naimittika</s>). Natural [fluidity is] in water. Incidental [fluidity is] in earth and fire. In earth, fluidity produced by fire-contact [is found] in ghee and the like. In fire, [it is found] in gold and the like.

children.text:
ādyasyandanāsamavāyikāraṇaṃ dravatvam/ pṛthivījalatejovṛtti/
tat dvividham - sāṃsiddhikaṃ naimittikaṃ ceti/ sāṃsidvikaṃ jale/
naikittikaṃ pṛthivītejasoḥ/ pṛthivyāṃ ghṛtādau agnisaṃyogajaṃ
dravatvam/ tejasi suvarṇādau/
children.translated_text: Fluidity is the non-inherent cause of the initial flowing. It resides in earth, water, and fire. It is twofold: natural and incidental. Natural [fluidity is] in water. Incidental [fluidity is] in earth and fire. In earth, fluidity produced by fire-contact [is found] in ghee and the like. In fire, [it is found] in gold and the like.

children.text: snehanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Viscidity (<s>Sneha</s>)

children.text: AnTs_32 cūrṇādipiṇḍībhāvahetur guṇaḥ snehaḥ / jalamātravṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 32:] Viscidity (<s>sneha</s>) is a quality that is the cause of the conglomeration of powder and the like into a lump. It resides in water alone.

children.text: cūrṇādipiṇḍībhāvahetuḥ guṇaḥ snehaḥ/ jalamātravṛttiḥ/
children.translated_text: Viscidity is a quality that is the cause of the conglomeration of powder and the like into a lump. It resides in water alone.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
gurutvaṃ lakṣayati -
ādyeti/ dvitīyādipatanasya vegāsamavāyikāraṇatvāt vege
ativyāptivāraṇāya ādyeti/
children.translated_text: He defines heaviness — with 'initial' and so forth. Since the non-inherent cause of the second and subsequent fallings is momentum (<s>vega</s>), to prevent over-extension to momentum, [the qualifier] 'initial' [is stated].

children.text:
dravatvaṃ lakṣayati -
ādyeti/ syandanam - prasravaṇam/ tejaḥsaṃyogajaṃ naimittikam/
tadbhinnaṃ sāṃsiddhikam/ pṛthivyāṃ naimittikamudāharati -
ghṛtādāviti/ tejasi tadāha - suvarṇādāviti/
children.translated_text: He defines fluidity — with 'initial' and so forth. Flowing (<s>syandana</s>) means streaming. Incidental [fluidity] is that produced by fire-contact. Natural [fluidity] is what is different from that. He gives an example of incidental [fluidity] in earth — with 'in ghee and the like.' He states that in fire — with 'in gold and the like.'

children.text:
snehaṃ lakṣayati -
cūrṇeti/ kālādau ativyāptivāraṇāya guṇapadam/
rūpādāvativyāptivāraṇāya cūrṇādipiṇḍībhāveti/
children.translated_text: He defines viscidity — with 'powder' and so forth. The word 'quality' is to prevent over-extension to time and the like. 'The cause of the conglomeration of powder and the like into a lump' is to prevent over-extension to color and the like.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
tadāheti -
naimittikamāha ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'He states that' — the meaning is: he states that it is incidental.

children.text:
piṇḍībhāveti -
piṇḍībhāvaḥ saṃyogaviśeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Conglomeration into a lump' — conglomeration into a lump is a specific type of conjunction.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: śabdanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Sound (<s>Śabda</s>)

children.text: AnTs_33 śrotragrāhyo guṇaḥ śabdaḥ / ākāśamātravṛttiḥ / sa dvividho dvanyātmako varṇātmakaś ceti / dvanyātmako bheryādau / varṇātmakaḥ saṃskṛtabhāṣādirūpaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 33:] Sound (<s>śabda</s>) is a quality apprehended by the ear. It exists only in <s>ākāśa</s> (space). It is twofold: tonal (<s>dhvanyātmaka</s>) and phonemic (<s>varṇātmaka</s>). The tonal [sound] is [produced] in drums and the like. The phonemic [sound] has the form of Sanskrit language and the like.

children.text:
śrotragrāhyo guṇaḥ
śabdaḥ/ ākāśamātravṛttiḥ/ saḥ dvividhaḥ dhvanyātmakaḥ varṇātmakaśceti/
dhvanyātmako bheryādau/ varṇātmakaḥ saṃskṛtabhāṣādirūpaḥ/
children.translated_text: Sound (<s>śabda</s>) is a quality apprehended by the ear. It exists only in <s>ākāśa</s>. It is twofold: tonal (<s>dhvanyātmaka</s>) and phonemic (<s>varṇātmaka</s>). The tonal is [produced] in drums and the like. The phonemic has the form of Sanskrit language and the like.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
śabdaṃ lakṣayati -
śrotreti/ śabdatve ativyāptivāraṇāya guṇapadam/
rūpādāvativyāptivāraṇāya śrotreti/ śabdaḥ trividhaḥ - saṃyogajaḥ
vibhāgajaḥ śabdajaśceti/ tatra ādyaḥ bherīdaṇḍasaṃyogajanyaḥ/ dvitīyo
vaṃśe pāṭyamāne daladvayavibhāgajanyaḥ caṭacaṭaśabdaḥ/
bheryādideśamārabhya śrotradeśaparyantaṃ dvitīyādiśabdāḥ śabdajāḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines sound — with '<s>śrotra</s>' (ear). The word 'quality' (<s>guṇa</s>) is to avert over-extension to sound-hood (<s>śabdatva</s>) [as a universal]. '<s>Śrotra</s>' (ear-apprehended) is to avert over-extension to form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like. Sound is threefold: born of conjunction (<s>saṃyogaja</s>), born of disjunction (<s>vibhāgaja</s>), and born of [another] sound (<s>śabdaja</s>). Of these, the first is produced by the conjunction of the drum and the drumstick. The second is the crackling sound (<s>caṭacaṭaśabda</s>) produced by the separation of the two halves when a bamboo is being split. Starting from the region of the drum and extending to the region of the ear, the second and subsequent sounds are sound-born.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
bherīdaṇḍasaṃyogajanya iti/ ādye asamavāyikāraṇaṃ
bheryākāśasaṃyogaḥ, nimittakāraṇaṃ bherīdaṇḍasaṃyogaḥ/ dvitīye
vaṃśadalākāśavibhāgo 'samavāyikāraṇam, daladvayavibhāgo
nimittakāraṇam/ tṛtīye tu pūrvaparvṛśabdaḥ asamavāyikāraṇam/
pavanādi nimittakāraṇamiti vivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Produced by the conjunction of the drum and the drumstick' — in the first [type], the non-inherent cause is the conjunction of the drum with <s>ākāśa</s> (space); the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>) is the conjunction of the drum and the drumstick. In the second, the separation of the bamboo-half and <s>ākāśa</s> is the non-inherent cause; the separation of the two halves is the efficient cause. In the third, the preceding sound is the non-inherent cause; wind and the like are the efficient cause — this is the distinction.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: buddhinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Buddhi</s> (Cognition)

children.text: AnTs_34 sarvavyavahārahetur buddhir jñānam / sā dvividhā smṛtiranubhavaś ca / saṃskāramātrajanyaṃ jñānaṃ smṛtiḥ / tadbhinnaṃ jñānam anubhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 34:] <s>Buddhi</s> (cognition), which is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), is the cause of all practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>). It is twofold: memory (<s>smṛti</s>) and experience (<s>anubhava</s>). Knowledge produced solely by impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is memory. Knowledge different from that is experience.

children.text:
sarvavyavahārahetuḥ
guṇaḥ jñānaṃ buddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: The quality that is the cause of all practical activity is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), [also called] <s>buddhi</s> (cognition).

children.text: buddhivibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of <s>Buddhi</s>

children.text:
sā dvividhā -
smṛtiḥ anubhavaśceti/ saṃskāramātrajanyaṃ jñānaṃ smṛtiḥ/ tadbhinnaṃ
jñānaṃ anubhavaḥ/
children.translated_text: It is twofold: memory (<s>smṛti</s>) and experience (<s>anubhava</s>). Knowledge produced solely by impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is memory. Knowledge different from that is experience.

children.text: AnTs_35[1] sa dvividho yathārtho 'yathārthaś ca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 35.1:] It (experience) is twofold: veridical (<s>yathārtha</s>) and non-veridical (<s>ayathārtha</s>).

children.text: saḥ dvividhaḥ - yathārthaḥ ayathārthaśceti
children.translated_text: It is twofold: veridical (<s>yathārtha</s>) and non-veridical (<s>ayathārtha</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
buddheḥ lakṣaṇamāha -
sarvavyavahāreti/ kālādau ativyāptivāraṇāya guṇa iti/ rūpādau
ativyāptivāraṇāya sarvavyavahāra iti/ 'jānāmi'
ityanuvyavasāyagamyaṃ jñānatvameva lakṣaṇaṃ iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>buddhi</s> (cognition) — with 'all practical activity.' The word 'quality' (<s>guṇa</s>) is to avert over-extension to time (<s>kāla</s>) and the like. 'All practical activity' is to avert over-extension to form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like. The purport is: the definition is precisely the property of being knowledge (<s>jñānatva</s>), which is apprehended by the introspective cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) 'I know.'

children.text:
buddhiṃ vibhajate -
seti/ smṛteḥ lakṣaṇamāha - saṃskāreti/ bhāvanākhyaḥ saṃskāraḥ/
saṃskāradhvaṃse ativyāptivāraṇāya jñānamiti/ anubhave
ativyāptivāraṇāya saṃskārajanyamiti/ pratyabhijñāyāṃ
ativyāptivāraṇāya mātrapadam/ anubhavaṃ lakṣayati/ tadbhinnamiti/
smṛtibhinnaṃ jñānaṃ anubhava ityarthaḥ/ anubhavaṃ vibhajate - sa dvividha
iti/
children.translated_text: He divides <s>buddhi</s> — with 'it.' He states the definition of memory — with '<s>saṃskāra</s>' (impression). The impression referred to is that called <s>bhāvanā</s> (dispositional trace). The word 'knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>) is to avert over-extension to the destruction of an impression. 'Produced by impression' is to avert over-extension to experience (<s>anubhava</s>). The word 'solely' (<s>mātra</s>) is to avert over-extension to recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>). He defines experience — with 'different from that.' The meaning is: knowledge different from memory is experience. He divides experience — with 'it is twofold.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
jānāmītīti/ jñānatvamātraṃ lakṣaṇam/
'jānāmi' ityanuvyavasāyagamyatvaṃ tu jñānatvasya
pramāṇasiddhatvasūcanāya/ tathā hi - 'ghaṭaṃ jānāmi'
ityādyanugatānuvyavasāyasyānugatadharmamantarānupapannetvena tasya
svīkartavyatvena lāghavāt jātitvasiddhiḥ/ itthaṃ ca mūle
sarvavyavahārahetuḥ iti buddheḥ svarūpakathanamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'I know' — <s>jñānatva</s> (knowledge-hood) alone is the definition. Its being apprehended by the introspective cognition 'I know' is [mentioned] to indicate that <s>jñānatva</s> is established by a means of valid knowledge. For the introspective cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) that pervades [cognitions of the form] 'I know the pot' and the like, being inexplicable without a pervading property, and since that [property] must be accepted, and [since its acceptance is favored] by parsimony, the establishment of [<s>jñānatva</s>] as a universal (<s>jāti</s>) is achieved. And accordingly, the root text 'the cause of all practical activity' is a statement of the essential nature of <s>buddhi</s>, [not its definition] — this is the purport.

children.text:
saṃskārasya
trividhatvādāha - bhāvanākhya iti/ pratyabhijñāyāṃ ativyāptīti/
'so 'yaṃ devadattaḥ' iti pratyabhijñāyāṃ
taddeśakālavṛttitvarūpatattāsaṃskārajanyatvasya sattvena
tatrātivyaptiriti bhāvaḥ/ mātrītīti/ yadyapi saṃskāramātrajanyatvaṃ
saṃskāretarājanyatve sati saṃskārajanyatvam/ tacca smṛtau asambhavi/
tatra saṃskāretarātmādijanyatvasya sattvāt/ tathāpi cakṣurādyajanyatve
sati saṃskārajanyatve tātparyamavaseyam/
children.translated_text: Since impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is threefold, he says: 'that called <s>bhāvanā</s>.' 'Over-extension to recognition' — in the recognition 'This is that same <s>Devadatta</s>,' since the property of being produced by the impression relating to the 'that-ness' in the form of existing at that place and time is present, there would be over-extension there — this is the purport. 'Solely' — even though 'produced solely by impression' means 'produced by impression while not produced by anything other than impression,' and this is impossible in memory, since memory is also produced by the self and other [factors] besides impression; nevertheless, the intended meaning should be understood as: produced by impression while not produced by the eye and the like [i.e. external sense organs].

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu
jñānatvajātimattvasyaiva jñānalakṣaṇtve mūle sarvavyavahārahetuḥ iti
gurulakṣaṇaṃ kutaḥ proktamityāśaṅkya mūlaṃ na lakṣaṇaparam, kiṃ tu
svarūpaparam/ ato nānupapattirityāha - itthaṃ ceti/ jñānatvasyaiva
jñānalakṣaṇatva ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, if the possession of the universal <s>jñānatva</s> (knowledge-hood) is itself the definition of knowledge, then why is the more cumbersome definition 'the cause of all practical activity' stated in the root text? — anticipating this doubt, [the author explains that] the root text is not aimed at providing a definition, but at stating the essential nature. Hence there is no inconsistency — he says: 'And accordingly.' The meaning is: <s>jñānatva</s> alone is the definition of knowledge.

children.text:
taddeśakālavṛttitveti/
taddeśakālavṛttitvarūpā yā tattā tadviṣayakasaṃskārajanyatvasyetyarthaḥ/
tathāpi cakṣurādyajanyatvaṃ iti/ pratyabhijñā tu
saṃskārasahakṛtacakṣuradijanyeti cakṣurādyajanyatvābhāvāt na tatra
ativyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Existing at that place and time' — the meaning is: the property of being produced by the impression relating to 'that-ness' (<s>tattā</s>) in the form of existing at that place and time. 'Nevertheless, [produced] while not [produced] by the eye and the like' — recognition is produced by impression assisted by the eye and the like; hence, due to the absence of non-production by the eye and the like, there is no over-extension there — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: yathārthānubhavalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of Veridical Experience

children.text: AnTs_35[2] tadvati tatprakārako 'nubhavo yathārthaḥ / yathā rajata idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam / sa eva pramety ucyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 35.2:] An experience whose qualifier-mode exists in the qualificand is veridical. For example, the cognition 'This is silver' regarding [actual] silver. That alone is called <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition).

children.text:
tadvati
tatprakārakānubhavo yathārthaḥ/ saiva prametyucyate/
children.translated_text: An experience whose qualifier-mode exists in the qualificand is veridical. That alone is called <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
yathārthānubhavasya
lakṣaṇamāha - tadvatīti/ nanu 'ghaṭe ghaṭatvam' iti pramāyāṃ avyāptiḥ/
ghaṭatve ghaṭābhāvāditi cet - na/ yatra yatsambandho 'sti tatra
tatsambandhānubhavaḥ ityarthāt ghaṭatve ghaṭasambandho 'stīti
nāvyāptiḥ/ saiveti/ yathārthānubhava eva śāstre pramā ityucyata
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of veridical experience — with '<s>tadvati</s>' (in what possesses that). Now, in the valid cognition 'pot-hood [resides] in the pot,' there is under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>), because the pot is absent in pot-hood — if thus objected: no, because the meaning is: wherever there is a certain relation, there the experience of that relation [obtains]; thus, since a pot-relation exists in pot-hood, there is no under-extension. 'That alone' — the meaning is: in the <s>śāstra</s> (philosophical treatise), only veridical experience is called <s>pramā</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mūle tadvati
tatprakārakānubhava iti/ saptamyartho viśeṣyitvaṃ
āśrayatāsambandhenānubhavānvayī/ tathā ca tadvadviśeṣyaka -
tatprakārakānubhavatvaṃ yathārthānubhavasya lakṣaṇam/ tatpadārthaḥ prakāraḥ,
tadvattavaṃ prakāratāvacchedakasambandhena grāhyam/ tena kālikasambandhena
śuktyādau rajatatvasattve 'pi 'idam rajatam' iti bhrame
nātivyāptiḥ/ na ca tathāpi raṅgatvena rajatāvagāhini, rajatatvena
ca raṅgāvagāhini 'hame raṅgarajate'
ityākārakasamūhālambanabhrame 'tivyāptiḥ/ tatra
raṅgaviśeṣyakatva-raṅgatvaprakārakatvayoḥ
rajataviśeṣyakatva-rajatatvaprakāranakatvayośca sattvāditi vācyam/
tadvadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnatatprakārakatvaviśiṣṭānubhavatvarūpārthavi vakṣaṇena
adoṣāt/ tathā hi - yayoḥ viṣayatayoḥ nirūpyanirūpakabhāvaḥ
tannirūpitaviṣayitayoḥ avacchedyāvacchedakabhāva iti siddhāntaḥ/
darśitabhrameraṅgatvaprakāratāyāṃ rāṅgaviśeṣyatānirūpitatvasya,
rajatatvaprakāratāyāṃ rajataviśeṣyatānirūpitatvasya ca abhāvena
raṅgaviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaraṅgatvaprakārakatva -
rajataviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnarajatatvaprakārakatvayośca asattvāt
nātivyāptiḥ/ smṛtivyāvṛttaye anubhavatvaniveśaḥ/ etatphalaṃ
anupadameva sphaṭībhaviṣyati/
children.translated_text: In the root text, '<s>tadvati tatprakārakānubhava</s>' (an experience whose qualifier-mode exists in the qualificand) — the meaning of the locative case is qualificand-hood (<s>viśeṣyitva</s>), which is connected with experience through the relation of locus-hood (<s>āśrayatā</s>). And accordingly, the definition of veridical experience is: experience-hood qualified by having-that-as-qualificand and having-that-as-qualifier-mode. The referent of the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) is the qualifier-mode; 'possessing that' (<s>tadvattva</s>) should be understood through the relation delimiting the qualifier-mode-hood. Therefore, even though silver-hood exists in a shell through the temporal relation, in the erroneous cognition 'This is silver,' there is no over-extension. Nor should it be said that there is over-extension in the composite-object-based error (<s>samūhālambanabhrama</s>) 'These are a stage and silver' — where the stage is apprehended as having stage-ness and silver is apprehended as having silver-ness — because there, stage-qualificand-hood and stage-ness-qualifier-mode-hood, as well as silver-qualificand-hood and silver-ness-qualifier-mode-hood, both obtain. [This objection does not hold] because there is no defect when the intended meaning is articulated as: experience-hood qualified by having-that-as-qualifier-mode delimited by having-that-as-qualificand. For the established doctrine is: between two object-relations (<s>viṣayatā</s>) that stand in the relation of determiner and determined, the corresponding subject-relations (<s>viṣayitā</s>) stand in the relation of delimited and delimitor. In the demonstrated error, in the stage-ness-qualifier-mode-hood, the property of being determined by stage-qualificand-hood is absent; and in the silver-ness-qualifier-mode-hood, the property of being determined by silver-qualificand-hood is absent — hence, stage-ness-qualifier-mode-hood delimited by stage-qualificand-hood, and silver-ness-qualifier-mode-hood delimited by silver-qualificand-hood, both do not obtain — hence there is no over-extension. The inclusion of experience-hood (<s>anubhavatva</s>) is for excluding memory. The result of this will become clear immediately hereafter.

children.text:
nanu 'tadvati' ityasya
'adhikaraṇe' ityarthakatayā 'ghaṭe ghaṭatvam' iti pramāyāmavyāptiḥ/
ādheyatāyā vṛttyaniyāmakatayā tena sambandhena
ghaṭarūpaprakārādhikaraṇāprasiddheḥ ityāśayena śaṅkate - nanu ghaṭe
ghaṭatvāmiti iti/
children.translated_text: Now, the meaning of '<s>tadvati</s>' being 'in the substratum,' since substratum-hood (<s>ādheyatā</s>) does not determine the locus-relation, the locus for the qualifier-mode of pot-form could not be established through that relation — with this intent, he raises the doubt in the valid cognition 'pot-hood in the pot': 'Now, pot-hood in the pot.'

children.text:
'tadvati' ityasya
tatsambandhinītyarthaḥ/ evaṃ ca ghaṭatvasyāpi ghaṭasambandhitayā
tādṛśapramāyāṃ ādheyatayā
children.translated_text: The meaning of '<s>tadvati</s>' is 'in what is related to that.' And accordingly, since pot-hood too is related to the pot, in such a valid cognition, through the relation of superstratum-hood,

children.text:
ghaṭasambandhighaṭatvaviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭaprakārakatvasya sattvāt
nāvyāptiriti samādhatte-yatreti/ yathārthānubhava eveti/ evakāreṇa
yathārthasmṛtivyavacchedaḥ/ yathārthajñānabhātrasya pramātve smṛtikaraṇasya
pramāṇāntaratāpatteḥ iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: since the property of having pot-as-qualifier-mode delimited by having-what-is-related-to-pot-as-qualificand obtains, there is no under-extension — he resolves with: 'wherever.' 'Only veridical experience' — by the word 'only' (<s>eva</s>), veridical memory is excluded. Because if veridical knowledge in general were <s>pramā</s>, then the causal instrument of memory would have the unwanted consequence of being an additional means of valid knowledge — this is the purport.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
saptamyartho
viśeṣyitvamiti/ 'tadvati' ityatra tacchabdaḥ prakārībhūtadharmaparaḥ/
saptamyartho viśeṣyitvam/ tatra prakṛtyarthasya tadvatpadārthasya
nirūpitatvasambandhena anvayaḥ/ viśeṣyitvasya āśrayatāsambandhena
anubhave anvayaḥ/ tathā ca tadvannirūpitaviśeṣyitvāśrayaḥ
tanniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpakaḥ anubhavaḥ yathārthaḥ/
tadvanniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpakatve sati tanniṣṭhaprakāratāpanirūpakatve
sati anubhavatvaṃ yathārthānubhavasya lakṣaṇam/ 'ayaṃ ghaṭa' iti pramāyāṃ
ghaṭatvavadghaṭaniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpakatvaṃ
ghaṭatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpakatvam anubhavatvaṃ ca astīti
lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ smṛtau ativyāptivāraṇāya anubhavatvaniveśaḥ/
śuktirajatabhrame rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpakatve sati anubhavatvasya
sattvāt
children.translated_text: 'The meaning of the locative case is qualificand-hood' — in '<s>tadvati</s>' here, the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) refers to the property that has become the qualifier-mode. The meaning of the locative case is qualificand-hood. There, the base-meaning, namely the referent of the word '<s>tadvat</s>' (possessor of that), is connected through the relation of being-determined (<s>nirūpitatva</s>). Qualificand-hood is connected with experience through the relation of locus-hood. And accordingly, an experience that is the locus of qualificand-hood determined by the possessor-of-that, and that determines the qualifier-mode-hood residing in that — is veridical. Being the determiner of qualificand-hood residing in the possessor-of-that, while being the determiner of qualifier-mode-hood residing in that, while being an experience — this is the definition of veridical experience. In the valid cognition 'This is a pot,' the property of being the determiner of qualificand-hood residing in the pot, which possesses pot-hood, and the property of being the determiner of qualifier-mode-hood residing in pot-hood, and experience-hood — these all exist — hence the definition applies. The inclusion of experience-hood is to avert over-extension to memory. In the erroneous cognition of shell-silver, since qualifier-mode-hood residing in silver-hood exists, and experience-hood exists,

children.text:
ativyāptiḥ syāt
iti tadvāraṇāya tadvanniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpakatvaniveśaḥ/
śuktirajatabhrame tu rajatatvābhāvavacchuktiniṣṭhaviśeṣyatākatvaniveśaḥ/
śuktirajatabhrame tu rajatatvābhāvavacchaktiniṣṭhāviśeṣyatākatvamevāsti,
na tu rajatatvavadrajataviśeṣyakatvamiti nātivyāptiḥ/
tadvadviśeṣyakatve sati anubhavatvamātroktau śuktau 'idaṃ rajatam'
ityayathārthānubhave ativyāptiḥ/ tatprakārakatvadalābhāve tatpadena
prakāra eva grāhya iti niyamālābhena tacchabdena śuktitve gṛhīte
śuktitvavadviśeṣyakatvānubhavatvayoḥ tatra sattvāt/ tadvāraṇāya
tatprakārakatvapadam/ tanniveśe ca ekatra uccaritayoḥ tacchabdayoḥ
ekārthabodhakatvamiti niyamena prathamagṛhītatatpadārthasyaiva
dvitīyatatpadenāpi grāhyatayā prathamatatpadagṛhītaśuktitvaprakārakatvasya
niruktānubhave abhāvāt na ativyāptiḥ iti kecit/ vastutastu
rajata eva dravyaṃ iti jñāne 1rajatatvapramātvāpattiḥ, ataḥ
tatprakārakatvaniveśaḥ spaṣṭaṃ cedaṃ dinakaryādau/
children.translated_text: there would be over-extension — to avert that, the inclusion of being-the-determiner-of-qualificand-hood-residing-in-the-possessor-of-that [is needed]. In the shell-silver error, what exists is qualificand-hood residing in the shell, which lacks silver-hood — not qualificand-hood residing in silver, which possesses silver-hood — hence there is no over-extension. If only having-that-as-qualificand while being an experience were stated, in the erroneous cognition 'This is silver' regarding a shell, there would be over-extension. Without obtaining the qualifier-mode-component, since the word 'that' must be taken to refer to the qualifier-mode itself, and since no rule prevents the word 'that' from referring to shell-hood, when the word 'that' refers to shell-hood, the properties of having-shell-hood-as-qualificand and experience-hood both obtain there. To avert that, the qualifier-mode-component [is needed]. When that is included, since the two occurrences of the word 'that' uttered in a single [definition] must convey the same meaning by rule, the referent grasped by the first word 'that' must also be grasped by the second — and hence, since the qualifier-mode-hood of shell-hood grasped by the first 'that' is absent in the stated experience, there is no over-extension. This is [the view of] some. In reality, in the cognition 'silver alone is a substance,' there would be the unwanted consequence of being a valid cognition of silver-hood — hence the qualifier-mode-component is included. This is clearly [stated] in the <s>Dinakarī</s> and other [texts].

children.text:
nanu śukte 'pi
kālikasambandhena rajatatvavattvāt
rajatatvavacchuktiviśaṣyakatvarajatvaprakārakatvayoḥ 'idaṃ rajatam'
iti bhrame 'pi sattvāt tatrātivyāptirityata āha - tadvattvaṃ
prakāratāvacchedakasambandhena grāhyamiti/ prakṛte samavāyasambandhaḥ
prakāratāvacchedakasambandhaḥ/ tena sambandhena rajatatvavat rajatameva, na
tu śuktiḥ/ rajataviśeṣyakatvaṃ ca rajatabhrame nāstīti
nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, since shell also possesses silver-hood through the temporal relation, and since the properties of having-silver-hood-possessed-shell-as-qualificand and silver-ness-qualifier-mode-hood both obtain even in the error 'This is silver,' there would be over-extension there — to this he says: 'possessing that' (<s>tadvattva</s>) should be understood through the relation delimiting the qualifier-mode-hood. In the present context, the inherence relation (<s>samavāya</s>) is the relation delimiting qualifier-mode-hood. Through that relation, what possesses silver-hood is silver alone, not the shell. And qualificand-hood of silver is absent in the silver-error — hence there is no over-extension. This is the purport.

children.text:
1.rajatatvapramātvāpattiriti/ rajatatvavadviśeṣyakatvāditi
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The unwanted consequence of being a valid cognition of silver-hood' — the purport is: because of having-silver-hood-as-qualificand.

children.text:
na ca tathāpītyādi/
purataḥ avasthitayoḥ rajataraṅgayoḥ indriyasannikṛṣṭayoḥ satoḥ
rajate raṅgatvaṃ raṅge rajatatvaṃ cāvagāhamānaḥ 'ime
raṅgarajate' ityākārakaḥ yaḥ samūhālambanabhramaḥ tatrātivyāptiḥ/
tasmin bhrame raṅgaṃ rajataṃ ca ubhayaṃ viśeṣyam/ raṅgatvaṃ rajatatvaṃ
ca ubhayaṃ prakāraḥ/ tathā ca raṅgatvavadraṅgaviśeṣyakatvasya
rajatatvavadrajataviśeṣyakatvasya raṅgatvaprakārakatvasya
rajatatvaprakārakatvasya ca sattvāt iti śaṅkiturāśayaḥ/
nānāmukhyaviśeṣyakaṃ jñānaṃ samūhālambanamityucyate/
children.translated_text: 'Nor should it be said' etc. When a stage and a piece of silver, both present before one and in contact with the sense organ, are before one, and one apprehends stage-ness in the silver and silver-ness in the stage — the composite-object-based error (<s>samūhālambanabhrama</s>) of the form 'These are a stage and silver' — there would be over-extension to that. In that error, both the stage and the silver are qualificands; both stage-ness and silver-ness are qualifier-modes. And accordingly, since stage-ness-possessed-stage-qualificand-hood, silver-ness-possessed-silver-qualificand-hood, stage-ness-qualifier-mode-hood, and silver-ness-qualifier-mode-hood all obtain — this is the intent of the objector. A cognition having multiple primary qualificands is called a composite-object-based cognition (<s>samūhālambana</s>).

children.text:
samādhatte -
tadvadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnetyādinā/ tadvadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaṃ yat
tatprakārakatvaṃ tadāśrayānubhavatvaṃ yathārthānubhavatvam/
viśeṣyatāprakāratayoḥ nirūpyanirūpakabhāve satyeva
viśeṣyitvaprakāritvayoḥ avacchedyāvacchedakabhāvo bhavati/
uktasamūhālambanabhrame yadyapi raṅgatvaṃ rajatatvaṃ ubhayaṃ prakāraḥ, yathāpi
raṅgatvaṃ rajatāṃśe prakāraḥ rajatatvaṃ raṅgāṃśe prakāra iti
raṅgatvaniṣṭhaprakāratā rajataniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitā na tu
raṅgatvavadraṅganiṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitā/ evaṃ rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratā
raṅganiṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitā na tu
rajatatvavadrajataniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitā/ tathā ca
raṅgatvaniṣṭhaprakāratāraṅganiṣṭhaviśeṣyatayoḥ
nirūpyanirūpakābhāvāt,
rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratārajataniṣṭhaviśeṣyatayoḥ tadabhāvācca
raṅgatvanirūpitaprakāritva - raṅganirūpitaviśeṣyitayoḥ
rajatatvanirūpitaprakāritvarajatanirūpitaviśeṣyitvayośca
avacchedyāvacchedakabhāvābhāvāt
raṅgatvaprakārakatvāvacchinnaraṅgaviśeṣyakatvasya
rajatatvaprakārakatvāvacchinnarajataviśeṣyakatvasya ca uktasamūhālambanabhrame
abhāvāt nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ anupadameva sphaṭībhaviṣyatīti/
'yathārthānubhava eva śāstre pramā ityucyata' iti
dīpikāgranthavyākhyānāvasara ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He resolves — with 'delimited by having that-possessing-thing as qualificand' and so forth. What is delimited by having what-possesses-that as qualificand, namely that particular qualifier-mode-hood, the experience-hood whose locus is that — is veridical experience-hood. Only when the qualificand-hood and qualifier-mode-hood have the relation of determined and determining does the delimited-delimiting relation between qualificandness and qualifier-ness obtain. In the stated aggregate-apprehending error, although both theatre-ness and silver-ness are qualifier-modes, theatre-ness is a qualifier-mode in the silver-component and silver-ness is a qualifier-mode in the theatre-component. Thus, the qualifier-mode-hood residing in theatre-ness is determined by the qualificand-hood residing in silver, and not by the qualificand-hood residing in the theatre which possesses theatre-ness. Similarly, the qualifier-mode-hood residing in silver-ness is determined by the qualificand-hood residing in the theatre, and not by the qualificand-hood residing in silver which possesses silver-ness. And accordingly, since there is no determined-determining relation between the qualifier-mode-hood residing in theatre-ness and the qualificand-hood residing in the theatre, and since there is no such relation between the qualifier-mode-hood residing in silver-ness and the qualificand-hood residing in silver, and since there is no delimited-delimiting relation between qualifier-ness determined by theatre-ness and qualificandness determined by the theatre, or between qualifier-ness determined by silver-ness and qualificandness determined by silver, the property of having the theatre as qualificand delimited by having theatre-ness as qualifier-mode, and the property of having silver as qualificand delimited by having silver-ness as qualifier-mode, do not exist in the stated aggregate-apprehending error — hence there is no over-extension. This is the purport. 'This will become clear immediately after' — the meaning is: at the point of explaining the <s>Dīpikā</s> passage 'In the <s>śāstra</s>, only veridical experience is called <s>pramā</s>.'

children.text:
adhikaraṇe
ityarthakatayeti/ tathā ca prakāratāvacchedakasambandhena
prakārādhikaraṇaviśeṣyakānubhavaḥ yathārtha iti
children.translated_text: 'Having the meaning of substratum' — and accordingly, what is obtained is that an experience having as qualificand the substratum of the qualifier through the relation that delimits the qualifier-mode-hood is veridical.

children.text:
labhyate/ 'ghaṭe
ghaṭatvam' iti pramāyāṃ ghaṭatvaṃ viśeṣyam, tatra ādheyatāsambandhena
ghaṭaḥ prakāraḥ/ prakāratāvacchedakasambandhaḥ ādheyatā/ ādheyatvaṃ
vṛttyaniyāmakam (ādheyatvāniyāmakam)/ ataḥ ādheyatāsambandhena
prakārībhūtaghaṭādhikaraṇāprasiddhyā pramālakṣaṇasya
tādṛśapramāyāmavyāptiriti śaṅkiturāśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the valid cognition 'pot-hood is in the pot,' pot-hood is the qualificand, and there the pot is the qualifier through the relation of superstratum-hood. The relation that delimits the qualifier-mode-hood is superstratum-hood. And superstratum-hood is non-determining of occurrence. Therefore, since the substratum of the pot which has become a qualifier through the superstratum-hood relation is not established, the intent of the objector is: there would be under-extension of the definition of <s>pramā</s> in such a valid cognition.

children.text:
tadvatītyasya
tatsambandhinītyartha iti/
tatpratiyogikaprakāratāvacchedakasambandhānuyoginītyartha iti
bhāvaḥ/ tathā ca 'tadvati' ityasya yadi
tanniṣṭhaprakāratāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnādheyatānirūpitādhikaraṇatāvānityarthaḥ
syāt, tadā ādheyatāyā vṛttyaniyāmakatayā
ghaṭaniṣṭhādheyatāsambandhāvacchinnādheyatānirūpitādhikaraṇatvāprasiddhyā
avyāptiḥ syāt/ sor'thastu prakṛte na vivakṣitaḥ/ ādheyatāsambandhena
ghaṭasambandhi ghaṭatvaṃ bhavatīti
1ghaṭasambandhighaṭatvaviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭaprakārakatvasya 'ghaṭe
ghaṭatvam' iti pramāyāṃ sattvāt nāvyāptiriti samādhāturāśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Of what possesses that' means 'of what is related to that' — the meaning is: of what is connected through the relation that delimits the qualifier-mode-hood of the counter-positive. And accordingly, if the meaning of 'of what possesses that' were 'the substratum-hood that determines the superstratum-hood delimited by the relation delimiting the qualifier-mode-hood of the pot,' then since superstratum-hood is non-determining of occurrence, the substratum delimited by superstratum-hood qualified by the superstratum-hood relation of the pot would not be established, and hence there would be under-extension. But that meaning is not intended in the present context. Since pot-hood is related to the pot through the superstratum-hood relation, the property of having as qualificand the pot-related pot-hood delimited by having the pot as qualifier-mode exists in the valid cognition 'pot-hood is in the pot' — hence there is no under-extension. This is the intent of the resolver.

children.text:
yathārthajñānamātrasya
pramātva iti/ yadi anubhavatvamaniveśya yathārthajñānatvaṃ pramātvaṃ
ityucyate tarhi smṛterapi yathārthajñānatvāt prakātvaṃ prasajyeta/ na
ceṣṭāpattiḥ/ pratyakṣādipramitivilakṣaṇasmṛtirūpapramākaraṇasya
vilakṣaṇasya pañcamapramāṇasya āvaśyakatayā pramāṇāni catvārīti
sūtrakāroktyasāṃgatyāpatteriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'If mere veridical knowledge were <s>pramā</s>-hood' — if it is said that veridical knowledge-hood, without incorporating the element of experience, is <s>pramā</s>-hood, then since memory too has veridical knowledge-hood, it would have the unwanted consequence of being <s>pramā</s>. And this is an undesirable consequence — because since memory-type <s>pramā</s>, which is distinct from the <s>pramā</s>-type such as perception, would be a distinct kind of <s>pramā</s>, a distinct fifth means of valid knowledge as its instrument would be necessitated, and the <s>Sūtrakāra</s>'s statement 'The means of valid knowledge are four' would become incoherent. This is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: ayathārthānubhavalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of Non-veridical Experience

children.text: AnTs_35[3] tadabhāvavati tatprakārako 'nubhavo 'yathārthaḥ / yathā śuktāv idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_35[3]: An experience having that as its qualifier-mode in what lacks that is non-veridical — as in the cognition 'This is silver' with respect to a shell.

children.text:
tadabhāvavati tatprakārakānubhavo 'yathārthaḥ/
saiva apramā ityucyate/ (sa eva bhrama ityucyate)/
children.translated_text: An experience having that as its qualifier-mode in what possesses the absence of that is non-veridical. That itself is called non-valid cognition (<s>apramā</s>). (That itself is called error (<s>bhrama</s>).)

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
ayathārthānubhavaṃ lakṣayati - tadabhāvavatīti/
nanu 'idaṃ saṃyogī' ti pramāyāmativyāptiriti cet - na/
yadavacchedena yatsambandhābhāvaḥ tadavacchedena tatsambandhajñānasya
vivakṣitatvāt/ saṃyogābhāvāvacchedena saṃyogajñānasya
children.translated_text: He defines non-veridical experience — 'in what possesses the absence of that.' Now, if there is over-extension in the valid cognition 'This is conjoined' — no, because what is intended is the knowledge of that relation [determined] by that particular delimitation by which the absence of that relation [obtains]. In the delimitation by [the absence of] conjunction,

children.text:
1. ghaṭasambandhīti/
ghaṭaprattiyogikādheyatāsambandhānuyogītyarḥtha/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Related to the pot' — the meaning is: what is connected through the superstratum-hood relation that has the pot as its counter-positive.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
ativyāptiriti/
saṃyogābhāvavati saṃyogaprakārakatvasya sattvāditi bhāvaḥ/
yadavacchedeneti/ yadavacchedena
yatsambadhāvacchinnapratiyogitākayadabhāvaḥ tadavacchedena tatsambandhena
tatprakārakānubhavasya vivakṣitatvādityarthaḥ/
saṃyogābhāvāvacchedeneti/ saṃyogābhāvāvacchedakāvacchedenetyarthaḥ/
saṃyogāvacchedeneti/ saṃyogāvacchedakāvacchedenetyarthaḥ/
saṃyogasambandhasyeti/ samavāyasambandhena saṃyogasyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Over-extension' — the purport is: because the property of having conjunction as qualifier-mode obtains in what possesses the absence of conjunction. 'By that delimitation' — the meaning is: the knowledge of that through that relation, by that delimitation by which the absence having counter-positive-hood delimited by that relation and delimited by that [property] obtains, is intended. 'By the delimitation of the absence of conjunction' — the meaning is: by the delimitation of the delimitor of the absence of conjunction. 'By the delimitation of conjunction' — the meaning is: by the delimitation of the delimitor of conjunction. 'Of the relation of conjunction' — the meaning is: of conjunction through the relation of inherence.

children.text:
atredamavadheyam -
idaṃ avyāpyavṛttisaṃyogādiprakārakabhramānurodhena/
vyāpyavṛttirajatatvādiprakārakabhramalakṣaṇaṃ tu -
tatsambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatadabhāvavān yaḥ
tadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinna-tatsambandhāvacchinna -
tatprakārakatvaviśiṣṭānubhavatvam/ pratiyogitāyāṃ prakāratāvacchedaka
- sambandhāvacchinnatvaniveśāt 'parvato vahnimān' iti pramāyāṃ
samavāyāvacchinnavahnyabhāvavatparvataviśeṣyakatvasya sattve 'pi
nātivyāptiḥ/
viśeṣyitvaprakāritvayoravacchedyāvacchedakabhāvavivakṣaṇena 'ime
raṅgarajate' ityākārakapramāyāṃ
raṅgatvādyabhāvavadrajatādiviśeṣyakatvaraṅgatvādiprakārakayoḥ
sattve 'pi nātivyāptiḥ ityalaṃ ativistareṇa//
children.translated_text: Here this should be noted — this [definition] is given in accordance with error having as qualifier-mode a property of partial occurrence (<s>avyāpyavṛtti</s>) such as conjunction and the like. But the definition of error having a property of complete occurrence (<s>vyāpyavṛtti</s>) such as silver-ness and the like as its qualifier-mode is: the experience-hood qualified by that relation-delimited qualifier-mode-hood, having as qualificand what possesses the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the relation delimiting the qualifier-mode-hood and delimited by that relation. Because of the incorporation in the counter-positive-hood of delimitation by the relation delimiting the qualifier-mode-hood, in the valid cognition 'The mountain possesses fire,' even though the mountain is the qualificand of the property of having the absence of fire through inherence, there is no over-extension. By the intention of the delimited-delimiting relation between qualificandness and qualifier-ness, in the valid cognition 'These are the theatre and silver,' even though the property of having silver as qualificand with the absence of theatre-ness and the like and the property of having theatre-ness and the like as qualifier-mode obtain, there is no over-extension. But enough of excessive elaboration.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
saṃyogābhāvavatīti/ saṃyogasyāvyāpyavṛttitvāt
saṃyogavatyapi saṃyogābhāvasya sattvāt 'idaṃ saṃyogi' iti
pramāyāṃ saṃyogābhāvavati saṃyogaprakārakatvasattvāt tadabhāvavati
tatprakārakatvarūpabhramalakṣaṇātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ yadavacchedenetyādi/
mūlāvacchedena samavāyasambandhāvacchinnakapisaṃyogābhāvaḥ vṛkṣe
vartate tadavacchedena cet kapisaṃyogāvagāhi jñānaṃ bhavati tarhi
tajjñānaṃ bhramaḥ/ agrāvacchedena kapisaṃyogajñānaṃ tu pramaiva,
tadavacchedena kapisaṃyogābhāvavirahāt/ agrāvacchedena
kapisaṃyogavati vṛkṣe tadavacchedenaiva
children.translated_text: 'In what possesses the absence of conjunction' — since conjunction is a property of partial occurrence, in what possesses conjunction, the absence of conjunction also exists.
