In the valid cognition 'This is conjoined,' since the property of having conjunction as qualifier-mode obtains in what possesses the absence of conjunction, there is over-extension of the definition of error in the form of 'having that as qualifier-mode in what possesses the absence of that' — this is the purport. 'By that delimitation' etc. By the delimitation of the trunk, the absence of monkey-conjunction delimited by the inherence relation exists in the tree. If, by that delimitation, the cognition apprehending monkey-conjunction occurs, then that cognition is an error. But the cognition of monkey-conjunction by the delimitation of the branches is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) itself, because by that delimitation the absence of monkey-conjunction does not exist. By the delimitation of the branches,

children.text:
samavāyātiriktasambandhāvacchinnakapisaṃyogābhāvasattvāt agre
vṛkṣaḥ kapisaṃyogīti pramāyāḥ bhramatvāpattiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
yatsambandhāvacchinneti/ mūlāvacchedena ramavāyasambandhāvacchinna -
kapisaṃyogābhāvavati vṛkṣe kālikasambandhena
kapisaṃyogaprakārakapramāyāmativyāptivāraṇāya tatsambandhenetyuktam
nanu 'saṃyogābhāvāvacchedena saṃyogajñānasya' iti
dīpikoktirayuktā; mūle vṛkṣaḥ kapisaṃyogīti bhramātmakajñānasya
mūlāvacchedena kapisaṃyogāvagāhitve 'pi saṃyogābhāvāvacchedena
saṃyogāvagāhitvābhāvāt/ na hi saṃyogasya
saṃyogābhāvo 'vacchedakaḥ, 1tathā apratīteḥ ityato vyācaṣṭe -
saṃyogābhāvāvacchedakāvacchedenetyartha iti/
saṃyogābhāvasyāvacchedako yaḥ mūlādiḥ tadavacchedenetyarthaḥ/
saṃyogāvacchedakāvacchedeneti/ saṃyogasya avacchedakaḥ yaḥ agrādiḥ
tadavacchedenetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: since the absence of monkey-conjunction delimited by a relation other than inherence exists in the tree which possesses monkey-conjunction by the delimitation of the branches, the valid cognition 'The tree is conjoined with a monkey at the branches' would have the unwanted consequence of being an error. To avert that, [it is said] 'of that relation' — by the delimitation of the trunk, in the tree which possesses the absence of monkey-conjunction delimited by the inherence relation, the valid cognition 'The tree is conjoined with a monkey' having monkey-conjunction as qualifier-mode through the temporal relation — to avert over-extension, it was said 'of that relation.' Now, the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'by the delimitation of the absence of conjunction, [the knowledge] of conjunction' is not proper; because even though the cognition that is erroneous and apprehends monkey-conjunction by the delimitation of the trunk does apprehend monkey-conjunction, it does not apprehend conjunction by the delimitation of the absence of conjunction. For the absence of conjunction is not the delimitor of conjunction, since such is not cognized — therefore he explains: 'the meaning is: by the delimitation of the delimitor of the absence of conjunction.' The meaning is: by the delimitation of the trunk and the like which is the delimitor of the absence of conjunction. 'By the delimitation of the delimitor of conjunction' — the meaning is: by the delimitation of the branches and the like which is the delimitor of conjunction.

children.text:
nanu
avyāpyavṛttipadārthaṃprakārakabhramasya sāvacchinnaviṣayakatve 'pi
vyāpyavṛttirajatatvādiprakārakabhramasya tadabhāvāt
yadavacchedenetyādiniruktabhramalakṣaṇaṃ sarvabhramānuyāyi na bhavatītyata
āha - atredamavadheyamiti/ tatsambandhāvacchinnetyādi/ śuktau
indriyasannikṛṣṭāyāṃ yaḥ 'idaṃ rajatam' iti bhramaḥ tatra samanvayaḥ
kriyate/ samavāyasambandhāvacchinna
children.translated_text: Now, although the error having as qualifier-mode a property of partial occurrence has a delimited-object-hood, since the error having silver-ness and the like as qualifier-mode — properties of complete occurrence — does not have such [delimited-object-hood], the definition of error stated with 'by that delimitation' and so forth does not apply to all errors — therefore he says: 'Here this should be noted' etc. 'Delimited by that relation' etc. The application is made to the error 'This is silver' with respect to the shell before one which is in contact with the sense organ. Through the relation of inherence,

children.text:
pratiyogitakarajatatvābhāvavān purovartiśuktirūpapadārthaḥ/
tadviśeṣyakatve sati rajatatvaprakārakatvaṃ uktabhrame 'sti iti /
prakāratāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ yadi pratiyogitāyāṃ na
niveśyate tadā
children.translated_text: the entity before one in the form of a shell possesses the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by silver-ness. In having that as qualificand, the property of having silver-ness as qualifier-mode exists in the stated error.

children.text:
yatkiñcitsambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatadabhāvavān yaḥ
tadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinna-tatprakārakatvaviśiṣṭānubhavatvaṃ bhramasya lakṣaṇaṃ
syāt/ tathā sati 'parvato vahnimān' iti pramāyāmativyāptiḥ/
tathā hi - tatpadena vahnirūpaḥ prakāraḥ gṛhītaścet tasya saṃyogena
parvate sattve 'pi samavāyena sattā nāsti/ ataḥ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnavahnyabhāvavān yaḥ
children.translated_text: If the delimitation by the relation that delimits the qualifier-mode-hood is not incorporated in the counter-positive-hood, then the definition of error would be: the experience-hood qualified by any-relation-delimited counter-positive-hood of that-absence-possessing qualificand-hood delimited by that-qualifier-mode-hood. In that case, there would be over-extension in the valid cognition 'The mountain possesses fire.' For if the qualifier-mode in the form of fire is taken by the word 'that,' even though fire exists on the mountain through conjunction, it does not exist through inherence. Therefore, the mountain possesses the absence of fire delimited by inherence,

children.text:
1. tathā apratīteriti/
saṃyogāvacchedakatayā saṃyogābhāvasyāpratīterityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Since such is not cognized' — the meaning is: since the absence of conjunction is not cognized as the delimitor of conjunction.

children.text:
parvataḥ tadviśeṣyakatve
sati vahniprakārakatvaṃ 'parvato vahnimān' iti pramāyāmastīti/
prakāratāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaniveśe tu saṃyogasambandhasyaiva
prakāratāvacchedakatayā tadavacchinnapratiyogitākavahnyabhāvavān
viśeṣya parvato na bhavatīti
prakāratāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatadabhāvavadviśeṣyakatvaṃ
'parvato vahnimān' iti pramāyāṃ nāstīti nātivyāptiriti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: and the mountain, having the property of having fire as qualifier-mode in what has that as qualificand, exists in the valid cognition 'The mountain possesses fire.' But with the incorporation of delimitation by the relation that delimits the qualifier-mode-hood, since the relation of conjunction alone is the delimitor of the qualifier-mode-hood, the mountain — as qualificand — does not possess the absence of fire whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by that [conjunction relation]. Hence the property of having as qualificand what possesses the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the qualifier-mode-delimiting relation does not exist in the valid cognition 'The mountain possesses fire' — hence there is no over-extension. This is the purport.

children.text:
viśeṣyitvaprakāritvayoriti/ tathā ca
viśeṣyitvaprakāritvayo avacchedyāvacchedakabhāvāvivakṣaṇe
tadabhāvavadviśeṣyakaḥ tatprakārakānubhavaḥ bhrama ityetāvanmātroktau
raṅge raṅgatvaṃ rajate rajatatvaṃ cāvagāhamānaḥ yaḥ 'ime
raṅgarajate' iti pramātmakānubhavaḥ tatra raṅgaṃ rajataṃ ca
viśeṣyam, raṅgatvaṃ rajatatvaṃ ca prakāra iti tatpadena
raṅgatvagrahaṇe tadabhāvavat rajataṃ uktapramāyāṃ viśeṣyaṃ bhavati
raṅgatvaṃ ca prakāro bhevatīti raṅgatvābhāvavadrajataviśeṣyakatvaṃ
raṅgatvaprakārakatvaṃ cāsti, evaṃ rajatatvābhāvavadraṅgaviśeṣyakatvaṃ
rajatatvaprakārakatvaṃ cāstītyativyāpti syāt/ atastayoḥ
avacchedyāvacchedakābhāvavivakṣā/ tathā ca tadabhāva vadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaṃ
yat tatprakārakatvaṃ tadviśiṣṭānubhavaḥ bhrama iti lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati/
uktasamūhālambanapramāyāṃ
raṅgatvaniṣṭhaprakārataraṅgatvavadraṅganiṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitā, na
tu raṅgatvābhāvavadrajataniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitā, rajate
raṅgatvasyāprakāratvāt/ evaṃ ca
raṅgatvaniṣṭhaprakāratārajataniṣṭhaviśeṣyatayorniṃrūpya
nirūpakabhāvābhāvataraṅgatvaprakārakatvaraṅgatvābhāvavadrajataviśeṣyakatvayoḥ
avacchedyāvacchedakabhāvo nāsti/ yayorviṣayatayoḥ nirūpyanirūpakabhāvaḥ
tannirūpitaviṣayitayoreva avacchedyāvacchedakabhāva iti niyamāt/
evaṃ ca raṅgatvābhāvavadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaraṅgatvaprakārakatvasya
rajatatvābhāvavadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnarajatatvaprakārakatvasya
children.translated_text: 'Of qualificand-hood and qualifier-mode-hood' — and accordingly, if the relation of delimited-delimitor between qualificand-hood and qualifier-mode-hood is not intended, then by merely stating 'a cognition having something as qualificand where the absence of that [qualifier-mode] exists, and having that as qualifier-mode, is error,' in the veridical cognition 'these are the stage and silver' that apprehends stage-ness in the stage and silver-ness in the silver as a collective cognition — since the stage and silver are qualificands, and stage-ness and silver-ness are qualifier-modes, by including stage-ness under 'that,' silver (in which the absence of stage-ness exists) becomes a qualificand in the said valid cognition, and stage-ness becomes a qualifier-mode; thus there would be over-pervasion, since the qualificand-hood of silver in which stage-ness is absent and the qualifier-mode-hood of stage-ness both exist; likewise, the qualificand-hood of the stage in which silver-ness is absent and the qualifier-mode-hood of silver-ness also exist. Therefore, the relation of delimited-delimitor between the two [qualificand-hood and qualifier-mode-hood] is intended. And accordingly, the definition becomes: a cognition in which the qualifier-mode-hood delimited by the qualificand-hood of something in which that absence exists, is error. In the said collective valid cognition, the qualifier-mode-hood residing in stage-ness determines the qualificand-hood residing in the stage, but not the qualificand-hood residing in silver in which stage-ness is absent — because stage-ness is not a qualifier-mode in silver. And thus, since there is no determiner-determined relation between the qualifier-mode-hood residing in stage-ness and the qualificand-hood residing in silver, the delimited-delimitor relation between the qualifier-mode-hood of stage-ness and the qualificand-hood of silver-in-which-stage-ness-is-absent does not obtain — because the delimited-delimitor relation between the determined object-hoods obtains only between the determining subject-hoods. And thus, since the qualifier-mode-hood of stage-ness delimited by the qualificand-hood of what lacks stage-ness, and the qualifier-mode-hood of silver-ness delimited by the qualificand-hood of what lacks silver-ness,

children.text:
coktasamūhālambanapramāyāṃ abhāvānnātivyāpitariti bhāvaḥ/
prakāratāviśiṣṭaviśeṣyatānirūpakatve satyanubhavatvaṃ bhramasya lakṣaṇam/
viśeṣyatāyāṃ prakāratāvaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
1svāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākasvāśrayābhāvavanniṣṭhatvasvanirūpitatvobhayasambandheneti
niṣkarṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: are absent in the said collective valid cognition, there is no over-pervasion — this is the purport. The definition of error is: cognition-hood (<s>anubhavatva</s>) when there is the determinacy of a qualifier-hood-qualified qualificand-hood. And the qualification of the qualificand-hood by the qualifier-hood is through both relations: (1) being located in something that possesses the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation that is the delimitor of one's own [qualifier-hood], and inhering in the substratum of one's own [qualifier-hood]; and (2) being determined by one's own [qualifier-hood] — this is the final conclusion.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: yathārthānubhavavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Classification of Veridical Cognition

children.text: AnTs_36 yathārthānubhavaś caturvidhaḥ pratyakṣānumityupamitiśabdabhedāt / tatkaraṇam api caturvidhaṃ pratyakṣānumānopamānaśabdabhedāt //
children.translated_text: [<s>AnTs</s> 36] Veridical cognition is fourfold, due to the distinction of perception, inference, comparison, and verbal testimony. Its instrument too is fourfold, due to the distinction of perception, inference-instrument, comparison-instrument, and verbal testimony.

children.text:
yathārthānubhavaḥ
caturvidhaḥ - pratyakṣa - anumiti - upamiti - śabdabhedāt/ tatkaraṇamapi
caturvidham - pratyakṣa - anumāna - upamāna - śabdabhedāt/
children.translated_text: Veridical cognition is fourfold — due to the distinction of perception, inference, comparison, and verbal testimony. Its instrument too is fourfold — due to the distinction of perception-instrument, inference-instrument, comparison-instrument, and verbal testimony.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
yathārthānubhavaṃ
vibhajate/ yathārtheti/ prasaṅgāt pramākaraṇaṃ vibhajate -
tatkaraṇamapīti/ prakākaraṇamityarthaḥ/ pramāyāḥ karaṇaṃ pramāṇam iti
pramāṇasāmānyalakṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: He classifies veridical cognition — 'veridical' etc. Incidentally, he classifies the instrument of valid cognition — 'its instrument too,' etc. 'Instrument of valid cognition' — this is the meaning. 'The instrument of <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)' — this is the general definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
prasaṅgāditi/
smṛtasya upekṣānarhatvaṃ prasaṅgaḥ tasmādityarthaḥ/
sāmānyato 'vagatasyaiva viśeṣarūpeṇa pratipādanaṃ saṃbhavatīti
sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sphuṭayati - pramāyāḥ karaṇaṃ pramāṇamiti/
children.translated_text: 'Incidentally' — the meaning is: because what has been recalled should not be neglected, therefore [it is mentioned]. Since what has been cognized in general can be presented in a specific form, he clarifies the general definition — 'the instrument of <s>pramā</s> is <s>pramāṇa</s>.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
smṛtasyeti/
pramāyāḥ lakṣaṇe ukte tatkaraṇaṃ smṛtaṃ bhavatīti tasya upekṣā na yukteti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Of what has been recalled' — the purport is: when the definition of <s>pramā</s> has been stated, its instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) comes to be recalled, and hence its neglect is not appropriate.

children.text:
1. svāvacchedaketi/
śuktāvidaṃ rajatamiti bhrame evaṃ samanvayaḥ - svaṃ rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratā
tadavacchedakasambandhaḥ samavāyasambandhaḥ tadavacchinnapratiyogitākaḥ
svāśrayasya prakāratāśrayasya rajatatvasya abhāvaḥ tadvacchuktiniṣṭhatvaṃ
viśeṣyatāyām; evaṃ svaṃ rajatvaniṣṭhaprakāratā tannirūpitatvaṃ ca
śuktiniṣṭhaviśeṣyatāyām/ tathā ca uktobhayasambandhena
rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratāviśiṣṭā yā śuktiniṣṭhā viśeṣyatā
tannirūpakatve sati anubhavatvaṃ idaṃ rajatamiti bhrame 'stīti/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Of its own delimitor' etc. — In the error 'this nacre is silver,' the correlation is as follows: 'self' is the qualifier-mode-hood residing in silver-ness; 'the relation that is its delimitor' is the relation of inherence; 'the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by that' is the absence of silver-ness inherent in the substratum of the qualifier-mode-hood; 'being located in what possesses that,' i.e. in the nacre — this is in the qualificand-hood. Similarly, 'self' is the qualifier-mode-hood residing in silver-ness; 'being determined by it' is in the qualificand-hood residing in the nacre. And accordingly, the qualificand-hood residing in the nacre, qualified by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in silver-ness through both the stated relations — when there is the determinacy of that, cognition-hood is present in the error 'this is silver.'

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: karaṇalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of Instrument (<s>Karaṇa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_37 asādhāraṇam kāraṇaṃ karaṇam /
children.translated_text: [<s>AnTs</s> 37] An uncommon cause is an instrument.

children.text:
(vyāpāravat)
asādhāraṇakāraṇaṃ karaṇam/
children.translated_text: An uncommon cause (possessing operation) is an instrument.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
karaṇalakṣaṇamāha -
asādhāraṇeti/ sādhāraṇakāraṇe dikkālādau ativyāptivāraṇāya
asādhāraṇeti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of instrument — 'uncommon' etc. 'Uncommon' is to avert over-pervasion in common causes such as space, time, and the like.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
asādhāraṇetīti/
dikkālādṛṣṭādeḥ kāryatvāvacchinnaṃ pratyeva kāraṇatvāt
anubhavatvavyāpyadharmāvacchinnapramāvṛttikāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvarūpāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvasya
tatra asattvāt nātivyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Uncommon' etc. — Since space, time, unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), and the like have causality only with respect to what is delimited by effect-hood [in general], and since the uncommon causality in the form of causality determined by effect-hood delimited by the property pervaded by cognition-hood, which occurs in valid cognition, does not exist in them — there is no over-pervasion.

children.text:
prācīnāstu-
'vyāpāravattve sati' ityapi vaktavyam/ ataḥ cakṣuḥ-saṃyogādau
nātivyāptiḥ/ śrotramanassaṃyogaḥ śabdo vā vyāpāraḥ saṃbhavatyeveti
na śrotrendriyo karaṇalakṣaṇāvyāptiḥ-iti vadanti/
children.translated_text: The ancients, however, [say]: 'when there is the possession of operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>)' should also be stated. And thus, there is no over-pervasion in eye-contact and the like. The contact of the ear with the mind, or sound, can serve as the operation — hence there is no under-pervasion of the definition of instrument in the ear-organ — thus they state.

children.text:
"yadvilambāt prakṛtakāryānutpādaḥ
tatkāraṇatvasyaivāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvātmakatayā kālādiṣu
tādṛśakāraṇatvābhāvāt na ativyāptiḥ/
vyāpāratvenābhimatendriyasaṃyogādikameva karaṇam/ etacca
'liṅgaparāmarśa evānumānam' iti mūle eva sphuṭībhaviṣyati/ ata
eva maṇikṛdbhiḥ uktam - 'tacca liṅgaparāmarśaḥ' iti granthena"iti
tu navyāḥ/ adhikam asmadīyacintāmaṇiprabhāyāṃ anusandheyam/
children.translated_text: 'That whose delay results in the non-production of the relevant effect — the causality of precisely that constitutes uncommon causality; since such causality is absent in time and the like, there is no over-pervasion. The sense-contact and the like, which are accepted as the operation, are themselves the instrument. And this will become clear in the root text "the reflective judgment of the inferential mark is itself inference." Hence the authors of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Tattvacintāmaṇi) said: "And that is the reflective judgment of the inferential mark"' — thus the <s>Navyas</s> (new logicians). More should be investigated in our <s>Cintāmaṇiprabhā</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
dikkālādṛṣṭāderiti/ pramānirūpitāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvaṃ
pramāṇasyalakṣaṇam/ pramāniṣṭhā yā anubhavatvavyāpyadharmāvacchinnā
kāryatā tannirūpitakāraṇatvamiti yāvat/ anubhavatvavyāpyadharmaḥ
pramātvam, kāryatāyāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Of space, time, unseen merit, and the like' — the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> is: uncommon causality as determined by <s>pramā</s>. What is meant is: the causality determined by the effect-hood residing in <s>pramā</s>, delimited by a property pervaded by cognition-hood. The property pervaded by cognition-hood is <s>pramātva</s> (valid-cognition-hood); in the effect-hood,

children.text:
anubhavatvavyāpyadharmāvacchinnatvasyāniveśe kāryasāmānyaṃ prati
dikkālādṛṣṭādeḥ kāraṇatvāt pramāṃ pratyapi kāraṇatvamastīti
pramāṇalakṣaṇasya dikkālādāvativyāptiḥ syāt/ tanniveśe tu
prabhāniṣṭhakāryatvāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatāyāḥ dikkālādau
sattve 'pi pramāniṣṭhapramātvāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvaṃ nāstīti
nātivyāptiḥ/ cakṣurāderiva tatsannikarṣāderapi
pratyakṣapramāhetutvāt pramāṇalakṣaṇasya vyāpāreṣu sannikarṣādiṣu
ativyāptivāraṇāya vyāpāradvārakaṃ kāraṇatvaṃ lakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: without the inclusion of the delimitation by a property pervaded by cognition-hood, since space, time, unseen merit, and the like have causality with respect to effects in general, they would also have causality with respect to valid cognition, and the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> would over-extend to space, time, and the like. But with that inclusion, even though in space, time, and the like there is causality determined by the effect-hood delimited by <s>pramā</s>-hood occurring in <s>pramā</s>, the causality determined by the effect-hood delimited by <s>pramātva</s>-hood (valid-cognition-hood) residing in <s>pramā</s> does not exist — hence there is no over-pervasion. Since just like the eye, its contact too has the status of being a cause of perceptual valid cognition, to avert over-pervasion of the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> in operations like contact, causality operating through operation should be included in the definition.

children.text:
niveśanīyam/ na ca
śrotrendriyo avyāptiḥ, śrotrasamavāyarūpasaṃnikarṣasya nityatvena
tajjanyatvaghaṭitavyāpāralakṣaṇābhāvāt vyāpāradvārakakāraṇatvarūpasya
pramāṇalakṣaṇasya śrotrendriye 'bhāvāditi vācyam/
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that there is under-pervasion in the ear-organ — because the contact with the ear in the form of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), being eternal, lacks the operation-nature constituted by being produced by it, and hence the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> in the form of causality-through-operation is absent in the ear-organ.

children.text:
śrotramanassaṃyogasya
śabdasya vā śrotravyāpāratvāt taddvārakapratyakṣakāraṇatvasya śrotre 'pi
sattvāt - iti prācīnamatam/
children.translated_text: Since the contact of the ear with the mind, or sound, serves as the operation of the ear, and the causality for perception through that [operation] exists in the ear too — this is the ancient view.

children.text:
navīnamatamāha -
yadvilambādityādinā/ na vyāpāravatkāraṇatvamasādhāraṇakāraṇatvam/
ati tu yadvilambāt prakṛtakāryānutpādaḥ tattvam/ kālādiṣu
etādṛśāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvābhāvāt nātivyāptiḥ/ vyāpāratvena
prācīnābhimateṣu
children.translated_text: He states the new view — 'that whose delay' and so forth. Uncommon causality is not causality-possessing-operation. Rather, it is: that whose delay results in the non-production of the relevant effect — such is [uncommon causality]. Since such uncommon causality is absent in time and the like, there is no over-pervasion. In the contacts and the like that were accepted by the ancients as operations,

children.text:
saṃnikarṣādiṣveva
īdṛśaṃ kāraṇatvamastīti sannikarṣaparāmarśādīnāmeva pramāṇatvamiti
navīnamatam/
children.translated_text: it is precisely such causality that exists — hence the instrument-hood belongs to contact, reflective judgment, and the like alone — this is the new view.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: kāraṇalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of Cause (<s>Kāraṇa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_38 kāryaniyatapūrvavṛtti kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: [<s>AnTs</s> 38] What invariably precedes the effect is the cause.

children.text: (ananyathāsiddhatve sati) kāryaniyatapūrvavṛtti kāraṇam/
children.translated_text: (When there is the absence of otherwise-established-ness,) what invariably precedes the effect is the cause.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
kāraṇalakṣaṇamāha - kāryeti/ 'pūrvavṛtti
kāraṇaṃ' ityukte rāsabhādau ativyāptiḥ syāt, ataḥ niyateti/
tāvanmātre kṛte kārye ativyāptiḥ, ataḥ pūrvavṛtti iti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of cause — 'of the effect' etc. If merely 'what precedes is the cause' were stated, there would be over-pervasion in a donkey and the like; therefore 'invariably' is stated. With that much alone, there would be over-pervasion in the effect [itself]; therefore 'what precedes' is stated.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
niyateti/
niyatatvaṃ hi vyāpakatvam/ tacca rāsabhādeḥ na saṃbhavatīti tatra na
ghaṭakāraṇatvātiprasaktiriti bhāvaḥ/ pūrvavṛttīti/ svavyāpakatvasya
svasmin sattve 'pi spūrvakālavṛttitvasya asattvena nātiprasaṅga iti
bhāvaḥ/ kāryatāvacchedakasambandhena kāryādhikaraṇe
kāryāvyavahitaprākkṣaṇāvacchedena
vidyamānātyantābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakataddharmavattvaṃ tena rūpeṇa
kāraṇatvamiti samuditār'tho bodhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Invariably' — invariability means pervasiveness (<s>vyāpakatva</s>). And that is not possible for a donkey and the like — hence there is no unwanted consequence of their being a cause of a pot — this is the purport. 'What precedes' — even though the pervasiveness of [the cause's own] self obtains in itself, since the property of existing at a prior time does not [obtain in itself], there is no over-extension — this is the purport. The composite meaning should be understood as: the possession of a property that does not delimit the counter-positiveness of an absolute absence that exists, as delimited by the moment immediately prior to the effect, in the locus of the effect through the relation that delimits the effect-hood — in that form is causality.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
kāryaniyatatve
sati kāryapūrvavṛttitvaṃ kāraṇasya lakṣaṇam/ kāryaniyatatvaṃ ca
kāryavyāpakatvam/ kāryapūrvavṛttitvamātroktau
rāsabhāderapikadācit ghaṭapūrvavartitvamastīti ghaṭakāraṇatvāpattiḥ/
tadvāraṇāya kāryavyāpakatvaniveśaḥ/ kāryasyāpi kāryavyāpakatvāt
tatrativyāptivāraṇāya kāryapūrvavartitatvaniveśaḥ/ tadāha-niyatatvaṃ
hītyādīnā/ kāryavyāpakatvaśarīra eva kāryapūrvavartitvamapi niveśya
pariṣkaroti - kāryatāvacchedakasambandhenetyādinā/
kāryatāvacchedakasambandhena saṃyogena kāryādhikaraṇe ghaṭādhikaraṇe
pradeśe ghaṭapūrvakṣaṇāvacchedena vartamāno yo 'bhāvaḥ na
daṇḍacakrādyabhāvaḥ, api tu rāsabhādyabhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitāvacchedakaṃ
rāsabhatvādi pratiyogitānavacchedakaṃ daṇḍatvādi, tadvattvaṃ
taṇḍādiṣvastīti lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ kāryatāvacchedakasambandhenetyanuktau
kālikasambandhena ghaṭādhikāraṇaṃ yatra ghaṭo notpadyate sa pradeśo 'pi
bhavati tadvṛttiryo 'bhāvaḥ daṇḍādyabhāvaḥ,
tatpratiyogitāvacchedakadharmavattvameva daṇḍādāvasti na
tadanavacchekadharmavattvamityasambhavaḥ syāt/
tadvāraṇāya-kārya-tāvacchedakasambandheneti/
kāryādhikaraṇavṛttyabhāvāpratiyogitvamātroktausaṃyogasambandhena
ghaṭādhikaraṇai vartate yo 'bhāvaḥ daṇḍatantūbhayābhāvaḥ
tatpratiyogitvameva daṇḍe astīti rītyā ubhayābhāvamādāya asambhavaḥ
syāt/ tadvāraṇāya pratiyogitānavacchedakadharmavattvaniveśaḥ/
yaddharmapuraskāreṇa kāraṇatvaṃ vivakṣitaṃ tasmin dharme
pratiyogitānavacchedakatvaṃ vivakṣitam/ daṇḍatvacakratvādinā
daṇḍacakrādīnāṃ kāraṇatvaṃ vivakṣitam/ daṇḍatvādestu
tādṛśapratiyogitānavacchedakatvamasttyeva iti lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ nātaḥ
prameyatvamādāya rāsabhādāvativyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: The definition of cause is: being invariably related to the effect while preceding the effect. And being invariably related to the effect means being pervaded by the effect. If only 'preceding the effect' were stated, then since even a donkey sometimes exists prior to a pot, there would be the unwanted consequence of its being a cause of the pot. To avert that, pervasiveness by the effect is included. Since the effect too is pervaded by the effect, to avert over-pervasion there, the property of existing prior to the effect is included. He states this — 'invariability means' etc. Including even the property of existing prior [to the effect] within the body of effect-pervasiveness, he refines [the definition] — 'through the relation that delimits the effect-hood' and so forth. Through the relation that delimits the effect-hood, namely conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), in the locus of the effect, i.e. the region that is the locus of the pot, what exists as delimited by the moment prior to the pot — that absence which is not the absence of stick, wheel, and the like, but rather the absence of donkey and the like — the delimitor of the counter-positiveness of that [absence] is donkey-ness and the like, while what does not delimit the counter-positiveness is stick-ness and the like; the possession of that [non-delimiting property] exists in stick and the like — this is the application of the definition. Without the phrase 'through the relation that delimits the effect-hood,' the locus of the pot through temporal relation includes even a region where the pot is not produced; the absence existing there, namely the absence of both stick and thread, its counter-positiveness-delimiting-property-possession alone exists in stick — not the non-delimiting-property-possession — and so there would be impossibility. To avert that, 'through the relation that delimits the effect-hood' [is stated]. If only non-counter-positiveness with respect to an absence existing in the locus of the effect were stated, taking the absence of both stick and thread existing through conjunction in the locus of the pot, its counter-positiveness alone exists in stick — and so there would be impossibility. To avert that, the inclusion of 'possession of a non-delimiting property' [is stated]. Whichever property is foregrounded in the intended causality — in that property, non-delimitation of counter-positiveness is intended. Causality of stick, wheel, and the like is intended through stick-ness, wheel-ness, and the like. And stick-ness and the like do indeed possess such non-delimitation of counter-positiveness — this is the application of the definition. Hence there is no over-pervasion in a donkey and the like by taking entity-ness (<s>prameyatva</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: anyathāsiddhinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of Otherwise-Established-ness (<s>Anyathāsiddhi</s>)

children.text:
nanu tanturūpamapi
paṭaṃ prati kāraṇaṃ syāt iti cet - napha 'ananyathāsiddhatve sati'
iti viśeṣaṇāt/ ananyathāsiddhatvam anyathāsiddhirahitatvam/
anyathāsiddhiḥ trividhā - yena sahaiva yasya yaṃ prati
pūrvavṛttitvamavagamyate taṃ prati tena tadanyathāsiddham/ yathā tantunā
tanturūpaṃ tantutvaṃ ca paṭaṃ prati/ anyaṃ prati pūrvavṛttitve jñāta eva
yasya yaṃ prati pūrvavṛttitvamavagamyate taṃ prati tadanyathāsiddham/ yathā
śabdaṃ prati pūrvavṛttitve jñāta eva paṭaṃ prati ākāśasya/
children.translated_text: Now, the form of thread too would be a cause with respect to cloth — if so, [the reply is:] no, because of the qualifier 'when there is the absence of otherwise-established-ness.' Being non-otherwise-established means being free from otherwise-established-ness. Otherwise-established-ness (<s>anyathāsiddhi</s>) is threefold: that with which alone something's preceding something else is cognized — with respect to that, by that, the former is otherwise-established. For example, the form of a thread and the nature of thread-ness are [otherwise-established] with respect to cloth, by the thread. [Second:] that whose preceding something else is cognized only when its preceding yet another thing is known — with respect to that, it is otherwise-established. For example, space with respect to cloth, when its preceding [the cloth] is known only through [knowing] its preceding sound.

children.text:
anyatra
kḷptaniyatapūrvavartina eva kāryasambhave tatsahabhūtaṃ anyathāsiddham/
yathā pākajasthale gandhaṃ prati rūpaprāgabhāvasya/ evaṃ ca
ananyathāsiddhaniyatapūrvavṛttitvaṃ kāraṇatvam/
children.translated_text: When, elsewhere, the effect is possible from an established, invariable antecedent alone, what co-occurs with that [established antecedent] is otherwise-established (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>). For example, the prior absence of color is otherwise-established with respect to smell in the case of transformation by heat. And accordingly, being an invariable antecedent that is not otherwise-established is causality.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
kāraṇaṃ syāditi/
tasya niyatapūrvavṛttitvāditi bhāvaḥ/ nibandhāntareṣu anyathāsiddheḥ
pañcavidhatve 'pi maṇikāramatābhiprāyeṇāha - trividheti/ yena
sahaivetyādi/ yena tantunā sahaiva yasya tatturūpasya tantutvasya ca yaṃ
paṭaṃ prati pūrvavṛttitvamavagamyate taṃ paṭaṃ prati tantanturūpaṃ
tantutvaṃ ca tena tantunā anyathāsiddhamityarthaḥ/ atra sahitatvam
ekajñānaviṣayatvaṃ bodhyam/ tanturūpasya paṭapūrvavṛttitvajñāne
anatiprasaktatanturūpatvenaiva viṣayatā vācyā/ tathā ca tanturūpaṃ
anyathāsiddhamiti/ evaṃ entutvasya pūrvavṛttitvajñānamapi
tantuviṣayakameveti tadapyanyathāsiddhamiti bhāvaḥ/ atra 'yena' ityasya
'svatantrānvayavyatirekaśālinā' iti 'yasya' ityasya ca
'svatantrānvayavyatirekaśūnyasya' iti viśeṣaṇaṃ bodhyam/ tena na
atathābhūtena tantutvena tantoranyathāsiddhiḥ, na vā tantusaṃyogasya
tantunā anyathāsiddhiriti saṅkṣepaḥ/"itarānvayavyatirekaprayuktānvayavyatirekaśāli yat yat
anyathāsiddham"iti tu pare/ śabdaṃ pratīti/ ākāśatvaṃ
hi śabdasamavāyikāraṇatvam/ tathā ca śabdakāraṇatvamagṛhītvā
ākāśasya ākāśatvena ghaṭapūrvavṛttitvaṃ grahītum aśakyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Would be a cause' — the purport is: because of its being an invariable antecedent. Although in other treatises, otherwise-establishedness is fivefold, following the view of the author of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Tattvacintāmaṇi), he says — 'threefold' and so forth. 'Together with which' and so forth — the meaning is: the form residing in a thread (<s>tanturūpa</s>) and thread-hood (<s>tantutva</s>), whose antecedence to a cloth is ascertained invariably together with that thread, are otherwise-established with respect to that cloth by that thread. Here, 'togetherness' should be understood as being the content of a single cognition. In the cognition of the antecedence of thread-form to cloth, the content-hood should be stated through the non-over-extended property of thread-form-hood. And accordingly, thread-form is otherwise-established. Similarly, the cognition of the antecedence of thread-hood is also specifically about threads; hence that too is otherwise-established — this is the purport. Here, 'which' should be qualified as 'possessing independent positive and negative concomitance,' and 'of which' should be qualified as 'lacking independent positive and negative concomitance.' Therefore, thread-hood, which is not of such a nature, does not make the thread otherwise-established; nor is the conjunction of threads otherwise-established by the thread — this is the summary. 'That whose positive and negative concomitance is caused by the positive and negative concomitance of another — that is otherwise-established' — thus say others. 'With respect to sound' — for space-hood (<s>ākāśatva</s>) is the inherent causality of sound. And accordingly, without grasping the causality of space for sound, it is impossible to grasp the antecedence of space to a pot through the property of space-hood.

children.text:
ityākāśo 'nyathāsiddha ityarthaḥ/ anyatra kḷpteti/
apākajasthale gandhaṃ prati kḷptaniyatapūrvavṛttinā gandhaprāgabhāvenaiva
pākajasthale 'pi tatsambhave rūpaprāgabhāvo 'nyathāsiddha ityarthaḥ/ atha evaṃ
niyatapadaṃ vyartham, aniyatarāsamabhādeḥ tṛtīyānyathāsiddhatvena
satyantenaiva vāraṇasambhavāt iti cet - na/ ghaṭasāmānyaṃ prati
anyathāsiddhyasaṃbhavāt anyatra ghaṭābhinne paṭādau kḷptapūrvavartinaḥ
tantvāditaḥ ghaṭotpattyasambhavāditi/
children.translated_text: Therefore space is otherwise-established — this is the meaning. 'Elsewhere, established' — when, in a non-heated case, the effect of smell is possible from the prior absence of smell alone — which is an established, invariable antecedent — even in the heated case, the prior absence of color is otherwise-established [with respect to smell] — this is the meaning. Now, if so, the word 'invariable' (<s>niyata</s>) is redundant, since the non-invariable 'prior-moment-ness of the taste' and the like can be excluded by the third type of otherwise-establishedness alone. Reply: No — because otherwise-establishedness is not possible with respect to pot-in-general; since the origination of a pot is not possible elsewhere — in cloth and the like, which are different from the pot — from an established antecedent such as thread and the like.

children.text:
navīnāḥ
punarevamāhuḥ - laghuniyatapūrvavartina eva kāryaṃsambhave tadbhinnaṃ
anyathāsiddhaṃ ityekavidhameva anyathāmiddhatvam/ laghutvaṃ ca
śarīrakṛtamupasthitikṛtaṃ saṃbandhakṛtam ca/ tatra prathamam -
anekadravyasamavetatvāpekṣayā mahattve/ dvitīyam - gandhaṃ prati
rūpaprāgabhāvāpekṣayā gandhaprāgabhāve, gandhasya pratīyogina
upasthitatvena śīghraṃ tadupasthiteḥ/ tṛtīyam -
daṇḍatvadaṇḍarūpādyapekṣayā daṇḍādau,
svāśrayadaṇḍasaṃyogādirūpaparamparayā gurutvāt/ evaṃ caitāvataiva
nirvāhe anyathāsiddhitrividha pañcavidhā ceti prapañco
vyutpattivaicitryāya/
children.translated_text: The later scholars (<s>Navīnas</s>), however, state as follows — when the effect is possible from a lighter invariable antecedent alone, what is different from that is otherwise-established; thus otherwise-establishedness is of only one kind. And lightness is of three types: body-produced, presentation-produced, and relation-produced. The first: in the case of magnitude, relative to what inheres in multiple substances. The second: in the case of the prior absence of smell relative to the prior absence of color with respect to smell — since smell, being the counter-positive, is rapidly presented. The third: in the case of the stick and the like relative to stick-hood and stick-form and the like — because of the heaviness through the intermediary chain of the conjunction of its own substratum with the stick and the like. And thus, when explanation is possible by this much alone, the elaboration that otherwise-establishedness is threefold or fivefold is merely for the variety of etymological exposition.

children.text:
na ca aniyatarāsabhādeḥ
tṛtīyānyathāsiddhatvenaiva vāraṇāt niyatapadaṃ vyarthamiti vācyam/
yataḥ anyathāsiddhatvasya anugatasya durvacatayā yatra yatra prāmāṇikānāṃ
anyathāsiddhatvavyavahāraḥ tattadbhedakūṭaṃ niveśanīyam/
laghuniyatetyādikaṃ tu bhedapratiyogitattadvyaktiparicāyakam/
itthaṃ ca aniyatānantarāsabhādīnāṃ ekena niyatatvaviśeṣaṇenaiva
vāraṇāt tattadbhedakūṭaniveśe gauravam/ niyatānāṃ
daṇḍatvādīnāṃ tu anāyatyā tattadbhedadavattve
niveśanīyamityabhisandhiḥ/
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that the word 'invariable' (<s>niyata</s>) is redundant because the non-invariable 'prior-moment-ness of the taste' and the like can be excluded by the third type of otherwise-establishedness alone. For, since it is difficult to state an invariant character of otherwise-establishedness [across all cases], the specific distinguishing features must be incorporated wherever the experts (<s>prāmāṇikas</s>) use the term 'otherwise-established.' 'Lighter, invariable' and the like serve as indicators familiarizing one with each such specific instance. And accordingly, since non-invariable, non-immediately-prior entities and the like are excluded by the single qualifier 'invariable' alone, incorporating the specific distinguishing features for each would involve heaviness. But for invariable [entities] like stick-hood and the like, since they are not [excluded] by that [qualifier alone], specific distinguishing features must necessarily be incorporated — this is the intent.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
nibandhāntareṣviti-kusumāñjalivyākhyāne prakāśe
vardhamānopādhyāyaiḥ pañcavidhā anyathāsiddhayaḥ pradarśitāḥ, tadanusādeṇa
muktavalpāṃ ca/ maṇikāraistu śaktivāde trividhā evānyathāsiddhayaḥ
pradarśitāḥ/ tadanusāreṇa dīpikāyāmapi/
sahitatvamekajñānaviṣayatvamiti/ tathā ca yasya
pūrvavṛttitvamavagāhamāne jñāne niyamena tadāśrayasyāpi bhānaṃ bhavati
tat anyathāsiddhamiti phalati/ 'tanturūpaṃ paṭapūrvavṛtti' iti jñāne
tanturūpāśrayasya tantorapi viṣayatvāt 'tantutvaṃ paṭapūrvavṛtti'
iti jñāne viśeṣyatāvacchedakatayā tantutvatvasya bhānāt
tantutvatvasya tantvitarāvṛttitve sati tantuvṛttitvarūpatvāt
tantūnāmapi bhānācca tanturūpaṃ tantutvaṃ ca paṭaṃ
pratyanyathāsiddhamityarthaḥ/
1tatkāryanirūpitaniyatapūrvavṛttitvagrahanirūpitasvaniṣṭhaveśaṣyatāvacchedakībhūtasvāśrayakatvaṃ
prathamānyathāsiddhatvamiti yāvat/
children.translated_text: 'In other treatises' — in the <s>Prakāśa</s>, the commentary on the <s>Kusumāñjali</s>, <s>Vardhamānopādhyāya</s> has shown five types of otherwise-establishedness; the <s>Muktāvalī</s> follows that. But the author of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Tattvacintāmaṇi), in the <s>Śaktivāda</s>, has shown only three types of otherwise-establishedness; the <s>Dīpikā</s> follows that. 'Togetherness is being the content of a single cognition' — and accordingly, the result is: that whose substratum also necessarily appears in the cognition that apprehends its antecedence — that is otherwise-established. Since in the cognition 'thread-form is antecedent to cloth,' the thread — the substratum of thread-form — is also a content; and since in the cognition 'thread-hood is antecedent to cloth,' thread-hood-hood appears as the delimiting property of qualificand-hood, and since thread-hood-hood has the form of residing in all threads while not residing in non-threads, the threads too appear [as content] — therefore thread-form and thread-hood are otherwise-established with respect to cloth — this is the meaning. [Footnote:] The first type of otherwise-establishedness is, in brief: the property of being the substratum of both the [otherwise-established entity] itself and the qualificand-hood-delimiting-property that is apprehended in the cognition of its invariable antecedence to the effect.

children.text:
nanu 'rūpaṃ
paṭapūrvaṃvṛtti' ityākārakaṃ rūpatvena
tanturūpāvagāhijñānamupagamyate tatra tantūnāmaviṣayatvāt tantunā
sahaiva pūrvavṛttitvaṃ nāvagamyata iti kathaṃ tanturūpasya
anyathāsiddhatvamityāśaṅkyāhatanturūpasyeti/ rūpatvasya
paṭapūrvavṛttitvātiprasaktatayā tadavacchedena paṭapūrvavṛttitvagraho na
sambhavati, anyūnānatiprasaktadharmasyaivāvacchedakatvāt/ api tu
anatiprasaktatanturūpatvāvacchinne eva paṭapūrvavṛttitvaṃ jñāyata iti
vaktavyam/ tasmin jñāne tu tantūnāmapi
children.translated_text: Now, in the cognition of the form 'form is antecedent to cloth,' the cognition apprehending thread-form is taken under the aspect of form-hood (<s>rūpatva</s>); since threads are not the content of that cognition, the antecedence is not apprehended together with the thread — so how can thread-form be otherwise-established? — anticipating this doubt, he says 'of thread-form' and so forth. Since form-hood, being over-extended to cloth-antecedence, cannot serve as the delimiting [property] for grasping cloth-antecedence — because only a non-deficient, non-over-extended property can serve as a delimitor — rather, the antecedence to cloth is cognized only as delimited by the non-over-extended property of thread-form-hood. And in that cognition, the threads too

children.text:
2viśeṣyatāvacchedakatayā viṣayatvamāvaśyakamiti bhāvaḥ/
tantutvasya pūrvavṛttitvajñānamapi tantuviṣayakameveti/ 'tantutvaṃ
paṭapūrvavṛtti' iti jñāne tantutvasya viśeṣyatvāt jāteḥ yatra
viśeṣyatayā bhānaṃ tatra kiñcidrūpeṇaiva bhānamiti niyamāt
tantutvatvena tantutvabhānaṃ vaktavyam/ tantutvatvaṃ ca
tantvitarāvṛttitve sati sakalatantuvṛttitvarūpamiti
children.translated_text: necessarily have content-hood as delimiting properties of qualificand-hood — this is the purport. 'The cognition of the antecedence of thread-hood is also specifically about threads' — in the cognition 'thread-hood is antecedent to cloth,' since thread-hood is the qualificand, and since when a universal appears as qualificand, it necessarily appears under some aspect, it must be said that thread-hood appears under the aspect of thread-hood-hood. And thread-hood-hood has the form of residing in all threads while not residing in non-threads; therefore

children.text:
1.
tatkāryanirūpitetyādi/ tatkāryaṃ paṭaḥ tannirūpitaṃ yat
niyatapūrvavṛttitvaṃ tadviṣayakagrahaḥ 'tanturūpaṃ tantutvaṃ vā
paṭaniyatapūrvavṛtti' ityākārako grahaḥ tannirūpitā yā svaniṣṭhā
viśeṣyatā tanturūpaniṣṭhā tantutvaniṣṭhā vā viśeṣyatā
tadavacchedakībhūtaḥ yaḥ svāśrayaḥ tanturūpasya tantutvasya vā āśrayaḥ
tantuḥ tatkatvaṃ tanturūpe tanatutve cāstīti samanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The effect is the cloth' and so forth. The effect is the cloth; its invariable antecedence — the cognition grasping that: a cognition of the form 'thread-form or thread-hood is invariably antecedent to cloth.' The qualificand-hood determined by that — the qualificand-hood residing in thread-form or thread-hood. The substratum that has become the delimiting property of that [qualificand-hood] — the substratum of thread-form or thread-hood, namely the thread. Being that — this is present in thread-form and thread-hood. This is the analysis.

children.text:
2.
viśeṣyatāvacchedakatayeti/ tanturūpamityasya samavāyasambandhena
tantuviśaṣṭa rūpamityarthaḥ/ tathā ca 'tanturūpaṃ paṭapūrvavṛtti' iti
jñāne viśeṣye rūpe tantūnāmapi viśeṣaṇatvāt
viśeṣyatāvacchedakatvamāvaśyakamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'As delimiting property of qualificand-hood' — the meaning of 'thread-form' is: form qualified by thread through the relation of inherence. And accordingly, in the cognition 'thread-form is antecedent to cloth,' since threads are also qualifiers of the qualificand — form — the purport is that qualificand-hood-delimiting-property-hood is necessary.

children.text:
tantutvatvaghaṭakatayā
tantūnāmarpiṃ bhānamavarjanīyam/ evaṃ ca
tantutvaviśeṣyakapūrvavṛttitvajñānasya
tantuviṣayakatvanaiyatyamityāśayaḥ/ yadvā yadviṣayakatvavyāpyaṃ
pūrvavṛttitvaprakārakajñānīyaṃ yadviśeṣyakatvaṃ tat anyathāsiddhamiti
yāvat/
children.translated_text: Since threads are constituents of thread-hood-hood, their appearance too is unavoidable. And accordingly, the intent is that the cognition having thread-hood as qualificand and antecedence as qualifier-mode is necessarily one that has threads as its content. Alternatively, that qualificand-hood of the cognition whose content-hood-of-the-entity is pervaded by the qualifier-mode-hood of antecedence — that is otherwise-established; this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu prathamayatpadena
tantumupādāya tadviṣayakatvavyāpyatvaṃ 'tantutvaṃ paṭapūrvavṛtti'
iti jñānīyatantutvaviśeṣyakatve 'stīti tantutvasyānyathā
siddhatvopapādane, prathamayatpadena tantutvamupādāya
tadviṣayakatvavyāpyatvaṃ 'tantuḥ paṭapūrvavartī' iti
children.translated_text: Now, by taking thread through the first 'which,' the pervaded-hood by content-hood-of-thread is present in the qualificand-hood of thread-hood in the cognition 'thread-hood is antecedent to cloth' — thus establishing the otherwise-establishedness of thread-hood; and by taking thread-hood through the first 'which,' the pervaded-hood by content-hood-of-thread-hood is present in the cognition 'a thread is antecedent to a cloth' —

ca
children.translated_text: since in the qualifier-hood of the thread in the cognition 'thread-hood is what invariably precedes the cloth,' the pervaded-ness by the content having thread as object exists, the dispensability (<s>anyathāsiddhatva</s>) of thread by thread-hood would follow. Similarly, since in the qualifier-hood of thread-conjunction in the cognition 'thread-conjunction invariably precedes cloth,' the pervaded-ness by thread-content-hood exists, the dispensability of thread-conjunction by thread would follow. To this he says — with 'here, by which' and so forth. And accordingly, the result is: that by which — [having] independent positive and negative concomitance and possessing pervaded-ness by being content of the cognition of invariable-prior-existence — what has qualifier-hood devoid of independent positive and negative concomitance in the same cognition, by that, that [latter entity] is dispensable. Thread-hood does not independently have positive and negative concomitance with respect to cloth — rather, only following the positive and negative concomitance of thread itself. Therefore, since the grasping of thread-hood by the first 'that-which' term is impossible, thread is not dispensable by thread-hood — this is the purport. Thread-conjunction, like thread itself, has independent positive and negative concomitance, due to being a non-inherent cause. Therefore, having grasped thread by the first 'that-which' term, although the pervaded-ness by thread-content-hood exists in the qualifier-hood of thread-conjunction in the cognition 'thread-conjunction invariably precedes cloth,' since thread-conjunction does not lack independent positive and negative concomitance, it cannot be grasped by the second 'that-which' term — hence its dispensability does not arise. This is the purport. And accordingly, he states the purpose of the qualifier 'having independent positive and negative concomitance' in the meaning of the first 'that-which' term — with 'thereby, not by what is not of such nature' and so forth. The meaning is: by what lacks independent positive and negative concomitance. He states the result of including 'devoid of independent positive and negative concomitance' in the meaning of the second 'that-which' term — with 'nor' and so forth. 'For the sake of brevity, he states the other two through positive and negative concomitance' and so forth. 'Space-hood indeed' — even though space invariably precedes a pot, the causality of space for a pot is not accepted, because it is dispensable. Its dispensability, however, relative to something else — this is the second type of dispensability. The invariable prior existence of space with respect to a pot is to be grasped through space-hood. And space-hood is being the inherent cause of sound. And accordingly, only after grasping the invariable prior existence of space with respect to sound can the invariable prior existence of space with respect to pot be grasped — hence space is dispensable. This is the purport. 'In the case of non-heat-produced' and so forth. In those pots and the like where, due to the heat-transformation consisting of contact with extraneous fire, the previous color, taste, smell, and touch are destroyed and a new color, new taste, and the rest arise — since the prior absences of all four, namely color, taste, smell, and the rest, invariably exist before the arising of the new color and the rest, one may doubt: let the prior absence of color, like the prior absence of smell, also be a cause of heat-produced smell. This doubt should be averted by [showing] the dispensability of the prior absence of color with respect to smell. It has the third type of dispensability stated by 'when established elsewhere' and so forth. 'Elsewhere' means in non-heat-produced smell, i.e. smell other than heat-produced; since even heat-produced smell can be produced from the prior absence of smell alone, which is established as invariably preceding [the smell produced] elsewhere [i.e. in non-heat-produced cases], the prior absence of color, being different from that, is dispensable — this is the purport. 'Now, if thus' — the meaning is: by the description of the third type of dispensability in the form of 'when established elsewhere' and so forth. 'The word "invariable" is purposeless' — when, in the definition of cause as 'what invariably precedes the effect,' only 'what precedes the effect' is stated, then a donkey, which by chance is also present before the production of a pot, would also have the property of preceding the pot, and hence would have the unwanted consequence of being a cause of the pot. To prevent that, the word 'invariable' is introduced. But when it is introduced,

children.text:
ghaṭavyāpakatvaṃ rāsabhe
nāstīti nātivyāptiḥ/ paraṃ tu tadghaṭādanyasmin ghaṭāntare
kḷptaniyatapūrvavartibhiḥ daṇḍacakrādibhireva tadaghaṭasyāpi sambhave
tadbhinnarāsabhasyānyathāsiddhatvāt ananyathāsiddhatvadalenaiva
rāsabhavāvaṇasambhavāt niyatapadaṃ vyarthamiti śaṅkiturāśayaḥ/
satyantenaiveti/ ananyathāsiddhatve satītyanenaivetyarthaḥ/ samādhatte -
ghaṭasāmānyaṃ pratīti/ tadghaṭatvāvacchinnaṃ prati rāsabhasya
pūrvoktarītyā anyathāsiddhatve 'pi
children.translated_text: since the pervasion by pot is absent in the donkey, there is no over-extension. However, in another pot different from that pot, since the pot's production is possible through the very rod, wheel, and the like that are established as invariably preceding, and since the donkey, being different from them, is dispensable, [the donkey's] dispensability alone can handle the exclusion of the donkey — hence the word 'invariable' is purposeless. This is the doubter's intent. 'By the word "when there is" (<s>sati</s>) alone' — the meaning is: by the word 'when there is' within 'when there is non-dispensability.' He resolves — 'With respect to pot-hood in general' — even though the donkey is dispensable in the stated manner with respect to [the pot] delimited by that particular pot-hood,

children.text:
1. etat
pīlupākavādināṃ matamanusṛtya/ tanmate paramāṇugandhasyaiva
pākajanyatvāt dvyaṇukādyavayavigandhasya
avayavagatagandhajanyatvāṅgīkāreṇa apākajagandhapadena
dvyaṇukādigandhasya grahītuṃ śakyatvāt/ piṭharapākavādināṃ mate tu
avayavigandhasyāpi pākajanyatvāt apākajaḥ pārthivagandhaḥ aprasiddhaḥ/ jale
tu gandhasyaivābhāvāt apākajagandhapadena
jalīyagandhasyopādānāsaṃbhavāt/ tanmatānusādeṇa pākajarūpaṃ prati
gandhaprāgabhāvasya rasaprāgabhāvasya
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] This is according to the view of those who hold the <s>pīlupāka</s> (atomic transformation) theory. In their view, since only the smell of atoms is produced by heat-transformation, and since the smell of composites such as dyads and the like is accepted as produced by the smell of its parts, the term 'non-heat-produced smell' can grasp the smell of dyads and the like. But in the view of those who hold the <s>piṭharapāka</s> (whole-level transformation) theory, since even the smell of composites is produced by heat-transformation, non-heat-produced earthy smell is not well-known. And in water, since smell itself is absent, the term 'non-heat-produced smell' cannot grasp aqueous smell. Therefore, following that view,

children.text:
vā kāraṇatvaṃ bhavatu
iti śaṅkā, anyathāsiddhatvena samādhānaṃ ca vaktavyam/
children.translated_text: the doubt — let the prior absence of smell or the prior absence of taste be a cause of heat-produced color — and the resolution through dispensability should be stated.

children.text:
ghaṭatvāvacchinnaṃ
pratyanyathāsiddhatvaṃ na sambhavati/ tadā hi 'anyatra' ityasya
ghaṭatvāvacchinnāt anyasmin ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca ghaṭasāmānyabhinne
paṭādau kḷptaniyatapūrvavartibhiḥ tantavādibhiḥ ghaṭasyāsaṃbhavāt
anyathāsiddhalakṣaṇaṃ rāsabhe nāstīti ananyathāsiddhe
tatrātivyāptivāraṇāya niyatapadamāvaśyakamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: dispensability with respect to [the pot] delimited by pot-hood is not possible. For then, the meaning of 'elsewhere' is: in something other than what is delimited by pot-hood. And accordingly, since the production of a pot [in general] from the rod, wheel, and the like — which are established as invariably preceding in a cloth and the like that are different from pot-in-general — is impossible, the definition of dispensability does not apply to the donkey. Hence, for preventing the donkey from being considered non-dispensable, the word 'invariable' is necessary — this is the purport.

children.text:
trayāṇāmanyathāsiddhānāṃ
saṃgrāhakamekaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vadatāṃ navīnānāṃ matamāha - navīnāḥ
punariti/ laghu yat kāryaniyatapūrvavṛtti tata eva kāryakambhave
tadbhinnaṃ anyathāsiddham/ laghutvaṃ śarīrataḥ upasthityā sambandheneti
trividham/ pratyakṣaṃ prati anekadravyasamavetatvaṃ kāraṇaṃ vā mahattvaṃ
kāraṇaṃ veti sandehe anekadravyasamavetatvāpekṣayā śarīrato lāghavaṃ
mahattve astīti laghuniyatapūrvavṛttinā mahattvenaiva pratyakṣasambhave
tadbhinnaṃ anekasamavetatvaṃ anyathāsiddham/ ato na tatpratyakṣakāraṇam/
children.translated_text: He states the view of the moderns who formulate a single definition that encompasses all three types of dispensability — with 'the moderns, however' and so forth. What is light (<s>laghu</s>) and invariably precedes the effect — when the effect can arise from that alone, what is different from that is dispensable. Lightness (<s>laghutva</s>) is of three kinds: through body, through proximity (<s>upasthiti</s>), and through relation. Regarding whether the cause of perception is co-inherence in multiple substances or magnitude — in this doubt, since magnitude has lightness relative to the body compared to co-inherence in multiple substances, and since perception can arise from magnitude alone, which invariably precedes and is lighter, co-inherence in multiple substances, being different from it, is dispensable. Therefore it is not a cause of perception.

children.text:
gandhaṃ prati
gandhaprāgabhāvaḥ kāraṇaṃ vā rūpaprāgabhāvo vā iti sandehe
gandharūpapratiyoginyupasthite jhaṭiti gandhaprāgabhāva evopasthito
bhavati na rūpaprāgabhāva iti śīghropasthitirūpalāghavena gandhaprāgabhāva
eva kāraṇaṃ rūpaprāgabhāvastu anyathāsiddhaḥ/ evaṃ ghaṭaṃ prati daṇḍaḥ kāraṇaṃ
vā daṇḍatvadaṇḍarūpādikaṃ kāraṇaṃ vā iti sandehe
ubhayorniyatapūrvavṛttitve 'pi daṇḍasya saṃyogasaṃbandhena kāraṇatvam/
daṇḍatvadaṇḍarūpādīnāṃ tu svāśrayadaṇḍasaṃyogarūpaparamparāsambandhena
kāraṇatvamiti sambandhalāghavaṃ daṇḍa evāstīti tata eva ghaṭasambabhave
tadbhinnaṃ daṇḍatvadaṇḍarūpādikaṃ anyathāsiddhamityarthaḥ/
vyutpattivaicitryāyeti/ buddhivaiśadyāyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Regarding whether the cause of [heat-produced] smell is the prior absence of smell or the prior absence of color — in this doubt, when the counter-positive of smell and color is presented, the prior absence of smell is immediately presented to cognition, but the prior absence of color is not — thus, by the lightness in the form of quicker mental presentation, the prior absence of smell alone is the cause, while the prior absence of color is dispensable. Similarly, regarding whether the cause of a pot is the rod or rod-hood, rod-color, and the like — in this doubt, even though both invariably precede, the rod has causality through the contact relation, while rod-hood, rod-color, and the like have causality through the indirect chain-relation via the contact of the rod which is their substratum — hence lightness of relation exists only in the rod. Therefore, since the pot can arise from the rod alone, rod-hood, rod-color, and the like, being different from it, are dispensable — this is the meaning. 'For the diversity of understanding' — the meaning is: for the clarity of intellect.

children.text:
anugatasya
durvacatayeti/ laghutvasya śarīrakṛtasambandhakṛtādibhedena
nānārūpatayā anyathāsiddhatvaṃ ekamanugataṃ na śakyate vaktum/ evaṃ
laghutvavirodhigurutvasyāpi bhinnatayā tadbhinnamityasya
gurubhūtamityarthakatayā gurutvameva anyathāsiddhatvamiti paryavasānāt/
tasmāt yatra yatra prāmāṇikānāṃ anyathāsiddhatvavyavahāraḥ
tāvatpratiyogikabhedakūṭakavattvaṃ kāraṇalakṣaṇe niveśanīyam/ tatra
kāryāvyāpakāḥ ye anantāḥ rāsabhādayaḥ teṣāṃ
vyāpakatvārthakaniyatapadenaiva vāraṇasambhavāt tāvadbhedānāṃ
niveśaḥ anāvaśyakaḥ/ kāryavyāpakānāṃ daṇḍatvādīnāṃ tu bhedaḥ
kāraṇalakṣaṇe niveśanīya iti niyatapadaṃ ananyathāsiddhatvaṃ ca
kāraṇalakṣaṇe niveśitavato granthakārasyāśaya iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Because the common [element] is difficult to state' — since lightness takes various forms according to its types such as bodily, relational, and the like, a single common definition of dispensability cannot be stated. Similarly, since heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>), which is the opposite of lightness, also takes different forms, and since 'different from that' means 'heavier,' the conclusion is that heaviness itself constitutes dispensability. Therefore, wherever the authoritative scholars use the term 'dispensability,' the definition of cause should include the difference from the corresponding counter-positive aggregate up to that point. Among those, since the infinitely many donkeys and the like, which do not pervade the effect, can be excluded by the word 'invariable' alone, which has the meaning of 'pervading,' the inclusion of those differences is unnecessary. But the difference from effect-pervading entities such as rod-hood and the like must be included in the definition of cause — thus the intent of the author is that both the word 'invariable' and non-dispensability are included in the definition of cause. This is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: AnTs_39 kāryaṃ prāgabhāvapratiyogi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 39:] An effect (<s>kārya</s>) is the counter-positive of a prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>).

children.text: kāryaṃprāgabhāvapratiyogi/
children.translated_text: An effect is the counter-positive of a prior absence.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
kāryalakṣaṇamāha -
kāryamiti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of an effect — with 'effect' and so forth.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: kāraṇavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of Causes

children.text: AnTs_40 kāraṇaṃ trividhaṃ samavāyyasamavāyinimittabhedāt / yat samavetaṃ kāryam utpadyate tat samavāyikāraṇam / yathā tantavaḥ paṭasya paṭaś ca khagatarūpādeḥ / kāryeṇa kāraṇena vā sahaikasminn arthe samavetatve sati yat kāraṇaṃ tad asamavāyikāraṇam / yathā tantusaṃyogaḥ paṭasya tanturūpaṃ paṭarūpasya / tadubhayabhinnaṃ kāraṇaṃ nimittakāraṇam / yathā turīvemādikaṃ paṭasya /
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 40:] A cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) is threefold, due to the distinction of inherent cause (<s>samavāyi</s>), non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyi</s>), and efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>). That in which the effect arises as inhering is the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>). For example, the threads are the inherent cause of the cloth, and the cloth is the inherent cause of the color and the rest residing in it. The cause that inheres in the same entity together with either the effect or the [inherent] cause is the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>). For example, the conjunction of threads is the non-inherent cause of the cloth, and the color of the thread is the non-inherent cause of the color of the cloth. A cause different from both of those is the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>). For example, the loom, shuttle, and the like are the efficient cause of the cloth.

children.text:
kāraṇaṃ trividham -
samavāyi-asamavāyi-nimittabhedāt/ yatsamavetaṃ kāryamutpadyate
tatsamavāyikāraṇam/ yathā
children.translated_text: A cause is threefold — due to the distinction of inherent, non-inherent, and efficient. That in which the effect arises as inhering is the inherent cause. For example,

children.text:
tantavaḥ paṭasya, paṭaśca
svagatarūpādeḥ/ kāryeṇa kāraṇena vā saha ekasmin arthe samavetaṃ
satkāraṇaṃ asamavāyikāraṇam/ yathā tantusaṃyogaḥ paṭasya, tanturūpaṃ
paṭagatarūpasya ca/ tadubhayabhinnaṃ kāraṇaṃ nimittakāraṇam/ yathā
turīvemādikaṃ paṭasya/
children.translated_text: the threads are [the inherent cause] of the cloth, and the cloth is [the inherent cause] of the color and the rest residing in it. The cause that inheres in the same entity together with either the effect or the [inherent] cause is the non-inherent cause. For example, the conjunction of threads is [the non-inherent cause] of the cloth, and the color of the thread is [the non-inherent cause] of the color residing in the cloth. A cause different from both of those is the efficient cause. For example, the loom, shuttle, and the like are [the efficient cause] of the cloth.

children.text: AnTs_41 tad etattrividhakāraṇamadhye yad asādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ tad eva karaṇam //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 41:] Among these three types of causes, the uncommon cause (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) alone is the instrumental cause (<s>karaṇa</s>).

children.text: tadetattrividhakāraṇamadhye yadasādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadeva kāraṇam/
children.translated_text: Among these three types of causes, the uncommon cause alone is the instrumental cause.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
kāraṇaṃ vibhajate -
kāraṇamiti/ samavāyikāraṇasya lakṣaṇamāha - yatsamavetamiti/ yasmin
samavetamityarthaḥ/ asamavāyikāraṇaṃ lakṣayatikāryeṇeti/ 'kāryeṇa'
ityetadudāharati - tantusaṃyoga iti/ kāryeṇa paṭena saha
ekasmin tantau samavetatvāt tantusaṃyogaḥ
paṭasyāsamavāyikāraṇamityarthaḥ/ 'kāraṇena' ityetat udāharati -
tanturūpamiti/ kāraṇena paṭena saha ekasmin tantau samavetatvāt
tanturūpaṃ paṭarūpasyāsamavāyikāraṇamityarthaḥ/ nimittakāraṇaṃ lakṣayati
- tadubhayeti/ samavāyyasamavāyibhinnakāraṇaṃ nimittakāraṇamityarthaḥ/
kāraṇalakṣaṇamupasaṃharati - tadetaditi/
children.translated_text: He divides the cause — with 'cause' and so forth. He states the definition of the inherent cause — with 'that in which it inheres.' The meaning is: that in which [the effect] inheres. He defines the non-inherent cause — with 'with the effect' and so forth. He exemplifies the [clause] 'with the effect' — with 'conjunction of threads.' Since thread-conjunction inheres in the same entity, namely the thread, together with the effect, namely the cloth, the conjunction of threads is the non-inherent cause of the cloth — this is the meaning. He exemplifies the [clause] 'with the cause' — with 'color of the thread.' Since the color of the thread inheres in the same entity, namely the thread, together with the [inherent] cause, namely the cloth [i.e. the cloth's inherent cause, the thread], the color of the thread is the non-inherent cause of the color of the cloth — this is the meaning. He defines the efficient cause — with 'different from both.' The meaning is: a cause different from both the inherent and non-inherent causes is the efficient cause. He concludes the definition of the instrumental cause — with 'among these.'

children.text: prākāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
yasmin
samavetamityartha iti/ yaddharmāvacchinnaṃ yaddharmāvacchinne
samavāyenotpadyate, taddharmāvacchinnaṃ prati taddharmāvacchinnaṃ
samavāyikāraṇamiti paramārthaḥ/ kāraṇena paṭeneti/
svakārya-samavāyikāraṇena paṭena ityarthaḥ/ svaṃ tanturūpam/
paṭādikaṃ prati turītantusaṃyogādīnāṃ asamavāyikāraṇatvavāraṇāya
tattadasamavāyikāraṇalakṣaṇe tattadbhinnatvaṃ deyamiti dik/
children.translated_text: 'The meaning is: that in which it inheres' — the ultimate meaning is: that which, delimited by a certain property, produces through inherence what is delimited by a certain property — that, as delimited by that property, is the inherent cause of what is delimited by that property. 'With the [inherent] cause, namely the cloth' — the meaning is: with the cloth, which is the inherent cause of its own effect. 'Own' refers to the color of the thread. To prevent the conjunction of the loom and thread and the like from being non-inherent causes of cloth and the like, the qualification 'different from such-and-such' should be given in each respective definition of the non-inherent cause — this is the indication.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
yaddharmāvacchinnamiti/ samavāyasambandhāvacchinnaghaṭatvāvacchinna -
kāryatānirūpita-tādātmyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatvaṃ
ghaṭasamavāyikāraṇasya lakṣaṇam/ samavāyena kāryasāmānyaṃ prati
tādātmyena dravyaṃ kāraṇamiti sāmānyakāryakāraṇabhāvo 'prāmāṇika
ityabhipretyaivamuktam/ tādṛśakāryaṅkāraṇabhāvasya prāmāṇikatve tu
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnakāryatānirūpita-tādātmyasambandhāvacchinna-kāraṇatvamamiti
sāmānyalakṣaṇamapi bhavitumarhati/ kāryatāyāṃ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvāniveśe viṣayatāsambandhena ghaṭapratyakṣaṃ prati
tādātmyasambandhena ghaṭasyanimittakāraṇatayā
children.translated_text: 'Delimited by whatever property' — the definition of the inherent cause of a pot is: causality delimited by the relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), which determines the effect-hood delimited by pot-hood delimited by the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). [The author] said this with the understanding that the general causal relation — that substance is a cause through the relation of identity for a product in general through inherence — is not established by valid knowledge. However, if such a general causal relation is established by valid knowledge, then the general definition could also be: causality delimited by the relation of identity, which determines the effect-hood delimited by the relation of inherence. If the delimitation by the relation of inherence is not incorporated in the effect-hood, then since the pot is an efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>) through the relation of identity for the perception of the pot through the object-relation (<s>viṣayatā</s>),

children.text:
viṣayatāsambandhāvacchinna-
ghaṭapratyakṣaniṣṭhakāryantānirūpita-tādātmyasambandhāvacchinna-kāraṇatāvati
ghaṭe ativyāptiḥ ataḥ tanniveśaḥ/ kāraṇatāyāṃ
tādātmyasambandhāvacchiṃnnatvāniveśe samavāyasambandhena ghaṭaṃ prati
kapālasaṃyogasya samavāyasambandhena kāraṇatayā
samavāyasambandhāvacchinna-ghaṭaniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatāvati
ghaṭāsamavāyikāraṇe kapāladvayasaṃyoge ativyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
tanniveśaḥ/ evaṃ samavāyasambandhāvacchinna -
kāryatānirūpita-samavāya-svasamavāyisamavetatvānyatarasambandhavacchinnakāraṇatvaṃ
asamavāyikāraṇatvam/ tatra kāryatāyāṃ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvāniveśe viṣayatāsambandhāvacchinna -
ghaṭapratyakṣaniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitāsamavāyasambandhāvacchinna -
nimittakāraṇatāvati ghaṭarūpe ativyāptiḥ/ kāraṇatāyāṃ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvāniveśe
tādātmyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatāvati samavāyikāraṇe 'tivyāptiḥ/
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvamātrasya kāraṇatāyāṃ niveśe paṭarūpaṃ
pratyasamavāyikāraṇe tanturūpe 'vyāptiḥ/ samavāyena paṭarūpaṃ prati
tanturūpasya samavāyena akāraṇatvāt/ ataḥ
svasamavāyisamavetatvasambandhāvacchinnatvaniveśaḥ/ tāvanmātraniveśe
paṭaṃ prati asamavāyikāraṇe tantusaṃyoge 'vyāptiḥ/ ataḥ
anyatarasambandhaniveśaḥ/ adhikamanyatra/
children.translated_text: there would be over-extension to the pot itself, which possesses causality delimited by the relation of identity determining the effect-hood residing in pot-perception delimited by the object-relation — hence that incorporation [is needed]. If the delimitation by the relation of identity is not incorporated in the causality, then since the conjunction of potsherds is a cause through the relation of inherence for the pot through the relation of inherence, there would be over-extension to the conjunction of two potsherds, which is the non-inherent cause of the pot and possesses causality delimited by the relation of inherence determining the pot-residing effect-hood delimited by the relation of inherence. To avert that, that incorporation [is needed]. Similarly, the definition of non-inherent-cause-hood (<s>asamavāyikāraṇatva</s>) is: causality delimited by the relation of inherence or the relation of being-co-inhered-in-one's-own-co-inherent (<s>svasamavāyisamavetatva</s>), which determines the effect-hood delimited by the relation of inherence. In that [definition], if the delimitation by the relation of inherence is not incorporated in the effect-hood, there would be over-extension to the form of the pot, which possesses efficient-cause-hood delimited by the non-inherence relation for the perception of the pot through the object-relation. If the delimitation by the relation of inherence is not incorporated in the causality, there would be over-extension to the inherent cause, which possesses causality delimited by the relation of identity. If only the delimitation by the relation of inherence is incorporated in the causality, there would be under-extension in thread-color, which is the non-inherent cause for cloth-color — because thread-color is not a cause of cloth-color through inherence. Hence the incorporation of the relation of being-co-inhered-in-one's-own-co-inherent. If only that much is incorporated, there would be under-extension in thread-conjunction, which is the non-inherent cause for cloth. Hence the incorporation of 'either relation.' Further details [should be pursued] elsewhere.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: pratyakṣalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of Perception (<s>Pratyakṣa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_42 tatra pratyakṣajñānakaraṇaṃ pratyakṣam / indriyārthasannikarṣajanyaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam /tad dvividhaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ savikalpakaṃ ceti / tatra nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ yathedaṃ kiṃcit / saparakārakaṃ jñānaṃ savikalpakaṃ yathā ḍittho'yam brahmaṇo'yaṃ śyāmo'yam iti //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 42:] Among these, the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) of perceptual knowledge is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). Knowledge produced from the contact of the sense-organ with the object is perception. It is twofold: indeterminate (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) and determinate (<s>savikalpaka</s>). Indeterminate knowledge is [that which cognizes] 'this is something' — without a qualifier-mode. Knowledge with a qualifier-mode is determinate — as in 'This is <s>Ḍittha</s>,' 'This is a Brahmin,' 'This is dark.'

children.text:
tatra
pratyakṣajñānakaraṇaṃ pratyakṣam/ indriyārthasannikarṣajanyaṃ jñānaṃ
pratyakṣam/
children.translated_text: Among these, the instrument of perceptual knowledge is <s>pratyakṣa</s>. Knowledge produced from the contact of the sense-organ with the object is perception.

children.text: tadvibhāga
children.translated_text: Division of Perception

children.text:
taddvividham -
nirvakalpakaṃ savikalpakaṃ ceti/ niṣprakārakaṃ jñānaṃ nirvikalpakam/
saprakārakaṃ jñānaṃ savikalpakam/ yathā 'ḍitthaḥ ayam', 'brāhmaṇaḥ ayam',
'śyāmaḥ ayam', 'pācakaḥ ayam' iti/
children.translated_text: It is twofold: indeterminate (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) and determinate (<s>savikalpaka</s>). Knowledge without a qualifier-mode is indeterminate. Knowledge with a qualifier-mode is determinate — as in 'This is <s>Ḍittha</s>,' 'This is a Brahmin,' 'This is dark,' 'This is a cook.'

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
pratyakṣapramāṇalakṣaṇamāha - tatreti/ pramāṇacatuṣṭayamadhya
ityarthaḥḥ/ pratyakṣajñānasya lakṣaṇamāha - indriyeti/ indriyaṃ
cakṣurādikam, arthaḥ ghaṭādiḥ, tayossaṃnikarṣaḥ saṃyogādiḥ, tajjanyaṃ
jñānamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of the means of valid knowledge called perception — with 'among these.' The meaning is: among the four means of valid knowledge. He states the definition of perceptual knowledge — with 'sense-organ' (<s>indriya</s>). The sense-organ is the eye and the like; the object (<s>artha</s>) is the pot and the like; the contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>) of these two is conjunction and the like; the meaning is: knowledge produced from that.

children.text:
tadvibhajate -
taddvividhamiti/ nirvikalpakasya lakṣaṇamāha - niṣprakārakamiti/
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasambandhānavagāhi jñānamityarthaḥ/ nanu nirvikalpake kiṃ
pramāṇamiti cet - na/ 'gauḥ' iti viśiṣṭajñānaṃ
viśeṣaṇajñānajanyaṃ, viśiṣṭajñānatvāt daṇḍīti jñānavat
ityanumānasya pramāṇatvāt/ viśeṣaṇajñānasyāpi savikalpakatve
anavasthāprasaṅgāt nirvikalpakasiddhiḥ/ savikalpakaṃ lakṣayati -
saprakārakamiti/ nāmajātyādiviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasambandhāvagāhi
jñānamityarthaḥ/ savikalpakamudāharati - yatheti/
children.translated_text: He divides it — with 'It is twofold.' He states the definition of indeterminate [perception] — with 'without qualifier-mode.' The meaning is: knowledge that does not apprehend the relation of qualifier and qualificand. Now, what is the means of valid knowledge for indeterminate [perception]? — if thus asked: no [defect]. Because the inference 'The cognition "[This is] a cow" is a qualified cognition produced by the cognition of the qualifier, because it is a qualified cognition, like the cognition "[this is] a man with a stick"' — this inference serves as the means of valid knowledge. If the cognition of the qualifier were also determinate, there would be an infinite regress — hence the establishment of indeterminate [perception]. He defines determinate [perception] — with 'with qualifier-mode.' The meaning is: knowledge that apprehends the relation of qualifier and qualificand, such as name, universal, and the like. He illustrates determinate [perception] — with 'as in.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanu
turīyaviṣayatānirūpakasya nirvikalpakajñānaspa nirūpakatāsambandhena
prakāratāśūnyatvamiva viśeṣyatāśūnyatvaṃ saṃsargatāśūnyatvamapi
lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati, vinigamanāvirahāt ityataḥ lakṣaṇatrayaṃ darśayati
-viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyeti/ viśeṣyādividhyā
viśeṣyādyanavagāhijñānamityarthaḥ/ tathā ca jñānatvaghaṭitaṃ
viśeṣyatāśūnyatvam, viśeṣaṇatāśūnyatvaṃ saṃsargatāśūnyatvaṃ ceti
lakṣaṇatrayaṃ paryavasitamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, since indeterminate knowledge, which determines a fourth type of object-relation [beyond qualifier-mode-hood, qualificand-hood, and relational-hood], is equally devoid of qualificand-hood and relational-hood as it is of qualifier-mode-hood, and since there is no way to select among them, there could be three possible definitions — hence he presents the three definitions with: 'qualifier, qualificand' etc. The meaning is: knowledge that does not apprehend qualificand-hood and the rest, in the manner of qualificand-hood and the rest. And accordingly, the three definitions that result, composed of knowledge-hood, are: devoid of qualificand-hood, devoid of qualifier-hood, and devoid of relational-hood — this is the purport.

children.text:
kecittu - nanu
niṣprakārakatvaṃ prakāratāśūnyatvam/ prakāratā ca
bhāsamānavaiśiṣṭyapratiyogitvam/ saṃsargāvacchinnaviṣayateti yāvat
tathā ca saṃsargānavagāhijñānatvameva saṃsargatāśūnyajñānatvena vā
lakṣaṇamāstāṃ lāghavādityataḥ tathaiva
mūlārthamāha-viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyetīnti-ityāhuḥ/ taccintyam -
siddhānte saṃsargatāyā iva prakāratāyā api
vilakṣaṇaviṣayatātmakatvena niṣprakārakatvarūpalakṣaṇe
gauravānavakāśāditi dik/
children.translated_text: Some, however, [say]: Now, 'devoid of qualifier-mode' means devoid of qualifier-mode-hood. Qualifier-mode-hood is counter-positive-ness of appearing qualification, i.e. relation-delimited object-relation. And accordingly, let the definition be knowledge-hood that does not apprehend the relation, or alternatively that is devoid of relational-hood — since this would be more parsimonious. Hence the root text meaning is explained as 'qualifier-qualificand' etc. — they say. That is to be reconsidered — because in the established view, since qualifier-mode-hood, like relational-hood, has the nature of a distinct kind of object-relation, there is no scope for prolixity in the definition in the form of devoid-of-qualifier-mode-hood. This is the indication.

children.text:
nirvikalpakajñānasya
atīndriyatayā tatra pratyakṣapramāṇāsambhavāt anumānaṃ pramāṇayati -
gauriti/ viśiṣṭajñānatvāditi/ viśiṣṭabuddhiṃ prati viśeṣaṇajñānasya
kāraṇatvāt nāprayojakatāśaṅketi bhāvaḥ/ anavasthāprasaṅgāditi/
savikalpakasya viśiṣṭabuddhitvena viśeṣaṇajñānajanyatvaniyamāditi
bhāvaḥ/ viśeṣaṇaviśeśyasambandhāvagāhīti/ atrāpyuktarītyā lakṣaṇatrayaṃ
bodhyam/
children.translated_text: Since indeterminate knowledge is super-sensory and hence perception cannot serve as the means of valid knowledge for it, he validates it through inference — with 'a cow.'
