'Because it is a qualified cognition' — since the cognition of the qualifier is a cause for the qualified cognition, there is no doubt about purposelessness — this is the purport. 'Because of the consequence of infinite regress' — the purport is: because a determinate cognition, being a qualified cognition, is necessarily produced by the cognition of the qualifier. 'Apprehending the relation of qualifier and qualificand' — here too, the three definitions should be understood in the manner stated.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
turīyaviṣayatānirūpakasyeti/ prakāratā -
viśeṣyatā saṃsargatātrayātiriktacaturthaviṣayatānirūpakasyetyarthaḥ/
viśeṣyādividhayeti/ viśeṣyatvādiprakāreṇetyarthaḥ/ nirvikalpake
ghaṭaḥ ghaṭatvaṃ sambandhaśca bhāsate/ parantu viśeṣyatvaṃ -
viśeṣaṇatva-saṃsargatvaiḥ ghaṭādikaṃ na bhāsate/ tathā ca mūle
prakāraśabdaḥ viśeṣyatva-viśeṣaṇatva-saṃsargatvarūpaprakāraparaḥ/
niṣprakārakamityasya tādṛśaviśeṣyatvādiprakāraśūnyamityartha iti
bhāvāḥ/ atrāpyuktarītyā lakṣaṇatrayamiti/ prakāratānirūpakatvaṃ
viśeṣyatānirūpakatvaṃ saṃsargatānirūpakatvamiti lakṣaṇatrayamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Determining a fourth object-relation' — the meaning is: determining a fourth object-relation beyond the three, namely qualifier-mode-hood, qualificand-hood, and relational-hood. 'In the manner of qualificand-hood and the rest' — the meaning is: in the form of qualificand-hood and the rest. In indeterminate [perception], the pot, pot-hood, and the relation all appear. However, the pot does not appear as having qualificand-hood, qualifier-hood, or relational-hood. And accordingly, the word 'qualifier-mode' in the root text refers to the qualifier-mode in the form of qualificand-hood, qualifier-hood, and relational-hood. The meaning of 'devoid of qualifier-mode' is: devoid of such qualifier-mode in the form of qualificand-hood and the rest — this is the purport. 'Here too, the three definitions should be understood in the manner stated' — the meaning is: the three definitions are: being the determiner of qualifier-mode-hood, being the determiner of qualificand-hood, and being the determiner of relational-hood.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: sannikarṣavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of Sense-Object Contact (<s>Sannikarṣa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_43 pratyakṣajñānahetur indriyārthasannikarṣaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / saṃyogaḥ saṃyuktasamavāyaḥ saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyaḥ samavāyaḥ samavetasamavāyo viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaś ceti / cakṣuṣā ghaṭapratyakṣajanane saṃyogaḥ sannikarṣaḥ / ghaṭarūpapratyakṣajanane saṃyuktasamavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ cakṣuḥsaṃyukte ghaṭe rūpasya samavāyāt / rūpatvasāmānyapratyakṣe saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ cakṣuḥsaṃyukte ghaṭe rūpaṃ samavetaṃ tatra rūpatvasya samavāyāt / śrotreṇa śabdasyākāśaguṇatvāt guṇaguṇinoś ca samavāyāt / śabdatvasākṣātkāre samavetasamavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ śrotrasamavete śabde śabdatvasya samavāyāt / abhāvaparatyakṣe viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ sannikarṣo ghaṭābhāvavad bhṛtalam ity atra cakṣuḥsaṃyukte bhūtale ghaṭābhāvasya viśeṣaṇatvāt / evaṃ snnikarṣaṣaṭkajanyaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam / tatkaraṇam indriyam / tasmād indriyaṃ pratyakṣapramāṇam iti siddham //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 43:] The cause of perceptual knowledge, the contact of the sense-organ with the object, is sixfold: conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence in what is conjoined (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>), inherence in what inheres in what is conjoined (<s>saṃyuktasamavetasamavāya</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), inherence in what inheres (<s>samavetasamavāya</s>), and the qualifier-qualificand relation (<s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s>). In the perceptual generation of a pot by the eye, conjunction is the contact. In the perception of the form of a pot, inherence-in-what-is-conjoined is the contact — because form inheres in the pot which is conjoined with the eye. In the perception of the universal form-hood, inherence-in-what-inheres-in-what-is-conjoined is the contact — because in the pot conjoined with the eye, form inheres, and form-hood inheres in that [form]. In the direct apprehension of sound by the ear, inherence is the contact — because the <s>ākāśa</s> existing in the cavity of the ear is the ear; because sound is a quality of <s>ākāśa</s>; and because quality and quality-bearer are related by inherence. In the direct apprehension of sound-hood, inherence-in-what-inheres is the contact — because sound-hood inheres in the sound that inheres in the ear. In the perception of absence, the qualifier-qualificand relation is the contact — because in 'the ground possesses the absence of a pot,' the absence of a pot is a qualifier of the ground which is conjoined with the eye.

children.text:
pratyakṣajñānahetuḥ
indriyārthasannikarṣaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ/ saṃyogaḥ, saṃyuktasamavāyaḥ,
saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyaḥ, samavāyaḥ, samavetasamavāyaḥ,
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaśceti/ cakṣuṣā ghaṭapratyakṣajanane saṃyogaḥ
sannikarṣaḥ/ ghaṭarūpapratyakṣe saṃyuktasamavāyaḥ/ cakṣussaṃyukte ghaṭe rūpasya
samavāyāt/ rūpatvasāmānyapratyakṣe saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyaḥ/
cakṣussaṃyukte ghaṭe rūpaṃ samavetam/ tatra rūpatvasrū samavāyāt/
śrotreṇa śabdasākṣātkāre samavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ/ karṇavivaravṛttyākāśasya
kṣotratvāt/ śabdasya ākāśaguṇatvāt/ guṇaguṇinoḥ samavāyāt/
śabdatvasākṣātkāre samavetasamavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ/ śrotrasamavete śabde
śabdatvasya samavāyāt/ abhāvapratyakṣe viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ sannikarṣaḥ/
bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat ityatra cakṣussaṃyukte bhūtale ghaṭābhāvasya
viśeṣaṇatvāt/
children.translated_text: The cause of perceptual knowledge, the contact of the sense-organ with the object, is sixfold: conjunction, inherence-in-what-is-conjoined, inherence-in-what-inheres-in-what-is-conjoined, inherence, inherence-in-what-inheres, and the qualifier-qualificand relation. In the perceptual generation of a pot by the eye, conjunction is the contact. In the perception of the form of a pot, inherence-in-what-is-conjoined — because form inheres in the pot conjoined with the eye. In the perception of the universal form-hood, inherence-in-what-inheres-in-what-is-conjoined — because in the pot conjoined with the eye, form inheres, and form-hood inheres in that. In the direct apprehension of sound by the ear, inherence is the contact — because the <s>ākāśa</s> existing in the cavity of the ear is the ear; because sound is a quality of <s>ākāśa</s>; and because quality and quality-bearer are related by inherence. In the direct apprehension of sound-hood, inherence-in-what-inheres is the contact — because sound-hood inheres in the sound that inheres in the ear. In the perception of absence, the qualifier-qualificand relation is the contact — because in 'the ground possesses the absence of a pot,' the absence of a pot is a qualifier of the ground conjoined with the eye.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
indriyārthaṃsannikarṣaṃ vibhajate -
pratyakṣeti/ saṃyogasannikarṣamudāharati - cakṣuṣeti/ dravyapratyakṣe
sarvatra saṃyogaḥ sannikarṣaḥ/ ātmā manasā saṃyujyate, mana indriyeṇa,
indriyamarthena tataḥ pratyakṣajñānamutpadyate ityarthaḥ/
saṃyuktasamavāyamudāharati - ghaṭarūpeti/ tatra yuktimāha - cakṣussaṃyukta
iti/ saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyamudāharati -
children.translated_text: He divides the contact of the sense-organ with the object — with 'perception.' He illustrates the contact of conjunction — with 'by the eye.' In the perception of substance, conjunction is the contact everywhere. The self is conjoined with mind (<s>manas</s>), mind with the sense-organ, and the sense-organ with the object — then perceptual knowledge arises. This is the meaning. He illustrates inherence-in-what-is-conjoined — with 'the form of the pot.' There he states the rationale — with 'conjoined with the eye.' He illustrates inherence-in-what-inheres-in-what-is-conjoined —

children.text:
rūpatveti/
samavāyamudāharati - śrotreṇeti/ tadupapādayati - karṇeti/ nana
dūrasthaśabdasya kathaṃ śrotrasambandha iti cet - na/
vīcītaraṅgnyāyena kadambamukulanyāyena vā śabdāt
śabdāntarotpattikrameṇa śrotradeśe jātasya śrotreṇa sambandhāt
pratyakṣatvasambhavāt/ samavetasamapāyamudāharati - śabdatveti/
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvamudāharati - abhāveti/ tadupapādayati -
ghaṭābhāvavaditi/ bhūtalaṃ viśeṣyam, ghaṭābhāvo viśeṣaṇam/ bhūtale
ghaṭo nāstītyatra abhāvasya viśeṣyatvaṃ draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: with 'form-hood.' He illustrates inherence — with 'by the ear.' He explains it — with 'the cavity of the ear.' Now, how can a distant sound be connected with the ear? — if thus asked: no [defect]. Because, through the principle of wave-propagation (<s>vīcītaraṅganyāya</s>) or the principle of the <s>kadamba</s>-bud (<s>kadambamukulanyāya</s>), by the successive production of one sound from another, the sound that has arisen in the region of the ear is connected with the ear — hence the possibility of perceptibility. He illustrates inherence-in-what-inheres — with 'sound-hood.' He illustrates the qualifier-qualificand relation — with 'absence.' He explains it — with 'possessing the absence of a pot.' The ground is the qualificand; the absence of a pot is the qualifier. In [the cognition] 'there is no pot on the ground,' the qualificand-hood of absence should be understood.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mana
indriyeṇeti/ saṃyujyate ityanenānvayaḥ/ evamagre 'pi/
ātmapratyakṣasaṅgrahastu ātmā manasā saṃyujyate, tataḥ pratyakṣajñānaṃ
utpadyate iti yojanāntareṇa/ kathaṃ śrotrasambandha iti/ na ca
śrotrasya nabhorūpatvena tatsamavāyaḥ dūrasthaśabde 'pyakṣata iti
śaṅkyam/ atiprasaṅgabhaṅgāya
karṇavivarāvacchinnanabho 'nuyogikatvaviśiṣṭasamavāyasyaiva
pratyakṣahetutvāṅgīkāreṇa tādṛśasambandhasya dūrasthaśabde 'bhāvāditi
bhāvaḥ/ prathamataḥ bherīdaṇḍasaṃyogena nabhasi śabda utpadyate, tena śabdāḥ,
taiśca punaḥ śabdāḥ ityevaṃ krameṇa nikhiladigavacchedena
śabdotpatteraṅgīkaraṇīyatayā tadaṃśe 'pi sāmyanirvāhāya āha -
kadamveti/ draṣṭavyamiti/
children.translated_text: [The word] '<s>mana</s>' [connects with] 'by the sense-organ' — the syntactic connection is with 'is conjoined.' Similarly for what follows. As for the inclusion of self-perception (<s>ātmapratyakṣa</s>), the self is conjoined with the mind (<s>manas</s>), and from that, perceptual cognition arises — this is through an alternative construal. [The question is:] how is the connection with the auditory organ [established]? Nor should it be objected that since the auditory organ has the nature of ether (<s>nabhas</s>), its inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) [with sound] would make even distant sounds perceptible — because, to prevent over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>), only the inherence qualified by counter-positive-hood delimited by the ether enclosed in the ear-cavity (<s>karṇavivara</s>) is accepted as the cause of perception, and such a relation is absent with respect to distant sounds — this is the purport. First, by the conjunction of the drum-stick with the drum, a sound is produced in ether; from that sound [arise further] sounds, and from those again [more] sounds — thus, in succession, since the production of sound extending in all directions must be accepted, to maintain consistency in that respect too, he says '<s>kadamba</s>' etc. '[This] should be seen' —

children.text:
atredamavadheyam -
viśeṣaṇatānāṃ saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatāvādirūpeṇa bahuvidhatve 'pi
viśeṣaṇatātvenaiva parigaṇanāt ca ṣaḍvidhatvahāniḥ/ na caivaṃ
samavāyatvenaiva saṃyuktasamavāyādīnāmanugamaḥ kuto na kṛta iti
vācyam; svatantrecchasyetyādinyāyānusāreṇa adoṣāditi/
children.translated_text: Here this should be noted: although qualifier-hoods (<s>viśeṣaṇatā</s>) are of many kinds in the form of conjoined-qualifier-hood (<s>saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatā</s>) and so forth, there is no loss of the sixfold classification, because [they are all] enumerated under the single category of qualifier-hood-ness (<s>viśeṣaṇatātva</s>). Nor should it be said: why was the same subsumption not done for conjoined-inherence etc. under the single category of inherence-ness (<s>samavāyatva</s>)? Because there is no fault in this, in accordance with the maxim 'according to the independent will [of the sage]' (<s>svatantrecchasyetyādi</s>).

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
evamagre 'pīti/
'indriyamarthena' ityasyāpi 'saṃyujyata' ityanenānvaya iti
bhāvaḥ/ atiprasaṅgabhaṅgāteti/ sarveṣāmapi śabdānāṃ
pratyakṣaprasaṅgavāraṇāyetyarthaḥ/ tathā ādyavīcī samīpadeśe
taraṅgāntaraṃ janayati tattaraṅgaḥ samīpadeśe taraṅgāntaraṃ
janayati, evaṃ bheryādyasamavāyikāraṇakādyaśabdo 'pi
samīpadeśāvacchedena śabdāntaraṃ janayati, so 'pi śabdaḥ
svasannihitadeśāvacchedena śabdāntaraṃ janayatīti rītyā
karṇavivarāvacchedena utpannaśabdo gṛhyate iti vīcītaraṅganyāyena
śabdotpattikramaḥ/ yathā prathamataḥ utpannaṃ kadambamukulaṃ
sarvadigavacchedena evadaivānekamukulāni janayati eva
children.translated_text: 'Similarly for what follows' — the syntactic connection of 'the sense-organ with the object' (<s>indriyam arthena</s>) is also with 'is conjoined' — this is the purport. 'To prevent over-extension' — the meaning is: for the purpose of blocking the absurd consequence that all sounds would be perceptible. Just as the first wave generates another wave in the adjacent region, and that wave generates yet another wave in the adjacent region, similarly the initial sound produced by the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) such as the drum etc. generates another sound delimited by the adjacent region, and that sound too generates yet another sound delimited by the region proximate to it — in this manner, the sound produced delimited by the ear-cavity is apprehended — this is the sequence of sound-production according to the maxim of wave-propagation (<s>vīcītaraṅganyāya</s>). Just as a bud that has first arisen simultaneously generates many buds in all directions,

children.text:
bheyādyākāśasaṃyāgāsamavāyikāraṇakādyaśabdo 'pi
sarvadigavacchedena adhikaśabdān janayatīti/ paraṃ tu yaddigabhimukho
vāyuḥ taddigavacchedena adhikaśabdān janayatīti kadambamukulanyāyena
śabdotpattikrama iti nṛsiṃhaprakāśikākārāḥ prāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: so too the initial sound produced by the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) such as the conjunction with the ether of a drum etc. generates additional sounds extending in all directions. However, in the direction toward which the wind blows, it generates more sounds in that direction — this is the sequence of sound-production according to the maxim of the <s>kadamba</s> flower-bud (<s>kadambamukulanyāya</s>), as stated by the authors of the <s>Nṛsiṃhaprakāśikā</s>.

children.text:
atredamavadheyamityādi/
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo nāma naikaḥ sannikarṣaḥ/ api tu viśeṣaṇatvaṃ
viśeṣyatvaṃ ceti sambandhadvayam/ tatrābhāvaviśeṣaṇakapratyakṣe
viśeṣaṇatvaṃ saṃnikarṣaḥ/ abhāvaviśeṣyakapratyakṣe viśeṣyatvaṃ
saṃnikarṣaḥ/ viśeṣaṇatvaṃ pañcavidham saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatvam,
saṃyuktasamavetaviśeṣaṇatvam, saṃyuktasamavetasamavetaviśeṣaṇatvam,
samavetaviśeṣaṇatvam, samavetasamavetaviśeṣaṇatvam ceti/ evaṃ
viśeśyatvamapi saṃyuktaviśeṣyatvam, saṃyuktasamavetaviśeṣyatvam,
saṃyuktasamavetasamavetaviśeṣyatvame, samavetaviśeṣyatvam,
samavetasamavetaviśeṣyatvam ceti pañcavidham/ āhatya
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo daśavidha iti nyāyabhūṣaṇe pratyapādi/
children.translated_text: 'Here this should be noted' etc. The qualifier-qualificand relation (<s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s>) is not a single sense-contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>), but rather two relations: qualifier-hood (<s>viśeṣaṇatva</s>) and qualificand-hood (<s>viśeṣyatva</s>). Of these, in the perception of something qualified by an absence, qualifier-hood is the sense-contact; in the perception of something that is the qualificand of an absence, qualificand-hood is the sense-contact. Qualifier-hood is fivefold: conjoined-qualifier-hood (<s>saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatva</s>), conjoined-inherent-qualifier-hood (<s>saṃyuktasamavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s>), conjoined-inherent-of-the-inherent-qualifier-hood (<s>saṃyuktasamavetasamavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s>), inherent-qualifier-hood (<s>samavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s>), and inherent-of-the-inherent-qualifier-hood (<s>samavetasamavetaviśeṣaṇatva</s>). Similarly, qualificand-hood is also fivefold: conjoined-qualificand-hood, conjoined-inherent-qualificand-hood, conjoined-inherent-of-the-inherent-qualificand-hood, inherent-qualificand-hood, and inherent-of-the-inherent-qualificand-hood. In total, the qualifier-qualificand relation is tenfold — thus it was established in the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s>.

children.text:
teṣāṃ krameṇa
udāharaṇāni - 1bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat, 2toyasparśaḥ uṣṇatvābhāvavān,
3nīlatvaṃ śuklatvābhāvavat,
children.translated_text: The examples of these in order are: (1) the ground-surface possesses the absence of a pot, (2) the touch of water possesses the absence of heat,  (3) blue-ness possesses the absence of white-ness,

children.text:
4vīṇāśabdaḥ
tīvratvābhāvavān, 5śabdatvaṃ bhedābhāvavat, 6bhūtale ghaṭābhāvaḥ,
7toyasparśe uṣṇatvābhāvaḥ, 8nīlatve śuklatvābhāvaḥ, 9vīṇāśabde
tīvratvābhāvaḥ, 10śabdatve bhedābhāvaḥ iti/ na caivaṃ
viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvasya bahuvidhatve ṣoḍhā sannikarṣa iti kathamiti
vācyam/ viśeṣaṇatātvena pañcavidhaviśeṣaṇatānāṃ viśeṣyatātvena
pañcavidhaviśeṣyatānāmanugamaṃ kṛtvā
viśeṣaṇatāviśeṣyatānyataratvena daśānāmapi parigaṇanāt
ṣaḍvidhatvasyāhāneḥ/ na ca samavāyarūpāṇāṃ saṃyuktasamavāya -
saṃyuktasamavetasamavāya - samavāya - samavetasamavāyānāṃ caturṇāmapi
samavāyatvena ekavargīkaraṇaṃ vidhāya saṃyogaḥ, samavāyaḥ,
viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvaśceti tridhaiva sannikarṣaḥ kuto na vyabhātīte
vācyam/ svatantrecchena muninā kṛte ṣoḍhā vibhāge
niyogaparyanuyogayoḥ kartumaśakyatvāt/ niyogaḥ ājñā,
paryanuyogaḥ praśnaḥ/
children.translated_text: (4) the sound of a <s>vīṇā</s> possesses the absence of intensity, (5) sound-hood possesses the absence of difference, (6) in the ground-surface there is the absence of a pot, (7) in the touch of water there is the absence of heat, (8) in blue-ness there is the absence of white-ness, (9) in the sound of a <s>vīṇā</s> there is the absence of intensity, (10) in sound-hood there is the absence of difference. Nor should it be said: if the qualifier-qualificand relation is thus of many kinds, how can there be [only] sixfold sense-contact? Because, having subsumed the five kinds of qualifier-hood under the single category of qualifier-hood-ness (<s>viśeṣaṇatātva</s>) and the five kinds of qualificand-hood under qualificand-hood-ness (<s>viśeṣyatātva</s>), and enumerating all ten under the disjunction of qualifier-hood-ness and qualificand-hood-ness, the sixfold classification is not undermined. Nor should it be said: why was a threefold classification of sense-contact — conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and qualifier-qualificand relation — not made by grouping the four inherence-based types under the single category of inherence? Because when the sage (<s>muni</s>), by his independent will, has made the sixfold division, neither command (<s>niyoga</s>) nor questioning (<s>paryanuyoga</s>) can be directed [at him]. <s>Niyoga</s> means command; <s>paryanuyoga</s> means questioning.

children.text:
1. cakṣussaṃyuktaṃ
bhūtalaṃ tadviśeṣaṇatvaṃ ghaṭābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (1) The ground-surface conjoined with the eye — its qualifier-hood belongs to the absence of a pot.

children.text:
2. cakṣussaṃyuktaṃ toyaṃ
tatsamavetaḥ sparśaḥ tadviśeṣaṇatvam uṣṇatvābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (2) Water conjoined with the eye — the touch inherent in it — its qualifier-hood belongs to the absence of heat.

children.text:
3. cakṣussaṃyukto ghaṭaḥ
tatsamaveto nīla tatsamavetaṃ nīlatvaṃ tadviśeṣaṇatvaṃ
śuklatvābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (3) The pot conjoined with the eye — the blue inherent in it — the blue-ness inherent in that — its qualifier-hood belongs to the absence of white-ness.

children.text:
4. śrotrasamavetaḥ
vīṇāśabdaḥ tadviśeṣaṇatvaṃ tīvratvābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (4) The sound of a <s>vīṇā</s> inherent in the auditory organ — its qualifier-hood belongs to the absence of intensity.

children.text:
5. śrotrasamavetaḥ śabdaḥ
tatsamavetaṃ śabdatvaṃ tadviśeṣaṇatvaṃ bhedābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (5) Sound inherent in the auditory organ — sound-hood inherent in that — its qualifier-hood belongs to the absence of difference.

children.text:
6. cakṣussaṃyuktaṃ
bhūtalaṃ tinnarūpitaviśeṣyatā ghaṭābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (6) The ground-surface conjoined with the eye — the qualificand-hood determined by it belongs to the absence of a pot.

children.text:
7. cakṣussaṃyuktaṃ toyaṃ
tatsamavetaḥ sparśaḥ tannirūpitaviśeṣyatā uṣṇatvābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (7) Water conjoined with the eye — the touch inherent in it — the qualificand-hood determined by it belongs to the absence of heat.

children.text:
8. cakṣussaṃyukto ghaṭaḥ
tatsamaveto nīlaḥ tatsamavetaṃ nīlatvaṃ tannirūpitaviśeṣyatā
śuklatvābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (8) The pot conjoined with the eye — the blue inherent in it — the blue-ness inherent in that — the qualificand-hood determined by it belongs to the absence of white-ness.

children.text:
9. śrotrasamaveto
vīṇāśabdaḥ tannirūpitaviśeṣyatā tīvratvābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (9) The sound of a <s>vīṇā</s> inherent in the auditory organ — the qualificand-hood determined by it belongs to the absence of intensity.

children.text:
10. śrotrasamavetaḥ
śabdaḥ tatsamavetaṃ śabdatvaṃ tannirūpitaviśeṣyatā bhedābhāvasya/
children.translated_text: (10) Sound inherent in the auditory organ — sound-hood inherent in that — the qualificand-hood determined by it belongs to the absence of difference.

children.text:
maṇikārāstu -
kevalaviśeṣaṇatā indriyasambaddhaviśeṣaṇatā ceti viśeṣaṇatā
dvividhā/ indriyasambaddhaviśeṣaṇatā, pūrvoktarītyā pañcavidhā/
kevalaviśeṣaṇatāyāḥ udāharaṇaṃ ākāśaṃ śabdābhāvavat iti
śabdābhāvapratyakṣam - ityabhiprayanti/ 'viśeṣaṇatayā śabdābhāvasya,
indriyasambaddhaviśeṣaṇatayā samavāyaghaṭābhāvādergrahaḥ' iti
saṃnikarṣavāde taiḥ kathanāt//
children.translated_text: The <s>Maṇikāras</s> (i.e., followers of <s>Gaṅgeśa</s>'s <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s>), however, [hold that] qualifier-hood is twofold: bare qualifier-hood (<s>kevalaviśeṣaṇatā</s>) and sense-organ-connected qualifier-hood (<s>indriyasambaddhaviśeṣaṇatā</s>). Sense-organ-connected qualifier-hood is, in the manner stated earlier, fivefold. An example of bare qualifier-hood is: the perception of the absence of sound in ether (<s>ākāśa</s>) — 'ether possesses the absence of sound' — thus they maintain. Because in their <s>Saṃnikarṣavāda</s> (treatise on sense-contact) they state: 'The apprehension of the absence of pot etc. in what is connected by inherence is through sense-organ-connected qualifier-hood; [the apprehension of the absence of sound in ether is] through [bare] qualifier-hood.'

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text:
evaṃ
sannikarṣajanyajñānam pratyakṣam/ tatkaraṇaṃ indriyam/ tasmādindriyaṃ
pratyakṣapramāṇam iti siddham//
children.translated_text: Thus, the cognition born of sense-contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>) is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Its instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is the sense-organ (<s>indriya</s>). Therefore, it is established that the sense-organ is the means of valid perceptual knowledge (<s>pratyakṣapramāṇa</s>).

children.text:
iti tarkasaṅgrahe
pratyakṣaparicchedaḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on perception (<s>pratyakṣapariccheda</s>) in the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
anupalabdheḥ
pramāṇāntaratvanirākaraṇam/
children.translated_text: The rejection of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) as a separate means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

children.text:
etena anupalabdheḥ
pramāṇāntaratvaṃ nirastam/ yadi atra ghaṭaḥ abhaviṣyat tarhi bhūtalamiva
adrakṣyata, darśanābhāvāt nāstīti
tarkitapratiyogisattvavirodhyanupalabdhisahakṛtendriyeṇaiva
abhāvajñānopapattau anupalabdhaiḥ pramāṇāntaratvāsambhavāt/
adhikaraṇajñānārthamapekṣaṇīyendriyasyaiva karaṇatvopapattau anupalabdheḥ
karaṇatvāyogāt/ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: By this, the status of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) as a separate means of valid knowledge is refuted. 'If a pot were present here, it would have been seen just like the ground-surface; from the absence of seeing, [we conclude] it does not exist' — since the cognition of absence can be accounted for by the sense-organ alone, assisted by non-apprehension that is opposed to the ascertained existence of the counter-positive (<s>pratiyogin</s>), it is impossible for non-apprehension to be a separate means of valid knowledge. Since the sense-organ, which must anyway be posited for the cognition of the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), can itself serve as the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), non-apprehension cannot be the instrument. The qualifier-qualificand relation (<s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s>)

children.text: viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasvarūpameva, nātiriktaḥ sambandhaḥ/
children.translated_text: is nothing but the very nature of the qualifier and qualificand themselves; it is not a relation over and above [them].

children.text:
pratyakṣajñānamupasaṃharan tasya karaṇamāha - evamiti/
asādhāraṇakāraṇatvāt indriyaṃ pratyakṣajñānakaraṇamityarthaḥ/
pratyakṣapramāṇamupasaṃharati - tasmāditi//
children.translated_text: Concluding the [discussion of] perceptual cognition, he states its instrument — with 'thus' (<s>evam</s>). The meaning is: because the sense-organ is the uncommon cause (<s>asādhāraṇakāraṇa</s>), it is the instrument of perceptual cognition. He concludes [the discussion of] the means of perceptual knowledge with 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>).

children.text:
iti dīpikāyāṃ
pratyakṣaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on perception (<s>pratyakṣapariccheda</s>) in the <s>Dīpikā</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
etena -
abhāvapramāyā viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvasaṃnikarṣajanyatvapradarśanena/
pramāṇāntaratvam - pratyakṣādyatiriktapramāṇatvam/ nanu anupalabdheḥ
pramāṇāntaratvānaṅgīkāre ghaṭopalabdhidaśāyāṃ tadabhāvapratyakṣāpattiḥ,
mama mate tu - anupalabdhyātmakapramāṇāntarābhāvāt nāpattiriti
bhāṭṭaśaṅkāṃ parijihīrṣuḥ yogyānupalabdheḥ
indriyasahakāritvamātreṇaiva nirvāhe atiriktapramāṇatvaṃ na
saṃbhavatītyāha - yadyatretyādinā/ atra - cakṣussaṃyogādimadbhūtale
tarkasyāpādakābhāvasādhakaviparyayapratiyogyāpādyakatvarūpaviparyaye
tatkoṭiparyavasāyitvaṃ darśayati - darśanābhāvāt nāstīti/
taddarśanābhāvāt tannāstītyarthaḥ/ tarkitetyādi/ tarkitā āpāditā
pratiyogino ghaṭādeḥ sattvasya sattvaprasakteḥ virodhinī ya upalabdhiḥ
tatpratiyogikaḥ abhāvaḥ anupalabdhiḥ tatsahakṛtenetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'By this' — by demonstrating that the valid cognition of absence arises from the sense-contact of the qualifier-qualificand relation. 'As a separate means of valid knowledge' — means: as a means of valid knowledge distinct from perception and the rest. Now, [an objection from the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> school:] if non-apprehension is not accepted as a separate means of valid knowledge, then at the time of perceiving the pot, there would be the undesirable consequence of perceiving its absence too; but in my view, since there is no separate means of knowledge in the form of non-apprehension, there is no such consequence — desiring to remove this <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> objection, [the author] says, since the matter is resolved merely by non-apprehension serving as an auxiliary to the sense-organ, there is no possibility of its being a separate means of knowledge — with 'if here' etc. 'Here' — at the ground-surface possessing conjunction with the eye etc. He shows the nature of <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) as consisting in arriving at one alternative of a disjunction between what establishes the absence of the producing-cause and the counter-positive of the erroneous [cognition] — with 'from the absence of seeing, it does not exist.' The meaning is: from the absence of seeing that, that does not exist. 'Ascertained' etc. — the ascertained, i.e. established, existence of the counter-positive such as the pot; the non-apprehension that is opposed to the predisposition toward its existence; the absence that has that as its counter-positive — 'assisted by that' is the meaning.

children.text:
virodhitvaviśeṣaṇaṃ
upalabdheḥ anāhāryatvasūcanāya/
pratiyogisattāpādanāpāditopalambhapratiyogikatvarūpayogyatāviśiṣṭānupalabdhisahakṛteneti
tu paramārthaḥ/ ālokasaṃyogādyasattvadaśāyāṃ yadyatra ghaṭaḥ syāt tarhi
upalabhyeta ityāpādanāsambhavena yogyānupalabdhyabhāvāt na tatra
ghaṭābhāvapratyakṣamiti saṃkṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: The qualification 'opposed' with respect to apprehension is to indicate its being non-erroneous (<s>anāhārya</s>). The ultimate meaning, however, is: assisted by non-apprehension qualified by the fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) consisting in being the counter-positive of the apprehension that would be produced by the production of the existence of the counter-positive. In the condition where the conjunction with light etc. is absent, since the supposition 'if a pot were here, it would be apprehended' cannot be made, and hence there is no qualified non-apprehension (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>), there is no perception of the absence of a pot in that case — this is the summary.

children.text:
kecittu -
tarkitetyādi/ tarkitaṃ āropitaṃ yat pratiyogisattvam,
tadvirodhinī yā anupalabdhiḥ
children.translated_text: Some, however, [explain] 'ascertained' etc. [as follows:] 'ascertained' means superimposed; the existence of the counter-positive that is superimposed — the non-apprehension that is opposed to it —

children.text:
tatsahakṛtenetyarthaḥ/
etāvatā pratiyogisattvarūpa-kāraṇābhāva-prayojyopalabdhyabhāvaḥ
abhāvapratyakṣe kāraṇam, na tu
itarakāraṇavirahaprayojyopalabdhyabhāvaḥ iti sūcitam/ ata
evāndhakāre upalambhābhāvasattve 'pi na ghaṭābhāvapratyakṣam - ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: 'assisted by that' is the meaning. By this it is indicated that the absence of apprehension caused by the absence of the cause in the form of the existence of the counter-positive is the cause of the perception of absence, and not the absence of apprehension caused by the absence of other causes. Hence, even though the absence of apprehension obtains in darkness, there is no perception of the absence of a pot — thus they say.

children.text:
nanu abhāvapramāyāṃ
indriyasya karaṇatvaṃ anupalabdheḥ sahakāritvaṃ ca tvayā kalpanīyam/
tadapekṣayā anupalabdhereva karaṇatvakalpanaṃ varam ityāśaṅkya
abhāvādhikaraṇabhūtalapratyakṣe indriyasya avaśyamapekṣaṇīyatayā
kḷptenaiva indriyakaraṇatvenābhāvapratyakṣopapattau
anupalabdherviñjātīyapramitikaraṇatvakalpanamayuktamityāha -
adhikaraṇeti/ nanu viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvākhyaḥ atiriktasambandhaḥ
kalpanīyaḥ tvayetyata āha - viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva iti/
children.translated_text: Now, [objection:] in the valid cognition of absence, you must postulate both the instrumentality (<s>karaṇatva</s>) of the sense-organ and the auxiliary status (<s>sahakāritva</s>) of non-apprehension; compared to that, it would be better to postulate the instrumentality of non-apprehension alone — anticipating this objection, [the author replies:] since the sense-organ must anyway be posited in the perception of the ground-surface that is the locus of the absence, and since the perception of absence is accounted for by the already-established instrumentality of the sense-organ, it is improper to postulate the instrumentality of non-apprehension as an instrument of a different class of valid cognition — he says with 'of the locus' (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>). Now, [another objection:] you must postulate an additional relation called the qualifier-qualificand relation — to this he says: the qualifier-qualificand relation (<s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s>)

children.text:
atredaṃ bodhyam -
pratyakṣaṃ dvividham laukikam alaukikaṃ ceti/ laukikatvaṃ ca
viṣayitāviśeṣaḥ/ laukike ṣoḍhā saṃnikarṣaḥ kāraṇam/ alaukike
tu sāmānyalakṣaṇā, jñānalakṣaṇā, yogajadharmaśceti trividhā pratyāsattiḥ/
tatra sāmānyalakṣaṇā dhūmatvādirūpā tajjñānarūpā vā/ sāmānyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ
svarūpaṃ viṣayo vā yasyā iti vyutpatteḥ/ sā cāśrayāṇāṃ
nikhiladhūmādīnāṃ alaukikapratyakṣe upayujyate/
atītānāgatadhūtādiṣu cakṣussaṃyogāderasambhavāt indriyāṇāṃ
asannikṛṣṭānāṃ pratyakṣājanakatvāt/ jñānalakṣaṇā tu surabhi candanamiti
cākṣuṣopanītabhāne saurabheṇa cakṣuṣo yogyasannikarṣābhāvāt/ evaṃ
yogināṃ deśakālaviprakṛṣṭapadārthapratyakṣe yogajadharmaḥ pratyāsattiḥ
kāraṇam iti saṃkṣepaḥ//
children.translated_text: Here this should be understood: perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is twofold — ordinary (<s>laukika</s>) and extraordinary (<s>alaukika</s>). Ordinary-ness is a specific kind of object-relation (<s>viṣayitā</s>). In ordinary perception, the sixfold sense-contact is the cause. In extraordinary perception, however, the connection (<s>pratyāsatti</s>) is of three kinds: <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā</s> (universality-characterized), <s>jñānalakṣaṇā</s> (knowledge-characterized), and <s>yogaja dharma</s> (born of yogic practice). Of these, <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā</s> takes the form of smoke-hood etc. or the form of cognition thereof — since the etymology is: that whose distinguishing mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), or essential nature, or object, is a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>). It serves in the extraordinary perception of all substrates such as all smoke-instances etc. — because conjunction with the eye etc. is impossible with respect to past and future smoke-instances, and because sense-organs that are not in contact [with their objects] cannot generate perception. <s>Jñānalakṣaṇā</s>, on the other hand, [functions] in the visual apprehension 'fragrant sandalwood,' because there is no appropriate sense-contact of the eye with the fragrance. Similarly, for yogins, in the perception of objects remote in space and time, the connection born of yogic merit (<s>yogaja dharma</s>) is the cause — this is the summary.

children.text:
iti prakāśikāyāṃ
pratyakṣaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on perception (<s>pratyakṣapariccheda</s>) in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanvanupalabdherityādi/ anupalabdhirnāma
pratiyogiviṣayakapratyakṣābhavaḥ/ 'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat'
ityākārakaghaṭādyabhāvaviṣayakapramāṃ prati ghaṭopalabdhyabhāvaḥ kāraṇam/
'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭavat' iti ghaṭopalambhakāle ghaṭābhāvapramityanudayāt/
yadi abhāvapramāṃ prati anupalabdhiḥ na kāraṇam tarhi pratiyogino
ghaṭāderupalambhakāle 'pi ghaṭādyabhāvapramāyāḥ āpattiḥ ataḥ anupalabdhiḥ
abhāvapramāṃ prati kāraṇatayā pṛthakpramāṇamiti bhāṭṭāḥ/ naiyāyikāstu
anupalabdhisahakṛtendriyaliṅgādibhireva
abhāvaviṣayakapratyakṣānumityāderupapattyā abhāvaviṣayakapramā na
pratyakṣādipramitivilakṣaṇā, tathā tatsādhanamapi na
pratyakṣādipramāṇavilakṣaṇam, api tu abhāvapramājanakendriyādeḥ
anupalabdhiḥ sahakāri kāraṇamātramityāśerate/ tarkasyetyādi/
children.translated_text: Now, regarding 'of <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension)' and so forth. <s>Anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) means the absence of perception directed at the counter-positive. The absence of apprehension of a pot is the cause of valid cognition whose content is the absence of a pot and so forth, having the form 'the ground possesses the absence of a pot.' This is because at the time of apprehending the pot in the form 'the ground possesses a pot,' the valid cognition of pot-absence does not arise. If <s>anupalabdhi</s> were not a cause of absence-cognition, then even at the time of apprehending the counter-positive such as a pot, there would be the undesirable consequence of valid cognition of pot-absence and so forth. Therefore, the <s>Bhāṭṭas</s> hold that <s>anupalabdhi</s> is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) by virtue of being a cause of absence-cognition. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, however, maintain that since perception, inference, and so forth whose content is absence can be accounted for through the senses, inferential marks, and other means assisted by non-apprehension alone, absence-cognition is not different in kind from perception and other valid cognitions; likewise its means of establishment is not different in kind from perception and other <s>pramāṇas</s>; rather, <s>anupalabdhi</s> is merely an auxiliary cause of the senses and other instruments that generate absence-cognition. Regarding 'of <s>tarka</s> (counterfactual reasoning)' and so forth.

children.text: 'vyāptistarkāpratihatiravasānaṃ viparyaye/
children.translated_text: '<s>Vyāpti</s> (pervasion), non-obstruction by <s>tarka</s>, termination in the contrary,

children.text:
aniṣṭānanukūlatve
iti tarkāṅgapañcakam//'
children.translated_text: undesirability, and non-conduciveness — thus the five limbs of <s>tarka</s>.'

children.text:
ityuktarītyā tarkasya
pañca aṅgāni apekṣitāni/ vyāptiḥ āpādakasya agnyabhāvādeḥ āpādyasya
dhūmābhāvādeśca vyāpyavyāpakabhāvaḥ/ tarkāpratihatiḥ -
pratikūlatarkābhāvaḥ/ viparyaye paryavasānam - yadi vahnyabhāvaḥ syāt
tarhiṃ dhūmābhāvaḥ syāt ityāpādanasya hi dhūmasattvādvahnireva yukta
ityevarūpe tadviparyaye paryavasānaṃ bhavati/ aniṣṭatvam - āpādyasya
dhūmābhāvādeḥ aniṣṭatvaṃ praṣṭuḥ/ ananukūlatvaṃ
prativādipakṣasādhakatvābhāvaḥ/ tatra viparyaye paryavasānaṃ pariṣkṛtyāha
- āpādakābhāveti/ āpādakaḥ vahnyabhāvaḥ tasyābhāvaḥ vahnyabhāvābhāvaḥ
vahnirūpaḥ tasya sādhakaḥ ya viparyayaḥ āpādyasya dhūmābhāvasyābhāvaḥ
dhūmarūpaḥ tasya pratiyogī dhūmābhāvaḥ āpādyaḥ yasya tarkasya tattvaṃ
viparyaye paryavasānamityarthaḥ/ prakṛte 'yadyatra ghaṭaḥ syāt tarhi
bhūtalamiva ghaṭo 'drakṣyata' ityākārake tarke āpādako ghaṭaḥ
tasyābhāvaḥ ghaṭābhāvaḥ tasya sādhako viparyayaḥ darśanābhāvaḥ tasya
pratiyogi darśanameva āpādyamiti
āpādakābhāvasādhakaviparyaṃyapratiyogyāpādyakatvaṃ tarkasya/ tathā ca
yasmiṃstarke āpādakābhāvasādhakābhāvapratiyogi āpādyaṃ bhavati
tādṛśasthale āpādyābhāvena hetunā āpādakābhāve eva paryavasānaṃ
bhavati iti darśanābhāvāt
children.translated_text: In the manner stated, five limbs are required for <s>tarka</s>. <s>Vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is the relation of pervaded and pervader between what is to be established — such as the absence of fire — and what establishes it — such as the absence of smoke. Non-obstruction by <s>tarka</s> means the absence of an opposing <s>tarka</s>. Termination in the contrary means: the establishment 'if there were absence of fire, there would be absence of smoke' terminates in its contrary, namely 'since smoke exists, fire alone is appropriate.' Undesirability means that the thing to be established, such as the absence of smoke, is undesirable to the questioner. Non-conduciveness means the absence of capacity to support the opponent's thesis. Among these, he clarifies 'termination in the contrary' by saying 'of the absence of the establisher' and so forth. The establisher is the absence of fire; the absence of that is the absence of the absence of fire, which is of the nature of fire; that which proves this — the contrary — is the absence of the absence of smoke, which is of the nature of smoke; the counter-positive of that is the absence of smoke, which is the thing to be established — this is the meaning of 'termination in the contrary.' In the present context, in the <s>tarka</s> of the form 'if there were a pot here, the pot would be seen just as the ground is,' the establisher is the pot; its absence is pot-absence; the contrary that proves this is the absence of seeing; the counter-positive of that is seeing itself, which is the thing to be established — thus the <s>tarka</s> has the character of having as its thing-to-be-established the counter-positive of the contrary that proves the absence of the establisher. And accordingly, in a <s>tarka</s> where the thing to be established is the counter-positive of the absence of that which proves the absence of the establisher, in such a case termination occurs precisely in the absence of the establisher, by reason of the absence of the thing to be established — from the absence of seeing,

children.text:
nāstītyanena
darśitam/ darśanābhāvādityasya ghaṭadarśanābhāvādityarthaḥ, nāstītyasya
ghaṭābhāva ityarthaḥ/ kevalānupalabdheḥ abhāvapratyakṣakāraṇatve
ālokasaṃyogādyasattvadaśāyāṃ ghaṭānupalabdheḥ sattvena
ghaṭābhāvapratyakṣāpattiḥ/ ataḥ yogyatāviśiṣṭānupalabdheḥ kāraṇatvaṃ
vaktavyam/ yogyatā ca
tarkitapratiyogisattvavirodhyupalabdhipratiyogikatvarūpā/
tadghaṭakatarkasya viparyaye paryavasānaṃ 'yadyatra' ityādigranthena
pradarśitamiti bhāvaḥ/ tarkitetyādimulaṃ vyācaṣṭetarkitā āpāditā
ityādinā/ yathāśrute pratiyogisattvasya
children.translated_text: it is shown by 'it does not exist.' The meaning of 'from the absence of seeing' is 'from the absence of seeing the pot'; the meaning of 'it does not exist' is 'there is absence of the pot.' If mere <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) alone were the cause of absence-perception, then in the condition where light, contact, and so forth are absent, since non-apprehension of the pot would still obtain, there would be the undesirable consequence of perception of pot-absence. Therefore, it must be stated that the cause is non-apprehension qualified by fitness. And fitness has the nature of being the counter-positive of an apprehension that contradicts the existence of the counter-positive as hypothesized by <s>tarka</s>. The termination in the contrary of the <s>tarka</s> involving that pot has been demonstrated by the passage beginning 'if here' and so forth — this is the purport. He glosses the root text beginning with 'hypothesized' by saying 'established' and so forth. As the text literally reads, it would be understood that

children.text:
pratiyogyupalabdhiḥ
virodhinīti pratīyate/ tadasaṅgatam - ghaṭopalabdheḥ
ghaṭasattvavirodhitvābhāvāt/ ataḥ sattvasya sattvaprasakteriti
vyākhyātam/ ghaṭasattvāroparūpaprasakteḥ ghaṭopalabdhi virodhinī/ na hi
ghaṭe upalabhyamāne 'yadyatra ghaṭaḥ syāt' iti ghaṭasattāṃ kaścit
prasañjayediti bhāvaḥ/ anāhāryatvasūcanāyeti/ anāhāryajñānasyaiva
virodhitvāditi bhāvaḥ/ sattvasya sattvaprasakteriti vyākhyāne 'pi
āpāditatvarūpaṃ tarkitatvaṃ pratiyogisattvasyaiva na tu tatprasakteḥ/ kiṃ
ca yatra āpādakaṃ āpādyaṃ ubhayamapi prasajyate tatraiva viparyaye
paryavasānaṃ dṛśyate/ mūlāttu pratiyogisattvarūpāpādakasyaiva
prasañjitatvaṃ labhyate, na tvāpādyāyā upalabdheḥ/ ataḥ tātparyārthamāha -
pratiyogisattāpādaneti/ pratiyoginaḥ ghaṭādeḥ sattvasya āpādanena
prasañjanena 'yadyatra ghaṭaḥ syāt' ityevaṃrūpeṇa āpāditaḥ prasañjitaḥ
yaḥ upalambhaḥ 'tarhyupalabhyeta' ityevaṃrūpaprasañjanaviṣayaḥ upalambhaḥ sa
pratiyogī yasyā anupalabdheḥ tatkatvarūpayogyatāviśiṣṭā
anupalabdhirityarthaḥ/ yogyatāviśeṣaṇaprayojanamāha -
ālokasaṃyogeti/ āpādanāsambhaveneti/ tathā ca
pratiyogisattvaprasañjanaprasañjitapratiyogikatvarūpayogyatāvirahāt
anupalabdheḥ yogyānupalabdhistatra nāsti/ ato na ghaṭābhāvapratyakṣamiti
bhāvaḥ/ nanu yatra pratiyogisattvasya upalabdheścāpādānaṃ vinaiva
bhūtacalakṣussaṃyogānantaraṃ ghaṭo nāstīti pratyakṣaṃ
tatrāpādanaghaṭitayogyatāvirahāt tatpratyakṣānupapattirityāśaṅkyāha
- saṃkṣepa iti/ pratiyogisattāpādanāpāditatvaṃ ca
pratiyogisattāpādakakāpattiyogyatvam/ ato nānupapattiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: apprehension of the counter-positive contradicts the existence of the counter-positive. That is incorrect — because the apprehension of a pot does not contradict the existence of the pot. Therefore it is explained as 'the presumption of existence.' The apprehension of a pot contradicts the presumption of pot-existence in the form of hypothetically attributing existence to the pot. For when the pot is being apprehended, no one would hypothesize 'if there were a pot here' — this is the purport. The phrase 'for indicating the character of being non-artificial' means: because only non-artificial cognition has the quality of being contradictory — this is the purport. Even in the explanation 'the presumption of existence,' the character of being hypothesized, which is of the nature of having been established by <s>tarka</s>, belongs to the existence of the counter-positive alone, not to its presumption. Moreover, termination in the contrary is observed only where both the establisher and the thing to be established are hypothesized. But from the root text, only the hypothesized character of the establisher, which is the existence of the counter-positive, is obtained, not of the thing to be established, namely apprehension. Therefore, stating the intended meaning, he says 'by the establishment of the counter-positive's existence.' By the establishment — that is, the hypothesizing — of the existence of the counter-positive such as a pot, the apprehension that is established — that is, hypothesized — in the form 'then it would be apprehended': that apprehension is the counter-positive of which <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) — <s>anupalabdhi</s> qualified by the fitness of having such a character is the meaning. He states the purpose of the qualifier 'fitness' by saying 'light and contact' and so forth. 'Due to the impossibility of establishment' means: and accordingly, because of the absence of the fitness whose nature is being the counter-positive of that which is hypothesized through the hypothesizing of the counter-positive's existence, the non-apprehension there is not qualified non-apprehension. Therefore there is no perception of pot-absence — this is the purport. Now, objecting that where perception 'the pot does not exist' arises immediately upon contact of the eye with the ground surface, without any hypothesizing of the counter-positive's existence and of apprehension, due to the absence of fitness constituted by such hypothesizing, that perception would be inexplicable — to this he replies with 'in brief.' The character of being established through establishment of the counter-positive's existence means fitness for the hypothetical reasoning that establishes the counter-positive's existence. Therefore there is no inexplicability — this is the purport.

children.text:
ata evāndhakāra iti/
andhakāre yo ghaṭopalambhābhāvaḥ sa na ghaṭasattvābhāvaprayojyaḥ api tu
ālokasaṃyogarūpakāraṇāntarābhāvaprayojyaḥ/ tathā ca
pratiyogisattvābhāvaprayojyopalabdhyabhāvarūpāyāḥ yogyānupalabdheḥ
tatrābhāvāt na ghaṭābhāvapratyakṣamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: For this very reason, 'in darkness' and so forth. The absence of pot-apprehension in darkness is not produced by the absence of pot-existence, but rather is produced by the absence of another cause in the form of contact with light. And accordingly, since the qualified non-apprehension — which is of the nature of absence of apprehension produced by the absence of the counter-positive's existence — is absent there, there is no perception of pot-absence — this is the purport.

children.text:
dhūmatvādirūpetyādi/
ādau lakṣaṇaśabda svarūpabodhakaḥ/ dvitīye tu viṣayabodhakaḥ/ prathamapakṣe
dhūmatvādyaviduṣo 'pi svarūpasaddhūmatvapratyāsattyā dhūmā ityevaṃ
yāvaddhūmapratyakṣāpattirityasvārasyāt dvitīyapakṣānudhāvanam/
cākṣuṣopanītabhāve iti/ cākṣuṣaṃ yat smṛtasaurabhaviṣayakaṃ
jñānamityarthaḥ//
children.translated_text: Regarding 'in the form of smoke-hood and so forth.' In the first instance, the word 'definition' conveys the essential nature. In the second instance, however, it conveys the object. In the first alternative, since even one who does not know smoke-hood and so forth would, by proximity to smoke-hood which exists in its own nature, have perception of smoke — and this being incongruous — the second alternative is followed. Regarding 'when presented by visual cognition': the meaning is that the visual cognition is the cognition whose object is the remembered fragrance.

children.text:
iti
tarkasaṅgrahadīpikāprakāśikāvyākhyāyāṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the commentary called <s>Bālapriyā</s> on the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha-Dīpikā-Prakāśikā</s>,

children.text:
bālapriyāyāṃ
pratyakṣaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: [this concludes] the chapter on <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception).

children.text: anumānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Chapter on <s>Anumāna</s> (Inference)

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: anumānalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Anumāna</s> (Inference)

children.text: AnTs_44 anumitikaraṇam anumānam / parāmarśajanyaṃ jñānam anumitiḥ / vyāptiviśiṣṭapakṣadharmatājñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ / yathā vahnivyāpyadhūmavān ayaṃ parvata iti jñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ / taj janyaṃ parvato vahnimān iti jñānam anumitiḥ / yatra yatra dhūmas tatrāgnir iti sāhacaryaniyamo vyāptiḥ / vyāpyasya parvatādivṛttitvaṃ pakṣadharmatā //
children.translated_text: The instrument of <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition) is <s>anumāna</s> (inference). The cognition produced by <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective consideration) is <s>anumiti</s>. The cognition of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (the property of the subject) qualified by <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is <s>parāmarśa</s>. For example, the cognition 'this mountain possesses smoke which is pervaded by fire' is <s>parāmarśa</s>. The cognition 'the mountain possesses fire' produced from that is <s>anumiti</s>. The invariable co-occurrence of the form 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire' is <s>vyāpti</s>. The presence of the pervaded property in the mountain and such loci is <s>pakṣadharmatā</s>.

children.text:
anumitikaraṇam
anumānam/
children.translated_text: The instrument of <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition) is <s>anumāna</s> (inference).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
anumānaṃ lakṣayati -
anumitikaraṇamiti/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>anumāna</s> by saying 'the instrument of <s>anumiti</s>.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
anumānaṃ
lakṣayatīti/ pratyakṣopajīvakasaṅgatyā anumānaṃ nirūpayatītyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'He defines <s>anumāna</s>' means: he explains <s>anumāna</s> in the order that follows upon <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) — this is the meaning.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pratyakṣopajīvakasaṅgatyeti/ pratyakṣakāryatvarūpayā saṅgatyā
ityarthaḥ/ indriyeṇa mahānasādau vyāptipratyakṣādeva anumānaṃ
bhavati/ vyāptismaraṇarūpānumānaṃ prati vyāptipratyakṣasya anubhavavidhayā
kāraṇatvāt/ tathā ca kāryakāraṇabhāvarūpasaṅgatyā
pratyakṣānantaramanumānanirūpaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/ anena pramāṇayo
kāryakāraṇabhāva uktaḥ/ anumityātmakapramiteḥ/
parāmarśātmakamānasapratyakṣakāryatvāt pramityoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ
jñeyaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'In the order that follows upon <s>pratyakṣa</s>' means: in the order characterized by being an effect of <s>pratyakṣa</s>. <s>Anumāna</s> arises from the perception of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) in the kitchen and such places through the senses. This is because the perception of <s>vyāpti</s> is a cause — in the manner of prior experience — of <s>anumāna</s>, which is of the nature of the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s>. And accordingly, the explanation of <s>anumāna</s> after <s>pratyakṣa</s> is due to their relation of cause and effect — this is the purport. By this, the cause-and-effect relation between the two <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) is stated. The cause-and-effect relation between the two <s>pramitis</s> (valid cognitions) should be understood from the fact that <s>anumiti</s>-type valid cognition is an effect of the mental <s>pratyakṣa</s> in the form of <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective consideration).

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: anumitilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Anumiti</s> (Inferential Cognition)

children.text:
parāmarśajanyaṃ
jñānaṃ anumitiḥ/
children.translated_text: The cognition produced by <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective consideration) is <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
anumitiṃ lakṣayati - parāmerśeti/ nanu
saṃśayottarapratyakṣe ativyāptiḥ sthāṇupuruṣasaṃśayānantaraṃ
'puruṣatvavyāpyakarādimān ayam' iti parāmarśe sati 'puruṣa eva'
iti pratyakṣajananāt/ na ca tatrānumitireva iti vācyam/
'puruṣaṃ sākṣātkaromi' ityanuvyavasāyavirodhāditi cet,
na-pakṣatāsahakṛtaparāmarśajanyatvasya vivakṣitatvāt/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>anumiti</s> by saying '<s>parāmarśa</s>' and so forth. Now, there is over-extension to perception following doubt: after doubt regarding whether something is a post or a person, when there is <s>parāmarśa</s> of the form 'this possesses hands and such features pervaded by person-hood,' a perceptual cognition 'it is indeed a person' is generated. Nor can it be said that this is itself an <s>anumiti</s>, because this contradicts the retrospective awareness '<s>I directly perceive the person</s>.' If one objects thus — no, because what is intended is 'being produced by <s>parāmarśa</s> assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s> (thesis-hood).'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
parāmarśetīti/
tathā ca pratyakṣapramityapekṣayā anumiteḥ vilakṣaṇapramātvāt anumānasya
pramāṇāntaratvaṃ sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ/ viparītajñānottarapratyakṣaṃ prati
viśeṣadarśanasya hetutvamaṅgīkurvatāṃ matamavalambya śaṅkate -
nanviti/ sthāṇupuruṣasaṃśayeti/ idaṃ
viruddhabhāvadvayakoṭikasaṃśayāṅgīkāreṇa/ pare tu - sthāṇupuruṣeti/
sthāṇutvatadabhāvapuruṣatvatadabhāvakoṭiketyarthaḥ - ityāhuḥ/ puruṣa
aivati nirṇayasūcanāya/ tatra - saṃśayottarapratyakṣasthale/
anuvyavasāyavirodhāditi/ idamupalakṣaṇam - 'puruṣaṃ anuminomi'
ityanuvyavasāyābhāvena pramāṇābhāvādityapi draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: '<s>Parāmarśa</s>' and so forth. And accordingly, since <s>anumiti</s> is a valid cognition of a different kind relative to perceptual valid cognition, the status of <s>anumāna</s> as a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> is established — this is the purport. He raises the objection by saying 'now' and so forth, relying on the view of those who accept that specific perception is the cause of perception following erroneous cognition. 'Doubt regarding post or person' means: this is based on the acceptance of doubt having two alternatives of contradictory natures. Others say: 'post-or-person' means having as alternatives post-hood, its absence, person-hood, and its absence. 'Indeed a person' is to indicate a determinate cognition. 'There' means in the case of perception following doubt. 'Due to contradiction with retrospective awareness' is illustrative — it should also be seen that due to the absence of the retrospective awareness 'I infer the person,' there is absence of the <s>pramāṇa</s> [of inference].

children.text:
saṃśayottarapratyakṣe
jananīye pakṣatāyāḥ parāmarśasahakāritve prayojanābhāvena
pakṣatāsahakṛtaparāmarśajanyatvavivakṣaṇāt nātivyāptiḥ ityāha -
pakṣateti/ aitena 'vahnivyāpyadhūmavatparvatavānayaṃ deśaḥ' iti
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhibuddhiṃ prati
viśeṣaṇatāvacchedakaprakārakanirṇayavidhayā 'vahnivyāpyadhūmavān
parvataḥ' iti parāmarśasya kāraṇatve 'pi na tatrātivyāptiḥ/
pakṣatāsahakṛtaparāmarśajanyatvasya asattvena ativyāpterabhāvāt iti
saṅkṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: Since in generating perception-following-doubt there is no purpose in <s>pakṣatā</s> (thesis-hood) being an auxiliary of <s>parāmarśa</s>, because what is intended is 'being produced by <s>parāmarśa</s> assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s>,' there is no over-extension — he says '<s>pakṣatā</s>' and so forth. By this, even regarding the cognition apprehending qualified-qualificand relation of the form 'this region has a mountain possessing smoke pervaded by fire,' although <s>parāmarśa</s> of the form 'the mountain possesses smoke pervaded by fire' is a cause — in the manner of a determinative cognition whose qualifier-hood-delimiting-property is a mode — there is no over-extension there either. This is because over-extension is absent due to the absence of the property of being produced by <s>parāmarśa</s> assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s> — this is the summary.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
vilakṣaṇapramātvāditi/ pratyakṣapramiteḥ yat karaṇaṃ indriyaṃ
tadapekṣayā vilakṣaṇena parāmarśātmakena kāraṇena janyatvāt
anumitervilakṣaṇapramātvamiti bhāvaḥ/ pramāṇāntaratvamiti/
pratyakṣāpekṣayā atiriktapramāṇatvamityarthaḥ/ dīpikāyām nanvityādinā
granthena yatra dūre ūrdhvavyaktidarśanānantaraṃ 'sthāṇurvā puruṣo vā
' iti saṃśayaḥ tataḥ 'puruṣatvavyāpyakarādimān' iti
vyāpyadharmavattājñānarūpaḥ parāmarśaḥ tataḥ 'ayaṃ puruṣa' iti pratyakṣam,
tasmin pratyakṣe
parāmarśajanyatvaviśiṣṭajñānatvarūpasyānumitilakṣaṇasyātivyāptiḥ
āśaṅkitā/ tadidaṃ na saṅgacchate/ saṃśayarūpaviparītajñānānantaraṃ
'ayaṃ puruṣaḥ' iti pratyakṣasyaiva asaṃbhavāt/ tadvattābuddhiṃ prati
tadabhāvavattājñānasya pratibandhakatvāditi śaṅkāyāṃ satyapi
viparītajñāne yadi viśeṣadarśanaṃ syāt tarhi tasya viśeṣadarśanasya
pratyakṣajanakatvaṃ bhavatīti 1viśeṣadarśanasyeti/
vyāpyadharmadarśanasyetyarthaḥ/ prakṛte 'puruṣatvavyāpyakarādimān
ayam' iti parāmarśo vivakṣitaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Being a valid cognition of a different kind' means: because <s>anumiti</s> is produced by a cause of a different kind, namely of the nature of <s>parāmarśa</s>, relative to the sense organ which is the instrument of perceptual valid cognition — this is the purport of <s>anumiti</s> being a valid cognition of a different kind. 'Being a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>' means: being a <s>pramāṇa</s> additional to <s>pratyakṣa</s>. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, by the passage beginning with 'now,' where after seeing an object at a distance or above, there is doubt 'is it a post or a person?', then <s>parāmarśa</s> of the nature of cognition of possessing the pervaded property, namely 'it possesses hands and such features pervaded by person-hood,' and from that, perception of the form 'this is a person' — the over-extension of the definition of <s>anumiti</s>, namely being a cognition qualified by being produced by <s>parāmarśa</s>, to that perception was raised as an objection. This does not hold. Because after an erroneous cognition in the form of doubt, the perception 'this is a person' is itself impossible — since the cognition of possessing a certain property is an obstructor to the cognition of possessing the absence of that property. Even so, if there were specific perception in the case of erroneous cognition, then that specific perception would have the capacity to generate perceptual cognition — hence 'of specific perception.' The meaning is: of the perception of the pervaded property. In the present context, the <s>parāmarśa</s> intended is 'this possesses hands and such features pervaded by person-hood.'

children.text:
bhāvadvayakoṭiketi/
sthāṇutvapuruṣatvāśyaṃ yat bhāvarūpaṃ dharmadvayaṃ
tatprakārakasaṃśayetyarthaḥ/ sthāṇutvatadabhāveti/ sthāṇutvaṃ tadabhāvaḥ
puruṣatvaṃ tadabhāvaśceti catuṣprakārakasaṃśayetyarthaḥ/ 'sthāṇurvā na
vā, puruṣo vā na vā' iti saṃśayasyākāraḥ/ 2dvikoṭikasaṃśayadvayaṃ
vātra vivakṣitam/ pramāṇābhāvāditi/ tatrānumitireva jāyata ityatra
pramāṇābhāvādityarthaḥ/ tathā ca 'ayaṃ puruṣaḥ' iti
niścayasyānumititve 'puruṣaṃ sākṣātkaromi' iti
sākṣātkāratvāvagāhī anuvyavasāyo nopapadyate/ anumititvāvagāhī
'puruṣamanuminomi' iti anuvyavasāya eva syāt/ ato
nānumititvaṃ tasya niścayasya, api tu pratyakṣatvameveti alakṣye tatra
lakṣaṇasattvāt anumitilakṣaṇasyātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ dīpikāyāṃ
pakṣatāsahakṛteti/ tathā ca parāmarśajanyatvamātraṃ nānumiterlakṣaṇam/
api tu pakṣatāsahakṛto yaḥ parāmarśaḥ tajjanyatvam/
saṃśayottarapratyakṣe tu parāmarśasya janakatve 'pi
children.translated_text: 'Having the two positive alternatives as its poles' — the meaning is: a doubt having as its qualifier-modes the two positive properties of post-hood and person-hood. 'Post-hood and the absence of that' — the meaning is: a doubt having four qualifier-modes: post-hood, the absence of that [i.e. of post-hood], person-hood, and the absence of that [i.e. of person-hood]. The form of the doubt is: 'Is it a post or not? Is it a person or not?' [Alternatively,] what is intended here is two doubts each having two poles. 'Because of the absence of a means of valid knowledge' — the meaning is: because there is no means of valid knowledge that mere inference arises there. And accordingly, if the ascertainment 'this is a person' were inferential, the introspective cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) 'I directly perceive a person' — which apprehends direct perceptuality — would be impossible. There would instead be only the introspective cognition apprehending inferential-ness: 'I infer a person.' Therefore, that ascertainment does not have inferential-ness but rather perceptual-ness alone. And since the definition of inference [namely, being generated by reflective judgment] is present in what is not a definiendum [i.e. in perception], there is over-extension of the definition of inference — this is the purport. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s> (subject-hood)' — and accordingly, mere being-generated-by-reflective-judgment is not the definition of inference; rather, being generated by a reflective judgment that is assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s> [is the definition]. In post-doubt-resolved perception, even though reflective judgment has causal efficacy,

children.text:
1. anena
matāntaramapyastīti darśitam/ tathā hi - saṃśayottarapratyakṣamātre
viśeṣadarśanaṃ na hetuḥ, andhakāre ghaṭasaṃśayottarapratyakṣasya
viśeṣadarśanaṃ vināpi ālokasamavadhānamātreṇaivopapatteḥ/ tathāpi
yatra viśeṣādarśanādidoṣādhīnaḥ saṃśayaḥ taduttarapratyakṣe tasya
hetutvam/ uktasthale ca vyañjakābhāvādhīnaḥ saṃśaya iti/ adhikaṃ
tattvacintāmaṇau prāmāṇyotpattivāde tadvyākhyāne prakāśe ca
draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] By this, another view too is indicated. Namely: in mere post-doubt-resolved perception, the seeing of a distinguishing feature is not the cause; since a post-doubt-resolved perception in darkness can be explained merely by the proximity of light, without the seeing of any distinguishing feature. Nevertheless, where the doubt is dependent on the defect of non-seeing of a distinguishing feature, the seeing [of the feature] is the cause of the subsequent perception. And in the stated case, the doubt is dependent on the absence of the revealer [i.e. light]. More should be seen in the <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s>, in the section on the origin of validity (<s>prāmāṇyotpattivāda</s>), and in its commentary the <s>Prakāśa</s>.

children.text:
2. dvikoṭiketi/
sthāṇurvā na vetyākārakaḥ ekaḥ saṃśayaḥ, puruṣo na vetyākārakaḥ
aparaḥ saṃśaya iti saṃśayadvayamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Two-poled' — the meaning is: two doubts — one of the form 'is it a post or not?' and the other of the form 'is it a person or not?'

children.text:
pakṣatāyāḥ
nopayogitvam, pramāṇābhāvāt; siddhisattve 'pi
dhārāvāhikapratyakṣotpattyā siddhyabhāvarūpāyāḥ pakṣatāyāḥ
pratyakṣahetutvāsambhavācca/ tathā ca
pakṣatāsahakṛtaparāmarśajanayatvābhāvāt nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
tadāha prakāśikāyām saṃśayottarapratyakṣe jananīya iti/
prayojanābhāveneti/ pakṣatāyāḥ sahakāritvānaṅgīkāre
anupapattyabhāvenetyarthaḥ/ eteneti/ vakṣyamāṇahetunā ityarthaḥ/ yadi
parāmarśajanyatvamātram anumiterlakṣaṇaṃ syāt tadā
'vahnivyāpyadhūmavatparvatavānayaṃ deśaḥ' ityākārakaṃ
vanhivyāpyadhūmaviśiṣṭaparvatavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhipratyakṣaṃ prati
'vahnivyāpyadhūmavānayaṃ parvataḥ' ityākārakaparāmarśasya
viśeṣaṇatāvacchedakībhūtaḥ yaḥ dhūmaḥ tatprakārakaniścayatvena hetutayā
tādṛśaviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhipratyakṣe 'pi parāmarśajanyatvarūpasya
anumitilakṣaṇasya sattvāt ativyāptiḥ prasaktā/ sāpi
pakṣatāsahakṛtaparāmarśajanyatvasya anumitilakṣaṇatavāt vārayituṃ
śakyata iti bhāvaḥ/ tādṛśapratyakṣasya 1pakṣatājanyatvābhāvāt/
children.translated_text: <s>Pakṣatā</s> (subject-hood) is not useful, because of the absence of a means of valid knowledge [for it being a cause]; and also because, even when establishment (<s>siddhi</s>) exists, inference is seen to arise from the desire to establish, and since establishment being present means that <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of absence-of-establishment cannot be a cause of perception due to the production of continuous perceptual cognition (<s>dhārāvāhikapratyakṣa</s>). And accordingly, since the reflective judgment assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s> does not generate [the cognition], there is no over-extension — this is the purport. This is stated in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'in post-doubt-resolved perception, is to be generated.' 'Because of the absence of purpose' — the meaning is: because of the absence of impossibility [that would require] accepting <s>pakṣatā</s> as an auxiliary cause. 'By this' — the meaning is: by the reason to be stated. If mere being-generated-by-reflective-judgment were the definition of inference, then with respect to the perception that apprehends the qualification of the mountain by the property of possessing fire and possessing smoke pervaded by fire, since the reflective judgment of the form 'this mountain possesses smoke pervaded by fire' — where the smoke that has become the delimiting property of qualifier-hood is [part of] the qualifier-mode — serves as a cause by virtue of being a determinate cognition whose qualifier-mode is that [smoke], over-extension of the definition of inference in the form of being-generated-by-reflective-judgment would result even in that perception apprehending qualified-qualification. But even that can be averted by the definition of inference being: generated by a reflective judgment assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s> — this is the purport. Since such perception lacks being-generated-by-<s>pakṣatā</s>.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: pakṣatālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Pakṣatā</s> (Subject-hood)

children.text:
siṣādhayiṣāvirahaviśiṣṭasiddhyabhāvaḥ pakṣatā/ sādhyasiddhiḥ
anumitipratibandhikā/ siddhisattve 'pi 'anuminuyām'
itīcchāyāmanumitidarśanāt siṣādhayiṣā uttejikā/ tataśca
uttajakābhāvaviśiṣṭamaṇyabhāvasya
children.translated_text: The absence of establishment (<s>siddhi</s>) qualified by the absence of the desire to establish (<s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>) is <s>pakṣatā</s> (subject-hood). Establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) obstructs inference. Even when establishment exists, since inference is observed to occur from the desire 'let me infer,' <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> (the desire to establish) serves as a stimulator (<s>uttejikā</s>). And accordingly, the absence of the inhibitor (<s>uttejaka</s>) qualified by

children.text:
1. yadyapi
dhyāpyapakṣobhayavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhijñānatvarūpaṃ yat parāmarśatva
tadavacchinnajanakatānirūpitajanyatāśālijñānatvamanumiterlakṣaṇami tyaktāvapi
uktaviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhipratyakṣe 'tivyāptivāraṇaṃ sambhavati
tādṛśabuddhau parāmarśasya viśeṣaṇatāvacchedakaprakārakanirṇayatvenaiva
hetutvena uktaparāmarśatvena hetutvābhāvāt/ tathāpi
saṃśayottarapratyakṣe vyāpyapakṣavaiśiṣṭhyāvagāhijñānatvena
vyāpyadarśanajanyatvasattvāt ativyāpteḥ
pakṣatāsahakṛtaparāmarśajanyatvavivakṣaṇanaiva bāraṇīyatā tenaiva
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhipratyakṣavāraṇasambhavāt
uktaparāmarśatvāvacchinnajanakatā na niveśyeti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] Although, even when the definition of inference is stated as: being generated by a cognition whose generative-hood is delimited by the reflective-judgment-hood having the form of apprehending the qualification of the subject by both the pervader and the probandum — it is possible to avert over-extension in the said perception apprehending qualified-qualification, because in such cognition, the reflective judgment serves as a cause through its being a determinate cognition whose qualifier-mode is the delimitor of qualifier-hood, and not through the said reflective-judgment-hood. Nevertheless, since in post-doubt-resolved perception, being-generated with generative-hood delimited by the said pervader-subject-qualification-apprehending-cognition-hood exists — there being over-extension, it must be averted only through the specification 'generated by reflective judgment assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s>'; and since that very specification also suffices to avert [the over-extension] in the perception apprehending qualified-qualification, the generative-hood delimited by the said reflective-judgment-hood should not be included — this is the purport.

children.text:
dāhakāraṇatvavat
siṣādhayiṣāvirahaviśiṣṭasiddhyabhāvasyāpyanumitikāraṇatvam/
children.translated_text: Just as in the case of burning, the absence of establishment qualified by the absence of the desire to establish also serves as a cause of inference.

children.text:
yadyapi sādhyasaṃśayasya
pakṣatātve 'pi sādhyaniścayakāle anumitivāraṇaṃ sambhavati, tathāpi
ghanagarjitena meghānumitau vyabhicāraḥ/ ataḥ anyādṛśīṃ pakṣatāmāha -
siṣādhayiṣeti/ rsiṣādhayiṣāyāḥ sādhyānumitīcchāyāḥ samavāyena yaḥ
abhāvaḥ svarūpasamavāyobhavaghaṭitasāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena
tadviśiṣṭāyāḥ siddheḥ samavāyena abhāva ityarthaḥ/ sādhyasiddhiḥ -
pakṣatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭe
sādhyatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭasādhyavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhiniścayaḥ/ siddhau
siṣādhayiṣāvirahavaiśiṣṭyaniveśanasya
children.translated_text: Even though, if doubt about the probandum were <s>pakṣatā</s>, it would be possible to avert inference at the time of the ascertainment of the probandum, nevertheless in the inference of clouds from loud thunder, there would be deviation [from this definition]. Therefore he states a different kind of <s>pakṣatā</s>: '<s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>' and so forth. The absence through the relation of inherence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> — the desire to infer the probandum — is [the first part]; and the absence through the relation of inherence of establishment qualified by <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> through the relation of co-referentiality constituted by self-linking-relation-and-inherence — is [the second part]; this is the meaning. 'Establishment of the <s>sādhya</s>' — an ascertainment apprehending the qualification of the <s>sādhya</s> qualified by the delimiting property of <s>sādhya</s>-hood, by that which is qualified by the delimiting property of <s>pakṣatā</s>. The purpose of including the qualification by the absence of the desire to establish in [the definition of] establishment

children.text:
prayojanaṃ darśayati -
siddhisattve 'pīti/ atra siddhiśca 'parvato vahnimān
vahnivyāpyadhūmavāṃśca' iti samūhālambanarūpā/ ataḥ
parāmarśasampattiriti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: he shows: 'even when establishment exists' and so forth. Here, the establishment has the form of a cognition grasping both 'the mountain has fire' and 'it has smoke pervaded by fire' — a collective cognition. Therefore, the reflective judgment is complete — this should be noted.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
'sādhyasaṃśayaḥ
pakṣatā' iti prācīnoktyupekṣāyāḥ bījamāha - yadyapītyādinā/
sādhyaniścayarūpasiddhikāle 'numitivāraṇaṃ hi pakṣatāyāḥ
anumitihetutvāṅgīkārasya uddeśyam/ tattu sādhyasaṃśayasya
pakṣatātve 'pi nirvahati/ sādhyaniścayakāle sādhyasaṃśayarūpapakṣatāyāḥ
abhāvādeva nānumitiḥ ityevaṃrītyā anumitivāraṇasambhavāt tathā
ca sādhyasaṃśaya eva pakṣatā astu iti śaṅkiturbhāvaḥ/ tathāpīti/
sādhyasaṃśayarūpapakṣatāyāḥ nānumitihetutvam/ vināpi sādhyasaṃśayaṃ
ghanagarjanaśravaṇena 1meghānumitteḥ vyatirekavyabhicārāditi
samādhāturāśayaḥ/ vyabhicāra iti/ kāraṇābhāve 'pi kāryotpattirūpo
vyatirekavyabhicāro 'tra
children.translated_text: He states the seed for setting aside the ancient statement '<s>sādhyasaṃśaya</s> (doubt about the probandum) is <s>pakṣatā</s>': 'although' and so forth. The purpose of accepting <s>pakṣatā</s> as a cause of inference is to avert inference at the time of the establishment of the probandum (<s>sādhyaniścaya</s>). And that works even if doubt about the probandum is <s>pakṣatā</s>: at the time of the ascertainment of the probandum, since the <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of doubt about the probandum is absent, there is no inference — in this manner the aversion of inference is possible. And accordingly, let doubt about the probandum itself be <s>pakṣatā</s> — this is the intent of the doubter. 'Nevertheless' — <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of doubt about the probandum is not a cause of inference; because of the negative-concomitance deviation that inference of clouds occurs through hearing loud thunder even without doubt about the probandum — this is the intent of the respondent. 'Deviation' — what is intended here is the negative-concomitance deviation: the production of the effect even in the absence of the cause.

children.text:
vivakṣitaḥ/
anyādṛśīmiti/ sādhyasaṃśayādanyavidhāmityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Of a different kind' — the meaning is: of a different form from doubt about the probandum.

children.text:
1. ayaṃ pradeśaḥ
meghavān dhanagarjajavattvādityanumānamatra vivakṣitam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] The inference intended here is: 'this region has clouds, because of possessing loud thunder' and so forth.

children.text:
dīpikāyām
siṣādhayiṣāvirahaviśiṣṭetyādi/ yatra sādhyaniścayarūpā siddhirasti

children.translated_text: present there. Therefore, the qualifier '<s>siṣādhayiṣāvirahaviśiṣṭa</s>' (qualified by the absence of the desire to establish) is given to establishment. In the said case, since <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> is present, the qualifier in the form of the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> is absent; hence, since the absence of establishment qualified by the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> remains intact, <s>pakṣatā</s> holds. And thus the result is that <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> is a stimulator. And stimulator-hood is: being the promoter of the production of the effect at the time of the co-presence of the inhibitor. Since even at the time of the presence of the inhibitor in the form of establishment, <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> serves as the promoter of the production of the effect in the form of inference — it has stimulator-hood; just as mantras and the like have stimulator-hood by promoting the production of burning at the time of the inhibitor in the form of a gem. Since the absence of the inhibitor qualified by the absence of the stimulator is a cause for the production of the effect, the absence of establishment qualified by the absence of the desire to establish is a cause of inference — this is the purport. <s>Siṣādhayiṣā</s> is the desire whose content is the inference of the probandum.

children.translated_text: The absence of the desire to establish is an absence whose counter-positive-hood is not determined by <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>. Therein, the counter-positive-hood must be qualified by the delimitation through the relation of inherence. Otherwise, even where establishment and the desire to establish both exist, since <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> is absent through the relation of conjunction, the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the conjunction-relation and determined by <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> — since the establishment qualified by that [absence] exists — the <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of the absence of that would not hold. But when that [inherence qualification] is included, since <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> exists through inherence there, the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by inherence and determined by <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> — the qualifier in that form — is absent; hence the <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of the absence of establishment qualified by the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> holds. And thus, the qualification of establishment by the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> is through the relation of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). Otherwise, if the qualification were through self-linking relation, then even when <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> is present, since the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> exists through self-linking relation in establishment — the establishment qualified by the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> would exist — and the <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of the absence of that would be impossible. Therefore the qualification must be through co-referentiality. And co-referentiality is: residing in one's own substratum. One's-own-substratum-hood is through self-linking relation; the residing determined by one's own substratum is through inherence. And accordingly, <s>pakṣatā</s> is the absence of establishment qualified by the absence of the desire to establish through the relation of co-referentiality in the form of superstratum-hood determined by the substratum-hood determined by the inherence-relation, and determined by the self-linking-relation. 'Self' is the absence of the desire to establish; its substratum through self-linking relation is the self (<s>ātman</s>); the establishment residing therein through inherence — the absence of that. Even without the inclusion of self-linking relation [in the substratum-hood], at the time of the desire to establish, since the establishment has residence through the co-referentiality-relation of co-content-of-a-single-cognition in the self which is the substratum of the absence of the desire to establish — since the establishment qualified by the absence of the desire to establish through such residence-relation exists — the <s>pakṣatā</s> [in the form of its absence] would be impossible. With the inclusion of self-linking relation, the substratum of the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> is not the self who possesses <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>, but rather a different self; the establishment residing in that [other self] does not reside in this self. Hence, since the absence of residence through the co-referentiality-relation exists for the establishment qualified by the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>, there is no impossibility of <s>pakṣatā</s>. Similarly, without the inclusion of inherence in the residence-relation, even though the establishment resides through inherence in the self that is the substratum of the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>, since it does not reside through conjunction and the like, the co-referentiality in the form of residence delimited by a relation other than inherence does not exist for the establishment. And the <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of the absence of the qualified [establishment] through the co-referentiality relation
