children.translated_text: <s>pakṣatā</s> (thesis-hood) would undesirably follow. Therefore, the property of being delimited by the relation of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) is stipulated in the <s>vṛtti</s> (occurrence) that constitutes <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-location). Similarly, the absence of <s>siddhi</s> (established cognition) means an absence whose counterpositive-hood is determined by the established cognition. In that counterpositive-hood, delimitation by the relation of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) must be stipulated. Otherwise, even at the time of established cognition, by taking an absence of established cognition delimited by some other relation, <s>pakṣatā</s> (thesis-hood) would undesirably follow. Having intended all this, he states in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'of the desire to establish, of the desire for the inference to be established' and so forth. 'Constituted by both <s>svarūpa</s> (intrinsic) and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence)' — the meaning is that in the substratum-hood constituting <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-location), delimitation by the <s>svarūpa</s> (intrinsic) relation must be stipulated, and in the <s>vṛttitā</s> (occurrence-hood), delimitation by the <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) relation must be stipulated. 'The absence by inherence of <s>siddhi</s>' — the meaning is: an absence whose counterpositive-hood is delimited by the relation of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) residing in the established cognition. 'Qualified by the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s>' and so forth — the meaning is: a determinate cognition possessing qualifier-hood residing in the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) delimited by the delimitor of <s>sādhyatā</s> (probandum-hood), which is determined by the qualificand-hood residing in the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) delimited by the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s> (thesis-hood). When, through substance-hood, there is a determinate cognition pervading the mountain of the form 'substance possesses fire,' since the inference 'the mountain possesses fire' arises, in order to prevent the determinate cognition of the form 'substance possesses fire' from being an obstacle to the inference 'the mountain possesses fire,' in the qualificand-hood residing in the <s>pakṣa</s>,

children.translated_text: co-occur. And that is difficult to achieve. For consider: where first there is established cognition, then the desire to establish, then <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection), and then <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition) — there, at the moment of <s>parāmarśa</s>, since the established cognition has already ceased, inference is justified by the very absence of the obstruction, so the qualification 'being qualified by the absence of desire to establish' is pointless. Where the desire to establish, the established cognition, and <s>parāmarśa</s> occur in sequence, there, at the moment of <s>parāmarśa</s>, since the desire to establish has ceased, established cognition qualified by the absence of desire to establish indeed obtains, so even with the stipulation of 'being qualified by the absence of desire to establish,' <s>pakṣatā</s> (thesis-hood) does not hold. And where <s>parāmarśa</s>, established cognition, and the desire to establish occur in sequence, there, at the moment of the desire to establish, since <s>parāmarśa</s> has ceased, inference does not arise due to the absence of the cause in the form of <s>parāmarśa</s>. Nor is it accepted that two cognitions, or a cognition and a desire, arise at the same moment. And so, how can the meaningfulness of 'being qualified by the absence of desire to establish' be maintained? — anticipating this objection, he says beginning with 'here the established cognition' and so forth. The intended <s>siddhi</s> (established cognition) that is a constituent of <s>pakṣatā</s> is a composite apprehension (<s>samūhālambana</s>) grasping both fire and smoke which is pervaded by fire, of the form 'the mountain possesses fire and possesses smoke pervaded by fire.' This very cognition, being of the nature of a determinate cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and also of the nature of a determinate cognition of what is pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s>, is called <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection) that is of the nature of established cognition. And accordingly, where first there is a <s>parāmarśa</s> of the nature of established cognition of the aforementioned form, then the desire to establish, and then inference — there, at the second moment, since the established cognition persists, mere absence of established cognition being <s>pakṣatā</s> would not work. Therefore, 'being qualified by the absence of desire to establish' is a qualification of the established cognition. In that case, since the desire to establish is present, the qualification in the form of the absence of desire to establish is absent, and hence <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of the absence of the qualified entity holds — thus the meaningfulness of that qualification is to be justified. This is the purport. 'Therefore there is the co-occurrence of <s>parāmarśa</s>' — the meaning is: at the moment immediately preceding inference, there is the co-occurrence of established cognition, the desire to establish, and <s>parāmarśa</s>.

children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: parāmarśalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection)

children.text:
vyāptiviśiṣṭapakṣadharmatājñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ/ yathā
'vahnivyāpyadhūmavān ayaṃ parvataḥ' iti jñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ/ tajjanyaṃ
'parvato vahnimān' iti jñānamanumitiḥ/
children.translated_text: The cognition of the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) as qualified by <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection). For example, the cognition 'this mountain possesses smoke which is pervaded by fire' is <s>parāmarśa</s>. The cognition 'the mountain possesses fire' that arises from that is <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:

vyāptīti/ vyāptiviṣayakaṃ yat pakṣadharmatājñānaṃ sa parāmarśa
ityarthaḥ/ parāmarśamabhinīya darśayati - yatheti/ anumitimabhinīya
darśayati - tajjanyamiti/ parāmarśajanyamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection) — '<s>vyāpti</s>' and so forth. A cognition of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (the property of belonging to the thesis-locus) that has <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) as its content is <s>parāmarśa</s> — this is the meaning. Having exemplified <s>parāmarśa</s>, he shows — 'for example' and so forth. Having exemplified <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition), he shows — 'born from that' and so forth. The meaning is: born from <s>parāmarśa</s>.

pakṣadharmatā vyāptiviśiṣṭapakṣadharmatā tajjñānamiti
saptamītatpuruṣāṅgīkāre vyabhicāriliṅgakānumitau
vyāptiviśiṣṭapakṣadharmatājñānajanyatvābhāvena avyāptiḥ; ataḥ
children.translated_text: In 'the cognition of the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> as qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>,' if one accepts a locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound meaning 'the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> that is qualified by <s>vyāpti</s> — the cognition thereof,' then in the case of inference with a deviant <s>liṅga</s> (probans), since there is no cognition born of the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> qualified by genuine <s>vyāpti</s>, there would be under-extension. Therefore,

children.text:
vyāptiviśiṣṭapadasya
vyāptiviṣayaketyarthamavalambya jñānāntapadena
karmadhārayamaṅgīkaroti - vyāptiviṣayakamiti/
vyāptyavacchinna-prakāratānirūpita -
pakṣatāvacchedakāvacchinna-viśeṣyatāśāliniścayaḥ parāmarśa iti tu
nirgalitārthaḥ/ abhinīya - abhilāpakaśabdamuccārya/
children.translated_text: accepting the word '<s>vyāpti</s>-qualified' in the sense of 'having <s>vyāpti</s> as its content,' he construes it as a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound with the word 'cognition' — 'having <s>vyāpti</s> as its content' and so forth. The refined meaning is: <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection) is a determinate cognition possessing qualificand-hood residing in the <s>pakṣa</s> delimited by the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s> (thesis-hood), which is determined by qualifier-hood delimited by <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). '<s>Abhinīya</s>' means: having uttered the expressive word.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
vyāptiviśiṣṭapakṣadharmatājñānamityatretyādi/ yatra liṅgaṃ
sādhyavyabhicāri bhavati tatrāpi vyāptyaśe bhramātmakāt
'dhūmavyāpyavahnimānayaṃ parvataḥ' iti parāmarśāt 'parvato
dhūmavān' ityanumitiḥ jāyate/ yadi tu vastuto vyāptiviśiṣṭe
pakṣadharmatvāvagāhi jñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ tajjanyatvaṃ anumiterlakṣaṇamucyeta
tarhi uktaparāmarśasya vyāptiviśiṣṭe tadavagāhitvābhāve
parāmarśatvābhāvāt tajjanyajñānasya anumititvaṃ na syāt/ ataḥ
vyāptiviṣayakaṃ yat pakṣadharmatvāvagāhi jñānaṃ tat parāmarśaḥ/
uktabhramātmakajñānasya vyāptiviṣayakatvamakṣatamiti parāmarśarūpatā, ata
children.translated_text: 'In the cognition of the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> as qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>' and so forth. Even where the <s>liṅga</s> (probans) deviates from the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), from an erroneous <s>parāmarśa</s> of the form 'this mountain possesses smoke pervaded by fire,' the inference 'the mountain possesses fire' arises. If, however, one were to say that <s>parāmarśa</s> is a cognition grasping the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> that is in reality qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>, and that the definition of <s>anumiti</s> is being born from such a <s>parāmarśa</s>, then since the said <s>parāmarśa</s> does not actually grasp something qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>, it would lack <s>parāmarśa</s>-hood, and the cognition born from it would not have <s>anumiti</s>-hood. Therefore, <s>parāmarśa</s> is a cognition that has <s>vyāpti</s> as its content and grasps the property of the <s>pakṣa</s>. Since the <s>vyāpti</s>-as-content character of the aforementioned erroneous cognition remains intact, its character as <s>parāmarśa</s> is preserved, and therefore

children.text:
eva tajjanyajñānasya
parāmarśajanyatvarūpānumitilakṣaṇākrāntatayā anumititvamapyupapadyata
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: the cognition born from it, being covered by the definition of <s>anumiti</s> which consists in being born from <s>parāmarśa</s>, also has its <s>anumiti</s>-hood justified. This is the purport.

children.text:
nanu vyāptiviṣayakaṃ
pakṣasambandhāvagāhi ca jñānaṃ parāmarśa iti parāmarśalakṣaṇakathane 'pi
'dhūmo vahnivyāpyaḥ dhūmavāṃśca parvataḥ'
ityākārakasamūhālambanajñānasyāpi vyāptiviṣayakatvāt
pakṣasambandhaviṣayakatvācca parāmarśatvāpattirityata āha -
vyāptyavacchinneti/ vyāptyavacchinna yā hetuniṣṭhā prakāratā
tannirūpitā yā pakṣatāvacchedakāvacchinnā pakṣaniṣṭhā viśeṣyatā
tannirūpako niścayaḥ parāmarśa ityarthaḥ/ bhavati ca
'vahnivyāpyadhūmavān parvata' iti niścayaḥ tādṛśaḥ/
parvataniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitāyāḥ dhūmaniṣṭhāyāḥ prakāratāyāḥ
vyāptyavacchinnatvāt/ vyāptyavacchinnatvaṃ ca
sādhyaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitavyāptiniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitatvam/ tena
'vyāpyadhūmavān parvataḥ' iti jñāne nātivyāptiḥ/ 'dhūmo
vahnivyāpyaḥ dhūmavāṃśca parvataḥ' iti
samūhālambanajñānīyadhūmaniṣṭhaprakāratāyāṃ
vyāptiniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitatvaṃ nāsti, dhūmāṃśe vyāpteḥ
prakāratayā abhānāt/ ato na tatrātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ tathā ca
sādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnasādhyaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitavyāptiniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitahetutāvacchedakāvacchinna-
children.translated_text: Objection: Even if the definition of <s>parāmarśa</s> is stated as 'a cognition that has <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) as its content and grasps the relation of the <s>pakṣa</s>,' a composite apprehension (<s>samūhālambana</s>) of the form 'smoke is pervaded by fire and the mountain possesses smoke' would also have <s>vyāpti</s> as its content and have the relation of the <s>pakṣa</s> as its content, so the undesirable consequence of its being a <s>parāmarśa</s> would follow. Anticipating this, he says — 'delimited by <s>vyāpti</s>' and so forth. The meaning is: <s>parāmarśa</s> is a determinate cognition whose qualificand-hood resides in the <s>pakṣa</s>, delimited by the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s>, and determined by the qualifier-hood residing in the <s>hetu</s> (probans) that is delimited by <s>vyāpti</s>. And the cognition 'the mountain possesses smoke pervaded by fire' is indeed of such a kind, because the qualifier-hood residing in smoke, which is determined by the qualificand-hood residing in the mountain, is delimited by <s>vyāpti</s>. The delimitation by <s>vyāpti</s> means: being determined by the qualifier-hood residing in <s>vyāpti</s> that is itself determined by the qualifier-hood residing in the <s>sādhya</s>. Hence, in the cognition 'the mountain possesses smoke that is pervaded,' there is no over-extension. In the composite apprehension 'smoke is pervaded by fire, and the mountain possesses smoke,' the qualifier-hood residing in the smoke-portion is not determined by qualifier-hood residing in <s>vyāpti</s>, because in the smoke-portion, <s>vyāpti</s> does not appear as a qualifier. Therefore, there is no over-extension to that case. This is the purport. And accordingly,

children.text:
hetuniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitapakṣatāvacchedakāvacchinnapakṣaniṣṭhaviśeṣyatāśāliniścayaḥ
parāmarśa iti niṣkarṣaḥ/ tena 'dravyavyāpyadhmavān parvataḥ',
'vahnivyāpyadravyavān parvataḥ' 'vahnivyāpyadhūmavaddravyam'
ityādiniścayānāṃ 'parvato vahnimān'
ityanumitihetubhūtaparāmarśatvaṃ na prasajyata ityavadheyam/
nirgalitārtha iti/ niṣkṛṣṭārtha ityarthaḥ/
abhilāpakaśabdamuccāryeti/ ākārapradarśakaśabdamuccāryetyarthaḥ/
kāyikaceṣṭārūpasyābhinayasyātrāsambhavāt/
children.translated_text: <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection) is, in conclusion, a determinate cognition possessing qualificand-hood residing in the <s>pakṣa</s> delimited by the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s>, determined by qualifier-hood residing in the <s>hetu</s> delimited by the delimitor of <s>hetutā</s> (probans-hood), which is itself determined by qualifier-hood residing in <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) determined by qualifier-hood residing in the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) delimited by the delimitor of <s>sādhyatā</s> (probandum-hood). Hence, determinate cognitions such as 'the mountain possesses smoke pervaded by substance,' 'the mountain possesses substance pervaded by fire,' and 'the substance possessing smoke pervaded by fire' do not qualify as <s>parāmarśa</s> that is the cause of the inference 'the mountain possesses fire' — this should be noted. 'The refined meaning' means: the extracted meaning. 'Having uttered the expressive word' means: having uttered the word that displays the form — because physical gestures as a mode of demonstration are not possible here.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: vyāptilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion)

children.text:
yatra dhūmaḥ tatra
agniḥ iti sāhacaryaniyamaḥ vyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: The invariable co-occurrence — 'where there is smoke, there is fire' — is <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
vyāptilakṣaṇamāha -
yatreti/ yatra dhūmastatrāgniriti vyāpterabhinayaḥ/ sāhacaryaniyamaḥ
iti lakṣaṇam/ sāhacaryaṃ sāmānādhiṅkaraṇyam, tasya niyamaḥ/
hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvāpratiyogisādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ
vyāptirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) — 'where' and so forth. 'Where there is smoke, there is fire' is the exemplification of <s>vyāpti</s>. 'Invariable co-occurrence' is the definition. Co-occurrence means <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-location); its invariability is what is meant. The meaning is: <s>vyāpti</s> is the co-location with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) that is not a counterpositive of a universal absence co-located with the <s>hetu</s> (probans).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
niyatasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ sādhyābhāvavadavṛttitvādirūpaṃ na
sambhavati; 'idaṃ vācyam jñeyatvāt' ityādau avyāpteḥ/
sādhyābhāvāprasiddherityālocyāha - hetusamānādhikaraṇeti/
'vahnimān dhūmāt' ityādau dhūmasamānādhikaraṇe yo 'tyantābhāvaḥ
ghaṭātyantābhāvaḥ, tadapratiyogī vahniḥ tatsāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ dhūme
astīti lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ 'dhūmavān vahneḥ' ityādau tu
dhūmasāmānyābhāvasyāpi hetusamānādhikaraṇatayā tatpratiyogyeva
dhūma iti nātivyāptiḥ/ na ca 'vahnimān dhūmāt' ityādau
tattadvahnyabhāvasya cālinīnyāyena dhūmasamānādhikaraṇatayā
tādṛśābhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ na kasyāpi vahnerityativyāptiriti
vācyam, apratiyogisādhyetyasya
pratiyogitānavacchedaka-sādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnetyarthatātparyaṅkatayādoṣāt/
pratiyogitāyāṃ sādhyatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśanīyam/
tena 'vahnimān dhūmāt' ityādau samavāyena
vahnitvāvacchinna-pratiyogitākābhāvasya dhūmasamānādhikaraṇatve 'pi na
kṣatiḥ/ hetupadaṃ hetutāvacchedakāvacchinnaparam/ ataḥ 'dravyam
viśiṣṭasattvāt' ityādau viśiṣṭasya śuddhānatirekitayā
hetvadhikaraṇaguṇādiniṣṭhatve 'pi dravyatvābhāvasya nāvyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: Invariable co-location in the form of 'non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>' and so forth is not tenable, because of under-extension in cases such as 'this is expressible, because it is knowable.' Since the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is not established — reflecting thus, he says: 'co-located with the <s>hetu</s>' and so forth. In cases such as 'possessing fire, from smoke,' a universal absence co-located with smoke — such as the universal absence of a pot — the <s>sādhya</s> fire that is not the counterpositive of that, its co-location in smoke exists — this is the application of the definition. In cases such as 'possessing smoke, from fire,' however, since even the universal absence of smoke-universal is co-located with the <s>hetu</s>, smoke itself is a counterpositive of that, so there is no over-extension. Nor should one object that in cases such as 'possessing fire, from smoke,' since each particular fire-absence is co-located with smoke by the <s>cālinī</s> principle, no fire at all would have the property of not being a counterpositive of such absence, leading to over-extension — because the intended meaning of 'the <s>sādhya</s> that is not a counterpositive' is: '<s>sādhya</s> delimited by the delimitor of <s>sādhyatā</s> (probandum-hood) that is not a delimitor of the counterpositive-hood,' so the defect is averted. In the counterpositive-hood, delimitation by the relation that is the delimitor of <s>sādhyatā</s> must be stipulated. Hence, in cases such as 'possessing fire, from smoke,' even though the absence whose counterpositive-hood is delimited by fire-hood through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) is co-located with smoke, there is no harm. The word '<s>hetu</s>' refers to what is delimited by the delimitor of <s>hetutā</s> (probans-hood). Therefore, in cases such as 'substance, from qualified existence,' even though the qualified entity, being not different from the pure entity, resides in qualities and other things that are the loci of the <s>hetu</s>, there is no under-extension of the absence of substance-hood.

children.text:
hetvadhikaraṇatā
hetutāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnā grāhyā/ tena 'vahnimān dhūmāt'
ityādau vahnisāmānyābhāvasya dhūmasamavāyiniṣṭhatve 'pi
nāvyāptiḥ/ na caivamapi 'kapisaṃyogī evadvṛkṣatvāt' ityādau
avyāptiḥ, sādhyasya
hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakāvacchinnatvāditi
vācyam/ hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāve pratiyogivaiyadhikaraṇyasya
niveśanīyatvāt/ kevalānvayisādhyake tādṛśasya ghaṭābhāvādeḥ
prasiddhatvāt nāvyāptiriti/ adhikaṃ asmadīya-maṇidīdhitivyākhyāyā
buddhikuśalairanusandheyam/
children.translated_text: The locus-hood of the probans should be understood as delimited by the relation that is the delimitor of the probans-hood. Thus, in 'it possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, even though the absolute absence of fire-in-general resides in the inherent locus of smoke, there is no under-pervasion. Nor should it be said that even so, in 'it possesses monkey-contact, because of this-tree-ness' and the like, there is under-pervasion, because the probandum is delimited by the delimitor of the counter-positiveness of an absolute absence co-located with the probans — [this should not be said] because the being-in-a-different-locus-from-the-counter-positive must be incorporated in the absolute absence co-located with the probans. Since in the case of a purely positive (<s>kevalānvayin</s>) probandum, such an [absence] like the absence of a pot is well-established, there is no under-pervasion. More should be investigated by the discerning in our commentary on the <s>Maṇidīdhiti</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
sādhyābhāvāprasiddheriti/ sādhyasya vācyatvasya kevalānvayitvena
sarvatra vidyamānatayā tadabhāvasyāprasiddheḥ
sādhyābhāvavadavṛttitvarūpa1vyāptalakṣaṇasya
kevalānvayisādhyakasaddhetāvavyāptirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Because the absence of the probandum is not established' — the meaning is: since the probandum, namely predicate-hood (<s>vācyatva</s>), being purely positive, exists everywhere, its absence is not established; hence the definition of the pervaded in the form of 'non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the probandum' has under-pervasion in a valid probans with a purely positive probandum.

children.text:
ityarthatātparyakatayādoṣāditi/ tathā ca
hetvadhikaraṇavṛttyatyantābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakasādadhyatāvacchedakā-
children.translated_text: 'Because the defect arises from that being the meaning and purport' — and accordingly,

children.text:
vacchinnasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ vyāptiḥ/ 'parvato vahnimān
dhūmāt' ityādau hetuḥ dhūmaḥ, tadadhikaraṇaṃ parvataḥ,
children.translated_text: co-location with the probandum delimited by the delimitor of probandum-hood which does not delimit the counter-positiveness of an absolute absence occurring in the locus of the probans — this is <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). In 'the mountain possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, the probans is smoke, its locus is the mountain,

children.text:
tadvṛttiryo 'tyantābhāvaḥ
ghaṭādyabhāva mahānasīyavahnyabhāvaśca tatpratiyogitāvacchedakaṃ
ghaṭatva-mahānasīyavahnitvādikam/ tatpratiyogitānavacchedakaṃ
vahnitvarūpaṃ sādhyatāvacchedakam, tadavacchinna-vahnisāmānādhikaraṇyasya
tādṛśavahnyadhikaraṇaparvatādivṛttitvarūpasya dhūme sattvāt
lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ parvato dhūmavān vahneḥ ityādau hetuḥ vahniḥ
tadadhikaraṇam ayogālakam tadvṛttiryo 'tyantābhāvaḥ dhūmābhāvaḥ
tatpratiyogitāvacchedakameva dhūmatvarūpaṃ
children.translated_text: the absolute absence occurring there includes the absence of a pot, the absence of kitchen-fire, and the like; the delimitor of counter-positiveness of those [absences] is pot-ness, kitchen-fire-ness, and the like. What does not delimit the counter-positiveness is fire-ness, which is the delimitor of probandum-hood; the co-location with fire delimited by that [fire-ness], i.e. the occurrence in the mountain and the like which are the loci of such fire, exists in smoke — hence the definition applies. In 'the mountain possesses smoke, because of fire' and the like, the probans is fire, its locus is the iron-smelting furnace; the absolute absence occurring there is the absence of smoke; the delimitor of counter-positiveness of that is precisely smoke-ness,

children.text:
1. vyāpteḥ svarūpaṃ
vyāptasya lakṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. The nature of pervasion is the definition of the pervaded — this is the purport.

children.text:
sādhyatāvacchedakamiti
sādhyatāvacchedake
hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakatvābhāvāt
nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ pratiyogitāyāṃ
sādhyatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśanīyamityādi/ 'parvanto
vahnimān dhūmāt' ityatra dhūtādhikaraṇe parvate vartate
yo 'tyantābhāvaḥ samavāyena vahnirnāstītyākārakapratītisiddhaḥ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnavahnitvāvacchinnapratiyogitāko 'bhāvaḥ/
tatpratiyogitāyāṃ avacchedakameva vahnitvaṃ ityavyāptiḥ syāt/
tadvāraṇāya hetvadhikaraṇavṛttyabhāvīyapratiyogitāyāṃ
sādhyatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśanīyam/ niveśe ca
hetvadhikaraṇavṛttyabhāva ityanena yasyābhāvasyopādāne
tadīyapratiyogitāyāḥ sādhyatāvacchedakasaṃyogasambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ
bhavet sa evopādeyaḥ iti saṃyogasambandhena ghaṭādyabhāva eva
tādṛśaḥ, na tu samavāyena vahnyabhāvaḥ tadīyapratiyogitāyāḥ
saṃyogasambandhāvacchinnatvāsambhavāt/ tathā ca
hetvadhikaraṇavṛttighaṭādyabhāvīyasaṃyogasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāyāmavacchedakaṃ
ghaṭatvādi anavacchedakaṃ ca vahnitvaṃ bhavatīti nāvyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ na
kṣatiriti/ nāvyāptirityarthaḥ/ tathā ca
hetvadhikaraṇavṛttyatyantābhāvanirūpitasādhyatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchi nnapratiyogitānavacchedaka
- sādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnasādhyasāmānādhi - karaṇyaṃ
vyāptirityetāvatā phalitam/ hetupadaṃ
hetutāvacchedakāvacchinnaparamityādi/ 'ghaṭo dravyam
guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattvāt' ityatra saddhetau hetuḥ śuddhasattāpi
viśiṣṭaśuddhayoranatirekāt/ hetoradadhikaraṇaṃ guṇakarmaṇī api;
tatra vartate yo 'tyantābhāvaḥ dravyatvābhāvo 'pi
tatpratiyogitāvacchedakameva dravyatvatvamiti sādhyatāvacchedake
dravyatvatve pratiyogitānavacchedakatvābhāvāt avyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
hetutāvacchedakāvacchinnahetvadhikaraṇatvaṃ niveśanīyam/ guṇe
karmaṇi va sattātvāvacchinnasattādhikaraṇatvasadbhāve 'pi
hetutāvacchedakaṃ yat guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattātvaṃ
tadavacchinnādhikaraṇatvaṃ na sambabhavati/ guṇaḥ karma ca
guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattāvaditi pratītyabhāvāt/ ataḥ
guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattātvāvacchinnādhikaraṇaṃ dravyameva
tadvṛttiryo 'bhāvaḥ na dravyatvābhāvaḥ ati tu guṇatvādyabhāvaḥ
tatpratiyogitāvacchedakaṃ guṇatvatvādi ananavacchedakaṃ dravyatvatvamiti
nāvyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ tathā ca

children.text: AnTs_45 anumānaṃ dvividhaṃ svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca / tatra svārthaṃ svānumitihetuḥ / tathā hi svayam eva bhūyo darśanena yatra dhūmas tatra agnir iti mahānasādau vyāptiṃ gṛhītvā parvatasamīpaṃ gatas tadgate cāgnau sandihānaḥ parvate dhūmaṃ paśyan vyāptiṃ smarati yatra dhūmas tatrāgnir iti / tadantaraṃ vahnivyāpyadhūmavān ayaṃ parvata iti jñānam utpadyate / ayam eva liṅgaparāmarṣaṃ ity ucyate / tasmāt parvato vahnimān iti jñānam anumitir utpadyate / tad etat svārthānumānam / yat tu svayaṃ dhūmād agnim anumāya parapratipattyarthaṃ pañcāvayavavākyaṃ prayukte tat parārthānumānam / yathā parvato vahnimān dhūmavattvāt / yo yo dhūmavān sa vahnimān yathā mahānasaḥ / tathā cāyam / tasmāt tatheti / anena pratipāditāl lingāt paro'py agniṃ pratipadyate //
children.translated_text: <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is of two kinds: <s>svārtha</s> (for oneself) and <s>parārtha</s> (for others). Of these, <s>svārtha</s> is the cause of one's own inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>). Thus: having grasped by repeated observation the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) that wherever there is smoke there is fire, as in the kitchen and the like, one goes near the mountain and, being in doubt about the fire present there, seeing smoke on the mountain, one remembers the <s>vyāpti</s>: 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire.' Thereafter arises the cognition 'this mountain possesses smoke which is pervaded by fire.' This itself is called <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> (apprehension of the inferential mark). From that arises the inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>): 'the mountain possesses fire.' This is <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself). But that which, having inferred fire from smoke oneself, employs a five-membered statement (<s>pañcāvayavavākya</s>) for the understanding of another — that is <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for others). For example: 'The mountain possesses fire, because of possessing smoke. Whatever possesses smoke possesses fire, like the kitchen. And so is this [mountain]. Therefore it is so.' From the inferential mark thus demonstrated, another person also cognizes fire.

children.text:
anumānaṃ
dvividham-svārtham, parārtham ceti/
children.translated_text: <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is of two kinds — <s>svārtha</s> (for oneself) and <s>parārtha</s> (for others).

pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnā ca yā pratiyoginiṣṭhā ādheyatā
tannirūpitādhikaraṇatāvadbhinnaṃ atha ca
hetutāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnā hetutāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnā ca yā
hetuniṣṭhādheyatā tannirūpitādhikaraṇatāvat yat tanniṣṭho
yo 'tyantābhāvaḥ tannirūpitā yā sādhyatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnā
pratiyogitā tadanavacchedakaṃ yat sādhyatāvacchedakaṃ tadavacchinnaṃ yat
sādhyaṃ tadadhikaraṇavṛttitvaṃ dhyāptirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [The full definition is:] The superstratum-hood belonging to the counterpositive, delimited by the counterpositive-hood delimiting relation and the counterpositive-hood delimiting property — the locus-hood determined by that, which is different [from the <s>hetu</s>'s locus-hood], and yet the superstratum-hood belonging to the <s>hetu</s>, delimited by the <s>hetu</s>-hood delimiting relation and the <s>hetu</s>-hood delimiting property — the locus-hood determined by that, in which resides a constant absence; the counterpositive-hood delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> relation, of which that [absence] is the non-delimitor; the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> delimited by that; the <s>sādhya</s> delimited by that — co-location with the locus of that <s>sādhya</s> is <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). This is the meaning.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: pakṣadharmatāsvarūpamāha - vyāpyasyeti/
children.translated_text: He states the nature of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> — 'of the pervaded' (<s>vyāpyasya</s>).

children.text:
anumānaṃ vibhajate -
anumānamiti/
children.translated_text: He divides <s>anumāna</s> (inference) — '<s>anumānam</s>' and so on.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: svārthānumānanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself)

children.text:
svārthaṃ svānumitihetuḥ/ tathā hi -
svayameva bhūyodarśanena yatra dhūmaḥ tatrāgniriti mahānasādau vyāptiṃ
gṛhītvā parvatasamīpaṃ gataḥ, tadgate ca parvate dhūmaṃ paśyan agnau
sandihānaḥ vyāptiṃ smarati 'yatra dhūmastatrāgniḥ' iti/ tadanantaraṃ
'vahnivyāpyadhūmavān ayaṃ parvataḥ' iti jñānamutpadyate/ ayameva
liṅgaparāmarśa ityucyate/ tasmāt 'parvato
children.translated_text: <s>Svārtha</s> (inference for oneself) is the cause of one's own inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>). Thus: having grasped by one's own repeated observation the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) — 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire' — in the kitchen and the like, one goes near the mountain; and seeing smoke on the mountain, being in doubt about fire, one remembers the <s>vyāpti</s>: 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire.' Thereafter arises the cognition: 'this mountain possesses smoke pervaded by fire.' This itself is called <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> (apprehension of the inferential mark). From that, 'the mountain

children.text:
vahnimān'
ityanumitirutpadyate/ tadetat svārthānumānam/
children.translated_text: possesses fire' — the inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>) arises. This is <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
svārthānumānaṃ
darśayati - svameveti/
children.translated_text: He illustrates <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself) — 'oneself alone' (<s>svameva</s>) and so on.

children.text: vyāptigrahopāyanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of the means of grasping <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion)

children.text:
nanu
pārthivatvalohalekhyatvādau śataśaḥ rahacāradarśane 'pi vajramaṇau
vyabhicāropalabdheḥ bhūyodarśanena kathaṃ vyāptigraha iti cet-na/
vyabhicārajñānavirahasahakṛtasahacārajñānasya vyāptigrāhakatvāt/
vyabhicārajñānaṃ niścayaḥ śaṅkā ca/ tadvirahaḥ kvacit tarkāt,
kvacit svatassiddha eva/ dhūmāgnyorvyāptigrahe
kāryakāraṇabhāvabhaṅgaprasaṅgalakṣaṇaḥ tarko vyabhicāraśaṅkānivartakaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: Even though the co-occurrence of earthen-ness and mark-ability-by-a-file has been observed hundreds of times, since deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is found in the diamond — how can <s>vyāpti</s> be grasped through repeated observation? Answer: No, because the cognition of co-occurrence, aided by the absence of cognition of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>), is capable of grasping <s>vyāpti</s>. The cognition of deviation is of two kinds: ascertainment (<s>niścaya</s>) and doubt (<s>śaṅkā</s>). The absence of these is sometimes due to <s>tarka</s> (counterfactual reasoning), and sometimes is self-established (<s>svataḥsiddha</s>). In the grasping of <s>vyāpti</s> between smoke and fire, the <s>tarka</s> characterized by the absurd consequence of the destruction of the cause-effect relation removes the doubt of deviation.

children.text:
nanu
sakalavahnidhūmayorasannikarṣāt kathaṃ vyāptigraha iti cet - na/
vahnitvadhūmatvarūpasāmānyapratyāsattyā sakalavahnidhūmajñānasambhavāt/
tasmāditi/ liṅgaparāmarśādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since there is no contact with all instances of fire and smoke, how can <s>vyāpti</s> be grasped? Answer: No, because through the proximity of the universals (<s>sāmānya</s>) fire-hood and smoke-hood, cognition of all instances of fire and smoke is possible. 'Therefore' — the meaning is: from the <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> (apprehension of the inferential mark).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
svārthānumānamiti/ svasyārthaḥ prayojanaṃ
sādhyasaṃśayanivṛttirūpaṃ yasmāditi vyutpattyā
svīyasaṃśayanivṛttiprayojakānumānamityarthaḥ/ paśyan iti/
ekasambandhijñānaṃ aparasambandhissamārakaṃ iti rītyā darśanasya
smṛtihetutvādityarthaḥ/ kathaṃ vyāptigraha itīti/
vyabhicārajñānadaśāyāṃ na kaścidapi vyāptiniścayaṃ abhyupaitīti
bhūyodarśanasya vyāptiniścayahetutvaṃ na sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/
idamupalakṣaṇam-bhūyodarśanamityasya bhūyasāṃ darśanānāṃ samāhāra
iti, bhūyasāṃ sādhyahetūnāṃ darśanam, iti, bhūyassu
adhikaraṇeṣu darśanamiti vārthaṃḥ/ nādyaḥ, ekatraiva sahacāradarśanadhārayā
vyāptiniścayaprasaṅgāt/ na dvitīyatṛtīyau, 'etadrūpavān
etadrasāt' ityādau sādhyahetvoradhikaraṇe ca 1bhūyastvābhāvena
vyāptyaniścayaprasaṅgādityapi bodhyam/ maṇikārasiddhāntamavalambyāha
- vyabhicārajñānaviraheti/ vyāptigrāhakatvāditi/ vyāptiśca
hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakasādhya-
children.translated_text: '<s>Svārthānumāna</s>' — that from which the purpose (<s>artha</s>) for oneself — namely, the removal of doubt regarding the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — [is achieved], by the etymological derivation 'that from which' (<s>yasmāt</s>), the meaning is: the inference that brings about the removal of one's own doubt. 'Seeing' — by the principle that cognition of one relatum causes recollection of another relatum, the meaning is that perception is the cause of memory. 'How can <s>vyāpti</s> be grasped?' — in the state where there is cognition of deviation, no one accepts a definite ascertainment of <s>vyāpti</s>, hence repeated observation cannot be the cause of definite <s>vyāpti</s>-ascertainment — this is the import. This is a condensed expression (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>): the meaning of 'repeated observation' (<s>bhūyodarśana</s>) can be parsed as: 'the aggregate of many observations,' or 'observation of many <s>sādhyas</s> and <s>hetus</s>,' or 'observation in many loci.' Not the first, because there would be the unwanted consequence that <s>vyāpti</s>-ascertainment arises from a stream of co-occurrence observations even in a single case. Not the second or third either, because in cases like 'possessing this form, because of this taste,' where there is no multiplicity of loci of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>hetu</s>, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-ascertainment of <s>vyāpti</s> — this too should be understood. Following the doctrine of the <s>Maṇikāra</s> [i.e., <s>Gaṅgeśa</s>], he says 'the absence of the cognition of deviation.' 'Because it grasps <s>vyāpti</s>' — and <s>vyāpti</s> is of the nature of: the <s>hetu</s>-hood delimitor qualified by co-location with the locus of the <s>sādhya</s> delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> that is the non-delimitor of the counterpositive-hood of the constant absence co-located with the <s>hetu</s> —

children.text:
tāvacchedakāvacchinnasādhyādhikaraṇavṛttitāviśiṣṭahetutāvacchedakarūpaiva/
sāmānādhikaraṇyāntasya rāsabhādisādhāraṇyāt/ dhūmatvādeḥ svarūpato
vyāpyatāvacchedakatvaṃ tādṛśadhūmatvatvādirūpeṇa ca
vyāptitvamityavacchedyāvacchedakayoraikye 'pi na kṣatiḥ/ itthaṃ ca
sādhyatāvacchedake
tathāvidhapratiyogitāvacchedakatvarūpavyabhicāragrahābhāvo
viparītagrahābhāvavidhayā hetuḥ/
sādhyasamānādadhikaraṇavṛttihetutāvacchedakāṃśagrahe tu
viśeṣaṇajñānavidhayā sāmānādhikaraṇyajñānaṃ heturiti rītyā
vyabhicārajñānābhāvasāmānādhikaraṇyajñānayoḥ vyāptigrahahetuteti
dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: which has the form of <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> qualified by the co-location with the locus of the <s>sādhya</s> delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> that does not delimit the counterpositive-hood of the constant absence. Because [the condition of] co-location is common to donkeys and other [irrelevant cases]. The <s>vyāpyatāvacchedakatva</s> (delimitor-hood of pervaded-ness) of smoke-hood and the like is by its own nature, while the <s>vyāptitva</s> (pervasion-hood) is in the form of such smoke-hood-hood and the like — even though the delimited and the delimitor are identical, there is no deficiency. And accordingly, in the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>, the absence of the grasping of deviation in the form of such counterpositive-hood delimitor-hood is the cause, in the manner of absence of contrary grasping. But in grasping the <s>hetu</s>-hood delimitor aspect that is co-located with the <s>sādhya</s>, the co-location cognition is the cause in the manner of qualifier-cognition — by this principle, both the absence of deviation-cognition and the co-location cognition are causes of grasping <s>vyāpti</s>. This should be reflected upon.

children.text:
vastutastu
hetuvyāpakasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyameva vyāptiḥ/ na ca vyāpteḥ
rāsabhādisādhāraṇyena pramātmakarāsabhaliṅgakaparāmarśāt
bhramātmakavahnyanumityāpattiḥ, pramātmakaparāmarśasya
children.translated_text: In reality, however, <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is simply co-location of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) with the pervader of the <s>hetu</s> (probans). Nor should it be said that because <s>vyāpti</s> is common to donkeys and the like, from a <s>parāmarśa</s> (apprehension) involving a donkey as the inferential mark, there would be the unwanted consequence of a false inferential cognition of fire — because [only] a veridical <s>parāmarśa</s>

children.text:
1. bhūyastvābhāveneti/
tatra sādhyahetvostadadhikaraṇasya caikaṣyaktitvena
bahutaratvarūpānekatvātmakabhūyastvābhāvenetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Due to absence of multiplicity' — there, since the <s>sādhya</s>, the <s>hetu</s>, and their locus are each singular, the meaning is: due to absence of multiplicity, which is the nature of being more-than-one.

children.text:
bhramātmakavahnyanumityajanakatvaniyamasattvena
iṣṭāpatterayogāditi vācyam/ yaddharmāṃvacchinnavyāpakatvaṃ
vyāptighaṭakam
children.translated_text: has the invariable restriction of not producing a false inferential cognition of fire, so the unwanted consequence does not arise. [Objection:] The pervader-hood delimited by whichever property is a component of <s>vyāpti</s>,

children.text:
taddharmitāvacchedakakavyāptiprakārakaniścayasyaiva
anumitihetutvopagamenādoṣāt/ ata eva vyāptiśarīre
dhūmatvāpraveśena
children.translated_text: only the definite ascertainment whose content is <s>vyāpti</s> with that property as the delimitor of the locus is accepted as the cause of <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition) — hence there is no defect. For this very reason, since smoke-hood does not enter the body of <s>vyāpti</s>,

children.text:
lāghavamiti dik/
śaṅkāceti/ vyābhicārasaṃśayasyāpi
vyāptigrahapratibandhakatvānubhavāt
tatsādhāraṇavyabhicārajñānatvāvacchinnābhāvo heturiti hṛdayam/
tadvirahaḥ - vyabhicāraśaṅkāvirahaḥ/ kvaciriti
tarkābhāvetaranikhilakāraṇasamavadhānasthala ityarthaḥ/ kvacit
svatassiddha eveti/ itarakāraṇavirahasthale
children.translated_text: parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>) is achieved — this is the indication. 'And doubt' (<s>śaṅkā</s> ca) — because it is experienced that even the doubt of deviation is an obstruction to the grasping of <s>vyāpti</s>, the essence is that the absence, delimited by the property of being cognition of deviation in the general sense including doubt, is the cause. 'The absence of that' — the absence of the doubt of deviation. 'Sometimes' — the meaning is: in contexts where all other causes except <s>tarka</s> are co-present. 'Sometimes self-established' — in contexts where the other causes are absent,

children.text:
tādṛśakāraṇavirahaprayukta evetyarthaḥ/ tathā ca tatra tarkāpekṣā
neti bhāvaḥ/ dhūmāgnyoriti/ dhūmāgnyorvyāptigrahe utpatsyamāne
vyabhicāraśaṅkānivartakaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvabhaṅgaprasaṅgalakṣaṇastarka
ityanvayaḥ/ sa ca tarkaḥ 'dhūmo yadi vahnivyabhicārī syāt tarhi
vahnijanyo na syāt' ityākārako bodhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: [the absence of doubt] is established by the very absence of such a cause. And accordingly, the import is that in those cases there is no need for <s>tarka</s>. 'Of smoke and fire' — the construction is: in the grasping of <s>vyāpti</s> between smoke and fire, which is about to arise, the <s>tarka</s> characterized by the absurd consequence of the destruction of the cause-effect relation removes the doubt of deviation. And that <s>tarka</s> should be understood as having the form: 'if smoke were to deviate from fire, then it would not be produced by fire.'

children.text:
nanu
mahānasīyavahnidhūmayoḥ sannikṛṣṭatvena sahacāragrahe 'pyanyeṣāṃ
vahnidhūmānāmasannikarṣeṇa
children.translated_text: Objection: Even when the co-occurrence of fire and smoke in the kitchen has been grasped through proximity, since there is no contact with other instances of fire and smoke,

children.text:
sahacārapratyakṣāsambhavena nikhiladhūmeṣu vyāptipratyakṣaṃ na
sambhavati/ tathā ca parvatīyadhūmadarśanena vyāptismaraṇāsambhavāt
parāmarśānupapattirityāśayena āśaṅkate - nanviti/
sakalavahnidhūmeṣu laukikasannikarṣābhāve 'pi
sāmānyalakṣaṇapratyāsattyātmakālaukikasannikarṣasadbhāvāt
vahnitvāvacchinnasāmānādhikaraṇyatvena
nikhilavahnidhūmasahacārapratyakṣasambhavāt nikhiladhūmeṣu vyāptigrahaḥ
sambhavati/ evaṃ ca parvatīyadhūme 'pi vyāptergṛhītatvena dhūmadarśanena
vyāptismaraṇasambhavāt na parāmarśānupapattiriti samādhatte -
vahnitvadhūmatveti/
children.translated_text: Since the perception of concomitance (<s>sahacāra-pratyakṣa</s>) is impossible, perceptual apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) with respect to all instances of smoke is not possible. And thus, since the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s> through seeing smoke on the mountain is impossible, the inferential judgment (<s>parāmarśa</s>) cannot be established — with this concern he raises the objection beginning with 'nanu.' Even though ordinary sensory contact (<s>laukika-sannikarṣa</s>) with all instances of fire and smoke is absent, because there exists an extraordinary sensory contact (<s>alaukika-sannikarṣa</s>) in the form of <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa pratyāsatti</s> (perceptual contact through universals), and because the perception of the concomitance of all instances of fire and smoke is possible through co-location delimited by <s>vahnitva</s> (fire-ness), the apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> with respect to all instances of smoke is indeed possible. And thus, since <s>vyāpti</s> has been apprehended even with respect to the smoke on the mountain, the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s> through seeing smoke is possible, and therefore there is no failure of the inferential judgment — he resolves this beginning with '<s>vahnitva-dhūmatva</s>.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
yadyapi svasyārthaḥ
anumitirūpaṃ prayojanaṃ yasmāttat svārthānumānamiti bahuṣu
grantheṣvasti tathāpi anumiterapi prayojanaṃ sādhyasaṃśayanivṛttiriti
matvā vyācaṣṭe---svasyārtha iti/ ekasambandhijñānamiti/
vyāptyākhyasambandhasya sambandhinau dvau hetuḥ sādhyaśca/ tayoḥ ekasya
sambandhino hatoḥ darśanātmakaṃ jñānaṃ aparasya sambandhinaḥ sādhyasya
smṛtiṃ janayati, sādhyasya smṛtau ca sādhyahetvorvyāptiḥ smaryata
iti bhāvaḥ/ vastutastu dhūmadarśanaṃ
vyāptismṛtihetusaṃskārodbodhanadvāraiva vyāpitasmṛtiṃ janayati,
na tu ekasambandhijñānamiti vidhayeti dhyeyam/
vyabhicārajñānābhāvasahakṛtasahacārajñānasya
vyāptigrahakāraṇatvamupapādayituṃ vyāptiṃ
pariṣkaroti---vyāptiścetyādinā/ yadyapi pūrvaṃ
hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakasādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ
vyāptirityevoktam, tathāpi tāvanmātre ukte 'parvato vahnimān
dhūmāt' ityatra rāsabhasyāpi
dhūmavyāpakavahnyadhikaraṇaparvatavṛttitayā
tādṛśasāmānādhikaraṇyākrāntatvāt vahnivyāpyatvaṃ prasajyeta/ ataḥ
hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedaka-sādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinna-
sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaviśiṣṭahetutāvacchedakavattvaṃ vyāptiriti
pariṣkāryam/ rāsabhe vahnisāmānādadhikaraṇyasattve 'pi
hetutāvacchedakībhūtadhūmatvavattvābhāvāt nātivyāptiḥ/ na ca
dhūmatvaparyantaṃ yadi vyāptiḥ tarhi dhūmatvaṃ vyāptyavacchedakamiti
vyavahāraḥ kathamupapadyate avacchedyāyāḥ vyāpteḥ dhūmatvarūpatayā dhūmatve
dhūmatvasyāvacchedakatvāsambhavāt/ avacchedyāvacchedakabhāvasya
bhedaniyatatvāditi vācyam/ dhūmatvatvena rūpeṇa dhūtvaṃ vyāptiḥ
svarūpato dhūmatvaṃ vyāptyavacchedakamityadoṣāt1/
children.translated_text: Although in many texts it is held that inference-for-oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>) is so called because its own purpose (<s>svasya arthaḥ</s>) is the result in the form of inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>), nevertheless, considering that the purpose of <s>anumiti</s> too is the removal of doubt regarding the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), he explains — with 'svasya arthaḥ.' 'Knowledge of one relatum' — the two relata of the relation called <s>vyāpti</s> are the <s>hetu</s> (reason) and the <s>sādhya</s>. The cognition in the form of perceiving one of the two relata, namely the <s>hetu</s>, generates the recollection of the other relatum, namely the <s>sādhya</s>, and upon the recollection of the <s>sādhya</s>, the <s>vyāpti</s> between <s>sādhya</s> and <s>hetu</s> is also recollected — this is the purport. In reality, however, the perception of smoke generates the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s> only through the arousal of the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) that are the cause of <s>vyāpti</s>-recollection, and not through the mode of 'knowledge of one relatum' — this should be noted. In order to establish that the cognition of concomitance assisted by the absence of deviation-knowledge (<s>vyabhicāra-jñāna-abhāva</s>) is the cause of apprehending <s>vyāpti</s>, he refines the definition of <s>vyāpti</s> — beginning with '<s>vyāptiś ca</s>.' Although previously <s>vyāpti</s> was stated as merely co-location with the <s>sādhya</s> delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> (delimitor of probandum-ness) that does not delimit the counter-positiveness of absolute absence co-located with the <s>hetu</s>, nevertheless, if only that much were stated, then in 'the mountain possesses fire, because of smoke,' even a donkey, being located on the mountain which is the locus of fire that pervades smoke, would be encompassed by such co-location, and the undesirable consequence of smoke-pervasion would follow. Therefore, <s>vyāpti</s> must be refined as: the possession of the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> (delimitor of reason-ness) qualified by co-location with the <s>sādhya</s> delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> that does not delimit the counter-positiveness of absolute absence co-located with the <s>hetu</s>. Even though there is co-location with fire in the donkey, since the donkey does not possess <s>dhūmatva</s> (smoke-ness) which is the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>, there is no over-pervasion. And if the objection is raised: if <s>vyāpti</s> extends only up to <s>dhūmatva</s>, then how can the usage '<s>dhūmatva</s> is the delimitor of <s>vyāpti</s>' be justified, since, <s>vyāpti</s> being of the nature of <s>dhūmatva</s> as the delimited entity, <s>dhūmatva</s> cannot be its own delimitor, because the relation of delimited and delimitor necessarily requires distinctness — the reply is: <s>dhūmatva</s> under the aspect of <s>dhūmatvatva</s> (smoke-ness-ness) is <s>vyāpti</s>, while <s>dhūmatva</s> in its own nature is the delimitor of <s>vyāpti</s> — hence there is no fault.

children.text:
etādṛśavyāptijñāne
vyabhicārajñānābhāvaḥ kathaṃ hetuḥ? kathaṃ ca sahacārajñānaṃ heturiti
cet-śrūyatām/ sāmānādhikaraṇyaviśiṣṭahetutāvacchedakamityasya
samānādadhikaraṇavṛttihetutāvacchedakamityarthaḥ/ tathā
children.translated_text: How is the absence of deviation-knowledge (<s>vyabhicāra-jñāna-abhāva</s>) a cause in such <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge? And how is concomitance-knowledge (<s>sahacāra-jñāna</s>) a cause? — if asked, listen. The meaning of 'possessing the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> qualified by co-location' is: possessing the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> that resides in a co-located entity. Furthermore,

children.text:
1. adoṣāditi/ yadyapi
dhūmatvameva vyāptiḥ vyāpyatāvacchedakaṃ ceti
avacchedyāvacchedakayoraikyam, tathāpi dhūmatvaniṣṭhā avacchedyatā
dhūmatvatvāvacchinnā, avacchedakatā tu niravacchinneti
avacchedyatāvacchedakatayorbhedāt ekasyaivāvacchedyāvachedakabhāva upapanna
evetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Regarding 'hence there is no fault' — although <s>dhūmatva</s> itself is <s>vyāpti</s> and also the delimitor of pervasion-hood (<s>vyāpyatāvacchedaka</s>), so that there is identity between the delimited and the delimitor, nevertheless, the delimited-ness residing in <s>dhūmatva</s> is delimited by <s>dhūmatvatva</s> (smoke-ness-ness), while the delimitor-ness is undelimited — therefore, because the delimited-ness and the delimitor-ness are distinct, the relation of being both delimited and delimitor in one and the same entity is indeed justified — this is the meaning.

children.text:
ca
dhūmasamānādadhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakavahnitvāvacchinna
- vahnyadhikaraṇavṛttidhūmavṛttidhūmatvavān dhūma iti vyāptijñānasya
ākāraḥ/
dhūmasamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakavahnitvāvacchinnasamānādhikaraṇadhūmavṛttidhūmatvavān
dhūma iti vyabhicārajñānasya ākāraḥ/ vyāptijñāne sādhyatāvacchedake
pratiyogitānavacchedakatvaṃ bhāsate, vyabhicārajñona tu
children.translated_text: And the form of <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge is: 'smoke possesses <s>dhūmatva</s> (smoke-ness), which resides in what is co-located with fire, where fire is delimited by <s>vahnitva</s> (fire-ness) that does not delimit the counter-positiveness of absolute absence co-located with smoke.' The form of deviation-knowledge (<s>vyabhicāra-jñāna</s>) is: 'smoke possesses <s>dhūmatva</s>, which resides in what is co-located with smoke, where fire is delimited by <s>vahnitva</s> that delimits the counter-positiveness of absolute absence co-located with smoke.' In <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge, the non-delimiting of counter-positiveness by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> is apprehended, whereas in deviation-knowledge,

children.text:
sādhyatāvacchedake
pratiyogitānavacchedakatvaṃ bhāsate, vyabhicārajñāne tu
sādhyatāvacchedake pratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ bhāsate/ tatra
pratiyogitānavacchedakatvāvagāhivyāptijñānaṃ prati
pratiyogitāvacchedakatvāvagāhivyabhicārajñānaṃ tadvattābuddhau
tadabhāvavattājñānavidhayā pratibandhakamiti vyabhicārajñānābhāvaḥ
pratibandhakābhāvavidhayā pratibandhakamiti vyabhicārajñānābhāvaḥ
pratibandhakābhāvavidhayā vyāptijñānaṃ prati hetuḥ/
children.translated_text: the non-delimiting of counter-positiveness by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> is apprehended [in <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge], whereas in deviation-knowledge, the delimiting of counter-positiveness by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> is apprehended. There, deviation-knowledge, which apprehends the delimiting of counter-positiveness, is an obstructor (<s>pratibandha</s>) of <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge, which apprehends the non-delimiting of counter-positiveness, by the mode of generating the cognition of the absence of possessing that property in a cognition of possessing that property. Therefore, the absence of deviation-knowledge is a cause of <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge by the mode of being the absence of an obstructor.

children.text:
sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaviśiṣṭahetuvṛttihetutāvacchedakamityaṃśo 'pi
vyāptijñāne bhāsate/ sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyagraha eva
children.translated_text: The component 'possessing the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> that resides in [what is qualified by] co-location with the <s>sādhya</s>' is also apprehended in <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge. The apprehension of co-location with the <s>sādhya</s> itself

children.text:
sahacāragraha
ityucyate/ tādṛśasahacāragrahaḥ sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaviśiṣṭo
heturitijñānaṃprati viśiṣṭabuddhau viśeṣaṇajñānaṃ kāraṇamiti rītyā
heturiti/ 1adhikamasmadīyapañcalakṣaṇīvyākhyāyāṃ bālabodhinyāṃ
draṣṭavyam/ sādhyādhikaraṇavṛttitāviśiṣṭeti/ hetutāvacchedake
sādhyādhikaraṇavṛttitāvaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena/
children.translated_text: is called the apprehension of concomitance (<s>sahacāra-graha</s>). Such apprehension of concomitance is a cause of the cognition 'the <s>hetu</s> is qualified by co-location with the <s>sādhya</s>' by the principle that knowledge of the qualifier is a cause of the cognition of the qualified entity — thus it is a cause. Further details should be seen in our commentary <s>Bālabodhinī</s> on the <s>Pañcalakṣaṇī</s>. 'Qualified by residence in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s>' — the qualification of the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> by residence in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s> is through the relation of co-location.

children.text:
dhūmatvasya
vahnyadhikaraṇavṛttitvasya ca ekatra dhūme sattvāt/
sādhyādhikaraṇavṛttihetuniṣṭhahetutāvacchedakarūpeti tu
phalitor'thaḥ/ viparītagrahābhāvavidhayeti/
tadabhāvavattājñānābhāvatvenetyarthaḥ/ atra tadvattābuddhiḥ
pratiyogitānavacchedakatvavat sādhyatāvacchedakamiti buddhiḥ/
tadabhāvavattājñānaṃ pratiyogitānavacchedakatvābhāvavat arthāt
pratiyogitāvacchedakaṃ sādhyatāvacchedakamiti buddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: Because <s>dhūmatva</s> (smoke-ness) and residence in the locus of fire both obtain in one and the same smoke. 'Of the nature of the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> residing in the <s>hetu</s> that resides in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s>' — this is the resultant meaning. 'By the mode of the absence of contrary apprehension' — the meaning is: by being the absence of the cognition of the absence of possessing that property. Here, the cognition of possessing that property is the cognition that the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> possesses the non-delimiting of counter-positiveness. The cognition of the absence of possessing that property is, in effect, the cognition that the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> possesses the absence of non-delimiting of counter-positiveness, that is, the delimiting of counter-positiveness.

children.text:
1. nanu viśiṣṭabuddhau
viśeṣaṇaviṣayakajñānasyaiva hetutayā sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaviśiṣṭo
heturiti buddhi prati sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyajñānameva hetuḥ, na tu
sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaviśiṣṭo heturityākārakaṃ sahacārajñānamapi,
hetuviṣayakatāyāḥ viśiṣṭabuddhikāraṇatāvacchedakakoṭāvapraveśāt
ityata āha-adhikamiti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ---
sādhyasāmānādadhikaraṇyaviśiṣṭahetuviśiṣṭaṃ
hetutāvacchedakamityākārakaṃ vyāptijñānamhetutāvacchadake
hetuvaiśiṣṭyaṃ cādheyatāsambandhena/ tādṛśavyāptijñānaṃ prati viśiṣṭa
vaiśiṣṭyāvagāhibuddhau viśeṣaṇatāvacchedakaprakārakajñānavidhayā
sāmānādadhikaraṇyarūpasahacāragraho heturiti/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since in the cognition of a qualified entity, only the cognition whose content is the qualifier is the cause, the cause of the cognition 'the <s>hetu</s> is qualified by co-location with the <s>sādhya</s>' is only the knowledge of the co-location with the <s>sādhya</s>, and not also the concomitance-knowledge (<s>sahacāra-jñāna</s>) having the form 'the <s>hetu</s> qualified by co-location with the <s>sādhya</s>,' because the <s>hetu</s>-content-ness does not enter the delimitor of the causality of qualified cognition — to this he says 'further details.' The purport is this: the <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge has the form 'the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> is qualified by the <s>hetu</s> qualified by co-location with the <s>sādhya</s>,' and the qualification of the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> by the <s>hetu</s> is through the relation of superstratum. For such <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge, the apprehension of concomitance in the form of co-location is a cause, by the principle that knowledge whose content is the property delimiting the qualifier-ness is a cause of the cognition apprehending the qualified qualification.

children.text:
sādhyasāmānādadhikaraṇyaṃ vyāptiḥ iti mūlavirodho mā
bhūdityāśayenāha - vastunastviti/ na ceti/
dhūmavyāpakavahnisāmānādhikaraṇyarūpāyāḥ vyāpteḥ rāsabhe 'pi
vartamānatayā dhūmavyāpakavahnisāmānādhikaraṇarāsabhavān parvata
ityākārakasya parāmarśasya pramātmakatayā tato 'pi
bhramātmakarāsabhaliṅgakavahnyanumityāpattiḥ ityarthaḥ/ yadyapi
children.translated_text: Lest there be a contradiction with the root text that '<s>vyāpti</s> is co-location with the <s>sādhya</s>,' he says — 'but in reality.' 'And not...' — Since the <s>vyāpti</s> in the form of co-location with fire that pervades smoke obtains even in a donkey, there would be the undesirable consequence of an inferential judgment of the form 'the mountain possesses a donkey co-located with fire that pervades smoke,' and since that judgment would be veridical, there would follow from it a false inference of fire based on the donkey as a mark — this is the meaning. Although

children.text:
'parvato vahnimān'
ityanumiteḥ pramātvāt kathamāpādyamānāyāḥ anumiterbhramatvam
ityāśaṅkā bhavati, tathāpi 1vyāpyaliṅgakānumitereva pramātvaṃ
na tvavyāpyaliṅgakānumiterityāśayenaivamuktamiti dhyeyam/
samādhatteyaddharmāvacchinneti/ dhūmatvāvacchinnavyāpakatvaṃ vyāptighaṭakam,
ataḥ dhataḥ dhūmatvadharmitāvacchedakakaḥ vyāptiprakārakaḥ niścayaḥ
dhūmavyāpakavahnisamānādhikaraṇadhūmavān parvata iti niścaya eva
parvato vahnimānityanumitihetuḥ,
dhūmavyāpakavahnisamānādhikaraṇarāsabhavāniti parāmarśastu
rāsabhatvadharmitāvacchedakakaḥ vyāptiprakāraka iti na
tasyānumitihetutvamiti bhāvaḥ/ ata eveti/
vyāpakatāpraviṣṭahetutāvacchedakadharmitāvacchedakakasāmānādhikaraṇyaprakārakaniścayasyānumitihetutvaṃ
svīkṛtya pramātmakarāsabhaliṅgakaparāmarśāt bhramātmakavahnyanumiteḥ
vāraṇena vyāpte rāsabhādisādhāraṇye 'pi kṣativirahādevetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the objection arises that since the inference 'the mountain possesses fire' is veridical, how can the inferred inference be said to be erroneous — nevertheless, this is stated with the understanding that only inference based on a pervaded mark (<s>vyāpya-liṅga</s>) is veridical, not inference based on a non-pervaded mark (<s>avyāpya-liṅga</s>) — this should be noted. He resolves this with 'delimited by the property.' The pervasion-pervadedness delimited by <s>dhūmatva</s> (smoke-ness) is a constituent of <s>vyāpti</s>; therefore, the determinate cognition with <s>dhūmatva</s> as the delimitor of the <s>dharmin</s> (substratum) and with <s>vyāpti</s> as the qualifier — namely, 'the mountain possesses smoke co-located with fire that pervades smoke' — that determinate cognition alone is the cause of the inference 'the mountain possesses fire.' But the inferential judgment 'possessing a donkey co-located with fire that pervades smoke,' having donkey-ness as the delimitor of the <s>dharmin</s> and <s>vyāpti</s> as the qualifier, is not the cause of inference — this is the purport. 'Therefore' — having accepted that the cause of inference is the determinate cognition whose co-location qualifier includes the <s>dharmin</s>-delimitor belonging to the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> contained in the pervader-ness, the undesirable consequence of a false inference of fire from a veridical inferential judgment based on the donkey as mark is averted, and hence even though <s>vyāpti</s> is common to donkeys and the like, there is no deficiency — this is the meaning.

children.text:
sāmānyalakṣaṇetyādi/
sāmānyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ svarūpaṃ yasyāḥ sā sāmānyalakṣaṇā pratyāsattiḥ
sannikarṣaḥ/ vahnitvadhūmatvātmakasaṃnikarṣeṇa
tadāśrayasakalavanhidhūmānāṃ pratyakṣe sati
vanhitvāvacchinnanirūpitasāmānādhikaraṇyatvena rūpeṇa
sakaladhūmaniṣṭhānāṃ sakalavanhisāmānādhikaraṇyānāmapi grahāt
parvatīyadhūmaniṣṭhaṃ parvatīyavahnisāmānādhikaraṇyamapi pūrvaṃ
pratyakṣitam/ ataḥ dhūmadarśanena
parvatīyadhūmaniṣṭhaparvatīyavahnisāmānādhikaraṇyarūpavyāpteḥ smaraṇaṃ
bhavitumarhatīti bhāvaḥ/ etena
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>' and so forth — <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā pratyāsattiḥ</s> is that sensory contact whose characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>). Through the sensory contact in the form of <s>vahnitva</s> (fire-ness) and <s>dhūmatva</s> (smoke-ness), when all instances of fire and smoke supported by those universals are perceived, then by grasping all the co-locations with fire belonging to all instances of smoke under the aspect of co-location-ness delimited by <s>vahnitva</s>, the co-location with fire belonging to the smoke on the mountain too was previously perceived. Therefore, through seeing smoke, the recollection of the <s>vyāpti</s> in the form of the co-location of the smoke on the mountain with the fire on the mountain can indeed arise — this is the purport. By this,

children.text:
1. vyāpyaliṅgakatvaṃ
ca vyāpyaṃ yalliṃṅgaṃ tadviṣayakajñānajanyatvam anumiterbhramatvaṃ
vyāptijñānasya bhramatvāt bhavati/ vyāpte rāsabhasādhāraṇye ca
vyāptijñānasya rāsabhadharmikasya pramātvāt tajjanyavahnyanumiterapi
pramātvameva syāt na tu
children.translated_text: the pervaded-mark-ness (<s>vyāpya-liṅgakatva</s>) is the property of being produced by a cognition whose object is that which is a pervaded mark; the erroneousness of an inference is due to the erroneousness of the <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge. And when <s>vyāpti</s> is common to donkeys, since the <s>vyāpti</s>-knowledge having the donkey as its <s>dharmin</s> is veridical, the inference of fire generated from it too would be veridical and not

children.text: bhramatvamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: erroneous — this is the purport.

children.text:
vahnitvadhūmatvarūpasāmānyalakṣaṇayā
sakalavahnidhūmānāmupasthitāvapi vahnisāmānādadhikaraṇyarūpāyāḥ
vyāpteḥ pratyekaviśrāntatayā pūrvaṃ mahānase
mahānasīyadhūniṣṭhasāmānādhikaraṇyasya gṛhītatve 'pi
children.translated_text: Even though all instances of fire and smoke are presented through <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā</s> (extraordinary perception through universals) in the form of <s>vahnitva</s> and <s>dhūmatva</s>, since the <s>vyāpti</s> in the form of co-location with fire rests on each individual instance, even if the co-location belonging to the smoke in the kitchen was previously apprehended in the kitchen,

children.text:
parvatīyadhūmaniṣṭhasāmānādadhikaraṇyasyāgrahaṇāt kathaṃ
tatsmṛtiritiśaṅkā parāstā/
vahnitvāvacchinnasāmānādhikaraṇyatvātmakasāmānyalakṣaṇapratyāsattyāparvatīyadhūniṣṭhasāmānādhikaraṇyasyāpi
grahasambhavāt/
children.translated_text: since the co-location belonging to the smoke on the mountain was not apprehended, how can the recollection of that arise? — this doubt is dispelled, because the apprehension of the co-location belonging to the smoke on the mountain too is possible through the <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa pratyāsatti</s> (extraordinary perceptual contact through universals) in the form of co-location-ness delimited by <s>vahnitva</s>.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: parārthānumānanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>)

children.text:
yattu svayameva
dhūmādagnimanumāya parapratipattyarthaṃ pañcāvayavavākyaṃ prayuṅkte
tatparārthānumānam/
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>:] That which, having oneself inferred fire from smoke, one then presents as a five-membered statement (<s>pañcāvayava-vākya</s>) for the purpose of conveying knowledge to another — that is inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
parārthānumānamāha - yattviti/ yacchabdasya
'tatparārthānumānam' iti tacchabdenānvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) — with 'yat tu.' The word 'yat' connects with the word 'tat' in 'that is inference-for-others.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
yadyapi
parārthānumānaśabdasya parasya madhyasthasya arthaḥ prayojanaṃ
sādhyānumitirūpaṃ yasmāt iti vyutpattyā
parasamavetānumitikaraṇaliṅgaparāmarśor'thaḥ/ ata eva
'svarthānumitiparārthānumityoḥ liṅgaparāmarśa eva karaṇam'
ityādyagrimamūlaṃ sādhu saṅgacchate, tathāpi parārthānumānaprayojake
pañcāvayavavākye parārthānumānaśabdasya aupacārikaḥ prayoga iti
manasi kṛtvā mūlamavatārayati - parārthānumānamāheti/
children.translated_text: Although the word <s>parārthānumāna</s> etymologically means 'that from which the purpose of another — that is, the <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition) in the form of the probandum — [is achieved] for another, namely the adjudicator,' and thus its meaning is the inferential judgment (<s>liṅga-parāmarśa</s>) which is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) of the inference belonging to the other person — and hence the subsequent root text 'the instrument of both inference-for-oneself and inference-for-others is the inferential judgment alone' fits well — nevertheless, bearing in mind that the word <s>parārthānumāna</s> is used figuratively (<s>aupacārika</s>) for the five-membered statement that occasions inference-for-others, he introduces the root text — with 'he states inference-for-others.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
parasya
madhyasthasyeti/ yadyapi paraśabdaḥ anyaparaḥ, tathā
cānyasamavetānumitikaraṇamityeva svarasataḥ parārthānumānaśabdārthaḥ/
tathāpi nyāyarūpasya parārthānumānasya vādādikathāyāmeva prāyaśa
upayogāt tatra paraśabdasya anyaprativādiparatve tasya bādhajñānasattvena
bādyuktanyāyāt aprāmāṇyaśaṅkārahitā anumitirna jāyate, madhyasthasya
tu pakṣadvaye 'pyāgraharahitasya anumitirbhavitumarhatītyāśayenaivaṃ
vyākhyānaṃ kṛtam/
children.translated_text: [The word 'para' means] 'of another, an impartial observer.' Although the word <s>para</s> (other) refers to 'another,' and thus the natural meaning of the term <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for the sake of another) is simply 'the instrument of inferential cognition residing in another,' nevertheless, since <s>parārthānumāna</s> in the form of the <s>nyāya</s> (syllogism) is employed mostly in discussions such as <s>vāda</s> (debate) and the like, if the word <s>para</s> there were taken to mean 'another, i.e., the opponent,' then because of the existence of <s>bādhajñāna</s> (sublating cognition) in the opponent, by the principle stated in the <s>bādyukta</s> maxim, inferential cognition free from the suspicion of invalidity would not arise in him; but for the impartial observer, who is free from bias toward either side, inferential cognition can indeed arise — it is with this intention that the explanation has been given thus.

children.text:
parārthānumānaprayojaka iti/ parārthānumānasya
parasamavetānumitikaraṇasya liṅgaparāmarśasya, prayojake paramparayā
kāraṇabhūte pañcāvayavakamahāvākyarūpe nyāye/ aupacārikaḥ
lākṣaṇikaḥ/ kāraṇe kāryopacāraḥ parārthānumānaśabda iti yāvat/
kathaṃ liṅgaparāmarśarūpaparārthānumānaprayojakatvaṃ nyāyasyeti cet
- ittham/ pratijñādibhiḥ pañcabhirvākyaiḥ prathamataḥ 2tattadvākyārthabodhaḥ
jāyate/ tarta ekavākyatāmāpannaiḥ
pañcabhirvākyairekamahāvākyārthabodho jāyate/ tataḥ tatsahakṛtena

children.translated_text: 'The instigator of <s>parārthānumāna</s>' — of <s>parārthānumāna</s>, that is, of <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> (the apprehension of the inferential mark) which is the instrument of inferential cognition residing in another; [the term applies] to the <s>nyāya</s> (syllogism) in the form of a <s>mahāvākya</s> (grand sentence) consisting of five members, which is the indirect cause serving as the instigator. [The usage is] figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>), based on secondary signification (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>). The meaning is: the term <s>parārthānumāna</s> involves a figurative transfer of the effect onto the cause. If one asks how the <s>nyāya</s> has the property of instigating <s>parārthānumāna</s> in the form of <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> — it is thus: from the five sentences beginning with the <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis), first there arises the comprehension of the meaning of each respective sentence. Then, from those five sentences having attained the unity of a single sentence, there arises comprehension of the meaning of the <s>mahāvākya</s>. Then, through the mind assisted by that [comprehension], <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> arises, and from that, <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition) — thus, the five-membered sentence constituting the <s>nyāya</s> has the property of instigating <s>parārthānumāna</s> by virtue of generating the comprehension of the <s>mahāvākya</s> meaning which generates the <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> which generates <s>anumiti</s>. The form of the comprehension of the <s>mahāvākya</s> meaning is: 'The mountain, which is non-different from that which possesses smoke that is indicated by smoke-cognition as possessing fire, and non-different from that which possesses fire that pervades smoke, and non-different from that which possesses smoke that is pervaded by fire — that mountain is non-different from that which possesses fire indicated by smoke-cognition as possessing fire, and which is unsublated and free from counterbalancing reasons.'

children.translated_text: <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis), <s>hetu</s> (reason), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (example), <s>upanaya</s> (application), and <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion) — these are the five members. 'The mountain possesses fire' — this is the <s>pratijñā</s>. 'Because it possesses smoke' — this is the <s>hetu</s>. 'Whatever possesses smoke possesses fire, like a kitchen' — this is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. 'And this [mountain] is so' — this is the <s>upanaya</s>. 'Therefore it is so' — this is the <s>nigamana</s>.

children.translated_text: By the expression 'five-membered sentence,' through the derivation 'a sentence of which there are five members,' one should understand that the definition of <s>nyāya</s> (syllogism) is: being the aggregate of the five members beginning with <s>pratijñā</s>. The root text's [expression] 'from the <s>liṅga</s> established by this' means: from the <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> (apprehension of the inferential mark) produced by the aggregate of five members beginning with <s>pratijñā</s>. 'A statement of the <s>pakṣa</s> as possessing the <s>sādhya</s>' means: a sentence that generates a cognition having as its qualifier what is delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> (the delimitor of probandum-hood) and having as its qualificand what is delimited by the <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s> (the delimitor of subject-hood). From the <s>udāharaṇa</s>, there arises cognition of the qualificandness delimited by <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> in what is qualified by the <s>hetu</s>, not in what is qualified by the <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>; and from the <s>upanaya</s>, there arises cognition of the qualificandness delimited by <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s> in what is qualified by the <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>, but not cognition apprehending qualificandness delimited by <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> — thus the refutation of both [objections]. Since the word <s>vākya</s> (sentence) refers to sentences that are members of the <s>nyāya</s>, sentences outside the <s>nyāya</s> are excluded. Similarly hereafter. In cases such as 'this is not [produced] from a stick, because it is a substance not produced from the contact of that stick,' since the fifth-case ending is present even in the <s>pratijñā</s>, to prevent over-extension, [the qualification] 'conveying the <s>liṅga</s>' is added — meaning: conveying the <s>hetu</s>. 'That which conveys the <s>vyāpti</s>' means: a sentence that generates cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> as pervading the <s>hetu</s> under consideration in the subject possessing the <s>hetu</s> under consideration. If one asks how the <s>udāharaṇa</s> conveys pervasion — it is thus: by established secondary signification (<s>nirūḍhalakṣaṇā</s>) of the word <s>sādhya</s> referring to the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the pervasion of the <s>hetu</s>. Nor should one object that the double occurrence of the <s>yat</s> word is redundant, for it serves meaningfully as an indicator of such purport. Alternatively, in the verbal cognition, the first <s>yat</s>-word refers to the kitchen, the second <s>yat</s>-word refers to something other than the kitchen that possesses the <s>hetu</s> under consideration; the first <s>tat</s>-word refers to the kitchen, the second <s>tat</s>-word refers to something other than the kitchen possessing the <s>sādhya</s> — and after such verbal cognition arises, the cognition of pervasion is subsequently mental. Thus the orientation of the <s>udāharaṇa</s> toward conveying <s>vyāpti</s> remains intact, so there is no fault. This is the general direction. 'Conveying the <s>liṅga</s> as qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>' means: a sentence that generates cognition having as its qualifier the <s>hetu</s> pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s> under consideration, with the qualificand delimited by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>. In the reading '<s>upanaya</s> is for the purpose of cognition of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (the property of being a property of the subject),' by supplying the complement 'is employed,' the intended meaning is to be reconciled somehow with the meaning already shown. 'A statement conveying the <s>pakṣa</s> as possessing the <s>sādhya</s> by virtue of the <s>hetu</s>' means: a sentence that generates cognition whose content is the <s>pakṣa</s> as possessing the <s>sādhya</s> qualified by the property of being indicated by <s>hetu</s>-cognition. The cognition pertaining to the properties of being unsublated and free from counterbalancing reasons should be understood as arising mentally at a subsequent time.

children.translated_text: He states the refined definition of <s>pratijñā</s> with 'delimited by <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>' and so forth. In the sentence 'the mountain possesses fire,' since the cognition of the form 'the mountain possesses fire' has its qualificand delimited by mountain-hood (<s>parvatatva</s>) which is the <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>, and has its qualifier delimited by fire-hood (<s>vahnitva</s>) which is the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>, the definition applies to the sentence 'the mountain possesses fire' which generates such cognition. If the condition of having a qualificand delimited by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s> were not included, then in the <s>udāharaṇa</s> 'whatever possesses smoke possesses fire,' from the portion 'it possesses fire,' a cognition of the form 'what possesses smoke possesses fire' would arise, and since that has its qualifier delimited by fire-hood, there would be over-extension to the <s>udāharaṇa</s> sentence which generates such cognition. But when the condition of having a qualificand delimited by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s> is included, since the said cognition, though having its qualificand delimited by smoke-possessing-hood, does not have its qualificand delimited by mountain-hood, there is no fault. If one were to state merely 'that which generates cognition with a qualificand delimited by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>' without including the condition of having a qualifier delimited by <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>, there would be over-extension to the <s>upanaya</s> sentence 'and this is so,' since the cognition it generates, of the form 'the mountain possesses smoke pervaded by fire,' has its qualificand delimited by mountain-hood.

children.translated_text: fault. Similarly, if only 'having the <s>pakṣa</s> as qualificand' were stated, there would be over-extension to the sentence 'substance possesses fire.' To prevent this, the condition of having the qualificand delimited by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s> is included. To prevent over-extension to the sentence 'the mountain possesses substance-hood,' instead of saying 'having the <s>sādhya</s> as qualificand,' it is said 'having the qualificand delimited by <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>.' Furthermore, since even the cognition generated by the aggregate-apprehending sentence 'the mountain possesses substance-hood, and the substance possesses fire' would have its qualificand delimited by mountain-hood and its qualifier delimited by fire-hood, to prevent over-extension to such a sentence, by incorporating the relation of determinans-determinandum between the qualificand-ness and qualifier-ness, <s>pratijñā</s> is [defined as]: a sentence that generates a cognition possessing qualificand-ness residing in the <s>pakṣa</s> delimited by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>, which [qualificand-ness] is the determinandum of the qualifier-ness residing in the <s>sādhya</s> delimited by <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>.
