children.translated_text: should be stated. 'External to the syllogism (<s>nyāya</s>)' — this is the exclusion of the indifferent person's sentence 'the mountain possesses fire,' which is not a member of the five-membered syllogism. 'This should be understood in subsequent passages as well' — the meaning is: the word 'sentence' in the definitions of the reason and the like, being limited to sentences that are members of the syllogism, does not over-extend to sentences external to the syllogism that have the same form as the reason and the like. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'The reason is a sentence ending in the fifth [case-ending] that presents the mark (<s>liṅga</s>).' Its meaning is: being a sentence that, while ending in the fifth case-ending, generates knowledge having the mark as its content. And the part 'because there is smoke' and so forth has that character — this is the application of the definition. If the qualifier 'while ending in the fifth case-ending' is not included, there would be over-extension to the three [members] starting with the example, since they too convey the mark. Therefore, 'while ending in the fifth case-ending' is stated. In cases like 'this is not from a stick, because it is a substance not produced by the conjunction of that stick,' since the proposition 'this is not from a stick' also ends in the fifth case-ending, to prevent over-extension there, 'that conveys the mark' is stated. What is intended is the mark-conveying [of the mark] that is the reason for the inference whose probandum is under discussion — hence there is no defect. Due to the word 'sentence' having the purport of being a member of the syllogism, there is no over-extension in the part 'therefore' within the conclusion, since that part, even while being a member of the syllogistic conclusion, does not [itself] have the status of being a syllogistic member. Nor should it be said that since the part 'from a stick' within the proposition 'this is not from a stick,' though being a member of the syllogistic proposition, lacks the status of being a syllogistic member and hence there is no over-extension — and therefore the qualifier 'that conveys the mark' is purposeless. For then, since even a part of the syllogistic-member proposition is itself a syllogistic member, over-extension would arise. Nor should it be said that in the conclusion-member 'therefore' part, there is then over-extension — because by 'ending in the fifth case-ending' what is intended is ending in the fifth case-ending that conveys the probandum conjoined with the qualifier of the subject under discussion, and hence there is no defect. Now, from the <s>Dīpikā</s> text 'the example is what presents invariable concomitance,' the definition of the example is understood to be: being a sentence that generates knowledge having invariable concomitance as its content. But that over-extends to the application (<s>upanaya</s>) and conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>), since those too present invariable concomitance — because the word <s>tathā</s> ('so') constituting the application has the meaning 'possessing smoke pervaded by fire,' and the word <s>tasmāt</s> ('therefore') constituting the conclusion has the meaning 'because of possessing smoke pervaded by fire.' Anticipating this doubt, he explains — with 'having the subject [which possesses] the reason in question' and so forth. In the example 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire,' the word 'fire' is used by secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) for fire pervading smoke; the repeated <s>yat</s>-<s>tat</s> words are indicative of secondary signification. And accordingly, the meaning is: possessing smoke is possessing fire pervading smoke. Thereby, the definition of example is obtained as: being a sentence that generates knowledge having as its qualificand what possesses the reason in question and as its qualifier-mode the probandum pervading the reason in question. Since the application and conclusion lack this definition, there is no over-extension — this is the purport. Now, even so, sentences like 'possessing smoke, possessing fire pervading smoke' and the like would also have the unwanted consequence of being examples. Nor is this a desired consequence — because it contradicts the tradition of logicians. To this he says — with 'the indication' and so forth. What is intended as the definition of example is precisely the collectivity of a word that conveys the possessor of the reason qualified by the delimitor of the reason-hood, following the repeated <s>yat</s>-word, and a word that conveys the possessor of the probandum qualified by the delimitor of the probandum-hood, following the <s>tat</s>-word. Therefore there is no defect — this is the purport. Further details are [to be found] elsewhere.

children.text:
pakṣatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭetyādi/ vahnivyāpyadhūmavāniti
vākye 'tivyāptivāraṇāya pakṣatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭaviśeṣyakatvaniveśaḥ/
parvato dhūmavāniti vākye 'tivyāptivāraṇāya
prakṛtasādhyavyāpyatvaniveśaḥ/
prakṛtasādhyaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitavyāptiniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitahetuniṣṭhaprakāratāśālibodhajanakavākyamityarthaḥ/
tena 'parvato dhūmavān' iti vākyasyāpi vastuto vahnivyāpyo
yo dhūmastatprakārakatvādativyāptiritiśaṅkāyāḥ nāvasaraḥ/
hetasādhyavattayā pakṣapratipādakamiti dīpikāgranthāt hetumattayā
sādhyavattayā ca pakṣapratipādakatvaṃ nigamanasya lakṣaṇamityavagamyate/ tathā
sati nigamane 'sambhavaḥ/ 'tasmāt tathā' iti nigamanavākyasya
sādhyavattayā pakṣabodhakatve 'pi hetumattayā pakṣabodhakatvābhāvāt/
pañcamyarthasya sādhye 'nvayena pakṣe 'nvayābhāvāt/ evaṃ 'dhūmavān
vahnimāśca parvataḥ' iti vākye 'tivyāptiśca/ ato vyācaṣṭe -
hetujñāneti/ pañcamyāḥ jñānajñāpyatvamarthaḥ/ jñāne
children.translated_text: 'Qualified by the delimitor of subject-hood' and so forth. To prevent over-extension in the sentence 'possessing smoke pervaded by fire,' the qualification of being qualified by the delimitor of subject-hood is included. To prevent over-extension in the sentence 'the mountain possesses smoke,' the qualification of being pervaded by the probandum in question is included. The meaning is: a sentence that generates knowledge whose qualifier-mode is the reason residing in the invariable concomitance that is the qualifier-mode of the cognition having the probandum in question as its qualifier-mode, and whose qualificand is delimited by the delimitor of subject-hood. Thereby, there is no occasion for the doubt that even the sentence 'the mountain possesses smoke' would actually have over-extension because the smoke which pervades fire is indeed its qualifier-mode. From the <s>Dīpikā</s> text 'the conclusion presents the subject as possessing the reason and the probandum,' it is understood that the definition of the conclusion is: presenting the subject as possessing the reason and as possessing the probandum. In that case, there is impossibility in the conclusion. Because the conclusion-sentence 'therefore so' (<s>tasmāt tathā</s>), even though it presents the subject as possessing the probandum, does not present the subject as possessing the reason — since the meaning of the fifth case-ending does not syntactically connect with the probandum so as to [connect with] the subject. Similarly, there is over-extension in the sentence 'possessing smoke and possessing fire is the mountain.' To this he explains — with 'knowledge of the reason' and so forth. The meaning of the fifth [case-ending] is being knowable by knowledge. In knowledge,

children.text:
prakṛtyarthasya hetoḥ
viṣayatāsambandhenānvayaḥ/ tathāśabdasya sādhyavānityarthaḥ/ sādhye
pañcamyarthasya jñānajñāpyatvasyāśrayatayānvayaḥ/ tathā ca
hetuviṣayakajñānajñāpyatvāśrayasādhyavān pakṣa ityākārakabodhaḥ
nigamanāt jāyata iti nigamanavākye lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/
abādhitatvādikaṃ nigamanaprayojanamiti katham? nigamanavākyāt
abādhitatvāsatpratipakṣitatvayorapratipakṣitatvayorapratipatterityāśaṅkyāha
- uttarakālamiti/ tathā ca pūrvoktarītyā śābdabodhānantaraṃ ayaṃ
heturabādhitaḥ asatpratipakṣaśceti mānasaṃ jñānamutpadyata iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: the meaning of the primary stem — the reason — has its syntactic connection through the content-relation. The word <s>tathā</s> has the meaning 'possessing the probandum.' In the probandum, the meaning of the fifth case-ending — the property of being knowable by knowledge — has its connection as the locus. And accordingly, the knowledge whose content is the conclusion generates from the conclusion the cognition: 'the subject possesses the probandum that is the locus of being-knowable-by-knowledge-having-the-reason-as-content' — this is the application of the definition to the conclusion-sentence. 'How [can] unsublatedness and the like [be] the purpose of the conclusion?' Anticipating the doubt that unsublatedness and the absence of a counter-argument cannot be known from the conclusion-sentence, he says — 'at a later time.' And accordingly, after the verbal cognition obtained in the stated manner, the mental cognition 'this reason is unsublated and without a counter-argument' arises — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: AnTs_47 svārthānumitiparārthānumityor liṅgaparāmarśa eva karaṇam / tasmāl liṅgaparāmarśā'numānam //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 47:] In both inference for oneself (<s>svārthānumiti</s>) and inference for others (<s>parārthānumiti</s>), the apprehension of the mark (<s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s>) alone is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). Therefore, the apprehension of the mark is inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

children.text:
svārthānumitiparārthānumityoḥ liṅgaparāmarśa eva karaṇam/
tasmāt liṅgaparāmarśo 'numānam/
children.translated_text: In both inference for oneself and inference for others, the apprehension of the mark alone is the instrument. Therefore, the apprehension of the mark is inference.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
anumitikaraṇamāha
- svārtheti/
children.translated_text: He states the instrument of inferential cognition — with 'inference for oneself' and so forth.

children.text: viśiṣṭaparāmarśasyānumitihetutvasthāpanam
children.translated_text: Establishment of the qualified apprehension (<s>viśiṣṭaparāmarśa</s>) as the cause of inferential cognition

children.text:
nanu
vyāptismṛtipakṣadharmatājñānābhyāmeva anumitisambhave
viśiṣṭaparāmarśaḥ kimarthamaṅgīkartavya iti cet-na/
children.translated_text: Now, when inferential cognition is possible from the memory of invariable concomitance and the knowledge of the reason's presence in the subject alone, why should a qualified apprehension be accepted? — if thus objected: no,

children.text:
'vahnivyāpyavānayam'
iti śābdaparāmarśasthale parāmarśaṃsyāvaśyakatayā lāghavena sarvatra
parāmarśasyaiva kāraṇatvāt/ liṅgaṃ na karaṇam, atītādau
vyabhicārāt/ 'vyāpāravat kāraṇaṃ karaṇam' iti mate
parāmarśandvārā vyāptijñānaṃ karaṇam/ tajjanyatve sati tajjanyajanako
vyāpāraḥ/ anumānamupasaṃharati - tasmāditi/
children.translated_text: because in the case where 'this possesses what is pervaded by fire' is a verbal apprehension, since the necessity of apprehension is established, by the principle of parsimony, apprehension alone has causality everywhere. The mark itself is not the instrument, because of deviation in cases of past [marks] and the like. In the view that 'the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is the cause that has an operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>),' knowledge of invariable concomitance is the instrument through the medium of apprehension. Operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>) is: being produced by it and being the producer of what is produced by it. He concludes [the discussion of] inference — with 'therefore' and so forth.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanu
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhiparāmarśasya anumitiṃ prati hetutve
tatrānanyathāsiddhatvaniyatapūrvavṛttitvayordvayoḥ kalpanīyatayā
gauravam/ 'vahnivyāpyo dhūmaḥ, dhūmavān parvataḥ' iti jñānadvayasya
tava mate viśiṣṭaparāmarśaṃ prati kāraṇatvena kḷpyatasya karaṇatve tu
ananyathāsiddhatvamātrasya kalpanīyatayā lāghavamiti prābhākaraḥ śaṅkate -
nanviti/ vahnivyāpyavānayamiti/ atra tvadabhimatakāraṇasya asattvena
vyabhicārāt na jñānadvayasya kāraṇatvaṃ sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/ kathañcidapi
vyāpyatāvacchedakadhūmatvāderbhānaṃ parāmarśe na sambhavatīti sphoraṇāya
śābdeti/ lāghaveneti/ kalpanālāghavenetyarthaḥ/ tathā hi - jñānadvaye
ananyathāsiddhatvaniyatapūrvavṛttitvayoḥ kalpanāpekṣayā
viśiṣṭaparāmarśe tatkalpanasyaiva laghīyastvamiti/
children.translated_text: Now, if the apprehension that apprehends the qualification constituted by invariable concomitance has causality for inferential cognition, then since both non-dispensability and invariable precedence must be postulated for it, there is heaviness [of postulation]. In your view, the two cognitions 'smoke is pervaded by fire' and 'the mountain possesses smoke,' since they are posited as having causality for the qualified apprehension, if their causality [for inference directly] were [accepted], only non-dispensability would need to be postulated — hence lightness [of postulation]. Thus the <s>Prābhākara</s> raises the doubt — with 'now' and so forth. 'This possesses what is pervaded by fire' — the purport is: since what you accept as the cause is absent there, and hence there is deviation, the causality of the two cognitions is not possible. To make explicit that the appearance of the pervaded-ness-delimiting property like smoke-ness in the apprehension is in no way possible, [he adds] the word 'verbal.' 'By parsimony' — the meaning is: by parsimony of postulation. Thus: compared to postulating both non-dispensability and invariable precedence for the two cognitions, the postulation of those for the qualified apprehension alone is lighter.

children.text:
vastutastu
taddharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyakavyāptiprakārakaniścayaviśiṣṭataddharmāvacchi nnaprakārakapakṣatāvacchedakāvacchi-
children.translated_text: In truth, the delimiting property of the causality is precisely the property of being an ascertainment having as its qualificand what is delimited by such-and-such a property and having as its qualifier-mode the invariable concomitance, qualified by an ascertainment having as its qualificand what is delimited by such-and-such a property and delimited by the delimitor of the subject-hood —

children.text:
nnaviśeṣyakaniścayasyaiva kāraṇatāvacchedakatvaṃ
jñānadvayasādhāraṇyenana tanmate mantavyam/ naiyāyikamate tu -
vyāptiviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhiniścayatvaṃ kāraṇatāvacchedakamiti
kāraṇatāvacchedakalāghavam avadheyam/ vinigamanāviraheṇa
jñānamānaliṅgatvenāpi karaṇatvaṃ vadatāṃ ācāryāṇāṃ mataṃ nirasyati
- liṅgaṃ na karaṇamiti/ vyabhicārāditi/
tatrāpyanumiteranubhavasiddhatvena tadavyavahitapūrvaṃ
bhūtabhaviṣyaddhūmāderasattvāditi bhāvaḥ/ mata iti/
'phalāyogavyavacchinnaṃ kāraṇaṃ karaṇam' iti mate parāmarśa eva
karaṇamiti dhyeyam/ karaṇe ativyāptivāraṇāya - tajjanyatve satīti/
children.translated_text: this should be understood as common to both the two cognitions [jointly] — and hence it should not be thought [that there is a difference] in that view. But in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view — the delimiting property of causality is the property of being an ascertainment apprehending the qualification constituted by invariable concomitance-qualification — the parsimony of the delimiting property of causality should be noted. He refutes the view of those teachers who, dispensing with analysis, state that even the mark itself, as a means of knowledge through non-cognition (<s>jñānaliṅga</s>), has instrument-hood — with 'the mark is not the instrument' and so forth. 'Because of deviation' — the purport is: since inference too is established through experience, what immediately precedes it — namely past and future smoke and the like — is absent. 'In the view' — in the view that 'the instrument is the cause that excludes the result' (<s>phalāyogavyavacchinnaṃ kāraṇaṃ karaṇam</s>), it should be noted that the apprehension alone is the instrument. To prevent over-extension in the instrument — [he adds] 'while being produced by it.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
naiyāyikenāpi
ādau dhūmadarśanam, tataḥ vyāptismaraṇam, tataḥ
vahnivyāpyadhūmavānayamiti viśiṣṭaparāmarśaḥ, tato 'numitiriti
kramasya svīkaraṇīyatayā dhūmadarśanavyāptismṛtibhyāmeva
anumitisambhavāt madhye viśiṣṭaparāmarśaḥ kimartha iti prābhākareṇa
śaṅkitam/ śaṅkeyaṃ nopapadyate/ viśiṣṭaparāmarśādeva
anumitisambhave jñānadvayasya nānumitihetutvam anyathāsiddhatvāditi
naiyāyikena vaktuṃ śakyatvāt/ ataḥ śaṅkiturāśayamabhivyanakti - nanu
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyetyādinā/ tathā ca viśiṣṭaparāmarśasya
ananyathāsiddhatvaṃ niyatapūrvavṛttitvaṃ cetyubhayaṃ kalpanīyam/
jñānadvayasya tu ananyathāsiddhatvaṃ niyatapūrvavṛttitvaṃ cetyubhayaṃ
kalpanīyam/ jñānadvayasya tu ananyathāsiddhatvamātraṃ kalpanīyam, na tu
niyatapūrvavṛttitvamapi, kḷptatvāt/ ato lāghavāt
jñānadvayamevānumitihetuḥ na tu viśiṣṭaparāmarśa iti prābhākarasya
bhāva ityāśayaḥ/ yatra 'vahnivyāpyavānayam' iti śabdaśravaṇāt
'ayaṃ vahnivyāpyavān' iti śābdabodhātmako viśiṣṭaparāmarśaḥ
jātaḥ tatra taduttarakṣaṇe 'numiterjāyamānatayā jñānadvayasya
vyatirekavyabhicārāt
children.translated_text: Even the <s>Naiyāyika</s> accepts the sequence: first, the perception of smoke; then, the memory of invariable concomitance; then, the qualified apprehension 'this possesses smoke pervaded by fire'; then, inferential cognition. Given this, the <s>Prābhākara</s> raises the doubt: since inferential cognition is possible from the two cognitions — perception of smoke and memory of invariable concomitance — alone, what is the purpose of a qualified apprehension in between? This doubt is not well-founded, because since inferential cognition is possible from the qualified apprehension alone, the <s>Naiyāyika</s> can say that the two cognitions do not have causality for inference due to dispensability. Therefore, he makes explicit the intent of the doubter — with 'Now, of the qualified qualification' and so forth. And accordingly, for the qualified apprehension, both non-dispensability and invariable precedence must be postulated. But for the two cognitions, only non-dispensability needs to be postulated, not also invariable precedence, since that is already established. Therefore, by parsimony, the two cognitions alone are the cause of inference, not the qualified apprehension — this is the <s>Prābhākara</s>'s intent. Where, from the hearing of the verbal expression 'this possesses what is pervaded by fire,' a qualified apprehension in the form of verbal cognition 'this possesses what is pervaded by fire' arises — there, since the inferential cognition arises at the very next moment, there is deviation in the negative concomitance of the two cognitions —

children.text:
nānumitihetutvamiti sarvatraiva tasya hetutvamiti rītyā
prābhākaramataṃ dīpikāyāṃ khaṇḍitam/ nanu prābhākaramate
jñānadvayasyāpi vyāptijñānatvena pakṣadharmatājñānatvena ca
kāraṇatvamiṣyate/ 'vahnivyāpyavānayam' iti śabdaparāmarśasyāpi
vyāptijñānatvapakṣadharmatājñānatvarūpakāraṇatāvacchedakākrāntatvāt
kāraṇatvamiṣyata eveti na vyabhicāra ityāśaṅkyāha -
kathañcidapīti/ yaṃa bhāvaḥ - vyāptijñānapakṣadharmatājñānayoḥ
vyāptijñānatvapakṣadharmatājñānatvābhyāṃ kāraṇatvasvīkāre 'āloko
vahnivyāpyaḥ dhūmavān parvataḥ' iti jñānābhyāmapi 'parvato
vahnimān' ityunamityāpattiḥ/ ato vyāpyatāvacchedakatayā
gṛhītadharmāṃvacchinne pakṣadharmatāvagāhi jñānatvena kāraṇatvaṃ vaktavyam/
tathā ca vahnivyāpyavānayamiti jñāne
vyāpyatāvacchedakadhūmatvāderabhānena
uktakāraṇatāvacchedakānākrāntatayā kāraṇatāvacchedakāvacchinnaṃ vināpi
kāryotpattyā vyatirekavyabhicāraḥ prābhākaramate durvāra iti/
sphoraṇāyeti/ dhūmatvopasthāpakapadābhāvādityarthaḥ/ tathā hātyādi/
śābdaparāmarśādanumitiḥ yatra bhavati tatra jñānadvayaṃ
vināpyanumiteranubhavasiddhatayā tatrāpi yadi
jñānadvayādevānumitiriti kalpyate tarhi jñānadvayasyānanyathāsiddhatvaṃ
niyatapūrvavṛttitvaṃ cetyubhaya kalpanīyam/ tatra viśiṣṭaparāmarśasya
niyatapūrvavṛttitāyāḥ kḷptatayā ananyathāsiddhatvamātraṃ kalpanīyamiti
naiyāyikamate lāghavamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: The Prābhākara view — that it is not inferential-cause-hood [of the qualified cognition], but rather cause-hood of that [two cognitions] everywhere — has been refuted in the <s>Dīpikā</s>. Objection: In the <s>Prābhākara</s> view, the causality of the two cognitions is accepted through their being vyāptijñāna (knowledge of pervasion) and pakṣadharmatājñāna (knowledge of the property belonging to the subject). Since even the verbal <s>parāmarśa</s> (qualified cognition) 'this possesses what is pervaded by fire' is pervaded by the delimiting conditions of causality in the form of being knowledge of pervasion and knowledge of the subject-property, its causality is accepted — hence there is no deviation. Anticipating this, he says — 'even somehow.' The purport is this: If the causality of <s>vyāptijñāna</s> and <s>pakṣadharmatājñāna</s> is accepted through the properties of being knowledge-of-pervasion and knowledge-of-subject-property, then from the two cognitions 'light is pervaded by fire' and 'the mountain possesses smoke,' the inference 'the mountain possesses fire' would absurdly follow. Therefore, causality must be stated through the property of being a cognition that apprehends the subject-property as delimited by the property grasped as the delimitor of the pervaded-ness. And accordingly, in the cognition 'this possesses what is pervaded by fire,' since smoke-hood and such — which are the delimitors of pervaded-ness — do not appear, because the stated delimiting conditions of causality are not satisfied, even without what is delimited by the delimitor of causality the effect arises — hence the deviation in negative concomitance is unavoidable in the <s>Prābhākara</s> view. 'For the purpose of elucidation' — the meaning is: because there is no word that presents smoke-hood. 'Similarly' and so forth: Where inference arises from verbal <s>parāmarśa</s>, there, since inference is established by experience even without the two cognitions, if even there it is supposed that inference arises only from the two cognitions, then both the indispensability and the invariable prior occurrence of the two cognitions must be supposed. In that case, since the invariable prior occurrence of the qualified <s>parāmarśa</s> is already established, only indispensability need be supposed — hence the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view has the advantage of parsimony. This is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
śābdaparāmarśasthale naiyāyikasya mate lāghave 'pi yatra
jñānadvayādevānumitiḥ tatra pūrvoktarītyā prābhākaramate lāghavamiti
sāmyamityāśaṅkyāha - vastutastviti/
dhūmatvāvacchinnaviśeṣyakavyāpti prakārakaniścayaḥ 'dhūmo vahnivyāpyaḥ'
ityākārakaḥ ekakālāvacchinnaikātmavṛttitvasambandhena tadviśiṣṭaḥ
dhūmatvāvacchinnaprakārakaparvatatvāvacchinnaviśeṣyakaniścayaḥ 'parvato
dhūmavān' ityākārakaḥ/ tathā coktaniścayaviśiṣṭoktaniścayatvaṃ
prābhākaramate anumitikāraṇatāvacchedakam/ naiyāyikamate tu
vyāptiviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhitvam/ tattu dhūmatvānavagāhini
vahnivyāpyavānayamiti śābdaparāmarśeṃ'pyasti/ ataḥ
kāraṇatāvacchedakalāghavāt naiyāyikamatameva yuktamiti bhāvaḥ/
vinigamanāviraheṇeti/ jñāyamānaṃ liṅgaṃ karaṇam atha vā
liṅgaviṣayakajñānaṃ karaṇamiti pakṣayoranyatarasya
sādhutvasādhakayuktyabhāvenetyarthaḥ/ liṅgasya anumitikaraṇatve
jñāyamānābhyāmatītānāgatābhyāṃ liṅgābhyāṃ anumitiḥ na syāt/
anumiteḥ avyavahitapūrvaṃ asatostayoḥ
avyavahitapūrvavṛttitvaghaṭitakaraṇatvāsambhavāt/ liṅgajñānasya
karaṇatve tu atītānāgataliṅgayorasattve 'pi
tadviṣayakajñānasattvādanumitirupapadyate/ tadāha - tatrāpyanumiteriti/
phalāyogavyavacchinnamiti/ kāryāvyavahitapūrvavṛttitvaviśiṣṭaṃ
kāraṇaṃ karaṇamiti mate
parāmarśasyaivānumityavyavahitapūrvaṃvṛttitayā tadave karaṇam,
vyāptijñānasya tu parāmarśavyavahitatvāt na karaṇatvamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: Even though in the case of verbal <s>parāmarśa</s> the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view has parsimony, where inference arises from the two cognitions alone, there in the previously stated manner the <s>Prābhākara</s> view has parsimony — so it is equal. Anticipating this, he says — 'but in reality.' A determinate cognition having as its qualifier the pervasion delimited by smoke-hood, of the form 'smoke is pervaded by fire,' qualified by the relation of belonging to the same temporal-delimitation and same self, combined with a determinate cognition having smoke-hood as qualifier-delimitor and mountain-hood as subject-delimitor, of the form 'the mountain possesses smoke' — thus, the property of being such a qualified determinate cognition is the delimitor of the causal condition of inference in the <s>Prābhākara</s> view. But in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, it is the property of apprehending the qualification by pervasion. And that exists even in the verbal <s>parāmarśa</s> 'this possesses what is pervaded by fire,' which does not apprehend smoke-hood. Therefore, due to the parsimony of the delimitor of the causal condition, the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view alone is justified — this is the purport. 'Due to the absence of a deciding reason' — the meaning is: because there is no reasoning that establishes the correctness of either of the two alternatives — whether the perceived <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) is the instrument, or the cognition having the <s>liṅga</s> as its object is the instrument. If the <s>liṅga</s> itself were the instrument of inference, then inference would not arise from past and future <s>liṅgas</s> that are being cognized, because those two, not existing immediately prior [to the inference], cannot have instrument-hood which requires being the immediately prior existent. But if cognition of the <s>liṅga</s> is the instrument, then even when past and future <s>liṅgas</s> do not exist, since the cognition having them as objects does exist, inference is explained. He states this — 'there too, of inference.' 'Delimited by the exclusion of the result' — in the view that the cause which has the property of existing immediately prior to the effect is the instrument, only the <s>parāmarśa</s> is the instrument since it alone exists immediately prior to inference; but <s>vyāptijñāna</s> (knowledge of pervasion), being mediated by <s>parāmarśa</s>, does not have instrument-hood. This is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: hetuvibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Classification of the inferential mark (<s>hetu</s>)

children.text: AnTs_48 liṅgaṃ trividham / anvayavyatireki kevalānvayi kevalavyatireki ceti / anvayena vyatirekeṇa ca vyāptimad anvayavyatireki / yathā vahnau sādhye dhūmavattvam / yatra dhūmas tatrāgnir yathā mahānasa ity anvayavyāptiḥ / yatra vahnir nāsti tatra dhūmo'pi nāsti yathā mahāhrada iti vyatirekavyāptiḥ / anvayamātravyāptikaṃ kevalānvayi yathā ghaṭo'bhidheyaḥ prameyatvāt paṭavat / atra prameyatvābhidhyatvayor vyatirekavyāptir nāsti sarvasyāpi prameyatvād abhidheyatvāc ca / vyatirekamātravyāptikaṃ kevalavyatireki yathā pṛthivī tarebhyo bhidyate gandhavattvāt / yad itarebhyo na bhidyate na tad gandhavat / yathā jalam / na ceyaṃ tathā / tasmān na tatheti atra yad gandhavat tad itarabhinnam ity anvayadṛṣṭanto nāsti pṛthivīmātrasya pakṣatvāt //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>'s sūtra 48:] The inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is threefold: <s>anvayavyatireki</s> (positive-and-negative), <s>kevalānvayi</s> (purely positive), and <s>kevalavyatireki</s> (purely negative). That which has pervasion through both positive and negative concomitance is <s>anvayavyatireki</s>. For example, when fire is what is to be proved, the property of possessing smoke [is the mark]. 'Where there is smoke, there is fire, as in a kitchen' — this is positive pervasion (<s>anvayavyāpti</s>). 'Where there is no fire, there is no smoke either, as in a great lake' — this is negative pervasion (<s>vyatirekavyāpti</s>). That which has pervasion through positive concomitance alone is <s>kevalānvayi</s>. For example: 'The pot is nameable, because of being knowable, like cloth.' Here there is no negative pervasion between knowability and nameability, since everything is knowable and nameable. That which has pervasion through negative concomitance alone is <s>kevalavyatireki</s>. For example: 'Earth differs from the other [elements], because of possessing smell.' 'Whatever does not differ from the others does not possess smell, like water. And this [earth] is not like that. Therefore it is not so [i.e., it differs].' Here, the positive example 'whatever possesses smell differs from the others' is absent, since earth alone is the subject [and there is no other instance].

children.text:
liṅgaṃ trividham
- anvayavyatireki, kevalānvayi, kevalavyatireki ceti/
children.translated_text: The inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is threefold — <s>anvayavyatireki</s>, <s>kevalānvayi</s>, and <s>kevalavyatireki</s>.

children.text: anvayavyatirekinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>anvayavyatireki</s>

children.text:
anvayena
vyatirekeṇa ca vyāptimat anvayavyatireki/ yathā vahnau sādhye
dhūmavattvam/ yatra dhūmastatrāgniḥ yathā mahānasaḥ ityanvayavyāptiḥ/
yatra vahnirnāsti, tatra dhūmo 'pi nāsti yathā mahāhradaḥ iti
vyatirekavyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: That which has pervasion through positive and negative concomitance is <s>anvayavyatireki</s>. For example, when fire is what is to be proved, the property of possessing smoke [is the mark]. 'Where there is smoke, there is fire, as in a kitchen' — this is positive pervasion (<s>anvayavyāpti</s>). 'Where there is no fire, there is no smoke either, as in a great lake' — this is negative pervasion (<s>vyatirekavyāpti</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
liṅgaṃ vibhajate -
liṅgamiti/
children.translated_text: He classifies the inferential mark — 'the <s>liṅga</s>.'

children.text:
anvayavyatirekiṇaṃ
lakṣaṇati - anvayeneti/ hetusādhyayoḥ vyāptiḥ anvayavyāptiḥ,
tadabhāvayorvyāptiḥ vyatirekavyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>anvayavyatirekin</s> — 'by positive concomitance.' The pervasion of the <s>hetu</s> (probans) and <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is positive pervasion (<s>anvayavyāpti</s>); the pervasion of their absences is negative pervasion (<s>vyatirekavyāpti</s>).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
yadyapyanumānanirūpaṇasyaiva pratijñātatvena tadvibhāga eva ucitaḥ,
tathāpi liṅgasya traividhye pradarśite tajjñānasya traividhyaṃ phalatīti
manasi kṛtvāha - liṅgaṃ vibhajata iti/
children.translated_text: Although, since the examination of inference itself was announced, only its classification would be appropriate, nevertheless, having thought that when the threefold nature of the <s>liṅga</s> is demonstrated, the threefold nature of its cognition follows, he says — 'he classifies the inferential mark.'

children.text:
'anvayena vyatirekeṇa
ca vyāptimat' iti mūlasya 'anvayasahacāragrahagrāhyavyāptimattve sati
children.translated_text: Having understood the root text 'having pervasion through positive and negative concomitance' as meaning 'having pervasion graspable through the apprehension of positive co-occurrence, and also

children.text:
vyatirekasahacāragrahagrāhyavyāptimat' ityarthaṃ manasi kṛtvā
tādṛśavyāptidvayaṃ prakāśayati - hetusādhyayoriti/
children.translated_text: having pervasion graspable through the apprehension of negative co-occurrence,' he elucidates the two such pervasions — 'of the probans and probandum.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
'anvayena
vyatirekeṇa ca vyāptimat' iti yathāśrutamūlāt
anvayavyāptimattve sati vyatirekavyāptimattvamanvayavyatirekiṇo
lakṣaṇamiti pratīyate/ tathā sati kevalavyatirekiṇyativyāptiḥ,
tatrāpi vastuto 'nvayavyāpterapi sattvāt ato vyācaṣṭe -
anvayasahacāragrahagrāhyeti/ sādhyahetvoḥ sāmānādadhikaraṇyaṃ
anvayasahacāraḥ tajjñānajanyajñānaviṣayībhūtā vyāptiḥ
hetuvyāpakasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyarūpā anvayavyāptiḥ/
sādhyābhāvahetvabhāvayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ vyatirekasahacāraḥ
tajjñānajanyajñānaviṣayībhūtā vyāptiḥ
sādhyābhāvavyāpakībhūtābhāvapratiyogitvarūpā vyatirekavyāptiḥ/
anvayenetyatra tṛtīyāyāḥ jñānajñāpyatvamarthaḥ, anvayaśabdaḥ
anvayasahacāraparaḥ, jñānajñāpyatvasya vyāptāvanvayaḥ,
tenānvayasahacārajñānajñāpyā vyāptiriti mūlāllabhyate/ evaṃ
vyatirekaśabdaḥ vyatirekasahacāraparaḥ, tṛtīyārthaḥ jñānajñāpyatvam,
tena vyatirekasahacārajñānajñāpyāvyāptiriti labhyata iti bhāvaḥ1/
children.translated_text: From the root text as it literally reads — 'having pervasion through positive and negative concomitance' — it would appear that the definition of <s>anvayavyatirekin</s> is: having positive pervasion and having negative pervasion. If so, there would be over-extension to <s>kevalavyatirekin</s>, since positive pervasion also actually obtains there. Therefore he explains — 'graspable through the apprehension of positive co-occurrence.' The co-presence of the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>hetu</s> in the same locus is positive co-occurrence (<s>anvayasahacāra</s>); the pervasion that is the content of a cognition born from the cognition of that [co-occurrence], having the form of co-location with that which pervades the <s>hetu</s> and the <s>sādhya</s>, is positive pervasion (<s>anvayavyāpti</s>). The co-presence of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> and the absence of the <s>hetu</s> in the same locus is negative co-occurrence (<s>vyatirekasahacāra</s>); the pervasion that is the content of a cognition born from the cognition of that [co-occurrence], having the form of counter-positive-hood of the absence that pervades the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, is negative pervasion (<s>vyatirekavyāpti</s>). In 'by positive concomitance,' the meaning of the instrumental case is 'being made known by cognition'; the word <s>anvaya</s> refers to positive co-occurrence; the application of 'being made known by cognition' is to pervasion — thus from the root text one obtains: 'pervasion made known by the cognition of positive co-occurrence.' Similarly, the word <s>vyatireka</s> refers to negative co-occurrence, and the meaning of the instrumental is 'being made known by cognition' — thus one obtains: 'pervasion made known by the cognition of negative co-occurrence.' This is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: kevalānvayinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>kevalānvayi</s>

children.text:
anvayamātravyāptikam kevalānvayi/ yathā ghaṭaḥ abhidheyaḥ
prameyatvāt paṭavat iti/ atra prameyatvābhidheyatvayoḥ
vyatirekavyāptiḥ nāsti, sarvasyāpi prameyatvāt abhidheyatvācca/
children.translated_text: That which has pervasion through positive concomitance alone is <s>kevalānvayi</s> (purely positive). For example: 'The pot is nameable, because of <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability), like cloth.' Here there is no negative pervasion between <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) and <s>abhidheyatva</s> (nameability), since everything is knowable and nameable.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
kevalānvayino
lakṣaṇamāha - anvayeti/ kevalānvayisādhyakaṃ liṅgaṃ kevalānvayi/
[vṛttimat] ityantābhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ
kevalānvayitvam/ īśvarapramāviṣayatvaṃ sarvapadābhidheyatvaṃ ca
sarvatra astīti vyatirekābhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>kevalānvayi</s> — 'by positive concomitance alone.' An inferential mark whose <s>sādhya</s> is a <s>kevalānvayi</s> property is <s>kevalānvayi</s>. The <s>kevalānvayi</s> nature is the non-counter-positive-hood of absolute absence having unrestricted occurrence. Being an object of <s>Īśvara</s>'s (God's) valid cognition and being denotable by the word 'all' exist everywhere — hence the absence of negative [concomitance].

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
anvayamātravyāptikatvarūpakevalānvayilakṣaṇe mātrapadena
vyatirekavyāptervyavacchedyatayā siddhyasiddhibhyāṃ vyāghāta
ityālocya prakārāntareṇa pariṣkaroti - kevalānvayisādhyakamiti/
kevalānvayisādhyakavyatirekihetoḥ
children.translated_text: Considering that in the definition of <s>kevalānvayi</s> as 'having pervasion through positive concomitance alone,' the word 'alone' (<s>mātra</s>) should exclude negative pervasion, and there would be a contradiction between its being established and not established, he refines it differently — '<s>kevalānvayi</s>-<s>sādhyaka</s>.' Of a <s>vyatireki</s> (negative) probans whose <s>sādhya</s> is a <s>kevalānvayi</s> property,

children.text:
1. tathā ca
anvayasahacārajñānajanyajñānaviṣayavyāptimatve sati
vyatirekasahacārajñānajanyajñānaviṣayavyāptimattvaṃ anvayavyatirekiṇo
lakṣaṇam/ tatra satyantānupādāne kevalavyatirekiṇyativyāptiḥ/
viśeśyānupādāne kevalānvayinyativyāptiḥ/
vyatirekasahacāreṇāpyanvayavyāptireva gṛhyata iti mate
anavayasahacārajñānavyatirekasahacārajñānobhajajanyajñānaviṣayavyāptimattvaṃ
anvayavyatirekiṇo lakṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] And accordingly, the definition of <s>anvayavyatirekin</s> is: having pervasion that is the content of a cognition born from the cognition of positive co-occurrence, and also having pervasion that is the content of a cognition born from the cognition of negative co-occurrence. If the word <s>sati</s> (the 'when' condition) is not supplied, there is over-extension to <s>kevalavyatirekin</s>. If the qualifier [<s>kevalānvayi</s>-<s>sādhyaka</s>] is not supplied, there is over-extension to <s>kevalānvayi</s>. In the view that through negative co-occurrence too it is only positive pervasion that is grasped, the definition of <s>anvayavyatirekin</s> is: having pervasion that is the content of a cognition born jointly from the cognition of positive co-occurrence and the cognition of negative co-occurrence, but not from either alone.

children.text:
saṅgrahāya sādhye
kevalānvayitvaṃ niveśitam/ tadeva nirvakti - atyantābhāveti/
niravacchinnavṛttimadatyantābhāvetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the <s>kevalānvayi</s> nature has been introduced into the <s>sādhya</s> for the sake of inclusion. He explains that very point — 'non-counter-positive-hood of absolute absence.' The meaning is: absolute absence of that which has unrestricted occurrence.

children.text:
tena
gaganābhāvasaṃyogābhāvādisādhyakahetoḥ saṅgrahaḥ/
ghaṭapadābhidheyatvasya paṭādāvasattvena sarvataḥ sattvāsambhavādāha -
sarvapadābhidheyatvamiti/
children.translated_text: Thereby, the inclusion of a probans whose <s>sādhya</s> is the absence of space, the absence of conjunction, and so forth [is secured]. Since the <s>abhidheyatva</s> (nameability) of the word 'pot' does not exist in cloth and so on, and thus cannot exist in everything, he says — 'denotable by the word all.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu
'anvayamātravyāptikaṃ kevalānvayī'ti mūlāt
vyatirekavyāptiśūnyatve sati anvayavyāptimattvaṃ kevalānvayino
lakṣaṇamiti pratīyate/ tathā sati kevalānvayini vyatirekavyāpteḥ
prasiddhatve tacchūnyatvaṃ na sambhavati/ tasyāḥ aprasiddhatve sutarāṃ
tacchūnyatvāprasiddhiriti lakṣaṇamidaṃ nopapadyata ityāśayena
dīpikāyāṃ kevalānvayisādhyakaṃ kevalānvayi ityuktamityāha -
anvayamātreti/ kevalānvayisādhyakaḥ kevalānvayī hetuḥ 'idaṃ vācyaṃ
jñeyatvāt' ityādiḥ yathā kevalānvayī, tathā kevalānvayisādhyakaḥ
vyatirekī heturapi 'idaṃ vācyaṃ ghaṭatvāt' ityādiḥ
kevalānvayyeva/ tathā cobhayasaṅgrahāya hetau
kevalānvayitvamaniveśya kevalānvayisādhyakahetutvaṃ kevalānvayino
lakṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Objection: From the root text '<s>kevalānvayi</s> is that which has pervasion through positive concomitance alone,' it appears that the definition of <s>kevalānvayi</s> is: having positive pervasion while being devoid of negative pervasion. If so, when negative pervasion of <s>kevalānvayi</s> is well-established, being devoid of it is not possible; and if it is not well-established, then all the more so its being-devoid-of cannot be established — thus this definition would not hold. With this intent, [explaining] that in the <s>Dīpikā</s> it was said '<s>kevalānvayi</s> is that whose <s>sādhya</s> is a <s>kevalānvayi</s> property,' he says — 'by positive concomitance alone' and so forth. Just as a <s>kevalānvayi</s> probans has a <s>kevalānvayi</s> <s>sādhya</s>, such as 'this is nameable, because of knowability,' similarly a <s>vyatireki</s> probans also has a <s>kevalānvayi</s> <s>sādhya</s>, such as 'this is nameable, because of pot-hood' — it too is purely <s>kevalānvayi</s>. And accordingly, for the inclusion of both, without introducing <s>kevalānvayi</s> nature into the probans itself, the property of being a probans whose <s>sādhya</s> is <s>kevalānvayi</s> is stated as the definition of <s>kevalānvayi</s>,

children.text:
kathitamityāha -
kevalānvayisādhyaketi/ vyatirekihetuḥ atyantābhāvapratiyogī
hetuḥ/ tadeveti/ kevalānvayitvamevetyarthaḥ/ nanu
atyantābhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ kevalānvayitvam, tatsādhyakahetutvaṃ
children.translated_text: he says — '<s>kevalānvayi</s>-<s>sādhyaka</s>.' A <s>vyatireki</s> probans is one that is the counter-positive of an absolute absence. The word 'that itself' means: <s>kevalānvayi</s> nature itself. Objection: If <s>kevalānvayi</s> nature is non-counter-positive-hood of absolute absence, and being a probans whose <s>sādhya</s> has that [nature] is

children.text:
kevalānvayiliṅgatvamityuktau ākāśābhāvasādhyakasya
ghaṭatvādihetoḥ saṅgraho na syāt ākāśābhāvasya
1ākāśarūpa-ākāśābhāvātyantābhāvapratiyogitvena
atyantābhāvāpratiyogitvābhāvāt/ evaṃ
saṃyogābhāvasādhyakahetorapi
children.translated_text: stated as <s>kevalānvayi</s> inferential-mark-hood, then there would be no inclusion of a probans such as pot-hood whose <s>sādhya</s> is the absence of space, because the absence of space, being the counter-positive of the absolute absence of that which has the nature of space, lacks non-counter-positive-hood of absolute absence. Similarly, even for a probans whose <s>sādhya</s> is the absence of conjunction,

children.text:
saṅgraho na syāt
saṃyogābhāvasya 2saṃyogātmakātyantābhāvapratiyogitvāt ityata
āha - niravacchinnetyādi/
children.translated_text: there would be no inclusion, because the absence of conjunction is the counter-positive of an absolute absence having the nature of conjunction. To address this, he says — 'unrestricted' and so forth.

children.text:
1. ākāśarūpaḥ yaḥ
ākāśābhāvātyantābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvenetyarthaḥ/ abhāvābhāvasya
pratiyogisvarūpatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 1:] The meaning is: by being the counter-positive of that absolute absence of the absence of space which has the form of space. The purport is: because the absence of an absence has the nature of the counter-positive [itself].

children.text:
2. saṃyogarūpaḥ yaḥ
saṃyogābhāvātyantabhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 2:] The meaning is: because [the absence of conjunction] is the counter-positive of that absolute absence of the absence of conjunction which has the form of conjunction.

children.text:
saṃyogasyāvyāpyavṛttitayā sāvacchinnavṛttikatvāt
niravacchinnavṛttimān abhāvaḥ na saṃyogātmakaḥ abhāvaḥ, api tu
ghaṭādyabhāvaḥ tadapratiyogitvaṃ saṃyogābhāve 'stīti tasya
kevalānvayitvopapattiḥ/ gaganarūpo 'bhāvastu na vṛttimān
tasyāvṛttitvāt, api tu vṛttimān ghaṭādyabhāvaḥ tadapratiyogitvaṃ
gaganābhāve 'stīti tasyāpi kevalānvayitvamupapadyata iti bhāvaḥ/ evaṃ
ca yat sarvatrāsti, na kvāpi tadabhāvaḥ tat kevalānvayīti labhyate/
nanvabhidheyatvasya kathaṃ kevalānvayitvam/ abhidheyatvaṃ hi
padaśaktimattvam/ tacca ghaṭapaṭādipadabhedena bhinnamiti
ghaṭapadābhidheyatvasya
paṭādiniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitvādityāśaṅkate - ghaṭapadeti/
sarvapadābhidheyatvamiti/ sarva iti yat padaṃ tadabhidheyatvaṃ
sarvatrāstīti sarvapadābhidheyatvaṃ kevalānvayi/ tathā ca
children.translated_text: Since saṃyoga (conjunction) has limited occurrence (avyāpyavṛtti), it possesses delimited occurrence; the absence that has undelimited occurrence is not an absence of the nature of conjunction, but rather the absence of a pot and the like — the property of not being the counter-positive of that exists in the absence of conjunction, hence the establishment of its being <s>kevalānvayin</s> (purely positive) is justified. As for an absence of the nature of the sky, it does not have occurrence, since it is non-occurring; rather, the absence of a pot and the like has occurrence — the property of not being the counter-positive of that exists in the absence of the sky, hence the purely positive nature of that too is justified — this is the purport. And thus what exists everywhere, the absence of which is nowhere found, that is <s>kevalānvayin</s> — this is obtained. Now, how can <s>abhidheyatva</s> (expressibility) be purely positive? For expressibility is the property of being the potency-locus of a word. And that differs according to the distinction of words like 'pot,' 'cloth,' etc. — thus the expressibility-by-the-word-'pot' would be the counter-positive of absolute absence residing in cloth and the like — he raises this objection with 'by the word pot.' 'Expressibility by the word "all"' — the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>), the expressibility by that word exists everywhere, hence expressibility-by-the-word-'all' is purely positive. And thus

children.text:
'ghaṭaḥ abhidheyaḥ
prameyatvāt' iti prayoge sarvapadābhidheyatvaṃ sādhyaṃ iti
kevalānvayitvamupapadyata iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: in the inferential usage 'a pot is expressible, because of being knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>),' the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is expressibility-by-the-word-'all,' hence the purely positive nature is justified — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: kevalavyatirekinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Kevalavyatirekin</s> (Purely Negative Inference)

children.text:
vyatirekamātravyāptikaṃ kevalavyatireki/ yathā pṛthivī
itarebhyo bhidyate gandhavattvāt/ yat itarebhyo na bhidyate na tat
gandhavat yathā jalam/ na ceyaṃ tathā/ tasmāt na tathā iti/ atra yat
gandhavat tat itarabhinnam ityanvayadṛṣṭāntaḥ nāsti,
pṛthivīmātrasya pakṣatvāt/
children.translated_text: That which has <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) only through negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is <s>kevalavyatirekin</s> (purely negative). For example: earth is different from the others, because it possesses smell (<s>gandhavatva</s>). Whatever is not different from the others does not possess smell, like water. But this [earth] is not so. Therefore it is not so [i.e., earth is different]. Here there is no positive example (<s>anvayadṛṣṭānta</s>) for 'whatever possesses smell is different from the others,' since only earth is the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject of inference).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
kavelavyatirekiṇo lakṣaṇamāha - vyatireketi/ tadudāharati -
yatheti/ nanu itarabhedaḥ prasiddho vā na vā/ ādye yatra prasiddhaḥ tatra
hetusattve anvayitvam, asattve asādhāraṇyam/ dvītīye
sādhyajñānābhāvāt kathaṃ tadviśiṣṭānumitiḥ/ viśeṣaṇajñānābhāve
viśiṣṭajñānānadayāt pratiyogijñānābhāvāt
vyatirekavyāptijñānamapi na syāditi cet - na/
jalāditrayodaśānyonyābhāvānāṃ trayodaśasu pratyekaṃ prasiddhānāṃ
melanaṃ pṛthivyāṃ sādhyate/ tatra
trayodaśatvāvacchinnabhedātmakasādhyasyaikādhikaraṇavṛttitvābhāvāt
nānvayitvāsādhāraṇye/ pratyekādhikaraṇaprasiddhyā
sādhyaviśiṣṭānumitiḥ vyatirekavyāptinirūpaṇaṃ ceti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>kevalavyatirekin</s> — with 'vyatireka.' He illustrates it — with 'for example.' [Objection:] Now, is the difference from the others well-established or not? In the first case, where it is well-established, if the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is present there, it would be <s>anvayitva</s> (positive concomitance); if absent, it would be <s>asādhāraṇya</s> (uncommon). In the second case, since there is no cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), how can there be an inference qualified by it? Because without cognition of the qualifier, there is no qualified cognition; and because without cognition of the counter-positive, there would be no knowledge of negative pervasion either — if thus objected: no. The mutual absences of the thirteen [categories] among water and the rest — which are individually well-established in each of the thirteen — their combination is what is proved in earth. Since the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of difference delimited by thirteen-ness does not occur in a single locus, there is neither positive concomitance nor uncommonness. Through individual well-establishment in each locus, the inference qualified by the <s>sādhya</s>, as well as the knowledge of negative pervasion, [is possible].

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mūle
vyatirekamātravyāptikamiti/ niścitavyatirekamātravyāptikamityarthaḥ/
tena 'pṛthivī itarebhyo bhidyate gandhavattvāt' ityādau
anvayavyāptessattve 'pi na lakṣaṇāsaṅgatiḥ/ itadabhedaḥ -
pṛthivītaratvāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedaḥ/ anvayitvamiti/
anvayasahacāragrahagrāhyavyāptimattvaṃ syādityarthaḥ/ asādhāraṇyamiti/
sapakṣavyāvṛttatvarūpāsādhāraṇalakṣaṇākrāntatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
aprasiddhasādhyake 'pi sādhyaviśeṣaṇakānumitirevetyābhiprāyeṇāha -
sādhyetyādi/ vyatirekavyāptīti/
sādhyābhāvavyāpakābhāvapratiyogitvarūpetyarthaḥ/
pṛthivītarasāmānyabhedo na sādhyate, api tu jalādibhedakṛṭaṃ
sādhyate/ tathā ca toktadoṣāvasara ityāhajalādīti/ jalādīnāṃ ce
trayodaśānyonyābhāvāsteṣāṃ kūṭaṃ sādhyata ityarthaḥ/ samudāyasya
prasiddhyasambhavādāha - pratyekamini/ trayodaśatvāvacchinneti/
anumiteḥ pūrvaṃ niścitasādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnavato dharmiṇa
evāprasiddhyā na tatra hetoḥ sattvāsattvanibandhane anvayitvāsādhāraṇye
iti samuditārthaḥ/ pratyekaṃ prasiddhau
apekṣābuddhiviśeṣaviṣayatvarūpasamudāyatvaviśiṣṭajñānaṃ sambhavati/
tathā ca viśeṣaṇatāvacchedakaprakārakanirṇayasya sadbhāvāt
sādhyatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhyanumitiḥ
children.translated_text: In the root text, 'vyatirekamātravyāptikam' — the meaning is: that which has pervasion only through ascertained negative concomitance. Therefore, in cases like 'earth is different from the others because of possessing smell,' even though positive pervasion actually obtains, there is no incongruity with the definition. 'Difference from the others' means difference whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by being-other-than-earth. 'Positive concomitance' — the meaning is: it would have pervasion apprehensible through the grasping of positive co-occurrence (<s>anvayasahacāragraha</s>). 'Uncommonness' — the purport is: because it would fall under the definition of uncommon [reason], which has the nature of being excluded from the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue). Even where the <s>sādhya</s> is not well-established, the inference is one qualified by the <s>sādhya</s> — with this intent he says 'sādhya' etc. 'Negative pervasion' — the meaning is: having the nature of counter-positive-ness of the absence that pervades the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>. The general difference from what is other than earth is not what is being proved; rather, the aggregate of individual differences from water and the like is being proved. And thus, since there is occasion for the stated defect, he says 'water and the like.' The mutual absences of the thirteen among water and the like — their aggregate is what is proved — this is the meaning. Since it is impossible for the aggregate to be well-established [all at once], he says 'individually.' 'Delimited by thirteen-ness' — since, prior to the inference, there is no well-establishment of a <s>dharmin</s> (property-locus) possessing the property delimited by the delimitor of probandum-hood, the positive concomitance and uncommonness — which depend on the presence or absence of the <s>hetu</s> there — [do not arise]: this is the collective meaning. When individual well-establishment obtains, a cognition of the aggregate, which has as its content the property of being the object of a particular desire-to-know, is possible. And thus, since the ascertainment in the form of the qualifier-mode delimited by the delimitor of the qualifier-relation exists, an inference that apprehends the qualificand-ness qualified by the delimitor of probandum-hood

children.text:
vyatirekavyāptijñānaṃ
ca sambhavatītyāha - pratyekādhikaraṇetyādinā/ yadyapi jalādi
caturdaśānyonyābhāvānāṃ caturdaśasu
children.translated_text: and the knowledge of negative pervasion is possible — he says this with 'individual-locus' and so on. Although among the fourteen [categories] of water and the like, the fourteen mutual absences are individually established in each of the fourteen,

children.text:
pratyeka prasiddhānāmiti
rītyā vaktumucitam, tathāpi arthāpatteḥ
pramāṇāntaratvamaṅgīkurvantaṃ prābhākaramākṣeptuṃ
vyatirekavyāpteranumityaṅgatvasya pradarśanīyatayā
tanmatasādhāraṇyena vyatirekavyāptiṃ pradarśayituṃ
jalāditrayodaśetyādikathanam/ na ca tanmate caturdaśānyonyābhāvaḥ
prasiddhāḥ/ abhāvasyādhikaraṇātmakasya tenāṅgīkārāditi dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: though it would be appropriate to speak in the manner of 'individually established among the fourteen,' nevertheless, in order to challenge the <s>Prābhākara</s> [Mīmāṃsaka] who accepts <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) as a separate means of valid cognition, and since the negative pervasion of <s>kevalavyatirekin</s> inference needs to be demonstrated, to show the negative pervasion in terms common to that school, the expression 'thirteen mutual absences among water and the like' is used. For in that school, fourteen mutual absences are not recognized — since absence is accepted as having the nature of the substratum by them — this should be noted.

children.text:
kecittu - jalamevādiḥ
yeṣāṃ trayodaśānāmiti vigraheṇa jalādipratiyogikānāṃ
caturdaśānāmityarthaḥ/ trayodaśasviti/ jalādītyādiḥ/ uktavigraheṇa
caturdaśasvityarthaḥ/ agre 'pyevaṃ bodhyam ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: Some, however, [explain]: by analyzing the compound as 'those thirteen of which water is the beginning,' i.e., the fourteen that have water and the like as counter-positives — this is the meaning. 'Among the thirteen' means among water and the like. By the stated analysis, the meaning is 'among the fourteen.' The same should be understood further ahead as well — thus they say.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu
vyatirekamātravyāptikaṃ kevalavyatirekītyasya anvayavyāptiśūnyatve
sati vyatirekavyāptimattvaṃ kevalavyatirekiṇo lakṣaṇamityarthaḥ/ tathā
ca 'pṛthivī itarebhyo bhidyate gandhavattvāt' ityatra
kevalavyatirekiṇi vastuto 'nvayavyāpterapi sattvādasambhavaḥ
ityato vyācaṣṭe - niścitavyatireketi/ tathā coktasthale vastutaḥ
anvayavyāpteḥ sattve 'pi sādhyasyāprasiddhyā (ajñānena)
hetuvyāpakasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyarūpānvayavyāptiniścayo nāsti,
vyatirekavyāptiniścayastvastīti niścitavyatirekamātravyāptikatvasya
sattvāt kevalavyatirekitvamupapadyata iti bhāvaḥ/
yatkiñciditarabhedasya prasiddhatvāt prasiddho na veti vikalpasyaiva
nāvasara ityataḥ vyācaṣṭe -
pṛthivītaratvāvacchinnapratiyogitākabheda iti/ pṛthivītareṣāṃ
sarveṣāṃ bheda ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca yadi pṛthivītareṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhedaḥ
kvacit ghaṭādau jñātaḥ tarhi tatra hetusattve
sādhyahetvostatraivānvayasahacāragrahāt
tadgrāhyānvayavyāptimattvamastīti
children.translated_text: Now, the meaning of 'vyatirekamātravyāptikaṃ kevalavyatireki' is: the definition of <s>kevalavyatirekin</s> is possessing negative pervasion alone in the absence of positive pervasion. And thus in the case 'earth is different from the others because of possessing smell,' since positive pervasion also actually obtains in the <s>kevalavyatirekin</s>, there would be an impossibility — therefore he glosses it with 'ascertained negative.' Accordingly, in the stated case, even though positive pervasion actually obtains, due to the non-well-establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> (i.e., through ignorance), there is no ascertainment of positive pervasion in the form of co-location of the <s>sādhya</s> that pervades the <s>hetu</s>; but there is ascertainment of negative pervasion — hence, since there is possession of only ascertained negative pervasion, the status of being <s>kevalavyatirekin</s> is justified — this is the purport. Since any-such-difference-from-others is well-established, there is no occasion for the very dilemma 'well-established or not' — therefore he glosses: 'difference whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by being-other-than-earth.' The meaning is: the difference from all those that are other than earth. And thus, if the difference from all those other than earth is known somewhere, say in a pot, then if the <s>hetu</s> is present there, since positive co-occurrence of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>hetu</s> is grasped right there, there would be

children.text:
anvayavyatirekyanumānameva bhavet na kevalavyatireke/ yadi
tatra heturnāsti tarhi hetorniścitasādhyavadavṛttitvena
sapakṣavyāvṛttatvarūpāsādhāraṇahetvābhāvalakṣaṇākrāntatayā
hetorasādhāraṇatvāpattiḥ/ yadi
pṛthivītaratvāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedarūpaṃ sādhyaṃ na jñātam tarhi
sādhyarūpaviśeṣaṇajñānābhāvāt sādhyaviśiṣṭapakṣajñānarūpā anumitirna
syāt viśiṣṭabuddhau viśeṣaṇajñānasya kāraṇatvāt/ evaṃ
sādhyasyājñātatve sādhyābhāvaghaṭitavyatirekavyāptijñānamapi na syāt/
abhāvabuddhau pratiyogijñānasya kāraṇatvāditi
dīpikāsthaśaṅkāgranthārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: an <s>anvayavyatirekin</s> (positive-and-negative) inference, not a purely negative one. If the <s>hetu</s> is not present there, then the <s>hetu</s>, by virtue of its non-occurrence in a locus where the <s>sādhya</s> is ascertained, would fall under the definition of an <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon) fallacious reason, which is characterized by exclusion from the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue) — hence the defect of uncommonness would arise. If the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of difference whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by being-other-than-earth is not known, then due to the absence of cognition of the qualifier that is the <s>sādhya</s>, there would be no inference in the form of qualified cognition of the <s>pakṣa</s> as possessing the <s>sādhya</s>, since cognition of the qualifier is the cause of qualified cognition. Likewise, if the <s>sādhya</s> is unknown, then knowledge of negative pervasion, which involves the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, would also not arise, since cognition of the counter-positive is the cause of cognition of absence — this is the meaning of the objection passage in the <s>Dīpikā</s>.

children.text:
nanu
aprasiddhasādhyakasthale sādhyaviśeṣaṇikā pakṣaḥ sādhyavānityākārāna
anumitirmā bhūt viśeṣaṇajñānarūpakāraṇavirahāt/
pṛthivyāmitarabhedaḥ ityākārā sādhyaviśeṣyikā anumitiḥ
bhavitumarhatyevetyāśaṅkyāha - aprasiddhasādhyake 'pīti/
sādhyaviśeṣaṇakānumitireveti/ sādhyaviśeṣaṇakānumitireva jāyata
iti pakṣe viśeṣaṇajñānābhāvāt sā prakṛte na sambhavatīti
dūṣaṇam/ sādhyaviśeṣyakānumitirjāyata iti pakṣe
pratiyogijñānābhāvāt vyatirekavyāptijñānarūpakāraṇābhāvāt na sā
sambhabatīti bhāvo varṇanīyaḥ/ jalādibhedakūṭamiti/ jalādīnāṃ
pṛthivyatiriktānāṃ caturdaśānāṃ pratyekaṃ ye caturdaśa bhedāḥ
tatsamūha ityarthaḥ/ jalādīnāṃ ye trayodaśānyonyābhāvā iti/
nanu jalādyaṣṭadravyāṇāṃ guṇādiṣaṭpadārthānāṃ ca bhedaḥ pṛthivyāṃ
sādhanīyaḥ/ tathā ca jalādicaturdaśānyonyābhāveti vaktavye
trayodaśetyabhidhānamanucitamiti cet-atra
kecit-mīmāṃsakairabhāvasyādhikaraṇātmakatvasvīkāreṇa
atiriktapadārthatvānaṅgīkārāt trayodaśānyonyābhāva iti
tanmatānusāreṇa kathitam/
arthāpatteratiriktapramāṇatvamaṅgīkurvatastān pratyeva
kevalavyatirekyanumānasya pradarśanīyatvāt ityāhuḥ - tanna/
tādṛśatrayodaśānyonyābhāvānāṃ jalādiṣu pratyekaṃ prasiddhānāṃ
tanmate jalādirūpatayā jalādirūpatrayodaśabhedasya pṛthivyāmasattvena
gandhavattvaliṅgena tatsādhanāsambhavāt/ pṛthivīniṣṭhasya
tādṛśatrayodaśabhedasya pṛthivīrūpatayā jalādiṣu pratyekaṃ
prasiddhyabhāvenāprasiddhyā uktarītyā vyatirekavyāptijñānāsambhavena
tatsādhanāsambhavāt/ ataḥ jalāditrayodaśānyonyābhāvānāmityasya
jalamādiryeṣāṃ tu jalādayaḥ, jalādayastrayodaśa jalāditrayodaśa
teṣāmanyonyābhāvā iti vigrahaḥ/ jalāditayatra
atadguṇasaṃvijñāno
children.translated_text: Now, in cases where the <s>sādhya</s> is not well-established, let there not be an inference of the form 'the <s>pakṣa</s> possesses the <s>sādhya</s>' — which is qualified by the <s>sādhya</s> as qualifier — due to the absence of the causal condition of qualifier-cognition. But an inference of the form 'in earth there is difference from the others' — which has the <s>sādhya</s> as qualificand — should certainly be possible — anticipating this, he says 'even where the <s>sādhya</s> is not established.' 'The inference is one qualified by the <s>sādhya</s> only' — the refutation is: if one holds that only an inference with the <s>sādhya</s> as qualifier arises, then in the present case it is not possible due to the absence of qualifier-cognition. If one holds that an inference with the <s>sādhya</s> as qualificand arises, then the purport to be elucidated is: it too is not possible, due to the absence of counter-positive cognition, which means the absence of the causal condition of knowledge of negative pervasion. 'The aggregate of differences from water and the like' — the meaning is: the collection of the fourteen individual differences of each of the fourteen [categories] other than earth, namely water and the like. 'The thirteen mutual absences of water and the like' — now, the differences of the eight substances such as water and the six categories such as quality should be proved in earth. And thus, where one should say 'fourteen mutual absences of water and the like,' the expression 'thirteen' is inappropriate — if thus objected: here some [say] — since the Mīmāṃsakas accept absence as having the nature of the substratum and do not acknowledge it as a separate category, 'thirteen mutual absences' is stated in accordance with their view, because <s>kevalavyatirekin</s> inference is to be demonstrated precisely against those who accept <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) as a separate means of valid cognition — thus they say. That is not correct. Because those thirteen mutual absences of that kind, which are individually well-established in each of the water-group, in that school have the nature of water etc. [i.e., of the substrata], and hence the thirteen-fold difference having the nature of water etc. does not exist in earth, so it cannot be proved through the mark of possessing smell. And because the thirteen-fold difference of that kind residing in earth, having the nature of earth, is not individually well-established in each of the water-group — and due to this non-well-establishment, the knowledge of negative pervasion is impossible in the stated manner, making proof impossible. Therefore, the analysis of 'thirteen mutual absences of water and the like' is: water is the beginning of which — those are the water-group; thirteen of the water-group — those are the thirteen-of-the-water-group; the mutual absences of those. In 'water-group' here,

children.text:
bahuvrīhiḥ/ ato
jalādīnāṃ caturdaśānāṃ ye caturdaśa anyonyābhāvāḥ teṣāṃ lābha
iti vyākhyātavyam/ upari prakāśikāyāṃ sarvamidaṃ spaṣṭībhaviṣyati/
children.translated_text: it is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound with the sense of 'not having that as a quality.' Therefore, one should explain it as: the obtaining of the fourteen mutual absences of the fourteen [categories] of the water-group. All this will become clear above in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text:
vastutastu jalādīnāṃ
caturdaśānāṃ ye bhedāḥ caturdaśa te sarveṃ jalādiṣu na prasiddhāḥ/ tathā
hi - jalabhedaḥ
children.translated_text: In reality, however, not all fourteen differences of the fourteen [categories] of the water-group are well-established in the water-group. For instance, the difference from water

children.text:
tejaḥprabhṛtiṣu
trayodaśasu prasiddhaḥ, na tejasi/ evaṃrītyā trayodaśasu prasiddhaḥ yaḥ
ekaikabhedaḥ teṣāṃ melanaṃ pṛthivyāṃ sādhyate/ arthāt
caturdaṃśabhedasamudāyaḥ pṛthivyāṃ sādhyate/ trayodaśatvāvacchedena
prasiddho yaḥ ekaikabhedaḥ tadghaṭitacaturdaśātmakasamudāyaḥ pṛthivyāṃ
sādhyata iti yāvat/ evaṃ ca caturdaśatvaviśiṣṭabhedasya
kutrāpyaprasiddhatvāt nānvayitvaṃ na vā asādhāraṇyam/
sādhyaghaṭakaikābhāvasya trayodaśatvāvacchedena prasiddhatayā
sādhyarūpaviśeṣaṇajñānasattvena sādhyaviśiṣṭānumitirupapadyate/ evaṃ
sādhyātmakapratiyogijñānasattve sādhyābhāvajñānasambhavāt
vyatirekavyāptijñānamapi sulabhamiti nṛsiṃhaśāstriṇaḥ prāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: is well-established in fire and the remaining thirteen, but not in fire [alone, i.e., not in water itself]. In this manner, each individual difference that is well-established in thirteen [loci] — their combination is what is proved in earth. That is, the aggregate of fourteen differences is proved in earth. Each individual difference that is well-established with the delimitor of thirteen-ness — the aggregate of fourteen constituted by those is proved in earth — this is the import. And thus, since the difference qualified by fourteen-ness is not well-established anywhere, there is neither positive concomitance nor uncommonness. Since each individual absence that constitutes the <s>sādhya</s> is well-established with the delimitor of thirteen-ness, the cognition of the qualifier that is the <s>sādhya</s>-form exists, and hence the inference qualified by the <s>sādhya</s> is justified. Likewise, since the cognition of the counter-positive that is of the nature of the <s>sādhya</s> exists, the cognition of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is possible, and therefore the knowledge of negative pervasion too is easily obtained — thus say the followers of <s>Nṛsiṃhaśāstrin</s>.

children.text:
niścitasādhyatāvacchedaketi/ sādhyatāvacchedakaṃ trayodaśatvaṃ
caturdaśatvaṃ vā tadavacchinnāḥ bhedāḥ tadvata ityarthaḥ/ pratyekaṃ
prasiddhāviti/ jalabhedādīnāṃ prasiddhatvāt tatra
apekṣābuddhiviśeṣaviṣayatvātmakaṃ yat caturdaśatvaṃ tajjñānaṃ bhavati/
tena caturdaśatvātmakaṃ yat viśeṣaṇatāvacchedakaṃ tatprakārakaḥ
nirṇayaḥ hame bhedāḥ caturdaśa ityākārakaḥ utpadyate/ tataḥ
caturdaśatvaviśiṣṭabhedavatī pṛthivī ityākārikā
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhinī anumitiḥ sulabhā/
caturdaśatvaviśiṣṭabhedābhāvavyāpakībhūtābhāvapratiyogi
gandhavattvamiti vyatirekavyāptijñānaṃ ca sulabhamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'With the determined delimitor of probandum-hood' — the delimitor of probandum-hood is thirteen-ness or fourteen-ness; 'possessing differences delimited by that' is the meaning. 'When each is individually well-known' — since the differences such as the difference from water are well-known, the cognition of fourteen-ness, which consists in being the object of a particular comparative cognition, arises there. From that, a determination having as its qualifier-mode fourteen-ness, which is the delimitor of qualifier-hood, arises in the form 'these differences are fourteen.' From that, the inference of the form 'earth possesses differences qualified by fourteen-ness,' apprehending the qualification of the qualified, is easily obtainable. And the cognition of negative concomitance (<s>vyatirekavyāpti</s>) — that smell-possession is the counter-positive of an absence that is a pervader of the absence of differences qualified by fourteen-ness — is also easily obtainable. This is the purport.

children.text:
vastutastu
kevalavyatirekyanumānasthale sādhyaviśeṣyikaivānumitiḥ/ ataḥ pūrvaṃ
sādhyasyāprasiddhāvapi na kṣatiḥ/ evaṃ pṛthivītarabhedābhāvatvena rūpeṇa
sādhyābhāvasya vyatirekavyāptighaṭakatayā na praveśaḥ, yena
pratiyogyapratisaddhyā abhāvāprasiddheḥ vyatirekavyāptijñānasya
daurlabhyaṃ bhavet/ api tu pṛthivītaratvavyāpakībhūtābhāvapratiyogi
gandhavatī pṛthivī ityeva parāmarśaḥ/ ataḥ dīpikāyāmāśritaḥ
prayāso viphala iti prāhuḥ/ 1pakṣatādīdhityādau spaṣṭametat/
children.translated_text: In reality, in the case of a purely negative inference (<s>kevalavyatirekin</s>), the inference has the probandum as qualificand only. Hence, even if the probandum is not previously well-known, there is no harm. Similarly, the absence of the probandum, in the form of absence of difference from what is other than earth, does not enter as a component of the negative concomitance — whereby, due to the non-establishment of the counter-positive, the non-establishment of the absence would make the cognition of negative concomitance difficult to obtain. Rather, the inferential cognition (<s>parāmarśa</s>) is precisely of the form 'Earth, which possesses smell, is the counter-positive of an absence that is a pervader of being-other-than-earth.' Hence, the effort undertaken in the <s>Dīpikā</s> is futile — they say. This is clearly [stated] in the <s>Pakṣatādīdhiti</s> and other texts.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: pakṣalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Pakṣa</s> (Subject of Inference)

children.text: AnTs_49 saṃdigdhasādhyavān pakṣaḥ / yathā dhūmavattve hetau parvataḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 49:] That which possesses a doubtful probandum is the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject). For example, when smoke-possession is the reason, the mountain [is the subject].

children.text: sandigdhasādhyavān pakṣaḥ/ yathā dhūmavattve hetau parvataḥ/
children.translated_text: That which possesses a doubtful probandum is the <s>pakṣa</s>. For example, when smoke-possession is the reason, the mountain [is the <s>pakṣa</s>].

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
pakṣalakṣaṇamāha -
sandigdheti/ nanu śravaṇānantarabhāvimananasthale avyāptiḥ/ tatra
vedavākyairātmano niścitatvena sandehābhāvāt/ kiṃ ca pratyakṣe 'pi
vahnau yatra icchayā anumitiḥ tatra avyāptiriti cet-na/
uktapakṣatāśrayatvasya pakṣalakṣaṇatvāt/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>pakṣa</s> — with 'doubtful.' Now, there is under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) in the case where reflection (<s>manana</s>) follows hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>). For there, since the self has been ascertained by Vedic sentences, doubt is absent. Moreover, even when fire is perceptible, wherever inference occurs by desire, there too there is under-extension — if thus objected: no, because being the locus of the stated <s>pakṣatā</s> (subject-hood) is the definition of <s>pakṣa</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mūle
sandigdhasādhyavāniti/ viśeṣyatāsambandhena
sādhyaprakārakasaṃśayaviśiṣṭa ityarthaḥ/ sapakṣalakṣaṇādikamapyevaṃ
pariṣkartavyam/ pakṣalakṣaṇasyāvyāptimāśaṅkte - dīpikāyāṃ nanviti/
saṃśayavighaṭakaśābdabuddhisthale 'vyāptimuktvā pratyakṣasthale 'pi tāmāha -
kiñcati/ ukteti/
siṣādhayiṣāvirahaviśiṣṭasiddhyabhāvarūpapakṣatāśrayatvasya
pakṣalakṣaṇatvādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the root text, 'possessing a doubtful probandum' — the meaning is: qualified by a doubt having the probandum as qualifier-mode, through the relation of qualificand-hood. The definitions of <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue) and the like should also be refined in this way. He raises the doubt of under-extension in the definition of <s>pakṣa</s> — in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, with 'now.' Having mentioned the under-extension in the case where verbal cognition (<s>śābdabuddhi</s>) dispels the doubt, he also mentions it in the case of perception — with 'moreover.' 'Stated' — the meaning is: being the locus of the <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of the absence of establishment qualified by the absence of the desire to establish is the definition of <s>pakṣa</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
viśeṣyatāsambandheneti/ 'parvato vahnimān na vā'
ityākārake saṃśaye vahniḥ prakāraḥ parvato viśeṣya iti
children.translated_text: 'Through the relation of qualificand-hood' — in the doubt of the form 'Does the mountain have fire or not?' fire is the qualifier-mode and the mountain is the qualificand —

children.text:
1. ata eva
prasiddhasādhyakasthale pakṣaviśeṣyikaivānumitiranubhūyate' iti
pakṣatāyāṃ dīdhitigranthaḥ/ atra prasiddhasādhyakasthale
pakṣaviśeṣyakānumitiriti kathanāt aprasiddhasādhyakasthale
sādhyaviśeṣyakānumitiriti sūcyate/ tatra gadādharīyavyākhyānaṃ 'kiṃ
tu aprasiddhasādhyakasthale viśeṣaṇajñānādiviraheṇa
sādhyaviśeṣaṇakānumiteranupapattyā sādhyaviśeṣyakānumitirūpeyate'
ityādyuktaṃ draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] For this very reason, the <s>Dīdhiti</s> text on <s>pakṣatā</s> states: 'In the case of a well-known probandum, the inference has the <s>pakṣa</s> as qualificand.' By stating that in the case of a well-known probandum the inference has the <s>pakṣa</s> as qualificand, it is indicated that in the case of an unfamiliar probandum the inference has the probandum as qualificand. For the <s>Gadādharī</s> commentary on that, see: 'Rather, in the case of an unfamiliar probandum, since the inference having the probandum as qualifier cannot arise due to the absence of cognition of the qualifier and the like, the inference takes the form of having the probandum as qualificand' — and so forth.

children.text:
sādhyaprakārakatādṛśasaṃśayasya viśeṣyatāsambandhena parvate
sattvāt parvatasya pakṣatā/ prakāratāsambandhena tādṛśasaṃśayasya vahnau
sattvāt vahneḥ pakṣatvavāraṇāya viśeṣyatāsambandhenetyuktam/
sapakṣalakṣaṇādikamapyevaṃ pariṣkartavyamiti/ viśeṣyatāsambandhena
sādhyaprakārakanirṇayaviśiṣṭaḥ sapakṣaḥ, viśeṣyatāsambandhena
sādhyābhāvaprakārakanirṇayaviśiṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Since the doubt having the probandum as qualifier-mode exists in the mountain through the relation of qualificand-hood, the mountain has <s>pakṣatā</s> (subject-hood). To prevent fire from being a <s>pakṣa</s>, since such a doubt exists in fire through the relation of qualifier-mode-hood, 'through the relation of qualificand-hood' was stated. 'The definitions of <s>sapakṣa</s> and the like should also be refined in this way' — the meaning is: the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue) is that which is qualified, through the relation of qualificand-hood, by the determination having the probandum as qualifier-mode; and the

children.text:
vipakṣaḥ iti rītyā
pariṣkartavyamityarthaḥ/ saṃśayavighaṭaketi/ ātmā
dehendriyādivilakṣaṇo na veti sandehasya pratibandhakaḥ yaḥ
vedavākyajanyaḥ śābdabodhaḥ ātmā dehendriyādivilakṣaṇaḥ
ityākārakaḥ tatra tādṛśaśābdabodhātmakaśravaṇānantaraṃ ātmā
dehendriyādivilakṣaṇa ityākārakānumitirūpaṃ mananaṃ na syāt/
ātmanaḥ viśeṣyatāsambandhena
sādadhyaprakārakasandehavattvarūpapakṣatvābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>vipakṣa</s> (counter-example) is that which is qualified, through the relation of qualificand-hood, by the determination having the absence of the probandum as qualifier-mode — it should be refined in this manner. 'Dispelling the doubt' — the verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>) generated by Vedic sentences, which takes the form 'The self is distinct from the body, sense-organs, and the like,' obstructs the doubt 'Is the self distinct from the body, sense-organs, and the like or not?' After the hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) consisting of such verbal cognition, the reflection (<s>manana</s>) in the form of the inference 'The self is distinct from the body, sense-organs, and the like' would not occur — because the <s>pakṣatva</s> (subject-hood) of the self in the form of possessing doubt having the probandum as qualifier-mode through the relation of qualificand-hood is absent. This is the purport.
