children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: sapakṣalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Sapakṣa</s> (Homologue)

children.text: AnTs_50 niścitasādhyavān sapakṣaḥ / yathā tatraiva mahānasaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 50:] That which possesses an ascertained probandum is the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue). For example, in the same [inference], the kitchen.

children.text:
niścitasādhyavān
sapakṣaḥ/ yathā tatraiva mahānasaḥ/
children.translated_text: That which possesses an ascertained probandum is the <s>sapakṣa</s>. For example, in the same [inference], the kitchen.

children.text: vipakṣalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Vipakṣa</s> (Counter-example)

children.text: AnTs_51 niścitasādhyābhāvavān vipakṣaḥ / yathā tatraiva mahāhradaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 51:] That which possesses the ascertained absence of the probandum is the <s>vipakṣa</s>. For example, in the same [inference], a large lake.

children.text: niścitasādhyābhāvavāna vipakṣaḥ/ yathā tatraiva mahāhradaḥ/
children.translated_text: That which possesses the ascertained absence of the probandum is the <s>vipakṣa</s>. For example, in the same [inference], a large lake.

children.text: hetvābhāsanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Pseudo-reasons (<s>Hetvābhāsa</s>)

children.text: AnTs_52 savyabhicāraviruddhasatpakṣāsiddhabādhitāḥ pañca hetvābhāsāḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> 52:] The five pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) are: the deviating (<s>savyabhicāra</s>), the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), the counter-balanced (<s>satpratipakṣa</s>), the unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), and the sublated (<s>bādhita</s>).

children.text:
savyabhicāra-viruddha-satpratipakṣa-asiddha-bādhitāḥ pañca
hetvābhāsāḥ/
children.translated_text: The five pseudo-reasons are: the deviating, the contradictory, the counter-balanced, the unestablished, and the sublated.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
sapakṣalakṣaṇamāha -
niściteti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>sapakṣa</s> — with 'ascertained.'

children.text:
vipakṣalakṣaṇamāha -
niściteti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>vipakṣa</s> — with 'ascertained.'

children.text:
evaṃ saddhetūnnirūpya
asaddhetūnnirūpayituṃ vibhajate - savyabhicāreti/
anumitipratibandhakayathārthajñānaviṣayatvaṃ hetvābhāsatvam/
children.translated_text: Having examined the valid reasons, he divides [the topic] in order to examine the invalid reasons — with '<s>savyabhicāra</s>' (deviating). The property of being the object of a veridical cognition that obstructs inference is pseudo-reason-hood (<s>hetvābhāsatva</s>).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
saddhetūnnirūpya -
vyāptyādiviśiṣṭahetūnnirūpyetyarthaḥ/ saddhetunirūpaṇe
asaddhetusmaraṇāta prasaṅgasaṅgatyā tannirūpaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/ mūle
hetvābhāsā iti/ hetuvadābhāsanta iti hetvābhāsāḥ/
duṣṭahetavo nirūpyanta ityarthaḥ/ nanu
children.translated_text: 'Having examined valid reasons' — the meaning is: having examined reasons qualified by pervasion and the like. 'Through the contextual connection arising from the recollection of invalid reasons upon the examination of valid reasons, the examination of those [invalid reasons follows]' — this is the purport. In the root text, '<s>hetvābhāsāḥ</s>' — [the term means:] they appear like reasons (<s>hetuvadābhāsante</s>) — hence they are pseudo-reasons. The meaning is: faulty reasons are being examined. Now,

children.text:
sāmānyadharmaprakārakajñānamantarā viśeṣajijñāsānudayena
savyabhicāretyādinā vibhāgo 'nucita ityāśaṅkāṃ parijihīrṣuḥ
doṣalakṣaṇe 'bhihite doṣavattvarūpaduṣṭalakṣaṇasyātisphaṭatvāt lābho
bhavatītyāśayena doṣasāmānyalakṣaṇamāha - anumitīti/
hetvābhāsatvamiti/ hetorābhāsāḥ hetvābhāsāḥ hetuniṣṭhāḥ doṣāḥ,
teṣāṃ bhāvaḥ tattvamityarthaḥ/ 'hrado vahnimān' ityādyanumitiṃ prati
'vahnyabhāvavān hrada' ityādibādhaniścayaḥ pratibandhakaḥ/
pramātmakatādṛśaniścayaviṣayatvaṃ vahnyabhāvavaddhradādau akṣatamiti
lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ atrānumitipadaṃ ajahallakṣaṇayā
anumititatkaraṇānyataraparam/ tena vyabhicārādijñānasya
parāmarśapratibandhakatayaiva nirvāhāt anumityapratibandhakatve 'pi
vyabhicārādiṣu nāvyāptiḥ/ 'parvato nirvahniḥ' iti bādhabhramasya
'parvato vahnimān' ityanumitipratibandhakatvāt
tadviṣayavahnyabhāvādau ativyāptiḥ ataḥ yathārtheti/ bhramābhinnetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: since without the cognition of a general property, the desire to know specifics does not arise, and hence the division by '<s>savyabhicāra</s>' and the like is inappropriate — wishing to resolve this doubt, with the understanding that since the general definition of defect (<s>doṣa</s>) has been stated, the definition of what-is-defective in the form of possessing-a-defect is extremely obvious and hence is obtained, he states the general definition of defect with: 'inference' etc. '<s>hetvābhāsatva</s>' — the faults (<s>ābhāsa</s>) of a reason are pseudo-reason [faults]; they reside in the reason; their being (<s>bhāva</s>) is their nature (<s>tattva</s>) — this is the meaning. The determination 'the lake possesses the absence of fire' and the like, being a sublating cognition, is an obstructor of the inference 'the lake has fire' and the like. The property of being the object of such a determination that is veridical — this remains unimpaired in the lake possessing the absence of fire and the like — this is the application of the definition. Here, the word 'inference' (<s>anumiti</s>), through non-exclusive secondary signification (<s>ajahallakṣaṇā</s>), refers to either inference or its instrument. Thereby, since the cognition of deviation and the like functions as an obstructor of the inferential cognition (<s>parāmarśa</s>) [rather than of the inference itself], even though it does not obstruct the inference [directly], there is no under-extension in deviation and the like. Since the sublating error 'the mountain lacks fire' obstructs the inference 'the mountain has fire,' there would be over-extension to the absence of fire and the like that is the object of that [erroneous sublation] — hence 'veridical' [is added]. The meaning is: different from error.

children.text:
athaivamapi
vahnyabhāvavaddhradātmakabādhaikadeśe vahnyabhāvādau ativyāptiḥ/
'vahnyabhāvavān hradaḥ' ityākārakayarthārthajñānaviṣayatvasya tatra
sattvāditi cet-na/ yadrūpāvacchinnaviṣayakajñānasāmānyaṃ
anumitipratibandhakaṃ tadrūpāvacchinnatvaṃ
doṣatvamityarthaparyavasānenādoṣāt/
vahnyabhāvatvāvacchinnaviṣayakasya 'vahnyabhāvavān hradaḥ' iti
jñānasyānumitipratibandhakatve 'pi tādṛśajñānasāmānyāntargatasya
'vahnyabhāva' ityākārakajñānasya apratibandhakatvena vahnyabhāvatvādeḥ
yadrūpapadenopādānāsambhavāt/ na ca tarhi yathārthapadaṃ vyartham/
'parvato nirvahniḥ' iti bhramaviṣaye 'pi vahnyabhāvādāvativyāpteḥ
uktarītyaiva vāraṇāditi vācyam/ jñānapadasya
jñānaviśeṣatātparyagrāhakatayā yathārthapadasārthakyāt/ evaṃ ca
yadrūpāvacchinnaviṣayakānāhāryāprāmāṇyajñānānāskanditaniścayasāmānyaṃ
prakṛtānumitipratibandhakaṃ tadrūpāvacchinnatvaṃ doṣatvamityarthaḥ
paryavasitaḥ/ tena vahnyabhāvavaddhradaviṣayakasya āhāryasya
aprāmāṇyajñānaviśiṣṭasya saṃśayasya ca anumityapratibandhakatve 'pi
nāsambhava ityalaṃ pallavitena/
children.translated_text: But even so, there would be over-extension to the absence of fire and the like, which is a part of the sublation consisting of the lake possessing the absence of fire — because the property of being the object of the veridical cognition of the form 'the lake possesses the absence of fire' exists there — if thus objected: no defect, because the purport amounts to: that property-delimitation, such that the generality of cognitions having objects delimited by that property obstructs the inference, is defect-hood. Even though the cognition 'the lake possesses the absence of fire,' which has an object delimited by the-absence-of-fire-hood, is an obstructor of inference, since the cognition of the form 'the absence of fire,' which is included in the generality of such cognitions, is not an obstructor, the-absence-of-fire-hood cannot be grasped by the expression 'that property.' Nor should it be said that the word 'veridical' is then purposeless — since even in the object of the error 'the mountain lacks fire,' namely the absence of fire and the like, the over-extension is prevented by the very same method. [The reply:] Because the word 'knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>) has the purpose of conveying that [a specific type of] knowledge is intended, the word 'veridical' is meaningful. And accordingly, the purport amounts to: that property-delimitation, such that the generality of veridical, non-feigned, non-impugned determinations having objects delimited by that property obstructs the inference in question, is defect-hood. Hence, even though the feigned [cognition], the cognition impugned by invalidity-cognition, and the doubt about the lake possessing the absence of fire do not obstruct inference, there is no [defect of] impossibility. Enough with elaboration.

children.text:
pare tu - idaṃ
duṣṭānāmeva lakṣaṇam/ parantu jñāyamānavyabhicārādeḥ
pratibandhakatvamabhyupetya/ tadarthastu anumitipratibandhakā ye
vyabhicārādayaḥ ekajñānaviṣayaprakṛtahetutāvacchedakavattvasambandhena
tatprakārakayathārthajñānaviśeṣyatvam/ 'dhūmavān vahneḥ' ityādau
dhūmābhāvavadvṛttitvaviśiṣṭavahniḥ vyabhicāraḥ,
children.translated_text: Others, however, [say]: this is the definition only of the defective [reasons]. But it presupposes that known deviation and the like have the capacity to obstruct. The meaning of that [definition] is: deviation and the like, which obstruct inference — the property of being a qualificand, through the relation of possessing the delimitor of the reason-hood of the reason in question as the content of a single cognition, of a veridical cognition having that as qualifier-mode. In [the inference] 'fire is smoky' and the like, fire qualified by the property of existing in what lacks smoke is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>);

children.text:
uktasambandhena 'tadvān
vahniḥ' ityākārakayathārthañjñānaviśeṣyatvamastīti lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/
anumitipadasya prakṛtānumitiparatayā saddhetau
anumitipratibandhakībhūtavyabhicārādīnāmaprasiddhatvāt nātivyāptiḥ/
yathārthapadānupādāne darśitasambandhena
vyabhicāraprakārakabhramaviśeṣyatvasya saddhetāvapi sattvenātivyāptiḥ
syāditi tanniveśa ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: since the property of being a qualificand of the veridical cognition of the form 'fire possesses that' through the stated relation exists there — this is the application of the definition. Since the word 'inference' refers to the inference in question, and since deviation and the like that obstruct a valid reason are not well-known in a valid reason, there is no over-extension. Without the inclusion of the word 'veridical,' since the property of being the qualificand of an error having deviation as qualifier-mode through the demonstrated relation exists even in a valid reason, there would be over-extension — hence that inclusion, they say.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
vyāptyādiviśiṣṭahetūniti/ ādipadena pakṣadharmatā gṛhyate/
tathā ca vyāpti-pakṣadharmatāviśiṣṭahetutvaṃ saddhetorlakṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/
hetuvadābhāsanta iti/ hetutvaprakārakabhramaviṣayāḥ ityarthaḥ/
hetutvaṃ ca vyāptipakṣadharmatāviśiṣṭatvam/ tathā ca
vyāptipakṣadharmatāviśiṣṭatvaprakārakabhramaviṣayatvaṃ hetvābhāsatvam/
tattu duṣṭahetūnāmeva bhavati, saddhetūnāṃ tatpramāviṣayatvāditi
hetvābhāsaśabdaḥ duṣṭahetupara iti bhāvaḥ/ lakṣaṇasamanvaya iti/
tathā ca 'hrado vahnimān dhūmāt' ityatra vahnyabhāvavaddhradātmakaḥ
bādhaḥ doṣaḥ/ tādṛśadoṣavattvaṃ ca hetoḥ dhūmasya
ekajñānaviṣayaprakṛtahetutāvacchedakavattvasambandhenāstīti duṣṭatvam/
'vahnyabhāvavaddhradaḥ dhūmatvaṃ ca' ityekajñāne bādhasya dhūmatvasya ca
viṣayatvādityādikamūhanīyam/
children.translated_text: 'Reasons qualified by pervasion and the like' — the word 'and the like' includes the property of being present in the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>). And accordingly, the definition of a valid reason is: reason-hood qualified by pervasion and <s>pakṣadharmatā</s>. This is the purport. 'They appear like reasons' — the meaning is: they are the objects of an error having reason-hood as qualifier-mode. Reason-hood is being qualified by pervasion and <s>pakṣadharmatā</s>. And accordingly, pseudo-reason-hood is: being the object of an error having the qualifier-mode of being qualified by pervasion and <s>pakṣadharmatā</s>. That belongs only to faulty reasons; valid reasons are the objects of valid cognition of that [reason-hood] — hence the word <s>hetvābhāsa</s> refers to faulty reasons. This is the purport. 'Application of the definition' — and accordingly, in 'the lake has fire because of smoke,' the sublation consisting of the lake possessing the absence of fire is a defect. And the smoke, which is the reason, has defective-ness through the relation of possessing the delimitor of the reason-hood of the reason in question as content of a single cognition — hence it is defective. Since the sublation and smoke-hood are contents of the single cognition 'the lake possesses the absence of fire and smoke-hood' — and so forth should be reflected upon.

children.text:
nanvanumitipratibandhakayathārthajñānaviṣayatvaṃ yadi doṣalakṣaṇaṃ
tadā bādhasatpratipakṣayorevedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ samanviyāt/ bādhaniścayasya
satpratipakṣaniścayasya ca 'hrado vahnyabhāvavān' ityākārakasya 'hrado
vahnyabhāvavyāpyaśaivālavān' ityākārakasya ca tadvattābuddhiṃ prati
tadabhāvavattāniścayavidhayā tadabhāvavyāpyavattāniścayavidhayā ca
pratibandhakatvāt, tadviṣayatvarūpalakṣaṇasattvāt/
vyabhicāravirodhasvarūpāsiddhiprabhṛtiṣu lakṣaṇamidaṃ na samanveti/
tajjñānānāmanumitipratibandhakatvābhāvāt,
anumitikaraṇaparāmarśapratibandhakatvasyaiva vyabhicārādijñāneṣu
sattvādityata āha - atrānumitipadamiti/ tathā ca
anumititatkaraṇānyatarapratibandhakayathārthajñānaviṣayatvaṃ
hetvābhāsalakṣaṇam/ parāmarśapratibandhakatayaiveti/ vyabhicārajñānaṃ
parāmarśe vyāptibhānāṃśe pratibandhakam/ virodhajñānaṃ
sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyāṃśabhāne pratibandhakam/ svarūpāsiddhijñānaṃ
pakṣadharmatvabhāne pratibandhakamiti sarveṣāṃ
anumitikaraṇaparāmarśapratibandhakasattvāt nāvyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
nirvāhāditi/ lakṣaṇopapatterityarthaḥ/ yathārthapadaprayojanamāha -
parvato nirvahniriti/ tathā ca yathārthapadānupādāne parvate
vahnyabhāvavānityākārakabhramasya 'parvato vahnimān'
ityanumitipratibandhakatvāt tādṛśabhramaviṣayasya vahnyabhāvasya
doṣatvaṃ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya yathārthapadam/ uktabhramasya
yathārthatvābhāvāt nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ nanu
children.translated_text: Objection: if being the object of a veridical cognition that obstructs inference is the definition of a defect (<s>doṣa</s>), then this definition would apply only to <s>bādha</s> (sublation) and <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (counter-balanced reason). For the ascertainment of sublation and the ascertainment of a counter-balanced reason — having the form 'the lake possesses the absence of fire' and 'the lake possesses <s>śaivāla</s> (algae) pervaded by the absence of fire' — obstruct the cognition of the subject's possessing the property, by way of the ascertainment that it possesses the absence of that, and by way of the ascertainment that it possesses what is pervaded by the absence of that, respectively; hence the defining characteristic of being the object of such [cognition] is present. This definition does not apply to <s>vyabhicāra</s> (deviation), <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), <s>svarūpāsiddhi</s> (essential unestablishedness) and the rest, because their cognitions do not obstruct inference itself, but only obstruct the <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective consideration) that is the instrument of inference. Therefore he says 'here the word <s>anumiti</s> (inference).' Accordingly, being the object of a veridical cognition that obstructs either inference or its instrument — this is the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reason). 'By way of obstructing the reflective consideration alone': the cognition of <s>vyabhicāra</s> obstructs the aspect of the appearance of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) in the <s>parāmarśa</s>; the cognition of <s>virodha</s> obstructs the aspect of the appearance of co-location with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum); the cognition of <s>svarūpāsiddhi</s> obstructs the aspect of the appearance of being a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject). Since all of them possess the character of obstructing <s>parāmarśa</s>, the instrument of inference, there is no under-extension. The purport is thus. 'By the feasibility' means: by the tenability of the definition. He states the purpose of the word 'veridical' — 'the mountain lacks fire.' Thus, without including the word 'veridical,' since the erroneous cognition of the form 'the mountain possesses the absence of fire' would obstruct the inference 'the mountain possesses fire,' the absence of fire, which is the object of such an error, would become a defect. To prevent that, the word 'veridical' is used. Since the said error lacks veridicality, there is no over-extension. The purport is thus. Objection:

children.text:
yathārthapadopādāne 'pi 'parvato vahnyabhāvavān' iti
bhramavāraṇamaśakyam/ tasyāpi parvatatvavati parvatatvaprakārakatvena
vahnyabhāvatvavati vahnabhāvatvaprakārakatvena ca tadvati
tatprakārakatvarūpayathārthalakṣaṇākrāntatvena yathārthatvādityata āha -
bhramabhinnetyartha iti/ tathā caprakṛtalakṣaṇaghaṭakaṃ yathārthapadaṃ
tadabhāvavati tatprakārakabhinnārthakam/ 'parvato vahnyabhāvavān' iti
jñānaṃ tu vahnyabhāvābhāvavati vahnyabhāvaprakārakatayā bhramātmakam,
tadbhinnaṃ na bhavatīti na doṣa iti bhāvaḥ/ bhramabhinnatvameva sarvāṃśe
pramātvamityucyate/ tacca 1svavyadhikaraṇaprakārāvacchinna yā yā
viśeṣyatā tattadanirūpakatvam/
children.translated_text: Even with the inclusion of the word 'veridical,' preventing the error 'the mountain possesses the absence of fire' is impossible. For that [cognition] too, by being a qualifier-mode cognition of mountain-hood in what possesses mountain-hood, and of fire-absence-hood in what possesses fire-absence-hood, falls under the definition of veridicality as having a qualifier-mode in what possesses that; hence it is veridical. To this he replies — 'the meaning is: different from error.' And thus the word 'veridical' that is a component of the present definition means 'different from an erroneous cognition of the absence of that in what possesses that absence.' The cognition 'the mountain possesses the absence of fire,' however, being erroneous in nature by having fire-absence as a qualifier-mode in what possesses the absence of fire-absence, is not different from error — hence there is no defect. The purport is thus. Being different from error is stated to be veridicality in all respects. And that is: non-being-delimited-by-a-qualifier-that-does-not-reside-in-its-own-locus — that is, not being the determinant of any <s>viśeṣyatā</s> (qualificand-ness) delimited by a qualifier not present in its own substrate.

children.text:
1. svavyadhikaraṇeti/
svavyadhikaraṇetyasya svādhikaraṇāvṛttītyarthaḥ/ śuktau idaṃ rajatamiti
bhramīyaśuktiniṣṭhaviśaṣyatāyā svapadena upādāne svādhikaraṇaṃ śuktiḥ
tadavṛttiḥ yaḥ prakāraḥ rajatatvaṃ tadavacchinnā yā viśeṣyatā
śuktiniṣṭhaviśeṣyatā tannirūpakatvam idaṃ rajatamiti bhrame
tadanirūpakatvaṃ idaṃ rajatamiti pramāyāmiti lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Residing in other than its own substrate': the meaning of 'residing in other than its own substrate' is 'not occurring in its own locus.' In the error 'this is silver' regarding a shell, if one takes the <s>viśeṣyatā</s> (qualificand-ness) residing in the shell by the word 'own,' then the shell is its own substrate; the qualifier that does not occur there is silver-hood; the <s>viśeṣyatā</s> delimited by that — namely the qualificand-ness residing in the shell — being a determinant of that is present in the error 'this is silver,' while not being its determinant is present in the valid cognition 'this is silver.' Thus the definition is shown to apply.

children.text:
1svānirūpitatvasvāśrayābhāvavadvṛttitvobhayasambandhena
prakāratāviśiṣṭā yā viśeṣyatā tadanirūpakatvamiti yāvat/
adhikamudgrantheṣu/
children.translated_text: That is to say: non-being-the-determinant of the <s>viśeṣyatā</s> qualified by a <s>prakāratā</s> (qualifier-mode) connected by the twofold relation of not-being-delimited-by-its-own and occurring-in-what-possesses-the-absence-of-its-own-substrate. Further details are in the advanced texts.

śaṅkate -
athaivamapīti/ bhramabhinnārthakayathārthapadaniveśe 'pītyarthaḥ/ 'hrado
vahnimān dhūmāt' ityatra 'hrado vahnyabhāvavān' iti niścayasya

samādhatte --- yadrūpāvacchinneti/ tathā ca yadrūpapadena
vahnyabhāvatvasyopādāne tadavacchinnaviṣayakasya 'vahnyabhāvavān
children.translated_text: He raises an objection — 'even if thus.' The meaning is: even with the inclusion of the word 'veridical' meaning 'different from error.' In the inference 'the lake possesses fire, because of smoke,' since the ascertainment 'the lake possesses the absence of fire' is an obstruction, the property of being its object belongs to the absence of fire in a lake possessing fire-absence, just as it does to sublation. Thus the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> as being the object of a veridical cognition obstructing inference over-extends to the absence of fire, which is not of the nature of sublation. He resolves this — 'delimited by whatever property.' Thus, when the term 'whatever property' specifies fire-absence-hood, the cognition delimited by that as its object, namely 'the lake possesses the absence of fire,'

children.text:
hradaḥ' iti
jñānasyānumitipratibandhakatve 'pi
vahnyabhāvatvāvacchinnaviṣayakajñānasāmānyāntargatasya 'vahnyabhāvaḥ'
ityākārakajñānasya 'hrado vahnimān'
ityākārakānumitipratibandhakatvaṃ nāsti/ ataḥ
vahnyabhāvavaddhradatvameva yadrūpapadena dhartavyam/
tadavacchinnaviṣayakajñānasāmānyasyānumitipratibandhakatvāt/
tadrūpāvacchinnatvaṃ ca vahnyabhāvavaddhrada evāsti na vanhyabhāva iti
nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ na ca tarhīti/ 'parvato vanhyabhāvavān' iti
bhramaviṣaye vanhyabhāve 'tivyāptivāraṇāya hi yathārthapadamupāttam/
niruktapariṣkāre tu yadrūpapadena na vanhyabhāvatvamupādātuṃ
children.translated_text: even though it obstructs inference, the cognition 'the absence of fire' — which falls within the general class of cognitions whose object is delimited by fire-absence-hood — does not obstruct the inference of the form 'the lake possesses fire.' Therefore, by the term 'whatever property,' what must be intended is specifically the property of being a lake possessing fire-absence. The general class of cognitions whose object is delimited by that does obstruct inference. And being delimited by that property belongs only to a lake possessing fire-absence, not to the absence of fire alone — hence there is no over-extension. The purport is thus. 'But then': for preventing the over-extension to the absence of fire, which is the object of the error 'the mountain possesses the absence of fire,' the word 'veridical' was included. But with the present refinement, the term 'whatever property' cannot accommodate fire-absence-hood,

children.text:
śakyate/
tadavacchinnaviṣayakajñānasāmānyāntargatasya vanhyabhāvaḥ iti jñānasya
'parvato vanhimān' ityanumitipratibandhakatvābhāvāt/ tathā ca
vanhyabhāve 'tivyāptyaprasaktyā yathārthapadaṃ vyarthamiti bhāvaḥ/

Therefore, since the over-extension to the absence of fire does not even arise, the word 'veridical' becomes purposeless. The purport is thus. 'By way of indicating the intended specific cognition': here by the word 'cognition' is meant a cognition that is

children.text:
1. svanirūpitatveti/
svaṃ idaṃ rajatamitibhramīyā rajatatvaniṣṭhā prakāratā tannirūpitatvaṃ
śuktiniṣṭhaviśeṣyatāyāmasti/
children.translated_text: 'Delimited by its own': 'own' refers to the <s>prakāratā</s> (qualifier-mode) residing in silver-hood in the erroneous cognition 'this is silver'; being delimited by that is present in the <s>viśeṣyatā</s> (qualificand-ness) residing in the shell.

children.text:
evaṃ svaṃ
rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratā tadāśrayaḥ rajatatvaṃ tadabhāvavacchaktivṛttitvaṃ ca
viśeṣyatāyāmasti/ tādṛśaviśeṣyatānirūpakatvaṃ bhrame anirūpakatvaṃ
pramāyāmiti samanvayo bodhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: Similarly, 'own' is the <s>prakāratā</s> residing in silver-hood; its substrate is silver-hood; and the property of occurring in what possesses the absence of that [substrate] belongs to the <s>viśeṣyatā</s>. One should understand the application [of the definition]: not being the determinant of such a <s>viśeṣyatā</s> is absent in error but present in valid cognition.

children.text:
vivakṣitamiti
sūcanāya yathārthapadamiti bhāvaḥ/ anāhāryatvaṃ
bādhakālīnecchājanyatvābhāvavattvam/ tadanupādāne 'hrado vanhimān'
iti bādhakajñānakāle 'hrade vanhyabhāvajñānaṃ bhavatu' itīcchayā

vanhyabhāvavaddhradatvāvacchinnaviṣayakajñānasāmānyāntargatatayā tasya
cānumitipratibandhakatvābhāvādavyāptisyāt bādhe/ tadvāraṇāya
pratibanadhakajñāne 'nāhāryatvaṃ niveśanīyam/ evaṃ
aprāmāṇyajñānānāskanditatvaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena
aprāmāṇyajñānābhāvaviśiṣṭatvam/ tadaniveśe 'yatra hrado vanhyabhāvavān'
iti jñānānantaraṃ 'idaṃ jñānaṃ apramā' iti jñānaṃ tatra
bādhajñānasyānumityapratibandhakatayā bādhe 'vyāptiḥ/ ataḥ tanniveśaḥ/
evaṃ niścayātmakatvāniveśe 'hrado vanhimān na vā' iti
saṃśayātmakajñānasya jñānasāmānyāntargatasya apratibandhakatayā avyāptiḥ
syāt/ ataḥ tanniveśaḥ/ tathā ca
yaddharmāvacchinnaviṣayakānāhāryāprāmāṇyajñānānāskanditaniścayasāmānyaṃ
prakṛtānumitipratibandhakaṃ taddharmāvacchinnatvaṃ hetudoṣasya lakṣaṇamiti
paryavasannam/
children.translated_text: the word 'veridical' is used to indicate that this is what is intended. The purport is thus. Non-producibility-by-desire (<s>anāhāryatva</s>) means the property of not being produced by a desire arising at the time of sublating cognition. Without including this, even the cognition 'the lake possesses the absence of fire' generated by the desire 'let there be a cognition of the absence of fire in the lake' at the time of the sublating cognition 'the lake possesses fire' — since it too falls within the general class of cognitions whose object is delimited by the property of being a lake possessing fire-absence, and since it does not obstruct inference — there would be under-extension with respect to sublation. To prevent that, non-producibility-by-desire must be included in the obstructing cognition. Similarly, the property of not being undermined by a cognition of invalidity (<s>aprāmāṇyajñānānāskanditatva</s>) means being qualified by the absence of a cognition of invalidity through the relation of co-location. Without including this, where after the cognition 'the lake possesses the absence of fire,' the cognition 'this cognition is not valid' [arises], there the sublating cognition would not obstruct inference, resulting in under-extension with respect to sublation. Hence its inclusion. Similarly, without including the nature of being a determinate cognition (<s>niścayātmakatva</s>), the doubtful cognition 'the lake possesses fire or not,' falling within the general class of cognitions and not being an obstruction, would cause under-extension. Hence its inclusion. Thus the final formulation is: the definition of a defect of the reason is being delimited by whatever property such that the general class of non-producible-by-desire, not-undermined-by-invalidity-cognition, determinate cognitions whose object is delimited by that property obstructs the inference in question.

In this [second] interpretation, 'veridical cognition of those that obstruct inference' is a <s>ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa</s> (genitive determinative) compound. In the inference 'the lake possesses fire, because of smoke,' [the cognition] 'the lake possesses fire'

ekajñānaviṣayaprakṛtahetutāvacchedakavattvasambanadhenetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: — the obstruction of inference is <s>bādha</s> (sublation) in the form of a lake possessing the absence of fire; the veridical cognition having that as its qualifier-mode, through the relation of possessing the delimitor of the reason-hood of the relevant reason as the content of a single cognition, has the form 'the smoke possesses a lake possessing the absence of fire'; the property of being the qualificand of that resides in smoke — hence smoke is defective. In the inference 'the mountain possesses smoke, because of fire,' regarding the deviating [reason], the obstruction of inference is <s>vyabhicāra</s> (deviation) in the form of fire qualified by occurring in what possesses the absence of smoke; the veridical cognition having that as its qualifier-mode, through the said relation, has the form 'the fire possesses such deviation'; the property of being the qualificand of that resides in fire — thus the definition applies. Objection: in 'the mountain possesses fire, because of smoke,' there is over-extension. Taking by the word 'inference' the inference 'the mountain possesses smoke,' the <s>vyabhicāra</s> that obstructs it — in the form of fire qualified by occurring in what possesses the absence of smoke — through the relation of possessing the delimitor of the reason-hood of the relevant reason as the content of a single cognition, the veridical cognition having that as its qualifier-mode has the form 'the smoke possesses such fire'; the property of being the qualificand of that resides in smoke. To this he replies — 'the word inference refers to the inference in question.' The meaning is: it refers to the inference having as its subject what is delimited by the delimitor of the relevant <s>pakṣatā</s> (subject-hood) and as its predicate what is delimited by the delimitor of the relevant <s>sādhyatā</s> (probandum-hood). Accordingly, only the inference 'the mountain possesses fire' is to be taken, and since the defect obstructing it is not established, there is no over-extension. The purport is thus. 'Through the demonstrated relation' means: through the relation of possessing the delimitor of the reason-hood of the relevant reason as the content of a single cognition.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: savyabhicāranirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>savyabhicāra</s> (the deviant reason)

children.text: AnTs_53 savyabhicāro'naikāntikaḥ / sa trividhaḥ / sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇānupasaṃhāribhedāt / tatra sādhyābhāvavadvṛttiḥ sādhāraṇo anaikāntikaḥ / yathā parvato vahnimān prameyatvād iti prameyatvasya vahnyabhāvavati hrade vidyamānatvāt / sarvasapakṣavipakṣavyāvṛtto'sādhāraṇaḥ / yathā śabdo nityaḥ śabdatvād iti / śabdatvaṃ sarvebhyo nityebhyo'ntyebhyaś ca vyāvṛttaṃ śabdamātravṛtti / anvayavyatirekadṛṣṭāntarahito'nupasaṃhārī / yathā sarvam anityaṃ prameyatvād iti / atra sarvasyāpi pakṣatvād dṛṣṭānto nāsti //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 53]: The deviant (<s>savyabhicāra</s>) is the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) [reason]. It is of three kinds, distinguished as <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (common), <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon), and <s>anupasaṃhārī</s> (non-exhaustive). Among these, that which occurs in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is the common inconclusive reason. For example: 'the mountain possesses fire, because of <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability)' — since <s>prameyatva</s> is present in the lake, which possesses the absence of fire. That which is excluded from all <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instances) and <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instances) is the uncommon [inconclusive reason]. For example: 'sound is eternal, because of <s>śabdatva</s> (sound-hood)' — <s>śabdatva</s> is excluded from all eternal and non-eternal things, residing only in sound. That which lacks both positive and negative examples is the non-exhaustive [inconclusive reason]. For example: 'everything is non-eternal, because of <s>prameyatva</s>' — here, since everything is the subject, there is no example.

children.text:
savyabhicāro 'naikāntikaḥ/ saḥ
trividhaḥ-sādhāraṇa-asādhāraṇa-anupasaṃhāribhedāt/
children.translated_text: The deviant (<s>savyabhicāra</s>) is the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). It is of three kinds — distinguished as <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (common), <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon), and <s>anupasaṃhārī</s> (non-exhaustive).

children.text:
tatra sādhyābhāvavadvṛttiḥ
sādhāraṇaḥ/ yathā parvato vanhimān prameyatvāt/ atra prameyatvasya
vanhyabhāvavati (sādhyābhāvavati) hrade vidyamānatvāt/
children.translated_text: Among these, that which occurs in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is the <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (common) [inconclusive reason]. For example: 'the mountain possesses fire, because of <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability).' Here, since <s>prameyatva</s> is present in the lake (which possesses the absence of fire, i.e., the absence of the probandum).

children.text:
sarvasapakṣavipakṣavyāvṛtto 'sādhāraṇaḥ/ yathā śabdo nityaḥ
śabdatvāt/ atra śabdatvaṃ sarvebhyaḥ nityebhyaḥ anityebhyo vyāvṛttam
śabdamātravṛtti/
children.translated_text: That which is excluded from all <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instances) and <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instances) is the <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon) [inconclusive reason]. For example: 'sound is eternal, because of <s>śabdatva</s> (sound-hood).' Here, <s>śabdatva</s> is excluded from all eternal and non-eternal things, residing only in sound.

children.text:
anvayavyatirekadṛṣṭāntarahito 'nupasaṃhārī/ yathā sarvamanityaṃ
prameyatvāt/ atra sarvasyāpi pakṣatvāt dṛṣṭānto nāsti/
children.translated_text: That which lacks both positive (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative (<s>vyatireka</s>) examples is the <s>anupasaṃhārī</s> (non-exhaustive) [inconclusive reason]. For example: 'everything is non-eternal, because of <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability).' Here, since everything is the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), there is no example.

children.translated_text: He classifies <s>savyabhicāra</s> (the deviant reason) — 'it is of three kinds.'

children.translated_text: He defines <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (the common [inconclusive reason]) — 'among these.' He illustrates — 'for example.'

children.translated_text: He defines <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (the uncommon [inconclusive reason]) — 'that which is excluded from all.'

lakṣaṇamāha---anvayeti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>anupasaṃhārī</s> (the non-exhaustive [inconclusive reason]) — 'that which lacks both positive and negative.'

children.translated_text: In the root text, 'therein' — the meaning is: among the common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) and others. 'Occurring in what possesses the absence of the probandum' — the meaning is: possessing the container-hood delimited by the relation that delimits probans-hood, determined by [the locus] that possesses the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation and property that delimit probandum-hood. Thus, in 'it possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, even though in the mountain and other loci of the probans, [various] absences of probanda through other relations and the absence of fire-in-general through another relation exist, and even though smoke and the like occur in the part of smoke and the like — which possesses the absence of the probandum — through inherence and the like, there is no over-pervasion. And here, if the qualification by a specific relation is not included in the 'possessing the absence of the probandum,' then in 'it possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, since the absence of fire and the like exists in the mountain and the like through temporal relation, there would be over-pervasion. If the qualification by the relation of spatial qualification (<s>daiśikaviśeṣaṇatā</s>) is included, then in a deviant probans with absence of pot-ness and the like as probandum, since the locus of the qualification-relation of the absence of the probandum such as pot-ness is not established, there would be under-pervasion. Therefore, the relevant relation in the 'possessing the absence of the probandum' should be intended as: the relation by which the determination of possessing the absence of the probandum is an obstructor to the cognition of possessing the probandum through the relation that delimits probandum-hood. When fire and the like are the probandum, such a relation is spatial qualification; when absence of pot-ness and the like is the probandum, such a relation is inherence — hence there is no defect. In 'it possesses monkey-contact, because of this-tree-ness' and the like, such a relation is undelimited spatial qualification — this is the indication.

children.translated_text: Nor should one err into thinking that there is over-pervasion in the contradictory [probans]. By the maxim that 'even when the superimposed is mixed, the <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) is not mixed,' since even when [the contradictory] is common with the contradicted, there is no harm. In the root text, 'excluded from all positive instances' — the meaning is: possessing the general absence of occurrence in any positive instance. The word 'all' makes explicit the inclusion of the general absence of occurrence in positive instances. The word 'positive instance' (<s>sapakṣa</s>) means that in which the probandum is ascertained as existing. Those who know the tradition [hold that] even in a valid probans establishing non-eternality in sound through sound-ness and the like, <s>asādhāraṇya</s> (uncommon-ness) is as desired in the state of doubt about the probandum in the thesis.

hetutāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnādheyatāvān sādhāraṇa iti
