children.translated_text: possessing the container-hood delimited by the relation delimiting probans-hood — is common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>). This is the conclusion.

children.text:
nanvevamapi 'ghaṭaḥ
dravyaṃ guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattvāt' ityatra saddhetāvativyāptiḥ,
dravyatvarūpasādhyābhāvavati guṇe sattāyāḥ sattvena
viśiṣṭaśuddhayoranatirekāt guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattāyāmapi
sādhyābhāvavannirūpitādhayatāyāḥ sattvāt ityata āha - digiti/
sādhyābhāvavannirūpitādheyatāvacchedakahetutāvacchedakavattvaṃ
sādhāraṇatvamitivivakṣitam/ viśiṣṭasattāyāḥ sattātvenaiva rūpeṇa
guṇavṛttitayā sādhyābhāvavadguṇanirūpitādheyatāvacchedakaṃ
sattātvameva na tu guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattātvarūpaṃ
hetutāvacchedakamiti nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: But even so, in the inference 'the pot is a substance, because of possessing <s>sattā</s> (existence) qualified by difference from qualities and actions,' there would be over-pervasion (<s>ativyāpti</s>) in the valid probans, since in quality — which possesses the absence of the probandum in the form of substance-ness — there is no distinction between <s>sattā</s> (existence) as qualified and as unqualified, and hence even in the case of <s>sattā</s> qualified by difference from qualities and actions, the property of being determined by the locus of the absence of the probandum would obtain. To this he replies — 'dik' (the direction). What is intended is that <s>sādhāraṇatva</s> (commonality) means possessing the delimitor of probans-hood that is the delimitor of superstratum-hood determined by the locus of the absence of the probandum. Since qualified <s>sattā</s>, in the form of <s>sattā</s>-ness alone, occurs in qualities, the delimitor of superstratum-hood determined by the quality that is the locus of the absence of the probandum is <s>sattā</s>-ness itself, and not the form of <s>sattā</s> qualified by difference from qualities and actions as the delimitor of probans-hood — hence there is no over-pervasion. This is the purport.

children.text:
nanu 'śabdo nityaḥ
kṛtakatvāt' ityatra viruddhe 'pi
nityatvarūpasādhyābhāvavadghaṭavṛttitvaṃ kṛtakatve 'stīti
sādhāraṇalakṣaṇasyātivyāptiriti śaṅkate - na ca viruddha iti/
upadheyasaṅkare 'pīti/ ekasmin aneke doṣāḥ saṃbhavantīti bhāvaḥ/
upadheyasaṅkare 'pi - duṣṭasya ekatve 'pi upādherasaṅkaraḥ -
doṣasyabhinnatā/
children.translated_text: But in 'sound is eternal, because of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>),' even in the case of <s>viruddha</s> (the contradictory), since the property of occurring in a pot — which possesses the absence of the probandum in the form of eternality — exists in <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being produced), the definition of <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (the common fallacy) would over-pervade. To this he raises the objection — 'na ca viruddha' (nor is it contradictory). 'Even when there is mixing of what is to be subsumed' — the meaning is that multiple defects can occur in a single [probans]. Even when there is mixing of what is to be subsumed — even though the defective [probans] is one, there is no mixing of the adventitious condition — the defect remains distinct.

children.text:
1. guṇādireveti/ na
tu vṛkṣaḥ, tatra mūlādyavacchinnaviśeṣaṇatāsambanadhanaiva
kapisaṃyogābhāvasattvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Quality and the like only' — not a tree, because in a tree, even through the relation of qualification delimited by root and so on, the absence of monkey-contact possessing <s>sattva</s> (existence) obtains. This is the purport.

children.text:
asādhāraṇalakṣaṇe
sapakṣaśabdasya niścitasādhyavānityarthaḥ/ viśeṣyatāsambandhena
sādhyaprakārakaniścayavāniti yāvat/ sapakṣavṛttitvasāmānyābhāvavān
sapakṣavṛttitvatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvavān asādhāraṇa iti
phalitam/ te 1saddhetorapi yatkiñcitsapakṣavṛttitvābhāvasattvāt
asādhāraṇatvaṃ syādityākṣepasya nāvasaraḥ/ śabdo 'nityaḥ śabdatvāt
ityatra saddhetau pakṣe śabde 'nityatvarūpasādhyasandehadaśāyāṃ
sādhyaprakārakaniścayavān śabdo na bhavati api tu ghaṭādireva,
tadavṛttitvaṃ śabdatve astīti śabdatvasya asādhāraṇatvam/ yadā tu
śabde 'nityatvaniścayo 'sti tadā śabdo 'pi
sādhyaprakārakaniścayavattvāt sapakṣaḥ tadavṛttitvaṃ śabdatve nāstīti
nāsādhāraṇyam/ tathā cāsādhāraṇyamanityadoṣa iti prācīnāḥ/
navīnāstu - saddhetoḥ kādācitkamasādhāraṇyaṃ necchanti/ tanmate
sapakṣapadaṃ sādhyavanmātraparam/ sādhyavadvṛttitvasāmānyābhāvaḥ
asādhāraṇyam/ saddhetau pakṣe sādhyasandehadaśāyāmapi pakṣaḥ sādhyavān
children.translated_text: In the definition of <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (the uncommon fallacy), the word '<s>sapakṣa</s>' (homologue) means 'that which is ascertained to possess the probandum.' It means: that which has an ascertainment in which the probandum is a qualifier, through the relation of qualificand-hood. The result is that the <s>asādhāraṇa</s> is that which possesses the absence of the generic property of occurring in the homologue — that is, possessing the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the property of occurring in the homologue. Therefore, since even a valid probans possesses the absence of some occurrence in the homologue, there is no occasion for the objection that it would become <s>asādhāraṇa</s>. In the example 'sound is non-eternal, because of <s>śabdatva</s> (sound-ness),' regarding the valid probans, in the state of doubt about the probandum in the form of non-eternality in the <s>pakṣa</s> (locus, i.e. sound), sound does not qualify as one ascertained to possess the probandum — rather only a pot and such does; and the non-occurrence in that [pot etc.] exists in <s>śabdatva</s>, hence <s>śabdatva</s> is <s>asādhāraṇa</s>. But when there is ascertainment of non-eternality in sound, then sound too, being ascertained to possess the probandum, becomes a homologue, and the non-occurrence in it does not exist in <s>śabdatva</s> — hence there is no <s>asādhāraṇya</s> (uncommon fallacy). Accordingly, the ancients hold that <s>asādhāraṇya</s> is a non-permanent defect. The moderns, however, do not accept that a valid probans has occasional <s>asādhāraṇya</s>. In their view, the word '<s>sapakṣa</s>' refers merely to whatever possesses the probandum. <s>Asādhāraṇya</s> is the absence of the generic property of occurring in what possesses the probandum. Regarding the valid probans, even in the state of doubt about the probandum in the <s>pakṣa</s>, the <s>pakṣa</s> itself possesses the probandum,

children.text:
bhavatīti tadavṛttitvaṃ
hetau nāstīti nāsādhāraṇyam/
children.translated_text: and therefore the non-occurrence in it does not exist in the probans — hence there is no <s>asādhāraṇya</s>.

children.text:
kiñcidviśeṣyaketi/
yatra kutrāpi sādhyaṃ niścitaṃ cet tadviśeṣyakaniścayaprakārībhūtaṃ
sādhyaṃ bhavet/ sarvamabhidheyaṃ prameyatvādityatra tu sarvasya pakṣatvāt
abhidheyatvaṃ na kvāpi niścitam/ ataḥ
kiñcidviśeṣyakaniścayāprakārībhūtaṃ sādhyaṃ bhavati tādṛśasādhyakaśca
heturbhavati/ paraṃ tu atra sādhyābhāvasyāpratiddhatayā
kiñcidviśeṣyakaniścayāviṣayasādhyābhāvakatvamiti dalaṃ na samanveti/
ato navīnāḥ atyantābhāvāpratiyogisādhyādikatvamanupasaṃhāritvam
ityāhaḥ/ nanu ghaṭo 'bhidheyaḥ prameyatvāt ityatra
children.translated_text: 'Having some qualificand' — if the probandum is ascertained somewhere, then the probandum becomes a qualifier in an ascertainment having that as its qualificand. But in 'everything is expressible, because of being knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>),' since everything is the <s>pakṣa</s> (locus of inference), expressibility is not ascertained anywhere. Therefore the probandum is one that is not a qualifier in any ascertainment having a qualificand, and the probans is one having such a probandum. However, here, since the absence of the probandum is not established, the clause 'having the absence of the probandum as a qualifier in an ascertainment of some qualificand' does not apply. Therefore the moderns say that <s>anupasaṃhāritva</s> (non-instantiability) means having a probandum that is not the counter-positive of an absolute absence. But in 'the pot is expressible, because of being knowable,'

children.text: saddhetāvapi
children.translated_text: even regarding the valid probans,

children.text:
1. saddhetorapīti/
śabdo 'nityaḥ śabdatvādityatra ghaṭādirūpasapakṣavṛttitvābhāvasya śabdatve
sattvādityarthaḥ/ śabde 'nityatvaniścayadaśāyāmasya saddhetutvāt
yatkiñcinniścitasādhyavatpadena ghaṭādikamupādāya tadavṛttitvasattvāt
ativyāptiḥ prasaktā/ sāmānyābhāvaniveśe ca
sapakṣabhūtaśabdavṛttitvasatvena sapakṣavṛttitvatvāvacchinnābhāvo nāstīti
nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Even of a valid probans' — the meaning is: in 'sound is non-eternal, because of <s>śabdatva</s> (sound-ness),' the absence of occurrence in the homologue in the form of pot and the like exists in <s>śabdatva</s>. Since this is a valid probans in the state of ascertainment of non-eternality in sound, taking pot and the like by the word 'whatever is ascertained to possess the probandum,' and since the non-occurrence in that [pot etc.] exists [in <s>śabdatva</s>], over-pervasion would follow. But when the absence of the generic property is stipulated, since the property of occurring in sound — which is a homologue — obtains, the absence delimited by the property of occurring in the homologue does not exist — hence there is no over-pervasion. This is the purport.

children.text:
atyantābhāvāpratiyogisādhyakatvasattvādanupasaṃhāritvāpattiriti
cet - na/ iṣṭāpatteḥ/ tatra anupasaṃhāritvajñānena
children.translated_text: If it be objected that there would be the unwanted consequence of <s>anupasaṃhāritva</s> (non-instantiability) due to the probandum having the property of not being the counter-positive of an absolute absence — no, because this consequence is accepted (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>). There, through the cognition of <s>anupasaṃhāritva</s>,

children.text:
vyatirekavyāptijñānasya pratibandhena
vyatirekavyāptijñānahetukānumitirna jāyate/
anvayavyāptijñānamūlā anumitistu nirābādhaiva/
kathamanupasaṃhāritvajñānasya vyatirekavyāptijñānapratibandhakatvamiti
cet-ittham/ sādhyam atyantābhāvāpratiyogi iti jñānakāle
sādhyam atyantābhāvapratiyogi iti jñānaṃ yathā na bhavati, tathā
sādhyapratiyogikaḥ atyantābhāvaḥ iti jñānaṃ ca na bhavati/ tathā ca
sādhyapratiyogikātyantābhāvaghaṭitavyatirekavyāptijñānamapi na
bhavatīti/
children.translated_text: since the cognition of <s>vyatireka-vyāpti</s> (negative concomitance) is obstructed, the inference based on the cognition of negative concomitance does not arise. But the inference based on the cognition of <s>anvaya-vyāpti</s> (positive concomitance) remains entirely unobstructed. If asked how the cognition of <s>anupasaṃhāritva</s> obstructs the cognition of negative concomitance — it is as follows: at the time of the cognition 'the probandum is not the counter-positive of an absolute absence,' the cognition 'the probandum is the counter-positive of an absolute absence' does not arise; similarly, the cognition 'there is an absolute absence having the probandum as counter-positive' also does not arise. And therefore, the cognition of negative concomitance constituted by the absolute absence having the probandum as counter-positive also does not arise.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: viruddhanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>viruddha</s> (the contradictory)

children.text: AnTs_54 sādhyābhāvavyāpto hetur viruddhaḥ / yatra śabdo nityaḥ kṛtakatvād iti / kṛtakatvaṃ hi nityatvābhāvenānityatvena vyāptam //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_54: A probans that is pervaded by the absence of the probandum is <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory). For example, 'sound is eternal, because of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>).' For <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being produced) is pervaded by non-eternality, which is the absence of eternality.

children.text:
sādhyābhāvavyāpto
heturviruddhaḥ/ yathā śabdo nityaḥ kāryatvāt (kṛtakatvāt) ghaṭavat/
(atra kṛtakatvam hi nityatvābhāvenānityatvena vyāptam)/
children.translated_text: A probans that is pervaded by the absence of the probandum is <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory). For example, 'sound is eternal, because of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>) (or: because of being produced), like a pot.' (Here, <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being produced) is indeed pervaded by non-eternality, which is the absence of eternality.)

children.text: satpratipakṣanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (the counter-balanced)

children.text: AnTs_55 yasya sādhyabhāvasādhakaṃ hetvantaraṃ vidyate sa satpratipakṣaḥ / yathā śabdo nityaḥ śrāvaṇatvāc chabdatvavad iti / śabdo'nityaḥ kāryatvād ghaṭavad iti //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_55: That [probans] for which there exists another probans establishing the absence of the probandum is <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (counter-balanced). For example, 'sound is eternal, because of being audible (<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>), like <s>śabdatva</s> (sound-ness).' [The counter:] 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>), like a pot.'

children.text:
yasya sādhyābhāvasādhakaṃ hetvantaraṃ vidyate sa satpratipakṣaḥ/ yathā śabdaḥ nityaḥ
śrāvaṇatvāt, śabdaḥ anityaḥ kāryatvāt ghaṭavat/
children.translated_text: That [probans] for which there exists another probans establishing the absence of the probandum is <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (counter-balanced). For example, 'sound is eternal, because of being audible (<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>)'; [and the counter:] 'sound is non-eternal, because of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>), like a pot.'

children.text: asiddhanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>asiddha</s> (the unestablished)

children.text: AnTs_56 asiddhas trividhaḥ / āśrayāsiddhaḥ svarūpāsiddho vyāpyatvāsiddhaś ceti / āśrayāsiddho yathā gaganāravindaṃ surabhy aravindatvāt sarojāravindavat / atra gaganāravindam āśrayaḥ / sa ca nāsty eva / svarūpāsiddho yathā śabdo guṇaś cākṣuṣatvāt / atra cākṣuṣatvaṃ śabde nāsti śabdasya śrāvaṇatvāt / sopādhiko vyāpyatvāsiddhaḥ / sādhyavyāpakatve sati sādhanāvyāpaka upādhiḥ / sādhyasamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ sādhyavyāpakatvam / sādhanavann iṣṭātyantābhāvapratiyogitvaṃ sādhāraṇāvyapakatvam / parvato dhūmavān vahnimattvād ity atrārdrendhasaṃyoga upādhiḥ / tathā hi / yatra dhūmas tatrārdrendhnasaṃyoga iti sādhyavyāpakatā / yatra vahnis tatrārdrendhanasaṃyogābhāvād iti sādhanāvyāpakatā / evaṃ sādhyavyāpakatve sati sādhanāvyāpakatvād ardrendhanasaṃyoga upādhiḥ / sopādhikatvād vahnimattvaṃ vyāpyatvāsiddham //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_56: <s>Asiddha</s> (the unestablished) is of three kinds: <s>āśrayāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to locus), <s>svarūpāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to own nature), and <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to pervasion). An example of <s>āśrayāsiddha</s>: 'the sky-lotus is fragrant, because of being a lotus, like the pond-lotus.' Here, the sky-lotus is the locus, and it simply does not exist. An example of <s>svarūpāsiddha</s>: 'sound is a quality, because of being visible (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>).' Here, visibility does not exist in sound, because sound is auditory. That which has an adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>) is <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s>. An <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) is that which pervades the probandum but does not pervade the probans. Pervading the probandum means not being the counter-positive of an absolute absence co-located with the probandum. Not pervading the probans means being the counter-positive of an absolute absence accepted [as existing] in the locus of the probans. In 'the mountain has smoke, because of having fire,' the contact with wet fuel is the <s>upādhi</s>. For: wherever there is smoke, there is contact with wet fuel — this is the pervading of the probandum; wherever there is fire, there is absence of contact with wet fuel — this is the non-pervading of the probans. Thus, because it pervades the probandum while not pervading the probans, contact with wet fuel is the <s>upādhi</s>. Because of having such an adventitious condition, 'having fire' is <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to pervasion).

children.text:
asiddhaḥ trividhaḥ -
āśrayāsiddhaḥ svarūpāsiddhaḥ vyāpyatvāsiddhaśceti/
children.translated_text: <s>Asiddha</s> (the unestablished) is of three kinds — <s>āśrayāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to locus), <s>svarūpāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to own nature), and <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to pervasion).

children.text:
āśrayāsiddho yathā -
gaganāravindaṃ surabhi aravindatvāt sarojāravindavat/ atra
gaganāravindamāśrayaḥ/ sa ca nāstyeva/
children.translated_text: An example of <s>āśrayāsiddha</s>: 'the sky-lotus is fragrant, because of being a lotus, like the pond-lotus.' Here the sky-lotus is the locus, and it simply does not exist.

children.text:
svarūpāsiddho yathā -
śabdaḥ guṇaḥ cākṣuṣatvāt/ atra cākṣaṣatvaṃ śabde nāsti, śabdasya
śrāvaṇatvāt/
children.translated_text: An example of <s>svarūpāsiddha</s>: 'sound is a quality, because of being visible (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>).' Here visibility does not exist in sound, because sound is auditory.

children.text:
sopādhikaḥ
vyāpyatvāsiddhaḥ/
children.translated_text: That which has an adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>) is <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to pervasion).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
viruddhaṃ lakṣayati -
sādhyeti/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>viruddha</s> (the contradictory) — '<s>sādhya</s>' etc.

children.text:
satpratipakṣaṃ lakṣayati -
yasyeti/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (the counter-balanced) — '<s>yasya</s>' etc.

children.text:
asiddhaṃ vibhajate -
asiddha iti/
children.translated_text: He classifies <s>asiddha</s> (the unestablished) — '<s>asiddha</s>' etc.

children.text:
āśrayāsiddhamudāharati
- gaganeti/
children.translated_text: He illustrates <s>āśrayāsiddha</s> (the unestablished as to locus) — '<s>gagana</s>' etc.

children.text:
svarūpāsiddhamudāharati
- yatheti/
children.translated_text: He illustrates <s>svarūpāsiddha</s> (the unestablished as to own nature) — '<s>yathā</s>' etc.

children.text:
vyāpyatvāsiddhasya
lakṣaṇamāha - sopādhika iti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> (the unestablished as to pervasion) — '<s>sopādhika</s>' etc.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
sādhyābhāvavyāpta
iti/ sādhyābhāvavyāptiḥ sādhyavadavṛttitvam/ asādhāraṇyasya tu
niścitasādhyavadavṛttitvarūpatayā nābhedaḥ/ navīnamate tu -
sādhyābhāvasya vyatirekavyāptiḥ sādhyavyāpakābhāvapratiyogitvarūpeti
nāsādhāraṇyābhedaḥ/ etādṛśavyāptiviśiṣṭahetumattājñānaṃ
sākṣādanumitipratibandhakamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: 'Pervaded by the absence of the probandum' — the pervasion by the absence of the probandum means non-occurrence in what possesses the probandum. As for <s>asādhāraṇya</s> (the uncommon fallacy), since it has the form of non-occurrence in what is ascertained to possess the probandum, there is no identity [with <s>viruddha</s>]. In the view of the moderns, however, since the <s>vyatireka-vyāpti</s> (negative concomitance) of the absence of the probandum has the form of being the counter-positive of an absence that pervades the probandum, there is no identity with <s>asādhāraṇya</s>. It should be noted that the cognition of a probans qualified by such pervasion directly obstructs inference.

children.text:
yasya
sādhyābhāvetyādi/ yatsambandhi yatsādhyaṃ tadabhāvavyāpyahetvantarasya
jñānaṃ pakṣe 'sti sa satpratipakṣa ityarthaḥ/ prakṛtasādhyavyāpyatvena
jñāyamāno yaḥ prakṛtahetuḥ tato 'nyasmin hetau
sāṃdhyābhāvavyāpyatvajñānadaśāyāmeva tasya satpratipakṣateti sūcanāya
hetvantaramiti iti prāñcaḥ/ navīnāḥ punarevaṃ varṇayanti -
yatsambandhisādhyābhāvavyāpyahetvantarasya pakṣe sattvaṃ sa tathāvidha
ityartha iti/
children.translated_text: 'For which there exists [another probans establishing] the absence of the probandum' and so on. The meaning is: that [probans] is <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (counter-balanced) in whose <s>pakṣa</s> (locus) there exists knowledge of another probans pervaded by the absence of the probandum related to it. The ancients use the expression 'another probans' to indicate that when the present probans is known as pervaded by the present probandum, it is precisely at the stage when there is knowledge of the other probans being pervaded by the absence of the probandum that it becomes counter-balanced. The moderns, however, explain it thus: that [probans] is of such a nature when there exists in the <s>pakṣa</s> another probans pervaded by the absence of the probandum related to it — this is the meaning.

children.text:
āśrayāsiddho yatheti/
āśrayāsiddhiśca pakṣe pakṣatāvacchedakavirahaḥ, pakṣatāvacchedakavirahavān
pakṣo vā/ sa ca
children.translated_text: 'An example of <s>āśrayāsiddha</s>' — <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s> (unestablishment as to locus) is the absence in the <s>pakṣa</s> of the delimitor of <s>pakṣa</s>-hood, or alternatively, a <s>pakṣa</s> that lacks the delimitor of <s>pakṣa</s>-hood. And that

children.text:
nāstyeveti/
aravindasya prasiddhatvāt 'saviśeṣaṇehi' iti nyāyena aravinde
gaganīyatvaṃ nāstīti paryavasitor'thaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'simply does not exist' — since the lotus is well-known, by the principle '<s>saviśeṣaṇehi</s>' (with the qualifier), the settled meaning is that the property of belonging to the sky does not exist in the lotus.

children.text:
svarūpāsiddhiśca pakṣe
hetvabhāvaḥ hetvabhāvavān pakṣo vā/
children.translated_text: <s>Svarūpāsiddhi</s> (unestablishment as to own nature) is the absence of the probans in the <s>pakṣa</s>, or alternatively, a <s>pakṣa</s> that lacks the probans.

children.text:
nanu sopādhikasya
atiriktasya sadbhāvāt katha pañcahetvābhāsā ityata āha -
sopādhika iti/ vyāpyatvāsiddhiḥ vyāptyabhāvaḥ, tasyāḥ
sopādhikahetau niyamena sattvāt sopādhiko vyāpyatvāsiddha eva na
tvatirikto
children.translated_text: If it be asked how there can be [only] five fallacious reasons when the one with an adventitious condition (<s>sopādhika</s>) exists as a separate [sixth], he replies — '<s>sopādhika</s>' etc. <s>Vyāpyatvāsiddhi</s> (unestablishment as to pervasion) means the absence of pervasion, and since this invariably obtains in a probans with an adventitious condition, the <s>sopādhika</s> is simply a case of <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> and not a separate

children.text:
hetvābhāsa iti
bhāvaḥ/ upādherdeṣatvamasambhavīti dīpikāyāṃ vyaktībhaviṣyatyagre/
children.translated_text: fallacious reason — this is the purport. That the adventitious condition does not constitute a [separate] defect will become clear later in the <s>Dīpikā</s>.

children.text:
atredamavadheyam -
sādhye sādhyatāvacchedakābhāvaḥ sādhyāprasiddhiḥ/ hetau
hetutāvacchedakābhāvaḥ sādhanāprasiddhiḥ/ yathā kāñcanamayavahrimān
kāñcanamayadhūmāt ityādau/ tadgrahadaśāyāṃ
hetutāvacchedakaviśiṣṭe
sādhyatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭavyāptigrahapratibandhaḥ phalam/
tayorvyāpyatvāsiddhāvantarbhāvāt na hetvābhāsādhikyamiti/
children.translated_text: Here this should be noted — the absence in the probandum of the delimitor of probandum-hood is <s>sādhyāprasiddhi</s> (unestablishment of the probandum). The absence in the probans of the delimitor of probans-hood is <s>sādhanāprasiddhi</s> (unestablishment of the means of proof). For example, in 'this has golden fire, because of golden smoke,' and so forth. The result is an obstruction to grasping the pervasion qualified by the delimitor of probans-hood in relation to [the probandum] qualified by the delimitor of probandum-hood, at the time of grasping those [terms]. Since both of these are subsumed under <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> (unestablished as to pervasion), there is no excess of fallacious reasons.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
sādhyābhāvavyāptiḥ
sādhyavadavṛttitvamiti/ sādhyābhāvavyāptiḥ,
sādhyābhāvābhāvavadavṛttitvam/ tacca sādhyavadavṛttitvameva,
sādhyābhāvābhāvasya sādhyātmakatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ asādhāraṇyaṃ
niścitasādhyavadavṛttitvam, virudhdatvaṃ tu sādhyavadavṛttitvamiti
tayorbheda iti bhāvaḥ/ navīnamate sādhyavadavṛttitvameva
asādhāraṇyam, ataḥ tanmatānusāreṇa asādhāraṇyavilakṣaṇaṃ
virodhapadārthamāha - navīnamate tviti/ sādhyābhāvasya
vyatirekavyāptiḥ sādhyābhāvābhāvavyāpakībhūtābhāvapratiyogitvam
sādhyavyāpakībhūtābhāvapratiyogitvaparyavasitam/ śabdaḥ nityaḥ
kṛtakatvāt ityatra sādhyaṃ nityatvam, tadvyāpakībhūtaḥ abhāvaḥ
kṛtakatvābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvaṃ kṛtakatve 'stīti lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/
sākṣādanumitipratibandhakamiti/ tadvattābuddhiṃ prati
tadabhāvavyāpyavattājñānasya pratibandhakatvāt śabdaḥ nityaḥ
ityanumitiṃ prati
nityatvābhāvanirūpitavyatirekavyāptimaddhetumattājñānasya
nityatvavyāpakībhūtābhāvapratiyogikṛtakatvavān śabda iti
virodhajñānasya tadabhāvavyāpyavattājñānarūpatayā pratibandhakatvamiti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Pervasion by the absence of the probandum means non-occurrence in what possesses the probandum. Pervasion by the absence of the probandum is non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the absence of the probandum. And that is precisely non-occurrence in what possesses the probandum, since the absence of the absence of the probandum is identical with the probandum itself — this is the purport. The uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) is ascertained non-occurrence in what possesses the probandum, whereas the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) is [merely] non-occurrence in what possesses the probandum — thus lies the distinction between the two, this is the purport. In the view of the Navya-logicians (<s>navīna</s>), non-occurrence in what possesses the probandum is itself the uncommon; therefore, following their view, he states the meaning of contradiction as distinct from the uncommon — 'In the Navya view, however...' The <s>vyatireka-vyāpti</s> (negative pervasion) of the absence of the probandum is counter-positiveness to an absence that has become a pervader of the absence of the absence of the probandum, which amounts to counter-positiveness to an absence that has become a pervader of the probandum. In 'sound is eternal, because of being produced,' the probandum is eternality; the absence that has become its pervader is the absence of producedness; the counter-positiveness to that exists in producedness — thus the definition applies. 'It directly obstructs inference' — since cognition of possessing what is pervaded by the absence of that obstructs the cognition of possessing that, the cognition of contradiction in the form 'sound possesses producedness which is the counter-positive of the absence that has become the pervader of eternality' obstructs the inference 'sound is eternal,' because such cognition of contradiction has the nature of cognition of possessing what is pervaded by the absence of the probandum — this is the purport.

children.text:
virodhiparāmarśadvayakāla eva satpratipakṣatvamiti prāñcaḥ/
parāmarśābhāvakāle 'pi prakṛtahetoryatsādhyaṃ
tadabhāvavyāpyahetvantaraṃ pakṣe 'sti cet satpratipakṣatvaṃ bhavatyeveti
navīnāḥ/ tadāha - yatsambandhi-yatsādhyamityādi/ yatsambandhītyasya
yaddhetusambanadhītyarthaḥ/ tathā ca yaddhetusambandhi yatsādhyaṃ
tadabhāvavyāpyahetvantarasya jñānaṃ tatpakṣe 'sti sa satpratipakṣaḥ/ yathā
śabdo 'nityaḥ kṛtakatvāt ityatra kṛtakatvasambandhi anityatvarūpaṃ
sādhyam, tādṛśānityatvābhāvavyāpyaśrāvaṇatvarūpaṃ hetvantar tajjñānaṃ
śabdarūpe pakṣe 'stīti saḥ kṛtakatvahetuḥ satpratipakṣaḥ/
yādṛśahetusādhyatvenābhimatadharmābhāvavyāpyahetvantaravattājñānaviṣayaḥ
pakṣo bhavati tādṛśahetuḥ satpratipakṣa iti yāvat/
hetvantaraviśeṣyakaprakṛtasādhyābhāvavyāpyatvaprakārakajñānakālīnaprakṛtasādhyavyāpyatvaprakārakajñānaviśeṣyabhūto
hetuḥ satpratipakṣa iti phalitor'thaḥ/ yatsambandhisādhyetyādi/
yādṛśahetusambandhi yat sādhyaṃ tadabhāvavyāpyahetvantarasattvaṃ pakṣe
tādṛśo hetuḥ satpratipakṣaḥ/ kṛtakatvasambandhi anityatvaṃ tadabhāvaḥ
nityatvamaṃ tadvyāpyaṃ hetvantaram śrāvaṇatvam tat pakṣe
śabde 'satīti kṛtakatvaṃ satpratipakṣam/
children.translated_text: The earlier logicians (<s>prāñcaḥ</s>) hold that <s>satpratipakṣatva</s> (having a genuine counter-probans) obtains only at the time of the two contradictory considerations (<s>parāmarśa</s>). The Navya-logicians hold that even at the time when there is no [actual] consideration, if in the <s>pakṣa</s> (locus of inference) there exists another probans pervaded by the absence of the probandum of the probans in question, then the status of having a genuine counter-probans indeed obtains. He states this — 'that which is related to... that whose probandum...' and so forth. 'That which is related to' means 'that which is related to [a particular] probans.' And thus: the cognition of another probans pervaded by the absence of the probandum of what is related to a given probans, existing in that <s>pakṣa</s> — that is the genuine counter-probans (<s>satpratipakṣa</s>). For example, in 'sound is non-eternal, because of being produced,' the probandum related to producedness is non-eternality; another probans in the form of auditoriness (<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>), which is pervaded by the absence of such non-eternality, and the cognition of it exists in the <s>pakṣa</s> which is sound — hence that probans of producedness is a genuine counter-probans. The <s>pakṣa</s> which is the object of cognition of possessing another probans pervaded by the absence of the property intended as the probandum of a given probans — such a probans is the genuine counter-probans, this is the import. The resultant meaning is: a probans which is the qualificand of a cognition whose qualifier is pervasion with the probandum in question, [existing] at the time of a cognition whose qualifier is the pervasion of the particular other probans with the absence of the probandum in question — that is the genuine counter-probans. 'That whose related probandum...' and so forth: the probans related to which has a certain probandum, and in the <s>pakṣa</s> there exists another probans pervaded by the absence of that probandum — such a probans is the genuine counter-probans. What is related to producedness is non-eternality; its absence is eternality; what is pervaded by that, i.e. another probans, is auditoriness; that exists in the <s>pakṣa</s>, namely sound — hence producedness is a genuine counter-probans.

children.text:
āśrayāsiddhiśca pakṣe
pakṣatāvacchedakaviraha iti/ gaganāravindaṃ surabhītyatra
gaganīyatvaviśiṣṭamaravindaṃ pakṣaḥ/ tatra pakṣe aravinde gaganīyatvaṃ
pakṣatāvacchedakaṃ nāstīti aravindaniṣṭhaḥ gaganīyatvābhāvo vā
gaganīyatvābhāvaviśiṣṭamaravindaṃ vā āśrayāsiddhirityarthaḥ/
saviśeṣaṇe hīti nyāyeneti/ 'saviśeṣaṇe hi vidhiniṣedhau sati
viśeṣye bādhe viśeṣaṇamupasaṃkrāmataḥ' iti nyāyaḥ/
viśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭhe vidhirvā niṣedho kriyamāṇaḥ viśeṣye
vidherniṣedhasya vā bādhe sati viśeṣaṇe vidhirvā niṣedho vā
saṃkrāmatīti nyāyasyārthaḥ/ yathā śikhī dhvasta ityatra
śikhāviśiṣṭapuruṣe vidhīyamānaḥ dhvaṃsaḥ puruṣe bādhāt
viśeṣaṇabhūtāṃ śikhāmāskandatīti śikhī dhvasta iti vākyāt
śikhāyāṃ dhvastatvaṃ paryavasyati, tathā gaganāravindaṃ nāstītyukte
abhāvarūpo niṣedhaḥ aravinde bādhitatvāt
gaganīyatvarūpaviśeṣaṇamāskandatīti 1gaganīyatvābhāvo paryavasyatīti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Āśrayāsiddhi</s> (unestablished substratum) is the absence of the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s> (the property of being the locus of inference) in the <s>pakṣa</s>. In 'the sky-lotus is fragrant,' what is qualified by sky-belonging-ness (<s>gaganīyatva</s>) is the lotus, which is the <s>pakṣa</s>. There, in the <s>pakṣa</s> which is the lotus, sky-belonging-ness, the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s>, does not exist — hence either the absence of sky-belonging-ness residing in the lotus, or the lotus qualified by the absence of sky-belonging-ness, is <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>, this is the meaning. 'By the maxim that in what has a qualifier...' — the maxim is: 'When an assertion or negation pertains to what has a qualifier, if there is a sublation in the qualificand, it transfers to the qualifier.' The meaning of the maxim is: when an assertion or negation is made regarding what is qualified by a qualifier, if the assertion or negation is sublated in the qualificand, then it transfers to the qualifier. For example, in 'the crested one is destroyed,' the destruction being predicated of the person qualified by a crest (<s>śikhā</s>), since it is sublated in the person, it transfers to the qualifier which is the crest — hence from the statement 'the crested one is destroyed,' the meaning that resolves is the destruction of the crest. Similarly, when it is said 'the sky-lotus does not exist,' the negation in the form of absence, since it is sublated in the lotus, transfers to the qualifier which is sky-belonging-ness — hence the meaning that resolves is the absence of sky-belonging-ness, this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu sopādhike
hetau upādhereva doṣatvamastu, kiṃ vyāpyatvāsiddheḥ
doṣatvenetyatrāha - upādherdeṣatvamasambhavīti/ vyaktībhaviṣyatīti/
'upādhistu vyabhicārajñānadvārā vyāptijñānapratibandhakaḥ' iti
grantheneti śeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: when a probans has a <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition), let the defect belong to the <s>upādhi</s> itself; why should <s>vyāpyatvāsiddhi</s> (unestablished pervasion) be [considered] the defect? To this he replies — 'The defectiveness of the <s>upādhi</s> is impossible.' 'It will become clear' — the supplement is: 'by the text that states the <s>upādhi</s> obstructs the cognition of pervasion through the cognition of deviation.'

children.text:
nanu
sādhyāprasiddhisādhanāpratiddhyorapi hetvābhāsatvāt tayorakathanena
nyūnatetyāśaṅkya tayorvyāpyatvāsiddhāvantarbhāvamāha - atre
damavadheyamiti/ kāñcanamayatvābhāvavān vahniḥ
ityākārakasādhyāprasiddhijñānadaśāyāṃ
children.translated_text: Objection: since <s>sādhyāprasiddhi</s> (unestablished probandum) and <s>sādhanāprasiddhi</s> (unestablished probans) are also fallacious reasons, not mentioning them constitutes an omission. Anticipating this, he states their inclusion within <s>vyāpyatvāsiddhi</s> — 'This should be noted here.' At the stage of the cognition of unestablished probandum in the form 'fire possesses the absence of being made of gold,'

children.text:
kāñcanamayatvaviśiṣṭavahnijñānāsambhavāt
'kāñcanamayatvaviśiṣṭavahnivyāpyadhūmavān' iti parāmarśe
kāñcanamayatvaviśiṣṭavahnibhānaṃ prati sādhyāprasiddhijñānaṃ
children.translated_text: since the cognition of fire qualified by being-made-of-gold (<s>kāñcanamayatva</s>) is impossible, in the consideration 'it possesses smoke which is pervaded by fire qualified by being-made-of-gold,' the cognition of unestablished probandum obstructs the appearance of fire qualified by being-made-of-gold

children.text:
pratibandhakam/ evaṃ
kāñcanamayatvābhāvavān dhūma ityākarakasādhanāprasiddhijñānadaśāyāṃ
'vahnivyāpyakāñcanamayadhūmavān parvata' iti parāmarśo na
sambhavati/ dhūmaviśeṣyakakāñcanamayatvaprakārakajñānaṃ prati
dhūmaviśeṣyakakāñcanamayatvābhāvaprakārakajñānasya pratibandhakatvāt/
tathā ca anumitijanakaparāmarśapratibandhakajñānaviṣayatayā
sādhyāprasiddhisādhanāprasiddhyorhetvābhāsatvam/ kathaṃ
vyāpyatvāsiddhāvanayorantarbhāva iti cet-śrūyatām/
hetutāvacchedakaviśiṣṭahetuvyāpakasādhyatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭasādhyasāmānādh ikaraṇyaṃ
hi vyāptiḥ/ sādhanāprasiddhisthale
hetutāvacchedakaviśiṣṭahetvabhāvāt
tādṛśahetughaṭitavyāptyabhāvarūpaṃ vyāpyatvāsiddhiḥ, sādhyāprasiddhisthale
sādhyatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭasādhyābhāvāt
tādṛśasādhyaghaṭitavyāptyabhāvavāt vyāpyatvāsiddhiḥ ityevaṃ
tayorvyāpyatvāsiddhāvantarbhāva iti/
children.translated_text: in the consideration. Similarly, at the stage of the cognition of unestablished probans in the form 'smoke possesses the absence of being-made-of-gold,' the consideration 'the mountain possesses smoke-made-of-gold which is pervaded by fire' is not possible, since the cognition of the absence of being-made-of-gold qualifying smoke obstructs the cognition having being-made-of-gold as a qualifier of smoke. And thus, <s>sādhyāprasiddhi</s> and <s>sādhanāprasiddhi</s> are fallacious reasons by virtue of being objects of cognitions that obstruct the consideration which generates inference. How are these two included in <s>vyāpyatvāsiddhi</s>? Listen: <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is the co-location of the probans qualified by the delimitor of probans-hood with the probandum qualified by the delimitor of probandum-hood. In the case of an unestablished probans, since there is no probans qualified by the delimitor of probans-hood, the absence of pervasion constituted by such a probans constitutes <s>vyāpyatvāsiddhi</s>. In the case of an unestablished probandum, since there is no probandum qualified by the delimitor of probandum-hood, the absence of pervasion constituted by such a probandum constitutes <s>vyāpyatvāsiddhi</s> — thus these two are included in <s>vyāpyatvāsiddhi</s>.

children.text:
1. gaganīyatvābhāve
paryavasyatīti/ etena paramamūle 'gaganāravindamāśrayaḥ, sa ca
nāsatyeva' iti vākyamasaṃgatam/ gaganāravindamityasya hi
gaganīyatvaviśiṣṭamaravindamityarthaḥ/ tatrāravindasya sattvāt tatra
nāstitvabādhāt - iti śaṅkā nirākṛtā aravinde
gaganīyatvābhāva ityeva 'sa ca nāstyeva' iti vākyasthārthaḥ
paryavasitaḥ, tatra cānupapatyabhāvāditi/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'The absence of sky-belonging-ness resolves' — by this, the statement in the original root text 'the sky-lotus is the substratum, and it indeed does not exist' is shown to be coherent. For 'sky-lotus' means a lotus qualified by sky-belonging-ness. Since the lotus exists there, the non-existence is sublated in the lotus — this objection is refuted: the meaning of the statement 'and it indeed does not exist' resolves precisely as the absence of sky-belonging-ness in the lotus, and there is no incoherence in that.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: upādhinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition)

children.text:
sādhyavyāpakatve
sati sādhanāvyāpakatvaṃ upādhitvam/
sādhyasamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ sādhyavyāpakatvam/
sādhanavanniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitvaṃ sādhanāvyāpakatvam/ (yathā)
parvataḥ dhūmavān vahneḥ ityatra ārdrendhanasaṃyogaḥ upādhiḥ/ yatra
dhūmaḥ tatra ārdrendhanasaṃyoga iti sādhyavyāpakatayā/ yatra vahniḥ tatra
ārdrendhanasaṃyoga iti nāsti/ ayogolake
ārdrenadhanasaṃyogābhāvāt/ evaṃ sādhyavyāpakatve sati
sādhanāvyāpakatvāt ārdrendhanasaṃyoga upādhiḥ/ sopādhikatvāt
vahnimattvaṃ vyāpyatvāsiddham/
children.translated_text: <s>Upādhitva</s> (the property of being an adventitious condition) is being a non-pervader of the probans while being a pervader of the probandum. Being a pervader of the probandum is not being the counter-positive of an absolute absence co-located with the probandum. Being a non-pervader of the probans is being the counter-positive of an absolute absence residing in what possesses the probans. For example, in 'the mountain possesses smoke, because of fire,' contact with wet fuel (<s>ārdrendhanasaṃyoga</s>) is the <s>upādhi</s>. Because wherever there is smoke, there is contact with wet fuel — thus it is a pervader of the probandum. But wherever there is fire, there is not [necessarily] contact with wet fuel — as in the case of the red-hot iron ball, due to the absence of contact with wet fuel. Thus, being a pervader of the probandum while being a non-pervader of the probans, contact with wet fuel is the <s>upādhi</s>. Because it has an <s>upādhi</s>, the possession of fire is an unestablished pervasion (<s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
upādherlakṣaṇamāha -
sādhyeti/ upādhiścaturvidhaḥ - kevala - sādhyavyāpakaḥ,
pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakaḥ, sādhanāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakaḥ,
udāsīnadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakaśceti/ ādyaḥ ārdrendhanasaṃyogaḥ/
dvitīyo yathā - vāyuḥ pratyakṣaḥ pratyakṣasparśāśrayatvāt ityatra
bahirdravyatvāvacchinnapratyakṣatvavyāpakaṃ udbhūtarūpavattvam/ tṛtīyo
yathā - prāgabhāvo vināśī janyatvāt ityatra
janyatvāvacchinnānityatvavyāpakaṃ bhāvatvam/ caturtho yathā - prāgabhāvo
vināśī prameyatvāt ityatra janayatvāvacchinnānityatvavyāpakaṃ
bhāvatvam/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>upādhi</s> — 'The probandum...' The <s>upādhi</s> is of four kinds: (1) a mere pervader of the probandum, (2) a pervader of the probandum delimited by a property of the <s>pakṣa</s>, (3) a pervader of the probandum delimited by the probans, and (4) a pervader of the probandum delimited by a neutral property. The first is contact with wet fuel. The second is as follows: in 'air is perceptible, because of being the substratum of perceptible touch,' possessing manifest color (<s>udbhūtarūpavattva</s>) is a pervader of perceptibility delimited by being an external substance (<s>bahirdravyatva</s>). The third is as follows: in 'prior absence is destructible, because of being produced,' being-ness (<s>bhāvatva</s>) is a pervader of non-eternality delimited by producedness. The fourth is as follows: in 'prior absence is destructible, because of being knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>),' being-ness is a pervader of non-eternality delimited by producedness.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
sādhyavyāpakatva
iti/ sādhyavyāpakatvasādhanāvyāpakatve ekarūpeṇa ekasambandhena ca
grāhye/ tena 'vahnimān dhūmāt' ityādau tattadvahnau vahnitvena
sādhyavyāpakatvasya tattadvanhitvena sādhanāvyāpakatvasya ca sattve 'pi
nātivyāptiḥ, na vā saṃyogena sādhyavyāpakasya vahneḥ samavāyena
sādhanāvyāpakatve 'pi tatrātivyāptiḥ/ mūloktopādhi lakṣaṇe 'vyāptiṃ
vārayituṃ lakṣyabhedena lakṣaṇabhedaṃ pradarśayati - upādhiścaturvidha
iti/ yaddharmaviśiṣṭasādhyavyāpakatvaṃ taddharmaviśiṣṭasādhanāvyāpakatvaṃ
lakṣaṇe niveśanīyam/ anyathā
parvatatvātmakapakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakasya kasyacit
dhūmatvāvacchinnāvyāpakatvāt ativyāptiḥ syāditi dhyeyam/
udāsīneti/ pakṣadharmasādhanadharmābhyāṃ bhinnetyarthaḥ/ bahirdravyatvam -
ātmānyadravyatvam/ idaṃ kevalapratyakṣatvasyaiva sādhyatvānusāreṇa/
prāgabhāvo vināśī janyatvāditi/ atra janyatvaṃ pakṣadharmo na bhavatīti
sādhanāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakatvaghaṭitalakṣaṇam/ anityatvavyāpakatiti/
vināśitvavyāpakamityarthaḥ/ janyatvasyodāsīnatvaṃ sampādayituṃ
prameyatvāditi/
children.translated_text: 'Pervasion of the probandum' — the pervasion of the probandum and the non-pervasion of the probans must be grasped through one form and through one relation. Therefore, in 'it possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, even though pervasion of the probandum through fire-ness exists in each particular fire, and non-pervasion of the probans through each particular fire-ness also exists, there is no over-pervasion; nor is there over-pervasion when fire, which is a pervader of the probandum through conjunction, is also a non-pervader of the probans through inherence. To prevent [such] over-pervasion in the definition of <s>upādhi</s> stated in the root text, he shows the difference in definitions according to the difference in definienda — 'The <s>upādhi</s> is of four kinds.' The pervasion of the probandum qualified by a certain property and the non-pervasion of the probans qualified by that same property must be incorporated in the definition. Otherwise, since something that is a pervader of the probandum delimited by the <s>pakṣa</s>-property of mountain-ness is not a non-pervader of the probans delimited by smoke-ness, there would be over-pervasion — this should be noted. 'Neutral' — the meaning is: different from both the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> and the property of the probans. 'Being an external substance' means being a substance other than the self (<s>ātman</s>). This is in accordance with mere perceptibility being the probandum. 'Prior absence is destructible, because of producedness' — here producedness is not a property of the <s>pakṣa</s>, hence the definition is constituted by pervasion of the probandum delimited by the probans. 'Pervader of non-eternality' — the meaning is: pervader of destructibility. To establish the neutrality of producedness, [the example is given as] 'because of knowability.'

ālokasyopādhitvāpattiḥ/ vahnimati sarvatra saṃyogasambandhena

sādhanadhūmavati parvate samavāyasambandhena ālokasyāvidyamānatayā

rūpeṇacopādheḥ sādhyavyāpakatvam, tenaiva sambandhena tenaiva rūpeṇa
ca tasya sādhanāvyāpakatvaṃ vivakṣitam/ ato vahnitvena

nātivyāptiḥ/ evaṃ saṃyogena vahnivyāpakasya ālokasya samavāyena
dhūmāvyāpakatve 'pi tenaiva saṃyogasambandhena dhūmāvyāpakatvaṃ

samavāyena sādhanāvyāpakatvaṃ
sādhanavanniṣṭhātyantābhāvanirūpitasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāvacchedakadharmavattvamiti
bodhyam/ avyāptiṃ vārayitumiti/ 'vāyuḥ pratyakṣaḥ

kevalasādhyavyāpakasyopādheḥ kevalasādhyavyāpakatve sati

udāsīnadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakasyopādheḥ

iti parvatīyavahnirupādhiḥ syāt/ dharmaikyavivakṣaṇe tu
parvatatvaviśiṣṭavahnivyāpakasya parvatīyavahneḥ parvatatvaviśiṣṭa
dhūmāvyāpakatvaṃ nāsti/ parvatatvaviśiṣṭadhūmavati parvate
parvatīyavahneḥ sattvāt/ ato nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: The definition of <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) stated in the root text — namely, non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) while there is pervasion of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — is over-extended (<s>ativyāpti</s>) in the case of a valid inferential mark such as 'the mountain possesses fire, because of smoke,' with respect to each particular fire (such as kitchen-fire). For kitchen-fire too, in the form of fire-ness (<s>vahnitva</s>), pervades the <s>sādhya</s> (fire-in-general), and in the form of kitchen-fire-ness, does not pervade the <s>sādhana</s> (smoke) — since kitchen-fire is absent in that which possesses the <s>sādhana</s>, namely in smoke-possessing [things]. Similarly, there would be the unwanted consequence of light (<s>āloka</s>) being an <s>upādhi</s> in the same inference, since light is present everywhere that possesses fire through the relation of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), and since light is absent on the mountain possessing smoke-as-<s>sādhana</s> through the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). Anticipating this objection, he says: 'the pervasion of the <s>sādhya</s> and non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s>.' Accordingly, it is intended that the non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> by the <s>upādhi</s> must be through the very same relation and the very same form by which the <s>upādhi</s> pervades the <s>sādhya</s>. Therefore, although kitchen-fire etc., which pervade fire through fire-ness, do not pervade smoke through kitchen-fire-ness, there is no non-pervasion of smoke through fire-ness — hence no over-extension. Similarly, although light, which pervades fire through conjunction, does not pervade smoke through inherence, there is no non-pervasion of smoke through that very relation of conjunction — hence no over-extension. This is the purport. 'Pervasion of the <s>sādhya</s> through fire-ness' means: the property of possessing fire-ness that is not a limitor of the counter-positive-ness of the absolute absence residing in the <s>sādhya</s>-possessor. 'Non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> through that particular fire-ness' means: the property of possessing that particular fire-ness that is a limitor of the counter-positive-ness of the absolute absence residing in the <s>sādhana</s>-possessor. Similarly, pervasion of the <s>sādhya</s> through conjunction is: the property of possessing a property that is not a limitor of the counter-positive-ness delimited by the relation of conjunction, of the absolute absence residing in the <s>sādhya</s>-possessor. Non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> through inherence is: the property of possessing a property that is a limitor of the counter-positive-ness delimited by the relation of inherence, of the absolute absence residing in the <s>sādhana</s>-possessor — this should be understood. 'In order to prevent under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>)': In the inference 'wind is perceptible, because it is a substratum of perceptible touch,' the property of possessing manifest color (<s>udbhūtarūpavattva</s>) is the <s>upādhi</s>. There, the definition involving pervasion of the <s>sādhya</s> as stated in the root text does not apply, since <s>udbhūtarūpa</s> (manifest color) is absent in the self (<s>ātman</s>), which possesses the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of perceptibility — hence under-extension would follow. To prevent this, a distinction in definition corresponding to distinctions in the definiendum must be stated — thus [the <s>Dīpikā</s> says] '<s>upādhi</s> is fourfold' and so on. This is the intent of the <s>Dīpikā</s>. Accordingly: for an <s>upādhi</s> that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> alone, the definition is non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> while pervading the <s>sādhya</s> alone. For an <s>upādhi</s> that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the locus), the definition is non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> so qualified while pervading the <s>sādhya</s> so qualified. For an <s>upādhi</s> that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>sādhana</s>, the definition is non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> while pervading the <s>sādhya</s> so qualified. For an <s>upādhi</s> that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by a neutral property (<s>udāsīnadharma</s>), the definition is non-pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> so qualified while pervading the <s>sādhya</s> so qualified — this is the intended distinction in definitions. Therefore he says: 'that which pervades the <s>sādhya</s> qualified by a [particular] property' and so on. The qualification is through the relation of co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). He states the purpose of intending identity of the qualifying property: 'otherwise.' In the inference 'the mountain possesses fire, because of smoke,' the fire on the mountain — [qualified by] the <s>pakṣadharma</s> which is mountain-ness — pervades fire qualified by mountain-ness, and also does not pervade smoke, since mountain-fire is absent in the kitchen which possesses smoke. Thus mountain-fire would be an <s>upādhi</s>. But if identity of the qualifying property is intended, then mountain-fire, which pervades fire qualified by mountain-ness, does not fail to pervade smoke qualified by mountain-ness, since mountain-fire is present on the mountain which possesses smoke qualified by mountain-ness. Therefore there is no over-extension — this is the purport.

pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpako 'yamupādhiḥ/ pakṣasya dharmaḥ pakṣadharmaḥ
tadavacchinnaḥ tadviśiṣṭaḥ tatsamānādhikaraṇaḥ ya sādhyaḥ tadvyāpakaḥ/
prakṛte pakṣaḥ vāyuḥ tadvṛttidharmaḥ bahirdravyatvaṃ tadviśiṣṭaṃ
yatpratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ tat ātmani nāsti, ātmano
bahirdravyatvarūpaviśeṣaṇābhāvāt/ ato
bahirdravyatvaviśiṣṭapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ yatra yatrāsti pṛthivyādau tatra
sarvatra udbhūtarūpavattvasattvāt udbhūtarūpavattvaṃ
pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakam/ tathā
bahirdravyatvaviśiṣṭapratyakṣasparśāśrayatvarūpaṃ pakṣadharmāvacchinnaṃ sādhanaṃ
yatrāstivāyau
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'the first [type]: contact with wet fuel (<s>ārdrendhana-saṃyoga</s>).' In the inference 'the mountain possesses smoke, because of fire,' contact with wet fuel is the <s>upādhi</s>. It pervades the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of smoke and does not pervade the <s>sādhana</s> in the form of fire — thus this <s>upādhi</s> pervades only the <s>sādhya</s> alone. 'The second is as follows': the <s>upādhi</s> pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s>. In the inference 'wind is an object of perception, because it is a substratum of perceptible touch,' the property of possessing manifest color (<s>udbhūtarūpavattva</s>) is the <s>upādhi</s>. It does not pervade the <s>sādhya</s> alone, since the property of possessing manifest color is absent in the self (<s>ātman</s>), which possesses the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of being an object of perception. Therefore this <s>upādhi</s> pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s>. The property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (locus) is the <s>pakṣadharma</s>; qualified by that means co-located with that; the <s>sādhya</s> so qualified — its pervader. In the present case, the <s>pakṣa</s> is wind; its resident property is being an external substance (<s>bahirdravyatva</s>); the perceptibility qualified by that is absent in the self, since the self lacks the qualifier of being an external substance. Therefore, wherever there is perceptibility qualified by being an external substance — in earth and so forth — there the property of possessing manifest color is present everywhere; hence <s>udbhūtarūpavattva</s> pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s>. Similarly, the <s>sādhana</s> qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s> — namely, being a substratum of perceptible touch qualified by being an external substance — wherever it exists, namely in wind,

children.text:
tatra udbhūtarūpaṃ
nāstīti pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhanāvyāpakaṃ codbhūtarūpavattvaṃ bhavatīti
lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ tṛtīyo yatheti/
children.translated_text: there manifest color is absent — thus <s>udbhūtarūpavattva</s> (the property of possessing manifest color) also does not pervade the <s>sādhana</s> as qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s>. This is the concordance with the definition. 'The third is as follows':,

children.text:
sādhanāvacchinnasādhyavyāpaka upādhirityarthaḥ/ sādhanāvacchinnatvaṃ
ca sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena sādhanaviśiṣṭatvam/ 'prāgabhāvo
vināśī janyatvāt' ityatra bhāvatvamupādhiriṣyate/ sa
kevalasādhyavyāpako na bhavati,
children.translated_text: the <s>upādhi</s> pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>sādhana</s>. The qualification by the <s>sādhana</s> means being qualified by the <s>sādhana</s> through the relation of co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). In the inference '<s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence) is destructible, because of being produced (<s>janyatva</s>),' <s>bhāvatva</s> (positive entity-ness) is intended as the <s>upādhi</s>. It does not pervade the <s>sādhya</s> alone,

children.text:
vināśitvarūpasādhyavati prāgabhāve bhāvatvābhāvāt/ ataḥ
sādhanāvacchinnasādhyavyāpako 'yamupādhiḥ/ janyatvarūpasādhanaviśiṣṭaṃ
vināśitvaṃ yatra yatrāsti ghaṭādau tatra bhāvatvasadbhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/
caturtho yatheti/ udāsīnadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpaka ityarthaḥ/
'prāgabhāvo vināśī pramevayatvāt' ityatra bhāvatvamupādhiḥ/
pakṣadharmāt sādhanāccānyo dharma udāsīnadharmaḥ/ janyatvaṃ hi pakṣe
children.translated_text: since <s>bhāvatva</s> (positive entity-ness) is absent in <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence), which possesses the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of destructibility (<s>vināśitva</s>). Therefore this <s>upādhi</s> pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>sādhana</s>: wherever destructibility qualified by producedness (<s>janyatva</s>) exists — in pots and so forth — there <s>bhāvatva</s> is present. This is the purport. 'The fourth is as follows': the <s>upādhi</s> pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by a neutral property (<s>udāsīnadharma</s>). In the inference '<s>prāgabhāva</s> is destructible, because of being knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>),' <s>bhāvatva</s> is the <s>upādhi</s>. A property other than the <s>pakṣadharma</s> and the <s>sādhana</s> is called a neutral property (<s>udāsīnadharma</s>). For producedness (<s>janyatva</s>),

children.text:
prāgabhāve nāstīti na
pakṣadharmaḥ/ evaṃ sādhanāt prameyatvāccānyat iti udāsīnadharmaḥ/
tadavacchinnaṃ janyatvaviśiṣṭaṃ vināśitvaṃ yatrāsti ghaṭādau tatra
bhāvatvasattvāt janyatvaviśiṣṭaprameyatvavati prāgabhāve
bhāvatvasyābhāvācca bhāvatvaṃ udāsīnadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakaḥ
udāsīnadharmāvacchinnasādhanāvyāpakaścopādhiriti bhāvaḥ/
prakāśikāyām pakṣadharmasādhanadharmābhyāmiti/ pakṣavṛttirdharmaḥ pakṣadharmaḥ
sādhanarūpo dharmaṃḥ sādhanadharmaḥ/ bahirdravyatvam ityasya vivaraṇaṃ
ātmānyadravyatvamiti/ vāyuḥ pratyakṣa ityatra pratyakṣapadasya
bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣaya iti yadyarthaḥ tadodbhūtarūpavattvaṃ
1kevalasādhyavyāpaka evopādhiḥ/ yadā tu pratyakṣaviṣayatvamātraṃ sādhyaṃ
2tadaiva pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpaka ityāśayenāha - idaṃ
kevalapratyakṣatvasyaiveti
bahirindriyajanyatvāghaṭitapratyakṣaviṣayatvamātrasyetyarthaḥ/ udāsīnatvaṃ
sampādayitumiti/ yadi janyatvameva hetuḥ syāt tadā
sādhanāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakatvamevopādherbhavet
nodāsīnadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakatvam/
sādhanādanyasyaivodāsīnaśabdārthatvāt/ ataḥ prameyatvasya
hetutvānusaraṇam/ adhunā tu janyatvaṃ sādhanāt prameyatvādanyaditi
janyatvaviśiṣṭavināśitvaṃ udāsīnadharmāvacchinnasādhyamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: is absent in the <s>pakṣa</s>, namely <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence), and hence is not a <s>pakṣadharma</s>. Similarly, it is different from the <s>sādhana</s>, knowability (<s>prameyatva</s>), and hence is a neutral property (<s>udāsīnadharma</s>). Wherever destructibility qualified by that — namely, destructibility qualified by producedness — exists, in pots and so forth, there <s>bhāvatva</s> is present; and since <s>bhāvatva</s> is absent in <s>prāgabhāva</s> which possesses knowability qualified by producedness, <s>bhāvatva</s> is an <s>upādhi</s> that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> qualified by the neutral property and does not pervade the <s>sādhana</s> qualified by the neutral property — this is the purport. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'by the <s>pakṣadharma</s> and the <s>sādhanadharma</s>': the property residing in the <s>pakṣa</s> is the <s>pakṣadharma</s>; the property in the form of the <s>sādhana</s> is the <s>sādhanadharma</s>. The gloss on 'being an external substance (<s>bahirdravyatva</s>)' is 'being a substance other than the self (<s>ātman</s>).' In the inference 'wind is perceptible,' if the word 'perceptible' means 'object of perception produced by external sense-organs,' then <s>udbhūtarūpavattva</s> would be an <s>upādhi</s> that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> alone. But when mere perceptibility is the <s>sādhya</s>, then alone it is an <s>upādhi</s> pervading the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s> — with this intent he says: 'this, of mere perceptibility,' meaning: of perceptibility alone, without the qualifier of being produced by external sense-organs. 'In order to establish the neutral character': if producedness (<s>janyatva</s>) alone were the <s>hetu</s> (inferential mark), then <s>bhāvatva</s> would only pervade the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by the <s>sādhana</s>, not the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified by a neutral property, since 'neutral' means precisely 'different from the <s>sādhana</s>.' Therefore, knowability (<s>prameyatva</s>) is adopted as the <s>hetu</s>. Now, producedness is different from the <s>sādhana</s>, knowability, and so destructibility qualified by producedness is the <s>sādhya</s> qualified by a neutral property — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: bādhitanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>bādhita</s> (the contradicted [inferential mark])

children.text: AnTs_57 yasya sādhyābhāvaḥ pramāṇāntareṇa niścitaḥ sa bādhitaḥ / yathā vahnir anuṣṇo dravyatvād iti / atrānuṣṇatvaṃ sādhyaṃ tadabhāva uṣṇatvaṃ spārśanapratyakṣeṇa gṛhyata iti bādhitatvam //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 57]: That [inferential mark] whose <s>sādhya</s>-absence is ascertained by another means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is called <s>bādhita</s> (contradicted). For example: 'fire is non-hot, because of being a substance.' Here, non-hotness is the <s>sādhya</s>; its absence, namely hotness, is apprehended by tactile perception — thus it is contradicted.

children.text:
yasya sādhyābhāvaḥ
pramāṇāntareṇa niścitaḥ saḥ bādhitaḥ/ yathā vahniḥ anuṣṇaḥ
padārthatvāt/ atra anuṣṇatvaṃ sādhyam, tadabhāva uṣṇatvaṃ tvācapratyakṣeṇa
gṛhyata iti bodhyam/ vyākhyātamanumānam/
children.translated_text: That [inferential mark] whose <s>sādhya</s>-absence is ascertained by another <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is <s>bādhita</s> (contradicted). For example: 'fire is non-hot, because of being a substance (<s>padārthatva</s>).' Here, non-hotness is the <s>sādhya</s>; its absence, namely hotness, is apprehended by tactile perception (<s>tvācapratyakṣa</s>) — this should be understood. Thus <s>anumāna</s> (inference) has been explained.

children.text:
iti tarkasaṅgrahe
anumānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus concludes the chapter on <s>anumāna</s> (inference) in the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>.

children.text:
1. kevalasādhyavyāpaka
iti/ bahirindrayajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ yatra yatra ghaṭādau tatra
udbhūtarūpavattvasattvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. '<s>upādhi</s> pervading the <s>sādhya</s> alone': Wherever there is perceptibility produced by external sense-organs — in pots and so forth — there the property of possessing manifest color (<s>udbhūtarūpavattva</s>) is present. This is the purport.

children.text:
2. tadaiva pakṣadharmeti/
yatra yatra pratyakṣaviṣayatvam ātmanyapi, tatrodbhūtarūpābhāvāt
udbhūtarūpasya kevalasādhyavyāpakatvaṃ na sambhavati/ ataḥ
bahirdravyatvarūpapakṣadharmaviśiṣṭapratyakṣaviṣayatvarūpasādhyavyāpakatvamapādheḥ
udbhūtarūpasyopapādanīyamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 2. 'Then alone [it pervades the sādhya] as qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s>': Wherever there is perceptibility — including in the self (<s>ātman</s>) — there, since manifest color is absent, the property of <s>udbhūtarūpa</s> (manifest color) pervading the <s>sādhya</s> alone is not possible. Therefore, the <s>upādhi</s>, namely <s>udbhūtarūpa</s>, must be established as pervading the <s>sādhya</s> — perceptibility — as qualified by the <s>pakṣadharma</s>, namely being an external substance (<s>bahirdravyatva</s>). This is the purport.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
bādhitasya
lakṣaṇamāha - yasyeti/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>bādhita</s> (the contradicted [inferential mark]): 'that whose...'

children.text: doṣāṇāmanumitipratibandhakatvaprakāraśodhanam
children.translated_text: Examination of the manner in which the defects (<s>doṣa</s>) obstruct inference (<s>anumiti</s>)

children.text:
atra bādhasya
grāhyābhāvaniścayatvena, satpratipakṣasya virodhijñānasāmagrītvena
sākṣādanumitipratibandhakatvam/ itareṣāṃ tu
parāmarśapratibandhakatvam/ tatrāpi sādhāraṇasyāvyabhicārābhāvarūpatayā,
viruddhasya sāmānādhikaraṇyābhāvatayā
children.translated_text: Here, <s>bādha</s> (contradiction), being the ascertainment of the absence of the provable, and <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (counter-argument), being the means for generating cognition of opposition, directly obstruct inference (<s>anumiti</s>). The remaining [defects], however, obstruct the inferential consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>). Among those, <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (the common [fallacy]), being the absence of non-deviation (<s>avyabhicāra</s>),and <s>viruddha</s> (the contradictory [fallacy]), being the absence of co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>),

children.text:
vyāpyatvāsiddhasya
viśiṣṭavyāptyabhāvatayā, asādhāraṇānupasaṃhāriṇoḥ
vyāptisaṃśayādhāyakatvena vyāptijñānapratibandhakatvam/
āchayāsiddhisvarūpāsiddhyoḥ pakṣadharmatājñānapratibandhakatvam/
upādhistu vyabhicārajñānadvārā vyāptijñānapratibandhakaḥ/ siddhasādhanaṃ tu
pakṣatāvighaṭakatayā āśrayāsiddhāvantarbhavatīti prāñcaḥ/
nigrahasthānāntaramiti navīnāḥ/
children.translated_text: and <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> (the unestablished-as-pervaded), being the absence of qualified pervasion — [these three] obstruct the cognition of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) by generating doubt about pervasion. <s>Āśrayāsiddhi</s> (unestablished substratum) and <s>svarūpāsiddhi</s> (unestablished-in-nature) obstruct the cognition of the <s>hetu</s>'s presence in the <s>pakṣa</s> (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>-knowledge). <s>Upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) obstructs the cognition of pervasion through [generating] the cognition of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). As for <s>siddhasādhana</s> (the already-established), the earlier logicians [hold that] it is subsumed under <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s> by vitiating the <s>pakṣatā</s> (locus-hood). The later logicians [hold that] it is a separate ground for defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>).

children.text:
iti
dīpikāyāmanumānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus concludes the chapter on <s>anumāna</s> (inference) in the <s>Dīpikā</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: bādhasya
sādhyābhāvavattāniścayasya/
children.translated_text: [It means] the ascertainment of the [<s>pakṣa</s>] possessing the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>.
Regarding <s>bādha</s> (contradiction) —

children.text:
grāhyābhāvaniścayatveneti/
anumitipratibandhakatvamityanenānvayi/ virodhijñānasāmagrītveneti/
idaṃ prācīnamate/ vastutastu virodhiparāmarśasya
sādhyābhāvavyāpyavattaniścayatvenaiva pratibandhakatvaṃ lāghavāditi
dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: 'Being the ascertainment of the absence of the provable': this is connected with [the statement that it] obstructs inference (<s>anumiti</s>). 'Being the means for generating cognition of opposition': this is according to the earlier view. In reality, the obstruction is due to the opposing inferential consideration (<s>virodhiparāmarśa</s>) being itself the ascertainment of the <s>pakṣa</s> possessing what is pervaded by the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> — this should be noted, as it is more parsimonious (<s>lāghava</s>).

children.text:
itareṣām -
vyabhicārādigrahāṇām/ tatrāpi - vyabhicārādigraheṣvapi/
sādhāraṇasyeti/ bhāvapradhānanirdeśatayā sādhāraṇyasyetyarthaḥ/
avyabhicārābhāvarūpatayā/ tadgrahasyeti śeṣaḥ/
vyāptijñānapratibandhakatvamityanenānvayaḥ/ evamagre 'pi/ hetau
sādhyābhāvavadvṛttitvasyeva sādhyatāvacchedake
hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasyāpi
vyabhicāratayā tadgrahasya
hetusamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakatvābhāvarūpo
yo 'vyabhicāraḥ tadgrahapratibandhakateti bhāvaḥ/ hetau
sādhyābhāvavadvṛttitvaprakārakagrahasya vyāptigrahapratibandhakatvaṃ tu
maṇimantrādinyāyena viśiṣṭavyāptyabhāvatayā -
hetuvyāpakatāvacchedakasādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnasāmānādhikaraṇyābhāvarūpatayā/
vyāptisaṃśayādhāyakatveneti/
children.translated_text: Of the others — of the cognitions of <s>vyabhicāra</s> (deviation) and the rest. 'Even there' — even in the cognitions of <s>vyabhicāra</s> and the rest. 'Of the common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>)' — since the expression is in the abstract form, the meaning is 'of commonality (<s>sādhāraṇya</s>),' i.e., having the form of the absence of non-deviation (<s>avyabhicāra</s>). 'Of the cognition of that' is to be supplied. The syntactic connection is with 'being an obstructor of <s>vyāpti</s>-cognition (<s>vyāptijñānapratibandhakatva</s>).' The same applies hereafter as well. Since in the probans, not only the property of occurring in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), but also the property of delimiting the counter-positiveness of an absolute absence co-located with the probans, is a form of <s>vyabhicāra</s>, the cognition of that — the cognition of the non-deviation which has the form of the absence of the property of delimiting the counter-positiveness of an absolute absence co-located with the probans — is an obstructor. This is the purport. However, the obstruction of <s>vyāpti</s>-cognition by a cognition whose qualifier is the property of occurring in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> in the probans operates by the principle of gems-and-mantras (<s>maṇimantrādinyāya</s>), through the absence of qualified <s>vyāpti</s> — i.e., having the form of the absence of co-location with the <s>sādhya</s> delimited by the delimitor of <s>sādhya</s>-hood and the delimitor of the pervasiveness of the probans — and thus by generating doubt about <s>vyāpti</s>.

children.text:
hetāvasādhāraṇyādijñānadaśāyāṃ hetusādhyayoḥ
sāmānādhikaraṇyaniścayāsaṃbhavena pakṣāntarbhāvena ca
sādhyasaṃśayasattvena vyāptisaṃśayasambhavāt na vyāptinirṇaya iti
prācīnamatamabhipretyedam/ pakṣadharmatājñānapratibandhakatvamiti/ pakṣe
pakṣatāvacchedakavirahasya hetuvirahasya ca niścayadaśāyāṃ hetau
pakṣatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭapakṣavṛttitvagrahāsaṃbhavāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: At the stage of cognition of non-exclusiveness (<s>asādhāraṇya</s>) and the like in the probans, since the ascertainment of co-location of the probans and <s>sādhya</s> is impossible, and since — the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) being included — doubt about the <s>sādhya</s> persists, doubt about <s>vyāpti</s> is possible, and hence there is no determination of <s>vyāpti</s> — this is stated with the intention of the view of the ancient logicians. 'Being an obstructor of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (the property of being a property of the thesis-locus) cognition' — at the stage of ascertaining the absence of the delimitor of <s>pakṣa</s>-hood and the absence of the probans in the <s>pakṣa</s>, the cognition of the probans as residing in the <s>pakṣa</s> qualified by the delimitor of <s>pakṣa</s>-hood is impossible. This is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
pañcatvoktirasaṅgatā, hetau upādhigrahadaśāyāmapi
vyāptiniścayāsaṃbhavena upādhijñānasya vyāptiniścayapratibandhakatāyā
avaśyaṃ vaktavyatayā upādherapi hetvābhāsalakṣaṇākrāntatvādata āha -
upādhistviti/ vyabhicārajñānadvāreti/ tathā ca hetvābhāsalakṣaṇe
sākṣādanumititatkaraṇānyatarapratibandhakatvasyaiva niveśanīyatayā
paramukhanirīkṣakasyopādherna hetvābhāsatvamiti bhāvaḥ/ nanu tathāpi
siddhisattve 'numityanudayāt tadviṣayasya sādhyavatpakṣasyāpi
hetvābhāsatvamāvaśyakamityāśaṅkāṃ jarannaiyāyikānāṃ

children.translated_text: Now, the statement that there are [only] five is incongruous, for at the stage of cognizing an <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) in the probans also, since the ascertainment of <s>vyāpti</s> is impossible due to the <s>vyabhicāra</s>-determination, the obstruction of <s>vyāpti</s>-ascertainment by <s>upādhi</s>-cognition must necessarily be stated, and hence the <s>upādhi</s> too falls under the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reason) — to this he says: 'The <s>upādhi</s>, however.' 'Through the door of <s>vyabhicāra</s>-cognition' — and thus, since in the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s>, only the property of directly obstructing inference or any one of its instruments is to be included, the <s>upādhi</s>, which operates by looking at something else, is not a <s>hetvābhāsa</s>. This is the purport. Now, even so, since when proof (<s>siddhi</s>) is present, inference does not arise, the <s>pakṣa</s> possessing the <s>sādhya</s> which is the object of that proof should also necessarily be a <s>hetvābhāsa</s> — anticipating this doubt, he resolves it by adopting the view of the ancient <s>Naiyāyikas</s> through a welcome consequence — 'The <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already established), however.' 'By destroying <s>pakṣa</s>-hood' — in their view, since <s>pakṣa</s>-hood has the form of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s>, the destruction of it means that the ascertainment of the <s>sādhya</s> remains intact. This is the purport. 'Is included' — and thus there is no conflict with the enumeration. This is the purport. Considering that the view presented is too loose, he says: 'The objection (<s>nigraha</s>).' And one should not say: how can there be <s>hetvābhāsa</s>-hood of the object of proof that obstructs inference in the established doctrine? Because when the <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> (desire to prove) is stimulated by the obstruction of proof, there is no obstruction in the case of proof accompanied only by <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>, and hence the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> stated does not apply to its object. The further details should be investigated by those skilled in the cleverness of rigorous logical analysis in our <s>Abhinavadīdhiti</s> commentary.

children.translated_text: 'By being an ascertainment of the absence of what is to be cognized' — the meaning is: by being an ascertainment whose qualifier is the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> which is to be cognized through inference. That is to say, it obstructs the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>-possessing [<s>pakṣa</s>] by producing the ascertainment of the <s>sādhya</s>-absence-possessing [<s>pakṣa</s>]. Of the <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (legitimate counter-probans) — of the cognition 'the <s>pakṣa</s> possesses a counter-probans pervaded by the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>.' 'By being the assemblage of cognition opposed [to it]' — by being the producer of the cognition of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, which is opposed to the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>-possessing [<s>pakṣa</s>]. And thus, the <s>satpratipakṣa</s>-cognition generates the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>-absence-possessing [<s>pakṣa</s>], and that obstructs the inference of the <s>sādhya</s> — in this way, the <s>satpratipakṣa</s> obstructs inference through the production of a cognition that obstructs inference. [This is according to] the ancient logicians. The modern logicians, however, [say that] the <s>satpratipakṣa</s>-cognition of the form 'the <s>pakṣa</s> possesses a counter-probans pervaded by the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>' obstructs inference in the manner that 'the cognition of possessing what is pervaded by the absence [of the <s>sādhya</s>] is an obstructor of the cognition of possessing [the <s>sādhya</s>],' and does not obstruct through the production of a cognition that obstructs inference; they say this because direct obstruction is possible, and [the alternative] involves the defect of unnecessarily postulating additional steps.

children.translated_text: Now, the statement that there are only five <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons) is improper, for at the stage of cognizing an <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) in the probans, since the ascertainment of <s>vyāpti</s> is absent due to the determination of <s>vyabhicāra</s>, the <s>upādhi</s> also falls under the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> by being the object of a cognition that obstructs <s>vyāpti</s>-ascertainment which is an instrument of inference, and hence one should say there are six <s>hetvābhāsas</s> — he raises this objection: 'Now, the statement of five-ness is improper.' [In reply:] only that whose object is a cognition that directly obstructs either inference or its instrument, the <s>parāmarśa</s>, is a <s>hetvābhāsa</s>. But the <s>upādhi</s>-cognition obstructs the <s>parāmarśa</s> only through the door of producing <s>vyabhicāra</s>-cognition, not directly — hence it is not a <s>hetvābhāsa</s>. Therefore there is no contradiction with the statement of five-ness.

children.translated_text: He states this — 'And thus, in the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s>.' The word 'directly' (<s>sākṣāt</s>) is connected with the obstruction. 'Of one that looks at something else (<s>paramukhanirīkṣaka</s>)' — the meaning is: of one that looks toward the <s>vyabhicāra</s>-cognition which obstructs the <s>parāmarśa</s>. By this, the absence of direct obstruction by <s>upādhi</s>-cognition is indicated. Now, just as in 'the lake possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, <s>bādha</s> (sublation), which is the lake-possessing-the-absence-of-fire, has <s>hetvābhāsa</s>-hood by being the object of the cognition 'the lake possesses the absence of fire' which obstructs the inference 'the lake possesses fire'; similarly, in 'the mountain possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, at the stage of the ascertainment of the <s>sādhya</s> 'the mountain possesses fire,' since doubt about whether the mountain possesses fire does not arise, and since due to the absence of <s>pakṣa</s>-hood — which has the form of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s> — the inference 'the mountain possesses fire' does not arise, the mountain possessing fire, which is the object of the <s>siddhi</s> (established proof) that obstructs inference, should also be a <s>hetvābhāsa</s>, since it falls under the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> — he raises this objection: 'Now, even so.'

children.translated_text: 'On that view' and so forth. And accordingly, on the ancient view, since <s>pakṣatā</s> has the form of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), and since the subject possessing the <s>sādhya</s> is the content of a cognition that obstructs <s>pakṣatā</s> which generates inference — it falls within the definition of a fallacious reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>); hence it is indeed accepted that the subject possessing the <s>sādhya</s> has the status of a fallacious reason. Nor should it be said that this contradicts the fivefold classification [of fallacious reasons] — because it is subsumed under <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s> (unestablishedness of the locus). How is it subsumed? — Thus: <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s> is twofold — non-establishment of the nature of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), and non-establishment of subject-hood (<s>pakṣatva</s>). In the latter — non-establishment of subject-hood — <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already proven) is subsumed. As stated in the <s>Kusumāñjali</s>: 'The intermediate one too is twofold: through non-cognition of the nature of the locus, and through non-cognition of the qualification of subject-hood. The latter is designated as <s>siddhasādhana</s> — because at the stage of [establishing] pervasion, subject-hood is irrevocably disrupted.' 'The view shown is too loose' — since <s>pakṣatā</s>, being a real entity, has separate causality, even when establishment obstructs it, in the case of <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already proven), there is neither the disruption of the reflective judgment that is the instrument of inference, nor the disruption of inference itself; hence <s>siddhasādhana</s> does not have the status of a fallacious reason. Due to the absence of the cause in the form of <s>pakṣatā</s>, the inference merely does not arise. Therefore, in the case of <s>siddhasādhana</s>, a fallacious reason is not generated; rather, there is merely the defeat of the debater — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu navīnamate 'pi
sādhyaniścayadaśāyāmanumityanudayena maṇimantrādinyāyena
siddheranumitipratibandhakatvaṃ vācyam/ tathā
cānumitipratibandhakasiddhiviṣayasya sādhyavatpakṣasya kuto na
hetvābhāsatvamiti śaṅkate - na ca
children.translated_text: Now, even on the new view, since inference does not arise at the stage of the ascertainment of the <s>sādhya</s>, it should be said — by the maxim of the gem and the mantra — that establishment has the status of an obstructor of inference. And accordingly, why would the subject possessing the <s>sādhya</s>, which is the content of [a cognition that obstructs] inference, not have the status of a fallacious reason? — he raises this doubt: 'Nor'

children.text:
siddhānta iti/
yatsattve niyamena yannotpadyate, yadabhāve ca yadutpadyate tasyaiva
pratibandhakatvam/ siddhisattve 'pi sā siddhiryadi siṣādhayiṣāsahitā
bhavati tadā anumityutpattyā siddhernānumitipratibandhakatvam/
ato 'numitipratibandhakajñānaviṣayatvarūpaṃ hetvābhāsalakṣaṇaṃ
sādhyavatpakṣe nāstīti samādhatte-siṣādhayiṣāyā ityādinā/
nanvevamapi siṣādhayiṣāvirahaviśiṣṭāyāḥ
siddheranumitipratibandhakatayā tadviṣayasyahetvābhāsatvaṃ
durvāramityata āha - adhikamiti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - pratyakṣitaviṣaye 'pi
saṃnikarṣe sati dhārāvāhikapratyakṣasya, pratītārthakaśabdaśravaṇe 'pi
punarbodhasya ca saṃmatatvāt tadvadeva siddhiviṣayasya
parāmarśasattve 'numityutpattau na saṃmatatvāt tadvadeva siddhiviṣayasya
parāmarśasattve 'numityutpattau na kiñcidbādhakam/ ataḥ
siddhernānumitiṃ prati pratibandhakatvam/ evaṃ
sādhyasaṃśayavirahe 'pyanumityutpattyā na sādhyasaṃśayarūpapakṣatā
anumitihetuḥ/ tathā ca siddheḥ anumitiṃ prati vā anumitikāraṇaṃ
prati vā pratibandhakatvābhāvāt na siddhiviṣayasya sādhyavatpakṣasya
hetvābhāsalakṣaṇākrāntateti/
children.translated_text: 'is the established position' and so forth.
