That in whose presence something invariably does not arise, and in whose absence it arises — only that has the status of an obstructor. Even when establishment is present, if that establishment is accompanied by the desire to establish (<s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>), then inference arises; hence establishment does not have the status of obstructing inference. Therefore, the definition of a fallacious reason in the form of being the content of a cognition that obstructs inference is not present in the subject possessing the <s>sādhya</s> — he resolves with 'of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>' and so forth. Now, even so, since establishment qualified by the absence of the desire to establish has the status of obstructing inference, the fallacious-reason-hood of its content is unavoidable — anticipating this, he says: 'more' and so forth. The intent is as follows: since continuous perceptual cognition of an already perceived object when the sense-contact continues is accepted, and since renewed verbal cognition upon hearing a word whose meaning is already known is also accepted, in the same way, when there is a reflective judgment whose content is the object of establishment, there is nothing obstructing the arising of inference. Therefore, establishment does not have the status of obstructing inference. Similarly, since inference arises even in the absence of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s>, <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s> is not a cause of inference. And accordingly, since establishment does not have the status of obstructing either inference or the cause of inference, the subject possessing the <s>sādhya</s> — the content of establishment — is not encompassed by the definition of a fallacious reason.

children.text:
iti
tarkasaṅgrahadīpikāprakāśikāvyākhyāyāṃ bālapriyāyāṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bālapriyā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha-dīpikā-prakāśikā</s>,

children.text: anumānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: [ends] the chapter on inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

children.text: upamānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Chapter on Comparison (<s>Upamāna</s>)

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: AnTs_58 upamitikaraṇam upamānam / saṃjñāsaṃjñisaṃbandhajñānam upamitiḥ / tatkaraṇaṃ sādṛśyajñānam / atideśavākyārthasmaraṇam avāntaravyāpāraḥ / tathā hi kaś cid gavayaśabdārtham ajānan kutaś cid āraṇyakapuruṣād gosadṛśo gavaya iti śrutvā vanaṃ gato vākyārthaṃ smaran gosadṛṣaṃ piṇḍaṃ paśyati / tadanantaram asau gavayaśabdavācya ity upamitir utpadyte //
children.translated_text: The instrument of comparative cognition (<s>upamiti</s>) is comparison (<s>upamāna</s>). Comparative cognition (<s>upamiti</s>) is the knowledge of the relation between a name and its referent. The instrument of that is the knowledge of similarity. The recollection of the meaning of the statement of comparison is the intermediate operation (<s>avāntaravyāpāra</s>). For example: someone, not knowing the meaning of the word <s>gavaya</s> (wild cow), having heard from a forest-dweller 'a <s>gavaya</s> is similar to a cow,' goes to the forest, and while recollecting the meaning of the statement, sees an animal similar to a cow. Thereupon, the comparative cognition arises: 'this is what is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>.'

children.text:
upamitikaraṇamupamānam/ saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandhajñānamupamitiḥ/
tatkaraṇaṃ sādṛśyajñānam/ tathā hi -kaścit gavayaśabdārthamajānan
kutaścit āraṇyakapuruṣāt gosadṛśo gavaya iti śrutvā vanaṃ
gataḥ vākyārthaṃ smaran gosadṛśaṃ piṇḍaṃ paśyati/ tadanantaraṃ ayaṃ
gavayapadavācyaḥ ityupamitirutpadyate/ vyākhyātamupamānam/
children.translated_text: The instrument of comparative cognition (<s>upamiti</s>) is comparison (<s>upamāna</s>). The knowledge of the relation between a name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and its referent (<s>saṃjñin</s>) is <s>upamiti</s>. The instrument of that is the knowledge of similarity. For example: someone, not knowing the meaning of the word <s>gavaya</s>, having heard from a forest-dweller 'a <s>gavaya</s> is similar to a cow,' goes to the forest; while recollecting the meaning of the statement, he sees an animal similar to a cow. Thereupon, the comparative cognition arises: 'this is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>.' Comparison has been explained.

children.text:
iti tarkasaṅgrahe
upamānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>, the chapter on comparison (<s>upamāna</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
upamānaṃ lakṣayati -
upamitikaraṇamiti/
children.translated_text: He defines comparison: 'the instrument of <s>upamiti</s>' and so forth.

children.text:
iti dīpikāyāṃ
upamānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, the chapter on comparison.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
upamānaṃ
lakṣayatīti/ avasarasaṅgatyā upamānaṃ nirūpayatītyarthaḥ/
upamitisvarūpaṃ vyutpādayati - mūle saṃjñeti/ saṃjñā - gavayapadam/
saṃjñī - gavayaḥ, tayoḥ sambandhaḥ śaktiḥ, tajjñānamityarthaḥ/ lakṣaṇaṃ tu
upaminomi ityanuvyavasāyagamyopamititvameva/ vākyārthaṃ smaran
gosadṛśaṃ piṇḍaṃ paśyatīti/ etane smaraṇaṃ sādṛśyadarśanajanyam
udbodhakāntarajanyaṃ vā/ ubhayamapi sādṛśyadarśanasahakāni, na tu
sādṛśyadarśanajanyameva smaraṇaṃ sahakārīti sūcitam/
children.translated_text: 'He defines comparison' — the meaning is: he determines comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) by contextual relevance. He etymologically derives the nature of <s>upamiti</s>: 'in the root text, <s>saṃjñā</s>' and so forth. <s>Saṃjñā</s> (name) is the word <s>gavaya</s>. <s>Saṃjñin</s> (referent) is the <s>gavaya</s> animal. The relation between them is the denotative power (<s>śakti</s>). The knowledge of that — this is the meaning. The definition, however, is the <s>upamiti</s>-hood itself, which is apprehensible through the introspective cognition 'I compare' (<s>upaminomi</s>). 'While recollecting the meaning of the statement, he sees an animal similar to a cow' — by this it is indicated that the recollection is either produced by the perception of similarity or produced by some other stimulus. Both are auxiliary to the perception of similarity; the recollection that is auxiliary is not necessarily only that which is produced by the perception of similarity — this is what is indicated.

children.text:
prāñcastu - 'vākyārthaṃ
smaran' ityatra vartamānasāmīpye pratyayaḥ/ vākyārthaṃ
smariṣyannityarthaḥ/ evaṃ ca vākyārthasmaraṇasya
sādṛśyadarśanajanyatālābhena vyāpāratālābhaḥ --- ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: The ancients, however, [say]: in 'while recollecting the meaning of the statement,' the suffix [of the present participle] has the meaning of proximity to the present. The meaning is: 'being about to recollect.' And accordingly, since the recollection of the meaning of the statement is produced by the perception of similarity, it obtains the status of an operation — thus they say.

children.text:
tadanantaramityādi/
sādṛśyadarśanānantaram 'gavayo gavayapadavācya' ityākārikā
gavayatvarūpalaghudharmadharmitāvacchedakakopamitirutpadyata ityarthaḥ/
idamupalakṣaṇam - vaidharmyadarśanenāpyupamitiriti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: 'Thereupon' and so forth. After the perception of similarity, the <s>upamiti</s> of the form '<s>gavaya</s> is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>' arises, having <s>gavayatva</s> (gavaya-hood) — a lighter property — as the delimiting property of the property-bearer — this is the meaning. This is an indication: it should be noted that <s>upamiti</s> also arises through the perception of dissimilarity.

children.text:
vaiśeṣikāstu -
padavācyatvavyāpyasādṛśyādiparāmarśāt padavācyatvasyānumitireva,
ato nopamānaṃ pramāṇāntaram - ityāhuḥ/
taccintyam-vyāptijñānamantareṇāpi
padavācyatvapramiteranubhavaddhitvāt/ ityantra vistaraḥ/
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, however, [say]: from the reflective judgment of similarity and the like pervaded by being-denotable-by-a-word, the knowledge of being-denotable-by-a-word is itself an inference; hence comparison is not a separate means of valid knowledge — thus they say. This is to be considered — because valid cognition of being-denotable-by-a-word is experienced even without knowledge of pervasion. More on this is [discussed] elsewhere.

children.text:
iti
prakāśikāyām upamānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, the chapter on comparison.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
avasarasaṅgatyeti/
pratibandhakajijñāsānivṛttau avaśyavaktavyatvamavasaraḥ/ anumānasya
bahuvādisaṃmatatvena nirasanīyālpavādivipratipattikatayā
prathamamanumāna eva vyutpitsorjijñāsā jāyate, na tūpamāne,
children.translated_text: 'By contextual relevance' — contextual relevance is the necessity of being stated when the student's doubt, which is an obstructor, has been removed. Since inference, being accepted by the majority of thinkers, has the character of having its opposition from the minority to be refuted, the student who wishes to learn first develops the desire to know inference, not comparison,

children.text:
tasyālpavādisaṃmatatvena
nirasanīyabahuvādivipratipattikatvāt/ tathā cānumāne
prathamamutpannāyāḥ 1pratibandhakībhūtaśiṣyajijñāsāyāḥ tannirūpaṇena
nivṛttau avaśyavaktavyatvarūpāvasarasaṃgatyā anumānānantaraṃ
upamānanirūpaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/ saṃjñā - vācakaḥ śabdaḥ, gavayādipadam/
saṃjñī - vācyor'thaḥ gavayādiḥ/ tayoḥ yaḥ sambandhaḥ śaktyākhyaḥ
tadviṣayakajñānamupamiti/ 'gavayo gavayapadavācyaḥ' ityādyākārakaṃ
śaktijñānamupamitiriti yāvat/ sādṛśyajñānakaraṇakaṃ
jñānamupamitiriti granthāntareṣu kathanāt sādṛśyajñānakaraṇakatvasya
upamitilakṣaṇatvasambhave 'pi tadapekṣayā lāghavāt upamititvajātimattvaṃ
lakṣaṇamucitamityabhipretyāha - lakṣaṇaṃ tviti/
children.translated_text: since comparison, being accepted by the minority, has the character of having its opposition from the majority to be refuted. And accordingly, when the student's doubt that has become an obstructor, having first arisen regarding inference, is removed by its determination, the determination of comparison comes after inference by the contextual relevance of necessity — this is the purport. <s>Saṃjñā</s> (name) is the denoting word — the word <s>gavaya</s> and the like. <s>Saṃjñin</s> (referent) is the denoted meaning — <s>gavaya</s> and the like. The relation between them that is called <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) — the knowledge having that as its content is <s>upamiti</s>. That is: the knowledge of denotative power of the form '<s>gavaya</s> is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>' is <s>upamiti</s>. Since in other texts it is stated that <s>upamiti</s> is a cognition whose instrument is the knowledge of similarity, even though being-instrumentality-of-similarity-knowledge could serve as the definition of <s>upamiti</s>, since possessing the universal <s>upamititva</s> (comparison-hood) is lighter than that — intending that it is the more appropriate definition, he says: 'the definition, however' and so forth.

children.text:
1. pratibandhakībhūteti/
upamānanirūpaṇa iti śeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Which is an obstructor' — the remainder is: of the determination of comparison.

children.text:
nanu 'vākyārthaṃ smaran
gosadṛśaṃ piṇḍaṃ paśyati' iti mūlāt ādau
1atideśavākyārthasmaraṇaṃ tataḥ 2gosadṛśapiṇḍadarśanamiti kramo
labhyate, tadayuktam/ gosadṛśapiṇḍadarśanānantarameva
atideśavākyārthasmaraṇāt ityāśaṅkyāha - eteneti/
vartamānasāmīpya iti/ 'vartamānasāmīpye vartamānavadvā'
ityanuśāsanena bhaviṣyati laṭi śatṛpratyayena smaranniti rūpam/
children.translated_text: Now, from the root text 'while recollecting the meaning of the statement, he sees an animal similar to a cow,' one obtains the sequence: first the recollection of the meaning of the statement of comparison, then the seeing of the animal similar to a cow. That is incorrect — because the recollection of the meaning of the statement of comparison occurs only after seeing the animal similar to a cow — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'by this' and so forth. 'Proximity to the present' — by the grammatical rule 'when there is proximity to the present, [the present tense is used] as if it were the present,' the present participle suffix produces the form 'recollecting' (<s>smaran</s>).

children.text:
smaran ityasya
smariṣyan ityarthaḥ/ evaṃ cādau sādṛśyaviśiṣṭagavayapiṇḍadarśanaṃ
tata atideśavākyārthasmaraṇaṃ tata upamitiriti kramasyaiva mūlato
lābhāt vākyārthasmaraṇavyāpārakasādṛśyadarśanasya upamitikaraṇatvaṃ
yujyata iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning of 'recollecting' is 'about to recollect.' And accordingly, the sequence obtained from the root text is: first the seeing of the <s>gavaya</s> animal qualified by similarity, then the recollection of the meaning of the statement of comparison, then <s>upamiti</s>. Since this sequence alone is obtained from the root text, the instrumentality of the perception of similarity — which operates through the recollection of the meaning of the statement — for <s>upamiti</s> is justified — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu 'gosadṛśo
gavayapadavācyaḥ' ityākārikaivopamitirastu/ na ceṣṭāpattiḥ,
gavayatvasya gavayapadaśakyatāvacchedakatvāsiddhyāpatteratyatrāha -
gavayo gavayapadavācya ityākāriketi/ upamiteḥ 'gosadṛśo
gavayapadavācyaḥ' ityākārakatve gosādṛśyaṃ dharmitāvacchedakaṃ
vācyam/ gosādṛśyaṃ gavayatvāpekṣayā guru iti jñānadaśāyāṃ
gosādṛśyāvacchedena gavayapadavācyatvajñānaṃ bhavituṃ nārhatīti
'gavayo gavayapadavācyaḥ' ityākārakataivopamiteryukteti bhāvaḥ/
idamupalakṣaṇam/ tatprakārakaśābdabodhe tadavacchedena śaktijñānasya
hetutvāt gavayapadāt gosādṛśyaprakāraka eva gavayabodhaḥ syāt, na
tu gavayatvaprakārakaḥ/ anubhūyate ca gavayapadāt gavayatvaprakāraka eva
śābdabodhaḥ/ ataḥ gavayatvāvacchedena gavayapadavācyatvāvagāhī 'gavayo
gavayapadavācya' iti jñānameva upamitirityapi bodhyam/
vaidharmyadarśanenāpyupamitiriti/ yatra kenacit govidharmā aśva
ityuktaṃ śrutavān kaścit kadācit kutracit govidhadharmāṇaṃ
aśvaṃ paśyati tatra vaidharmyaviśiṣṭapiṇḍadarśanaṃ karaṇam, govidharmā aśva
children.translated_text: Now, let the <s>upamiti</s> have the form 'what is similar to a cow is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>.' Nor is there the undesired consequence — because [that form would entail] the non-establishment of <s>gavayatva</s> (gavaya-hood) as the delimiting property of the denotative capacity of the word <s>gavaya</s> — to this he says: '<s>gavaya</s> is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>, of such a form' and so forth. If the <s>upamiti</s> had the form 'what is similar to a cow is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>,' similarity-to-a-cow would have to be stated as the delimiting property of the property-bearer-hood. Similarity-to-a-cow is heavier than <s>gavayatva</s> (gavaya-hood); hence, at the cognitive level, the knowledge of being-denoted-by-the-word-<s>gavaya</s> delimited by similarity-to-a-cow is not appropriate. Therefore, it is appropriate that <s>upamiti</s> has the form '<s>gavaya</s> is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>' — this is the purport. This is an indication: since in the verbal cognition whose qualifier-mode is that [similarity], the knowledge of denotative power delimited by that [similarity] is a cause, from the word <s>gavaya</s>, the verbal cognition would have similarity-to-a-cow as its qualifier-mode, not <s>gavayatva</s>. But it is experienced that the verbal cognition from the word <s>gavaya</s> has <s>gavayatva</s> alone as its qualifier-mode. Therefore, the knowledge apprehending being-denoted-by-the-word-<s>gavaya</s> delimited by <s>gavayatva</s>, having the form '<s>gavaya</s> is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>,' is itself <s>upamiti</s> — this too should be understood. 'Through the perception of dissimilarity too, <s>upamiti</s> [arises]' — when someone has heard from someone 'a horse has dissimilarities from a cow' and at some time, somewhere, sees a horse having dissimilarities from a cow — there the perception of the animal qualified by dissimilarity is the instrument, 'a horse has dissimilarities from a cow'

children.text:
1. atideśavākyeti/
tadvadidamiti vākyamatideśavākyam/ prakṛte gosadṛśo gavaya iti
vākyam atideśavākyam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The statement of comparison' — a statement of the form 'this is like that' is a statement of comparison. In the present case, the statement 'a <s>gavaya</s> is similar to a cow' is the statement of comparison.

children.text:
2. gosadṛśapiṇḍeti/
piṇḍaśabdaḥ ākṛtiviśiṣṭavyaktiparaḥ/
gosadṛśākāragavayavyaktidarśanamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'An animal similar to a cow' — the word <s>piṇḍa</s> refers to an individual qualified by a specific form. The meaning is: the seeing of a <s>gavaya</s> individual having a cow-like appearance.

children.text:
ityatideśavākyārthasmaraṇaṃ vyāpāraḥ aśvo 'śvapadavācya iti
jñānamupamitiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: is the statement of comparison whose meaning is recollected — this is the operation; and 'the horse is denoted by the word horse' — this cognition is the <s>upamiti</s> — this is the purport.

children.text:
vaiśeṣikāstvityādi/
'gavayo gavayapadavācyaḥ, gosādṛśyāt, yo gavayapadavācyo na
bhavati nāsau gosadṛśaḥ, gosadṛśaścāyam, tasmāt gavayapadavācyaḥ'
ityunamānaprayogo 'tra vivakṣitaḥ/ tathā ca
gavayapadavācyatvavyāpyagosādṛśyavānayamiti parāmarśāt jāyamānā
gavayo gavayapadavācya iti pramā anumitireva na tadvilakṣaṇā/ ato
nopamānaṃ pramāṇāntaramiti vaiśeṣikāśayaḥ/ tanmataṃ nirākaroti -
vyāptijñānamantareṇāpīti/ anyatreti/
kusumāñjalyādigrantheṣvityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, however' and so forth. The inferential application intended here is: 'the <s>gavaya</s> is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>, because of similarity to a cow; whatever is not denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s> is not similar to a cow; and this is similar to a cow; therefore it is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>.' And accordingly, the valid cognition '<s>gavaya</s> is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>' that arises from the reflective judgment 'this possesses similarity-to-a-cow, which is pervaded by being-denoted-by-the-word-<s>gavaya</s>' is itself an inference, not something distinct from it. Therefore comparison is not a separate means of valid knowledge — this is the intent of the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>. He refutes their view: 'even without knowledge of pervasion' and so forth. 'Elsewhere' — the meaning is: in texts such as the <s>Kusumāñjali</s> and the like.

children.text:
iti
tarkasaṅgrahadīpikāprakāśikāvyākhyāyāṃ bālapriyāyāṃ
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Bālapriyā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha-dīpikā-prakāśikā</s>,

children.text: upamānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: [ends] the chapter on comparison (<s>upamāna</s>).

children.text: śabdaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Chapter on Verbal Testimony (<s>Śabda</s>)

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: śabdalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of Verbal Testimony (<s>Śabda</s>)

children.text: AnTs_59 āptavākyaṃ śabdaḥ / āptas tu yathārthavaktā / vākyaṃ padasamūhaḥ / yathā gām ānayeti / śaktaṃ padam / asmāt padād ayam artho boddhavya itīśvarasaṃketaḥ śaktiḥ //
children.translated_text: The statement of a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). A trustworthy person is one who speaks the truth. A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is a collection of words — for example, 'bring the cow.' A word (<s>pada</s>) is that which has denotative power (<s>śakti</s>). 'From this word, this meaning is to be understood' — such a convention established by God (<s>Īśvara</s>) is <s>śakti</s> (denotative power).

children.text:
āptavākyaṃ śabdaḥ/
āptastu yathārthavaktā/
children.translated_text: The statement of a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). A trustworthy person is one who speaks the truth.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
śabdaṃ lakṣayati -
āpteti/ āptaṃ lakṣayati - āptastviti/
children.translated_text: He defines verbal testimony: '<s>āpta</s>' and so forth. He defines a trustworthy person: 'a trustworthy person, however' and so forth.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
śabdaṃ lakṣayatīti/
upajīvyopajīvakatvasaṅgatyā śabdaṃ ni - payatītyarthaḥ/ atra
jñāyamānaśabdasya śabdapramāṇatayā śabde upamānopajīvakatvābhāvāt
upamitiśābdabodharūphalayoḥ saṅgatirbodhyā/ tathā hi -
śaktiparicchittirevopamitiḥ/ tasyāśca śābdabodhopajīvyatvena
phalayorupajīvyopajīvakatvasambhavaḥ/ tādṛśasaṅgateśca
phalaniṣṭhatve 'pi svāśrayakaraṇatvātmakaparamparāsambandhena
karaṇaniṣṭhatvāt karaṇayoranantarābhidhānaprayojakatvam/ śabdajñānasya
pramāṇatvāṅgīkartṛnavīnamate tu upamiteḥ śaktapadaviṣayakatvena
śabdapramāṇatayā tatra copamānajanyatvasyākṣatatayā svarūpayorapi
saṅgatiriti mantavyam/
children.translated_text: [He] defines <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony). The meaning is: by the connection of being the dependent and the depended-upon, [he] determines <s>śabda</s>. Here, since the <s>śabda</s> being cognized has the nature of <s>śabda-pramāṇa</s> (verbal testimony as a means of valid cognition), there is no dependence on <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) in <s>śabda</s> [itself]; therefore the connection should be understood between the results, namely <s>upamiti</s> (comparative cognition) and <s>śābdabodha</s> (verbal comprehension). For indeed, <s>upamiti</s> is precisely the ascertainment of <s>śakti</s> (denotative power). And since that [ascertainment of denotative power] is depended upon by <s>śābdabodha</s>, the dependent-depended-upon relation between the results is possible. And although such a connection resides in the results, because it resides in the instruments through the indirect relation of being the instrument-hood of its own locus, it serves as the reason for the sequential exposition of the instruments. However, according to the new view that accepts <s>śabdajñāna</s> (verbal cognition) as the <s>pramāṇa</s>, since <s>upamiti</s> has as its object a word possessing <s>śakti</s> and thus has the nature of <s>śabda-pramāṇa</s>, and since therein the property of being produced by <s>upamāna</s> is unimpaired, it should be considered that there is a connection between the two even in their intrinsic natures.

children.text:
mūle āptavākyaṃ śabda
iti/ śabda iti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ/ pramāṇaśabda iti tadarthaḥ/
āptavākyamiti lakṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: In the root text, '<s>āptavākya</s> (authoritative statement) is <s>śabda</s>.' '<s>Śabda</s>' is the indication of the definiendum. Its meaning is '<s>pramāṇa-śabda</s>' (verbal testimony as a means of valid cognition). '<s>Āptavākya</s>' is the definition.

children.text:
bhavati hi payasā
siñcatītyādiśabdaḥ āptoktavākyam/ na tu vahninā
siñcatītyādiśabdaḥ, taduccāraṇakartuḥ
yathārthavaktṛtvarūpāptatvābhāvāt/
prakṛtavākyārthagocarayathārthajñānajanyavākyaṃ pramāṇaśabda iti tu
niṣkarṣaḥ/ vākyaprayoge vākyārthañjñānasya hetutvāt lakṣaṇasaṅgatiḥ/
sphuṭametat śabdamaṇau/
children.translated_text: For instance, the statement 'he sprinkles with milk' and the like is a sentence uttered by an <s>āpta</s> (trustworthy person). But the statement 'he sprinkles with fire' and the like is not, because of the absence of the <s>āpta</s>-nature, which consists in being a veridical speaker, in the person who utters it. The conclusion, however, is that a sentence produced from veridical cognition whose object is the meaning of the sentence under consideration is <s>pramāṇa-śabda</s>. The connection of the definition [is established] because in the employment of a sentence, the cognition of sentence-meaning serves as the cause. This is clearly [explained] in the <s>Śabdamaṇi</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
upajīvyopajīvakatvasaṅgatyeti/ upamānam upajīvyaṃ
kāraṇam, śabdaḥ upajīvakaḥ kāryaḥ/ tathā ca śabdopamānayoḥ
kāryakāraṇabhāvasadbhāvāt kāryakāraṇabhāvarūpasaṅgatyā
upamānānantaraṃ śabdanirūpaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/
upajīvyopajīvakabhāvamevopapādayati - atretyādinā/
children.translated_text: 'By the connection of being the dependent and the depended-upon' — <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) is the depended-upon, i.e., the cause; <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is the dependent, i.e., the effect. And thus, since the cause-effect relation between <s>śabda</s> and <s>upamāna</s> actually exists, through the connection that has the form of a cause-effect relation, the determination of <s>śabda</s> after <s>upamāna</s> [is justified] — this is the purport. [The commentator] establishes precisely this dependent-depended-upon relation — with 'here' and so forth.

children.text:
ayaṃ
bhāvaḥ-pramāṇayorūpajīvyojīvakabhāvo 'tra durvacaḥ/ śabdapramāṇaṃ hi
jñāyamānaḥ vākyātmakaḥ śabdaḥ/ upamānapramāṇaṃ tu sādṛśyadarśanam/
tatkāryatvaṃ tu śabde nāstīti/ śabdopamānātmakapramāṇayoḥ
kāryakāraṇabhāvo na sambhavati/
śabdopamānajanyapramityorevātrakāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ/ śabdajanyāpramitiḥ
śābdabodhaḥ/ upamānajanyā pramitiḥ ayamasau gavayapadavācya
ityādyākārakaḥ śaktigrāhaḥ/ śaktigrahajanyatvaṃ ca śābdabodhe vartata
iti/ na ca kāryakāraṇabhāvātmakasaṅgateḥ pramitidvayaniṣṭhatve 'pi
pramāṇadvayaniṣṭhatvābhāvāt upamānapramāṇanirūpaṇānantaraṃ
śabdapramāṇanirūpaṇe tādṛśasaṅgaternopayoga iti vācyam/
upamitiśābdabodharūpapramitidvayaniṣṭhasya kāryakāraṇabhāvasya
svāśrayajanakatvasambandhena pramāṇaniṣṭhatvāt/ svaṃ - kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ,
svāśrayau upamitiśābdabodhau, tajjanakatvamupamānaśabdayoriti/ tathā
ca kāryakāraṇabhāvarūpasaṅgateḥ svāśrayajanakatvasambandheṃna
pramāṇaniṣṭhatvāt upamānānantaraṃ śabdanirūpaṇaṃ saṅgatamiti/ idaṃ
prācīnamatānusāreṇa/
children.translated_text: The purport is this: the dependent-depended-upon relation between the two <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) is difficult to state here. For <s>śabda-pramāṇa</s> is the cognized <s>śabda</s> consisting of a sentence. And <s>upamāna-pramāṇa</s> is the perception of similarity. The property of being an effect of that does not exist in <s>śabda</s>. Therefore, the cause-effect relation between the two <s>pramāṇas</s> in the form of <s>śabda</s> and <s>upamāna</s> is not possible. Rather, the cause-effect relation here is between the <s>pramitis</s> (resultant cognitions) produced by <s>śabda</s> and <s>upamāna</s>. The <s>pramiti</s> produced by <s>śabda</s> is <s>śābdabodha</s> (verbal comprehension). The <s>pramiti</s> produced by <s>upamāna</s> is the apprehension of <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) having the form 'this is what is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox)' and the like. And the property of being produced by the apprehension of <s>śakti</s> is present in <s>śābdabodha</s>. Nor should one say that since the connection in the form of a cause-effect relation, though residing in the pair of <s>pramitis</s>, does not reside in the pair of <s>pramāṇas</s>, such a connection is of no use in determining <s>śabda-pramāṇa</s> after <s>upamāna-pramāṇa</s> — because the cause-effect relation residing in the pair of <s>pramitis</s>, namely <s>upamiti</s> and <s>śābdabodha</s>, resides in the <s>pramāṇas</s> through the relation of being the producer of its own locus. 'Own' means the cause-effect relation; its loci are <s>upamiti</s> and <s>śābdabodha</s>; their producers are <s>upamāna</s> and <s>śabda</s> respectively. And thus, since the connection in the form of a cause-effect relation resides in the <s>pramāṇas</s> through the relation of being the producer of its own locus, the determination of <s>śabda</s> after <s>upamāna</s> is well-connected. This follows the old view.

children.text:
navīnamate tu
śabdajñānameva śabdapramāṇam/ upamitirapi gavayo gavayapadavācya
ityākārikā gavayadharmikā gavayapadavācyatvaprakārikā gavayapadaṃ
gavayavācakamityākārikā gavayapadadharmikā gavayavācakatvaprakārikā vā
pakṣaviṣayakatvāt śabdajñānarūpaiva/ sā ca
sādṛśyajñānarūpopamānapramāṇajanyā/ evaṃ ca
śabdapramāṇarūpaśabdajñānātmakopamiteḥ
sādṛśyajñānātmakopamānapramāṇajanyatvāt pramāṇayorapi
kāryakāraṇabhāvarūpā saṅgatirastīti/
children.translated_text: According to the new view, however, <s>śabdajñāna</s> (verbal cognition) itself is <s>śabda-pramāṇa</s>. <s>Upamiti</s> (comparative cognition) too, being of the form 'the <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is what is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>,' having <s>gavaya</s> as its qualificand and <s>gavaya</s>-word-denotability as its qualifier, or being of the form 'the word <s>gavaya</s> denotes <s>gavaya</s>,' having the word <s>gavaya</s> as its qualificand and <s>gavaya</s>-denotingness as its qualifier — since its content falls within the scope of a word possessing <s>śakti</s>, [<s>upamiti</s>] is itself of the nature of <s>śabdajñāna</s>. And that is produced by <s>upamāna-pramāṇa</s>, which has the nature of the cognition of similarity. Thus, since <s>upamiti</s>, which is of the nature of <s>śabdajñāna</s> and hence of the nature of <s>śabda-pramāṇa</s>, is produced by <s>upamāna-pramāṇa</s> which has the nature of the cognition of similarity, the connection in the form of a cause-effect relation exists even between the <s>pramāṇas</s> themselves.

children.text:
upamānopajīvakatvābhāvāditi/
upamānapramāṇajanyatvābhāvādityarthaḥ/ śaktiparicchittiriti/
śaktiviṣayakajñānamityarthaḥ/ tasyāśca - śaktiparicchitteśca/
śābdabodhopajīvyatvena - śābdabodhajanakatvena/
karaṇayoranantarābhidhānaprayojakatvamiti/ karaṇayoḥ pramāṇayoḥ yat
anantarābhidhānaṃ paurvāparyeṃṇābhidhānaṃ tatprayojakatvaṃ taddhetutvaṃ
saṃgaterityarthaḥ/ āptoktavākyamiti/ āptakartṛkoccāraṇaviṣayabhūtaṃ
vākyamityarthaḥ/ āptastu yathārthavakteti
children.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of dependence on <s>upamāna</s>' — the meaning is: because of the absence of being produced by <s>upamāna-pramāṇa</s>. 'The ascertainment of <s>śakti</s>' — the meaning is: cognition whose object is <s>śakti</s> (denotative power). 'And of that' — and of the ascertainment of <s>śakti</s>. 'By being depended upon by <s>śābdabodha</s>' — by being the producer of <s>śābdabodha</s>. 'The reason for the sequential exposition of the instruments' — of the instruments, i.e., of the <s>pramāṇas</s>, the sequential exposition, i.e., the exposition in a certain order — the meaning is that the connection is what occasions that. 'A sentence uttered by an <s>āpta</s>' — the meaning is: a sentence that is the object of utterance by an agent who is an <s>āpta</s>. And an <s>āpta</s> is one who speaks veridically —

children.text:
mūlāt
abādhitārthaviṣayakajñānajanakaśabdaprayogakartetyartho labhyate/
yathābhūto 'bādhitār'tho yathārthaḥ/ tasya vaktā iti vigrahāt/ vaktā
tadviṣayakajñānajanakaśabdaprayogakartā/ āptavākyaṃ śabda iti mūlācca
abādhitārthaviṣayakajñānajanakaśabdaprayogakartṛkoccāraṇaviṣayaśabdatvaṃ
śabdapramāṇasya lakṣaṇamiti pratīyate/ tadapekṣayā
children.translated_text: from the root text, the meaning obtained is: one who employs words that produce cognition whose object is an unsublated meaning. 'Unsublated meaning' means veridical meaning — that which is as it is. From the analysis 'speaker of that,' the speaker is one who employs words that produce cognition having that as its object. And from the root text '<s>āptavākya</s> is <s>śabda</s>,' the definition of <s>śabda-pramāṇa</s> is understood to be: being a word that is the object of utterance by one who employs words producing cognition whose object is an unsublated meaning. In comparison with that,

children.text:
lāghavāt
abādhitārthaviṣayakajñānajanyavākyatvameva pramāṇaśabdasya lakṣaṇaṃ
bhavitumarhatītyāśayenāha - prakṛtavākyārtheti/
children.translated_text: because of greater parsimony, the definition of <s>pramāṇa-śabda</s> should rather be: being a sentence produced from veridical cognition whose object is an unsublated meaning — with this intent [the commentator] says 'of the sentence-meaning under consideration' and so forth.

children.text:
'artha buddhvā
śabdaracanā' iti nyāyāt vaktṛniṣṭhena
vākyārthaviṣayakayathārthajñānenaiva vākyarūpaḥ śabdo jāyata iti
lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ tadāha - vākyaprayoga iti/ sphuṭametat
śabdamaṇāviti/ tattvacintāmaṇau śabdakhaṇḍe -
'prayogahetubhūtārthatattvajñānajanyaśabdaḥ pramāṇam' iti
gaṅgeśavākyamatrābhisaṃhitam/
children.translated_text: By the maxim 'having understood the meaning, one constructs the words,' the word in the form of a sentence is produced by the veridical cognition residing in the speaker whose object is the sentence-meaning — this is the coordination with the definition. [The commentator] states this: 'in the employment of a sentence' and so forth. 'This is clearly [explained] in the <s>Śabdamaṇi</s>' — the statement of <s>Gaṅgeśa</s> in the <s>Śabda</s> section of the <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s>, namely 'a word produced from cognition of the true nature of the meaning that is the cause of [its] employment is a <s>pramāṇa</s>,' is what is intended here.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text:
vākyaṃ tu
padasamūhaḥ/ śaktaṃ padam/ asmāt padāt ayamartho boddhavya iti
īśvarasaṅgetaḥ śaktiḥ/
children.translated_text: A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is a collection of words (<s>pada</s>). A word that has <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) is a <s>pada</s>. <s>Śakti</s> is the convention of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) [in the form]: 'from this word, this meaning is to be understood.'

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
vākyalakṣaṇamāha -
vākyamiti/ padalakṣaṇamāha - śaktamiti/
children.translated_text: [The author] states the definition of a sentence (<s>vākya</s>) — with 'a sentence.' [He] states the definition of a word (<s>pada</s>) — with 'that which has <s>śakti</s>.'

children.text: śaktinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of <s>śakti</s> (denotative power)

children.text:
arthasmṛtyanukūlapadapadārthasambandhaḥ śaktiḥ/ sā ca
padārthāntaramiti mīmāṃsakāḥ/ tannirāsārthamāha - asmāditi/
ḍitthādīnāmiva ghaṭādīnāmapi saṅketa eva śaktiḥ, na tu
padārthāntaramityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s> (denotative power) is the relation between a word and its meaning that is conducive to the recollection of the meaning. And that is a separate category — [so say] the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> (exegetes). To refute that, [the author] says 'from this' and so forth. The meaning is: just as for <s>ḍittha</s> (proper names) and the like, so too for <s>ghaṭa</s> (pot) and the like, <s>śakti</s> is merely convention (<s>saṅketa</s>), and not a separate category.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mīmāṃsakamatanirāsakatvena
agrimamūlamavatārayituṃ tanmatasādhāraṇyena śaktipadārthamāha -
arthasmṛtyanukūleti/ śābdabodhajanaka-arthasmṛtyanukūlaḥ
ghaṭādipadaghaṭādirūpārthayoḥ sambandhaḥ śaktirityarthaḥ/ anukūlatvam/
iha prayojakatvam/ tacca
kāraṇatāvacchedakapadapadārthasambanadhe 'pyakṣatam/
ghaṭādipadatadarthayoranyasambandhavāraṇāya anukūlāntaṃ
vivakṣitārthakam/ anyasambandhajñānasyārthasmṛtijanakatve 'pi
śābdabodhajanakasmṛtijanakatvābhāvāt/ arthasmṛtyanukūlatvasya
adṛṣṭādisādhāraṇyāt viśeṣyamiti dhyeyam/ padārthāntaramiti/
tattatpadārthatāvacchedakābhāvakūṭavadityarthaḥ/ tenātiriktapadārthatvasya
anyamatāprasiddhatve 'pi na vyāghātaḥ/ asmāt padāt ayamartho boddhavya
iti mūlasya 'etatpadajanyabodhaviṣayo 'yamarthaḥ'
ityākārakeśvarecchā śaktirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: In order to introduce the next root text by way of refuting the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view, [the commentator] states the meaning of the term <s>śakti</s> in a manner common [to both views] — with 'conducive to the recollection of the meaning' and so forth. The meaning is: <s>śakti</s> is the relation between a word such as <s>ghaṭa</s> (pot) and its meaning such as a pot, which is conducive to the recollection of the meaning that produces <s>śābdabodha</s> (verbal comprehension). 'Conduciveness' here means being a causal factor. And that is unimpaired even in the relation between word and meaning that serves as the delimitor of the condition of being a cause. The qualification 'conducive' is intended to exclude other relations between words such as <s>ghaṭa</s> and their meanings — because although cognition of other relations can produce recollection of the meaning, it cannot produce the recollection that generates <s>śābdabodha</s>. Since the property of being conducive to the recollection of meaning is common to <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) and the like as well, it should be noted that it is a qualifier [requiring further specification]. 'A separate category' — the meaning is: like a <s>kūṭastha</s> (immutable entity) that is the absence of the delimitor of the category-hood of each respective [word-meaning pair]. Therefore, even though the property of being a category beyond [the conventional] is not accepted in other systems, there is no contradiction. The meaning of the root text 'from this word, this meaning is to be understood' is: <s>śakti</s> is the will of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) of the form 'this meaning is the object of the comprehension produced by this word.'

children.text:
na tu
padārthāntaramiti/ na ceśvarīyajñānasyecchāyāḥ kṛtervā
śaktirūpatvamiti vinigamanāvirahāt atiriktaiva śaktiriti vācyam/
ādhunikasaṅketasya icchārūpatayā śakterapi icchārūpatve
saṅketajñānasya anugatakāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ sambhavati nānyathā ityevaṃ
vinigamakasaṃbhavena, icchāyā eva śaktitvasvīkārāt/
children.translated_text: 'And not a separate category' — nor should one say that since there is no way to determine whether <s>śakti</s> is the Lord's cognition, His will, or His action, <s>śakti</s> must be a category beyond [these]; because, since conventional designation by modern [speakers] has the nature of will, if <s>śakti</s> too has the nature of will, a uniform cause-effect relation with the cognition of convention is possible, but not otherwise — thus a means of determination is available; and because <s>śakti</s> is accepted as being of the nature of will.

children.text:
na ca - bhagavadicchāyāḥ
sakalaviṣayiṇyāḥ śaktitvasvīkāre
ghaṭapadaboddhavyatvaprakārakatadicchāyāḥ paṭe 'pi sattvāt
ghaṭapadavācyatvasya atiprasaṅgaḥ/ evaṃ
gaṅgāpadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakārakecchāyāḥ tīre 'pi sattvena
śaktyaiva tadbodhasambhave lakṣaṇocchedāpattiriti - vācyam/ yataḥ
tattatpadavācyatvaṃ
tattatpadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakāratānirūpiteśvarecchīyaviśeṣyatāvattvam/
tādṛśaprakāratānirūpitaviśeṣyatāsambandhena tadicchāvattvaṃ vā/ tathā ca
tādṛśasya ghaṭapadavācyatvasya paṭe 'sattvāt nātiprasaṅgaḥ/
gaṅgādipadajanyatvasya bodhāṃśe, bodhaviṣayatvasya ca tīrāṃśe,
svātantryeṇa bhānamīśvarecchāyāṃ upeyate/ itthaṃ ca
viśakalitabhānasthale nirūpyanirūpakabhāvāpannaviṣayatāyā abhāvena
gaṅgāpadajanyatvaprakāratānirūpitabodhaviṣayatvaprakāratānirūpitav iśeṣyatāsambandhena
icchāvattvasya tīre 'sattvena na kṣatiriti saṅkṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: Nor should one object: if the will of the Lord, which has all things as its objects, is accepted as <s>śakti</s>, then since that will of His which has as its qualifier the property of being comprehensible by the word <s>ghaṭa</s> (pot) exists also in cloth, there would be the unwanted consequence of cloth being denoted by the word <s>ghaṭa</s>; similarly, since the will having as its qualifier the property of being the object of comprehension produced by the word <s>gaṅgā</s> exists also in the bank, there would be the unwanted consequence that verbal comprehension of the bank would be possible through <s>śakti</s> alone, leading to the destruction of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) — because the denotability of each word is the property of being the locus of the qualificand-hood delimited by the qualifier-hood determined by the property of being the object of comprehension produced by that word, as [qualified by] the Lord's will. Or it is the possession of such a will of the Lord connected by the relation of qualificand-hood delimited by the qualifier-hood of that kind. And thus, since such <s>ghaṭa</s>-word-denotability does not exist in cloth, there is no over-extension. Regarding the word <s>gaṅgā</s> and the like, it is maintained that in the Lord's will, the property of being produced by the word <s>gaṅgā</s> appears in the comprehension-aspect, while the property of being the object of comprehension appears in the bank-aspect, each independently. And thus, in the case of such disaggregated appearance, since a qualificand-hood that has entered into the determiner-determined relation is absent, because the possession of a will connected by the relation of qualificand-hood delimited by the qualifier-hood of being-produced-by-the-word-<s>gaṅgā</s> as determined by the qualifier-hood of being-the-object-of-comprehension does not exist in the bank, there is no difficulty — this is the summary.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
śābdabodhajanaketi/ anekapadārthasaṃsargāvagāhijñānaṃ
śābdabodhaḥ/ tasya janakaṃ padārthānāṃ smaraṇam, tadanukūlaḥ
padapadārthasambandhaḥ śaktiḥ/ tadanukūlatvaṃ ca tajjanakajñānaviṣayatvam/
tathā ca yasya padapadārthayoḥ sambandhajñānamasti tasyaiva
vākyaghaṭakapadajñānāt tattatpadārthasmaraṇaṃ bhavati/ padajñānaṃ hi
ekasambandhijñānamaparasambandhismārakamiti rītyā padārthasmṛtiṃ
janayati/ yathā pūrvaṃ sambaddhatayā dṛṣṭayoḥ hastihastapakayordhadhye
paścāt kadācit ekasya hastipakarūpasambandhino darśanena aparasya
hastirūpasya sambandhinaḥ smaraṇaṃ bhavati tadvat pūrvaṃ padapadārthayoḥ
sambandhaṃ yaḥ jānāti sa eva ekasya padarūpasya sambandhinaḥ jñāne sati
aparamartharūpaṃ sambandhinaṃ smartuṃ śaknoti/ tathā ca
sambandhajñānasahakṛtāt padajñānāt padārthasmṛtiḥ tataḥ śābdabodha
children.translated_text: 'Conducive to the production of <s>śābdabodha</s>' — <s>śābdabodha</s> (verbal comprehension) is a cognition that apprehends the connection of multiple word-meanings. Its producer is the recollection of the word-meanings; the relation between word and meaning that is conducive to that [recollection] is <s>śakti</s> (denotative power). And such conduciveness is the property of being the object of the cognition that produces it. Thus, only one who has cognition of the relation between a word and its meaning can have, from the cognition of a word that is a component of a sentence, the recollection of the respective word-meaning. For the cognition of a word, being the cognition of one relatum, causes the recollection of the other relatum — in this manner it produces the recollection of the meaning. Just as, when two things previously seen as related — say, an elephant and a palm leaf — one subsequently perceives one of them, namely the palm leaf which is a relatum, and thereby the recollection of the other, namely the elephant which is the [other] relatum, arises; similarly, one who previously knows the relation between a word and its meaning, when the cognition of one relatum, namely the word, arises, is able to recollect the other, namely the meaning, which is the [other] relatum. And thus, from the cognition of a word assisted by the cognition of the relation, there arises the recollection of the meaning, and from that, <s>śābdabodha</s> —

children.text:
iti kramo 'tra
vivakṣitaḥ/
children.translated_text: this is the sequence intended here.

children.text:
nanu
'athasmṛtyanukūlapadapadārthasambandhaḥ śaktiḥ' iti dīpikāvākye
anukūlaśabdasya yadi kāraṇamityarthaḥ tadā
padapadārthasambandhajñānasyārthasmṛtijanakatve 'pi
padapadārthasambandhasyārthasmṛtijanakatvābhāvādasambhavaḥ/ ata āha -
anukūlatvāmiha prayojakatvamiti prayojakatvaṃ ca
kāraṇakāraṇatāvacchedakobhayasādhārāṇam/
padapadārthasambandhajñānamityasya viṣayitāsambandheta
sambandhaviśiṣṭajñānaṃ ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca arthasmṛtikāraṇam
sambandhaviśiṣṭajñānam/ tatra viṣayitāsambandhena vidyamānatayā
padapadārthasambandhasya kāraṇatāvacchedakatvamakṣatam/ kāraṇe
vidyamānasyaiva kāraṇatāvacchedakatvāt/ tathā ca padapadārthasambandhasya
arthasmṛtiprayojakatvāt tadanukūlatvaṃ sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/ tathā ca
śābdabodhajanakārthasmṛtiprayojakatve sati padapadārthasambandhatvaṃ
śakterlakṣaṇamiti paryavasannam/ tatra viśeṣyānupādāne
adṛṣṭādiṣvativyāptiḥ/ teṣāṃ kāryasāmānyaṃ prati kāraṇatayā
arthasmṛtiṃ pratyapi kāraṇatvāt/ tadvāraṇāya viśeṣyopādānam/
adṛṣṭādeḥ padapadārthasambandhatvābhāvāt nātivyāptiḥ/
viśeṣaṇānupādāne ghaṭapadasya kambugrīvādimadrūpatadarthasya ca yaḥ
kālikādisambandhaḥ tatrātivyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya viśeṣaṇam/
ghaṭapadatadarthayoḥ kālikasambandhasya kathañcit arthasmṛtyanukūlatve 'pi
tasyāḥ smṛteḥ śābdabodhajanakatvaṃ nāsti/ ataḥ
śābdabodhajanakārthasmṛtyanukūlatvasya kālikasambandhe 'bhāvāt
nātivyāptiḥ/ tadāha ghaṭādipadetyādinā/ vivakṣitārthakamiti/
śābdabodhajanakasmṛtyanukūlatvārthakamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, in the Dīpikā sentence 'the relation between word, meaning, and their connection that is conducive to the recollection of meaning is <s>śakti</s> (denotative power),' if the word 'conducive' (<s>anukūla</s>) means 'being a cause,' then since the cognition of the word-meaning relation is the generator of meaning-recollection but the word-meaning relation itself is not a generator of meaning-recollection, this would be impossible. Therefore he says: 'conducive' here means 'being a promoter' (<s>prayojakatva</s>), and promoter-hood is common to both — being a cause and being a delimitor of cause-hood. 'The cognition of the word-meaning relation' means: cognition qualified by the relation through the relation of object-hood (<s>viṣayitā</s>) — that is, cognition qualified by the relation. Accordingly, the cause of meaning-recollection is cognition qualified by the relation. Therein, since [the word-meaning relation] exists through the relation of object-hood, the delimitor-of-cause-hood status of the word-meaning relation is preserved — because only what exists in the cause can be a delimitor of cause-hood. Accordingly, since the word-meaning relation promotes meaning-recollection, its being conducive is possible — this is the purport. Thus, the definition of <s>śakti</s> that emerges is: being a word-meaning relation when [that relation] promotes the meaning-recollection that generates verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>). Therein, without including the qualificand, there would be over-pervasion (<s>ativyāpti</s>) to unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) and the like — because they too are causes with respect to effects in general, and hence would be causes with respect to meaning-recollection as well. To block this, the qualificand is included — since unseen merit etc. do not possess the property of being a word-meaning relation, there is no over-pervasion. Without including the qualifier, there would be over-pervasion to the temporal relation etc. between the word 'pot' and its referent — the form possessing a conch-shaped neck etc. To block this, the qualifier [is included]. Even though the temporal relation between the word 'pot' and its referent may somehow be conducive to meaning-recollection, that recollection does not generate verbal cognition. Hence, since the property of being conducive to meaning-recollection that generates verbal cognition is absent in the temporal relation, there is no over-pervasion. This he states with 'of the word pot etc.' 'Having the intended meaning' — the meaning is: having the sense of being conducive to the recollection that generates verbal cognition.

children.text:
'sā ca padārthāntaram'
iti dīpikātaḥ śaktiḥ kḷptasaptapadārthātiriktaḥ padārthaḥ ityartho
labhyate/ tathā sati naiyāyikamate 'prasaddhiḥ/ kḷptapadārthātiriktatvasya
aprasiddhatvāt/ tathā ca mīmāṃsakena naiyāyikaṃ prati tatsādhane
naiyāyikenāprasiddhaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ udbhāvyatetyālocya
vyācaṣṭe-tattatpadārthatāvacchedakābhāvakūṭavadityartha iti/ pratyekaṃ
dravyādau prasiddhāḥ ye dravyatvādīnāmabhāvāḥ tadghaṭita samudāyavatī
śaktirityarthaḥ/ anyamatāprasiddhatve 'pīti/ naiyāyikamate 'prasiddhatve 'pi
ityarthaḥ/ na vyāghātaḥ - nānupapattiḥ/ asmāt padādityatra pañcamyāḥ
janyatvamarthaḥ/ tasya budhadhātvarthabodhe 'nvayaḥ/ ṇyatpratyayasya
vaṣiyatvamarthaḥ/ tathā ca etatpadajanyabodhaviṣayo 'yamartha iti
labhyate/ tadāha-iti mūlasyeti/ ādhunikasaṅketasyetyādi/
ḍitthādipadādayamartho boddhavya
ityākārakādhunikecchārūpasaṅketagrahāt ḍitthādipadāt
vyaktiviśeṣabodho bhavatīti svīkāraṇīyam/ 'ghaṭadipadāt ayamartho
bodhya' ityākārakeśvarecchārūpasaṅketagrahāt ghaṭādipadāt
ghaṭādibodha iti vaktavyam/ saṅketatvaṃ ca
tattatpadaboddhavyatvaprakārakādhunikecchā - īśvarecchayoḥsādhāraṇo
dharmaḥ/ tathā ceśvarecchāyāḥ śaktitve
ubhayasādhāraṇasṅketatvāvacchinnaviṣayakajñānatvena śābdabodhaṃ prati
ekavidhameva kāraṇatvam/ tattatpadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakārakasya
īśvarajñānasya īśvaraprayatnasya vā śaktitve tu ḍitthādipadasthale
icchārūpasaṅketajñānāt śābdabodhaḥ ghaṭādipadasthale tu
īśvarajñānarūpā īśvarapratnarūpa vā yā śaktiḥ tajjñānādapi
śābdabodha ityevaṃ aneke kāryakāraṇabhāvāḥ kalpanīyā iti
gauravam/ ataḥ īśvarecchaiva śaktirityarthaḥ/ vinigamakaṃ vinigamanā
iti padayoḥ anyatarapakṣasādhakayuktirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'And that is a separate category' — from the <s>Dīpikā</s>, the meaning obtained is that <s>śakti</s> is a category (<s>padārtha</s>) over and above the established seven categories. In that case, this would be unestablished (<s>aprasiddhi</s>) in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, because the property of being over and above the established categories is unestablished [for them]. Accordingly, since the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>, in proving this to the <s>Naiyāyika</s>, would be raising a qualifier unestablished [for the opponent] — reflecting on this, he explains: 'The meaning is: like a collection of absences of the respective category-delimitors in each [substance etc.].' The meaning is: <s>śakti</s> is an entity constituted by the collection of the absences of substance-hood etc. that are established in each of the [categories] substance and so forth. 'Even though unestablished in the other school' — the meaning is: even though unestablished in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view. 'No contradiction' — no impossibility. In 'from this word' (<s>asmāt padāt</s>), the fifth case-ending has the meaning of 'being produced by.' Its syntactic connection is with the meaning of the root 'budh' (to know), [yielding] 'cognition.' The meaning of the <s>ṇyat</s> suffix is 'fitness' (<s>vaṣiyatva</s>). Thus what is obtained is: 'this meaning is the object of the cognition generated by this word.' This he states with 'of the root text' etc. 'Of the modern convention' etc. — since a modern convention of the form 'from the word <s>Ḍittha</s> etc. this meaning should be understood' is grasped — being a convention in the form of a modern [speaker's] desire — it must be accepted that from the word <s>Ḍittha</s> etc. a cognition of the particular individual arises. [Similarly,] it should be said that from the word 'pot' etc. the cognition of pot etc. [arises] through grasping the convention in the form of God's will (<s>Īśvarecchā</s>) of the form 'from the word pot this meaning should be understood.' Convention-hood (<s>saṅketatva</s>) is a property common to both the modern [speaker's] desire of the form 'the meaning to be understood from such-and-such a word' and God's will. Accordingly, if God's will is <s>śakti</s>, then since [convention-grasping] takes the form of cognition whose object is delimited by convention-hood common to both, there is only one type of causal relation with respect to verbal cognition. However, if God's cognition or God's effort of the form 'the object of the cognition generated by such-and-such a word [is such-and-such]' were <s>śakti</s>, then in the case of the word <s>Ḍittha</s> etc., verbal cognition would arise from the cognition of a convention in the form of desire, while in the case of the word 'pot' etc., verbal cognition would arise also from the cognition of <s>śakti</s> in the form of God's cognition or God's effort — thus many causal relations would have to be postulated, which is cumbersome (<s>gaurava</s>). Therefore, the meaning is that God's will alone is <s>śakti</s>. 'Determiner' (<s>vinigamaka</s>) and 'determination' (<s>vinigamanā</s>) — the meaning of [these] words is: a reason that establishes one of the two alternatives.

children.text:
na ca bhagavadicchāyā
ityādi/ īśvarecchāyāḥ sarvaviṣayakatvamekatvaṃ cāṅgīkriyate/
sā cet śaktiḥ tarhi paṭāderapi 'ghaṭādipadavācyatvaṃ prasajyeta/ tathā
hi - viśeṣyatāsambandhena
ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakārakabhagavadicchāvatvaṃ ghaṭapadaśakyatvamiti
vaktavyam/ 'ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayo ghaṭo bhavatu' ityākārikāyāṃ
bhagavadicchāyāṃ ghaṭo viśeṣyaḥ ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaṃ prakāraḥ/
ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakārakeśvarecchāyāḥ
svanirūpitaviśeṣyatāsambandhena ghaṭe sattvāt ghaṭasya
ghaṭapadaśakyatvam/ īśvarecchāyāśca ekatvāt tasyāḥ
'paṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayaḥ paṭo bhavatu', 'kuḍyapadajanyabodhaviṣayaḥ
kuḍyaṃ bhavatu' ityādyākārakatvamapyaṅgīkaraṇīyam/ tathā
ceśvarecchāyāṃ paṭāderapi viśeṣyatvāt
ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakārakeśvarecchāyāḥ viśeṣyatāsambandhena
paṭādāvapi sattvāt paṭāderapi ghaṭapadavācyatvaprasaṅgaḥ/ evaṃ
'gaṅgāpadajanyabondhaviṣayaḥ pravāho bhavatu',
'tīrapadajanyabodhaviṣayaḥ tīraṃ bhavatu' ityākārakatāyā
apīśvarecchāyāḥ vaktavyatayā tatra gaṅgāpadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaṃ
prakāraḥtīraṃ viśeṣyamiti
gaṅgāpadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakārakeśvarecchāyāḥ viśeṣyatāsambandhena
tīre 'pi sattvāt tīrasyāpi gaṅgāpadavācyatvāt
children.translated_text: 'Nor [should it be objected regarding] the will of the Lord' etc. It is accepted that God's will (<s>Īśvarecchā</s>) has all things as its object and is one. If that is <s>śakti</s>, then the undesirable consequence would follow that even cloth (<s>paṭa</s>) etc. would be denotable by the word 'pot' etc. For thus: what should be stated as the denotability of the word 'pot' (<s>ghaṭapadaśakyatva</s>) is the property of possessing God's will whose qualifier-mode is being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot,' through the relation of qualificand-hood (<s>viśeṣyatā</s>). In God's will of the form 'let the pot be the object of cognition generated by the word pot,' the pot is the qualificand and being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot' is the qualifier-mode. Since God's will whose qualifier-mode is being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot' exists in the pot through the relation of qualificand-hood determined by itself, the pot has the denotability of the word 'pot.' And since God's will is one, it must also be accepted as having the forms 'let cloth be the object of cognition generated by the word cloth,' 'let wall be the object of cognition generated by the word wall,' and so forth. Accordingly, since cloth etc. too are qualificands in God's will, and since God's will whose qualifier-mode is being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot' exists even in cloth etc. through the relation of qualificand-hood, the undesirable consequence follows that cloth etc. too would be denotable by the word 'pot.' Similarly, since God's will must be stated as also having the forms 'let the cognition generated by the word Gaṅgā arise,' 'let the object of that cognition be the bank,' therein, being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-Gaṅgā is the qualifier-mode and the bank is the qualificand — and since God's will whose qualifier-mode is being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-Gaṅgā exists even in the bank through the relation of qualificand-hood, even the bank would be denotable by the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text:
śaktyaiva gaṅgāpadāt
tīrasya bodhasambhavena tīre gaṅgāpadasya lakṣaṇā anāvaśyikīti
lakṣaṇāyāḥ bhaṅgaśca prasajyeteti śaṅkāyāḥ āśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: and since the cognition of the bank from the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> would be possible through <s>śakti</s> (primary denotation) alone, secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) for the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> with respect to the bank would be unnecessary — thus the destruction of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> too would follow. This is the purport of the objection.

children.text:
ghaṭapadaboddhavyatvaprakārakatadicchāyā iti/
ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakārakeśvarecchāyā ityarthaṃḥ/
yatastatpadavācyatvamityādi/ viśeṣyatāsambandhena
tatpadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaprakārakeśvarecchāvattvaṃ na tatpadavācyatvam,
yena pūrvoktadoṣau syātām/ api tu
tatpadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitā yā
īśvarecchānirūpitā viśeṣyatā tadvattvam
tatpadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitaviśeṣyatāsambandhenaneśvarecchāvattvaṃvā
tatpadavācyatvam/ īśvarecchāyā ekatvena tasyāṃ sarvasya viśeṣyatve
prakāratve 'pi ca īśvarecchīyā tattatpadārthaniṣṭhā viśeṣyatā
prakārabhedena bhinnabhinnā bhavati/ evaṃ ca 'ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayo
ghaṭo bhavatu,' 'paṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayaḥ paṭo bhavatu'
ityadyākārakeśvarecchānirūpitā ghaṭaniṣṭhā viśeṣyataiva
ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitā, na paṭaniṣṭhā
viśeṣyatā, paṭāṃśe ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayatvasyeśvarecchāyā
anavagāhanāt/ ataḥ
ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣayatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitaviśeṣyatāsambandhena
īśvarecchāyāḥ ghaṭe eva sattvāt ghaṭasyaiva ghaṭapadavācyatvaṃ na
paṭādeḥ/ evaṃ lakṣaṇāsthale 'gaṅgāpadajanyo bodho bhavatu'
'bodhaviṣayaḥ tīraṃ bhavatu' ityākārakatvameva
īśvarecchāyāmaṅgīkriyate/
gaṅgāpadajanyatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpita -
bodhaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpita -
viṣayatva-niṣṭhaprakāratānirūpita-viśeṣyatāsambandhena
īśvarecchāvattvameva gaṅgāpadavācyatvam/
pūrvapradarśitaviśakalitabhānātmikāyāmīśvarecchāyāṃ
bodhaniṣṭhaprakāratāyāṃ
gaṅgāpadajanyatvāniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitatvaṃnāstīti
uktasambandheneśvarecchāvattvasya tīre 'bhāvāt gaṅgāpadavācyatvaṃ
tīrasya nāstīti tīre gaṅgāpadalakṣaṇāyāḥ svīkāryatayā/ na
lakṣaṇocchedāpattiśceti bhāvaḥ/ tadṛśasya ghaṭapadavācyatvasyeti/
children.translated_text: 'Of God's will whose qualifier-mode is to-be-understood-from-the-word-pot' — the meaning is: of God's will whose qualifier-mode is being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot.' 'By which the denotability of that word [is established]' etc. — the denotability of a given word is not the property of possessing God's will whose qualifier-mode is being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-that-word, through the relation of qualificand-hood — for then the two previously mentioned defects would arise. Rather, the denotability of a given word is the property of possessing [God's will] through the relation of qualificand-hood that is determined by God's will, which is determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-that-word — or, [equivalently,] possessing God's will through the relation of qualificand-hood determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-that-word. Even though, due to the oneness of God's will, everything is both a qualificand and a qualifier-mode in it, the qualificand-hood residing in the respective word-meanings in God's will is distinct according to the difference in qualifier-modes. Thus, only the qualificand-hood residing in the pot, which is determined by God's will of the forms 'let the pot be the object of cognition generated by the word pot,' 'let cloth be the object of cognition generated by the word cloth,' and so forth, is determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot' — not the qualificand-hood residing in cloth, because being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot' does not pervade God's will with respect to the cloth-portion. Therefore, since God's will exists only in the pot through the relation of qualificand-hood determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot,' only the pot has the denotability of the word 'pot,' not cloth etc. Similarly, in the case of secondary signification, what is accepted in God's will is only the form: 'let cognition generated by the word Gaṅgā arise,' 'let the object of [that] cognition be the bank.' The denotability of the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> is precisely the property of possessing God's will through the relation of qualificand-hood determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in object-hood, determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in cognition, determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in being-generated-by-the-word-Gaṅgā. Since in God's will as analyzed above, in the qualifier-mode-hood residing in cognition, the property of being determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in being-generated-by-the-word-Gaṅgā is absent — and hence the property of possessing God's will through the stated relation is absent in the bank — the bank does not have the denotability of the word <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and therefore secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) of the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> for the bank must be accepted. Thus, the undesirable consequence of the destruction of secondary signification does not arise — this is the purport. 'Of such denotability of the word pot' —

children.text:
ghaṭapadajanyabodhaviṣaśyatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitaviśeṣyatāsambandheneśvarecchāvattvarūpasya
ghaṭapadavācyatvasyetyarthaḥ/ nātiprasaṅgaḥ - na paṭasya
ghaṭapadavācyatvaprasaṅgaḥ/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: of the denotability of the word 'pot' in the form of possessing God's will through the relation of qualificand-hood determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in being-the-object-of-cognition-generated-by-the-word-'pot.' 'There is no over-extension' — there is no undesirable consequence that cloth would have the denotability of the word 'pot.'

children.text:
nanu śaktyā yatra
padārthabodho bhavati tatraiveśvarecchāyāṃ āvaśyakatā/ lakṣaṇatā yatra
bodhaḥ, tatra neśvarecchāyā āvaśyakatvam/
śakyasambandhamātrasyaivāpekṣitatvāt/ tathā ca 'gaṅgāpadajanyo bodho
bhavatu, bodhaviṣayastīraṃ bhavatu', ityadyākārakecchākalpanaṃ mudhā/
tīrasya gaṅgāpadavācyatvaṃ tu prāguktaprakāreṇaiva vāryate/
vācyārthaṃpravāhasambandhamātreṇa tīrasya gaṅgāpadalakṣyatvopapatterityata
āha - saṅkṣepa iti/ kāryasāmānyaṃ prati īśvarecchāyāḥ
kāraṇatvāt gaṅgāpadāt tīraviṣayakabodhaṃ pratyapi īśvarecchā
kāraṇamiti vaktavyam/ tatra kimākārā īśvarecchā kāraṇamiti
jijñāsāyāṃ tīrādau gaṅgāpadavācyatvavyavahārābhāvāt
uktaviśakalitabhānavatī īśvarecchaiva kāraṇamityavaśyavaktavyatvāt
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, [objection:] God's will (<s>Īśvarecchā</s>) is necessarily required only where verbal cognition of the referent occurs through <s>śakti</s> (primary denotation). Where cognition occurs through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), God's will is not necessary, since only the relation to the primary denotatum is required. Accordingly, postulating a [divine] will of the form 'let cognition generated by the word Gaṅgā arise, let the bank be the object of cognition' is futile. The denotability of the bank by the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> is blocked in the manner previously stated. Since the status of the bank as the secondary referent (<s>lakṣya</s>) of the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> is accounted for merely by the relation to the primary referent — the river-flow — to this he says 'in brief' (<s>saṅkṣepa</s>). Since God's will is a cause with respect to effects in general, it must be said that God's will is a cause also with respect to the cognition of the bank from the word <s>Gaṅgā</s>. In the inquiry into what form of God's will is the cause there — since there is no usage of 'denotability of the word Gaṅgā' with respect to the bank etc., it is necessarily the case that only God's will possessing the analyzed cognition-content [described above] is the cause — this is the purport.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: viśiṣṭaśaktisthāpanam
children.translated_text: The establishment of <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) as [residing] in the qualified [entity] (<s>viśiṣṭa</s>).

children.text:
nanu
gavādipadānāṃ jātāveva śaktiḥ, viśeṣaṇatayā jāteḥ
prathamamupasthitatvāt/ vyaktilābhastu ākṣepāditi kecit/ tanna -
'gāmānaya' ityādau vṛddhavyavahāreṇa sarvatrānayanādeḥ vyaktāveva
sambhavena, jātiviśiṣṭavyaktāveva śaktikalpanāt/
children.translated_text: Now, [the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view:] the denotative power of words like 'cow' etc. resides in the universal (<s>jāti</s>) alone, because the universal, as a qualifier, is what is first presented [to cognition]. The apprehension of the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) is through implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>) — thus say some. That is not so — because in [sentences] like 'bring the cow,' the act of bringing etc. in the behavior of the learned (<s>vṛddha</s>) is everywhere possible only with respect to the individual, and therefore <s>śakti</s> is to be postulated only in the individual qualified by the universal (<s>jātiviśiṣṭavyakti</s>).

children.text: pramāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
viśiṣṭe śaktiṃ
vyavasthāpayituṃ mīmāṃsakamataṃ upanyasya dūṣayatigavādīti/
viśeṣaṇībhūtajātigrahamantarā viśiṣṭagrahāsambhavena viśiṣṭe
śaktikalpanaṃ na sambhavati/ ataḥ jātigrahasya prathamamapekṣitatvena
jātāveva śaktikalpanaṃ ucitam lāghavāt ityāha - viśeṣaṇatayeti/
prathamamupasthitatvāditi/ viśiṣṭagrahāt pūrvamavagatatvādityarthaḥ/
kathaṃ tarhi vyaktilābha ityata āha - vyaktīti/ ākṣepāditi/
arthāpattipramāṇādityarthaḥ/ vyaktāveva sambhaveneti/
anupapattipratisandhānaśūnyatādaśāyāmapi vyaktibhānasya
anubhavasiddhatvena cetyapi bodhyam/ viśiṣṭavyaktāveveti/ evakāreṇa
kevalajātikalpanavyavacchedaḥ/
children.translated_text: In order to establish <s>śakti</s> as [residing] in the qualified [entity], he presents and refutes the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view — with 'of [words like] cow etc.' Since without the prior apprehension of the qualifying universal, apprehension of the qualified [entity] is impossible, the postulation of <s>śakti</s> in the qualified [entity] cannot work. Hence, since the apprehension of the universal must be prior, it is appropriate to postulate <s>śakti</s> in the universal alone, by parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>) — this he states with 'as a qualifier' (<s>viśeṣaṇatayā</s>). 'Because it is first presented' — the meaning is: because it is apprehended prior to the apprehension of the qualified [entity]. How then is the individual apprehended? To this he says 'individual' (<s>vyakti</s>). 'Through implication' (<s>ākṣepa</s>) — the meaning is: through the means of knowledge called presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>). 'Since it is possible only with respect to the individual' — it should also be understood that even in a state devoid of the reflection of impossibility, the appearance of the individual is established by experience. 'In the individual qualified [by the universal] alone' — by the word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>), the postulation of the universal by itself is excluded.

children.text:
atredaṃ
bodhyam-jāti-tadvaiśiṣṭya-tadāśrayeṣu triṣu śaktiḥ kalpanīyā/
padārthadvayasambandhasyaiva padadvayasamabhivyāhāralabhyatvenānyasyāśakyasya
śābdabodhe bhānāsambhavāditi/
children.translated_text: Here this should be understood: <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) must be postulated in three [things] — the universal (<s>jāti</s>), the qualification by it (<s>tadvaiśiṣṭya</s>), and its substrate (<s>tadāśraya</s>). Because the relation between two referents is obtainable only through the co-occurrence of two words, and it is impossible for something that cannot be [independently] denoted to appear in verbal cognition.

children.text:
navyāstu -
lakṣyatāvacchedakatvagrahamātreṇa lakṣyatāvacchedakasya yathā śābdabodhe
bhānaṃ tathā śakyatāvacchedakatvagrahamātreṇa śakyatāvacchedakasyāpi
śābdabodhe bhānaṃ sambhavatīti śakyatāvacchedake ca śaktiḥ na
kalpanīyeti vadanti/
children.translated_text: The <s>Navya</s> (new) logicians, however, say: just as the <s>lakṣyatāvacchedaka</s> (delimiting property of the indicated meaning) appears in verbal cognition merely by grasping its character as a delimiting property of indicated-ness, so too the <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s> (delimiting property of denotation) can appear in verbal cognition merely by grasping its character as a delimiting property of denotability — and therefore <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) need not be postulated in the delimiting property of denotation.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
viśiṣṭe śaktiṃ
vyavasthāpayitumiti/ gavādipadānāṃ gotvādijātiviśiṣṭavyaktau
śaktiṃ nirdhārayitumityarthaḥ/ viśiṣṭagrahāsambhaveneti/
viśiṣṭaviṣayakabuddhau viśeṣaṇaviṣayakajñānasya kāraṇatvena
gotvaviśiṣṭavyaktijñānāt pūrvaṃ gotvarūpaviśeṣaṇajñānaṃ āvaśyakam/
tathā ca prathamopasthitatvāt lāghavācca jātāveva
śaktikalpanamucitam, na tu tadviśiṣṭavyaktāviti bhāvaḥ/ jātāveveti/
evakāreṇa vyaktiṣu śaktivyavacchedaḥ/ lāghavāditi/ vyaktīnāmānantyāt
jāteścaikatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ nanu jātau śaktisvīkāre gavādipadāt
gotvādijātereva bodhaḥ syāt na tu vyakteḥ/ gopadaśakyatvāt/
gopadāśakyasyāpi gopadāt bodhāṅgīkāre gopadāt
ghaṭāderapi bodhaḥ syādityaśayena śaṅkate - kathaṃ tarhīti/
arthāpattipramāṇādityartha iti/ jātiviṣayakajñānasya
vyaktiviṣayakatāniyamāt vyaktibhānaṃ vinā
jātibhānamanupapannamityanupapattipratisandhānarūpārthāpattipramāṇajanyavyaktyupasthityā
gopadajanyaśābdabodhe vyakterbhānamiti bhāvaḥ/ idamupalakṣaṇam/
gopadasya govyaktau śaktyabhāve 'pi lakṣaṇā aṅgīkriyate/ ato
lakṣaṇayā śābdabodhe vyaktibhānamityapi draṣṭavyam/ etena
govyaktivācakapadābhāve 'pi arthāpattipramāṇopasthitagovyakteḥ
śābdabodhe bhānāṅgīkāre padādanupasthitasya
pratyakṣādinopasthitasyāpi ghaṭādeḥ śābdabodhe
bhānāpattirityapāstam/ anupapattipratisandhāneti/ vyaktibhānaṃ vinā
jātibhānamanupapannamityākārakānupapattipratisandhānaśūnyakāle 'pi
vyaktibhānasyānubhavasiddhatayā nārthāpattipramāṇāt vyaktibhānam/
anvayānupapattipratisandhānaśūnyakāle 'pi vyaktibhānasyānubhavasiddhatayā
na lakṣaṇayā vyaktibhānamityarthaḥ/ kevalajātikalpanavyaccheda iti/
kevalajātau śaktikalpanasya vyavaccheda ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'To establish <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) in the qualified' means: to determine the <s>śakti</s> of words like 'cow' and so forth in individuals qualified by universals such as cow-hood — this is the meaning. 'Due to the impossibility of apprehending the qualified' means: since in a cognition whose content is a qualified entity, a cognition whose content is the qualifier is a cause, cognition of the qualifier in the form of cow-hood is necessarily prior to the cognition of an individual qualified by cow-hood. And accordingly, since it is presented first and due to parsimony, it is appropriate to postulate <s>śakti</s> in the universal alone, not in the individual qualified by it — this is the purport. 'In the universal alone': by the word 'alone,' individuals are excluded from having <s>śakti</s>. 'Due to parsimony': because individuals are infinite while the universal is one — this is the purport. Now, if <s>śakti</s> is accepted in the universal, then from the word 'cow' and such words, cognition of the universal cow-hood alone would arise, not of the individual — since it is the denotatum of the word 'cow.' If cognition from the word 'cow' is accepted even of what is not denoted by the word 'cow,' then cognition of a pot and such things would also arise from the word 'cow' — with this concern he raises the objection 'how then.' 'From the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption)' is the meaning. Since cognition whose content is the universal necessarily has the particular as its content, the appearance of the universal is impossible without the appearance of the particular — through the presentation of the particular generated by the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>arthāpatti</s>, which is of the nature of recognizing the impossibility, the particular appears in the verbal cognition produced by the word 'cow' — this is the purport. This is illustrative. Even in the absence of <s>śakti</s> of the word 'cow' in the cow-individual, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) is accepted. Therefore it should also be understood that the particular appears in verbal cognition through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. By this, the following objection is set aside: even without a word denoting the cow-individual, if the appearance of the cow-individual presented by <s>arthāpatti</s> in verbal cognition is accepted, then the appearance in verbal cognition of a pot and such things — which are not presented by the word but are presented by perception and other means — would also follow. 'Recognizing the impossibility' means: even at a time devoid of the recognition of impossibility of the form 'the appearance of the universal is impossible without the appearance of the particular,' since the appearance of the particular is established through experience, the appearance of the particular is not from the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>arthāpatti</s>. The meaning is: even at a time devoid of the recognition of concomitance-impossibility, since the appearance of the particular is established through experience, the appearance of the particular is not through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. 'Exclusion of postulating the universal alone' means: exclusion of the postulation of <s>śakti</s> in the universal alone — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu
jātiviśiṣṭavyakttau śaktikalpane jātau, jātivyaktyoḥ yaḥ
samavāyarūpaḥ sambandhaḥ tatra ca śaktyabhāvāt kathaṃ gopadajanyabodhe
gotvajāteḥ gotvasamavāyasya ca bhānopapattiḥ/ śakyatāvacchedakatvāt
kathañcit gotvabhānopapattāvapi
children.translated_text: Now, if <s>śakti</s> is postulated in the individual qualified by the universal, and not in the universal itself nor in the relation of inherence between universal and individual, then how can the appearance of the universal cow-hood and of the inherence of cow-hood in verbal cognition produced by the word 'cow' be accounted for? Even if the appearance of cow-hood is somehow accounted for by its being a delimiting property of denotation,

children.text:
śakyatānavacchedakasya
samavāyasya kathaṃ bhānam/ na cākāṅkṣayā bhānamiti vācyam/ dvābhyāṃ
padābhyāṃ upasthitayorarthayoḥ yaḥ sambandhaḥ tasya dvābhyāṃ śaktibhyāṃ
upasthitayorarthayoryaḥ sambandhaḥ tasya vā
samabhivyāhārarūpākāṅkṣābhāsyatvāt padārthatadavacchedakayoḥ
sambandhasyākāṅkṣābhāsyatvānupapatteḥ ityāśaṅkyāha - atredaṃ
bodhyamityādinā/ tathā ca ghaṭatva-samavāya-ghaṭeṣu triṣu ghaṭapadasyaikā
śaktiḥ, tathā ca śakyatvāt trayāṇāmapi ghaṭapadajanyabodhe bhānaṃ
sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/ padārthadvayasambandhasyaiveti/
padadvayopasthapyārthadvayasambandho vā bhinnābhyāṃ
vṛttibhyāmekapadopasthāpyārthadvayasambandho vā padārthadvayasambandha
ityanena vivakṣitaḥ/ evakāreṇa śakya-śakyatāvacchedakayoḥ sambandho
vyavacchidyate/ padadvayasamabhivyāhāralabhyatveneti/
āvakāṅkṣābhāsyatvenetyarthaḥ/ anyasyāśakyasyeti/ akāṅkṣayā alabhyasya
saṃsargasya śakyatvarahitasya śakyatāvacchedakasya
ghaṭatvādijāteścetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: how can <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), which is not a delimiting property of denotation, appear? Nor can it be said that it appears through <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> (expectancy). For the relation between the two meanings presented by two words, or the relation between two meanings presented by two <s>śaktis</s> — since that is what is expressible through the expectancy constituted by <s>samabhivyāhāra</s> (co-occurrence), the relation between the word-meaning and its delimiting property cannot be accounted for through expectancy. Anticipating this, he says 'here the following should be understood' and so forth. And accordingly, the word 'pot' has a single <s>śakti</s> in all three — pot-hood, inherence, and pots — and since all three are denotata, their appearance in the cognition produced by the word 'pot' is possible — this is the purport. 'The relation between two word-meanings alone': what is intended by this is either the relation between the two meanings presented by two words, or the relation between two meanings presented by a single word through different <s>vṛttis</s> (semantic functions). By the word 'alone,' the relation between the denotatum and the delimiting property of denotation is excluded. 'As obtainable through co-occurrence of two words' means: as expressible through expectancy — this is the meaning. 'Of the other, which is not denoted' means: of the <s>saṃsarga</s> (connection) not obtainable through expectancy, of the <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s> (delimiting property of denotation) lacking denotatum-hood, and of the universal such as pot-hood — this is the meaning.

children.text:
navyāstviti/ yathā
gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityādau tīre gaṅgāpadasya lakṣaṇāsvīkāre 'pi
tīratve lakṣaṇāvirahe 'pi tīratvasya lakṣyatāvacchedakatvāt tīratvaṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakamityākārakalakṣyatāvacchedakatvaprakārakajñānamātreṇa
alakṣyasyāpi tīratvasya śābdabodhe bhānam, tathā ghaṭatve
śaktivirahe 'pi ghaṭatvaṃ
śakyatāvacchedakamityākārakaśakyatāvacchedakatvaprakārakajñānamātreṇa
ghaṭapadāt ghaṭatvasya bhānaṃ sambhavatīti śakyatāvacchedake ghaṭādau
śaktiḥ na kalpanīyeti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Navya</s> logicians, however' and so forth. Just as in the case of 'the village is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' and similar expressions, even though <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) of the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' for the bank is not accepted, and even in the absence of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in bank-hood, since bank-hood is the <s>lakṣyatāvacchedaka</s> (delimiting property of the indicated meaning), the bank-hood — which is not itself the indicated meaning — appears in verbal cognition merely through the cognition having as its mode the character of being a delimiting property of indication of the form 'bank-hood is the delimiting property of indication'; similarly, even in the absence of <s>śakti</s> in pot-hood, since pot-hood is the <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s>, the cognition of pot-hood from the word 'pot' is possible merely through the cognition having as its mode the character of being a delimiting property of denotation of the form 'pot-hood is the delimiting property of denotation' — therefore <s>śakti</s> need not be postulated in pot-hood and such things — this is the purport.

children.text:
atra kecit -
śakyatāvacchedake śaktyasvīkāre pṛthivīpadāt kadācit
aṣṭadravyātiriktadravyatvena kadācidgandhavattvena kadācitpṛthivītvena
ca śābdabodhāpattiḥ/ pṛthivī pṛthivīpadaśakyā itivat
aṣṭadravyātiriktadravyaṃ
children.translated_text: Here some hold: if <s>śakti</s> is not accepted in the <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s>, then from the word 'earth,' sometimes verbal cognition would arise under the aspect of 'substance other than the eight substances,' sometimes under the aspect of 'possessing smell,' and sometimes under the aspect of 'earth-hood.' Just as the <s>śakti</s>-apprehension of the form 'earth is denoted by the word earth' is possible, so too the form

children.text:
gandhavān vā
pṛthivīpadaśakyamityākārasya śaktigrahasya sambhavāt/ tīratvāvacchinne
gaṅgāpadaśakyasambandharūpalakṣaṇājñānāt tīratvena tīrabodhaḥ,
gaṅgātīratvāvacchinne gaṅgāpadalakṣaṇājñānāt gaṅgātīratvena
tīrabodha itivat/ tathā ca lakṣaṇayā
yatkiñcidekadharmāvacchinnaviṣayaka eva śābdabodha iti yathā na
children.translated_text: 'substance possessing smell' or 'substance other than the eight substances is denoted by the word earth' — since such <s>śakti</s>-apprehension is possible. Just as from the cognition of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in the form of the relation of denotation of the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' delimited by bank-hood, cognition of the bank arises under the aspect of bank-hood, and from the cognition of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' delimited by <s>Gaṅgā</s>-bank-hood, cognition of the bank arises under the aspect of <s>Gaṅgā</s>-bank-hood; similarly, there would be no

children.text:
niyamaḥ tathā
śakyārthabodhe 'pi niyamo na syāt/ śakyatāvacchedake śaktisvīkāre
tu pṛthivīpadāt pṛthivītvenaiva śābdabodha iti niyama upapadyate/
