ataḥ śakyatāvacchedake 'pi śaktiḥ svīkaraṇīyetyāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: restriction that verbal cognition in the domain of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> has as its content only what is delimited by some one particular property, and likewise there would be no restriction in the cognition of the denoted meaning either. But if <s>śakti</s> is accepted in the <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s>, then the restriction that verbal cognition from the word 'earth' arises only under the aspect of earth-hood is accounted for. Therefore, <s>śakti</s> should be accepted in the <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s> as well — thus they say.

children.text:
taccintyam/
yaddharmaprakārakaśābdabodha iṣyate
taddharmadharmikaśakyatāvacchedakatvaprakārakaśaktijñānameva
tādṛśaśābdabodhahetuḥ/ śakyatāvacchedakaśca sarvatra
śakyatvānyūnānatiprasaktaḥ laghureva dharmaḥ, sambhavati
laghudharmasyāvacchedakatve gurudharmasya
svarūpasambandharūpāvacchedakatvānaṅgīkārāt/ tathā ca
pṛthivītvāpekṣayā aṣṭadravyātiriktadravyatvādergurutvāt na
śakyatāvacchedakatvam/ atastatra śakyatāvacchedakatvajñānaṃ pramātmakaṃ na
sambhavatīti na tasya pramātmakaśābdabodhahetutvam/ lakṣaṇāsthale tu
'tīraṃ pravāhasambandhavat' ityākārakasyeva 'gaṅgātīraṃ
pravāhasambandhavat' ityākārakasyāpi lakṣaṇājñānasyānubhavasiddhatayā
gurāvapi svarūpasambandharūpalakṣyatāvacchedakatvajñānaṃ
śābdabodhaheturupeyate/ tathā ca śaktisthale pṛthivītvenaiva śaktyā
pṛthivīpadāt pṛthivībodhaḥ, na tu aṣṭadravyātiriktadravyatvādineti
niyamaḥ, lakṣaṇāsthale kadācit tīratvena kadācit gaṅgātīratvena
bodha ityaniyamaścopapadyata iti lakṣyatāvacchedake yathā na lakṣaṇā
tathā śakyatāvacchedake 'pi na śaktiriti navīnānāmāśayaḥ/ tadetatsarvaṃ
lakṣyatāvacchedakatvagrahamātreṇa śakyatāvacchedakatvagrahamātreṇa iti
padābhyāṃ sūcitamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: That is to be examined. A cognition having a particular property as its mode in verbal understanding is caused precisely by the <s>śakti</s>-cognition having as its mode the character of being a delimiting property of denotation whose <s>dharmin</s> (substrate) possesses that very property. And the <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s> is everywhere a property that is parsimonious — neither deficient nor over-extended relative to the denotatum-hood. Since when a parsimonious property can serve as the delimiting property, a more complex property is not accepted as the delimiting property in the form of <s>svarūpa-sambandha</s> (identity relation). And accordingly, since earth-hood is more parsimonious than 'substance-other-than-the-eight-substances-hood' and the like, the latter does not have the status of <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s>. Therefore, a cognition of <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s>-hood with respect to that cannot be a valid cognition, and hence it cannot be a cause of valid verbal cognition. In the domain of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, however, since the cognition of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> having the form 'the bank is related to the current' as well as the form '<s>Gaṅgā</s>-bank is related to the current' is both established through experience — even for a more complex property, the cognition of being a delimiting property of indication in the form of identity relation serves as a cause of verbal cognition. And accordingly, in the domain of <s>śakti</s>, cognition of earth arises from the word 'earth' only through the <s>śakti</s> of earth-hood — not through substance-other-than-the-eight-substances-hood and the like — this accounts for the restriction; while in the domain of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, cognition sometimes under the aspect of bank-hood and sometimes under the aspect of <s>Gaṅgā</s>-bank-hood — this accounts for the non-restriction. Thus, just as <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is not postulated in the <s>lakṣyatāvacchedaka</s>, so too <s>śakti</s> is not postulated in the <s>śakyatāvacchedaka</s> — this is the intent of the <s>Navīnas</s> (new logicians). All this is indicated by the two phrases 'merely by grasping the character of being a delimiting property of indication' and 'merely by grasping the character of being a delimiting property of denotation' — this should be noted.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: śaktigrahopāyapratipādanam
children.translated_text: Exposition of the means of apprehending <s>śakti</s> (denotative power)

children.text:
śaktigrahaśca
vṛddhavyavahāreṇa/ vyutpitsurbālaḥ 'gāmānaya' iti
uttamavṛddhavākyaśravaṇānantaraṃ madhyamavṛddhasya pravṛttimupalabhya gavānayanaṃ
ca dṛṣṭvā madhyamavṛddhapravṛttijanakajñānasya anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ
vākyajanyatvaṃ niścitya 'aśvamānaya, gāṃ badhāna' iti vākyāntare
āvāpodvāpābhyāṃ gopadasya gotvaviśiṣṭe śaktiḥ, aśvapadasya
aśvatvaviśiṣṭe śaktiriti vyutpadyate/
children.translated_text: And <s>śaktigraha</s> (apprehension of denotative power) is through the usage of the learned. A child wishing to learn, upon hearing the sentence '<s>gām ānaya</s>' ('bring the cow') uttered by a primary learned speaker, observes the activity of a secondary learned person and sees him bringing a cow; ascertaining through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) that the cognition generating the activity is produced by the sentence; and through inclusion and exclusion in other sentences such as '<s>aśvam ānaya</s>' ('bring the horse') and '<s>gāṃ badhāna</s>' ('tie the cow'), the child learns that the word 'cow' has <s>śakti</s> in individuals qualified by cow-hood, and the word 'horse' has <s>śakti</s> in individuals qualified by horse-hood.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
śaktigrahaśca
vṛddhavyavahāreṇeti/ śaktigrahastu vṛddhavyavahārādinā sambhavatītyarthaḥ/
ādinā vyākaraṇādiparigrahaḥ/ ata eva
children.translated_text: 'And <s>śaktigraha</s> is through the usage of the learned' means: <s>śaktigraha</s> is possible through the usage of the learned and other means — this is the meaning. By 'and other means,' grammar and such are included. Hence,

children.text:
"śaktigrahaṃ
vyākaraṇopamānakośāptavākyādvyavahārataśca/
children.translated_text: 'The apprehension of <s>śakti</s> [is] from grammar, analogy, lexicon, the statement of a trustworthy person, from usage,

children.text:
vākyasya
śeṣādvivṛtervadanti sānnidhyataḥ siddhapadasya vṛddhāḥ//
children.translated_text: from the remainder of a sentence, from exposition — the learned declare — and from the proximity of a well-known word.'

children.text:
ityabhiyuktoktiḥ
saṅgacchate/ vyākaraṇāt prakṛtipratyayādīnāṃ śaktigrahaḥ/ upamānāt
śaktigrahastu adhastāddarśitaḥ/
children.translated_text: This statement of the authorities is consistent. From grammar, apprehension of <s>śakti</s> of roots, suffixes, and the like. Apprehension of <s>śakti</s> from analogy has been shown below.

children.text:
'apyekadantaherambalambodaragajānanāḥ' iti
kośādekadantādiśabdāḥ gaṇeśatvaviśiṣṭe śaktā ityarthakāt
gaṇeśatvaviśiṣṭe śaktigrahaḥ/ tatraikadantādiśabdānāmeva padārthatayā
teṣāṃ vibhinnatvena dvandvopapattiḥ/ 'kokilaḥ pikaśabdavācyaḥ'
ityāptavākyāt pikapadasya kokile śaktigrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: From the lexicon — as in '<s>ekadanta</s>, <s>heramba</s>, <s>lambodara</s>, <s>gajānana</s>' — since the lexical entry conveys that the words '<s>ekadanta</s>' and so forth have <s>śakti</s> in what is qualified by <s>Gaṇeśa</s>-hood, <s>śaktigraha</s> in what is qualified by <s>Gaṇeśa</s>-hood is obtained. There, since the words '<s>ekadanta</s>' and so forth are themselves the word-meanings and they are mutually distinct, the <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) is accounted for. From the trustworthy statement '<s>kokila</s> is denoted by the word <s>pika</s>,' <s>śaktigraha</s> of the word <s>pika</s> in the cuckoo is obtained.

children.text:
vyavahārataḥ śaktigrahaṃ
upapādayati - vyutpitsuriti/ śaktigrahecchāvānityarthaḥ/ uttamavṛdveti/
prayojakavṛddhetyarthaḥ/ madhyamavṛddhasyeti/ prayojyavṛddhasyetyarthaḥ/
gavānayanaṃ dṛṣṭvā pravṛttimupalabhya cetyanvayaḥ/
upalabhyetyasyānumāyetyarthaḥ/ 'iyaṃ kriyā prayatnapūrvikā
vilakṣaṇakriyātvāt svīyakriyāvat' ityanumānaprayogo bodhyaḥ/
pravṛttijanakajñānasya - gavānayanagocaraprayatnajanakagavānayanajñānasya/
vākyasya viśiṣṭer'the śaktirna kalpanīyā, tādṛśārthasya
samabhivyāhāralabhyatvāt/ 'ananyalabhyo hi śabdārtha' iti
nyāyādityabhisandhimāha - aśvamānayetyādi/ āvāpodvāpābhyāmiti/
āvāpaḥ - saṅgrahaḥ/ udvāpaḥ - tyāgaḥ/ vyutpadyata iti/ vyutpattyāśrayo
bhavatītyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He demonstrates <s>śaktigraha</s> through usage by saying 'one who wishes to learn.' The meaning is: one who has the desire to apprehend <s>śakti</s>. 'Primary learned person' means: the instigating learned person. 'Of the secondary learned person' means: of the instructed learned person. The syntactic connection is: having seen the bringing of the cow and having observed the activity. The meaning of 'having observed' is 'having inferred.' The inferential application to be understood is: 'this action is preceded by effort, because it is a distinctive action, like one's own action.' 'The cognition generating the activity' means: the cognition of bringing the cow that generates the effort directed at bringing the cow. <s>Śakti</s> should not be postulated in the sentence's meaning as a qualified entity, since such a meaning is obtainable through <s>samabhivyāhāra</s> (co-occurrence). Indicating the principle 'the word-meaning is that which is not obtainable by other means,' he says '<s>aśvam ānaya</s>' and so forth. 'Through inclusion and exclusion': inclusion means gathering in; exclusion means setting aside. 'Learns' means: becomes the locus of linguistic competence — this is the meaning.

children.text:
vākyaśeṣāt yathā -
'yavamayaścarurbhavati' ityatra yavaśabdaḥ āryavyavahārāt
dīrghaśūkaviśiṣṭasya vācakaḥ, mlecchavyavahārāt priyaṅgorvācako
veti saṃndehe -
children.translated_text: From the remainder of a sentence, for example: in '<s>yavamayaś catur bhavati</s>' ('the four-month cake is made of barley'), when there is doubt whether the word '<s>yava</s>' denotes what is qualified by long awns — according to <s>Ārya</s> (learned) usage — or denotes <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet) — according to <s>mleccha</s> (barbarian) usage —

children.text:
'vasante sarvasasyānāṃ
jāyate patraśātanam/
children.translated_text: 'In spring, the shedding of leaves of all crops occurs,

children.text:
modamānāśca tiṣṭhanti
yavāḥ kaṇiśaśālinaḥ//'
children.translated_text: while barley plants stand rejoicing, bearing ears of grain.'

children.text:
iti vākyaśeṣāt
dīrghaśūkaviśiṣṭe śaktinirṇayaḥ/ priyaṅgau tu śaktibhramāt prayogaḥ/
children.translated_text: From this remainder of the sentence, the determination of <s>śakti</s> is in what is qualified by long awns. The usage in the sense of <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet) is due to erroneous apprehension of <s>śakti</s>.

children.text:
vivaraṇāt yathā-
'payati pākaṃ karoti' ityatra yatnārthakakarotinā
sarvākhyātavyākhyānāt ākhyātasya
children.translated_text: From exposition, for example: in '<s>payati</s>' means '<s>pākaṃ karoti</s>' ('performs cooking'), since all verbal forms are explained by the effort-denoting root '<s>karoti</s>' ('does'),

children.text:
yatnatvaviśiṣṭe
śaktigrahaḥ/ prasiddhapadasānnidhyāt śaktigrahastu 'vikasitapadme
madhukaraḥ' ityādyagrimagranthena sphuṭībhaviṣyati ityalaṃ pallavitena/
children.translated_text: apprehension of <s>śakti</s> of verbal forms in what is qualified by effort is obtained. Apprehension of <s>śakti</s> through the proximity of a well-known word will become clear from the subsequent passage beginning with '<s>vikasita-padme madhukaraḥ</s>' ('the bee on the blossoming lotus') — enough of this elaboration.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
vṛddhavyavahāreṇeti/ vaddhayoḥ jñānavatoḥ vyavahāraḥ pravṛttiḥ
śabdaprayogaśca vṛddhavyavahāraḥ/ prakṛtipratyapādīnāmiti/ 'bhū
sattāyām' ityādivyākaraṇāt bhūprabhṛtīnāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ
sattādirūpārthe śaktigrahaḥ/ 'laḥ karmaṇi ca bhāve cākarmakebhyaḥ'
ityādivyākaraṇāt pratyayasyārthaṃviśeṣe śaktigrahaḥ/ adhastāddarśita
iti/ pūrvamupamānapariccheda darśitaḥ/ nanu 'apyekadantaheramba'
ityādikośe ekadantaherambādiśabdānāṃ paryāyatvena
ekārthavācakatayā kathaṃ dvandvasamāsaḥ/ padārthabheda eva
dvandvasamāsāṅgīkārādityatrāha - tatraikadantādīti/ ete śabdāḥ
etādṛśārthabodhakā iti jñāpanārthaṃ hi kośaḥ/ tatraikadantādayaḥ
śabdāḥ tattadānupūrvīkaśabdarthakā eveti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Regarding 'by the behavior of the learned' (<s>vṛddhavyavahāreṇa</s>) — the behavior, that is, the activity and the usage of words by two learned persons possessing knowledge, is called <s>vṛddhavyavahāra</s> (behavior of the learned). Regarding 'of verbal roots and suffixes' (<s>prakṛtipratyayādīnām</s>) — from grammatical rules such as '<s>bhū sattāyām</s>' (the root <s>bhū</s> means existence), the apprehension of the <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) of verbal roots like <s>bhū</s> etc. in meanings of the form of existence and so on is obtained. From grammatical rules such as '<s>laḥ karmaṇi ca bhāve cākarmakebhyaḥ</s>' (verbal suffixes denote the object, and the state from intransitive verbs), the apprehension of <s>śakti</s> of the suffix in a particular meaning is obtained. Regarding 'as shown below' — it was shown earlier in the section on <s>upamāna</s> (comparison). Now, an objection: in a lexicon such as '<s>apyekadantaheramba</s>' etc., since the words <s>ekadanta</s>, <s>heramba</s>, etc. are synonyms denoting a single meaning, how can there be a <s>dvandva</s> compound? Since a <s>dvandva</s> compound is accepted only where there is a difference in the referents, to this he says — 'therein <s>ekadanta</s> etc.' The lexicon is for the purpose of indicating that these words convey such-and-such meanings. The purport is that therein the words <s>ekadanta</s> etc. have as their meanings the words with their respective sequential arrangements.

children.text:
dīpikāyām
vyutpitsurbāla ityādi/ kaścit bālakaḥ gavādipadānāṃ kasminnarthe
śaktiriti jijñāsate/ sa kadācit kenacit prerakeṇa ācāryādināṃ
śiṣyaṃ prati uktaṃ 'gāmānaya' iti vākyaṃ śṛṇvataḥ śiṣyasya gavānayanaṃ
paśyati/ tataḥ gavānayanarūpakriyāṃ prati kāraṇabhūtaṃ
prayatnamanuminoti/ tataḥ kiñcitkriyāviṣayakaprayatnaṃ prati
tatkriyāviṣayakajñānasya kāraṇatvāt tādṛśajñānaṃ prati
prayojakavṛddhaprayuktaṃ vākyameva kāraṇamityanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ
niścinoti/ tataśca prayojyavṛddhasya gokarmakānayanaviṣayakaṃ jñānaṃ
'gāmānaya' iti vākyajanyamiti niścinoti/ tatra
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: regarding '<s>vyutpitsurbāla</s>' (a child desiring to learn) etc. — A certain child desires to know in what meaning the words such as <s>go</s> (cow) etc. have their <s>śakti</s> (denotative power). He sometimes, upon some instigator instructing a disciple of a teacher etc., observes the disciple who hears the sentence 'bring the cow' (<s>gāmānaya</s>) bringing the cow. From that, he infers the effort that is the cause of the action in the form of bringing the cow. Then, since knowledge having a particular action as its object is the cause of effort directed toward that action, he ascertains through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) that the sentence uttered by the instigating learned person is itself the cause of such knowledge. And then he ascertains that the knowledge of the prompted learned person concerning bringing with the cow as object is produced by the sentence '<s>gāmānaya</s>' (bring the cow). Therein,

children.text:
gopadasya
gotvaviśiṣṭe śaktiṃ vinā gopadārthasya karmatve 'nvayāsambhavāt
gopadasya gotvaviśiṣṭe śaktirityapi niścinoti ityanayā rītyā
vyavahārasya śaktigrāhakatvamiti bhāvaḥ/ pravṛttiśabdaḥ prayatnaparaḥ/
children.translated_text: without the <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) of the word <s>go</s> in what is qualified by <s>gotva</s> (cowness), since the syntactic connection of the meaning of the word <s>go</s> as the object would be impossible, he also ascertains that the word <s>go</s> has <s>śakti</s> in what is qualified by <s>gotva</s>. The purport is that in this manner, behavior (<s>vyavahāra</s>) is the means of apprehending <s>śakti</s>. The word <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity) here means effort (<s>prayatna</s>).

children.text:
nanu pravṛttijanakasya
gavānayanaviṣayakajñānasya vākyajanyatvāt vākyasyaiva gokarmakānayane
śaktiḥ kalpyatāmityatrāha - prakāśikāyām vākyasyeti/ viśiṣṭer'the
iti/ gokarmakatvaviśiṣṭānayanarūpe vākyārthe ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca
padaśaktyā upasthitānāmarthānāṃ anvayarūpasya vākyārthasya
samabhivyāhārarūpākāṅkṣayaiva bhānopapattyā vākyārthe na śaktiriti
bhāvaḥ/ api ca gopadasyānayanānvitagavi śaktisvīkāre 'gāṃ badhāna'
ityatrāpi tādṛśagobodhopapattiḥ/ evamānayapadasya gokarmakānayane
śaktisvīkāre 'aśvamānaya' ityatrāpi tadbodhāpattiḥ/ ataḥ gopadasya
gotvaviśiṣṭe ānayapadasya ānayanatvaviśiṣṭe ca śaktirniścīyate/
kriyākārakayoranvitatvaṃ tu samabhivyāhāralabhyamityāvāpodvāpābhyāṃ
suniścayam/ etadabhiprāyeṇaiva āvāpodvāpopanyāsa iti bhāvaḥ/
vyutpatyāśrayo bhavatīti/ śaktiniścayavān bhavatītyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, since the knowledge concerning bringing with the cow as object, which generates the activity, is produced by the sentence, let the <s>śakti</s> be postulated for the sentence itself in the action of bringing with cow as object — to this he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: 'of the sentence.' 'In the qualified meaning' — meaning: in the sentence-meaning of the form of bringing qualified by having the cow as object. And thus, since the cognition of the sentence-meaning, which is the syntactic connection of the meanings presented through the <s>śakti</s> of the individual words, is explained through <s>sāmabhivyāhāra</s> (mutual co-occurrence) alone as <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> (expectancy), there is no <s>śakti</s> in the sentence-meaning — this is the purport. Moreover, if one accepts the <s>śakti</s> of the word <s>go</s> in the cow as connected with bringing, then even in '<s>gāṃ badhāna</s>' (tie the cow), there would follow the cognition of such a cow. Similarly, if one accepts the <s>śakti</s> of the word <s>ānaya</s> (bring) in bringing with cow as object, then even in '<s>aśvamānaya</s>' (bring the horse), that cognition would follow. Therefore, the <s>śakti</s> of the word <s>go</s> is ascertained in what is qualified by <s>gotva</s> (cowness), and the <s>śakti</s> of the word <s>ānaya</s> in what is qualified by the property of being an act of bringing. The syntactic connection of action and <s>kāraka</s> (case-relation) is obtained through <s>sāmabhivyāhāra</s> (mutual co-occurrence), and this is well-established through the method of inclusion and exclusion (<s>āvāpodvāpa</s>). It is with this intention that the illustration of <s>āvāpodvāpa</s> is given — this is the purport. 'Becomes the basis of <s>vyutpatti</s>' means: becomes one who has ascertained the <s>śakti</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text:
vivaraṇādyatheti/
tatsamānārthakapadāntareṇa tadarthakathanaṃ vivaraṇam/ 'śaktigrahaṃ
vyākaraṇopamāna' ityādiślokānuktānāṃ
aṅgulinirdeśapūrvakaśabdaprayogādīnāmapi śaktigrāhakatvaṃ
manasikṛtyoktam - alaṃ pallaviteneti/
children.translated_text: Regarding 'by explanation' (<s>vivaraṇa</s>) etc. — <s>vivaraṇa</s> (explanation) is the statement of the meaning of a word through another word having the same meaning. Having kept in mind that pointing with the finger accompanied by the use of the word, etc., which are not mentioned in the verse '<s>śaktigrahaṃ vyākaraṇopamāna</s>' etc., are also means of apprehending <s>śakti</s>, he says — 'enough of elaboration' (<s>alaṃ pallavitena</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
śabdānāṃ
siddhaparatvamapīti nirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of the fact that words can also denote established entities (<s>siddha</s>)

children.text:
nanu sarvatra
kāryaparatvāt vyavahārasya kāryaparavākya eva vyutpattiḥ na siddhapara
iti cet - na/ 'kāśyāṃ tribhuvanatilako bhūpatirāste' ityādau
siddhe 'pi vyavahārāt 'vikasitapadme madhukaraḥ tiṣṭhati' ityādau
prasiddhapadasamabhivyāhārāt siddhe 'pi madhukarādivyutpattidarśanāt
ca/
children.translated_text: Now, if one objects that since behavioral usage everywhere pertains to actions (<s>kārya</s>), <s>vyutpatti</s> (semantic learning) occurs only in sentences referring to actions and not to established entities (<s>siddha</s>) — no; because there is usage even regarding established entities in cases like '<s>kāśyāṃ tribhuvanatilako bhūpatirāste</s>' (in <s>Kāśī</s>, the ornament of the three worlds, the king resides), and because <s>vyutpatti</s> of words like <s>madhukara</s> (bee) etc. is observed even in established meanings through co-occurrence with well-known words in cases like '<s>vikasitapadme madhukaraḥ tiṣṭhati</s>' (the bee rests on the blossomed lotus).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
vyavahārasya/
kāryaparatvāditi yojanā/ kāryaparatvaṃ ca
kṛtisādhyānayanādirūpakriyātātparyakatvam/ vyutpattiḥ - śaktigrahaḥ/
vyavacchedyaṃ sphuṭayati - na siddheti/ siddhe 'pi vyavahārāditi/ tathā ca
siddhe 'pi śaktigrahastvāvaśyakaḥ/ anyathā tatrānubhavasiddhasya śabdabodhasya
apalāpāpatteriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: The construction is: 'of behavior — because of pertaining to actions.' Pertaining to actions (<s>kāryaparatva</s>) means having as its purport an action of the form of bringing etc. that is accomplishable by effort (<s>kṛti</s>). <s>Vyutpatti</s> means apprehension of <s>śakti</s>. He clarifies what is being excluded — 'not in established entities.' 'Even regarding established entities, from the behavioral usage' — and thus the apprehension of <s>śakti</s> even in established entities is absolutely necessary; otherwise, the denial of <s>śābdabodha</s> (verbal cognition) that is established by experience in such cases would result — this is the purport.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
siddhe 'pi śaktigraha
ityatra siddhaśabdaḥ kriyāvyatiriktaparaḥ/
children.translated_text: In 'apprehension of <s>śakti</s> even in established entities,' the word <s>siddha</s> (established) refers to what is other than an action (<s>kriyā</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: lakṣaṇānirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification)

children.text:
lakṣaṇāpi
śabdavṛttiḥ/ śakyasambandho lakṣaṇā/ gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityatra
gaṅgāpadavācyapravāhasambandhādeva tīropasthitau tīre 'pi śaktirna
kalpyate/ saindhavādau lavaṇāśvayoḥ parasparasambandhābhāvāt
nānāśaktikalpanam/
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) is also a function of words (<s>śabdavṛtti</s>). <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> is the relation with the denoted meaning (<s>śakyasambandha</s>). In '<s>gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' (the hamlet is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>), through the relation with the river-flow that is the denoted meaning of the word <s>gaṅgā</s>, when the bank is presented, <s>śakti</s> (primary denotative power) is not postulated even for the bank. In cases like <s>saindhava</s> (which means both salt and horse), since there is no mutual relation between salt and horse, multiple <s>śaktis</s> (denotative powers) are postulated.

children.text:
lakṣaṇā trividhā -
jahallakṣaṇā, ajahallakṣaṇā, jahadajahallakṣaṇā ceti/ yatra
vācyārthasyānvayābhāvaḥ tatra jahallakṣaṇā/ yathā mañcāḥ krośantīti/ yatra
vācyārthasyāpyanvayaḥ tatra ajahaditi/ yathā chatriṇo gacchantīti/ yatra
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) is of three kinds — <s>jahallakṣaṇā</s> (exclusive secondary signification), <s>ajahallakṣaṇā</s> (inclusive secondary signification), and <s>jahadajahallakṣaṇā</s> (partially exclusive secondary signification). Where there is no syntactic connection of the denoted meaning, there is <s>jahallakṣaṇā</s>; for example, 'the platforms are crying' (<s>mañcāḥ krośanti</s>). Where even the denoted meaning has syntactic connection, there is <s>ajahallakṣaṇā</s>; for example, 'the umbrella-bearers go' (<s>chatriṇo gacchanti</s>). Where,

children.text:
vācyaikadeśatyāgena
ekadeśānvayaḥ tatra jahadajahaditi/ yathā tattvamasīti/
children.translated_text: by abandoning a part of the denoted meaning, there is syntactic connection of a part, there is <s>jahadajahallakṣaṇā</s>; for example, '<s>tattvamasi</s>' (That thou art).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
tīre 'pi śaktirna
kalpyata iti/ gaṅgāpadasyeti śeṣaḥ/ nanu evaṃ saindhavādipadānāṃ
nānārthakatvānupapattiḥ, ekatra śaktiḥ anyatra lakṣaṇetyeva nirvāhādata
āha - saindhavādāviti/ ādinā haryādiparigrahaḥ/ sambandhābhāvāditi/
saṃyogādirūpasambandhābhāvādityarthaḥ/
idamupalakṣaṇam-prasiddhayorarthayoḥ kutra lakṣaṇetyatra
vinigamakābhāvena ubhayatra śaktikalpanasyāvaśyakateti/
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>śakti</s> is not postulated even for the bank' — the complement is 'of the word <s>gaṅgā</s>.' Now, an objection: in that case, the multiple-meaning nature of words like <s>saindhava</s> etc. would not be possible, since it could be resolved by positing <s>śakti</s> in one meaning and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in the other. To this he says — 'in <s>saindhava</s> etc.' The word 'etc.' includes <s>hari</s> and similar words. 'Due to the absence of relation' — meaning: due to the absence of a relation of the form of contact (<s>saṃyoga</s>) etc. This is an <s>upalakṣaṇa</s> (suggestive example) — where two well-known meanings exist, in determining where <s>lakṣaṇā</s> applies, since there is no ground for deciding one way or the other, the postulation of <s>śakti</s> in both is necessary.

children.text:
mañcā iti/ mañcapadaṃ
mañcasthapuruṣe lākṣaṇikam/ vācyāryasya
krośanakartṛtvānvayābhāvādityarthaḥ/ vācyārthasyāpīti/ apinā
lakṣyasamuccayaḥ/ chatriṇa iti/ ekasārthavāhitvena chatryacchatriṣu
gamanakartṛtvānvayaḥ/ tātparyānupapattireva lakṣaṇābījam/ na ca
chatrītyasya matubarthakenipratyayāntasya padasamūharūpatvena
tacchakyāprasiddhyā tatsambandharūpalakṣaṇāyā abhāvena
kathamidamudāharaṇamiti vācyam/ 'pratipādyasambandha eva lakṣaṇā'
ityetadabhiprāyeṇa tadudāharaṇadānāt/ anyathā 'kākebhyo dadhi
rakṣyatām' ityādyudāhartavyam/ tatra kākapadasya
kākataditarasādhāraṇadadhyupavātakatvāvacchinnaparatvāt/
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>mañcāḥ</s>' (the platforms) — the word <s>mañca</s> is used in a secondary sense (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) for the person standing on the platform, because the denoted meaning cannot have syntactic connection with being the agent of crying — this is the meaning. 'Even the denoted meaning' — the word 'even' (<s>api</s>) indicates the inclusion of the secondary referent as well. Regarding '<s>chatriṇaḥ</s>' (umbrella-bearers) — since they are part of one group (<s>ekasārthavāhitva</s>), there is syntactic connection of being the agent of going for both those who carry umbrellas and those who do not. The impossibility of the intended purport (<s>tātparya</s>) alone is the ground for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. And one should not object: how can this be an example, since the word <s>chatrī</s>, being a word ending in the <s>ini</s> suffix with possessive meaning (<s>matubarthaka</s>), being in the form of a group of words, its denoted meaning is not well-established, and hence <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in the form of relation with that denoted meaning is absent? Because this example is given with the intention that '<s>lakṣaṇā</s> is the relation with what is to be conveyed' (<s>pratipādyasambandha</s>). Otherwise, one should cite the example '<s>kākebhyo dadhi rakṣyatām</s>' (protect the curds from the crows). There, the word <s>kāka</s> (crow) has as its secondary meaning what is delimited by the capacity to destroy curds, which is common to crows and other creatures.

children.text:
kecittu - chatrapadasya
ekasārthe lakṣaṇā/ taddhitārthaḥ sambandhī/ tathā caikasārthaṃsambandhino
gacchantītyanvayabodhaḥ ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: Some, however, say — <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word <s>chatra</s> (umbrella) is in the group traveling together (<s>ekasārtha</s>). The meaning of the <s>taddhita</s> suffix is 'possessor.' And thus the verbal cognition is: 'those who are possessors of the group traveling together are going.'

children.text:
tattvamasīti/
tatpadavācye sarvajñatvādiviśiṣṭe
tvaṃpadavācyasyāntaḥ-karaṇādiviśiṣṭasyābhedānvayānupapattyā ubhayatra
viśeṣaṇāṃśaparityāgaḥ/ tathā ca tatpadalakṣyasya śuddhasya tvaṃpadalakṣyeṇa
saha abhedānvayopapattirityabhiprāyaḥ/ idamudāharaṇaṃ tu
jīvabrahmaṇoraikyaṃ bruvatāṃ brahmavādināṃ matābhiprāyeṇa/ naiyāyikamate
tasyāsaṃmatatvāt/ naiyāyikamatarītyā tu 'sāyam devadatta'
ityādau tattāṃśasya idānīmasambhavāddhānam, idantvāṃśasya
sambhavādahānamiti jahadajahallakṣaṇāmācakṣate/
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>tattvamasi</s>' (That thou art) — since the identity-relation cannot hold between the denoted meaning of the word <s>tat</s> (That), which is qualified by omniscience etc., and the denoted meaning of the word <s>tvam</s> (thou), which is qualified by the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) etc., there is abandonment of the qualifying aspects on both sides. Thus, the intended meaning is that the identity-relation becomes possible between the pure entity indicated by <s>tat</s> through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> and the entity indicated by <s>tvam</s> through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. This example, however, is given according to the view of the <s>Brahmavādins</s> (Advaitins) who hold the identity of <s>jīva</s> (individual self) and <s>Brahman</s>, since this is not accepted in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> (logician's) view. According to the method of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, in cases like '<s>sāyaṃ devadattaḥ</s>' (this is the same <s>Devadatta</s> [seen before]), the 'that'-aspect is abandoned because of the impossibility of [past time] now, while the 'this'-aspect is not abandoned because it is possible — thus they describe <s>jahadajahallakṣaṇā</s>.

children.text:
pare tu - 'ghaṭo
nityaḥ' ityādau ghaṭatvasyeva 'so 'yam devadatta' ityādau
tattāṃśasyopalakṣaṇatayā bhāne na kiñcit bādhakamiti kiṃ
jahadajahallakṣaṇayeti vadanti/
children.translated_text: Others, however, say — in cases like '<s>ghaṭo nityaḥ</s>' (the pot is eternal), just as <s>ghaṭatva</s> (potness) appears as an <s>upalakṣaṇa</s> (suggestive indicator), similarly in '<s>so'yaṃ devadattaḥ</s>' (this is that <s>Devadatta</s>), since the 'that'-aspect appears as an <s>upalakṣaṇa</s>, there is no obstruction — so what need is there for <s>jahadajahallakṣaṇā</s>?

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
saṃyogādirūpasambandhābhāvāditi/ tathā ca
śakyasambandharūpalakṣaṇāyā asambhavāt lavaṇāśvayorūbhayoreva
saindhavapadasya śaktirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Due to the absence of a relation of the form of contact etc.' — and thus, since <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in the form of relation with the denoted meaning (<s>śakyasambandha</s>) is impossible, the word <s>saindhava</s> has <s>śakti</s> (primary denotative power) in both salt and horse — this is the meaning.

children.text:
mañcasthapuruṣa iti/
mañcasthaśiśāviti yuktam, rodanādirūpakrośanakartṛtvasya tatraiva
svārasikatvādityāhuḥ/ vācyārthasyeti/ mañcapadaśakyārthasya mañcasya
samabhivyāhṛtakrośatipadārthakrośanakartṛtvānvayavirahāt
anvayānupapattirūpalakṣaṇābījasattvāt - mañcapadasya mañcasthe puruṣe
lakṣaṇeti bhāvaḥ/ tathā ca yādṛśapade
vācyārthaviśeṣyaketarapadārthānvayaviṣayakaśābdabodhajanakatvaṃ na
sambhavati tatra pade jahallakṣaṇā, yā lakṣaṇā vācyārthaṃ tyajati sā
jahallakṣaṇā, jahatī ca sā lakṣaṇā ceti karmadhārayāt/ athavā śakyārthaṃ
jahataḥ tyajataḥ padasya lakṣaṇā jahallakṣaṇeti ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣaḥ/ yatra
śakyārtho na parityajyate śakyārthāparityāgena lakṣyārthabodhaḥ tatra
ajahallakṣaṇā/ 'yathā chatriṇo gacchanti' iti/ atra chatripadasya
chatryacchatrighaṭitasamudāye lakṣaṇā/ ekasārthavāhitveneti/
ekasamudāyaghaṭakatvenetyarthaḥ/ tṛtīyāyāḥ vaiśiṣṭyamarthaḥ/ tasya
chatryacchatriṣvanvayaḥ/ chatripadalakṣyeṣu ekasamudāyaghaṭakatvaviśiṣṭeṣu
chatryacchatriṣu gamanakartṛtvānvaya iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Regarding 'the person standing on the platform' (<s>mañcasthapuruṣa</s>) — it would be more appropriate to say 'the child standing on the platform' (<s>mañcasthaśiśau</s>), since the capacity for crying in the form of wailing etc. is natural only there — so some say. Regarding 'of the denoted meaning' — since there is the ground for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in the form of the impossibility of syntactic connection, namely the absence of connection between the denoted meaning of the word <s>mañca</s> (platform) and the meaning of the co-occurring word <s>krośati</s> (cries), i.e., being the agent of crying, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word <s>mañca</s> is in the person standing on the platform — this is the purport. And thus, in whatever word the generation of <s>śābdabodha</s> (verbal cognition) having as its content the syntactic connection with the meaning of the other word, with the denoted meaning as the qualificand, is not possible — in that word there is <s>jahallakṣaṇā</s>. <s>Jahallakṣaṇā</s> is the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> that abandons the denoted meaning — it is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound (the abandoning <s>lakṣaṇā</s>). Alternatively, it is a <s>ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣa</s> compound: the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of a word that abandons, that is, gives up its denoted meaning. Where the denoted meaning is not abandoned, that is, where the cognition of the secondary meaning occurs without abandoning the denoted meaning, there is <s>ajahallakṣaṇā</s>. 'For example, the umbrella-bearers go' (<s>chatriṇo gacchanti</s>) — here <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word <s>chatrī</s> is in the group composed of those with and without umbrellas. 'By virtue of being part of one caravan' (<s>ekasārthavāhitva</s>) — meaning: by virtue of being a constituent of one group. The meaning of the third case-ending is the specification. Its syntactic connection is with those who carry umbrellas and those who do not, who are the secondary referents of the word <s>chatrī</s> — the purport is that there is syntactic connection of being the agent of going with those who carry and do not carry umbrellas, who are qualified by being constituents of one group.

children.text:
nanvanvayānupapattirna
lakṣaṇāyā bījam/ 'yaṣṭīḥ praveśaya' ityādau yaṣṭipadavācyānāṃ
yaṣṭīnāmapi
praveśanakarmatvānvayasambhavenānvayānupapattirūpabījābhāvāt
yaṣṭipadasya yaṣṭidhare lakṣaṇāyā ayogādityata āha -
tātparyānupapattireva lakṣaṇābījamiti/ yaṣṭidharatātparyeṇaiva 'yaṣṭīḥ
praveśaya' iti vākyaprayogāt lakṣaṇānaṅgīkāre
children.translated_text: Now, an objection: the impossibility of syntactic connection is not the ground for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. In '<s>yaṣṭīḥ praveśaya</s>' (make the staffs enter), since there is the possibility of syntactic connection of the denoted sticks themselves as objects of the action of entering, the ground in the form of impossibility of syntactic connection is absent, and hence <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word <s>yaṣṭi</s> (staff) in the staff-bearer would be unjustified. To this he says — 'the impossibility of the intended purport (<s>tātparya</s>) alone is the ground for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.' Since the sentence '<s>yaṣṭīḥ praveśaya</s>' is used with the purport of the staff-bearers, if <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is not accepted,

children.text:
tādṛśatātparyaṃ
nopapadyeteti lakṣaṇābījaṃ tatrāpyastīti bhāvaḥ/
ekakāreṇānvayānupapattivyavacchedaḥ/
children.translated_text: such a purport would not be possible — hence the ground for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> exists there too — this is the purport. The word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>) excludes the impossibility of syntactic connection [as the ground].

children.text:
nanu tārkikamate śaktaṃ
padamiti padalakṣaṇāt chatrin iti vākyameva/ chatrapadasya chatre
śaktatvāt inipratyayasya sambandhe śaktatvāt
prakṛtipratyayarūpapadadvayasamūharūpatvāt chatripadasya/ vākye ca
śaktyabhāvāt vākyaśakyārthāprasiddhyā śakyasambandharūpā lakṣaṇā na
sambhavati/ tathā ca chatrinnityasya ajahallakṣaṇodāharaṇatvaṃ na sambhavatīti
śaṅkate-na ca chatrītyasyeti/ matubarthaketi/ sambandhārthaketyarthaḥ/
pratipādyasambandha iti/ bodhyārthasambandha
children.translated_text: Now, an objection: according to the logicians' (<s>tārkika</s>) view, since a word is 'that which has <s>śakti</s>' according to the definition of a word, <s>chatrī</s> is itself a sentence [composed of the stem <s>chatra</s> having <s>śakti</s> in 'umbrella' and the <s>ini</s> suffix having <s>śakti</s> in the relation of possession, being in the form of a collection of two words — stem and suffix]. And since a sentence lacks <s>śakti</s>, and the denoted meaning of the sentence is not well-established, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in the form of relation with the denoted meaning cannot occur. Thus, the status of <s>chatrī</s> as an example of <s>ajahallakṣaṇā</s> would not be possible — this is the objection raised with 'nor should one say regarding <s>chatrī</s>.' 'With possessive meaning' (<s>matubarthaka</s>) — meaning: having the sense of relation. 'The relation with what is to be conveyed' (<s>pratipādyasambandha</s>) — the relation with the meaning to be cognized,

children.text:
ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca
chatrinniti vākyaśakyārthāprasiddhāvapi tādṛśavākyajanyabodhaviṣayo
yor'thaḥ chatravāniti tatsambandhasya samudāye sattvāt vākye 'pi
lakṣaṇopapadyata iti bhāvaḥ/ anyatheti/ śakyasambandha eva lakṣaṇeti
svīkāra ityarthaḥ/ kākataditareti/ kākataditarabiḍālādisādhāraṇaṃ
yat dadhināśakatvaṃ tadavacchinne kākapadasya lakṣaṇetyarthaḥ/
dadhināśakatvena rūpeṇa kākasyāpi bodhāt ajahallakṣaṇātvam/
children.translated_text: this is the meaning. And thus, even though the denoted meaning of the sentence <s>chatrī</s> is not well-established, the meaning that is the content of the cognition produced by such a sentence, namely 'one who possesses an umbrella' — since the relation with that exists in the collection, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is possible even in the sentence — this is the purport. 'Otherwise' (<s>anyathā</s>) — meaning: if one accepts that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is only the relation with the denoted meaning. Regarding '<s>kākatadidara</s>' (other than crows etc.) — the meaning is that the word <s>kāka</s> (crow) has <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in what is delimited by the capacity to destroy curds, which is common to crows and other creatures like cats etc. Since even the crow is cognized in the form of having the capacity to destroy curds, it is a case of <s>ajahallakṣaṇā</s> (inclusive secondary signification).

children.text:
padalakṣaṇayaiva nirvāhaṃ
vadatāṃ matamāha - kecittviti/ ekasārtha iti/ ekasamudāyatva
ityarthaḥ/ chatriṇo gacchantītyasya ekasamudāyatvavavanto
gacchantītyarthaḥ/ samudāyatvaṃ cāpekṣābuddhiviśeṣaviṣayatvam/ atha vā
chatrapadasya ekasamudāyor'thaḥ, ini pratyayasya
ghaṭakatvarūpasambandhaviśiṣṭor'thaḥ/ āhuḥ ityasvarasodbhāvanam/
tadbījaṃ tu chatrapadasya chatrighaṭitasamudāyatvārthakatve
chatrapadajanyaśābdabodhe chatrapadamukhyārthasśya chatrasya mukhyaviśeṣyatayā
bhānābhāvāt atratyalakṣaṇāyā ajahatsvārthatvānupapattiriti/
children.translated_text: He states the view of those who maintain that it can be accomplished through word-denotation alone — 'some, however,' etc. 'Of one meaning' — the meaning is: having the nature of one collective group. 'Those having umbrellas go' means: those having the nature of one group go. And group-ness is being the object of a particular cognition of expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>). Alternatively, the word 'umbrella' has the meaning 'one group,' and the suffix '-in' has the meaning qualified by the relation of constituent-hood. 'They say' expresses [the author's] dissatisfaction. The reason for that is: if the word 'umbrella' meant group-ness constituted by umbrella-holders, then in the verbal cognition generated by the word 'umbrella,' since the umbrella — the primary meaning of the umbrella-word — would not appear as the primary qualificand, the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) here would not be of the non-abandoning type (<s>ajahatsvārtha</s>).

children.text:
atra tatpadavācya
ityādi/ tattvamasītyatra tatpadasya sarvajñatvādiviśiṣṭacaitanyaṃ
vācyor'thaḥ/ tvaṃpadasya antaḥkaraṇaviśiṣṭacaitanyaṃ vācyor'thaḥ/
samānavibhakterabhedor'thaḥ/ sa ca viśiṣṭayorbādhitaḥ/ ataḥ
vācyārthaikadeśayoḥ sarvajñatva-antaḥkaraṇarūpaviśeṣaṇayoḥ tyāgena
caitanyamātraṃ dvābhyāṃ padābhyāṃ lakṣyate/ so 'yaṃ devadatta
ityādāviti/ tatpadasya taddeśatatkālavṛttitvaviśiṣṭor'thaḥ/
idaṃpadasya etaddeśaitatkālaviśiṣṭor'thaṃḥ/ viśiṣṭayoraikyaṃ ca
bādhitam/ ataḥ tatpadaśakyārthaviśiṣṭaikadeśasya
tattaddeśatattatkālavṛttitvarūpaviśeṣaṇasya tyāgena viśeṣye devadatte
tatpadasya lakṣaṇā/ evaṃ ca yatra viśeṣaṇasya śakyaikadeśasya tyāgena
viśeṣyasya śakyaikadeśasya bodhastatra jahadajahallakṣaṇetyuktaṃ bhavati/
children.translated_text: Here, 'the referent of the word "tat"' etc. In '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art), the denoted meaning of the word 'tat' (that) is consciousness qualified by omniscience and the like. The denoted meaning of the word 'tvam' (thou) is consciousness qualified by the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>). The same case-ending conveys identity. And that [identity] is contradicted with respect to the qualified [meanings]. Therefore, by abandoning the qualifying elements of each denoted meaning — the qualifiers of omniscience and internal-organ-nature — pure consciousness alone is indicated (<s>lakṣita</s>) by both words. In 'He is this <s>Devadatta</s>' and the like — the meaning of the word 'tat' (that) is qualified by existing-in-that-place-and-that-time; the meaning of the word 'idam' (this) is qualified by this-place-and-this-time. And the identity of the qualified [meanings] is contradicted. Therefore, by abandoning the qualifying part of the denoted meaning of 'tat' — namely the qualification of existing-in-that-place-and-that-time — <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word 'tat' operates on the qualificand <s>Devadatta</s>. And thus, where the qualificand — which is part of the denoted meaning — is cognized by abandoning the qualifier — which is another part of the denoted meaning — there is <s>jahadajahallakṣaṇā</s> (partly-abandoning secondary signification) — this is what is stated.

children.text:
pare tviti/ yathā
ghaṭo 'nitya ityatra ghaṭatvaviśiṣṭe anityatvaviśiṣṭābhedo na
sambhavati, ghaṭatve 'nityatvābhāvāditi
ghaṭatvopalakṣite 'nityatvānvayasvīkāreṇopapattiḥ, tathā so 'yaṃ
devadatta ityādāvapi tattopalakṣite idantvānvayenopapattyā
jahadajahallakṣaṇā māstviti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Others, however' — just as in 'the pot is non-eternal,' identity of what is qualified by pot-ness with what is qualified by non-eternality is not possible, because non-eternality is absent in pot-ness, and hence the matter is resolved by accepting the connection of non-eternality with what is merely indicated by pot-ness — similarly, in 'He is this <s>Devadatta</s>' and the like too, since the matter can be resolved by the connection of this-ness with what is indicated by that-ness, <s>jahadajahallakṣaṇā</s> need not be accepted — this is the purport.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: gauṇīvyañjanayorvṛtyantaratvakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of the claim that <s>gauṇī</s> (figurative usage) and <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) are separate types of signification

children.text:
gauṇyapi lakṣaṇaiva
lakṣyamāṇaguṇasambandhasvarūpā/ yathā agnirmāṇavaka iti/ vyañjanāpi
śaktilakṣaṇāntarbhūtā, śabdaśaktimūlā, arthaśaktimūlā ca anumānādinā
anyathāsiddhā/
children.translated_text: <s>Gauṇī</s> (figurative usage) too is just <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) — of the nature of the relation of the quality being indicated. For example, 'The boy is fire.' <s>Vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) too is included within denotative power (<s>śakti</s>) and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, because the denotative power of the word

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
gauṇyā
vṛttyantaratvaṃ nirācaṣṭe - gauṇyapīti/ nanu 'gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa'
ityatra tīre śakyasya pravāhasyeva 'agnirmāṇavaka' ityādau
māṇavake śakyasya agneḥ sākṣātsambandho na saṃbhavati iti kathaṃ
lakṣaṇayā nirvāha ityata āha - lakṣyamāṇeti/ lakṣyamāṇo yo guṇaḥ
śucitvādiḥ tatsambandharūpāṃ ityarthaḥ/ ayamabhiprāyaḥ - śakyasambandho
hi lakṣaṇā/ sa ca kvacitsākṣātsambandhaḥ, kvacitparamparāsambandhaḥ/ evaṃ ca
śakyasyāgneḥ svaniṣṭhaśucitvavattvasambandha eva lakṣaṇeti/
children.translated_text: He rejects the status of <s>gauṇī</s> as a separate type of signification — '<s>gauṇī</s> too,' etc. Now, in 'the settlement [is] on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' just as the bank is indicated by <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the river-flow which is the denoted meaning, so too in 'the boy is fire,'

children.text:
ālaṅkārikāḥ
punarevamāhuḥ - 'tīre ghoṣa' iti śabdaprayoge svāyatte
'gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ' ityananvitābhidhānaṃ
śaityapāvanatvādipratītyartham/ na ca sā pratītirlakṣaṇayā upapadyate
kevalatīralakṣaṇayaiva anvayānupapattiparihāre
śaityapāvanatvādiviśiṣṭalakṣaṇāyāṃ mānābhāvāt/ tasmāt
vyañjanāvṛttiraṅgīkartavyeti/ tanmataṃ nirasyati -
children.translated_text: The <s>Ālaṅkārikas</s> (rhetoricians), however, state thus: when it is within one's power to use the expression 'the settlement [is] on the bank,' the usage of the non-connected expression 'the settlement [is] on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' [is employed to convey] coolness, sanctity, and the like

children.text:
vyañjanāpīti/
śaktilakṣaṇāntarbhūteti/ ayambhāvaḥ - nānārthakasthale 'dūrasthā bhūdharā
ramyāḥ' ityādau bhūdharaśabdena parvatānāmiva rājñāmapi śaktyaiva
pratītiḥ sambhavati/ 'gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa' ityādau tu
śaityapāvanatvādiviśiṣṭatīrapratītirapi lakṣaṇāsāmrājyādeva/ tatra
lakṣaṇākalpikāyāḥ tātparyānupapattereva sadbhāvāt
children.translated_text: '<s>Vyañjanā</s> too' — 'is included within denotative power and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>' — the idea is as follows: in the case of a word with multiple meanings, as in 'the mountains seen from afar are beautiful,' by the word 'mountain' (<s>bhūdhara</s>)

children.text: kiṃ vyañjanayeti/
children.translated_text: Is it <s>vyañjanā</s>?

children.text:
nanu śabdaśaktimūlāyā
vyañjanāyā anyathāsiddhatve 'pi arthaśaktimūlāyāstasyā nānyathāsiddhiḥ/
tathā hi -
children.translated_text: Now, even if the otherwise-established-ness of <s>vyañjanā</s> that is rooted in the power of the word [is granted], the <s>vyañjanā</s> rooted in the power of the meaning is not otherwise-established. For consider:

children.text:
"gaccha gacchasi cetkānta panthānaḥ santu te
śivāḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Go, if you must go, dear one — may the paths be auspicious for you!

children.text:
mamāpi janma tatraiva
bhūyāt yatra gato bhavān//"
children.translated_text: May my birth too occur in the very place where you have gone!'

children.text:
ityādau 'he priya
tava gamanottaraṃ mama prāṇanāśo bhaviṣyati/ ato na gantavyam'
ityādyartho vyajyate/ na hyatra śaktilakṣaṇābhyāṃ nirvāhaḥ/ itthaṃ ca
vyañjanāyā āvaśyakatetyata āha - arthaśaktimūlā ceti/ castvarthaḥ/
anumānādineti/ anumānaprayogastu - 'iyaṃ
madīyagamanottarakālikaprāṇaviyogavatī vilakṣaṇaśabdaprayoktṛtvāt'
ityādirūpaḥ/ ādinā saṃbhāvanādi parigrahaḥ/
utkaṭaikatarakoṭikasaṃśayassambhāvanā/ autkaṭyaṃ ca viṣayatāviśeṣaḥ/
yadi punarānubhaviko lokānāṃ svarasavāhī 'śabdāt amumarthaṃ
pratyemi' ityanubhavaḥ tadā vaiyañjanikī pratītiḥ
gīrvāṇaguruṇāpyaśakyavāraṇeti vyañjanāsiddhi niṣpratyūhaiveti
mantavyam/
children.translated_text: In such [verses], the meaning 'O beloved, after your departure, the destruction of my life will occur; therefore you should not go' and the like is suggested. For here, neither through denotative power

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
lakṣyamāṇo yo
guṇa ityādi/ lakṣyamāṇaḥ śakyārthavṛttiryo guṇaḥ
tatsajātīyaguṇavattvaṃ gauṇīvṛttirityarthaḥ/ agnirmāṇavaka ityatra
agnipadaśakyārthavahnivṛttiryo guṇaḥ śucitvaṃ
tatsajātīyaśucitvavān māṇavaka iti bodhaḥ/ nanvetādṛśyāḥ
gauṇyā vṛtteḥ kathaṃ śakyasambandharūpalakṣaṇāyāmantarbhāva ityatrāha -
ayamabhiprāya iti/ śakyārthapratiyogikaḥ sambandho lakṣaṇā/ sambandhaśca
sākṣātparamparāsādhāraṇaḥ/ gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityādau
gaṅgāpadaśakyārthasya saṃyogarūpaḥ sākṣātsambandhastīre 'sti/
agnirmāṇavaka ityatra tu śakyārthasyāgneḥ
svavṛttiguṇasajātīyaguṇavattvarūpaḥ paramparāsambandhaḥ māṇavake 'sti/
ubhayorapi sambandhayorlakṣaṇātvameveti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The quality being indicated' and so forth — the meaning is: <s>gauṇī</s> signification is the possession of a quality of the same kind as the quality that is being indicated, i.e. that resides in the denoted meaning. In 'the boy is fire,' since the boy possesses fierceness, which is of the same kind as the heat that is the quality of fire — the denoted meaning — through the connection with that similar quality, the word 'fire' denotes the boy through <s>gauṇī lakṣaṇā</s>.

children.text:
vyañjanākhyāmatiriktāṃ
vṛttiṃ vadatāmālaṅkārikāṇāṃ matamanuvadati - ālaṅkārikāḥ
punariti/ yadi 'gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa' ityādau tīravṛttirghoṣa
ityākārakabodho vivakṣitaḥ, tarhi tīravācakaṃ śabdameva prayuñjīta
tīre ghoṣa iti/ ghoṣānanvitārthavācakaṃ gaṅgāpadaṃ ca prayuñjīta/
ato 'tra śakyārthavṛttiśaityapāvanatvādirūpor'tho 'pi ghoṣe vivakṣitaḥ/
sa ca 'tīre ghoṣa' ityato na budhyeta/ gaṅgāpadaprayoge tu
tatsāmarthyāt gaṅgāpravāhagataśaityapāvanatvādirvyajyata iti vaktuṃ
śakyate/ na ca gaṅgāpadasyaiva śaityapāvanatvādiviśiṣṭatīre
lakṣaṇāstu, tathā ca lakṣaṇayaiva śaityapāvanatvādipratītyupapatteḥ
vyañjanayā na prayojanamiti vācyam/ anvayānupapattirhi lakṣaṇābījam/
sā ca tīralakṣaṇayaiva parihartuṃ śakyeti śaityapāvanatvādilakṣaṇāyāṃ
pramāṇābhāvāt/ tasmāt vyañjanākhyā atiriktā vṛttiḥ svīkaraṇīyā,
yā śaktilakṣaṇābhyāmanavagamyamarthaṃ pratyāyayatītyālaṅkārikāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: He restates the view of the <s>Ālaṅkārikas</s> who advocate a distinct signification called <s>vyañjanā</s> — 'the <s>Ālaṅkārikas</s>, again,' etc. If in 'the settlement [is] on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' and the like,

children.text: bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: the purport.

children.text:
ayaṃ bhāva ityādi/
'dūrastho bhūdharo ramya' ityatra bhūdharaśabdavācyasya parvatasya
dūrasthitasya ramyatvaṃ prakṛtor'thaḥ/ asthiracittatvāt rājāno 'pi
dūrasthā eva ramyā ityaprakṛtor'tho 'pyatra pratīyate/ sā ca pratītiḥ
bhūdharaśabdaśaktimūlā/ tathā ca nānārthasthale arthaprakaraṇādinā
nivāritasyāprakṛtārthasya pratītiḥ yadbalāt bhavati sā
śabdaśaktimūlāvyañjanā ityālaṅkārikāḥ/ tatra bhūdharaśabdena
parvatānāmiva rājñāmapi śabdaśaktyaiva pratītisambhavāt nāsti
vyañjanāyāḥ
children.translated_text: 'The idea is as follows' and so forth — in 'the mountain seen from afar is beautiful,' the beauty of the mountain — the denotation of the word <s>bhūdhara</s> — when seen from a distance is the primary meaning;

children.text:
āvaśyakateti
naiyāyikāḥ/ evaṃ gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityādau gaṅgāpadasya
śaityapāvanatvādiviśiṣṭatīre lakṣaṇāṅgīkāreṇaiva
śaityādipratītirupapadyate/ yadyapyatrānvayānupapattirnāsti, tathāpi
tātparyānupapattirasti, śaityapāvanatvādibodhatātparyeṇaiva tīrapadaṃ
parityajya gaṅgāpadaprayogāt tasya tātparyasya lakṣaṇāṃ
vinānupapatteḥ/ tātparyānupapattireva lakṣaṇābījam
nānvayānupapattiriti pūrvamevoktaṃ vakṣyati ca dīpikāyām/ tathā ca
kṛtaṃ vyañjanayeti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: is necessarily [understood through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>] — thus the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>. Similarly, in 'the settlement [is] on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' and the like, by accepting <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> for the bank qualified by coolness, sanctity, and the like, the coolness

children.text:
śaṅkate - nanviti/
anyathāsiddhatve 'pi - śaktyā lakṣaṇayā vā gatārthatve 'pi/ arthasāmarthyāt
yatrārthāntaraṃ pratīyate tatrārthaśaktimūlā vyañjanā/ yathā 'gaccha gacchasi
cet' ityatra bhartā yatra gacchati tatra deśe nāyikāyāḥ janmakathanena
janmanaśca maraṇānantarakālikatvena janmarūpapadārthasāmarthyāt
pravāsottarakālikamaraṇarūpor'tho 'bhivyajyate/ tena ca gamanābhāvo
vyajyate/ asyārthasya padavṛttyā śaktyā lakṣaṇayā vā pratītyasambhavāt
vyañjanākhyā vṛttiḥ svīkāryetyāśayaḥ śaṅkituḥ/ śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam/
children.translated_text: He raises the objection — 'Now' etc. 'Even if otherwise-established' — even if the matter is already accomplished through denotative power or <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. Where, from the capacity of the meaning (<s>arthasāmarthya</s>), an additional meaning is cognized,

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: lakṣaṇābījanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of the Basis of <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (Secondary Signification)

children.text:
tātparyānupapattiḥ
lakṣaṇābījam/ tatpratītīcchayoccaritatvaṃ tātparyam/ tātparyajñānaṃ ca
vākyārthajñāne hetuḥ nānārthānu rodhāt/ prakaraṇādikaṃ
tātparyagrāhakam/
children.translated_text: The impossibility of the intended meaning (<s>tātparya</s>) is the basis of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. <s>Tātparya</s> (intended purport) is the property of having been uttered with the desire to convey that [meaning]. And the knowledge of <s>tātparya</s> is a cause of the cognition of sentence-meaning; in the case of words with multiple meanings,

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
anvayānupapatteḥ
lakṣaṇābījatve yaṣṭīḥ praveśaya ityādau lakṣaṇānupapattiḥ/
tātparyānupapatteḥ tathātve tu tasyāstatrāpi sattvena yaṣṭipadasya
yaṣṭidhare lakṣaṇā sambhavatītyāśayenāha - tātparyānupapattiriti/
tatpratītīti/ tīrādirūpārthapratītītyarthaḥ/ nānārtheti/
'saindhavamānaya' ityādinānārthakasthale saindhavapadasya aśve lavaṇe ca
śakteḥ tulyatayā śābdabodhe tātparyagrahasya kāraṇatvamantarā
niyatakāle tattadbodhopapattiḥ nāstīti tatra
tatkāraṇatvasyāvaśyakatve tadanurodhena sarvatra tadāvaśyakateti bhāvaḥ/
na caṃ mauniślokādau śābdabodhānupapattiḥ/ tatra niruktatātparyasya
asattvāditi vācyam, tātparyasya tatpratītīcchārūpatvaparyavasānena tatra
tādṛśatātparyasya sattvenādoṣāt/ na ca tathāpi
tatpratītīcchārahitaśukādyuccaritavākyādapi
śābdabodhasyānubhavikatayā tatrānupapatteḥ parihārāsambhava iti
śaṅkyam/ tatreśvarecchāmādāyaivānupapatteḥ parihārasambhavāt iti
śaṅkyam/ tatreśvarecchāmādāyaivānupapatteḥ parihārasambhavāt
parihārasambhavāt ityalamadhikajalpanena/ prakaraṇādikamiti/ ādinā
'saśaṅkhacakro hariḥ pūjyaḥ' ityādau hariśabdasya bhagavati
tātparyanirṇāyakasya 'saśaṅkhacakra' iti viśeṣaṇādeḥ parigrahaḥ/
kathaṃ prakaraṇādeḥ tātparyagrāhakatvamiti cet - ittham/ 'idaṃ
saindhavapadaṃ lavaṇabodhecchayā uccaritam bhojanaprakaraṇe uktatvāt'
iti rītyā gṛhāṇa/
children.translated_text: Because syntactical connection would not be established — if the basis of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) were accepted, then in cases like 'bring in the sticks,' <s>lakṣaṇā</s> would not be established. Because <s>tātparya</s> (purport) would not be established — with the intent that if it were so, since that secondary signification is present even there, the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word 'stick' for a stick-bearer would be possible, he says — '<s>tātparya</s> would not be established.' 'The cognition of that' means: the cognition of the intended meaning in the form of a riverbank and so forth. 'Equivocal words' — in the case of equivocal words like 'bring the <s>saindhava</s>,' since the word <s>saindhava</s> has equal potency to signify both horse and salt, without the causal role of grasping <s>tātparya</s> (purport) in verbal cognition, the production of the particular cognition at a particular time cannot be explained. Hence, the necessity of that causal role there entails its necessity everywhere — this is the purport. Nor should one object that in verses composed by a silent author and so forth, verbal cognition is not established, because the stated <s>tātparya</s> is absent — since <s>tātparya</s> ultimately amounts to the desire for that cognition, and such <s>tātparya</s> is present there, so there is no defect. Nor should one raise the doubt that even so, since verbal cognition from sentences uttered by parrots and the like, who lack the desire for that cognition, is established by experience, the difficulty there cannot be resolved — because the difficulty can be resolved by taking recourse to the will of <s>Īśvara</s> (God). Enough of excessive argumentation. 'Context and so forth' — by 'and so forth,' in cases such as '<s>Hari</s> who bears the conch and discus is to be worshipped,' the qualifier 'bearing the conch and discus' and similar elements that determine the <s>tātparya</s> of the word <s>Hari</s> toward the Lord are included. How does context and the like serve as the apprehender of <s>tātparya</s>? Thus: understand it in this manner — 'this word <s>saindhava</s> was uttered with the desire for the cognition of salt, because it was said in the context of dining.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
niyatakāla iti/
kadācit lavaṇaviṣayakaḥ kadācit aśvaviṣayaka ityevaṃ
kālavyavasthetyarthaḥ/ tadanurodheneti/ nānārthakasthale śābdabodhe
tātparyajñānasya kāraṇatvānusāreṇetyarthaḥ/ tadāvaśyakateti/
tātparyajñānasyāvaśvakatetyarthaḥ/ nanu
tatpratītīcchayoccaritatvarūpatātparyajñānasya
śābdabodhahetutvasvīkāre maunikartṛkeṇa vākyabodhakalipyādinā
yatra śābdabodhastatra tatpratītīcchayoccaritatvarūpatātparyābhāvāt
tātparyajñānamasambhavīti śaṅkate - na ca mauniślokādāviti/
maunikartṛkavākyabodhakalipyādāvityarthaḥ/ nirūktatātparyasya -
tatpratītīcchayā uccaritatvarūpatātparyasya/ tātparyaṃ
tatpratītīcchāmātram/ tattu maunināmapyasti/ tajjñānācca lipyāditaḥ
śābdabodha upapadyata ityāśayena samādhatte - tātparyasyeti/ nanu
tatpratītīcchāpi na tātparyam/ śukādeḥ tādṛśecchāvirahe 'pi
śukādyuccāritavākyāt śābdabodhasyānubhavasiddhatvādityāśaṅkate -
na ca tathāpīti/ īśvarecchāmiti/ śukoccāritādasmādvākyāt
etādṛśārthabodho bhavatu ityākārakeśvarecchaiva tatra tātparyam/
tajjñānācca śābdabodha iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'At a particular time' means: sometimes the cognition pertains to salt, sometimes to a horse — thus there is a temporal determination. 'In accordance with that' means: in accordance with the causal role of the knowledge of <s>tātparya</s> (purport) in verbal cognition in the case of equivocal words. 'The necessity of that' means: the necessity of the knowledge of <s>tātparya</s>. Objection: if one accepts that <s>tātparya</s>-knowledge in the form of 'uttered with the desire for that cognition' is a cause of verbal cognition, then in cases where verbal cognition arises from written texts composed by a silent author, since <s>tātparya</s> in the form of 'uttered with the desire for that cognition' is absent, <s>tātparya</s>-knowledge would be impossible — he raises this objection: 'Nor in verses by a silent author' and so forth. 'In verses by a silent author' means: in written texts and the like whose author is silent. 'The stated <s>tātparya</s>' — <s>tātparya</s> in the form of being uttered with the desire for that cognition. <s>Tātparya</s> is merely the desire for that cognition. And that exists even in silent authors. And from the knowledge of that, verbal cognition from written texts and the like is explained — with this intent, he resolves the objection: '<s>tātparya</s>' and so forth. Objection: even the desire for that cognition is not <s>tātparya</s>, because verbal cognition from sentences uttered by parrots and the like is established by experience even in the absence of such desire — he raises this objection: 'nor even so' and so forth. 'The will of <s>Īśvara</s>' — the will of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) of the form 'let such-and-such meaning-cognition arise from this sentence uttered by the parrot' is the <s>tātparya</s> there. And from the knowledge of that, verbal cognition arises — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
pramājanakaśukavākyādau īśvarecchāyāstātparyatve 'pi bhramajanake
'vahninā siñcati' ityādiśukavākye īśvarecchāyāstātparyatvaṃ na
sambhavati, tathā sajīśvarecchāyāḥ visaṃvāditvāpatterityatrāha -
alamadhikajalpaneneti/ visaṃvādiśukavākye śikṣakasyecchaiva
tātparyam, ato na doṣa iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: even if the will of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) serves as <s>tātparya</s> in parrot-utterances that generate valid cognition, in error-generating parrot-utterances such as 'sprinkle with fire,' the will of <s>Īśvara</s> cannot serve as <s>tātparya</s>, because it would lead to the undesirable consequence of <s>Īśvara</s>'s will being discordant with reality. To this he says — 'enough of excessive argumentation.' In the case of misleading parrot-utterances, the will of the trainer alone is the <s>tātparya</s>, so there is no defect — this is the purport.

children.text:
ekārthavācakaśabdaghaṭitavākyāt śābdabodho yatra, tatra
tātparyajñānasyānupayoge 'pi nānārthakasaindhavādipadaghaṭitāt
'saindhavamānaya' ityādivākyāt kadācidaśvānayanabodhaḥ
kadācillavaṇānayanabodhaḥ iti vyavasthāyāḥ tātparyajñānenaiva
nirvāhāt tātparyajñānasya śābdabodhahetutvamāvaśyakam/
saindhavapadasya asminnarthe tātparyamiti jñānaṃ ca prakaraṇādinā bhavatīti
dīpikāyām
children.translated_text: Where verbal cognition arises from a sentence composed of words having a single meaning, the knowledge of <s>tātparya</s> (purport) is not required. Nevertheless, since the determination as to whether the cognition from a sentence like 'bring the <s>saindhava</s>' — composed of the equivocal word <s>saindhava</s> — is sometimes the cognition of bringing a horse and sometimes the cognition of bringing salt, is accomplished only through the knowledge of <s>tātparya</s>, the knowledge of <s>tātparya</s> must be accepted as a cause of verbal cognition. And the knowledge that 'the <s>tātparya</s> of the word <s>saindhava</s> is in this particular meaning' arises through context and the like — this was stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s>,

children.text:
uktam/
tatrādipadagrāhyamāha - ādineti/ prakaraṇaṃ nāma
bhojanagamanādiprastāvaḥ/ viśeṣaṇādaiḥ ityādipadane
ābhimukhyādiparigrahaḥ/ bhojanaprakaraṇe uktatvāditi/ yannaivaṃ tannaivaṃ
yathā pramāṇaprakaraṇe prayuktaṃ saindhavapadamiti śeṣaḥ pūraṇīyaḥ/ iti
rītyeti/ ityanumānavidhayetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He explains what is included by the word 'and so forth' — 'and so forth' and so forth. Context means: a setting such as dining, traveling, and so forth. By the word 'and so forth' in 'qualifiers and so forth,' the inclusion of directional orientation and similar factors is intended. 'Because it was said in the context of dining' — what is not so is not so; the remainder to be supplied is: 'just as the word <s>saindhava</s> employed in the context of valid means of knowledge.' 'In this manner' means: by way of this inference.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: arthādhyāhārakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of ellipsis of meaning (<s>arthādhyāhāra</s>)

children.text:
'dvāram'
ityādau 'pidhehi' iti śabdādhyāhāraḥ/ nanu arthajñānārthatvāt
śabdasyārthamavijñāya
children.translated_text: In cases like 'door,' the ellipsis is of the word 'shut' (<s>śabdādhyāhāra</s>). Objection: since the purpose of a word is the cognition of its meaning, without knowing the meaning,

children.text:
śabdādhyāhārāsambhavāt arthādhyāhāra eva yukta iti cet-na/
padaviśeṣajanyapadārthopasthiteḥ śābdajñāne hetutvāt/ anyathā 'ghaṭaḥ
karmatvamānayanaṃ kṛtiḥ' ityatrāpi śābdajñānaprasaṅgāt/
children.translated_text: since ellipsis of the word is impossible, ellipsis of the meaning alone is appropriate — if so, no. Because the presentation of the word-meaning generated by a specific word is the cause of verbal cognition. Otherwise, even in the case of 'pot, object-hood, bringing, effort,' verbal cognition would absurdly follow.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
prābhākaramataṃ
nirākariṣyamāṇaḥ svasiddhāntaṃ darśayati - dvāramiti/
arthajñānārthatvācchabdasyeti/ śabdajñānasya arthajñānaphalakatvādityarthaḥ/
etāvatā prathamata evārthānusandhāne lāghavamiti sūcitam/ kiṃ ca 'arthaṃ
buddhvā śabdaracanā' iti nyāyenārthajñānamantarā
ākāṅkṣādimacchabdānusandhānarūpaśabdādhyāhārasyaivāsambhavena prathamataḥ
arthāndhyāhārasyaivāvaśyakatetyāha-arthamavijñāyeti/
yathākathañcidupasthitapadārthānāṃ śābdabodhānudayena
padajanyatatvasyopasthitiviśeṣaṇatāyā āvaśyakatayā
tādṛśopasthitisampattaye śabdādhyāhāra eva anāyattyā anusartavya
ityāha - padaviśeṣeti/ viśeṣapadasyāpi prayojanaṃ darśayituṃ
'ghaṭaḥ karmatvam' ityādyanudhāvanam/ tatra
karmatvādipadajanyakarmatvādyupasthiteḥ sattve 'pi
ghaṭapadottarāmpadajanyakarmatvādyupasthiterasattvena na siddhāntimate
śābdabodhaprasaṅga iti bhāvaḥ/ padaviśeṣajanyetyatra vṛttyā
padaviśeṣajanyetyapi bodhyam/ tena 'ghaṭamānaya' ityādau
ghaṭādipadādākāśāderupasthitāvapi na śābdabodha iti dik/
children.translated_text: Intending to refute the <s>Prābhākara</s> view, he first presents his own established doctrine — 'door' and so forth. 'Since the purpose of a word is the cognition of meaning' means: since word-knowledge has the cognition of meaning as its result. By this much, it is indicated that there is greater parsimony in first investigating the meaning. Moreover, by the principle 'word-composition follows the understanding of meaning,' since without the cognition of meaning the ellipsis of the word — which consists in the investigation of words possessing <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> (expectancy) and so forth — is itself impossible, the ellipsis of meaning alone is necessarily primary. He says this: 'without knowing the meaning' and so forth. Since verbal cognition does not arise from word-meanings presented in just any manner, the condition of being generated by a word is necessary as a qualifier of the presentation, and in order for such presentation to be achieved, word-ellipsis alone must be resorted to inevitably — he says this: 'a specific word' and so forth. To show the purpose of the word 'specific' as well, he pursues the example 'pot, object-hood' and so forth. There, although the presentation of object-hood and so forth generated by the word 'object-hood' and so forth is present, since the presentation of object-hood and so forth generated by the word following the word 'pot' is absent, on the established view verbal cognition does not absurdly follow — this is the purport. In 'generated by a specific word,' one should also understand 'generated by a specific word through its <s>vṛtti</s> (denotative function).' Hence, in cases like 'bring the pot,' even though there is a presentation of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) from the word 'pot' and similar words, verbal cognition does not arise — this is the direction.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
arthajñānaphalakatvāditi/
śābdabodhātmakārthajñānahetutvādityarthaḥ/ iti nyāyeneti/ yathā
śabdaprayogātmakaśabdaracanāṃ prati arthajñānaṃ kāraṇam, tathā
śabdānusandhānarūpaśabdādhyāhāraṃ pratyapi arthajñānaṃ kāraṇam/ tataśca
śabdādhyāhārāt pūrvabhāvinā arthajñānātmakena arthādhyahāreṇaiva
śābdabodhanirvohe kiṃ śabdādhyāhāreṇeti bhāvaḥ/ yathākathañciditi/
śābdabodhaṃ prati padārthasmaraṇaṃ kāraṇam/ padārthasmaraṇe
padajñānajanyatvaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ anyathā yatra padāt na
padārthasmaraṇam, api tūdbodhakādinā,
tatrodbodhakādijanyapadārthasmaraṇasya śābdabodhahetutvāpatteḥ/ evaṃ
ca dvāramityādau padajñānajanyapidhānopasthitisampattaye
padajñānarūpaśabdādhyāhāra evāvaśyaka iti bhāvaḥ/ yathākathañcidityasya
padajñānātiriktenodbodhakādirūpopāyenetyarthaḥ/
tādṛśopasthitisampattaya iti/ padajanyapadārthopasthitiniṣpattaya
ityarthaḥ/ anāyatyā - agatyā/ ghaṭādipadāditi/ ghaṭādipadasya
śabdarūpasyākāśe samavāyasambandhena vidyamānatayā samavāyasya
ghaṭādiśabdaḥ ākāśaśceti dvau sambandhinau/ tatraikasya ghaṭādipadasya
jñānāt aparasya ākāśasya smaraṇaṃ bhavati,
ekasambandhijñānamaparasambandhismārakamiti nyāyāt/ tathā ca
tādṛśasmaraṇaviṣayasyākāśasya śābdabodhavāraṇāya vṛttyā
padajñānajanyapadārthasmaraṇaṃ śābdabodhaheturiti vācyam/ vṛttiśca
śaktilakṣaṇānyatararūpaḥ sambandhaḥ/ ghaṭapadādākāśasmaraṇasya
ghaṭapadavṛttiprayojyatvābhāvāt na tasya śābdabodhahetutvamiti
bhāvaḥ/ vṛttyā padajñānajanyatvaṃ ca vṛttijñānasahakṛtapadajñānajanyatvam/
children.translated_text: 'Since it has the cognition of meaning as its result' means: since it has the causality of producing cognition of meaning in the form of verbal comprehension. 'By the principle' means: just as the cognition of meaning is a cause for word-composition in the form of word-usage, similarly the cognition of meaning is a cause for word-ellipsis which consists in the investigation of words. And consequently, since verbal cognition is accomplished by the ellipsis of meaning alone — which is prior to word-ellipsis — what need is there for word-ellipsis? This is the purport. 'In just any manner' — recollection of word-meaning is a cause for verbal cognition. In the recollection of word-meaning, the condition of being generated by word-knowledge must be given as a qualifier. Otherwise, where recollection of word-meaning arises not from the word but through a prompter and so forth, the recollection of word-meaning generated by the prompter and so forth would absurdly be a cause of verbal cognition. And accordingly, in cases like 'door,' for the achievement of the presentation of 'shutting' generated by word-knowledge, word-ellipsis alone in the form of word-knowledge is necessarily required — this is the purport. 'In just any manner' means: by means such as a prompter and so forth, which are other than word-knowledge. 'For the achievement of such presentation' means: for the production of the presentation of word-meaning generated by the word. 'Inevitably' means: necessarily. 'From the word pot and similar words' — since the word-form of the word 'pot' and so forth exists in <s>ākāśa</s> (space) through the relation of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), <s>samavāya</s> has two relata: the word 'pot' and <s>ākāśa</s>. From the knowledge of one relatum, the word 'pot,' there arises the recollection of the other relatum, <s>ākāśa</s>, by the principle that the knowledge of one relatum prompts the recollection of the other. And accordingly, to prevent the verbal cognition of <s>ākāśa</s> which is the object of such recollection, one must say: the recollection of word-meaning generated by a word through its <s>vṛtti</s> (denotative function) is the cause of verbal cognition. And <s>vṛtti</s> is a relation in the form of either <s>śakti</s> (primary denotation) or <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification). Since the recollection of <s>ākāśa</s> from the word 'pot' is not produced by the <s>vṛtti</s> of the word 'pot,' it does not serve as a cause of verbal cognition — this is the purport. And the condition of being generated by a word through <s>vṛtti</s> means: being generated by word-knowledge assisted by the knowledge of <s>vṛtti</s>.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: padavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of words

children.text:
paṅkajādipadeṣu
yogarūḍhiḥ/ avayavaśaktiryogaḥ/ samudāyaśaktī rūḍhiḥ/
niyatapadmatvādijñānārthaṃ samudāyaśaktiḥ/ anyathā kukude 'pi
prayogaprasaṅgāt/
children.translated_text: In words like <s>paṅkaja</s> ('mud-born,' i.e. lotus), there is <s>yogarūḍhi</s> (conventional-cum-etymological denotation). The potency of the component parts is <s>yoga</s> (etymology). The potency of the whole is <s>rūḍhi</s> (convention). The potency of the whole serves the purpose of producing the invariable cognition of lotus-hood and so forth. Otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of usage even for a hump on an ox's back.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
yadyapi, padam
tāvat caturvidham - yaugikam, rūḍham, yogarūḍham, yaugikarūḍham
ceti/ yogo 'vayavaśaktiḥ/ tanmātreṇārthapratipādakamādyam/ yathā
pācakādipadam/ rūḍhiḥ samudāyaśaktiḥ/ tanmātreṇārthapratipādakaṃ
dvitīyam/ yathā gavādipadam/ yogarūḍhibhyāṃ
parasparasahakāreṇārthapratipādakaṃ tṛtīyam/ yathā paṅkajādipadam/
yogaśaktyā samudāyaśaktyā ca parasparasahāyena vibhinnārthapratipādakaṃ
caturtham/ yathā udbhitpadam yogena tarugulmādeḥ rūḍhyā tu
yāgaviśeṣasya ca vācakam/ tathāpi yogarūḍhaṃ
children.translated_text: Although a word is of four kinds — <s>yaugika</s> (purely etymological), <s>rūḍha</s> (purely conventional), <s>yogarūḍha</s> (conventional-cum-etymological), and <s>yaugikarūḍha</s> (etymological-cum-conventional). <s>Yoga</s> is the potency of the component parts. The first type, which conveys meaning through that alone, is like the word <s>pācaka</s> (cook). <s>Rūḍhi</s> is the potency of the whole. The second type, which conveys meaning through that alone, is like the word <s>go</s> (cow). The third type conveys meaning through the mutual cooperation of both <s>yoga</s> and <s>rūḍhi</s>, like the word <s>paṅkaja</s> (lotus). The fourth type conveys distinct meanings through the potency of etymology and the potency of convention independently aiding each other, like the word <s>udbhit</s>, which denotes trees, shrubs, and so forth by etymology, and a particular sacrifice by convention. Nevertheless, having presented <s>yogarūḍha</s>,

children.text:
pradarśya tatra
yogarūḍhyoḥ svarūpapradarśanena tadrītyā anyatrāpi boddhuṃ
śakyamityabhiprāyeṇa paṅkajādipade yogarūḍhiṃ pradarśaṃyati -
paṅkajādīti/ yogarūḍhiriti/
children.translated_text: by demonstrating the nature of <s>yoga</s> and <s>rūḍhi</s> in that context, with the intention that others can also be understood in the same manner, he illustrates <s>yogarūḍhi</s> in words like <s>paṅkaja</s> — '<s>paṅkaja</s> and so forth.' '<s>Yogarūḍhi</s>' —

children.text:
yogasahitā
rūḍhirityarthaḥ/ nanu paṅkajādiśabdeṣvapi yoga evāstu tāvataiva
nirvāhāt ityāśaṅkya paṅkajaśabdasya padmatvāvacchinne
vṛttimantarā niyamena padmatvāvacchinnabhānamanubhavasiddhaṃ na
nirvahatīti
children.translated_text: <s>rūḍhi</s> (convention) accompanied by <s>yoga</s> (etymology) — this is the meaning. Objection: even in words like <s>paṅkaja</s>, let there be <s>yoga</s> alone, since that suffices for explanation. Anticipating this objection, since without the <s>vṛtti</s> (denotative function) of the word <s>paṅkaja</s> restricted to lotus-hood, the invariable appearance as restricted to lotus-hood that is established by experience cannot be accounted for,

children.text:
padmatvāvacchinne
rūḍhirāvaśyikītyāha - niyateti/ niyatapadmatvāvacchinnabhānānubhave
vipratipannaṃna pratyāha - anyatheti/
niyatapadmatvāvacchinnabhānopayogisamudāyaśaktyanaṅkīkāra
ityarthaḥ/ prayogeti/ paṅkajapadaprayogetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>rūḍhi</s> (convention) restricted to lotus-hood is necessarily required — he says this: 'invariable' and so forth. To one who disputes the experience of invariable appearance restricted to lotus-hood, he responds — 'otherwise' and so forth. The meaning is: without accepting the potency of the whole that serves the invariable appearance restricted to lotus-hood. 'Usage' means: usage of the word <s>paṅkaja</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
yogo 'vayavaśaktirityādi/ avayavaśaktimātreṇārthabodhakaṃ padaṃ
yaugikam/ pācakapade pac aka ityavayadvayamasti/ tatra pacdhātoḥ
pākor'thaḥ, akapratyayasya kartā arthaḥ/ pācakapadena pākakartā budhyate/
avayavārthamātrasyaiva bodhāt pācakapadaṃ yaugikam/ mātrapadena
yogarūḍhapadavyavacchedaḥ/ samudāyaśaktimātreṇārthabodhakaṃ rūḍham,
mātrapadenāvayavaśaktivyavacchedadvārā yogarūḍhapadavyāvṛttiḥ/ yathā
gavādipade samudāyagatā śaktireva vartate/ śaktapadaghaṭitatve sati
samāsabhinnatve sati śaktinirūpakatvaṃ yaugikatvam/ yathā pācakapade
pākaśaktapacadhātukartṛśakta-akapadaghaṭitatve sati
pākakartṛtvarūpaikadharmāvacchinnaśaktikatvamastīti samanvayaḥ/
rūḍhe 'tivyāptivāraṇāya śaktapadaghaṭitatve satīti/
1samāse 'tivyāptivāraṇāya samāsabhinnatve satīti/ yadyapyevamapi
yogarūḍhe paṅkajādipade 'tivyāptiḥ prasajati, tathāpi
avayavārthaghaṭitadharmāvacchinnaśaktikatvaṃ
children.translated_text: [The text begins] 'yoga is constituent-potency' and so on. A word that conveys meaning solely through the potency of its constituents is <s>yaugika</s> (derivative). In the word <s>pācaka</s> (cook), there are two constituents: 'pac' and 'aka'. Of these, the root 'pac' has the meaning of cooking, and the suffix 'aka' has the meaning of agent. Through the word <s>pācaka</s>, one cognizes 'the agent of cooking.' Since cognition arises from the constituent-meanings alone, the word <s>pācaka</s> is <s>yaugika</s>. The word 'mātra' (only) serves to exclude <s>yogarūḍha</s> (mixed-conventional) words. A word that conveys meaning solely through the potency of the aggregate is <s>rūḍha</s> (conventional); the word 'mātra' here excludes <s>yogarūḍha</s> words by excluding constituent-potency. For example, in words like <s>go</s> (cow), only the aggregate-level potency operates. <s>Yaugikatva</s> (derivative-ness) is: being a determiner of <s>śakti</s> (denotative potency), when constituted by potency-bearing words, and when being other than a compound. For instance, in the word <s>pācaka</s>, it is constituted by the root 'pac' bearing potency for cooking and the suffix 'aka' bearing potency for agenthood, and it possesses a potency delimited by the single property of being an agent-of-cooking — thus the consistency is established. To prevent over-pervasion to <s>rūḍha</s> words, the condition 'being constituted by potency-bearing words' is added. To prevent over-pervasion to compounds, the condition 'being other than a compound' is added. Although even so, over-pervasion to <s>yogarūḍha</s> words like <s>paṅkaja</s> (lotus, lit. 'mud-born') would follow, nevertheless the property of possessing a potency delimited by a property constituted by the constituent-meanings

children.text:
1.
samāse 'tivyāptivāraṇāyeti/ na ca samāse śaktyanaṅgīkārāt
śaktinirūpakatvābhāvāt kathamativyāptiprasaktiriti vācyam/
pācakapadasya yathā pākakartṛtvarūpaikadharmāvacchinnaśaktatvaṃ tathā
rājapuruṣādisamāsasyāpi
rājaviśiṣṭapuruṣatvarūpaikadharmāvacchinnaśaktikatvamastītyāśayāt/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'To prevent over-pervasion to compounds' — nor should one object: 'since <s>śakti</s> is not accepted in compounds, how can there be a possibility of over-pervasion, given the absence of being a determiner of <s>śakti</s>?' The intention is that just as the word <s>pācaka</s> has the property of bearing potency delimited by the single property of agent-of-cooking-ness, so too compounds like <s>rājapuruṣa</s> (king's man) possess potency delimited by the single property of being-a-person-qualified-by-a-king.
