children.translated_text: is what is intended by 'being a determiner of <s>śakti</s>.' The consistency for the word <s>pācaka</s> is established through its possessing potency delimited by such a property as agent-of-cooking-ness. But the word <s>paṅkaja</s> possesses potency delimited by lotus-ness, which is not constituted by the constituent-meanings — hence there is no over-pervasion there. <s>Rūḍhatva</s> (conventional-ness) is: being a determiner of <s>śakti</s> when not constituted by [potency-bearing] words. In the word <s>go</s> (cow), no potency-bearing word is a constituent, hence there is non-constitution by words; and since it bears potency delimited by cow-ness, it is a determiner of <s>śakti</s> — thus consistency is established. To prevent over-pervasion to <s>yaugika</s> words, the qualifying condition ends with 'sati.' To prevent over-pervasion to corrupt words (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>), the qualified term is specified. <s>Yogarūḍhatva</s> (mixed-conventional-ness) is: being constituted by potency-bearing words, and possessing potency delimited by a property not co-referential with the constituent-meanings. In the word <s>paṅkaja</s>, there is constitution by two potency-bearing words 'paṅka' and 'ja,' and it possesses potency delimited by lotus-ness which is not constituted by the constituent-meanings — thus consistency. The definition of <s>yaugikarūḍhatva</s> is: possessing an aggregate-type that is constituted by potency-bearing words whose potency is delimited by a property not co-referential with the delimiter of the denotation of the conventional usage, which delimiter determines the <s>rūḍhi</s>-determiner-hood. In words like <s>udbhid</s> (a type of sacrifice), the aggregate 'ud-bhid' is constituted by the root 'bhid' bearing potency delimited by upward-splitting-ness (which is not co-referential with the delimiter of <s>rūḍhi</s>-denotation, namely sacrifice-ness) — hence consistency, since the aggregate-type is present. To prevent over-pervasion to <s>yaugika</s> words like <s>pācaka</s>, the qualifier 'being a determiner of <s>rūḍhi</s>-determiner-hood' is added to aggregate-type. To prevent over-pervasion to <s>rūḍha</s> words like <s>go</s>, the condition of 'being constituted by potency-bearing words' is introduced. To prevent over-pervasion to <s>yogarūḍha</s> words like <s>paṅkaja</s>, the qualification that 'potency is delimited by a property not co-referential with the delimiter of <s>rūḍhi</s>-denotation' modifies the word — this is the path shown by <s>Nṛsiṃhaśāstri</s>. 'Through the mutual cooperation of <s>yoga</s> and <s>rūḍhi</s>' — through <s>yoga</s>-potency, 'born from mud' is expressed; through <s>rūḍhi</s>, 'lotus' is expressed. Through the mutual cooperation of both, 'a lotus born from mud' is expressed.

children.text: anvitaśaktikhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (the theory that words denote meanings as connected)

children.text:
'itarānvite
śaktiḥ' iti prābhākarāḥ/ anvayasya vākyārthatayā bhānasambhavāt
anvayāṃśe 'pi śaktirna kalpanīyeti gautamīyāḥ/
children.translated_text: '<s>Śakti</s> (denotative potency) resides in what is connected with the other [co-occurring word-meanings]' — thus hold the <s>Prābhākara</s> school. Since the syntactic connection can appear as sentence-meaning [without requiring word-level potency for it], <s>śakti</s> need not be postulated for the relational aspect as well — thus hold the followers of <s>Gautama</s> (the Naiyāyikas).

children.text:
1.

rūḍhyarthatāvacchedakāsamānādhikaraṇeti dharmaviśeṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'The delimiter of <s>rūḍhi</s>-determiner-hood' — this connects with 'aggregate-type.' 'Not co-referential with the delimiter of <s>rūḍhi</s>-denotation' — this is a qualifier of the property.

ayamabhiprāyaḥ -
children.translated_text: Although the <s>Prābhākara</s> doctrine is '<s>śakti</s> resides in what is connected with the action-to-be-accomplished (<s>kārya</s>),' nevertheless, since linguistic convention is established even in sentences whose purport concerns an already-accomplished state, in order to make the theory applicable universally, [the author] presents the <s>Prābhākara</s> view in a refined form — hence 'connected with the other.' The conclusion, however, is: '<s>śakti</s> resides in what is connected.' The intention is as follows —

children.text:
kathañcidupasthitānāṃ
padārthānāṃ śābdabodhavāraṇāya tadviṣayakaśābdabodhaṃ prati
vṛttijñānajanyatadupasthititvena hetutāyāḥ kalpanīyatayā
anvayāṃśe 'pi śaktirapekṣitā/ anyathā
tādṛśasāmānyakāryakāraṇabhāvabhaṅgaprasaṅgāt/ na ca
saṃsargaviṣayatābhinnatattadviṣayatāśāliśābdabodhaṃ prati
vṛttijñānādhīnatattadupasthititvena hetutvamāstām, tathā cānvayāṃśe
śaktyanaṅgīkāre 'pi na kṣatiriti vācyam/ tathā sati
kāryatāvacchedakagauravāpatteḥ/ evaṃ ca 'anvito ghaṭo ghaṭapadavācyaḥ'
ityākārakaśaktijñānameva śābdabodhaprayojakamiti/
kecittu-itarānvite śaktirityasya kāryānvite śaktirityarthaṃ āhuḥ/
children.translated_text: In order to prevent verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>) of word-meanings that have been presented somehow [through other means], since it is necessary to postulate causality in the form of 'the presentation of those [meanings] being generated by knowledge of the <s>vṛtti</s> (denotative relation) pertaining to them' as a cause of verbal cognition directed at those objects, <s>śakti</s> is required even for the relational aspect (<s>anvayāṃśa</s>). Otherwise, the general causal relation of that kind would collapse. Nor should one say: 'Let the causality consist in the presentation of each [meaning] being dependent on <s>vṛtti</s>-knowledge, with respect to verbal cognition possessing object-hood for each that is distinct from relational object-hood — and thus even without accepting <s>śakti</s> for the relational aspect, there is no deficiency.' For in that case, there would be the fault of complexity in the delimiter of effect-hood (<s>kāryatāvacchedaka</s>). And accordingly, the knowledge of <s>śakti</s> in the form 'the pot, as connected, is the denotatum of the word pot' is itself the cause of verbal cognition. Some, however, explain 'śakti in what is connected with the other' as meaning 'śakti in what is connected with the action-to-be-accomplished (<s>kārya</s>).'

svīkartavyā/ parasparatattadupasthitijanyaśābdabodhe vyabhicāravāraṇāya

niveśanīyam/ evaṃ ca vṛttyanupasthitasyāpi padārthadvayasaṃsargasya
children.translated_text: [The commentator] presents the <s>Naiyāyika</s> position with its reasoning — [beginning with] 'of the syntactic connection.' Since the syntactic connection of word-meanings can appear in verbal cognition merely by the force of co-occurrence (<s>samabhivyāhāra</s>) of words, <s>śakti</s> need not be postulated even for such relational aspects — this is the conclusion regarding the combined meaning. The intention is this: a uniform causal relation in the form of 'the presentation of each [meaning] being dependent on <s>vṛtti</s>-knowledge' directed at verbal cognition of the respective objects is not possible, because the <s>vṛtti</s>-hood that is common to both <s>śakti</s> and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary denotation) is difficult to specify. Rather, one type of causality should be accepted in the form of 'the presentation of that [meaning] being generated by knowledge of the word bearing <s>śakti</s> for it,' and another type of causality in the form of 'the presentation of that [meaning] being generated by knowledge of the word having <s>lakṣaṇā</s> for it.' And to prevent deviation in verbal cognition arising from mutual presentation of those [meanings], the condition of being immediately subsequent to each respective cause must be placed within the delimiting condition of each respective effect-hood. And thus, even the syntactic connection of two word-meanings, which is not presented through <s>vṛtti</s>,

śābdabodhopagame
vyabhicāraprasaktyā darśitadvividhakāryakāraṇabhāvasya niṣpratyūhateti
kimanvayāṃśe śaktikalpanena/
children.translated_text: since upon accepting [its appearance in] verbal cognition, the two-fold causal relation that has been demonstrated [above] remains unobstructed due to the absence of deviation — what need is there for postulating <s>śakti</s> for the relational aspect?

children.translated_text: If one objects that the statement '<s>śakti</s> resides in what is connected with the other — thus the <s>Prābhākaras</s>' is improper, since their established doctrine is '<s>śakti</s> resides in what is connected with the action-to-be-accomplished' — anticipating this, [the commentator] says 'although connected with the action.' 'Nevertheless' — in sentences like '<s>Kāśyāṃ tribhuvanatilako bhūpatirāste</s>' ('The king, the ornament of the three worlds, resides in <s>Kāśī</s>'), since words are used even when the meaning is already accomplished, and since it was already established earlier that 'comprehension of <s>śakti</s> of words occurs even regarding already-accomplished meanings,' it is not appropriate to hold that <s>śakti</s> resides in what is connected with an action-to-be-accomplished through effort — reflecting thus, certain <s>Prābhākara</s> sub-schools refined [the doctrine] as '<s>śakti</s> resides in what is connected with the other,' and it is that refined view which is being cited — this is the purport. Even in sentences whose purport is an accomplished state, the word-meanings possess the quality of 'being connected with the other,' hence by stating '<s>śakti</s> in what is connected with the other,' consistency obtains everywhere. 'The other' means the meaning of a co-occurring word; <s>śakti</s> resides in what is connected with that. And the co-occurring word-meaning may be either of the nature of an action or of an accomplished fact. Since the 'other'-aspect is itself obtained through another word, the refinement should be stated simply as '<s>śakti</s> resides in what is connected' — with this intention [the commentator] says 'in the connected, <s>śakti</s>.' Now, since the relational aspect is obtainable through <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> (expectancy) in the form of co-occurrence, postulating <s>śakti</s> for that aspect is improper — therefore, [the commentator] reveals the intention of the <s>Prābhākaras</s> who maintain <s>śakti</s> for the relational aspect — 'the intention is this.' 'Of [word-meanings] that have been somehow presented' — meaning: of those whose presentation is generated by a cause other than knowledge of the word's <s>vṛtti</s>. The syntactic connection of word-meanings appears in verbal cognition. If <s>śakti</s> is not accepted for the relational aspect, then since the cause in the form of knowledge of word-<s>śakti</s> pertaining to the relational content would be absent, verbal cognition directed at the relational content would not arise — this is the purport. 'Nor should one say' — in the case of 'bring the pot' (<s>ghaṭam ānaya</s>), the presentation of the pot generated by <s>vṛtti</s>-knowledge in the form 'the pot is the <s>śakya</s> (denotatum) of the word pot' is the cause of verbal cognition possessing pot-directed object-hood distinct from relation-directed object-hood. But for verbal cognition possessing relation-directed object-hood, the presentation of the syntactic connection generated by <s>śakti</s>-knowledge is not required — because verbal cognition of the relational content does not fall under the delimiting condition of effect-hood that is of the form 'possessing object-hood for each [meaning] distinct from relational object-hood' — this is the purport. 'Due to the fault of complexity in the delimiter of effect-hood' — because 'possessing object-hood for each that is distinct from relational object-hood' is more complex than simply 'verbal cognition directed at that' — this is the purport. [The commentator] states the form of <s>śakti</s>-comprehension according to this view — 'and accordingly.' Thus in 'bring the pot,' the syntactic connections between pot and object-hood, between object-hood and bringing, and between bringing and the meaning of the optative suffix appear in verbal cognition — since from verbal cognition [we understand]: 'bringing, whose object is the pot, is to be done.' There, if <s>śakti</s> of the word 'pot' is accepted only for the bare meaning 'pot,' then the relation of superstratum-ness (<s>ādheyatva</s>) between pot and object-hood, having no denoting word, would not appear in verbal cognition. Therefore, the word 'pot' has <s>śakti</s> for the pot as qualified by the relation of superstratum-ness whose counter-correlate is object-hood — which is the meaning of the co-occurring word denoted by the affix. The qualification of the pot by the relation is in the form of being a counter-correlate of the relation. And since object-hood, being the meaning of the other word, is obtained through the affix alone, and since only what is not obtainable through another [word] constitutes word-meaning, with respect to the object-hood aspect

children.text:
ghaṭapadasya śaktiḥ/ evaṃ
ampadasyāpi ghaṭapratiyogikatvopalakṣitānvayaviśiṣṭe karmatve śaktiḥ/
evaṃ ca ghaṭakarmatvayoḥ saṃsargaḥ ghaṭapada-ampadaśaktibhyāṃ labhya iti
anvayāṃśaḥ padaśaktyaiva bhāsate/ evaṃ ampadārthakarmatvadhātvarthānayanayoḥ
saṃsargo 'pi padadvayaśaktilabhya iti prābhākarāśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: the word 'pot' does not have <s>śakti</s>. Similarly, the affix also has <s>śakti</s> for object-hood as qualified by the syntactic connection characterized by counter-correlate-hood with respect to the pot. And thus the syntactic connection between pot and object-hood is obtained through the <s>śaktis</s> of the word 'pot' and the affix — hence the relational aspect is manifested through word-<s>śakti</s> alone. Similarly, the syntactic connection between object-hood (the meaning of the affix) and bringing (the meaning of the verbal root) is also obtained through the <s>śaktis</s> of two words — this is the <s>Prābhākara</s> intention.

AnTs_62 vākyaṃ dvividham / vaidikaṃ laukikaṃ ca / vaidikam īśvaroktatvāt sarvam eva pramāṇam / laukikaṃ tv āptoktaṃ pramāṇam / anyad apramāṇam //
AnTs_63 vākyārthajñānaṃ śabdajñānam / tatkaraṇaṃ śabdaḥ //
children.translated_text: AnTs 63: The cognition of the meaning of a sentence is verbal cognition (<s>śabdajñāna</s>). Its instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is word (<s>śabda</s>).

children.text:
vākyaṃ dvividham -
vaidikaṃ laukikaṃ ceti/ vaidikaṃ īśvaroktatvāt sarvamapi
pramāṇam/ laukikaṃ tu āptavākyaṃ pramāṇam/ anyadapramāṇam/
vākyārthajñānaṃ śābdajñānam/ tatkaraṇaṃ śabdaḥ/ evaṃ yathārthānubhavo
nirūpitaḥ/
children.translated_text: Sentences (<s>vākya</s>) are of two kinds — Vedic (<s>vaidika</s>) and secular (<s>laukika</s>). The Vedic, because of being spoken by <s>Īśvara</s> (God), is entirely a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Among the secular, the statement of a trustworthy person (<s>āptavākya</s>) is a means of valid knowledge; the rest is not a means of valid knowledge. The cognition of the meaning of a sentence is verbal cognition (<s>śābdajñāna</s>). Its instrument is word (<s>śabda</s>). Thus, veridical experience (<s>yathārthānubhava</s>) has been ascertained.

children.text:
iti tarkasaṅgrahe
śabdaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on word (<s>śabdapariccheda</s>) in the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
vākyaṃ vibhajate -
vākyamiti/ vaidikasya viśeṣamāha - vaidikamīśvaroktatvātaditi/
children.translated_text: He divides the sentence — [this is the meaning of] 'sentence' (<s>vākyam</s>). He states the distinguishing feature of the Vedic — [this is the meaning of] 'the Vedic, because of being spoken by <s>Īśvara</s>.'

children.text: vedapauruṣeyatvam
children.translated_text: The authorship of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>vedapauruṣeyatva</s>)

children.text:
nanu vedasya
anāditvāt kathamīśvaroktatvamiti cet - na/ 'vedaḥ pauruṣeyaḥ
vākyasamhatvāt bhāratādivat' ityanumānena pauruṣeyatvasiddheḥ/
na ca smaryamāṇakartṛkatvamupādhiḥ, gautamādibhiḥ śiṣyaparamparayā
vede 'pi sakartṛkatvasmaraṇena sādhanavyāpakatvāt/
'tasmāttepānāttrayo vedā ajāyanta' iti śruteśca/
children.translated_text: If one objects: since the <s>Vedas</s> are beginningless (<s>anādi</s>), how can they be spoken by <s>Īśvara</s>? — No. Because the authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>) is established by the inference: 'The <s>Vedas</s> are authored by a person, because they consist of a collection of sentences, like the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and so forth.' Nor is 'having a remembered author' (<s>smaryamāṇakartṛkatva</s>) a vitiating condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because through the teacher-disciple lineage of <s>Gautama</s> and others, the authorship of the <s>Vedas</s> too is remembered, and thus [having a remembered author] pervades the probans (<s>sādhana</s>). And because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'From Him who performed austerities, the three <s>Vedas</s> were born.'

children.text:
nanu varṇāḥ nityāḥ, sa
evāyaṃ gakāra iti pratyabhijñābalāt/ tathā ca katha vedasya
anityatvam iti cet - na/ 'utpanno gakāraḥ, vinaṣṭo gakāraḥ'
ityādipratītyā varṇānāmanityatvāt, 'so 'yaṃ gakāraḥ' iti
pratyabhijñāyāḥ 'seyaṃ dīpajvālā' itivat sājātyāvalambanatvāt/
varṇānāṃ nityatve 'pyānupūrvīviśiṣṭavākyasya atityatvācca/ tasmāt
īśvaroktāḥ vedāḥ/
children.translated_text: If one objects: the phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) are eternal, on the strength of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), 'This is the very same ga-sound.' And if so, how can the <s>Vedas</s> be non-eternal? — No. Because of the non-eternality of phonemes, established through cognitions such as 'The ga-sound has arisen' and 'The ga-sound has perished.' And because the recognition 'This is that same ga-sound' rests upon generic similarity (<s>sājātya</s>), just like [the cognition] 'This is the same lamp-flame.' And even if the phonemes were eternal, the sentence qualified by a particular sequence (<s>ānupūrvī</s>) would be non-eternal. Therefore, the <s>Vedas</s> are spoken by <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mīmāṃsakaḥ śaṅkate - nanviti/ vedasya
īśvaroktatvaṃ anumānena vyavasthāpayati - veda iti/ nanu
'aṣṭādaśapurāṇānāṃ kartā satyavatīsutaḥ' ityādi pramāṇabalena
bhāratādau kartā upalabhyate/ na hi tathā vede/ tathā ca
smaryamāṇakartṛkatvasya bhāratādau sādhyavyāpakatvena pakṣe
sādhanāvyapakatvena ca upādhitvāt kathamidamanumānaṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> raises an objection — [this is the meaning of] 'but' (<s>nanu</s>). He establishes the authorship of the <s>Vedas</s> by <s>Īśvara</s> through inference — [this is the meaning of] 'Veda' and so forth. Now, on the strength of evidence such as 'The author of the eighteen <s>Purāṇas</s> is the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>,' an author is apprehended for the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and the like. But not so for the <s>Vedas</s>. And thus, since 'having a remembered author' pervades the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) in the case of the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and the like, while it does not pervade the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) in the case [of the <s>Vedas</s>], and hence constitutes a vitiating condition (<s>upādhi</s>), how can this inference be

children.text:
sādhakaṃ
bhevadityāśaṅkate - na ceti/ gautamādibhiḥśiṣyaparamparayā vede
kartuṃrūpadeśe vivadantaṃ pratyāha - tasmāditi/
children.translated_text: probative? — this is the objection raised [by the meaning of] 'nor' (<s>na ca</s>). In response to one who disputes the teaching of authorship in the <s>Vedas</s> through the teacher-disciple lineage of <s>Gautama</s> and others, he replies — [this is the meaning of] 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>).

children.text:
sa evāya gakāra iti/
atra etatkālikagakāre pūrvakālikagakārābhedo bhāsate/ sa ca
varṇānāmanityatve na sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/ anityatvāditi/ tarhi
pratyabhijñāvirodha ityata āha - so 'yamiti/
utpattivināśapratyayayoranyārthakatvakalpanāpekṣayā tatpratyayasya
tathātvakalpane lāghavamiti hadayam/ 'agnimīle' ityādau ānupūrvīṃ
- ākārottaragakārottaranatvādirūpā/
tatrottaratvamavyavahitottarakṣaṇavṛttitvaṃ vācyam/ itthaṃ ca varṇanāṃ
atityatvānaṅgīkāre 'pyanityakṣaṇaghaṭitāyā ānupūrvyā anityatvāt
tadviśiṣṭavākyasamudāyatmakavedasya tvadabhimatamanityatvaṃ na
sidhyatīti varṇānāmanityatvamevocitamityāha-varṇānāmiti/
children.translated_text: 'This is the very same ga-sound' — here, in the present ga-sound, the identity with the earlier ga-sound appears. And this [identity] is impossible if phonemes are non-eternal — this is the intent. 'Because of non-eternality' — then there would be a contradiction with recognition, and so he says 'this same' (<s>so 'yam</s>). The gist is: rather than supposing that the cognitions of origination and destruction have a different referent, it is more parsimonious to suppose that the recognition-cognition itself is of that nature [i.e., based on similarity]. The sequence (<s>ānupūrvī</s>) in 'Agnim īle' and so forth — is of the form: having a-sound immediately followed by ga-sound, immediately followed by na-sound, and so on. Here, 'immediately following' should be understood as 'occurring in the immediately succeeding moment.' And thus, even without accepting the non-eternality of phonemes, since the sequence composed of non-eternal moments is itself non-eternal, the non-eternality of the <s>Vedas</s> — which is a collection of sentences qualified by such sequence — as you maintain, is not established; therefore the non-eternality of phonemes alone is appropriate — this he states with 'of phonemes' (<s>varṇānām</s>).

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
mīmāṃsaka iti/
vedāpauruṣeyatvavādīti śeṣaḥ/ vyavasthāpayatīti/ sādhayatītyarthaḥ/
dīpikāyām pauruṣeyatvasiddheriti/ tathā coktānumānena vedānāṃ
puruṣanirmitatvasiddhyā anāditvamasiddham/ ato 'nāditvāt
kathamīśvaroktatvamiti śaṅkāyā nāvasara iti bhāvaḥ/
upādhitvāditi/ yatrayatra pauruṣeyatvaṃ bhāratādau tatra
smaryamāṇakartṛkatvamastīti smaryamāṇakartṛkatvasya
pauruṣeyatvarūpasādhyavyāpakatvam - yatra sādhanaṃ vākyasamūhatvamasti
pakṣe vede tatra smaryamāṇakartṛkatvaṃ nāstīti tasya
sādhanāvyāpakatvam/ ataḥ smaryabhāṇakartṛkatvamupādhiriti uktānumānaṃ
sopādhikatvāt duṣṭamiti kathaṃ pauruṣeyatvasādhakamityarthaḥ/
gotamādibhiriti/ gotamaḥ svaśiṣyāya vedāḥ sakartṛkā
ityupadideśa, so 'pi svaśiṣyāya tathopadideśetyevaṃ
śiṣyaparamparayā gautamīyāḥ vedānāṃ sakartṛkatvaṃ smaranti/ tathā ca
smaryamāṇakartṛkatvasya pakṣavṛttitayā sādhanāvyāpakatvābhāvāt
nopādhitvamiti dīpikoktaṃ na saṅgacchate/ gotamādayaḥ
tathopadidiśurityatra pramāṇābhāvāt iti śaṅkāyā arthaḥ/
tasmāditīti/ tepānāt tapaḥ kurvata īśvarāt trayo vedā
ajāyanteti śrutyarthaḥ/ tathā ca anayā śrutyaiva
vedānāmīśvarasṛṣṭatvarūpaṃ pauruṣaiyatvaṃ pramitamiti anumānasya
nāpekṣeti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Mīmāṃsaka' — the remainder is: one who maintains the doctrine that the <s>Vedas</s> are not authored by any person (<s>vedāpauruṣeyatva</s>). 'Establishes' — means 'proves.' In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'because of the establishment of authorship' — and thus, since the authorship of the <s>Vedas</s> by a person is established through the stated inference, their beginninglessness (<s>anāditva</s>) is not established. Therefore, the objection 'how can they be spoken by <s>Īśvara</s> since they are beginningless?' has no occasion — this is the intent. 'Because of being a vitiating condition' — wherever there is authorship, as in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, there is a remembered author; thus 'having a remembered author' pervades the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>), namely authorship. But where the probans (<s>sādhana</s>), namely being a collection of sentences, is present — in the case of the <s>Vedas</s> — there is no remembered author; thus [having a remembered author] does not pervade the probans. Therefore, since 'having a remembered author' is a vitiating condition, the stated inference is defective as being subject to a vitiating condition — how then can it prove authorship? This is the meaning. 'By <s>Gautama</s> and others' — <s>Gautama</s> taught his disciple that the <s>Vedas</s> have an author, and that disciple similarly taught his own disciple; thus through the teacher-disciple lineage, the followers of <s>Gautama</s> remember the authorship of the <s>Vedas</s>. And thus, since 'having a remembered author' is present in the case [of the <s>Vedas</s> too], there is no failure to pervade the probans, and hence it is not a vitiating condition — but this statement in the <s>Dīpikā</s> does not hold, because there is no evidence that <s>Gautama</s> and others taught thus. This is the meaning of the objection. 'Therefore' — the meaning of the śruti is: 'From Him who performs austerities, from <s>Īśvara</s>, the three <s>Vedas</s> were born.' And thus, since the authorship of the <s>Vedas</s> in the form of being created by <s>Īśvara</s> is already established by this very śruti, the inference is not needed — this is the intent.

children.text:
anityatve na
sambhavatīti/ yadi varṇāḥ utpattivināśavantaḥ tarhi
pūrvakālikagakārasya naṣṭatvāt etatkālikagakāre tadabhedāvagāhinī
pratyabhijñā na saṅgaccheteti bhāvaḥ/ nanu
varṇānāmutpattivināśāvagāhipratītibalāt utpattivināśavattve siddhe
pūrvottarakālikagakārayorabhedāsambhavāt 'so 'yaṃ gakāraḥ' iti
pratyabhijñā nābhedamavagāhate/ api tu tajjātīyatvam/
pūrvakālikagakāravṛttigatvajātimān etatkālikagakāra iti
pratijñāyā arthaḥ iti dīpikoktaṃ na yujyate/ 'so 'yaṃ gakāra' iti
pratyabhijñayā gakārayorabhede siddhe tadvirodhāt 'utpanno gakāraḥ,
vinaṣṭo gakāra' iti pratītiḥ na gakāre utpattiṃ vināśaṃ vā
avagāhate, api tu varṇavyañjakavāyuviśeṣasaṃyogādigatasya
utpattervināśasya ca varṇe āropamātramityapi vaktuṃ śakyatvāt/ atha vā
utpanna ityasya abhivyakta iti vinaṣṭa ityasya nābhivyakta iti
cārtha ityapi vaktuṃ śakyatvāt/ tathā ca varṇanityatvaṃ
nirbādhamityāśaṅkyāha - utpattivināśapratyayayoriti/ utpanno
gakāraḥ vinaṣṭo gakāraḥ iti pratītyorityarthaḥ/
anyārthakatvakalpaneti/ abhivyaktyādyarthakatvakalpanamapekṣyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Is impossible if non-eternal' — if phonemes possess origination and destruction, then since the earlier ga-sound has perished, the recognition cognizing identity with the earlier ga-sound in the present ga-sound would be impossible — this is the intent. Now, since the non-eternality [of phonemes] — their possessing origination and destruction — is established on the strength of cognitions apprehending origination and destruction of phonemes, and since the identity of the earlier and later ga-sounds is impossible [given non-eternality], the recognition 'This is that same ga-sound' does not apprehend identity but rather generic similarity (<s>tajjātīyatva</s>) — the meaning of the recognition is: 'The present ga-sound possesses the universal (<s>jāti</s>) residing in the earlier ga-sound.' But this statement in the <s>Dīpikā</s> is not tenable. Since the identity of the two ga-sounds is established through the recognition 'This is that same ga-sound,' and since that [identity] contradicts [non-eternality], the cognition 'The ga-sound has arisen, the ga-sound has perished' does not apprehend origination and destruction in the ga-sound itself; rather, it is merely a superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) onto the phoneme of the origination and destruction belonging to the particular air-currents and contacts that manifest the phoneme — this too can be maintained. Or alternatively, 'arisen' means 'manifested' (<s>abhivyakta</s>) and 'perished' means 'not manifested' (<s>nābhivyakta</s>) — this too can be maintained. And thus the eternality of phonemes is unobstructed — anticipating [this objection], he says 'of the cognitions of origination and destruction.' 'Of the cognitions "the ga-sound has arisen" and "the ga-sound has perished"' — this is the meaning. 'Supposing them to have a different referent' — means: depending on the supposition that they refer to manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) and the like.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
smṛtyācārayoḥ
prāmāṇyam
children.translated_text: The authority of <s>Smṛti</s> and customary practice (<s>ācāra</s>)

children.text:
manvādismṛtīnāṃ
ācārāṇāṃ ca vedamūlakatayā prāmāṇyam/ smṛtimūlavākyānāṃ
idānīmanadhyayanāt tanmūlabhūtā kācit śākhā utsanneti kalpyate/
nanu paṭhyamānavedavākyotsādanasya kalpayitumaśakyatayā
viprakīrṇavādasyāyuktatvāt nityānumeyo vedo mūlamiti cet -
na/ tathā sati kadāpi varṇānupūrvījñānābhāvena bodhakatvāsambhavāt/
children.translated_text: The <s>Smṛtis</s> of <s>Manu</s> and others, and customary practices (<s>ācāra</s>), have authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) because they are rooted in the <s>Vedas</s>. Since the Vedic sentences that are the basis of <s>Smṛti</s> are not currently studied, it is postulated that some branch (<s>śākhā</s>) that was their source has been lost. If one objects: since it is impossible to postulate the loss of currently recited Vedic sentences, the theory of dispersal (<s>viprakīrṇavāda</s>) is untenable, and therefore an eternally inferred <s>Veda</s> should be the source — No. Because in that case, since there would never be knowledge of the sequence of phonemes (<s>varṇānupūrvī</s>), [the Veda] could never produce cognition [of its meaning].

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
yadyapi smṛtyādīnāṃ
āptoktatvādeva pramāṇatvaṃ sidhyati tatkartṛmanvādīnāmāptatvāt,
tathāpi teṣāmāptatve vipratipannaṃ pratyāha - manvādīti/
ācārāṇāmiti/ ācārapratipādakaśiṣṭavākyānāmityarthaḥ/ etena
pramāṇavibhāgavyāghātaśaṅkā nirastā/ vedārthaṃ jñātvaiva manvādibhiḥ
tadarthakasmṛtyādīni viracitāni/ atasteṣāṃ prāmāṇyamiti mana si
kṛtvāha - vedamūlakatayeti/ nanu tarhi sa vedaḥ kuto nopalabhyata
ityata āha - smṛtimūleti/
children.translated_text: Although the authority of <s>Smṛti</s> and the like could be established merely by being spoken by a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>), since their authors <s>Manu</s> and others are trustworthy, nevertheless, in response to one who disputes the trustworthiness of those [authors], he says 'Manu and others' and so forth. 'Of customary practices' — means: of the statements of learned persons (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) that convey customary practice. By this, the doubt of inconsistency with the division of means of valid knowledge is removed. Having considered that <s>Manu</s> and others composed the <s>Smṛtis</s> and the like after knowing the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>, and hence their authority [derives from the Vedas], he says 'because of being rooted in the <s>Vedas</s>.' But then, why is that <s>Veda</s> not found? To this he says 'the basis of Smṛti' and so forth.

children.text:
tanmūletyādi/
smṛtyādimūlabhūtā kācit śākhā pāṭhataḥ paribhraṣṭetyanumīyata
ityarthaḥ/ vākyotsādanasya - vākyocchedasya/ nanu
samānānupūrvīkavedapāṭhasya saṃpradāyasiddhatvāt tādṛśavede
katipayavākyocchedasya kalpayitumaśakyatve 'pi paṭhyamānaveda eva
viśakalitatayā vidyamānavākyānāṃ smṛtimūlatvamastītyatāha -
viprakīrṇeti/ ayuktatvāditi/ smṛtyādisamānārthakavākyānāṃ
paṭhyamānavede 'nupalambhāditi bhāvaḥ/ nityānumeya iti/
nityo 'numeyarūpa ityarthaḥ/ varṇānupūrvījñānābhāveneti/
tādṛśajñānasyāpiśābdabodhahetutvāt/ anyathā nadīdīnādiśabdaiḥ
arthaviśeṣabodhānāpattiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Their source' and so forth — it is inferred that some branch that was the source of the <s>Smṛtis</s> and the like has been lost from recitation — this is the meaning. 'Loss of sentences' — means: cessation of sentences. Now, since the recitation of the <s>Vedas</s> with the same sequence of phonemes is established through tradition, even if it is impossible to postulate the loss of certain sentences in such a <s>Veda</s>, the sentences present in the currently recited <s>Veda</s> in a dispersed form could be the source of the <s>Smṛtis</s> — to this he says 'dispersal' (<s>viprakīrṇa</s>). 'Because of being untenable' — because sentences with the same meaning as the <s>Smṛtis</s> and the like are not found in the currently recited <s>Vedas</s> — this is the intent. 'Eternally inferred' — means: eternal and of the nature of being inferred. 'Because of the absence of knowledge of the sequence of phonemes' — because such knowledge is also a cause of verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>). Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that words like 'river' and the like would produce cognition of specific meanings [arbitrarily] — this is the intent.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu ācārasya
vedamūlakatayā pramāṇatvāṅgīkāraṃ kṛtirūpasyācārasya vibhakteṣu
pratyakṣādiṣu caturṣu pramāṇeṣvanantargatatayā atiriktapramāṇatvāpattau
caturdhā pramāṇavibhajanamasaṅgatamityato vyācaṣṭai -
ācārapratipādaketi/ ācārasya anuṣṭhānasya bodhakāni yāni
śiṣṭānāṃ vākyāni teṣāmityarthaḥ/ eteneti/
ācārapadasyoktavākyaparatayāvyākhyānenetyarthaḥ/ vedārthaṃ jñātvaiveti/
tathā ca vedārthajñānapūrvakaṃ viracitatvaṃ vedārthajñānajanyatvaṃ vā
vedamūlakatvamityuktaṃ bhavati/
children.translated_text: Now, if the authority of customary practice (<s>ācāra</s>) is accepted because it is rooted in the <s>Vedas</s>, then since customary practice, being an action, is not included within the four means of valid knowledge — namely perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and the rest — which have been separately enumerated, there would be the unwanted consequence of an additional means of valid knowledge, and the fourfold division of means of valid knowledge would be inconsistent. Therefore he glosses — 'conveying customary practice' and so forth. [The meaning is:] those statements of learned persons (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) that make known the customary practice — of those [statements is the authority]. 'By this' — means: by this gloss that explains the word 'ācāra' as referring to [such] statements. 'After knowing the meaning of the Vedas' — and thus, being composed after knowing the Vedic meaning, or being born from knowledge of the Vedic meaning — this is what is meant by 'being rooted in the Vedas.'

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: śabdasyānumānāntarbhāvaravaṇḍanam/
children.translated_text: Refutation of the subsumption of word (<s>śabda</s>) under inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

children.text:
nanu 'etāni
padāni smāritārthasaṃsargavanti ākāṅkṣādimatpadakadambakatvāt
gāmānaya daṇḍeneti madvākyavat' ityanumānādeva
saṃsargajñānasambhavāt śabdo na pramāṇāntaramiti cet - na/
anumityapekṣayā vilakṣaṇasya śābdajñānasya 'śabdātpratyemi'
ityanuvyavasāyasākṣikasya sarvasaṃmatatvāt/
children.translated_text: If one objects: since cognition of the relation [among word-meanings] is possible through the inference alone — 'These words possess the connection of the meanings recalled [by them], because they are a collection of words possessing mutual expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) and the like, just like my sentence "bring the cow with a stick"' — word (<s>śabda</s>) is not a separate means of valid knowledge. — No. Because verbal cognition (<s>śābdajñāna</s>), which is distinct from inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>), is universally accepted, as attested by the post-cognitive awareness (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>): 'I cognize from word.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
śabdasya pṛthak
pramāṇatvamanaṅgīkurvatāṃ vaiśeṣikāṇāṃ mataṃ dūṣayitumupanyasyati
- nanvetānītyādinā/ etāni padāni - ghaṭamānaya ityādipadāni/
smāritārthasaṃsargavantīti/ smāritārthasaṃsargajñānapūrvakāṇītyarthaḥ/
saṃsarge tātparyaviṣayatvaṃ niveśanīyam/ tena saṃsargāntaramādāya
nārthāntaratā/ ākāṅkṣādītyādinā yogyatāsatyoḥ parigrahaḥ/
ākāṅkṣādirahite padakadambake vyabhicāravāraṇāya ākāṅkṣādīti/
sarvasaṃmatatvāditi/ tathā ca kāryavailakṣaṇyānurodhena śabdaḥ
pramāṇāntaraṃ iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: He presents the view of the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, who do not accept word (<s>śabda</s>) as a separate means of valid knowledge, in order to refute it — with 'but these' (<s>nanu etāni</s>) and so forth. 'These words' — words such as 'bring the pot' and so forth. 'Possess the connection of the meanings recalled' — means: are preceded by the cognition of the connection of the meanings recalled [by the words]. In 'connection,' the qualification of being the object of the speaker's intention (<s>tātparya</s>) should be included. Thereby, by taking a different connection [than the intended one], there is no fallacy of proving something other than what is intended. By 'and the like' in 'expectancy and the like,' fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) and proximity (<s>sannidhi</s>) are included. 'Possessing expectancy and the like' [is stated] to prevent over-pervasion (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in a collection of words lacking expectancy and the like. 'Because it is universally accepted' — and thus, in accordance with the distinctness of the resultant cognition (<s>kārya</s>), word (<s>śabda</s>) is a separate means of valid knowledge — this is the intent.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
smāritārthasaṃsargajñānapūrvakāṇītyartha iti/
ghaṭamānayetyādivākyaghaṭakaghaṭādipadaiḥ smāritāḥ
tādṛśapadajanyasmṛtiviṣayabhūtāḥ ye padārthāḥ teṣāṃ yaḥ saṃsargaḥ
tadbiṣayakajñānapūrvakāṇītyarthaḥ/ tathā ca smāritārthajñānapūrvakatvaṃ
sādhyam/ sādhyaghaṭakaṃ yat jñānaṃ tat 'arthaṃ buddhvā śabdaracanā'
iti nyāyasiddhaṃ śabdaracanāhetubhūtaṃ vaktṛgataṃ jñānaṃ,
tajjanyatvātmakaṃ tatpūrvakatvaṃ ghaṭamānayetyādivākyaghaṭakapadeṣu
vartate/ na caivamapi vākyārthajñānapūrvakatvasya vākyārthajñānasya vā
sādhyatve 'pi saṃsargarūpasya vākyārthasyāsādhyatvāt vākyārthajñānasya
kathamanumitirūpatvam, tadabhāve kathaṃ tajjanakavākyasyānumānavidhayā
pramāṇatvamiti vācyam/ saṃsargaviṣayakatvaviśiṣṭajñānasya sādhyatvena
vidheyakoṭipraviṣṭasya saṃsargasyāpi sādhyatvāt/
saṃsargāntaramādāyeti/ ghaṭamānayetyādau ghaṭakarmatvayoḥ
karmatvānayanayośca
tātparyāviṣayakālīkasaṃsargajñānapūrvakatvasiddhiprayuktasyārthāntarasya
vāraṇāya saṃsarge tātparyaviṣayatvaṃ viśeṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/ padārthe
children.translated_text: 'Means: preceded by the cognition of the connection of the meanings recalled' — the meanings that are recalled — that is, the word-meanings that are the objects of the remembrance produced by words such as 'pot' and so forth, which are components of sentences like 'bring the pot' — their connection, the cognition having that [connection] as its object, preceded by that [cognition] — this is the meaning. And thus, being preceded by the cognition of the recalled meanings is the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>). The cognition that is a component of the probandum is the speaker's cognition that is the cause of sentence-composition, established by the principle 'sentence-composition [occurs] after knowing the meaning' (<s>arthaṃ buddhvā śabdaracanā</s>). The property of being produced by that [cognition], which constitutes being preceded by it, is present in the words that are components of sentences like 'bring the pot.' Nor should one say: even if the probandum is being preceded by the cognition of the sentence-meaning, or even if it is the cognition of the sentence-meaning itself, since the sentence-meaning in the form of the connection [of word-meanings] is not to be proved, how can the cognition of the sentence-meaning be of the nature of inference, and in the absence of that, how can the sentence that produces it have the status of a means of valid knowledge in the manner of inference? — [This should not be said] because the connection, which enters the predicate-side of the probandum qualified by having-the-connection-as-its-object, is also to be proved. 'By taking a different connection' — in [sentences like] 'bring the pot,' cognition preceded by the cognition of the connection between pot-hood and object-hood, and between object-hood and bringing — the establishment of being preceded by cognition of a connection that is not the object of the speaker's intention, which would result in proving something other than intended — to prevent this, the qualification 'being the object of the speaker's intention' is applied to 'connection' — this is the intent. In the word-meanings,

children.text:
smāritatvaviśeṣaṇasya
prayojanamitthamuktam muktāvalīprabhāyām-"naiyāyikamate
ghaṭamityādivākyajanye ādheyatāsambandhena
ghaṭaprakārakakarmatvaviśiṣyakaśābdabodhe 'ghaṭamiti vākyam
ghaṭapadārthaṃprakārakādheyatvasaṃsargakāmpadārthaviśeṣyakapratītīcchayā
uccaritam' ityākārakaṃ padārthatvena
padārthāvagāhitātparyajñānameva kāraṇam/ tathā
cāmpadārthaviśeṣyakādheyatāsaṃsargakaghaṭapadārthaprakārakajñānasyāpi
tātparyaviṣayapadārthasaṃsargajñānarūpatayā
tādṛśajñānapūrvakatvasiddhimādāyārthāntaram/ karmantvam
ādheyatāsambandhena ghaṭaviśiṣṭamiti
ghaṭatvāvacchinnaghaṭīyatvenādheyatāsaṃsargakajñānasyaivābhimatatvāt/
ataḥsmāritatvaṃ padārthaviśeṣaṇam
padanirūpitavṛttijñānajanyopasthitiviṣayatāvacchedakatvopalakṣitadhamārvacchinna
ityarthaḥ/ evaṃ cāmpadārthaḥ
children.translated_text: The purpose of the qualifier 'being recollected' (<s>smāritatva</s>) is stated thus in the <s>Muktāvalīprabhā</s>: 'In the Naiyāyika view, in the verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>) produced by a sentence such as 'ghaṭam' (the pot [as object]), which has pot-ness as its qualifier and objecthood (<s>karmatva</s>) as its qualificand through the relation of superstratum (<s>ādheyatā</s>), the cause is solely the <s>tātparya</s>-knowledge (knowledge of purport) that apprehends the word-meaning as word-meaning, having the form: the sentence 'ghaṭam' is uttered with the desire for a cognition having the meaning of the accusative suffix as qualificand, superstratum-relation as relator, and the meaning of the word 'ghaṭa' as qualifier.' And thus, since the cognition having the meaning of the accusative suffix as qualificand, superstratum-relation as relator, and the meaning of the word 'ghaṭa' as qualifier also has the nature of knowledge of the relation of word-meanings that are the objects of purport, establishing its being preceded by such knowledge leads to a different conclusion. Since the intended cognition is only that which apprehends superstratum-relation through pot-ness-delimited pot-belonging-ness, where objecthood is qualified by pot through the superstratum relation — therefore 'being recollected' is a qualifier of word-meaning, meaning: delimited by a property indicated by being the delimitor of the content of the presentation generated by the knowledge of the denotative function determined by the word. And thus the meaning of the accusative suffix

children.text:
ādheyatvasambandhena
ghaṭapadārthaviśiṣṭa iti jñānasya ghaṭapadārthatvaviśiṣṭīyatvena
ādheyatāsaṃsargāvagāhitve 'pi
niruktaviṣayatāvacchedakatvopalakṣitaghaṭatvādyavacchinnīyatvena
ādheyatvānavagāhitvānnārthāntaraprasaktiḥ"iti/ dinakaryāmapi -"tātparyajñāne itarapadārthasyetarapadārthatvena praveśāt
ghaṭatvādinā smṛtasya saṃsargona sidhyet ataḥ samāriteti"iti
saṅkṣipyoktamatrānusandheyam/ ākāṅkṣādirahite padakadambaka
iti/ ghaṭaḥ karmatvam ānayanaṃ kṛtirityādau/
kāryavailakṣṇyānurodheneti/ kāryamatrānuvyavasayaḥ anumitisthale
anuminomītyākārakaḥ śābdabodhasthapale
children.translated_text: is qualified by the meaning of the word 'ghaṭa' through the superstratum relation' — even though this cognition apprehends superstratum-relation through pot-word-meaning-ness-qualified-belonging-ness, since it does not apprehend superstratum through belonging-ness delimited by pot-ness and the like as indicated by the stated delimitor of content, there is no undesirable consequence of a different conclusion.' In the <s>Dinakarī</s> too: 'Since in <s>tātparya</s>-knowledge (purport-knowledge) the other word-meaning enters as the other word-meaning, the relation with what is recollected through pot-ness and the like would not be established; hence [the qualifier] being recollected' — this is stated in brief and should be investigated here. 'A mere collection of words devoid of expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) and the rest' — as in [the unconnected collection] 'pot, objecthood, bringing, effort' and so on. 'In accordance with the distinctiveness of the result' — the result here is the reflective judgment (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>); in the case of inference it has the form 'I infer,' while in the case of verbal cognition,

children.text:
śabdāt
pratyemītyekārakaḥ/ atha vā kāryaṃ anumitiḥ śābdabodhaśca
tayorviṃlakṣaṇatvānusāreṇetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: it has the form 'I cognize from the word.' Alternatively, the results are inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>) and verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>), and the meaning is: in accordance with the distinctiveness of those two.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
arthāpatyādīnāṃ
pramāṇāntaratvanirāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Refutation of the status of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) and others as separate means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)

children.text:
nanu arthāpattirapi
pramāṇāntaramasti, 'pīno devadatto divā na bhuṅkte' iti dṛṣṭe
śrute vā pīnatvānyathānupapattyā rātribhojanaṃ arthāpattyā kalpyata
iti cet - na/ 'devadatto rātrau bhuṅkte divābhuñjānatve sati
pīnatvāt' ityanumānenaiva rātribhojanasya siddhatvāt/
śatepañcāśaditi sambhavo 'pyanumānamave/ 'iha vaṭe yakṣastiṣṭhati'
ityaitihyamapi ajñātamūlavaktṛkaśabda eva/ ceṣṭāpi śabdānumānadvārā
vyavahāraheturiti na pramāṇāntaram/ tasmāt
pratyakṣānumānopamānaśabdāḥ catvāryeva pramāṇāni/
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>:] Objection: <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) too is an additional <s>pramāṇa</s>. When it is seen or heard that 'the stout <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day,' eating at night is postulated through <s>arthāpatti</s> due to the impossibility of accounting for his stoutness otherwise. Reply: No. Because eating at night is established by inference (<s>anumāna</s>) alone, in the form: '<s>Devadatta</s> eats at night, because of his stoutness despite not eating during the day.' <s>Sambhava</s> (inclusion), as in 'fifty in a hundred,' is also inference alone. <s>Aitihya</s> (tradition), as in 'a <s>Yakṣa</s> dwells in this banyan tree,' is merely testimony (<s>śabda</s>) whose original speaker is unknown. <s>Ceṣṭā</s> (gesture) too is a cause of practical activity only through the medium of testimony and inference, and is therefore not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. Hence, perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), and testimony (<s>śabda</s>) — these four alone are the means of valid knowledge.

children.text:
iti dīpikāyāṃ
śabdaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) in the <s>Dīpikā</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
mīmāṃsakaḥ
śaṅkate - nanviti/ 'divā na bhuṅkte' ityarthe dṛṣṭe - pratyakṣato
jñāte, śrute - śabdādavagate/ etena dṛṣṭārthāpattiḥ
śrutārthāpattiścetyarthāpattidvaividhyaṃ sūcitam/
pīnatvānyathānupapattyeti/ pīnatvasyarātribhojanaṃ
vinānupapattyetyarthaḥ/ atredamavadheyam - yadvinā yadanupapannaṃ
tattadupapādakamiti rātribhojanamupapādakam, pīnatvamupapādyam,
upapādakajñānaṃ phalam, upapādyajñānaṃ karaṇam/
phalakaraṇayorarthāpattiśabdo vartate/ phale 'arthasya āpattiḥ kalpanā'
iti vyutpattyā/ karaṇe tu 'arthasya āpattiḥ kalpanā yasmāt' iti
vyutpattyeti/ vyatirekyanumānenaiva gatārthatvāt arthāpatteḥ
pramāṇāntaratvaṃ anucitamiti samādhattedevadatta iti/
divāmātrabhojini pīṃne vyabhicāravāraṇāya satyantam/
ahorātrābhojinyapīṃne vyabhicāravāraṇāya viśeṣyam/ tacca
yogādyajanyapīnatvaparam/ tena bhojanaśūnye yogini pīne na
vyabhicāraḥ/
children.translated_text: The <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> raises an objection — with 'nanu.' 'When the meaning that he does not eat during the day is seen' — known through perception; 'heard' — known through testimony. By this the twofold division of <s>arthāpatti</s> into <s>dṛṣṭārthāpatti</s> (presumption from what is seen) and <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (presumption from what is heard) is indicated. 'Due to the impossibility of accounting for stoutness otherwise' — the meaning is: due to the impossibility of accounting for stoutness without eating at night. Here the following should be noted: that without which something cannot be accounted for, that is the explainer (<s>upapādaka</s>) of the latter — thus eating at night is the explainer, stoutness is the explained (<s>upapādya</s>), knowledge of the explainer is the result (<s>phala</s>), and knowledge of the explained is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). The term <s>arthāpatti</s> applies to both the result and the instrument: to the result by the etymology 'the postulation, i.e. assumption, of a fact,' and to the instrument by the etymology 'that from which the postulation of a fact [arises].' Since the matter is already established by negative inference (<s>vyatirekyānumāna</s>) alone, the status of <s>arthāpatti</s> as a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> is inappropriate — he resolves this with '<s>Devadatta</s>.' The word 'sati' [in the inference] is to prevent deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in the case of one who is stout but eats only during the day. The qualificand [stoutness] is to prevent deviation in the case of one who is not stout and eats neither during the day nor at night. And that [stoutness] refers to stoutness not produced by yoga and the like. Hence there is no deviation in the case of a stout <s>yogin</s> who does not eat.

children.text:
sambhavaitihyayoratiriktapramāṇatvaṃ vadatāṃ paurāṇikānāṃ mataṃ
dūṣayati - śate pañcāśadityādinā/ anumānameveti/ anumānameva, na
tu pramāṇāntaramityarthaḥ/ śatavānityukte pañcāśadvāniti jñānaṃ
sambhavati tasyānumānenaiva nirvāhāt/ śatasya
pañcāśadvyāpyatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ ajñātamūleti/
viśiṣyāniścitaprathamavaktṛkaḥ śabdaḥ na tu pramāṇāntaramityarthaḥ/
tādṛśaśabdasya yathārthatve śabdapramāṇamadhye 'ntarbhāvaḥ/ anyathā tu
apramāṇameveti hṛdayam/ nanvanayā ceṣṭayā ayamartho boddhavya iti
saṅketitaceṣṭayā vijātīyapramājananāt ceṣṭāyā api
pramāṇāntaratvaṃ iti vadantaṃ nirasyati - ceṣṭāpīti/
śabdānumānadvāreti/ śabdadvārā anumānadvārā vā, na tu
svātantryeṇetyarthaḥ/ ceṣṭayā kalpitasya śabdasya pramāpakatve gauravāt
anumānānusaraṇam/ vyavahāreti/ pramātmakajñānetyarthaṃḥ/ upasaṃharati -
tasmāditi/
children.translated_text: He refutes the view of the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> who hold that <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion) and <s>aitihya</s> (tradition) are additional <s>pramāṇas</s> — beginning with 'fifty in a hundred.' 'Inference alone' — the meaning is: inference alone, not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. When it is stated that something possesses a hundred, the knowledge that it possesses fifty arises, and this is accomplished by inference alone. The purport is: because a hundred pervades fifty. 'Of unknown origin' — the meaning is: it is testimony whose first speaker is specifically undetermined, not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. If such testimony is veridical, it is subsumed under verbal testimony (<s>śabda-pramāṇa</s>); otherwise it is simply not a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all — this is the underlying thought. Objection: Since gesture (<s>ceṣṭā</s>), when conventionally established as 'this meaning should be understood by this gesture,' generates valid cognition of a different kind, gesture too should be a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> — he refutes this with '<s>ceṣṭā</s> too.' 'Through the medium of testimony and inference' — through the medium of testimony or through the medium of inference, not independently — this is the meaning. When the word conventionally established through gesture has the capacity to generate valid knowledge, inference is followed due to the cumbersomeness [of an independent account]. 'Cause of practical activity' — he explains the word 'practical activity' (<s>vyavahāra</s>) as meaning valid cognition — with 'meaning valid cognition.' By the derivation 'that by which one transacts,' the word <s>vyavahāra</s> in this context means valid cognition — this is the meaning.

children.text:
iti prakāśikāyāṃ
śabdaparicchadaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
ityartha iti/
divā bhojanābhāvarūper'the ityarthaḥ/ dṛṣṭārthāpattiriti/ pratyakṣato
jñātasya divā abhañjānaniṣṭhasya pīnatvasya yamarthaṃ rātribhojanākhyaṃ
vinānupapattiḥ tasya rātribhojanākhyasyārthasya kalpanaṃ dṛṣṭārthāpattiḥ/
śrutasya 'pīnāṃ devadatto
children.translated_text: 'This is the meaning' — the meaning is: regarding the fact that he does not eat during the day. '<s>Dṛṣṭārthāpatti</s>' — the stoutness residing in [<s>Devadatta</s>] who is perceived as not eating during the day — the postulation of eating at night, without which that stoutness cannot be accounted for, is <s>dṛṣṭārthāpatti</s> (presumption from what is seen). The stoutness known from the heard statement '<s>Devadatta</s> is stout

children.text:
divā na bhuṅkte'
ityādivākyādavagatasya pīnatvasya yamarthaṃ vinānupapattiḥ tasya
rātribhojanasya kalpanaṃ śrutārthāpattiḥ/ nanvarthāpattipramiteḥ
arthāpattipramāṇasya ca kiṃ lakṣaṇam/ na hi tallakṣaṇamavijñāya
tatpramāṇāntaratvavicāraḥ kartuṃ śakya ityata āha -
atredamavadheyamityādi/ yadvinā rātribhojanaṃ vinā yadanupapannaṃ
pīnatvamanupapannam/ tat rātribhojanaṃ tadupapādakaṃ
pīnatvasyopapādakam/ upapādyajñānena upapādakajñānamarthāpattirūpā
pramitiḥ/ upapādyasya pīnatvasya jñānena upapādakasya rātribhojanasya
jñānaṃ bhavati iti
children.translated_text: and does not eat during the day' — the postulation of eating at night, without which that stoutness cannot be accounted for, is <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (presumption from what is heard). Objection: What is the definition of the cognition produced by <s>arthāpatti</s> and of the <s>arthāpatti-pramāṇa</s> itself? For without knowing that definition, one cannot investigate whether it is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. To this he says — 'here the following should be noted' and so forth. 'That without which' — without eating at night; 'that which cannot be accounted for' — stoutness cannot be accounted for. 'That' — eating at night — 'is the explainer of that' — the explainer of stoutness. The valid cognition in the form of <s>arthāpatti</s> is: through the knowledge of the explained (<s>upapādya</s>), the knowledge of the explainer (<s>upapādaka</s>) arises. That is, through the knowledge of stoutness, the knowledge of eating at night arises —

children.text:
samanvayaḥ/ na ca
upapādyajñānaviṣayako yo 'nuvyavasāyaḥ pīnatvamahaṃ jānāmītyākārakaḥ
tasyāpi upapādyajñānaviṣayako yo 'nuvyavasāyaḥ pīnatvamahaṃ
jānāmītyākārakaḥ tasyāpi upapādyajñānajanyatvāt tatrātivyāptiriti
vācyam/ upapādyajñānatvenopapādyajñānajanyatvasya vivakṣitatvāt/
anuvyavasāyātmakamānasapratyakṣasya viṣayavidhayā upapādyajñānajanyatve 'pi
upapādyajñānatvena tajjanyatvābhāvāt nātivyāptiḥ/ tathā
copapādyaviṣayakajñānatvāvacchinnajanakatānirūpitajanyatāśālijñānatvamarthāpattipramāyāḥ
lakṣaṇam ityuktaṃ bhavati/ tādṛśajñānakaraṇatvamarthāpattipramāṇasya
lakṣaṇam/ phalakaraṇayoriti/ pramitau pramāṇe cetyarthaḥ/
vyatirekyanumānenaiveti/"devadatto rātrau bhuṅkte divā
abhuñjānatve sati pīnatvāt yo rātrau na bhuṅkte sa divā
abhuñjānatve sati pīno na bhavati yathā rātrau divā cābhuñjānaḥ
kṛśo maharṣiḥ na tathā cāyam tasmānna tathā"iti prayogo 'tra
vivakṣitaḥ/ kecitu - yo divā abhuñjānatve sati pīnaḥ saḥ rātrau
bhuṅkte yathā pratinaktamātraṃ bhuñjāno yajñadattaḥ
ityanvayyanumānenāpyarthāpattergantārthatāmāhuḥ/ satyantāmiti/
satyantānupādāne rātribhojanarūpasādhyābhāvavati
divāmātrabhojanakartari pīne yajñadatte pīnatvarūpahetusatvāt
vyabhicāraḥ/ tadvāraṇāya divā abhuñjānatve satīti viśeṣaṇam/ divā
bhuñjānatvameva yajñadatte 'stīti na vyabhicāraḥ/ ahorātrābhojinīti/
tathā ca pīnatvāditi viśeṣyānupādāne devadatto rātrau bhuṅkte
divā abhuñjānatvādityeva hetuḥ syāt/ tathā sati yastāpasaḥ
divāpi na bhuṅkte rātrāvapi na bhuṅkte ata eva kṛśaḥ tasmin
rātribhojanarūpasādadhyābhāvavati divā abhuñjānatvarūpahetusatvāt
tatra vyabhicāraḥ/ tadvāraṇāya pīnatvāditi/ tasmiṃstāpase ca
pīnatvābhāvāt na vyabhicāraḥ/ nanvevamapi yo yogī na bhuṅkte
athāpi yogamāhātmyāt pīno bhavati, tasmin
rātribhojanakartṛtvarūpasādhyābhāvavati divā abhuñjānatve sati
pīnatvarūpahetusatvāt vyabhicāra ityāśaṅkyāha - tacca
yogādyajanyapīnatvaparamiti tathā ca yogini yat pīnatvaṃ tat
yogajanyamiti yogajanyapīnatvābhāvāt na vyabhicāra iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: this is the synthesis. And it cannot be objected that the reflective judgment (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) directed at the knowledge of the explained, having the form 'I know stoutness,' since that too is produced by the knowledge of the explained, would lead to over-pervasion — because what is intended is being produced by the knowledge of the explained qua knowledge of the explained. Since mental perception in the form of reflective judgment, though produced by the knowledge of the explained in the mode of having it as its object, is not produced by it qua knowledge of the explained, there is no over-pervasion. And thus it is stated that the definition of the valid cognition of <s>arthāpatti</s> is: being a cognition possessing the product-ness determined by the producer-ness delimited by being cognition of the explained. The definition of the <s>arthāpatti-pramāṇa</s> (instrument) is: being the instrument of such cognition. 'Of the result and the instrument' — meaning: of the valid cognition and of the means of knowledge. 'By negative inference alone' — the intended formulation is: '<s>Devadatta</s> eats at night, because of stoutness despite not eating during the day. Whoever does not eat at night is not stout despite not eating during the day, like an emaciated great sage who eats neither during the day nor at night. But this [<s>Devadatta</s>] is not like that; therefore he is not like that.' Some say that the matter of <s>arthāpatti</s> can also be established by positive inference (<s>anvayānumāna</s>): 'Whoever is stout despite not eating during the day eats at night, like <s>Yajñadatta</s> who eats only at night.' 'The word sati' — if sati were not included, there would be deviation in the case of stout <s>Yajñadatta</s> who eats during the day [only], since the <s>hetu</s> in the form of stoutness would be present in him while the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of eating at night would be absent. To prevent that, 'despite not eating during the day' is the qualifier. Since the property of eating during the day is present in <s>Yajñadatta</s>, there is no deviation. 'One who eats neither during the day nor at night' — and thus, if the qualificand 'because of stoutness' were not included, the <s>hetu</s> would be merely 'because of not eating during the day.' In that case, an ascetic who eats neither during the day nor at night and is therefore emaciated — since the <s>hetu</s> in the form of not eating during the day would be present in him while the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of eating at night would be absent, there would be deviation. To prevent that, 'because of stoutness' [is added]. Since stoutness is absent in that ascetic, there is no deviation. But even so, a <s>yogin</s> who does not eat yet is stout due to the power of yoga — since the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of being one who eats at night would be absent in him, while the <s>hetu</s> in the form of stoutness despite not eating during the day would be present, there would be deviation — anticipating this he says 'and that refers to stoutness not produced by yoga and the like.' And thus, since the stoutness in the <s>yogin</s> is produced by yoga, and stoutness not produced by yoga is absent [in him], there is no deviation — this is the purport.

children.text:
śatavānityukta
ityādi/ śatasaṅkhyākabrāhyaṇādhikaraṇe adhiveśane
pañcāśatsaṅkhyākabrāhmaṇāḥ santi na veti sandehānantaraṃ
śatatvasaṅkhyāvataḥ samūhasya pañcāśatsaṅkhyāvadghaṭitatvena
śatavastvadhikaraṇe pañcāśadvastusambhava ityākārakajñānarūpāt
sambhavapramāṇāt iha pañcāśat brāhmaṇāḥ santīti
nirṇayātmakapramittyutpatyā sambhavo 'pi pramāṇāntaramiti kecit/ tanna
- idamadhiveśanaṃ pañcāśadbrāhmaṇavat śatabrāhmaṇavatvāt yat
śatasaṅkhyākavastumat tat pañcāśatsaṅkhyākavastumat yathā
śataghaṭādhikaraṇaṃ bhūtalam iti
sāmānyamukhavyāptiparāmarśajanyānumitirūpaiva sambhavātmikā
pramitiḥ, ato na sambhavaḥ pramāṇāntaramiti bhāvaḥ/ śatasya
pañcāśavdyāpyatvāditi/ yatra śatasaṅvyākapadārthāḥ tatra
pañcāśatsaṅkhyākapadārthā iti vyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'When it is stated that [a place] possesses a hundred' and so forth — after there arises doubt whether fifty <s>brāhmaṇas</s> are present or not in a gathering that is the locus of a hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, some hold that <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion) is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>, on the ground that from the <s>sambhava-pramāṇa</s> — the cognition having the form 'since a group possessing the number hundred is constituted by [groups] possessing the number fifty, it is possible that there are fifty in the locus of a hundred' — the definitive valid cognition arises that 'there are fifty <s>brāhmaṇas</s> here.' That is not so — [the reply is:] the cognition constituting <s>sambhava</s> is nothing but an inference in the form: 'This gathering possesses fifty <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, because it possesses a hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s>; whatever possesses things numbering a hundred possesses things numbering fifty, like a ground that is the locus of a hundred pots' — generated from an inferential judgment via a general pervasion. Hence <s>sambhava</s> is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the purport. 'Because a hundred pervades fifty' — the <s>vyāpti</s> is: wherever there are objects numbering a hundred, there are objects numbering fifty.

children.text:
śabdadvāreti/ yathā
lipidarśanaṃ śabdasmṛtiṃ janayitvā śābdabodhaṃ prayojayatīti
paramparayā kāraṇatve 'pi karaṇatvābhāvāt na pramāṇam, tathā ceṣṭāpi
dvitvabodhakaśabdasmṛtidvārā dvitvādibodhaprayojikā na tatkaraṇamiti
na pramāṇamiti bhāvaḥ/ anumānadvāreti/
ceṣṭamānasyābhiprāyaviśeṣānumānadvāretyarthaḥ/ ayaṃ
dvitvabodhatātparyavān
dvitvabodhakatvāvinābhūtavilakṣaṇaceṣṭāvatvādityanumānākāro
vivakṣitaḥ/ nanu vyavahāraheturityatra vyavahārapadasya pravṛttiparatve
taddhetutvaṃ dvitvādijñāna evāsti na tu paramparayā
jñānajanakaceṣṭāyāmityāśaṅkya vyavahārapadaṃ pramāparatayā vyācaṣṭe -
pramātmakajñānetyartha iti/ vyavahriyate aneneti vyutpatyā
vyavahārapadaṃ prakṛte pramātmakajñānārthakamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Through the medium of testimony' — just as seeing a written letter, though indirectly causal by generating the recollection of the word and thereby occasioning verbal cognition, is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> because it lacks instrumentality (<s>karaṇatva</s>), similarly gesture too, though it occasions the cognition of duality and the like through the medium of recollection of the word that signifies duality, is not the instrument thereof and hence not a <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the purport. 'Through the medium of inference' — the meaning is: through the medium of inferring the specific intention of the person who is gesticulating. The intended form of inference is: 'This person has the purport of communicating duality, because he possesses a distinctive gesture that is invariably concomitant with the capacity to communicate duality.' Objection: In 'cause of practical activity,' if the word 'practical activity' (<s>vyavahāra</s>) means purposive action, then its being caused belongs to the cognition of duality and the like, not to gesture which is only an indirect cause of knowledge — anticipating this, he explains the word <s>vyavahāra</s> as meaning valid cognition — with 'meaning valid cognition.' By the derivation 'that by which one transacts,' the word <s>vyavahāra</s> in this context means valid cognition — this is the meaning.

children.text:
iti
tarkasaṅgrahadīpikāprakāśikāvyāravyāyāṃ bālapriyāyāṃ
śabdaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) in the <s>Bālapriyā</s>, which is a super-commentary on the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha-Dīpikā-Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text: prāmāṇyavādaḥ
children.translated_text: The doctrine of validity (<s>prāmāṇyavāda</s>)

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
tatra
vipratipattipradarśanam
children.translated_text: Therein, the presentation of disagreement (<s>vipratipatti</s>)

children.text:
jñānānāṃ tadvati
tatprakārakatvaṃ svatogrāhyaṃ parato veti vicāryate/ tatra vipratipattiḥ
- jñānaprāmāṇyaṃ tadaprāmāṇyāgrāhakayāvajjñānagrāhakasāmagrīgrāhyaṃ na vā
iti/ atra vidhikoṭiḥ svatastvam niṣeghakoṭiḥ paratastvam/
children.translated_text: It is investigated whether the property of cognitions being qualificative of what is real (<s>tadvati tatprakārakatva</s>) is grasped intrinsically (<s>svataḥ</s>) or extrinsically (<s>parataḥ</s>). The dispute therein is: is the validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of cognition grasped by the same aggregate of causes that grasps the cognition, which does not grasp invalidity — or not? Here the affirmative side is <s>svatastva</s> (intrinsic validity), and the negative side is <s>paratastva</s> (extrinsic validity).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
pramāṇaprasaṅgāt
pramātvasya parato grāhyatvaṃ vyavasthāpayiṣyan āha - jñānānāmiti/
ṣaṣṭyartha ādheyatvam/ tasya cānvayaḥ tadvati tatprakārakatve/ tacca
tadvadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnatatprakārakatvam/ tacchabdārthoghaṭatvādirūpaḥ/
svatogrāhyamiti/ jñānagrāhakasāmagrījanyagrahaviṣaya ityarthaḥ/ parata
iti/ grāhyamityanuṣajyate/ anumānādijanyagrahaviṣaya ityarthaḥ/ tatra
- vicāre/ prayojakatvaṃ saptamyarthaḥ vipratipattāvanveti/ kathaṃ tasyāḥ
vicāraprayojakatvamiti cet - atra vadanti/
viruddhārthapratipādakavākyadvayaṃ hi vipratipattiḥ/ tayā
aprāmāṇyaśaṅkākabalitatattadvākyārthabodhadvārā madhyasthasya saṃśayo
janyata ityekatarakoṭiniścayāya nyāyaprayogādirūpo vicāraḥ/
evaṃ ca vicāropayogisaṃśayajananyā
vipratipattervicāropayogitvamakṣatamiti/ jñānaprāmāṇyamiti
pakṣanirdeśaḥ/ atra tadvati tatprakārakajñānatvarūpameva prāmāṇyaṃ pakṣaḥ, na
tu pramitikaraṇatvarūpam iti
children.translated_text: Intending to establish that validity (<s>prāmātva</s>) is grasped extrinsically, due to the occasion of [discussing] <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), he says 'of cognitions' (<s>jñānānām</s>). The meaning of the genitive is superstratum-hood (<s>ādheyatva</s>). Its syntactic connection is with 'being qualificative of what possesses that.' And that [qualification] is the being-qualificative-of-that delimited by having-that-as-qualificandum. The referent of the word 'that' is of the form of pot-hood, cloth-hood, and so forth. 'Grasped intrinsically' (<s>svataḥ grāhyam</s>) — the meaning is: the object of a grasping produced by the same aggregate that grasps the cognition. 'Extrinsically' (<s>parataḥ</s>) — 'grasped' is carried over; the meaning is: the object of a grasping produced by inference and the like. 'Therein' — in the investigation. The meaning of the locative is causality, which connects with 'dispute' (<s>vipratipatti</s>). How is the dispute the cause of investigation? To this they say: A dispute is indeed a pair of statements conveying contradictory meanings. Through the understanding of the respective statement-meanings, which are engulfed by the doubt of invalidity, doubt is generated in a neutral observer — hence investigation, in the form of application of reasoning (<s>nyāyaprayoga</s>) and the like, is undertaken to ascertain one of the two alternatives. Thus, the usefulness of dispute for investigation remains intact, since the dispute generates the doubt that is useful for investigation. '<s>Jñānaprāmāṇya</s>' — this is the statement of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). Here, what is intended as the thesis is validity in the form of cognition-hood that is qualificative of what possesses that, not in the form of being an instrument of valid cognition (<s>pramitikaraṇatva</s>) —

children.text:
tātparyagrāhakaṃ
jñānapadam/ vastutastu tadvati tatprakārakatvasya
ghaṭatvapaṭatvādirūpārthabhedena bhinnatayā kasyāpi prāmāṇyasya
yāvajjñānagrāhakasāmagrīgrāhyatvaṃ na sambhavati ityato
yaddharmaghaṭitaprāmāṇyaṃ yadā pakṣaḥ tadā
taddharmaprakārakajñānagrāhakayāvadgrāhyatvameva sādhanīyam/ na tu
sāmānyato jñānagrāhakayāvadgrāhyatvamiti tātparyagrāhakaṃ jñānapadam/
tadaprāmāṇyetyādi/ tadaprāmāṇyāgrāhikā yāvatī jñānagrāhikā sāmagrī
tajjanyagrahaviṣayo na vetyarthaḥ/ tādṛśagrahaḥ gurumate vyavasāyaḥ/
murārimiśramate anuvyavasāyaḥ/ bhāṭṭamate ca
jñātatāliṅgakānumitiḥ/ atra gurumate sarvasminneva jñāne
mitimātṛ-meya-etattrayaṃ bhāsate/ tanmate 'ghaṭatvena ghaṭaṃ ahaṃ
jānāmi' ityākārakasyaiva vyavasāyasya utpatteḥ/ evaṃ ca vyavasāyasya
svaprakāśātmakatayā svenaiva svagataprāmāṇyasya grahaṇāt bhavati
prāmāṇyasya svatogrāhyatvam/ viśiṣṭabuddhiṃ prati viśeṣaṇajñānasya
kāraṇatāyāḥ tairanaṅgīkārāt anupasthitasyāpi prāmāṇyasya
bhānasambhavāt/ miśramate 'ayaṃ ghaṭaḥ' ityākārakajñānānantaraṃ
'ghaṭatvena ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmi' iti
jñānaviṣayakalaukikamānasamutpadyate, tena prāmāṇyasya grahaṇam/
bhaṭṭamate tu jñānasyātīndriyatayā jñātatāliṅgakānumitereva
prāthamikajñānagraharūpatayā tayā prāmāṇyaṃ gṛhyate/ anumānaprayogastu -
ghaṭaḥ ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakaghaṭatvaprakārakajñānaviṣayaḥ
ghaṭatvaprakārakajñātatāvattvāt yannaivaṃ tannaivam iti/ jñātatā ca
saviṣayako jñānajanyaḥ atirikta padārtha iti matavivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: the word '<s>jñāna</s>' (cognition) serves to indicate this purport. In reality, however, since the property of being qualificative of what possesses that (<s>tadvati tatprakārakatva</s>) is differentiated by different object-properties such as pot-hood, cloth-hood, and the like, it is not possible for the validity of any [particular] cognition to be grasped by the aggregate that grasps all cognitions. Therefore, when the validity constituted by a particular property is the thesis, only the grasping by the aggregate that grasps the cognition having that property as qualifier is to be proved — not the grasping by the aggregate that grasps cognition in general. This is why the word '<s>jñāna</s>' indicates the purport. 'Of its invalidity' and so forth — the meaning is: is [validity] the object of a grasping produced by the aggregate that grasps cognition, which is as extensive as [what is needed] but does not grasp the invalidity of that [cognition], or not? Such grasping, in the view of the Teacher [<s>Prabhākara</s>], is <s>vyavasāya</s> (determinate cognition). In the view of <s>Murārimiśra</s>, it is <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (reflective cognition). And in the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> view, it is inference based on the mark of being-cognized (<s>jñātatā</s>). Here, in the Teacher's view, in every cognition, the triad of the cognized, the cognizer, and the cognizable appears. In that view, only the <s>vyavasāya</s> of the form 'I cognize the pot as pot-hood' arises. And thus, since <s>vyavasāya</s>, being self-luminous, grasps by itself the validity present in itself, the intrinsic graspability of validity follows. Because they do not accept the causality of qualifier-cognition with respect to qualified cognition, it is possible for validity to appear even when not previously presented. In the view of <s>Miśra</s>, after the cognition of the form 'this is a pot,' there arises an extra-ordinary perception (<s>alaukikamānasa</s>) having the cognition as its object, of the form 'I cognize the pot as pot-hood,' and through that, validity is grasped. In the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> view, however, since cognition is beyond the senses, only the inference based on the mark of being-cognized is the primary grasping of cognition, and through that, validity is grasped. The inferential application is: the pot is the object of a cognition qualified by pot-hood having pot-hood-possessing-entity as qualificandum, because it possesses being-cognized-ness qualified by pot-hood-qualifier; whatever is not so is not so. And being-cognized (<s>jñātatā</s>) is an additional category produced by cognition, having a content — this is the distinction of views.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
etāvatā prabandhena
catvāri pramāṇāni nirūpitāni/ evaṃ ca pramāṇe jñāte 1tadghaṭakasya
pramātvasyopasthitiḥ bhavatīti
smṛtasyopekṣānarhatvarūpaprasaṅgasaṅgatyā pramātvaviṣayakaṃ vicāraṃ
pravartayatītyāha pramāṇaprasaṅgāditi/
pramāṇanirūpitaprasaṅgasaṅgatyetyarthaḥ/ vyavasthāpayiṣyanniti/
paramatanirākaraṇapūrvakaṃ sādhayiṣyan ityarthaḥ/ ṣaṣṭyartha
ādheyatvamityādi/ tathā ca ayaṃ ghaṭa ityādijñānaniṣṭhaṃ
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭatvaprakārakatvādirūpapramātvaṃ
svatogrāhyaṃ parato veti vicāryata ityarthaḥ/
icchādiniṣṭhapramātvasya mīmāṃsakairapi paratogrāhyatvasvīkākarāt
tatra vivādo nāstīti tasya vicāro 'nāvaśyaka iti sūcanāya
jñānaniṣṭhamiti pramātve viśeṣaṇamupāttam/
children.translated_text: By this much of the treatise, the four <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) have been examined. And thus, when <s>pramāṇa</s> is known, the presentation of validity (<s>prāmātva</s>), which is a component thereof, occurs — hence, through the connection of the occasion having the form of the unfitness to ignore what has been recalled, he initiates the investigation concerning validity, saying 'due to the occasion of <s>pramāṇa</s>.' The meaning is: through the connection of the occasion determined by <s>pramāṇa</s>. 'Intending to establish' — the meaning is: intending to prove, preceded by refutation of the opposing view. 'The meaning of the genitive is superstratum-hood' and so forth — accordingly, the meaning is: it is investigated whether the validity in the form of pot-hood-qualifier-hood delimited by having-a-pot-hood-possessing-entity-as-qualificandum, which resides in the cognition 'this is a pot' and the like, is grasped intrinsically or extrinsically. Since even the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> accept that the validity residing in desire and the like is grasped extrinsically, there is no dispute about that — to indicate that its investigation is unnecessary, the qualifier 'residing in cognition' has been added to validity.

children.text:
1. taddhaṭakasyeti/
pramātvaviśiṣṭapramājanakasya pramāṇaśabdārthatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Of its component' — the import is: because the referent of the word <s>pramāṇa</s> is that which produces valid cognition qualified by validity.

children.text:
sakalajñānasādhāraṇamekaṃ pramātvaṃ nāsti, jātyatiriktasya
ghaṭatvādiviṣayaghaṭitasya tasya pratijñānaṃ bhinnatvāditi sūcanāya
jñānānāṃ iti bahuvacanam/ jñānagrāhaketi/ jñānaviṣayakajñānajanikā
yā sāmagrī tajjanyaṃ yat jñānaṃ tadviṣaya ityarthaḥ/ asya
samanvayaprakāraḥ paścādbhaviṣyati/ anumānādi ityādipadena
āptavākyarūpaḥ śabdo gṛhyate/ vākyadvayamiti/ pramātvaṃ svatogrāhyaṃ
ityekaṃ vākyam, pramātvaṃ parato grāhyam ityaparaṃ vākyam/ tatra
prathamaṃ mīmāṃsakasya, dvatīyaṃ naiyāyikasya/ etat
parasparaviruddhārthapratipādakavākyadvayaṃ śṛṇvataḥ madhyasthasya prathamaṃ
aprāmāṇyaśaṅkāviṣayabhūtaḥ tattadvākyārthabodho jāyate, tataḥ
children.translated_text: There is no single universal validity common to all cognitions, since that [validity], being constituted by different object-properties such as pot-hood and the like, and being a property beyond the universal, is different for each cognition — to indicate this, the plural 'of cognitions' is used. 'The aggregate that grasps cognition' — the meaning is: the cognition that is the object of the cognition produced by the aggregate that produces cognition about cognition. The mode of syntactic connection will be explained later. 'And the like' in 'inference and the like' — by this, verbal testimony in the form of authoritative statement is included. 'A pair of statements' — one statement is 'validity is grasped intrinsically,' and the other is 'validity is grasped extrinsically.' Of these, the first belongs to the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>, and the second to the <s>Naiyāyika</s>. Upon hearing this pair of statements conveying mutually contradictory meanings, there first arises in the neutral observer an understanding of the respective statement-meanings, which is the object of the doubt of invalidity; then,

children.text:
pramātvaṃ svatogrāhyaṃ vā
paratogrāhyaṃ veti saṃśayo jāyate/ tataḥ madhyasthasya prathamaṃ
aprāmāṇyaśaṅkāviṣayabhūtaḥ tattadvākyārthabodho jāyate, tataḥ pramātvaṃ
svatogrāhyaṃ vā paratogrāhyaṃ
children.translated_text: the doubt arises: 'is validity grasped intrinsically or extrinsically?' Then, in the neutral observer, there first arises the understanding of the respective statement-meanings, which is the object of the doubt of invalidity; then [the doubt:] 'validity is grasped intrinsically or extrinsically'

children.text:
veti saṃśayo jāyate/
tataḥ madhyasthasya ekatarakoṭikaniścayamutpādayituṃ nyāyaprayogarūpo
vicāraḥ kriyate/ tathā ca
children.translated_text: — such doubt arises. Then, in order to produce in the neutral observer a definite ascertainment of one of the two alternatives, investigation in the form of application of reasoning is undertaken. And accordingly,

children.text:
nyāyaprayogarūpavicāraṃ prati madhyasthasaṃśayaḥ kāraṇam/
madhyasthasaṃśayaṃ prati vipratipattiḥ kāraṇamiti vipratipatteḥ
vicāraprayojakatvamiti bhāvaḥ/ atra"vicāro jalpaḥ,
viparītodbhāvakaparavijigīṣayā nyāyaprayogarūpaḥ/
jijñāsāsampādanena tadaṅgasya tadupayogino madhyasthasaṃśayasya
jananīrvipratipattīrityartha"iti gadādharagrantho 'nusandheyaḥ/
dīpikāyāṃ pradarśitaṃ vipratipattivākyaṃ tattanmatānuvādarūpaṃ
dīpikākārasyaivetyāhuḥ/ saṃśayajananyā iti/ saṃśayajanikāyā
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the doubt of the neutral observer is the cause of investigation in the form of application of reasoning; the dispute is the cause of the neutral observer's doubt — thus the dispute is the cause of investigation. This is the purport. Here, 'investigation is debate (<s>jalpa</s>), in the form of application of reasoning, with the desire to defeat the opponent by producing the opposite [conclusion]. The disputes generate the doubt of the neutral observer, which is useful for investigation, as a component and instrument thereof, through the fulfillment of the desire to know' — thus the text of <s>Gadādhara</s> should be consulted. The dispute-statements shown in the <s>Dīpikā</s> are said to be in the form of restatement of various doctrines by the author of the <s>Dīpikā</s> himself. 'That generates doubt' — the meaning is: which is capable of generating doubt.

children.text:
nanu jñānaprāmāṇyamiti
pakṣanirdeśa ityuktam/ tatra prāmāṇyamityeva pakṣanirdeśo 'stu,
jñānapadaṃ kimarthamityāśaṅkāyāmāha-atra tadvatīti/
karaṇārthakalyuḍantāt pramāṇaśabdāt bhāveṣvajñā niṣpannasya
prāmāṇyaśabdasya pramākaraṇatvamarthaḥ/ bhāvārthakalyuḍantāt
pramāṇaśabdāt bhāveṣyañā niṣpannasya prāmāṇyaśabdasya pramātvamarthaḥ/
prakṛte ca pramātvarūpaḥ prāmāṇyapadārtha eva pakṣaḥ, na tu pramākaraṇatvarūpa
iti sūcanāya jñānapadam/ na ca pramākaraṇatvameva pakṣo 'stviti
vācyam/ tatra svatogrāhyatvarūpasādhyābhāvena bādhāt/ na ca
jñānapadopādānena kathaṃ pramākaraṇatvavyāvṛttiḥ/ pramākaraṇatvasya
vyāptijñānasādṛśyajñānāditānaniṣṭhatvāt iti vācyam/ jñānasyaiva
prāmāṇyaṃ jñānaprāmāṇyamityavadhāraṇasyābhipretatvāt
jñānamātravṛttiprāmāṇyaṃ pakṣatayābhimatam/ pramākaraṇatvarūpaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ
tu na jñānamātravṛtti, tasya 1manaḥ prabhṛtivṛttitvāt/ pramātvarūpaṃ
prāmāṇyaṃ tu jñānamātravṛttīti jñānapadena pramitikaraṇatvavyavaccheda
ityāśayāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: It was said that '<s>jñānaprāmāṇya</s>' is the statement of the thesis. There, let '<s>prāmāṇya</s>' alone be the thesis-statement; what purpose does the word '<s>jñāna</s>' serve? In response to this doubt, he says: 'Here, having that' (<s>tadvati</s>) and so forth.
