From the word <s>pramāṇa</s> ending in the instrumental <s>lyuṭ</s> affix, the word <s>prāmāṇya</s> derived by the <s>aṇ</s> affix denoting abstract states means 'being an instrument of valid cognition' (<s>pramākaraṇatva</s>). From the word <s>pramāṇa</s> ending in the abstract-sense <s>lyuṭ</s> affix, the word <s>prāmāṇya</s> derived by the <s>aṇ</s> affix denoting abstract states means 'validity-hood' (<s>pramātva</s>). In the present context, the referent of the word <s>prāmāṇya</s> that is the thesis is validity-hood, not being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition — the word '<s>jñāna</s>' indicates this. Nor should it be said that being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition should be the thesis, because there would be a counter-example (<s>bādha</s>) — the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) in the form of intrinsic graspability would apply there. Nor should it be asked: how does the addition of the word '<s>jñāna</s>' exclude being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition, since being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition belongs also to <s>vyāpti</s>-cognition, similarity-cognition, and the like? Because the restrictive sense 'the validity of cognition alone is <s>jñāna</s>-<s>prāmāṇya</s>' is intended, the validity that occurs only in cognition is intended as the thesis. But validity in the form of being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition does not occur only in cognition, since it also occurs in mind (<s>manas</s>) and other [faculties]. Validity in the form of <s>pramātva</s>, however, occurs only in cognition — hence the word '<s>jñāna</s>' excludes being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition. This is the intention.

children.text:
nanu jñānamātravṛttīti
viśeṣaṇe datte 'pi vyāptijñānādiniṣṭhaṃ yat
anumityādipramākaraṇatvaṃ tat jñānamātravṛttīti tadvyavacchedaḥ
kathamiti cet - atrāhuḥ/ viśeṣyatāvacchedakāvacchedena
viśeṣaṇānvayasyautsargikatvāt prakṛte
pramākaraṇatvatvarūpaviśeṣyatāvacchedakāvacchedena
jñānamātravṛttitvānvayo vācyaḥ/ pramākaraṇatvatvākrānte
pratyakṣapramākaraṇatve jñānamātravṛttitvabādhāt/ ataḥ pramātvamevātra
prāmāṇyapadārthaḥ/ tadvati tatprakārakajñānatvatvarūpapramātvatvāvacchinne tu
jñānamātravṛttitvānvayaḥ/ sabhbhavatīti tadvalāt atra pramātvarūpaṃ
prāmāṇyameva gṛhyata iti/
children.translated_text: Objection: Even when the qualifier 'occurring only in cognition' is given, the being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition that belongs to inference and the like, which resides in <s>vyāpti</s>-cognition and the like, also occurs only in cognition — so how is that excluded? To this they say: Since the default rule is that the qualifier connects with the qualificandum through the delimitor of qualificandum-hood, in the present case the occurrence-only-in-cognition must be stated as delimited by the delimitor of qualificandum-hood, which is of the form of being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition-hood. Since occurrence-only-in-cognition is contradicted in perceptual being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition, which is subsumed under being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition-hood, therefore <s>pramātva</s> alone is the referent of the word <s>prāmāṇya</s> here. But the connection of occurrence-only-in-cognition with [the property] delimited by <s>pramātvatva</s> (validity-hood-hood), which is of the form of cognition-hood qualificative of what possesses that — that is possible. By that force, it is validity in the form of <s>pramātva</s> that is grasped here.

children.text:
nanu
prāmāṇyapadārthatvena prāmāṇyapadārthasya pakṣatve bhavedevaṃ
jñānapadasārthaṅkyam/ viśiṣya tadvati tatprakārakajñānatvasya pakṣatve
jñānapadaṃ vyarthamityatastātparyagrāhakatayā tatsārthakyamāha - vastuta
iti/ kasyāpi prāmāṇyasyeti / ghaṭatvavati
ghaṭatvaprakārakajñānatvarūpaprāmāṇyasya
tadāśrayabhūtajñānagrāhakasāmagrīgrahyatve 'pi
tadanāśrayayāvadantargatapaṭādijñānagrāhakasāmagrīgrāhyatvaṃ nāstīti bādhaḥ
syāt/ ato ghaṭatvaghaṭitaṃ
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭatvaprakārakajñānatvarūpaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ yadā
pakṣaḥ tadā ghaṭatvaprakārakajñānagrāhakasāmagrīgāhyatvameva sādhyam/ na tu
jñānatvena sāmānyena jñānaghaṭitaṃ jñānagrāhakasāmagrīgrāhyatvamiti
sūcanāya jñānapadamiti bhāvaḥ/ na tu sāmānyata iti/
idamupalakṣaṇam, dharmāntaraprakārakajñānagrāhakayāvatsāmāgrīgrāhyatvaṃ na
sādhyamiti lābhāyetyapi bodhyam/
children.translated_text: Objection: If the referent of the word <s>prāmāṇya</s> in its capacity as referent of <s>prāmāṇya</s> were the thesis, then the word '<s>jñāna</s>' would indeed have purpose. But if the thesis is specifically 'cognition-hood that is qualificative of what possesses that,' then the word '<s>jñāna</s>' is purposeless. Therefore, he states its purposefulness as indicating the purport — 'In reality' (<s>vastutas</s>) and so forth. 'Of any validity' — even though the validity of the form of cognition-hood qualificative of pot-hood in what possesses pot-hood is graspable by the aggregate that grasps the cognition that is its substratum, the graspability by the aggregate that grasps cognitions of cloth and the like that are included within [the range] but are not its substratum does not hold — there would be a counter-example. Therefore, when the validity constituted by pot-hood, of the form of cognition-hood qualificative of pot-hood in what possesses pot-hood, is the thesis, only the graspability by the aggregate that grasps the cognition having pot-hood as qualifier is the <s>sādhya</s> — not the graspability by the aggregate that grasps cognition in general by cognition-hood. The word '<s>jñāna</s>' indicates this — this is the import. 'Not in general' — this is a condensed expression (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>); it should also be understood as implying that the graspability by the aggregate that grasps cognition having other properties as qualifiers is not the <s>sādhya</s>.

children.text:
1. manaḥ prabhṛtīti/
manasaḥ mānasapratyakṣarūpapramākaraṇatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 'Mind and the like' — the import is: because the mind has being-an-instrument-of-valid-cognition in the form of being the instrument of mental perception (<s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s>).

children.text:
tadaprāmāṇyetyādi/
jñānaṃ yayā sāmagryā jñāyate tayaiva sāmagryā jñānagataṃ pramātvamapi
jñāyate/ jñānaviṣayakajñāne eva jñānagataṃ pramātvamapi viṣaya ityarthaḥ/
tatra prābhākaramate jñānaṃ tripuṭīrūpamaṅgīkriyate/ tripuṭītyasya
jñātṛ-jñeya-jñānaitattritayaviṣayakamityarthaḥ/ tanmate ādau 'ayaṃ ghaṭa'
iti vyavasāyātmakaṃ jñānaṃ tataḥ 'ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmi'
ityanuvyavasāyātmakaṃ jñānamiti nāṅgīkriyate/ api tu prathamata eva
ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmītyākārakameva
children.translated_text: 'Of its invalidity' and so forth — the validity residing in cognition is also cognized by the very same aggregate by which the cognition is cognized. The meaning is: in the cognition that has cognition as its object, the validity residing in cognition too is an object. Now, in the <s>Prābhākara</s> view, cognition is accepted as having a threefold form (<s>tripuṭī</s>). The meaning of '<s>tripuṭī</s>' is: having as its content the triad of knower, known, and knowing. In that view, it is not accepted that first there is a determinate cognition (<s>vyavasāya</s>) of the form 'this is a pot,' and then a reflective cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) of the form 'I cognize the pot.' Rather, from the very beginning, only the cognition of the form 'I cognize the pot'

children.text:
jñānaṃ jāyate, tadave
vyavasāyātmakam/ tasmin jñāne viṣayaḥ ghaṭaḥ, jñātā ahamarthaḥ,
jñādhātvarthajñānaṃ ceti trayaṃ viṣayaḥ/ ata eva jñānasya svaviṣayakatvarūpaṃ
svayaṃprakāśatvam/ tathā ca jñānaviṣayakaṃ svātmakaṃ jñānaṃ
svagatapramātvamapi viṣayīkaroti, yathā jñānagataṃ jñānatvamapi
viṣayīkaroti tadvat/ jñānatvaviśiṣṭajñānaviṣayakatvavat
pramātvaviśiṣṭajñānaviṣayakatvamapi vyavasāyasya svīkriyate/ na ca
viśiṣṭabuddhau viśeṣaṇajñānasya kāraṇatvāt
children.translated_text: cognition arises, and that itself is the determinate cognition (<s>vyavasāya</s>). In that cognition, the object is the pot, the knower is the self, and the cognition which is the meaning of the root 'jñā' — these three constitute the content. Hence, the self-luminosity (<s>svayaṃprakāśatva</s>) of cognition consists in its having itself as its own content. And thus, a cognition that has cognition as its object and is of its own nature also makes its own validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) its content, just as it also makes cognition-hood (<s>jñānatva</s>) residing in the cognition its content. Just as the determinate cognition is accepted as having cognition-qualified-by-cognition-hood as its content, so too it is accepted as having cognition-qualified-by-validity as its content. Nor should one object that since cognition of the qualifier is a cause of qualified cognition,

children.text:
pūrvamanupasthitasya
pramātvasya kathaṃ bhānamiti vācyam/ tādṛśakāraṇatāyā
anaṅgīkārāt/ tathā ca
children.translated_text: how can validity, which was not previously apprehended, appear [in the determinate cognition]? — because such a causal requirement is not accepted. And thus,

children.text:
jñānaviṣayakajñānaviṣayatvasyaiva svatastvarūpatayā gurumate
jñānaviṣayakaṃ jñānaṃ svayameva tadviṣayatvaṃ pramātvasyāstīti
svatastvopapattiḥ/
children.translated_text: since in the teacher's (<s>Guru</s>'s) view, the very fact of being the content of a cognition that has cognition as its content is the nature of <s>svatastva</s> (intrinsic validity), in the teacher's view, a cognition that has cognition as its content itself possesses the property of having that [validity] as its content — thus the establishment of <s>svatastva</s> is accomplished.

children.text:
murārimiśrāṇāṃ mate
ādau ayaṃ ghaṭa iti vyavasāyātmakaṃ jñānam, tataḥ ghaṭatvena ghaṭamahaṃ
jānāmītyakārakaḥ anuvyavasāyaḥ/ tasya
ghaṭatvaprakārakaghaṭaviśeṣyakajñānavānityarthaḥ/ tathā ca tanmate
jñānaviṣayakajñānamanuvyavasāyaḥ/ tena jñāne viṣayīkriyamāṇe
tadviśeṣaṇatayā ghaṭatvaprakārakatvāvacchinnaghaṭaviśeṣyakatvarūpaṃ
pramātvamapi viṣayīkriyate/ ataḥ
jñānaviṣayakajñānaviṣayatvarūpasvatastvopapattiḥ/
children.translated_text: In the view of <s>Murāri Miśra</s>, first there arises the determinate cognition of the form 'this is a pot,' and then the post-determinate cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) of the form 'I know the pot as possessing pot-hood.' Its meaning is: one who possesses cognition having pot-hood as qualifier-mode and pot as qualificand. And thus, in his view, the post-determinate cognition is a cognition having cognition as its content. When cognition is made the content through that [post-determinate cognition], the validity in the form of having pot as qualificand delimited by pot-hood and having pot-hood as qualifier-mode is also made the content, as a qualifier of the cognition. Hence, the establishment of <s>svatastva</s> in the form of being the content of a cognition that has cognition as its content is accomplished.

children.text:
bhāṭṭānāṃ mate
jñānasyātīndriyatayā aindriyakaṃ ghaṭādijñānaṃ jñānaviṣayakaṃ na bhavatīti
prathamataḥ ayaṃ ghaṭa ityeva jñānamudeti/ tena jñānena ghaṭe
jñātatāravyaḥ kaścit saviṣayako dharmo jāyate/ tayā jñātatayā
jñānamanumīyate/ tathā ca jñātatāliṅgakānumitireva tanmate
jñānaviṣayakajñānam/ tayā anumityā jñānagataṃ pramātvamapi
viṣayīkriyata iti jñānaviṣayatvarūpasvatastvopapattiḥ/
children.translated_text: In the view of the <s>Bhāṭṭas</s>, since cognition is beyond the reach of the senses, the sensory cognition of pot and the like does not have cognition as its content, and thus first there arises only the cognition 'this is a pot.' Through that cognition, a certain property called <s>jñātatā</s> (known-ness), which has content and is a real property, arises in the pot. Through that <s>jñātatā</s>, the cognition is inferred. And thus, in their view, the cognition having cognition as its content is precisely the inference based on the inferential mark of <s>jñātatā</s>. Through that inference, the validity residing in the cognition is also made the content — thus the establishment of <s>svatastva</s> in the form of being the content of [a cognition that has] cognition as its content is accomplished.

children.text:
1prāthamikajñānagrahaviṣayatvaṃ svatogrāhyatvamiti matatrayasādhāraṇaṃ
nirvācyam/ jñānagrahe prāthamikatvaviśeṣaṇāt
naiyāyikasaṃmatapravṛttyādiliṅgakānumityātmakadvitīyajñānagraho
vyavacchidyate/
children.translated_text: The common definition applicable to all three views should be stated thus: <s>svatastva</s> (intrinsic apprehensibility) is the property of being the content of the primary apprehension of cognition. By the qualification 'primary' in the apprehension of cognition, the secondary apprehension of cognition in the form of inference based on successful activity and the like, accepted by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, is excluded.

children.text:
vyavasāyasya
svaprakāśātmakatayeti/ svaviṣayakatayetyarthaḥ/ grahaṇāditi/
viṣayīkaraṇādityarthaḥ/ jñānaviṣayakalaukikamānasamiti/
jñānaviṣayakamātmamanassaṃyogarūpalaukikasannikarṣajanyaṃ
mānasapratyakṣamityarthaḥ/ idameva mānasam anuvyavasāya ityucyate/
tena prāmāṇyasya grahaṇamiti/ tena mānasapratyakṣeṇa pramātvasya
viṣayīkaraṇamityarthaḥ/ jñānaviṣayakamānasapratyakṣanirūpitā
pramātvaniṣṭhaviṣayateti yāvat/ tayā pramāṇyaṃ gṛhyate - anumityā
prāmāṇyaṃ viṣayīkriyate/ ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyaketi/ tathā cāsyāmanumitau
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakaghaṭatvaprakārakajñānaṃ viṣaṃyaḥ, jñānaviśeṣaṇatayā
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakaghaṭatvaprakārakatvarūpapramātvamapi viṣayaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Because of the self-luminous nature of the determinate cognition' — the meaning is: because of having itself as its own content. 'Because of apprehension' — the meaning is: because of being made the content. 'The ordinary means of knowledge having cognition as its content' — the meaning is: the mental perception (<s>mānasa pratyakṣa</s>) produced by the ordinary contact in the form of the conjunction of the self and the mind, which has cognition as its content. This very mental [perception] is called <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (post-determinate cognition). 'Through that, the apprehension of validity' — the meaning is: through that mental perception, validity is made the content. The purport is: the contentness of validity as determined by the mental perception having cognition as its content. 'Through that, validity is apprehended' — through the inference, validity is made the content. 'Having a qualificand possessing pot-hood' — and thus, in this inference, cognition having pot as qualificand possessing pot-hood and pot-hood as qualifier-mode is the content, and as a qualifier of the cognition, the validity in the form of having pot as qualificand possessing pot-hood and pot-hood as qualifier-mode is also the content.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: svatastvaghaṭakadalaprayojanam
children.translated_text: The purpose of the component terms of <s>svatastva</s> (intrinsic validity)

children.text:
anumānādigrāhyatvena siddhasādhanavāraṇāya yāvaditi/ 'idaṃ
jñānaṃ apramā' iti jñānena prāmāṇyāgrahāt bādhavāraṇāya
aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketi/ 'idaṃ jñānaṃ apramā'
ityanuvyavasāyaniṣṭhaprāmāṇyagrāhakasyāpi
aprāmāṇyāgrāhakatvābhāvāt svatastvaṃ na syāt ataḥ taditi/ tasmin
grāhyaprāmāṇyāśraye aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketyarthaḥ/ udāhṛtasthale
vyavasāye 'prāmāṇyagrāhakasyāpyanuvyavasāye tadagrāhakatvāt
svatastvasiddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'As much as' — to prevent the defect of proving what is already established, since [validity] is also apprehensible through inference and the like. 'Not apprehending invalidity' — to prevent the defect of sublation, since the cognition 'this cognition is not valid' does not apprehend validity. [One might ask:] since even the aggregate that apprehends validity in the <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (post-determinate cognition) 'this cognition is not valid' also lacks the property of apprehending invalidity, <s>svatastva</s> would not hold — hence 'in that.' The meaning is: not apprehending invalidity in that which is the locus of the validity to be apprehended. In the illustrated case, since even in the <s>anuvyavasāya</s> of the apprehender of validity in the determinate cognition, that [validity] is not apprehended, the establishment of <s>svatastva</s> is achieved.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
yāvattvaviśeṣaṇe
satyeva agrāhakāntaṃ sārthakamityabhipretya prathamatastasyaiva prayojanaṃ
darśayati - anumāneti/ prāmāṇyasyetyādiḥ/ siddhasādhaneti/
naiyāyikamate 'pi 'idam jñānam pramā samarthapravṛttijanakatvāt'
children.translated_text: Intending that the portion ending with 'not apprehending' is meaningful only when the qualification 'as much as' is present, he first shows the purpose of that very [qualification] — with 'through inference' and so forth. [Supply:] 'of validity.' 'Proving what is already established' — [this is because] even in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, [validity is apprehensible] through the inference 'this cognition is valid, because it generates successful activity'

children.text:
1. prāthamiketi/
prāthamikaṃ yat jñānaviṣayakajñānaṃ tadviṣayatvamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Primary' — the meaning is: the property of being the content of that primary cognition which has cognition as its content.

children.text:
ityanumānena
'idam jñānam pramā' ityāptavākyena ca grāhyatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
naiyāyikamate 'pi niṣedhe sādhye bādhavāraṇāyetyapi bodhyam/
yāvaditīti/ nanu sāmagryāṃ yāvattvaviśeṣaṇamayuktam,
yāvatsāmagrījanyagrahāprasiddheḥ/ na hi sarvābhiḥ jñānasāmagrībhiḥ ekaṃ
jñānaṃ janyate/ na ca yāvatīḥ sāmagīḥ viśiṣyopādāya
tattajjanyagrahaviṣayatvaṃ sādhyata iti vācyam/
anuvyavavāyādisāmagrīṇāṃ tādrūpyeṇa niveśe
matatrayasādhāraṇyānirvāhāditi cet - na/ yato yāvaditi phalato
grahaviśeṣaṇm/ tathā ca jñānagrāhakasāmagrījanyayāvadgrahaviṣayatvamiti
phalitam/
tattaddharmaprakārakajñānagrāhakasāmagrījanyagrahatvavyāpakaviṣayitāpratiyogitvamiti
niṣkarṣa iti saṅkṣepaḥ/ prāmāṇyāgrahāditi/ vyavasāyaniṣṭhetyādiḥ/
prāmāṇyāviṣayīkaraṇādityarthaḥ/ aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketīti/ tathā ca
tādṛśajñānasāmagryāḥ sādhyakoṭyapraviṣṭatvāt tayā
prāmāṇyasyāgrahaṇe 'pi na bādha iti bhāvaḥ/ anuvyavasāyaniṣṭhetyādi/
tādṛśānuvyavasāyaniṣṭhaṃ
yadaprāmāṇyavadviśeṣyakatvaviśiṣṭāprāmāṇyaprakārakatvarūpaprāmāṇyaṃ
tadgrāhakasyetyarthaḥ/ 'sāmānye napuṃsakam' iti napuṃsakanirdeśaḥ/
svatastvaṃ na syāditi/ yadā niruktaprāmāṇyasya
children.translated_text: and through the authoritative statement 'this cognition is valid' — because of being apprehensible [through these means as well]. This is the purport. It should also be understood that in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view too, 'to prevent sublation when negation is the probandum.' 'As much as' — now, the qualification 'as much as' in the aggregate is inappropriate, since the apprehension generated by [all possible] aggregates is not well-known, for not all aggregates of cognition generate a single cognition. Nor should one say that the probandum is the content-hood of the apprehension generated by each respective aggregate, specifying as many aggregates as there are — if thus objected, because the aggregates of post-determinate cognition and the like, when included under that description, would not support commonality across the three views — no, because 'as much as' is a qualification of the apprehension from the standpoint of the result. And thus, the upshot is: the property of being the content of as-much apprehension as is generated by the aggregate that apprehends cognition. The conclusion is: the counter-positive-hood of the contentness that pervades the apprehension-hood of the apprehension generated by the aggregate that apprehends cognition having a given property as qualifier-mode. 'Because of non-apprehension of validity' — [supply:] 'residing in the determinate cognition' and so forth. The meaning is: because of not making validity the content. 'Not apprehending invalidity' — and thus, since such an aggregate of cognition does not enter the range of the probandum, even though validity is not apprehended by it, there is no sublation. This is the purport. 'Residing in the <s>anuvyavasāya</s>' and so forth — the meaning is: of the apprehender of that validity which resides in the <s>anuvyavasāya</s> of the form 'this cognition is not valid,' and which consists in having a qualificand possessing invalidity, qualified by invalidity as qualifier-mode. '[The usage] in the neuter' is by the rule '<s>sāmānye napuṃsakam</s>' (the neuter is used for general terms). '<s>Svatastva</s> would not hold' — when the stated validity is

children.text:
pakṣatā, tadā
aprāmāṇyāgrāhakaprāmāṇyagrāhakasāmāgryā eva sādhyakoṭau
niveśanīyatayā tādṛśasāmagryā aprasiddhatvāt tasya svatogrāhyatvaṃ na
sidhyedityarthaḥ/ saptamītatpuruṣamabhipretyāha - tasminniti/ etasyaiva
vivaraṇaṃ grāhyaprāmāṇyāśraya iti/ yādṛśaprāmāṇyaṃ
prakṛtānumitavuddheśyaṃ
tādṛśaprāmāṇyāśrayaviśeṣyakāprāmāṇyaprakārakajñānājanaketi
agrāhakāntārthaḥ/ idaṃ jñānaṃ apramā
ityanuvyavasāyaniṣṭhaprāmāṇyagrāhakasāmagryāḥ
vyavasāyaviśeṣyakāprāmāṇyagrahajanakatve 'pi
anuvyavasāyaviśeṣyakāprāmāṇyagrahājanakatvāt jñānagrāhakatvācca
aprāmāṇyavadviśeṣyakatvādighaṭitaprāmāṇyasya svatogrāhyatvasiddhirityāha
- udāhṛtasthala iti/ idaṃ jñānaṃ aprametyatretyarthaḥ/ adhikaṃ
asmadīyamaṇidīdhitivyākhyāyāmanusandheyam/
children.translated_text: the subject, since only the aggregate that apprehends validity and does not apprehend invalidity should enter the range of the probandum, and since such an aggregate is not well-known, its intrinsic apprehensibility would not be established — this is the meaning. Intending a locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound, he says 'in that.' The elaboration of this is: 'the locus of the validity to be apprehended.' The meaning of 'not apprehending' ending with that is: not generating a cognition having invalidity as qualifier-mode with a qualificand that is the locus of the type of validity that is the subject of the present inference. Even though the aggregate that apprehends validity in the <s>anuvyavasāya</s> 'this cognition is not valid' does generate the apprehension of invalidity having the determinate cognition as qualificand, since it does not generate the apprehension of invalidity having the <s>anuvyavasāya</s> as qualificand, and since it is an apprehender of cognition, the establishment of the intrinsic apprehensibility of the validity constituted by having-a-qualificand-possessing-invalidity and so forth is achieved — he says this with 'in the illustrated case.' The meaning of 'in the illustrated case' is: in the case of 'this cognition is not valid.' Further details should be consulted in our commentary on the <s>Maṇidīdhiti</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
tadaprāmāṇyāgrāhakayāvajjñānagrahakasāmagrīgrāhyatvaṃ svatastvam
iti dīpikāyāmuktam/ tasmin aprāmāṇyāgrāhikā yāvatī
jñānagrāhikā sāmagrī tajjanyagrahaviṣayatvamiti tadarthaḥ/
aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketyasya aprāmāṇyaprakārakajñānājanaketyarthaḥ/
tadekadeśajñāne tasminniti saptamyantārthasya tadviśeṣyakatvasyānvayaḥ/
tacchabdena
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> it was stated that <s>svatastva</s> is: the property of being apprehensible by the aggregate that apprehends cognition and does not apprehend invalidity. Its meaning is: the property of being the content of the apprehension generated by the aggregate that apprehends cognition and does not apprehend invalidity — as much of such aggregate as there is. The meaning of 'not apprehending invalidity' is: not generating a cognition having invalidity as qualifier-mode. The meaning of the locative seventh-case ending in 'in that' — having that as qualificand — connects [syntactically]. By the word 'that'

children.text:
yādṛśaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ
anumityā grāhyaṃ tādṛśaprāmāṇyāśraya ucyate/ tathā ca
grāhyaprāmāṇyāśrayaviśeṣyakāprāmāṇyaprākarakajñānājanakajñānaviṣayakajñānajanakayāvatsāmagrījanyajñānaviṣayatvaṃ
svatastvamiti paryavasannam/ ayaṃ ghaṭaḥ ityākārakajñāne idaṃ jñānaṃ
pramā samarthapravṛttijanakatvāt ityanumityā grāhyaṃ yat ghaṭatvavati
ghaṭatvaprakārakatvarūpaṃ pramātvaṃ asti tadāśrayaḥ ayaṃ ghaṭa iti jñānam,
tadviśeṣyakaṃ yat apramātvaprakārakaṃ jñānaṃ idaṃ jñānamaprametyākārakaṃ
tadajanikā bhavati ghaṭajñānaviṣayakajñānajanikā sāmagrī, na hi tayā
ghaṭajñānaviśeṣyakāpramātvajñānaṃ jāyata iti/ tādṛśasāmagrījanyaṃ
jñānaṃ ca jñānaviṣayakaṃ jñānaṃ pūrvoktarītyā
vyavasāya-anuvyavasāya-anumityātmakaṃ matabhedena, tadviṣayatvaṃ
pramātve 'stīti samanvayaḥ/ atra dalaprayojanakathanāvasare prathamaṃ
yāvatpadasya prayojanamuktvā tadanantaraṃ tadaprāmāṇyagrāhaketyasya
prayojanamuktaṃ dīpikāyām/ tatra prathamopasthitasya agrāhakāntasya
prathamaṃ prayojanamuktvā tadanantaramevānantaropasthitasya yāvatpadasya
prayojanakathanaṃ nyāyyam/ tatparityajya kimarthaṃ viparyayeṇa
prayojanamuktamityāśaṅkāyāmāha - yāvatvaviśeṣaṇe satyeveti/
idaṃ tu dvayorapi viśeṣaṇayoḥ prayojane jñāte satyeva
spaṣṭīkartuṃ śakyat iti ādau tayoḥ prayojanaṃ pratipādyate/
aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketi viśeṣaṇānupādāne
yāvajjñānagrāhakasāmagrīgrāhyatvaṃ svatastvamiti bhavet/ tathā ca 'idaṃ
jñānaṃ apramā' ityākārakajñānamapi jñānaviṣayakayāvajjñānāntargataṃ
tadgrāhyatvabhapramātva evāsti, na tu pramātva iti bādhaḥ syāt/
tadvāraṇāya sāmāgryāṃ aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketi viśeṣaṇamupāttam/ idaṃ
jñānaṃ apramā ityākārako yo jñānagrahaḥ tajjanakasāmagrī
aprāmāṇyagrāhikaiva bhavet tādṛśagrahasyāprāmāṇyaviṣayakatayā
tādṛśagrahajanakasāmagryāḥ aprāmāṇyagrāhakatvāvaśyambhāvāt/ tathā ca
tādṛśasāmagryāḥ aprāmāṇyāgrāhakatvābhāvāt aprāmāṇyāgrāhikā
jñānagrāhakasāmagrī anuvyavasāyādisāmagryeva
tajjanyānuvyavasāyādirūpajñānagrahaviṣayatvaṃ pramātve astīti na bādhaḥ/
yāvatpadānupādāne apramātvāgrāhikā yā jñānagrāhakasāmagrī
ityanena idaṃ jñānaṃ pramā samarthapravṛttijanakatvāt
ityanumānarūpāṃ idaṃ jñānaṃ pramā ityāptavākyarūpāṃ vā
sāmagrīmupādāya tajjanyānumiti-śābdabodharūpayoḥ 'idaṃ jñānaṃ
pramā' ityākārakayoḥ jñānagrahayorviṣayatvaṃ pramātve
naiyāyikasyāpyabhimatamiti tatsādhane siddhasādhanaṃ syāditi
tadvāraṇāya yāvatpadam/ tathā sati vyavasāyānuvyavasāyādīnāmapi
yāvajjñānagrahāntargatatayā tadviṣayatvasya pramātve 'naṅgīkārāt na
siddhasādhanamiti dvayoḥ dalayoḥ prayojanasthitiḥ/ tatra yāvattvadale
satyeva aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketi sārthakam/ anyathā
jñānagrahakasāmagrījanyagrahaviṣayatvaṃ svatastvamityuktau na bādhaprasaktiḥ,
jñānagrahapadena vyavasāyasyānuvyavasāyasya jñātatāliṅgakānumitervā
grahaṇena tadviṣayatvasya pramātve sambhavāt/ tathā ca bādhāprasaktyā
tadvāraṇaphalakamagrāhakāntaṃ vyarthaṃ syāt/ yāvatpade sati tu 'idaṃ
jñānaṃ aprāmā' ityākārakagrahasyāpi yāvajjñānagrahāntargatatayā
tadviṣayatvaṃ pramātve nāstīti bādhaḥ prasajyate, tadvārakatayā
cāgrāhakāntaṃ sārthakamityāśayena yāvatvaviśeṣaṇe satyeva
agrāhakāntaṃ sārthakamityuktaṃ pramāśikayāmiti/
children.translated_text: The locus of that kind of <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity) which is apprehended by inference is stated. And thus, the conclusion is that <s>svatastva</s> (intrinsic validity) consists in being the content of a cognition produced by whatever aggregate of causal conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>) generates cognitions having as their object the cognition whose qualificand possesses the apprehended validity, and which does not generate a cognition having the mode of invalidity (<s>aprāmāṇya</s>) as qualifier. In the cognition of the form 'this is a pot,' the <s>pramātva</s> (valid-cognition-hood), which consists in pot-hood-qualifierness in what possesses pot-hood, is apprehended through the inference 'this cognition is valid (<s>pramā</s>), because it generates competent activity.' The locus of that is the cognition 'this is a pot.' The aggregate that generates cognitions having that cognition as their object does not produce a cognition having invalidity as qualifier with that [cognition] as qualificand — that is, it does not generate a cognition of the form 'this cognition is invalid.' And the cognition produced by such an aggregate, being a cognition having a cognition as its object, takes the form of <s>vyavasāya</s> (determinate cognition), <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (reflective cognition), or inference, according to the difference of doctrinal positions — the fact that it is the content of such [cognitions] exists in <s>pramātva</s>: this is the correlation. Here, in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, at the occasion of stating the purpose of the clauses, the purpose of the term '<s>yāvat</s>' was stated first, and then afterward the purpose of '<s>tadaprāmāṇyagrāhaka</s>' was stated. There, it would be proper to first state the purpose of '<s>agrāhaka</s>-ending' which is presented first, and then afterward state the purpose of the term '<s>yāvat</s>' which is presented next. Abandoning that [order], to the doubt 'why was the purpose stated in reverse order?' — he says: 'only when the qualifier <s>yāvattva</s> is present.' But this is because the purpose of both qualifiers can be made clear only when both purposes are known; therefore, the purposes of both are first explained. If the qualifier '<s>aprāmāṇyāgrāhaka</s>' (not apprehending invalidity) were not included, <s>svatastva</s> would amount to being apprehensible by whatever aggregate apprehends cognition. And in that case, even a cognition of the form 'this cognition is invalid' would be included within the cognitions having cognition as their object, and its apprehensibility would exist only in <s>apramātva</s> (invalidity), not in <s>pramātva</s> — thus there would be a contradiction (<s>bādha</s>). To prevent that, the qualifier '<s>aprāmāṇyāgrāhaka</s>' is added to the aggregate. Whatever apprehension of cognition has the form 'this cognition is invalid,' the aggregate generating it would necessarily be one that apprehends invalidity, because such an apprehension has invalidity as its content, and therefore the aggregate generating such an apprehension necessarily has the character of apprehending invalidity. And thus, since such an aggregate lacks the character of not-apprehending-invalidity, the aggregate that apprehends cognition and does not apprehend invalidity is only the aggregate of <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (reflective cognition) and the like — that being the content of the cognition-apprehension produced by it exists in <s>pramātva</s>: hence no contradiction. Without the term '<s>yāvat</s>,' by the expression 'the aggregate that apprehends cognition and does not apprehend invalidity,' taking the aggregate in the form of the inference 'this cognition is valid, because it generates competent activity' or the reliable testimony (<s>āptavākya</s>) 'this cognition is valid,' the content-hood of the cognition-apprehensions of the form 'this cognition is valid' produced by those [aggregates] in <s>pramātva</s> would be accepted even by the <s>Naiyāyika</s> — thus in establishing it there would be the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). To prevent that, the term '<s>yāvat</s>' is used. In that case, since <s>vyavasāya</s>, <s>anuvyavasāya</s> and the like are also included within the cognition-apprehensions covered by '<s>yāvat</s>,' and since their content-hood in <s>pramātva</s> is not accepted [by the Naiyāyika], there is no fallacy of proving the already established — this is the settled purpose of both clauses. There, only when the '<s>yāvattva</s>' clause is present does '<s>aprāmāṇyāgrāhaka</s>' become meaningful. Otherwise, if it were said that <s>svatastva</s> is the content-hood of apprehension produced by the aggregate that apprehends cognition, there would be no occasion for contradiction, because by the term 'cognition-apprehension,' <s>vyavasāya</s>, <s>anuvyavasāya</s>, or inference based on the mark of being-known are included, and their content-hood in <s>pramātva</s> is possible. And since there is no occasion for contradiction, the '<s>agrāhaka</s>-ending' whose function is to prevent it would be purposeless. But when the term '<s>yāvat</s>' is present, since even an apprehension of the form 'this cognition is invalid' is included within the cognition-apprehensions covered by '<s>yāvat</s>,' its content-hood in <s>pramātva</s> does not exist — thus contradiction arises, and by preventing it the '<s>agrāhaka</s>-ending' becomes meaningful: with this intention, the <s>Prakāśikā</s> states that the '<s>agrāhaka</s>-ending' is meaningful only when the qualifier '<s>yāvattva</s>' is present.

children.text:
niṣedhe sādhye
bādhavāraṇāyeti/
tadaprāmāṇyāgrāhakayāvajjñānagrāhakasāmagrīgrāhyatvābhāvaḥ naiyāyikasya
sādhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: When negation is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), [the qualifier is included] to prevent contradiction. The absence of apprehensibility by the aggregate that apprehends cognition covered by '<s>yāvat</s>' and does not apprehend invalidity — this is the probandum for the <s>Naiyāyika</s>.

children.text:
tatra yāvatyapadābhāve
samarthapravṛttijanakatvaliṅgakānumāna-āptavākyagrāhyatvāt
tadabhāvarūpasādhyābhāvāt bādhaḥ
children.translated_text: In that case, without the term '<s>yāvat</s>,' since [<s>pramātva</s>] is apprehensible through inference having 'generating competent activity' as its probans and through reliable testimony (<s>āptavākya</s>), and since the probandum in the form of the absence of that [apprehensibility] does not exist, there would be contradiction (<s>bādha</s>).

children.text:
tadvāraṇāya
yāvatpadamiti bhāvaḥ/ abhāvasādhyakasthalepakṣe pratiyogimattvameva bādha
ityāśayenedam/ nanu sāmagryāmiti/ yāvatpadasya
sāmagrīpadaviśeṣaṇatve yāvatyaḥ jñānagrahajanakasāmagryaḥ
tajjanyagrahaviṣayatvaṃ sādhyamiti phalati/ tathā sati yāvatsāmagrījanyaḥ
ekaḥ jñānagrahaḥ aprasiddha iti sādhyāprasiddhiḥ prasajyate/ yataḥ
anuvyavasāyajanaka-vyavasāyajanaka-jñātatāliṅgakānumitijanaka-samarthapravṛttiliṅgakānumitijanakasāmagrīṇāṃ
sarvāsāmapi pratyekaṃ jñānagrāhakatayā tādṛśayāvatsāmagrījanyaḥ eko
jñānagraho na bhavatīti/ sāmagrīṇāṃ yāvatvena na niveśaḥ, api tu
viśiṣyaiva/ tathā ca
tattajjñānagrahajanakatattatsāmagrījanyatattadgrahaviṣayatvaṃ svatastvamiti
pariṣkāreṇa
children.translated_text: To prevent that, the term '<s>yāvat</s>' is used — this is the meaning. This is stated with the intention that in a thesis where an absence is the probandum, possessing the counter-positive itself constitutes the contradiction. Now, [regarding] 'in the aggregate': if the term '<s>yāvat</s>' qualifies the term 'aggregate,' then the result would be that the probandum is the content-hood of the apprehension produced by whatever aggregates generate the apprehension of cognition. In that case, the objection of the probandum being unestablished (<s>sādhyāprasiddhi</s>) would arise, because since each of the aggregates — those generating <s>anuvyavasāya</s>, those generating <s>vyavasāya</s>, those generating inference based on the mark of being-known, and those generating inference based on the mark of competent activity — each individually apprehends cognition, there is no single cognition-apprehension produced by all such aggregates collectively. The aggregates do not enter [the definition] collectively, but rather distinctively. And thus, with the refinement that <s>svatastva</s> consists in the content-hood of each respective apprehension produced by each respective aggregate that generates each respective cognition-apprehension,

children.text:
sādhyāprasiddhivāraṇe 'pi matatrayasādhāraṇyaṃ na nirvahatīti
śaṅkāgranthārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: even in preventing the unestablishedness of the probandum, the commonality to the three doctrinal positions (<s>matatrayasādhāraṇya</s>) would not be maintained — this is the meaning of the objection passage.

children.text:
samādhatte - yato
yāvaditi/ nanu jñānagrāhakasāmagrījanya yāvadgrahaviṣayatvasya
sādhyatve 'pi
paṭajñānagrāhakasāmagrījanyayāvadgrahānatargatapaṭajñānajñānena
ghaṭatvaghaṭitaprāmāṇyasyāgrahāt bādho durvāra ityāśaṅkya
jñānagrāhaketyatra jñāne taddharmaprakārakatvaviśeṣaṇāt na doṣa iti
samādhānaṃ vivakṣuḥ yāvatpadasya
svasamabhivyāhṛtapadārthatāvacchedakavyāpakatvabodhakatvavyutpattimapyabhisandhāya
phalitārthamāha - tattaddharmeti/ yaddharmaghaṭitaprāmāṇyaṃ pakṣaḥ
taddharmaprakāretyarthaḥ/ tathā ca
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭatvaprakārakatvaṃ
ghaṭatvaprakārakajñānagrāhakasāmagrījanyagrahatvavyāpakaviṣayitānirūpakamiti
pratijñāvākyam/ ghaṭatvaprakārakajñānam ayaṃ ghaṭa ityākārakajñānaṃ
tadviṣayakajñānajanakasāmagrī anuvyavasāyādisāmagrī tajjanyagrahatvaṃ yatra
yatra anuvyavasāyādau tatra
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakaghaṭatvaprakārakatvarūpapramātvanirūpitaviṣay itāsti,
tādṛśaviṣayitānirūpakatvaṃ ca pramātve 'stīti samanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: He resolves [the objection] — [beginning with] 'since <s>yāvat</s>.' Now, even if the probandum is the content-hood of whatever apprehension produced by the aggregate that apprehends cognition, since the cognition-of-cloth-cognition — which is not included in whatever apprehensions produced by the aggregate that apprehends cloth-cognition — does not apprehend the validity constituted by cloth-hood, there would be an unavoidable contradiction. Anticipating this objection, intending to resolve it by [pointing out that] through the qualifier 'having that-property as mode' in 'apprehending cognition,' there is no defect — and also bearing in mind the etymological derivation that the term '<s>yāvat</s>' conveys pervasion by the delimiting property of the meaning of the term with which it is co-employed — he states the resultant meaning: 'that-that-property.' The meaning is: 'having as mode that property by which the validity of the thesis is constituted.' And thus, the thesis-statement is: pot-hood-qualifierness delimited by possessing-pot-hood-as-qualificand-hood is the determiner of the content-hood that pervades the apprehension-hood of what is produced by the aggregate apprehending cognition having pot-hood as mode. The cognition having pot-hood as mode is the cognition of the form 'this is a pot'; the aggregate generating cognitions having that as their object is the aggregate of <s>anuvyavasāya</s> and the like; the apprehension-hood produced by it exists wherever there is <s>anuvyavasāya</s> and the like — the content-hood determined by the <s>pramātva</s> consisting in pot-hood-qualifierness in what possesses pot-hood exists there, and the determiner-hood of such content-hood exists in <s>pramātva</s>: this is the correlation.

children.text:
nanu naiyāyikamate 'pi
prāmāṇyanirūpitaviṣayitāyāḥ
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭatvanirūpitaprakāritātvena
tādṛśagrahatvavyāpakatvābhāve 'pi ghaṭatvanirūpitaprākāritātvena
anuvyavasāyādisāmagrījanyagrahatvavyāpakatvāt siddhasādhanam/
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭatvanirūpitaprakāritātvena
prāmāṇyaviṣayitāyāḥ vyāpakatvaṃ tu na vivakṣituṃ śakyam/
naiyāyikamate sādhyāprasiddheḥ/ 'ghaṭatvena imaṃ jānāmi'
ityākārakānuvyavasāye ghaṭatvanirūpitaprakāritātvenaiva
tādṛśaprakāritāyāḥ bhānāt na tu
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭatvaprakāritātvenetya śaṅkyāha -
saṅkṣepa iti/
children.translated_text: But even in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, although the content-hood determined by <s>prāmāṇya</s> does not pervade apprehension-hood produced by the aggregate of <s>anuvyavasāya</s> and the like in the form of qualifierness delimited by pot-hood-possessing-qualificand-hood and delimited by pot-hood-determined-mode-hood, it does pervade it in the form of pot-hood-determined-mode-hood — hence there would be the fallacy of proving the already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). The pervasion of the content-hood of <s>prāmāṇya</s> in the form of qualifierness delimited by pot-hood-possessing-qualificand-hood and delimited by pot-hood-determined-mode-hood cannot be intended, because of the unestablishedness of the probandum in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view. Since in the <s>anuvyavasāya</s> of the form 'I cognize this through pot-hood,' only the mode-hood determined by pot-hood appears, and not in the form of pot-hood-determined-mode-hood delimited by pot-hood-possessing-qualificand-hood — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'in brief.'

children.text:
atra ghaṭatvavati
ghaṭatvaprakārakatvaṃ
ghaṭatvaprakārakajñānagrāhakasāmagrījanyagrahaniṣṭhābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakadharmavadviṣayitānirūpakamiti
pratijñā na vivakṣitā, yenoktadoṣaḥ syāt/ apitu
ghaṭatvaprakārakajñānagrāhakasāmagrījanyagrahaniṣṭhābhāvapratiyogitā,
ghaṭatvavadbiśeṣyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭatvaprakārakatvarūpaprāmāṇyaviṣayakatvatvānavacchinnā
iti pratijñā vivakṣitā/ ato na sādhyāprasiddhyādikamiti bhāvaḥ/
adhikaṃ prāmāṇyavādagādādharyāṃ draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: Here, the thesis is not intended to be: pot-hood-qualifierness in what possesses pot-hood is the determiner of content-hood possessing a property that does not delimit the counter-positiveness of the absence residing in the apprehension produced by the aggregate apprehending cognition having pot-hood as mode — for then the stated defect would apply. Rather, the intended thesis is: the counter-positiveness residing in the absence in the apprehension produced by the aggregate apprehending cognition having pot-hood as mode is not delimited by the content-hood-of-<s>prāmāṇya</s>-hood consisting in pot-hood-qualifierness delimited by pot-hood-possessing-qualificand-hood. Hence there is no unestablishedness of the probandum and the like — this is the meaning. For further details, see the <s>Prāmāṇyavādagādādharī</s>.

children.text:
dīpikāyām idaṃ
jñānamaprameti jñāneneti/ tathā ca aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketi
sāmagrīviśeṣaṇānupādāne
jñānagrāhakasāmagrījanayayāvadgrahaviṣayatvaṃ svatastvamiti syāt/ tathā
sati rajate idaṃ rajatamiti vyavasāyānantaraṃ yat idaṃ
jñānamaprameti bhramātmakaṃ jñānaṃ tasya jñānagraharūpatayā
tajjanakasāmagrījanyayāvadgrahāntargatatādṛśajñānaviṣayatvamapramātva
evāsti na tu pramātvarūpapakṣa iti bādhaḥ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya
aprāmāṇyāgrāhaketiviśeṣaṇam/ apramātvagrāhājanaketi tadarthaḥ/
niruktajñānagrahasya apramātvaviṣayakatvena apramātvagraharūpatayā
niruktajñānagrahajanakasāmagryāḥ apramātvagrahajanakatvāt tadajanakatvaṃ
nāstīti jñānagrahapadena 'idaṃ jñānamapramā' ityākārako jñānagraho
na grāhyaḥ, api tu 'rajatatvena imaṃ jānāmi'
ityanuvyavasāyādireva grāhyaḥ tajjanakasāmagryāḥ aprāmāṇyagrāhakatvāt
tajjanyānuvyavasāyādyātmakagrahaviṣayatvaṃ pramātve 'stīti na bādha iti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [it says] 'by the cognition "this cognition is invalid".' And thus, without the qualifier '<s>aprāmāṇyāgrāhaka</s>' on the aggregate, <s>svatastva</s> would be: the content-hood of whatever apprehension produced by the aggregate that generates cognition-apprehension. In that case, after the <s>vyavasāya</s> (determinate cognition) 'this is silver' regarding silver, the erroneous cognition 'this cognition is invalid' — having the nature of a cognition-apprehension — its being the content of whatever apprehension produced by the aggregate that generates it would exist in <s>apramātva</s> (invalidity) alone, and not in the thesis which is <s>pramātva</s> — thus there would be contradiction. To prevent that, the qualifier '<s>aprāmāṇyāgrāhaka</s>' [is added]. Its meaning is: not generating the apprehension of invalidity. Since the cognition-apprehension as described has invalidity as its content and thus has the nature of an invalidity-apprehension, the aggregate generating such a cognition-apprehension necessarily generates the apprehension of invalidity; therefore, the absence of such generation does not exist — hence by the term 'cognition-apprehension,' the cognition-apprehension of the form 'this cognition is invalid' is not to be included. Rather, only the <s>anuvyavasāya</s> and the like of the form 'I cognize this through silver-hood' are to be included, since their generating aggregate does not apprehend invalidity. The content-hood of the apprehension in the form of <s>anuvyavasāya</s> and the like produced by it exists in <s>pramātva</s> — hence no contradiction: this is the meaning.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām
vyavasāyaniṣṭhetyādiriti/ idaṃ rajatam ityākārakavyasāyaniṣṭhaṃ
yat pramātvaṃ rajatatvavati rajatatvaprakārakatvarūpaṃ
tadaviṣayakatvādityarthaṃḥ/ tathā ca pramātve
yāvadantargatatādṛśajñānāviṣayatvāt bādha iti bhāvaḥ/
tādṛśajñānasāmagryā iti/ idaṃ jñānaṃ apramā
ityākārakajñānajanakasāmagryā ityarthaḥ/
sādhyakoṭyapraviṣṭatvāditi/ apramātvagrāhakatvena
aprāmāṇyāgrāhakatvarūpaviśeṣaṇānākrāntatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [the passage beginning with] '<s>vyavasāyaniṣṭha</s>' and so forth. The meaning is: the <s>pramātva</s> residing in the <s>vyavasāya</s> of the form 'this is silver,' which consists in silver-hood-qualifierness in what possesses silver-hood — because that is not the content [of the relevant apprehension]. And thus, since [that <s>pramātva</s>] is not the content of any cognition included within the scope of '<s>yāvat</s>,' there is contradiction — this is the meaning. 'By the aggregate of such cognition' means: by the aggregate generating the cognition of the form 'this cognition is invalid.' 'Because of not entering the probandum' means: because [that aggregate] is not covered by the qualifier having the form of '<s>aprāmāṇyāgrāhakatva</s>' (not-apprehending-invalidity), due to its being an apprehender of invalidity — this is the meaning.

children.text:
tadaprāmāṇyagrāhaketyatra
tatpadasya dīpikoktaṃ prayojanamevam - idaṃ
rajatamitibhramātmakavyavasāyottara-idaṃ
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>tadaprāmāṇyagrāhaka</s>' in that [passage], the purpose of the word '<s>tat</s>' as stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s> is as follows: after the erroneous <s>vyavasāya</s> of the form 'this is silver,' [there arises] this —

children.text:
jñānam apramā
ityāvakārakajñānaniṣṭhasya apramātvavati apramātvaprakārakajñānatvarūpasya
pramātvasya apramātvagrāhakasāmagryaiva grahaṇāt
aprāmāṇyāgrāhakasāmagrīgrāhyatvātmakasvatastvabādhaḥ tādṛśapramātve
syāditi tadvāraṇāya tadaprāmāṇyāgrāhaketi tatpadam/
children.translated_text: the cognition 'this cognition is invalid' — since the <s>pramātva</s> residing in it, which consists in invalidity-qualifierness in what possesses invalidity, i.e., the nature of being a cognition having invalidity as mode, is apprehended only by the aggregate that apprehends invalidity, there would be a contradiction to <s>svatastva</s> consisting in apprehensibility by an aggregate that does not apprehend invalidity, with respect to such <s>pramātva</s>. To prevent that, the word '<s>tat</s>' in '<s>tadaprāmāṇyāgrāhaka</s>' [is used].

children.text:
tasmin
aprāmāṇyagrāhaketi tadarthaḥ/ yādṛśapramātve svatastvamiṣyate
tādṛśapramātvāśrayaviśeṣyakāpramātvaprakārakajñānājanaketi
tadaprāmāṇyāgrāhaketyasyārthaḥ/ idaṃ jñānaṃ apramā
ityākārakajñānaniṣṭhapramātvagrāhakasāmagryāḥ idañjñānapadena
vivakṣitaṃ yat idaṃ rajatam ityākārakajñānaṃ
tadviśeṣyakāpramātvagrāhakatve 'pi prakṛtasyāpramātvavati
apramātvaprakārakatvarūpapramātvasya āśrayabhūtaṃ yat idaṃ jñānaṃ
aprametyākārakajñānaṃ tadviśeṣyakāpramātvaprakārakajñānajanakatvāt
noktadoṣa iti/ idaṃ jñānaṃ aprametyanuvyavasāyaniṣṭheti/
jñānaviṣayakatvādasya jñānasyānuvyavasāyaśabdena vyapadeśaḥ/ ataḥ
jānāmītyādyākārakatāvirahāt kathamasyānuvyavasāyatvamiti
nāśaṅkanīyam/
children.translated_text: 'Not apprehending invalidity in that' — this is the meaning. The meaning of 'not apprehending invalidity' is: that aggregate [of causes], of whatever type of validity is accepted as self-established, does not generate a cognition having invalidity as qualifier-mode and having as qualificand the locus of such validity. Even though the aggregate of causes that apprehends the validity residing in the cognition of the form 'This cognition is invalid' does apprehend the invalidity having as its qualificand the cognition intended by the words 'this cognition,' namely the cognition 'This is silver,' nonetheless, because the cognition 'This cognition is invalid,' which is the locus of the validity in the form of having invalidity as qualifier-mode in what possesses invalidity, generates cognition having invalidity as qualifier-mode and having that [cognition] as qualificand — hence the stated defect does not arise. 'Residing in the introspective cognition of the form "This cognition is invalid"' — because this cognition has knowledge as its content, it is designated by the word 'introspective cognition' (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>). Hence, one should not doubt: how can it be an introspective cognition when it lacks the form 'I know'?

children.text:
nanu
viśeṣyabhūtasāmagrīpadānusāreṇa prāmāṇyagrāhikāyā apīti vaktavye
kathaṃ prāmāṇyagrāhakasyāpītyuktaṃ dīpikāyām ityāśaṅkyāha -
sāmānye naṃpusakamiti/ (grāhakatvarūpa) sāmānyadharmāśrayavivakṣayā
tadāśrayaviśeṣāvivakṣāyāṃ napuṃsakamityanuśāsanāt atra
napuṃsakatvamiti bhāvaḥ/ niruktaprāmāṇyasyeti/
aprāmāṇyavadviśeṣyakatvaviśiṣṭāprāmāṇyaprakārakatvarūpaprāmāṇyasyetyarthaḥ/
tasyeti/ niruktaprāmāṇyasyetyarthaḥ/ na sidhyediti/ tathā ca bādha iti
bhāvaḥ/ svatogrāhyatvasiddhiriti/ tādṛśaprāmāṇyāśrayabhūtaḥ yaḥ idaṃ
jñānaṃ aprametyākārakānuvyavasāyaḥ tadviṣayakajñānajanakasāmagryāḥ
svāśrayatādṛśānuvyavasāyaviśeṣyakaprāmāṇyaprakārakajñānājanakatayā
tādṛśasāmagryāḥ prasiddhatvāt
tajjanyānuvyavasāyaviṣayakajñānaviṣayatvasya anuvyavasāyaniṣṭhapramātve
satvāt na bādha iti bhāvaḥ//
children.translated_text: Now, following the word '<s>sāmagrī</s>' (aggregate) which is the qualificand [and which is feminine], it should be said 'of what apprehends validity also' [using the feminine form] — how then is the masculine 'of what apprehends' used in the <s>Dīpikā</s>? — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'In a general [sense], the neuter [is used].' Because of the grammatical rule that the neuter is used when one intends to convey the general property — in the form of the apprehending capacity — as the locus, without specifying its particular locus, the neuter is used here — this is the purport. 'Of the stated validity' — the meaning is: of the validity in the form of having invalidity as qualifier-mode qualified by having-what-possesses-invalidity-as-qualificand. 'Of that' — the meaning is: of the stated validity. 'Would not be established' — and accordingly, there would be sublation — this is the purport. 'The establishment of self-apprehended-ness' — the introspective cognition 'This cognition is invalid,' which is the locus of such validity, is itself the object of a cognition generated by the aggregate of causes; since it is well-known that such an aggregate does not generate a cognition having validity as qualifier-mode and having as qualificand its own locus, namely such an introspective cognition, the property of being the object of the cognition whose object is a cognition generated by such an aggregate — this obtains in the validity residing in the introspective cognition — hence there is no sublation. This is the purport.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: prāmāṇyajñaptivādapūrvapakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Opponent's Position on the Apprehension of Validity

children.text:
nanu svata eva
prāmāṇyaṃ gṛhyate, 'ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmi' ityanuvyavasāyena
ghaṭaghaṭatvayoriva tatsambanadhasyāpi viṣayīkaraṇāt
vyavasāyarūpapratyāsattestulyatvāt/ purovartini prakārasambandhasyaiva
pramātvapadārthatvāditi cet---
children.translated_text: Now, validity is apprehended intrinsically (<s>svataḥ</s>) alone — because through the introspective cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) 'I know the pot,' just as the pot and pot-hood are made objects, so too the relation between them is made an object; because the proximity in the form of the [first-order] cognition (<s>vyavasāya</s>) is equal [for all]; and because the meaning of the term <s>pramātva</s> (validity) is precisely the relation of the qualifier-mode with [the object] that is before one — if thus objected:

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
itthaṃ
vipratipattimupanyasya mīmāṃsakamatamupanyasyati - nanviti/ svata
evetyādi/ ghaṭatvādighaṭitaprāmāṇyaṃ niruktasāmagrīta eva gṛhyata
ityarthaḥ/ apyarthakenaivakāreṇa anumānādiparigrahaḥ/
anuvyavasāyeneti/ idaṃ ca miśramatābhiprāyeṇa/ matatrayasādhāraṇyena
tu prāthamikajñānagraheṇeti dhyeyam/ tatsambandhasyāpīti/
ghaṭaghaṭatvayoḥ yaḥ sambandhaḥ tasyāpītyarthaḥ/ nanu anuvyavasāye kathaṃ
sambandhasya bhānamityāśaṅkya yathā ghaṭaghaṭatvayoḥ
vyavasāyarūpapratyāsattyā bhānam tathā tatsambandhasyāpi,
vyavasāyarūpapratyāsatteraviśeṣādityāha - vyavasāyeti/ tāvatā kathaṃ
prāmāṇyasya bhānamata āha - purovartini prakārasambandhasyaiveti/
purovartini yaḥ prakārasambandhaḥ tadghaṭitasyaivetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Having thus presented the divergence of views, he presents the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> position — with 'now.' 'Intrinsically alone' etc. — the meaning is: the validity constituted by pot-hood and the like is apprehended by the very same aggregate [of causes that produced the original cognition]. The word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>), which would otherwise be meaningless, serves to include inference and the like. 'By introspective cognition' — this is according to the <s>Miśra</s> view. In common with all three views, [it should be understood as] through the apprehension of the primary cognition. This should be noted. 'Of their relation also' — the meaning is: of the relation between the pot and pot-hood also. Now, how does the relation appear in the introspective cognition? — anticipating this doubt, just as the pot and pot-hood appear through the proximity in the form of the [first-order] cognition, so too their relation [appears], because the proximity in the form of the cognition is undifferentiated — he says: 'the proximity in the form of the cognition' etc. Merely by that, how does validity appear? — to this he says: 'the relation of the qualifier-mode with what is before one' etc. The meaning is: [validity] is constituted precisely by the relation of the qualifier-mode with what is before one.

children.text:
ayamāśayaḥ - naiyāyikā
api anuvyavasāye viśeṣyatvaprakāratvayorbhānamaṅgīkurvanti,
purovartinaṃ ghaṭatvena jānāmītyākārakasyaiva anuvyavasāyasya
tairaṅgīkārāt/ parantu purovartini ghaṭādau
ghaṭatvādirūpaprakārasambandhabhānaṃnāṅgīkurvanti/ atastatra
prakārasambandhabhānasya vyavasthāpane kimapi nāvaśiṣṭamiti prāmāṇyasya
bhānaṃ sidhyati, anupasthitayorapi viśeṣyatvaprakāratvayorbhānasya
sarvasaṃmatatvāditi/
children.translated_text: The intent is this: even the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> accept the appearance of qualificand-hood and qualifier-mode-hood in the introspective cognition — because they accept the introspective cognition as having the form 'I know the object before me as having pot-hood.' However, they do not accept the appearance of the relation of the qualifier-mode such as pot-hood with the object before one such as the pot. Therefore, since nothing remains to establish the appearance of the qualifier-mode-relation there, the appearance of validity is established — because even the appearance of qualificand-hood and qualifier-mode-hood, which are not presented [to the mind], is universally accepted.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
ghaṭatvādighaṭitaprāmāṇyamiti/
ghaṭatvavadviśeśyakatvāvacchinnaghaṭatvaprakārakatvarūpaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ
tadāśrayajñānagrāhakasāmagryaiva gṛhyata ityarthaḥ/ ayaṃ ghaṭa
ityākārakavyavasāyaviṣayakaṃ yat jñānaṃ ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmītyākārakaṃ
tasmin ahamarthaḥ ātmā jñānaṃ ca ātmamanassaṃyogena
manassaṃyuktasamavāyena ca bhāsete iti tadaṃśe laukikatvam/
ghaṭaghaṭatvayostu jñānalakṣaṇayā pratyāsattyā bhānam/
tādṛśānuvyavasāyāt pūrvaṃ ayaṃ ghaṭa ityākārakavyavasāyasya
sattvāt vyavasāyasya ghaṭaghaṭatvobhayaviṣayakatvāt/ tathā ca
ghaṭaghaṭatvaviṣayakavyavasāyātmakajñānalakṣaṇasannikarṣeṃṇa yathā vā 'ghaṭamahaṃ
jānāmi' ityanuvyavasāye ghaṭaghaṭatvayorbhānam,
children.translated_text: 'Validity constituted by pot-hood and the like' — the meaning is: the validity in the form of having pot-hood-possessor as qualificand delimited by pot-hood-qualifier-mode-hood is apprehended by the very aggregate that apprehends the cognition that is the locus [of that validity]. In the cognition having as its object the first-order cognition (<s>vyavasāya</s>) of the form 'This is a pot,' namely the [introspective cognition] 'I know the pot' — in that, the referent of 'I,' namely the self, and the cognition, both appear through the conjunction of the self with mind (<s>manas</s>) and through inherence-in-what-is-conjoined-with-mind respectively — hence that portion is ordinary [perception]. But the pot and pot-hood appear through the extraordinary contact (<s>pratyāsatti</s>) in the form of the knowledge-based relation (<s>jñānalakṣaṇā</s>). Since the first-order cognition of the form 'This is a pot' exists prior to such an introspective cognition, and since the first-order cognition has both the pot and pot-hood as its objects, accordingly, through the extraordinary contact in the form of the knowledge-based relation consisting of the first-order cognition that has both the pot and pot-hood as its objects, just as the pot and pot-hood appear in the introspective cognition 'I know the pot,'

children.text:
tathaiva ghaṭaghaṭatvayoḥ
yaḥ sambandhaḥ samavāyarūpaḥ tasyāpi bhānamāvaśyakam/ vyavasāye tasyāpi
bhānena vyavasāyātmakasannikarṣāt tatsambandhabhānasyāvaśyambhāvāt/ na
ca ghaṭaghaṭatvasambandho bhāsatām, tāvatā pramātvābhānāt
children.translated_text: so too the relation between the pot and pot-hood, which is in the form of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), must necessarily also appear. Because since that [relation] too appears in the first-order cognition, the appearance of their relation is necessarily entailed by the extraordinary contact in the form of the first-order cognition. Nor should it be said: let the relation of the pot and pot-hood appear, but merely by that, the appearance of validity [does not follow] —

children.text:
pramātvasya
jñānaviṣayakagrahaviṣayatvāravyaṃ svatastvaṃ kathaṃ sidhyediti vācyam/
purovartini prakārasambandhasyaiva pramātvapadārthatvāt
sambandhabhānasyaiva pramātvabhānarūpatvāt/ etadeva kathamiti cet -
śrūyatām - jñānasya prāmāṇye viśodhyamāne viṣayatathātva eva
tatparyavasyati/ viṣayo yādṛśadharmavattayā vyavasāye bhāsate
tādṛśadharmasambandha eva viṣayasya tathātvam, tadeva ca pramātvamiti
tasyānuvyavasāyena viṣayīkaraṇāt pramātvasya svatogrāhyatvamiti
mīmāṃsakāśayaḥ/ sa eva dīpikāyāṃ prakāśikāyāṃ cānūdita
children.translated_text: how would self-apprehended-ness of validity be established if validity must be the object of a cognition that has knowledge as its content? — [for] because the meaning of the term <s>pramātva</s> (validity) is precisely the relation of the qualifier-mode with what is before one, the appearance of the relation itself constitutes the appearance of validity. If asked how this is so — listen: when the validity of a cognition is examined, it ultimately resolves to the 'such-ness' (<s>tathātva</s>) of the object. The 'such-ness' of the object is precisely the relation of whatever property the object appears as possessing in the first-order cognition — and that itself is validity. Since that is made an object by the introspective cognition, the self-apprehended-ness of validity [is established] — this is the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> intent. That itself has been restated in the <s>Dīpikā</s> and the <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text:
iti/ yadyapi
arthantathātvasya viṣayaniṣṭhasya jñānagatapramātvarūpatvaṃ na sambhavatīti
tadvanniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpakatve sati tanniṣṭhaprakāratāśālijñānatvameva
pramātvaṃ vācyamiti śaṅkā avatarati, tathāpi naiyāyikaiḥ
purovartiniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpakatve sati
rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpakatvamanuvyavasāye bhāsata iti
svīkriyate/ tatra viṃśeṣyatāprakāratayoranupasthitayo 'pi bhānam/
purovartirajatatvayoḥ vyavasāyarūpapratyāsatyā bhānam, purovartini
rajatatvavatvaṃ na bhāsate ityaṅgīkriyate/ mīmāṃsakāstu
vyavasāyarūpapratyāsattisāmyāt rajatatvavatvamapi bhāsata iti nirūpya
tadghaṭitapramātvaṃ anuvyavasāyena viṣayīkriyata iti nirūpayantīti
viśeṣaḥ/ purovartinaṃ ghaṭatvena jānāmītyākārakasyeti/
purovartiniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpakaghaṭatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpakajñānavānahamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Even though the 'such-ness of the object' (<s>arthatathātva</s>), which resides in the object, cannot have the nature of validity, which resides in the cognition — and hence the doubt arises that validity should be stated as: knowledge-hood that has qualificand-hood residing in the possessor-of-that while having qualifier-mode-hood residing in that — nevertheless, the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> accept that in the introspective cognition, the qualifier-mode-hood residing in silver-ness that determines the qualificand-hood residing in the object before one does appear. There, even though qualificand-hood and qualifier-mode-hood are not presented [to the mind], they appear. The pot and pot-hood appear through the proximity in the form of the first-order cognition — but the possessing-of-pot-hood-by-the-object-before-one does not appear — this is accepted [by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>]. The <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, however, ascertain that through the equality of the proximity in the form of the first-order cognition, even the possessing-of-silver-hood [by the object] appears, and then ascertain that the validity constituted by that is made an object by the introspective cognition — this is the distinction. 'Having the object before one as possessing pot-hood, I know' — the meaning is: I possess knowledge that determines the qualifier-mode-hood residing in pot-hood and determines the qualificand-hood residing in the object before one.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: prāmāṇyajñaptivādasiddhāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Established Conclusion on the Apprehension of Validity

children.text:
svataḥprāmāṇyagrahe
'jalajñānaṃ pramā na vā' ityanabhyāsadaśāyāṃ pramātvasaṃśayo na syāt/
anuvyavasāyena prāmāṇyasya niścitatvāt/ tasmāt
svatogrāhyatvābhāvāt parato grāhyatvameva/ tathāhi - prathamaṃ
jalajñānānantaraṃ pravṛttau satyāṃ jalalābhe sati pūrvotpannaṃ jalajñānaṃ
pramā samarthapravṛttijanakatvāt yannaivaṃ tannaivaṃ, yathā apramā iti
vyatirekiṇā pramātvaṃ niścīyate/ dvitīyādijñāneṣu
pūrvajñānadṛṣṭāntena tatsajātīyatvaliṅgena anvayavyatirekiṇāpi
gṛhyate//
children.translated_text: If validity were apprehended intrinsically, then in the stage of non-habituation, doubt regarding the validity of the form 'Is the cognition of water valid or not?' would not arise — because validity would have been ascertained by the introspective cognition. Therefore, due to the absence of self-apprehended-ness, extrinsic apprehended-ness alone [obtains]. Thus: initially, after the cognition of water, when activity [directed toward the water] has occurred and water has been obtained, the validity of the previously arisen cognition of water is ascertained by a purely negative inference (<s>vyatirekin</s>): 'It is valid because it generates competent activity; what is not so is not so — like an invalid cognition.' In the second and subsequent cognitions, [validity] is apprehended even through a positive-negative inference (<s>anvayavyatirekin</s>), using the first cognition as an example and the mark of being of the same kind as that [first cognition] — i.e. of generating competent activity.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
jalajñānamityādi/
jalajñānaṃ pramā na vā ityākārakaḥ/ anabhyāsadaśāyām -
prāthamikajalajñānagrahottaradaśāyām/ anubhavasiddhaḥ pramātvasaṃśayo na
syādityarthaḥ/ niścitatvāditi/ tadvattāniścayasya tadabhāvavattājñānaṃ
prati pratibandhakatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ atra 'jñāto ghaṭa' iti pratīteḥ
jñānaviṣayatāviṣayakatvakalpanenaiva nirvāhe atiriktajñātatā na
kalpanīyā gauravāt mānābhāvācca iti tannirasanaprakāro
children.translated_text: 'Cognition of water' etc. The doubt of the form 'Is the cognition of water valid or not?' — 'in the stage of non-habituation' means: in the stage after the apprehension of the initial cognition of water. [The doubt that] is established by experience would not arise — this is the meaning. 'Because it has been ascertained' — because the ascertainment that 'it possesses that' is an obstructor of the cognition that 'it possesses the absence of that.' This is the purport. Here, since the experience 'the pot is known' can be explained by postulating merely the property of being the content of the object-relation of the cognition, an additional property of 'known-ness' (<s>jñātatā</s>) should not be postulated — due to prolixity and the absence of evidence. The method of refuting that [additional postulation] should

children.text:
bodhyaḥ/ tasmāditi/
anabhyāsadaśāyāṃ saṃśayānubhavādityarthaḥ/ etasya
svatogrāhyatvābhāve 'nvayaḥ/ paratīgrāhyatvamiti/ prāmāṇyasyānumānāditi
eva grāhyatvamityarthaḥ/ pravṛttau satyāmiti/
children.translated_text: be understood. 'Therefore' — the meaning is: because doubt is experienced in the stage of non-habituation. This connects with the absence of self-apprehended-ness. 'Extrinsic apprehended-ness' — the meaning is: the validity is apprehended only through inference and the like. 'When activity has occurred' —

children.text:
etena
mīmāṃsakairabhyupagatāyāṃ prāmāṇyaniścayasya pravṛttihetutāyāṃ
vyabhicāro darśitaḥ/ na ca niṣkampapravṛttāveva prāmaṇyaniścasya
hetutā, sakampapravṛttau tu pramāṇyasaṃśayasya, niṣkampatvaṃ sakampatvaṃ ca
viṣayitāviśeṣaḥ evaṃ ca tatra sakampapravṛttyaṅgīkāre 'pi
prāmāṇyaniścayasya hetutāyāṃ kathaṃ vyabhicāra iti vācyam, tathāpi
yatra prāmāṇyasyāprāmāṇyasya vā jñānaṃ nāsīt, āsīcca
kevalajalādijñānaṃ tatra pravṛttipradarśanena prāmāṇyasaṃśayahetutāyāṃ
vyabhicārasya durvāratvāt/ na caivaṃ jalādijñāne aprāmāṇyaniścakāle
pravṛttiḥsyāditi śaṅkanīyam/ agṛhītāprāmāṇyakajalādijñānatvena,
taddhetutāsvīkāreṇa adoṣāditi saṅkṣepaḥ/ jalalābhe satīti/
etāvatā vakṣyamāṇasya prāmāṇyavyavasthāpakahetoḥ svarūpāsiddhiśaṅkā
nirākṛtā/ idānīṃ pakṣasyāsattvādāha - pūrvotpannamiti/ samartheti/
tadvadviśeṣyakatatprakāraketyarthaḥ/ anvayyudāharaṇāsambhavāt
vyatirekyudāharaṇaṃ sadṛṣṭāntamāha - yannaivaṃ tannaivamiti/ yadapramā
tatsamarthapravṛtyajanakamityarthaḥ/ vyatirekiṇā - vyatirekavyāptimatā/
niścīyate - anumīyate/ dvitīyādijñāneṣu - dvitīyādijalajñāneṣu/
tatsajātīyatvaliṅgena - pūrvajñānasajātīyatvarūpaliṅgena/
samarthapravṛttijanakatveneti yāvat/ gṛhyata iti/ prāmāṇyamanumīyata
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: By this, a deviation has been shown in the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>' accepted position that the ascertainment of validity is the cause of activity. Nor should it be said: the causality of the ascertainment of validity pertains only to unwavering activity, while for wavering activity the doubt about validity [is the cause], and since wavering-ness and unwavering-ness are distinctions of the subject-relation [of the activity], and accordingly, even if wavering activity is accepted there, [the objection of] how there can be deviation in the causality of the ascertainment of validity [does not arise] — nonetheless, wherever there was no cognition of either validity or invalidity, and there was merely a cognition of water and the like, there the demonstration of activity [shows] that the deviation from the causality of the doubt about validity is insurmountable. Nor should it be doubted: if so, when the invalidity of the cognition of water and the like has been ascertained, there should be activity [regardless] — because, by accepting causality through the property 'cognition of water and the like whose invalidity has not been apprehended,' there is no defect. This is the summary. 'When water has been obtained' — by this much, the doubt regarding the essential unestablishedness of the forthcoming reason for establishing validity is averted. Now he states the subject — with 'previously arisen.' 'Competent' (<s>samartha</s>) — the meaning is: having that-possessor as qualificand and that as qualifier-mode. Since a corroborating positive example is not available, he states the negative example — with 'what is not so is not so.' The meaning is: what is invalid does not generate competent activity. 'Through a purely negative [inference]' means through one possessing [only] negative concomitance. 'Is ascertained' means: is inferred. 'In the second and subsequent cognitions' means: in the second and subsequent cognitions of water. 'Through the mark of being of the same kind as that' means: through the mark in the form of being of the same kind as the previous cognition — i.e. generating competent activity. 'Is apprehended' — the meaning is: validity is inferred.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
prāthamikajalajñānagrahottaradaśāyāmiti/ prāthamikaṃ yat
jalajñānaṃ tadviṣayako yo grahaḥ jalamahaṃ
children.translated_text: 'In the stage after the apprehension of the initial cognition of water' — the initial cognition of water, and its apprehension (<s>graha</s>), i.e. [the introspective cognition] of the form 'I know

children.text:
jānāmītyākārakaḥ
taduttarakāle ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca prāthamikajalajñānagrahe yadi
jalajñānaniṣṭhaṃ pramātvamapi gṛhītaṃ tarhi
children.translated_text: water' — at the time after that is the meaning. And accordingly, if in the apprehension of the initial cognition of water, the validity residing in the cognition of water were also apprehended, then

children.text:
jalajñānaṃ pramā na veti
jalajñānadharmikapramātvasaṃśayo na syāt,
jalajñānadharmikapramātvaniścayātmakapratibanadhakasatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ jātu
jalāśaye jalamālokya tatra vihitasnānapānādeḥ puṃsaḥ paradine
madhyāhne dūrāt tatra yajjaladarśanaṃ tat dvitīyaṃ jalajñānaṃ
abhyāsadaśāpannamityucyate/ tasya
gṛhītaprāmāṇyakapūrvajñānasajātīyatvānusandhānena idaṃ jñānaṃ pramā
na vā iti saṃśayasya na prasaktiriti paryālocya
prāthamikajalajñānagrahottaramityuktam/ tadabhāvavattājñānaṃ/
pramātvasaṃśaye pramātvābhāvakoṭerapi bhānena tadaṃśajñānaṃ prati
pramātvaniścayasya pratibandhakatvādityarthaḥ/ tannirasanaprakāra iti/
jñātatānirāsaprakāra ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The doubt regarding <s>pramātva</s> (validity) qualifying the cognition of water — 'is the cognition of water a <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) or not?' — would not arise, because the obstructor in the form of the ascertainment of <s>pramātva</s> qualifying the cognition of water is present. This is the purport. When someone, having once seen water in a reservoir and performed bathing, drinking and so forth there, sees that water again from a distance at noon the next day — that second cognition of water is said to have reached the stage of familiarity (<s>abhyāsadaśā</s>). Considering that, through the recognition of homogeneity with the prior cognition whose validity has already been grasped, there is no occasion for the doubt 'is this cognition valid or not?' — it was stated that [this occurs] after the apprehension of the initial cognition of water. 'The cognition possessing the absence of that' — since in the doubt about <s>pramātva</s>, even the alternative of the absence of <s>pramātva</s> appears, the ascertainment of <s>pramātva</s> serves as an obstructor with respect to the cognition of that component. This is the meaning. 'The method of removing that' — means the method of removing the known-ness. This is the meaning.

children.text:
eteneti/
prāthamikajalajñānānantarameva pravṛttiriti kathanenetyarthaḥ/
mīmāṃsakairabhyupagatāyāmiti/ kasmiṃścit viṣaye jñāte sati jāte
jñāne prāmāṇyaniścayaṃ vinā viṣaye pravṛttiḥ na bhavatīti
tadviṣayakapravṛttiṃ prati
children.translated_text: 'By this' — the meaning is: by the statement that activity occurs immediately after the initial cognition of water. 'In the [activity] accepted by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>' — when a particular object has been cognized, the activity toward that object does not occur without the ascertainment of validity in the cognition that has arisen; therefore, with respect to the activity directed toward that object,

children.text:
tadviṣayakajñānadharmikaprāmāṇyaniścayaḥ kāraṇamiti mīmāṃsakāḥ
vadanti/ tanna yuktam/ jalajñānānantaraṃ idaṃ jñānaṃ pramā
ityākārakajalajñānadharmikaprāmāṇyaniścayaṃ vināpi pravṛtterūtpattyā
vyatirekavyabhicārāditi/ bhāvaḥ/ na ca niṣkampeti/ pravṛttirdvividhā -
niṣkampā sakampā ceti/ utkaṭā pravṛttiḥ niṣkampā, anutkaṭā pravṛttiḥ
sakampā/ utkaṭatvānutkaṭatve pravṛttigatau viṣayitāviśeṣau/ tatra
tadviṣayiṇīṃ utkaṭapravṛtti prati tadviṣayakajñāne prāmāṇyaniścayaḥ
kāraṇam, tadviṣayakānutkaṭapravṛttiṃ prati tu prāmāṇyasaṃśayaḥ kāraṇam/
prāmāṇyaniścayasya niṣkampapravṛttitvaṃ kāryatāvacchedakam,
prāmāṇyasaṃśayasya sakampapravṛttitvaṃ kāryatāvacchedakam/ yatra
jalajñānānantaraṃ tatra prāmāṇyaniścayaṃ vināpi pravṛttiḥ jāyate tatra sā
pravṛttiḥ sakampetyaṅgīkriyate/ tasyāṃ ca
niṣkampapravṛttitvarūpakāryatāvacchedakavirahāt prāmāṇyaniścayaṃ vinā
niṣkampapravṛttitvāvacchinnasyānupattyā na vyatirekavyabhicāra iti
prāmāṇyaniścayasya pravṛttihetutvaṃ nirbādhamiti śaṅkiturāśayaḥ/
tathāpīti/ yatra prāmāṇyasya aprāmāṇyasya vā saṃśayo vā niścayo vā
nābhūt jalajñānaṃ paramabhūt tatrāpi pravṛtterdarśanenasakampāyāḥ
tādṛśapravṛtteḥ prāmāṇyasaṃśayaṃ vināpyutpatyā vyatirekavyabhicārāt
prāmāṇyasaṃśayasya pravṛttihetutā na bhavatīti samādhāturāśayaḥ/ na
caivamiti/ prāmāṇyaniścayasya vā prāmāṇyasaṃśayasya vā pravṛttiṃ prati
hetutvānaṅgīkāre yatra jalajñāne aprāmāṇyaniścayaḥ tatkāle/pi
pravṛttiḥ syāt, pravṛttihetoḥ jalajñānasya satvādityarthaḥ/
agṛhīteti/ aprāmāṇyajñānābhāvaviśiṣṭajalādijñānameva
jalādiviṣayakapravṛttiheturityaṅgīkārāt jalādijñāne
aprāmāṇyajñānakāle aprāmāṇyajñānaviśiṣṭajalādijñānamevāstīti na
pravṛtyāpattiḥ, aprāmāṇyajñānābhāvaviśiṣṭajalajñānarūpasya
pravṛttihetorabhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> maintain that the ascertainment of validity qualifying the cognition directed toward that object is the cause. That is not correct, because even without the ascertainment of validity in the form 'this cognition is a <s>pramā</s>' qualifying the cognition of water, activity does arise after the cognition of water — hence there is deviation in the method of agreement-in-absence (<s>vyatirekavyabhicāra</s>). This is the purport. 'Nor is it unwavering' — activity is of two kinds: unwavering (<s>niṣkampa</s>) and wavering (<s>sakampa</s>). Intense activity is unwavering; non-intense activity is wavering. Intensity and non-intensity are specific qualifications of activity belonging to the agent. There, the ascertainment of validity in the cognition directed toward that object is the cause of the intense unwavering activity directed toward it, while doubt about validity is the cause of the non-intense wavering activity directed toward it. The delimitor of the effect-hood of the ascertainment of validity is unwavering-activity-hood; the delimitor of the effect-hood of doubt about validity is wavering-activity-hood. Where activity arises after the cognition of water even without the ascertainment of validity, that activity is accepted as wavering. And in that case, since the delimitor of effect-hood in the form of unwavering-activity-hood is absent, because the effect delimited by unwavering-activity-hood does not arise without the ascertainment of validity, there is no deviation in the method of agreement-in-absence — thus the intention of the objector is that the causal status of the ascertainment of validity with respect to activity remains unobstructed. 'Even so' — where neither doubt nor ascertainment of validity or invalidity arose, and yet only the cognition of water arose and activity is still observed — since even wavering activity of that kind arises without doubt about validity, there is deviation in the method of agreement-in-absence, and hence doubt about validity does not have causal status with respect to activity. This is the intention of the respondent. 'Nor thus' — if the causal status with respect to activity of either the ascertainment of validity or doubt about validity is not accepted, then even where there is an ascertainment of invalidity in the cognition of water, activity would still occur at that time, since the cognition of water, which is the cause of activity, is present. This is the meaning. 'Not apprehended' — since it is accepted that only the cognition of water and the like qualified by the absence of the cognition of invalidity is the cause of activity directed toward water and the like, at the time of the cognition of invalidity in the cognition of water and the like, only the cognition of water qualified by the cognition of invalidity exists — hence there is no undesirable consequence of activity arising, because the cause of activity in the form of the cognition of water qualified by the absence of the cognition of invalidity is absent. This is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
bahuvittavyayāyāsasādhyeṣu vaidikeṣu vyavahāreṣu prāmāṇyaniścayaṃ
vinā niṣkampapravṛttirna dṛśyata iti
prāmāṇyagrahaviśiṣṭārthaniścayasyaiva pravṛttihetutvam/ yuktaṃ
caitat-aprāmāṇyajñānābhāvaviśiṣṭārthaniścayasya pravṛttihetutve
taccharīre tadabhāvavati tatprakārakatvarūpasya tadvati
tatprakāratvābhāvarūpasya cāprāmāṇyasya niveśāpekṣayā
prāmāṇyagrahaviśiṣṭatvaniveśe lāghavādityāśaṅkyāha - saṅkṣepa
iti/ prāmāṇyagrahasya kathañcit pravṛttyupayogitve 'pi parataḥ
prāmāṇyagrahasaṃbhavāt svata eva prāmāṇyagraha iti
nābhiniveṣṭavyamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: In Vedic transactions that require much wealth, expenditure, and effort, unwavering activity is not observed without the ascertainment of validity; therefore, it is fitting that the ascertainment of an object qualified by the apprehension of validity alone is the cause of activity. And this is appropriate — compared to positing the ascertainment of an object qualified by the absence of the cognition of invalidity as the cause of activity, positing qualification by the apprehension of validity is more parsimonious, since it avoids the need to include in that body [of conditions] the form of having-that-as-qualifier in what possesses the absence of that, and the form of absence-of-having-that-as-qualifier in what possesses that, with respect to invalidity. Anticipating this, [the author] says 'in brief.' Even if the apprehension of validity has some utility for activity, since the apprehension of validity can occur extrinsically (<s>parataḥ</s>), one should not insist that the apprehension of validity is intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>) alone. This is the purport.

children.text:
etāvateti/ jalalābhe
satīti kathanenetyarthaḥ/ vakṣyamāṇasya prāmāṇyavyavasthāpakahetoriti/
prāmāṇyasādhakasya
children.translated_text: 'This much' — the meaning is: by the statement that water is obtained. 'Of the forthcoming ground establishing validity' — of the ground that establishes <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity),

children.text:
samarthapravṛttijanakatvarūpahetorityarthaḥ/ svarūpāsiddhiśaṅkā -
pakṣāvṛttitvaśaṅkā/ pravṛtteḥ sāmarthyaṃ hi jalalābhenaiva/ tathā ca
jalalābhakathanena jalajñāne samarthapravṛttijanakatvarūpaheturastīti
sūcitamiti bhāvaḥ/ idānīmiti/ prāmāṇyānumitisamaya ityarthaḥ/
pūrvajñānasajātīyatveti/
gṛhītaprāmāṇyakapūrvajñānasajātīyatvaliṅgenetyarthaḥ/
dvitīyādijñānasya pūrvajñānasajātīyatvaṃ ca
saphalapravṛttijanakatvarūpeṇa/ tathā ca saphalapravṛttijanakatvameva hetuḥ,
pūrvajñānamanvayadṛṣṭānta iti sūcanāya pūrvajñānasajātīyetyuktam/
anumānaprayogastu - dvitīyādijalajñānaṃ pramā
samarthapravṛttijanakatvāt yat samarthapravṛttijanakam tatpramā yathā
prāthamikajalajñānamiti/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: the ground in the form of generating capable activity. The doubt of non-establishment of the essential nature is the doubt of non-occurrence in the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>). For the capability of activity is [demonstrated] precisely by the obtaining of water. And thus, by the statement of obtaining water, it is indicated that the ground in the form of generating capable activity exists in the cognition of water. This is the purport. 'Now' — means at the time of the inference of validity.
