'Homogeneity with the prior cognition' — the meaning is: through the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of homogeneity with the prior cognition whose validity has been grasped. The homogeneity of the second and subsequent cognitions with the prior cognition is in the form of generating fruitful activity. Accordingly, the generating of fruitful activity itself is the probans (<s>hetu</s>); the prior cognition is the corroborative instance (<s>anvayadṛṣṭānta</s>). To indicate this, 'homogeneity with the prior cognition' was stated. The formulation of the inference is: the second and subsequent cognition of water is a <s>pramā</s>, because it generates capable activity; whatever generates capable activity is a <s>pramā</s>, like the initial cognition of water.

children.text:
atredaṃ tattvam-ayaṃ ghaṭa
iti jñānānantaraṃ imaṃ ghaṭaṃ jānāmi, imaṃ ghaṭatvena jānāmi
ityanavyavasāyo bhavati, na tu ghaṭaṃ ghaṭatvena jānāmīti/ pramātvaṃ
tu na kevalaṃ dharmiviśeṣyakatvaviśiṣṭaghaṭatvaprakārakatvam, tasya
children.translated_text: Here is the true state of affairs: after the cognition 'this is a pot,' the reflective awareness (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) arises in the form 'I know this pot' or 'I know this as possessing pot-ness,' but not in the form 'I know the pot as possessing pot-ness.' Now, <s>pramātva</s> (validity) is not merely having pot-ness as a qualifier conjoined with having the particular individual as the qualificand, since that

children.text:
pramābhramobhayaniṣṭhatvāt/ kiṃ tu
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakatvaviśiṣṭaghaṭatvaprakārakatvam/ idaṃ ca
nānuvyavasāye bhāsate/ tatra ghaṭatvaviśiṣṭaniṣṭhatayā viśeṣyatāyā
agrahaṇāt/ vyavasāye idantvenaiva ghaṭasya viśeṣyatvāt
ghaṭatvaviśiṣṭatvena ghaṭasya viśeṣyatvābhāvāt
ghaṭatvaviśiṣṭaniṣṭhatayā viśeṣyatāyāḥ anuvyavasāyane
grahaṇāsaṃbhavāt/ ataḥ prāmāṇyaṃ na svatogrāhyamiti naiyāyikānāmāśayaḥ
iti kecit/"tathāpyanuvyavasāyānantaraṃ vyavasāyasya
prāmāṇye arthasya tadvattve ca saṃśayasyānubhavasiddhatvāt nārthatadvattvaṃ
tadbiṣayaḥ"iti maṇigranthaḥ teṣaramanukūlaḥ/
children.translated_text: is common to both <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) and <s>bhrama</s> (error). Rather, it is having pot-ness as a qualifier conjoined with having as qualificand what possesses pot-ness. And this does not appear in the reflective awareness (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>), because in it the qualificand-hood as residing in what is qualified by pot-ness is not grasped. In the primary cognition (<s>vyavasāya</s>), the pot is the qualificand only through this-ness (<s>idantva</s>); since the pot is not the qualificand through being qualified by pot-ness, the qualificand-hood as residing in what is qualified by pot-ness cannot possibly be grasped in the reflective awareness. Therefore, <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity) is not apprehensible intrinsically (<s>svataḥ</s>) — this is the view of certain <s>Naiyāyikas</s>. 'Even so, since after the reflective awareness, doubt regarding the validity of the primary cognition and the object's possessing that [property] is established by experience, the object's possessing that is not its content' — thus the <s>Maṇi</s> text [of <s>Gaṅgeśa</s>] is favorable to them.

children.text:
dīdhitikārā api-"prāmāṇyasya saṃśayānyathānupapattyā taddharmaviśiṣṭe
tatprakārakatvasya grāhakatve 'nuvyavasāyasyāsāmatharyaṃ kalpyate/ tena
purovarttini rajatatvaprakārakamiti grahe 'pi purovartini rajate
rajatatvaprakārakamiti na grahaḥ"iti prāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Dīdhiti</s> [<s>Raghunātha Śiromaṇi</s>] also states: 'Since validity requires the apprehension of having-that-as-qualifier in what is qualified by that property, and the doubt about it can only be explained [if that component is not grasped], the incapacity of reflective awareness to grasp it must be postulated. Consequently, even though there is apprehension of the form "the thing before me has silver-ness as qualifier," there is no apprehension of the form "the silver before me has silver-ness as qualifier."'

children.text:
gadādharabhaṭṭācāryāstu -"tadvadviśeśyakatvatatprakārakatvayoravacchedyāvacchedakabhāvagraheṇa
prāmāṇyasaṃśayasya tadadhīnasyārthatadvattvasaṃśayasya copapatteḥ
arthatadvattvāviṣayakatve nirbharo nocita"ityāhuḥ1/
children.translated_text: <s>Gadādhara Bhaṭṭācārya</s>, however, states: 'Since the doubt about <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity), and consequently the doubt about the object's possessing that [property] which depends on it, can be explained through the apprehension of the delimitor-delimited relation between having-that-as-qualificand-hood and having-that-as-qualifier-hood, one need not insist that [validity] does not have that [object's possessing the property] as its content.' [Footnote 1]

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: prāmāṇyotpattiparatasttvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of the extrinsic nature (<s>paratastva</s>) of the origination of <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity)

children.text:
pramāyā
guṇajanyatvamutpatau paratastvam/ pramāsādhāraṇakāraṇa guṇaḥ,
apramāsādhāraṇakāraṇaṃ doṣaḥ/ tatra pratyakṣe viśeṣaṇavadviśeṣyasannikarṣo
guṇaḥ/ anumitau vyāpakavati vyāpyajñānam/ upamitau
yathārthasādṛśyajñānam/ śābdajñāne yathārthayogyatājñānam
ityādyūhanīyam/
children.translated_text: The extrinsic nature of origination means that <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is produced by a <s>guṇa</s> (excellence). A <s>guṇa</s> is the uncommon cause of <s>pramā</s>; a <s>doṣa</s> (defect) is the uncommon cause of <s>apramā</s> (invalid cognition). Among these, in perception, the <s>guṇa</s> is the contact of the qualificand possessing the qualifier with the sense organ (<s>viśeṣaṇavadviśeṣyasannikarṣa</s>). In inference, it is the cognition of the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) in what possesses the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>). In comparison (<s>upamiti</s>), it is the veridical cognition of similarity. In verbal testimony (<s>śābdajñāna</s>), it is the cognition of veridical semantic fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>). And so on — this should be inferred [for other cases].

children.text:
1. ityāhuriti/
jñāne gṛhīte 'pi jñāne prāmāṇyasya saṃśayo bhavatīti tadanurodhena
prāmāṇyaghaṭakaḥ kaścidaṃśaḥ jñānajñāne na bhāsata iti vaktavyam/ sa
cāṃśaḥ purovartini ghaṭatvavattvarūpa iti dīdhitikārādayaḥ/
ghaṭatvavadviśeṣyakatvaghaṭatvaprakārakatvayoravacchedyāvacchedakabhāvarūpaḥ sa
iti gadādharabhaṭṭācārtha iti vivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Thus they state' — even when a cognition is grasped, doubt about the validity of that cognition arises; accordingly, some component constituting validity does not appear in the cognition of the cognition — this must be maintained. That component is the form of the object before one possessing pot-ness (i.e. being-qualified-by-pot-ness-of-the-qualificand) — so say the author of the <s>Dīdhiti</s> and others. That component is rather the delimitor-delimited relation between having-pot-ness-possessor-as-qualificand-hood and having-pot-ness-as-qualifier-hood — so says <s>Gadādhara Bhaṭṭācārya</s>. This is the distinction.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
evaṃ jñaptau
paratastvaṃ vyavasthāpya utpattau paratastvaṃ nirūpayati pramāyā iti/
pramāsādhāraṇakāraṇamiti/
pramātvādhikadeśavṛttidharmānavacchinnapramāniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatāśālītyarthaḥ/
tena jñānamātrahetubhūtātmamanassaṃyogādeḥ
bhramajanakapittādidoṣāṇāṃ ca vyudāsaḥ/
apramāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvamapyevaṃ pariṣkartavyam/ caturvidhapramāyāṃ
hetubhūtaṃ guṇaṃ krameṇopapādayati tatreti/ caturvidhapramāmadhya
ityarthaḥ/ ityādyūhanīyamiti/ 'pītaḥ śaṅkhaḥ' ityādibhrame
pittādidoṣaḥ, idaṃ rajatamityādibhrame ca cākacakyādiḥ iti
ūhanīyamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Having thus established the extrinsic nature (<s>paratastva</s>) with respect to apprehension, [the author of the <s>Dīpikā</s>] now determines the extrinsic nature with respect to origination, beginning with 'of <s>pramā</s>.' 'The uncommon cause of <s>pramā</s>' — the meaning is: that which possesses causal-hood determined by the effect-hood residing in <s>pramā</s>, not delimited by a property occurring in a locus wider than <s>pramātva</s> (validity). By this, the self-mind conjunction (<s>ātma-manas-saṃyoga</s>) and the like, which are causes of cognition in general, and the defects such as bile (<s>pitta</s>) that generate erroneous cognition, are excluded. The uncommon causal-hood of <s>apramā</s> (invalid cognition) should also be refined in the same manner. [The author] illustrates the <s>guṇa</s> (excellence) that is the cause in the four types of <s>pramā</s>, in order, with 'among these.' 'Among the four types of <s>pramā</s>' — this is the meaning. 'And so on, this should be inferred' — in the case of the error 'the conch is yellow,' the defect is bile (<s>pitta</s>) and the like; in the error 'this is silver,' the defect is glittering surface (<s>cākacakya</s>) and so forth — this should be inferred. This is the meaning.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pramātvādhikadeśavṛttīti/ pramātvavyāpakadharmānavacchinnā yā
pramāniṣṭhā kāryatā tannirūpitakāraṇatvaṃ pramātvaprayojakasya guṇasya
lakṣaṇamityarthaḥ/ pramāniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvamātroktau
jñānasāmānyaṃ prati hetubhūte ātmamanassaṃyogādāvativyāptiḥ/
tadvāraṇāya kāryatāyāṃ
pramātvādhikadeśavṛttidharmānavacchinnatvaniveśaḥ/ ātmamanassaṃyogādau
tu pramātvādhikadeśavṛttiḥ yo dharmaḥ jñānatvaṃ
tadavacchinnakāryantānirūpitakāraṇatvamevāsti, na
tadanavacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvamiti nātivyāptiḥ/
bhramāsādhāraṇakāraṇeṣu pittādidoṣeṣu
pramātvavyāpakajñānatvādyanavacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvasattvāt
tatrānivyāptivāraṇāya kāryatāyāṃ pramāniṣṭhatvaniveśaḥ/ pittādeḥ
bhramaniṣṭakāryatānirūpitākāraṇatāśālitve 'pi
pramāniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatāśālitvābhāvāt nātivyāptiḥ/
tadāha - teneti/ evaṃ pariṣkartavyamiti/
apramātvādhikadeśavṛttidharmānavacchinnāpramāniṣṭhakāryapariṣkartavyami ti/
apramātvādhikadeśavṛttidharmānavacchinnāpramāniṣṭhakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatāśālitvaṃ
doṣasya lakṣaṇamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Occurring in a locus wider than <s>pramātva</s>' — the definition of the <s>guṇa</s> (excellence) that brings about <s>pramātva</s> is: possessing causal-hood determined by the effect-hood residing in <s>pramā</s>, not delimited by a property that pervades <s>pramātva</s>. This is the meaning. If only 'possessing causal-hood determined by the effect-hood residing in <s>pramā</s>' were stated, there would be over-pervasion (<s>ativyāpti</s>) to the self-mind conjunction and the like, which are causes of cognition in general. To prevent this, the qualification 'not delimited by a property occurring in a locus wider than <s>pramātva</s>' is included in the effect-hood. In the self-mind conjunction and the like, there exists only causal-hood determined by effect-hood delimited by cognition-hood (<s>jñānatva</s>), which is a property occurring in a locus wider than <s>pramātva</s>, but not causal-hood determined by effect-hood not delimited by it — hence there is no over-pervasion. To prevent the failure to cover (<s>anivyāpti</s>) the defects such as bile (<s>pitta</s>), which are uncommon causes of erroneous cognition, and which do possess causal-hood determined by effect-hood not delimited by cognition-hood and the like that pervade <s>pramātva</s>, the qualification 'residing in <s>pramā</s>' is included in the effect-hood. Even though bile and the like possess causal-hood determined by effect-hood residing in <s>bhrama</s> (error), they do not possess causal-hood determined by effect-hood residing in <s>pramā</s> — hence there is no over-pervasion. This is stated with 'by this.' 'Should be refined in the same manner' — the definition of <s>doṣa</s> (defect) is: possessing causal-hood determined by the effect-hood residing in <s>apramā</s>, not delimited by a property occurring in a locus wider than <s>apramātva</s> (invalidity). This is the meaning.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
aprāmāṇyasya
paratastvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of the extrinsic nature (<s>paratastva</s>) of <s>aprāmāṇya</s> (invalidity)

children.text:
purovartini
prakārābhāvasya anuvyavasāyena anupasthitatvāt apramātvaṃ parata eva
gṛhyate/
children.translated_text: Since the absence of the qualifier (<s>prakāra</s>) in the object before one is not presented by the reflective awareness (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>), <s>apramātva</s> (invalidity) is apprehended only extrinsically (<s>parataḥ</s>).

children.text: pittādidoṣajanyatvamutpattau paratastvam/
children.translated_text: The extrinsic nature of origination [of invalidity] consists in being produced by defects such as bile (<s>pitta</s>) and the like.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
apramātvasya
paratastvaṃ sayuktikaṃ darśayati - purovartinīti/ anupasthitatvāditi/
aviṣayīkaraṇādityarthaḥ/ tathā ca pratyāsatterabhāvāt
apramātvasyānuvyavasāyena grahaṇaṃ na sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/ apramātvam -
tadabhāvavadviśeṣyakatvaviśiṣṭatatprakārakatvam/ parata eva gṛhyata iti/
anumānādita eva gṛhyata ityarthaḥ/ anumānaprayogastu - idaṃ jñānaṃ
apramā visaṃvādipravṛttijanakatvāt yannaivaṃ tannaivaṃ yathā pramā iti/
children.translated_text: [The author of the <s>Dīpikā</s>] shows the extrinsic nature of <s>apramātva</s> (invalidity) with reasons, beginning with 'in the object before one.' 'Because it is not presented' — means because it is not made the object [of awareness]. Accordingly, since proximity is absent, the apprehension of <s>apramātva</s> through reflective awareness (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) is not possible. This is the purport. <s>Apramātva</s> (invalidity) is: having-that-as-qualifier-hood conjoined with having-as-qualificand what possesses the absence of that. 'Is apprehended only extrinsically' — the meaning is: is apprehended only through inference (<s>anumāna</s>) and the like. The formulation of the inference is: this cognition is an <s>apramā</s> (invalid cognition), because it generates discordant activity (<s>visaṃvādipravṛtti</s>); whatever is not so is not so, like a <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition).

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pratyāsatterabhāvāditi/ saṃnikarṣābhāvādityarthaḥ/ viśeṣye
prakārasambandhasya vyavasāyaviṣayatvāt
vyavasāyarūpajñānalakṣaṇapratyāsattyā anuvyavasāyena
prakārasaṃbandhaghaṭitapramātvagrahaṇaṃ kathañcit prasaktaṃ pūrvaṃ nirākṛtam/
purovartini prakārābhāvasambandhasya vyavasāyaviṣayatvāt
tadghaṭitasyāpramātvasya kathamapi bhramānuvyavasāyena grahaṇaṃ na
sambhavatīti apramātvaṃ na prāthamikajñānagrahaviṣayatvarūpasvatastvavat/
api tu anumānavedyatvākhyaparatastvavaditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: "Due to the absence of <s>pratyāsatti</s> (proximity)" — the meaning is: due to the absence of <s>saṃnikarṣa</s> (sense-contact). Since the relation of the qualifier to the qualificand is the object of determinate cognition (<s>vyavasāya</s>), the apprehension of <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity), which involves the qualifier-relation, through <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (reflective cognition) by means of the proximity that has the nature of determinate cognition — this was somehow applicable but was previously refuted. Since the relation of the absence of the qualifier in the object before one is the content of determinate cognition, the apprehension of <s>aprāmāṇya</s> (invalidity), which involves that, through reflective cognition of error is not possible at all — therefore invalidity is not of the nature of <s>svatastva</s> (intrinsic validity) in the form of being the object of apprehension by primary cognition, but rather is of the nature of <s>paratastva</s> (extrinsic validity) called knowability through inference. This is the purport.

children.text:
visaṃvādipravṛttīti/
viphalapravṛttītyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: "Leading to discordant activity (<s>visaṃvādipravṛtti</s>)" — the meaning is: activity that is fruitless (<s>viphalapravṛtti</s>).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: anyathākhyātisamarthanam/
children.translated_text: Justification of <s>anyathākhyāti</s> (the theory of erroneous cognition as apprehension of the other).

children.text:
nanu sarveṣāṃ
jñānānāṃ yathārthatvāt ayathārthajñānameva nāstīti/ na ca 'śuktau
idaṃ rajatamṛ' iti jñānāt pravṛttidarśanāt
anyathākhyātisiddhiriti vācyam/ rajatasmṛtipurovartijñānābhyāmeva
pravṛttisambhavāt/ svatantropasthiteṣṭabhedāgrahasyaiva sarvatra
pravartakatvena 'nedam rajatamṛ' ityādau atiprasaṅgābhāvāditi
cet - na/ satyarajatasthale purovartiviśeṣyakarajatatvaprakārakajñānasya
lāghavena pravṛttijanakatayā śuktāvapi rajatārthipravṛttijanakatavena
viśiṣṭajñānasyaiva kalpanāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since all cognitions are veridical (<s>yathārtha</s>), there is simply no non-veridical cognition. Nor can it be said that <s>anyathākhyāti</s> is established from observing activity arising from the cognition 'this is silver' in the case of nacre, because activity is possible from the memory of silver and the cognition of the object before one alone. Since the non-apprehension of the difference from the desired object independently presented is the cause of activity in all cases, there is no over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>) in cases like 'this is not silver' — if so, no. Because, by the principle of parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>), since the cognition having silver-ness as qualifier and the object before one as qualificand is what generates activity in the case of real silver, in the case of nacre too, only a qualified cognition must be postulated as generating the activity of one desiring silver.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
gurumataṃ nirasya
anyathākhyātiṃ vyavasthāpayati - nanvityādinā/ yathārthatvāt -
pramātvāt/ ayathārthajñānameva nāstīti/
tadabhāvavadviśeṣyakatatprakārakatvarūpāyathārthatvaṃ jñānavṛtti netyarthaḥ/
tena na siddhyasiddhibhyāṃ vyāghātaḥ/ ayathārthatvasya tu
prasiddhiricchādau bodhyā/ anyathākhyātīti/ tadanaṅgīkāre
purovarttiviśeṣyakarajatatvādirūpeṣṭatāvacchedakaprakārakajñānasya
saṃvādivisaṃvādisādhāraṇapravṛttijanakatayā tatra pravṛttireva na
syāditi bhāvaḥ/ rajatasmṛtīti/ klptaniyatapūrvavartibhyāmityādiḥ/
sambhavāditi/ tathā ca pravṛttiṃ prati viśiṣṭajñānatvena kāraṇataiva
nāstīti tadanurodhena anyathākhyātikalpanaṃ na sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/
nanvevaṃ yatra 'nedam rajatam' ityādibādhagrahaḥ tatrāpi pravṛttiḥ
syādityata āha - upasthiteti/ etāvatā smṛtirūpakāraṇāpekṣā
sphuṭīkṛtā/ iṣṭabhedāgrahasyaiva -
rajatādirūpeṣṭabhedagrahābhāvasyaiva/ evakāreṇa viśiṣṭajñānasya
pravartakatvavyavacchedaḥ/ sarvatreti/ rajate śuktau cetyarthaḥ/
satyarajatasthale viśiṣṭajñānatvenaiva pravṛttiṃ prati kāraṇatvameṣṭavyam/
anyathā dharmadharmijñānayoḥ iṣṭabhedāgrahatvarūpagurudharmāvacchinnasya ca
kāraṇatāpatteḥ/ evaṃ ca tatra pravṛttiṃ pratyanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ
viśiṣṭajñānasya kāraṇatāyāṃ lāghavāt sāmānyataḥ pravṛttitvāvacchinnaṃ
prati viśiṣṭajñānatvena anugatakāryakāraṇabhāvasyaiva kalpanīyatayā
visaṃvādipravṛtterapi tatkāryatāvacchedakāvalīḍhatayā tatpūrvaṃ
viśiṣṭajñānasya kalpanīyatvāt anyathākhyātirnirābādhaiveti samādhatte
- satyarajateti/ rajatatvaprakārakajñānasyeti/
tādṛśajñānatvāvacchinnasyetyarthaḥ/ pravṛttijanakatayā -
pravṛttitvāvacchinnajanakatayā/ viśiṣṭajñānasyaiva -
purovartiviśeṣyakeṣṭatāvacchedakaprakārakajñānasyaiva/ etena
iṣṭabhedāgrahasya vyavacchedaḥ/ kalpanāt - anumānāt/ tatprayogastu
- 'iyam purovartiviśeṣyakeṣṭatāvacchedakaprakārakajñānajanyā,
pravṛttitvāt, rajatasthalīyapravṛttivat' iti/ syādetat - pratyakṣe
sannikarṣasya kāraṇatayā rajatatvāṃśe tadabhāvena kathaṃ śuktau 'idam
rajatam' iti pratyakṣamiti cet,
children.translated_text: Having rejected the teacher's view, he establishes <s>anyathākhyāti</s> beginning with 'nanu' etc. "Due to veridicality (<s>yathārthatva</s>)" — meaning: due to validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>). "There is simply no non-veridical cognition" — the meaning is that <s>ayathārthatva</s> (non-veridicality), which has the nature of having as qualificand what lacks that [property] and having that as qualifier, does not occur in cognition. Therefore there is no contradiction through establishment and non-establishment. The well-knownness of non-veridicality, however, should be understood in the context of desire and so forth. "<s>Anyathākhyāti</s>" — the purport is that without accepting this, since the cognition having the object before one as qualificand and the desired-ness-delimiting property such as silver-ness as qualifier would generate activity common to both concordant and discordant cases, there would be no activity at all in such cases. "Memory of silver (<s>rajatasmṛti</s>)" etc. — supply 'from the two that are established and necessarily prior.' "Due to possibility (<s>sambhavāt</s>)" — and thus, since there is simply no causal role in the form of qualified-cognition-hood for activity, the postulation of <s>anyathākhyāti</s> in accordance with that is not possible. This is the purport. Now, if wherever there is the sublating cognition 'this is not silver,' there too activity would follow — to this he says: "of the presented" etc. By this much, the dependence on the cause in the form of memory is made clear. "Of the non-apprehension of the difference from the desired alone" — meaning: of the absence alone of the apprehension of difference in the form of the desired, such as silver-ness. By the word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>), qualified cognition is excluded from being the cause of activity. "Everywhere" — meaning: both in silver and in nacre. In the case of real silver, causal role for activity must be accepted only in the form of qualified-cognition-hood; otherwise there would be the undesirable consequence of causal status delimited by the heavier property of non-apprehension of the difference between the desired, in the case of cognition of property and property-bearer. And thus, since by positive and negative concomitance the causal role of qualified cognition for activity there is established by parsimony, since what is to be postulated is only the universal cause-effect relation delimited by qualified-cognition-hood for activity-hood in general (common to concordant and discordant cases), and since discordant activity too, being subsumed under that effect-delimiting property, requires the postulation of a qualified cognition prior to it — he resolves that <s>anyathākhyāti</s> is entirely unobstructed — with "in the case of real silver" etc. "Of the cognition having silver-ness as qualifier" — the meaning is: delimited by such-cognition-hood. "In generating activity (<s>pravṛttijanakatayā</s>)" — meaning: in generating what is delimited by activity-hood. "Of the qualified cognition alone" — meaning: of the cognition alone having the object before one as qualificand and the desired-ness-delimiting property as qualifier. By this, the non-apprehension of the desired difference is excluded. "Due to postulation (<s>kalpanāt</s>)" — meaning: by inference. The formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>) for this is: 'This is produced by a cognition having the desired-ness-delimiting property as qualifier and the object before one as qualificand, because it has activity-hood, like the activity in the case of real silver.' If it be objected — since in perception, sense-contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>) is the cause, and since in the silver-ness aspect there is its absence, how can 'this is silver' in the case of nacre be perceptual?

children.text:
maivam/
alaukikasannikarṣasyāpi pratyakṣajanakatāyā vyavasthāpitatvena
jñānalakṣaṇapratyāsattereva prakṛte sambhavāt/
children.translated_text: This is not so. Since even non-ordinary sense-contact (<s>alaukikasannikarṣa</s>) has been established as capable of generating perception, in the present case it is possible through <s>jñānalakṣaṇapratyāsatti</s> (proximity characterized by cognition) alone.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
gurumatamiti/
sarvāṇi jñānāni tadvati tatprakārakatvarūpapramātvavanti/ tadabhāvavati
children.translated_text: "The teacher's view" — all cognitions possess validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) in the form of having that as qualifier in what possesses that [property]. What lacks that [property]

children.text:
tatprakārakatvarūpāpramātvavat kimapi jānaṃ na bhavatīti
prābhākaramatamityarthaḥ/ nanu dīpikāyām ayathārthajñānameva nāstīti
gurumatānuvādo na yuktaḥ/ ayathārthajñānasya prasaddhitve taninaṣedho na
yuktaḥ/ ayathārthajñānasyāprasiddhatve ca pratiyogyaprasiddhyā tanniṣedho
na yukta iti siddhyasiddhibhyāṃ vyāghātādityata āha -
tadabhāvavaditi/ ayathārthatvaṃ pakṣaḥ, jñānavṛttitvābhāvaḥ sādhyaḥ,
jñānatvavyāpakapramātvaviruddhatvāt iti hetuḥ/ tadanaṅgīkāra
iti/ tadabhāvavadviśeṣyakatatprakārakajñānarūpānyathākhyātyanaṅgīkāra
ityarthaḥ/ purovartiviśeṣyaketi/ purovartiviśeṣyakapravṛttiṃ prati
purovartiviśeṣyakeṣṭatāvacchedakaprakārakajñānaṃ hetuḥ/ rajatārthinaḥ
puruṣasya purovartini idaṅkārāspade vastuni
iṣṭatāvacchedakarajatatvajñāne vinā pravṛtteranudayāt/ tathā ca
śuktiviśeṣyakarajatatvaprakārakajñānātmakānyathākhyātimantareṇa
pravṛttirna ghaṭate/ ataḥ pravṛttyanusāreṇa taddhetubhūtā
anyathākhyātiraṅgīkāryeti śaṅkiturāśayaḥ/ saṃvādipravṛttiḥ
saphalapravṛttiḥ/ visaṃvādipravṛttiḥ/ viphalapravṛttiḥ/
children.translated_text: — no cognition whatsoever possesses invalidity (<s>aprāmāṇya</s>) in the form of having that as qualifier — this is the <s>Prābhākara</s> view, is the meaning. Objection: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, the restatement of the teacher's view as 'there is simply no non-veridical cognition' is not proper. If non-veridical cognition is well-established, its denial is not proper. And if non-veridical cognition is not well-established, then due to the counter-positive being not well-established, its denial is not proper — thus there would be a contradiction through establishment and non-establishment. To this he says: "what lacks that" etc. Non-veridicality (<s>ayathārthatva</s>) is the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>); the absence of occurrence in cognition is the property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>); and the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is: because it is contradictory to validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) which pervades cognition-hood. "Without accepting that" — the meaning is: without accepting <s>anyathākhyāti</s> in the form of cognition having what lacks that as qualificand and that as qualifier. "Having the object before one as qualificand" — the cognition having the desired-ness-delimiting property such as silver-ness as qualifier and the object before one as qualificand is the reason for activity directed at the object before one. Because without the cognition of silver-ness, which is the delimiter of the desired-ness, in the object before one that is the locus of the 'this'-apprehension, activity does not arise for a person desiring silver. And thus, without <s>anyathākhyāti</s> in the form of cognition having nacre as qualificand and silver-ness as qualifier, activity is not possible. Therefore, in accordance with observed activity, the <s>anyathākhyāti</s> that is its cause must be accepted — this is the intent of the objector. Concordant activity (<s>saṃvādipravṛtti</s>) is successful activity. Discordant activity (<s>visaṃvādipravṛtti</s>) is fruitless activity.

children.text:
nanu viśiṣṭajñānaṃ
pravṛttikāraṇaṃ vā jñānadvayaṃ tatkāraṇaṃ vetyatra vinigamanāvirahāt
'rajatasmṛtipurovartijñānābhyāmeva pravṛttisambhavāt'
ityuktamityatrāha - kḷptaniyatapūrvavartibhyāmityādiriti/
viśiṣṭajñānasya pravṛttikāraṇatvaṃ vadatā naiyāyikenāpi
viśiṣṭajñānātpūrvaṃ idamityākārakaṃ purovartiviṣayakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ
rajatasmaraṇaṃ ceti jñānadvayaṃ bhavatītyaṅgīkriyate/
children.translated_text: Objection: Whether qualified cognition is the cause of activity or the pair of cognitions is its cause — since there is no means to decide between these, the statement 'activity is possible from the memory of silver and the cognition of the object before one alone' — regarding this he says: "from the two that are established and necessarily prior" etc. Even the <s>Naiyāyika</s> who maintains that qualified cognition is the cause of activity accepts that prior to the qualified cognition there exists a pair of cognitions, namely, the perception directed at the object before one in the form 'this' and the memory of silver.

children.text:
tathā ca
kḷptaniyatapūrvavartibhyāṃ idañjñānarajatasmaraṇābhyāmeva pravṛtteḥ
children.translated_text: And thus, since activity is possible from the two that are established and necessarily prior, namely the 'this'-cognition and the memory of silver alone,

children.text:
sambhave
viśiṣṭajñānamanāvaśyakamiti bhāvaḥ/ viśiṣṭajñānatveneti/
purovartiviśeṣyakarajatatvādiprakārakajñānatvenetyarthaḥ/
nanvevamiti/ rajatasmṛtipurovartijñāne eva pravṛttikāraṇe;
viśiṣṭajñānaṃ tu na pravṛttikāraṇamityaṅgīkāra ityarthaḥ/ pravṛttiḥ
syāditi/ rajatasmṛtipurovartijñānayoḥ sattvāditi bhāvaḥ/
rajatādirūpeti/ rajatādirūpaṃ yat iṣṭaṃ
tatpratiyogikabhedajñānābhāvasyetyarthaḥ/ tathā ca
purovartiviśeṣyakarajatādirūpeṣṭapratiyogikabhedaprakārakajñānābhāvav i
- śiṣṭe purovartijñānarajatasmaraṇe purovartini
rajatārthipravṛttiheturiti 'nedam rajatam' iti bādhajñānakāle na
pravṛttyāpattiriti bhāvaḥ/ idamiti
dharmijñāna-rajatatvajñānabhedāgrahāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ kāraṇatvāpekṣayā
viśiṣṭajñānasyaikasya kāraṇatve lāghavamiti mūle 'bhipretam/ tadāha -
satyarajatasthala ityādinā/ yadyapi dharmadharmijñānayoḥ kāraṇatvaṃ
viśiṣṭajñānakāraṇatāvādyapi
children.translated_text: the qualified cognition is unnecessary — this is the purport. "In the form of qualified-cognition-hood" — the meaning is: in the form of cognition having silver-ness and the like as qualifier and the object before one as qualificand. "Now if so" — the meaning is: accepting that the memory of silver and the cognition of the object before one alone are the causes of activity, while qualified cognition is not the cause of activity. "Activity would follow" — the purport is: because the memory of silver and the cognition of the object before one are both present. "In the form of the desired, such as silver-ness" — the meaning is: of the absence of cognition of difference whose counter-positive is the desired in the form of silver-ness and the like. And thus, when the pair consisting of the cognition of the object before one having silver-ness and the like as the desired-ness-delimiting property as qualifier and the cognition of the object before one are accompanied by the absence of cognition of difference whose counter-positive is the desired in the form of silver-ness and the like directed at the object before one, they are the cause of the activity of one desiring silver directed at the object before one — hence there is no undesirable consequence of activity at the time of the sublating cognition 'this is not silver.' This is the purport. "This" refers to the parsimony in taking only one thing, namely qualified cognition, as the cause, as opposed to taking three things as causes — the cognition of the property-bearer, the cognition of silver-ness, and the non-apprehension of difference. This is what is intended in the root text. He explains this with "in the case of real silver" etc. Although the proponent of qualified-cognition causation also accepts the causal role of the cognition of the property and the property-bearer,

children.translated_text: nevertheless, the <s>Prābhākara</s> maintains that the causal role for preventing activity at the time of the sublating cognition 'this is not silver' is delimited by the absence of apprehension of the desired difference, while the <s>Naiyāyika</s> maintains that the causal role is delimited by qualified-cognition-hood. In this matter, the parsimony of the causal delimitor belongs to the <s>Naiyāyika</s> alone — this is the purport. "Delimited by activity-hood in general" — the meaning is: delimited by activity-hood common to concordant and discordant activities. "Being subsumed under the effect-delimiting property" — the meaning is: by virtue of being the locus of activity-hood, which is the effect-delimiting property of that qualified cognition. "Prior to that" — the meaning is: prior to the discordant activity. "Due to the absence of that in the silver-ness aspect" — the meaning is: due to the absence of sense-contact, namely the absence of the inherence of the potency conjoined with the eye. "Characterized by cognition (<s>jñānalakṣaṇa</s>)" — the purport is that the cognition having silver-ness as qualifier in the form of memory of silver is itself the sense-contact that occasions the appearance of silver-ness.

children.text: ayathārthānubhavanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Description of non-veridical experience (<s>ayathārthānubhava</s>).

children.text: AnTs_64 ayathārthānubhavas trividhaḥ saṃśayaviparyayatarkabhedāt / ekasmin dharmini viruddhanānādharmavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhi jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ / yathā sthāṇur vā purṣo veti / mithyājñānaṃ viparyayaḥ / yathā śuktāv idaṃ rajatam iti / vyāpyāropeṇa vyāpakāropas tarkaḥ yathā yadi vahnir na syāt tarhi dhūmo'pi na syād iti //
children.translated_text: <s>AnTs</s>_64: Non-veridical experience (<s>ayathārthānubhava</s>) is threefold, due to the distinction of doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), and hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>). Cognition that apprehends the qualification by contradictory and manifold properties in a single property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>). For example: 'Is it a post or a person?' False cognition is error (<s>viparyaya</s>). For example: 'This is silver' in the case of nacre. The attribution of the pervader through the attribution of the pervaded is hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>). For example: 'If fire were not present, then smoke too would not be present.'

children.translated_text: Non-veridical experience (<s>ayathārthānubhava</s>) is threefold — due to the distinction of doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), and hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>). Cognition that apprehends the qualification by contradictory and manifold properties in a single property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>). For example: 'Is it a post or a person?' False cognition is error (<s>viparyaya</s>). For example: 'This is silver' in the case of nacre. The attribution of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) through the attribution of the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) is hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>). For example: 'If fire were not present, then smoke too would not be present.'

children.text:
ayathārthānubhāvaṃ vibhajate - ayathārtha
iti/ svapnasya mānasaviparyayarūpatvāt na traividhyavirodhaḥ/
saṃśayalakṣaṇamāha - eketi/ ghaṭapaṭāviti
samūhālambane 'tivyāptivāraṇāya eketi/ 'ghaṭaḥ dravyam'
ityādāvativyāptivāraṇāya viruddheti/ 'ghaṭatvaviruddhapaṭatvavān'
ityatra ativyāpitavāraṇāya nāneti/ viparyayalakṣaṇamāha - mithyeti/
tadabhāvavati tatprakārakanirṇaya ityarthaḥ/ tarkaṃ lakṣayati - vyāpyeti/
yadyapi tarkaḥ viparyaye 'ntarbhavati, tathāpi pramāṇānugrāhakatvāt
bhedena saṅkīrtanam/
children.translated_text: He classifies non-veridical experience — with "<s>ayathārtha</s>" etc. Since dreams have the nature of mental error (<s>mānasaviparyaya</s>), there is no contradiction with the threefold classification. He states the definition of doubt — with "eka" etc. To prevent over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) to collective apprehension as in 'a pot and a cloth,' [he says] "in a single" (<s>eka</s>). To prevent over-extension to cases like 'a pot is a substance,' [he says] "contradictory" (<s>viruddha</s>). To prevent over-extension to cases like 'possessing cloth-ness contradictory to pot-ness,' [he says] "manifold" (<s>nānā</s>). He states the definition of error — with "<s>mithyā</s>" etc. The meaning is: a determination having that as qualifier in what lacks that. He defines hypothetical reasoning — with "<s>vyāpya</s>" etc. Although <s>tarka</s> is included within error (<s>viparyaya</s>), it is mentioned separately because it assists the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

ca bādhakālīnecchājanyatvam/ tṛtīyāyāḥ janyatvamarthaḥ/ tasya
vyāpakārope 'nvayaḥ/ vyāpyasyāropaḥ vyāpyāropaḥ/ ṣaṣṭhyāḥ
viṣayatvamarthaḥ/ tathā ca bādhakālīnecchājanyavyāpyaviṣayakabhramajanyaḥ
bādhakālīnecchājanyavyāpakaviṣayako bhramastarka iti phalati/ yadi
parvato vahnyabhāvavān syāt tarhi dhūmābhāvavān syāt
ityākārakastarkaḥ/ tatra vyāpyaḥ vahnyabhāvaḥ tadviṣayakaḥ āropaḥ
parvato vahnyamāniti bādhakālīnayā icchayā janyaḥ bhramaḥ yadi
parvato vahnya bhāvavān syāt ityākārakaḥ, tajjanyaḥ vyāpakasya
dhūmābhāvasya āropaḥ tarhi dhūtābhāvavān syādityākārakaḥ/ sa eva
tarkaḥ/ vyāpyaviṣayakabhrame āhāryatvaviśeṣaṇādāne śākhāyāṃ
puruṣatvavyāpyakarabhramāt yatra ayaṃ puruṣa ityāhāryāropaḥ
tatrātivyāptiḥ tadvāraṇāya āhāryatvaviśeṣaṇam/ śākhāyāṃ karabhramaḥ na
āhārya iti nātivyāptiḥ/ vyāpakārope āhāryatvaviśeṣaṇādāne
āhāryāt rajatatvavyāpyavat idamiti jñānāt jāyamāne idaṃ
rajataṃ ityākārake anāhāryabhrame 'tivyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya tat/
tadāha - āhāryavyāpyavattetyādi/ nāyaṃ puruṣa iti niścayasatva
iti/ 'ayaṃ puruṣa' iti bhramasya āhāryatvasampādanāyaitaduktm/
rajatatvavyāpyavattājñānasya āhāryatvasampādanāya
rajatatvavyāpyābhāvavattāgrahakāle iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Tarka</s> (suppositional reasoning) is the superimposition of the pervader by means of the superimposition of the pervaded. The word 'superimposition' (<s>āropa</s>) means <s>āhāryabhrama</s> (deliberately entertained error). <s>Āhāryatva</s> (the character of being deliberately entertained) is being produced by a desire occurring at the time of sublation. The instrumental case [in the compound] has the meaning of 'being produced by.' Its syntactic connection is with the superimposition of the pervader. The superimposition of the pervaded is the superimposition whose object is the pervaded; the genitive has the meaning of objecthood. Thus the result is: <s>tarka</s> is a deliberately entertained error whose object is the pervader, produced by a deliberately entertained error whose object is the pervaded. [For example,] the <s>tarka</s> of the form: 'if the mountain were to possess the absence of fire, then it would possess the absence of smoke.' There, the pervaded is the absence of fire; the superimposition having that as its object is the error produced by a desire occurring at the time of sublation, of the form 'if the mountain were to possess the absence of fire'; produced by that is the superimposition of the pervader, namely the absence of smoke, of the form 'then it would possess the absence of smoke.' That itself is <s>tarka</s>. If the qualification of being deliberately entertained is included in the error whose object is the pervaded, then where from the error of seeing a hand on a branch [as a person] — which is pervaded by person-hood — the deliberately entertained superimposition 'this is a person' [arises], there would be over-extension; to prevent that, the qualification of being deliberately entertained [is added]. Since the error of [seeing] a hand on a branch is not deliberately entertained, there is no over-extension. If the qualification of being deliberately entertained is not included in the superimposition of the pervader, then in the non-deliberately-entertained error of the form 'this is silver' arising from the deliberately entertained cognition 'this possesses what is pervaded by silver-hood,' there would be over-extension; to prevent that, [the qualification is added]. He states this — 'possessing what is pervaded by the deliberately entertained' and so forth. 'Since the ascertainment "this is not a person" exists': this is said to establish the deliberately entertained character of the error 'this is a person.' 'At the time of non-apprehension of possessing the absence of what is pervaded by silver-hood': this is to establish the deliberately entertained character of the cognition of possessing what is pervaded by silver-hood.

children.text:
āpādyavyatirekaniścaya
iti/ āpādyaḥ prasañjanīyaḥ, dhūmābhāvaḥ tadvyatirekaḥ
dhūmābhāvābhāvaḥ dhūmarūpaḥ tanniścayaḥ, āpādyasya dhūmābhāvasya āpādakasya
vahnyabhāvasya ca yā vyāptiḥ tanniścayaśca tarke kāraṇamityarthaḥ/
kathamayathārthasya traividhyakathanamiti/ saṃśayo viparyayaśceti
dvaividhyakathanasyaiva yuktatvādityarthaḥ/ pratibandhakavighaṭanadvāreti/
pratibandhakībhūtavyabhicāraśaṅkānivartanadvāretyarthaḥ/
tarkātiriktaviparyayāṇāṃ tu nāsti pramāṇānugrāhakatvam, tarkasya tu
tadastīti vailakṣaṇyasūcanāya viparyayayāntarbhūtasyāpi tarkasya
pṛthaṅnirdeśa ityarthaḥ/ tathā ca viparyaye tarkatvākāraḥ
pramāṇānugrāhakatāvacchedakaḥ, viparyayatvaṃ tu na tatheti
viśeṣajñāpanāya viparyayatvatarkatvābhyāṃ vibhāga iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The ascertainment of the absence of the consequent (<s>āpādya</s>)': the <s>āpādya</s> is what is to be deduced, namely the absence of smoke; its absence (<s>vyatireka</s>) is the absence of the absence of smoke, which is of the nature of smoke; the ascertainment of that, together with the ascertainment of the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) between the consequent (the absence of smoke) and the ground (the absence of fire) — these are the causes of <s>tarka</s>. The meaning is thus. 'How can there be a threefold classification of what is not veridical?': the meaning is that only a twofold classification — doubt and error — would be appropriate. 'Through the removal of the obstruction': the meaning is through the removal of the doubt regarding <s>vyabhicāra</s> (deviation) that has become an obstruction. For errors other than <s>tarka</s>, there is no capacity to assist <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), but <s>tarka</s> does have that capacity — to indicate this distinction, <s>tarka</s>, though included within error, is separately mentioned. Thus, in the case of error, the form of being <s>tarka</s> is the delimitor of the capacity to assist <s>pramāṇa</s>, while the property of being an error is not such — to convey this distinction, the division is made by the properties of error-hood and <s>tarka</s>-hood. The purport is thus.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: smṛtinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>smṛti</s> (memory)

children.text: AnTs_65 smṛtir api dvividhā / yathārthāyathārthā ca pramājanyā yathārthā / apramājanyāyathārthā //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 65]: <s>Smṛti</s> (memory) also is of two kinds — veridical and non-veridical. That which is produced by valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) is veridical. That which is produced by invalid cognition is non-veridical.

children.text:
smṛtirapi dbividhā - yathārthā ayathārthā
ceti/ pramājanayā yathārthā/ apramājanyā ayathārthā/
children.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> (memory) also is of two kinds — veridical and non-veridical. That produced by valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) is veridical. That produced by invalid cognition is non-veridical.

children.text: sukhādinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) and the rest

children.text: AnTs_66 sarveśām anukūlatayā vedanīyaṃ sukham //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 66]: <s>Sukha</s> (pleasure) is that which is experienced by all as agreeable.

children.text: AnTs_67 sarveśāṃ pratikūlatayā vedanīyaṃ duḥkham //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 67]: <s>Duḥkha</s> (pain) is that which is experienced by all as disagreeable.

children.text: AnTs_68 icchā kāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 68]: <s>Icchā</s> (desire) is <s>kāma</s> (want).

children.text: AnTs_69 krodho dveṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 69]: <s>Krodha</s> (anger) is <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion).

children.text: AnTs_70 kṛtiḥ prayatnaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 70]: <s>Kṛti</s> (volition) is <s>prayatna</s> (effort).

children.text: AnTs_71 vihitakarmajanyo dharmaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 71]: <s>Dharma</s> (merit) is produced by enjoined action.

children.text: AnTs_72 niṣiddhakarmajanyas tv adharmaḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 72]: <s>Adharma</s> (demerit), however, is produced by prohibited action.

children.text: AnTs_73 buddhyādayo'ṣṭāv ātmamātraviśeṣaguṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 73]: <s>Buddhi</s> (cognition) and the other eight are <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) specific to the <s>ātman</s> (self) alone.

children.text: AnTs_74 buddhīcchāprayatnā dvividhāḥ / nityā anityāś ca / nityā īśvarasya / anityā jīvasya //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 74]: <s>Buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>icchā</s> (desire), and <s>prayatna</s> (effort) are of two kinds — eternal and non-eternal. The eternal ones belong to <s>Īśvara</s> (God). The non-eternal ones belong to the <s>jīva</s> (individual self).

children.text:
sarveṣāṃ
anukūlatayā vedanīyaṃ sukham/ pratikūlatayā vedanīyaṃ duḥkham/
icchā kāmaḥ/ krodho dveṣaḥ/ kṛtiḥ prayatnaḥ/ vihitakarmajanyo dharmaḥ/
niṣiddhakarmajanyo 'dharmaḥ/ buddhyādayaḥ aṣṭau ātmamātraviśeṣaguṇāḥ/
buddhīcchāprayatnā
children.translated_text: <s>Sukha</s> (pleasure) is that which is experienced by all as agreeable. <s>Duḥkha</s> (pain) is that which is experienced as disagreeable. <s>Icchā</s> (desire) is <s>kāma</s> (want). <s>Krodha</s> (anger) is <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion). <s>Kṛti</s> (volition) is <s>prayatna</s> (effort). <s>Dharma</s> (merit) is produced by enjoined action. <s>Adharma</s> (demerit) is produced by prohibited action. <s>Buddhi</s> (cognition) and the other eight are qualities specific to the <s>ātman</s> (self) alone. <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>icchā</s>, and <s>prayatna</s> are

children.text:
nityā anityaśca/
nityā īśvarasya/ anityā jīvasya/
children.translated_text: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal ones belong to <s>Īśvara</s> (God). The non-eternal ones belong to the <s>jīva</s> (individual self).

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
smṛtiṃ vibhajate -
smṛtiriti/ sukhaṃ lakṣayati - sarveṣāmiti/ 'sukhī aham'
ityādyanuvyasāyagamyaṃ sukhatvādikameva lakṣaṇam/ yathāśrutaṃ tu
svarūpakathanamiti draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: He classifies <s>smṛti</s> (memory) — 'memory.' He defines <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) — 'of all.' The definition is properly pleasure-hood and the like, which are known through subsequent reflective awareness (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) of the form 'I am happy.' But what is stated literally [in the root text] should be regarded as a description of the essential nature.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanu 'sarveṣāṃ
anukūlatayā vedanīyam' ityādi mūlaṃ sukhādilakṣaṇaparaṃ na
sambhavati, padadravnayopabhogādijanyasakhe sādhūnāṃ dveṣadarśanāt
avyāpterityāśaṅkāyāṃ 'sukhyaham' ityādipratyakṣasiddhaṃ
sukhatvādikameva lakṣaṇamityāha - sukhī ahamityādyanuvyavasāyeti/
sukhatvādītyādinā dukhatvaparigrahaḥ/ yathāśrutaṃ tviti/
sarveṣāmanukūlatayā ityādikamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: the root text 'that which is experienced by all as agreeable' and so forth cannot be intended as a definition of pleasure and the rest, because there would be under-extension, since aversion is observed in virtuous people (<s>sādhus</s>) toward pleasure born from the enjoyment of others' wealth and the like. In response to this doubt, he says — 'through the subsequent reflective awareness "I am happy" and so forth': the definition is properly pleasure-hood and the like, which are established through such perceptual reflective awareness. By the word 'and the like' after 'pleasure-hood,' pain-hood is also included. 'What is stated literally, however': the meaning is 'that which is experienced by all as agreeable' and so forth [is merely a description of the nature].

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
sarveṣāṃ
anukūlatayā vedanīyaṃ sukham iti mūlāt
anukūlatvaprakārakajñānaviṣayatvaṃ sukhasya lakṣaṇamiti pratīyate/ tathā
sati parakīyadravyopabhogajanye sukhe sādhūnāṃ dveṣadarśanena
sādhuvṛttipratikūlatvaprakārakajñānaviṣayatvasyaiva
children.translated_text: From the root text 'that which is experienced by all as agreeable is pleasure,' it appears that being the object of a cognition qualified by agreeableness is the definition of pleasure. If so, since aversion is observed in virtuous people toward pleasure born from the enjoyment of another's wealth, the property of being the object of a cognition qualified by being disagreeable to virtuous conduct

children.text:
tatra sattvena sarveṣāṃ
anukūlatayā vedanīyatvasya tādṛśasukhe 'bhāvenāvyāptyāpatteḥ idaṃ
lakṣaṇaṃ ayuktamiti śaṅkānivāraṇārthaḥ sukhyahamityādidīpikāgrantha
ityāha - nanu sarveṣāmityādinā/
children.translated_text: is present there; hence the property of being experienced by all as agreeable would be absent in such pleasure, and the definition would suffer from under-extension. To remove this doubt, the <s>Dīpikā</s> passage beginning with 'through the subsequent reflective awareness "I am happy"' is stated. He explains this — 'objection: of all' and so forth.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: saṃskāranirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>saṃskāra</s> (dispositional impression)

children.text: AnTs_75 saṃskāras trividhaḥ / vego bhāvanā sthitisthāpakaś ceti / vegaḥ pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayamanovṛttiḥ / anubhavajanyā smṛtihetur bhāvanātmamātravṛttiḥ / anyathā kṛtasya punas tadavasthāpādakaḥ sthitisthāpakaḥ kaṭādipṛthivīvṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: [<s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 75]: <s>Saṃskāra</s> (dispositional impression) is of three kinds: <s>vega</s> (velocity), <s>bhāvanā</s> (reproductive impression), and <s>sthitisthāpaka</s> (elasticity). <s>Vega</s> is an occurrence in earth, water, fire, air, and <s>manas</s> (mind). <s>Bhāvanā</s> is that which is produced by experience and is the cause of <s>smṛti</s> (memory); it occurs only in the <s>ātman</s> (self). <s>Sthitisthāpaka</s> (elasticity) is that which restores to its original state something that has been displaced; it occurs only in earth-substances such as mats.

children.text:
saṃskāraḥ trividhaḥ -
vegaḥ bhāvanā sthitasthāpakaśceti/ vegaḥ
pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayamanovṛttiḥ/ anubhavajanyā smṛtihetuḥ bhāvanā/
ātmamātravṛttiḥ/ anyathā kṛtasya (sthitasya) punaḥ tādavasthyāpādakaḥ
sthitasthāpakaḥ/ kaṭādipṛthivīmātravṛttiḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃskāra</s> (dispositional impression) is of three kinds — <s>vega</s> (velocity), <s>bhāvanā</s> (reproductive impression), and <s>sthitisthāpaka</s> (elasticity). <s>Vega</s> is an occurrence in earth, water, fire, air, and <s>manas</s> (mind). <s>Bhāvanā</s> is that which is produced by experience and is the cause of <s>smṛti</s> (memory). It occurs only in the <s>ātman</s> (self). <s>Sthitisthāpaka</s> (elasticity) is that which restores to its original state something that has been made otherwise (displaced). It occurs only in earth-substances such as mats.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
saṃskāraṃ vibhajate
- saṃskāra iti/ saṃskāratvajātimān saṃskāra/ vegasyāśrayamāha -
vega iti/ vegatvajātimān vegaḥ/ bhāvanāṃ lakṣayati - anubhaveti/
anubhavadhvaṃse 'tivyāptivāraṇāya smṛtīti/
ātmādāvativyāptivāraṇāya anubhaveti/ smṛterapi saṃskārajanakatvaṃ
navīnairuktam/ sthitasthāpakaṃ lakṣayati - anyatheti/ saṅkhyādayaḥ aṣṭau
naimittikadravatvavegasthitasthāpakāḥ sāmānyaguṇāḥ/
children.translated_text: He classifies <s>saṃskāra</s> — 'dispositional impression.' <s>Saṃskāra</s> is that which possesses the universal <s>saṃskāratva</s> (impression-hood). He states the substrate of <s>vega</s> (velocity) — 'velocity.' <s>Vega</s> is that which possesses the universal <s>vegatva</s> (velocity-hood). He defines <s>bhāvanā</s> (reproductive impression) — 'by experience.' To prevent over-extension to the destruction of experience, [the qualification] 'cause of memory' [is added]. To prevent over-extension to the self and the like, [the qualification] 'produced by experience' [is added]. The moderns state that memory too has the capacity to produce <s>saṃskāra</s>. He defines <s>sthitisthāpaka</s> (elasticity) — 'otherwise.' The eight [qualities] beginning with number — including occasional fluidity, velocity, and elasticity — are general qualities.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
anubhavetīti/
smṛtiṃ saṃskāraṃ prati ca anubhavatvenaiva kāraṇatvaṃ vadatāṃ prācāṃ
ayamabhiprāyaḥ - tattadviṣayakasmṛtiṃ prati tattadviṣayakasaṃskāraṃ prati ca
tattadviṣayakānubhavatvenaiva hetutā na tu tattadbiṣayakajñānatvena,
anubhavatvasyāpi jātitvena jñānatvāpekṣayā gauravāsaṃbhavāt/ na ca
vinigamanāviraha iti śaṅkyam, vyāpyadharmapuraskāreṇa
kāraṇatvasambhave vyāpakadharmasyānyathāsiddhinirūpakatvāditi/
children.translated_text: 'By experience': the view of the ancients (<s>prācas</s>), who maintain that causality toward memory and toward <s>saṃskāra</s> operates precisely through the property of being experience of the respective objects, is as follows — the causality toward memory of the respective objects and toward <s>saṃskāra</s> of the respective objects operates precisely through being experience of the respective objects, not through being cognition of the respective objects, because experience-hood too, being a universal, involves no greater complexity than cognition-hood. Nor should it be objected that there is no basis for determination [between the two], because when causality is possible by foregrounding a pervaded property, the pervading property has the status of being otherwise-established.

children.text:
navīnāḥ punaḥ -
anubhavānāṃ tattadviṣayakasmṛtiṃ tādṛśasaṃskāraṃ prati ca
tattadviṣayakajñānatvenaiva hetutā, na tu anubhavatvena, saṃskārasya
phalanāśyatayā prathamasmaraṇenaiva anubhavajanyasaṃskārasya nāśena
sakṛtadanubhūtasya smaraṇottaraṃ asmaraṇaprasaṅgāt/ na ca
svajanyasmaraṇasya saṃskāranāśakatve smṛtisādhāraṇena jñānatvena
hetutve 'pi ghaṭapaṭādirūpanānāviṣayāvagāhinā anubhavena janitasya
tāvadviṣayakasaṃskārasya ghaṭādyekaikagocarasmaraṇenāpi vināśāt
taduttaraṃ paṭādismaraṇānupapattiḥ, tattadviṣayakasaṃskārābhāvāt/
smṛtijanyapaṭādigocarasaṃskārasya ca bhinnarviṣayakatayā
paṭādismārakatvāyogāt/ ataḥ svajanyacaramasmṛterevānāyatyā
tattadvyaktitvena tattatsaṃskāranāśakatāyā aṅgīkartavyatayā
children.translated_text: The moderns (<s>navīnas</s>), however, [hold that]: the causality of experiences toward memory of the respective objects and toward such <s>saṃskāra</s> operates precisely through the property of being cognition of the respective objects, not through being experience, because — since <s>saṃskāra</s> is destroyed by its fruit — the <s>saṃskāra</s> produced by experience would be destroyed by the first recollection, and there would be the absurd consequence that what has been experienced once could not be remembered after the [first] recollection. Nor should one say that even if memory has the capacity to destroy <s>saṃskāra</s>, and even if causality operates through the property of cognition-hood common to memory too, still — since a <s>saṃskāra</s> produced by an experience apprehending diverse objects such as a pot, a cloth, and so forth would also be destroyed by a recollection directed at even one of them such as a pot — recollection of cloth and the rest after that would be impossible, due to the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> of the respective objects. And a <s>saṃskāra</s> concerning cloth and the rest produced by memory, being of a different object-scope, would be incapable of generating recollection of cloth and the rest. Therefore, since one must accept that only the final recollection of the respective particular destroys the respective <s>saṃskāra</s> prospectively,

children.text:
anubhavatvena
janakatāyāmapi na doṣa iti vācyam/, anyūnaviṣayakasyaiva phalasya
nāśakatvāṅgīkāreṇa adoṣāt/ jāyate ca punaḥ punaḥ smaraṇāt
dṛḍhataraḥ saṃskāraḥ/ dārḍhyaṃ ca saṃskāragataḥ jātiviśeṣaḥ jhaṭiti
smṛtyutpādaprayojakaḥ/ na ca daivavaśasampannāt jhaṭiti
udbodhakasamavadhānādeva jhaṭiti smṛtiniyamopapattau na

children.translated_text: even with causality through experience-hood there is no defect — [this] should not be said, because there is no defect when one accepts that only a fruit whose object-scope is no less [than the cause's] has the power to destroy. Moreover, from repeated recollection, an increasingly firm <s>saṃskāra</s> is produced. And firmness is a particular universal residing in <s>saṃskāra</s>, which serves to produce swift recollection. Nor should one say that — since swift recollection is explained by the mere co-presence of a swift stimulus obtained through fortune, the particular universal residing in <s>saṃskāra</s> is not established as having that purpose — because, upon rejecting the superiority of <s>saṃskāra</s>, the very practice of study and repetition in scriptural learning and the like would have no basis. Furthermore, abandoning an ascertained non-deviating form and postulating causality through a form in which deviation is observed is [logically inappropriate]. Therefore, causality of experience-hood toward memory and <s>saṃskāra</s> is not impossible — thus they maintain. He presents their view — 'of memory also.' By the word 'also,' experience is included. According to this view, in the definition, instead of 'produced by experience,' one should insert 'produced by cognition.'

children.translated_text: 'By foregrounding a pervaded property': the pervaded property is experience-hood; the pervading property is cognition-hood. 'Because of having the status of being otherwise-established': the purport is that a staff does not have causality toward a pot in its aspect of being a substance. 'Because <s>saṃskāra</s> is destroyed by its fruit': the meaning is that it is destroyed by the fruit in the form of recollection. Accordingly, if causality toward <s>saṃskāra</s> operates through experience-hood, then where a recollection of a pot has arisen from a <s>saṃskāra</s> produced by an experience of a pot, there at a later time a recollection of the pot would not occur, because the pot-<s>saṃskāra</s> has been destroyed by the initial pot-recollection. Nor can one say that from the pot-recollection a <s>saṃskāra</s> arises again, and from that a further pot-recollection [follows], because — on the view that causality operates through experience-hood — since the pot-recollection lacks experience-hood, which is the delimitor of causality toward <s>saṃskāra</s>, it cannot produce <s>saṃskāra</s>. But on the view that causality operates through cognition-hood, since cognition-hood is present in recollection too, it too has causality toward <s>saṃskāra</s>; hence from the initially arisen pot-recollection a <s>saṃskāra</s> [arises] again, and from that a [further] recollection — thus recollection subsequent to recollection

smṛtihetutvamastu iti śaṅkāgranthābhiprāyaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Nor should it be said that what is produced by itself' and so forth. If it is accepted that <s>saṃskāra</s> (impression) is destroyed by the memory produced from it, then even though causality in the form of cognition-hood (<s>jñānatva</s>) is accepted — namely that a cognition having a certain object is the cause of memory having that object — in the case where, after an experience having as its object multiple entities like pot, cloth, etc. in the form of collective apprehension (<s>samūhālambana</s>), memories of pot, cloth, etc. arise individually, not as a single memory having as its object all the experienced entities — there, since the <s>saṃskāra</s> having as its object multiple entities like pot, cloth, etc. produced from the collective apprehension experience is destroyed by the memory of pot alone, the memory of cloth and the like would be impossible, because the <s>saṃskāra</s> having cloth etc. as its object has been destroyed. Nor should it be said that the <s>saṃskāra</s> produced from the memory of pot generates the memory of cloth and the like — because the <s>saṃskāra</s> produced from the memory of pot, having pot alone as its object, cannot possibly generate the memory of cloth and the like; because the <s>saṃskāra</s> having a particular object is the cause of memory having that same object, and a <s>saṃskāra</s> having one object cannot produce memory having a different object. And thus, only the final memory, by virtue of being an instance of that [cognition], should be stated as the cause of the destruction of the <s>saṃskāra</s>. In this way, even in the view that cognition-hood (<s>anubhavatva</s>) as delimited is the cause of both <s>saṃskāra</s> and memory, since the initial memory of pot does not destroy the <s>saṃskāra</s> produced from the experience of pot, by its force another memory of pot can arise — therefore let experience-hood (<s>anubhavatva</s>) alone be the cause of memory — this is the purport of the objection passage.

children.translated_text: 'Of what has fewer objects' and so forth. Only a memory having as its object as many entities as are objects of the <s>saṃskāra</s> destroys the <s>saṃskāra</s>. And thus, the <s>saṃskāra</s> having as its object multiple entities like pot, cloth, etc. produced from the collective apprehension experience is not destroyed by the memory of pot alone, which has fewer objects than that <s>saṃskāra</s> — hence the successive memories of cloth and the like are explained — this is the purport. The property of having fewer objects than the <s>saṃskāra</s> in the memory means: having a content-relation that is pervaded by the content-relation of the <s>saṃskāra</s>. He states the further reasoning for cognition-hood (<s>jñānatva</s>) being the cause of <s>saṃskāra</s> — 'and it arises.' It is established by experience that from repeated memory of pot, a <s>saṃskāra</s> qualified by a particular universal (<s>jātiviśeṣa</s>) in the form of firmness (<s>dārḍhya</s>) that facilitates rapid pot-memory arises. And that is consistent only with cognition-hood being the cause of <s>saṃskāra</s>, since even from memory, being a cognition, the production of <s>saṃskāra</s> from it is possible — this is the purport. 'From the proximity of an awakener' — an awakener is seeing a related object and the like. 'Refutation of the excess of <s>saṃskāra</s>' — the meaning is: refutation of the particular universal called firmness (<s>dārḍhya</s>) residing in <s>saṃskāra</s>. 'Because practice itself would not be accounted for' — the purport is: practice is done only for the purpose of firmness of <s>saṃskāra</s>. Objection: practice of scripture is done for the purpose of rapid memory, or for the purpose of the proximity of an awakener that causes rapid memory, not for the purpose of firmness of <s>saṃskāra</s> — to this he states another defect — 'moreover.' 'A form that is ascertained to be non-deviating' — the meaning is: a property delimited by which there is ascertainment of non-deviation in the form of not being the counter-positive of an absence of occurrence in what immediately precedes the effect — a property that is ascertained not to delimit the counter-positiveness of such absence. 'By what has observed deviation' — the meaning is: by a property delimited by which deviation is observed. In the present case, experience-hood (<s>anubhavatva</s>) as delimited is not necessarily present before memory, due to the absence of experience before the second memory. And thus, experience-hood as delimited has observed deviation. Since cognition-hood (<s>jñānatva</s>) as delimited — the first memory — is present even before the second memory, cognition-hood

children.translated_text: is ascertained to be non-deviating. Therefore, the cause of memory is cognition-hood alone, as ascertained to be non-deviating, not experience-hood, which has observed deviation — this is the purport. Objection: in the Navya view, since memory too, like experience, is a cause of <s>saṃskāra</s>, in a <s>saṃskāra</s> produced from memory, experience-produced-ness (<s>anubhavajanyatva</s>) is absent; therefore the definition 'impression (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is the cause of memory that is produced from experience' would suffer from under-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>). To this he replies — 'In this view.' And thus, in this view, the definition of <s>saṃskāra</s> is precisely: being a cause of memory while being produced from cognition (<s>jñānajanya</s>). Since even in a <s>saṃskāra</s> produced from memory, the property of being produced from cognition in the form of memory exists, there is no under-pervasion — this is the purport.

children.translated_text: The other [qualities] such as <s>rūpa</s> (color) and the like are <s>viśeṣaguṇas</s> (particular qualities). The definition of being a <s>viśeṣaguṇa</s> is: being a quality that possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in what is co-located with any two substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s> (adventitious conditions).

children.translated_text: 'Substance-differentiating <s>upādhi</s>' — that which is a pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s>, each in the form of earth-ness (<s>pṛthivītva</s>), water-ness (<s>jalatva</s>), and the like — the meaning is: being a quality that possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in what is co-located with each of those pairs individually, such as <s>dvitva</s> (duality), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), and the like. The application of the definition is as follows: in the four [qualities] such as <s>rūpa</s> (color) and the like, taking the universal such as <s>nīlatva</s> (blue-ness) and the like [or <s>rūpatva</s> (color-hood) and the like]; in natural fluidity (<s>sāṃsiddhikadravatva</s>), taking the sub-universal of fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>); in the ten [qualities] such as <s>sneha</s> (viscosity) and the like, taking the universal such as <s>snehatva</s> (viscosity-hood) and the like; and in <s>bhāvanā</s> (impression), taking the sub-universal of <s>saṃskāratva</s> (impression-hood). Objection: this definition over-extends to <s>ekatva</s> (oneness) and the like, since the <s>jāti</s> such as <s>ekatvatva</s> (oneness-hood) also has that character. Nor should it be said

Even so, there is over-extension in <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude) and the like. Since <s>parimāṇatva</s> (magnitude-hood) and the like being such a <s>jāti</s> is impossible — if thus [objected]:

atra
pravadantyabhijñāḥ -
yadyadrūpāvacchinnasamānādhikaraṇaṃ yatkiñciddravyavibhājakopādhidvayaṃ

vijātīyasyaiva anubhavasiddhatvāt/ saṅkhyādayastu sāmānyaguṇā

tatra nātivyāptiḥ/ tādṛśajātimadbhinnaguṇatvameva sāmānyaguṇānāṃ

children.translated_text: Here the experts declare: the meaning of the definition is: being a quality that possesses a <s>jāti</s> that is different from the <s>sthitasthāpaka</s> (restoring) <s>vṛtti</s> (occurrence) and is such that for whatever form delimits the co-location with some pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s>, the <s>jāti</s> is different from that. Since the co-location delimited by a certain form is to be understood as constituted by the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and since forms like pot-hood (<s>ghaṭatva</s>) and the like cannot be grasped by the expression 'whatever form,' there is over-extension in pot and the like — hence this is the qualificand. To prevent over-extension in the <s>sthitasthāpaka</s>, 'different from the <s>sthitasthāpaka</s> occurrence' [is added]. In the view that the <s>sthitasthāpaka</s> occurs in the four [substances] earth and the like, this [qualification] need not be given. The application of the definition in <s>rūpa</s> (color) and the like is by taking the sub-universal, even though color-hood and the like cannot be grasped by the expression 'whatever form.' Since the touch that is earthy, non-hot-non-cold (<s>pārthivānuṣṇāśītasparśa</s>), is established by experience as being of a different kind (<s>vijātīya</s>) compared to the airy [touch], and since general qualities like number and the like are not established by <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) as being of different kinds according to the distinction of water, earth, and the like — therefore there is no over-extension there. The definition of general qualities (<s>sāmānyaguṇa</s>) should be understood as: being a quality different from what possesses such a <s>jāti</s>.

prasiddham/ tadvṛttayaḥ dvitvapṛthaktvasaṃyogādayaḥ tadavṛttirjātiḥ
rūpatvarasatvādiḥ tadvān guṇaḥ rūparasādiriti
tādṛśajātimadguṇatvasya rūparasādau sattvāt lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/
rūpādikaṃ tu dravyavibhājakopādhidvayasamānādhikaraṇaṃ na bhavati,
dravyavibhājakapṛthivītvajalatvadvayādhikaraṇapṛthivījalayoḥ ekasya
rūpasya rasādeḥ vā avṛtteḥ/ ato dviniṣṭhaṃ dvitvādikameva tādṛśaṃ
tadavṛttitvaṃ rūpatvādijātāvastīti bhāvaḥ/ atra pratyekamityasya
tatsamānādhikaraṇetyatrādhikaraṇa evānvayaḥ na tu
tadadhikaraṇavṛttitve 'pītyavadheyam/ nīlatvādikamiti/ ādipadena
