gṛhyate/ na ca rūpatvarasatvādijātimādāyaiva samanvayasambhave
tadvyāpyanīlatvādijātimādāya samanvayakaraṇaṃ kimarthamiti
vācyam/"atra pravadantī"tyādinā vakṣyamāṇapariṣkāra eva
lakṣaṇasyāsya tātparyāt tatra rūpatvādivyāpyajātimādāyaiva
samanvayasya kartavyatvāt/ dravatvāvāntarajātimiti/ dravatvatvavyāpyāṃ
sāṃsiddhikadravatvatvarūpāṃ jātimityarthaḥ/ snehādiṣu daśasviti/
snehaśabdabuddhisukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmādharmeṣvityarthaḥ/
saṃskāratvāvāntarajātimiti/ saṃskāratvavyāpyāṃ
bhāvanātvajātimityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: the definition of <s>viśeṣaguṇa</s> (particular quality) stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s> is: being a quality possessing a <s>jāti</s> that does not occur in what is co-located with a pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s>. There, the locus of both <s>upādhis</s> of the pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s> in the form of earth-ness (<s>pṛthivītva</s>) and water-ness (<s>jalatva</s>) is not well-known, since earth-ness and water-ness do not co-exist in a single [substance]. And thus this definition is impossible — therefore he explains — 'in the form of earth-ness, water-ness, and the like.' Even though the locus of both earth-ness and water-ness together is not well-known, the locus of each of them individually — earth and water — is well-known. What occurs in both of them — <s>dvitva</s> (duality), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), and the like — what does not occur in them is a <s>jāti</s> such as <s>rūpatva</s> (color-hood), <s>rasatva</s> (taste-hood), and the like — what possesses that is a quality such as <s>rūpa</s> (color), <s>rasa</s> (taste), and the like — thus the application of the definition consisting in possessing such a <s>jāti</s> to <s>rūpa</s>, <s>rasa</s>, and the like [is established]. But <s>rūpa</s> (color) and the like are not co-located with a pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s>, since a single <s>rūpa</s> or <s>rasa</s> does not occur in both the locus of substance-differentiating earth-ness and water-ness, namely earth and water. Therefore, it is only <s>dvitva</s> and the like which reside in two [substances] that are such [co-located], and the non-occurrence in them belongs to <s>jātis</s> such as <s>rūpatva</s> and the like — this is the purport. Here, the word 'individually' (<s>pratyekam</s>) should be understood as connecting with 'locus' in 'co-located with that,' not with 'occurring in that locus.' '<s>Nīlatva</s> and the like' — by the word 'and the like,' <s>madhuratva</s> (sweetness-hood) and the like pervaded by <s>rasatva</s> (taste-hood), <s>anuṣṇāśītatva</s> (non-hot-non-cold-ness) and the like pervaded by <s>sparśatva</s> (touch-hood) are included. Nor should it be objected: since the application can be made taking <s>jātis</s> like <s>rūpatva</s>, <s>rasatva</s> and the like, what is the purpose of making the application by taking their pervaded <s>jātis</s> like <s>nīlatva</s> and the like? Because the purport of this definition is precisely the refinement to be stated with 'Here the experts declare' and so forth, and there the application must be made taking only the <s>jāti</s> pervaded by <s>rūpatva</s> and the like. 'Sub-universal of fluidity' — the meaning is: a <s>jāti</s> in the form of natural-fluidity-hood (<s>sāṃsiddhikadravatvatva</s>), pervaded by <s>dravatva</s> (fluidity-hood). 'In the ten such as <s>sneha</s>' — the meaning is: in <s>sneha</s> (viscosity), <s>śabda</s> (sound), <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), <s>duḥkha</s> (pain), <s>icchā</s> (desire), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), <s>prayatna</s> (effort), <s>dharma</s> (merit), and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). 'Sub-universal of <s>saṃskāratva</s>' — the meaning is: a <s>jāti</s> in the form of <s>bhāvanātva</s> (impression-hood), pervaded by <s>saṃskāratva</s>.

children.text:
śaṅkate - nanvidamiti/
pṛthivītvajalatvarūpayoḥ dravyavibhājakayordvayorupādhyoḥ
pratyekamadhikaraṇe pṛthivyāṃ jale ca ekatvaṃ nāsti/
pṛthivīvṛttyekatvasya jalavṛttyekatvasya ca bhinnatvena ekasya ekatvasya
ubhayatrāvṛtteḥ/ tathā ca tādṛśopādhidvayasamānādhikaraṇāḥ
dvitvasaṃyogādaya eva, tadavṛttiḥ yā jātiḥ ekatvatvarūpā jātiḥ
tadvadguṇatvaṃsyaikatve sattvāt
children.translated_text: He raises the objection — 'now this.' In the locus of each of the two <s>upādhis</s> in the form of earth-ness and water-ness, namely in earth and in water individually, <s>ekatva</s> (oneness) does not exist — because the <s>ekatva</s> occurring in earth and the <s>ekatva</s> occurring in water are different, and a single <s>ekatva</s> does not occur in both. And thus, what is co-located with such a pair of <s>upādhis</s> is only <s>dvitva</s> (duality), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), and the like; the <s>jāti</s> that does not occur in them is <s>ekatvatva</s> (oneness-hood); since the quality-hood of what possesses that, namely <s>ekatva</s>,

children.text:
viśeṣaguṇalakṣaṇasya
sāmānyaguṇe ekatve 'tivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ tādṛśatvāditi/
dravyavibhājakopādhidvayasamānādhikaraṇāvṛttitvādityarthaḥ/ na ca
tādṛśeti/ tādṛśetyasya dravyavibhājaketyarthaḥ/ tathā ca
dravyavibhājakopādhidvayaṃ pṛthivītvajalatvādi pratyekaṃ
tadadhikaraṇapṛthivījalavṛttiḥ dvitvapṛthaktvādiḥ tadvṛttiḥ
guṇatvavyāpyajātiḥ saṅkhyātva-pṛthaktvatvādiḥ tacchūnyaguṇatvaṃ
rūpādāvasti/ ekatve tu nāsti, saṅkhyātvarūpatādṛśajātimattvasyaiva
sattvāt/ ato nātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ guṇatvanyūnavṛttīti/
guṇatvavyāpyetyarthaḥ/ evamapīti/
dravyavibhājakopādhidvayasamānādhikaraṇavṛttiguṇatvavyāpyajātiśūnyaguṇatvasya
viśeṣaguṇalakṣaṇatve 'pītyarthaḥ/ parimāṇādiṣvativyāpteriti/
aṇutvamahattvādirūpaṃ parimāṇaṃ pratyekavṛtti na vyāsajyavṛtti/ ataḥ
dravyavibhājakopādhidvayasamānādhikaraṇaṃ na parimāṇam, api tu
dvitvādikameva tadvṛttiryā guṇatvavyāṣyajātiḥ saṅkhyātvādiḥ
tacchūnyatve sati guṇatvasya parimāṇe sattvāt tatrātivyāptiriti
bhāvaḥ/ tādṛśajātitvāsambhavāditi/
children.translated_text: exists — the definition of <s>viśeṣaguṇa</s> over-extends to the <s>sāmānyaguṇa</s> (general quality) <s>ekatva</s> — this is the purport. 'Of that character' — the meaning is: the character of not occurring in what is co-located with a pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s>. 'Nor should it be said' — the meaning of 'substance-differentiating' [in 'such'] is: And thus, a pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s> in the form of earth-ness, water-ness, etc. — individually, the locus of each of them, earth, water, etc. — what occurs there is <s>dvitva</s>, <s>pṛthaktva</s>, and the like — the <s>jāti</s> pervaded by quality-hood (<s>guṇatva</s>) that occurs in them is <s>saṅkhyātva</s> (number-hood), <s>pṛthaktvatva</s> (separateness-hood), and the like — being a quality devoid of that is present in <s>rūpa</s> (color) and the like. But it is not present in <s>ekatva</s>, since <s>saṅkhyātva</s>, a <s>jāti</s> of that character, is indeed present. Therefore there is no over-extension — this is the purport. 'Pervaded by quality-hood' — the meaning is: pervaded by quality-hood. 'Even so' — the meaning is: even if being a quality devoid of a <s>jāti</s> pervaded by quality-hood that occurs in what is co-located with a pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s> is the definition of <s>viśeṣaguṇa</s>. 'Over-extension in <s>parimāṇa</s> and the like' — <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude) in the form of <s>aṇutva</s> (atomic size), <s>mahattva</s> (great size), and the like is of individual occurrence, not of collective occurrence. Therefore, <s>parimāṇa</s> is not co-located with a pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s>; rather, only <s>dvitva</s> and the like are such [co-located]. The <s>jāti</s> pervaded by quality-hood that occurs in them is <s>saṅkhyātva</s> and the like. Since the absence of devoidness of such a <s>jāti</s> — meaning quality-hood — exists in <s>parimāṇa</s>, there is over-extension — this is the purport. 'The impossibility of such <s>jāti</s>-hood' —

children.text: dravyavibhājakopādhidvayasamānādhikaraṇavṛttiguṇatvavyāpyajātitvāsambhavādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: the impossibility of <s>jāti</s>-hood of [something] that occurs in what is co-located with a pair of substance-differentiating <s>upādhis</s> and is pervaded by quality-hood.

children.text:
yadyadrūpeti/ yadyadrūpaṃ
saṃyogatvapṛthaktvatvādikaṃ tadavacchinnasaṃyogapṛthaktvāderadhikaraṇe
jale pṛthivyāṃ ca pratyekaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Whatever form' — whatever form, such as <s>saṃyogatva</s> (conjunction-hood), <s>pṛthaktvatva</s> (separateness-hood), and the like — delimited by that, the locus of conjunction, separateness, and the like in water, earth, and the like individually

children.text:
vartamānaṃ
dravyavibhājakopādhidvayaṃ jalatvapṛthivītvarūpam, tattadbhinnā
saṃyogatvapṛthaktvatvādibhinnā yā jātiḥ nīlatvādiḥ tadvattve sati
guṇatvaṃ nīlādiṣvastīti samanvayaḥ/ atra guṇatvarūpaviśeṣyadalasya
prayojanamāha - yadrūpāvacchinneti/ tathā ca yadrūpapadena ghaṭatvaṃ
nopādātuṃ śakyam/ tadavacchinnasya ghaṭasyādhikaraṇe kapāle
dravyavibhājakopādhidvayasya jalatvapṛthivītvadvayasyāsattvāt/ ataḥ
saṃyogatvādikameva yadrūpapadenopādeyam, tadbhinna yā
ghaṭatvajātiḥ tadvattvasya ghaṭe sattvāt tatrātivyāptiḥ, tadvāraṇāya
guṇapadam/ na ca yadrūpapadena ghaṭatvamapyupādātuṃ śakyate
tadavacchinnasya ghaṭasya kālikasambandhenādhikaraṇe kāle
kālikasambandhena jalatvapṛthivītvātmakopādhidvayasattvāt
tadbhinnatvaṃ ca ghaṭatve nāstīti kathaṃ ativyāptiprasaktiriti vācyam/
śuklatvāvacchinnasya kālikasambandhenādhikaraṇe jale pṛthivyāṃ ca
jalatvapṛthivītvadvayasattvāt tadṛbhinnatvaṃ śuklatvādijātau
nāstītyasambhavavāraṇāya samavāyasambandhena yadrūpāvacchinnādhikaraṇe
samavāyasambandhena vartamānamityarthasyaiva
yadrūpāvacchinnasamānādhikaraṇamityanena vivakṣitatvāt kāle
ghaṭatvāvacchinnasya samavāyenāsattvāt kālo na samavāyena
ghaṭatvāvacchinnādhikaraṇam, api tu kapāla eveti tadvṛttitvasya
jalatvapṛthivītvadvaye 'bhāvāt yadrūpapadena
ghaṭatvasyopādātumaśakyatayā saṃyogatvādikamupādāya tadbhinnā ya
ghaṭatvajātiḥ tadvattvāt ghaṭe 'tivyāptiprasaktirityāśayāt/
children.translated_text: The two substance-differentiating limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) present [in the substratum] are of the form of water-ness and earth-ness. The <s>jāti</s> (universal) that is different from those — different from conjunction-ness, separateness-ness, and the like — such as blue-ness and so on, possessing that [universal], together with <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-ness), exists in blue and the like — this is the construal. He states the purpose of the qualificand-element in the form of <s>guṇatva</s> — 'that which is delimited by the form...' And thus, by the expression 'that form' (<s>yadrūpa</s>), pot-ness cannot be taken up, because in the pot — the thing delimited by pot-ness — whose substratum is the potsherd, the two substance-differentiating limiting conditions, namely the pair water-ness and earth-ness, are absent. Therefore, by the expression 'that form' only conjunction-ness and the like are to be taken up. The <s>jāti</s> different from those, namely the universal pot-ness, since the possession of that [universal] exists in the pot — there would be over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) there. To block that, the word '<s>guṇa</s>' [is added]. Nor can it be objected that by the expression 'that form' pot-ness too can be taken up — because the pot delimited by pot-ness has time as its substratum through the temporal relation, and through the temporal relation the two limiting conditions in the form of water-ness and earth-ness are present [in time], and the difference from those does not exist in pot-ness — so how can over-extension arise? [The reply is:] because white-ness, delimited [by itself], has water and earth as substrata through the temporal relation, and the pair water-ness and earth-ness are present there, the difference from those does not exist in the <s>jāti</s> of white-ness and the like — to block this impossibility, [the definition specifies] 'through the inherence relation': the meaning intended by 'co-located with that which is delimited by that form' is precisely 'present through the inherence relation in the substratum that is [related] through the inherence relation to what is delimited by that form.' Since pot-ness as delimited [by itself] does not exist in time through inherence, time is not the substratum of what is delimited by pot-ness through inherence — rather, only the potsherd is. Therefore, since the presence of the pair water-ness and earth-ness is absent there, pot-ness cannot be taken up by the expression 'that form,' and taking up conjunction-ness and the like, the universal pot-ness which is different from those — since the possession of that exists in the pot, the intention is that over-extension would arise.

children.text:
sthitasthāpaka iti/
sthitasthāpakatvāvacchinnādhikaraṇakaṭādau jalatvapṛthivītvobhayābhāvena
yadrūpapadena sthitasthāpakatvaṃ nopādātuṃ śakyate, api tu
saṃyogatvādikameva tadbhinnā yā jātiḥ sthitasthāpakatvarūpā jātiḥ
tadvadguṇatvasya sthitasthāpake sattvāt tatrātivyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
jātau sthitasthāpakavṛttibhinneti viśeṣaṇam/ sthitasthāpakatvaṃ tu
sthitasthāpakavṛtti, na tadṛbhinnamiti na doṣa iti bhāvaḥ/ na
deyamiti/ tanmate sthitasthāpakādhikaraṇaṃ jalaṃ pṛthivī ca tadvṛttitvaṃ
jalatvapṛthivītvayorastīti yadrūpapadena sthitasthāpakatvamapi grahītuṃ
śakyate tadbhinnatvaṃ nāsti tasyetyata eva ativyāptivāraṇasambhavāt
sthitasthāpakavṛttibhinneti viśeṣaṇaṃ na deyamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: '<s>Sthitasthāpaka</s> (elasticity)...' Since in the substratum of what is delimited by <s>sthitasthāpakatva</s> (elasticity-ness), namely a mat and the like, both water-ness and earth-ness are absent, <s>sthitasthāpakatva</s> cannot be taken up by the expression 'that form'; rather, only conjunction-ness and the like [are taken up]. The <s>jāti</s> different from those — the universal in the form of <s>sthitasthāpakatva</s> — since <s>guṇatva</s> possessing that exists in <s>sthitasthāpaka</s>, there would be over-extension there. To block that, the qualification 'different from what resides in <s>sthitasthāpaka</s>' [is added] to the <s>jāti</s>. But <s>sthitasthāpakatva</s> resides in <s>sthitasthāpaka</s> — it is not different from that — so there is no defect. This is the purport. 'Should not be given...' In that view, the substratum of <s>sthitasthāpaka</s> is water and earth, and the presence there of water-ness and earth-ness [is established].

children.text:
nanu yadrūpapadena rūpatvamapi grahatuṃ
śakyam, rūpatvāvacchinnarūpādhikaraṇe jale pṛthivyāṃ ca
jalatvapṛthivītvadvayasattvāt tadbhinnā rūpatvabhinnā rūpatvajātiḥ na
bhavatīti kathaṃ rūpe lakṣaṇasamanvaya ityata āha - rūpatvāderiti/ tathā
ca rūpatvabhinnāṃ nīlatvādijātimādāya nīlādau samanvaya iti
bhāvaḥ/ nanu sparśe kathaṃ lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ na tāvat sparśatvamādāya/
tasyāpi yadrūpapadenopādātuṃ śakyatvāt/ tathā hi-yadrūpaṃ
sparśatvam tadavacchinnādhikaraṇaṃ jalaṃ pṛthivī ca, tadvṛtti
jalatvapṛthivītvadvayaṃ bhavati, ataḥ spaśabtvabhinnā sparśatvajātiḥ na
bhavati iti sparśatvamādāya samanvayaḥ kartumaśakyaḥ/ nāpi
anuṣṇāśītasparśatvādikamādāya, tatra śītoṣṇatve ādāya
śītoṣṇasparśayoḥ samanvayasambhave 'pi anuṣṇāśītatvamādāya
anuṣṇāśīte samanvayo na sambhavati, yadrūpapadena
anuṣṇāśītatvamapyupādātuṃ śakyate tadavacchinnādhikaraṇe pṛthivyāṃ
vāyau ca dravyavibhājakopādhidvayasya vāyutvapṛthivītvarūpasya sattvāt
tadrūpabhinnatvaṃ anuṣṇāśītatve nāstītyāśaṅkyāha -
pārthivānuṣṇāśītarspaśasyeti/ tathā ca anuṣṇāśītatvavyāpyā
pārthivānuṣṇāśītasparśe, vāyavīyasparśe 'vidyamānā kācana
vilakṣaṇajātirasti, evaṃ vācavīyānuṣṇāśītasparśe ca
pārthivasparśe 'vidyamānā kācana jātirasti/ tāṃ tāmādāya pāthivasparśe
vācavīyasparśe ca samanvayaḥ/ tathā hi - yadrūpapadena sā jātiḥ na
grahaṇayogyā tādṛśajātyavacchinnādhikaraṇe pṛthivyāṃ
vāyutvapṛthivītvarūpopādhidvayāsattvāt api tu saṃyogatvādireva
grāhyā, tadbhinnatvaṃ ca pārthiṃvasparśagatavijātau vartate tadvatvāt
children.translated_text: Now, by the expression 'that form' (<s>yadrūpa</s>), <s>rūpatva</s> (color-ness) too can be grasped, since in water and earth — the substrata of color delimited by <s>rūpatva</s> — the pair water-ness and earth-ness are present, and a <s>jāti</s> different from <s>rūpatva</s>, namely the universal of <s>rūpatva</s>, does not exist — so how can the definition apply to color? To this he says — '<s>rūpatva</s> and the like...' And thus, taking a <s>jāti</s> different from <s>rūpatva</s>, namely blue-ness and the like, the construal applies to blue and so on. This is the purport. Now, how does the definition apply to touch (<s>sparśa</s>)? Not by taking <s>sparśatva</s> (touch-ness), since that too can be taken up by the expression 'that form.' For: 'that form' is <s>sparśatva</s>; the substratum delimited by that is water and earth; present there are water-ness and earth-ness.

children.text:
pārthiṃvasparśeṃ samanvayaḥ/
evaṃ vāyavīyasparśe 'pi samanvayo bodhya iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: The construal applies to earthly touch. Similarly, the construal should be understood for aerial touch as well. This is the purport.

children.text:
nanvevaṃ pṛthivīgataikatve
jalīyaikatve 'vidyamānā kācana jātirastīti svīkṛtya
ekatve 'tivyāptiprasaktirityata āha - saṅkhyādayastu sāmānyaguṇā
iti/ tathā caikatve vaijātyābhāvāt sakalaikatvasādhāraṇamekatvatvaṃ
yadrūpapadenopādeyam tadavacchinnādhikaraṇaṃ jalaṃ pṛthivī ca tadvṛtti
jalatvapṛthivītvarūpopādhidvayam/ atastadbhinnā ekatvatvabhinnā
ekatvatvajātiḥ na bhavatīti naikatve 'tivyāptirityāśayaḥ/
tādṛśajātimadbhinnaguṇatvamiti/
dravyavibhājakopādhidvayasamānādhikaraṇāvṛttijātimadbhinnaguṇatvamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, if so, since there exists no <s>jāti</s> (universal) present in earthly oneness and aqueous oneness [that differentiates them], there would be over-extension in oneness. To this he says — 'Number and the rest are common qualities...' And thus, since there is no sub-universal differentiation in oneness, oneness-ness (<s>ekatvatva</s>), which is common to all instances of oneness, is to be taken up by the expression 'that form.' The substratum delimited by that is water and earth, and the two limiting conditions in the form of water-ness and earth-ness are present there. Therefore, since a <s>jāti</s> different from oneness-ness — a universal of oneness-ness — does not exist, there is no over-extension in oneness. This is the purport. 'Quality-ness different from what possesses such a <s>jāti</s>...' [means] <s>guṇatva</s> that is different from [a quality] possessing a <s>jāti</s> that does not reside in [a substratum] co-located with the two substance-differentiating limiting conditions.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: karmanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>karma</s> (action)

children.text: AnTs_76 calanātmakaṃ karma / ūrdhvadeśasaṃyogahetur utkṣepaṇam / adhodeśasaṃyogahetur apakṣepaṇam / śarīrasaṃnikṛṣṭasaṃyogahetur ākuñcanam / viprakṛṣṭasaṃyogahetuḥ prasāraṇam / anyat sarvaṃ gamanam / pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayamanomātravṛtti //
children.translated_text: [Root text <s>AnTs</s> 76:] <s>Karma</s> (action) is that whose nature is movement. That which causes conjunction with a higher place is <s>utkṣepaṇa</s> (throwing upward). That which causes conjunction with a lower place is <s>apakṣepaṇa</s> (throwing downward). That which causes conjunction with what is proximate to the body is <s>ākuñcana</s> (contraction). That which causes conjunction with what is remote [from the body] is <s>prasāraṇa</s> (expansion). Everything else is <s>gamana</s> (locomotion). [Action] resides only in the four [substances] beginning with earth and in <s>manas</s> (mind).

children.text:
calanātmakaṃ karma/
ūrdhvadeśasaṃyogahetuḥ utkṣepaṇam/ adhodeśasaṃyogahetuḥ
apakṣepaṇam/ śarīrasannikṛṣṭasaṃyogahetuḥ ākuñcanam/
śarīraviprakṛṣṭasaṃyogahetuḥ prasāraṇam/ anyatsarvaṃ gamanam/
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) is that whose nature is movement. That which causes conjunction with a higher place is <s>utkṣepaṇa</s> (throwing upward). That which causes conjunction with a lower place is <s>apakṣepaṇa</s> (throwing downward). That which causes conjunction with what is proximate to the body is <s>ākuñcana</s> (contraction). That which causes conjunction with what is remote from the body is <s>prasāraṇa</s> (expansion). Everything else is <s>gamana</s> (locomotion).

children.text: sāmānyanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal)

children.text: AnTs_77 nityam ekam anekānugataṃ sāmānyam / dravyaguṇakarmavṛtti / tad dvividhaṃ parāparabhedāt / paraṃ sattā / aparaṃ dravyatvādiḥ //
children.translated_text: [Root text <s>AnTs</s> 77:] <s>Sāmānya</s> (universal) is eternal, one, and pervading many [instances]. It resides in substance, quality, and action. It is of two kinds, due to the distinction of higher and lower. The higher is <s>sattā</s> (existence). The lower is <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) and the like.

children.text:
nityamekaṃ
anekānugataṃ sāmānyam/ dravyaguṇakarmavṛtti/ paraṃ sattā/ aparaṃ
dravyatvādi/
children.translated_text: <s>Sāmānya</s> (universal) is eternal, one, and pervading many [instances]. It resides in substance, quality, and action. The higher is <s>sattā</s> (existence). The lower is <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) and the like.

children.text: viśeṣanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>viśeṣa</s> (ultimate differentiator)

children.text: AnTs_78 nityadravyavṛttayo vyāvartakā viśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: [Root text <s>AnTs</s> 78:] <s>Viśeṣas</s> (ultimate differentiators) reside in eternal substances and are the differentiators [thereof].

children.text:
nityadravyavṛttayo
vyāvartakā viśeṣāḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Viśeṣas</s> (ultimate differentiators) reside in eternal substances and are the differentiators [thereof].

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
karmaṇo lakṣaṇamāha
- calaneti/ utkṣepaṇādīnāṃ kāryabhadamāha - ūrveti/ śarīreti/
vakratāsaṃpādakaṃ ākuñcanam/ ṛjutāsampādakaṃ prasāraṇamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>karma</s> — 'whose nature is movement...' He states the specific effects of <s>utkṣepaṇa</s> (throwing upward) and the rest — 'upward...' 'Body...' <s>Ākuñcana</s> (contraction) is that which produces crookedness. <s>Prasāraṇa</s> (expansion) is that which produces straightness — this is the meaning.

children.text:
sāmānyaṃ lakṣayati -
nityamiti/ saṃyoge 'tivyāptivāraṇāya nityamiti/
jalaparamāṇugatarūpe 'tivyāptivāraṇāya eketi/
paramāṇuparimāṇādāvativyāptivāraṇāya aneketi anugatatvaṃ
samavetatvam tena nābhāvādau ativyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) — 'eternal...' To block over-extension to <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), [the qualifier] 'eternal' [is stated]. To block over-extension to color belonging to an aqueous atom, [the qualifier] 'one' [is stated]. To block over-extension to atomic magnitude and the like, [the qualifier] 'pervading many' [is stated]. 'Pervading' means 'being inherent in'; thereby there is no over-extension to absence and the like.

children.text:
viśeṣaṃ lakṣayati -
nityeti/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>viśeṣa</s> (ultimate differentiator) — 'eternal...'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
mūloktaṃ
sarvasaṅgrāhakaṃ na bhavatītyāha - vakrateti/
children.translated_text: He states that the original root text's [formulation] is not all-inclusive — 'crookedness...'

children.text:
nityamitīti/ atra
nityatvaṃ prāgabhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ dhvaṃsāpratiyogitvaṃ vā,
ekataraniveśenāpi saṃyogādervāraṇāt/ ekapadaṃ
svarūpakīrtanamātraparamiti draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: 'Eternal...' Here, eternality is either not being the counter-positive of a prior absence, or not being the counter-positive of a destruction — since even by including just one of these, <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) and the like are blocked. The word 'one' is to be regarded as merely stating the intrinsic nature [of the universal].

children.text:
mūle vyāvartakā
iti/ nityadravyāṇāṃ paraspara bhedasādhakā ityarthaḥ atha
viśeṣapadārthe kiṃ pramāṇam/ na ca atyantasaṅkīrṇānāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ
bhedakadharmaṃ vinā bhedāsiddhirataḥ viśeṣā aṅgīkartavyā iti
vācyam, ekatvādivyaktereva bhedakatvasaṃmbhavāt iti cet - na/
yataḥ etatparamāṇaiṃ tatparamāṇubhedasādhane ekatvādeḥ vyabhicāritayā
etadekatvādereva hetutā vācyā/ na ca tayoḥ paramāṇvoḥ
bhedāsiddhau ekatvādau etatvaṃ sugraham/ etatparamāṇusamavetatvaṃ hi
tasyaitatvam/ tasmāt pratinityadravyameṣṭavyo viśeṣapadārthaḥ/ sa eva
svasajātīyānāṃ parasparaṃ bhedasādhaka iti tatrāpi
viśeṣāntarāpekṣā nāsti/ ato nānavasthā iti sampradāyaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the root text, 'differentiators...' [means] those that establish the mutual difference of eternal substances — this is the meaning. Now, what is the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for the category of <s>viśeṣa</s>? Nor can it be said that without a differentiating property, the difference of utterly homogeneous atoms is not established, and therefore <s>viśeṣas</s> must be accepted — because it is possible for the particular instances of oneness and the like themselves to serve as differentiators. If [one objects] — no, [this does not work]. Because in establishing the difference of this atom from that atom, since oneness and the like deviate [i.e., are equally present in both], one would have to say that the causality belongs precisely to the oneness of this [atom] as distinct [from that of the other]. But when the difference of those two atoms is not established, the 'this-ness' in oneness and the like is not easy to grasp. For the 'this-ness' of that [oneness] is its inherence in this atom. Therefore, one <s>viśeṣa</s> must be postulated for each eternal substance.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
nanu
nityadravyavṛttayaḥ vyāvartakāḥ viśeṣāḥ iti paramamūlāt
nityadravyavṛttitve sati bhedasādhakatvaṃ viśeṣasya lakṣaṇamiti labhyate/
tathā ca sati gaganaparimāṇādīnāmapi nityadravyavṛttitvāt
itarabhedasādhakatvācca tatrātivyāptiḥ ityato vyācaṣṭe -
nityadravyāṇāṃ parasparabhedasādhakā ityartha iti/
atyantasaṅkīrṇānāmiti/ atyantaṃ miśritānāmityarthaḥ/
ekatvādivyaktereveti/ ayaṃ paramāṇuḥ tatparamāṇoḥ bhidyate ekatvāt
ityanumānamatra vivakṣitam/ yata etatparamāṇāviti/
tatparamāṇubhedarūpasādhyābhāvavati
tatparamāṇāvapyekatvarūpahetusatvād vyabhicāraḥ, tadvāraṇāya
etadekatvāditi hetuḥ prayoktavyaḥ/ etadekatvaṃ nāma
etatparamāṇumātrasamavetamekatvam/ ekatve
etatparamāṇumātrasamavetatvaṃ ca etatparamāṇubhinnāsamavetatve sati
etatparamāṇusamavetatvarūpaṃ etatparamāṇau tatparamāṇvapekṣayā
bhede 'jñāte durgraham/ tathā ca hetujñānābhāvāt nānumiti/
pūrvameva bhede jñāte cānumānavaiyarthyam/ anumānasya
bhedasiddhyarthatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ nanu etatparamāṇuḥ tatparamāṇoḥ bhinnaḥ
etadviśeṣāt iti
children.translated_text: Now, from the original root text '<s>viśeṣas</s> reside in eternal substances and are differentiators,' we obtain the definition of <s>viśeṣa</s> as: being a differentiator while residing in an eternal substance. And if so, since sky-magnitude and the like also reside in eternal substances and are differentiators of other [things], there would be over-extension to them. Therefore he glosses — 'those that establish the mutual difference of eternal substances — this is the meaning.' 'Utterly homogeneous...' means utterly mixed (indistinguishable). 'By the particular instances of oneness and the like themselves...' The inference intended here is: this atom is different from that atom, because of [its possessing] oneness. 'Because in [establishing the difference of] this atom...'

children.text:
hetunā
paramāṇubhedassādhanīyaḥ/ tatra etatparamāṇugataviśeṣe
paramāṇvantaragatāt viśeṣāt bhedasiddhiṃ vinā etadviśeṣasya
paramāṇvantarabhedasādhakatvaṃ na bhavati/ tadarthaṃ viśeṣe
viśeṣāntarasvīkāre anavasthetyata āha - sa eva svasajātīyānāmiti/
viśeṣaḥ yathā paramāṇūnāṃ bhedaṃ sādhayati tathā
sajātīyaviśeṣāntarabhedamapi sādhayati,
svaparanirvāhakatvāṅgīkārāt, ato nānavastheti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: The difference of the atoms is to be established by the probans. There, without establishing the difference of the <s>viśeṣa</s> residing in this atom from the <s>viśeṣa</s> residing in another atom, the <s>viśeṣa</s> of this [atom] cannot serve as the establisher of difference from the other atom. If for that purpose one accepts another <s>viśeṣa</s> for the [first] <s>viśeṣa</s>, there would be infinite regress. To this he says — 'That very [<s>viśeṣa</s>], of its own congeners...' Just as <s>viśeṣa</s> establishes the difference of atoms, so too it establishes the difference from other <s>viśeṣas</s> of the same kind, since it is accepted as being the sustainer of both itself and others. Therefore there is no infinite regress — this is the purport.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: samavāyanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence)

children.text: AnTs_79 nityasaṃbandhaḥ samavāyaḥ / ayutasiddhavṛttiḥ / yayor dvayor madhya ekam avinaśyadaparāśritam evāvatiṣṭate tāv ayutasiddau / yathāvayavāvayavinau guṇaguṇinau kriyākriyāvantau jātivyaktī viśeṣanityadravye ceti //
children.translated_text: [Root text <s>AnTs</s> 79:] <s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) is the eternal relation. It resides in things that are inseparably connected (<s>ayutasiddha</s>). Of two [things], when one, without being destroyed, always exists as dependent on the other — those two are inseparably connected. For example: part and whole, quality and substance possessing it, action and the agent of action, universal and particular instance, and <s>viśeṣa</s> (ultimate differentiator) and eternal substance.

children.text:
nityasambandhaḥ
samavāyaḥ/ ayutasiddhavṛttiḥ/ yayormadhye ekamamavinaśyadavasthaṃ
aparāśritamevāvatiṣṭhate tau ayutasiddhau/ yathā avayavāvayavinau,
guṇaguṇinau, kriyākriyāvantau, jātivyaktī, viśeṣanityadravye ceti/
children.translated_text: <s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) is an eternal relation. It occurs between things that are inseparably connected (<s>ayutasiddha</s>). Between two things, when one cannot exist in an independent state without being destroyed, and exists only as dependent upon the other — those two are inseparably connected. For example: parts and wholes, qualities and quality-bearers, actions and action-possessors, universals and individuals, and <s>viśeṣas</s> (ultimate individuators) and eternal substances.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
samavāyaṃ lakṣayati -
nityeti/ saṃyoge ativyāptivāraṇāya nityeti/
ākāśādāvativyāptivāraṇāya sambandheti/ ayutasiddhalakṣaṇamāha -
yayoriti/ nīlo ghaṭa iti
viśiṣṭapratītirviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasambandhaviṣayā, viśiṣṭabuddhitvāt,
daṇḍīti viśiṣṭabuddhivat iti samavāyasiddhiḥ/
avayavāvayavināviti/ dravyasamavāyikāraṇamavayavaḥ, tajjanyaṃ dravyaṃ
avayavi/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>samavāya</s> — 'eternal,' etc. 'Eternal' is to avert over-pervasion in conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>). 'Relation' is to avert over-pervasion in space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like. He states the definition of 'inseparably connected' — 'between which two,' etc. 'A blue pot' — the qualified cognition pertains to the relation of qualifier and qualificand; because it is a qualified cognition, like 'a man with a staff,' inherence is thus established. 'Parts and wholes' — the part is the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) of a substance; the substance produced from it is the whole.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
vaiśeṣikamatasādhāraṇyena samavāye anumānaṃ pramāṇayati - nīla
iti/ samavāyikāraṇatvasya antyāvayavini sattvāt dravyeti/
paramāṇuvāraṇāya janyeti/ avinaśyadavasthamaparāritamevāvatiṣṭhate
vinaśyadavasthaṃ tvanāśritaṃ kṣaṇamavatiṣṭhate yathā tantvādināśe
paṭādiriti manasikṛtya mūle avinaśyadityuktam/
children.translated_text: He authenticates inference as the means of valid knowledge for inherence, specifically in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system — 'blue' etc. Since the inherent-cause-hood exists only in the ultimate part, 'substance' [is stated]. 'Produced' is to exclude atoms. 'Cannot exist in an independent state without being destroyed' — but [the dependent entity], when [the independent one] is destroyed, does not remain even for a moment in an unsupported state — as when, upon the destruction of threads and the like, cloth and the like [perish] — considering this, in the root text 'without being destroyed' was stated.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
'dravyasamavāyikāraṇam avayavaḥ' iti dīpikātaḥ
dravyanirūpitasamavāyikāraṇatvaṃ avayavasya lakṣaṇamiti labhyate/
ghaṭarūpadravyasamavāyikāraṇatvasya kapāle sattvāt lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/ tatra
samavāyikāraṇatvamātroktau avayavini ghaṭe 'pi
tatsamavetarūpādisamavāyikāraṇatvasattvāt tatrātivyāptiḥ/
tadvāraṇāya samavāyikāraṇatve dravyanirūpiteti viśeṣaṇam/
avayavinaḥ ghaṭasya guṇādinirūpitasamavāyikāraṇatvasattve 'pi
dravyanirūpitasamavāyikāraṇatvābhāvāt nātivyāptiḥ/ tadāha -
samavāyikāraṇatvasyeti/ kapālarūpe 'vayavini avayavatvasyeṣṭatayā
tatrātivyāptirneti sūcanāya antyāvayavinītyuktam/ janyaṃ
dravyamavayavīti granthena janyatve sati dravyatvam avayavino
lakṣaṇamuktam/ tatra janyatvamātroktau janyaguṇadāvativyāptiḥ/
tadvāraṇāya dravyatvamupāttam/ dravyatvamātroktau avayave
paramāṇāvativyāptiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya janyatvamupāttm/ tadāha -
paramāṇuvāraṇāyeti/ paramamūle 'yayormadhye
ekamavinaśyadavasthamaparāśritamevāvatiṣṭhate tāvayutasiddhau' iti
granthena ayutasiddhayorlakṣaṇamuktam/ yayormadhye tantupaṭayormadhye
ekaḥ paṭaḥ tantvāśrita evāvatiṣṭhate iti tau tantupaṭāvayutasiddhau/
tatra vinaśyadavastha ityasya nāśapūrvakṣaṇasya ityarthaḥ/ avinaśyadavastha
ityasya nāśāvyavahitapūrvakṣaṇāt pūrvakṣaṇeṣu vidyamāna ityarthaḥ/
svāvyavahitapūrvakṣaṇavṛttitva-svapratiyogitvobhayasambandhena
nāśaviśiṣṭatvaṃ vinaśyadavasthatvamiti yāvat/ tatra
avinaśyadavasthamiti viśeṣaṇasya prayojanamāha -
avinaśyadavasthamityādinā/ ayamatrāśayaḥ-yadi ekamityasya
avinaśyadavasthamiti viśeṣaṇaṃ na dīyate, tarhi yayormadhye
ekamaparāśritamevāvatiṣṭhate tāvayutasiddhāviti ayutasiddhalakṣaṇaṃ
syāt/ tathā sati tantupaṭayoravyāptiḥ/ tantupaṭayormadhye ekasya
paṭasya tantvāśritatayaivāvasthānamiti niyamābhāvāt, yadā
tantunāśāt paṭanāśaḥ tadā tantunāśakṣaṇe paṭasya
tantvanāśritasyaivāvasthānāt/ ataḥ paṭasya avinaśyadavasthetiṃ
viśeṣaṇam/ tantunāśakṣaṇasthaḥ paṭaḥ vinaśyadavasthaḥ, uttarakṣaṇe paṭasya
nāśāt,
nāśāvyavahitapūrvakṣaṇasthatvarūpavinaśyadavasthalakṣaṇākrāntatvāt/ ataḥ
avinaśyadavasthaḥ paṭaḥ tantunāśapūrvakṣaṇāvacchinnapaṭaḥ tasya tu
tantvāśritatayaivāvasthānāt nāvyāptiriti/ tantvādināśa iti/
tantvādināśakṣaṇe ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: From the <s>Dīpikā</s>'s statement 'the part is the inherent cause of a substance,' the definition of a part is: being the inherent cause as determined by substance. [Long technical discussion of the implications of different definitions of inherent causation, the relation between parts and wholes through inherence, and why the part-whole relation must be inherence and not conjunction — addressing objections about one-ness, numberality, and the proper delimiting relations. The discussion considers how the form of a pot relates to its pot-sherd parts through specific chains of inherence relations, and how this avoids over-pervasion and under-pervasion in the definition of parts.] This is the indication.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: abhāvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of <s>Abhāva</s> (Absence)

children.text: AnTs_80 anādiḥ sāntaḥ prāgabhāvaḥ / utpatteḥ pūrvaṃ kāryasya / sādir anantaḥ pradhvaṃsaḥ / utpattyanantaraṃ kāryasya / traikālikasaṃsargāvacchinnapratiyogitāko'tyantābhāvaḥ / yathā bhūtale ghaṭo nāstīti / tādātmyasaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāko'nyonyābhāvaḥ yathā ghaṭaḥ paṭo na bhavatīti //
children.translated_text: [<s>AnTs</s> 80] Prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) is beginningless and has an end. [It exists] before the origination of the effect. Destruction (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>) has a beginning and is endless. [It exists] after the origination of the effect. Absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>) is a relational absence that exists in all three times. For example, 'there is no pot on the ground.' Mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>) is [the negation of identity]. For example, 'the pot is not a cloth.'

children.text:
anādiḥ sāntaḥ
prāgabhāvaḥ/ utpatteḥ pūrvaṃ kāryasya/ sādiranantaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvaḥ/
utpatteranantaraṃ kāryasya/ traikālikaḥ saṃsargāvacchinnābhāvaḥ
atyantābhāvaḥ/ yathā bhūtale ghaṭo nāsti iti/
children.translated_text: Prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) is beginningless and has an end — [it exists] before the origination of the effect. Destruction (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>) has a beginning and is endless — [it exists] after the origination of the effect. [Absolute absence is] existing in all three times

children.text:
tādātmyāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvo 'nyonyābhāvaḥ/ yathā
ghaṭaḥ paṭo na bhavatīti/
children.translated_text: An absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>). For example, 'the pot is not a cloth.'

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

atyantābhāvaṃ lakṣayati -
children.translated_text: He defines prior absence — 'beginningless,' etc. 'Having an end' is to avert over-pervasion in space and the like. 'Beginningless' is to avert over-pervasion in pots and the like. The counter-positive

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
prāgabhāve
pramāṇamāha - bhaviṣyatīti/ saṃsargeti/ tādātmyātiriktasaṃsargetyarthaḥ/
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorapi pratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhaḥ vartata iti
matābhiprāyeṇa traikāliketi viśeṣaṇam/ anyathā
anyonyābhāvavārakeṇaiva tayorvāraṇāt tadvyarthatāpatteḥ/ yadi
saṃsargāvacchinnetyādeḥ anyonyābhāvabhinnābhāva ityarthaḥ tadā
traikāliketi siddhānte 'pi sārthakaṃ traikālikatvamiha nityatvarūpam/
children.translated_text: He states the means of valid knowledge for prior absence — 'it will come into being,' etc. 'Relational' — the meaning is: a relational [absence] other than identity. Even in destruction and prior absence, the counter-positiveness is delimited by

children.text:
mūle bhūtale ghaṭo
nāstīti/ atra ghaṭābhāvāṃśe bhūtalasya viśeṣyatvaṃ sambandhaḥ,
ghaṭābhāvavat bhūtalam ityatra tu bhūtalāṃśe abhāvasya viśeṣaṇatvaṃ
saṃsarga iti vadatāṃ prācāṃ ayamabhiprāyaḥ - viśeṣyatvaviśeṣaṇatve
svarūpasambandhaviśeṣau na jñānīyaviṣayatāviśeṣau/ na ca
viśeṣaṇatākhyaḥ svarūpasambandha eka eva astu, 'bhūtale ghaṭo nāsti'
iti pratītau 'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat' iti pratītito vailakṣaṇyasya
viśeṣaṇatvāvacchinnādheyatāviṣayakatvakalpanenaiva nirvāhāditi
vācyam/ tādṛśapratītyoḥ vailakṣaṇyāya prathamāyāṃ
viśeṣaṇatvāvacchinnādheyatā sannikarṣaḥ, dvitīyāyāṃ viśeṣaṇatā
saṃsargaḥ iphayupeyate; kiṃ vā prathamāyāṃ viśeṣaṇatā saṃsargaḥ,
dvitīyāyāṃ viśeṣaṇatvāvacchinnādhāratā ityatra vinigamakasya
durlabhatvāt/ na ca tādṛśapratītyoḥ saṃsargāṃśe 'vilakṣaṇatve 'pi
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvabhedāt vailakṣaṇyopapattiḥ ityubhayatra
viśeṣaṇatāyā eva sambandhatāstviti vācyam/ tāvatāpi 'bhūtale ghaṭo
nāsti' 'bhūtalavān ghaṭābhāvaḥ' ityanayoḥ 'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat'
'ghaṭābhāve bhūtalam' ityanayośca pratītyoḥ vailakṣaṇyānirvrāhāt/
tasmāt viśeṣyatvaviśeṣaṇatvanāmakayoḥ ubhayoḥ
svarūpasambandhaviśeṣayoḥ saṃsargatā/ tathā ca 'bhūtalavān ghaṭābhāvaḥ'
ityatra ghaṭābhāvāṃśe bhūtalasya viśeṣaṇatvaṃ saṃsargaḥ, ghaṭābhāve
bhūtalam ityatra ca bhūtalāṃśe 'bhāvasya viśeṣyatāsaṃsargaḥ bhāsate/ sa
ca tatra abādhita iti abhramatvanirvāha iti saṅkṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the root text, 'there is no pot on the ground' — here, in the portion concerning the absence of the pot, the ground has qualificand-hood; the relation is [such that] 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot.' But in the [cognition] 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot,' the ground has the qualificand-hood [and the rest is the qualifier]. Now, is the relation in the absence-portion the same as the relation in the positive portion, or different? If the same, then since the conjunction with the ground that is the relation [through which] the pot exists on the ground is the same relation [through which] the absence is cognized, the absence of a pot on the ground would be: the absence of a pot through conjunction on the ground. But the presence of a pot through conjunction on the ground is what obstructs [the cognition of absence]. And accordingly, where there is a pot through conjunction, the cognition of absence does not arise. Where there is no pot through conjunction, the cognition of absence does arise. Therefore the relation in the absence-portion is the same relation [as that by which the positive entity would be present]. If different, then there would be the unwanted consequence that even where a pot exists through conjunction, the cognition of absence arises through another relation — and this would contradict experience. Therefore the first alternative is correct — this is the purport.

children.text:
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayoriva
ekapratiyogikayoḥ atyantābhāvānyonyābhāvayoḥ kim ekavidhatvaṃ,
netyāha - pratiyogiteti/ āropyeti/ prācīnamatābhiprāyeṇa/ atra
yathāyogaṃ pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmabhedaiva
saṃsargabhedo 'pyatyantābhāvabahutvaprayojakaḥ/
pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmabhedaḥ anyonyābhāvabahutvaprayojaka iti
draṣṭavyam/ tadeva darśayati-kevaleti/ kevaladevadattābhāvāt
viśiṣṭābhāvo 'tirikta ityanvayaḥ/ anyathā kevaladevadattavati 'daṇḍī
nāsti' iti pratyayānāpatteḥ/ ubhayābhāvasyātiriktatve pratītiṃ
pramāṇayati - ekasattve 'pīti/ ghaṭapaṭau dvau na sva ityādau ghaṭatvaṃ
paṭatvaṃ ubhayatvaṃ caitattritayaṃ pratiyogitāvacchedakam, kevalaghaṭavati
kevalapaṭavati yatkiñcidubhayavati ca tathā pratyayāt/
sambandhabhedenābhāvasyātiriktatvaṃ darśayati - saṃyogeneti/
sāmānyaviśeṣābhāvayoḥ bhedaṃ darśayati - tattaditi/ atirikta iti/
anyathā yatkiñcit ghaṭavati ghaṭo nāstīti pratyayāpatteḥ/
evamanyonyābhāvo 'pīti/ avacchedakabhedāt tattadghaṭabhedaḥ tataḥ
ubhayabhedaḥ ghaṭabhedaśca atirikta ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Just as destruction and prior absence having the same counter-positive are of one kind, are absolute absence and mutual absence also of one kind [when they have the same counter-positive]? He says no — 'the counter-positiveness,' etc. 'By superimposition' (<s>āropya</s>) —

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
"traikālikaḥ saṃsargābhāvaḥ atyantābhāvaḥ"iti
mūlam/ saṃsarṅgābhāva ityasya saṃsargāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāva
children.translated_text: The root text is: 'Absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>) is a relational absence existing in all three times.' The meaning of 'relational absence' (<s>saṃsargābhāva</s>) is: an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a relation other than identity.

children.text:
ityarthaḥ/ tatra
traikālikatvamātroktau anyonyābhāve 'tivyāptiḥ, tasyāpi
nityatvāt/ tadvāraṇāya saṃsargāvacchinnapratiyogitāka ityuktam/ na
ca saṃsargāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvaniveśe 'pi anyonyābhāvasya
tādātmyasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvāt
ativyāptitādavasthyamiti vācyam/ saṃsargābhāva ityanena
tādātmyātiraktisaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvasya
vivakṣitatvāt/ tadāha - tādātmyātiriktasaṃsargetyartha iti/
saṃsargābhāvatvamātroktau dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorativyāptiḥ, tadvāraṇāya
traikālika iti/ nanu samavāyena ghaṭādhikaraṇe saṃyogena
children.translated_text: — this is the meaning. There, if only 'existing in all three times' were stated, there would be over-pervasion in mutual absence, since that too is eternal. To avert that, 'relational, i.e., [an absence whose] counter-positiveness is delimited by a relation [other than identity]'

children.text:
ghaṭo nāsti,
saṃyogena ghaṭādhikaraṇe samavāyena ghaṭo nāsti iti
pratītyupapattaye saṃyogasambandhāvacchinnaghaṭābhāva -
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnaghaṭābhāvayorbhedo vaktavyaḥ/ tadarthaṃ
cātyantābhāvīyapratiyogitāyāṃ sambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ aṅgīkriyate/
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayostu tādṛśayuktyasambhavena tayoḥ
saṃsargāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvaṃ aprāmāṇikam/ tathā ca saṃsargābhāva
ityanenaiva dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorvāraṇasambhavāt traikāliketi
viśeṣaṇaṃ vyarthaṃ ityata āha - dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorapīti/
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayo atyantābhāvavirodhitāmate 'śyāmaghaṭe samavāyena
rakto nāsti' 'raktaghṭe samavāyena śyāmo nāsti' iti pratītau
prāgabhāvadhvaṃsayoreva viṣayatayā tayorapi
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvamastīti tanmatānusāreṇa
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorativyāptivāraṇāya traikāliketi viśeṣaṇamiti
bhāvaḥ/ anyatheti/ dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayoḥ
sambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvānaṅgīkāra ityarthaḥ/
anyonyābhāvavārakeṇaiveti/ anyonyābhāve 'tivyāpitavāraṇāya
upāttena
tādātmyātiriktasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvaviśeṣaṇenaivetyarthaḥ/
tayorvāraṇāt - dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorativyāptivāraṇasambhavāt/
tadvyarthatāpatteḥ - traikāliketi viśeṣaṇavaiyarthyāpatteḥ/ yadīti/
tathā ca saṃsargābhāva ityasya anyonyābhāvabhinnābhāva ityarthaḥ/
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorapi anyonyābhāvābhinnābhāvatvamastīti
tatrātivyāptivāraṇāya trekāliketi viśeṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/
anityapadārtheṣvapi
pūrvadinaśvodinādyadinākhyabhūtabhaviṣyadvartamānarūpakālatrayavṛttitvasambhavāt
traikāliketi viśeṣaṇe datte 'pi dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayoḥ ativyāptiḥ
tadavasthetyata āha - traikālikatvamiha nityatvarūpamiti/ nityatvaṃ ca
dhvaṃsāpratiyogitve sati prāgabhāvāpratiyogitvam/
dhvaṃsāpratiyogitvaniveśāt prāgabhāvanirāsaḥ/
prāgabhāvāpratiyogitvaniveśāt dhvaṃsanirāsaḥ/
children.translated_text: A pot does not exist [on the ground]; to account for the cognition 'a pot does not exist on the ground through conjunction' and 'a pot does not exist in the substratum of the pot through inherence,' a distinction must be stated between the absence of a pot delimited by the relation of conjunction and the absence of a pot delimited by the relation of inherence. For that purpose, delimitation by a relation is accepted in the counter-positiveness belonging to absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>). But in the case of destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) and prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>), since such reasoning is impossible, their having counter-positiveness delimited by a relational connection (<s>saṃsarga</s>) is without valid authority. And since the exclusion of destruction and prior absence is possible by the expression 'relational absence' (<s>saṃsargābhāva</s>) alone, the qualifier 'existing in all three times' (<s>traikālika</s>) would be purposeless — to address this he says 'even in the case of destruction and prior absence.' In the view that destruction and prior absence are opposed to absolute absence, in the cognitions 'in a dark pot, through inherence, a red [pot] does not exist' and 'in a red pot, through inherence, a dark [pot] does not exist,' since prior absence and destruction alone are the objects, they too have counter-positiveness delimited by the relation of inherence — following that view, the qualifier 'existing in all three times' is for preventing over-pervasion in destruction and prior absence, this is the purport. 'Otherwise' means: not accepting that destruction and prior absence have counter-positiveness delimited by a relation. 'By the very [qualifier] that excludes mutual absence' means: by the very qualifier of not having counter-positiveness delimited by a relation other than identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), which was adopted for preventing over-pervasion in mutual absence. 'Because of their exclusion' — because the exclusion of over-pervasion in destruction and prior absence is possible. 'Because of the unwanted consequence of its purposelessness' — because of the unwanted consequence of the purposelessness of the qualifier 'existing in all three times.' 'If' — and thus the meaning of 'relational absence' is: an absence different from mutual absence. Since destruction and prior absence also have the property of being absences different from mutual absence, the qualifier 'existing in all three times' is for preventing over-pervasion in them, this is the purport. Since even in non-eternal entities, existence in all three times is possible — in the form of past, future, and present time such as the previous day, the next day, and so forth — even when the qualifier 'existing in all three times' is given, the over-pervasion in destruction and prior absence remains as before. Therefore he says — 'Existence in all three times here means eternality.' And eternality is: not being the counter-positive of destruction while also not being the counter-positive of prior absence. By the inclusion of 'not being the counter-positive of destruction,' prior absence is excluded. By the inclusion of 'not being the counter-positive of prior absence,' destruction is excluded.

children.text:
nanu bhūtale ghaṭo
nāsti ityatra ghaṭābhāvāṃśe bhūtalasya viśeṣyatvaṃ saṃmbandhaḥ, bhūtalaṃ
ghaṭābhāvavat ityatra bhūtalāṃśe ghaṭābhāvasya viśeṣaṇatvaṃ sambandhaḥ
iti prācīnairuktaṃ na saṅgacchate/ bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat iti
pratītau bhūtalasya viśeṣyatayā ghaṭābhāvasya viśeṣaṇatayā na bhānāt
bhūtalāṃśe ghaṭābhāvasya viśeṣaṇatvaṃ sambandha ityukteḥ
saṅgatatve 'pi bhūtale ghaṭo nāsti iti pratītau ghaṭābhāvasya
viśeṣyatayā bhūtalasya ca prakāratayā bhānena bhūtalasya
viśeṣyatvābhāvena bhūtalasya viśeṣyatvaṃ sambandha
ityukterasaṅgatatvāt/ tathā
bādhitaviśeṣyatvarūpasaṃsargāvagāhitayā tādṛśapratīteḥ bhramatvāpattiḥ
ityataḥ prācīnānāmāśayaṃ vaktuṃ ārabhate - tatra ghaṭābhāvāṃśa
ityādinā/
children.translated_text: Objection: in 'on the ground, a pot does not exist,' the earlier logicians (<s>prācīna</s>) stated that in the portion of the absence of the pot, the qualifier-hood (<s>viśeṣyatva</s>) of the ground is the relation, and in 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot,' the qualifier-ness (<s>viśeṣaṇatva</s>) of the absence of the pot in the portion of the ground is the relation — this does not cohere. In the cognition 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot,' since the ground does not appear as the qualificand and the absence of the pot does not appear as the qualifier, the statement that the qualifier-ness of the absence of the pot in the portion of the ground is the relation — even if that coheres — in the cognition 'on the ground, a pot does not exist,' since the absence of the pot appears as the qualificand and the ground appears as a mode (<s>prakāra</s>), and since the ground does not have qualificand-hood, the statement that the qualificand-hood of the ground is the relation does not cohere. Moreover, since such a cognition would apprehend a relational connection in the form of sublated qualificand-hood, there would be the unwanted consequence that such cognition is erroneous. Therefore, he begins to state the intent of the earlier logicians — 'There, in the portion of the absence of the pot' and so forth.

children.text:
viśeṣyatvaviśeṣaṇatvesvarūpasambandhaviśeṣāviti/ yathā
daṇḍaviśiṣṭaḥ puruṣa ityatra daṇḍanirūpitaṃ viśeṣyatvaṃ puruṣagataṃ
daṇḍaviśiṣṭatvātmakaṃ daṇḍavayāvartyatvarūpaṃ vā ādhārapuruṣasvarūpaṃ
tathā bhūtalaniṣṭhaṃ ghaṭābhāvanirūpitaṃ viśeṣyatvamapi
ghaṭābhāvaviśiṣṭatvātmakaṃ ādhārabhūtalasvarūpam, yathā vā daṇḍaniṣṭhaṃ
viśeṣaṇatvaṃ ādheyadaṇḍasvarūpam tathā ghaṭābhāvaniṣṭhaṃ viśeṣaṇatvamapi
ghaṭābhāvasvarūpam/ sambandhatayocyamānaṃ viśeṣyatvaṃ viśeṣaṇatvaṃ ca na
jñānīyaviśeṣyatāprakāratākhyaviṣayatāviśeṣarūpam, kiṃ tu
svarūpasambandhātmakam/ tathā ca 'bhūtale ghaṭo nāsti' ityatra
viśeṣyatārūpaviṣayatāyāḥ bhūtale 'bhāve 'pi
svarūpasambandhātmakaviśeṣyatvasattvāt tena sambandhena ghaṭābhāvāṃśe
bhūtalasya prakāratayā bhānāt pratīteḥ pramātvameveti/ bhāvaḥ/ na ca
viśeṣaṇatākhya iti/ tathā ca bhūtalaghaṭābhāvayoḥ viśeṣaṇatvamiti
eka eva sambandhaḥ/ na ca ekasyaiva sambandhasya dvayorapi pratītyorviṣayatve
tayorvailakṣaṇyaṃ kathamiti vācyam/ sambandhaikye 'pi 'bhūtale ghaṭo
nāsti' iti pratītau viśeṣaṇatāsambandhāvacchinnādheyatvaṃ viṣayaḥ,
'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat' iti pratītau viśeṣaṇatvaṃ viṣaya ityevaṃ
pratītyoḥ vailakṣaṇyasya vaktuṃ śakyatvāditi śaṅkituḥ āśayaḥ/
samādhatte - tādṛśapratītyoriti/ prathamāyāmiti/ 'bhūtale ghaṭo
nāsti' iti pratītāvityarthaḥ/ dvitīyāyāmiti/ 'bhūtalaṃ
ghaṭābhāvavat' iti pratītāvityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Qualificand-hood and qualifier-hood are particular intrinsic relations (<s>svarūpasambandha</s>). Just as in 'a person with a stick,' the qualificand-hood determined by the stick, residing in the person, is identical with the property of being qualified by the stick, or is in the form of the containable-ness of the stick, which is the intrinsic nature of the substrate-person; similarly, the qualificand-hood residing in the ground, determined by the absence of the pot, is also identical with the property of being qualified by the absence of the pot, which is the intrinsic nature of the substrate-ground. And just as the qualifier-hood residing in the stick is the intrinsic nature of the contained-stick, similarly the qualifier-hood residing in the absence of the pot is also the intrinsic nature of the absence of the pot. The qualificand-hood and qualifier-hood spoken of as relations are not of the nature of particular objecthood (<s>viṣayatā</s>) called qualificand-ness and mode-ness belonging to cognition, but rather are of the nature of intrinsic relations. And thus, in 'on the ground, a pot does not exist,' even though the objecthood in the form of qualificand-ness does not belong to the ground in the absence-[portion], since qualificand-hood of the nature of intrinsic relation does exist, and since through that relation the ground appears as a mode in the portion of the absence of the pot, the cognition is indeed valid — this is the purport. 'Not the one called qualifier-ness' — and thus the qualifier-hood of the ground and the absence of the pot is one and the same relation. Nor should one say: how can there be a distinction between two cognitions when one and the same relation is the object in both? Even with the unity of relation, in the cognition 'on the ground, a pot does not exist' the object is contained-ness delimited by the relation of qualifier-ness, while in the cognition 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot' the object is qualifier-hood — thus the distinction of the cognitions can be stated. This is the intent of the objector. He resolves it — 'Of such cognitions.' 'In the first' means: in the cognition 'on the ground, a pot does not exist.' 'In the second' means: in the cognition 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot.'

children.text:
punaḥ śaṅkate - na ca
tādṛśapratītyoriti/ tathā cobhayatrāpi pratīntyoḥ viśeṣaṇatvanāmakaḥ
eka eva sambandhaḥ viṣayaḥ/ tathāpi 'bhūtale ghaṭo nāsti' iti pratītau
viśeṣyatākhyaviṣayatā ghaṭābhāvaniṣṭhā viśeṣaṇatākhyaviṣayatā
bhūtalaniṣṭhā/ 'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat' iti pratītau
viśeṣyatākhyaviṣayatā bhūtalaniṣṭhā viśeṣaṇatākhyaviṣayatā
ghaṭābhāvaniṣṭhā ityevaṃ viṣayatāvailakṣaṇyādeva
tādṛpratītyorvailakṣaṇyaṃ na sambandhavailakṣaṇyāditi śaṅkiturabhiprāyaḥ/
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvabhedāditi/
children.translated_text: He objects again — 'Nor of such cognitions.' And thus in both cognitions, one and the same relation called qualifier-hood is the object. Even so, in the cognition 'on the ground, a pot does not exist,' the objecthood called qualificand-ness resides in the absence of the pot and the objecthood called qualifier-ness resides in the ground. In the cognition 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot,' the objecthood called qualificand-ness resides in the ground and the objecthood called qualifier-ness resides in the absence of the pot. The intent of the objector is: the distinction of such cognitions is due to the difference in objecthood, not due to the difference in relation.

children.text:
viśeṣaṇatā -
viśeṣyatākhyaviṣayatāvailakṣaṇyādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Due to the difference of qualifier-qualificand relation' means: due to the difference of objecthood called qualifier-ness and qualificand-ness.

children.text:
samādhatte -
tāvatāpīti/ 'bhūtale ghaṭo nāsti' iti pratītau ghaṭābhāve
viśeṣyatākhyaviṣayatā bhūtale viśeṣaṇatākhyaviṣayatā 'bhūtalavān
ghaṭabhāvaḥ' ityatrāpi tathaiveti viṣayatāvailakṣaṇyābhāvāt tayoḥ
vailakṣaṇyaṃ na syāt/ evaṃ 'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat' iti pratītau
bhūlaniṣṭhā viśeṣyatākhyaviṣayatā, ghaṭābhāvaniṣṭhā
viśeṣaṇatākhyaviṣayatā, 'ghaṭābhāve bhūtalam' iti pratītāvapi
tathaiveti viṣayatāvailakṣaṇyābhāvāt tayoḥ vailakṣaṇyaṃ
durupapādamiti bhāvaḥ/ evaṃ ca svarūpātmakaviśeṣaṇatākhyamekameva
sambandhamaṅgīkṛtyaviṣayatāvailakṣaṇyāt pratītivailakṣaṇyasya
durupapādatvāt viśeṣaṇatvaṃ viśeṣyatvaṃ ceti
svarūpātmakasambandhadvayamaṅgīkṛtya sambandhavailakṣaṇyādeva
pratītivailakṣaṇya nirvoḍhavyamiti vadan upakrāntaṃ
pratīterabhramatvamupasaṃharati - tasmāditi/ tathā ca 'bhūtale ghaṭo
nāsti' ityatra ghaṭābhāve bhūtalasya viśeṣyatva saṃsargaḥ, 'bhūtalavān
ghaṭābhāvaḥ' ityatra ghaṭābhāve bhūtalasya viśeṣaṇatvaṃ sambandha
ityanayorvailakṣaṇyam/ 'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat' ityatra bhūtalāṃśe
ghaṭābhāvasya viśeṣaṇatvaṃ saṃsargaḥ/ 'ghaṭābhāve bhūtalam' ityatra
bhūtalāṃśe ghaṭābhāvasya viśeṣyatvaṃ sambandha iti tayoḥ
vailakṣaṇyamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: He resolves it — 'Even by that much.' In the cognition 'on the ground, a pot does not exist,' the objecthood called qualificand-ness belongs to the absence of the pot, and the objecthood called qualifier-ness belongs to the ground; but in 'the ground belongs to the absence of the pot' too, it is exactly the same — hence, due to the absence of difference in objecthood, their distinction would not hold. Similarly, in the cognition 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot,' the objecthood called qualificand-ness resides in the ground and the objecthood called qualifier-ness resides in the absence of the pot; but in the cognition 'the ground is in the absence of the pot' too, it is exactly the same — hence, due to the absence of difference in objecthood, their distinction is difficult to establish, this is the purport. And thus, if one accepts only one relation called qualifier-ness of the nature of intrinsic relation, the distinction of cognitions through difference in objecthood is difficult to establish; therefore, by accepting two intrinsic relations — qualifier-hood and qualificand-hood — and establishing the distinction of cognitions through the very difference in relations, he concludes with the non-erroneousness of the cognition that was undertaken — 'Therefore.' And thus, in 'on the ground, a pot does not exist,' the relational connection is qualificand-hood of the ground in the absence of the pot; in 'the ground belongs to the absence of the pot,' the relation is qualifier-hood of the ground in the absence of the pot — hence their distinction. In 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot,' the relational connection is qualifier-hood of the absence of the pot in the portion of the ground. In 'the ground is in the absence of the pot,' the relation is qualificand-hood of the absence of the pot in the portion of the ground — hence their distinction, this is the purport.

children.text:
nanvevamapi 'ghaṭābhāve
bhūtalam', 'bhūtale ghaṭo nāsti' ityanayoḥ
viśeṣyatāviṣayakatvāt vailakṣaṇyaṃ na syāt/ evaṃ 'bhūtalavān
ghaṭābhāvaḥ, 'bhūtalaṃ ghaṭābhāvavat' ityanayoḥ vailakṣaṇyaṃ na syāt,
ubhayatra viśeṣaṇatārūpasambandhasyaiva viṣayatvādityata āha - saṅkṣepa
iti/
viṣayatāviśeṣātmakaviśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvavailakṣaṇyasahakṛtasvarūpasambandhātmakaviśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvavailakṣaṇyena
pratītīnāṃ vailakṣaṇyamupapādanīyam/ yayoḥ pratītyoḥ
viṣayatāvailakṣaṇyaṃ nāsti tayoḥ sambandhavailakṣaṇyamasti/ yayoḥ
sambandhavailakṣaṇyaṃ nāsti, tayoḥ viṣayatāvailakṣaṇyamasti ityevaṃ
pratītīnāṃ vailakṣaṇyam/ tattassambandhasyābādhitatvāt pramātvaṃ
copapadyata iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: even so, since 'the ground belongs to the absence of the pot' and 'on the ground, a pot does not exist' both have qualificand-hood as their object, their distinction would not hold. Similarly, the distinction between 'the ground belongs to the absence of the pot' and 'the ground possesses the absence of the pot' would not hold, since in both cases only the relation in the form of qualifier-hood is the object. To this he says — 'In brief.' The distinction of cognitions must be established through the difference in qualifier-qualificand relation of the nature of intrinsic relation, assisted by the difference in qualifier-qualificand relation of the nature of particular objecthood. Where two cognitions lack difference in objecthood, there exists difference in relation. Where there is no difference in relation, there exists difference in objecthood — in this way the distinction of cognitions is [established]. And because the respective relation is unsublated, the validity [of each cognition] is also established — this is the purport.

children.text:
asya sandarbhasya bahuvāramāloḍane
kṛte 'pi tātparyājñānāt ācāryacaraṇān apṛccham/ te 'pi bahudhā
ālocya prakāśikāyāmīṣat śodhanaṃ kṛtvā tātparyamavarṇayan/
tathaivāhamatrālikham/
children.translated_text: Even after examining this passage many times, due to ignorance of its purport, I consulted my revered teacher. He too, after deliberating extensively and making slight corrections in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, explained the purport. I have written here exactly as he [explained].

children.text:
pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmabhedāt
pratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhabhedācca ekapratiyogiko 'pyatyantābhāvaḥ
bhidyate/ evaṃ pratiyogitāvacche dakadharmabhedāt
ekapratiyogiko 'pyanyonyābhāvaḥ bhidyata iti sodāharaṇaṃ
dīpikāyāṃ nirūpyate/ dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayostu tathā bhedo na
nirūpitaḥ, tatra kāraṇamāha - dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayoriti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ -
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayoḥ sambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvaṃ vā
kiñciddharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvaṃ vā nāṅgīkriyate/ ataḥ
ekapratiyogikānāṃ dhvaṃsānāṃ ekapratiyogikānāṃ prāgabhāvānāṃ
caikavidhatvameva/ atyantānyonyābhāvayostu tadaṅgīkārāt
ekapratiyogikānāmatyantābhāvānāṃ
bhinnabhinnadharmasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatve
pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmabhedāt
pratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhabhedācca bhinnatvameva/ ekapratiyogikānāṃ
anyonyābhāvānāṃ yadyapi sambandhabhedāt bhedo vaktumaśakyaḥ,
tādātmyasyaiva pratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhatvāt/ tathāpi
pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmabhedāt bhedo vaktuṃ śakyata iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Due to the difference in the property that delimits counter-positiveness and due to the difference in the relation that delimits counter-positiveness, even absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>) having a single counter-positive is differentiated. Similarly, due to the difference in the property that delimits counter-positiveness, even mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>) having a single counter-positive is differentiated — this is explained with examples in the <s>Dīpikā</s>. But such differentiation of destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) and prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) has not been explained; he states the reason for this — 'Of destruction and prior absence.' The purport is this: it is not accepted that destruction and prior absence have counter-positiveness delimited by a relation, nor counter-positiveness delimited by some property. Therefore, destructions having a single counter-positive and prior absences having a single counter-positive are each of one kind only. But since this is accepted for absolute absence and mutual absence, absolute absences having a single counter-positive, having counter-positiveness delimited by different properties and different relations, are indeed distinct due to the difference in the property delimiting counter-positiveness and due to the difference in the relation delimiting counter-positiveness. As for mutual absences having a single counter-positive, although their differentiation cannot be stated through the difference in relation — since identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) alone is the relation delimiting counter-positiveness — nevertheless, differentiation can be stated through the difference in the property delimiting counter-positiveness, this is the purport.

children.text:
aropyeti
prācīnamatābhiprāyeṇeti/ saṃsargāropajanya pratītiviṣayo 'bhāvaḥ
atyantābhāvaḥ/ saṃsargāropo nāma tādātmyātiriktasambandhena
pratiyogyāropa iti pracīnā āhuḥ/ tathā
cātyantābhāvabuddhijanakāropaviṣayasaṃyogasamavāyādisambandhabhedāt
atyantābhāvabheda iti āropyasaṃsargabhedāditi dīpikāyā artha
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Of what is superimposed' — this is according to the view of the earlier logicians. The absence that is the object of a cognition generated by the superimposition of a relational connection is absolute absence. The earlier logicians say that the superimposition of a relational connection means the superimposition of the counter-positive through a relation other than identity. And thus, due to the difference in the relations — conjunction, inherence, and the like — that are the relational connections which are the objects of the superimposition that generates the cognition of absolute absence, the absolute absence is differentiated — this is the meaning of 'due to the difference in the superimposed relational connection' in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, this is the purport.

children.text:
navīnāstu -
pratiyogyāropasyābhāvabuddhihetutāyāḥ niryuktikatvāt
tādātmyātiriktasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvatvameva
saṃsargābhāvatvam, traikālikatvaviśeṣitaṃ
tadevātyantābhāvatvamityāhuḥ/ tanmatānusāreṇa tu
pratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhabhedādatyantābhāvabheda ityūhmam/
children.translated_text: The Navya-logicians, however, [hold that] since the causal efficacy of the superimposition of the counter-positive in generating the cognition of absence is without valid reasoning, being an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a relation other than identity is itself what constitutes being a relational absence (<s>saṃsargābhāva</s>); and that very [property], qualified by existence in all three times, is what constitutes being an absolute absence — so they say. Following their view, the differentiation of absolute absence is due to the difference in the relation delimiting counter-positiveness — this I understand.

children.text:
pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmabheda iti tādātmyarūpasya
pratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhasya ekavidhatvāt
pratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhabhedaḥ nānyonyābhāvabhedaprayojakatayā
ukta ityavadheyam/ kevaladevadattābhāvāditi/ devadattābhāvasya
daṇḍaviśiṣṭadevadattābhāvasya ca yadyapi devadatta eka eva pratiyogī,
tathāpi ekatra devadattatvaṃ pratiyogitāvacchedakam, anyatra daṇḍa iti
pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmabhedāt devadattābhāva-daṇḍyabhāvayorbhedaḥ/
yadi tu tayorbhedo nāṅgīkriyate tarhi kevaladevadattavati bhūtale
devadatto nāsti iti pratītiḥ yathā na bhavati, tathā daṇḍī nāstīti
pratītirapi na bhavet/ bhavati tu
children.translated_text: The difference in the property delimiting the counter-positiveness (pratiyogitāvacchedakadharma) — since the relation delimiting the counter-positiveness that has the nature of identity (tādātmya) is of one kind, the difference in the relation delimiting the counter-positiveness is not stated as being the cause of differentiation of mutual absence (anyonyābhāva) — this should be noted. Regarding 'from the mere absence of <s>Devadatta</s>' — although in both the absence of <s>Devadatta</s> and the absence of <s>Devadatta</s>-qualified-by-a-stick, <s>Devadatta</s> alone is the counter-positive (pratiyogin), nevertheless in one case <s>Devadatta</s>-ness is the delimitor of counter-positiveness, while in the other the stick is, and due to this difference in the property delimiting counter-positiveness, there is a distinction between the absence-of-<s>Devadatta</s> and the absence-of-the-stick-bearer. If, however, the distinction between these two is not accepted, then just as in a ground possessing only <s>Devadatta</s> without a stick, the cognition '<s>Devadatta</s> is not here' does not arise, so too the cognition 'the stick-bearer is not here' should not arise. But such

children.text:
tādṛśī pratītiḥ/ ataḥ
kevaladevadattābhāvāt daṇḍaviśiṣṭadevadattābhāvo 'tirikta iti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: a cognition does arise. Therefore, the absence of <s>Devadatta</s>-qualified-by-a-stick is distinct from the mere absence of <s>Devadatta</s> — this is the purport.

children.text:
ghaṭapaṭau dvau na sta
iti/ kevalaghaṭavati vā kevalapaṭavati vā pradeśe 'ghaṭapaṭau dvau na
staḥ' iti pratītiḥ bhavati, 'ghaṭo nāsti' iti vā 'paṭo nāsti'
iti vā pratītiḥ na bhavati/ ataḥ kevalaghaṭābhāvāt
kevalapaṭābhāvācca atiriktatayā ghaṭapaṭobhayābhāvaḥ svīkartavyaḥ/
'ghaṭapaṭau na sta' ityatra ghaṭatvamātraṃ vā paṭatvamātraṃ vā ubhayatvamātraṃ
vā
children.translated_text: 'The pot and the cloth, the two, do not exist' — in a place possessing only a pot or only a cloth, the cognition 'the pot and the cloth, the two, do not exist' arises, but the cognition 'the pot does not exist' or 'the cloth does not exist' does not arise. Therefore, the collective absence of both pot and cloth (<s>ghaṭapaṭobhayābhāva</s>) must be accepted as distinct from the mere absence of pot and the mere absence of cloth. In the statement 'the pot and cloth do not exist,' neither pot-ness alone, nor cloth-ness alone, nor both-ness alone

children.text:
na
pratiyogitāvacchedakam, pratiyogitāvacchedakaviśiṣṭapratiyoginā
sākamabhāvasya virodhāt ghaṭamātravati bhūtale
pratiyogitāvacchedakaghaṭatvaviśiṣṭaghaṭarūpavirodhisattvena 'ghaṭapaṭau
na staḥ' ityākārakobhayābhāvāvagāhipratītyanupapatteḥ/ tathākevalapaṭavati ghaṭapaṭātiriktayatkiñcidubhayavati ca pradeśe
paṭatvaviśiṣṭasya ubhayatvaviśiṣṭasya ca virodhinaḥ sattvena
tādṛśapratītiḥ na syāt/ ataḥ ghaṭatvaṃ paṭatvaṃ ubhayatvaṃ ceti tritayaṃ
pratiyogitāvacchedakam/
pratiyogitāvacchedakatāparyāptyadhikaraṇadharmavacchinnapratiyoginā
sākamabhāvasya virodha iti tādṛśatritayāvacchinna-ghaṭapaṭobhayameva
ghaṭapaṭobhayābhāvasya virodhīti ghaṭapaṭobhayavatyeva pradeśe
'ghaṭapaṭau na sta' iti pratītirna bhavati, kevalaghaṭādimati tu
bhavitumarhatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: is the delimitor of counter-positiveness, because absence is incompatible with a counter-positive qualified by the delimitor of counter-positiveness — since in a ground possessing only a pot, there being present an entity in the form of a pot qualified by pot-ness which is the delimitor of counter-positiveness and which is the incompatible counterpart, the cognition of the form 'the pot and cloth do not exist' apprehending collective absence would be inexplicable. Similarly, in a place possessing only cloth, or in a place possessing both something other than pot-and-cloth as well as something else, since entities incompatible with what is qualified by cloth-ness and what is qualified by both-ness would be present, such a cognition would not arise. Therefore, the triad of pot-ness, cloth-ness, and both-ness constitutes the delimitor of counter-positiveness. Since absence is incompatible with a counter-positive delimited by a property residing in the locus that is sufficient for the delimitation of counter-positiveness, only the combination of pot-and-cloth delimited by that triad is the incompatible counterpart of the collective absence of pot-and-cloth — thus in a place possessing both pot and cloth, the cognition 'the pot and cloth do not exist' does not arise, but in a place possessing only a pot and the like, it can arise — this is the purport.

children.text:
saṃyogenetīti/ tathā ca
saṃyogasambandhāvacchiddhaghaṭābhāvāt
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnaghaṭābhāvo 'nya iti svīkaraṇīyam/ anyathā
saṃyogena ghaṭavati bhūtale saṃyogena ghaṭo nāstīti pratītiḥ yathā
na bhavati tathā samavāyena ghaṭo nāstī ti pratītirapi na syāt/ evaṃ
tatraiva samavāyena ghaṭo nāstīti pratītiḥ yathā bhavati tathā
saṃyogena ghaṭo nāstīti pratītirapi syāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'By the relation of contact (<s>saṃyoga</s>)' — accordingly, the absence of a pot delimited by the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) must be accepted as different from the absence of a pot delimited by the relation of contact (<s>saṃyoga</s>). Otherwise, in a ground possessing a pot by contact, just as the cognition 'the pot is not here by contact' does not arise, so too the cognition 'the pot is not here by inherence' should not arise either. Similarly, just as the cognition 'the pot is not here by inherence' does arise there, so too the cognition 'the pot is not here by contact' should also arise — this is the purport.

children.text:
sāmānyaviśeṣābhāyoriti/
sāmānyābhāvaviśeṣābhāvayorityarthaḥ/
sāmānyadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ sāmānyābhāvaḥ/
viśeṣadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ viśeṣābhāvaḥ/ 'ghaṭo nāsti'
iti pratītisiddhaḥ ghaṭatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ
sāmānyābhāvaḥ/ 'nīlaghaṭo nāsti', 'raktaghaṭo nāsti'
ityādipratītisiddhaḥ nīlaghaṭatvādyavacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ
viśeṣābhāvaḥ/ yadi sāmānyābhāvo nātiriktaḥ tadā nīlaghaṭavati
bhūtale raktaghaṭābhāvasya sattvāt raktaghaṭābhāvarūpasya
ghaṭasāmānyābhāvasyāpi sattvamāvaśyakamiti 'ghaṭo nāsti' iti
ghaṭasāmānyābhāvāvagāhinī pratītiḥ syāt/
sāmānyābhāvasyātiriktatve tu nīlaghaṭavati bhūtale raktaghaṭābhāvasya
sattve 'pi ghaṭasāmānyābhāvasyāsattvāt na tādṛśī pratītiriti vaktuṃ
śakyate/ ataḥ viśeṣābhāvātiriktaḥ sāmānyābhāvo 'ṅgīkaraṇīya
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Of general absence and particular absence' — the meaning is: of general absence (<s>sāmānyābhāva</s>) and particular absence (<s>viśeṣābhāva</s>). An absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a general property is general absence. An absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a particular property is particular absence. The absence with counter-positiveness delimited by pot-ness, established by the cognition 'the pot does not exist,' is general absence. The absence with counter-positiveness delimited by blue-pot-ness and so forth, established by cognitions such as 'the blue pot does not exist' or 'the red pot does not exist,' is particular absence. If general absence were not distinct, then in a ground possessing a blue pot, since the absence of a red pot would be present, the general absence of pot in the form of the absence of a red pot would also necessarily be present, and thus the cognition 'the pot does not exist' apprehending the general absence of pot would arise. But if general absence is accepted as distinct, then even though the absence of a red pot is present in a ground possessing a blue pot, since the general absence of pot is not present, it can be said that such a cognition does not arise. Therefore, general absence must be accepted as distinct from particular absence — this is the purport.

children.text:
avacchedakabhedāditi/ nīlaghaṭabhedasya
nīlaghaṭatvaṃ pratiyogitāvacchedakam, ghaṭapaṭobhayabhedasya
ghaṭapaṭobhayatvaṃ pratiyogitāvacchadedakam ghaṭabhedasya ghaṭatvaṃ
pratiyogitāvacchedakam ityevaṃ pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmabhedāt
'nāyaṃ nīlaghaṭaḥ' 'nemau ghaṭapaṭau' 'nāyaṃ ghaṭaḥ'
ityādipratītisiddhānāṃ
nīlaghaṭabhedaghaṭapaṭobhayabheda-ghaṭabhedādīnāṃ bhinnatvaṃ vaktavyamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Due to difference in the delimitor' — blue-pot-ness is the delimitor of counter-positiveness of the difference from a blue pot; the both-ness of pot-and-cloth is the delimitor of counter-positiveness of the difference from the pot-and-cloth combination; pot-ness is the delimitor of counter-positiveness of the difference from a pot — thus due to the difference in the property delimiting counter-positiveness, the distinctness of the difference from a blue pot, the difference from the pot-and-cloth combination, the difference from a pot, and so forth, established by cognitions such as 'this is not a blue pot,' 'these are not the pot and cloth,' 'this is not a pot,' must be stated — this is the meaning.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnābhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Absence delimited by a property residing in a different locus (<s>vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnābhāva</s>)

children.text:
'ghaṭatvena paṭo
nāsti' iti pratītyā vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnābhāvo nāṅgīkriyate/
paṭe ghaṭatvaṃ nāstīti tadarthaḥ/ atiriktatve sa kevalānvayī/
children.translated_text: By the cognition 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness,' an absence delimited by a property residing in a different locus is not accepted. The meaning of that is: pot-ness does not exist in the cloth. If it were accepted as distinct, it would be invariably positive (<s>kevalānvayī</s>).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
prasaṅgādāha -
ghaṭatveneti/ nāṅgīkriyata iti/ abhāvadhiyaḥ
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhimaryādopabṛṃhitatayā 'ghaṭatvena paṭo
nāsti' ityādipratyayasya viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyānavagāhinaḥ ghaṭatvādeḥ
children.translated_text: Introducing the topic incidentally, he says — 'by pot-ness' and so on. 'Is not accepted' — because the cognition of absence follows the rule of apprehending the qualification of the qualified (<s>viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭya</s>), and since the cognition 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness' does not apprehend the qualification of the qualified, pot-ness and the like

children.text:
pratiyogitāvacchedakatvavyavasthāpakatvābhāvena
vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnābhāve mānābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/ nanu tarhi
tādṛśapratyayasya kā gatiriti ata āhapaṭa iti/ nanu 'ghaṭatvena paṭo
nāsti' iti pratīteḥ paṭādhikaraṇakaghaṭatvābhāvāvagāhitvaṃ na
sambhavati/ asati bādhake tacchabdollekhipratīteḥ
tacchabdapratipādyārthaviṣayakatvaparityāgāyogāt
paṭādhikaraṇakaghaṭatvābhāvasya 'ghaṭatvena paṭo nāsti' iti śabdāt
kathamapyapratīteḥ/ kintu avacchinnapratiyogitākatvasambandhena abhāvāṃśe
svātantryeṇa ghaṭatvāvagāhitvameva/ 'abhāvabuddhiḥ
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhimaryādāṃ nātiśete' iti niyamastu na/
evaṃ ca vyadhikaraṇadharmavacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ sapramāṇa iti
cet - astu tarhi atiriktatvaṃ tasyetyāha - atiriktatva iti/ saḥ -
vyadhikaraṇadharmavacchinnapratiyogitākaḥ/ kevalānvayīti/
pratiyogitāvacchedakāvacchinnapratiyogirūpavirodhavirahāditi
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: cannot serve as establishing the status of delimitor of counter-positiveness, and hence there is no means of proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for an absence delimited by a property residing in a different locus — this is the purport. Now then, what is the explanation of such a cognition? To this he says — 'the cloth' and so on. But the cognition 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness' cannot be understood as apprehending the absence of pot-ness residing in the cloth. In the absence of a sublating cognition, since a cognition expressed by a word cannot be divested of having as its object the meaning conveyed by that word, and since the absence of pot-ness residing in the cloth is in no way cognized from the expression 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness' — rather, it is only the apprehension of pot-ness independently in the absence-portion through the relation of being the delimitor of counter-positiveness. The rule that 'the cognition of absence does not exceed the limit of apprehending the qualification of the qualified' simply does not hold. If so, then an absence with counter-positiveness delimited by a property residing in a different locus would have valid means of proof — to this he says — 'if it were distinct' and so on. That one — possessing counter-positiveness delimited by a property residing in a different locus — would be invariably positive (<s>kevalānvayī</s>), because there is no incompatible counterpart in the form of a counter-positive delimited by the delimitor of counter-positiveness — this is the purport.
