children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu abhāvānāṃ
anekavidhatvanirūpaṇaprasaṅge vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnābhāvakhaṇḍanaṃ
ayuktamityata āha - prasaṅgāditi/ smṛtasya
upekṣānarhatvarūpaprasaṅgasaṅgatyetyarthaḥ/
pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmasaṃbandhabhedādiva
pratiyogitāvacchedakadharmagatāt
pratiyogitāsāmānādhikaraṇyatadasamānādhikaraṇyabhedādapi abhāvabhedaḥ
bhavati, tathaiva
vyadhikaraṇasamānādhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākayorabhāvayorbhedasiddhedityāśaṅkya
vyadhikaraṇadharmavacchinnābhāva eva nāsti, kutastadarthaṃ
bhedakāntarānveṣaṇamityāśayena
vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnābhāvakhaṇḍanamapi saṅgatameva iti tu
nṛsiṃhaśāstricaraṇāḥ prāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: Objecting that refuting the absence delimited by a property residing in a different locus is inappropriate in the context of establishing the many varieties of absence, he says — 'incidentally' and so on. The meaning is: it is connected with the incidental relevance in the form of something recalled that ought not to be disregarded. Just as difference of absence arises from difference in the relation of the property delimiting counter-positiveness, so too from the difference of co-locatedness and non-co-locatedness with respect to the property characterizing counter-positiveness, difference of absence would obtain — and thus anticipating that the distinction between absences with counter-positiveness delimited by a property residing in a different locus and by a property residing in the same locus would be established, the refutation is offered with the intent that the absence delimited by a property residing in a different locus simply does not exist, so why search for an additional differentiator for its sake — thus the refutation of absence delimited by a property in a different locus is indeed appropriate. Thus declare the followers of <s>Nṛsiṃha Śāstri</s>.

children.text:
dīpikāyām ghaṭatvena paṭo nāstītyādi/
ghaṭatvena paṭo nāstīti pratītyā siddhyatītyuktaḥ
vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnābhāvo nāsmābhiraṅgīkriyate/ tādṛśapratīteḥ
paṭānuyogikaghaṭatvābhāvaviṣayakatvena
ghaṭatvāvacchinnapaṭaniṣṭhapratiyogitānirūpakābhāvaviṣayakatvādityarthaḥ/
atra saundaḍopādhyāyāḥ - abhāvaḥ dvividhaḥ -
vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākaḥ
samānādhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākaśceti/
pratiyogitāśrayāvṛttirdharmaḥ vyadhikaraṇadharmaḥ/
pratiyogitāśrayavṛttirdharmaḥ samānādhikaraṇadharmaḥ/ 'ghaṭatvena paṭo
nāsti' ityatra pratiyogitāśrayaḥ paṭaḥ tadavṛttirdharmaḥ ghaṭatvaṃ
tadavacchinnā yā paṭaniṣṭhā pratiyogitā tannirūpako 'bhāvaḥ
vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnābhāvaḥ/ 'ghaṭo nāsti' ityatra
pratiyogitāśrayaḥ ghaṭaḥ tadvṛttidharmaḥ ghaṭatvam
tadavacchinnaghaṭaniṣṭhapratiyogitāko 'bhāvaḥ
samānādhikaraṇardhmavacchinnābhāvaḥ ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness' and so on. The absence delimited by a property residing in a different locus, stated as established by the cognition 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness,' is not accepted by us, because such a cognition has as its object the absence of pot-ness which has the cloth as its locus, and thus has as its object an absence whose counter-positiveness residing in the cloth is not determined by pot-ness — this is the meaning. Here the <s>Sauṇḍa Upādhyāyas</s> hold: absence is of two kinds — that whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a property residing in a different locus, and that whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a property residing in the same locus. A property that does not reside in the locus of the counter-positiveness is a property residing in a different locus. A property that resides in the locus of the counter-positiveness is a property residing in the same locus. In 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness,' the locus of counter-positiveness is the cloth; the property not residing therein is pot-ness; the absence determined by the counter-positiveness residing in the cloth that is delimited by that is an absence delimited by a property in a different locus. In 'the pot does not exist,' the locus of counter-positiveness is the pot; the property residing therein is pot-ness; the absence having counter-positiveness residing in the pot delimited by that is an absence delimited by a property residing in the same locus — thus they say.

children.text:
tatkhaṇḍanaprakāramāha prakāśikāyām -
abhāvadhiya iti/ abhāvabuddhirviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhimaryādāṃ
nātiśete'
children.translated_text: The method of refutation is stated in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> — 'of the cognition of absence' and so on. 'The cognition of absence does not exceed the limit of apprehending the qualification of the qualified' —

children.text:
itiniyamāt abhāvatvaprakārakabuddhiḥ sarvāpi
pratiyogitāvacchedakaviśiṣṭapratiyogivaiśiṣṭyamabhāve 'vagāhata
iti vaktavyam/ prakṛte ghaṭatvaviśiṣṭapaṭāprasiddhyā
tadvaiśiṣṭyāvagāhitvaṃ na sambhavatīti 'ghaṭatvena paṭo nāsti' iti
pratītiḥ na ghaṭatvāvacchinnapaṭaniṣṭhapratiyogitākābhāvaṃ
viṣayīkaroti/ api tu śaśaśṛṅgaṃ nāstīti pratītiḥ yathā śṛṅge
śaśīyatvābhāvaṃ viṣayīkaroti tathā ghaṭatvena paṭo nāstīti
pratītirapi paṭe ghaṭatvābhāvamavagāhate/ ataḥ uktapratītiḥ
vyadhikaraṇadharmasya pratiyogitāvacchedakatvasādhanāya nālamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: due to this rule, every cognition having absence as its qualifier must be said to apprehend in the absence the qualification of a counter-positive qualified by the delimitor of counter-positiveness. In the present case, since a cloth qualified by pot-ness is not well-established, the apprehension of its qualification is not possible, and therefore the cognition 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness' does not take as its object an absence whose counter-positiveness resides in the cloth and is delimited by pot-ness. Rather, just as the cognition 'the hare's horn does not exist' takes as its object the absence of hare-ness in the horn, so too the cognition 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness' apprehends the absence of pot-ness in the cloth. Therefore, the said cognition is insufficient for establishing that a property residing in a different locus can serve as a delimitor of counter-positiveness — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu ghaṭatvenetyādi/
asati bādhake
tacchabdollikhitapratīntestacchabdapratipādyārthaviṣayakatvamiti niyamāt
'ghaṭatvena paṭo nāsti' iti śabdāt yor'thaḥ pratipādyate sa eva
tadullikhatapratītāvapi viṣaya iti vācyam/ tatra tādṛśaśabdāt
ghaṭatvāvacchinnapaṭaniṣṭhapratiyogitākābhāvasyaiva pratipatteḥ
tādṛśaśabdollikhitapratīterapi tadviṣayakatvameva yuktamiti bhāvaḥ/
kintu iti/ ghaṭatvenetyatra tṛtīyāyāḥ
avacchinnapratiyogitākatvamarthaḥ, tasyābhāve 'nvaya ityabhiprāyaḥ/
vibhaktyartharūpeṇa sambandhenānvaya iṣṭa eva/ ata eva dinakaryām
'bhūtale ghaṭa' ityādau ādheyatāsaṃsargeṇāpi ghaṭabhūtalayoranvayāt
sākṣādityasyāpi vyutpattau niveśāt"ityuktam/ tatra rāmarudrīye
-"yadyapi ghaṭe bhūtalavṛttitvaprakārakabodhasvīkāreṇaivopapattau
ādheyatāsambandhena bhūtalasyāpi ghaṭe prakāratvopagamo 'nucitaḥ,
padārthasya saṃsargavidhayā bhānānaṅgīkārāt/ tathāpi 'bhūtale ghaṭa'
iti vākyajajñānānantaraṃ ghaṭo bhūtalīyo na veti
saṃśayānutpādasyāpyanubhavasiddhatayā vibhaktyarthasya saṃsargavidhayāpi
bhānamādṛtamṛ"ityuktam/ etena
avacchinnapratiyogitākatvasya tṛtīyāvibhaktyarthatvāt tasya prakāratayā
bhānasyaivocitatvāt
children.translated_text: Now, 'by pot-ness' and so on. In the absence of a sublating cognition, since there is a rule that a cognition expressed by a given word has as its object the meaning conveyed by that word, whatever meaning is conveyed by the expression 'the cloth does not exist as possessing pot-ness' is indeed the object also of the cognition expressed thereby — this must be said. And from such an expression, since what is cognized is precisely the absence whose counter-positiveness resides in the cloth and is delimited by pot-ness, it is proper that the cognition expressed by such an expression also has that as its object — this is the purport. 'But' — the meaning of the instrumental case in 'by pot-ness' is the relation of being the delimitor of counter-positiveness, and the intention is that it connects with the absence-portion. The connection through the relation in the form of the case-ending meaning is indeed accepted. For this very reason, in the <s>Dīnakarī</s>, regarding 'on the ground, a pot' and so forth, it is stated that 'since even through the relation of being-the-contained (<s>ādheyatā</s>), there is a connection between pot and ground, the word directly (<s>sākṣāt</s>) is also included in the derivation.' There in the <s>Rāmarudrī</s> it is stated: 'Although by accepting a cognition with ground-residing-ness as a qualifier in the pot, the explanation is possible, and thus accepting ground also as a qualifier in the pot through the relation of being-the-contained is improper, since we do not accept that an entity appears in the mode of a relational connection; nevertheless, since the non-arising of the doubt whether the pot is on the ground or not after the verbal cognition from on the ground, a pot is established by experience, the appearing of the case-ending meaning also in the mode of a relational connection is accepted.' By this,

children.text:
avacchinnapratiyogitākatvasambandhenetyuktirna yukteti śaṅkā
apastā/
children.translated_text: the objection that the statement 'through the relation of being the delimitor of counter-positiveness' is improper — since the relation of being the delimitor of counter-positiveness is the meaning of the instrumental case-ending and it is fitting that it appears only as a qualifier — is refuted.

children.text:
nanu 'ghaṭatvena ghaṭo nāsti'
ityādāvayuktanyāne ghaṭatvasya
avacchinnapratiyogitākatvasambandhenābhāve 'nvayo vaktavyaḥ/ tathā ca ghaṭe
ghaṭatvasyānanvayāt ghaṭatvaviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhitvaṃ nāstīti
'abhāvabuddhirviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhitvamaryādāṃ nātiśete' iti
niyamasya bhaṅga itya āha - abhāvabuddhiriti/ 'ghaṭatvena ghaṭo
nāsti' ityākārakasyābhāvapratyayasyānubhavikatayā yatra
pratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ bhāsate
tadviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhitvamabhāvabuddheriti niyamāsambhavaḥ/ tathā ca
tādṛśaniyamabhaṅgaiṣṭa eva iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: But in cases such as 'a pot does not exist by pot-ness,' when in a non-standard inference one must state the positive concomitance of pot-ness with absence through the relation of being the delimitor of counter-positiveness, then since pot-ness does not positively pervade the pot, the property of apprehending the qualifiedness qualified by it does not exist — and thus the rule that 'the cognition of absence does not exceed the boundary of apprehending qualifiedness qualified [by the delimitor]' would be violated. To this he says — 'the cognition of absence' etc. In the experience of the cognition of absence having the form 'a pot does not exist by pot-ness,' wherever the delimitor of counter-positiveness appears, the cognition of absence consists in apprehending qualifiedness qualified by that — hence such a rule is impossible. And accordingly, the violation of such a rule is itself the desired [conclusion] — this is the purport.

children.text:
astu tarhīti/ tathā ca ghaṭatvena ghaṭo
nāstīti pratītyā yathā svātantryeṇa bhāsamāne ghaṭatvādau
pratiyogitāvacchedakatvāvagāhanāt pratiyogiviśeṣaṇatāpannasyaiva
pratiyogitāvacchedakatvamiti niyamo nāstīti
samānādhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ sidhyati, tathaiva
ghaṭatvena paṭo nāstīti pratītyāpi vyadhikaraṇe
ghaṭatve 'vacchedakatvāvagāhanāt
vyadhikaraṇadharmāvacchinnāpratiyogitākābhāvo 'pi sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Let it be so, then' — and accordingly, just as from the cognition 'a pot does not exist by pot-ness,' since the delimitor of counter-positiveness is apprehended in pot-ness and the like that appear independently, the rule that only what has attained the status of qualifier of the counter-positive has the delimitor of counter-positiveness does not hold — and thus an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a property co-located [with the counter-positive] is established; similarly, from the cognition 'a cloth does not exist by pot-ness,' since the delimitor of counter-positiveness is apprehended in pot-ness which is in a different locus, an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a property [residing] in a different locus is also established — this is the purport.

children.text:
virodhivirahāditi/
pratiyogitāvacchedakaviśiṣṭaḥ pratiyogiyogitāśrayaḥ abhāvasya
virodhī/ ghaṭatvaviśiṣṭasya ghaṭasya sattveghaṭatvāvacchinnaghaṭābhāvaḥ na
sambhavati/ ghaṭaśūnyasthala eva tādṛśābhāva iti sa na kevalānvayī/
ghaṭatvena paṭābhāvastu ghaṭaviśiṣṭapaṭarūpavirodhyaprasiddhyā
tadabhāvāt paṭavati paṭaśūnye ca sarvatrāstīti
children.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of the contradictory' — the contradictory of the absence is the locus of the counter-positive qualified by the delimitor of counter-positiveness. When a pot qualified by pot-ness exists, the absence of the pot delimited by pot-ness is not possible. Such an absence exists only in a locus devoid of the pot — hence it is not <s>kevalānvayī</s> (purely positive). But the absence of cloth by pot-ness, since the contradictory in the form of cloth qualified by pot is not established,

children.text: kevalānvayīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: and [hence that absence] is absent [nowhere] — it exists everywhere, in what possesses cloth and in what is devoid of cloth — therefore it is <s>kevalānvayī</s> (purely positive). This is the purport.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: sāmayikābhāvasyātiriktatvakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of the claim that <s>sāmayikābhāva</s> (temporal absence) is a distinct [category]

children.text:
sāmayikābhāvo 'pi
atyantābhāva eva samayaviśeṣe pratīyamānaḥ/ ghaṭābhāvavati ghaṭānayane
atyantābhāvasya anyatra gamanābhāve 'pi apratīteḥ, ghaṭāpasaraṇe sati
pratīteḥ, bhūtalaghaṭasaṃyogaprāgabhāvadhvaṃsayoḥ
ghaṭatyantābhāvapratītiniyāmakatvaṃ kalpyate/ ghaṭavati
tatsaṃyogaprāgabhāvadhvaṃsayorasattvādeva atyantābhāvasyāpratītiḥ/
ghaṭāpasaraṇe tu saṃyogadhvaṃsasya sattvāt pratītiriti/
children.translated_text: <s>Sāmayikābhāva</s> (temporal absence) too is just <s>atyantābhāva</s> (absolute absence), being cognized at a particular time. In a locus possessing the absence of a pot, when the pot is brought there, even though the absolute absence has not gone elsewhere, since it is not cognized [at that time], and since it is cognized when the pot is removed — it is postulated that the <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence) and <s>dhvaṃsa</s> (destruction) of the conjunction of the ground with the pot are the determinants of the cognition of the absolute absence of the pot. In a locus possessing the pot, since the prior absence and destruction of that conjunction do not obtain, the absolute absence is simply not cognized. But upon the removal of the pot, since the destruction of the conjunction obtains, the [absolute absence] is cognized.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanu bhūtalādau
ghaṭasattvadaśāyāṃ na tadabhāvabuddhiḥ anyadā tu jāyate/ ataḥ
sāmayikābhāvo 'tirikta evāṅgīkartavya iti vadantaṃ
nirākartumāha - sāmayiketi/ pratiyogivirahasamaye
pratīyamāno 'tyantābhāva eva sāmayikābhāvaḥ/ na tu
utpādavināśaśālyatirikta iti samuditor'thaḥ/ nanvevaṃ bhūtale
ghaṭasya ānayanadaśāyāmapi tadabhāvasya nityatvena tatpratyayāpattiḥ ata
āha - ghaṭābhāvavatīti/ niyāmakatvameva samupapādayati - ghaṭavatīti/
tattatkālāvacchinnabhūlādeve ghaṭādyabhāvasaṃsargatayā ghaṭakāle ca
tacchūnyakālaviśiṣṭabhūtalādirūpasaṃsargābhāvena tadā na
tadatyantābhāvabuddhirityapi draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: Now, in the ground and the like, at the time when the pot exists there, no cognition of its absence arises, but at other times it does arise. Therefore, <s>sāmayikābhāva</s> (temporal absence) must be accepted as a distinct [category] — anticipating this objection, he says — '<s>sāmayika</s>' etc. The <s>sāmayikābhāva</s> is just the <s>atyantābhāva</s> (absolute absence) cognized at the time of the absence of the counter-positive — not something distinct possessing origination and destruction. This is the collective meaning. But if so, then even at the time of bringing the pot to the ground, since the absolute absence of the pot is eternal, there would be the unwanted consequence of its cognition [even then]. To this he says — 'in a locus possessing the absence of the pot' etc. He establishes the determinacy itself — 'in a locus possessing the pot' etc. It should also be seen that the absence of the pot and the like [is cognized] through its connection with the ground as delimited by the particular time [when the pot is absent], and at the time of the pot, since the connection in the form of the ground qualified by the time of the pot's absence does not obtain, the cognition of the absolute absence of the pot does not arise then either.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
na tu
utpādavināśaśālyatirikta iti/ pratiyogivirahakāle utpadyamānaḥ
pratiyogikāle vinaśyaṃścātyantābhāvaḥ sāmayiko 'tyantābhāvaḥ/ tathā
ca ghaṭādyatyantābhāvaḥ sāmayikātyantābhāvaḥ, śaśaśṛṅgādyatyantābhāvastu
traikāliko 'tyantābhāva iti teṣāmāśayaḥ/ dīpikākārāstu
sāmayikābhāvastu traikālikātyantābhāvāt nātiricyate/ sarvadā
vidyamāno 'pi samayaviśeṣe pratīyamānatvamātreṇa sāmayikābhāva
ityucyate, na tu samayaviśeṣe utpattimattvena/ nanu
sāmayikābhāvasya atyantābhāvādanatiriktatve ghaṭābhāvavati bhūtale
ghaṭānayanānantaramapi ghaṭātyantābhāvapratītiprasaṅgaḥ,
ghaṭātyantābhāvasya nityatvāt niṣkriyatvena anyatra agamanācca
ghaṭānayanānantaraṃ ghaṭavati bhūtale ghaṭātyantābhāvarūpaviṣayasattvāt
iti cet - na/ yataḥ ghaṭānayanānantaraṃ vidyamāno 'pi
ghaṭātyantābhāvo na pratīyate, ghaṭāpasaraṇānantaraṃ pratīyate, ataḥ
ghaṭātyantābhāvapratyakṣaṃ prati bhūtalaghaṭasaṃyogaprāgabhāvaḥ
bhūtalaghaṭasaṃyogadhvaṃsaśca prayojaka iti kalpyate/ ghaṭānayanānantaraṃ
tu bhūtalaghaṭasaṃyogadhvaṃsaśca sattvāt tatprāgabhāvo vā taddhvaṃso
vā nāstīti kāraṇābhāvāt na ghaṭātyantābhāvapratyakṣam/
ghaṭāpasaraṇānantaraṃ tu bhūtalaghaṭasaṃyogadhvaṃsasya sattvāt
ghaṭātyantābhāvapratyakṣaṃ bhavati/ evaṃ ca nityasyaivātyantābhāvasya
children.translated_text: 'Not something distinct possessing origination and destruction' — the <s>atyantābhāva</s> (absolute absence) that arises at the time of the absence of the counter-positive and perishes at the time of the counter-positive is the <s>sāmayikābhāva</s> (temporal absolute absence). And accordingly, the absolute absence of a pot and the like is a temporal absolute absence, while the absolute absence of a hare's horn and the like is a permanent (<s>traikālika</s>) absolute absence — this is their intent. The author of the <s>Dīpikā</s>, however, [holds that] temporal absence is not distinct from permanent absolute absence. Even though it exists at all times, it is called <s>sāmayikābhāva</s> merely because it is cognized at a particular time, not because it originates at a particular time. Now, if temporal absence is not distinct from absolute absence, then even after bringing the pot to the ground possessing the absence of the pot, there would be the unwanted consequence of cognizing the absolute absence of the pot, since the absolute absence of the pot is eternal, and being inactive, does not go elsewhere — hence even after bringing the pot, since the object in the form of the absolute absence of the pot exists in the ground possessing the pot. To this he says — no, because even though the absolute absence of the pot exists after bringing the pot, it is not cognized; it is cognized after the removal of the pot. Therefore, it is postulated that the <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence) of the conjunction of the ground with the pot and the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> (destruction) of the conjunction of the ground with the pot are the efficient causes for the perception of the absolute absence of the pot. But after bringing the pot, since neither the prior absence nor the destruction of the conjunction of the ground with the pot exists, due to the absence of the cause, there is no perception of the absolute absence of the pot. But after the removal of the pot, since the destruction of the conjunction of the ground with the pot obtains, the perception of the absolute absence of the pot arises. And thus, of the eternal absolute absence itself,

children.text:
samayaviśeṣe
pratītitadabhāvayorupapattyā tadarthaṃ sāmayikābhāvo 'tiriktatayā na
svīkartavya iti nirūpayantīti
children.translated_text: since the cognition and non-cognition at particular times are both accounted for, <s>sāmayikābhāva</s> (temporal absence) need not be accepted as a distinct [category] — this is what they establish.

children.text: praghaṭṭakārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: This is the meaning of the introductory passage.

children.text:
prakāśikāyāṃ
samādhānāntaramāha - tattatkālāvacchinneti/ yasmin ghaṭaśūnyakāle
bhūtale ghaṭātyantābhāvabuddhirbhavati
tādṛśaghaṭaśūnyakālāvacchinnabhūtalasvarūpameva bhūtalaghaṭātyantābhāvayoḥ
sambandhaḥ, ghaṭānayanānantaraṃ ca bhūtalasya ghaṭātyantābhāvasya ca sattve 'pi
ghaṭaśūnyaḥ yaḥ kālatadavacchinnabhūtalasvarūpātmakasya sambandhasyābhāvāt
na bhūtale ghaṭātyantābhāvapratītiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, an alternative resolution is stated — 'delimited by such-and-such time' etc. At the time when the ground is devoid of the pot and the cognition of the absolute absence of the pot in the ground arises, the relation between the ground and the absolute absence of the pot is just the intrinsic nature of the ground as delimited by the time when the pot is absent. And even though both the ground and the absolute absence of the pot exist after bringing the pot, since the relation in the form of the intrinsic nature of the ground delimited by a time when the pot is absent does not obtain, the cognition of the absolute absence of the pot in the ground does not arise — this is the purport.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: abhāvasyādhikaraṇātmakatvakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of the claim that absence is identical with its locus

children.text:
kevalādhikaraṇādeva nāstīti vyavahāropapattau abhāvaḥ na
padārthāntaramiti guravaḥ/ tanna-abhāvānaṅgīkāre kaivalyasya
nirvaktumaśakyatvāt/
children.translated_text: If the usage 'it is not' can be accounted for from the bare locus alone, then absence is not a separate category — so say the teachers. That is not so — because if absence is not accepted, the bare state [of the locus] cannot be explained.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanvabhāvaḥ nāsti
atiriktaḥ padārthaḥ, yasmin adhikaraṇe 'ghaṭo nāsti' ityādipratyayaḥ
tasmin adhikaraṇe paṭādyabhāvatvakalpanenaiva tathā pratītinirvāhāt,
kḷptadharmiṇi dharmakalpanāyā akḷptadharmikalpanāto laghīyastvāditi
children.translated_text: Now, absence is not a distinct category. In whatever locus the cognition 'there is no pot' and so on arises, by postulating the property of absence-of-pot-ness in that locus, such cognition can be accounted for. And postulating a property in an already-established property-bearer is lighter than postulating an un-established property-bearer —

children.text:
gurumatamāśaṅkya
nirācaṣṭe - kevaleti/ yadyapyananteṣu adhikaraṇeṣu
dharmakalpanāto 'tiriktaikadharmikalpanasyaiva laghīyastvāt
atroktanyāyasyānavatāraḥ/ kiṃ ca abhāvasyādhikaraṇasvarūpatve jalādau
vidyamānasya gandhādyabhāvasya
jalādirūpatvāditarendriyagrāhyatāpattirityādidūṣaṇāni prasphuranti,
tathāpi 'kevalādhikaraṇādeva' iti tadvacananirāsādeva
tannivṛttisambhave kimetānyapekṣitānītyālocya tadeva nirākaroti
- abhāvāvaṅgīkāra iti/ atiriktābhāvānaṅgīkāra ityarthaḥ/ atha
kimidaṃ kaivalyam? bhūtalasvarūpamiti cet - ghaṭavadbhūtalasyāpi
tadabhāvasvarūpatāpattvāta tadānīmapi ghaṭābhāvavattābuddhiprasaṅgaḥ/
ghaṭābhāvavattvamiti cet siddhamatiriktābhāvena, ataḥ
kaivalyanirvacanamaśakyamityāha - kaivalyasyeti/
children.translated_text: anticipating the view of the teachers, he refutes it — 'bare' etc. Although the postulation of a single distinct property-bearer is lighter than the postulation of a property in infinitely many loci, and hence the aforementioned principle has no scope here — moreover, if absence were identical with the nature of its locus, the defects become evident: the absence of smell and the like, which exists in water and the like, being identical with water and the like, would become graspable by sense-organs other [than the appropriate one] — nevertheless, since the refutation of their statement 'from the bare locus alone' itself suffices for the removal of their view, why should these [additional objections] be required? Considering this, he refutes that very [view] — 'if absence is not accepted' etc. The meaning is: if the distinct absence is not accepted. Now what is this 'bare state' (<s>kaivalya</s>)? If one says it is the intrinsic nature of the ground — then since the ground possessing a pot also has the nature of that [ground], even then there would be the unwanted consequence of the cognition that [the ground] possesses pot-absence. If one says it is the property of possessing pot-absence — then a distinct absence is already established. Therefore, the bare state cannot be explained — so he says: 'of the bare state' etc.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
yadyapyananteṣviti/
yeṣu yeṣu adhikaraṇeṣu ghaṭātyantābhāvapratītiḥ bhavati teṣu teṣu
adhikaraṇeṣu ghaṭābhāvatvakalpanāpekṣayā kḷpteṣu tāvatsvadhikaraṇeṣu
ekasya ghaṭātyantābhāvarūpasya dharmiṇaḥ kalpanaṃ laghutaramiti bhāvaḥ/ nanu
dharmikalpanāpakṣe abhāvarūpo dharmī abhāvatvarūpadharmaśca ityubhayaṃ
kalpanīyam/ dharmakalpanāpakṣe tu abhāvatvarūpadharmamātraṃ kalpanīyam/
dharmiṇāmadhikaraṇānāṃ kḷptatvāditi kuto lāghavāvakāśa ityato
dūṣaṇāntaramāha - kiṃ ceti/ abhāvaḥ yadyadhikaraṇasvarūpaḥ tarhi jale
vidyamānasya gandhābhāvasya jalasvarūpatayā 'yo guṇo yadindriyagrāhyaḥ,
tanniṣṭhā jātiḥ tadabhāvaśca tadindriyagrāhyaḥ' iti nyāyāt
gandhābhāvasya ghrāṇendriyagrāhyatayā gandhābhāvātmakasya jalasya
ghrāṇendriyagrāhyatvāpattiḥ, jalasya cakṣurādigrāhyatayā ghrāṇendriyāgrāhyatayā
ca talātmakasya gandhābhāvasya cakṣurādigrāhyatvāpattiḥ
ghrāṇendriyāgrāhyatvāpattirvā iti bhāvaḥ/
itarendriyagrāhyatāpattiriti/ ghrāṇetaracakṣurādigrāhyatāpattirityarthaḥ/
ityādidūṣaṇānīti/ abhāvasyādhikaraṇātmakatve
bhūtalaghaṭābhāvayorādhārādheyabhāvānupapattiḥ ādhārādheyatabhāvasya
bhedavyāpyatvāditi dūṣaṇamādipadagrāhyam/
children.translated_text: 'Although in infinitely many' etc. — the meaning is: compared to postulating the property of pot-absence-ness in each and every locus where the cognition of the absolute absence of the pot arises, postulating a single property-bearer in the form of the absolute absence of the pot in the already-established loci is lighter. Now, in the alternative of postulating a property-bearer, both the property-bearer in the form of absence and the property in the form of absence-ness must be postulated. In the alternative of postulating a property, only the property in the form of absence-ness need be postulated, since the property-bearers, i.e. the loci, are already established — so where is the scope for economy? Therefore he states another objection — 'moreover' etc. If absence were identical with the nature of whatever locus [it resides in], then the absence of smell, which exists in water, being identical with water, by the principle 'whatever quality is graspable by whatever sense-organ, the universal residing in it and its absence are graspable by that same sense-organ,' the absence of smell would be graspable by the olfactory organ; and since the absence-of-smell that is identical with water would be graspable by the olfactory organ, water itself would be graspable by the olfactory organ. Alternatively, since water is graspable by the visual organ and the like but not by the olfactory organ, the absence of smell which is identical with it would also become graspable by the visual organ and the like, or non-graspable by the olfactory organ — this is the purport. 'Graspable by another sense-organ' — the meaning is: graspable by a sense-organ other than the olfactory, such as the visual organ and the like. 'And so forth among the defects' — the defect to be grasped by the word 'and so forth' is: if absence were identical with the nature of the locus, the relation of container and contained between the ground and the absence of the pot would be impossible, since the container-contained relation is pervaded by difference.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
abhāvābhāvasya
bhāvarūpatā
children.translated_text: The absence of absence has the nature of a positive entity

children.text:
abhāvābhāvaḥ bhāva
eva/ nātiriktaḥ, anavasthāprasaṅgāt/ dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvaḥ prāgabhāvadhvaṃsaśca
pratiyogyeveti prāñcaḥ/ abhāvābhāvaḥ atirikta eva tṛtīyābhāvasya
prathamābhāvarūpatvāt na anavastheti navīnāḥ/
children.translated_text: The absence of absence is just a positive entity (<s>bhāva</s>), not something distinct, because of the unwanted consequence of infinite regress. The <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence) of <s>dhvaṃsa</s> (destruction) and the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> of <s>prāgabhāva</s> are just the counter-positive itself — so say the ancients. The absence of absence is indeed distinct, because the third absence has the nature of the first absence, and hence there is no infinite regress — so say the moderns.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanvabhāvasya
atiriktatve tadabhāvo 'pyatiriktaḥ, tasyāpyabhāvaḥ tathetyanavasthā
syādata āha - abhāvābhāva iti/ dhvaṃsetyādi/ dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvaḥ
pratiyogisvarūpaḥ, tatprāgabhāvarūpaśca/ prāgabhāvadhvaṃsastu
pratiyogisvarūpaḥ, taddhvaṃsarūpaśca ityasyārthaḥ avaseyaḥ/ tena
pratiyogiprāgabhāvadaśāyāmapi 'dhvaṃso bhaviṣyati' iti pratyayasya
pratiyogidhvaṃsadaśāyāmapi 'prāgabhāvo naṣṭaḥ' iti pratyayasya
copapattiḥ/ nanu kāle dravyatvaṃ nāsti iti pratyayaḥ na jāyate,
dravyatvābhāva iti tu jāyate iti vaiṣamyanirvāhāya nāstīti
pratyaye daiśikasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvabhānaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, if absence is distinct [from its locus], then the absence of that [absence] would also be distinct, and the absence of that would likewise be so — resulting in an infinite regress. To this he says — 'the absence of absence' etc. '<s>Dhvaṃsa</s>' and so forth — the <s>prāgabhāva</s> of <s>dhvaṃsa</s> has the nature of the counter-positive, and also has the nature of the <s>prāgabhāva</s> of that [counter-positive]. And the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> of <s>prāgabhāva</s> has the nature of the counter-positive, and also has the nature of the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> of that [counter-positive] — this meaning should be understood. Thereby, even in the state of the <s>prāgabhāva</s> of the counter-positive, the cognition 'the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> will occur' is accounted for, and even in the state of the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> of the counter-positive, the cognition 'the <s>prāgabhāva</s> has perished' is accounted for. Now, regarding time, the cognition 'substance-ness does not exist [in time]' does not arise, but the cognition 'the absence of substance-ness [exists in time]' does arise — to account for this asymmetry, in the cognition expressed by 'does not exist,' the appearance of superstratum-hood delimited by a spatial relation

children.text:
kalpanīyam/ itthaṃ ca
ghaṭābhāvābhāvādeḥ ghaṭādirūpatvetviha ghaṭābhāvo nāstīti pratyayasya
bhramatvameva syāt/ bhāvasya viśeṣaṇatāviśeṣeṇa vṛttyanaṅgīkārāt/
ataḥ abhāvābhāvaḥ atiriktaḥ na tu bhāvarūpa iti navīnamataṃ darśayati -
abhāveti/ tarhi anavasthetyata āha - tṛtīyeti/
children.translated_text: must be postulated. And accordingly, since the absence of the absence of a pot and the like would have the nature of a pot and the like, the cognition 'the absence of the pot does not exist here' would necessarily be erroneous — because the occurrence of the positive entity through the relation of qualification is not accepted. Therefore, the absence of absence is distinct and not of the nature of a positive entity — he presents the view of the moderns: 'absence' etc. Then there would be an infinite regress — to this he replies: 'the third' etc.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nanu
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvaḥ prāgabhāvadhvaṃsaśca pratiyogyeva iti dīpikātaḥ
ghaṭadhvaṃsaprāgabhāvaḥ ghaṭaprāgabhāvadhvaṃsaśca ghaṭasvarūpa iti labhyate/
tathā sati ghaṭānutpattidaśāyāṃ 'ghaṭadhvaṃso bhaviṣyati' iti
ghaṭadhvaṃsaprāgabhāvaviṣayakapratītiḥ na syāt tadānīṃ ghaṭābhāvāt/ evaṃ
ghaṭadhvaṃsadaśāyāṃ 'ghaṭaprāgabhāvo naṣṭa' iti
ghaṭaprāgabhāvadhvaṃsaviṣayakapratītirnasyāt,
children.translated_text: Now, from the <s>Dīpikā</s> [statement] that 'the <s>prāgabhāva</s> of <s>dhvaṃsa</s> and the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> of <s>prāgabhāva</s> are just the counter-positive itself,' one obtains that the <s>prāgabhāva</s> of the destruction of a pot and the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> of the prior absence of a pot are the pot itself. If so, at the stage when the pot has not yet arisen, the cognition 'the destruction of the pot will occur' — which has as its object the <s>prāgabhāva</s> of the destruction of the pot — would not be possible, since at that time the pot is absent. Similarly, at the stage of the destruction of the pot, the cognition 'the prior absence of the pot has perished' — which has as its object the <s>dhvaṃsa</s> of the prior absence of the pot — would not be possible,

children.text:
tadātmakasya
ghaṭasyābhāvādityataḥ tātparyamāha - dhvaṃsaprāgabhāva iti/
ghaṭadhvaṃsaprāgabhāvaḥ ghaṭasvarūpaḥ ghaṭaprāgabhāvasvarūpaśca/ tathā ca
ghaṭānutpattidaśāyāṃ ghaṭaprāgabhāvasya sattvāt tadātmakaṃ
ghaṭadhvaṃsaprāgabhāvaṃ viṣayīkurvan 'ghaṭadhvaṃso bhaviṣyati' iti
pratītiḥ udayate/ ghaṭotpatyanantaraṃ jāyamānā 'ghaṭadhvaṃso bhaviṣyati'
iti pratītistu ghaṭātmakaṃ ghaṭadhvaṃsaprāgabhāvaṃ viṣayīkaroti/ evaṃ
ghaṭaprāgabhāvadhvaṃsaḥ ghaṭasvarūpaḥ, ghaṭadhvaṃsasvarūpaśca/ ataḥ ghaṭakāle
'ghaṭaprāgabhāvo naṣṭaḥ' iti pratītiḥ ghaṭarūpaṃ ghaṭaprāgabhāvadhvaṃsaṃ
viṣayīkaroti/ ghaṭadhvaṃsakāle 'ghaṭaprāgabhāvo naṣṭaḥ' iti pratītiḥ
ghaṭadhvaṃsarūpaṃ ghaṭaprāgabhāvadhvaṃsaṃ viṣayīkaroti/ tathā ca na
kāpyanupapattiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Since there is no pot which is of that nature — with this intent he states the purport: 'the prior absence of destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa-prāgabhāva</s>).' The prior absence of the pot's destruction is identical with the pot's own nature and with the nature of the pot's prior absence. Accordingly, in the state before the pot's production, since the pot's prior absence exists, the cognition 'the pot's destruction will occur' arises by taking as its object the prior absence of the pot's destruction, which is identical with it. The cognition 'the pot's destruction will occur' that arises immediately after the pot's production takes as its object the prior absence of the pot's destruction, which is identical with the pot. Similarly, the destruction of the pot's prior absence is identical with the pot's own nature and with the nature of the pot's destruction. Therefore, at the time of the pot, the cognition 'the pot's prior absence has perished' takes as its object the destruction of the pot's prior absence in the form of the pot. At the time of the pot's destruction, the cognition 'the pot's prior absence has perished' takes as its object the destruction of the pot's prior absence in the form of the pot's destruction. Thus there is no inconsistency whatsoever — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu kāle dravyatvaṃ
nāstītyādi/ kāle dravyatvaṃ nāstīti pratītiḥ na jāyate, kāle
dravyatvābhāva iti pratitistu jāyate/ tadarthaṃ nañapadaṃ
daiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhāvacchinnādheyatvānvitābhāvabodhakamiti
vyutpattiḥ svīkaraṇīyā/ ghaṭe paṭatvaṃ nāstītyasya
ghaṭanirūpitadaiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhāvacchinnādheyatāvān
paṭatvābhāva ityarthaḥ/ kāle kālikasambandhena dravyatvābhāvasya
sattve 'pi daiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambāndhena dravyatvābhāvaṃ prati
samavāyasambandhena dravyatvasya virodhitatayakāle samavāyena
dravyatvasattvāt
kālanirūpitadaiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhāvacchinnādheyatāvān
dravyatvābhāvo na bhavatīti kāle dravyatvaṃ nāstīti pratītiḥ na
bhavatīti vaktavyam/ itthaṃ ca bhūtale ghaṭābhāvo nāstīnti
pratītirapi ghaṭābhāvābhāve
bhūtalanirūpitadaiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhāvacchinnādheyatvamavagāhata
iti vaktavyam/ ghaṭābhāvābhāvo yadi ghaṭasvarūpaḥ syāt tadā
bhāvānāṃ daiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhena vṛtteranaṅgīkārāt
tatsambandhāvacchinnādheyatvābhāvavati ghaṭe tadavagāhitayā
tādṛśapratīterbhramatvaṃ syāt/ iṣyate tu pramātvam/ ataḥ abhāvābhāvaḥ
na bhāvarūpaḥ api tu atiriktaḥ/ na ca anavasthā/ ghaṭābhāvābhāvasya
atiriktatve 'pi ghaṭābhāvābhāvābhāvasya ghaṭābhāvarūpatvāṅgīṅkārāt
iti navīnānāmāśayaḥ/ navīnatarāstu bhāvānāmapi
daiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhena vṛttiṃ aṅgīkurvanti/ tanmate
abhāvābhāvaḥ nātiriktaḥ/ etattattvaṃ kūṭaghaṭitalakṣaṇagādādharyāṃ
draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'substance-ness does not exist in time' and so on. The cognition 'substance-ness does not exist in time' does not arise, but the cognition 'the absence of substance-ness exists in time' does arise. For this purpose, the etymological derivation should be accepted that the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) conveys absence conjoined with superstratum-ness delimited by the relation of spatial qualification (<s>daiśika-viśeṣaṇatā</s>). The meaning of 'cloth-ness does not exist in the pot' is: there is an absence of cloth-ness possessing superstratum-ness delimited by the relation of spatial qualification determined by the pot. Although the absence of substance-ness exists in time through temporal relation (<s>kālika-sambandha</s>), since substance-ness through the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) is opposed to the absence of substance-ness through the relation of spatial qualification, and since substance-ness exists in time through inherence, it must be said that the absence of substance-ness possessing superstratum-ness delimited by the relation of spatial qualification determined by time does not obtain — and hence the cognition 'substance-ness does not exist in time' does not arise. Accordingly, the cognition 'the absence of a pot does not exist on the ground' must also be said to apprehend, in the absence of the pot's absence, superstratum-ness delimited by the relation of spatial qualification determined by the ground. If the absence of pot-absence were identical with the pot itself, then since positive entities are not accepted as occurring through the relation of spatial qualification, the pot — lacking superstratum-ness delimited by that relation — would make such a cognition erroneous by apprehending it. But it is accepted as valid knowledge. Therefore, the absence of an absence is not identical with a positive entity but is rather a distinct entity. Nor is there an infinite regress: even though the absence of pot-absence is a distinct entity, the absence of pot-absence-absence is accepted as identical with pot-absence. This is the view of the later logicians (<s>Navīna</s>). The most recent logicians (<s>Navīnatara</s>), however, accept that positive entities too occur through the relation of spatial qualification. On their view, the absence of an absence is not a distinct entity. The truth of this matter should be examined in the <s>Kūṭaghaṭita-lakṣaṇa</s> of <s>Gadādharī</s>.

children.text: tarkasaṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>

children.text: ṣoḍaśapadārthānāṃ saptapadārtheṣvantarbhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: The subsumption of the sixteen categories under the seven categories

children.text: AnTs_81 sarveṣāṃ padārthānāṃ yathāyatham ukteṣv antarbhāvāt saptaiva padārthā iti siddham //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 81]: Since all categories are subsumed, each in its appropriate place, under those [seven] already stated, it is established that there are only seven categories.

children.text: sarveṣāmapi padārthānāṃ ukteṣveva antarbhāvāt saptaiva padārthā iti siddham/
children.translated_text: Since all categories whatsoever are subsumed under those already stated, it is established that there are only seven categories.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
nanu"pramāṇaprameyasaṃśayaprayojanadṛṣṭāntasiddhāntāvayavatarkan irṇayavādajalpavitaṇḍāhetvābhāsacchalajātinigrahasthānāṃ
tattvajñānāt niḥreyasādhigamaḥ"
[nyā. sū. 1-1-1] iti
nyāyasūtre ṣoḍaśapadārthānāmuktatvāt kathaṃ saptaivetya āha -
sarveṣāmiti/ sarveṣāṃ saptasvevāntarbhāva ityarthaḥ/"ātmaśarīrendriyārthabuddhimanaḥ
pravṛttidoṣapretyabhāvaphaladuḥkhāpavargāstu prameyam"iti
dvādaśabidhaṃ prameyam/ pravṛttiḥ-dharmādharmau/ rāgadveṣamohāḥ doṣāḥ/
rāgaḥ-icchā/ dveṣaḥ-manyuḥ/ mohaḥ-śarīrādau ātmabhramaḥ/
pretyabhāvaḥ-maraṇam/ phalam-bhogaḥ/ apavargaḥ-mokṣaḥ/ sa ca
svasamānādhikaraṇuduḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīnaduḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ/
prayojanam-sukhaprātiptaḥ duḥkhahāniśca/ dṛṣṭāntaḥ-mahānasādiḥ/
prāmāṇikatvena abhyupagator'thaḥ siddhāntaḥ/ nirṇayaḥ-niścayaḥ/ sa ca
pramāṇaphalam/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since sixteen categories are mentioned in the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> — 'From the true knowledge of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge), <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>prayojana</s> (purpose), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), <s>avayava</s> (members of syllogism), <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning), <s>nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment), <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling), <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil), <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious marks), <s>chala</s> (quibble), <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (grounds for defeat), there is attainment of the highest good' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.1] — how can there be only seven? To this he replies: 'of all.' The meaning is: all [sixteen] are subsumed under the seven alone. '<s>Ātman</s> (self), body, sense-organs, objects, intellect, mind, activity, defects, transmigration, fruit, suffering, and liberation — these are the objects of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>)' — thus <s>prameya</s> is twelvefold. Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) [here means] <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> (merit and demerit). The defects (<s>doṣa</s>) are passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>). Passion is desire (<s>icchā</s>). Aversion is anger (<s>manyu</s>). Delusion is the erroneous cognition of the self in the body and such. Transmigration (<s>pretyabhāva</s>) is death. Fruit (<s>phala</s>) is experience (<s>bhoga</s>). Liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) is <s>mokṣa</s>. And that [<s>mokṣa</s>] is the destruction of suffering that is not contemporaneous with the prior absence of suffering co-located with itself. Purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) is the attainment of pleasure and the removal of pain. Example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is a kitchen and the like. An object accepted as authoritative is an established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>). Ascertainment (<s>nirṇaya</s>) is definite knowledge — and that is the result of a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
paramakāruṇikena
muninā duḥkhapaṅkanimagnaṃ janaṃ uddidhīrṃṣuṇā praṇītam"pramāṇaprameya"ityādisūtraṃ, tadvirodhaṃ parihartuṃ
ākṣipati - nanviti/ pratyakṣapramāṇasya dravye, anumānādīnāṃ ca
guṇe 'ntarbhāvasya sphuṭatvāt prameyādīnāṃ dravyādiṣvantarbhāvamāha -
ātmetyādinā/ ātmaśarīrendriyāṇāṃ dravye, arthasya pṛthivyādirūpasya
dravyādiṣu, buddheḥ guṇe, antarindriyasya manasaḥ dravye 'ntarbhāvaḥ/
evamagre 'pi yathāyathamantarbhāvaḥ draṣṭavyaḥ/ dharmādharmau iti/
tajjaniketyarthaḥ/ etacca sphuṭamākare/ rāgaḥ / icchāviśeṣaḥ/
maraṇamiti/ maraṇānantarabhāvi jananamityarthaḥ/ tathā ca padavyutpattiḥ
pretya mṛtvā bhāvaḥ jananamitiḥ/ caramaprāṇaśarīrasaṃyogadhvaṃsaḥ
maraṇam/ ādyaśarīraprāṇasaṃyogaḥ jananam/ muktātmasaṃyogadhvaṃsavataḥ
ghaṭasya muktatvāpattivāraṇāya - duḥkhadhvaṃsa iti/ duḥkhadhvaṃsavatāṃ
asmadādīnāmapi muktatvāpattivāraṇāya kālīnāntam/
anyadīyaduḥkhaprāgabhāvasamānakālikaduḥkhadhvaṃsavatāṃ
śukādyātmanāmapyamuktatvaprasaṅgāt svasamānādhikaraṇeti
duḥkhaprāgabhāvaviśeṣaṇam/ na ca
svasamānādhikaraṇaduḥkhāsamānakalīnetyanenaiva
suṣuptikālikaduḥkhadhvaṃsasyāpi agrimaduḥkhakṣaṇavṛttervāraṇāt
prāgabhāveti vyarthamiti vācyam/ yathāsanniveśe vaiyarthyābhāvāditi
dik/ saṃśayasya nirūpitatvāt prayojanasvarūpaṃ darśayati -
prayojanamiti/
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> beginning with '<s>pramāṇa</s>, <s>prameya</s>...' was composed by the supremely compassionate sage (<s>Muni</s>) [<s>Gautama</s>] desiring to rescue people sunk in the mire of suffering. To resolve the apparent conflict [with the sevenfold scheme], he raises the objection: 'But...' Since the subsumption of the <s>pramāṇa</s> of perception under substance, and of inference and other [<s>pramāṇa</s>s] under quality, is evident, he states the subsumption of <s>prameya</s> and the rest under substance and so on with '<s>ātman</s>' and so forth. <s>Ātman</s>, body, and sense-organs are subsumed under substance; objects in the form of earth and so forth under substance and other [categories]; intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) under quality; the internal organ, mind (<s>manas</s>), under substance. Similarly, the subsumption of the remaining [categories] should be understood each in its appropriate place. '<s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>': the meaning is 'that which produces them.' This is clear in the source texts. 'Passion (<s>rāga</s>)': a particular kind of desire. 'Death (<s>maraṇa</s>)': the meaning is birth occurring after death. Accordingly, the etymological derivation is: <s>pretya</s> means 'having died,' <s>bhāva</s> means 'birth.' Death is the destruction of the final conjunction of the vital breath and the body. Birth is the first conjunction of the body and the vital breath. And transmigration is subsumed under quality in the form of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>). 'Final-ness' of the breath-body conjunction means: not being the locus of the prior absence of a breath-conjunction residing in a body of the same kind. 'First-ness' means: not being the locus of the destruction of a breath-conjunction residing in a body of the same kind.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pratyakṣapramāṇasya
dravya iti/ indriyaṃ pratyakṣapramākaraṇam/ tatra cakṣuṣaḥ tejasi,
rasanāyāḥ jale, ghrāṇasya pṛthivyām, tvacaḥ vāyau, śrotrasya
ākāśe 'ntarbhāvāt manasaḥ pṛthak dravyatvācca pratyakṣapramāṇasya
dravye 'ntarbhāva ityarthaḥ/ anumānādīnāṃ ca guṇa iti/
vyāptijñānamanumānam, sādṛśyajñānamupamānam, padajñānaṃ śabda
ityevamanumānādīnāṃ jñānarūpe guṇe 'ntarbhāva ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The <s>pramāṇa</s> of perception under substance': the sense-organ is the instrument of perceptual <s>pramāṇa</s>. Among them, the eye is subsumed under fire (<s>tejas</s>), the tongue under water, the nose under earth, the skin under air, and the ear under space (<s>ākāśa</s>); and since the mind is a separate substance, the <s>pramāṇa</s> of perception is subsumed under substance — this is the meaning. 'And inference and the rest under quality': inference is the cognition of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) is the cognition of similarity, verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is the cognition of word-meanings — thus inference and the rest are subsumed under quality in the form of cognition. This is the meaning.

children.text:
evamagre 'pīti/
pravṛttidoṣādīnāmapi yathāyathaṃ sapatasvevāntarbhāva ityarthaḥ/ nanu
pravṛtteḥ prayatnaviśeṣarūpatvāt dharmādharmayostu
adṛṣṭaviśeṣarūpatvāt 'pravṛttiḥ dharmādharmau' iti
dīpikāgrantho 'saṅgata ityata āha - tajjaniketyartha iti/
dharmādharmayorjanikā pravṛttirityarthaṃḥ/ kārye kāraṇopacāra iti
bhāvaḥ/ tathā ca pravṛtteḥ guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/ sphuṭamākara iti/"pravṛttisādhano dharmādharmau pravṛttiśabdenoktau yathā annasādhanāḥ
prāṇāḥ"iti dvitīyasūtre bhāṣye,"pravṛttiphale dharmādharmau
āsmin sūtre pravṛttirityucyete/ kasmāt, tatsādhanatvāt annaṃ vai
prāṇinaḥ prāṇā iti yathā"iti saptadaśasūtre vārtike coktatvāt
pravṛtterdharmādharmajanakatvaṃ mūlagrantheṣu spaṣṭamiti bhāvaḥ/
icchāviśeṣa iti/ utkaṭecchetyarthaḥ/ tathā ca rāgasyecchātmake
guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ, dveṣasya guṇe, mithyājñānarūpasya mohasya ca
guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/ mithyājñānaṃ nāma bhramātmakajñānam/ maraṇānantareti/
pretya-mṛtvā bhāvaḥ/ jananamiti vyutpattyā maraṇānantarakālikajanya
pretyabhāvaśabdārthaḥ/ caramasya prāṇaśarīrasaṃyogasya dhvaṃsaḥ maraṇam/
ādyaḥ śarīraprāṇasaṃyogaḥ janmaḥ/ tathā ca pretyabhāvasya saṃyogarūpe
guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/ prāṇaśarīrasaṃyoge caramatvaṃ ca
svasajātīyaśarīravṛttiprāṇasaṃyogaprāgabhāvānadhikaraṇatvam/ ādyatvaṃ ca
svasajātīyaśarīravṛttiprāṇasaṃyogadhvaṃsānadhikaraṇatvam/
children.translated_text: 'Similarly, the rest too': the meaning is that activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), defects (<s>doṣa</s>), and the rest too are subsumed, each in its appropriate place, under the seven categories alone. Objection: since <s>pravṛtti</s> is a particular form of effort (<s>prayatna</s>), and <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are particular forms of unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), the <s>Dīpikā</s>'s statement '<s>pravṛtti</s> [means] <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>' is inconsistent. To this he says: 'the meaning is: that which produces them.' <s>Pravṛtti</s> means the producer of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — this is the meaning. This is a case of figurative usage of the cause for the effect — this is the purport. And thus <s>pravṛtti</s> is subsumed under quality. 'It is clear in the source texts': since it is stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the second <s>sūtra</s> — '<s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, being accomplished by activity, are denoted by the word <s>pravṛtti</s>, just as vital breaths are [called] the means of food' — and in the <s>Vārtika</s> on the seventeenth <s>sūtra</s> — '<s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, being the fruits of activity, are called <s>pravṛtti</s> in this <s>sūtra</s>; why? because they are accomplished by it, just as vital breaths are the life of living beings' — the fact that <s>pravṛtti</s> produces <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> is explicit in the root texts. This is the purport. 'A particular desire (<s>icchā</s>)': meaning intense desire. And thus passion (<s>rāga</s>) is subsumed under quality in the form of desire; aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) under quality; and delusion (<s>moha</s>), being in the form of erroneous cognition (<s>mithyājñāna</s>), under quality. Erroneous cognition means cognition that is of the nature of error (<s>bhrama</s>). 'After death': <s>pretya</s> means 'having died,' <s>bhāva</s> means birth — by this etymology, the meaning of the word <s>pretyabhāva</s> is birth occurring at the time after death. The destruction of the final breath-body conjunction is death. The first body-breath conjunction is birth. And thus transmigration (<s>pretyabhāva</s>) is subsumed under quality in the form of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>). 'Final-ness' in a breath-body conjunction means: not being the locus of the prior absence of a breath-conjunction residing in a body of the same kind. 'First-ness' means: not being the locus of the destruction of a breath-conjunction residing in a body of the same kind.

children.text:
dīpikāyām phalaṃ
bhoga iti/ bhogo nāma sukhaduḥkhānubhavaḥ/ tathā ca phalasya
anubhavarūpajñānātmake gaṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/ svasamānādhikaraṇeti/
svasamānādhikaraṇaḥ yaḥ duḥkhaprāgabhāvaḥ/ tadasamānakālīna duḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ
mokṣa ityarthaḥ/ idānīmasmākaṃ vidyamānaḥ yatkiñcidduḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ
bhaviṣyadduḥkhaprāgabhāvasamānakālikaḥ/ muktau yaḥ duḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ saḥ
dukhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālikaḥ punarduḥkhasyājaniṣyamāṇatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
apavargalakṣaṇaghaṭakadalānāṃ prayojanamāha prakāśikāyām -
muktātmasaṃyogetyādinā/ duḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ ityatra duḥkhapadānupādāne
svasamānādhikaraṇaduḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīnaḥ dhvaṃsaḥ mokṣa iti
etāvanmātroktau muktātmano ghaṭasya ca yaḥ saṃyogaḥ taddhvaṃso 'pi
duḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīna iti tādṛśasaṃyogadhvaṃsavato
ghaṭasyāpi muktatvaṃ syāt/ tadvāraṇāya duḥkhadhvaṃsa ityuktam/
saṃyogadhvaso na duḥkhadhvaṃsa iti tasya na muktitvamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'fruit (<s>phala</s>) is experience (<s>bhoga</s>)': experience means the undergoing of pleasure and pain. And thus fruit is subsumed under quality in the form of cognition that is experiential. 'Co-located with itself (<s>svasamānādhikaraṇa</s>)': the destruction of suffering that is not contemporaneous with the prior absence of suffering co-located with itself — that is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). This is the meaning. Any destruction of suffering that exists for us now is contemporaneous with the prior absence of future suffering. But the destruction of suffering in the state of liberation is not contemporaneous with the prior absence of suffering, since suffering will never again be produced — this is the purport. He states the purpose of each component in the definition of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, beginning with 'the conjunction of the liberated self (<s>muktātma</s>)' and so on. If the word 'suffering' were not included in 'destruction of suffering,' then saying merely 'destruction that is not contemporaneous with the prior absence of suffering co-located with itself' would mean that the destruction of the conjunction between a liberated self and a pot — that too being not contemporaneous with the prior absence of suffering — would qualify as <s>mokṣa</s>, and hence even the pot possessing such conjunction-destruction would be liberated. To prevent this, 'destruction of suffering' is specified — the destruction of conjunction is not a destruction of suffering, and hence the pot does not have liberation. This is the purport.

children.text:
nanu muktātmano
vibhutvāt yāvadghaṭasthiti ghaṭe muktātmasaṃyogo 'styeveti
taddhvaṃsavatvaṃ ghaṭasya kathaṃ bhavet/ ghaṭe naṣṭe tu
muktātmaghaṭasaṃyogadhvaṃsasattve 'pi ghaṭasyābhāvāt sutarāṃ na ghaṭasya
muktatvamiti kathamiyamāśaṅkā? atrocyate - ghaṭaḥ ādau kutrañcit
pradeśe 'sti, tadā tatpradeśāvacchedena muktātmaghaṭasaṃyogo 'sti/ sa
eva ghaṭaḥ pradeśāntaraṃ nītaścet pūrvapradeśāvacchinnātmasaṃyogo
naśyati, pradeśāntarāvacchedena anyaḥ saṃyogo jāyate/ tathā cānaṣṭe
children.translated_text: Objection: Since the liberated self (<s>muktātman</s>) is all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>), as long as the pot exists, the conjunction of the liberated self with the pot does exist — so how could the pot possess the destruction of that [conjunction]? And when the pot is destroyed, although the destruction of the liberated-self-pot conjunction exists, since the pot itself is absent, all the more so the pot cannot be liberated — so how does this objection arise? To this it is replied: A pot first exists in a certain location; at that time, the conjunction of the liberated self with the pot exists as delimited by that location. If that very pot is moved to another location, the conjunction with the self delimited by the former location is destroyed, and another conjunction delimited by the new location is produced. And thus, while the pot is not destroyed,

children.text:
eva ghaṭe
pradeśaviśeṣāvacchinnamuktātmasaṃyogadhvaso 'stīti ghaṭasya
muktatvaprasaṅga ityāśayāt/ duḥkhadhvaṃsavatāmiti/ tathā ca
duḥkhadhvaṃso mokṣa ityetāvanmātroktau saṃsāriṇāmasmadādīnāmapi
suṣuptikāle duḥkhadhvaṃsasattvāt muktatvāpattiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
kālīnāntam/ adya vidyamānasya asmadīya duḥkhadhvaṃsasya
śvobhāviduḥkhaprāgabhāvasamānakālīnatvāt
tādṛśaduḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīnatvaṃ nāstīti na muktitvamiti
bhāvaḥ/ anyadīyeti/ tathā ca duḥkhaprāgabhāve svasamānādhikaraṇeti
viśeṣaṇānupādāne muktānāṃ śukādīnāṃ yo duḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ saḥ
śukādyanyasaṃsāryātmavṛtti yat bhāvi duḥkhaṃ
tatprāgabhāvasamānakālīnameva bhavatīti
tadasamānakālīnaduḥkhadhvaṃsavatvābhāvāt śukādīnāmamuktatvaṃ syāt/
tadvāraṇāya svasamānādhikaraṇeti viśeṣaṇam/ tadupādāne ca svaṃ
śukātmavṛttiḥ duḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ tadadhikaraṇaṃ śukātmā tadvattitvaṃ
anyadīyaduḥkhaprāgabhāve nāstīti na tatsamānakālīnatvamādāya
pūrvoktadoṣa iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: even in a pot, there exists the destruction of the conjunction of a liberated soul with a specific region; hence there would be the unwanted consequence of the pot being liberated — this is the intent. 'Of those possessing the destruction of suffering' — and accordingly, if only 'the destruction of suffering is liberation' were stated, then even for worldly beings like ourselves, since the destruction of suffering exists at the time of deep sleep, the unwanted consequence of being liberated would arise. To prevent that, 'that is not co-temporal [with prior absence of suffering].' The purport is: since the destruction of our present suffering is co-temporal with the prior absence of future suffering, it does not possess the property of not being co-temporal with such prior absence of suffering — hence it is not liberation. 'Of another' — and accordingly, if the qualifier 'co-located with oneself' is not included in [the reference to] the prior absence of suffering, then the destruction of suffering of liberated beings like <s>Śuka</s> and the like — since it is co-temporal with the prior absence of future suffering residing in a worldly soul other than <s>Śuka</s> — would lack the property of possessing a destruction of suffering not co-temporal with it; hence <s>Śuka</s> and the like would be non-liberated. To prevent that, the qualifier 'co-located with oneself.' With that included, 'self' is the destruction of suffering residing in <s>Śuka</s>'s soul; its substratum is <s>Śuka</s>'s soul; the property of residing therein is absent in the prior absence of suffering belonging to another — hence there is no co-temporality to take, and hence no previously stated defect — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
svasamānādhikaraṇaduḥkhāsamānakālīnetyevāstu, kiṃ
tādṛśaduḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīneti viśeṣaṇena/ na ca asmākaṃ
suṣuptau yo duḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ tasya duḥkhasamānakālīnatvaṃ nāsti,
suṣuptau duḥkhābhāvāt/ tathā ca
duḥkhāsamānakālīnaduḥkhadhvaṃsasatvāt asmākaṃ muktatvāpattibhavet
duḥkhāsamānakālīnetyuktau/ duḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīnetyuktau tu
suṣuptau asmāsu bhāviduḥkhaprāgabhāvo 'stīti tadātanaduḥkhadhvaṃsasya
duḥkhaprāgabhāvasamānakālīnatvāt vāraṇamiti vācyam/ dhvaṃsasya
dhvaṃsāsambhavena suṣupitakāliko yo duḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ tasya
jāgratkṣaṇe 'pyanuvartamānatayā jāgratkāle yaddukhaṃ
tatsamānakālīnatvamastīti
samānādhikaraṇaduḥkhāsamānakālīnatvābhāvāt vāraṇaṃ bhavatīti
duḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīnatvaparyantasyānāvaśyakatvāt ityāśayena
śaṅkate - na ca sbasamānādhikaraṇeti/
children.translated_text: Objection: Let the qualifier simply be 'not co-temporal with suffering co-located with oneself' — what is the point of the qualifier 'not co-temporal with prior absence of such suffering'? For the destruction of suffering during our deep sleep is not co-temporal with suffering, since suffering is absent during deep sleep. And accordingly, if only 'not co-temporal with suffering' were stated, since we possess a destruction of suffering not co-temporal with suffering, the unwanted consequence of our being liberated would arise. But if 'not co-temporal with prior absence of suffering' is stated, since the prior absence of future suffering exists in us during deep sleep, and the destruction of suffering at that time is co-temporal with the prior absence of suffering, it is averted — this should be said. [Reply:] Since the destruction of a destruction is impossible, the destruction of suffering that exists at the time of deep sleep continues even at the waking moment; hence it is co-temporal with the suffering present during waking. Therefore, since there is absence of the property of not being co-temporal with suffering co-located with oneself, aversion is achieved — and hence the extension up to 'not co-temporal with prior absence of suffering' is unnecessary — with this intent, he raises the doubt: 'Nor co-located with oneself' and so forth.

children.text:
samādhatte -
yathāsaṃniveśa iti/ yadyapi duḥkhāsamānakālīnatvaviśeṣaṇena vāraṇaṃ
bhavati, tathāpi duḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīnatvenāpi vāraṇasambhavāt
tasya na vaiyarthyathmati bhāvaḥ/ na ca laghunāduḥkhāsamānakālīnatvenaiva
vāraṇe guruṇaḥ duḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīnatvaviśiṣaṇasya
vaiyarthyameveti vācyam/ yatra gurudharmaghaṭakena laghudharmeṇa nirvāhaḥ
tatraiva gurudharmasya vaiyarthyam/ prakṛte tu
duḥkhāsamānakālīnatvatvāvacchinnābhāvaḥ duḥkhāsamānakālīnatvam/
children.translated_text: He resolves: 'according to the arrangement [of the text]' and so forth. Although aversion is achieved by the qualifier 'not co-temporal with suffering,' nevertheless, since aversion is also possible through 'not co-temporal with prior absence of suffering,' there is no redundancy of the latter — this is the purport. Nor should it be said that when aversion is achieved by the lighter [qualifier] 'not co-temporal with suffering' alone, the heavier qualifier 'not co-temporal with prior absence of suffering' is indeed redundant. The heaviness of a property results in redundancy only when the lighter property that is a component of the heavier one suffices by itself. In the present case, however, 'not being co-temporal with suffering' is the absence delimited by the counter-positive-hood-delimitor of 'being co-temporal with suffering';

children.text:
duḥkhaprāgabhāvasamānakālīnatvatvāvacchinnābhāvaḥ
duḥkhaprāgabhāvāsamānakālīnatvam/ anayoścābhāvayoḥ
pratiyogitāvacchedakabhedena bhinnatvāt ekasmin abhāve 'nyasya
ghaṭakatvābhāvāt na vaiyathyavikāśa ityāśayāt/ nanu
svatvasyānanugatatayā tadghaṭitamukterapyanekatvena muktipadasya
nānārthakatvāpattiḥ ityata āha - digiti/ atrānuyogini svatvaṃ na
vivakṣitam, kiṃ tu pratiyogini/ tathā ca
svasamānādhikaraṇaduḥkhaprāgabhāvasamānakālīnaṃ yadyatsvaṃ
tattadvyaktibhedaviśiṣṭaduḥkhadhvaṃso mokṣaḥ/ evaṃ ca
tādṛśabhedakūṭaviśiṣṭatvopalakṣitaduḥkhadhvaṃsatvasya
sakalamuktisādhāraṇatayā na muktipadasya nānārthakatāpattiriti bhāvaḥ/
irttha cāpavargasya mokṣe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/ saṃśayasya
ayathārthānubhavarūpatvasya pūrvamuktatvāt jñānarūpe guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ ukta
ityāśayena mūle saṃśayasyākathanam/ tadāha - saṃśayasya
nirūpitatvāditi/ sukhaprāptirnāma sukhameva/ duḥkhahāniśca
duḥkhadhvaṃsaḥ/ tathā ca prayojanasya guṇe 'bhāve cāntarbhāṃvaḥ/ dṛṣṭāntasya
yathāyathaṃ dravyaguṇādiṣvantarbhāvaḥ/ siddhānto 'pi dravyādirūpa eva/
prāmāṇikatvena svīkṛtārthasyaiva siddhāntatvāt/ nirṇayasya jñānarūpe
guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/ avayavānāṃ śabdarūpatayā prāguktatvāt
guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ, tarkasyāroparūpatāyā uktatvāt
bhramātmakajñāne 'ntarbhāvaḥ iti tayoḥ atrākathanam/
vādajalpavitaṇḍānāṃ śabdarūpatayā guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: and 'not being co-temporal with prior absence of suffering' is the absence delimited by the counter-positive-hood-delimitor of 'being co-temporal with prior absence of suffering.' Since these two absences differ in their delimiting properties of counter-positive-hood, neither is a component of the other — hence there is no scope for redundancy; this is the intent. Now, since 'self-ness' is not a uniform [property across all liberated souls], the liberation constituted by it would also be non-uniform; and hence the word 'liberation' would become equivocal — anticipating this, he says: 'the gist' and so forth. Here, 'self-ness' is not intended with respect to the qualificandum but with respect to the counter-positive. And accordingly, the destruction of suffering qualified by the specific individual instances of [the property] 'self-co-located prior-absence-of-suffering-co-temporal' — whatever is 'self' — that is liberation. And thus, since the property of being a destruction-of-suffering characterized by such a cluster of distinguishing features is common to all instances of liberation, there is no unwanted consequence of the word 'liberation' becoming equivocal — this is the purport. And in this way, <s>apavarga</s> (final release) is subsumed under liberation. Since doubt, having the nature of a non-veridical experience, has been previously mentioned [as such], it is subsumed under quality in the form of cognition — with this intent, doubt is not [separately] mentioned in the root text. This is stated: 'since doubt has been determined' and so forth. The attainment of pleasure is pleasure itself. And the cessation of suffering is the destruction of suffering. And accordingly, the purpose [of valid knowledge] is subsumed under quality and under absence. An example is subsumed under substance, quality, and the like as appropriate. The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) too has the form of substance and the like — since what is accepted as authoritative is itself the established conclusion. Ascertainment is subsumed under quality in the form of cognition. Since the members [of a syllogism], being words, have been previously stated, they are subsumed under quality. Since <s>tarka</s> (suppositional reasoning) has the nature of superimposition, which has been mentioned, it is subsumed under erroneous cognition — hence those two are not mentioned here. Debate (<s>vāda</s>), disputation (<s>jalpa</s>), and cavil (<s>vitaṇḍā</s>), being in the nature of words, are subsumed under quality.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: kathānirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of Debate (<s>Kathā</s>)

children.text:
tattvabubhutsoḥ
kathā vādaḥ/ ubhayasādhanavatī vijigīṣukathā jalpaḥ/ svapakṣasthāpanāhīnā
aparapakṣavidalanamātrāvasānā vitaṇḍā/ kathā nāma
nānāvaktṛkapūrvottarapakṣapratipādakavākyasandarbhaḥ/
children.translated_text: The discourse of one who desires to know the truth is <s>vāda</s> (honest debate). A disputation in which both sides have means of proof and the disputant desires victory is <s>jalpa</s> (disputation). That which lacks the establishment of one's own position and ends merely in the demolition of the opponent's position is <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil). A discourse (<s>kathā</s>) is a series of statements presenting objection and reply by different speakers.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
ubhayasādhanavatīti/
parapakṣanirākaraṇasvapakṣasādhanavatī/ idaṃ ca vitaṇḍāyāṃ
ativyāptivāraṇāyeti dhyeyam/ svapakṣeti/ atra vijigīṣu
kathetyanuvartate/ nāneti/ ekena pūrvapakṣaḥ kriyate, anyena ca
samādhānam, evaṃ krameṇa
children.translated_text: 'Having means of proof for both sides' — having both the refutation of the opponent's position and the establishment of one's own position. This [qualifier] should be noted as serving to prevent over-extension to <s>vitaṇḍā</s>. 'One's own position' — here, the phrase 'disputation in which the disputant desires victory' continues [to apply]. 'By different' — one raises the objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>), and another gives the resolution (<s>samādhāna</s>); thus the multiplicity of agents

children.text:
nānākartṛkatvaṃ
vākyasamūhasyāvaseyam/
children.translated_text: in the collection of statements should be understood.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
parapakṣetyādi/
vijigīṣukathā jalpaḥ ityetāvanmātroktau vitaṇḍāyāmativyāptiḥ/
ataḥ svapakṣasādhanavatītyuktam/ parapakṣanirākaraṇasvapakṣasādhanavatītyatra
parapakṣanirākaraṇamapi jalpe āvaśyakamiti sūcanāya antarbhāvitam,
nātivyāptyādivāraṇāya/ vijigīṣupadenaiva vādasya vāraṇasambhavāta/
duṣṭaheturūpāṇāṃ hetvābhāsānāṃ yathāyathaṃ dravyādiṣvantarbhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Refutation of the opponent's position' and so forth. If only 'disputation in which the disputant desires victory is <s>jalpa</s>' were stated, there would be over-extension to <s>vitaṇḍā</s>. Therefore 'having the establishment of one's own position' is stated. The inclusion of 'refutation of the opponent's position' along with 'establishment of one's own position' in the definition of <s>jalpa</s> is to indicate that the refutation of the opponent is also necessary in <s>jalpa</s>, not to prevent over-extension and the like — since the aversion [of <s>vāda</s>] is possible by the word 'desiring victory' alone. The fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), which are defective reasons, are subsumed under substance and the like as appropriate.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: chalanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of Quibbling (<s>Chala</s>)

children.text:
abhiprāyāntareṇā
pratyuktasyārthāntaraṃ parikalpya dūṣaṇaṃ chalam/
children.translated_text: Quibbling (<s>chala</s>) is: fabricating a different meaning for what is stated by the [opponent] with a different intention, and then refuting [the fabricated meaning].

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
chalamiti/ yathā
'navakambalo 'yaṃ devadattaḥ' iti nūtanatātparyeṇa prayuktasya
navatvasaṅkhyāviśiṣṭamarthāntaraṃ parikalpya kaścit dūṣayati 'nāsya
nava kambalāḥ santi ati daridratvāt' ityādi/
children.translated_text: 'Quibbling' — for example, when someone uses the expression '<s>navakambalaḥ ayaṃ Devadattaḥ</s>' (this <s>Devadatta</s> has a new blanket) with the intention of 'new,' someone else fabricates the alternative meaning qualified by the number nine — 'he does not have nine blankets, because he is extremely poor' — and refutes it thus.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
chalamapi
śabdarūpatvāt guṇe 'ntarbhavati/
children.translated_text: Quibbling too, being in the nature of words, is subsumed under quality.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text: jātinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination of Futile Rejoinder (<s>Jāti</s>)

children.text: asaduttaraṃ jātiḥ/
children.translated_text: A futile rejoinder (<s>jāti</s>) is an unsound reply.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
asaduttaramiti/
uttarasya asatvaṃ tu svāsādhakatāsādhāraṇyena parāsādhakatāsādhakatayā
svavyāghātakatvam/ tathā ca svavyāghātamuttaraṃ jātiriti lakṣaṇaṃ
paryavasyati/
children.translated_text: 'An unsound reply' — the unsoundness of a reply consists in its being self-defeating (<s>svavyāghātaka</s>), in the sense that, by virtue of the uncommon capacity to undermine one's own position, it also undermines the opponent's position. And accordingly, the definition amounts to: a self-defeating reply is a futile rejoinder.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
svāsādhakatāsādhāraṇyeneti/ paramatāsādhakatvasādhanāya hi
jātirūpamuttaramucyate/ taccet svamatāsādhakatāmapi sādhayet tadā
jātirityarthaḥ/ parakīyahetoḥ parāsādhakatve sādhyamāne
svakīyahetoḥ svāsādhakatvamapi yena bhavati tat
children.translated_text: 'By virtue of the uncommon capacity to undermine one's own position' — a reply in the form of a futile rejoinder is uttered for the purpose of undermining the opponent's view. If it should also undermine one's own view, then it is a futile rejoinder — this is the meaning. When the opponent's reason is being shown to be incapable of establishing the opponent's probandum, if by the same token one's own reason is also shown to be incapable of establishing one's own [probandum], then

children.text:
jātyuttaramiti bhāvaḥ/
paramatabādhanārthaṃ ucyamānamuttaraṃ svamatamapi vihanti cet
tādṛguttaraviśeṣo jātiriti phalitor'thaḥ/
children.translated_text: that is a futile rejoinder — this is the purport. A reply uttered for refuting the opponent's view that also harms one's own view — such a specific type of reply is a futile rejoinder — this is the resultant meaning.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>:

children.text:
sādharmya-
vaidharmya-utkarṣa-
apakarṣa-varṇya-avarṇya-vikalpa-sādhya-prāpti-aprāpti-prasaṅga-prati dṛṣṭānta-anutpatti
children.translated_text: Similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>), superiority (<s>utkarṣa</s>), inferiority (<s>apakarṣa</s>), describable (<s>varṇya</s>), indescribable (<s>avarṇya</s>), alternative (<s>vikalpa</s>), established-by-the-opponent's-own-proof (<s>sādhya</s>), obtainment (<s>prāpti</s>), non-obtainment (<s>aprāpti</s>), implication (<s>prasaṅga</s>), counter-example (<s>pratidṛṣṭānta</s>), non-origination (<s>anutpatti</s>),

children.text:
-saṃśaya-prakāraṇa-ahetu- arthāpatti-aviśeṣa-upapatti-upalabdhi -
anupalabdhi - nitya - anitya - kāryaṃ-akārya-samā jātayāḥ/
children.translated_text: doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), elaboration (<s>prakāraṇa</s>), non-reason (<s>ahetu</s>), implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>), non-distinction (<s>aviśeṣa</s>), establishment (<s>upapatti</s>), perception (<s>upalabdhi</s>), non-perception (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), eternal (<s>nitya</s>), non-eternal (<s>anitya</s>), effect (<s>kārya</s>), homogeneous (<s>samā</s>) — these are the [twenty-four types of] futile rejoinders.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text: sādharmyasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of the Similarity-based Futile Rejoinder (<s>Sādharmyasamā</s>)

children.text:
tadabāntarabhedāt
darśayati - sādharmyetyādinā/ dvandvānte śruyamāṇasya samāśabdasya
pratyekaṃ yogaḥ/ sādharmyasamā vaidharmyasametyādayaḥ caturviśatiḥ
jātayaḥ/ sādharmyeṃṇa sthānāhetudūṣakamuttaram sādharmyasamā/ yathā
ātmā
children.translated_text: He shows the sub-varieties: 'similarity' and so forth. The word <s>samā</s> heard at the end of the <s>dvandva</s> compound connects with each [preceding term]. [Thus there are] twenty-four types of futile rejoinders: similarity-based (<s>sādharmyasamā</s>), dissimilarity-based (<s>vaidharmyasamā</s>), and so forth. A reply that refutes the proponent's reason on the basis of similarity is the similarity-based futile rejoinder. For example: the self

children.text:
sakriyaḥ
kriyāhetuguṇavattvātṛ loṣṭavat, kriyā hetuguṇaścātra
kriyājanakavāyusaṃyogādireveti sthāpanāyamuttaram - 'yadi
sakriyasādharmyāt sakriyaḥ tadā vibhutvarūpaniṣkrayasādharmyāt niṣkriya
eva kiṃ na syāta/ na ca atra kiṃñcit vinigamakamasti' iti/
children.translated_text: is active (<s>sakriya</s>), because of possessing a quality that is a cause of activity, like a clod of earth — and the quality that is the cause of activity here is the conjunction with air and the like — to this establishment, the reply is: 'If it is active because of the similarity with active [things], then by the similarity with the all-pervading, which has the nature of inactivity, why should it not be inactive? There is no determining factor here [to prefer one over the other].'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
sādharmyasamāyāḥ
sodāharaṇaṃ lakṣaṇamāha - sādharmyeṇeti/ vādinā svasādhyasādhanārthaṃ
hetau prayukte sati prativādinaḥ dṛṣṭāntasādṛśyamātrāvaṣṭabdhena
hetunā vādyabhimatasādhyābhāvasādhanamukhena vādyuktahetoḥ
svasādhyāsādhakatvasādhakamuttaraṃ sādharmyasametyathaiḥ/ yathā ātmetyādi/
yo yaḥ kriyāhetubhūtaguṇavān sa kriyāvān;
children.translated_text: He states the definition of the similarity-based futile rejoinder with an example: 'on the basis of similarity' and so forth. When the proponent has employed his reason for the purpose of establishing his own <s>sādhya</s>, the opponent, relying merely on the similarity with the example, by means of a reason that [purports to] establish the absence of the proponent's <s>sādhya</s>, gives a reply that proves the proponent's reason to be incapable of establishing his own <s>sādhya</s> — that is the similarity-based futile rejoinder; thus say others. For example, 'the self' and so forth. Whatever possesses a quality that is a cause of activity is active;

children.text:
yathā loṣṭaḥ
kriyāhetubhūtavāyusaṃyogarūpaguṇavattvāt kriyāvān tadvat
ātmāpi tādṛśaguṇavattvāt kriyāvān iti vādinokte sati,
prativādī vadati 'yadi kriyāhetuguṇavattvena rūpeṇa loṣṭasādṛśyāt
ātmanaḥ kriyāvattvaṃ tarhi yathā paramamahatparimāṇavataḥ ākāśasya
niṣkriyatvaṃ tathā ātmano 'pi paramamahatparimāṇavattvāt niṣkriyatvaṃ
kiṃ na-syāt; ātmā niṣkriyaḥ paramamahatparimāṇavattvāt
ākāśavadityapi vaktuṃ śakyatvāt' iti dūṣayati/ etādṛśaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ
sādharmyasametyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: just as a clod of earth is active because of possessing the quality of conjunction with air that is a cause of activity, similarly the self too is active because of possessing such a quality — when the proponent states thus, the opponent retorts: 'If the self is active because of the similarity with a clod through possessing a quality that is a cause of activity, then just as space, which possesses the largest magnitude, is inactive, similarly the self too, possessing the largest magnitude, why should it not be inactive? Since one could equally say: the self is inactive, because of possessing the largest magnitude, like space.' Such a refutation is the similarity-based futile rejoinder — this is the meaning.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text: vaidharmyasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of the Dissimilarity-based Futile Rejoinder (<s>Vaidharmyasamā</s>)

children.text:
vaidharmyeṇa
dūṣakamuttaram vaidharmyasamā/ yathā tatraiva kriyāvato loṣṭasya
sādharmyāt yadi kriyāvānātmā, tadā vibhutvarūpatadvaidharmyāt
niṣkriya eva kiṃ na syāt/ na hi tatsādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyam,
tadvaidharmyāt niṣkriyeṇa na bhavitavyam ityatra kiñcit
niyāmakamasti iti/
children.translated_text: A reply that refutes on the basis of dissimilarity is the dissimilarity-based futile rejoinder. For example, in the same context: 'If the self is active because of similarity with the active clod of earth, then by the dissimilarity with it in the form of being all-pervading, why should it not be inactive? There is no determining factor that [dictates] one must be active because of that similarity, and one must not be inactive because of that dissimilarity.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
evaṃ
dṛṣṭāntāvṛttidharmavattvarūpeṇa dṛṣṭāntavaidhārmyeṇa vādyuktahetoḥ
svasādhyāsādhakatvakathanaṃ vaidharmyaṃsamā/ vibhutvarūpeti/ vibhutvaṃ
paramamahatparimāṇavattvam/ tathā ca vādinā ātmā kriyāvān
kriyāhetuguṇavattvāt loṣṭavat ityukte, ātmā niṣkriyaḥ
sakriyaloṣṭavidharmatvāt iti prativādī vadati/ sakriye loṣṭe
vidyamānasya dharmasya sattvāt
children.translated_text: Thus, stating the incapacity of the proponent's reason to establish his own <s>sādhya</s> on the basis of dissimilarity — in the form of possessing a property absent from the example — is the dissimilarity-based futile rejoinder. 'Of the nature of being all-pervading' — being all-pervading means possessing the largest magnitude. And accordingly, when the proponent states 'the self is active, because of possessing a quality that is a cause of activity, like a clod of earth,' the opponent says 'the self is inactive, because of being dissimilar from an active clod.' Since there is a property present in the clod [that is absent from the self],

children.text:
ātmā loṣṭavat
sakriyaścet loṣṭe avidyamānasya vibhutvasya ātmani sattvāt ātmā
niṣkriya eva kuto na syāditi dūṣanaṃ vaidharmyasametyuktaṃ bhavati/
children.translated_text: if the self is active like a clod, then since all-pervasiveness — which is absent from the clod — is present in the self, why should the self not be inactive? — such a refutation is what is called the dissimilarity-based futile rejoinder.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text: utkarṣasamālakṣaṇam
