children.translated_text: Definition of the Superiority-based Futile Rejoinder (<s>Utkarṣasamā</s>)

children.text:
paroktasādhanādeva
tadavyāpakasya dharmasya pakṣe āpādanam utkarṣasamā/ yathā śabdo 'nityaḥ
kṛtakatvāt ghaṭavat ityādau kaścidevamāha 'yadi kṛtakatvena
hetunā śabdaḥ ghaṭavadanityaḥ syāt, tarhi tenaiva śabdaḥ
ghaṭavadaśrāvaṇo 'pi syāt' iti/
children.translated_text: Attributing to the subject a property not pervaded by the opponent's stated reason [i.e. a superior property] is the superiority-based futile rejoinder. For example, in 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being produced, like a pot' — someone says thus: 'If by the reason of being produced, sound is non-eternal like a pot, then by that very [reason], sound should also be inaudible like a pot.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>:

children.text:
utkarṣasamāyā
lakṣaṇamāha - paroktasādhanādeveti/ pareṇa svasādhyasādhanāya yo
heturucyate tenaiva tādṛśahetoravyāpako yaḥ dharmaḥ tasya pakṣe
prasañjanaṃ utkarṣasametyarthaḥ/ yathā śabdo 'nityaḥ kṛtakatvādityatra
kaścidāha - yadi kṛtakatvena hetunā śabdaḥ ghaṭavadanityaḥ tarhi
tenaiva hetunā śabdaḥ ghaṭavad aśrāvaṇo 'pi syāditi/ atra hetoḥ
kṛtakatvasya avyāpakaḥ dharmaḥ aśrāvaṇatvaṃ tasya pakṣe āpādanaṃ kriyate/
īdṛśamuttaraṃ utkarṣasamā/"vyāptimapuraskṛtya
pakṣadṛṣṭāntānyatarasmin sādhyasādhanānyatareṇa
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>utkarṣasamā</s> (rejoinder by over-attribution) — 'from the very means stated by the opponent' and so forth. The meaning is: <s>utkarṣasamā</s> is the attribution to the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) of a property that is not pervaded by the very <s>hetu</s> (reason) that the opponent states for establishing his own <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). For example, in the inference 'sound is impermanent, because of being produced,' someone says — if by the reason of being produced, sound is impermanent like a pot, then by that very reason, sound should also be inaudible like a pot. Here, the property of inaudibility, which is not pervaded by the <s>hetu</s> — being produced — is attributed to the <s>pakṣa</s>. Such a reply is <s>utkarṣasamā</s>. 'Without regard for <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), the attribution of a property not present in either the <s>pakṣa</s> or the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) by either the <s>sādhya</s> or the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof)

children.text:
avidyamānadharmaprasañjanaṃ
utkarṣasamaḥ/ yathā śabdo 'nityaḥ kṛtakatvāt iti sthāpanāyām
anityatvaṃ kṛtakatvaṃ ca ghaṭe rūpasahacaritam, ataḥ śabdo 'pi rūpavān
syāt/ evaṃ śrāvaṇaśabdasādharmyāt kṛtakatvāt ghaṭo 'pi śrāvaṇaḥ
syādaviśeṣāt"iti viśvanāthaḥ/
children.translated_text: is <s>utkarṣasamā</s> (rejoinder by over-attribution). For example, in the establishment 'sound is impermanent, because of being produced,' impermanence and being produced are accompanied by color in the pot; therefore, sound too should possess color. Similarly, by the similarity with audible sound, from being produced, the pot too should be audible, since there is no distinction' — thus says <s>Viśvanātha</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: apakarṣasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>apakarṣasamā</s> (rejoinder by under-attribution)

children.text:
paroktadṛṣṭāntasādharmyeṇa pakṣe parābhimatadharmāntarasya
abhāvasādhanam apakarṣasamā/ yathā tasminneva anumāne 'yadi
kṛtakatvena śabdaḥ ghaṭavadanityaḥ syāt tarhiṃ tenaiva śabdo
ghaṭavadaśrāvaṇo 'pi syāt' iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Apakarṣasamā</s> (rejoinder by under-attribution) is the proof of the absence in the <s>pakṣa</s> of another property accepted by the opponent, on the basis of similarity with the example stated by the opponent. For example, in that very inference: 'if by being produced, sound were impermanent like a pot, then by that very reason, sound should also be inaudible like a pot.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
avidyamānadharmaprasañjanaṃ utkarṣaṃsamā/ vidyamānadharmābhāvaprasañjanaṃ
apakarṣasamā/ tadāha - paroktadṛṣṭāntasādharmyeṇeti/ pareṇa vādinā
ukto yo dṛṣṭāntaḥ tatsādharmyeṇa pakṣe vādyabhimatasya
arthāntarasyābhāvasādhanam apakarṣasamā/ yathā śabdo 'nityaḥ
kṛtakatvāt iti vādinokte prativādī vadati - yadi
kṛtakatvarūpāt ghaṭasādharmyāt śabdo ghaṭavadanityaḥ tarhi tasmādeva
hetoḥ śabdaḥ ghaṭavat aśrāvaṇo 'pi syāditi/ atra pakṣe śabde
anityatvavat vādyabhimataṃ arthāntaraṃ śrāvaṇatvaṃ tadabhāvasya prasañjanaṃ
kriyate iti samanvayaḥ/"sādhye dharmābhāvaṃ dṛṣṭāntāt
prasajato 'pakarṣasamaḥ"iti bhāṣyam/
children.translated_text: <s>Utkarṣasamā</s> (rejoinder by over-attribution) is the attribution of a property not present. <s>Apakarṣasamā</s> (rejoinder by under-attribution) is the attribution of the absence of a property that is present. He says this — 'by similarity with the example stated by the opponent' and so forth. <s>Apakarṣasamā</s> is the proof of the absence in the <s>pakṣa</s> of some other thing accepted by the proponent, based on similarity with the example stated by the opponent, the proponent. For example, when the proponent states 'sound is impermanent, because of being produced,' the opponent replies — if from the similarity with the pot in the form of being produced, sound is impermanent like a pot, then from that very reason, sound should also be inaudible like a pot. Here the application is: in the <s>pakṣa</s>, sound, the absence of audibility — which is another property accepted by the proponent, just like impermanence — is attributed. 'The <s>apakarṣasama</s> attributes the absence of a property to the <s>sādhya</s> from the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>' — thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: varṇyasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>varṇyasamā</s> (rejoinder by reciprocal establishment)

children.text:
varṇyasya
sthāpanīyasya dṛṣṭāntadharmasya pakṣe sādhanam varṇyasamā/ yathā
pūrvoktānumāne 'kriyājanakanodanākhyasaṃyogavattvāt loṣṭādeḥ
bhavatu kriyāvattvam/ ātmanastu kriyāvattve
tajjanakanodanākhyasaṃyogavattvamapi syāt' iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Varṇyasamā</s> (rejoinder by reciprocal establishment) is the proof in the <s>pakṣa</s> of a property of the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) that is to be established. For example, in the aforementioned inference: 'since the clod of earth and such things possess contact called impulsion that produces action, let them have the property of possessing action. But if the <s>ātman</s> (self) possesses action, it should also possess the contact called impulsion that produces action.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
varṇyasamāṃ lakṣayati
- varṇyasyeti/ dṛṣṭānte vidyamānasya pakṣe sthāpanīyasya sādhanaṃ
varṇyasamā/ yathā ātmā kriyāvān kriyāhetuguṇavattvāt
loṣṭavaditi vādinokte prativādī uttarayati-loṣṭādeḥ
kriyājanakanodanākhyasaṃyogavattvāt kriyāvattvaṃ bhavatu/ ātmanastu
kriyāvattve loṣṭavat kriyājanakanodanākhyasaṃyogavānātmā
bhavediti/ īdṛśamuttaraṃ varṇyasamā/"khyāpanīyo varṇyo
viparyayādavarṇyaḥ"iti bhāṣyam/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>varṇyasamā</s> — 'of what is to be described' and so forth. <s>Varṇyasamā</s> is the proof in the <s>pakṣa</s> of what is present in the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> and is to be established. For example, when the proponent states 'the self possesses action, because of possessing a quality that is the cause of action, like a clod of earth,' the opponent replies — let the clod of earth have the property of possessing action because of possessing contact called impulsion that causes action. But if the self has action, then like the clod of earth, the self should also possess contact called impulsion that causes action. Such a reply is <s>varṇyasamā</s>. 'What is to be demonstrated is <s>varṇya</s>; its opposite is <s>avarṇya</s>' — thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: avarṇyasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>avarṇyasamā</s> (rejoinder by reciprocal non-establishment)

children.text:
sādhyahetvordharmayorapi pakṣe tulyatāsādhanam avarṇyasamā/
yathā tatraivānumāne loṣṭādigatanodanādirūpakriyāhetuguṇavattvaṃ
ātmanyasiddham/ tathā ca tulyatayā yathā asiddhena kriyāhetuguṇena
ātmanikriyāvattvaṃ sādhyate, tathā tādṛśena kriyāvattvena
tajjanakaguṇavattvamapi kimiti na sādhyate niyāmakābhāvāt iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Avarṇyasamā</s> (rejoinder by reciprocal non-establishment) is the proof of the equality of both the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and the <s>hetu</s> (reason) in the <s>pakṣa</s>. For example, in that very inference — the quality that is the cause of action, in the form of impulsion and so forth found in clods of earth, is unestablished in the <s>ātman</s> (self). And accordingly, since both are equally unestablished, just as the property of possessing action is established in the self through the unestablished quality that causes action, why should not the possession of such a quality also be established through such a property of possessing action? — because there is no determining factor.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
avarṇyasamāmāha - sādhyahetvoriti/ pakṣe
sādhyahetvordvayorapi tulyatvāt yat vādidūṣakamuttaraṃ
tadavarṇyasamā/ yathā ātmā sakriyaḥ kriyāhetuguṇavattvāt loṣṭavat
ityanumāne eva ātmani kriyāvattvamapi asiddham,
kriyāhetunodanākhyasaṃyogavattvamapyasiddham/ tatrāsiddhena
nodanākhyena kriyāhetuguṇena ātmanaḥ sakriyatvaṃ sādhyate cet
asiddhena kriyāvattvena kriyājanakanodanākhyasaṃyogavattvamapi kuto na
sādhyate niyāmakābhāvāt ityevaṃ yaduttaraṃ tadavarṇyasametyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states <s>avarṇyasamā</s> — 'of the <s>sādhya</s> and the <s>hetu</s>' and so forth. <s>Avarṇyasamā</s> is the reply that defeats the proponent by virtue of the equality of both the <s>sādhya</s> and the <s>hetu</s> in the <s>pakṣa</s>. For example, when the inference 'the self possesses action, because of possessing a quality that is the cause of action, like a clod of earth' is stated, in the self, both the possession of action and the possession of the quality in the form of contact called impulsion that is the cause of action are unestablished. If the proponent establishes the possession of action in the self through the unestablished quality that is the cause of action in the form of impulsion, then why should not the possession of contact called impulsion that causes action also be established through the unestablished property of possessing action? — because there is no determining factor. Such a reply is <s>avarṇyasamā</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: vikalpasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>vikalpasamā</s> (rejoinder by disjunction)

children.text:
dṛṣṭāntavikalpaṃ
pradarśya dārṣṭāntikavikalpakathanaṃ vikalpasamā/ yathā tatraiva anumāne
'kriyāhetuguṇayuktaṃ kiñcit laghu, yathāsa vāyuḥ, evaṃ
kriyāhetuguṇayuktaṃ kiñcit kriyāvat syāt yathā loṣṭādi
kiñcidakriyam yathā ātmā/ pūrvavikalpo bhavati ayaṃ tu na
bhavatītyatra kiṃ nayāmakaṃ syāt' iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Vikalpasamā</s> (rejoinder by disjunction) is showing a disjunction in the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) and then stating a corresponding disjunction in the case of the subject under discussion. For example, in that very inference: 'something possessing the quality that causes action is light, like air; likewise, something possessing the quality that causes action may have action, like a clod of earth, or something may lack action, like the self. What would be the determining factor for the first disjunct to hold but not this one?'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
vikalpasamāmāha -
dṛṣṭāntāvikalpaṃ pradarśyeti/ dṛṣṭānte vividhaṃ kalpaṃ pradarśya
dārṣṭāntike 'pi vividhakalpapradarśanaṃ vikalpasametyarthaḥ/ yathā
pūrvokte ātmā sakriyaḥ kriyāhetuguṇavattvāt ityanumāne eva
kriyāhetuguṇayuktaṃ kiñcit guru yathā
children.translated_text: He states <s>vikalpasamā</s> — 'showing a disjunction in the example' and so forth. Having shown diverse alternatives in the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, the showing of diverse alternatives also in the case of the subject is <s>vikalpasamā</s> — this is the meaning. For example, in the very aforementioned inference 'the self possesses action, because of possessing the quality that causes action,' something possessing the quality that causes action is heavy, like

children.text:
loṣṭādi kiñcillaghu
yathā vāyuḥ, evaṃ kiṃyāhetuguṇayuktaṃ kiñcitsakriyaṃ yathā ghaṭādi,
kiñcidakriyaṃ yathā ātmā/ tatra pūrvo vikalpa eva samīcīṃnaḥ ayaṃ tu
vikalpaḥ na samīcīnaḥ ityatra niyāmakaṃ kimapi nāsti/ tathā ca
kriyāhetuguṇavattve samāne 'pi kasyacit sakriyatvamityapi
sambhavatīti tena hetunā ātmano niṣkriyattvamevāstu iti rītyā
yaduttaraṃ tat vikalpasamā/
children.translated_text: a clod of earth, and something is light, like air. Similarly, something possessing the quality that causes action has action, like a pot and so forth, and something lacks action, like the self. There, only the first alternative is correct, but this alternative is not correct — for this there is no determining factor whatsoever. And accordingly, even though the quality that causes action is equally present, it is also possible that something lacks action. Therefore, by that reason, let the self be devoid of action indeed — such a reply in this manner is <s>vikalpasamā</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: sādhyasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>sādhyasamā</s> (rejoinder by reversibility of thesis and example)

children.text:
dṛṣṭāntasya
pakṣatulyatākathanam sādhyasamā/ sādhyaśabdo 'tra pakṣavācī/ yathā tatraiva
yadi 'yathā loṣṭaḥ tathā ātmā' iti tvayā ucyate tadā 'yathā ātmā
tathā loṣṭaḥ' ityapyāyātam/ tathā ca yadyātmani kriyāvattvaṃ sādhyate
tarhi loṣṭe 'pi tatsādhanīyam neti cettarhi yathā loṣṭaḥ tathā
ātmeti na vācyam/ 'loṣṭasadṛśa ātmā, nātmasadṛśo
children.translated_text: <s>Sādhyasamā</s> (rejoinder by reversibility) is the statement that the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) is on par with the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus). Here the word <s>sādhya</s> denotes the <s>pakṣa</s>. For example, in that very inference: if you say 'as the clod of earth, so the self,' then it also follows that 'as the self, so the clod of earth.' And accordingly, if the possession of action is to be established in the self, then it should also be established in the clod of earth. If not, then one should not say 'as the clod of earth, so the self' — because there is no determining factor for saying 'the self is like the clod of earth' but not 'the clod of earth is like the self.'

children.text:
loṣṭaḥ' ityatra
niyāmakābhāvāt iti/
children.translated_text: Because there is no determining factor.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
sādhyasamāmāha -
dṛṣṭāntasya pakṣatulyatākathanamiti/ sādhyate 'sminniti vyutpattyā
sādhyaśabdaḥ pakṣavācī/ dṛṣṭāntaḥ pakṣatulya ityāpādanaṃ sādhyasamā/
śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam/"hetvādyavayavasāmarthyayogī dharmaḥ sādhyaḥ tra
dṛṣṭānte prasajataḥ sādhyasamaḥ/ yadi yathā loṣṭaḥ tathā ātmā,
prāptastarhi yathā ātmā tathā loṣṭa iti/ sādhyaścāyamātmā
kriyāvāniti kāmaṃ loṣṭo 'pi sādhyaḥ/ atha naivam, na tarhi yathā
loṣṭaḥ tathā ātmā"iti bhāṣyam/
children.translated_text: He states <s>sādhyasamā</s> — 'the statement that the example is on par with the thesis-locus' and so forth. By the derivation 'that in which something is to be established,' the word <s>sādhya</s> denotes the <s>pakṣa</s>. <s>Sādhyasamā</s> is the attribution that the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> is equal to the <s>pakṣa</s>. The rest is clear. 'The property that is connected with the capacity of the members such as the <s>hetu</s> is <s>sādhya</s>; the <s>sādhyasama</s> attributes it in the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>. If as the clod of earth so the self, then it follows that as the self so the clod of earth. And this self is <s>sādhya</s> — to be established as possessing action — so let the clod of earth too be <s>sādhya</s>. If not so, then it is not the case that as the clod of earth so the self' — thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: prāptisamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>prāptisamā</s> (rejoinder from co-location)

children.text:
prāptyā
pratyavasthānam prāptisamā/ prāptiśca sādhyahetvoḥ
sāmānādhikaraṇyam/ yathā tatraiva kriyāhetuguṇavattvenaiva kimiti
kriyāvattvaṃ sādhyate kimiti kriyāvattvena tādṛśaguṇavattvaṃ na
ubhayoraviśeṣāt iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Prāptisamā</s> (rejoinder from co-location) is the counter-argument through <s>prāpti</s> (co-location). And <s>prāpti</s> is the <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-location) of the <s>sādhya</s> and the <s>hetu</s>. For example, in that very inference: why is the property of possessing action established by the quality that causes action alone? Why should not the possession of such a quality be established by the property of possessing action? — because there is no distinction between the two.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
prāptisamāmāha -
prāptyā pratyavasthānamiti/ sādhyena saha ekādhikaraṇavṛttitvaṃ
hetorasti cet hetunā sākaṃ ekādhikaraṇavṛttitvaṃ
sādhyasyāpyastītyaṅgīkaraṇīyam/ tathā ca sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ
puraskṛtya hetunā sādhyaṃ sādhyate cet hetusāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ
puraskṛtya sādhyenaiva hetuḥ sādhyatām/ evaṃ ca ātmā kriyāvān
kriyāhetuguṇavattvāt itivat ātmā kriyāhetuguṇavān
kriyāvattvāt ityapi sādhyatām aviśeṣāt iti pratyavasthānaṃ
prāptisametyarthaḥ/ ubhayoraviśeṣāditi/ ubhayoḥ
sāmānādhikaraṇyāviśeṣādityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states <s>prāptisamā</s> — '<s>prāpti</s> as the counter-argument' and so forth. If the <s>hetu</s> (reason) has the property of occurring in the same locus as the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), then the <s>sādhya</s> too must be acknowledged to have the property of occurring in the same locus as the <s>hetu</s>. And accordingly, if the <s>sādhya</s> is established by the <s>hetu</s> on the basis of the co-location of the <s>hetu</s> with the <s>sādhya</s>, then let the <s>hetu</s> itself be established by the <s>sādhya</s> on the basis of the co-location of the <s>sādhya</s> with the <s>hetu</s>. And thus, just as 'the self possesses action, because of possessing the quality that causes action,' so too 'the self possesses the quality that causes action, because of possessing action' should also be established, since there is no distinction — such a counter-argument is <s>prāptisamā</s>. 'Because there is no distinction between the two' means: because there is no distinction in the co-location of both.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: aprāptisamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>aprāptisamā</s> (rejoinder from non-co-location)

children.text:
aprāptyā
pratyavasthānam aprāptisamā/ yathā tatraiva pūrvoktadoṣādaprāptasya
hetoḥ sādhyasādhakatvaṃ vācyam, tathā cāprāptatvāviśeṣāt sarvaḥ
sarvaṃ sādhayet iti/ ayameva hetuḥ sādhyābhāvaṃ kimiti na
sādhayet/ sādhyameva tu sādhayedityatra vinigamakābhāvāt iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Aprāptisamā</s> (rejoinder from non-co-location) is the counter-argument through <s>aprāpti</s> (non-co-location). For example, in that very inference: it must be said that the <s>hetu</s>, which has not arrived at the <s>sādhya</s> due to the aforementioned defect, has the capacity to establish the <s>sādhya</s>. And accordingly, since there is no distinction in the non-arrival, everything should establish everything. Why should not this very <s>hetu</s> establish the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>? That it should establish the <s>sādhya</s> alone — for this there is no determining factor.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
aprāptisamāmāha -
aprāptyā pratyavasthānamiti/ aprāptiḥ sādhyahetvoḥ
asāmānādhikaraṇyam/ atraivaṃ vikalpaḥ kartavyaḥ/ ātmā kriyāvān
kriyāhetuguṇavattvāt ityukte ayaṃ hetuḥ sādhyasamānādhikaraṇaḥ
san sādhyaṃ sādhayati vā? sādhyāsamānādhikaraṇaḥ san sādhyaṃ sādhayati
vā? ādye sāmānādhikaraṇyāviśeṣāt sādhyenāpi kuto na hetuḥ
sādhyata iti pratyavasthānāt prāptisamā/ dvitīye
asāmānādhikaraṇyāviśeṣāt sādhyamiva anyat sarvaṃmapi hetuḥ kuto
na sādhayet/ tathā ca sarvaḥ sarvaṃ sādhayet/ tathā heturyathā
sādhyenāsamānādhikaraṇo 'pi sādhyaṃ sādhayati tathā
sādhābhāvenāsamānādhikaraṇatvāt sādhyābhāvameva kuto na
sādhayet? iti rītyā pratyavasthānam - dūṣaṇakathanam
aprāptisametyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states <s>aprāptisamā</s> — '<s>aprāpti</s> as the counter-argument' and so forth. <s>Aprāpti</s> is the non-co-location of the <s>sādhya</s> and the <s>hetu</s>. Here the following dilemma must be constructed: when it is stated 'the self possesses action, because of possessing the quality that causes action,' does this <s>hetu</s> establish the <s>sādhya</s> while being co-located with the <s>sādhya</s>, or does it establish the <s>sādhya</s> while not being co-located with the <s>sādhya</s>? In the first case, since there is no distinction in co-location, why should not the <s>hetu</s> also be established by the <s>sādhya</s>? — this counter-argument is <s>prāptisamā</s>. In the second case, since there is no distinction in non-co-location, why should not the <s>hetu</s> also establish everything else besides the <s>sādhya</s>? And accordingly, everything would establish everything. Moreover, just as the <s>hetu</s>, despite not being co-located with the <s>sādhya</s>, establishes the <s>sādhya</s>, so too, since it is not co-located with the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, why should it not establish the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> alone? — the counter-argument, i.e., the statement of the objection, in this manner is <s>aprāptisamā</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: prasaṅgasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>prasaṅgasamā</s> (rejoinder by infinite regress)

children.text:
sādhanaparamparāpraśnaḥ prasaṅgasamā/ yathā kriyāvattve
kriyāhetuguṇavattvaṃ sādhanam/ tatra kiṃ sādhanam? na hi sādhanaṃ vinā
kasyacit siddhirasti/ evaṃ tatrāpi kiṃ sādhanamityādi/
children.translated_text: <s>Prasaṅgasamā</s> (rejoinder by infinite regress) is the questioning of an infinite chain of means of proof. For example: for the possession of action, the quality that causes action is the means of proof. But what is the means of proof for that? For nothing is established without a means of proof. And likewise for that too, what is the means of proof? — and so on.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
prasaṅgasamāṃ
lakṣayati - sādhanaparamparāpraśna iti/ sādhanaparamparā viṣayakaḥ praśnaḥ
prasaṅgasamā/"sādhanasyāpi sādhanaṃ vaktavyamiti
prasaṅgena pratyavasthānaṃ prasaṅgasamaḥ"iti bhāṣyam/ śiṣṭaṃ
spaṣṭam/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>prasaṅgasamā</s> — 'the questioning of an infinite chain of means of proof' and so forth. <s>Prasaṅgasamā</s> is the question having as its object an infinite chain of means of proof. 'One must state the means of proof of the means of proof as well — the counter-argument through such an implication is <s>prasaṅgasama</s>' — thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. The rest is clear.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: pratidṛṣṭāntasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>pratidṛṣṭāntasamā</s> (rejoinder by counter-example)

children.text:
dṛṣṭāntāntareṇa
sādhyābhāvasādhanam pratidṛṣṭāntasamā/ yathā 'tatraiva loṣṭadṛṣṭāntena
kriyāvattve sādhite niṣkriyākāśadṛṣṭāntena ātmano niṣkriyattvameva
kiṃ na syāt/ loṣṭadṛṣṭāntena kriyāvattvaṃ ākāśadṛṣṭāntena
children.translated_text: <s>Pratidṛṣṭāntasamā</s> (rejoinder by counter-example) is the proof of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> through a different example. For example, 'in that very inference, when the possession of action is established through the example of a clod of earth, why should not the actionlessness of the self follow from the example of actionless <s>ākāśa</s> (space)? That the example of the clod of earth proves the possession of action while the example of <s>ākāśa</s> proves

children.text:
niṣkriyattvaṃ na ityatra
niyāmakābhāvāt' iti/
children.translated_text: the absence of action — for this there is no determining factor.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pratidṛṣṭāntasamāmāha - dṛṣṭāntāntareṇeti/ ātmā kriyāvān
kriyāhetuguṇayuktatvāt loṣṭavat iti loṣṭadṛṣṭāntena
kriyāvattvaṃ sādhyate cet ātmā niṣkriyaḥ
kriyāhetuvāyusaṃyogavattvāt ākāśavat ityākāśadṛṣṭāntena
kuto na sādhayituṃ śakyata iti prakṛtasādhyaśūnyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaṃ pradarśya
dūṣaṇodbhāvanaṃ pratidṛṣṭāntasamā/"kriyāvān ātmā
kriyāhetuguṇayogāt loṣṭavat ityukte pratidṛṣṭānta upādīyate
kriyāhetuguṇayuktaṃ ākāśaṃ niṣkriyaṃ dṛṣṭathmati/ kaḥ punarākāśasyaṃ
kriyāhetuguṇaḥ, vāyunā saṃyogaḥ"iti bhāṣyam/
children.translated_text: He states <s>pratidṛṣṭāntasamā</s> — 'through a different example' and so forth. If it is said that the possession of action is established through the example of the clod of earth in the inference 'the self possesses action, because of possessing the quality that causes action, like a clod of earth,' then why can it not be established through the example of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) that 'the self is actionless, because of possessing contact with air, like <s>ākāśa</s>'? <s>Pratidṛṣṭāntasamā</s> is the raising of an objection by presenting an example devoid of the <s>sādhya</s> in question. 'When it is said that the self possesses action because of possessing the quality that causes action, like a clod of earth, a counter-example is adduced: <s>ākāśa</s>, which possesses the quality that causes action, is seen to be actionless. And what is the quality that causes action in <s>ākāśa</s>? Contact with air' — thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: anutpattisamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>anutpattisamā</s> (rejoinder by non-origination)

children.text:
anutpattyā
pratyavasthānam anutpattisamā/ yathā 'ghaṭo na nityaḥ janyaikātvāt'
ityādau kaścidāha - yadi janyaikatvaṃ anityatve pramāṇam tadā ghaṭe
ekatvotpatteḥ pūrvaṃ tadabhāvāt nityatvam/ nityaścet tarhi anutpanna
eveti/
children.translated_text: Objection by [pointing to] non-origination is <s>anutpattisama</s> (the futile rejoinder of non-origination). For example, in 'the pot is not eternal because it has originated oneness,' someone says: if originated oneness is the proof of non-eternality, then prior to the origination of oneness in the pot, due to the absence of that [oneness], [the pot would be] eternal. And if eternal, then it is simply unoriginated.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
anutpattisamāmāha -
anutpattyā pratyavasthānamiti/ janyaikatvāditi/ janyaṃ ca tat ekatvaṃ ca
janyaikatvam, tasmāt/ anutpanna eveti/ tathā ca anityatvaṃ
bādhitāmiti bhāvaḥ/"tathā ca sādhanāṅgapakṣahetudṛṣṭāntānāṃ
utpatteḥ prāk hetvabhāva ityanutpattyā pratyavasthānaṃ anutpattisamaḥ/
utpatteḥ pūrvaṃ hetvādyabhāvena pratyavasthānasyaiva lakṣaṇatvāt"iti
viśvanārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states <s>anutpattisama</s> by saying 'objection by non-origination.' 'Because of originated oneness' means: originated and oneness — originated oneness; from that. 'Simply unoriginated' — and accordingly, the purport is that non-eternality is contradicted. '<s>Viśvanātha</s>' says: 'And accordingly, the objection by non-origination — namely, the absence of the reason prior to the origination of the components of the proof such as the thesis, the reason, and the example — is <s>anutpattisama</s>. Because the definition is precisely the objection through the absence of the reason and so forth prior to origination.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: saṃśayasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>saṃśayasama</s> (the futile rejoinder of doubt)

children.text:
sādhāraṇadharmaṃ
pradarśyaṃ saṃśayodbhāvanaṃ saṃśayasamā/ yathā 'śabdo 'nityaḥ
kāryatvāt' ityādau 'śabdasya anityaghaṭena saha kāryatvarūpaṃ
sādharmyaṃ yathā asti tathā nityena śabdatvena saha śrāvaṇapratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ
sādharmyaṃ astīti ubhayasādharmyadarśanāt saṃśayaḥ syāt/ ekapariśeṣe
niyāmakābhāvāt' iti/
children.translated_text: Raising doubt by displaying a common property is <s>saṃśayasama</s>. For example, in 'sound is non-eternal because of being an effect' and so forth: 'just as sound has the common property of being an effect with the non-eternal pot, so too it has the common property of being an object of auditory perception with the eternal entity sound-hood. From perceiving similarity with both, there would be doubt — since in a case where one alternative remains, there is no determining factor.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
saṃśayasamāmāha -
sādhāraṇadharmaṃ pradarśyeti/ spaṣṭārtham/"nityānityasādharmyāditi
saṃśayakāraṇopalakṣaṇam/ tena samānadharmadarśanādi
yatkiñcitsaṃśayakāraṇabalāt saṃśayena pratyavasthānaṃ saṃśayasamaḥ"iti
viśvanāthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states <s>saṃśayasama</s> by saying 'displaying a common property.' The meaning is clear. <s>Viśvanātha</s> says: ''From similarity with eternal and non-eternal' is an indication of the cause of doubt. Therefore, objection through doubt on the strength of any cause of doubt such as perceiving a common property is <s>saṃśayasama</s>.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: prakaraṇasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>prakaraṇasama</s> (the futile rejoinder of counter-thesis)

children.text:
vādyuktahetoḥ
sādhyaviparītasādhakahetvantarodbhāvanam prakaraṇasamā/
satpratipakṣodāharaṇameva atrodāharaṇaṃ bodhyam/
children.translated_text: Adducing another reason that establishes the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) against the reason stated by the proponent is <s>prakaraṇasama</s>. The example of <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (established counter-reason) itself should be understood as the example here.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
prakaraṇasamāmāha
vādyaktahetoriti/ śabdaḥ anityaḥ kṛtakatvāt ghaṭavat iti vādinā
anityatvasādhanāya kṛtakatvahetau ukte sati tādṛśahetusādhyasya
anityatvasya viparītaṃ yat śabdaḥ nityaḥ śrāvaṇatvāt śabdatvavat
ityevaṃ prayujyamānaṃ hetvantaram śrāvaṇatvākhyaṃ tadudbhāvanena
pratyavasthānaṃ prakaraṇasametyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states <s>prakaraṇasama</s> by saying 'of the reason stated by the proponent.' When the proponent states the reason of being-produced for establishing non-eternality in the form 'sound is non-eternal because of being produced, like a pot,' then adducing another reason called audibility — in the form 'sound is eternal because of audibility, like sound-hood' — which establishes the opposite of non-eternality, which is the <s>sādhya</s> of that reason: objection through such adduction is <s>prakaraṇasama</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: ahetusamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>ahetusama</s> (the futile rejoinder of non-reason)

children.text:
kālatraye 'pi
hetutvāsambhavena ahetutvakathanam ahetusamā/ yathā
'kāryatvādirūpasādhanaṃ sādhyādanityatvāt pūrvakālavṛtti cet
tadānityatvarūpasādhyasya tadānīmabhāvāt kasya sādhakam/ atha
paścātkālavṛtti cet tadā pūrvakāle sādhanābhāvāt kasya
sādhyamanityatvam/ yadi ca ubhayaṃ ekakālavṛtti tadā kiṃ kasya sādhanaṃ
kiṃ kasya sādhyam/ vinigamakābhāvāditi/ hetusameti pāṭhe tu
kālatraye 'pi hetutvasya asambhavakathanaṃ hetusametyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Stating the absence of reason-hood by [showing] the impossibility of reason-hood in all three times is <s>ahetusama</s>. For example: 'if the proof in the form of being-an-effect exists in a time prior to the <s>sādhya</s>, namely non-eternality, then since the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of non-eternality is absent at that time, what does it prove? If, on the other hand, it exists in a subsequent time, then due to the absence of the proof in the prior time, of what is non-eternality the <s>sādhya</s>? And if both exist at the same time, then what is the proof of what, and what is the <s>sādhya</s> of what? — since there is no determining factor.' In the reading <s>hetusama</s>, the meaning is: stating the impossibility of reason-hood in all three times is <s>hetusama</s>.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
ahetusamāṃ
lakṣayati - kālatraye 'pīti/ kālatraye 'pi hetutvāsambhavakathanapūrvakaṃ
ahetutvakathanam ahetusamā/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>ahetusama</s> by saying 'in all three times.' Stating the absence of reason-hood preceded by stating the impossibility of reason-hood in all three times is <s>ahetusama</s>.

children.text:
kasya sādhakamiti/
anityatvasya kāryatvaṃ na sādhakamityarthaḥ/ pūrvakālāvacchedena
avidyamānasya sādhyasya hetuḥ kathaṃ
children.translated_text: 'What does it prove?' means: being-an-effect is not the proof of non-eternality — this is the meaning. The purport is: how can a reason be a proof of a <s>sādhya</s> that does not exist as delimited by the prior time?

children.text:
sādhako bhavet
iti bhāvaḥ/ kasya sādhyamanityatvamiti/ anityatvaṃ kāryatvasya sādhyaṃ
na bhavatītyarthaḥ/ kālatrayaśabdena kāryakālatatpūrvakālatatpaścātkālāḥ
vivakṣitāḥ/"heturahetunā na viśiṣṭayate/ ahetunā
sādharmyāt pratyavasthānam ahetusamaḥ"iti bhāṣyam/
children.translated_text: — this is the purport. 'Of what is non-eternality the <s>sādhya</s>?' means: non-eternality is not the <s>sādhya</s> of being-an-effect — this is the meaning. By the word 'three times,' the time of the effect, the time prior to it, and the time subsequent to it are intended. The <s>Bhāṣya</s> states: 'A reason is not differentiated by being a non-reason. Objection through similarity with a non-reason is <s>ahetusama</s>.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: arthāpattisamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>arthāpattisama</s> (the futile rejoinder of presumption)

children.text:
arthāpattipuraskāreṇa sādhyābhāvodbhāvanam arthāpattisamā/
yathā"pūrvoktānumāne śabdasya anityasādharmyādanityatvaṃ yadi, tadā
arthāpattyā siddhaṃ nityasādharmyāt nityatvamapi ekatarāvadhāraṇe
niyāmakābhāvāt"iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Arthāpattisama</s> is raising the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> by means of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). For example: 'in the aforementioned inference, if sound is non-eternal due to similarity with the non-eternal, then by <s>arthāpatti</s> it is established that it is also eternal due to similarity with the eternal, since there is no determining factor for ascertaining one alternative over the other.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
arthāpattisamāṃ
lakṣayati - arthāpattipuraskāreṇeti/ śabdaḥ anityaḥ kṛtakatvāt iti
anityena ghaṭena kṛtakatvasādharmyāt śabdaḥ anityaḥ ityukte
arthādāpadyate nityasādharmyāt nitya iti/ asti ca nityena ākāśena
asparśatvarūpaṃ sādharmyaṃ śabdasya iti śabdo nitya eva kiṃ na
syādityevam arthāpattipūrvakaṃ dūṣaṇodbhāvanaṃ
arthāpattisametyarthaḥ/"arthāpattyā pratipakṣaṃ sādhayataḥ
arthāpattisamaḥ/ yadi prāyatnānantarīyakatvāt anityasādharmyāt
anityaḥ śabda iti, tadā arthādāpadyate nityasādharmyāt nitya iti/
asti tvasya nityena sādharmyaṃ asparśatvam"iti bhāṣyam/
ekatarāvadhāraṇa iti/ anityasādharmyādanityatvamevetyavadhāraṇa
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>arthāpattisama</s> by saying 'by means of <s>arthāpatti</s>.' When it is said that sound is non-eternal due to similarity in being-produced with the non-eternal pot — 'sound is non-eternal because of being produced' — it follows by implication that it is eternal due to similarity with the eternal. And there is indeed similarity of sound with the eternal <s>ākāśa</s> (space) in the form of intangibility. So why should sound not be eternal? — raising a fault preceded by <s>arthāpatti</s> in this manner is <s>arthāpattisama</s> — this is the meaning. The <s>Bhāṣya</s> states: 'One who establishes the counter-thesis by <s>arthāpatti</s> commits <s>arthāpattisama</s>. If sound is non-eternal due to similarity with the non-eternal because of being preceded by effort, then by implication it is eternal due to similarity with the eternal. And it has similarity with the eternal, namely intangibility.' 'Ascertaining one alternative' means: the ascertainment that it is non-eternal alone due to similarity with the non-eternal — this is the meaning.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: aviśeṣasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>aviśeṣasama</s> (the futile rejoinder of non-distinction)

children.text:
sarvāviśeṣaprasaṅgodbhāvanam aviśeṣasamā/ yathā tatraiva
'yadi kṛtakatvādinā anityaghaṭādisādharmyeṇa śabdasya anityatvaṃ tadā
prameyatvādirūpeṇa tatsādharmyeṇa sarvasyaivānityatvaṃ syāt/
maduktasādharmyeṇa tatsidhyati, na tu tvaduktenetyatra niyāmakābhāvāt'
iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Aviśeṣasama</s> is raising the undesirable consequence of universal non-distinction. For example, in the same context: 'if sound is non-eternal due to similarity with the non-eternal pot through being-produced and so forth, then since everything has similarity with that [pot] through some property such as being-knowable, there would be the undesirable consequence of everything being non-eternal. Since there is no determining factor [to say] that it is established through the similarity I state, but not through the similarity you state.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
aviśeṣasamāṃ
lakṣayati - sarvāviśeṣaprasaṅgodbhāvanamiti/ śabdo 'nityaḥ
kṛtakatvāt ityatra ekasya dharmasyaś kṛtakatvādeḥ śabde ghaṭe ca
sattvāt yadi śabdaghaṭayoranityatvenāviśeṣa ucyate, tadā
sarveṃṣāmaviśeṣaprasaṅgaḥ/ sattvaprameyatvādirūpasya ekasya dharmasya
sarveṣu sattvāt/ tathā ca
sanmātravṛttidharmeṇāviśeṣāpādanamaviśeṣasamā/ tathā ca sarveṣāmabhede
pakṣādivibhāgo na syāt/ sarveṣāmekajātīyatve 'vāntarajātyucchedaḥ,
sarveṣāmanityatve jātyādivilaya iti viśvanāthaḥ nirūpayati/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>aviśeṣasama</s> by saying 'raising the undesirable consequence of universal non-distinction.' In 'sound is non-eternal because of being produced,' if non-distinction in non-eternality between sound and pot is asserted because a single property such as being-produced exists in both sound and pot, then there would be the undesirable consequence of non-distinction of all things — since a single property in the form of existence, knowability, and so forth exists in all things. And accordingly, <s>aviśeṣasama</s> is establishing non-distinction through a property that pervades mere existence. And accordingly, if there were no distinction among all things, the division into thesis, and so forth would not obtain. <s>Viśvanātha</s> explains: when all things are of the same class, sub-classes would be destroyed; when all things are non-eternal, universals and so forth would be dissolved.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: upapattisamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>upapattisama</s> (the futile rejoinder of cogency)

children.text:
ubhayapakṣasādharmyeṇa
sādhanopapattikathanam upapattisamā/ yathā 'yadi anityatvasādhanaṃ
kāryatvamupapadyata iti śabdasyānityatvaṃ tadā nityatvasādhanamapi
kiñcidupapadyata iti nityatvaṃ kiṃ na syāt' iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Upapattisama</s> is stating the cogency of the proof through similarity with both theses. For example: 'if the being-an-effect that proves non-eternality is cogent, and therefore sound is non-eternal, then why should something that proves eternality not also be cogent, and therefore [sound] be eternal?'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
upapattisamāṃ
lakṣayati - ubhayapakṣasādharmyeṇeti/ dvayorapi pakṣayoḥ sādhanamupapadyata
iti kathanam upapattisamā/ śabdasya anityatvapakṣe yathā sādhane
kāryatvamupapadyate, tathā śabdanityatvapakṣe 'pi sādhanaṃ
śrāvaṇatvādikamupapadyata iti dvayorapi pakṣayoḥ
sādhanasyopapannatvākhyaṃ samānadharmaṃ puraskṛtya pratyavasthānam
upapattisameti yāvat/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>upapattisama</s> by saying 'through similarity with both theses.' Stating that the proof is cogent for both theses is <s>upapattisama</s>. Just as the proof, namely being-an-effect, is cogent for the thesis of sound's non-eternality, so too for the thesis of sound's eternality, a proof such as audibility is also cogent — thus the objection invoking the common property of cogency of proof for both theses is <s>upapattisama</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: upalabdhisamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>upalabdhisama</s> (the futile rejoinder of apprehension)

children.text:
vādyupadarśitasādhanābhāve 'pi sādhyasya upalabdhikathanam
upalabdhisamā/ yathā śabdo 'nityaḥ prayatnānuvidhāyitvāt ghaṭavat
ityatra prayatnaṃ vināpi vāyunodanavāśāt vṛkṣaśākhābhaṅgajanyasya
śabdasya upalabdheḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Upalabdhisama</s> is stating the apprehension of the <s>sādhya</s> even in the absence of the proof adduced by the proponent. For example, in 'sound is non-eternal because it conforms to effort, like a pot,' [the objector says:] since sound produced by the breaking of a tree branch due to the force of wind is apprehended even without effort,

children.text:
na
prayatnānuvidhāyitvaṃ śabde 'sti iti/
children.translated_text: the property of conforming to effort does not exist in sound.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
upalabdhisamāṃ
sodāharaṇaṃ lakṣayati - vādyakteti/ vādinā nirdiṣṭasya
kāraṇasyābhāve 'pi sādhyopalambhāt pratyavasthānam upalabdhisamaḥ/ tathā
hi - parvato vahnimān dhūmāt ityādikaṃ vahnyavadhāraṇārthaṃ
ucyate, na tatsambhavati, dhūmaṃ vinā ālokādito 'pi vahnisiddheḥ/
tathā ca na tasya sādhakatvamiti pratikūlatarkaḥ iti viśvanāthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>upalabdhisama</s> with an example by saying 'stated by the proponent.' The objection through the apprehension of the <s>sādhya</s> even in the absence of the cause specified by the proponent is <s>upalabdhisama</s>. To illustrate: 'the mountain possesses fire because of smoke' and similar [inferences] are stated for the ascertainment of fire, [but the objector says] that is not possible, since fire is established even from light and so forth without smoke. And accordingly, [the reason] does not have the character of being a proof — this is a hostile <s>tarka</s>, according to <s>Viśvanātha</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: anupalabdhisamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>anupalabdhisama</s> (the futile rejoinder of non-apprehension)

children.text:
vādinānupalabdhivaśāt kasyacit padārthasya anaṅgīkāre
anupalabdhivaśādeva vādyabhimatasyāpi yatkiñcitpadārthasya abhāvasādhanam
anupalabdhisamā/ yathā - 'jalādeḥ vidyamānasyāpi āvaraṇavaśāt
yathānupalabdhiḥ tathā uccāraṇātpūrvaṃ śabdasya vidyamānasyāpi
āvaraṇavaśāt anupalabdhiḥ ityetanmataṃ vādināṃ
dūṣyate-yadyāvaraṇavaśāt śabdo nopalabhyete, tadā jalādyāvaraṇamiva
śabdādyāvaraṇamapyupalabhyeteti/ atrottaram-yadi bhavadbhiḥ
anupalabdhita āvaraṇaṃ nābhyupeyate tadā anupalabdherapi
anupalabdhyābhāvo siddhe tadabhāvāt āvaraṇābhāvāsiddhau
āvaraṇasiddhiḥ' iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Anupalabdhisama</s> is proving the absence of some entity accepted by the proponent, by the same force of non-apprehension by which the proponent refuses to accept [some other entity]. For example: 'Just as water and the like, even though existing, are not apprehended due to obstruction, so too sound, even though existing before utterance, is not apprehended due to obstruction — this is the view of the proponents [of sound's eternality]. It is refuted thus: if sound is not apprehended due to obstruction, then the obstruction of sound and so forth should itself be apprehended, just as the obstruction of water and so forth. To this, the reply is: if you do not accept the obstruction on the basis of non-apprehension, then by the non-apprehension of non-apprehension itself, the absence [of non-apprehension] is established; and from the absence of that, the non-establishment of the absence of obstruction leads to the establishment of obstruction.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
anupalabdhisamāṃ
lakṣayati - vādineti/ naiyāyikaistāvat śabdānityatvaṃ evaṃ sādhyate
- yadi śabdaḥ nityaḥ syāt tarhi uccāraṇāt prāk kuto
nopalabhyate/ na hi ghaṭādyāvaraṇakuḍyādivat śabdasyāvaraṇamasti,
tadanupalabdheriti/ tatraivaṃ jātivādī
pratyavatiṣṭhate-yadyāvaraṇānupalabdheḥ āvaraṇābhāvaḥ sidhyati tadā
āvaraṇānupalabdherapyanupalambhāt āvaraṇānupalabdherapyabhāvaḥ
sidhyet/ tathā ca anupalabdhipramāṇakaḥ āvaraṇābhāvo na syāt api tu
āvaraṇopapattireva syāditi śabdanityatve noktaṃ bādhakaṃ yuktamiti/
itthaṃ ca evaṃrūpeṇa pratyavasthānam anupalabdhisametyartha iti
viśvanāthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>anupalabdhisama</s> by saying 'by the proponent.' The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> establish the non-eternality of sound thus: if sound were eternal, why is it not apprehended before utterance? For there is no obstruction of sound like walls and such that obstruct pots — hence [it is non-eternal] because of its non-apprehension. Thereupon, the <s>jātivādin</s> (sophist) objects thus: if the absence of obstruction is established from the non-apprehension of obstruction, then from the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of obstruction itself, the absence of that non-apprehension of obstruction would also be established. And accordingly, the absence of obstruction would not be based on the <s>pramāṇa</s> of non-apprehension; rather, the cogency of obstruction itself would follow — and therefore the stated contradiction of sound's eternality is not valid. And thus, objection in this form is <s>anupalabdhisama</s> — this is the meaning, according to <s>Viśvanātha</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: nityasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>nityasama</s> (the futile rejoinder of eternality)

children.text:
dharmasya
nityatvānityatvavikalpāt dharmiṇo nityatvasādhanam nityasamā/ yathā
'śabdasya yat anityatvaṃ bhavadbhiḥ ucyate tat nityaṃ anityaṃ vā/
yadi nityaṃ tadā śabdavṛttereva tasya sadātanatvāt śabdasyāpi
tathātvamāgatam/ atha anityaṃ tadā śabde kadācit
anityatvābhāvo 'stīti nitya eva śabda ityubhayathāpi śabdasya
nityatvam' iti/
children.translated_text: Establishing the eternality of the property-bearer through the dilemma of the property being either eternal or non-eternal is <s>nityasama</s>. For example: 'the non-eternality of sound that you assert — is it eternal or non-eternal? If eternal, then since it eternally resides in sound, sound too would have that character [of eternality]. If, however, it is non-eternal, then there is sometimes the absence of non-eternality in sound, and hence sound is simply eternal — thus in both cases, the eternality of sound [follows].'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
nityasamāṃ lakṣayati
- dharmasyeti/ śabdasyāpi tathātvamāgatamiti/ śabdasyāpi nityatvaṃ
prasaktamityarthaḥ/ dharmiṇaṃ vinā dharmasya sthityabhāvena dharmasyānityatvasya
nityatve sadātanatve dharmī śabdo 'pi nityaḥ syāditi bhāvaḥ/ śabde
anityatvasya nityaṃ sarvakālaṃ svīkāre anitye śabde nityatvaṃ
syādityāpādanaṃ nityasamā iti viśvanārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>nityasama</s> by saying 'of the property.' 'Sound too would have that character' means: the eternality of sound too would follow — this is the meaning. Since a property cannot persist without its substrate, if the non-eternality — which is the property — is eternal, that is, perpetual, then the substrate, sound, would also be eternal — this is the purport. <s>Viśvanātha</s> says: the establishment, in the case of accepting the non-eternality of sound as perpetual, that a non-eternal sound would be eternal — this is <s>nityasama</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: anityasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>anityasama</s> (the futile rejoinder of non-eternality)

children.text:
anityadṛṣṭāntasādharmyāt sarvānityatvaprasaṅgodbhāvanam
anityasamā/ yathā 'yadi anityena ghaṭane sādṛśyāt śabdaḥ anityaḥ
ityucyate tadā yena kenacit dharmeṃṇa sarvasyaiva tatsadṛśatvāt
sarvasyānityatvaprasaṅgaḥ' iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Anityasama</s> is raising the undesirable consequence that everything is non-eternal, based on similarity with a non-eternal example. For example: 'if sound is said to be non-eternal because of similarity with the non-eternal pot, then since everything is similar to that [pot] through some property or other, there would be the undesirable consequence of everything being non-eternal.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
anityasamāṃ
lakṣayati - anityadṛṣṭānteti/ anityena ghaṭena sādharmyāt
(kṛtakatvarūpāt) anityaḥ śabda iti bruvataḥ asti ghaṭenānityena
sarvabhāvānāṃ sādharmyaṃ (sattvādirūpam) iti sarvasya
anityatvamaniṣṭaṃ sampadyate/ so 'yaṃ anityatvena pratyavasthānāt
anityasama iti bhāṣyam/ vyāptimapuraskṛtya
yatkiñciddṛṣṭāntasādharmyeṇa sarvasya
children.translated_text: He defines <s>anityasama</s> by saying 'with a non-eternal example.' When someone says sound is non-eternal due to similarity (in the form of being-produced) with the non-eternal pot, there is similarity of all entities with the non-eternal pot (in the form of existence and so forth), and thus the undesirable result that everything is non-eternal follows. This is <s>anityasama</s>, because the objection is by [attributing] non-eternality [to all]. The <s>Bhāṣya</s> states this. Without regard to pervasion, through whatever similarity with the example, of everything —

children.text:
sādhyavattvāpādanāt
anityasamā/ sādhyapadādaviśeṣasamāto vyavacchedaḥ tatra sarvāviśeṣa
evāpadyate na tu sarvasya sādhyavattvam iti viśvanārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: because it leads to the property of possessing the <s>sādhya</s> [in everything], it is <s>anityasamā</s> (the fallacy of equating with impermanence). The distinction from <s>aviśeṣasamā</s> (the fallacy of non-distinction) is that from the word '<s>sādhya</s>' [in the definition], there what results is merely universal non-distinction, not the possession of the <s>sādhya</s> by everything — this is the meaning according to <s>Viśvanātha</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: kāryasamālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Kāryasamā</s> (the Fallacy of Equating with the Effect)

children.text:
vādyuktahetoḥ
anyakoryeṇāpi sambhavābhidhānaṃ kāryaṃsamā/ yathā tatraiva
prayatnānuvidhāyitvaṃ ubhayathāpi sambhavati ghaṭādivat
śabdasvarūpotpattau jalādivat āvarakanivṛttau ca ubhayatrāpi
prayatnānuvidhāyitvadarśanāt/ tathā ca tasya
āvarakanivṛttirūpakāryāntarasya sambhavāt nānityatvaniyatatvaṃ
iti/ kvacit kāraṇasameti pāṭhaḥ/ tasyāpi 'kāraṇasya
prayatnānuvidhāyitvasya ubhayatra śabdasyotpattau tadāvarakanivṛttau ca
samatvābhidhānam' iti rītyā ukta evārthe paryavasānamavaseyam/ atra
granthagauravabhayāt sūkṣmaprakārāḥ na darśitāḥ ityabhiyuktairanyatra
te 'nusandheyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Stating that the <s>hetu</s> (reason) adduced by the proponent is possible through another effect as well is <s>kāryasamā</s>. For example, in the same [inference], <s>prayatnānuvidhāyitva</s> (conformity to effort) is possible in both ways: like a pot etc. in the origination of the thing's own nature, and like water etc. in the removal of an obstruction — since conformity to effort is observed in both cases. And thus, since another effect in the form of removal of obstruction is possible, [the <s>hetu</s>] is not necessarily connected to impermanence — this [is the objection]. In some [manuscripts] the reading is <s>kāraṇasamā</s> (the fallacy of equating with the cause). For that too, one should understand the resolution in the same meaning stated above, in the manner of 'stating that the cause, namely conformity to effort, is equal in both — in the origination of sound and in the removal of its obstruction.' Here, due to fear of prolixity, the subtle details have not been shown — they should be investigated elsewhere by the learned.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
kāryasamāṃ lakṣayati
- vādyuktahetoriti/ yathā śabdaḥ anityaḥ prayatnānuvidhāyitvāt
ityatra prayatnānuvidhāyitvaṃ kāryadvaye 'sti svarūpotpattau
āvarakanivṛttau ceti/ tatra svarūpotpattyabhiprāyeṇa vādinokte
jātivādala āha āvarakanivṛttāveva prayatnānuvidhāyitvasyopayogaḥ
na svarūpotpattāviti śabdasyānityatvaṃ na sidhyatīti/ evaṃrītyā
pratyavasthānaṃ kāryasametyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>kāryasamā</s> — with 'of the <s>hetu</s> stated by the proponent.' For example, in 'sound is impermanent because of conformity to effort,' here conformity to effort exists in two effects — in the origination of the thing's own nature and in the removal of an obstruction. There, when the proponent states [the <s>hetu</s>] with the intention of origination of the thing's own nature, the <s>jāti</s>-disputant says: conformity to effort is useful only in the removal of an obstruction, not in the origination of the thing's own nature — therefore the impermanence of sound is not established. In this manner, the counter-argument is <s>kāryasamā</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text:
atredamavadheyam-keṣucit grantheṣu
sādharmyasamā vaidharmyasamā ityādirūpeṇa strīliṅgatayā samaśabdaḥ
prayujyate, keṣucittu sādharmyasamaḥ vaidharmyasamaḥ ityādirūpeṇa
pulliṅgatayā prayujyate/ tatra jāterviśeṣyatvavivakṣāyāṃ samaśabdasya
strīliṅgatvam/ nyāyasūtrakārastu-'sādharmyavaidharmyasamau'
ityādirūpeṇa pulliṅgatayaiva nirdiśati/ tasyāyaṃ bhāvaḥ - vādyaktasya
pratiṣedhaḥ kila jātivādinā kriyate, tatra pratiṣeghaśabdaḥ pulliṅga
iti tadanurodhena samaśabdasya pulliṅgeteti/ taduktaṃ
nyāyapariśuddhau vedāntadeśikaiḥ -"akṣapādīyeṣu ca
jātiviśeṣalakṣaṇasūtreṣu pulliṅgāntasamaśabdanirdeśaḥ
svapakṣasthāpanaparapakṣapratikṣeparūpeṇa vibhāge pratyavasthāne
pratiṣedhabhāgenātra jātitvaṃ vivakṣitam
ityuktarūpajātiviśeṣābhiprāya ityāhuḥ"iti/ nyāyabhāṣyakārādayo 'pīti pratiṣedhaśabdasya sūtre
bahulaṃ prayogāt pratiṣedhaśabdamādāyeva samaśabde
pulliṅganirvāhaṃ manyante/ viśvanāthanyāyapañcānanastu
'sādharmyasamādayo jātivikalpāḥ/ vividhaḥ kalpaḥ vikalpaḥ prabhedaḥ'
iti vadan vikalpaśabdānusāreṇa samaśabdasya pulliṅgatāṃ
nirvahati/ evaṃ vādinā sādhane kriyāmāṇe tatra prativādinā
udbhāvyamānaḥ asaduttaraviśeṣaḥ jātiḥ/ tasya jātiśabdavācyatā
jāyamānatvanibandhanā/ tathā ca"sādharmyavaidharmyābhyām
pratyavasthānam jātiḥ"iti/ kathāyāṃ pravṛttayoḥ
vādiprativādinoḥ madhye vādinā sādhane kṛte
yathāvasthitottarasphurtirahitasya jigīṣoḥ prativādinaḥ mukhāt
children.translated_text: Here this should be noted — in some texts the word <s>sama</s> is used in the feminine gender in the form '<s>sādharmyasamā</s>, <s>vaidharmyasamā</s>' etc., while in other texts it is used in the masculine gender in the form '<s>sādharmyasamaḥ</s>, <s>vaidharmyasamaḥ</s>' etc. There, when the <s>jāti</s> (futile objection) is intended as the qualificand, the word <s>sama</s> takes the feminine gender. The author of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>, however, designates it only in the masculine gender in the form '<s>sādharmyavaidharmyasamau</s>' etc. His intent is as follows: it is indeed the refutation that is made by the <s>jāti</s>-disputant; there, the word '<s>pratiṣedha</s>' (refutation) is masculine, and in conformity with that the word <s>sama</s> also takes the masculine gender. Thus it has been stated in the <s>Nyāyapari</s>[-śiṣṭa]

children.text:
yaḥ kaścit
hetvābhāsaḥ avaśāt āgataḥ jāyamāna eva bhavati na tu jātaḥ san
kāryakaro 'pītyāśayena avadhāraṇārthatayā jātiśabdaḥ pravartata iti
uttamūruvīrarāghavācāryasvāminaḥ nirūpayanti/ te eva svāminaḥ
sāmyārthakasamaśabdaghaṭanasya tātparyamevaṃ varṇayanti -
vādiprativādiprayuktayorheṃtvoḥ(?) sāmyam, vādiprativādinorapi
sāmyaṃ ca samaśabdena lakṣyate/ sūtre samaśabdaḥ
pratiṣedharūpahetuviśeṣaṇībhūtaḥ hetugataṃ sāmyaṃ darśayati/ athāpi
vaktṛgatasāmyamapi vivakṣitam/ tadāha vārtikakāraḥ -"samīkaraṇārthaṃ prayogasamaḥ/ sādharmyameva samaṃ tasya prayogasya sa
sādharmyasamaḥ"iti/ atra samīkaraṇārthamityanena vastutaḥ
sāmyābhāve 'pi samīkaraṇoddheśo jñāpyate/ na hi saddhetorasaddhetunā
nirākaraṇaṃ sāmyāpādanaṃ vā bhavati/ kena kasya samīkaraṇamiti cet
- vādinā prativādinaḥ samīkaraṇam/ tathā ca prativādinā
svāpakarṣaparihārārthamantataḥ samīkaraṇārthaṃ jātiprayogaḥ kriyata
ityuktaṃ bhavati/ deśikacaraṇāstu nyāyapariśuddhau jātiprayogaḥ
kriyata ityuktaṃ bhavati/ deśikacaraṇāstu nyāyapariśuddhau
jātivādiprayuktahetoḥ paraghātakatvavat svavyāghātakatvamapyastīti
tadeva sāmyaṃ samaśabdena pratipādyata iti nirvahanti/
children.translated_text: whatever fallacious reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) comes about inevitably, it arises as it is born but does not produce any effect even after being born — with this intent, the word <s>jāti</s> is employed in the sense of emphatic restriction — thus explain <s>Uttamūru Vīrarāghavācārya Svāmin</s>. Those same masters describe the purport of the construction with the word <s>sama</s> meaning 'equality' thus: the equality of the two reasons adduced by the proponent and the opponent, and also the equality of the proponent and the opponent themselves, is denoted by the word <s>sama</s>. In the <s>sūtra</s>, the word <s>sama</s>, functioning as a qualifier of the refutation, shows the equality pertaining to the reason. Moreover, the equality pertaining to the speakers is also intended. Thus says the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> — 'samīk[-ṣya]'

children.text:
evaṃ caturviśatidhā nirdiṣṭadāsu jātiṣu
kāsāṃcit jātīnāṃ lakṣaṇeṣu pariśīralyamāneṣu samānatvaṃ
sthūladṛṣṭyā pratīyate/ tataḥ nāmabhedamātramiti śaṅkā avatarati/
tatrāpi sūṣmadṛṣṭyā vicāryaṃmāṇe lakṣaṇeṣu bhado 'vagantuṃśakyate/ tadetanmanasi nidhāyāha - atra granthagauravabhayāt
sūkṣmaprakārāḥ na darśitāḥ iti/ kiṃ ca āsāṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, when the definitions of the twenty-four <s>jātis</s> (futile objections) that have been enumerated are examined, a similarity among some of the <s>jātis</s> is perceived from a broad perspective. Hence the doubt arises that these are merely differences in name. Yet, when examined with a subtle perspective, a difference in the definitions can be discerned. Keeping this in mind, he says: 'Here, due to fear of prolixity, the subtle details have not been shown.' Moreover, of these

children.text:
jātīnāṃ saptāṅgāni
bhavantīti udayanācārthaiḥ nyāyapariśiṣṭasyānte -
children.translated_text: <s>jātis</s> there are seven components — as stated by <s>Udayanācārya</s> at the end of the <s>Nyāyapariśiṣṭa</s>:

children.text:
"lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇamutthitiḥ sthitipadaṃ mūlaṃ
phalaṃ śātanaṃ
children.translated_text: "The defined instance, the definition, the origin, the ground of stability, the root, the fruit, and the destruction —

children.text:
jātīnāṃ
saviśeṣametadakhilaṃ pravyaktamuktaṃ rahaḥ"//
children.translated_text: of <s>jātis</s>, all this with its distinctions has been clearly stated in private."

children.text:
iti ślokārdheṃna
pratipāditam/ tatra prativādinā yat asaduttaramucyate tadeva
lakṣyam/ tasya sādharmyaṃsamādiṣu yatrānatarbhāvaḥ tallakṣaṇameva lakṣaṇam/
utthitirnāma janma/ sthiteḥ padaṃ sthitipadaṃ jātyuttarasthiteḥ āśrayaḥ/
asatisādhanaprayoge jātyuttarāpravṛtteḥ dūṣyo hetureva
sthitipadatvena vivakṣitaḥ/ īdṛśajātiprayogasya mūlaṃ
sādharmyādyākārakadarśanam/ phalaṃ tu vādinaḥ svoktahetau prativādinā
duṣṭatvabhramotpādanam/ śātanaṃ vādinā prativādyuktasyāsaduttarasya
jātirūpasya nirākaraṇam/ sūtrakārastu jātyuttarasya
nirākaraṇaprakāraṃ pratijāti viśadaṃ pratipāditavān/ saptāṅgakatvaṃ
tu nyāyapariśiṣṭe tatra tatra sūcitameva/ sarvamidaṃ vistarabhayāt
atropekṣitamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus it has been set forth in a half-verse. There, the unsound rejoinder uttered by the opponent — that is the 'defined instance' (<s>lakṣya</s>). Its definition, in terms of belonging to <s>sādharmyasamā</s> etc. where it is subsumed — that definition itself is the 'definition' (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). 'Origin' (<s>utthiti</s>) means birth [of the futile objection]. The 'ground of stability' (<s>sthitipada</s>) is the basis of the <s>jāti</s>-rejoinder's persistence — since a <s>jāti</s>-rejoinder does not arise without the application of a [valid] means of proof, the defective reason itself is intended as the ground of stability. The 'root' (<s>mūla</s>) of such a <s>jāti</s>-deployment is the perception of apparent similarity and other such forms. The 'fruit' (<s>phala</s>) is the production, by the opponent, of a false impression of defectiveness regarding the proponent's stated reason. 'Destruction' (<s>śātana</s>) is the refutation by the proponent of the unsound rejoinder in the form of a <s>jāti</s> uttered by the opponent.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: nigrahasthānanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Nigrahasthāna</s> (Grounds of Defeat)

children.text:
vādinaḥ
apajayahetuḥ nigrahasthānam/
children.translated_text: The cause of the defeat of the debater is <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (ground of defeat).

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nigrahasthānaṃ
lakṣayati - vādina iti/ idaṃ ca yadyapi chalādāvapyasti
tathāpyarthāntarādirūpanigrahasthānamadhye 'ntarbhāvāt adoṣaḥ/
chalatvādināpi jñānasyopayogitvāt pṛthigupādānaṃ
hetvābhāsavat/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>nigrahasthāna</s> — with 'of the debater.' And although this [ground of defeat] exists in <s>chala</s> (equivocation) and the like as well, there is no fault, since those are subsumed under the grounds of defeat such as <s>arthāntara</s> (shifting the topic) and the like. Because knowledge of <s>chalatva</s> (equivocation) and the like is also useful, their separate mention — like that of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reason) — [is justified].

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
pratijñāhāniḥ,
pratijñāntaram, pratijñāvirodhaḥ, pratijñāsannyāsaḥ, hetvantaram,
arthāntaram, nirarthakam, avijñātārthakam, apārthakam, aprāptakālam,
nyūnam, adhikam, punaruktam, ananubhāṣaṇam, ajñānam, apratibhā,
vikṣepaḥ, matānujñā, paryanuyojyopekṣaṇam, niranuyojyānuyogaḥ,
apasiddhāntaḥ, hetvābhāsāśca nigrahasthānāni/ śeṣaṃ sugamam/
children.translated_text: <s>Pratijñāhāni</s> (abandoning the thesis), <s>pratijñāntara</s> (shifting the thesis), <s>pratijñāvirodha</s> (contradicting the thesis), <s>pratijñāsannyāsa</s> (renouncing the thesis), <s>hetvantara</s> (shifting the reason), <s>arthāntara</s> (shifting the topic), <s>nirarthaka</s> (meaningless utterance), <s>avijñātārthaka</s> (incomprehensible utterance), <s>apārthaka</s> (incoherent utterance), <s>aprāptakāla</s> (untimely utterance), <s>nyūna</s> (deficiency), <s>adhika</s> (redundancy), <s>punarukta</s> (repetition), <s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s> (failure to respond), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>apratibhā</s> (inability to respond), <s>vikṣepa</s> (evasion), <s>matānujñā</s> (conceding the opponent's view), <s>paryanuyojyopekṣaṇa</s> (overlooking what is censurable), <s>niranuyojyānuyoga</s> (censuring what is not censurable), <s>apasiddhānta</s> (deviation from one's own doctrine), and <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reasons) — these are the grounds of defeat. The rest is easy to understand.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: pratijñāhānilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Pratijñāhāni</s> (Abandoning the Thesis)

children.text:
tasyāvāntarabhedān daśayati -- pratijñetyādinā/ yatra
pratijñātārthaviruddhābhyupagamaḥ pratijñātārthaparityāgo vā tatra
pratijñāhāniḥ/ yathā 'śabdo 'nityaḥ pratyakṣaguṇatvāt' ityatra
'so 'yam gakāraḥ' ityādipratyabhijñābalātpareṇa bādhe udbhāvite
'astu tarhi nityaḥ śabdaḥ' iti nityatvamaṅgīkurvan vādī śabdasya
anityatvapratijñāṃ jahāti/
children.translated_text: He shows its sub-varieties — with '<s>pratijñā</s>' and so on. Where there is acceptance of something contrary to the asserted thesis, or abandonment of the asserted thesis — there is <s>pratijñāhāni</s>. For example, in 'sound is impermanent because it is a perceptible quality,' when the opponent raises a sublation through the force of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) such as 'this is that very same <s>ga</s>-sound,' the debater who accepts permanence [of sound] by saying 'let sound then be permanent' abandons his thesis of the impermanence of sound.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pratijñāhāniṃ
lakṣayati - yatra pratijñātārtheti/ pratijñātasya sādhyasya yat viruddhaṃ
tadaṅgīkāraḥ pratijñātasya sādhyasya tyāgo vā pratijñāhāniḥ/ idaṃ
ca"sādhyadharmapratyanīkena dharmeṇa pratyavasthite pratidṛṣṭāntadharmaṃ
svadṛṣṭānte 'bhyanujānan pratijñāṃ jahātīti pratijñāhāniḥ"ityādi bhāṣyānusāri lakṣaṇam/ viśvanāthastu -"svapakṣeparapakṣadharmābhyanujñā pratijñāhāniḥ/ svayaṃ
viśiṣyābhihitaparityāga iti phalitārthaḥ/ seyaṃ
pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntasādhyatadanyahānibhedāt pañcadhā bhāvati/ yathā śabdaḥ
anityaḥ kṛtakatvāt ityukte
pratyabhijñābādhitaviṣayo 'yamityuttarite astu tarhi ghaṭa eva pakṣa
iti/ evaṃ tatraiva śabdo 'nityaḥ aindriyakatvāt ityukte
hetoranaikāntikatvamiti pratyukte astu kṛtakatvāditi heturiti/
evaṃ parvato vahnimān dhūmāt ālokavadityukte dṛṣṭāntaḥ
sādhanavikala iti pratyukte astu tarhi mahānasaviditi/ evaṃ atraiva
siddhasādhanena pratyukte astu tarhiṃ indhanavāniti/ anyahānistu
viśeṣaṇahānyādiḥ, yathā tatraiva
nīladhūmādityukte 'samarthaviśeṣaṇatvena pratyukte astu tarhiṃ dhūtāditi
hetoriti"ityāha/ tadanusāreṇa dinakaryām -
'viśiṣya pratijñātasya pakṣādeḥ parityāgarūpapratijñāhāneḥ' iti
proktam/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>pratijñāhāni</s> — with 'where the asserted thesis.' The acceptance of what is contrary to the asserted <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), or the abandonment of the asserted <s>sādhya</s>, is <s>pratijñāhāni</s>. And this conforms to the <s>Bhāṣya</s> definition: 'When the opponent counter-argues with a property opposed to the property of the <s>sādhya</s>, one who concedes the property of the counter-example in one's own example abandons the thesis — this is <s>pratijñāhāni</s>.' <s>Viśvanātha</s>, however, [says]: 'Conceding the property of the opponent's position regarding one's own position is <s>pratijñāhāni</s>. The resultant meaning is: the abandonment of what one has oneself specifically stated. This is fivefold, according to the divisions of abandoning the thesis, the reason, the example, the <s>sādhya</s>, and others. For example, [in the inference about] sound

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: pratijñāntaralakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Pratijñāntara</s> (Shifting the Thesis)

children.text:
paroktadoṣoddidhīrṣayā pūrvānuktaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭatayā
pratijñātārthakathanam pratijñāntaram/ yathā -- kṣityādikaṃ guṇajanyam
kāryatvāt ityatra adṛṣṭajanyatvena siddhasādhanodbhāvane
'saviṣayaka' iti guṇaviśeṣaṇadānam/
children.translated_text: Stating the asserted thesis as qualified by a previously unstated qualifier, with the desire to ward off a fault pointed out by the opponent, is <s>pratijñāntara</s>. For example, in 'earth and the like are produced by a [volitional] agent, because of being an effect,' when the objection of proving what is already established is raised on the grounds that [they are] produced by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), [the debater] adds the qualifier of [a specific] quality [to the agent], saying '<s>saviṣayaka</s>' (having a cognizing subject).

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pratijñāntaraṃ
lakṣayati - parokteti/ guṇaviśeṣaṇadānamiti/ saviṣayakaguṇajanyatvaṃ
sādhyam/ adṛṣṭasya tu saviṣayakatvābhāvāt tajjanyatvamādāya na
siddhasādhanamiti bhāvaḥ/ 'pratijñātārthasyetyupalakṣaṇam/
hetvatiriktārthaṃsyeti tattvam/ tena udāharaṇāntaram, upanayāntaram,
nigamanāntaraṃ ca pratijñāntaratvena saṅgṛhītaṃ bhavati' iti
viśvanāthaḥ/ hetvantaraṃ tu sūtrakāreṇa pṛthaṅnigrahasthānatvena
nirdiṣṭam/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>pratijñāntara</s> — with 'by the opponent.' 'Adding the qualifier of quality' — the <s>sādhya</s> [now becomes] being produced by a quality-possessing [agent]. But since <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) does not have a cognizing subject (<s>saviṣayakatva</s>), taking it as such would not constitute proving what is already established — this is the purport. 'Of the asserted thesis' is a general indication. The truth is: of something other than the <s>hetu</s>. Therefore, shifting the example, shifting the application (<s>upanaya</s>), and shifting the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) are also included under <s>pratijñāntara</s> — thus says <s>Viśvanātha</s>. <s>Hetvantara</s> (shifting the reason), however, has been separately designated as a ground of defeat by the <s>Sūtrakāra</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: pratijñāvirodhalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Pratijñāvirodha</s> (Contradicting the Thesis)

children.text:
svoktasādhyaviruddhahetukathanam pratijñāvirodhaḥ/ yathā - dravyaṃ
guṇabhinnam rūpāditaḥ pṛthaktvena anupalabhyamānatvāt iti/
children.translated_text: Stating a reason that contradicts one's own stated <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is <s>pratijñāvirodha</s>. For example: substance is different from quality, because it is not perceived as separate from form and the like.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pratijñāvirodhaṃ
lakṣayati - svoktasādhyeti/ rūpāditaḥ pṛthaktvena anupalabhyamānatvaṃ hi
guṇābhinnatvavyāpyam, na guṇabhinnatvasādhakam/ ato
guṇabhinnatvābhāvavyāptasya hetoḥ kathanāt pratijñāvirodha ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>pratijñāvirodha</s> — with 'one's own stated <s>sādhya</s>.' For the property of not being perceived as separate from form and the like is pervaded by non-difference from quality, not a prover of difference from quality. Therefore, since a reason pervaded by the absence of difference from quality is stated, it is <s>pratijñāvirodha</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: pratijñāsannyāsalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>Pratijñāsannyāsa</s> (Renouncing the Thesis)

children.text:
svokter'the pareṇa
dūṣite tadapalāpaḥ pratijñāsannyāsaḥ/ yathā -- 'śabdo 'nityaḥ
aindriyakatvāt' ityukte pareṇa sāmānye vyabhicāramudbhāvya
dūṣite svoktamapalapati 'kenocyate śabdo 'nityaḥ' iti/
children.translated_text: When one's own statement is refuted by the opponent, the denial of that is <s>pratijñāsannyāsa</s> (abandonment of the thesis). For example — when one states 'sound is non-eternal, because of being perceptible,' and the opponent refutes it by showing <s>vyabhicāra</s> (deviation) in the universal, one denies one's own statement [saying] 'who says sound is non-eternal?'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
pratijñāsannyāsaṃ
lakṣayati -- svokter'the iti/ pratijñāhānau pratijñātārthasya tyāgaḥ
pratijñāsannyāse tu tasyāpalāpa iti bhedaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>pratijñāsannyāsa</s> — 'When one's own statement.' In <s>pratijñāhāni</s> (abandonment of the thesis), there is relinquishment of the stated meaning; in <s>pratijñāsannyāsa</s>, however, there is denial of it — this is the difference.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: hetvantaralakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>hetvantara</s> (shift of reason)

children.text:
paroktadūṣaṇoddidhīrṣayā pūrvoktahetukoṭau
viśeṣaṇāntaropādānam hetvantaram/ yathā 'śabdo 'nityaḥ
pratyakṣatvāt' ityatra sāmānye vyabhicārodbhāvane 'jātimattve
sati' iti viśeṣaṇadānam/
children.translated_text: <s>Hetvantara</s> (shift of reason) is the adoption of a different qualifier in the category of the previously stated probans, with the desire to counter the refutation stated by the opponent. For example, in 'sound is non-eternal, because of being perceptible,' when <s>vyabhicāra</s> is shown in the universal, the addition of the qualifier 'when possessing universality (<s>jātimattva</s>).'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
hetvantaraṃ lakṣayati
- parokteti/ paroktadūṣaṇoddidhīrṣayā
pūrvoktahetutāvacchedakātiriktahetutāvacchedakaviśiṣṭavacanaṃ
hetvantaramityarthaḥ/ jātimattve satīti viśeṣaṇe datte tu sāmānye
jātimattvābhāvāt na vyabhicāraḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>hetvantara</s> — 'By the opponent's.' The meaning is: <s>hetvantara</s> is a statement qualified by a delimitor of probans-hood different from the delimitor of probans-hood of the previously stated reason, with the desire to counter the refutation stated by the opponent. When the qualifier 'when possessing universality' is given, since universality-possessing-ness is absent in the universal, there is no <s>vyabhicāra</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: arthāntaralakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>arthāntara</s> (shifting the topic)

children.text:
prakṛtānupayuktārthakathanam arthāntaram/
yathā-nityaḥ śabdaḥ asparśavattvāt iti hetuḥ/ hetupadaṃ ca
hinotestunipratyaye niṣpannam; padaṃ ca suptiṅantam ityādi/
children.translated_text: <s>Arthāntara</s> (shifting the topic) is the statement of a matter not relevant to the subject at hand. For example — 'sound is eternal, because of being intangible' is the reason. The word 'reason' (<s>hetu</s>) is derived with the suffix <s>tun</s> from the root <s>hi</s>; and a word ends in a <s>sup</s> or <s>tiṅ</s> suffix — and so forth.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
arthāntaraṃ lakṣayati
- prakṛtānupayukteti/ prakṛtānākāṅkṣitārthābhidhānamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>arthāntara</s> — 'Not relevant to the subject at hand.' The meaning is: the statement of a matter not required by the topic under discussion.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: nirarthakalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>nirarthaka</s> (meaningless utterance)

children.text:
avācakaśabdaprayogo nirarthakam/ yathā śabdaḥ anityaḥ
jabagaḍadaśatvāt ityādi/
children.translated_text: <s>Nirarthaka</s> (meaningless utterance) is the use of non-denotative words. For example, 'sound is non-eternal, because of <s>jabagaḍadaśatva</s>' and the like.

children.text: avijñātārthalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>avijñātārtha</s> (incomprehensible utterance)

children.text:
pariṣatprativādyabodhaprayojakapadaprayogaḥ avijñātārtham/ tacca
'kliṣṭānvayaṃ aprasiddhārthakaṃ tvaritoccāritam' ityādirūpam/
children.translated_text: <s>Avijñātārtha</s> (incomprehensible utterance) is the use of words that fail to produce understanding in the assembly and the opponent. And that takes the form of 'having a tortured construction, having an unfamiliar meaning, uttered too rapidly' and so forth.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
avijñātārthaṃ
lakṣayati - pariṣaditi/ vādināṃ trivāramuktamapiprativādinā
sadasyaiśca yanna budhyate tat avijñātārtham/
'avahitāvikalavyutpannapariṣatprativādibodhānukūlopasthitya
janakavācakavākyaprayogo 'vijñātārtham/ vācaketyanena
nirarthakāpārthaṅkavyudāsaḥ' iti viśvanārthaḥ/ tādṛśaṃ vākyaṃ 'bhūstanaṃ
himabheṣajavat' ityādikam/ bhūstanamityasya parvata ityarthaṃḥ/
himasya bheṣajam agniḥ tadvān iti himabheṣajavadityasthārthaḥ/
'agnirhimasya bheṣajam' iti śruteḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>avijñātārtha</s> — 'The assembly.' That which is not understood by the opponent and the assessors even when stated three times by the debater is <s>avijñātārtha</s>. <s>Viśvanātha</s>'s [explanation]: '<s>Avijñātārtha</s> is the use of a denotative sentence that produces the presentation conducive to the understanding of an attentive, unimpaired, and learned assembly and opponent. By the word denotative, meaningless and topic-shifting [utterances] are excluded.' Such a sentence is like '<s>bhūstanaṃ himabheṣajavat</s>' and the like. The meaning of '<s>bhūstanam</s>' is 'mountain.' The medicine (<s>bheṣaja</s>) for snow (<s>hima</s>) is fire; possessing that is the meaning of '<s>himabheṣajavat</s>.' Because of the <s>śruti</s> text 'fire is the medicine for snow.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: apārthakalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>apārthaka</s> (incoherent utterance)

children.text:
parasparānanvitapadasamūhaḥ apārthakam/ yathā-śabdatvaṃ ghaṭaḥ paṭaḥ
nityaṃ anityaṃ ca prameyatvāt ityādi/
children.translated_text: <s>Apārthaka</s> (incoherent utterance) is a collection of words not connected with each other. For example — 'sound-ness, pot, cloth, eternal, non-eternal, because of being knowable' and the like.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
apārthakaṃ lakṣayati -
paraspareti/ abhimatavākyārthabodhānukūlākāṅkṣāśūnyapadasamūhaḥ
apārthakamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>apārthaka</s> — 'Not connected with each other.' The meaning is: <s>apārthaka</s> is a collection of words devoid of the mutual expectancy conducive to the understanding of the intended sentence-meaning.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: aprāptakālalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>aprāptakāla</s> (untimely statement)

children.text:
avayavānāṃ
vyutkrameṇa kathanam aprāptakālam/ yathā śabdatvāt śabdaḥ anityaḥ
ityādi/
children.translated_text: <s>Aprāptakāla</s> (untimely statement) is the statement of the members [of a syllogism] in a disordered sequence. For example, 'because of sound-ness, sound is non-eternal' and the like.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
aprāptakālaṃ
lakṣayati - avayavānāmiti/"pratijñādīnāṃ avayavānāṃ yathālakṣaṇaṃ
arthavaśāt kramaḥ/ tatrāvayavaviparyāsena vacanaṃ aprāptakālam"iti
bhāṣyānusārīdaṃ lakṣaṇam/ viśvanāthastu-avayavasya kathaikadeśasya
viparyāsaḥ vaiparītyam/ tathā ca
samayabandhaviṣayībhūtakathākramaviparītakrameṇābhidhānaṃ paryavasannam/
tatrāyaṃ kramaḥ-vādinā sādhanamuktvā sāmānyate hetvābhāsā uddharaṇīyāḥ
ityekaḥ pādaḥ, prativādinaśca tatropālambhaḥ dvitīṃyaḥ pādaḥ,
prativādinaḥ svapakṣasādhanaṃ tatra hetvābhāsoddhāraṇaṃ ceti tṛtīyaḥ
