pādaḥ/ jayaparājayavyavasthā caturthaḥ pādaḥ/ evaṃ pratijñāhetvādīnāṃ
kramaḥ/ tatra sabhākṣobhavyāmohādinā vyatyastābhidhānaṃ aprāptakālam'
iti pratipādayati/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>aprāptakāla</s> — 'Of the members.' 'The order of the members such as the thesis and the rest is [determined] by the force of meaning according to their definitions. Therein, a statement with the transposition of members is <s>aprāptakāla</s>' — this definition follows the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. <s>Viśvanātha</s>, however, [says]: the transposition of a member is the reversal of a portion of the discourse. And thus, the outcome is a statement in an order contrary to the order of discourse that is the subject of the convention. Therein, this is the order: the first quarter is where the proponent, having stated the proof, should extract the fallacious reasons in general; the second quarter is the opponent's objection thereto; the third quarter is the opponent's proof of his own position and the extraction of fallacious reasons therein; the fourth quarter is the determination of victory and defeat. Similarly, the order of the thesis, reason, and so forth [is fixed]. Therein, a statement in transposed order due to agitation of the assembly, confusion, and the like is <s>aprāptakāla</s>' — thus he explains.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: nyūnalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>nyūna</s> (deficient statement)

children.text: yatkiñcidavayavaśūnyāvayavābhidhānam nyūnam/ spaṣṭam/
children.translated_text: <s>Nyūna</s> (deficient statement) is the statement of members lacking any one of the [required] members. This is clear.

children.text: adhikalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>adhika</s> (redundant statement)

children.text:
adhikahetvādikathanam adhikam/ yathā śabdaḥ anityaḥ śabdatvāt
śrāvaṇatvācca ityādi/
children.translated_text: <s>Adhika</s> (redundant statement) is the statement of an additional reason and the like. For example, 'sound is non-eternal, because of sound-ness and because of being audible' and the like.

children.text: punaruktalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>punarukta</s> (repetition)

children.text:
anuvādaṃ vinā
kathitasya punaḥ kathanam punaruktam/ yathā -- śabdaḥ anityaḥ, śabdaḥ
anityaḥ ityādi/
children.translated_text: <s>Punarukta</s> (repetition) is the re-statement of what has been said, without [it being] a restatement [for the purpose of explanation]. For example — 'sound is non-eternal, sound is non-eternal' and the like.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
punaruktaṃ lakṣayati - anuvādaṃ vineti/
niṣprayojanaṃ punarabhidhānaṃ punaruktam/ anuvādastu vyakhyārūpaḥ
saprayojanakaḥ/ ato na tatrātivyāptiḥ/ tathā ca
samānārthakasamānānupūrvīkaśabdasya niṣprayojanaṃ punarabhidhānaṃ
śabdapunaruktam/ yathā śabdaḥ anityaḥ śabdaḥ anitya iti/
samānārthabhinnānupūrvīkaśabdasya niṣprayojanaṃ punaḥ
abhidhānamarthapunaruktam/ yathā śabdaḥ anityaḥ dhvanirnirodhadharmaka
iti/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>punarukta</s> — 'Without restatement.' <s>Punarukta</s> is purposeless re-utterance. But restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) is in the form of explanation and has a purpose. Therefore there is no over-pervasion with respect to it. And thus, the purposeless re-utterance of a word having the same meaning and the same letter-sequence is verbal repetition (<s>śabdapunarukta</s>). For example, 'sound is non-eternal, sound is non-eternal.' The purposeless re-utterance of a word having the same meaning but a different letter-sequence is meaning-repetition (<s>arthapunarukta</s>). For example, 'sound is non-eternal, vibration is subject to cessation.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: ananubhāṣaṇalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s> (non-response)

children.text:
pariṣadā
trirabhihitasyāpi ananuvādaḥ ananubhāṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: <s>Ananubhāṣaṇa</s> (non-response) is the failure to repeat [and address] what has been stated three times by the assembly.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
ananubhāṣaṇaṃ
lakṣayati -- pariṣadeti/ vādinā triruktasya pariṣadā vijñātārthasya
vākyasya prativādinā
children.translated_text: He defines <s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s> — 'By the assembly.' When the proponent has stated it three times, and the assembly has understood its meaning,

children.text:
ananuvādaḥ
ananubhāṣaṇam/ ajñānasāṅkaryanirāsāya ajñānamanāviṣkurvateti
vikṣepasāṅkaryanirāsāya kathāmavicchindateti ca viśeṣaṇīyam
ityācāryāḥ/ na ca apratibhāsāṅkaryam, uttarapratipattāvapi
sabhākṣobhādinā ananubhāṣaṇasambhavāditi viśvanāthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the failure of the opponent to repeat [and respond to] that sentence is <s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s>. It should be qualified as: 'not manifesting ignorance' — for the exclusion of confusion with ignorance; and 'not interrupting the debate' — for the exclusion of confusion with evasion (<s>vikṣepa</s>). Thus [say] the teachers. And it is not [to be confused with] <s>apratibhā</s> (lack of wit), because <s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s> is possible even when one understands the response, due to agitation of the assembly and the like — thus [says] <s>Viśvanātha</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: ajñānalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance)

children.text:
pariṣadā vijñātasya
vādinā trirabhihitasyāpi vākyārthasyābodhaḥ ajñānam
children.translated_text: <s>Ajñāna</s> (ignorance) is the non-comprehension of the meaning of a sentence that has been understood by the assembly and stated three times by the proponent.

children.text: apratibhīlakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>apratibhā</s> (lack of wit)

children.text:
uttarārhaṃ paroktaṃ
buddhvāpi uttarasya asphūrtivaśāt tūṣṇīṃbhāvaḥ apratibhā/
children.translated_text: <s>Apratibhā</s> (lack of wit) is silence due to the non-manifestation of a reply, even after understanding the opponent's statement that merits a response.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
apratibhāṃ lakṣayati
-- uttarārhamiti/ na cātra ananubhāṣaṇasyāvaśyakatvāt tadeva
dūṣaṇamastviti vācyam/ paroktānanuvāde hi tat/ apratibhāyāṃ tu
paroktānuvāde 'pi uttarāpratipattiriti viśeṣāt/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>apratibhā</s> — 'Meriting a response.' And one should not say here that since <s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s> is necessarily [present], let that alone be the point of defeat. For <s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s> applies to the non-repetition of the opponent's statement; but in <s>apratibhā</s>, even when the opponent's statement is repeated, there is failure to produce a response — this is the distinction.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: vikṣepalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>vikṣepa</s> (evasion)

children.text:
asambhavatkālāntarakāryavyāsaṅgānudbhāvya kathāvicchedaḥ
vikṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Vikṣepa</s> (evasion) is the interruption of debate by raising the pretext of a task at another time that does not [actually need to] occur [now].

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
vikṣepaṃ lakṣayati --
asambhavaditi/ kālāntare kartuṃ śakyaṃ vastuta idānīṃ bhavitumanarhaṃ
yat kāryaṃ tatra vyāsaṅgamudbhāvya kathāvicchedo vikṣepaḥ/ tena
rājapuruṣādibhirākāraṇe gṛhajanādibhirvā
āvaśyakakāryārthamākāraṇa svagṛhadāhādikaṃ paśyato gamane
vāstavaśirorogādinā pratibandhe vā na vikṣepaḥ/ 'yatra kartavyaṃ
vyāsajya kathāṃ vyavacchinnatti idaṃ me karaṇīyaṃ vidyate tasminnavasite
paścāt kathayāmīti vikṣepo nāma nigrahasthānam' iti bhāṣyam/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>vikṣepa</s> — 'That does not [actually need to] occur.' <s>Vikṣepa</s> is the interruption of debate by raising the pretext of a task that can be done at another time and in reality does not deserve to occur now. Therefore, when summoned by royal officers and the like, or when summoned by household members for an essential task, or when seeing one's own house on fire and departing, or when obstructed by a genuine headache and the like, it is not <s>vikṣepa</s>. 'Where one interrupts the debate by engaging in a task [saying] "I have this to do, after it is completed I will debate afterwards" — that is the point of defeat called <s>vikṣepa</s>' — thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: matānujñālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>matānujñā</s> (conceding the opponent's position)

children.text:
svapakṣe
doṣamanuddhṛtya parapakṣe doṣābhidhānam matānujñā/
children.translated_text: <s>Matānujñā</s> (conceding the opponent's position) is the statement of a fault in the opponent's position without having extracted [and refuted] the fault in one's own position.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
matānujñāṃ lakṣayati
- svapakṣa iti/ svasiddhānte paroktaṃ doṣamaṅgīkṛtyānuddhṛtya ca
parasiddhānte 'pi samāno doṣa ityudbhāvanaṃ matānujñetyarthaḥ/
yathā-puruṣatvāccedahaṃ coraḥ tata eva bhavānapi cora ityādikam/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>matānujñā</s> — 'In one's own position.' The meaning is: accepting and not extracting [i.e. refuting] the fault stated by the opponent in one's own established doctrine, and then raising 'there is the same fault in your established doctrine also' — this is <s>matānujñā</s>. For example — 'If I am a thief because of being a man, then by the same [reason] you too are a thief' and the like.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: paryanuyojyopekṣaṇanapalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>paryanuyojyopekṣaṇa</s> (ignoring what deserves censure)

children.text:
udbhāvanārhaparakīyanigrahasthānānudbhāvanaṃ
paryanuyojyopekṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: <s>Paryanuyojyopekṣaṇa</s> (ignoring what deserves censure) is the failure to point out a point of defeat of the opponent that deserves to be pointed out.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
paryanuyojyopekṣaṇaṃ lakṣayati - udbhāvanārheti/
paryanuyojyo nāma nigrahopapattyā codanīyaḥ, tasyopekṣaṇaṃ
nigrahasthānaṃ prāpto 'sītyananuyogaḥ/ etacca kasya parājaya
ityanuyuktayā pariṣadā vacanīyam/ na khalu nigrahaṃ prāptaḥ
svakaupīnaṃ vivṛṇuyāt' iti bhāṣyam/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>paryanuyojyopekṣaṇa</s> — 'That deserves to be pointed out.' <s>Paryanuyojya</s> means one who deserves to be challenged on the ground that a point of defeat applies; the ignoring of such a one is the failure to charge 'you have reached a point of defeat.' And this is to be stated by the assembly when asked 'whose defeat is it?' 'Indeed, one who has reached a point of defeat would not expose his own loincloth' — thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text:
'nanu vādinā
kathamidamudbhāvyam, svakaupīnaviraṇasyāyuktatvāditi
cet-satyam/ madhyasthenaiva idamudbhāvyam, vāde ca
svayamudbhāvane 'pyadoṣaḥ' iti viśvanāthaḥ/ śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam/
children.translated_text: 'Now, how can the proponent point this out, since it is improper to expose one's own loincloth?' — if so, that is true. This should be pointed out by the impartial [assessor] alone; and in a formal debate (<s>vāda</s>), there is no fault even in pointing it out oneself — thus [says] <s>Viśvanātha</s>. The rest is clear.

children.text:
atra
jātinigrahasthānaviṣaye
bhāṣya-vārtika-tātparyaṭīkā-pariśuddhi-nyāyapariśiṣṭa-nyāyapariśiṣṭa-nyāyamañjarī
children.translated_text: Regarding the subject of <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders) and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat), there is extensive discussion in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, <s>Vārtika</s>, <s>Tātparyaṭīkā</s>, <s>Pariśuddhi</s>, <s>Nyāyapariśiṣṭa</s>, <s>Nyāyamañjarī</s>,

children.text:
-tārkikarakṣādiṣu
grantheṣu vedāntadeśikakṛtanyāyapariśuddhau ca bahuvivecitamasti/
tatsarvaṃ sāvadhānaṃ parāmṛśya kaścinmahānprabandhaḥ pṛthageva lekhanīyaḥ/
prakaraṇagranthe etāvadeva paryāptamiti vistarabhayāduparamyate/
children.translated_text: <s>Tārkikarakṣā</s> and other texts, as well as in the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> composed by <s>Vedāntadeśika</s>. Having carefully considered all of that, a separate extensive treatise should be written by some great [scholar]. In a handbook text, this much alone is sufficient — thus, out of fear of prolixity, [the author] desists.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text: niranuyojyānuyogalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>niranuyojyānuyoga</s> (censuring the blameless)

children.text:
nigrahasthānarahite
nigrahasthānodbhāvanam niranuyojyānuyogaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Niranuyojyānuyoga</s> (censuring the blameless) is the pointing out of a point of defeat in one who is free from any point of defeat.

children.text: apasiddhāntalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>apasiddhānta</s> (contradicting one's own doctrine)

children.text:
ekasiddhāntamatamāśritya kathāpravṛttau
tadviruddhasiddhāntamatamālambyottaradānam upasiddhāntaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Apasiddhānta</s> (contradicting one's own doctrine) is giving a response that relies on a doctrinal position contradicting the doctrinal position upon which the debate was entered.

children.text:
pratijñāhāni -
ananubhāṣaṇa - ajñāna - apratibhā -
vikṣepaparyanuyojyopekṣaṇānāmabhāve, manyeṣāṃ
hetvābhāsavyatiriktanigrahasthānānāṃ guṇe, hetvābhāsānāṃ ca
dravyādiṣu antarbhāvaḥ yathāyathaṃ bodhyaḥ/ atiriktaḥ sūtrārthaḥ sugama
ityabhiprāyeṇāha - śeṣamiti/
children.translated_text: In the absence of <s>pratijñāhāni</s> (thesis-abandonment), <s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s> (non-response), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>apratibhā</s> (lack of wit), <s>vikṣepa</s> (evasion), and <s>paryanuyojyopekṣaṇa</s> (ignoring what deserves censure) — and treating the remaining points of defeat other than <s>hetvābhāsa</s> as [falling under] quality (<s>guṇa</s>), and the <s>hetvābhāsas</s> as included in substance (<s>dravya</s>) and the rest — the inclusion should be understood appropriately. The remaining content of the <s>sūtras</s> being easily accessible, he says with this intention: 'The rest.'

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
jātīnāṃ
nigrahasthānānāṃ ca kḷpteṣu saptasu padārtheṣu antarbhāva-prakāramāha -
pratijñāhānītyādinā/ dinakarīgranthe pratijñāhānyādīnāṃ
nigrahasthānānāṃ pratyekamupādānena tatra tatrāntarbhāvaḥ viśadamuktaḥ
tata evāvaseyaḥ/ asaduttararūpajāteḥ
svābhimatārthavyāghātakasvottaravākyarūpatayā śabdātmake
guṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the manner of inclusion of <s>jātis</s> (futile rejoinders) and <s>nigrahasthānas</s> (points of defeat) within the established seven categories — beginning with '<s>pratijñāhāni</s>' and so forth. In the <s>Dinakarī</s> text, by taking up each of the points of defeat such as <s>pratijñāhāni</s> and the rest individually, their inclusion in the respective [categories] is stated clearly; it should be ascertained from that. The <s>jāti</s> in the form of an invalid rejoinder is included in quality (<s>guṇa</s>), which is of the nature of word (<s>śabda</s>), since it has the form of one's own response-sentence that contradicts one's own intended meaning.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: śakteratiriktapadārthatvakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of <s>śakti</s> (potency) being a separate category

children.text:
nanu
karatalānalasaṃyoge satyapi pratibandhake sati dāhānutpatteḥ śaktiḥ
padārthāntaramiti cet - na/ pratibandhakābhāvasya kāryamātre
kāraṇatvena śakteranupayogāt/ kāraṇatvasyaiva śaktipadārthatvāt/
children.translated_text: Now, [if one argues:] even when contact with fire on the palm is present, since burning does not arise when an obstructor is present, <s>śakti</s> (potency) is a separate category — [we reply:] no, because since the absence of an obstructor is a cause in all effects, <s>śakti</s> serves no [additional] purpose, [and] because causal-ness itself is the category denoted by the word '<s>śakti</s>.'

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanu analasaṃyoge
satyapi maṇyādisamavadhāne dāho na jāyata iti maṇyādeḥ
pratibandhakatā vācyā/ sā ca vahnau dāhānukūlaśaktisvīkāra eva
nirvahati/ pratibandhakatāyāḥ kāryāṃnukūlaśaktivighaṭakatvarūpatvāt/
ataḥ tadanyathānupapattisiddhāyāḥ śakteratiriktatvāt 'saptaiva padārthāḥ'
ityasaṅgatamiti prābhākaraḥ śaṅkate - nanviti/ nanvevaṃ
śaktisiddhāvapi tasyā atiriktatvāsiddhiriti cet - na/ yato na
tāvaddravyātmikā śaktiḥ guṇādivṛttitvāt/
children.translated_text: Now, even when contact with fire is present, when a gem and the like are placed nearby, burning does not arise — hence the obstructive capacity of the gem and the like must be stated. And that can be sustained only by accepting a potency (<s>śakti</s>) in fire favorable to burning, since obstructive capacity has the nature of destroying a potency favorable to the effect. Therefore, since that <s>śakti</s>, established by the impossibility of explaining [the phenomenon] otherwise, is a separate [category], the statement 'there are only seven categories' is incongruous — thus the <s>Prābhākara</s> raises the objection: 'Now.' If [one says] even granting the establishment of <s>śakti</s>, its separateness is not established — [we reply:] no, because <s>śakti</s> is not of the nature of substance (<s>dravya</s>), since it resides in qualities and the like.

children.text:
ata eva na
guṇakarmānyatararūpā, na ca sāmānyādyanyatamarūpā, utpatti
vināśaśālitvāt/ evaṃ cātiriktapadārthatvasiddhiriti/ nanu
pratibandhakatvaṃ na kāryānukūlaśaktivighaṭakatvame kiṃ tu
kāraṇībhūtābhāvapratiyogitvam/ tacca maṇyabhāvasya hetutvādeva
upapadyate, maṇisamavadhānadaśāyāṃ ca tadabhāvarūpakāraṇāntarābhāvādeva
dāhānutpattisambhavaḥ/ itthaṃ cātiriktaśaktisvīkāro 'nucita iti
samādhatte - pratibandhakābhāvasyeti/ nanu 'dāhotpāde vahniḥ śaktaḥ'
iti vyavahārānyathānupapattyā setsyati atiriktā śaktirityāśaṅkya
tasyāḥ kāraṇatārūpatve 'pi vyavahāropapatteḥ nātiriktā śaktirityāha
- kāraṇatvasyeti/ nanu maṇyādyabhāvasya hetutve maṇisamavadhānadaśāyāṃ
satyapyuttejake dāho na syāt/ manmate tu maṇyādyapasāraṇadaśāyāmiva
uttejakasamavadhānadaśānayāmapi vahnau dāhānukūlaśaktyantarotpatteḥ
aṅgīkāreṇa na doṣa iti cet - na/
uttejakābhāvaviśiṣṭamaṇyādyabhāvasya kāraṇatvāṅgīkāreṇa adoṣāt/ na
ca uttejakānāṃ ananugatatvāt
tattaduttejakābhāvakūṭaviśiṣṭamaṇyādyabhāvasyaiva kāraṇatāyāḥ
kalpanīyatayā gauravamiti vācyam/ dāhānukūlaśakti prati
etādṛśakāraṇatāyāḥ tavāpyāvaśyakatvāt
anantaśaktitatprāgabhāvataddhvaṃsakalpane gauravāditi saṅkṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: For this very reason, [<s>śakti</s> (capacity)] is not of the nature of either <s>guṇa</s> (quality) or <s>karma</s> (action), nor is it of the nature of any one among <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) and so forth, because it is subject to origination and destruction. And thus the existence of <s>śakti</s> as a separate category (<s>padārtha</s>) is established. Objection: Obstruction (<s>pratibandhakatva</s>) is not the disruption of the capacity favorable to the effect, but rather the counter-positive-hood of the absence that has become a cause. And that is explained simply by the causal status of the absence of the gem. And in the state where the gem is present, the non-origination of burning is possible simply due to the absence of the other cause in the form of that absence [of the gem]. Thus, accepting a separate <s>śakti</s> is inappropriate — he resolves this with 'of the absence of the obstructor.' Objection: The separate <s>śakti</s> will be established through the impossibility of otherwise explaining the usage 'fire is capable of producing burning.' Anticipating this, since the usage is explained even if that [capacity] has the form of causality, he says that <s>śakti</s> is not separate — with 'of causality.' Objection: If the absence of gems and such is the cause, then even when a stimulant is present during the state of gem-contact, burning would not occur. But in our view, just as in the state of removing the gem, so too in the state of the stimulant's presence, by accepting the origination of another capacity favorable to burning in fire, there is no fault. To this — no, because there is no fault in accepting the causality of the absence of gems qualified by the absence of the stimulant. And one should not say that since stimulants are not uniform, the causality of only the absence of gems qualified by the aggregate of respective stimulant-absences must be postulated, resulting in complexity — because such causality is necessary for you too with respect to the capacity favorable to burning, and there is complexity in postulating infinite capacities, their prior absences, and their destructions. This is the summary.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
karatalasya agneśca
saṃyoge satyapi maṇiyapapratibandhakasattve karatalasya dāho na jāyata
iti śaktiḥ padārthāntaram/ ityāśaṅkitaṃ dīpikāyām/ tatra
dāhānutpattimātreṇa śakteḥ padārthāntaratvaṃ katha sidhyet, ataḥ
śaṅkeyamanupapannā ityataḥ śaṅkāgranthasyāśayaṃ vadan avatārayati
-- nanvanalaṃsayoge satyapīti/ karatalasya analasaṃyoge satyapi
maṇyādisattve karatalasya dāho na jāyate maṇyādyasattve dāho jāyate/
yatsattve kāryaṃ notpadyate yadasattve cotpadyate tasya pratibandhakatvāt
maṇyādeḥ sattve dāho na jāyate tadasattve dāho jāyata iti
maṇyādeḥ dāhapratibandhakatvaṃ vācyam/ pratibandhakatvaṃ ca
kāryānukūlaśaktivighaṭakatvam/ tathā ca dāhānukūlā yā agniniṣṭhā
śaktiḥ sā maṇinā nāśyate/ ataḥ śaktiviśiṣṭavahnereva dāhajanakatvāt
maṇisattve dāhaśakternāśāt śaktiviśiṣṭavahnereva dāhajanakatvāt
maṇisattve dāhaśakternāśāt śaktiviśiṣṭavahnirūpakāraṇābhāvāt na
dāhaḥ/ itthaṃ ca kāryānukūlaśaktivighaṭakatvāt vinā nopapadyata
ityevamarthāpattipramāṇena śaktirūpasyātiriktasya padārthasya siddhau
padārthā ityuktiḥ saṅgacchata iti śaṅkiturbhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Even when there is conjunction of the palm and fire, if the obstructor gem is present, burning of the palm does not arise — therefore <s>śakti</s> (capacity) is a separate category. This was the objection raised in the <s>Dīpikā</s>. There, how can the separate-category-hood of <s>śakti</s> be established merely by the non-origination of burning? Therefore, since the objection is unjustified, he introduces the intent behind the objection passage — with 'even when there is conjunction with fire.' Even when there is conjunction of the palm with fire, if gems and such are present, burning of the palm does not arise; when gems and such are absent, burning arises. Since that in whose presence the effect does not arise and in whose absence it arises has the nature of an obstructor, it must be said that gems and such have the nature of obstructing burning. And obstruction is the disruption of the capacity favorable to the effect. Accordingly, the capacity residing in fire that is favorable to burning is destroyed by the gem. Therefore, since only fire qualified by capacity produces burning, when the gem is present and the burning-capacity is destroyed, due to the absence of the cause in the form of fire qualified by capacity, there is no burning. And thus, since [the phenomenon] cannot be explained without the disruption of the capacity favorable to the effect, the establishment of a separate category in the form of <s>śakti</s> through the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) makes the statement 'the categories' coherent — this is the intent of the objector.

children.text:
nanvevamiti/
arthāṃpattipramāṇena pūrvoktarītyā śaktirūpapadārthasya siddhāvipa tasyāḥ
saptapadārthātiriktatvaṃ kathamityarthaḥ/ yato na tāvat
dravyātmiketyādi/ śaktiḥ dravyabhinnā guṇādivṛttitvāt
guṇatvādivat/ śaktirhi rūpādiguṇeṣu kriyādau cāsti/
avayavarūpādau avayavirūpādikāraṇatvena tadanuguṇaśakteḥ sattvāt
tasyāḥ rūpādiguṇavṛttitvāt kriyāyāḥ saṃyogādijanakatvena
tadanukūlaśaktimattvāt śakteḥ kriyāvṛttitvācca/ tathā ca
guṇādivṛttiguṇatvakriyātvādikaṃ yathā na dravyaṃ tathā śaktirapi
children.translated_text: 'But in this way' — even if the category in the form of <s>śakti</s> is established through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) in the previously stated manner, how can its being beyond the seven categories be [established]? This is the meaning. 'Since it is not of the nature of substance' and so forth: <s>Śakti</s> is different from <s>dravya</s> (substance), because it resides in <s>guṇa</s> (quality) and <s>karma</s> (action), just like <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood) and the like. For <s>śakti</s> exists in qualities like <s>rūpa</s> (color) and in actions. Since in the color and other qualities of a part, there is the capacity appropriate for the causality of the color and other qualities of the whole, <s>śakti</s> resides in qualities like color; and since action, being the producer of conjunction and such, possesses a capacity appropriate to that, <s>śakti</s> resides in action as well. Accordingly, just as <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood), <s>kriyātva</s> (action-hood), and such, which reside in quality and action, are not <s>dravya</s> (substance), so too <s>śakti</s>,

children.text:
guṇādivṛttitvāt na
dravyamityarthaḥ/ ata eveti/ guṇādivṛttitvādevetyarthaḥ/ śaktiḥ
guṇakarmānyatarabhinnā guṇādivṛttitvāt guṇatvādivat/
guṇakarmobhayabhedasya sādhyatve guṇarūpatve karmaṃrūpatve 'pi ca 'evaṃ
nobhayam' iti nyāyena ubhayabhedasambhāvāt uddheśyāsiddhiḥ
syādityālocya anyatarabhedasya sādhyatvamanusṛtam/ yatra guṇabhedaḥ
karmabhedaśca ubhayamasti tatraiva guṇakarmānyatarabhedaḥ saṃbhavatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: because it resides in quality and action, is not <s>dravya</s> (substance) — this is the meaning. 'For this very reason' — means: because it resides in quality and action. <s>Śakti</s> is different from either <s>guṇa</s> (quality) or <s>karma</s> (action), because it resides in quality and action, just like <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood) and the like. Since, if the difference from both quality and action were the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), due to the possibility of such difference even if it has the form of quality or the form of action — by the principle 'thus not both' — there would be unestablished-ness of the subject, therefore the difference from either one is adopted as the <s>sādhya</s>. The purport is that the difference from either quality or action is possible only where both difference from quality and difference from action are present.

children.text:
na ca
sāmānyādyanyatamarūpeti/ śaktiḥ sāmānyādyanyatamabhinne
utpattivināśaśālitvāt ghaṭādivat/ utpattimattvamātrasya hetutvaṃ
sāmānyādyanyatamabhedābhāvavati dhvaṃse utpattimattvasattvāt vyabhicāraḥ/
tadvāraṇāya vināśaśālitvāditi/ dhvaṃsasya vināśābhāvāt na
vyabhicāraḥ/ vināśāśālitvāmātroktau uktasādhyābhāvavati prāgabhāve
vināśitvasattvāt vyabhicāraḥ/ tadvāraṇāya utpattiniveśaḥ/
prāgabhāvasyānādeḥ utpattivirāhat na vyabhicāraḥ/ tathā ca
utpattivināśobhayavattvaṃ utpattiviśiṣṭavināśavattvaṃ vā hetuḥ/
sāmānyādītyatra ādiśabdena viśeṣasamavāyābhāsava gṛhyata/ evaṃ ceti/
pūvauktānumānairarthāpattyā cānugṛjahītena śaktiḥ atiriktaḥ padārthaḥ
kḷptapadārthānantarbhūtatve sati padārthatvāt iti
pariśeṣānumānena śakteratiriktapadārthatvaṃ sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Nor is it of the nature of any among <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) and the rest': <s>Śakti</s> is different from any one among <s>sāmānya</s> and the rest, because it is subject to origination and destruction, like a pot. If mere possession of origination were the reason, there would be deviation, since origination-possession exists in <s>dhvaṃsa</s> (destruction) which lacks the absence of difference from any among <s>sāmānya</s> and the rest. To block this, [he adds] 'subject to destruction.' Since <s>dhvaṃsa</s> has no destruction, there is no deviation. If mere subject-to-destruction were stated, there would be deviation in <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence) which possesses destruction but lacks the stated <s>sādhya</s>. To block this, origination is included. Since <s>prāgabhāva</s>, being beginningless, lacks origination, there is no deviation. Accordingly, the reason is possession of both origination and destruction, or possession of destruction qualified by origination. By the word 'and the rest' in 'universal and the rest,' <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity), <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), and <s>abhāva</s> (absence) are included. 'And thus' — through the aforementioned inferences and supported by <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>śakti</s> is a separate category: because it has category-hood while not being included in the established categories — by this eliminative inference, the separate-category-hood of <s>śakti</s> is established. This is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
'pratibandhakābhāvasya kāryaṃmātre kāraṇatvena śakteranupayogāt'
iti dīpikāgranthaḥ śakteḥ padārthatvakhaṇḍanāya pravṛttaḥ/ kāryamātre
pratibandhakābhāvasya kāraṇatvamastu nāma/ tāvatā śakteḥ padārthatvaṃ
kuto na bhavatī iti śaṅkāyāṃ dīpikāyāḥ
tātparyamāha-pratibandhakatvaṃ neti/ tacceti/ pratibandhakatvaṃ cetyarthaḥ/
maṇyabhāvasya hetutvādeveti/ evakāreṇa
kāryānukūlaśaktivighaṭakatvavyavacchedaḥ/ tathā ca maṇeḥ
kāryānukūlaśaktivighaṭakatvābhāve 'pi kāraṇībhūto yo maṇyabhāvaḥ
tatpratiyogitvāt pratibandhakatvamupapadyate/ tathā ca
anyathānupapattirūpārthāpattipramāṇasyābhāvāt na śaktisiddhiriti bhāvaḥ/
tadabhāvarūpakāraṇāntarābhāvādeveti/ maṇyabhāvarūpaṃ yat kāraṇāntaraṃ
tadabhāvādevetyarthaḥ/ atra antaraśabdaprayogāt dāhaṃ prati vahniḥ
maṇyabhāvaśca ityubhayaṃ pṛthak kāraṇam, na tu
maṇyabhāvaviśiṣṭavahniḥ kāraṇam/ vahniviśiṣṭamaṇyabhāvaḥ kāraṇaṃ vā
maṇyabhāvaviśiṣṭavahniḥ kāraṇaṃ ceti viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāve
vinanigamanāviraheṇa gurubhūtakāryakāraṇabhāvadvayāpatteriti
sūcitam/
children.translated_text: Objection: The <s>Dīpikā</s> passage 'because the absence of the obstructor has causality with respect to every effect, <s>śakti</s> is of no use' is directed at refuting the category-hood of <s>śakti</s>. Let the absence of the obstructor have causality with respect to every effect — by that much alone, why should the category-hood of <s>śakti</s> not obtain? In response to this doubt, he states the purport of the <s>Dīpikā</s> — 'obstruction is not.' 'And that' means: and obstruction. 'Simply by the causal status of the absence of the gem' — by the word 'simply,' the disruption of the capacity favorable to the effect is excluded. Accordingly, even without the gem's disruption of the capacity favorable to the effect, since the absence of the gem that has become a cause has counter-positive-hood [i.e., obstruction], obstruction is explained. And thus, since the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>arthāpatti</s> in the form of 'otherwise inexplicable' is absent, <s>śakti</s> is not established — this is the purport. 'Simply by the absence of the other cause in the form of that absence' — meaning: simply by the absence of that other cause which is the absence of the gem. Here, from the use of the word 'other,' both fire and the absence of the gem are separately causes of burning, and not fire qualified by the absence of the gem. It is indicated that [to determine] whether the absence of the gem qualified by fire is the cause, or fire qualified by the absence of the gem is the cause — in the qualifier-qualificand relation, due to the absence of a deciding reason, two burdensome causal relations would absurdly follow.

children.text:
nanu
pratibandhakatvānyathānupapattyā śaktyasiddhāvapi vyavahārānyathānupapattyā
śakt sidhyatīti śaṅkate - nanu dāhotpāda iti
śaktirūpātiriktapadārtha vināpi kḷptena kāraṇatvarūpapadārthenaiva
vyavahārasyopapattyā na vyavahārānupapattirastītyāha - tasyāḥ
kāraṇatārūpatve 'pīti/ nanu kāraṇatvaṃ kathaṃ nātiriktaṃ iti cet -
atrāhuḥ/ kāraṇatvamiti āgnitvā udijātau vā abhāva vā
kāraṇatvasyāntarbhāva iti/ spaṣṭamidaṃ kusumāñjalādau/
children.translated_text: Objection: Even if <s>śakti</s> is not established through the otherwise-inexplicability of obstruction, it will be established through the otherwise-inexplicability of the usage [that fire is 'capable']. He raises the objection — 'fire is capable of producing burning.' Since the usage is explained even without a separate category in the form of <s>śakti</s>, by the established category in the form of <s>kāraṇatva</s> (causality) itself, there is no inexplicability of the usage — he says with 'even if that has the form of causality.' Objection: How is causality not separate? To this they say: Causality is included either in the universal born of fire-hood, or in absence — thus in <s>Kusumāñjali</s> and elsewhere this is clear.

children.text:
śaṅkate -- nanu
maṇyādyabhāvasya hetutva iti/ candrakāntamaṇiḥ dāhapratibandhakaḥ
tadabhāvaḥ dāhahetuḥ/ yatra vahnau candrakāntamaṇisaṃyogakāle
sūryakāntamaṇisaṃyogo vā mantroddheśyatvaṃ vā asti tadā dāho
jāyate/ tatra candrakāntamaṇyabhāvarūpasya kāraṇasyābhāvāt tava mate
kathaṃ dāhaḥ? mama mate tu maṇyabhāvaḥ na dāhakāraṇam/ api tu
śaktiviśiṣṭavahnireva kāraṇam/ candrakāntamaṇinā
vahnigataśakternāśe 'pi sūryakāntamaṇimantrādisamavadhānadaśāyāṃ punaḥ
vahnau dāhānukūlaśaktyantaramutpadyata iti svīkāreṇa
śaktiviśiṣṭavahneḥ sattvāt dāhaḥ sambhavati, ataḥ śaktiḥ
aṅgīkaraṇīyeti śaṅkiturbhāvaḥ/ atra uttejakaśabdena
pratibandhakasattve 'pi kāryotpattiprayojakaḥ sūryakāntamaṇyādirucyate/
pratibandhakasamavadhānakālikakāryotpattiprayojakatvaṃ uttejakatvamityuktaṃ
bhavati/
children.translated_text: He raises the objection — 'but if the absence of gems is the cause.' The <s>candrakānta</s> (moonstone) gem is an obstructor of burning; its absence is the cause of burning. When, in fire during the time of moonstone contact, there is conjunction with a <s>sūryakānta</s> (sunstone) gem, or there is being the object of a <s>mantra</s>, then burning arises. There, in your view, since the cause in the form of the absence of the moonstone is absent, how does burning occur? But in our view, the absence of the gem is not the cause of burning; rather, only fire qualified by <s>śakti</s> (capacity) is the cause. Even when the capacity residing in fire is destroyed by the moonstone, in the state of contact with a stimulant such as the sunstone or <s>mantra</s>, another capacity favorable to burning arises anew in the fire — by accepting this, since fire qualified by capacity exists, burning is possible. Therefore <s>śakti</s> must be accepted — this is the objector's intent. Here, by the word 'stimulant' (<s>uttejaka</s>), what is meant is a sunstone gem and such that brings about the origination of the effect even when the obstructor is present. The stimulant-hood is stated to be the property of bringing about the origination of the effect contemporaneous with the obstructor.

children.text:
samādhatte --
uttejakābhāvaviśiṣṭeti/ yatra maṇiḥ uttejakaṃ ca vartate tatra
uttejakābhāvarūpaviśeṣaṇābhāvāt viśiṣṭābhāvarūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ astīti
dāhotpattirūpapadyata iti śakteranupayoga iti bhāvaḥ/
ananugatatvāditi/ anekatvādityarthaḥ/ gauravamiti/ anekeṣāṃ
uttejakābhāvānāṃ kāraṇatāvacchedakakukṣau praveśāditi bhāvaḥ/
dāhānukūlaśaktiṃ pratīti/ maṇisattve
dāhānukūlaśakternāśāṅkīkārāt maṇyapasāraṇe
tādaśaśaktyutpatteśca
children.translated_text: He resolves this — 'qualified by the absence of the stimulant.' Where the gem and the stimulant are both present, since the qualifier in the form of the absence of the stimulant is absent, the cause in the form of the qualified [absence] exists — thus the origination of burning is explained, and <s>śakti</s> is of no use. This is the purport. 'Due to non-uniformity' — means: due to multiplicity. 'Complexity' — the purport is: because multiple stimulant-absences must enter the scope of the delimitor of causality. 'With respect to the capacity favorable to burning' — since it is accepted that when the gem is present the capacity favorable to burning is destroyed, and when the gem is removed such capacity arises,

children.text:
aṅgīkārāt
vahniniṣṭhāṃ dāhānukūlaśaktiṃ prati maṇyabhāvaḥ kāraṇam, tatrāpi
maṇimattve śaktināśāt uttejake sati śakterutpatteśca
uttejakābhāvaviśiṣṭamaṇyabhāvaḥ śaktiṃ prati kāraṇamiti vācyam/
tadapekṣayā dāhaṃ pratyeva tasya kāraṇatvamastu kiṃ anantānāṃ śaktīnāṃ
tatprāgabhāvataddhvaṃsādīnāṃ ca kalpaneneti bhāvaḥ/ nanu
uttejakābhāvakūṭaviśiṣṭamaṇyabhāvasya dāhaṃ prati hetutve
mantrarūpottejakadaśāyāmapi śabdātmakasya mantrasya gagananiṣṭhatvena
vahnyādhikaraṇe deśe tadabhāvasattvāt sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena
taduttejakābhāvaviśiṣṭamaṇisattvāt dāhānutpādaprasaṅgaḥ/ kiṃ ca
saṃyogavat saṃyogena dravyasyāpi avyāpyavṛttitayā maṇisattvepi
kiñcidavacchedena saṃyogena
children.translated_text: by this acceptance, the absence of the gem is a cause with respect to the capacity favorable to burning residing in fire. There too, since when the gem is present the capacity is destroyed, and when the stimulant is present the capacity arises, one must say that the absence of the gem qualified by the absence of the stimulant is a cause with respect to <s>śakti</s>. In comparison with that, let the causality of that [qualified absence] be with respect to burning directly — what is the point of postulating infinite capacities, their prior absences, their destructions, and so forth? This is the purport. Objection: If the absence of the gem qualified by the aggregate of stimulant-absences is the cause of burning, then even in the state of a stimulant in the form of a <s>mantra</s>, since the <s>mantra</s> being of the nature of sound resides in space, in the locus where fire abides its absence exists, and thus by the relation of co-location the absence of the gem qualified by the absence of that stimulant exists — there would be the absurd consequence of non-origination of burning. Moreover, just as conjunction, through conjunction, substance too has non-pervasive occurrence, so even when the gem is present, since by some delimitation through conjunction

children.text:
maṇyabhāvasattvāt
dāhotpattiprasaṅgaśca ityata āha--saṅkṣepa iti/
abhāvīyaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhena dāhatvāvacchinnaṃ prati
uddeśyatā-daiśikaviśeṣaṇatānyatarasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākānāṃ
tattaduttejakābhāvānāṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyarūpaṃ yadvaiśiṣṭyaṃ tadavacchinnasya
maṇyādeḥ
daiśikaviśeṣaṇatā-uddeśyatānyatarasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvasyābhāvīyaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhena
hetutvamiti dinakaryuktarītyā kāryakāraṇabhāvaṃ parikalpya
pūrvoktadoṣau vāraṇīyau iti bhāvaḥ/ etāvatā/
sahajaśaktirniṃrākṛtā/
children.translated_text: the absence of the gem exists, there would be the absurd consequence of the origination of burning. Therefore he says — 'in summary.' By the relation of being a qualifier in the absence-domain, with respect to [the effect] delimited by burning-hood, the causality of the absence of gems and such — whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the relation of either locational qualification or intentional reference with respect to the respective stimulant-absences — [takes the form of] a qualification by co-location, and the absence having counter-positive-hood delimited by the relation of either locational qualification or intentional reference — its causality by the relation of being a qualifier in the absence-domain. By devising the causal relation in the manner stated in the <s>Dīnakarī</s>, the two previously stated faults are to be avoided — this is the purport. 'By this much' — the inherent <s>śakti</s> has been refuted.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: ādheyaśaktinirāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Refutation of superimposed <s>śakti</s> (<s>ādheyaśakti</s>)

children.text:
nanu bhasmādinā
kāṃsyādau śuddhidarśanāt ādheyaśaktiḥ aṅgīkāryā iti cet - na/
bhasmādisaṃyogasamānakālīnāspṛśyasparśapratiyogikayāvadabhāvasahitabhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsasya
śuddhipadārthatvāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since purification of bronze and such is observed through ash and the like, superimposed <s>śakti</s> (<s>ādheyaśakti</s>) should be accepted. To this — no, because the entity denoted by 'purification' is the destruction of the conjunction with ash and the like that is contemporaneous with a contact whose counter-positive is an untouchable-touch lasting as long as [there exists the prior state], combined with the absence lasting until [that destruction].

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
nanu evamapi
kāṃsyādeḥ aspṛśyavastusparśe sati na bhojanādirūpakāryārhatā
śaktimatkāṃsyādereva tadarhatvāt/ aspṛśyasparśeṃ sati śakternāśāt
bhasmasaṃyoge tu punaḥ śakterutpādāt tadarhatā/ evaṃ ca kāṃsyādau
ādheyaśaktiḥ svīkāryā/ na ca kāṃsyādau bhojanādikaṃ prati
aspṛśyasparśasya pratibandhakatvakalpanādeva upapattau tadanaṅgīkāra
iti vācyam/ prakṛte ca aspṛśyasparśasya asaṃspṛśyasaṃyogarūpatayā
sati sannāśe pratibandhakābhāvasadbhāvāt, kāṃsyādau antarā
bhasmādisaṃyojanaṃ bhojanādyarhatāpatteriti punaḥ pratyavatiṣṭhate -
nanu bhasmādineti/ prathamenādipadena amlādeḥ dvitīyena ca tāmrādeḥ
parigrahaḥ/ kḷptadhvaṃsaviśeṣeṇaiva kāṃsyādeḥ śuddhatvopapattau
atiriktaśaktyaṅgīkāro 'nucita iti samādhatte -
bhasmādisaṃyogeti/ yatra kāṃsyādau bhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsānantaraṃ
punaraspṛśyasparśaḥ tatrāpi bhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsasya sattvāt
śuddhyāpattiḥ ataḥ sahitāntaṃ dhvaṃsaviśeṣaṇam/ sāhityaṃ cātra
sambandhaviśeṣaniyantritaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyam aspṛśyavastūnāṃ
anugamakarūpasya durvacatayā
sāmānyadharmāvacchinnānabhāvaniveśāsambhavāt
yaktiñcidaspṛśyasparśābhāvasya ca tatra sattvāt tadāpattiḥ tadavasthaiva
ityataḥ yāvaditi/ tathā ca tatra yāvatāṃ aspṛśyasparśābhāvānāṃ
niravacchinnaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhena asattvāt noktadoṣa iti bhāvaḥ/
yatra ca bhasmādisaṃyogāspṛśyavastusparśau yugapadevotpannau vinaṣṭau
ca tatra tattadaspṛśyasparśābhāva
kūṭasāmānādhikaraṇyaviśiṣṭabhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsamādāya śuddhatāpattiḥ
ataḥ bhasamādisaṃyogakālāvacchedena tatra vidyamānārthakaṃ
kālīnāntamabhāvaviśeṣaṇam/ tathā ca tava
bhasmādisaṃyogakṣaṇāvacchedena yāvattadabhāvānāmasattvāt na doṣa
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: But even so, when an untouchable object comes into contact with bronze and the like, there is no fitness for activities such as eating, since only bronze and the like that possess the capacity (<s>śakti</s>) are fit for that. When there is contact with an untouchable, the capacity is destroyed; but upon contact with ash, the capacity is produced again, and hence the fitness [is restored]. Thus, a superimposed capacity (<s>ādheyaśakti</s>) in bronze and the like must be accepted. Nor should one say that since the matter is explained simply by postulating that the contact of an untouchable is an obstructor (<s>pratibandha</s>) of eating and the like in bronze, that [capacity] need not be accepted — because in the present case, since the contact of an untouchable has the form of conjunction with what should not be touched, and since when that conjunction is destroyed the absence of the obstructor obtains, there would be the unwanted consequence that bronze and the like become fit for eating even without the intervening application of ash and the like. He raises the objection again with 'but with ash' and so forth. By the first word 'and the like,' sour substances and the like are included; by the second, copper and the like are included. He resolves [the matter] by showing that since the purity of bronze and the like is explained by a specific destruction already established, the acceptance of an additional capacity is inappropriate — with 'the conjunction with ash' and so forth. Where, in bronze and the like, after the destruction of the conjunction with ash and the like, there is again contact with an untouchable — even there, since the destruction of the conjunction with ash exists, there would be the unwanted consequence of purity; hence the qualifier of the destruction ends with 'accompanied by.' The accompaniment (<s>sāhitya</s>) here is co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) governed by a specific relation, because the common form characterizing untouchable objects is difficult to state, because the inclusion of non-existence delimited by a general property is impossible, and because even the absence of contact with some particular untouchable thing exists there — hence the unwanted consequence remains the same. Therefore [the qualifier] 'as many as' [is added]. And thus, since the 'as many' absences of contact with untouchable things do not exist there through the relation of undelimited qualifier-hood, the stated defect does not arise — this is the purport. And where the conjunction with ash and the contact with an untouchable object arise and perish simultaneously in the bronze vessel, there, taking the destruction of the conjunction with ash qualified by the pseudo-co-location of the respective absences of untouchable-contact, the unwanted consequence of purity [would arise]; hence the qualifier of the absence [includes] 'contemporaneous with,' meaning 'existing at the time delimited by the moment of the conjunction with ash.' And thus, since the 'as many' absences [of untouchable contact] do not exist as delimited by the moment of the conjunction with ash, there is no defect — this is the purport.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
atha prokṣaṇādibhiḥ
vrīhyādiṣu bhasmādinā kāṃsyādiṣu ādheyā śaktirnirākriyate 'nanu
bhasmādinā' ityādinā dīpikāyām/ sahajaśaktiḥ ādheyaśaktiśceti
śaktidvayasya mīmāṃsakairaṅgīkārāt/ prathamenādipadenāmlāderiti/
children.translated_text: Now, the superimposed capacity in rice and the like through sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and the like, and in bronze and the like through ash and the like, is refuted in the <s>Dīpikā</s> with 'but with ash' and so forth. For the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> accept two kinds of capacity: innate capacity (<s>sahajaśakti</s>) and superimposed capacity (<s>ādheyaśakti</s>). 'By the first word "and the like," sour substances and the like [are included]' —

children.text:
bhasmanā śudhyate
kāṃsyaṃ tāmramāmlena śudhyati/
children.translated_text: 'Bronze is purified by ash, copper is purified by sour [substances],

children.text:
gomayāt śudhyate
bhūmiḥ nārī tu rajasā tathā//'
children.translated_text: the earth is purified by cow-dung, and a woman likewise by her menstrual flow.'

children.text:
iti
vacanamatrānusaṃhitam/ dīpikāyām bhasmādisaṃyogeti/
bhasmādisaṃyogasamānakālīnāḥ yāvantaḥ
aspṛśyasparśapratiyogikābhāvāḥ tatsamudāyaviśiṣṭa
bhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsa eva kāṃsyādeḥ śuddhirityarthaḥ/ yatra kāṃsyādau
ādau aspṛśyavastusaṃyogaḥ tataḥ bhasmādisaṃyogaḥ tataḥ
bhasmādisaṃyoganāśānantaraṃ punaraspṛśyavasatusparśaḥ/ tatkāle
pūrvatanabhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsasattvāt bhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsamātrasya
śuddhipadārthatve tadānīmapi śuddhatvāpattiḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
children.translated_text: This scriptural passage is referred to here. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'the conjunction with ash' and so forth — the meaning is: the purity of bronze and the like consists precisely in the destruction of the conjunction with ash and the like, qualified by the aggregate of all absences whose counter-positives are contacts with untouchables that are contemporaneous with the conjunction with ash. Where in bronze and the like, first there is conjunction with an untouchable object, then conjunction with ash and the like, then after the destruction of the conjunction with ash, again contact with an untouchable object — at that time, since the destruction of the earlier conjunction with ash exists, if the mere destruction of the conjunction with ash were the referent of 'purity,' there would be the unwanted consequence of purity even then. To prevent that,

children.text:
sahitāntaṃ
bhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃse viśeṣaṇam/ aspṛśyasparśakāle
aspṛśyasparśapatiyogikābhāvaviśiṣṭatvaṃ nāstīti na doṣaḥ/
sāhityaṃ ca atra svarūpasaṃbandhaghaṭitasāmānādhikaraṇyarūpam/ ataḥ
vyadhikaraṇaṃ kālikādisambandhena sāmānādhikaraṇaṃ vā
aspṛśyasparśapratiyogikābhāvamādāya tādṛśasparśakāle śuddhatvāpattiḥ
na bhavati/ kāṃsyādau yatkiñcidaspṛśyavastusparśakāle 'pi
aspṛśyavastvantarasaṃyogābhāvasattvāt tadviśiṣṭaḥ
pūrvatanabhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃso 'stīti śuddhatvāpattiḥ/ ataḥ
yāvattvaniveśaḥ/ tadānīṃ yāvadabhāvāntargatasya
yādṛśāspṛśyavastusparśo 'sti tadabhāvasya asattvāt na doṣaḥ/ na
cābhāve yāvattvaniveśāpekṣayā aspṛśyavastusparśattvāvacchinnābhāva eva
niveśyatāmiti vācyam/ vijātīyeṣvanekeṣu
aspṛśyavastuṣvanugatadharmasyābhāvāt pratiyogitāvacchedakasya
sāmānyadharmasyātrāsambhavāt/ saṃyogasyāvyāpyavṛttitayā
kāṃsyādāvaspṛśyavastusaṃyogakāle 'pi kiñcidavacchedena tadabhāvasya
daiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhena sattvāt tadviśiṣṭaṃ
pūrvakālīnabhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsamādāya śuddhatvāpattivāraṇāya
sāmānādhikaraṇyaghaṭakādheyatāya
niravacchinnadaiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsambandhāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśyam/ yatra
children.translated_text: the qualifier of the destruction of the conjunction with ash ends with 'accompanied by.' At the time of contact with the untouchable, since the qualification by the absence of the counter-positive of untouchable-contact does not exist, there is no defect. The accompaniment here has the form of co-location constituted by the self-linking relation (<s>svarūpasambandha</s>). Hence, by taking the absence of the counter-positive of untouchable-contact that is in a different locus, or in co-location through a temporal or other relation, the unwanted consequence of purity at the time of such contact does not arise. In bronze and the like, even at the time of contact with some particular untouchable object, since the absence of conjunction with another untouchable object exists, the earlier destruction of the conjunction with ash qualified by that [absence] exists — hence the unwanted consequence of purity. Therefore the inclusion of 'as many as.' At that time, since the absence of whichever kind of untouchable-contact exists is included among the 'as many' absences, there is no defect. Nor should one say that instead of including 'as many as' in the absence, let the absence delimited by untouchable-contact-hood be included — because there is no common property pervading the diverse untouchable objects. Since conjunction is a non-pervasive occurrence, even at the time of untouchable-contact in bronze and the like, the absence of that [contact] delimited by some portion exists through the relation of spatial qualification; to prevent the unwanted consequence of purity by taking the earlier destruction of the conjunction with ash qualified by that, the relation delimiting the superimposed-ness constituting the co-location component must be specified as undelimited spatial qualification relation. Where

children.text:
kāṃsyādipātre
bhasamādisaṃyogaḥ aspṛśyasparśaśca ekakāle utpannau vinaṣṭau ca tatra
bhasamādisaṃyogadhvaṃsaḥ aspṛśyasparśābhāvaviśiṣṭo bhavatīti pātrasya
tadvataḥ śuddhatvāpattivāraṇāya aspṛśyasparśapratiyogikābhāve
bhasmādisaṃyogasamānakālīnatvaviśeṣaṇam/
bhasmādisaṃyogāvacchedakakṣaṇāvacchedena bhasmādisaṃyogādhikaraṇe
vidyamāna iti tadarthaḥ/ evaṃ ca tatra vidyamānasya aspṛśyasparśābhāvasya
bhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsakālikatve 'pi bhasmādisaṃyogakṣaṇāvacchedena
vidyamānatvaṃ nāstīti na doṣaḥ/ evaṃ ca
bhasmādisaṃyogāvacchedakakṣaṇāvacchinnatadadhikaraṇavṛttikāspṛśyaspaśarpratiyogikayāvadabhāvaniṣṭhaniravacchinna-
daiśikaviśeṣaṇatāsaṃbandhāvacchinnādheyatāniyapitādhikaraṇatāvadvṛtti -
bhasmādisaṃyogadhvaṃsa śuddhiriti phalitam/ tadāha - yatra
kāṃsyādāvityādinā/ saṃbandhaviśeṣaniyantritamiti/
niravacchinnadaiśikāviśeṣaṇa tāsambandhaghaṭitamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: in a bronze vessel, the conjunction with ash and the contact with an untouchable arise and perish at the same time — there, the destruction of the conjunction with ash is qualified by the absence of the counter-positive of untouchable-contact, and hence there would be the unwanted consequence that the vessel possessing that is pure. To prevent this, the absence of the counter-positive of untouchable-contact is qualified as 'contemporaneous with the conjunction with ash.' Its meaning is: existing in the locus of the conjunction with ash as delimited by the moment that delimits the conjunction with ash. And thus, even though the absence of untouchable-contact existing there has the property of being contemporaneous with the destruction of the conjunction with ash, since it does not have the property of existing as delimited by the moment of the conjunction with ash, there is no defect. And thus the upshot is: purity consists in the destruction of the conjunction with ash, which has as its locus what possesses the container-hood delimited by the non-pervasive spatial-qualification relation constituting the superimposed-ness governed by the aggregate-co-location of as-many absences whose counter-positives are untouchable-contacts, occurring in the locus of the conjunction with ash delimited by the moment delimiting the conjunction with ash. He states this with 'where in bronze and the like' and so forth. 'Governed by a specific relation' — the meaning is: constituted by the undelimited spatial-qualification relation.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: svatvasyātiriktapadārthatvakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of Ownership (<s>Svatva</s>) as a Separate Category

children.text:
svatvamapi na
padārthāntaram, yatheṣṭaviniyogayogyatvasya svatvarūpatvāt/
tadavacchedakaṃ ca pratigrahādilabdhatvameveti/
children.translated_text: Ownership (<s>svatva</s>) too is not a separate category, since the fitness for disposal as one wishes constitutes the nature of ownership. And the delimitor of that is simply the property of having been obtained through gift (<s>pratigraha</s>) and the like.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
'caitrasya idaṃ
dhanam' ityādau dhanādau yatsvatvaṃ pratīyate tatpadārthāntaramiti
mataṃ nirasyati - svatvamapīti/ apinā anuktasamuccānayakena
pratiyogitvādiparigrahaḥ/ nanu tarhi svatvaṃ kiṃsvarūpam ityata āha
- yatheṣṭeti/ tadavacchedakaṃ ceti/ tādṛśayogyatvaprayojakamityarthaḥ/
pratiyogitvaṃ pratiyogirūpaṃ pratiyogitāvacchedakarūpaṃ vetyādikaṃ
bahutaramūhanīyam/
children.translated_text: He refutes the view that the ownership perceived in cases such as 'this is <s>Caitra</s>'s wealth' is a separate category — with '<s>svatva</s> too.' By the word 'too,' through the unmentioned-inclusion-conjunction, counter-positive-hood and the like are included. Now then, if ownership is not a separate category, what is its nature? — to this he says: 'as one wishes.' 'And the delimitor of that' — the meaning is: that which brings about such fitness. Whether counter-positive-hood has the form of the counter-positive itself or the form of the delimitor of counter-positive-hood — such matters and more should be extensively reflected upon.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
yatsvatvaṃ pratīyata
iti/ ṣaṣṭhyeti śeṣaḥ/ tatpadārthantaramiti/ svatvaṃ na dravyātmakam
guṇādivṛttitvāt/ ata eva na guṇakarmānyatarātmakam/ na ca
sāmānyādirūpam, nityatvaprasaṅgāt/ mama svatvaṃ utpannam, tava
svatvaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ ityādi pratītyā svatvasyānityatvāvagamena
iṣṭāpatteḥ kartumaśakyatvāt/ nāpyabhāvātmakam, bhāvatvena
pratīyamānatvāt/ ataḥ kḷptapadārthānantarbhūtatvāt svatvaṃ
padārthāntaramiti pūrvapakṣaḥ/ yatheṣṭaviniyogayogyatāniyāmakaṃ
pratigrahādinā labdhatvameva svatvam/ tacca saṃyogādirūpam,
nātiriktapadārtha iti siddhāntaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The ownership that is perceived' — supply: 'through the sixth case [genitive].' 'That is a separate category' — ownership is not of the nature of substance, because it occurs in qualities and the like. For this very reason, it is not of the nature of either quality or action. Nor is it of the nature of universal and the like, because there would be the unwanted consequence of eternality. Since the experience 'my ownership has arisen,' 'your ownership has perished' and the like reveals the non-eternality of ownership, the desired conclusion [of eternality] cannot be maintained. Nor is it of the nature of absence, because it is experienced as a positive entity. Therefore, since it is not included among the established categories, the prima facie view is that ownership is a separate category. The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is: ownership is simply the property of having been obtained through gift and the like, which determines the fitness for disposal as one wishes; and that has the form of conjunction and the like, not a separate category.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: vidhivādaḥ
children.translated_text: The Doctrine of Injunction (<s>Vidhi</s>)

children.text:
atha vidhiḥ nirūpyate --
prayatnajanakacikīrṣājanakajñānaviṣayo vidhiḥ/ tatpratipādakaḥ
liṅādirvā/ kṛtyasādhye pravṛttyadarśanāt-kṛtisādhye
pravṛttidarśanāt kṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ pravartakam/ na ca viṣabhakṣaṇādau
pravṛttiprasaṅgaḥ, iṣṭasādhanatāliṅgakakṛtisādhyatājñānasya
kāmyasthale vihitakālaśucijīvitvanimittajñānajanyasya
nityanaimittikasthale pravartakatvāt/ na cānanugamaḥ,
svaviśeṣaṇavattāpratisandhānajanyatvasyānugatatvāditi guravaḥ/ tanna -
children.translated_text: Now injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) is examined. An injunction is: the content of a cognition that generates the desire to act (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) which generates effort (<s>prayatna</s>). Or alternatively, it is the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) and the like that convey that [content]. Since activity is not observed when [something is understood as] accomplishable by action [alone without desire], and since activity is observed when [something is understood as] accomplishable by effort, the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort is the motivator. Nor is there the unwanted consequence of activity in cases such as eating poison, because in the case of desired [rituals], the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort that is inferential — based on the inferential mark of being a means to what is desired — is the motivator; and in the case of obligatory and occasional [rituals], the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort that is generated by the knowledge of [conditions such as] the prescribed time, purity, and being alive is the motivator. Nor is there a lack of common thread, because the common element is being generated by the awareness of possessing one's own qualifier — thus say the teachers. That is not correct —

children.text:
lāghavena
kṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanatājñānasyaiva cikīrṣādvārā prayatnajanakatvāt/ na
ca nityanaimittikasthale
children.translated_text: because, by the principle of parsimony, the cognition of being-a-means-to-what-is-desired-and-accomplishable-by-effort alone generates effort through the intermediary of the desire to act. Nor is there the unwanted consequence of non-activity in the case of obligatory and occasional [rituals]

children.text:
iṣṭasādhanatvābhāvāt apravṛttiprasaṅgaḥ, tatrāpi
pratyavāyaparihārasya pāpakṣayasya ca phalatvakalpanāt/ tasmāt
kṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanatvameva liṅādyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: due to the absence of being a means to what is desired — because even there, the avoidance of adverse consequences (<s>pratyavāya</s>) and the diminution of sin are postulated as the results. Therefore, being-a-means-to-what-is-desired-and-accomplishable-by-effort is itself the meaning of the optative suffix and the like.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
sarveṣāṃ
padārthānāṃ uktapadārtheṣu yathāyathamantarbhāvaṃ nirūpya mūlanyūnatāṃ
parihartuṃ vidhiṃ nirūpayiṣyamāṇaḥ śiṣyāvadhānāya tannirūpaṇaṃ
pratijānīte -- atheti/ svaparamatasādhāraṇaṃ vidhitvaṃ tāvat nirvakti
- prayatneti/ prayatnajanikā yā cikīrṣā tajjanakaṃ yajjñānaṃ tadviṣaya
ityarthaḥ/ gurumate kṛtisādhyatājñānasya, svamate
kṛtisādhyatvaviśiṣṭeṣṭasādhanatājñānasya cikīrṣādvārā
prayatnajanakatvāt tanmate kṛtisādhyatve svamate
kṛtisādhyatvaviśiṣṭesādhanatve ca lakṣaṇasaṅgatiḥ/ abhidhāyakasya
vidhimatābhiproyaṇāha - tatpratīti/
tādṛśajñānaviṣayakāryatvādipratipādakaliṅādirityarthaḥ/
liṅādirityādinā loṭtavyādisaṅgrahaḥ/ vākāro 'nāsthāyām/
gurumatamāśaṅkate -- kṛtyasādhya iti/ kṛtyasādhyatvenāvagata
ityarthaḥ/ pravartakamiti/ cikīrṣādvārā pravṛttijanakamityarthaḥ/ na ca
kṛtyasādhyatvajñānābhāva eva pravartako 'stviti śaṅkyam,
kṛtyasādhyatvajñānābhāvatvena tattve gauravāt/
kṛtisādhyatvābhāvakṛtisādhyabhedatattadvyāpyādidarśanānāṃ pravṛttau
pratibandhakatvakalpanena mahāgauravācca iti dik/
children.translated_text: Having examined the inclusion of all categories under the previously stated categories as appropriate, wishing to remedy the deficiency of the root text [by covering what remains], and about to examine injunction, he announces that examination to focus the student's attention — with 'now.' He first states the definition of injunction-hood that is common to both his own and the opponent's views — with 'effort' and so forth. The meaning is: that which is the content of a cognition that generates the desire to act (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) which generates effort. In the teacher's view, the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort is the motivator through the desire to act; in his own view, the cognition of being-a-means-to-what-is-desired qualified by accomplishability-by-effort is the motivator through the desire to act. Thus in the teacher's view, the definition fits accomplishability-by-effort, and in his own view, it fits being-a-means-to-what-is-desired qualified by accomplishability-by-effort. He states the view of those who consider the denoter [rather than the denoted] as the injunction — with 'that which conveys.' The meaning is: the optative suffix and the like that convey the object-hood, result-hood, and the like of the content of such cognition. By 'the optative and the like,' the imperative (<s>loṭ</s>), the potential suffix (<s>tavya</s>), and the like are included. The particle 'vā' (or) indicates non-commitment. He raises the teacher's view as an objection — with 'accomplishable by action' and so forth. The meaning is: understood as accomplishable by effort. 'Is the motivator' — the meaning is: it generates activity through the intermediary of desire. Nor should one object that the mere absence of the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort should be the motivator — because that would involve the cumbersomeness of that having the nature of the absence of the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort. And because of the great cumbersomeness of postulating that the perception of the absence of accomplishability-by-effort, the perception of difference from what is accomplishable by effort, and the perception of what is pervaded by those, are obstructors of activity — this is the general direction.

children.text:
nanu viṣabhakṣaṇādau
pravṛttyāpattiḥ/ kṛtisādhyatājñānasya tatrāpi sattvādityāśaṅkāṃ
nirācaṣṭe -- na cetyādinā/ iṣṭasādhanatāliṅgaketi/ 'ayam
matkṛtisādhyaḥ, matkṛtiṃ vinā anupapadyamānatve sati
madiṣṭasādhanatvāt' ityānumāniketyarthaḥ/ kāmyasthala iti/
pravartakatvādityanenānvayaḥ/ jyotiṣṭomayāgādāvityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: But there would be the unwanted consequence of activity in cases such as eating poison — since the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort exists even there. He resolves this doubt with 'nor' and so forth. 'Based on the inferential mark of being a means to what is desired' — the meaning is: [this cognition is] inferential, of the form 'this is accomplishable by my effort, because it is a means to what I desire, given that it cannot be accomplished without my effort.' 'In the case of desired [rituals]' — this connects with 'is the motivator' and so forth. The meaning is: in the case of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice and the like.

children.text:
vihitakāletyādi/
vihitakālaśucitīvitvajñānādhīnasya kṛtisādhyatājñānasya nitye
sandhyāvandanādau, āśaucādirūpanimittajñānādhīnasya tasya naimittike
snānādau pravartakatvādityarthaḥ/ 'aham
etatkālikakṛtisādhyasandhyāvandanakaḥ, etatkālikaśucijīvitvāt'
ityevaṃrītyā kṛtisādhyatvajñānasya
vihitakālaśucijīvitvādijñānajanyatvamavaseyam/
children.translated_text: 'The prescribed time' and so forth — the meaning is: in the case of obligatory [rites] such as the <s>sandhyāvandana</s> (twilight worship), the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort that depends on the knowledge of the prescribed time, purity, and being alive is the motivator; and in the case of occasional [rites] such as bathing [after impurity], the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort that depends on the knowledge of the occasion in the form of impurity (<s>āśauca</s>) and the like is the motivator. The dependence of the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort on the knowledge of the prescribed time, purity of life, and the like should be understood in this manner: through an inference of the form 'I am one who must perform the <s>sandhyāvandana</s> accomplishable at this time by my effort, because of my purity and being alive at this time.'

children.text:
ananugama iti/
pravṛttisāmānyaprayojakasya ekasyābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/
svaviśeṣaṇavattevyādi/ svaṃ pravartamānapuruṣaḥ, tasya viśeṣaṇaṃ
tanniṣṭho dharmaḥ kāmanādiḥ, tadvattāyāḥ svaviṣayasādhanatvādirūpasya
tatsambandhasya pratisandhānaṃ jñānaṃ tajjanyatvasyetyarthaḥ/ lāghaveneti/
kāraṇatāvacchedakalāghavenetyarthaḥ/ tanmate kāraṇatāvacchedakasya
janyatvādighaṭitatvāt gauravamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'There is no uniformity' — the purport is: because there is no single [property] that is the common instigator of activity in general. 'The possession by oneself of the qualifier' and so forth — 'oneself' is the person who is acting; his qualifier is the property residing in him, such as desire and the like; the meaning is: being produced by the cognition that is the apprehension of the relation, which has the form of being a means to the object of that [desire], of the possession of that [qualifier]. 'By parsimony' — the meaning is: by the parsimony of the delimitor of the condition of being a cause. The purport is: in that view, since the delimitor of the condition of being a cause is constituted by being-produced-by and the like, there is prolixity.

children.text:
kṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanateti/ tatra
balabadaniṣṭānanubandhitvamapyantarbhāvanīyam/ tena na kṛtisādhyatvena
tṛptirūpeṣṭasādhatvena cāvagate viṣasaṃpṛkte bhojanādau
pravṛttyāpattiḥ/ viśiṣṭajñānatvāvacchinnasya kāraṇatvakathanaṃ tu prācāṃ
matena/ navyamate kṛtisādhyatvādijñānānāṃ pṛthageva
daṇḍacakrādinyāyenana kāraṇatvāt/ prayatneti/ pravṛttītyarthaḥ/
pratyavāyeti/ pratyavāyasya parihāraḥ prāgabhāvaḥ, tasya
duḥkhajanakābhāvatayā tannāśasyaiva iṣṭatvena phalatvamiti bhāvaḥ/ na ca
kathaṃ tatprāgabhāvasya phalatvaṃ tasyājanyatvāditi vācyam; yatsattve
yatsattvamiti vyavahāralabhyasya svarūpasaṃbandharūpasya
sandhyāvandanaprayojyatvasya tatra sattvena phalatvākṣaterityavadheyam/
children.translated_text: 'Being a means to what is desired and accomplishable by effort (<s>kṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanatā</s>)' — therein, the property of not being accompanied by a predominant undesirable [consequence] should also be included. Therefore, there is no unwanted consequence of activity toward food and the like that is mixed with poison, even though it is cognized as accomplishable by effort and as a means to the desired [end] in the form of satisfaction. The statement that the causality is delimited by the property of being a qualified cognition follows the old view. According to the new view, the cognitions of accomplishability-by-effort and the like are each independently causes, by the maxim of the stick and the wheel. 'Effort' — the meaning is: activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>). 'Regarding <s>pratyavāya</s> (sin of omission)' — the avoidance of <s>pratyavāya</s> is its prior absence; since that has the nature of being the absence of what produces suffering, only its destruction has the status of a result because it is desired — this is the purport. Nor should one say: how can that prior absence have the status of a result, since it is not producible? It should be noted that, since the property of being occasioned by the <s>sandhyāvandana</s> (twilight prayer), which has the form of the intrinsic relation obtainable through the convention 'when this exists, that exists,' is present there, the status of being a result is unimpaired.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
mūlanyūnatāṃ
parihartumiti/ na ca vidhyanirūpaṇena kathaṃ mūlasya nyūnatā, saptānāṃ
ṣoḍaśānāṃ vā padārthānāṃ nirūpaṇenaiva 'kriyate tarkasaṃgrahaḥ' iti
pratijñāyāḥ nirūḍhatvāditi vācyam/ sarvaprameyasaṃgrāhake 'tra
maṇyādigrantheṣu vistareṇa nirūpitasya vidheranirūpaṇe
nyūnataivetyāśayāt/ prayatnajaniketyādi/ pravṛttirūpaprayatnaṃ prati
'idaṃ kuryām' ityākārikā cikīrṣā kāraṇam/ cikīrṣāṃ prati
gurumate 'idaṃ matkṛtisādhyam' ityākārakaṃ kṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ
kāraṇam/ naiyāyikamate 'idaṃ matkṛtisādhyatve sati
madiṣṭasādhanam' ityākārakaṃ jñānaṃ kāraṇam, tadviṣayatvaṃ
kṛtisādhyatve, kṛtisādhyatvaviśiṣṭeṣṭasādhanatve cāstīti
vidhilakṣaṇasya tayoḥ samanvaya ityarthaḥ/ abhidhāyakasyeti/
vidhivācakasya liṅāderapi vidhiśabdavācyatvamiti
matābhiprāyeṇetyarthaḥ/ tathā ca vātsyāyanabhāṣyam --"yadvākyaṃ vidhāyakaṃ codakaṃ sa vidhiḥ" [nyāṇsū-2-9-63] iti"yadvākyaṃ vidhāyakaṃ deśakaṃ sa
vidhiḥ"iti tatra vārtikam/ vākāro 'nāsthāyāmiti/
vidhinimantraṇetyādipāṇinisūtrasvārasyāt liṅādyabhidheye eva
vidhiśabdaḥ pravartate, na
children.translated_text: 'In order to remedy the deficiency of the root text' — nor should one say: how is the root text deficient by the non-determination of <s>vidhi</s> (injunction), since the promise 'the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> is composed' is fulfilled by the determination of merely seven or sixteen categories? Because the intent is that in the absence of the determination of <s>vidhi</s>, which is elaborately determined in comprehensive treatises such as the <s>Maṇi</s> (Tattvacintāmaṇi) and others, there is indeed a deficiency. 'Generated by effort' and so forth — desire (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) of the form 'I should do this' is the cause of effort in the form of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>). According to the teacher's (<s>Guru</s>) view, cognition of accomplishability-by-effort (<s>kṛtisādhyatājñāna</s>) of the form 'this is accomplishable by my effort' is the cause of desire. According to the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, the cognition of the form 'this is a means to what I desire, while being accomplishable by my effort' is the cause; since the content of that cognition includes both accomplishability-by-effort and being-a-means-to-the-desired-qualified-by-accomplishability-by-effort, the coordination of these two with the definition of <s>vidhi</s> [is established] — this is the meaning. 'Of the expressor' — the meaning is: according to the view that even the verbal suffix <s>liṅ</s> and the like, which express injunction, are denoted by the word <s>vidhi</s>. And thus the <s>Vātsyāyana-bhāṣya</s> [states]: 'That sentence which enjoins, which impels, is <s>vidhi</s>' [Nyāyasūtra 2.9.63]; and the <s>Vārtika</s> thereon [states]: 'That sentence which enjoins, which instructs, is <s>vidhi</s>.' 'The letter va indicates non-insistence' —

children.text:
tvabhidhāyake
ityavagamāt iti bhāvaḥ/ 'nanu kṛtyasādhye pravṛttyadarśanāt'
iti dīpikoktamayuktam/ kṛtyasādhye 'pi kṛtisādhyatābhrameṇa
pravṛttidarśanādityata āha -- kṛtyasādhyatvenāvagata ityartha iti/
kṛtyasādhye kṛtisādhyatvabhramāt pravṛttāvapi kṛtyasādhyatvajñāne sati
na pravṛttiḥ ataḥ nāsaṅgatiriti bhāvaḥ/ nanu pravṛttiṃ prati cikīrṣāyā
eva kāraṇatvāt kṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ pravartakamiti na saṅgatamityata
āha -- cikīrṣādvārā pravṛttijanakamityartha iti/ na ca
kṛtyasādhyatveti/ kṛtyasādhyatvajñānakāle pravṛttivāraṇāya hi
kṛtisādhyatājñānasya pravṛttihetutvamuktam/ pravṛttiṃ prati
kṛtyasādhtājñānābhāvaḥ kāraṇamityuktyaiva kṛtyasādhyatvajñānakāle
pravṛttivariyituṃ śakyate/ na ca lāghavānavakāśa iti vācyam/
pratibandhakābhāvasya kāryasāmānye kāraṇatāyāḥ kḷptatvāt
kṛtyasādhyatājñānābhāvasya kāraṇatvaṃ na kalpanīyam iti lāghavam,
kṛtisādhyatājñānasya tu akḷptaṃ kāraṇatvaṃ kalpanīyam iti
gauravamiti śaṅkiturāśayāt/ samādhatte --
kṛtyasādhyatājñānābhāvatveneti/ kṛtisādhyatājñānatvāpekṣayā
kṛtyasādhyatājñānābhāvatvasya kāraṇatāvacchedakasya gurutvādityarthaḥ/
kṛtisādhyatvābhāveti/ pravṛttiṃ prati kṛtisādhyatvābhāvajñānasya
kṛtisādhyabhedajñānasya kṛtisādhyatvābhāvavyāpyavattājñānasya
kṛtisādhyabhedavyāpyavattājñānasya ca pratibandhakatvāt teṣāṃ ye 'bhāvāḥ
teṣāṃ api kāraṇatvaṃ vaktavyamiti mahāgauravam/ tadapekṣayā
kṛtisādhyatājñānasyaikasya kāraṇatve lāghavamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: because from the natural import of <s>Pāṇini</s>'s sūtra '<s>vidhinimantraṇa</s>' and so forth, the word <s>vidhi</s> applies only to what is expressed [by <s>liṅ</s> and the like], not to the expressor — this is the purport. 'Now, the statement in the <s>Dīpikā</s> that activity is not observed toward what is accomplishable by [another's] effort is improper' — since even toward what is accomplishable by another's effort, activity is observed due to the erroneous cognition that it is accomplishable by one's own effort — therefore [the commentator] says: 'the meaning is: cognized as accomplishable by [another's] effort.' The purport is: when there is cognition of accomplishability-by-another's-effort [alone, without the error of taking it as one's own], there is no activity; hence there is no incongruity. Now, since desire (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) alone is the cause of activity, it is not proper [to say] that cognition of accomplishability-by-effort is the instigator — therefore [the commentator] says: 'the meaning is: it produces activity through the intermediary of desire.' 'Nor [can one say] accomplishability-by-another's-effort [cognition blocks activity]' — for the causal role of cognition of accomplishability-by-one's-own-effort in producing activity was stated in order to block activity at the time of cognition of accomplishability-by-another's-effort. [The objector says:] by merely stating that the absence of cognition of accomplishability-by-another's-effort is a cause of activity, one can block activity at the time of cognition of accomplishability-by-another's-effort. Nor should one say there is no scope for parsimony; because since the causality of the absence of an obstructor with respect to the effect in general is already established, the causality of the absence of cognition of accomplishability-by-another's-effort need not be postulated — this is parsimony; whereas the causality of cognition of accomplishability-by-one's-own-effort, being unestablished, would need to be postulated — this is prolixity — such is the intent of the objector. [The commentator] resolves this: 'as the absence of cognition of accomplishability-by-another's-effort' — the meaning is: because the delimitor of the condition of being a cause, namely the property of being the absence of cognition of accomplishability-by-another's-effort, is more prolix than the property of being cognition of accomplishability-by-one's-own-effort. 'The absence of accomplishability-by-one's-own-effort' — since the cognition of the absence of accomplishability-by-one's-own-effort, the cognition of difference from what is accomplishable-by-one's-own-effort, the cognition of the possession of what pervades the absence of accomplishability-by-one's-own-effort, and the cognition of the possession of what pervades the difference from what is accomplishable-by-one's-own-effort are all obstructors of activity, the absences of all these too would have to be stated as causes — this is great prolixity. In comparison with that, the causality of the single [factor], namely cognition of accomplishability-by-one's-own-effort, involves parsimony — this is the purport.

children.text:
dīpikāyām
iṣṭasādhanatāliṅgaketyādi/ kāmyakarmasu pravṛttiṃ prati
iṣṭasādhanatvaliṅgakakṛtisādhyatvavidheyakānumityātmakaṃ
kṛtisādhyatvajñānaṃ hetuḥ/ 'idava jyotiṣṭomādirūpaṃ kāmyakarma
matkṛtisādhyam matkṛtiṃ vinā asattve sati madiṣṭasādhanatvāt
yannaivaṃ tannaivaṃ yathā caityavandanam' ityanumānaṃ draṣṭavyam/
sandhyāvandanādinityanaimittikakarmasu pravṛttiṃ prati
nimittarūpaliṅgajñānajanyakṛtisādhtvavidheyakānumityātmakaṃ
kṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ kāraṇam/ vihitakāle śucitve sati jīvitvaṃ
sandhyāvandanādinityakarmasu nimittam/ snānādirūpanaimittikakarmasu
aśucittve sati jīvitvaṃ nimittam/ tathā ca tatra 'aham
idānīntanakṛtisādhyasandhyāvandanakaḥ etatkāle śucitve sati
jīvitvāt yo naivam sa naivam yathā bauddhaḥ', 'aham
etatkālikakṛtisādhyasnānakaḥ etatkāle aśucitve sati jīvitvāt
yo naivaṃ sa naivaṃ yathā nāstikaḥ ityanumānaṃ pravartate/ na ca
kvacit iṣṭasādhanatāliṅgakakṛtisādhyatājñānasya
kvacidvihitakālikaśucijīvitvādiliṅgakakṛtisāṃdhyatājñānasya ca
pravṛttihetutve tayoḥ parasparaṃ vināpi pravṛtterjāyamānatayā
vyatirekavyabhicārāt pravṛttisāmānyaṃ prati kṛtisādhyatājñānasya
hetutvaṃ na sambhavati, abhayasādhāraṇasyaikasya
kāraṇatāvacchedakadharmasyābhāvāditi vācyam/
svaviśeṣaṇavattājñānajanyatvasyānugatasya kāraṇatāvacchedakasya
sadbhāvāt/ svaṃ pravartamānaḥ puruṣaḥ tasya viśeṣaṇaṃ tadvṛttidharmaḥ
phalakāmanā tadvattvaṃ tadviṣayaphalasādhanatvarūpaḥ tatsambandhaḥ tajjñānaṃ
'kāmyaṃ iṣṭasādhanam' ityākārakaṃ tajjanyatvaṃ
iṣṭasādhanatāliṅgakakṛtisādhyatājñona, evaṃ svaṃ pravartamānapuruṣaḥ
tadviśeṣaṇa vihitakālikaśucitvaviśiṣṭajīvitvam
aśucitvaviśiṣṭajīvitvaṃ ca tadvattājñānaṃ 'tādṛśadharmavānaham'
ityākārakajñānaṃ tajjanyatvaṃ sandhyā
vandanasnānādinityanaimittikakarmaviśeṣyakakṛtisādhyatājñāne
nimittaliṅgakānumityātmake 'stīti
svaviśeṣaṇavattājñānajanyatvasyānugatakāraṇatāvacchedakatvamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'having the property of being a means to the desired as the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>)' and so forth — the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort (<s>kṛtisādhyatājñāna</s>) that is the cause of activity toward optional rituals (<s>kāmyakarma</s>) is an inference having the property of being a means to the desired as its inferential mark and accomplishability-by-effort as its probandum. The inference to be seen is: 'This optional ritual in the form of <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like is accomplishable by my effort — because, given that it cannot exist without my effort, it is a means to what I desire — whatever is not so is not so, like the reverencing of a <s>caitya</s> (Buddhist shrine).' The cognition of accomplishability-by-effort that is the cause of activity toward obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) and occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) rites such as <s>sandhyāvandana</s> (twilight prayer) is an inference having the cognition of the occasion as its inferential mark and accomplishability-by-effort as its probandum. For obligatory rites such as <s>sandhyāvandana</s>, the occasion is being alive when ritually pure at the prescribed time. For occasional rites such as bathing, the occasion is being alive when ritually impure. And thus the inferences that operate there are: 'I am one who should perform <s>sandhyāvandana</s> accomplishable by my present effort — because of being alive when ritually pure at the prescribed time — whoever is not so is not so, like a Buddhist'; 'I am one who should perform bathing accomplishable by my present effort — because of being alive when ritually impure at the prescribed time — whoever is not so is not so, like a nihilist.'
