Nor should one say that if the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort having the property of being a means to the desired as its inferential mark is the cause of activity in some cases, and the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort having cognition of being alive when ritually pure at the prescribed time as its inferential mark is the cause in other cases, then since each can produce activity without the other, there is deviation in the negative concomitance, and therefore the causality of cognition of accomplishability-by-effort with respect to activity in general is not possible, because there is no single delimitor of the condition of being a cause that is common to both — because the common delimitor of the condition of being a cause, namely the property of being produced by the cognition of the possession by oneself of the qualifier, does exist. 'Oneself' is the person who is acting; his qualifier is the property residing in him — desire for the result; the possession of that; the relation of that [possession] which has the form of being a means to the result that is its object; the cognition of that — the cognition of the form 'this optional rite is a means to what I desire'; being produced by that is [the common delimitor] in the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort having the property of being a means to the desired as its inferential mark. Similarly, 'oneself' is the person acting; his qualifier is being alive qualified by ritual purity at the prescribed time, or being alive qualified by ritual impurity; the cognition of the possession of that — the cognition of the form 'I possess such a property'; being produced by that is present in the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort regarding specific obligatory and occasional rites such as <s>sandhyāvandana</s> and bathing, which is an inference having the occasion as its inferential mark — thus the property of being produced by the cognition of the possession by oneself of the qualifier is the common delimitor of the condition of being a cause — this is the purport.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām ayaṃ
matkṛtisādhya ityādi/ ayam kāmyaḥ jyotiṣṭomādiḥ/ atra hetau
madiṣṭasādhanatvamātropādāne matkṛtisādhyatvarūpasādhyābhāvavati
vṛṣṭyādau madiṣṭasādhanatvarūpahetusattvāt vyabhicāraḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
satyantam/ vṛṣṭyādeḥ matkṛtiṃ vināpi sattvāt matkṛtiṃ vinā asattvaṃ
nāstīti na vyabhicāraḥ/ anupapadyamānatve sati ityasya asattve
satītyarthaḥ/ matkṛtiṃ vinetyatra matpadānupādāne madiṣṭasādhane
parakṛtapākādau matkṛtisādhyatvarūpasādhyābhāvavati kṛtiṃ vanā
anupapadyamānatve sati madiṣṭasādhanatvarūpahetusattvāt vyabhicāraḥ/
tadvāraṇāya tatra matpadam/ parakṛtapākasya matkṛtiṃ vināpi
parakīyakṛtyā upapadyamānatayā satyantābhāvāt na vyabhicāraḥ/
duḥkhaviśeṣarūpe śrame svecchādhīnakṛtisādhyatvarūpasādhyābhāvavati
matkṛtiṃ vinā asattvarūpahetusattvāt vyabhicāraḥ/ tadvāraṇāya
iṣṭasādhanatvāditi viśeṣyam/ madīyaśrame
macchatroriṣṭasādhanatvāt vyabhicāratādavasthyam/ tadvāraṇāya
madiṣṭasādhanatvāditi/ madīyaśramasya macchatrviṣṭasādhanatve 'pi
madiṣṭasādhanatvaṃ nāstīti na vyabhicāraḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'this is accomplishable by my effort' and so forth — 'this' refers to the optional <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like. Here, if in the probans only the property of being a means to what I desire is mentioned, then in rain and the like, which lack the probandum in the form of accomplishability-by-my-effort, the probans in the form of being a means to what I desire is present — hence there would be deviation. To block that, [the qualification] 'given that it cannot exist [without my effort].' Since rain and the like can exist even without my effort, the property of not being able to exist without my effort is absent — hence there is no deviation. 'Given that it cannot be accomplished otherwise' means 'given that it cannot exist [without my effort].' If in 'without my effort,' the word 'my' is not included, then in cooking performed by another, which is a means to what I desire but lacks the probandum of accomplishability-by-my-effort, since the probans in the form of being a means to what I desire is present given that it cannot be accomplished without effort [in general], there would be deviation. To block that, the word 'my' is used there. Since cooking by another can be accomplished even without my effort, through another's effort, the property of not being able to exist [without my effort] is absent — hence there is no deviation. In exertion, which is a particular form of suffering, since the probandum of accomplishability-by-effort-dependent-on-one's-own-will is absent, yet the probans in the form of not being able to exist without my effort is present, there would be deviation. To block that, the qualificand 'being a means to the desired.' [But] the situation remains the same due to deviation, since my exertion is a means to my student's desired [end]. To block that, 'being a means to what I desire.' Although my exertion is a means to my student's desired [end], the property of being a means to what I desire is absent — hence there is no deviation.

svecchādhīnatvaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ deyam/ anyathā nāntarīyakaśrame 'pi
uktahetujñānajanyakṛtisādhyatājñānasattvena taduddeśena pravṛttyāpatteḥ/
svapadaṃ yatra pravartate tatparam/ nāntarīyakaśrame tu na

vadanti/ vihitakālaśucijīvitvajñānādhīnasyeti/ vihitakālikaṃ
yat śucitvaviśiṣṭajīvitvaṃ tadviṣayakajñānajanyasyetyarthaḥ/
āśaucam/ aśucitvam/ tasya kṛtisādhyatājñānasya/
pravṛttisāmānyaprayojakasyeti/
pravṛttitvāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatāvacchedakasyetyarthaḥ/
kāraṇatāvacchedakalāghavenetyartha iti/
svaviśeṣaṇavattājñānajanyatvāpekṣayā
kṛtisādhyatvaviśiṣṭeṣṭasādhanatvajñānatvarūpasya kāraṇatāvacchedakasya
laghutvenetyarthaḥ/ laghutvamevopapādayati --- tanmata iti/ gurumata
ityarthaḥ/ janyatvādighaṭitatvādityatra ādipadena kāryatājñānatvaṃ
parāmṛśyate/ tathā hi -- svaviśeṣaṇavattājñānajanyatvamātraṃ na
pravṛttikāraṇatāvacchedakam, tādṛśajñānaviṣayakānuvyavasāyasyāpi
tajjanyatvena pravṛttiṃ prati kāraṇatvāpatteḥ/ api tu
svaviśeṣaṇavattājñānajanyakṛtisādhyatājñānatvenaiva kāraṇatvaṃ vācyam/
tatra ca niyamaghaṭitajanyatvasya kṛtisādhtājñānatvasya ca praveśāt
gauravamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Here, the qualification 'being dependent on one's own will' should be given to the effort in the probandum. Otherwise, even with respect to unavoidable exertion, since the cognition of accomplishability-by-effort produced by the stated probans would be present, there would be the unwanted consequence of activity directed toward it. The word 'own' refers to what is relevant in the given context. But with respect to unavoidable exertion, there is no cognition of accomplishability-by-effort-dependent-on-one's-own-will — hence there is no unwanted consequence of activity toward it. And thus, in the probans too, in 'without my effort,' the qualification 'dependent on one's own will' should be given to the effort. Otherwise, with respect to the unavoidable contact with water and the like, which is a means to what I desire and accomplishable by another's will rather than my own effort, there would be the unwanted consequence of deviation. Nor should one say that in this case, since in unavoidable exertion the property of not being able to exist without effort dependent on one's own will obtains, deviation can be blocked by the absence of the 'given that' condition alone, making the qualificand clause 'being a means to the desired' redundant — because this is [actually] welcome. Since this constitutes a separate probans, there is no fault — so they say. 'Dependent on the cognition of being alive when ritually pure at the prescribed time' — the meaning is: produced by the cognition whose object is being alive qualified by ritual purity at the prescribed time. '<s>Āśauca</s>' means ritual impurity. Of that cognition of accomplishability-by-effort. 'The common instigator of activity in general' — the meaning is: the delimitor of the condition of being a cause as determined by the effect-hood delimited by the property of being activity. 'By the parsimony of the delimitor of the condition of being a cause' — the meaning is: by the lightness of the delimitor of the condition of being a cause, namely the property of being cognition of accomplishability-by-effort qualified by being-a-means-to-the-desired, compared to the property of being produced by the cognition of the possession by oneself of the qualifier. [The commentator] establishes the lightness itself — 'in that view.' The meaning is: in the teacher's (<s>Guru</s>) view. In 'being constituted by being-produced-by and the like,' the word 'and the like' refers to the property of being a cognition of effect-hood. For indeed, the mere property of being produced by the cognition of the possession by oneself of the qualifier is not the delimitor of the condition of being a cause of activity, since even a subsequent reflective cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) having such a cognition as its object, being produced by it, would unwarrantedly become a cause of activity. Rather, the causality should be stated as delimited by the property of being a cognition of accomplishability-by-effort that is produced by the cognition of the possession by oneself of the qualifier. And therein, since both the property of being-produced-by constituted by a restrictive rule and the property of being a cognition of accomplishability-by-effort enter [the delimitor], there is prolixity — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu
kṛtisādhyatvaviśiṣṭeṣṭasādhanatvaprakārakajñānasya pravṛttihetutve
madhuviṣasampṛktānnabhojane 'pi idaṃ matkṛtisādhyatve sati
mattṛptirūpeṣṭasādhanamiti jñānasattvāt pravṛttyāpattirityata āha - atra
balavadaniṣṭeti/ tathā ca
children.translated_text: Now, if the cognition having as qualifier-mode 'being achievable by effort and being a means to what is desired' is the cause of activity, then even in eating food mixed with honey and poison, since the cognition 'this, when achievable by my effort, is a means to my desired satisfaction' exists, there would be the unwanted consequence of activity — to this he says: 'here, [not being a producer of] a stronger undesirable [result],' etc. And accordingly,

children.text:
balavadaniṣṭājanakatvaviśiṣṭakṛtisādhyatvaviśiṣṭeṣṭasādhanatvaprakārakajñānaṃ
pravṛttihetuḥ/ madhuviṣasampṛktānnabhojane tu tatkāle
tṛptirūpeṣṭasādhanatve 'pi kālāntare
maraṇarūpabalavadaniṣṭasādhanamitijñānasyaiva sattvena tatra na pravṛttiriti
bhāvaḥ/ balavadaniṣṭānanubandhitvaṃ nāma
iṣṭotpattināntarīyakaduḥkhādhikaduḥkhājanakatvam/
balavaddveṣaviṣayaduḥkhājanakatvaṃ vā/ nanu
balavadaniṣṭājanakatvaviśiṣṭakṛtisādhyatvaviśiṣṭesādhanatājñānasya
kāraṇatve balavadaniṣṭājanakatvādīnāṃ viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāve
vinigamanāvirahāt gurubhūtāḥ aneke kāryakāraṇabhāvāḥ prasajyanta
iti kathaṃ tatkāraṇatvaṃ dīpikākāreṇoktamityāśaṅkya
prācīnamatānusāreṇa tathoktamityāha - viśiṣṭajñānatvāvacchinnsyeti/
navyamata iti/ pūrvoktāsvārasyāt na viśiṣṭajñānatvāvacchinnasya
kāraṇatvam/ kintu balavadaniṣṭānanubandhitvajñānatvāvacchinnasya
kṛtisādhyatājñānatvāvacchinnasya iṣṭasādhanatājñānatvāvacchinnasya ca
pṛthageva kāraṇatvam/ yathā daṇḍacakrādīnāṃ ghaṭaṃ prati
daṇḍatvacaktatvādinā pṛthageva kāraṇatvam na tu
daṇḍaviśiṣṭacakratvādinā tadvaditi bhāvaḥ/niṣphale pravṛttyabhāvāt
iṣṭasādhanatājñānasyaiṣṭasādhanatvena jñāyamāne 'pi
madhuviṣasampṛktānnabhojane apravṛtteḥ balavadaniṣṭānanubandhitvajñānasya,
kṛtyasādhye sumeruśṛṅgānayanādau pravṛttyabhāvāt
kṛtisādhyatājñānasya ceti trayāṇāmapi pravṛttihetutvamāvaśyakamiti
bhāvaḥ/ nivṛttyātmakaprayatnavyāvartanāyoktam pravṛttītyartha iti/ na
hi nivṛttirūpayatnaṃ prati kṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanatājñānasya hetutvamiti
bhāvaḥ/ duḥkhajanakābhāvatayeti/
duḥkhajanakapratiyogikābhāvatayetyarthaḥ/ pratyavāyasya duḥkhajanakatayā
tadabhāvasya duḥkhajanakābhāvatvam/ svarūpasambandharūpasyeti/ siddhasya
saṃrakṣaṇarūpo yaḥ tatkāraṇatvamatra vivakṣitam/ ataḥ
pratyavāyaprāgabhāvasattārūpaḥ kṣemaḥ sandhyāvandana prayojyatvenābhimata
iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: the cognition having as qualifier-mode 'being a means to what is desired, qualified by achievability by effort, qualified by not being a producer of a stronger undesirable result' is the cause of activity. In eating food mixed with honey and poison, even though at that time it is a means to the desired satisfaction, since the cognition 'at a later time it is a means to the stronger undesirable result of death' exists, there is no activity — this is the purport. 'Not being accompanied by a stronger undesirable result' means: not being a producer of suffering greater than the suffering inseparable from the production of the desired [result]. Or: not being a producer of suffering that is the object of a stronger aversion. Now, if the causality of the cognition qualified by not-producing-a-stronger-undesirable-result, qualified by achievability-by-effort, and qualified by means-to-the-desired [is accepted], then since there is no determinate basis for the qualifier-qualificand relation among the elements like not-producing-a-stronger-undesirable-result and the like, many cumbersome causal relations would follow — how then could the author of the <s>Dīpikā</s> state that causality? Anticipating this, he says that it was stated following the ancient view — 'delimited by qualified-cognition-hood,' etc. 'On the new view' — from the natural reading of the earlier [passage], the causality is not delimited by qualified-cognition-hood. Rather, the causality of the cognition of not-being-accompanied-by-a-stronger-undesirable-result, the causality of the cognition of achievability-by-effort, and the causality of the cognition of means-to-the-desired — each is separately causal. Just as sticks, wheels, and the like are separately causal with respect to a pot through stick-ness, wheel-ness, and the like — not through stick-qualified-wheel-ness and the like — so likewise. Since there is no activity toward what is fruitless, the cognition of means-to-the-desired is [needed]; since even when known to be a means to the desired, there is no activity toward eating food mixed with honey and poison, the cognition of not-being-accompanied-by-a-stronger-undesirable-result [is needed]; and since there is no activity toward what is unachievable by effort, like bringing the peak of <s>Sumeru</s>, the cognition of achievability-by-effort [is needed] — thus all three are necessarily causes of activity. 'Activity' is said to exclude the effort of the nature of cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>). For the cognition of means-to-desired-achievable-by-effort is not a cause of the effort of the nature of cessation — this is the purport. 'As the absence of what produces suffering' — the meaning is: as the absence of the counter-positive of what produces suffering. Since <s>pratyavāya</s> (sin of omission) produces suffering, its absence, as the absence of what produces suffering,

children.translated_text: Refutation of the view that <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit) is the meaning of the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>)

Since sacrifice, being of the nature of a particular desire, perishes quickly,

kutracit śaktigrahaḥ/ yogyatābalācca aparvūrūpakāryasya śābdabodhe

vākyādiṣṭasādhanatvena yoge 'vagate
children.translated_text: He raises as an objection the teacher's view that the denotative power of the optative suffix resides in the effect — 'Now,' etc. Since sacrifice, being of the nature of a particular desire, perishes quickly,

children.text:
tasyāśutaravināśinaḥ
vyāpāraṃ vinā phalajanakatvāsambhavāt tannirvāhāya aparvūṃ kalpyata
ityāha - tannirvāhārthamiti/ nanu yāgadhvaṃsasyaiva vyāpāratvamastu
kimapūrvakalpanenetyata āha-kīrtanādineti/ ādinā
children.translated_text: since without an intermediary operation, it is impossible for [the sacrifice] which perishes quickly to produce the fruit, <s>apūrva</s> is postulated for the sake of that [mediation] — he states this —

children.text: "karmanāśājalasparśātkaratoyāvilaṅghanāt/
children.translated_text: 'From the touch of the water of destruction of ritual action, from transgressing the holy-water boundary,

children.text:
gaṇḍakībāhutaraṇāt
dharmaḥ kṣarati kīrtanāt//"
children.translated_text: from crossing the <s>Gaṇḍakī</s> river by swimming, <s>dharma</s> (merit) flows away — so it is declared.'

ityatroktakarmanāśājalasparśādiparigrahaḥ/ dhvaṃsasya
vyāpāratve svargadhārāpattirityapi dūṣaṇāntaraṃ vibhāvanīyam/

children.translated_text: The inclusion of the touch of the water of destruction of ritual action and the like mentioned here [shows that even merit is destroyed]. If destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) were the intermediary operation, there would be the unwanted consequence that it leads to heaven — this is another objection.

lokavyutpattibalāt kriyāyāmeva kṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanatvaṃ

children.translated_text: By the force of worldly linguistic convention, the optative suffix conveys that the action itself has the property of being achievable by effort and being a means to what is desired — thus it functions as an injunctive through its optative-suffix-hood.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>:

children.text:
lokavyutpattīti/
lokavyavahāretyarthaḥ/ sa ca yo yatra pravartate sa
kṛtisādhyatveneṣṭasādhanatvena ca tajjñānavānityevaṃrūpaḥ/ kecittu
yadicchayā yatra pravṛttiḥ tattatsādhanamiti lokavyavahāra ityāhuḥ/
navyāḥ punaḥ loke pacetetyādiliṅādisamabhivyāhārasthale
kriyāyāmeva kṛtisādhyatvaviśiṣṭesādhanatvabodha iti

ākhyātatveneti/ tacca saṅketasambandhenākhyātapadavattvaṃ
tiptvādikameva śaktatāvacchedakamiti tu navyāḥ/ yatnārthakatvam -
kṛtitvāvacchinnavācakatvam/ kiṃ karotīti/ kṛtitvāvacchinne
jijñāsitasambandhabodhakatva eva
children.translated_text: 'Worldly usage' (<s>lokavyutpatti</s>) — the meaning is: worldly linguistic practice (<s>lokavyavahāra</s>). And that is of the following form: he who engages in a particular activity does so knowing it to be achievable by effort (<s>kṛtisādhya</s>) and to be a means to a desired end (<s>iṣṭasādhana</s>). Some, however, say that worldly usage is: that activity in which one engages by desire, that is the means to that [desired end]. The Navyas (modern logicians), on the other hand, [explain] that by the force of restriction, in worldly usage where verbal forms with the optative (<s>liṅ</s>) and other suffixes are employed alongside the verb 'cooks' and the like, the cognition of means-ness qualified by achievability through effort (<s>kṛtisādhyatva</s>) arises only with respect to the action — that is the meaning. They explain that 'everywhere' is to be supplied. 'As having verb-form-ness' (<s>ākhyātatva</s>) — and that is: possessing a verb-form through the relation of convention (<s>saṅketa</s>); the Navyas hold that the suffixes <s>tip</s> and the like alone are the delimitors of denotative capacity (<s>śaktatāvacchedaka</s>). 'Denoting effort' (<s>yatnārthakatva</s>) — means: being an expression delimited by effort-ness (<s>kṛtitva</s>). 'What does he do?' — only the capacity to convey the relation that is the object of inquiry, delimited by effort-ness,

tannivartakatvaṃ
nānyatheti bhāvaḥ/ nanu ratho gacchati ityādau ākhyātasya

prathamāntārthe gamanāderanvayena nirvāhe āśrayatve nirūḍhalakṣaṇākalpanaṃ
nirarthakamiti/ vācyam/ nāmārthayoriva
dhātvarthanāmārthayorabhedātiriktasambandhenānvayasyāvyutpannatvāt tatra
tathānvayāsambhavāt/ stokaṃ pacatītyādau stokādeḥ dhātvarthe
poke 'nvayāt abhedātirikteti dhyeyam/ vaiyākaraṇamataṃ nirācaṣṭe
- devadatta iti/ nākhyātārthatvamiti/ ākhyātasya kartrādau
śaktisvīkāre 'nantakṛtyādeḥ śakyatāvacchedakatvamaṅgīkartavyam/
kṛtyādau śaktisvīkāre tu kṛtitvādijāteḥ śakyatāvacchedakatvāt
lāghavamiti bhāvaḥ/ tadgataikatvādīnāmeveti/ ākhyātārthatvamiti
pūrveṇānvayaḥ/ ādinā kṛtyādiparigrahaḥ/ nanu tarhi kartṛkarmaṇoḥ
kathaṃ lābha ityata āha - tayoriti/ ākṣepādeveti/ paramatena/
svamate tu prathamantapadenaiva tallābhāt/ 'devadattaḥ taṇḍulaṃ pacati'
ityatra 'taṇḍulakarmakapākānukūlakṛtimān devadattaḥ'
ityanvayabodhaḥ/ 'devadattena pacyate taṇḍula' ityatra tu
'devadattasamavetakṛtijanyapākakarmībhūtastaṇḍulaḥ' iti śābdabodhaḥ/
na ca 'devadattaḥ pacati' ityatra tṛtīyā, 'taṇḍulaḥ pacyate' ityatra
ca dvitīyā syāt/ tatra kartṛkarmaṇoḥ ākhyātenānabhidhānāditi
vācyam/ anabhihite kartṛtve tṛtīyāyāḥ tādṛśe ca karmatve
dvitīyāyā vidhānenādoṣāditi dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: is the capacity to remove that [inquiry], and not otherwise — this is the purport. Objection: In sentences like 'the chariot goes,' since the verb form cannot denote effort (<s>kṛti</s>) [because the chariot is non-conscious], accordingly the denotative power should be stated to be in activity (<s>vyāpāra</s>) alone. To this he says — with 'in the chariot goes and so forth.' The mention of 'favorableness' (<s>anukūlatva</s>) with respect to activity is for the purpose of obtaining the connection of motion with activity through that relation. The Navyas, however, hold that in 'goes' (<s>gacchati</s>), the verb form has a conventionally fixed secondary meaning (<s>nirūḍhalakṣaṇā</s>) denoting the substratum, just as in 'knows' (<s>jānāti</s>) and the like. And it cannot be objected that postulating a conventionally fixed secondary meaning for the substratum is pointless when the connection of motion and the like with the meaning of the nominative case can be accomplished through the substratum-relation alone — because the connection of verb-meaning and noun-meaning through a relation other than identity is not established [in ordinary usage], just as with noun-meanings [among themselves], and hence such a connection is impossible there. It should be noted that the relation [meant is] other than identity, since in 'cooks a little' (<s>stokaṃ pacati</s>) and the like, the connection of 'a little' with the verb-meaning 'cooking' [requires a relation other than identity]. He explains the Vaiyākaraṇa (grammarian) view — with '<s>Devadatta</s>.' 'Not being the meaning of the verb form' — if the denotative power of the verb form is accepted as [denoting] the agent and the like, then the delimitor of denotative capacity in the form of the suffix <s>kṛtya</s> and the rest must be accepted. But if the denotative power is accepted in the suffix <s>kṛtya</s> and the rest, then since the universal effort-ness (<s>kṛtitva</s>) and the like serve as the delimitor of denotative capacity, there is economy — this is the purport. 'Only the unity and the like residing in that' — this connects with the preceding [statement about] verb-form-meaning. By 'and the like,' the suffixes <s>kṛtya</s> and the rest are included. Objection: If so, how are the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>) and the object (<s>karman</s>) obtained? To this he says — with 'of those two.' 'By implication alone' — according to the other view. But in our own view, their obtainment is through the nominative-case word itself. In '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks rice,' the verbal cognition (<s>anvayabodha</s>) is: '<s>Devadatta</s> possesses effort favorable to cooking whose object is rice.' In 'rice is cooked by <s>Devadatta</s>,' the verbal cognition is: 'rice is the object of cooking produced by effort inhering in <s>Devadatta</s>.' And it cannot be objected that in '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks,' there should be an instrumental case, and in 'rice is cooked,' there should be an accusative case, because the agent and object are not denoted by the verb form — because this is without fault, since the instrumental case is enjoined when agency is unexpressed, and the accusative when such objecthood is unexpressed — this should be noted.

children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

lokavyavahārāt yāgādikriyāyāmeva liṅā

vyutpattipadaṃ vyākhyāya, niyamaparatayā vyutpattipadaṃ vyācakṣāṇānāṃ
navyānāṃ matamāha - navyāḥ panuriti/ tacca saṅketasaṃbandheneti/
ākhyātapadasya yatra tibādau pāṇinyādīnāṃ icchāviśeṣātmakaḥ
saṅketo 'sti sa tibādiḥ saṅketasaṃbandhena ākhyātapadavān/
ākhyātapadavattvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'He who engages in a particular [activity]' — the person who engages in a sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and the like, that person possesses the knowledge of the sacrifice as qualificand, qualified by achievability through effort (<s>kṛtisādhyatva</s>) and means-ness to a desired end (<s>iṣṭasādhanatva</s>) — from worldly usage of this form, it is understood that the optative (<s>liṅ</s>) and the like [convey] achievability through effort and means-ness to a desired end only with respect to ritual actions such as sacrifice — this is the meaning. Having explained the word <s>vyutpatti</s> as referring to [worldly] usage, he states the view of the Navyas who explain the word <s>vyutpatti</s> as referring to restriction — with 'the Navyas, however.' 'And that, through the convention-relation' — of the verb-form word, that which has the convention in the form of a specific desire of <s>Pāṇini</s> and others with respect to the suffix <s>ti</s> and the like, that <s>ti</s> suffix and the like possesses the verb-form word through the convention-relation. Verb-form-word-possession

children.text:
tibādiniṣṭham/ tat
śaktatāvacchedakamityarthaḥ/ yathā tibādiṣu aṣṭādaśasu ākhyātapadasya

pacatītyādau karmatāsambandhena taṇḍulasya dhātvarthe

children.translated_text: resides in the suffix <s>ti</s> and the like — that is the delimitor of denotative capacity, this is the meaning. Just as <s>Pāṇini</s> or another [grammarian] has established convention for the verb-form word in the eighteen [personal endings beginning with] <s>ti</s>, so too, since the convention of other persons for other words is also possible, and since the possession of those words cannot be discriminated [from the intended ones], it would also serve as a delimitor of denotative capacity — reflecting thus, the modern logicians say that only <s>ti</s>-suffix-ness and the like is the delimitor of the denotative capacity for effort (<s>kṛti</s>). He states their view — with 'only <s>ti</s>-suffix-ness and the like.' Here the <s>Vyutpattivāda</s> text should be consulted: 'Since the apprehension of denotative capacity is only for <s>ti</s> suffixes and the like, and accordingly the postulation that the knowledge of the word-sequence such as 'pacati' occasions verbal cognition with the assistance of the presentation generated by the <s>ti</s> suffix is necessary, it is appropriate to postulate denotative capacity of that form for the <s>ti</s> suffix alone.' To indicate that there is economy in the delimitor of denotative capacity when effort-meaning is [accepted] as compared to agent-meaning, it is said 'being an expression delimited by effort-ness.' In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'pacati [means] performs cooking.' The explanation of its meaning by means of another expression of the same meaning is a <s>vivaraṇa</s> (gloss). In the word to be glossed, 'pacati,' there are two parts: 'pac' and 'ti.' In the glossing sentence 'pākaṃ karoti,' 'pākam' glosses the verbal root, and 'karoti' glosses the verb-ending 'ti.' Effort (<s>yatna</s>) is the meaning of the root <s>kṛ</s>. And thus, since it is glossed by 'karoti,' the verb-ending denotes effort. Similarly, to the question 'kiṃ karoti' (what does he do?), the answer given is 'pacati.' In the question-sentence, the meaning of the word 'kim' is: delimited by the property that is the object of inquiry. The meaning of the accusative case is objecthood. There, the meaning of the word 'kim' is connected through the superstratum relation. The connection of objecthood with effort is through the determined-ness relation. And thus the cognition arises: effort that determines the objecthood residing in [that which is] delimited by the property that is the object of inquiry. Through the sentence 'pacati,' the cognition arises: effort that determines the objecthood residing in cooking. And thus, the answer to a question expressing effort with respect to the property that is the object of inquiry can only be a word expressing effort with respect to a specific property — hence the verb-ending denotes effort, this is the purport. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'conveying the queried relation' — meaning: conveying the relation in the form of objecthood whose counter-positive is delimited by the property that is the object of inquiry. 'The capacity to convey the cooking-relation' — meaning: the capacity to convey cooking-objecthood. 'The capacity to remove that' — meaning: the capacity to remove the inquiry. 'Because of the impossibility of denoting effort' — the purport is: because effort in the form of volition is contradicted in the case of a non-conscious chariot. Objection: The statement that in 'the chariot goes' and the like, the verb-form has a secondary meaning denoting favorable activity is not correct, because since favorableness can appear as a relator, verbal denotation for that component is unnecessary, and it would be more appropriate to state the secondary meaning as mere activity — anticipating this, he indicates that the purport of the <s>Dīpikā</s> too is the same — with 'the mention of favorableness with respect to activity.' 'The Navyas, however' — meaning: <s>Dīghiti</s>-kāra and others. He raises the objection according to the view of <s>Maṇi</s>-kṛt (<s>Gaṅgeśa</s>) — with 'and it cannot be said that through the substratum-relation alone.' 'Because it is not established [in usage]' — otherwise, in 'Caitra is cooked,' the verb-meaning cooking would connect with <s>Caitra</s> through the agent-relation, and in 'rice cooks,' rice would connect with the verb-meaning cooking through the object-relation — this would be the undesirable consequence, this is the purport.

children.text:
vaiyākaraṇamatamiti/
'devadattaḥ taṇḍulaṃ pacati' ityatra taṇḍulapadottaradvitīyāyāḥ karma
arthaḥ tatrābhedena taṇḍulasyānvayaḥ/ karmaṇaḥ
svaniṃṣṭhakarmatānirūpakatvasambandhena dhātvarthe pāke 'nvayaḥ/ 'pacati'
ityatra tipaḥ kartā arthaḥ/ tatra devadattasyābhedenānvayaḥ/ kartuḥ
dhātvarthapāke svaniṣṭhakartṛtānirūpakatvasambandhenānvayaḥ/ tathā ca
devadattābhinnakartṛkaḥ taṇḍulābhinnakarmakaḥ pākaḥ iti
dhātvarthamukhyaviśeṣyako bodhaḥ/ devadattena pacyate taṇḍulaḥ ityatra
tṛtīyāyāḥ kartā arthaḥ/ tatra devadattasya abhedenānvayaḥ, kartuśca
pāke 'nvayaḥ/ ākhyātasya karma arthaḥ tatra taṇḍulasyābhedena karmaṇaśca
dhātvarthe 'nvayaḥ/ devadattābhinnakartṛkaḥ taṇḍulābhinnakarmakaḥ pāka iti
śābdabodhaḥ/
children.translated_text: The Vaiyākaraṇa (grammarian) view — in '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks rice' (<s>devadattaḥ taṇḍulaṃ pacati</s>), the meaning of the accusative case following the word 'rice' is objecthood (<s>karman</s>); there, rice connects through identity. Objecthood connects with the verb-meaning cooking through the relation of being determined by its own objecthood. In 'pacati,' the meaning of the suffix <s>tip</s> is the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>); there, <s>Devadatta</s> connects through identity. The agent connects with the verb-meaning cooking through the relation of being determined by its own agency. And thus the verbal cognition with the verb-meaning as the chief qualificand is: 'cooking whose agent is non-different from <s>Devadatta</s> and whose object is non-different from rice.' In '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks rice' [in the passive: '<s>devadattena pacyate taṇḍulaḥ</s>'], the meaning of the instrumental case is the agent; there, <s>Devadatta</s> connects through identity, and the agent connects with cooking. The meaning of the verb-ending is objecthood; there, rice connects through identity, and objecthood connects with the verb-meaning. The verbal cognition is: 'cooking whose agent is non-different from <s>Devadatta</s> and whose object is non-different from rice.'

children.text:
naiyāyikamate tu
devadattaḥ taṇḍulaṃ pacati ityatra dvitīyāyāḥ karmatvamarthaḥ/
tatrādheyatāsambandhena taṇḍulasyānvayaḥ/ karmatvasya nirūpakatāsambandhena
dhātvarthe pāke 'nvayaḥ/ ākhyātasya kṛtirarthaḥ/ tatrānukūlatāsambandhena
dhātvarthapākasyānvayaḥ/ kṛterāśrayatāsambandhena devadatte 'nvaya iti
taṇḍulaniṣṭhakarmatānirūpakapākānukūlakṛtimān devadatta iti
prathamāntārthamukhyaviśeṣyako bodhaḥ/ devadattena pacyate taṇḍula
ityatra tṛtīyāyāḥ kṛtirarthaḥ/ tatra devadattasya samavāyenānvayaḥ/
kṛterjanyatāsambandhena dhātvarthapāke 'nvayaḥ/ ākhyātasya karmatvamarthaḥ/
tatra nirūpitatvasambandhena pākasyānvayaḥ/ karmatvasyāśrayatāsambandhena
prathamāntārthe taṇḍule 'nvaya iti
devadattasamevatakṛtijanyapākanirūpitakarmatāvān taṇḍula iti
bodhaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the Naiyāyika view, however, in '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks rice' (<s>devadattaḥ taṇḍulaṃ pacati</s>), the meaning of the accusative case is objecthood (<s>karmatva</s>); there, rice connects through the superstratum relation (<s>ādheyatā</s>). Objecthood connects with the verb-meaning cooking through the determined-ness relation (<s>nirūpakatā</s>). The meaning of the verb-ending is effort (<s>kṛti</s>); there, the verb-meaning cooking connects with effort through the relation of favorableness (<s>anukūlatā</s>). Effort connects with <s>Devadatta</s> through the substratum relation (<s>āśrayatā</s>). Thus the verbal cognition, with the meaning of the nominative case as chief qualificand, is: '<s>Devadatta</s> possesses effort favorable to cooking that determines the objecthood residing in rice.' In 'rice is cooked by <s>Devadatta</s>' (<s>devadattena pacyate taṇḍulaḥ</s>), the meaning of the instrumental case is effort (<s>kṛti</s>); there, <s>Devadatta</s> connects through inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). Effort connects with the verb-meaning cooking through the relation of being-produced-by (<s>janyatā</s>). The meaning of the verb-ending is objecthood (<s>karmatva</s>); there, cooking connects with objecthood through the determined-ness relation. Objecthood connects with rice, the meaning of the nominative case, through the substratum relation. Thus the verbal cognition is: 'rice possesses objecthood determined by cooking produced by effort inhering in <s>Devadatta</s>.'

children.text:
bhāṭṭamīmāṃsakānāṃ
mate devadattaḥ odanaṃ pacati ityatrākhyātasya kṛtirūpā bhāvanā
arthaḥ/ odanapadottaradvitīyāyāḥ akhaṇḍopādhirūpaṃ karmatvamarthaḥ/
tatrādheyatāsambandhena taṇḍulasyānvayaḥ/ karmatvasya
svanirūpakadhātvarthapākānukūlatvasambandhena ākhyātārthakṛtāvanvayaḥ/
devadattasyāpi tatraivānvayaḥ/ dhātvarthapākasya
children.translated_text: In the view of the <s>Bhāṭṭa Mīmāṃsakas</s>, in '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks rice' (<s>devadattaḥ odanaṃ pacati</s>), the meaning of the verb-ending is <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation) in the form of effort (<s>kṛti</s>). The meaning of the accusative case following the word 'rice' (<s>odana</s>) is objecthood (<s>karmatva</s>) in the form of an unanalyzable imposed property (<s>akhaṇḍopādhi</s>); there, rice connects through the superstratum relation. Objecthood connects with effort, the meaning of the verb-ending, through the relation of favorableness to cooking, which is the verb-meaning determined by [objecthood] itself. <s>Devadatta</s> too connects with effort in the same way. The verb-meaning cooking

children.text:
karaṇatvasambandhena
kṛtāvanvayaḥ/ svaniṣṭhakaraṇatānirūpakaudanoddeśyakatvasambandhena
pākasya kṛtāvanvaya iti paryavasyati/ tathā ca devadattasamavetā
taṇḍulakarmakapākānukūlā pākakaraṇikā kṛtiriti bodhaḥ/ aiteṣāṃ
mate ākhyātarthakṛtiḥ śābdabodhe mukhyaviśeṣyatayā bhāsate/ pākasya
kṛtau karaṇatvaṃ ca kṛtiṃ prati uddeśyabhūtaudanakaraṇatvāt/ yatra tu
dvitīyāntaṃ vinā pacati ityetāvanmātramuktam tatra dhātvarthapākasya
karmatāsambanadhena kṛtāvanvayaḥ/ devadattasamavetā pākakarmikā
kṛtiriti bodhaḥ/ caitreṇa odanaḥ pacyate ityatrāpi tṛtīyāyāḥ
kartṛtvamarthaḥ/ tasya svanirūpakapākānukūlatvasambandhena
ākhyātārthakṛtāvanvayaḥ/ dhātvarthasya pākasya
svakaraṇakaudanoddeśyakatvasambandhena kṛtāvanvayaḥ/ ākhyātasya tatra
karmatvaṃ bhāvanā cārthaḥ/ karmatve odanasyānvayaḥ/ karmatvasya
svanirūpakapākānukūlatvasambandhena bhāvanāyāmanvayaḥ/ tathā ca
devadattakartṛkapākānukūlā odanakarmakapākānukūlā
pākakaraṇakaudanoddeśyikā bhāvenati śābdabodha iti/
children.translated_text: connects with effort through the relation of instrumentality (<s>karaṇatva</s>). Cooking connects with effort through the relation of being instrumental to the purposiveness directed at rice that is determined by its own instrumentality — thus the analysis culminates. And thus the verbal cognition is: 'effort inhering in <s>Devadatta</s>, favorable to cooking whose object is rice, [effort] for which cooking is the instrument.' In the view of these [<s>Bhāṭṭas</s>], the verb-meaning effort (<s>kṛti</s>) appears as the chief qualificand in verbal cognition. And the instrumentality of cooking with respect to effort is because cooking is the instrument directed at rice as its purpose. Where, however, only 'pacati' is uttered without an accusative-case word, there the verb-meaning cooking connects with effort through the object-relation. The verbal cognition is: 'effort inhering in <s>Devadatta</s>, whose object is cooking.' In 'rice is cooked by <s>Caitra</s>' (<s>caitreṇa odanaḥ pacyate</s>) as well, the meaning of the instrumental case is agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>); that connects with effort, the meaning of the verb-ending, through the relation of favorableness to cooking determined by [agency] itself. The verb-meaning cooking connects with effort through the relation of purposiveness directed at rice as its instrument. The meaning of the verb-ending there is objecthood and <s>bhāvanā</s>; in objecthood, rice connects; objecthood connects with <s>bhāvanā</s> through the relation of favorableness to cooking determined by [objecthood] itself. And thus the verbal cognition is: '<s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation) favorable to cooking whose agent is <s>Devadatta</s>, favorable to cooking whose object is rice, purposive with respect to rice through cooking as instrument.'

children.text:
pūrveṇānvaya iti/
tathā ca ca kartṛkarmagatā ekatvādisaṅkhyā kṛtiḥ kālaśca ākhyātārthaḥ/
asmin mate anabhihite iti sūtrasya
kartṛkarmagatasaṅkhyāyāmanabhihitāyāmityarthaḥ/ atha vā kartṛtve
karmatve cānabhihite ityarthaḥ/ nātaḥ devadattaḥ pacati ityatra
devadattapadottaraṃ tṛtīyāyāḥ, taṇḍulaḥ pacyate ityatra
taṇḍulapadottaraṃ dvitīyāyā vā apattiḥ/ agre ca spaṣṭamidam/
kṛtyādiparigraha iti/ ādinā kālo gṛhyate/ paramateneti/
mīmāṃsakamatenetyarthaḥ/ 'kartā cākṣepalabhyaḥ' iti nyāyaprakāśādau
nirūpitatvāt/
children.translated_text: 'The syntactic connection is through the preceding [verbal element].' Accordingly, the number such as singularity etc. residing in the agent and object, the effort (<s>kṛti</s>), and time are the meanings of the finite verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>). In this view, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>anabhihite</s>' (when not expressed) is: 'when the number residing in the agent or object is not expressed.' Alternatively, the meaning is: 'when agent-hood or object-hood is not expressed.' Therefore, in '<s>Devadattaḥ pacati</s>' (Devadatta cooks), there is no contingency of the instrumental case after the word <s>Devadatta</s>; nor in '<s>Taṇḍulaḥ pacyate</s>' (rice is cooked), of the accusative case after the word <s>taṇḍula</s>. This will be made clear further on. 'The inclusion of <s>kṛtya</s> etc.' — by the word 'etc.,' time is included. 'According to the other view' — meaning according to the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view; because it has been established in the <s>Nyāyaprakāśa</s> and other works that 'the agent is obtained through implication.'

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text:
upasargāṇāṃ
dyotakatvam
children.translated_text: The suggestive function (<s>dyotakatva</s>) of verbal prefixes (<s>upasarga</s>)

children.text:
prajayati ityādau
dhātoreva prakarṣe śaktiḥ/ upasargāṇāṃ dyotakatvameva, na tatra śaktiḥ/
children.translated_text: In usages like '<s>prajayati</s>' (excels in producing), the <s>śakti</s> (denotative potency) for the sense of excellence belongs to the verbal root itself. Verbal prefixes (<s>upasargas</s>) have only a suggestive function (<s>dyotakatva</s>); they do not possess <s>śakti</s>.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
upasargāṇāṃ
vācakatvamataṃ nirasyati prajayatītyādāviti/ nanu dhātunaiva
prakarṣāderbodhe praśabdādervaiyarthyamata āha
children.translated_text: [The commentator] refutes the view that verbal prefixes (<s>upasargas</s>) are denotative — [beginning with] 'in cases like <s>prajayati</s>.' Now, if the verbal root alone conveys the sense of excellence etc., then the prefix '<s>pra</s>' and the like would be redundant — anticipating this, he says:

children.text:
- upasargāṇāmiti/
dyotakatvam - tātparyagrāhakatvam/ tena 'itaranipātānām
vācakatvam' iti sūcitam/ tathā hi-ekakārasya
ayogavyavacchedor'thaḥ 'śaṅkhaḥ pāṇḍura eva' ityādau,
anyayogavyavacchedaśca 'pārtha eva dhanurdhara' ityādau ityādikaṃ
bahutaramūhanīyam/
children.translated_text: 'Of verbal prefixes' — <s>dyotakatva</s> (suggestive function) means the capacity to indicate the speaker's intention (<s>tātparyagrāhakatva</s>). By this, it is implied that 'the other <s>nipātas</s> (particles) have denotative function.' For example, the particle <s>eva</s> has the meaning of exclusion-of-non-connection (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>) in cases like '<s>śaṅkhaḥ pāṇḍura eva</s>' (the conch is indeed white), and exclusion-of-other-connection (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>) in cases like '<s>Pārtha eva dhanurdhara</s>' (only <s>Pārtha</s> is the archer) — and much more is to be inferred along these lines.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
tātparyagrāhakatvam
- yatra pra iti upasargaḥ dhātunā saha uccāryate tatra dhātoḥ prakarṣe
tātparyamiti graho bhavati/ ataḥ dhātorarthaviśeṣe
tātparyagrahajanakatvamupasargāṇāmiti bhāvaḥ/ itaranipātānāmiti/
upasargātiriktanipātānāmityarthaḥ/ ityādikaṃ
bahutaramūhanīyamiti/ 'nīlam sarojaṃ bhavatyeva' ityādau
evakārasya atyantāyogavyavacchedor'tha ityūhanīyamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Tātparyagrāhakatva</s> (capacity to indicate intention) — where the prefix '<s>pra</s>' is uttered together with a verbal root, there arises the understanding that the speaker's intention (<s>tātparya</s>) is the excellence of the root's meaning. Therefore, the purport is that verbal prefixes have the capacity to generate understanding of the speaker's intention regarding a particular sense of the verbal root. 'Of the other <s>nipātas</s>' — meaning the <s>nipātas</s> other than verbal prefixes. 'And much more is to be inferred along these lines' — meaning that in cases like '<s>nīlaṃ sarojaṃ bhavatyeva</s>' (the lotus is indeed blue), the meaning of the particle <s>eva</s> is exclusion-of-absolute-non-connection (<s>atyantāyogavyavaccheda</s>), and this is to be inferred.

children.text:
atredaṃ bodhyam -
evakārārthastrividhaḥ-anyayogavyavacchedaḥ, ayogavyavacchedaḥ,
atyantāyogavyavacchedaśceti/ viśeṣyasaṅgataivakārasya
anyayogavyavacchedor'thaḥ/ yathā pārtha eva dhanurdhara ityādau
pārthānyasmin dhanurdhaṃratvayogo vyavacchidyate/ tatra anyaḥ, yogaḥ,
abhāvaśceti trayaḥ evakārasya pṛthak śakyāḥ/ anyaśabdārthaḥ bhedavān/
bhede pārthasya pratiyogitāsambandhenānvayaḥ/ sambandharūpe yoge
prakṛte tādātmyātmake pratiyogitvena dhunardhaṃrasyānvayaḥ/
yogasyābhāve pratiyogitvenānvayaḥ/ abhāvasya svarūpasambandhena
anyasminnanvayaḥ/ evaṃ dhanurdharasya abhedasambandhena pārthe 'nvayaḥ/ tathā ca
pārthapratiyogikabhedavān (pārthānyaḥ)
dhanurdharapratiyogikatādātmyābhāvavān (dhanurdharatvābhāvavān)
pārthaḥ dhanurdharābhinnaśceti śābdabodho jāyate/ pārthasya
viśeṣyatayā anyaviśeṣaṇatayā ca dvirbhānam/ evaṃ dhunardharasya
evakārārthayogaviśeṣaṇatayā pārthaviśeṣaṇatayā ca dvirbhānam/
children.translated_text: Here the following should be understood: the meaning of the particle <s>eva</s> is threefold — <s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s> (exclusion of other connections), <s>ayogavyavaccheda</s> (exclusion of non-connection), and <s>atyantāyogavyavaccheda</s> (exclusion of absolute non-connection). When <s>eva</s> is connected with the qualificand (<s>viśeṣya</s>), its meaning is <s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>. For example, in '<s>Pārtha eva dhanurdharaḥ</s>' (only <s>Pārtha</s> is the archer), the connection of archership with anyone other than <s>Pārtha</s> is excluded. There, 'other,' 'connection,' and 'absence' are the three separate denotata of <s>eva</s>. The meaning of the word 'other' involves difference; the difference has syntactic connection with <s>Pārtha</s> through the relation of counter-correlate-hood. In the connection that is of the nature of a relation, archership has syntactic connection through counter-correlate-hood with identity-relation as the relevant relation. In the absence of that connection, there is syntactic connection through counter-correlate-hood. The absence has syntactic connection with 'the other' through the <s>svarūpa</s> relation (intrinsic relation). Similarly, archership has syntactic connection with <s>Pārtha</s> through the relation of non-difference. And thus the verbal cognition arises: '<s>Pārtha</s>, who possesses difference having <s>Pārtha</s> as counter-correlate (i.e. other than <s>Pārtha</s>), possesses the absence of identity with archership (i.e. lacks archer-hood) — [while] <s>Pārtha</s> is non-different from an archer.' <s>Pārtha</s> appears twice — as the qualificand and as a qualifier of 'other.' Similarly, archership appears twice — as a qualifier of the <s>eva</s>-meaning 'connection' and as a qualifier of <s>Pārtha</s>.

children.text:
viśeṣaṇasaṅgataivakārasya ayogavyavacchedor'thaḥ/ yathā
'śaṅkhaḥ pāṇḍara eva' ityādau śaṅkhe pāṇḍarāyogo vyavacchidyate/
tatraivakārasya yogābhāve abhāve ca śaktiḥ/ sambandhātmake yoge
pāṇḍarasya pratiyogitayā anvayaḥ/ yogābhāvasya pratiyogitayā
abhāve 'nvayaḥ/ abhāvasya svarūpasaṃbandhena śaṅkhe 'nvayaḥ/ tathā ca śaṅkhaḥ
pāṇḍarayogābhāvābhāvavān iti śābdabodhaḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>eva</s> is connected with a qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>), its meaning is <s>ayogavyavaccheda</s> (exclusion of non-connection). For example, in '<s>śaṅkhaḥ pāṇḍara eva</s>' (the conch is indeed white), the non-connection of whiteness with the conch is excluded. There, <s>eva</s> has <s>śakti</s> for the absence of connection and for absence. In the connection that is of the nature of a relation, whiteness has syntactic connection through counter-correlate-hood. The absence of connection has syntactic connection with absence through counter-correlate-hood. The absence has syntactic connection with the conch through the <s>svarūpa</s> relation. And thus the verbal cognition is: 'the conch possesses the absence of the absence of connection with whiteness' [i.e. the conch is indeed connected with whiteness].

children.text:
kriyāsaṅgataivakārasya
atyantāyogavyavacchedor'thaḥ/ yathā 'nīlaṃ sarojaṃ bhavatyeva'
ityādau saroje
children.translated_text: When <s>eva</s> is connected with the action (<s>kriyā</s>), its meaning is <s>atyantāyogavyavaccheda</s> (exclusion of absolute non-connection). For example, in '<s>nīlaṃ sarojaṃ bhavatyeva</s>' (the lotus is indeed blue), in the lotus

children.text:
nīlabhavanātyantāyogo vyavacchidyate/ atyantatvaṃ abhāvaśca tatra
evakārārthaḥ/ atyantatvaṃ ca vyāpakatvam/ tacca
bhedapratiyogitānavacchedakatvam/ bhede
sarojasyādheyatāsambandhenānvayaḥ/ bhedapratiyogitānavacchedakatvasya
pratiyogitayā
children.translated_text: the absolute non-connection of being-blue is excluded. 'Absoluteness' and 'absence' — these are the meanings of <s>eva</s> there. And absoluteness means pervasiveness (<s>vyāpakatva</s>), which is the property of not being a delimiter of the counter-correlate-hood of difference. The difference has syntactic connection with the lotus through the superstratum relation. The property of not delimiting the counter-correlate-hood of difference has syntactic connection

children.text:
abhāve 'nvayaḥ/ abhāvasya
svarūpasambandhena ayoge 'nvayaḥ/ evaṃ nīlakartṛkabhavanasya
nīlatvātmakasya ayogaikadeśe yoge pratiyogitvenānvayaḥ/ tathā ca
sarojaniṣṭhabhedapratiyogitānavacchedakatvābhāvavān
nīlatvapratiyogikasambandhābhāvaḥ iti śābdabodhaḥ/
nīlatvasambandhābhāve sarojatvavyāpakatvasyāsambhavena
sarojatvavyāpakatvaviśiṣṭāyogābhāvasya bodhayitumaśakyatvāt
ayoge sarojatvavyāpakatvavyavacchedabodho varṇita iti/ adhikam
dīdhikārīyaivakārārthavivecane
jayarāmanyāyapañcānanakṛtapadārthamālāyāṃ ca draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: with absence through counter-correlate-hood. The absence has syntactic connection with non-connection through the <s>svarūpa</s> relation. Similarly, being-produced-by-blue, which is a part of non-connection that is of the nature of blue-ness, has syntactic connection through counter-correlate-hood with connection. And thus the verbal cognition is: 'the absence of blue-ness-characterized connection is one that possesses the absence of the property of not delimiting counter-correlate-hood of difference residing in the lotus' [i.e. the lotus's being blue is not merely occasional but invariable]. Since the pervasiveness over lotus-hood is impossible in the absence of the blue-ness-relation, and since the absence of non-connection qualified by pervasiveness over lotus-hood cannot be conveyed, the exclusion of pervasiveness over lotus-hood is described within the non-connection. More on this should be seen in the <s>Dīdhiti</s> commentary's analysis of the meaning of <s>eva</s> and in the <s>Padārthamālā</s> by <s>Jayarāma Nyāyapañcānana</s>.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: padārthatattvajñānasya mokṣahetutvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Establishing that knowledge of the true nature of the categories (<s>padārtha</s>) is the means to liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>)

children.text:
padārthajñānasya
paramaprayojanaṃ mokṣaḥ/ tathā hi-- 'ātmā vāre draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo
mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ' iti śrutyā śravaṇādīnāṃ
ātmasākṣātkārahetutvabodhanāt śruttā dehādivilakṣaṇātmajāne
satyapyasambhāvanānivṛtteḥ yuktyanusandhānarūpamananasādhyatvāt/
mananopayogipadārthanirūpaṇadvārā śāstrasyāpi mokṣopayogitvam/
tadanantaraṃ śrutyupadiṣṭayogavidhinā nididhyāsane kṛte tadanantaraṃ
dehādiṃvilakṣaṇātmasākṣātkāre sati dehādau
ahamityabhimānarūpamithyājñānanāśe doṣābhāvāt pravṛttyabhāve
dharmādharmayorabhāve janmābhāve pūrvadharmādharmayoranubhavena nāśe
caramaduḥkhadhvaṃsalakṣaṇamokṣo jāyate/ jñānameva mokṣasādhanam/
mithyājñānanivṛtterjñānamātrasādhyatvāt/ 'tamevaṃ
viditvātimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya' iti śrutyā
sādhanāntaraniṣedhācca/
children.translated_text: The supreme purpose of the knowledge of categories is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). For it is thus: from the <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text) '<s>Ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ</s>' ('The Self indeed must be seen, heard about, reflected upon, and meditated upon'), it is understood that hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and the rest are the means to direct realization of the Self. Even when knowledge of the Self as distinct from the body etc. arises through hearing, since the doubt of impossibility (<s>asambhāvanā</s>) is not removed — because this is accomplished through reflection (<s>manana</s>) in the form of reasoning and investigation — the <s>śāstra</s> (philosophical treatise) too becomes instrumental to liberation through the elucidation of categories useful for reflection. After that, when meditation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>) is practiced according to the <s>yoga</s> injunction taught by the <s>śruti</s>, and subsequently when direct realization of the Self as distinct from the body etc. occurs, the false cognition in the form of the ego-identification 'I' with regard to the body etc. is destroyed; due to the absence of defects (<s>doṣa</s>), there is no activity; due to the absence of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, there is no birth; and when the prior <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are exhausted through experience, <s>mokṣa</s> in the form of the destruction of the final suffering arises. Knowledge alone is the means to liberation — because the removal of false cognition is accomplished by knowledge alone; and because of the Vedic negation of any other means: '<s>Tamevaṃ viditvā atimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya</s>' ('Having known Him thus, one transcends death; there is no other path for release').

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
prekṣāvatpravṛttaye
sakalakāmanāviṣayamuktiprayojanakatāṃ granthasya darśayati -
padārthajñānasyeti/ padārthatattvajñānasyetyarthaḥ/
anyeṣāmavāntaraprayojanānāmapi sadbhāvādāha - parameti/
śruterayamarthaḥ -- are mumukṣuṇā ātmā draṣṭavyaḥ mumukṣoḥ
ātmadarśanamiṣṭasādhanamiti yāvat/ ātmadarśanopāyaṃ darśayati ---
śrotavya ityādinā/ ārtha-krameṇa śābdakramaḥ tyakto bhavati,
'agnihotraṃ juhoti' 'yāvagūṃ pacati' ityādivat/
asambhāvanānivṛtteriti/ aprāmāṇyajñānanivṛtterityarthaḥ/
yuktyanusandhāneti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ--- yuktibhiranucintanaṃ mananam/ tacca
ātmana itarabhinnatvenānumānam/ tacca
bhedapratiyogītarajñānasādhyam/ tadarthaṃ sakalapadārthanirūpaṇamiti/
mokṣopayogitvaṃ viśadayati --- tadanantaramiti/
mananānantaramityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [The commentator] shows that the purpose of the treatise is liberation, which is the object of all desires, so as to motivate the engagement of discerning persons — [beginning with] 'of the knowledge of categories.' The meaning is: 'of the knowledge of the true nature of the categories.' Since intermediate purposes also exist, he says 'supreme.' The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is this: O seeker, the Self must be seen by one desiring liberation; that is, seeing the Self is the desired means for the seeker of liberation. [The <s>śruti</s>] shows the method of seeing the Self — by the words 'must be heard about' etc. The textual order is abandoned in favor of the logical order, as in '<s>agnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' ('one offers the fire-ritual') and '<s>yāvagūṃ pacati</s>' ('one cooks the rice-gruel'). 'Removal of the doubt of impossibility' — meaning the removal of the cognition of non-validity. 'Reasoning and investigation' — the idea is this: deliberation through reasoning is <s>manana</s> (reflection), and that is inference of the Self as different from all else. That is accomplished by knowledge of the entities that are counter-correlates of difference [from the Self]. For that purpose, the elucidation of all categories [is undertaken]. [The commentator] elaborates on the instrumentality for liberation — [with] 'after that,' meaning after reflection.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
sakalakāmanāviṣayeti/ apunarbhavarūpatvāt sarveṣāmapīṣṭaḥ yo
mokṣaḥ tatprayojanakatvamityarthaṃḥ/ yadapekṣayā anyat prayojanaṃ na
bhavati tat paramaprayojanam/ yadapekṣayā anyat prayojanaṃ bhavati
tat avāntaraprayojanam/ prayojanāntarāsādhanatve sati prayojanatvaṃ
paramaprayojanatvam/ prayojanāntarasādhanatve sati prayojanatvaṃ
avāntaraprayojanatvam/ nanu"ātmā vā are
children.translated_text: 'The object of all desires' — since <s>mokṣa</s> has the nature of non-return [to <s>saṃsāra</s>], it is desired by all; hence the meaning is that the treatise has liberation as its purpose. That with respect to which there is no other purpose is the supreme purpose. That with respect to which there is another purpose is an intermediate purpose (<s>avāntaraprayojana</s>). Being a purpose while not being a means to another purpose is supreme-purpose-hood. Being a purpose while being a means to another purpose is intermediate-purpose-hood. Now, in the <s>śruti</s> '<s>Ātmā vā are</s>

children.text:
draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyaḥ"iti
śrutau pāṭhakramānusāreṇa darśanasyaiva śravaṇasādhanatvamavagamyate na tu
śravaṇāderdarśanasādhanatvamityāśaṅkyāha - ārthakrameṇeti/
prayojanavaśena yaḥ kramaḥ saḥ ārthakramaḥ/ yathā agnihotrayavāgūpākayoḥ/
atra hi yavāgvāḥ homaprayojanakatvena tatpākaḥ prayojanavaśena
pūrvamanuṣṭhīyate/ padārthabodhakavākyānāṃ yaḥ kramaḥ saḥ pāṭhakramaḥ/
tena ca padārthānāṃ kamaḥ āśrīyate/ aprāmāṇyajñānanivṛtteriti/
śrutivāvayajanye dehādivilakṣaṇātmaviṣayakaśābdabodhātmakaśravaṇe
aprāmāṇyajñānasya nivṛttiḥ mananena bhavati/ mananaṃ cānu mityātmakam/
ātmā dehādibhinnaḥ jñānecchādyāśrayatvāt yannaivaṃ tannaivam iti
vyatirekyanumānaprayogo draṣṭavyaḥ/
bhedapratiyogītarajñānasādhyamiti/
ātmānuyogikabhedapratiyogibhūtāḥ ye ātmetarapadārthāḥ tadviṣa
yakajñānajanyamanumityātmakaṃ mananamityarthaḥ/ tadarthamiti/ ātmetara
padārthaviṣayakajñānotpādanārthamityarthaḥ/ pratyāhṛtya-nigṛhya,
viṣayasaṃyuktāni yathā na bhaveyustathā kṛtvetyarthaḥ/ manaḥpratyāhṛtya -
manaḥ indriyasaṃyuktaṃ yathā na syāt tathā kṛtvā/ sākṣātkartavye
ātmani manasaḥ praṇidhānaṃ sthāpanaṃ yogaḥ/ viśeṣadarśanenaiveti/
rajatavyāvartakasya śuktigatasyāsādhāraṇadharmasya śuktitvasya
darśanenaivetyarthaḥ/ tathā prakṛte 'pīti/ ātmagatasya
taditaravyāvartakasya dharmasya darśanenaiva dehādibhramarūpaṃ mithyājñānaṃ
nivartate ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyaḥ</s>' — if one objects that following the textual order, it is understood that seeing itself is accomplished through hearing, not that hearing etc. is the means to seeing — anticipating this, [the commentator] says 'by the logical order.' The order determined by purpose is the logical order (<s>ārthakrama</s>). For example, in the case of the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-ritual) and cooking of rice-gruel — since the rice-gruel serves the purpose of the oblation, its cooking is performed first according to the purpose-determined order. The order of sentences that convey the meanings of words is the textual order (<s>pāṭhakrama</s>); and through that, the order of the categories is adopted. 'Removal of the cognition of non-validity' — the doubt regarding the invalidity of the verbal cognition about the Self as distinct from body etc., arising from hearing the <s>śruti</s>, is removed through <s>manana</s> (reflection). And <s>manana</s> is of the nature of inference (<s>anumiti</s>). The inferential reasoning to be applied is: 'the Self is different from the body etc., because it is the substratum of cognition, desire, etc.; whatever is not so is not so' — a negative concomitance inference. 'Accomplished by knowledge of entities that are counter-correlates of difference' — meaning that <s>manana</s>, which is of the nature of inference, is generated by knowledge of the entities other than the Self that are counter-correlates of difference with the Self as the subjunct. 'For that purpose' — meaning for the purpose of generating knowledge about entities other than the Self. 'Having withdrawn' — meaning having restrained, having made it so that [the senses] are not connected with objects. 'Having withdrawn the mind' — having made it so that the mind is not connected with the senses. <s>Yoga</s> is the fixing, the placing of the mind upon the Self that is to be directly realized. 'Through the perception of the distinguishing feature alone' — meaning through the perception of the uncommon property of shell-ness residing in the shell, which distinguishes it from silver. 'So too in the present case' — meaning that false cognition in the form of the delusion of body etc. is removed through the perception of the distinguishing property of the Self that differentiates it from everything else.

children.text: tarkasaṃgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s>

children.text: kāṇādanyāyamatayorbālavyutpattisiddhaye/
children.translated_text: For the instruction of beginners in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and <s>Nyāya</s> systems,

children.text:
annambhaṭṭena viduṣā
racitastarkasaṅgrahaḥ//
children.translated_text: the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> was composed by the learned <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>.

children.text:
// it.i
tarkasaṃgrahaḥ samāptaḥ//
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> is concluded.

children.text: dīpikā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s>

children.text: jñānakarmasamuccayavādanirāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Refutation of the doctrine of the combination of knowledge and action (<s>jñānakarmasamuccayavāda</s>)

children.text:
nanu
'tatprāptiheturvijñānaṃ karmacoktaṃ mahāmune' iti karmaṇo 'pi
mokṣasādhanatvasmaraṇāt jñānakarmaṇoḥ samuccaya iti cet - na/
children.translated_text: Now, if one objects that since it is remembered in texts like '<s>tatprāptiheturvijñānaṃ karmacoktaṃ mahāmune</s>' ('Knowledge is the means to attaining that, and action too is prescribed, O great sage') that action too is a means to liberation, therefore knowledge and action should be combined — no, [that is not so].

children.text:
"nityanaimittikaireva kurvāṇo
duritakṣayam/
children.translated_text: 'By performing the destruction of sins through obligatory and occasional rites alone,

children.text:
jñānaṃ ca
vimalīkurvannabhyāsena ca pācayet//
children.translated_text: and purifying one's knowledge, one should ripen it through practice.

children.text:
abhyāsācca
kvacijjñānāt kaivalyaṃ labhate naraḥ"//
children.translated_text: Through practice and at some point through knowledge, a person attains liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>).'

children.text:
ityādināṃ karmaṇo
jñānasādhanatvapratipādanāt jñānadvāraiva karmaṇo mokṣasādhanatvaṃ na
sākṣāt/ tasmāt padārthatattvajñānasya mokṣaḥ paramaprayojanamiti sarvaṃ
ramaṇīyam/
children.translated_text: Since such texts establish that action is a means to knowledge [not directly to liberation], it is only through the intermediary of knowledge that action serves as a means to liberation, not directly. Therefore, <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is the supreme purpose of the knowledge of the true nature of the categories — and thus everything is harmonious.

children.text:
iti
tarkasaṃgrahadīpikā samāptā
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Tarkasaṃgraha-Dīpikā</s> is concluded.

children.text: prakāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśikā</s>

children.text:
'kaivalyaṃ labhate
naraḥ' ityādineti/ ādinā 'kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe
parāvare' ityādiśruteḥ 'jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute
tathā' ityādismṛteśca saṃgrahaḥ/ jñānadvāraiveti/ atrāyaṃ kramaḥ --
niṣkāmanayā bhagavatprītyarthaṃ kṛtaiḥ karmabhiḥ
duritakṣayarūpātmaśuddhirbhavati/ tato viṣayeṣu vairāgyam/ tataḥ
śravaṇādau pravṛttiḥ/ tataḥ śravaṇādikrameṇa tattvajñānotpattau
pūrvoktamithyājñānanāśādikrameṇa mokṣaniṣpattiḥ/ adhikam
asmadīyacintāmaṇidīdhitivyākhyāyāmanusandheyaṃ
tarkakarkaśavicāracāturīdhurīṇairiti/
children.translated_text: 'A person attains <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation)' etc. — by 'etc.' are included the <s>śruti</s> '<s>kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare</s>' ('His actions are destroyed when that Supreme is seen') and the <s>smṛti</s> '<s>jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā</s>' ('The fire of knowledge likewise reduces all actions to ashes'). 'Only through the intermediary of knowledge' — here the sequence is as follows: through actions performed without desire, for the sake of pleasing the Lord, purification of the self in the form of destruction of sins occurs; from that arises dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) toward sense-objects; from that arises engagement in hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and the rest; from that, through the sequential process of hearing etc., when knowledge of reality arises, liberation is accomplished through the previously described sequence of destruction of false cognition etc. More on this should be consulted in our commentary on the <s>Cintāmaṇi-Dīdhiti</s>, by those skilled in the rigorous deliberation of logical inquiry.

children.text: kauṇḍinyagotrasambhūto nīlakaṇṭhākhyapaṇḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: The learned one named <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, born in the <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> <s>gotra</s> (lineage),

children.text:
kṛtimārpipadetasmai
candracūḍāya maṅgalam//
children.translated_text: May there be auspiciousness for <s>Candracūḍa</s> (the moon-crested one, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>), to whom this composition is offered.

children.text:
iti prakāśikā
samāptā
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Prakāśikā</s> is concluded.

children.text: bālapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapriyā</s>

children.text:
śrīyante ceti/
parāvare-- pare avarā yasmāt tasmin paramātmani sākṣātkṛte sati
puṇyapāparūpāṇi karmāṇi naśyantītyarthaḥ/ jñānāgniriti/
jñānarūpo 'gniḥ sarvāṇyapi puṇyapāparūpāṇi karmāṇi
bhasmīkarotītyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'They perish' (<s>śrīyante</s>) and so forth. 'In the Supreme-and-Lower' (<s>parāvare</s>) — the lower ones (<s>avarāḥ</s>) [perish] because of the Supreme (<s>para</s>); when that <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is directly realized, <s>karmas</s> (actions) in the form of merit and demerit are destroyed — this is the meaning. 'The fire of knowledge' (<s>jñānāgni</s>) — the fire that is of the nature of knowledge reduces to ashes all <s>karmas</s> in the form of merit and demerit — this is the meaning.

children.text:
dīpikāyām
ātmasākṣātkāre satītyādi/"duḥkhajanyapravṛttidoṣaḥ
mithyājñānānāmuttarottarāpoya tadanantarāpāyādapavargaḥ"iti
nyāyasūtramatrābhisaṃhitam/ prathamataḥ avicchinnatailadhārāvat
śravaṇamananasamānaviṣayakānavaratātmānusandhānarūpe nididhyāsane sati
ātmā dehādibhinnatvena sākṣātkriyate/ ayaṃ sākṣātkāra eva
tattvajñānamityucyate/ anena tattvajñānena dehādau ātmābhedabhramarūpaṃ
mithyājñānaṃ nivartate/ tādṛśadoṣāṇāmanutpattau rāgadveṣamoharūpā
doṣāḥ notpadyanate/ tādṛśadoṣāṇāmanutpattau vihitaniṣiddhakarmasu
pravṛttiḥ na bhavati/ pravṛttyabhāvācca puṇyapāparūpau dharmāndharmau
notpadyete/ dharmādharmayoranutpattau ca śarīraprāṇasaṃyogarūpaṃ janma
ātmano
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'when the direct realization of the self [occurs]' and so forth. The <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> intended here is: 'From the successive removal of false knowledge, faults, activity, birth, and suffering, there is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).' First, when <s>nididhyāsana</s> (sustained meditation), which is of the nature of uninterrupted contemplation of the self on the same subject as hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and reflection (<s>manana</s>), like an unbroken flow of oil, takes place, the self is directly realized as distinct from the body and the like. This direct realization itself is called knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>). By this knowledge of reality, the false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) in the form of the erroneous non-distinction of the self from the body and the like is removed. When such defects do not arise, the faults (<s>doṣas</s>) in the form of attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) do not arise. When such faults do not arise, there is no activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) toward enjoined and prohibited actions. Due to the absence of activity, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> in the form of merit and demerit do not arise. When <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> do not arise, birth in the form of the conjunction of the body and the vital breath with the self

children.text:
na bhavati/
janmāntarābhāve asmin janmani prārabdhayoḥ puṇyapāpayoranubhavena
vināśe ca caramaduḥkhasya dhvaṃsarūpo mokṣo bhavati iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: does not occur. In the absence of future birth, when the merit and demerit that have begun to bear fruit in this life are exhausted through experience, liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) in the form of the destruction of the final suffering occurs — this is the import.

children.text:
tameva viditveti/ taṃ
paramātmānaṃ viditvaiva jñātvaiva pumān mṛtyuṃ saṃsāraṃ atyeti
atikrāmati/ ātmatattvajñānavāneva saṃsāranāśavān bhavatītyarthaḥ/
ayanāya-mokṣaprāptaye anyaḥ tattvajñānādanya panthāḥ upāyaḥ na
children.translated_text: 'Having known Him alone' (<s>tameva viditvā</s>) — having known, that is, having realized that <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) alone, a person transcends death, that is, <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of transmigration). The meaning is: only one who possesses knowledge of the reality of the self attains the destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s>. 'For attainment' (<s>ayanāya</s>) — for the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), there is no other path, no other means apart from knowledge of reality —

children.text:
vi/te ityarthaḥ/
sādhanāntaraniṣedhāditi/ ātmatattvajñānādanyasya sādhanasya
niṣedhādityarthaṃḥ/ tatprāptiheturiti/ mokṣāprāpteḥ tattvajñānaṃ
bhagavatprīṇanayāgādirūpaṃ karma cobhayaṃ sādhanamityarthaḥ/ samuccaya
iti/ jñānakarmasamudāyaḥ mokṣasādhanam/ parasparasahakāreṇa
jñānakarmaṇorūbhayoḥ mokṣasādhanatvaṃ na jñānamātrasyetyarthaṃḥ/ jñānaṃ ca
vimalīkurvanniti/ dehendriyādivilakṣaṇātmajñānaṃ
mananenāprāmāṇyajñānānāskanditaṃ kurvannityarthaḥ/ abhyāseneti/
indriyanigrahapūrvakāsakṛtsamaraṇarūpanididhyāsanena pācayet
phalonmukhaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ/ prakāśikāyāṃ tarkakarkaśeti/ tarkamūlakaḥ
yaḥ karkaśaḥ kaṭhinataraḥ vicāraḥ vimarśaḥ tatra yā cāturī cāturyaṃ tayā
tatra vā dhuriṇaiḥ samarthairityarthaḥ/ vimarśaḥ tatra yā cāturī cāturthaṃ
tayā tatra vā dhuviṇaiḥ samarthairityarthaḥ/ candracūḍāya maṅgalamiti /
maṅgalamiti samarpaṇākriyāviśeṣaṇam/ maṅgalaṃ yathā syāt tathā
candracūḍāya samārpayadityarthaḥ/ yathā īśvarārpaṇabuddhyā kriyamāṇaṃ
yāgadānādi maṅgakalaraṃ tathā tattvajñānadvārā sakalojjīvakasnapaya
granthasya īśvarāya samarpaṇamapi svasya pareṣāṃ ca maṅgalakaramiti
bhāvaḥ//
children.translated_text: this is the meaning. 'By the prohibition of other means' — the meaning is: because of the prohibition of any means other than knowledge of the reality of the self. 'The cause of its attainment' — the meaning is: both knowledge of reality and action in the form of sacrifices pleasing to the Lord are the means of <s>mokṣa</s>. 'Combination' (<s>samuccaya</s>) — the aggregate of knowledge and action is the means to liberation; through mutual cooperation, both knowledge and action serve as the means of liberation, not knowledge alone — this is the meaning. 'And purifying knowledge' — the meaning is: making the knowledge of the self as distinct from the body, senses, and the like, through reflection (<s>manana</s>), free from being assailed by cognitions of invalidity. 'Through practice' (<s>abhyāsena</s>) — the meaning is: through <s>nididhyāsana</s> (sustained meditation) in the form of repeated recollection preceded by restraint of the senses, one should ripen it, that is, bring it to fruition. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'hardened in reasoning' (<s>tarkakarkaśa</s>) — the investigation or deliberation that is hardened, that is, made most rigorous, through reasoning — the dexterity (<s>cāturī</s>) therein, or by those who are proficient (<s>dhuriṇa</s>), that is, capable in that [field] — this is the meaning. 'Auspiciousness to <s>Candracūḍa</s>' — 'auspiciousness' is a qualifier of the act of offering. The meaning is: he offers to <s>Candracūḍa</s> in such a way that there may be auspiciousness. Just as sacrifice, charity, and the like performed with the attitude of offering to the Lord are auspicious, so too the offering of this work, which revives all, to the Lord through the door of knowledge of reality is auspicious for oneself and others — this is the import.

children.text: nirañjanāñjanādrīśarīnivāsakṛpābalāt
children.translated_text: By the grace and power of the Lord who dwells on the mountain of <s>Nirañjana</s> (<s>Añjanādri</s>),

children.text:
sadācāryakaṭākṣācca
vyākhyeyaṃ samapūryata//
children.translated_text: and by the glance of the noble teacher, this commentary has been completed.

children.text:
prauḍhavidvanmanastuṣṭiṃ
vyākhyaiṣā janayenna vā/
children.translated_text: Whether or not this commentary generates delight in the minds of learned scholars,

children.text:
bālānāṃ tu manaḥ
prītiṃ parāmāvakṣyati dhruvam//
children.translated_text: it will certainly bring joy to the minds of beginners (<s>bālas</s>).

children.text:
iti

children.text: pṛ.1

nidhāyetyādiślokasyāyaṃ vākyārthaḥ/
tathā hi - hṛdi ityatra saptamyāḥ nirūpitatvamarthaḥ/ tasya ca
vṛttitvaprakārakāhāryajñānarūpanipūrvakadhādhātvarthaghaṭakavṛttitve 'nvayaḥ/
[1] viśveśamityatra nirūpakatayā jñānānvayi āśrayatayā tadanvayi vā
viśeṣyatvaṃ viśeṣyitvaṃ vār'thaḥ/ prakṛtyarthasya viśeṣyatve ādheyatayā
viśeṣyitve vā nirūpitatvasambandhenānvayaḥ/ lyapaḥ
samānakartṛkatvasahitottarakālīnatvaparatvāt lyapapratyayasya
dhvaṃsor'thaḥ/ tatra prakṛtyarthasya pratiyogitayānvayaḥ/ dhvaṃsasya ca
svapratiyogisamānakartṛkatvasvādhikaraṇakālavṛttitvobhayasambandhena
kriyata ityatra kṛdhātvarthakṛtāvanvayaḥ/ [1] guruvandanamityatra
children.translated_text: The sentence-meaning of the verse beginning with '<s>nidhāya</s>' and so forth is as follows. Thus: the meaning of the locative in 'in the heart' (<s>hṛdi</s>) is the relation of being-determined-by (<s>nirūpitatva</s>). Its syntactic connection is with the occurrence-hood that is a component of the verbal root <s>dhā</s> (to place) prefixed by <s>ni</s>, having the form of non-perceptual cognition (<s>āhāryajñāna</s>) whose qualifier is occurrence-hood. [1] In '<s>viśveśam</s>' (the Lord of all), the meaning is qualificandum-hood or being-a-qualificandum, as a determinand connecting with cognition, or connecting with it as a substratum. When the root-meaning has qualificandum-hood, the connection is through the relation of being-determined-by, either as superstratum-hood or as being-a-qualificandum. The absolutive (<s>lyap</s>) has the meaning of destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>), since the <s>lyap</s> suffix denotes being-later-than accompanied by same-agent-hood. The root-meaning connects therein through counterpositive-hood. And the destruction connects with the verbal root <s>kṛ</s> (to do) through the dual relation of same-agent-hood-with-its-counterpositive and occurring-at-the-time-of-its-locus. [1] In 'salutation to the teacher' (<s>guruvandanam</s>),

children.text: svoccārayitṛtāvacchedakaikakālīnobhayāvṛttijātitvopalakṣitajātiyuktaśarīrāvacchinnacetananiṣṭhāpakarṣāvadhitvaprakāraka-
children.translated_text: salutation is an action performed by a conscious being delimited by a body possessing a universal characterized by the non-occurrence at any single moment of both [i.e., not occurring in the same instant], whose qualifier-content is the limit-of-inferiority residing in the conscious being delimited by that body —

children.text:
bodhānukūlatādṛśacetanakartṛko vyāpāro vandanam/
gurupadasya samāsāntargatatayā luptaṣaṣṭhīkasya
viśeṣyatānirūpitor'thaḥ/ tasya cābhedasambandhena prakāratāyāmanvayaḥ/
