vipūrvakadhādhātvarthakṛtyanvitaṃ vidheyatvaṃ vidheyitvaṃ vā
dvitīyārthaḥ/ atrāpi lyapaḥ pūrvavadevārthaḥ/ [1] bālānāmityatra ṣaṣṭhyāḥ bodhānvayi samavetatvam arthaḥ/ tatra
nirūpitatvasambandhena prakṛtyarthasyānvayaḥ/ [1] sukhabodhāyetyatra sukhaṃ
yathā syāttathā bodhaḥ/ sukhaścāsau bodhaśceti samānādhikaraṇasamāsaḥ/
dīpikāyām [1] sūkhena bodha iti vyākhyānam
arthapradarśanamātraparam/ anyathā tṛtīyāsamāsānupapatteḥ/ sukhaśabdaśca
'bhārāpagame sukhī saṃvṛtto 'ham' itivat duḥkhābhāve upacaryate/
sa ceha dharmiparaḥ/ bodhāyetyatra 'edhānāhartuṃ vrajati' ityarthe
'edhebhyo vrajati' itivat 'bodhaṃ janayituṃ kriyata' ityarthe
'bodhāya kriyata' iti"kriyārthopapadasya ca karmaṇi sthānina"iti
sūtreṇa prāptā caturthī utpattyanukūlavyāpāraviṣayakecchāṃ bodhayati/
tasyāḥ svaviṣayasamānakartṛkatvasvaprayojyecchāviṣayatvobhayasambandhena
kṛtāvanvayaḥ/ utpattau ca bodhānvayaḥ/ ākhyātasyādheyatayā
prakṛtyarthānvito vartamānakṣaṇaḥ, āśrayatayā
children.translated_text: an action whose agent is such a conscious being, conducive to cognition. The word '<s>guru</s>' (teacher), being internal to the compound with an elided genitive, has the meaning of qualificandum-hood as determined. Its connection is with the mode of being-a-qualifier through the relation of identity. The root-meaning connects with qualificandum-hood as superstratum-hood. The meaning of the accusative is object-hood or being-an-object, which connects with the verbal root <s>dhā</s> prefixed by <s>vi</s>. Here too the absolutive has the same meaning as before. [1] In 'of the beginners' (<s>bālānām</s>), the meaning of the genitive is co-inherence (<s>samavetatva</s>), connecting with cognition. The root-meaning connects therein through the relation of being-determined-by. [1] In 'for easy understanding' (<s>sukhabodhāya</s>), the understanding is such that it is pleasant; [it is] a co-referential compound meaning 'that which is pleasant and is understanding.' In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [1] the gloss 'understanding through ease' is merely to indicate the meaning; otherwise, the instrumental compound would be untenable. The word <s>sukha</s> (ease/pleasure) is used figuratively for absence of pain, as in 'I have become happy upon the removal of the burden.' And here it refers to the qualificandum. In 'for understanding' (<s>bodhāya</s>), just as 'he goes to fetch firewood' is expressed as 'he goes for firewood,' so 'done in order to produce understanding' is expressed as 'done for understanding' — the fourth case obtained by the rule 'and the object [takes the fourth case] when the [upapada] denotes purpose' expresses a desire whose content is an activity conducive to production. Its connection with the verbal root <s>kṛ</s> is through the dual relation of same-agent-hood-with-its-content and being-the-content-of-the-desire-prompted-by-it. And the understanding connects with production. The verb connects the present moment with the root-meaning through superstratum-hood, and connects with the nominative-ending word through substratum-hood,

children.text:
prathamāntārthānvayi,
vidheyatvaṃ cārthaḥ/ viśiṣṭabodhaḥ spaṣaṭaḥ dīpikāyām [1] viśveśvaramiti/
svaniṣṭhakarmāsādhāraṇahetuprayatnavattavasambandhenāmbāsahitamūrtivi śiṣṭābhinnanikhilavidyopadeśakartrabhinnaviśveśvaraviśeṣyaka-
children.translated_text: and the meaning is object-hood. The qualified cognition is clear. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [1] '<s>Viśveśvara</s>' (the Lord of all) — [the cognition is:] I am the doer of a present-time composition, whose object is the commentary that is non-different from the means of producing cognition whose content is the subject matter expounded in the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>, qualified by the destruction of one's own activity conducive to the cognition whose qualifier-content is the limit-of-inferiority, with <s>Viśveśvara</s> as qualificandum — who is non-different from the teacher of all knowledge, accompanied by the Mother (<s>Ambā</s>), [connected] through the relation of possessing effort that is the uncommon cause of [His] own action —

children.text: svāpakarṣāvadhitvaprakārakajñānānukūlasvīyavyāpāradhvaṃsaviśeṣitatakarsaṅgrahapratipādyārthaviṣayakajñānajanakābhinnabālasama-
children.translated_text: [the commentary being] non-different from the means of producing cognition whose content is the subject matter of the <s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s>, qualified by the destruction of one's own activity conducive to the cognition whose qualifier-content is the limit-of-inferiority, which is non-different from that which produces understanding of substance and other categories, qualified by effortlessness, co-inhering in the beginners —

children.text:
vetānāyāsaviśiṣṭadravyādipadārthaviṣyakabodhanakābhinnavyākhyāna
- vidheyakavartamānakālīnakṛtimānahaṃ iti bodhaḥ/
vyāpāradhvaṃsavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svapratiyogisamānakartṛkatvasvādhikaraṇakālavṛttitvobhayasambandhena/
children.translated_text: [the commentary being] non-different from the exposition that produces understanding of substance and other categories, qualified by effortlessness — the cognition is: 'I am a present-time doer of composition, with that as the predicate.' And the qualification by destruction of activity is through the dual relation of same-agent-hood-with-its-counterpositive and occurring-at-the-time-of-its-locus.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām [2] vande
śivamityādi/ pūrvārdhasya
upadeṣṭrabhinnāmbāviśiṣṭābhinnadakṣiṇāmūrtiśivaviśeṣyaka-
svāpakarṣāvadhitvaprakārakabodhānukūlavyāpārānukūlakṛtimānahamiti
bodhaḥ/ [2] yadvandanenetyādyuttarārthasya
yannamaskāraprayojyagurunirūpitasādṛśyapratiyogikasambandhāśrayo
mando 'pīti bodhaḥ/ apiśabdārthaḥ
svasamabhivyāhṛtapadārthatāvacchedakamandatvādivirodhaḥ, sa
caikakṣaṇāvacchedena ekādhikaraṇāvṛttitvaṃ sādṛśyānvayi/
upadeśaścājñātajñāpanaṃe viṣayatāviśiṣṭaśabdarūpam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
snirūpakajñānajanakatvasvasāmānādhikaraṇyobhayasambandhena/
sāmānādhikaraṇyaghaṭakacaramavṛttitvaṃ
svaprākkālāvacchinnajñānaviṣayatvābhāvasambandhena/ 'asyārthasyopadeśa'
ityādau ṣaṣṭhyartha ādheyatvam/ tasya
copadadeśapadārthaghaṭakaviṣayatāyāmanvaya iti bodhyam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [2] 'I salute <s>Śiva</s>' and so forth. The cognition of the first half is: 'I am the doer of effort conducive to the activity conducive to cognition whose qualifier-content is the limit-of-inferiority, with <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti Śiva</s> as qualificandum — who is non-different [from <s>Śiva</s>], accompanied by the Mother (<s>Ambā</s>), non-different from the teacher.' [2] The cognition of the second half, 'by whose salutation' and so forth, is: 'even a dull person, who is the substratum of the relation whose counterpositive is the similarity determined by the teacher effected by whose salutation.' The meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' (even) is the contradiction with dullness and the like, which is the delimitor of the being-the-referent-of-the-co-uttered-word, and that [contradiction], delimited by a single moment, is the non-occurrence in a single locus, which connects with similarity. And teaching (<s>upadeśa</s>) is of the nature of words qualified by content-hood, which is the making-known of what is unknown. The qualification is through the dual relation of being-the-producer-of-the-determinative-cognition and co-location. The final-occurrence-hood that is a component of co-location is through the relation of absence of being-the-content-of-cognition-delimited-by-a-prior-moment. In passages like 'the teaching of this meaning,' the genitive means superstratum-hood, and its connection is with the content-hood that is a component of the referent of the word 'teaching' — this should be understood.

children.text:
dīpikāyām [1] cikīrṣitasyetyādi/ kṛñdhātoḥ kṛtirarthaḥ sanaḥ icchā/
niṣṭhāyāśca
kṛtiniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitaviṣayatāsambandhāvacchinnaprakāratāśrayor'thaḥ/
kṛteḥ viśeṣyatāsambandhenecchāyāmanvayaḥ/ tasyāśca
nirūpitatvasambandhena prakāratāyāmanvayaḥ/ sā ca icchā
'granthaviṣayakakṛtirbhavatu' ityākārikā/ [1] nirvighnaparisamāptyarthamityatra nirvighnaṃ yathā yathā
samāptiriti vigrahaḥ/ [2] nirvighnaparisamāptaya ityatra tu
pūrvavadutpādakavyāpārecchaiva caturthyarthaḥ/ vyāpāraśca
pratibhādirūpaḥ/ samāptiśca caramavarṇaghvaṃsaḥ tadanvitaṣaṣṭyarthaḥ
granthasyetyatra sambandhaḥ svaghaṭakacaramavarṇapratiyogitvarūpaḥ/
etattattvamasmadviracitasamāpti [vicāre] draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [1] 'of what is desired to be done' (<s>cikīrṣitasya</s>) and so forth. The meaning of the verbal root <s>kṛ</s> is action (<s>kṛti</s>); of <s>san</s>, desire (<s>icchā</s>). The meaning of the past participle suffix is: the substratum of the qualifier-hood delimited by the relation of content-hood determined by qualificandum-hood of the action. The action connects with desire through the relation of qualificandum-hood. And that [desire] connects with qualifier-hood through the relation of being-determined-by. That desire is of the form 'may the action concerning the treatise take place.' [1] In 'for the sake of unobstructed completion,' the analysis is: completion such that it is unobstructed. [2] In 'for unobstructed completion,' just as before, the meaning of the fourth case is the desire for the productive activity. And the activity is of the nature of creative inspiration (<s>pratibhā</s>) and the like. And completion is the destruction of the final letter; the genitive connected therewith in 'of the treatise' has the relation of being-the-counterpositive-of-the-final-letter-constituting-it. This truth should be seen in our composition on [the analysis of] completion.

children.text:
śiṣyaśikṣāyai -- śiṣyān
śikṣayitumityarthaḥ/ 'tumarthācca bhāvavacanāt' iti sutraṇa caturthī/
'paktuṃ vrajati' ityarthe 'pākāya vrajati' ityādivat/ tatrecchaiva
caturthyarthaḥ/ tasyāśca
svaviṣayasamānakartṛkatvasvaprayojyecchajñaviṣayatvobhayasambandhena
nibandhapadārthajñānajanakaśabdarūpabindhane 'nvayaḥ/ 'śiṣyā apyevaṃ
kuryuḥ' ityākārakānugraharūpecchaiva śikṣāpadārthaḥ/ tatra śiṣyāṇāṃ
viśeṣyatāsambandhenānvayaḥ/ 'avaśyakartavyatvaprakārakajñānaṃ śikṣā'
iti tu asmaddinakaraṭiṣpaṇyāmativistareṇa nirastam/ ktapratyayasya
viśeṣyatānirūpitaviṣayatāsambandhāvacchinnaprakāratāśrayor'thaḥ/
dhātvarthaḥ ādyakṛtiḥ/ kṛtāvadyatvaṃ ca dhvaṃsaviśiṣṭānyatvaparyavasitam/
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ svottaratvasvapratiyogikṛtiviśiṣṭatvobhayasambandhena/
kṛtivaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svasāmānādhikaraṇyasvaviṣayagranthaviṣayakatvobhayasambandhena/ atra
maṅgalatadupanibandhanayoḥ phaladarśanāt 'tayorācaraṇe
tattaddharmikeṣṭaviśeṣasādhanatābhramaprayukte maṅgalācaraṇarūpatvāt,
bhrāntapuruṣīyajalatāḍanādyācaraṇavat' ityanumānaṃ nirastam/
children.translated_text: 'For the instruction of students' (<s>śiṣyaśikṣāyai</s>) — the meaning is: in order to teach students. The fourth case is by the rule 'and from an expression denoting purpose, [the fourth case applies] to an action-word.' Just as 'he goes to cook' [is expressed as] 'he goes for cooking.' There the meaning of the fourth case is desire itself. Its connection with the verbal expression that is the word-form producing knowledge of the meaning of the bound word is through the dual relation of same-agent-hood-with-its-content and being-the-content-of-the-desire-prompted-by-it. The referent of the word '<s>śikṣā</s>' (instruction) is the desire in the form of grace of the kind 'may the students also do thus.' The connection of students therein is through the relation of qualificandum-hood. But [the view that] 'instruction is cognition whose qualifier is obligatoriness' has been refuted at great length in our <s>Dinakara</s> gloss. The meaning of the past participle suffix (<s>kta</s>) is: the substratum of the qualifier-hood delimited by the relation of content-hood determined by qualificandum-hood. The verbal root meaning is the primary action. And the first-ness in action is ultimately the otherness qualified by destruction. The qualification is through the dual relation of its-being-later and being-qualified-by-the-action-whose-counterpositive-it-is. The qualification of action is through the dual relation of co-location and having-the-treatise-as-content-of-its-content. Here, since the fruit of both the auspicious invocation and its occasion is observed, the inference 'because it is of the nature of performing an auspicious rite prompted by the erroneous belief that it is a means to a desired end for the one possessing that property, like the striking of water by a deluded person' is refuted.

children.text:
yattu --
'maṅgalādikamanuṣṭheyam niṣphalatvāt' ityanumānapradarśanam --
tattuccham/ bhrāntapuruṣīyānuṣṭhānaviṣayatayā bādhāpatteḥ/
iṣṭasādhanatvapramādhīna1 kṛtiviśiṣṭatvābhāvasādhane 'pi kṛtau
children.translated_text: As for the presentation of the inference 'the auspicious invocation and the like should be performed, because [otherwise] it would be fruitless' — that is worthless. Because there would be a counter-example, since it is the content of the performance by a deluded person. Even in proving the absence of the qualification of being-a-means-to-a-desired-end dependent on valid cognition of being-a-means-to-a-desired-end, in the [primary] action itself

children.text:
1.
kṛtiviśiṣṭatvābhāveti/ kṛtiviśiṣṭatvaṃ ca viṣayatāsambandhena/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. Regarding 'the absence of being qualified by volition' (<s>kṛtiviśiṣṭatvābhāva</s>) — the qualification by volition (<s>kṛti</s>) is through the relation of objecthood (<s>viṣayatā</s>).

children.text:
pramādhīnatvābhāva eva
paryavasānena tadapekṣayā asmaduktasyaiva yuktatvāt/ yadapi
'maṅgalādyācaraṇaṃ pāpajanakam' ityunamānam tadapi heyam/
vyāpārasya niṣphalatve tadācaraṇaphalāsidśyā abhrāntānāṃ
phalaviśeṣasādhanatājñānādeva pravṛttyupapattau tadācaraṇena
pāpotpattikalpane pramāṇābhāvāt/ yadyapi pratijñāyāṃ na
kuryādityasyāpi
iṣṭasādhanatājñānābhāvādhīnābhrāntapuruṣīyapravṛttyabhāvānuvāditvāt,
prāptārthe 'pi 'bhuñjate' ityādau vidhiprayayadarśanāt, kṛteḥ
'karomi', 'kriyate', 'kurva' ityādirūpāyā niṣphalatvāt
tadācaraṇamayuktamiti śaṅkā sambhavati, tathāpi tasyāḥ
śiṣyāvadhānaphalakatvāt na doṣaḥ/ ata eva 'śiṣyāvadhānāya
pratijānīta' ityādilekhanaṃ granthakṛtāṃ tatra tatra
children.translated_text: Since the ultimate purport is the absence of dependence on valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>), and with respect to that, what we have stated alone is correct. And the objection that 'the performance of auspicious acts etc. produces sin' is also to be rejected, because when the ritual act is fruitless, since the activity of non-deluded persons is explained by their knowledge of it being a means to a particular result through the non-establishment of a fruit of that performance, there is no valid means of knowledge for postulating the production of sin through that performance. Although the doubt may arise that even the statement 'one should not do' in the thesis, being a mere restatement of the absence of activity of non-deluded persons which depends on the absence of knowledge of it being a means to a desired end, and since injunctive suffixes are seen even in cases where the meaning is already obtained, as in '<s>bhuñjate</s>' (they eat) etc., and since volition (<s>kṛti</s>) of the form 'I do,' 'it is done,' 'do' etc. is fruitless, its performance would be unjustified — nevertheless, since it serves the purpose of the students' attentiveness, there is no fault. Hence the writings of the authors of treatises in various places stating 'make a thesis for the sake of students' attentiveness'

children.text:
saṅgacchate/ avadhānaṃ
ca manaso vikṣeparāhityaṃ vijātīyamanoyoga iti yāvat/
caturthyarthaḥ utpattyanukūlavyāpārecchā/ anyat pūrvavat/ sa ca
vyāpāraḥ 'mayā pratijñā kṛtā, bhavadbhissāvadhānena bhavitavyam'
iti śiṣyān prati guroḥ śabdaprayogaḥ/ [2] svagranthasya itaragranthanetyādi/
svagranthaviśeṣyaketaragranthajanyaprayojanajanakatvābhāvaprakārakajñānajanakaśabdānukalūkṛtimānityanvayabodhaḥ/
children.translated_text: are consistent. And attentiveness (<s>avadhāna</s>) is the absence of mental distraction — that is, the absence of heterogeneous mental engagement (<s>vijātīyamanoyoga</s>). The meaning of the dative case is the desire for an activity conducive to production. The rest is as before. And that activity is the teacher's utterance of words to the students: 'I have made a thesis; you must be attentive.' [2] Regarding 'of one's own treatise, from another treatise' etc. — the verbal cognition is: [one's own treatise] possesses a volition that is conducive to words that generate knowledge having as its qualifier the absence of the capacity to produce the purpose generated by another treatise that is other than the qualificand of one's own treatise.

children.text:
dīpikāyām [1] maṅgalasya samāptisādhanatvaṃ nāstīti/ maṅgalaṃ
samāptisādhanatvābhāvavadityarthaḥ/ tādṛśasādhanatvābhāvo
maṅgalavṛttiriti vā/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: [1] 'The auspicious invocation (<s>maṅgala</s>) does not have the property of being a means to completion' — meaning: the auspicious invocation possesses the absence of the property of being a means to completion. Or alternatively, the absence of such instrumentality is the meaning of the term <s>maṅgala</s>.

children.text:
anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ vyabhicārāditi/
anvayavyabhicāraśca kāraṇasattve 'pi kāryānutpattirūpaḥ, tanniṣṭakarṣaśca
1svāvacchinnavyāpyatānavacchedakakāraṇatāvacchedakāvacchinnakāraṇakūṭavanniṣṭhābhāvīyakāryatāva
- cchedakasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāvacchedakakāryatāvacchedakakatvam,
children.translated_text: Regarding 'there is deviation through positive and negative concomitance' (<s>anvayavyatirekābhyām</s>) — positive deviation (<s>anvayavyabhicāra</s>) is of the form of non-production of the effect even when the cause is present. Its defining characteristic is: possessing the property of being delimited by the counter-positiveness — delimited by the relation that delimits the effecthood-delimiting property — of the absence residing in a locus that possesses the aggregate of causes delimited by the cause-hood delimitor that is not the delimitor of the pervaded-ness delimited by itself,

children.text:
1. svāvacchinnetyādi/
svapadena yaddharmāvacchinnasattve 'pi kāryaṃ na jāyate tadgrāhyam/ tacca
kapālākāśasaṃyogatvaṃ tadavacchinnavyāpyatāvacchedakaṃ
kapāladvayasaṃyogatvaṃ vyāpyatānavacchedakaṃ yat kāraṇatāvacchedakaṃ
daṇḍatvādi tadavacchinnakāraṇakūṭavati kapāladvayasaṃyogaśūnye pradeśe
vartate yaḥ ghaṭābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitāvacchedakaghaṭatvakatvasya
kalālakāśasaṃyogatve sattvāt tadvataḥ kapālakāśasaṃyogasya
anvayavyabhicāritvam atra kāraṇatāvacchedake
vyāpyatānavacchedakāntānupādāne
kapālākāśasaṃyogasyānvayavyabhicāritvaṃ na nirvahati/
atastudapādānam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. Regarding '<s>svāvacchinna</s>' etc. — the word 'self' (<s>sva</s>) should be taken as that property-delimited [entity] despite whose presence the effect is not produced. And that is the property of being the contact of a potsherd with space; the delimitor of the pervaded-ness delimited by that is the property of being the contact of two potsherds, which is not the delimitor of pervaded-ness; that which is the cause-hood delimitor such as stick-hood etc. — in a region devoid of the contact of two potsherds, which possesses the aggregate of causes delimited by that, there exists the absence of a pot; since the property of being a pot, which is the delimitor of the counter-positiveness of that [absence], exists in the property of being the contact of a potsherd with space, the contact of potsherd with space is a positive deviant. Here, without including the phrase 'not the delimitor of pervaded-ness' in the cause-hood delimitor, the positive deviation of the contact of potsherd with space cannot be maintained. Hence that inclusion.

children.text:
kāryatāvacchedakanirūpitatādṛśāvacchedakasambandhāvacchedakatvābhimatadharmavattvam/
vyatirekavyabhicāraśca kāraṇābhāve 'pi kāryotpattirūpaḥ/
kāryatāvacchedakasambandhena
kāryatāvacchedakāvacchinnādhikaraṇaviśiṣṭakāraṇatāvacchedakavattvam/
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ1svaniṣṭhābhāvīyakāraṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasvāvacchinnavyāpyatānavacchedaka
children.translated_text: It is the possession of the property that is accepted as the delimitor of the relation of the said delimitor determined by the effect-hood delimitor. And negative deviation (<s>vyatirekavyabhicāra</s>) is of the form of production of the effect even when the cause is absent. It is the possession of a cause-hood delimitor qualified by the locus delimited by the cause-hood delimitor through the relation of effect-hood delimitor. The qualification is through both relations: the relation of being the substratum delimited by the relation that delimits the aggregate-possession delimited by as many [entities] as are delimited by the non-delimitor-of-pervaded-ness delimited by itself, and the counter-positiveness delimited by the relation that delimits cause-hood of the absence residing in itself,

children.text:
yāvadavacchinnādhikaraṇakūṭavattvasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvobhāyasambandhena/
tādṛśakūṭavattvaṃ ca
svasamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvani ṣṭhāvacchedakatāka
pratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena svaviśiṣṭatvaparyavasitam/
svādhikaraṇatā
svaviśiṣṭakaraṇatāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnanirūpitādhikaraṇatātvasambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāvacchinnavyāpyatāvacchedakatvasambandhāvacchinnatvasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena/
children.translated_text: through both the relation of substratum-hood delimited by the relation of aggregate-possession delimited by as many as are delimited, and the said aggregate-possession, which amounts to being qualified by itself through the relation of possessing a difference whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of being the delimitor co-located with its own counter-positiveness-delimitor located in itself. Its own locus-hood is through the relation of being the locus-hood determined by the property delimited by the cause-hood delimitor property qualified by itself. Its own qualification is through the relation of possessing a difference whose counter-positiveness-delimitor is located in itself, delimited by the relation of being the delimitor of pervaded-ness delimited by itself.

children.text:
pratiyogitāvacchedakatā cādheyatāsambandhena/
tādṛśādheyatāśūnyakāraṇatāvacchedakadharmavattvam anvayasahacāraḥ/
niruktobhayasambandhena kāryādhikaraṇaviśiṣṭānyakāraṇatāvacchedakavattvaṃ
vyatirekasahacāraḥ/
anvayavyabhicāragrastakapālākāśasaṃyogavāraṇāyānvayasahacāragrahaḥ
kāraṇatāgrahahetuḥ/ vyatirekavyabhicāragrastarāsabhādivāraṇāya
vyatirekasahacāragrahaḥ tathā/ 2vyabhicāra grahau ca krameṇa
sahacāragrahapratibandhakau/
children.translated_text: And the counter-positiveness delimitor is through the relation of substratum-hood. The possession of a cause-hood delimiting property devoid of such substratum-hood is positive co-occurrence (<s>anvayasahacāra</s>). Through the stated both-relations, the possession of another cause-hood delimitor qualified by the locus of the effect is negative co-occurrence (<s>vyatirekasahacāra</s>). The apprehension of positive co-occurrence, which serves to exclude the contact of potsherd with space that is vitiated by positive deviation, is the ground for apprehending cause-hood. Similarly, the apprehension of negative co-occurrence is [the ground] for excluding entities like donkeys etc. that are vitiated by negative deviation. 2. And the apprehensions of deviation are respectively obstructors of the apprehension of co-occurrence.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām [3] ato
na vyabhicāra ityanenānvaya iti/ ato na vyabhicāra
ityuttaravākyenānvaya ityarthaḥ/ vighnānyūnasaṃkhyākatvasya
kāraṇatāvacchedakatve gauravamabhisandhāna kalpāntaramāha -
balavattarasyeti/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [3] 'Therefore there is no deviation' — by means of this, 'positive [concomitance]' is meant. 'Therefore there is no deviation' — by means of the subsequent sentence, [this is] the meaning. Since there would be cumbersomeness in making the property of being a number that is not less than the number of obstacles the delimitor of cause-hood, he states an alternative position — 'of that which is more powerful' (<s>balavattarasya</s>).

children.text:
1.svaniṣṭhābhāvīyetyādi/ prathamasvapadaṃ
kāryatāvacchedakāvacchinnādhikaraṇaparam/ dvitīyasvapadaṃ
kāraṇatāvacchedakaparam/ evamuparitanasvapadāni
kāraṇatāvacchedakadharmaparāṇi/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. Regarding '<s>svaniṣṭhābhāvīya</s>' etc. — the first occurrence of the word 'self' (<s>sva</s>) refers to the locus delimited by the effect-hood delimitor. The second occurrence of 'self' refers to the cause-hood delimitor. Similarly, the subsequent occurrences of 'self' refer to the cause-hood delimiting properties.

children.text:
2.
vyabhicāragrahauceti/ anvayavyabhicāragrahaḥ
anvayasahacāragrahapratibandhakaḥ, vyatirekavyabhicāragrahaḥ
vyatirekasahacāragrahapratibandhaka ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 2. Regarding 'the apprehensions of deviation' — the apprehension of positive deviation is the obstructor of the apprehension of positive co-occurrence, and the apprehension of negative deviation is the obstructor of the apprehension of negative co-occurrence — this is the meaning.

children.text:
vighnadhvaṃsadvāreti/
svajanyavighnadhvaṃsasambandhenetyarthaḥ/ evamagre 'pi/ ata eva
vighnabahutve 'pi yatra balavattaramekaṃ maṅgalaṃ vartante tatrāpi
samāptirbhavati/ balavattaratvaṃ ca vaijātyaviśeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Through the destruction of obstacles' (<s>vighnadhvaṃsadvāra</s>) — meaning: through the relation of destruction of obstacles produced by itself. Similarly in what follows. Hence, even where there are many obstacles, wherever there exists a single more powerful auspicious act, completion occurs even there. And the greater power (<s>balavattaratva</s>) is a specific difference of type (<s>vaijātyaviśeṣa</s>).

children.text:
āhuḥ ityasvarassūcitaḥ/ tadbījantu
'sakṛduccaritaḥ śabdaḥ sakṛdevārthaṃ gamayati' iti nyāyāt ata
ityādipadānāmāvṛttānāmarthadvayabodhakatvānupapattireva/ nanu
śiṣṭācārānumitaśrutibodhikartavyatākamityanena
children.translated_text: 'They say' — this is indicated by the context. The basis for that is the principle '<s>sakṛduccaritaḥ śabdaḥ sakṛdevārthaṃ gamayati</s>' (a word uttered once conveys meaning only once) — hence it is simply the impossibility of repeated words like '<s>atas</s>' etc. conveying two meanings. Now, by the statement 'the obligatory nature is indicated by a <s>Śruti</s> inferred from the conduct of the learned,'

children.text:
śiṣṭācārasya
maṅgalakartavyatābodhakaśrutyanumāpakatvaṃ labhyate/ tacca noṃpapadyate/
śiṣṭācāramātrasya
śrutibodhitāpravṛttapravṛttiviṣayatvalakṣaṇakartavyatārahitabhojanasādhāraṇatvāt/
'snātvā bhuñjīta' ityādiḥ tatkartavyatābodhiketi vācyam/ tasyāḥ
bhojane snānottarakālīnatāmātravidhānaparatvāt/ bhojanasya
rāgaprāptatayā tadvidhiparatvāsambhavāt/ 'aprāpte hi śāstramathavat'
iti nyāyenetyāśayena śaṅkate - [1] nanu maṅgalasya kartavyatva
iti/ kartavayatve kṛtividheyatve/ kiṃ śabdaḥ kṣepe/ tathā ca
maṅgalakartavyatāpramitikaraṇaṃ na kimapītyarthaḥ/
śiṣṭācārasyoktayuktyā śrutyanumāpakatvāsambhavāt iti bhāvaḥ/
yattu kartavyatvaṃ kṛtividheyatāprayojakatvamityarthaḥ iti,
tadapahāsyam/ viṣayatātmakagauṇakarmārthakasya tavyādipratyayasya
viṣayatāprayojakadharmavadarthakatāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt/ anyathā
boddhavyaśabdādāvapi tathā prasaṅgāt/ ata eva [3] maṅgalasya śrutibodhitakartavyatākatvaṃ vyavasthāpayituṃ
śaṅkata ityavataraṇikādānamapi saṅgacchate/
aprāmāṇyajñānānāskanditaniścayānukūlasamīcīnayuktikathanaṃ
vyavasthāpanam/ tumunaḥ icchaivārthaḥ/ tasya
1svaviṣayasamānakartṛkatvasvaprayojyecchāviṣayatvobhayasambandhena
śaṅkāyāmanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: what is obtained is that the conduct of the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>) serves as a ground for inferring a <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic text) that teaches the obligatory nature of the auspicious invocation. But that is not tenable, because the mere conduct of the learned is common to eating etc. which lack the obligatory nature characterized by being the object of activity prompted by <s>Śruti</s>-taught duty. Nor can one say that '<s>snātvā bhuñjīta</s>' (one should eat after bathing) etc. is the teaching of that obligatory nature, because that [text] has the purport of merely prescribing the posteriority to bathing in the case of eating, and since eating is already motivated by desire, it is impossible for it to be the object of a prescriptive injunction, in accordance with the principle '<s>aprāpte hi śāstramarthavat</s>' (scripture has purpose only where [the action] is not already obtained). With this intent, the objection is raised — [1] 'Now, regarding the obligatory nature of the auspicious invocation.' 'Obligatory nature' means being enjoined with respect to volition (<s>kṛti</s>). The word <s>kim</s> is used in the sense of reproach. Thus the meaning is: there is nothing whatsoever that serves as a means of valid cognition of the obligatory nature of the auspicious invocation, because, by the reasoning stated, the conduct of the learned cannot serve as a ground for inferring <s>Śruti</s> — this is the purport. However, the interpretation that 'obligatory nature means being the motivator of the enjoined volition' is laughable, because there is no valid means of knowledge for the suffix <s>tavya</s> etc., which has as its meaning an object in the form of a secondary action of objecthood-type, to mean a property possessing the capacity to motivate objecthood. Otherwise, such a consequence would arise even for words like <s>boddhavya</s> (to be known) etc. Hence [3] the presentation of the introductory remark 'he raises an objection in order to establish that the auspicious invocation possesses <s>Śruti</s>-taught obligatory nature' is also consistent. Establishment (<s>vyavasthāpana</s>) is the statement of a proper reasoning that is conducive to a determination not undermined by the knowledge of invalidity. The meaning of the <s>tumun</s> suffix is desire. Its syntactic connection in the objection is through both relations: being of the same agent as its own object, and being the object of the desire prompted by itself.

children.text:
1. svaviṣayetyādi/
svaṃ vvavasthāpanecchā tadviṣayaḥ vyavasthāpanaṃ tatsamānakartṛkatvaṃ
śaṅkāyām, tathā svaṃ vyavasthāpanecchā tatprayojyā
śaṅgāviṣayakecchā tadviṣayatvaṃ ca śaṅkāyām/ maṅgalasya
śrutibodhitakartavyatākatvaṃ vyavasthāpayeyamitīcchayā pūrvapakṣaṃ
kuryāmiti pūrvapakṣecchā jāyata iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. Regarding '<s>svaviṣaya</s>' etc. — 'self' is the desire to establish; its object is the establishment; being of the same agent as that is [connected] to the objection. Similarly, 'self' is the desire to establish; prompted by that is the desire having the objection as its object; and its objecthood is [connected] to the objection. The purport is: from the desire 'I wish to establish that the auspicious invocation possesses <s>Śruti</s>-taught obligatory nature,' the desire for the prima facie position arises — 'I shall raise the prima facie objection.'

children.text:
dīpikāyāṃ samādhatte-
[1] śiṣṭetyādi/ hetusādhyādipradarśanapūrvakamanumānasvarūpaṃ
vivṛṇoti - [1] tathāhītyalaukikāvigītaśiṣṭācāraviṣayatvāditi/
atrālaukikatvasamānādhikaraṇāvigītatvasamānādhikaraṇaśiṣṭācāraviṣayatvādityāśayaḥ/
karmadhārayopari śrūyamāṇabhāvapratyayasya
pūrvapadārthatāvacchedakasamānādhikaraṇottarapadārthatāvacchedakabodhakatvavyutpatteḥ/
nanu śiṣṭācārānumitaśruterityatra
śiṣṭasamavetakṛtiviṣayakaparāmarśajanyānumitividheyatvaṃ śrutau
bodhitaṃ na saṃghaṭate/ 'maṅgalaṃ śrutibodhitakartavyatākam'
ityanumitividheyatvasya śrutibodhitakartavyatākatva eva sattvāt/
śruteśca 1tadavacchedakakoṭipraviṣṭatvāt/ vidheyakoṭipraviṣṭatve 'pi
vidheyatvaṃ na svīkartuṃ śakyam/ tathā sati vahnitvamanumitamiti
vyavahāraprasaṅgāt ityāśaṅkāyāṃ śrutervidheyatvamupapādayati -
[3] atrāyamāśaya ityādinā/ anumiteḥ pūrvamasiddhatvāditi/
anumitiprākkālīnajñānaviṣayatānavacchedakatvādityarthaḥ/ tena
parāmarśaviṣayatve 'pi mahānasīyavahnyādeḥ na vidheyatānupapattiḥ/ atra
ca maṅgalakartavyatābondhakaśrutirūpaviśeṣastu pakṣe
sādhyasambandhasiddhimātreṇaiva sambhavati/ parvato vahnimānityādau
parvatīyavahnyādivadityavadheyam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, the resolution is presented — [1] '<s>śiṣṭa</s>' etc. He elaborates the form of the inference by first presenting the reason (<s>hetu</s>), the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>), etc. — [1] 'For, because it is the object of the extraordinary and uncensured conduct of the learned.' The intention here is: because it is the object of the conduct of the learned that is co-located with being extraordinary and co-located with being uncensured. [This follows] from the semantic convention that the abstract suffix heard after a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound conveys the co-location of the prior member's meaning-delimitor with the latter member's meaning-delimitor. Now, in '<s>śiṣṭācārānumitaśruteḥ</s>' (from the <s>Śruti</s> inferred from the conduct of the learned), the enjoined nature — inferred through a consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>) having as its object the volition inherent in the learned — being taught in <s>Śruti</s>, does not fit. Because the inferred enjoined nature exists precisely in the form of <s>Śruti</s>-taught obligatory nature of '<s>maṅgalaṃ śrutibodhitakartavyatākam</s>' (the auspicious invocation possesses <s>Śruti</s>-taught obligatory nature). And because <s>Śruti</s> belongs to the delimitor-class of that. Even if it enters the enjoined-class, one cannot accept its being the content of the injunction; for if so, the usage 'fire-hood is inferred' would follow — in response to this doubt, he establishes the enjoined nature of <s>Śruti</s> with — [3] 'Here the intention is' etc. 'Because of being unestablished prior to the inference' — meaning: because of not being the delimitor of the objecthood of the cognition prior to the inference. Hence, even though it is the object of the consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>), the fire in the kitchen etc. does not have the untenability of being the content of the injunction. Here, the specific <s>Śruti</s> in the form of teaching the obligatory nature of the auspicious invocation is possible in the thesis merely through the establishment of the relation with the probandum. This should be understood as analogous to the fire on the mountain etc. in 'the mountain possesses fire.'

children.text:
nanu [1] śiṣṭācāranumitarutereveti dīpikāvākyasthenaivakāreṇa
tādṛśaśrutyatiriktasya maṅgalakartavyatāyāṃ pramāṇatvaṃ vyavacchidyate/
tacca na yujyate/ 'maṅgalaṃ kartavyaṃ samāptiphalakatvāt'
ityanumānasya tatra pramāṇatvaṃ sambhavatītyata āha - [3] evakāro 'pyarthaka iti/ āhurityasvarasaḥ/ tadbījantu
vṛttyaniyāmakasambandhasya
vyāpakatāghaṭakatvasāmānādhikaraṇyaghaṭakatvayorasambhavaḥ/
yathāśrutadīpikāvākyārthāsvārasyaṃ ceti/ vidhimantarā rāgādīti/
atra cāntarāśabdasyābhāvor'thaṃḥ/ tasya sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena rāge
anvayaḥ/ atra ca vidheḥ
children.translated_text: Now, [1] by the word 'only' (<s>eva</s>) in the <s>Dīpikā</s> sentence '<s>śiṣṭācārānumitaśrutereva</s>' (only from the <s>Śruti</s> inferred from the conduct of the learned), what is excluded is the status of being a valid means of knowledge for anything other than such <s>Śruti</s> with respect to the obligatory nature of the auspicious invocation. But that is not correct, since the inference 'the auspicious invocation is obligatory, because of being a means to completion' is possible as a valid means of knowledge there. To this he says — [3] 'the word <s>eva</s> is also meaningful.' 'They say' — this is contextual. The basis for that is the impossibility of the relation that determines the meaning of a word-function being a constituent of pervader-hood and being a constituent of co-location. And also the contextual implication of the <s>Dīpikā</s> sentence taken as stated. 'Without an injunction, through desire etc.' — here the word <s>antarā</s> (without) has the meaning of absence. Its syntactic connection with desire is through the relation of co-location. And here the connection of the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>)

children.text:
svabodhitakartavyatākatvasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvasambandhenānvayaḥ/
sāmānādhikaraṇyaghaṭakadvitīyavṛttirviṃṣayatayā/
children.translated_text: is through the relation of being the counter-positiveness delimited by the relation that delimits the <s>Śruti</s>-taught obligatory nature. The second word-function constituting the co-location is through objecthood.

children.text:
1. tadavacchedaketi/
vidheyatāvacchedaketyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. Regarding '<s>tadavacchedaka</s>' — meaning: the delimitor of the enjoined nature (<s>vidheyatā</s>).

children.text:
tasilaḥ
prayojyatvamarthaḥ/ prāptiḥ pravṛttiḥ/ ktapratyayārthaḥ vidheyaḥ/ tathā ca
viddhyabhāvasamānādhikaraṇarāgādhīnapravṛttividheyabhinnatvamiti
phalitam/ yadyapi maṅgale rutibodhatakartavyatākatvasandehena
tādṛśarāgādhīnapravṛttiviṣayatvasya sandigdhatayā viśiṣṭahetoḥ
sādhyāviśeṣo durvāraḥ,
children.translated_text: The suffix <s>tasil</s> has the meaning of being the prompted agent. Attainment (<s>prāpti</s>) means activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>). The meaning of the <s>kta</s> suffix is 'the content of the injunction' (<s>vidheya</s>). And thus the result is: the content of the injunction is different from the activity that depends on desire which is co-located with the absence of an injunction. Although, due to the doubt about the auspicious invocation possessing <s>Śruti</s>-taught obligatory nature, the objecthood of such desire-dependent activity is also doubtful, and thus the non-distinction of the probandum from the qualified reason is difficult to avoid,

children.text:
niścitahetoreva
niścāyakatvāt, tathāpi pravṛttiviṣayatvena ubhayavādimatasiddhaṃ
yadyadbhojanādikaṃ tattadbhinnatvaniveśe
children.translated_text: since only a determined probans is determinative; nevertheless, the intention in including distinctness from each and every [prohibited action] such as eating and the like, which is established in the view of both disputants as being the object of activity,

children.text:
tātparyam/ ata eva
rātriśrāddhādivāraṇāyāvigītatvaviśeṣaṇamapi saphalam/ anyathā tatra
śrutibodhitakartavyatvavirahe vidhimantarā rāgataḥ prāptatvena
tadvaiyarthyāt/ avigītatvaṃ dharmaśāstrādyadhīnanivṛttiviṣayabhinnatvam/
ādipadena niṣphalatvapramāsaṅgrahaḥ/ tena 'nu kuryāt niṣphalam'
ityādeḥ anuvādarūpatve vyutkramakṛtadarśādau na vyabhicāraḥ/
etatsarvamabhipretyāgre [4] saṅkṣepa ityuktam/
children.translated_text: is the purport. For this very reason, the qualifier '<s>avigītatva</s>' (non-disputedness) is also fruitful for excluding night-<s>śrāddha</s> and the like. Otherwise, in those cases, due to the absence of obligation taught by <s>śruti</s>, since they are already obtained through attachment without a [separate] injunction, that [qualifier] would be purposeless. '<s>Avigītatva</s>' means distinctness from what is the object of cessation dependent on <s>dharmaśāstra</s> and the like. By the word '<s>ādi</s>,' fruitlessness and erroneous cognition are also included. By that, when [injunctions like] 'one should not perform what is fruitless' and the like have the nature of restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), there is no deviation in cases such as the <s>darśa</s> rite performed out of sequence. Intending all this, ahead [4] it was said 'in brief.'

children.translated_text: 'Through the cognition of being stated in the <s>Veda</s>': the meaning is that <s>śiṣṭatva</s> (being a learned person) consists in possessing effort favorable to actions enjoined by the <s>Veda</s>, generated by the cognition of being stated in the <s>Veda</s>. The purport is that the cognition of being stated in the <s>Veda</s> must be in the form of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>), in order to exclude one who performs actions such as violence not enjoined by the <s>Veda</s> through the erroneous belief that they are stated in the <s>Veda</s>. [3] 'One who performs <s>ahiṃsā</s> and the like': here by the word '<s>ahiṃsā</s>,' an activity contrary to violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>) is intended. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [1] 'because it is prohibited': this is at first glance, since the restatement-nature of 'one should not do' and the like was already stated previously. [4] The sixth case ending in '<s>tarkapadasya</s>' and so forth has the meaning of being the qualificand. Its connection is with 'erroneous cognition.' In '<s>bhramam</s>' here, counter-positiveness connected with cessation is the meaning of the accusative case. An activity favorable to cessation is prevention (<s>vāraṇa</s>); the meaning of the infinitive suffix is desire; and the connection in the etymological derivation is through both relations: having the same agent as one's own object, and being the content of a desire prompted by oneself. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'briefly' means 'in a concise manner.' The instrumental case indicates qualification, and that is connected with the statement.

1. atrāhiṃsāśabdeneti/

children.translated_text: 1. 'Here by the word <s>ahiṃsā</s>': if the word '<s>ahiṃsā</s>' meant the absence of violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>), then since an absence cannot be the object of an action-suffix (<s>kṛtya</s>), the expression 'one who performs <s>ahiṃsā</s>' would be untenable.

hiṃsāvirodhivyāpāro 'hiṃsetyarthaḥ/ naño 'tra virodhyarthakatvaṃ

children.translated_text: Therefore, '<s>ahiṃsā</s>' means an activity contrary to violence — this is the meaning. The negative particle '<s>nañ</s>' here has the sense of contrariety. The statement of the author of the <s>śāstra</s> is: 'the <s>nañ</s> [is used] in the senses of otherness, contrariety, and absence of that [thing].'

children.translated_text: 'Of what is related to the word': nor should it be objected 'since denotation-nature would be purposeless when content-hood [is already given], what is the point of mentioning it?' — because since content-hood not determined by denotation also exists for the object, the character of being the general definition of <s>padārtha</s> (word-referent) would not be possible for mere object-hood of what is denoted; hence there is no fault in including determination-by-denotation in the content-hood, for the purpose of preventing such error. And since the denotation related to the word is connected with the object precisely through the relation of content-hood, although it would be proper to state that possessing denotation through the relation of content-hood itself is the definition, and hence its inclusion in the mode of qualifier would be fruitless — nevertheless, the intention is that, following the principle 'differentiation or usage is the purpose of a definition,' in establishing usage, since content-hood does not invariably determine occurrence, whether it is the relation delimiting the reason-hood is a matter of dispute. Nor should it be objected that, since denotation-hood is constituted by another property in the form of content-hood that is the delimiter of co-occurring pervasion-hood, it would not delimit pervasion-hood, and hence pervasion would be unestablished — because the intention is that denotation-content-hood is the definition through the relation of determination by denotation, i.e., as qualified by denotation.

children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [15] 'He classifies the <s>padārthas</s> (categories)': from the root '<s>bhaj</s>' prefixed with '<s>vi</s>,' the meaning of the word is: that which generates a cognition having as mode a property that is pervaded by the delimiting property of the presentability of the word ending in the accusative case with which it is co-employed. The delimiter-of-presentability-hood of the word ending in the accusative is a suggestive indication. The same should be understood in what follows as well. Now, since <s>padārthas</s> such as earth and the like are infinite, to the doubt 'how does the statement that categories are seven accord with the <s>Saṅgraha</s>?' — anticipating that the word 'seven' refers to any one of the seven limiting properties in the form of <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood) and the like, he resolves this in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [15] 'in the form of <s>dravyatva</s> and the like.' 'Seven limiting properties (<s>upādhis</s>)': now, what exactly is 'seven-ness' among these limiting properties? It cannot be in the form of a number (<s>saṅkhyā</s>), for the reason already stated. Even though oneness is in the form of number, seven-ness as a qualifier of <s>dravyatva</s> and the like cannot be in the form of number. Nor should it be said that its explanation is possible by admitting an error — because for those who are not in error, since such an error is impossible, the usage of 'seven' regarding the limiting properties would be untenable for them. Nevertheless, oneness is a property occurring in only one [thing]. And the occurrence-in-only-one-hood is

children.translated_text: it should be stated as: qualification through the relation of possessing a set of seven differences whose counter-positiveness-hood and delimiter-hood reside in oneself, delimited by the relation of possessing difference whose counter-positiveness-hood and delimiter-hood reside in oneself. And if it be objected that even there, since seven-ness among the differences must be stated in the same manner, and since only a particular relational cognition (<s>apekṣābuddhi</s>) must be stated, there would be an infinite regress — no, [that is not so]. The content-hood of the particular relational cognition here is: the cognition qualified by oneness-mode-hood residing in substance-hood-residing-qualificand-hood, qualified by oneness-mode-hood residing in quality-hood-residing-qualificand-hood, and so forth — the possession of that [cognition] through the relation of qualificand-hood; and since the possession of that qualified [cognition] through the relation of qualificand-hood is admitted only in <s>dravyatva</s> and the like, there is no over-extension even admitting a collective apprehension (<s>samūhālambana</s>). 'The qualification is through the relation of co-occurrence (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>).' [15] 'Thus of the subsequent passage also': the meaning is 'there are exactly nine substances' and the like. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'because it serves to exclude a higher number': here, the word 'higher number' refers to an eighth category. 'Exclusion' means the establishment of negation. And thus, just as in 'bring three <s>brāhmaṇas</s>' and the like, the fourth and subsequent <s>brāhmaṇas</s> are negated, so too the eighth category is established as negated — this is the meaning. The number qualified by the seven-ness in question, through both relations of occurring-in-what-occurs-in-one's-own-locus and occurring-in-what-does-not-occur-in-one's-own-locus, is the referent of 'higher number.' [15] 'Now, an additional category': although this alternative — that either the <s>dharmin</s> in the form of an additional-category-property is unestablished, or the extreme of not-being-validly-cognized is unestablished — does not hold, nevertheless the meaning is: whether or not a validly cognized category, or a property that divides categories, is additional.

children.text:
1. svāśrayavṛttitveti/

tadvṛttitvaṃ aṣṭatvasaṃkhyāyām/
children.translated_text: 1. '<s>Svāśrayavṛttitva</s>': 'self' is the number seven-ness; 'its loci' are the seven categories; 'occurring in them' pertains to the number eight-ness. Similarly, 'self' is seven-ness; 'what is not its locus' is the eighth category; 'occurring in it' pertains to the number eight-ness.

children.text:
atiriktatvaṃ ca
dravyatvādyabhāvatvāntānyatamādhikaraṇavṛttitvam/ tathā ca
padārthavibhājakadharmaḥ tādṛśādhikaraṇavṛttirnavetyartho labhyata iti
dharmiprasiddhyā koṭiprasiddhyā ca vikalpasiddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: And 'additionalness' (<s>atiriktatva</s>) means occurring in a locus that is any one among <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood) through <s>abhāvatva</s> (absence-hood). And thus, the meaning obtained is that the property dividing categories does not occur in such a locus — in nine [categories rather than seven]. Hence, through the establishment of the <s>dharmin</s> and through the establishment of the extreme, both alternatives are established.

children.translated_text: As for the [objection]: 'since the aggregate-possessing-ness (<s>kūṭavattva</s>) of the distinctions of <s>dravya</s> and the like, being itself of the nature of a set of such distinctions, due to the non-additionalness of each component of the aggregate, lacks occurrence in a validly cognized category — this is untenable; since in an alternative there is the rule that one extreme must not be contradicted; since the absence having counter-positiveness delimited by a universally occurring (<s>vyāsajyavṛtti</s>) property and occurring in only a part is not authoritative; since the aggregate-locus-hood of such a kind is also unestablished; and since aggregate-hood is difficult to state — therefore the meaning of the alternative is: does a validly cognized category possess the aggregate of distinctions from <s>dravya</s> and the like, or not?' — even that is not [correct]. Because when the distinctions are included as each qualified by another, since such-content-hood of a cognition having that many objects exists individually in each distinction, there is no occasion for unestablishedness. [16] 'Because it serves to exclude' — the meaning is: because it has as its result a determinate cognition of such a form. Nor should it be doubted that 'let there simply not be such a determination' — because in establishing that the sixteen categories [of <s>Nyāya</s>] are subsumed within the established categories, such a determination of pervasion is necessarily required. [15] 'In the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, substance, quality' and so forth: here, the connection of <s>dravya</s> and the like with what is delimited by <s>padārthatva</s> (category-hood) is through the relation of being-any-one-of-<s>dravya</s>-and-the-like, in the manner of 'two in one [place],' due to the variety of derivational analysis. But the cognition '<s>padārthatva</s> is pervaded by being-any-one-of-the-seven-<s>dravya</s>-and-the-like' is a subsequent mental cognition. This has been elaborated by us elsewhere.

children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [15] 'being-any-one-of-the-seven-<s>dravya</s>-and-the-like' and so forth: here the intention is as follows — the distinction of quality qualified by the distinction of substance through the relation of co-occurrence, the distinction of action (<s>karma</s>) qualified by that, the distinction of universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) qualified by that, the distinction of particularity (<s>viśeṣa</s>) qualified by that, the distinction of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) qualified by that, the distinction of absence (<s>abhāva</s>) qualified by that — being-any-one-of-<s>dravya</s>-and-the-like is precisely the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by <s>abhāvatva</s> (absence-hood) through the relation of self-nature (<s>svarūpasambandha</s>) as co-relatum, and whose substratum-hood is delimited by [the same]. The reverse should be understood similarly. Otherwise, if it were in the form of an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the seven-ness of the distinctions of <s>dravya</s> and the like, then since seven-ness would be difficult to state, the consequence would be that such an absence too would be unestablished. Although it is easy to state that seven-ness has the nature of being the content of a particular cognition having that as its object, nevertheless, since there is no authoritative basis for content-hood being universally occurring (<s>vyāsajyavṛtti</s>), the absolute absence delimited by it occurs in each of <s>dravya</s> and the like individually. But in our view, since such a relation is

vyadhikaraṇatayā
