sudhībhiḥ vibhāvanīyam/ [16] vastutastvityādi/ idamatra
cintyam-padārthatvaṃ dravyādyanyatamatvavyāpyam, saptatvaṃ ca
tadviṣayakadhīviṣayakatvarūpamityuktayaiva sāmāñjasye dravyapadasya
dravyatvaparatvaṃ anyatamapadasyānyatamavatparatvaṃ ca vinā lakṣaṇāṃ na
nirvahatīti lakṣaṇāśrayaṇamayuktam/ kiñcillakṣaṇā hi śakyasambandharūpā
dravyādyanyatamasya
children.translated_text: in a different locus with respect to such a distinction, and since the establishment of an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a relation occurring in a different locus is easy — this should be discerned by the wise. [16] 'But in reality' and so forth: this should be considered here — if it is said that <s>padārthatva</s> is pervaded by being-any-one-of-<s>dravya</s>-and-the-like, and that seven-ness has the nature of being the content of a cognition having that as its object, then for this to be consistent, without secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), the word '<s>dravya</s>' cannot refer to <s>dravyatva</s>, nor can the word '<s>anyatama</s>' refer to what possesses <s>anyatama</s>-ness — hence it does not work without recourse to secondary signification. And the adoption of secondary signification is improper. For secondary signification is in the form of a relation with what is denoted (<s>śakyasambandha</s>), and since being-any-one-of-<s>dravya</s>-and-the-like

children.text:
śakyārthatvābhāvāt
tādṛśānyatamavati lakṣaṇā na śakyate/ tathā śaktyaprasiddhiḥ
upapādanāyaiva/
children.translated_text: lacks the status of being a denoted meaning, secondary signification cannot apply to what possesses such <s>anyatama</s>-ness. Similarly, [the argument regarding] the unestablishedness of denotative power is precisely for the purpose of demonstrating [this point].

children.text: dravyavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Classification of Substances (<s>Dravyavibhāga</s>)

children.text:
dravyamiti jātyekavacanamiti/ nanvatra kiṃ
nāma jātigatamekatvam? na tāvat guṇaḥ/ tatra tadanaṅgīkārāt/
nāpi sajātīyadvitīyaṃrāhityam, siddhyasiddhibhyāṃ vyāghātām
iti cet, ucyate-ekamātravṛttidharmāvacchinne ekavacanasya śaktiḥ/
vyaktyekatvaparavākyasthale 'paśunā yajeta' ityādau
1svāśrayatvasvavṛttipratiyogitāvacchedakatvobhayasambandhena
prakṛtyarthe 'nvayaḥ/ avacchedakatvaṃ ca
svakaraṇakayāgakaraṇībhūtapaśvādivṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasambandhena
avacchedakatā cāśrayatāsambandhena/ jātyekatvaparavākyasthale
dravyamityādau tu
2svāśrayāśrayatvasvakarmakavibhāgakarmībhūtadravyavṛttibhedapratiyog itāvacchedaka-
children.translated_text: 'Substance' — this is the singular number denoting a universal (<s>jāti</s>). Objection: what exactly is the oneness belonging to the universal here? It is not, first of all, a quality, since that is not accepted there. Nor is it the absence of a second of the same kind, since there would be a contradiction from [the alternatives of] its being established or not established. Reply: the denotative power of the singular number pertains to what is delimited by a property that resides in only one [entity]. In the case of sentences where the singular refers to individual oneness, such as 'one should sacrifice with an animal,' the connection with the meaning of the nominal stem is through both relations: substratum-hood of itself and being the delimitor of counter-positiveness of a difference residing in what it resides in. The delimitor-hood is through the relation of being the delimitor of counter-positiveness of a difference residing in the animal and the like that constitute the instrument of the sacrifice whose instrument is itself. And the delimitor-ness is through the relation of substratum-hood. In the case of sentences where the singular refers to the oneness of the universal, such as 'substance' and so forth, however, [the connection with the meaning of the nominal stem is through both relations:] being the delimitor of counter-positiveness delimited by the relation of the delimitor-hood of counter-positiveness of a difference residing in the substance that has become the object of the division whose agent is itself, [and]

children.text:
tvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhapratiyogitāvacchedakatākatvobhayasambandhena
prakṛtyarthe 'nvayaḥ/ sā ca svāśrayāśrayatvasambandhena/ ekatvamanyatrāpi
bodhyam/
children.translated_text: the connection with the meaning of the nominal stem is through both relations of the having-ness of the delimitor-hood of counter-positiveness residing in itself, delimited by the relation of that [delimitor-hood]. And that [delimitor-ness] is through the relation of substratum-hood of the substratum of itself. Oneness elsewhere too should be understood [in a similar manner].

children.text:
1. svāśrayatveti/ svaṃ
ekatvam, tadāśrayatvaṃ prakṛtyarthe paśau, evaṃ svaṃ ekatvaṃ tadvṛttiḥ
paśumadbhedaḥ tatpratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ ca paśau/ svakaraṇaketyatra
svaśabdaḥ prakṛtyarthapaśuparaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Substratum-hood of itself' — 'itself' refers to oneness; its substratum-hood is in the animal, which is the meaning of the nominal stem. Thus, 'itself' is oneness; what it resides in is the difference possessing the animal; the delimitor-hood of counter-positiveness of that is in the animal. In 'whose instrument is itself,' the word 'itself' refers to the animal, which is the meaning of the nominal stem.

children.text:
2.
svāśrayāśrayatvetyādi/ prathavasvaśabdaḥ ekatvaparaḥ/ dvitīyasvaśabdaḥ
tṛtīyasvaśabdaśca prakṛtyarthadravyaparaḥ/
svaniṣṭhapratiyogitāvacchedakatākatvamityasya svaniṣṭhā yā
bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā tatkatvamityarthaḥ/
svaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvamiti yāvat/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 2. 'Substratum-hood of the substratum of itself' and so forth — the first word 'itself' refers to oneness. The second and third words 'itself' refer to substance, which is the meaning of the nominal stem. The meaning of 'having the delimitor-hood of counter-positiveness residing in itself' is: having-ness of the delimitor-hood of counter-positiveness of the difference residing in itself. That is to say: possessing a difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor-hood residing in itself.

children.text:
mīmāṃsakamatamityādi/ dūṣaṇaṃ
anupapannatvaprakārakajñānānukūlayuktikathanam/ tumuna icchaivārthaḥ,
tasyāḥ upanyāse 1pūrvavadevānvayaḥ/ [24] atiriktatvaṃ
vyasthāpayitum ityatrāpi uktarītireva/ nirākaraṇaṃ tu
abhāvaprakārakajñānānukūlaśabdaḥ/ [24] antarbhāvamityatra
dvitīyāyāḥ pratiyogitvamarthaḥ/ tasya nirākaraṇaikadeśe 'bhāve 'nvayaḥ/
dīpikāyāñ [24] pratītibalādityatra balaśabdena
viṣayasādhakatvaṃ dyotyate/ ataḥ tasyā bhramatve na viṣayasādhakatvamiti
śaṅkānirāsāyābādhitetyuktam/ nīletyādi/ atra ca
dravyasādhakahetudvayakathanaṃ 2nyūnādhikadṛṣṭāntamabhisandhāya/ [24] kālikādisambandheneti/ atrādipadena viṣayatāsambandhasya
parigrahaḥ/ na tu daiśikaviśeṣaṇatāyāḥ, tathā sati mūrteṣu
sādhyasattvena vyabhicārānavakāśāt/ [24] atiprasaktatve 'pīti/
janyaguṇadāvityādiḥ/ dravyatve siddhe satīti/ atra dravyatva iti
saptamyāḥ anumitirūpasiddhirarthaḥ/ tasyā uttarakālīnatvasambandhena
nirākaraṇe 'nvayaḥ/ dīpikāyām [23] tamaso
nākāśādipañcake 'ntarbhāva iti/
ākāśādipañcakānyatamatvatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ
tamovṛttirityanvayabodhaḥ/ [23]
na vāyāviti pṛthakkaraṇaṃ
vāyāvanantarbhūtatvasādhakahetvantarasattvāt/ na hi sparśābhāvāderapi
ākāśādyanantarbhūntatvasādhakatvaṃ sambhavati, 3vyabhicārāt/
navīnamatamanusṛtya prakāśikāyām [24] vastutastviti/
children.translated_text: 'The view of the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>s' and so forth. A refutation is the statement of a reason favorable to a cognition having the form 'it is untenable.' The infinitive suffix (<s>tumun</s>) means desire; when it is presented, the connection is just as before. [24] In 'to establish the distinctness' too, the same method applies. 'Rejection' is a word favorable to a cognition having the form of absence. [24] In 'the inclusion,' the meaning of the accusative is counter-positiveness; its connection is with the absence that is a part of the rejection. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [24] in 'by the force of cognition,' the word 'force' indicates the capacity to establish the object. Therefore, to remove the doubt that if it is erroneous it would not have the capacity to establish the object, 'unsublated' is stated. 'Blue' and so forth — and here the statement of two reasons establishing substance-hood is with a view to examples that are fewer or greater [than the probandum's extension]. [24] 'Through the relation of time and the like' — here the word 'and the like' includes the relation of objecthood, but not of spatial qualifier-ness, since in that case there would be no room for deviation in corporeal things where the probandum exists. [24] 'Even when over-extension [applies]' — and so forth such as 'in produced qualities.' 'When substance-hood is established' — here the meaning of the locative 'in substance-hood' is establishment in the form of inference; the connection with the rejection is through the relation of subsequence to that. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [23] 'Darkness is not included in the group of five beginning with <s>ākāśa</s>' — the understanding of the connection is: an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by being any one of the five beginning with <s>ākāśa</s> resides in darkness. [23] 'Not in air' — the separate treatment is because there exists another reason establishing non-inclusion. For the absence of touch and the like cannot establish non-inclusion in <s>ākāśa</s> and the like, because of deviation.

children.text:
1. pūrvavadevānvaya
iti/
svaviṣayasamānakartṛkatvasvaprayojyecchāviṣayatvobhayasaṃbandhenānvayaḥ
ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'The connection is just as before' — the meaning is: the connection is through both relations of being the same agent as what is one's own object and being the object of the desire prompted by oneself.

children.text:
2.
nyūnādhikadṛṣṭāntamabhisamndhāyeti/ tamaso
dravyatvasādhakanīlatvahetoḥ nīladravyāṇyeva ddaṣṭhāntaḥ, tamaso
dravyatvasādhakakriyāvattvahetostu mūrtadravyāṇi dṛṣṭānta ityevaṃ
tātpayam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 2. 'With a view to examples that are fewer or greater' — the purport is thus: for the reason of blueness establishing the substance-hood of darkness, only blue substances are the example; but for the reason of possessing activity establishing the substance-hood of darkness, corporeal substances are the example.

children.text:
3. vyabhicārāditi/
tamaḥ ākāśādyanantarbhūtaṃ sparśābhāvāditi hi prayoktavyam/ tatra ca
sādhyābhāvavati ākāśādau sparśābhāvasattvāt vyabhicāra ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 3. 'Because of deviation' — for the inference should be: 'darkness is not included in <s>ākāśa</s> and the like, because of the absence of touch.' But there, in <s>ākāśa</s> and the like where the probandum's absence obtains, the absence of touch exists — hence there is deviation, this is the meaning.

children.text:
viṣamavyāptamiti/ viṣamavyāptatvaṃ ca
sādhyāvyāpakatve sati sādhyavyāpyatvam/ samavyāptatvaṃ ca
sādhyavyāpakatve sati sādhyavyāpyatvam/ nanu
sadāgatimattvābhāvādityatra hetau sadāgatiśabdena yogavyutpattyā
sārvakālikagamanaṃ labhyate/
children.translated_text: 'Unevenly pervaded' — unevenly pervaded means being pervaded by the probandum while not being a pervader of the probandum. Evenly pervaded means being pervaded by the probandum while also being a pervader of the probandum. Objection: in the probans 'because of the absence of possessing perpetual motion,' the word 'perpetual motion' (<s>sadāgati</s>) yields, through etymological derivation, 'motion at all times.'

children.text:
sārvakālikatvaṃ ca
kālatvanirūpitakālikasaṃbandhāvacchinnavyāpakatvaṃ, pralayādau
janyavāyorabhāvāt tadīyakriyāyāḥ tadānīṃ viraheṇa
kālatvavyāpakagamanarūpasadāgatiśabdārthasya janyavāyāvabhāvena
children.translated_text: And 'at-all-times-ness' is pervader-hood delimited by the temporal relation determined by time-ness. Since produced air does not exist at the time of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) and the like, and since its activity is absent at that time, the referent of the word 'perpetual motion' in the form of motion that pervades time-ness does not exist in produced air,

children.text:
1tadabhāvena
vāyvanantarbhūntatvasādhane vyabhicāra ityata āha -- [24] sadāgatiḥ vijātīyakriyeti/ evaṃ ca vaijātyaviśeṣasya
janyavāyukriyāyāmapi sattvāt na doṣa iti bhāvaḥ/
kḷptadravyeṣvanantarbhāvādityartha iti/ idamatra pariśeṣānumānaṃ
vivakṣitam - tamaḥ pṛthivyādibhedakūṭadravyatvobhayavat
pṛthivyādyanantarbhūntatvadravyatvobhayasmāt yannaivaṃ tannaivaṃ
children.translated_text: and due to its absence, there would be deviation in establishing non-inclusion in air. Therefore he says — [24] 'Perpetual motion means activity different in kind.' And thus, since the particular difference in kind exists even in the activity of produced air, there is no defect — this is the purport. 'Because of non-inclusion in established substances' — this is the meaning. The inference by elimination intended here is: darkness possesses both the property of being different from earth and the like and the property of being a particular substance (<s>kūṭadravyatva</s>); [this is inferred] from both the property of non-inclusion in earth and the like and the property of substance-hood; whatever is not so is not so,

children.text:
yathā ghaṭa iti/
atrābhāvarūpatayā tamasaḥ naiyāyikairabhyupagamāt siddhasādhanavāraṇāya
sādhyakoṭau dravyatvaniveśaḥ/ guṇādau vyabhicāravāraṇāya
hetukoṭau dravyatvaniveśaḥ/ guṇādau vyabhicāravāraṇāya
hetukoṭau dravyatvaniveśaḥ/ guṇādau vyabhicāravāraṇāya
hetukoṭau dravyatvaniveśaḥ/ pṛthivyādau vyabhicāravāraṇāya
pṛthivyādīti/
children.translated_text: as in the case of a pot. Here, since darkness is accepted by the <s>Naiyāyika</s>s as having the nature of absence, substance-hood is included in the probandum-side to prevent the fallacy of proving what is already established. Substance-hood is included in the probans-side to prevent deviation in qualities and the like. Substance-hood is included in the probans-side to prevent deviation in qualities and the like. Substance-hood is included in the probans-side to prevent deviation in qualities and the like. 'Earth and the like' is to prevent deviation in earth and the like.

children.text:
yattu-sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena
pṛthivyādibhedakūṭaviśiṣṭadravyatvaṃ sādhyaṃ
pṛthivyādyanantarbhūntatvaviśiṣṭadravyatvaṃ heturiti/ tanna/
naiyāyikamate 'numiteḥ prāk sādhyahetvoraprasiddhatayā
vyatirekavyāpterdurgrahatvāditi/ dīpikāyām [23] prauḍhetyādi/ prauḍhatvamutkṛṣṭatvaṃ mahattvāśrayatvam, tejaḥ
paramāṇuvāraṇāya mahatvaniveśaḥ/
tejastruṭivāraṇayotkṛṣṭatvaniveśaḥ/ prakāśakatvaṃ
codbhūtānabhibhūtarūpavattvam/ cakṣurādivāraṇāyodbhūteti/
suvarṇādivāraṇāyānabhibhūteti/ ghaṭādivāraṇāya tejaḥ- padam/
yadyapi udbhūtatvasya vakṣyamāṇarītyā
tattadanudbhūtatvābhāvakūṭarūpatayā
pratiyogitānavacchedakānanugamāt tamaḥ padārthanānātvaṃ prasajyate,
children.translated_text: As for [the alternative formulation that] the probandum is substance-hood qualified by the aggregate of differences from earth and the like through the relation of co-location, and the probans is substance-hood qualified by non-inclusion in earth and the like — that is not correct, because in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, since the probandum and probans are not established prior to the inference, the negative pervasion (<s>vyatirekavyāpti</s>) is difficult to grasp. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [23] 'Intense' and so forth — intensity means excellence, i.e. being the substratum of greatness. The inclusion of 'greatness' is to exclude the atoms of <s>tejas</s> (fire-element). The inclusion of 'excellence' is to exclude the triads (<s>truṭi</s>) of <s>tejas</s>. Illuminating capacity is possessing manifest and unsuppressed color. 'Manifest' is to exclude the sense-organs such as the eye. 'Unsuppressed' is to exclude gold and the like. The word '<s>tejas</s>' is to exclude pots and the like. Although, since manifest-ness, being in the form of an aggregate of absences of respective non-manifest-nesses, does not allow a common delimitor of counter-positiveness to be tracked, there would be the unwanted consequence that the category of darkness would become manifold,

children.text:
1. tadabhāveneti/
sadāgatimattvabhāvene tyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Due to its absence' — the meaning is: due to the absence of possessing perpetual motion.

children.text:
tathāpi
mahāprabhāvatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāva eva tamaḥ/
prauḍhaprakāśakatejaḥśabdena ca mahāprabhaiva vivakṣitamiti abhipretyaivāgre
digityuktam/ prakāśikāyām [24]
ālokāsahakṛteti/
ālokājanyacākṣuṣanirūpitalaukikaviṣayatvāditi paryavasitārthaḥ/
tenānyatra cakṣuṣaḥ ālokarūpasahakārikāraṇaviśiṣṭatve 'pi na kṣatiḥ/
children.translated_text: nevertheless, darkness is precisely the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by possessing great luminosity (<s>mahāprabhāvatva</s>). And the word 'intense illuminating fire-element' (<s>prauḍhaprakāśakatejas</s>) is intended to denote precisely great luminosity — understanding this, 'direction' is stated later. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [24] 'Not assisted by light' — the resolved meaning is: because of being the object of ordinary visual cognition not produced by light (<s>āloka</s>). Therefore, even though the eye elsewhere has the specific character of being assisted by the auxiliary cause in the form of light, there is no harm.

children.text:
nanu tamaḥ pratyakṣe 'pi
kālavidhayā ālokasya kāraṇatvāt asiddhiriti cet - na/
kālatvāvacchinnālokaniṣṭhajanakatākatvābhāvasya niveśāt/
spārśanamādāya ghaṭādau vyabhicāravāraṇāya cākṣuṣeti/ viṣayatāyāṃ
laukikatvaniveśe prayojanamāha - [24] tamasaścākṣuṣe 'pi
ghaṭādīnāmityādinā/ 'ghaṭe tama' ityākārakapratyakṣe 'laukikyā
jñānapratyāsattyā ghaṭādīnāṃ viṣayatve 'pi na tatra vyabhicāra ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: even in the perception of darkness, since light is a cause in the mode of time, there is non-establishment [of the probans]. Reply: no, because what is included is the absence of the having-ness of a generative capacity residing in light delimited by time-ness. 'Visual' is to prevent deviation in pots and the like by taking tactile [perception into account]. He states the purpose of including 'ordinary' in the objecthood — [24] 'Even in the visual [perception] of darkness, pots and the like' and so forth. In the perception of the form 'the pot has darkness,' even though pots and the like have objecthood through extraordinary (<s>alaukika</s>) cognitive proximity (<s>jñānapratyāsatti</s>), there is no deviation there — this is the meaning.

children.text:
atra cādhunātaneṣu
pustakepu 'tamovān ghaṭaḥ' iti pāṭho 'nupapannaḥ/"asmāyāmedhāsrajoviniḥ"
iti sūtreṇa tasmasvītyeva
rūpaniṣpatteḥ/ matupguṇayorasambhavāt/ upanītaṃ viśeṣaṇatayaiveti
niyamenālaukikajñānapratyāsattyā ghaṭādīnāṃ viśeṣyatayā
bhānāsaṃbhavenālaukikaviṣayatāmādāya ghaṭādau vyabhicārāsambhavācca/
atastādṛśapāṭho bhrāntatamaḥ
children.translated_text: And here, in modern manuscripts the reading 'the pot possesses darkness' (<s>tamovān ghaṭaḥ</s>) is incorrect. Since by the <s>sūtra</s> 'asmāyāmedhāsrajoviniḥ,' the form must be 'tasmasvī,' [and] since the <s>matup</s> suffix is impossible with qualities. Since what is cognized [in perception] is presented only as a qualifier, and by this restriction, since the appearance of pots and the like as qualificands through extraordinary cognitive proximity is impossible, and since by taking extraordinary objecthood there is no possibility of deviation in pots and the like — therefore such a reading is utterly erroneous,

children.text:
prakṣipta iti
vidāṅkurvantu vidvāṃsaḥ/ [24]
viśeṣābhāvaṃ
vyāpyadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvam/ idaṃ ca
pakṣadṛṣṭāntayorabhedaśaṅkānirāsāya/ ayamatra bhāvaḥ -
kāryatāvacchedakakoṭau tamobhinnatvasya dravyaviśeṣaṇatvamupagamya
tamobhinnadravyavṛttilaukikaviṣayatāsambandhena cākṣuṣaṃ prati
saṃyogenālokasya kāraṇatve yadyapi na doṣaḥ, tathāpi tamaso
dravyatve kāryatāvacchedakakoṭau tamobhinnatvaniveśāt
gauravamanantāvayavakalpanayāpi/ tattamaścākṣuṣasyākasmikatvavāraṇāya
asādhāraṇakāraṇāntarakalpanasyāvaśyakatayā gauravamiti/ [25] prāgabhāvādītyādipadenadhvaṃsaparigrahaḥ/ [25] āvaśyaketi/ idaṃ ca tamobhāva eva tejaḥ kiṃ na syāditi
vinigamanāvirahaśaṅkānirāsāya/ anyathā 'uṣṇaṃ tejaḥ' iti
uṣṇasparśapratītyanupapattiprasaṅgāt/
children.translated_text: interpolated — let the learned recognize this. [24] 'The absence of a particular' means an absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by a property that delimits the pervaded. And this is for removing the doubt of non-difference between the <s>pakṣa</s> and the example. The purport here is this: even if one accepts, in the delimitor-side of the effect-hood, the being-different-from-darkness as a qualifier of substance, and [holds that] light is a cause of visual perception through the relation of conjunction with respect to ordinary objecthood pertaining to substances different from darkness — although there is no defect in that — nevertheless, if darkness is [accepted as] a substance, since being-different-from-darkness must be included in the delimitor-side of effect-hood, there is prolixity even with the postulation of infinite components. For, to prevent the visual perception of darkness from being causeless, the postulation of another uncommon cause is necessary, hence the prolixity. [25] 'Prior absence and the like' — the word 'and the like' includes destruction. [25] 'Necessary' — and this is for removing the doubt of the lack of determination, namely 'why should not fire-element itself be the absence of darkness?' Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that the cognition of hot touch in 'fire-element is hot' would be inexplicable.

children.text: dravyalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of substance (<s>dravya</s>)

children.text:
dīpikāyām [31] dravyatvajātimattvamiti/ atra jātipadaṃ samavāyena dravyatvasya
lakṣaṇatvalābhāya/ na tu tadapi lakṣaṇaghaṭakaṃ, tathā sati
svasamānādhikaraṇavyāpyatāvacchedakadharmāntaraghaṭitatayā
vyāpyatānavacchedakatvena vyāpyatvāsiddhyāpātāt/ prakāśikāyām
[31] saṃyogajanakatāvacchedakatayeti/ atredamanumānamabhimatam -
saṃyoganiṣṭhasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitatādātmyasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatā
kiñciddharmāvacchinnā kāraṇatāttvāt
daṇḍādiniṣṭhaghaṭādikāraṇatāvaditi/ 'siṃdhyato dharmasya jātitve
lāghavam' iti tarkasahakṛtājjātitve bādhakābhāvasahitācca
parāmarśāt dravyatvajātyavacchinnatvasiddhiḥ/ kiñcijjātyavacchinnatvasya
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [31] 'Possessing the universal substance-hood' — here the word 'universal' (<s>jāti</s>) is for the purpose of <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood) obtaining the status of a definition through [the relation of] inherence. It is not itself a component of the definition, since in that case, being constituted by another property that delimits the pervaded-ness co-located with itself, it would not delimit the pervaded-ness, and there would be the unwanted consequence of unestablished pervasion. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [31] 'As the delimitor of the causal capacity of conjunction' — the inference intended here is: the causal capacity, delimited by the relation of identity, that determines the effect-hood delimited by the relation of inherence residing in conjunction, is delimited by some property, because it is a causal capacity — as in the causal capacity of a stick and the like for a pot and the like. From the <s>tarka</s> (suppositional reasoning) assisted by 'there is economy in the universal-hood of the establishing property,' together with the consideration accompanied by the absence of a sublator regarding universal-hood, the establishment that [substance-hood] is delimited by a universal is achieved. Of the having-ness delimited by some universal,

children.text:
sādhyatve
pratibandhakābhāvaniṣṭhakāraṇatāyāṃ vyabhicāraḥ syāditi tadupekṣitam/
na ca sattāṃ pṛthivītvādikāṃ ca jātimādāyānumānaparyavasānāt
arthāntaramiti vācyam/ tatsamaniyatadharmasyaiva tadavacchedakatvāt
sattādau tadvyāpyatvādigrahasya prakṛte sattvena
tadādāyānumānaparyavasānāsambhavāt/ 'sattādikaṃ yadi
saṃyogasamavāyikāraṇatāvacchedakaṃ syāt tarhi
saṃyogasamavāyikāraṇatāsamaniyataṃ syāt' iti tarkavalāt
sattādijātyavacchinnatvānumityasambhavāt/ evamuttaratrāpi bodhyam/
samavāyena saṃyogaṃ prati tādātmyena dravyatvena kāraṇatvaṃ guṇādau
samavāyena saṃyogāpattivāraṇāya bodhyam/
children.translated_text: if that were the probandum, there would be deviation in the causal capacity residing in the absence of an obstructor — hence that is disregarded. Nor should one say that since the inference terminates in accepting <s>sattā</s> (existence) or a universal like <s>pṛthivītva</s> (earth-ness), this is a different matter — because only a property co-extensive with it can be its delimitor, and since the grasp of pervaded-ness and the like in <s>sattā</s> and the like is relevant to the present context, the inference cannot terminate in accepting those. Because from the force of the <s>tarka</s> 'if <s>sattā</s> and the like were the delimitor of the causal capacity as the material cause of conjunction, then they would be co-extensive with that causal capacity,' the inference of delimitation by the universal <s>sattā</s> and the like is impossible. The same should be understood in subsequent cases as well. It should be understood that substance-hood is the cause through the relation of identity with respect to conjunction through the relation of inherence — this is to prevent the unwanted consequence of conjunction arising through inherence in qualities and the like.

children.text:
lakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchedakayorabheda iti/
tathā sati lakṣaṇenetarabhedānumāne parāmarśakāle
itarabhedasamānādhikaraṇadravyatvaṃ dravyatvavyāpaketarabhedaḥ
ityākārakasiddhisattvāt anumityanupapattiḥ/
asamānākārakaniścayasyāpi pratibandhakatvāt/ siṣādhayiṣānudhāvane
ca prayāsagauravamityabhiprāyaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The definition and the delimitor of the defined-hood are non-different.' In that case, in the inference of difference-from-other through the definition, at the time of subsumptive reflection (<s>parāmarśa</s>), since there already exists the established cognition of the form 'substance-hood co-located with difference-from-other, and difference-from-other pervaded by substance-hood,' the inferential cognition becomes impossible — because even a determinate cognition of a different form [than the desired one] acts as an obstruction. And in pursuing the intended conclusion (<s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>), there would be the cumbersomeness of excessive effort — this is the purport.

children.text:
yattu -
lakṣaṇalakṣyatāvacchedakayorabhede upanayavākyāt śābdabodhānupapattiḥ
prakṛte 'pi sambhavati iti, tattuccham - dravyatvasya svarūpato
lakṣyatāvacchedakatvāt, dravyatvatvena ca lakṣaṇatvāt 'dravyatvavat
dravyam' ityākārakaprācīnamatopanayasya bādhakābhāvāt/
taddharmaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitaviśeṣyatānirūpitāvacchedakatāvacchedakatāsambandhena
śābdabuddhiṃ pratyeva taddharmabhedasya kāraṇatvasya vaktavyatvāt/ anyathā
'dravyaṃ jātimat' ityādiprayogānupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: As for [the objection] that even in the present context, the impossibility of verbal cognition from the application-sentence (<s>upanayavākya</s>) would obtain when the definition and the delimitor of defined-hood are non-different — that is trifling. Because substance-hood is a delimitor of defined-hood by its own nature (<s>svarūpataḥ</s>), and because it has definition-hood through substance-hood-ness, since there is no defeater for the application in the form 'substance has substance-hood' according to the old view. Because the causal role of the difference of that property must be stated only with respect to verbal cognition, through the relation of delimitor-hood-of-delimitor-hood that is determined by the qualificand-hood determined by the qualifier-mode-hood residing in that property. Otherwise, usages such as 'substance possesses a universal' would become impossible.

children.text: avyāptyādilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: The definition of under-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) and other [defects].

children.text:
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakatvābhimatasaṃbandhena
yatkiñcillakṣyāvṛttitvamityartha iti/
lakṣyatāvacchedakasamānādhikaraṇābhāvīyalakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitve
sati
lakṣyatāvacchedakādhikaraṇanirūpitalakṣaṇatāvacchedakasaṃbandhenādheyatvamavyāptiriti
niṣkarṣaḥ/ anyathā yathāśrute
lakṣyaikadeśamātrasādhāraṇānugatānatiprasaktasya durvacatayā
asambhavāpatteḥ/ asambhavino vāraṇāya dvitīyadalam,
gandhādisallakṣaṇavāraṇāya prathamadalam, pṛthivyādaiṃ saṃyogādinā
gandhādyabhāvasya sattvāt abhāvapratiyogitāyāṃ
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaniveśaḥ/ kālikasambandhena
gavāvṛttāvekaśaphādau tadvāraṇāya dvitīyadalaghaṭakādheyatāyāṃ
tatsambandhāvacchinnatvaniveśaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Non-occurrence in some defined instance through the relation accepted as the delimitor of definition-hood' — this is the meaning. The conclusion is: under-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) is the property of being a superstratum, through the relation that is the delimitor of definition-hood determined by the locus of the delimitor of defined-hood, while possessing counter-positive-hood delimited by the relation delimiting the definition-hood that belongs to the absence co-located with the delimitor of defined-hood. Otherwise, if taken literally, since [a property that is] common to merely a part of the defined instances, [which is] unextended [to all] and [yet] not over-extended, would be difficult to express, impossibility (<s>asambhava</s>) would result. The second clause is for blocking impossibility; the first clause is for blocking the [unwanted inclusion of] good definitions such as smell etc. — since the absence of smell etc. exists in earth etc. through conjunction and the like, the specification of being delimited by the relation that is the delimitor of definition-hood is inserted with respect to the counter-positive-hood of the absence. To block [the unwanted case] where single-hoofedness etc. are absent from cows through the temporal relation, the specification of being delimited by that relation is inserted with respect to the superstratum-hood that constitutes the second clause.

children.text:
na caivamapi
gandhaghaṭobhayābhāvaghaṭādivṛttitvaviśiṣṭagandhādyabhāvāderghaṭādau
sattvāt taddoṣatādavasthyamiti vācyam/
tādṛśābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakaḥ tādṛśādheyatāvacchedakaśca yo
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakadharmaḥ tasya vivakṣitatvāt/ yadyapi
tādṛśābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakaṃ ghaṭatvagandhatvādikamapi, tathāpi
tādṛśapratiyogitāvacchedakatāparyāptyadhikaraṇatvavivakṣayā na doṣaḥ/
[33] alakṣye lakṣaṇasyeti/ 1viśeṣaṇatāviśeṣeṇa
lakṣyatāvacchedakāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedavannirūpitalakṣaṇatāghaṭakasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvamityarthaḥ/
ghaṭādau ghaṭādibhedāsattvāt gandhādaiṃ nātivyāptiḥ/ na vā kālikena
jalādau gandhasattvamādāya/
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that even so, the same defect persists because the absence of smell etc. qualified by the property of occurring in pots etc. — such as the absence of the pair smell-and-pot — exists in pots etc. [This does not hold] because the intended definition-hood-delimiting property is one that is the delimitor of the counter-positive-hood of such an absence and the delimitor of such superstratum-hood. Even though pot-hood, smell-hood etc. are also delimitors of the counter-positive-hood of such absences, there is no defect because the intention is that the locus-hood be co-extensive with (<s>paryāpti</s>) the delimitor of such counter-positive-hood. [33] 'Of the definition in what is not defined' — the meaning is: superstratum-hood delimited by the relation constituting definition-hood, which is determined by what possesses difference determined by counter-positive-hood delimited by the delimitor of defined-hood. Since the difference of pot etc. does not exist in pots etc., there is no over-pervasion to smell etc. Nor [is there over-pervasion] by accepting the existence of smell in water etc. through the temporal relation.

children.text:
1.
viśeṣaṇatāviśeṣeṇetyasya bhedavatve 'nvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: The syntactic connection of 'by the specific qualifier-hood' is with 'possessing difference.'

children.text:
nāpi pṛthivyādāveva
pṛthivyādibhedasya kālikasaṃbandhena sattvāt taddoṣatādavasthyam/
lakṣyamātrāvṛttitvamiti dīpikāvākyāt
mātrapadasyetaravyavacchedaparatve
lakṣyetarāvṛttitvaviśiṣṭalakṣyavṛttitvaṃ syābhāvaḥ asambhava iti
labhyate/ tacca na yujyate - ativyāptadharme 'tiprasaṅgāt ityataḥ
prakāśikāyāṃ mātrapadaṃ kṛtsnārthakatayā vyācaṣṭe [33] mātrapadamiti/ [33] sambandhaviśeṣetyādi/
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnodheyatāpratiyogitākasvarūpamevātrasaṃbandhaviśeṣaḥ/
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnādheyatāpratiyogikasvarūpasambandhāvacchinnalakṣyavṛttitvatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākā-
children.translated_text: Nor does the same defect persist because difference from earth etc. exists in earth etc. through the temporal relation. From the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'non-occurrence in the defined alone' (<s>lakṣyamātrāvṛttitva</s>), when the word 'alone' (<s>mātra</s>) is taken as excluding the other, what is obtained is that impossibility (<s>asambhava</s>) is non-occurrence in what is not defined, qualified by occurrence in the defined. But that is not tenable — because of over-extension to over-pervading properties. Therefore, in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, the word 'alone' is explained as having the sense of totality. [33] 'The word mātra' — [33] 'A specific relation' etc. The specific relation here is precisely the self-nature of the counter-positive-hood of the superstratum-hood delimited by the relation delimiting definition-hood. The impossibility (<s>asambhava</s>) that emerges is: an absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by occurrence-in-the-defined-ness delimited by the relation of self-nature — which is the counter-positive-hood of the superstratum-hood delimited by the relation delimiting definition-hood.

children.text:
bhāvo 'sambhava iti
paryavasitam/ tena dvitvādyavacchinnādheyatāpratiyogitākasvarūpasya
guṇādivṛttitvaṃ prati vyadhikaraṇatvāt/ atra ca mātrapadasya
samabhivyāhṛtapadārthatāvacchedakavyāpakatvārthakatayā
nirūpakatāsambandhāvacchinnalakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatvaṃ ādheyatve
labhyate/ tathā satyativyāptadharme 'tiprasaṅgāt
children.translated_text: Thus it is concluded that [impossibility is an absence]. Thereby, since the self-nature [relation] that is the counter-positive of superstratum-hood delimited by duality etc. is a different locus from the occurrence-in-quality-etc.-ness. And here, the word 'alone' (<s>mātra</s>), by having the sense of being pervader of the delimitor of the co-occurring word-meaning, yields in the superstratum-hood the property of being pervader of the delimitor of defined-hood delimited by the relation of determiner-hood. That being so, there is over-extension in an over-pervading property.

children.text:
yāvatyo lakṣyavyaktayaḥ
tattadvyaktitvābhāvakūṭavattvaṃ tu durjñeyam, vinigamanāvirahābhyāṃ
vivakṣitumaśakyaṃ cetyālocya etat [33] lakṣyavṛttitvasāmānyābhāvasphorakamiti/
children.translated_text: As for the collection of absences of the respective individual-hoods corresponding to all the defined instances — that is difficult to ascertain, and since it cannot be intended [as the definition] due to the absence of a determiner — reflecting thus, this [formulation is offered]: [33] 'The absence of the general property of occurrence-in-the-defined makes it clear.'

children.text:
vastutastu
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakābhāvīyalakṣaṇatāghaṭasambandhāvacchinnaprati yogitāvacchedakalakṣaṇatāvacchedaka-
children.translated_text: In reality, however, impossibility is: possessing the definition-hood-delimiting property — [where the relevant conditions involve] counter-positive-hood of the definition-hood-delimiting relation constituting definition-hood, which [relates to] the absence that pervades the delimitor of defined-hood.

children.text:
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakadharmavattvamasambhavaḥ/ lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatvaṃ
ca
lakṣyatāvacchedakasamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakadhamravattvam,
na tu tādṛśābhāvāpratiyogitvam; sarveṣāmeva
dvitvādyavacchinnapratiyogitayā asambhavāpatteḥ/ etena viśeṣarūpeṇa
saṃsargatvānabhyupagame 'pi na kṣatiḥ/
lakṣyatāvacchedakatāghaṭakasambandhādinā
lakṣyatāvacchedakādiprakāreṇaivādhikaraṇapraveśaḥ/ tena sambandhāntareṇa
lakṣyatāvacchedakādyadhikaraṇamādāya na doṣaḥ/ na vānavasthā/
children.translated_text: And being-pervader-of-the-delimitor-of-defined-hood is possessing a property that does not delimit the counter-positive-hood of an absolute absence co-located with the delimitor of defined-hood — not being a non-counter-positive of such an absence; because if so, everything would result in impossibility through counter-positive-hood delimited by duality etc. By this, even without accepting a specific relation as a relational qualifier, there is no difficulty — the entry into the locus is through the relation etc. constituting defined-hood-delimitor-hood, in the mode of the delimitor of defined-hood etc. Therefore, by taking the locus of the delimitor of defined-hood etc. through another relation, there is no defect. Nor is there an infinite regress.

children.text:
ekaśaphavattvamitīti/ yadyapi śate
pañcāśannyāyena gavāderapyekaśaphavattvamakṣatam, tathāpyekatvamatra na
saḍkhyārūpam/ api tu svāśrayapādavṛttitvasvabhinnatvobhayasambandhena
śaphaviśiṣṭānyatvarūpaṃ pāribhāṣikaṃ jñeyam/ ativyāptiśarīre
lakṣyavṛttitvaniveśanamanāvaśyakamityabhiprāyeṇa [33] duṣṭasaṅkarepīti, nyāyāditi/ duṣṭasvarūpaikye 'pi
doṣasvarūpayoḥ parasparaṃ bhinnatvāt tanniveśanamanāvaśyakamiti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Single-hoofedness' — although, by the maxim of 'fifty out of a hundred,' single-hoofedness is also preserved in cows etc., here 'oneness' (<s>ekatva</s>) is not in the sense of the number. Rather, it should be understood as a conventional (<s>pāribhāṣika</s>) term meaning: the otherness from hooves qualified by the dual relation of occurrence-in-hooves-of-one's-own-substrate and non-difference-from-oneself. With the intention that it is not necessary to include occurrence-in-the-defined in the body of the over-pervasion [definition] — [33] 'Even in a faulty conflation' — 'by the maxim' — the purport is that even though the faulty natures are the same, since the natures of the two defects are mutually different, including [both] is not necessary.

children.text:
atra kvacit
prācīnagrantheṣu digiti dṛśyate/ tatra cāyaṃ bhāvaḥ -
asambhavinyekaśaphavattvādau 'idamatrātivyāptam' iti
vyavahārābhāvāt lakṣyavṛttitvamavaśyaṃ niveśanīyamiti na
tatroktanyāyāvakāśaḥ/ ekatrāsambhavina evānyatra vyavahāre
bādhakābhāvāt tatroktanyāyāvakāśa iti/
children.translated_text: Here, in some old texts, [the reading] 'thus' (<s>dig</s>) is seen. The purport there is: since in impossibility-instances like single-hoofedness etc., the usage 'this is over-pervading here' does not occur, occurrence-in-the-defined must necessarily be included — hence the maxim stated there has no scope. Since when the impossibility-instance in one case is [used as] a usage in another, there is no defeater — the maxim stated there has scope.

children.text: lakṣaṇalakṣaṇavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Investigation of the definition of a [valid] definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>).

children.text:
nanu [30] 'etaddūṣaṇatrayarahito dharma' iti dīpikāvākyāt
tādṛśadoṣatrayatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāva eva lakṣaṇalakṣaṇamiti
labhyate/ tacca na yujyate/ avyāptyādipratyekadoṣagrastadharmeṃ'pi
tatsattvenātivyāpteḥ ityata āha [38] uktadūṣaṇābhāvatrayaviśiṣṭa
ityartha iti/ yāvat pratyekādhikaraṇasyaiva kūṭādhikaraṇatvāt na
doṣa iti bhāvaḥ/ [38] avyāptyādītyādipadenāsambhavaparigrahaḥ/
[38] anyādṛśamiti/ tathā ca asādhāraṇapadaṃ vakṣyamāṇārthe
pāribhāṣikamiti/ sādhāraṇaṃ na bhavatītyasādhāraṇaṃ iti vyutpattyā
sādhāraṇapadārthaḥ lakṣyavṛttitvaviśiṣṭālakṣyavṛttitvarūpaḥ
tadabhāvarūpāsādhāraṇapadārthasya yaugikasyāvyāptyasambhavagrastayoḥ
sattvena tādṛśārthānupapattiḥ, kiṃ ca 'etaddūṣaṇatrayarahitadharmo lakṣaṇam'
iti granthena virodhaśca ityasvārasyadvayaṃ manasi nidhāya
pāribhāṣikaṃ nirvaktītyapi bodhyamiti
prakāśikāvataraṇikātātparyam/ 'avyāptyasambhavagrastayorvāraṇāya
satyantam' iti
children.translated_text: Now, [33] from the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'a property free from these three defects,' what is obtained is that the definition of a [valid] definition is: the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the three-defect-hood of that kind. But that is not tenable — because there would be over-pervasion even to a property afflicted by each individual defect, since the triad [of defects] exists there. Therefore he says: [38] 'The meaning is: qualified by the triad of absences of the stated defects.' The purport is: since the locus of each individual [defect] is itself the locus of the collection, there is no defect. [38] Under-pervasion etc. — by the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), impossibility is included. [38] 'Of a different kind' — accordingly, the word 'uncommon' (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) is conventional (<s>pāribhāṣika</s>) in the sense to be stated. By the etymological derivation 'not common, hence uncommon,' the meaning of the word 'common' is: occurrence-in-what-is-not-defined qualified by occurrence-in-the-defined — whose absence-form is the conventional meaning of 'uncommon.' Since [this literal meaning of] uncommon exists even in [cases afflicted by] under-pervasion and impossibility, such a meaning would not work. Moreover, there would be a contradiction with the text 'a property free from these three defects is a definition.' Keeping these two undesirable consequences in mind, the <s>Prakāśikā</s> introduction indicates that [the author] explains it as conventional — this should also be understood. 'For blocking what is afflicted by under-pervasion and impossibility, [the word] absolute' —

children.text:
pāṭhaḥ prāmādikaḥ/
ekaśaphavattvādirūpasyāsambhavinaḥ
svavyāpakatatkatvarūpalakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvaviraheṇa
tatrāvyāptyaprasakteḥ/ [38] avyāptasyeti prācīnakośeṣu pāṭho
dṛśyate/ sa eva yuktaḥ/
children.translated_text: this reading is erroneous. Because since the impossibility-instance in the form of single-hoofedness etc. lacks the property of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-hood in the form of the pervader of itself, under-pervasion does not apply there. [38] 'Of the under-pervading' — this reading is seen in old manuscripts. That alone is correct.

children.text:
yattu - pṛthivyādikaṃ
samavāyena lakṣaṇamityādāvasambhavini gaganadāvativyāptiḥ/

children.translated_text: As for [the objection:] in [the definition] 'earth etc. is a definition through inherence,' in the impossibility-instance such as the sky, there is over-pervasion — because the property of being pervaded by the delimitor of defined-hood, in the form of occurrence in what possesses the absence of the delimitor of defined-hood, exists there. Thus the reading 'of what is afflicted by under-pervasion and impossibility' is also correct — this is not right. Because there would be the absurd consequence of incoherence with the over-pervasion to be stated regarding denotability (<s>abhidheyatva</s>) etc. Since the property of being pervaded in the form of its own pervader-hood-ness must necessarily be included, the correctness of that reading is impossible. If, however, one insists on the correctness of that reading, then it must be justified by including the property of being pervaded in the form of counter-positive-hood of difference co-located with itself — [where the difference is] one whose delimitor of counter-positive-hood is that of the absence belonging to what occurs in the locus of the delimitor of defined-hood, delimited by the relation delimiting that —

svāvacchinnādhikaraṇavṛttibhedapratiyogitānavacchedaka

vivakṣaṇīyamityarthaḥ/ [38] vyāpakatvādityādinā vyāpyatvaparigrahaḥ/
tathā ca lakṣyatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭa lakṣaṇatāvacchedakavattvaṃ
asādhāraṇatvamiti niṣkarṣaḥ/ vaiśiṣyaṃ ca
svavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasvādhikaraṇavṛttyabhāvīyatādṛśapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhā-
children.translated_text: which is the property of being pervaded in the form of counter-positive-hood delimited by the relation of delimitor-of-counter-positive-hood-hood. [38] From the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'that very uncommon property is called [a definition],' what is obtained is: being a property while being uncommon. Therein, the inclusion of the property-hood component is fruitless — because things like the sky, which occur in nothing, lack the property of being pervader of the delimitor of defined-hood, and hence under-pervasion does not extend there. Therefore, to show the purpose of that word, he says: [38] 'the word dharma (property).' [38] 'Through the relation constituting definition-hood' — the meaning is: what is to be intended is the possession of the definition-hood-delimiting property that does not delimit the counter-positive-hood of the difference occurring in the locus delimited by the relation delimiting defined-hood — [as well as being] that which does not delimit the counter-positive-hood of the absence occurring in the locus of the delimitor of defined-hood through the relation that is the delimitor of definition-hood — and is a delimitor of defined-hood. [38] 'Because of being a pervader' etc. — by this, the property of being pervaded is included. Accordingly, the conclusion is that uncommon-ness (<s>asādhāraṇatva</s>) is possessing the delimitor of definition-hood qualified by the delimitor of defined-hood. And the qualification is through the dual relation of possessing difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the delimitor of occurrence-in-oneself and by the delimitor of the counter-positive-hood of the absence occurring in one's own locus, of such a kind —

children.text:
1. avacchadekatvamiti/
prathamasambandhaghaṭakamavacchedakatvamityarthaḥ/ tathā ca lakṣyatāvacchedake
gotve yo bhedaḥ sāsnāditvavadbhedaḥ, tathā hi svaṃ sāsnāditvarūpaṃ
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakaṃ tadavacchinnasya sāsnādeḥ

tadvṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasya gotve 'bhāvāt
tādṛśabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakattvasambandhena na sāsnāditvavat
gotvaṃ iti gotvavṛttiḥ sāsnāditvavadbhedaḥ bhavati
tatpratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ sāsnāditve/ evaṃ svaṃ gotvaṃ
tadadhikaraṇavṛtyabhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ sāsnādittve nāstīti
tādṛśapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasambandhena gotvavadbhedaḥ
sāsnāditve 'stīti ubhayasambandhena lakṣyatāvacchedakagotvaviśiṣṭatvaṃ
lakṣaṇatāvacchedake sāsnāditve draṣṭavyam/ evaṃ ca
prathamadvitīyatṛtīyasva padāni lakṣyatāvacchedakaparāṇi, caturthasvapadaṃ
lakṣaṇatāvacchedakaparamiti vivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: "Unity of the delimitor" — the meaning is: the delimitor-hood that constitutes the first relation. And thus, the difference that exists in <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness), which is the delimitor of the definiendum-hood (<s>lakṣyatāvacchedaka</s>), is the difference possessing <s>sāsnāditva</s> (dewlap-possession-ness). That is to say: one's own <s>sāsnāditva</s> is the delimitor of the definition-hood (<s>lakṣaṇatāvacchedaka</s>); since in <s>gotva</s> there is no counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood of difference residing in that which is the locus of <s>sāsnādi</s> (dewlap etc.) — delimited by the definition-hood-delimitor through the relation of inherence — therefore <s>gotva</s> does not possess <s>sāsnāditva</s> through the relation of such difference-counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood. Thus, the difference possessing <s>sāsnāditva</s> that resides in <s>gotva</s> obtains, and its counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood is in <s>sāsnāditva</s>. Similarly, since one's own <s>gotva</s> — the counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood of the absence residing in the locus of that — does not exist in <s>sāsnāditva</s>, through the relation of such counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood there is in <s>sāsnāditva</s> a difference possessing <s>gotva</s>. Thus, through both relations, the qualification by <s>gotva</s> which is the delimitor of the definiendum-hood should be seen in <s>sāsnāditva</s> which is the delimitor of the definition-hood. And accordingly, the first, second, and third occurrences of the word 'sva' (own) refer to the delimitor of the definiendum-hood, while the fourth occurrence of 'sva' refers to the delimitor of the definition-hood — this is the distinction.

svāvacchinnādhikaraṇavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasaṃbandhena/

abhāvor'thaḥ/ ṇvulassampādakaḥ/ tathā ca
lakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpakatvasahitalakṣyatāvacchedaka1vyāpyatvarūpaviśiṣṭābhāvasampādakā
ityarthaḥ/ tādṛśābhāvaścātivyāpte2viśeṣyābhāvaprayuktaḥ/
avyāptyasambhavinośca viśeṣaṇābhāvaprayukta ityabhipretyāha - [38] ativyāptāviti/ pakṣatāvacchedakasāmānādhikaraṇyamātreṇa
hetvabhāvavattvaṃ bhāgāsiddhiḥ/ tadavacchedena tadabhāvavattvaṃ
svarūpāsiddhiriti vivekaḥ/ atra ca bhāgāsiddheḥ avacchedakāvacchedena
pakṣe hetumattājñānavirodhitayā, svarūpāsiddheḥ avacchedakāvacchedena
sāmānādhikaraṇyena ca pakṣe hetumattājñānavirodhitayā dvayorapi
pakṣadharmatājñānaṃ prati virodhitayā hetvābhāsatvamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: Through the relation of counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood of difference residing in the locus delimited by itself. To prevent the exclusion of smell and the like by conjunction and other [relations], in the pervader-hood the delimitation by the relation that constitutes the definition-hood is included. Since in water and the like, smell and the like exist through temporal and other relations, in the pervaded-hood that [delimitation] is included. The rest should be inferred by oneself. [38] "Those that undermine uncommonness (<s>asādhāraṇatva</s>)" — here, the prefix 'vi-' with the root 'ghaṭ' has the meaning of absence. The <s>ṇvul</s> suffix has the meaning of 'producer.' And thus the meaning is: those that produce the absence of the qualified [entity] having the form of pervaded-hood of the definiendum-hood-delimitor together with pervader-hood of the definiendum-hood-delimitor. Such an absence, in the case of over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>), is occasioned by the absence of the qualificand; and in the case of non-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) and impossibility, it is occasioned by the absence of the qualifier — intending this, he says: [38] "In over-extension" etc. Possessing the absence of the probans merely through co-location with the thesis-delimitor (<s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>) is partial non-establishment (<s>bhāgāsiddhi</s>). Possessing the absence of that delimited by that [delimitor] is intrinsic non-establishment (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>) — this is the distinction. And here it should be noted that both are pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) because of their opposition to the cognition of the thesis-property (<s>pakṣadharmatājñāna</s>) — partial non-establishment through delimitation by the delimitor opposing the cognition of the thesis possessing the probans, and intrinsic non-establishment through delimitation by the delimitor and through co-location opposing the cognition of the thesis possessing the probans.

ativyāptiriti/ vyāvartakasyetyatra
children.translated_text: "Exclusion alone" — the intent is this: 'The purpose of a definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is either exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) or conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>).' Exclusion is difference from others. Conventional usage is the word that generates cognition. Purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) is what is to be made known. And thus, having the capacity to exclude (<s>vyāvartakatva</s>) means being the means of inferring difference from others. Having conventional capacity (<s>vyāvahārikatva</s>) means being the means of inferring conventional usage. In the present context, one view holds that exclusion alone is what is to be conveyed by the definition. Another view holds that both exclusion and conventional usage are to be conveyed. On the first alternative, since only the capacity to exclude would be the delimitor of the definiendum-hood, there is over-extension in the manner to be stated. "Of the excluder" — here

"The absence of the qualifier" — the meaning is: occasioned by the absence of the qualifier whose form is the pervader-hood of the definiendum-hood-delimitor.

vyāṅpūrvakavṛtudhātoritarabhedor'thaḥ/
akapratyayasyānumitijanaka ityabhiprāyeṇāha [39] itarabhedānumitijanakasyetyartha iti/ anumitijanakatvaṃ
liṅgaparāmarśasyaiva, na tu parāmṛśyamānaliṅgasya/ tathā ca
gandhādervyāvartaṅkatvānupapattiḥ/ na

lakṣyatvāt/ na ca tādṛśajanakatāvacchedakaviṣayatāśrayatvaṃ taditi
vācyam/ evamapi itarabhedavyāptidhaṭakābhāvādāvativyāpteḥ
gotvādyavacchedena gavetarabhedavyāpakakapilarūpavatī gauḥ
ityādyākārakabhramātmakaparāmarśaviṣayatāmādāya kapilarūpāderapi
vyāvartakatāpatteśca/ tathā ca dharmatvameva lakṣaṇalakṣaṇamityāśaṅkāyāṃ
niṣkarṣārthamāha [39] itarabhedavidheyetyādi/
itarabhedavidheyakānumitijanakajñānīya
pakṣatāvacchedakāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitaviṣayatetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The prefix 'vyā-' with the root 'vṛt' has the meaning of difference from others. The 'ka' suffix has the sense of 'generator of inference' — intending this, he says: [39] "the meaning is: of the generator of the inference of difference from others." The capacity to generate inference belongs to the inferential consideration (<s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s>) itself, not to the probans being considered. And thus, the capacity of smell and the like to exclude is untenable. Nor should it be said that there is no fault because the capacity to exclude is being the object of a cognition that generates the inference of difference from others. Even so, because it would fail to exclude what is indifferent and what is the object of collective apprehension (<s>samūhālambana</s>), and because the statement of over-extension in the case of name-ability (<s>abhidheyatva</s>) and the like would be incoherent — since that too is a definiendum in the manner stated. Nor should it be said that [the capacity to exclude] is being the locus of the object-hood that delimits the generator-hood of such [inference], because even so, there would be over-extension in the absence and the like that constitutes the pervader of difference from others, and since — taking the object-hood of an inferential consideration in the form of an erroneous cognition like 'the cow possesses tawny color that pervades the difference from non-cows' delimited by <s>gotva</s> and the like — even tawny color and the like would undesirably have the capacity to exclude. And thus, when the doubt arises that property-hood (<s>dharmatva</s>) alone would be the definition of a definition, in order to settle the matter he says: [39] "whose predicate is difference from others" etc. The meaning is: the object-hood delimited by the thesis-delimitor, which determines the qualificand-hood in the cognition that generates the inference whose predicate is difference from others.

Because among cognitions of the same form, since there is no difference in object-hood, the impossibility of taking collective apprehension in the indifferent portion is insurmountable. Taking the qualifier-hood of difference from others, which determines the qualificand-hood constituting the thesis that constitutes the co-location, to prevent over-extension in [other] differences from others,

Here, if the condition of having difference from others as the object is included in inference, then taking the generator-hood of the inference 'difference from others is knowable, because of name-ability,' there would be the undesirable consequence of the capacity to exclude in name-ability and the like. Therefore, the condition of having difference from others as predicate is included there. What is intended is: having predicate-hood delimited by difference-from-others-hood. Taking the generator-hood of the inference 'a pot possesses name-ability through the self-linking relation, because of knowability,' to prevent that fault, in the predicate-hood the delimitation by the self-linking relation qualified by the pervader-hood of the thesis-delimitor must be included. Otherwise, taking the generator-hood of a cognition in the form of an inference that apprehends merely the co-location with <s>gotva</s> and the like — 'the cow is different from both pot and cloth, because of name-ability,' 'earth is different from both pot and cloth, because of difference-from-non-earth' —
