What should be included is the generator-hood that is the counter-positive of the product-hood delimited by inference-hood delimited by such predicate-hood. Otherwise, merely through co-location with the thesis-delimitor delimited by it, taking the generator-hood of an inferential consideration that apprehends merely the co-location with the generator of an inference apprehending difference from others through collective apprehension, the same difficulty would persist. Now even so, taking the generator-hood of an inference to be postulated — through the commonality with the cognition of possessing difference from pot and the like that pervades difference from earth, through temporal and other relations, or through the commonality with the cognition of possessing difference from earth that pervades difference from earth — over-extension in difference from earth and the like is simply insurmountable. Nor should it be said that there is no fault because the condition of belonging to a cognition that is preparatory to such inference is included in the object-hood. Even so, because a cognition in the form 'earth possesses difference-from-earth-pervading-difference-from-earth, and also possesses difference-from-other-than-pervaded-substance' — which has not been blocked by a cognition of invalidity in the portion of difference from earth and the like — qualifies as such. Since the condition of occurring in a cognition not preparatory to such inference cannot be included, because it would fail to capture the object-hood of smell and the like that is common to doubt and other [cognitions] not preparatory to such inference — if it be objected thus, no. Because what is intended is: the locus of such object-hood that occurs in a cognition preparatory to such inference, which delimits the generator-hood determined by the product-hood delimited by such inference-hood, and which is a cognition that has not been blocked by a cognition of invalidity. The conclusion is: object-hood qualified by such product-hood. The qualification is through both relations — the delimitor-hood of the generator-hood determined by itself, and belonging to a cognition that is preparatory to such inference and that has not been blocked by a cognition of invalidity. Not being blocked by a cognition of invalidity is: being other than what is qualified by error, through the three relations of co-location with the object-hood, temporal qualification, and qualifier-hood. Being other than what is qualified by conjunction, through the three relations of residing in the counter-positive, residing in the co-relative, and being delimited by the qualificand-hood determined by that — with respect to the qualifier-hood that determines the qualifier-hood — this is the path explored by me alone.

children.text:
eveneti/ evakāreṇetyarthaḥ/ nanu
sāsnādīnāṃ gavādilakṣaṇatvasya kathaṃ ativyāptiprayojakatvaṃ,
pṛṣṭhatāḍanena daṇḍabhaṅganyāyāt; ata āha [39] uktalakṣaṇeti [39] abhidheyatvādibhinnatvaṃ ceti/ idamatra
cintyam -- vyāvartakamātrasyoktalakṣaṇalakṣyatve
lakṣyatāvacchedakābhāvavadavṛttitvarūpalakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvani veśenaivavyāvahārikavāraṇe
svavyāpakatatkatvatvarūpalakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvaṃ
niveśyābhidheyatvādāvativyāptiṃ saṃpādya tadvāraṇāya
tadbhinnatvaniveśanaṃ prakṣālanādinyāyenāyuktam/
children.translated_text: "'Eva' alone" — the meaning is: by the word 'eva.' Objection: How does the fact that <s>sāsnādi</s> (dewlap etc.) is the definition of cow and the like cause over-extension, given the maxim that 'striking the back breaks the stick'? To this he says: [39] "the stated definition" etc. [39] "And being different from name-ability and the like" — here the following should be considered: If mere excluder-hood is the definiendum of the stated definition, then since merely by including pervaded-hood of the definiendum-hood-delimitor in the form of not occurring in what possesses the absence of the definiendum-hood-delimitor, the conventional [capacity] would be excluded, it is improper — in the manner of the maxim 'washing what was already clean' — to include pervader-hood of the definiendum-hood-delimitor in the form of one's own pervader having that as such, and then, having produced over-extension in name-ability and the like, to include the condition of being different from those to prevent it.

children.text:
yattu -
pṛthivitvādirūpalakṣyatāvacchedakaśūnye jalādau kālikādinā
sattvāt ativyāptiḥ - iti tanna/ ghaṭādilakṣaṇe jñānavadanyatvādāveva
lakṣaṇagamanāt/ ato
lakṣyatāvacchedakābhāvavyāpakībhūtābhāvīyalakṣaṇatāghaṭakasambandhāvacchi nnapratiyogitvarūpalakṣyatāvacchedakavyāpyatvasya
vivakṣitatvāditi/ [39] na tāvatsāmānyato bhedānumāpakatvamiti/
sāmānyato bhedatvena/ tasilo 'vacchinnatvamarthaḥ/ tasya ca
bhedānumāpakatvaghaṭakabhedavidheyatāyāmanvayaḥ/ [39] yatkiñcidubhayatvāvacchinnapratiyogitāketi/ 'ghaṭaḥ
ghaṭapaṭobhayabhinnaḥ abhidheyatvāt', 'pṛthivī ghaṭapaṭobhayabhinnā
pṛthivītarabhedāt' ityādyanumitijanakatāmādāya tatra
vyāvartakatvasya sūpapādatvāt iti bhāvaḥ/ yadyapi 'ghaṭo bhedavān
abhidheyatvāt' ityādyanumitijanakatāmādāya tat suvacaṃ iti
dvitvāvacchinnabhedasādhyakānumānaparyantānudhāvanaṃ viphalam, tathāpiṃ
rkiñciddharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvasahitabhedatvāvacchinnavidheyatāpayrantaniveśe 'pi
kathaṃ doṣo bhavati ityetadarthaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, [the objection] that there is over-extension because in water and the like, which lack the definiendum-hood-delimitor in the form of earth-ness and the like, [the property] exists through temporal and other relations — that is not so. Because in the case of definitions like that of pot and the like, the definition applies only to being-other-than-what-possesses-cognition and the like. Therefore, because what is intended is the pervaded-hood of the definiendum-hood-delimitor in the form of counter-positive-hood delimited by the relation constituting the definition-hood, which is the absence that is the pervader of the absence of the definiendum-hood-delimitor. [39] "Not, first of all, the capacity to infer difference in general" — meaning: delimited by difference-hood in general. The suffix 'tasil' has the meaning of being delimited by that. And its anvaya (positive concomitance) is in the predicate-hood constituting the generator-hood of the inference of difference. [39] "The counter-positive-hood delimited by whatever-both-ness" — the purport is that since, taking the generator-hood of inferences like 'a pot is different from both pot and cloth, because of name-ability' and 'earth is different from both pot and cloth, because of difference from non-earth,' the capacity to exclude in those cases is easily established. Although, taking the generator-hood of an inference like 'a pot possesses difference, because of name-ability,' that is easy to state, and thus pursuing as far as inferences proving difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by duality is fruitless — nevertheless, even when one includes up to the predicate-hood of difference-hood together with counter-positive-hood delimited by some-property-hood, how the fault arises — for this purpose

children.text:
vyāvṛttisādhāraṇyārthamapi tathoktiḥ/ anyathā siddhasādhanāpatteḥ
iti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: and also for the purpose of [showing] the generality of exclusion, such a statement is made. Otherwise there would be the fault of proving what is already established — this should be noted.

children.text:
nanu
vyāsajyavṛttyatiriktakiñciddharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvasahitabhedatvāvacchinnavidheyatāniveśāt
na ko 'pi doṣa ityata āha -- [39] sarveṣāmapi
vyatirekidharmāṇāṃ yakiñcibdyavartakatayeti/ gauḥ
paṭabhinnāśṛṅgitvāt', 'kapilagauḥ ghaṭabhinna kapilarūpavattvāt'
ityādyanumitijanakatāmādāya śṛṅgitvakapilarūpādau
tadupapādanasambhavāditi bhāvaḥ/ [39] nāpi
children.translated_text: Now, since by including in the predicate-hood the qualification of difference-hood (<s>bhedatva</s>) combined with counter-positiveness delimited by some property other than a collectively-occurring one, there would be no defect — to this he says: [39] 'Because all differentiating properties without exception are excluders of something' etc. Taking the capacity to generate inferences such as 'the cow is different from cloth, because of possessing horns' and 'the tawny cow is different from the pot, because of possessing a tawny color,' the establishment of that [capacity] in horn-possessing-ness, tawny-color, and the like is possible — this is the purport. [39] 'Nor

children.text:
viśiṣyetyādi/
pṛthivīvyāpakatvaviśiṣṭasvarūpasambandhāvacchinnapṛthivītvādyavacchinna -
itarabhedatvāvacchinnavidheyatākānumitijanakatāvacchedakaniruktaviṣayatāśrayatvamityarthaḥ/
yadyapi 'kapilagauḥ ghaṭabhinnā kapilalarūpavattvāt' ityanumitimādāya
kapilarūpādervyāvartakatāprasaṃgaḥ, tathāpi
dharmintāvacchedaketyādinyāyena na doṣaḥ/ [40] gotvādisamanaiyatyasya
tatrāsattvāditi/ padārthatvasamaniyatatvasya lakṣyāprasiddhyā alakṣaṇatvena
tatra tatsattvasyākiñcitkaratvāt iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: is it qualified' etc. The meaning is: having as its locus the content-relation (<s>viṣayatā</s>) delimited by the specified inference-generating capacity, the predicate-hood being delimited by difference-from-the-other delimited by earth-ness (<s>pṛthivītva</s>) and the like, which is delimited by the intrinsic relation qualified by pervasion over earth. Even though, taking the inference 'the tawny cow is different from the pot, because of possessing a tawny color,' there would be the unwanted consequence that tawny color and the like are excluders, nevertheless by the maxim that 'the delimitor of the property of being the inferential subject...' and so forth, there is no defect. [40] 'Because the co-extensiveness with pot-hood and the like does not exist there' — because the co-extensiveness with category-hood (<s>padārthatva</s>) is not established in the <s>lakṣya</s> (definiendum), and hence the [proposed] definition fails to be a definition, the presence of such co-extensiveness there is inconsequential — this is the purport.

children.text:
gotvāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakatve sādhya
iti/ svāvacchinnetarabhedānumāpakatvasambandhena gotve sādhya
ityarthaḥ/ tenāgre 'bhidheyatvādau vyabhicārakathanaṃ saṃgacchate/ anyathā
padārthatvāvacchinnetarāprasiddhyātadghaṭitasādhyābhāvasya
sutarāmaprasiddhatvena sādhyābhāvavadvṛttitvarūpavyabhicārasya
durvacatvāt/ asmatpakṣe tu padārthatvaṃ prati uktasambandhasya
vyadhikaraṇatayā sādhyābhāvasya prasiddhatvena vyabhicāraḥ suvaca eva/
children.translated_text: 'In the capacity to generate an inference of difference from what is delimited by pot-hood as the probandum' — the meaning is: pot-hood is the probandum through the relation of capacity to generate an inference of difference from what is delimited by oneself. By this, the subsequent statement of deviation in denotability (<s>abhidheyatva</s>) and the like is consistent. Otherwise, since what is other than what is delimited by category-hood (<s>padārthatva</s>) is not established, and hence the absence of probandum constituted thereby is all the more unestablished, the deviation in the form of occurring in what possesses the absence of the probandum would be difficult to state. But in our view, since the stated relation is of wider extension than category-hood, the absence of the probandum is well-established, and hence the deviation is easy to state.

children.text:
abhidheyatvādibhinnatvaṃ ceti/ cakāro
vākārārthaḥ/ anyathā taddharmāvacchinnetarabhedabhinnatvasya niveśenaiva
padārthetarāprasiddhyā abhidheyatvādau vyabhicāravāraṇena
abhidheyatvādibhinnatvasva hetukoṭau niveśasya niṣphalatayā
tatsamuccāyakatvāsambhavādasaṅgateḥ/ atra sāmānyavyāptisthale
taddhetudharmikatattatsādhyavyāptigrahābhāvaviśiṣṭatattatsādhyahetūbhayasthiteḥ
anumitipramāyāḥ siddhāntalakṣaṇaprāmāṇyavādayoruktatvāt na
prakṛte 'numitisambhavaḥ ityabhipretyāha - [40] adhikavicāra iti/
children.translated_text: 'And difference from denotability and the like' — the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) has the meaning of 'or' (<s>vā</s>). Otherwise, since by the inclusion of difference from difference-delimited-by-that-property alone, the non-establishment of what is other than category-hood prevents deviation in denotability and the like, the inclusion of difference from denotability and the like in the reason-side would be fruitless, and hence its being aggregated [with the other] would be impossible — thus it would be incongruous. Here, in the locus of general pervasion (<s>sāmānyavyāpti</s>), since the absence of apprehension of the respective pervasion with the respective probandum of the respective inferential subject of the respective reason, and the existence of both the respective probandum and the respective reason [in the subject], have been stated as belonging to the validity of inference by the established definition and the doctrine of validity — with the intention that in the present case, the possibility of inference [does not arise], he says — [40] 'Further investigation' etc.

children.text:
tena rūpeṇa vyavahartavyajñānaṃ vineti/
itarabhedādiprakāreṇa pakṣaviṣayakaparāmarśaṃ vinetyarthaḥ/
tadrūpāvacchinneti/
lakṣyatāvacchedakapṛthivītvādyavacchinanapratipādaketyarthaḥ/
vyavahārāsambhavāt - vyavahārānumānāsambhavāt/ tathā ca
taddharmāvacchinnabodhakaśabdarūpavyavahāravidheyakānumitijanakatāvacchedakatvaṃ
taddharmāṃvacchinnavyāvahārikatvam/ tacca 'ghaṭaḥ pṛthivīti vyavahartavyaḥ,
pṛthivītarabhedāt', 'ghaṭaḥ padārtha iti vyavahartavyaḥ,
abhidheyatvāt' ityādyanumitimādāya vyāvṛttyabhidheyatvādāvapi
akṣatamiti bhāvaḥ/ etena dīpikāyāṃ lakṣaṇaprayojanatve lakṣaṇajñāpyatve
vyavahārasādhanatvāt vyavahārānumāpakatvādityartho bodhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Without a cognition that should be applied in that form' — the meaning is: without a reflective judgment (<s>parāmarśa</s>) regarding the subject in the form of difference-from-the-other and the like. 'Delimited by that form' — the meaning is: one that conveys the delimitor of the <s>lakṣya</s>-hood such as earth-ness and the like. 'Because of the impossibility of application' — because of the impossibility of the inference constituting the application (<s>vyavahāra</s>). And thus, the capacity to generate an inference whose predicate conveys a word-form indicative of [something] delimited by that property is the being-applicable-ness (<s>vyāvahārikatva</s>) delimited by that property. And that [capacity], taking inferences like 'the pot should be applied as earth, because of difference from what is other than earth' and 'the pot should be applied as a category, because of denotability,' remains intact even in the excluder denotability and the like — this is the purport. By this, the meaning of the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement on the purpose of definitions as 'because of being the means of application, because of generating an inference of application' should be understood.

children.text:
guṇavattvasya
dravyalakṣaṇatvasthāpanam
children.translated_text: Establishment of possessing qualities (<s>guṇavattva</s>) as the definition of substance (<s>dravya</s>)

children.text:
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvavati
atyantābhāvasya prācīnairananumatatvāt nātyantābhāvaghaṭitā vyāptiḥ
sambhavati/ yadvā pratiyogivyadhikaraṇalakṣyaniṣṭhābhāvapratiyogitvasyaiva
vyāptiśarīre praviṣṭatvāt gandhādyabhāvasya cātathātvāt
nāvyāptirityāśayena śaṅkate -- prakāśikāyām [53] nanvityādi/ guṇāśrayatvalakṣaṇamiti/ guṇātmakalakṣaṇamityarthaḥ/
āśrayatvakathanaṃ lakṣaṇatāghaṭakasambandhapradarśanāya/ etena -
guṇādhikaraṇatvasyāpyutpattinirūpitādhikaraṇatāyā
avyāpyavṛttittvāt/ guṇapratiyogikatvopalakṣitasamavāyena
guṇavattvasya samavāyaikyapakṣe guṇādāvativyāptiḥ/
tatpratiyogikatvaviśiṣṭasamavāyasyotpattikālāvacchedenābhāvasattvāt
children.translated_text: Since the earlier logicians (<s>prācīna</s>) did not accept absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>) in what possesses destruction and prior absence, the pervasion constituted by absolute absence is not possible. Alternatively, since the counter-positiveness of the absence residing in the <s>lakṣya</s> (definiendum) that is in a different locus from the counter-positive has already entered the body of the pervasion, and since the absence of smell and the like is not of that nature, there is no under-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) — with this intent, he raises the objection in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [53] 'Now' etc. 'The definition consisting in being the substratum of qualities' — the meaning is: the definition having quality as its content. The mention of 'substratum-hood' is for indicating the relation that constitutes the definition. By this — even the substratum-hood constituted by <s>utpatti</s>-determined (origination-determined) substratum-hood is of non-pervading occurrence (<s>avyāpyavṛtti</s>); in the view that quality-possessing-ness constituted by inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) is identical with inherence, there is over-extension in qualities themselves; since the inherence qualified by counter-positiveness is absent at the time of origination,

children.text:
avyāptiḥ iti
dūṣaṇamanavakāśam/ sattāviśeṣaṇatvabhramavāraṇāya [53] jātiviśeṣaṇamiti/ atra ca guṇasamānādhikaraṇatvaṃ
guṇaniṣṭhasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnādheyatānirūpakanirūpitasamavāyasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvaṃ,
tena kālikena guṇavadguṇasamavetasya, kālikena
guṇasamavāyivṛtterguṇatvasya vyudāsaḥ/ [53] bhāva iti/ atha 'ekaṃ rūpaṃ
rasāt pṛthak' iti vyavahārasya sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena guṇe
guṇaviṣayakatvasyopagame rūpādāvapi svasmāt
pṛthagvyavahāraprasaṅgaḥ/ svāvadhikapṛthaktvasāmānādhikaraṇyasya
svasminnapyabādhāt iti cet - na/ sāmānādhikaraṇyasya svasmin
svāvadhikapṛthaktvasambandhatvānupagamāt/ kalpanākalpanayośca
phalānurodhitvāt/ vastutastu 'rūpaṃ rasāt pṛthak' ityādau
pṛthaktvasya
svanirūpakatāvacchedakāvacchinnabhinnatvasāmānādhikaraṇyobhayasambandhena
bhānābhyupagamāt na doṣa iti/ [53] kālikādītyādipadena
samavāyasvarūpobhayaghaṭitasāmānādhikaraṇyaparigrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: under-pervasion — this objection has no scope. To prevent the error of [taking it as] qualified by <s>sattā</s> (existence), [he says] [53] 'qualified by a particular universal.' And here, the co-location with quality (<s>guṇasamānādhikaraṇatva</s>) means: being a superstratum delimited by the inherence-relation that determines the content-ness that determines the superstratum-ness delimited by the inherence-relation residing in the quality. By that, a quality co-located with quality through a temporal [relation] and quality-hood (<s>guṇatva</s>), which is an occurrence in what is co-inhered with quality through a temporal [relation], are excluded. [53] 'Positive entity' — Now, if by the co-location relation (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), the quality-directedness in a quality [itself] is accepted in the usage 'one color is different from taste,' then even in color and the like, there would be the unwanted consequence of the usage of being different from oneself. Because the co-location of self-delimited separateness with oneself is unsublated even in oneself — if thus [objected]: no, because the co-location relation is not accepted in oneself as being the relation of self-delimited separateness. And because of choosing between postulations and non-postulations being governed by results. In truth, in 'color is different from taste' and the like, since the appearance of separateness through the co-location constituted by both the relations — the otherness-co-location delimited by the delimitor of the content-relation of separateness determined by oneself — is accepted, there is no defect. [53] 'Temporal and so forth' — by the word 'and so forth,' the co-location constituted by both inherence and intrinsic nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) is included.

children.text:
hetudharmitāvacchedakaketi/
hetvavacchinnaviśeṣyatāketyarthaḥ/
asamānākārakasiddheścāvirodhitvāditi bhāvaḥ/ [56] saṅkṣepa iti/ ayamatrāśayaḥ -
vyatirekavyāpteranumānāṅgatvena na kāpyanupapattiḥ/
upanayavākyāt śābdabodhānupapattirapi parārthānumānasthala eva
doṣaḥ na svārthānumānasthale 'pīti
lakṣaṇaprayojanasiddhirnirābādhaiveti/
children.translated_text: 'Delimited by the property of the inferential subject of the reason' — the meaning is: having the qualificand-hood delimited by the reason. And because the <s>siddhi</s> (establishment) of different-form (<s>asamānākāra</s>) is not contradictory — this is the purport. [56] 'In brief' — the intent here is: since negative pervasion (<s>vyatirekavyāpti</s>) is a component of inference, there is no impossibility [in the definition]. The impossibility of verbal cognition from the application-sentence is a defect only in the case of inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>), not also in the case of inference for oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>) — hence the establishment of the purpose of the definition is unobstructed.

children.text:
nanu bhūtatvasya
jātitvābhāvāt kathaṃ tatsaṅkarasya bādhakatvam
upādhisaṅkarasyādoṣatvādityata āha - [57] jātitvenābhimateti/
jātitvenāpāditetyarthaḥ/ tathā ca tulyayuktyā
bhūtapadaśakyatāvacchedakatayā bhūtatvajātisiddhyā na sāṃkaryaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, since <s>bhūtatva</s> (element-hood) does not have the status of <s>jāti</s> (universal), how can its intermixture (<s>saṅkara</s>) serve as an obstructor — since the intermixture of <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious conditions) is not a defect? To this he says — [57] 'Accepted as a universal' — the meaning is: postulated as a universal. And thus, by parity of reasoning, since the <s>jāti</s> of element-hood is established through its being the delimitor of the denotative capacity of the word 'element,' the intermixture is not

children.text:
doṣa iti bhāvaḥ/
[57] vyakterabheda ityādi śloke iti padādhyāhāreṇa
jñānajanakasvalpaśabdarūpasaṅgrahābhedabodho varṇanīyaḥ/ prathamatrikasya
jātitve dvitīyatrikasya jātimattve bādhakatvamiti viśeṣasūcanāya
madhye 'thaśabdaḥ/ vyakterityādiślokoktajātibādhakatvaṃ ca
jātijātimattvānyataraprakārakajñānapratibandhakajñānaviṣayatvam/
children.translated_text: a defect — this is the purport. [57] 'Non-difference of the individual' etc. — by supplying 'in the verse' (<s>śloke</s>), the comprehension of the concise word-form that generates cognition should be explained as non-difference. The first triad [of verses] serves as an obstructor of <s>jāti</s>-hood, and the second triad serves as an obstructor of possessing a <s>jāti</s> — to indicate this distinction, the word 'now' (<s>atha</s>) is placed in between. And the <s>jāti</s>-obstructing-ness stated in the verse 'non-difference of the individual' etc. is: being the object of a cognition that obstructs a cognition having as its mode either <s>jāti</s>-hood or possessing-a-<s>jāti</s>.

children.text:
vyakterabhedaḥ
1svasamevatatvasvabhinnasamavetatvobhayasambandhena prameyaviśiṣṭānyatvaṃ
svapratiyogisamavetatvasvānuyogisamavetatvobhayasambandhena
bhedavadanyatvaṃ vā/ tajjñānasya tadvadanyatvajñānavidhayā uktobhayasambandhena
prameyaviśiṣṭatvādirūpānekasamavetatvaghaṭitajātitvajñānapratibandhakatvam/
children.translated_text: Non-difference of the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) [means]: being other than what is qualified by <s>prameya</s> (knowable), through both the relations — the relation of being co-inhered with oneself (<s>svasamavetatva</s>) and the relation of being co-inhered with what is different from oneself (<s>svabhinnasamavetatva</s>). Or, being other than what possesses difference, through both the relations — the relation of being co-inhered with one's own counter-positive (<s>svapratiyogisamavetatva</s>) and the relation of being co-inhered with one's own relatum (<s>svānuyogisamavetatva</s>). The cognition of that [non-difference], in the manner of cognition of such otherness through both the stated relations, obstructs the cognition of <s>jāti</s>-hood constituted by multiple co-inherence-ness qualified by <s>prameya</s>-hood and the like.

children.text:
1. svasamavetatveti/
svaṃ nīlaghaṭaḥ tatsamavetatvaṃ ghaṭatve, evaṃ svaṃ nīlaghaṭaḥ
tadbhinnapītaghaṭasamavetatvaṃ ca ghaṭatve iti uktobhayasambandhena
nīlaghaṭarūpaprameyaviśiṣṭe ghaṭatvaṃ tadbhinnatvamākāśatve/ evaṃ svaṃ
nīlaghaṭabhedaḥ tatpratiyoginīlaghaṭasamavetatvaṃ ghaṭatve, svaṃ
nīlaghaṭabhedaḥ tadanuyogipītaghaṭasamavetatvaṃ ca ghaṭatve iti
tādṛśobhayasaṃbandhena bhedavat - nīlaghaṭabhedavat ghaṭatve
tadanyatvamākāśe iti bodhyam/
children.translated_text: 1. 'Co-inhered with oneself' — oneself is the blue pot; being co-inhered with that is [a property] of pot-hood. Similarly, oneself is the blue pot; being co-inhered with what is different from that, namely the yellow pot, is also [a property] of pot-hood — thus through both the stated relations, pot-hood is [qualified] in what is qualified by the <s>prameya</s> (knowable) in the form of the blue pot; and difference from that is in space-hood (<s>ākāśatva</s>). Similarly, oneself is the difference of the blue pot; being co-inhered with its counter-positive, the blue pot, is [a property] of pot-hood. Oneself is the difference of the blue pot; being co-inhered with its relatum, the yellow pot, is also [a property] of pot-hood — thus through both such relations, what possesses such difference — what possesses blue-pot-difference — pot-hood has otherness from that in space — this should be understood.

children.text:
tulyatvaṃ
svabhinnajātisamaniyatatvam, svabhinnatvasvasamaniyatatvobhayasambandhena
jātiviśiṣṭatvaparyavasitam/ tacca jātitvābhāvavyāpyamiti
tadgrahasya tadabhāvavyāpyavattāgrahavidhayā kalaśatvādeḥ
ghaṭatvādijātibhinnajātitvopagame
children.translated_text: Equality (<s>tulyatva</s>) is being co-extensive with a <s>jāti</s> different from oneself; it culminates in being qualified by a <s>jāti</s> through both the relations — the relation of being co-extensive with what is different from oneself and the relation of being co-extensive with oneself. And since that is pervaded by the absence of <s>jāti</s>-hood, the apprehension of it, in the manner of apprehending the possession of what is pervaded by the absence of that, [obstructs] — if <s>kalaśatva</s> (water-vessel-hood) is accepted as a <s>jāti</s> different from <s>ghaṭatva</s> (pot-hood) and the like,

children.text:
virodhitvam/ tasya ca
jātitvābhāvavyāpyatvaṃ ghaṭatvakalaśatvayorbhinnajātitve ghaṭādipadasya
dharmadvayāvacchinne śaktidvayakalpanaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvadvayakalpanaṃ ca
nānyatheti lāghavamiti dhīsahakṛtena
jātiviśiṣṭatvapakṣakajātitvābhāvavyāpyatadabhāvānyatarasādhyakaprameyatvādihetukānumānena
siddham/
children.translated_text: it is contradictory. And its being pervaded by the absence of <s>jāti</s>-hood is established by an inference whose reason is <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability), whose thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is being qualified by a <s>jāti</s> constituting equality, and whose probandum is either the absence of <s>jāti</s>-hood or its absence — [an inference] assisted by the economy [principle] that, if pot-hood and water-vessel-hood are different <s>jātis</s>, the postulation of two denotative capacities for the word 'pot' etc. delimited by both properties, and the postulation of two causal relations, cannot be otherwise — and hence economy [supports the conclusion].

children.text:
saṅkaraśca
svasāmānādhikaraṇyasvābhāvasāmānādhikaraṇyasvasamānādhikaraṇābhāvaprati yogitvatrayasambandhena
jātiviśiṣṭatvam/ tadapi ca jātitvābhāvavyāpyameva/ tasya tathātvaṃ
ca dharmaśāstrasiddham/ viruddhajātīnāṃ parasparaṃ vyāpyajātyā
vyāpakajāteḥ, vyāpakajātyā vyāpyajāteśca jātisāṅkaryavāraṇāya
saṃbandhatrayaniveśaḥ/
children.translated_text: And intermixture (<s>saṅkara</s>) is: being qualified by a <s>jāti</s> through the three relations — co-location with oneself, co-location with the absence of oneself, and being the counter-positive of an absence co-located with oneself. And that too is pervaded by the absence of <s>jāti</s>-hood. Its being so is established by <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (scripture on dharma). The inclusion of the three relations is for preventing the intermixture of <s>jātis</s> — of mutually pervaded <s>jātis</s>, namely the pervaded <s>jāti</s> by the pervading <s>jāti</s>, and the pervading <s>jāti</s> by the pervaded <s>jāti</s>.

children.text:
anavasthitiḥ anavasthā ca
jātyanāśrayavṛttipadārthavibhājakopādhiparamparāropādhīnajātiviśiṣṭabuddhinirūpitata-
children.translated_text: Non-groundedness (<s>anavasthiti</s>) and infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) — [the intended meaning here is] the unwanted consequence of an infinite series of causal relations for the cognition qualified by the <s>jāti</s>, which is dependent on a chain of <s>upādhis</s> (adventitious conditions) that differentiate categories and are non-substantial-universals-residing —

children.text:
ttajjātijñānakāraṇatānantyarūpāniṣṭaprasañjanarūpeha vivakṣitā/
tasyāśca tadāpādakakāpattividhayā
jātirjātimatītyākārakajñānavirodhitvam/
children.translated_text: this is what is intended as the unwanted consequence in the form of infinity of the causal conditions for the cognition of such-and-such <s>jāti</s>. And its status as an obstructor of the cognition having the form 'a <s>jāti</s> possesses a <s>jāti</s>' is in the manner of the reductio (<s>āpatti</s>) that produces it.

children.text:
rūpahāniḥ
svatovyāvṛttatvarūpalakṣaṇasvarūpasya hāniḥ/ svatovyāvṛttatvaṃ ca
viśeṣāṇāṃ svataḥsiddhaparasparabhedavattvam tasya viśeṣāṇāṃ
jātimattve 'nupapattiḥ/ sajātīyānāṃ padārthānāṃ parasparaṃ bhedaḥ
pratyakṣeṇa vyāvartakāntareṇa vā siddhyatīti nyāyāt viśeṣo yadi
jātimān syāt svatovyāvṛttattvavān na syāt
ityāpattiviṣayatayā viśeṣasya jātimattve bādhakatvam/ 'ayaṃ
paramāṇuḥ tatparamāṇubhinnaḥ etadviśeṣāt' ityanumānena viśeṣasya
jātimattve jātyāśrayasya jātipuraskāreṇaiva vyāvartakatvaṃ iti
niyamena jātipuraskāreṇaiva vyāvartakatāyā vyabhicārāpatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Loss of essential nature (<s>rūpahāni</s>) is the loss of the essential nature constituted by the defining characteristic of self-differentiation (<s>svatovyāvṛttatva</s>). Self-differentiation is the possession of mutual difference from one another that is self-established in the case of <s>viśeṣas</s> (individuators). Its impossibility arises if <s>viśeṣas</s> possess <s>jātis</s>. By the principle that mutual difference among entities of the same kind is established either by perception or by some other differentiator — if a <s>viśeṣa</s> were to possess a <s>jāti</s>, it would not possess self-differentiation — by the reductio (<s>āpatti</s>) having this as its object, [it serves as] an obstructor of <s>viśeṣas</s> possessing <s>jātis</s>. [Since] in the inference 'this atom is different from that atom, because of this <s>viśeṣa</s>,' if the <s>viśeṣa</s> possesses a <s>jāti</s>, then its differentiating capacity would be only through the intermediary of the <s>jāti</s> — the reductio would arise that differentiating capacity is only through the intermediary of a <s>jāti</s> [generally], which would deviate [from cases where it doesn't hold].

children.text:
asaṃbandhaḥ
asamavetatvam/ tacca bahuvrīhibalāt
samavetatvasāmānyābhāvaparyavasitam/ tajjñānasya
nityānekasamavetatvarūpajātyabhāvavyāpyavattājñānavidhayā
nityānekasamavetarūpajātimattājñānavirodhitvam/
etatsarvamabhipretyaiva [57] saṅkṣepa ityuktam/ dīpikāyām [56] laghutvasya gurutvābhāvarūpatvāditi/ na ca gurutvasya
laghutvābhāvarūpatvamādāya vinigamanāviraha iti/ vācyam/
svatantrecchasyeti nyāyenādoṣāt iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Non-relation (<s>asaṃbandha</s>) is non-inherence (<s>asamavetatva</s>). And that, by the force of the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, culminates in the general absence of inherence. The cognition of that [non-relation], in the manner of cognition of possessing what is pervaded by the absence of <s>jāti</s>-hood constituted by being inhered in by eternal and multiple [entities], obstructs the cognition of possessing a <s>jāti</s> constituted by being inhered in by what has an eternal and multiple <s>jāti</s>. All this has been said with the intention expressed in [57] 'in brief.' In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [56] 'lightness being of the nature of the absence of heaviness' — nor should one err into thinking there is an absence of a decisive reason (<s>vinigamana</s>) by taking heaviness to be of the nature of the absence of lightness. Because by the maxim 'of one who has independent volition,' there is no defect — this is the purport.

children.text: karmavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Classification of <s>karma</s> (action)

children.text:
asamavāyīti/ na cātra saṃyogabhinnatve sati
asamavāyikāraṇamāstāmiti vācyam/ ādyapatanāsamavāyikāraṇādau
ativyāptivāraṇāya saṃyogāṃśasyāpi sārthakyāt/
children.translated_text: 'Non-inherent' — nor should one say here 'let it be stated that [the cause is] a non-inherent cause while being different from conjunction' — because, in order to prevent over-extension in the non-inherent cause of the initial falling and the like, even the conjunction-portion serves a purpose.

children.text: sāmānyavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: General classification (<s>sāmānyavibhāga</s>)

children.text:
sattāyāḥ dravyatvāpekṣayetyādi/
apekṣāśabdasya pratiyogitānirūpakatvamarthaḥ/ tṛtīyāyāśca
vaiśiṣṭyam/ adhikadeśavṛttitvaṃ ca
svapratiyogyadhikaraṇavṛttitvasvādhikaraṇavṛttitvobhayasambandhenābhāvaviśiṣṭatvam/
sakadeśe 'bhāve
tṛtīyāntārthadravyatvaniṣṭhapratiyogitānirūpitatvaviśiṣṭatvānvayaḥ/
adhikadeśavṛttitvenetyatra tṛtīyāyā abhedor'thaḥ/
dravyatvaniṣṭhapratiyogitākābhāvavaiśiṣṭyābhinnaṃ dravyatvāpekṣayā
paratvamiti vākyārthaḥ/ [63] dravyatvādīnāṃ sattāto 'paratvamiti/
children.translated_text: 'In relation to substance-hood from <s>sattā</s> (existence)' and so forth. The meaning of the word 'in relation to' is being the determinant of counter-positive-ness. The instrumental case has the meaning of qualification. And occurring in more loci means being qualified by an absence through the twofold relation of occurring in what is the substrate of its own counter-positive and occurring in the substrate of itself. Where there is absence at some locus, the syntactic connection is with qualification by the determinant of counter-positive-ness residing in substance-hood, [which is] the meaning of the instrumental ending. In the phrase 'by occurring in more loci,' the instrumental has the meaning of identity. The sentence-meaning is: higher-ness in relation to substance-hood is identical with the qualification by the absence whose counter-positive-ness resides in substance-hood. [63] The lower-ness of substance-hood and the rest relative to <s>sattā</s>.

children.text:
tacca
1svāśrayādhikaraṇavṛttyabhāvapratiyogitvarūpam/
children.translated_text: And that [lower-ness] has the form of counter-positive-ness of the absence occurring in the substrate of its own substrate.

children.text: viśeṣavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Section on <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularities)

children.text:
viśeṣāsatvanantā eveti vākye anantatvaṃ
ca na vidyate antaḥ
saṅkhyātvavyāpyadharmāvacchinnaprakāratākāsmadādisamavetaniścayaḥ
viśeṣyatāsambandhena yeṣu nāstīti vigrahān
saṅkhyātvavyāpyadharmāvacchinnaprakāratākatādṛśaniścayaviśeṣyatvābhāvavattvam/
prakāśikāyām [63]
children.translated_text: In the statement 'particularities are indeed infinite': infinity means there does not exist an end — [that is,] the absence, through the relation of qualificand-ness, of a determinate cognition inhering in us and others whose qualifier-mode is delimited by a property pervaded by number-hood; [infinity is] the property of possessing the absence of being the qualificand of such a determinate cognition delimited by a qualifier-mode delimited by a property pervaded by number-hood. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [63]:

children.text:
1. svāśrayeti/ svaṃ
sattā tadāśrayaḥ guṇaḥ tanniṣṭhābhāvaḥ dravyatvābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvaṃ
dravyatve iti dravyatvasya sattāto 'paratvamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Its own substrate': 'own' is <s>sattā</s> (existence); its substrate is a <s>guṇa</s> (quality); the absence residing in that is the absence of substance-hood; counter-positive-ness of that resides in substance-hood — thus substance-hood is lower than <s>sattā</s>. The purport is thus.

children.text:
viveka iti/ tathā ca
sāmānyaṃ trividham --- kevalaparam, kevalāparam, parāparam ceti/
saṅgrahe ca kevalaparāparapradarśanādeva parāparajāteḥ, sphuṭatayā
lābhāt tadakathanamiti bhāvaḥ/ nanu sattāyāḥ
kevalaparatvakathanamanupapannam/ premayatvādijātisattvāt sattāyāḥ
1parāparatvādityata āha --- dīpikāyām [63] sāmānyādicatuṣṭaya
iti/
children.translated_text: 'Distinction': accordingly, <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is of three kinds — exclusively higher (<s>kevalapara</s>), exclusively lower (<s>kevalāpara</s>), and both higher and lower (<s>parāpara</s>). And in the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, since only the exclusively higher and the both-higher-and-lower are exhibited, the both-higher-and-lower universal is clearly obtained, hence it is not mentioned [separately]. The purport is thus. Objection: the statement that <s>sattā</s> is exclusively higher is untenable, because since universals such as <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) exist, <s>sattā</s> would be both higher and lower. To this he replies — in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [63], 'the four beginning with <s>sāmānya</s>.'

children.text: samavāyalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence)

children.text:
samavāyastveka evetyatra saṅgrahapaṅktau samavāyasyaikatvaṃ
samavāyaniṣṭhabhedapratiyogitānavacchedakadharmavattvaṃ na tu
saṅkhyārūpam, samavāyāvṛttitvāt avyāvartakatvāt ca/ evakāraśca
īdṛśapāribhāṣikatve tātparyagrahaḥ/ yadvā ekatvamubhayāvṛttidharmaḥ/
ubhayāvṛttitvaṃ ca svapratiyogivṛttitvasvabhinnavṛttitvobhayasambandhena
rkiñcidviśiṣṭānyatvam/ evakārasya
cādheyatāśrayabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvam abhāvaśca khaṇḍaśor'thaḥ/
ādheyatāyāṃ vyutpattivaicitryeṇa prathamāntapadopasthāpyasyāpi
samavāyasya nirūpitatvasambandhenānvayaḥ/
samavāyanirūpitādheyatāśrayabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasya ca
vidheyatāvacchedakatvābhimatasambandhāvacchinnāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākasvarūpasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvasambandhe-
children.translated_text: In the [statement] '<s>samavāya</s> is indeed one': in the text of the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, the oneness of <s>samavāya</s> is the property of not possessing a property that delimits the counter-positive-ness of difference residing in <s>samavāya</s>, not [oneness] in the form of number — since it does not occur in <s>samavāya</s> and since [number] is non-distinguishing. The restrictive particle 'eva' (indeed) indicates the conventional technical sense. Alternatively, oneness is a property excluded from both [i.e., from both the counter-positive and from what is different]. Being excluded from both is otherness qualified by something, through the twofold relation of occurring in what is the counter-positive of itself and occurring in what is different from itself. The two parts of 'eva' have the meanings of delimiting the counter-positive-ness of difference in the substrate of the superstratum-relation, and the absence [of such]. In the superstratum-relation, through the variety of derivational procedures, <s>samavāya</s> too, though introduced by the nominative-ending word, is syntactically connected through the relation of being a determinant. And of the delimiting of the counter-positive-ness of difference in the substrate of the superstratum-relation determined by <s>samavāya</s>,

children.text:
nābhāve 'nvayaḥ/
tādṛśābhāvasyacaikapadārthe 'nvayaḥ/ tathā ca samavāyaḥ
samavāyanirūpitādheyatāśrayabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvaviśeṣitābhāvavadabhinna
iti bodhaḥ iti abhiprāyeṇāvatārayati - dīpikāyām [64] samavāyasya bhedo nāstītyāheti/ atra ca bhedaḥ
ādheyatāśrayabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakadharmaḥ/ samavāyasyetyatra ṣaṣṭyā
nirūpitatvamarthaḥ/ tasya ca bhedapadārthaghaṭakādheyatāyāmanvayaḥ/
asadhātvarthādheyatāyāmapi vyutpattivaicitryādanvayaḥ/
asadhātvarthādheyatāyāśca nañarthābhāve tasya ca prathamāntapadārthe
bhede 'nvayaḥ/ tathā ca
samavāyanirūpitādheyatāśrayabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakadharmaḥ
samavāyanirūpitādheyatvābhāvavāniti bodhaḥ/
children.translated_text: the syntactic connection with the absence is through the relation of counter-positive-ness of self-linking relation delimited by counter-positive-ness delimited by the relation-delimited delimitation intended as the delimitor of predicate-ness. And the syntactic connection of such an absence is with the meaning of the word 'one.' Thus the understanding is: <s>samavāya</s> is non-different from what possesses the absence qualified by the delimiting of the counter-positive-ness of difference in the substrate of the superstratum-relation determined by <s>samavāya</s>. With this intention he introduces — in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [64], 'he says that there is no difference of <s>samavāya</s>.' Here, 'difference' is a property that delimits the counter-positive-ness of difference in the substrate of the superstratum-relation. In '<s>samavāyasya</s>' (of inherence), the genitive has the meaning of being a determinant. And its syntactic connection is with the superstratum-relation that is a component of the meaning of the word 'difference.' The syntactic connection is also with the superstratum-relation in the meaning of the negative particle. And the absence that is the meaning of the negative particle has its syntactic connection with 'difference,' the meaning of the nominative-ending word. Thus the understanding is: the property delimiting the counter-positive-ness of difference in the substrate of the superstratum-relation determined by <s>samavāya</s> possesses the absence of the superstratum-relation determined by <s>samavāya</s>.

children.text:
1. taparāparatvāditi/
sattāyāḥ prameyatvāpekṣayā aparatvam, dravyatvādyapekṣayā paratvamiti
rītyā parāparatvamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Both higher and lower': <s>sattā</s> is lower relative to <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) and higher relative to substance-hood and the rest — in this way it is both higher and lower. The purport is thus.

children.text:
anuyogitāvacchedakāvacchedenābhāvabodhakatāyā nañaḥ
vyutpannatayā samavāyadvitvapakṣe 'pyuktavākyārthasaṅgatiḥ/ yadvā bhedaḥ
children.translated_text: Since the negative particle is conventionally understood as producing the cognition of absence delimited by the delimitor of counter-positive-ness, the stated sentence-meaning is coherent even on the view that there are two <s>samavāyas</s>. Alternatively, 'difference' is

children.text:
anyonyābhāvaḥ/
samavāyasyetyatra ṣaṣṭhyāḥ
ekamātravṛttidharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvamarthaḥ/ samavāyasyeti
punarāvṛttyā
children.translated_text: mutual absence. In '<s>samavāyasya</s>' (of inherence), the meaning of the genitive is counter-positive-ness delimited by a property occurring in one [<s>samavāya</s>] alone. By the repetition of '<s>samavāyasya</s>,'

children.text:
tadarthasya
samavāyavṛttitvasyāsadhātvarthādheyatāyāmanvayaḥ/ tathā ca samavāyaniṣṭhā
yā ekamātravṛttidharmāvacchinnapratiyogitā tannirūpitānyonyābhāvaḥ
samavāyanirūpitavṛttitvavāniti/ bodhaḥ/ itiśabdasya
ityākārakamarthaḥ/ tasya cābhedasambandhena
jñānotpattiprayojakaśabdarūpabrūñarthaikadeśe jñāne 'nvayaḥ/ tasya
cākhyātārthakṛtāvanvayaḥ/ anukūlatāsambandhena tādṛśajñānaṃ ca prakṛte
mānasarūpaṃ bodhyam/ tena prakṛte tasya śabdarūpatvāsaṃbhave 'pi na
kṣatiḥ/
children.translated_text: its meaning — namely, occurring in <s>samavāya</s> — is syntactically connected with the superstratum-relation in the meaning of the negative particle. Thus the understanding is: the mutual absence whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by a property occurring in one [<s>samavāya</s>] alone and residing in <s>samavāya</s> possesses the property of occurring as determined by <s>samavāya</s>. The word 'iti' has the meaning of 'having such a form.' Its syntactic connection is with cognition, which is a part of the meaning of the verbal root 'brū' (to speak), namely a word that produces cognition, through the relation of identity. And its syntactic connection is with the action that is the meaning of the finite verb. The relevant cognition should be understood as being of a mental form, through the relation of conduciveness. Therefore, even though in the present context [the cognition] cannot be of a verbal form, there is no difficulty.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām [64] rūpasamavāyeti/ ayamatrāśayaḥ-tatsambandhena tatprakārakabhramatvaṃ ca

children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [64], 'form-inherence.' The idea here is: being an error having that as a qualifier through that relation is [analyzed as] being a qualifier-mode delimited by that relation and having as its qualificand what possesses the absence whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by that relation. And this is fully intact in the cognition 'air possesses form through inherence.' Being a valid cognition having that as qualifier through that relation is not constituted by having a qualificand-ness that is the locus of the relation-property of that relation as indicated by such valid cognition, but rather is constituted by having a qualificand-ness that is the substrate of the relation-property of that relation whose determinant-ness is delimited by the counter-positive-ness of that. Since it is not accepted that in air, which is devoid of form, the relation-property of inherence delimited by counter-positive-ness of form exists, there is no unwanted consequence of such cognition being valid. Similarly, since it is accepted that the relation-property of that relation qualified by the counter-positive-ness of that and determined by that is pervaded by the existence of that through that relation, there is no [unwanted consequence that] in air

children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> [65], 'following the order of enumeration' and so forth. The fifth case-ending has the meaning of being effected. The understanding is: one who possesses the volition conducive to words that are occasioned by the purpose of the cognition whose qualificand is earth as a component of the aggregate of earth and the rest, which is non-different from what is prior to the statement of the definition of water and the rest that is effected by such following of order.

children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [65], 'regarding priority' means: regarding being what is to be stated first. [66] 'Pertaining to every entity that is the object of the definition': the meaning is the extent of every entity that is the substrate of the definition in question. Hence there is no infinite regress of over-extension with respect to the word 'pot' and the like when they denote pot and the like that are substrates of the definition in question. Accordingly, the qualification of the cognition should be given as possessing objecthood residing in every entity that is the substrate of the definition in question. The purport is thus.

children.translated_text: 'The word <s>mātra</s> (only)': here some say — what is obtained from the word <s>mātra</s> is the property of not having as a qualifier anything other than the delimitor of the defined-ness. Since the definitional sentence denotes only that definition and not others, there is no over-extension. The purport is thus — so they say. That is worthless. Because the word <s>mātra</s> has the conventional capacity to produce the cognition of exclusion of the connection with other meanings of co-occurring words, as in 'on this ground there is only a pot,' and since what is obtained from it is precisely that [exclusionary function]. The conflict with derivational convention in [the proposed interpretation of] producing the cognition of exclusion of connections other than the delimitor of the defined-ness is evident. Since verbal cognition is essentially of the form of the cognition of the connection of two word-meanings, and since ultimately even verbal cognition having earth and the like as qualificand and number as qualifier-mode is possible, the alleged verbal cognition not having any qualifier other than the delimitor of the defined-ness is not established. Thus, the definition of enumeration (<s>uddeśa</s>) is: aggregate-hood that pervades the letter-hood that is the substrate of some objecthood belonging to a cognition that delimits the capacity for verbal generation having the qualifier-mode that is the delimitor of the defined-ness. Hence there is no over-extension with respect to the earth-portion and the rest. And such aggregate-hood should be qualified by not being the determinant of lesser-occurrence-ness residing in such aggregate-hood. By that, there is no over-extension in definitional sentences and the like. And such aggregate-hood is the ground for the application of the word 'enumeration' through the relation of pervasion. Therefore, even if it is common to a part of the substrate, there is no difficulty. Since aggregate-hood is included as having disjunctive occurrence, even if it is not co-extensive with being the object of a particular cognition, there is no difficulty. If, however, it is maintained that objecthood does not have disjunctive occurrence and hence this approach is not the best, then one should state the definition of enumeration as simply: possessing a property that pervades the letter-hood of such a kind.

children.translated_text: Since the capacity to convey the exclusion of relations other than those with the meaning of co-occurring words is already obtained through conventional understanding (<s>vyutpatti</s>) in sentences like '<s>atra bhūtale ghaṭo 'sti</s>' ('the pot exists on this ground'), that alone is obtainable in language without postulating the indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>); since the conflict with conventional understanding is evident when there is no capacity to convey the exclusion of relations other than the delimitor of the indicated meaning (<s>lakṣyatāvacchedaka</s>); and since verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>) has the nature of cognizing the connection of two word-meanings, even verbal cognition having earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) and the like as qualificand with at least the number-qualifier of the stem-meaning is possible, and verbal cognition without the indicated-meaning-delimitor as qualifier is unknown. Accordingly, the definition of designation (<s>uddeśa</s>) is: being a collective (<s>samudāya</s>) that pervades the letter-hood (<s>varṇatva</s>) that is the locus of the object-hood belonging to some cognition that delimits the generative capacity (<s>janakatāvacchedaka</s>) of verbal cognition having the indicated-meaning-delimitor as qualifier. Hence there is no over-pervasion (<s>ativyāpti</s>) to the part [consisting of] earth and the like. And such collective-hood must be qualified by not being the determiner of a narrower occurrence residing in such collective-hood. By this there is no over-pervasion in definitional sentences and the like. And such collective-hood is the ground of application (<s>pravṛttinimitta</s>) of the designation-word through the relation of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>). Therefore, even though it is common to one part through the relation of substratum-hood, there is no defect. The inclusion of collective-hood is through disjunctive occurrence (<s>vyāsajyavṛttitva</s>). Hence, even though what has the form of being the object of a specific cognition applies, there is no defect. If it is said that object-hood does not have disjunctive occurrence and therefore this approach is not preferable, then the definition of designation should be stated simply as possessing a property that pervades such letter-hood. And by accepting the conventional understanding that such property-hood conveys the delimiting property of qualificand-hood, there is no occasion for over-extension. Although, to prevent deviation in verbal cognition where a synonymous word is learned,

kiñcittvaniveśādananugama iti vācyam/

vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svasamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvani ṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena

svāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedavadvṛttitvasvasāmānādhikaraṇyobhayasaṃbandhena
tādṛśadharmaviśiṣṭānyatvam/ adhikaraṇatāvaiśiṣṭyaghaṭakatayā
svaviśiṣṭadharmaviśiṣṭatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasaṃbandhaḥ
paryavasitaḥ/ ata eva 'pṛthivī gandhavatī' iti vākye nātiprasaṅga
iti madekapariśīlitaḥ panthāḥ/
children.translated_text: the inclusion of the qualifier-hood delimited by earth-ness and the like, which has become the indicated-meaning-delimitor, in the generative capacity is impossible [without further qualification]; nevertheless, what should be included in the definition is precisely the generative capacity delimited by the verbal-hood that is immediately subsequent to the cognition of that particular word. Hence there is no defect. Thus, the definition of the designation of earth should be understood in this manner: it is that property which pervades the letter-hood that is the locus of the object-hood belonging to some cognition that delimits the generative capacity determined by the verbal-hood immediately subsequent to the cognition of the word 'earth,' and which does not determine a narrower occurrence residing in such pervading collective. And the definition of designation for each respective [substance] should be understood in this fashion. Nor should it be objected that there is failure to apply (<s>ananugama</s>) due to the non-inclusion of a universal qualifier; for what is intended is possessing a property qualified by the substratum-hood (<s>adhikaraṇatā</s>) that determines such generative capacity. The qualification is through the relation of possessing a difference whose counter-positive-hood-delimitor is identical with the delimitor-hood residing in oneself, delimited by the relation of co-located-difference-counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood, through the relation of the letter-hood that is the locus of the object-hood qualified by the qualification of one's own substratum-hood. The qualification in the object-hood is through the dual relation of the generative-capacity-delimitor-hood that determines oneself and the cognition-belonging-hood of one's own locus. And the difference that does not determine a narrower occurrence residing in such property is otherness qualified by such property, through the dual relation of occurring in what possesses the difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by oneself and co-location with oneself. Because the qualification of substratum-hood is a component, the relation of possessing the difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the delimitor-hood residing in oneself, delimited by the relation of the property qualified by oneself, is the final result. For this very reason, there is no over-extension in the sentence '<s>pṛthivī gandhavatī</s>' ('earth possesses smell'). This is the path I have carefully investigated.

dīpikāvākye tādṛśāvayavābhyāmārabdhamiti vigrahāt

surabhigandhaṃ prati
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākasyāsurabhigandhābhāvasya
samavāyasaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākasya surabhigandhābhāvasyaiva vā
kāryakālavṛttitayā kāraṇatvena pratītibalena
surabhyasurabhyubhayorasaṃbandhayoreva samavāyenotpattau
kāryakālāvachedena pratibandhakābhāvarūpakāraṇābhāvāt
nobhayagandhotpattiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: in the <s>Dīpikā</s> sentence '<s>surabhyasurabhyavayavārabdha</s>' ('produced from fragrant and non-fragrant parts'), since the analysis yields 'produced from two such parts,' what is obtained is possessing the initial origination co-inhering in such parts. For the verb '<s>rabhateḥ</s>' with the prefix '<s>āṅ</s>' conveys initial origination, and the meaning of the '<s>kta</s>' suffix is what-is-to-be-predicated. But that is inconsistent, since origination is a property of the self alone. Therefore [the author] says — [66] 'In "produced" (<s>ārabdha</s>), [the meaning is] "generated" (<s>janya</s>).' [66] 'Through mutual opposition' — opposition means obstructor-hood. There, mutuality means being determined by the locus of the obstructor-hood that determines one's own locus, which amounts to being qualified by obstructor-hood, through the dual relation of occurring in the determiner of oneself and occurring in one's own locus. [66] 'Fragrant smell as against non-fragrant smell,' and so forth — here, with respect to fragrant smell through the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), since the absence of non-fragrant smell whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the inherence relation, or the absence of fragrant smell whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the inherence relation, exists at the time of the effect — by the force of the cognition that [one of these] has causal status as existing at the time of the effect — since fragrant and non-fragrant [smells], being mutually unrelated, when origination is through inherence, lack the cause in the form of the absence of an obstructor delimited by the time of the effect, the origination of both smells [simultaneously] does not occur. This is the purport.

pratītisaṃbhavenetyatra pratītāvanveti/ tṛtīyāyāḥ prayojyatvamarthaḥ/

children.translated_text: is the meaning of the instrumental case. And that is established by the possibility of the cognition stated in 'by the possibility of cognition.' The meaning of the instrumental case is being-an-instrument. Its instrumental role in the cognition of smell through inherence should be understood as having causal capacity in the manner of an error-defect. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [65] 'because mixed smell (<s>citragandha</s>) is not accepted' — accordingly, since mixed smell does not exist, under-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) does remain. This is the purport.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām tuṣyatu durjana iti
nyāyeneti/ atrāyamāśayaḥ-- surabhyasurabhigandhavatparamāṇubhyāṃ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'by the maxim of "let the wicked be satisfied"' — here the intention is: from atoms possessing fragrant and non-fragrant smell,

children.text:
dvyaṇukamārabdham/
tatastryaṇukādikrameṇa mahāvayaviparyantamutpannam/ tatra ghaṭe
gandhapratītirnopeyata eva tadavayavakapālādau gandhābhāvena tatra
gandhāsaṃbhavāt paramāṇugandhasya cāpratyakṣatvāt/ vastutastu
paramāṇugandhasya laukikapratyakṣaviṣayatvābhāve 'pi
svasamavāyighaṭitaparaṃparāsaṃbandhena tatra
paramāṇugandhaviṣayakālaukikapratyakṣaṃ saṃbhavatyeva/ yadi cāyaṃ
gandhavāniti laukikapratītirjāyate ityāgrahastadāstu citragandha
iti/ [65] gandhasamānādhikareṇeti/ atrāpi
pūrvavadevārtho bodhyaḥ/ anyathā pūrvarītyā doṣāt/
children.translated_text: a dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) is produced. From that, through the sequence of triads (<s>tryaṇuka</s>) and so forth, up to the gross parts, [the substance] is produced. There, the cognition of smell in the pot need not be resorted to at all, since smell is absent in the pot's component parts such as potsherds, and hence smell is impossible there, and the smell of atoms is imperceptible. In reality, however, even though the smell of atoms is not an object of ordinary perception, extra-ordinary perception (<s>alaukikapratyakṣa</s>) of the smell of atoms is indeed possible there through the indirect sequential relation (<s>paraṃparāsaṃbandha</s>) constituted by the co-inherents of one's own co-inherent. If there is insistence that ordinary cognition 'this possesses smell' does arise, then let there be mixed smell (<s>citragandha</s>). [65] 'Co-located with smell' — here too, the meaning should be understood as before. Otherwise, there would be the defect stated in the previous manner.

children.text:
nanu dravyatvāparatvaṃ
dravyabhinnabhinnatvam, tathā ca kathamasaṃbhavavāraṇamityata āha - [66] dravyatvanyūnavṛttītyarthakamiti/ dravyatvābhāvavadavṛttitvameva
sattāvāraṇāya kuto na niveśyata ityata āha - [66] teneti/ [66] dravyatvavyudāsa iti/ dravyatvasya
svābhāvavadavṛtti'pi svasamānādhikaraṇābhāvapratiyogitvavirahāt/
kālikasaṃbandhena tādṛśadharmavattvamādāyātivyāptivāraṇāya [65] jātīti/ nityatvamātramatra vivakṣitam/ anekasamavetatvasya
prakṛte 'vyāvartakatvāt/ pṛthivījalānyataratvasya
samavāyasaṃbandhaghaṭitasāmānādhikaraṇyavirahāt/ kālikasaṃbandhena
tādṛśadharmavattvamādāyātivyāptivāraṇāya samavāyena
tādṛśadharmavattvasya vivakṣaṇīyatayā uktānyataratvamādāya doṣāprasakteśca/
pṛthivījaladvitvādīnāmapi apekṣābuddhiviśeṣaviṣayatvarūpatayā
nityatvaviraheṇaiva vāraṇaṃ bodhyam/ [66] svāśrayasaṃyuktatvasaṃbandhenetyādiriti/ atrāpi pūrvavadevārtho
varṇanīyaḥ/ [66] anugatarūpeṇa -
svaniṣṭhādheyatāvacchedakātiriktatvenetyarthaḥ/
sarvaniṣṭhādheyatānavacchedakasaṃbandhena ghaṭādeḥ kapālādilakṣaṇatve
bhūtalādau ghaṭādisaṃyogini ativyāpteḥ/ evaṃ samavāyādīnāṃ
tādṛśarūpeṇa saṃbandhatvamapyaprāmāṇikam/ [66] vastutastviti/
bodhyamiti/ pṛthivyāḥ samavāyena gandho lakṣaṇaṃ, samavāyena kapālasya
ghaṭo lakṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: the otherness-from-substance-hood (<s>dravyatvāparatva</s>) is being-different-from-what-is-different-from-substance. How then can the impossibility [of over-pervasion] be prevented? Therefore [the author] says — [66] 'The meaning is: having a narrower occurrence than substance-hood.' Why is the non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of substance-hood not included to prevent [the inclusion of] existence (<s>sattā</s>)? Therefore [the author] says — [66] 'By that.' [66] 'The exclusion of substance-hood' — although substance-hood does not occur in what possesses its own absence, it lacks the counter-positive-hood of an absence co-located with itself. To prevent over-pervasion by adopting the possession of such a property through a temporal relation — [65] '<s>jāti</s> (universal)' — here only eternality is intended. Since the property of inhering-in-many has no distinguishing power in the present context; and since the either-earth-or-water-hood lacks co-location through the inherence relation; and since by adopting the possession of such a property through a temporal relation, it must be intended that such property-possession is through inherence, and by adopting the said either-hood the defect does not arise. The exclusion of the duality of earth-water and the like should also be understood through the absence of eternality alone, since these are in the form of being objects of a specific relative cognition. [66] 'Through the relation of being-conjoined-with-one's-own-locus,' and so forth — here too the meaning should be explained as before. [66] 'In a pervading form' — the meaning is: through a form other than the delimitor of the superimposed-ness residing in oneself. If the definition of potsherds and the like for pots were through the relation of co-location with all [loci], with a relation that is not the delimitor of any superimposed-ness, there would be over-pervasion to the ground and the like that are conjoined with pots. Similarly, the relation-hood of inherence and the like in such a form is also without warrant. [66] 'In reality, however' — 'it should be understood' — the meaning is: smell through the relation of inherence is the definition of earth; the pot through the relation of inherence is the definition of the potsherd. This is the purport.

children.text: pṛthivīvibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of Earth (<s>Pṛthivī</s>)

children.text:
saṃgrahe [69] sā
dvividhā nityā anityā ceti/ dve vidhe yasyāḥ sā dvividhā, vidhā
nāma vibhājakadharmaḥ,
uddeśyatāvacchedakapṛthivītvādisākṣādvyāpyadharma iti yāvat/
bahuvrīhāvuttarapadasyānyapadārthe nirūḍhalakṣaṇāyāḥ sarvasaṃmatatayā
dvitvasaṃkhyāśrayavibhājakadharmavati prakṛte vidhāpadasya nirūḍhalakṣaṇā/
dvipadaṃ tātparyagrāhakam/ nityānityayoḥ
nityānityānyataratvasaṃbandhenānvayaḥ pṛthivyām/ sarvatra
vibhāgavākyasthale tathā vyutpatteḥ svīkārāt/ iti śabdaḥ
hetugarbhaviśeṣaṇadyotakaḥ/ tathā ca yataḥ tathā tataḥ pṛthivī
dvitvāśrayatādṛśadharmavatīti bodhaḥ/ ata eva nityānityapadayoḥ
strīliṅgatvamupapannam, tayoḥ pṛthivīpadasamānādhikaraṇatvāt/
yattu-nityānityapade nityatvānityatvapare/ tayorabhedasaṃbandhena
vibhājakadharme 'nvaya - iti, tattuccham/ ubhayābhedasya
vibhājakadharme 'saṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṃgraha</s> [69], '<s>sā dvividhā nityā anityā ca</s>' ('it is of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal'). That which has two kinds is two-fold; a 'kind' (<s>vidhā</s>) means a dividing property — that is, a property that is directly pervaded by earth-ness and the like which delimit the designandum-hood. In the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, since the settled secondary signification (<s>nirūḍhalakṣaṇā</s>) of the latter member [referring] to the meaning of another member is universally accepted, the word '<s>vidhā</s>' has settled secondary signification in the present context where it applies to what possesses a dividing property that is the locus of the number duality. The two words [eternal and non-eternal] are the indicators of the intended meaning (<s>tātparyagrāhaka</s>). The connection (<s>anvaya</s>) of 'eternal' and 'non-eternal' with earth is through the relation of either-eternality-or-non-eternality. Because such conventional understanding is accepted in all cases of division-statements. The word '<s>iti</s>' indicates a qualifying reason. Accordingly, the verbal cognition is: because it is so, therefore earth possesses such a property that is the locus of duality. For this very reason, the feminine gender of the words 'eternal' and 'non-eternal' is justified, since they are co-referential with the word 'earth.' As for the view that the words 'eternal' and 'non-eternal' refer to eternality and non-eternality, and their connection with the dividing property is through the relation of identity — that is worthless, since identity with both cannot apply to the dividing property.

children.text:
anyataratvabodhakapadābhāvena
nityatvānityatvānyatarabhedabodhāsaṃbhavāt tayorlakṣaṇāyāṃ
mānābhāvāt/ yādṛśārthasya lakṣaṇayā yatkiñcitpadārthabodhaḥ
tādṛśārthabodhasya śaktādapi padādānubhāvikatvena pṛthivī dvividhā
nityatvamanityatvamiti prayogāpatteḥ/
vidhāpadārthatāvacchedakavibhājakadharmaniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitābhedasaṃbandhāvacchinnaprakāratāsabandhena
śābdabodhaṃ prati
vidhāpadasamabhivyāhṛtaitipadasamabhivyāhṛtayakiñcitpadanirūpitaśakti jñānādeḥ
pratibandhakatvādikalpane mahāgauravāpatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Since, in the absence of a word conveying either-hood, the cognition of the difference that is either eternality or non-eternality is impossible; and since there is no warrant for secondary signification of those [words]; whatever verbal cognition of any word-meaning arises through secondary signification of such a meaning — since such cognition of meaning is experientially possible even from a word having primary denotative power, the undesirable consequence would follow that one could construct '<s>pṛthivī dvividhā nityatvam anityatvam</s>' ('earth is two-fold: eternality, non-eternality') [as an acceptable sentence]. And because postulating that the cognition of the denotative power of any word co-occurring with the '<s>iti</s>' word co-occurring with the '<s>vidhā</s>' word serves as an obstructor of verbal cognition through the relation of qualifier-hood delimited by the identity-relation delimited by the dividing-property-delimiting-qualificand-hood-determining connection that is the meaning of the word '<s>vidhā</s>' — [such postulation] would lead to the undesirable consequence of extreme cumbersomeness (<s>mahāgaurava</s>).

children.text:
atha
paramāṇurdviṃvidhaḥ-nityo 'nityaśca/ dravyaṃ dvividham-pṛthivī jalaṃ
ceti prayogāpattiriti cet-na/ dvividhetyādibahuvrīhau
vidhāpadārthatayā yāvanto dharmāḥ pratīyante
tāvaddharmamātraviṣayakadhīviśeṣaviṣayatvarūpadvitvādiviśeṣitadharmavati
nirūḍhalakṣaṇā/ viśeṣitatvaṃ ca
svavyāpakapṛthivītvādisākṣādvyāpyavyāpyatvāśrayatvasvāśrayatvobhayasambandhenetyadoṣaḥ/
uddeśyatāvacchedakībhūtapṛthivītvādyavacchedena
tādṛśadharmavadanvayasvīkārāt na dravyaṃ dvividham pṛthivī jalaṃ
cetyādiprayogaḥ/ yadyapi nityatvānityatvayorjalādisādhāraṇatayā na
pṛthivītvādivyāpyatvaṃ tathāpi
pṛthivītvādyanyatamatvaviśiṣṭasvarūpādisambandhena
tayostathātvamakṣatam/ sākṣātpadaṃ ca 'pṛthivī trividhā
nityānityapaṭaśceti' ityādi prayogavāraṇāya/ 'āpo dvividhāḥ-
nityānityāśceti' ityādāvapyuktaiva rītiḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, if it be objected that there would be the unwanted consequence of usages such as 'an atom is of two kinds — eternal and non-eternal' and 'substance is of two kinds — earth and water' — no. In the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) 'of two kinds' and the like, the conventional meaning (<s>nirūḍhalakṣaṇā</s>) applies to that which possesses a property qualified by duality and the like, which has the nature of being the object of a particular cognition whose content is merely the properties — as many as are apprehended as the referent of the word 'kind' (<s>vidhā</s>). And the qualification is through the double relation of being the locus of the substratum-hood of what is directly pervaded by earth-ness and the like, which pervades [the property in question], and being the self-locus — hence there is no defect. Since the positive concomitance with what possesses such a property is accepted through the delimitation by earth-ness and the like, which have become the delimitors of the subject-hood, the usage 'substance is of two kinds — earth and water' does not arise. Although eternality and non-eternality, being common to water and the like, are not pervaded by earth-ness and the like, nevertheless their being so [i.e. serving as classifiers] remains intact through the relation of intrinsic nature and the like qualified by the disjunctive property of earth-ness and the like. And the word 'directly' (<s>sākṣāt</s>) is for preventing usages such as 'earth is of three kinds — eternal, non-eternal, and cloth.' The same procedure applies in cases such as 'waters are of two kinds — eternal and non-eternal.'

children.text:
yadi ca 'punastrividhā
- śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt' ityādeḥ
pṛthivīsāmānyavibhāgaparatāmate
'tādṛśabhedaprayuktatritvasaṅkhyāviśiṣṭapṛthivītvasākṣādvyāpyadharmavatī
pṛthivī' itayādirītyaiva bodhasya vaktavyatayā śarītatvādīnāṃ
tādṛśavyāpyatāviraheṇāsaṅgatiriti vibhāvyate, tadā
uddeśyatāvacchedakapṛthivītvādisākṣādvyāpyatvaṃ
children.translated_text: And if, regarding '[earth is] again of three kinds — due to the distinction of body, sense-organ, and object,' when on the view that this concerns the general division of earth, the understanding must be expressed only in the manner 'earth possesses a property directly pervaded by earth-ness, qualified by the number three occasioned by such distinction,' and since body-ness and the like lack such pervadedness, there would be incoherence — if this is considered, then the direct pervadedness by earth-ness and the like as delimitors of subject-hood

children.text:
nopādeyam/
vibhājakadharmāṇāṃ parasparaṃ vaiyadhikaraṇyabhānavyutpatteḥ
dvividhetyādau svīkārāt 'pṛthivī trividhā, nityānityaghaṭaśca'
iti prayogānavakāśaḥ/ evaṃ ca bahuvrīhau
tādṛśadvitvaviśiṣṭāśrayadharmavati nirūḍhalakṣaṇā/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
children.translated_text: need not be adopted. Since the dividing properties are understood from convention to be mutually in different loci, and since this is accepted in 'of two kinds' and the like, there is no occasion for the usage 'earth is of three kinds — eternal, non-eternal, and pot.' And accordingly, in the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, the conventional meaning applies to that which possesses the property of being the locus qualified by such duality. The qualification

children.text:
1svasetyādibhedavattvatādātmyobhayasambandhena/
bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā
uddeśyatāvacchedakapṛthivītvādisamānādhikaraṇaniṣṭhatvaviśeṣitasvaniṣṭhā
- vacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattva
avacchedakatāniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvobhayasambandhāvacchinnā
tatraikāvacchedakatā nityatvātiriktā
svāśrayādhikaraṇakālavṛttitvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Of its own' and so forth — through both the relations of identity and possessing difference [from others]. The delimitor of the counter-positiveness of difference is that which resides in oneself, qualified by residing in a co-located entity with earth-ness and the like that are the delimitors of subject-hood. The counter-positiveness of the delimitor-hood of the delimitor of the counter-positiveness of difference — through both the relations of possessing difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor that is the delimitor-hood residing in the delimitor-hood of the counter-positiveness [and so on]. Among these, the single delimitor-hood distinct from eternality is through the relation of possessing difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor-hood that is one's own, residing [in what is] delimited by the relation of existing at the time of the locus of one's own substratum.

children.text:
nanu purastrividheti
pṛthivīsāmānyavibhāgo vā kāryapṛthivīvibhāgo vā/ nādyaḥ,
nityapṛthivyāḥ śarīrādāvantarbhāvāsambhavāt/ nāpi rdvintīyaḥ,
punaśśabdasvārasyavirodhāt/ tena hi yaddharmāvacchinnasya prāgvibhāgaḥ
kṛti taddharmāvacchinnasyaiva rūpāntareṇa - vibhajanaṃ sūcyata ityata āha
prakāśikāyām [70] atreti/ tathā ca 'punastrividhā' ityādau
pṛthivīsāmānyasyaiva vibhāgaḥ/ 'viṣayo mṛtpāṣāṇādiḥ- ityatra
ādipadena paramāṇuparigrahasambhavāt/
bhaumadivyaudaryākarajabhedāditi taijasaviṣayavibhāgasthale 'pi
bhūmeridaṃ bhaumamamiti vigrahāt bhūmi sambandhyādiparatvāt tenaiva
taijasaparamāṇusaṅgrahāditi bhāvaḥ/ [70] varṇayantīti/ atra
punaśśabdāsvārasyamavasarabījam/ idamatra bodhyam - atra 'punaḥ
trividhā śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt' ityatra
śarīrapratiyogikatvenrdiya -
pratiyogikatvānyataravanniṣṭhādheyatatvaśarīrapratiyogikatvaviṣayapratiyogikatvānyataravanniṣṭhadheyatvānyatamasambandhena
śarīrāderekatra dvayamiti rītyā bhedapadārthe anyonyābhāve anvayaḥ/
pañcamyāḥ prayojyatvamarthaḥ/
śarīrādiviśeṣitabhedavṛttitritvaviśiṣṭavibhājakadharmavatīti bodhaḥ/
bhedasya prayojakatvaṃ ca svajñānādhīnāpekṣāba1ddhidvārā/ uktarītyā
anyatrāpi bodhaḥ ūhyaḥ/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca pūrvavaditi/
children.translated_text: Now, '[earth is] again of three kinds' — is this a general division of earth or a division of produced earth? Not the first, because it is impossible to include eternal earth under body and the like. Nor the second, because it would conflict with the natural import of the word 'again' (<s>punaḥ</s>), for by that word it is indicated that what was previously divided under one property is being further divided under a different aspect of the same property. To this he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [70] — 'here' etc. And accordingly, in 'again of three kinds' and the like, it is the general [class of] earth itself that is being divided. In 'the object is clay, stone, and so forth,' since the inclusion of atoms is possible through the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>). In the section on the division of fiery objects too, [the passage] 'of the earth, hence earthly' — since by derivation the word '<s>bhauma</s>' refers to what is related to earth and the like — by that very [relation], fiery atoms are also included. This is the purport. [70] 'They explain' etc. Here, the natural import of the word 'again' is the basis for the occasion [of the division]. This should be understood here — in 'again of three kinds, due to the distinction of body, sense-organ, and object,' the positive concomitance of the word 'difference' (<s>bheda</s>) is with mutual absence, in the manner that in one [entity] there are two [differences] — the difference as counter-positive of body, and the difference as counter-positive of sense-organ and object (or either of them), through the relation of superstratum-hood residing in the disjunctive [property]. The fifth case-ending has the meaning of causality. The understanding is: 'possessing dividing properties qualified by the number three, which resides in difference qualified by body and the like.' And the causality of difference is through the cognition of expectancy dependent on the knowledge of it. The understanding in other cases too should be inferred in the same manner. And the qualification is as before.

children.text:
1.
svasetyādibhedavāveti/
svasamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvani ṣṭhavacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Of its own' and so forth — 'possessing difference' — the meaning is: possessing difference whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of co-location with difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor residing in oneself, which is co-located with earth-ness and the like that are the delimitors of subject-hood.

children.text:
viṣayo mṛtpāṣāṇādiriti/
mṛtpāṣāṇāvādī yasyeti vyutpattyā
mṛtpāṣāṇādiniṣṭhāditānirūpakaḥ pārthivaviṣaya iti bodhaḥ/
taddharmāvacchinnasya tadāditvaṃ nāma
uddeśyatāvacchedakaniṣṭhatannirūpitādheyatāviśiṣṭatvam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāśrayadharmatāviśiṣṭataddharmavattvasambandhena/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svavyāpyadharmāvacchinnabodhakapadapūrvapadapratipādyatāvacchedakatvasvavyāpyatvobhayasambandhena/
children.translated_text: 'The object is clay, stone, and so forth' — by the derivation 'clay, stone, and so forth are its beginning (<s>ādi</s>),' the understanding is: the earthly object is that which determines the <s>ādi</s>-ness (initial-ness) residing in clay, stone, and the like. The <s>ādi</s>-ness of what is delimited by that property is the qualifiedness by the superstratum-hood determined by the [property] that resides in the delimitor of subject-hood. The qualification is through the relation of possessing that property, which is qualified by the property-hood of one's own locus. And the qualification is through both the relations of being the explicandum of the preceding word and being pervaded by one's own pervaded property, delimited by the property delimiting the denotation of the preceding word.

children.text:
kecittu -
svaviṣayakajñānaviṣayasamudāyaghaṭakatvaṃ āditvam/ svaṃ
pārthivādiviṣayaḥ/ tathā ca
mṛtpāṣāṇādiviṣayakajñānaviṣayasamudāyaghaṭakatānirūpakaḥ
mṛtpāṣāṇādighaṭitasamudāyaviṣayakajñānaviṣayaḥ pārthivaviṣaya
children.translated_text: Some, however, [say]: <s>ādi</s>-ness (initial-ness) is being a constituent of the aggregate that is the object of the cognition of one's own object. 'One's own' [refers to] the earthly and other objects. And accordingly, the earthly object is that which determines the <s>ādi</s>-ness consisting in being a constituent of the aggregate that is the object of the cognition of clay, stone, and so forth — i.e., it is the object of a cognition whose object is the aggregate constituted by clay, stone, and the like.

children.text:
ityarthaḥ-iti
vyācakruḥ/ atastantusamadāyatvasya dhīviśeṣaviṣayatvarūpatayā viśiṣya
tattatpadārthajñāne samudāyatvasyaiva durnirūpatvāt/
tattatpadāsarvajñajīve 'sambhavāt/ sambandhakoṭau
svavyāpyatvopādanāt, viṣayo mṛtpāṣāṇajalādiriti vākyasya na
prāmāṇyam/ vyāpyatvaṃ cātra
tatsamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatve sati
tatsāmānādhikaraṇyam, na tu tadabhāvavadavṛttitvam/ tena 'prameyaḥ
pṛthivyādiḥ' ityādivākyasya na prāmāṇyānupapattiḥ/
satyantaniveśācca 'pṛthivī dravyādi gandhavadādi' rityādivākyasya na
prāmāṇyam/ sāmānādhikaraṇyaniveśācca mṛtpāṣāṇādiriti vākyasya
na prāmāṇyam ityalamativistareṇa/ [70] antyeti/
dravyasamānādhikaraṇabhinnatvamantyāvayavitvamiha vivakṣitam/
children.translated_text: This is the meaning — so they explain. Therefore, since aggregate-hood in the form of being the object of a particular cognition is difficult to define when specifically applied to each particular entity — and since such a term [as 'aggregate-ness'] is impossible in an omniscient being — and since pervadedness is adopted in the relational component, the statement 'the object is clay, stone, water, and so forth' is not authoritative.
