And pervadedness here means: being co-located with something while possessing the delimitor of counter-positiveness of difference co-located with it — not non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of that. Hence there is no failure of authoritativeness for statements like 'the knowable is earth and the like.' And because of the stipulation of the word 'and so forth' (<s>sati</s>), statements like 'earth is substance and so forth, possessing smell and so forth' are not authoritative. And because of the stipulation of co-location, the statement 'clay, stone, and so forth' is not authoritative — enough of excessive elaboration. [70] 'Final' etc. — the final constituent-hood intended here is the property of being a different [entity] co-located with substance.

children.text:
nanu śarīrasya
śarīratvajātireva kuto lakṣaṇatayā noktā/ evamindriyasyāpi
indriyatvajātimattvam/ na ca śarīṃratvāderjātitvemānābhāvaḥ/
1padavācyatāpakṣakānumānasyaiva tathātvāt ata āha - śarīratvamiti/
children.translated_text: Now, why is the universal body-ness (<s>śarīratva-jāti</s>) not stated as the definition of body? Similarly, the sense-organ too would have the universal sense-organ-ness. Nor is there an absence of evidence for body-ness and the like being universals, since the inference on the alternative that they are word-denotations is itself of that nature. To this he says — '<s>śarīratva</s>' (body-ness) etc.

children.text:
1.
padavācyatāpakṣakānumānasyeti/ śarīrapadavācyatā kiñciddharmāvacchinnā
padavācyatātvāt ghaṭapadavācyatāvat ityanumānasyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'The inference on the alternative of word-denotation' — the meaning is: the inference 'the denotation of the word body is delimited by some property, because of being a word-denotation, like the denotation of the word pot.'

children.text:
śabdetaretyādīndriyalakṣaṇe viśeṣapadavaiyarthyaṃ
saṃyogasyodbhūtatvarūpajātyanākrāntatvāt/ ataḥ tatpadaṃ
sārthakayitumāha-
children.translated_text: In the definition of sense-organs other than the auditory, the word '<s>viśeṣa</s>' (particular) would be otiose, since conjunction is not pervaded by a universal in the form of <s>udbhūtatva</s> (prominence). Therefore, to make that word meaningful, he says —

children.text:
udtatvaṃ na jātiriti/ [70] śuklanvādinā sāṅkaryāditi/ saṅkara eva sāṅkaryam/
cāturvarṇyāditvāt svārthe ṣyañ/ tena pṛthivītvādinā
saṅkarāditi pūrvagranthenāvirodhaḥ/ [70] kāraṇatvānupapatteriti/
idamatra cintyam-śuklatvādivyāpyanānodbhūtatvābhyupagame 'pi
tattududbhūtānyatamatvena cākṣuṣaṃ prati ekahetutvaṃ suvacam/
anyatamatvaghaṭakabhedānāṃ mitho viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāve
vinigamanāviraha iti tu nāśaṅkanīyam/ udbhūtatvasya
tattadanudbhūtatvābhāvakūṭarūpatvapakṣe 'pi kūṭatvasya
tattadviṣayakadhīviśeṣaviṣayatvarūparūpatayā tattadviṣayakatvānāṃ
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāve vinigamanāvirahasya tulyatvāt/
saṃyogādikamādāyākāśādicākṣuṣavāraṇāya rūpatvasya
kāraṇatāvacchedakakoṭau antarbhāvanīyatayā
rūpatvatādṛśodbhūtatvayoḥ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatāvacchedakabhāve
vinigamanāviraheṇa mahāgauravaprasaṅgācceti/ [71] viśeṣetīti/ sāmānyaguṇabhinnetyarthaḥ/ tena
dravyatvādikamādāyāsambhavavāraṇāya guṇapadamiti dhyeyam/
rūpābhāveti/ udbhūtarūpābhāvetyarthaḥ/ tena nābhāvasya
yogyatānupapattiḥ/ [71] sannikarṣaghaṭakatayeti/ ayamatra bhāvaḥ-
jñānakāraṇatvaṃ jñānaniyatapūrvavṛttitvaṃ tacca
kālacakṣussaṃyoge 'kṣatameva/ anyathā
cakṣussaṃyogaviśiṣṭanirūpitaviśeṣaṇatāviraheṇa kāle
rūpābhāvapratyakṣānupapatteriti/
children.translated_text: '<s>Udbhūtatva</s> (prominence) is not a universal' etc. [70] 'Because of the mixing with white and the like' etc. — mixing itself is <s>sāṅkarya</s>. The suffix <s>ṣyañ</s> is in the sense of the abstract noun, because of [words like] <s>cāturvarṇya</s> and the like. Hence there is no contradiction with the earlier text [which says] 'because of mixing with earth-ness and the like.' [70] 'Because of the impossibility of causality' etc. — this should be considered here: even if one accepts that <s>udbhūtatva</s> (prominence) is not pervaded by white-ness and the like, since it is perceptible to the eye through the disjunctive property of being either that or <s>udbhūta</s> (prominent), its being a single cause [for visual perception] is easily stated. Nor should it be objected that when the differences constituting the disjunctive property stand in the relation of qualifier and qualificand to each other, there is no ground for determination — for even on the view that <s>udbhūtatva</s> is a composite form (<s>kūṭarūpa</s>) consisting of the absence of each non-prominence, since the composite-ness has the nature of being the object of particular cognitions of each [non-prominence], the same difficulty of lack of determination when the particular object-hoods stand in the qualifier-qualificand relation applies equally. Since, in order to prevent sky and the like from being visual objects by taking conjunction and the like [as causes], <s>rūpatva</s> (colour-ness) must be included in the delimitor of causality, and since when <s>rūpatva</s> and such <s>udbhūtatva</s> stand in the qualifier-qualificand relation, the lack of determination would result in great heaviness — [hence the objection fails]. [71] '<s>Viśeṣa</s>' etc. — the meaning is: different from generic qualities. Hence the word 'quality' should be noted as intended to prevent the impossibility by taking substance-ness and the like [as the referent]. 'Absence of colour' — the meaning is: absence of prominent colour. Hence there is no failure of eligibility for absence [itself]. [71] 'As a constituent of the sense-contact' etc. — the purport here is: causality for cognition means invariable prior occurrence to the cognition, and that is unimpaired in the conjunction of time with the eye. Otherwise, since the relation of qualificand-hood determined by the conjunction with the eye would be absent in time, the perception of the absence of colour in time would be impossible.

children.text:
manaḥ padamiti/ kāle sukhaṃ nāstīti
pratyakṣantu na sambhavatyeva, vijātīyātmamanassaṃyogasya jñānamātraṃ prati
hetutvaṃsvīkārāt/ tathā ca tattadbhedakūṭaniveśagauravabhayena
sarvamatasādhāraṇyāyoktaviśeṣaṇaṃ niveśitamiti bhāvaḥ/ [71] prayojanakathanaparatayeti/ etena ghrāṇendriye 'numānapramāṇamapi
sūcitam/ tathā hi gandhasākṣātkāraḥ manobhinnendriyakaraṇakaḥ
mānasānyapratyakṣasāmānyasākṣātkāratvāt/ ghaṭādicākṣuṣajñānasāmānyaṃ
prati samavāyikāraṇatvāt siddhasādhanavāraṇāya sādhyaśarīre
manobhinneti mānasasākṣātkāre vyabhicāravāraṇāya hetukoṭau
mānasānyeti/ [71] evamuttaratra jñeyamiti/
śītasparśasamānādhikaraṇeti padaṃ śītatvaṃ sparśaniṣṭhajātiviśeṣa
iti sūcanāya/ śītasparśavatyaḥ āpaḥ ityādisaṅgrahavākye 'pi
children.translated_text: 'The word <s>manas</s> (mind)' etc. — the perception 'pleasure does not exist in time,' however, is simply not possible, since the conjunction of the mind with a self of a different class is accepted as a cause for cognition only. And accordingly, out of fear of the heaviness of stipulating composite [properties] of each difference, the qualifier stated as common to all views is adopted — this is the purport. [71] 'With the intention of stating the purpose' etc. — by this, inferential proof regarding the olfactory organ is also indicated. Namely: the direct perception of smell has as its instrument a sense-organ different from the mind — because of being a non-mental perceptual cognition of a universal, like the visual cognition of a pot and the like. Since it is an <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherence-cause) for the visual cognition of pot and the like as a universal, to prevent the defect of proving what is already established, 'different from mind' is [stated] with respect to the body that is the locus of the probandum; and to prevent deviation in mental perception, 'non-mental' is [stated] in the probans-component. [71] 'Thus it should be known further' etc. — the expression 'co-located with cold touch' is to indicate that coldness is a particular universal residing in touch. In the summary statement 'waters possess cold touch' and the like too,

children.text:
evameva bodhyam/ na
tu tadapi lakṣaṇapraviṣṭam/ evaṃ uttaratrāpi/
children.translated_text: the same understanding applies. But that too is not included within the definition. Similarly in what follows.

children.text: tejonirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>tejas</s> (fire/light)

children.text:
saṅgrahe [76] abindhanaṃ vidyudādi āpaḥ indhanāni yasyeti bahuvrīhiṃ
varṇayati/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, [76] he explains the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound '<s>abindhana</s>' as 'that whose fuel is not water' — '<s>āpaḥ indhanāni yasya</s> (that whose fuel is water) [negated].'

children.text:
kecittu-karaṇe
lyuḍantasyendhanaśabdasyāpśabdasamānādhikaraṇatve viśeṣyanighnatve na
strīliṅgatvāpattyā 'ṭiḍhḍhāṇañi'tyādinā ṅīp(?) prasaṅgena
abindhanamiti rūpāniṣptteḥ abindhanikamityeva vaktavyatvāt
indhanaśabdasya pūrvanipātāpatteśca
indhanaśabdasyā1tathātvādityabhiprāyeṇa vyadhikaraṇabahuvrīhiṃ
pradarśayati adbhiḥ indhanamityādinā/ tathā ca indhanaśabdaḥ bhāve
lyuḍanta iti bhāvaḥ-ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: Some, however, [say]: since the word <s>indhana</s> (fuel), ending in the <s>lyuṭ</s> suffix in the instrumental sense, when co-located with the word <s>ap</s> (water), would be subject to the rule of qualifier-predominance, and since by the application of the <s>ṅīp</s> suffix through the rule '<s>ṭiḍḍhāṇañ</s>' and the like, the form '<s>abindhana</s>' would not be derived — rather '<s>abindhanika</s>' would have to be said — and since there would be the unwanted consequence of the prior member placement of the word <s>indhana</s>, and since the word <s>indhana</s> is not of such a nature [as to allow it] — with this intent, they present a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> with terms in different loci: '<s>adbhiḥ indhanam</s>' (fuel by means of water) and so forth. And accordingly, the word <s>indhana</s> ends in the <s>lyuṭ</s> suffix in the sense of the action — this is the purport. So they say.

children.text: suvarṇataijasatvavādaḥ
children.translated_text: The doctrine that gold is fiery (<s>taijasa</s>)

children.text:
suvarṇasyetyādi/
suvarṇaviśeṣyakataijasatvaprakārakaniścayānukūlaparamatanirākaraṇapūrvaka2vyāpāraviṣayakecchāviśiṣṭapūrvapakṣānukūlakṛtimāniti
bodhaḥ/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaprayojyecchāviṣayatvasvaviṣayasamānakartṛkatvobhayasambandhena/ [76] sūvarṇaṃ pārthivamiti dīpikāvākyam sarvaṃ vākyamasati bādhake
sāvadhāraṇamiti nyāyenāvadhāraṇagarbhamityāśayenāvatārayati -
children.translated_text: 'Of gold' and so forth. The understanding is: [the author] is one who has made an effort favoring the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>), preceded by the refutation of the opposing doctrine that is conducive to the ascertainment having gold as qualificand and fiery-ness as qualifier. The qualification is through both the relations of being the object of the volition whose effect is one's own, and having the same agent as one's own object. [76] The statement of the <s>Dīpikā</s> 'gold is earthly' — he introduces it with the intent that, by the principle 'every statement, in the absence of a contradicting factor, carries restrictive force,' it contains a restrictive sense —

children.text:
1.
atathātvāt-apśabdasamānādhikaraṇatvābhāvāt
viśeṣyanighnatvābhāvāccetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Because of not being of such a nature' — the meaning is: because of the absence of co-location with the word <s>ap</s> (water), and because of the absence of qualifier-predominance.

children.text:
2.
vyāpāraviṣayaketyādi/ vyāpāraḥ svamatasthāpanarūpaḥ/ svaprayojyeti/
svaṃ vyāpāraviṣayakecchā tatprayojyā/ icchā pūrvapakṣaṃ
kuryāmityākārā tadviṣayatvaṃ pūrvapakṣānukūlakṛtau, evaṃ svaṃ
vyāpāraviṣayakecchā tadviṣayaḥ vyāpāraḥ tatsamānakartṛkatvaṃ ca
tādṛśakṛtau/
children.translated_text:
2.
'Having the activity as object' and so forth. The activity (<s>vyāpāra</s>) is of the nature of establishing one's own position. 'Prompted by oneself' — the desire having one's own activity as object is prompted by that. The desire is of the form 'I shall make the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opponent's position)'; its objecthood consists in being conducive to the action favorable to the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. Similarly, the desire having one's own activity as object, the activity that is its object, and the property of having the same agent as that — [these all obtain] in such an action.

children.text:
suvarṇaviśeṣyaketyādi/ prathamaviśiṣṭāntasya
śaṅkānivṛttyanukūlavyāpāre dvitīyaviśiṣṭāntasya kṛtau cānbayaḥ/
prathamavaiśiṣṭyaṃ svaprayojyatvasvasāmānādhikaraṇyobhayasaṃbandhena/
dvitīyavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svaprayojyecchāviṣayatvasvaviṣayasamānakartṛkatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
children.translated_text: 'Having gold as qualificand' and so forth. The first qualified example has positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) in the activity conducive to the removal of doubt, and the second qualified example in the action. The first qualification is through the dual relation of being-prompted-by-oneself and co-locatedness-with-oneself. The second qualification is through the dual relation of being-the-object-of-the-desire-prompted-by-oneself and having-the-same-agent-as-what-is-one's-own-object.

children.text:
pārthivatvasādhakamityādinā/ tena
gurutvasya jale vyabhicāreṇa pārthivatvasādhakatvāsambhavāt
children.translated_text: 'Establishing earth-nature (<s>pārthivatva</s>)' and so forth. Because, due to the deviation of heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) in water, the capacity to establish earth-nature is not possible,

children.text:
taijasatvābhāvasādhakatvasyaiva vaktavyatvena taijasatvābhāvasya ca
pratijñāvākyenālābhāt tatsādhakahetukathanamanucitamiti śaṅkā
niravakāśā/ suvarṇaṃ pārthivamevetyeva pratijñārthasya vācyatayā tatra
caivakāreṇa taijasatvābhāvalābhāt/ [77] etena
children.translated_text: since only the capacity to establish the absence of fire-nature (<s>taijasatvābhāva</s>) is to be stated, and since the absence of fire-nature is not obtainable from the statement of the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), the doubt that stating a reason establishing that is inappropriate is groundless — because since the meaning of the thesis is expressible as 'gold is earthen alone,' the absence of fire-nature is obtainable through the restrictive particle 'alone' (<s>eva</s>) therein. [77] By this

children.text:
taijasatvābhāvasādhakahetukathanena/ [77] digiti/ ayaṃ
bhāvaḥ-samavāyena pītarūpaṃ prati tādātmyasambandhena pṛthivītvena
kāraṇatāyāḥ kḷptatvāt suvarṇasya taijasatve vijātīyapītarūpaṃ
prati kāraṇatāntaraṃ kalpanīyam/ tasya pārthivatve tu na
tatkalpanāvaśyambhāva iti lāghavamiti tarkānugṛhītaṃ 'suvarṇaṃ
pārthivatvatadabhāvānyataravat prameyatvāt' ityanumānaṃ tasya
pṛthivītvasādhakapramāṇatayā sambhavatīti/
children.translated_text: statement of a reason establishing the absence of fire-nature. [77] 'In a direction' etc. The purport is this: since the causal capacity of earth-nature (<s>pṛthivītva</s>) through the relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) with respect to yellow color (<s>pītarūpa</s>) through the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) is already established, if gold were of fire-nature, an additional causal capacity would need to be postulated for the heterogeneous yellow color. But if it is of earth-nature, there is no necessity for such postulation — hence the economy (<s>lāghava</s>). Thus, the inference 'Gold possesses either earth-nature or the absence thereof, because it is knowable (<s>prameya</s>),' supported by this reasoning (<s>tarka</s>), is possible as a valid means of establishing its earth-nature — this is the purport.

children.text:
suvarṇasya pītimagurutvāśrayata ityādi/
suvarṇaviśeṣyakapītimagurūtvāśrayavyatiriktatvaprakārakāprāmāṇyagrahānāskanditaniścayānukūlayuktikathanaviṣayakecchāviśiṣṭānumānaviśeṣyakāprayojakatvaprakārakaśaṅkānivṛttyanukūlavyāpāraviṣayakecchāviśiṣṭānukūlatarkavyavasthāpanānukūlakṛtimāniti
bodhaḥ/ [77] asati pratibandhaka ityādi/
pratibandhakātyantābhāvaviśiṣṭātyantānalasaṃyogaviśiṣṭadravatvādityarthaḥ/
agnisaṃyuktaghaṭe vyabhicāravāraṇāya dravatvaniveśanam/ vaiśiṣṭyadvayaṃ
ekakṣaṇāvacchinnaikādhikaraṇavṛttitvarūpam/ [77] atyantānalasaṃyogī
pītimāśraya ityādi/ atra cātyantānalasaṃyogīti
pakṣaviśeṣaṇānupādāne jalamadhyasthapītarūpāśrayadravadravyaviśeṣe
sāmānādhikaraṇyena
siddhasādhanavāraṇāyāvacchedakāvacchedenānumiteruddeśyatāyā
vaktavyatvena haridrāyāṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyena bādhaḥ syāditi
tadupādānam/ jalamadhyasthaghṛte sāmānādhikaraṇyena
siddhasādhanavāraṇāyāvacchedakāvacchedenānumiteruddeśyatāyā
vācyatvena ghaṭadāvaṃśato bādhavāraṇāya pītimāśrayatvamupāttam/
yadyapyevamapi pītarūpavati tādṛśaghaṭādau bādhaḥ tathāpi
svāvyavahitāttarapyevamapi pītarūpavati tādṛśaghaṭādau bādhaḥ tathāpi
svāvyavahitottarakṣaṇāvacchinnasāmānādhikaraṇyasaṃbandhena
vijatīyāgnisaṃyogaviśiṣṭapītarūpavattvasyaiva
pakṣatāvacchedakatvasvīkārāt na doṣa iti bhāvaḥ/
svāvyavahitottarakṣaṇāvacchinnaikādhikaraṇavṛttitvalakṣaṇasāmānādhikaraṇyasaṃbandhenāgnisaṃyogaviśiṣṭadravatvasahitagurutvaṃ
hetuḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Gold being the locus of yellow color and non-heaviness' and so forth. The understanding is: [it] possesses action conducive to the establishment of a reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) favorable to the activity conducive to the removal of the doubt — which has as its qualificand an inference qualified by non-being-the-means-of-proving, which has the qualifier-mode of being distinct from being the locus of yellow color and non-heaviness, and which has gold as qualificand — and which has as its qualifier-mode the cognition that is not impugned by the apprehension of invalidity, and which is conducive to a determination having such qualifier-mode. [77] 'In the absence of an obstructor' and so forth. The meaning is: fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>) and the like, qualified by conjunction with fire that is not an absolute [conjunction], qualified by the absolute absence of an obstructor. The inclusion of fluidity is to prevent deviation in a pot conjoined with fire. The twofold qualification is of the nature of existing in a single substratum at a single moment. [77] 'The locus of yellow color that is absolutely not conjoined with fire' and so forth. Here, if the qualifier of the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) 'absolutely not conjoined with fire' is not included, then in a particular fluid substance possessing yellow color that is in the midst of water, there would be the defect of <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already established) through co-locatedness — and since the purpose of inference with the delimitor of the delimiting condition is to be stated, there would be sublation (<s>bādha</s>) in turmeric through co-locatedness; hence that inclusion. To prevent <s>siddhasādhana</s> through co-locatedness in ghee that is in the midst of water — and since the purpose of inference with the delimitor of the delimiting condition is to be stated — 'being the locus of yellow color' is included to prevent sublation from the perspective of pots and the like. Although even so there is sublation in such pots possessing yellow color, nevertheless, since being-the-possessor-of-yellow-color-qualified-by-heterogeneous-fire-conjunction delimited by co-locatedness in the immediately succeeding moment is accepted as the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s> (subject-hood), there is no defect — this is the purport. Heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) qualified by fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>) accompanied by fire-conjunction, delimited by the co-locatedness in the form of existing in a single substratum at the immediately succeeding moment, is the reason.

children.text:
svasamavetadravatvanāśapratibandhakadravadravyāntarasaṃyuktatvaṃ
sādhyam/ na ca dṛṣṭāntapakṣasādhāraṇasvatvānanugamāt pakṣe bodho
dṛṣṭānte sādhyavaikalyaṃ vā/ evaṃ dravadravyāntaretyatra
svānyonyābhāvāśrayadravadravyavivakṣāyāṃ anupayogaḥ anyathāsiddhiśceti
vācyam/
1svasaṃyuktatva-svapratibadhyanāśapratiyogidravatvasamavāyitvasvāsamavetajapatimattvatritayasambandhena
dravadravyaviśiṣṭatvasya sādhyatvābhyupagamāt sādhyaśarīre uddeśyasiddhaye
tṛtīyasaṃbandhaniveśaḥ/ sidhyati dravye vyabhicārāvāraṇāya
hetukoṭau gurutvaniveśaḥ/
children.translated_text: The property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) is: being qualified by a fluid substance other [than itself], which is conjoined with what is self-conjoined, and which has fluidity that is the counter-positive of the destruction obstructed by itself, and which is inherent in that [other fluid substance], and which does not have earth-nature inherent in itself — [this being qualified] through the triple relation. Nor should it be said that since the self-nature (<s>svatva</s>) common to both the example and the subject is not carried over, there is lack of understanding in the subject or lack of the <s>sādhya</s> in the example; similarly, that in the expression 'another fluid substance,' if the intended meaning is a fluid substance that is the locus of mutual absence of itself, there is inapplicability and otherwise the defect of already-established-ness — because, by accepting the <s>sādhya</s> as qualified through the triple relation consisting of being-conjoined-with-oneself, having-fluidity-that-is-the-counter-positive-of-the-destruction-obstructed-by-one's-own-destruction-as-inherent, and having-earth-nature-not-inherent-in-oneself, the third relation is included in the body of the <s>sādhya</s> for establishing the intended [conclusion]. The inclusion of heaviness in the reason-side is to prevent deviation in an already-established substance.

children.text:
yadyapi tādṛśadravyasiddhitaḥ prāk tatra
vyabhicāragrahasya na sambhavaḥ, tathāpi
yadyatyantānalasaṃyogaviśiṣṭadravatvamuktasādhyavyāpyaṃ sayāt tarhi
prakṛtapakṣatāvacchedakāvacchedena darśitāsādhyasādhakaṃ syāditi
rītyāanavasthā syāditi gurutvopādānam [77] jalādikamādāyeti/ atra ādānaṃ grahaṇam/ tacca prakṛte
viṣayatārūpam/ lyapaḥ samānakartṛkatvamātramarthaḥ
viṣayatārūpaparyavasānaśabdārthānvitam/ samānakartṛkatvaṃ ceha
tannirūpakanirūpitatvam/ jalādikamityatra dvitīyāyāḥ ādheyatvamarthaḥ/
tathā ca jalādiniṣṭhaṃ yadviṣayatvaṃ
tannirūpakanirūpitānumānaviṣayatvarūpārthāntaradharmikasaṃbhavitvaprakārakajñānānukūlavyāpārakartetivākyārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Although prior to the establishment of such a substance, the apprehension of deviation is not possible there, nevertheless, if fluidity qualified by conjunction with absolutely-no-fire were pervaded by the stated <s>sādhya</s>, then it would establish an undesired <s>sādhya</s> through the delimitor of the delimiting condition of the subject-hood in question — hence there would be an infinite regress; therefore heaviness is included. [77] 'Taking water and the like' — here, 'taking' (<s>ādāna</s>) means apprehension (<s>grahaṇa</s>), and that, in the present context, is of the nature of objecthood. The <s>lyap</s> suffix conveys merely the sense of same-agentship, which culminates in the meaning of objecthood. And same-agentship here means being determined by, and determining, that [objecthood]. The accusative case in 'water and the like' has the meaning of being the content. And thus the sentence means: one whose activity is conducive to the cognition having the qualifier-mode of being possible in [another] subject that has as its content the objecthood residing in water and the like, that objecthood being determined by, and determining, the objecthood of the inference in question.

children.text:
1.
svasaṃyuktatvetyādi/ svaṃ dravadravyaṃ jalaṃ tatsaṃyuktatvaṃ dhṛte, svaṃ jalaṃ
tatpratibadhyaḥ dravatvanāśaḥ tatpratiyogi dravatvaṃ tatsamavāyitvaṃ dhṛte,
svaṃ jalaṃ tadasamavetapṛthivītvajātimatvaṃ ca dhṛte iti
jalamadhyasthadhṛte samanvayaḥ/ pakṣe tu svaṃ suvaṇagatatejobhāgaḥ
tatsaṃyuktatvaṃ pārthivabhāge, svaṃ tejobhāgaḥ tatpratibadhyo yo
dravatvanāśaḥ tatpratiyogidravatvaṃ tatsamavāyavattvaṃ pārthivabhāge, svaṃ
tejobhāgaḥ tadasamavetā pṛthivītvajātiḥ tadvavattvaṃ pārthivabhāge
iti samanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text:
1.
'Being-conjoined-with-oneself' and so forth. 'Oneself' is the fluid substance, i.e. water; 'being conjoined with that' [obtains] in ghee. 'Oneself' is water; 'the destruction obstructed by that' is the destruction of fluidity; 'the counter-positive of that,' fluidity, 'being inherent in that' [obtains] in ghee. 'Oneself' is water; 'earth-nature (<s>pṛthivītva</s>) not inherent in that' — possessing that universal [obtains] in ghee — this is the concomitance in ghee that is in the midst of water. In the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), however, 'oneself' is the fire-component (<s>tejobhāga</s>) in gold; 'being conjoined with that' [obtains] in the earth-component. 'Oneself' is the fire-component; 'the destruction obstructed by that' — the destruction of fluidity whose counter-positive is that fluidity — 'being inherent in that' [obtains] in the earth-component. 'Oneself' is the fire-component; 'earth-nature (<s>pṛthivītva</s>) not inherent in that' — possessing that universal [obtains] in the earth-component — this is the concomitance.

children.text: vāyunirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>)

children.text:
dīpikāyāñ [82] sparśānumeyo vāyuriti/ atra ca sparśapadaṃ sparśatvaparam/
tena parvatānumayo vahniriti
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: [82] 'Wind (<s>vāyu</s>) is inferred from touch (<s>sparśa</s>).' Here, the word 'touch' refers to the universal touch-hood (<s>sparśatva</s>). Thereby, [the objection that this parallels] 'fire is inferred from a mountain'

children.text:
vyavahāravāraṇāya
tṛtīyāyāḥ viśeśyatārthakatvamapahāya
prakāratārthakatvasyopagantavyatayā sparśānumeyo
vāyurityasaṃgatamityapāstam/ yadvā tādātmyasaṃbandhena sparśasyaiva
hetutvaṃ vivakṣitamiti nāsaṃgatiḥ/ anumānaprakāraśca
'upalabhyamānasparśaḥ kvacidāśritaḥ sparśatvāt, tādātmyena sparśādvā,
pārthivādisparśavat' u iti [82] vāyauvātīti/ atra ca
vāyau iti saptamyāḥ gaganamarthaḥ/ tasya ca samānakālīnatvasambandhena
upalambhe 'nvayaḥ/ yadyapi guṇatvādrūpavaditi hetudṛṣṭāntayorabhidhānaṃ
[na] yuktam; sparśānumeya ityatra prāguktaviroghāt; tathāpi
sparśatvādihetukānumānamupalakṣaṇamityabhiprāyeṇa
guṇatvahetukānumānāntaramapyuktamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: — [the response is:] by abandoning the meaning of the instrumental case as [indicating] the qualificand and adopting [the meaning of] qualifier-mode-hood, the statement 'wind is inferred from touch' is not incoherent — this is set aside. Alternatively, since the intention is that touch itself is the reason through the relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), there is no incoherence. And the form of the inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is: 'The perceived touch resides in something, because of touch-hood, or because of touch through identity, like earthen touch and the like.' [82] 'In wind' etc. Here, the locative 'in wind' has the meaning of 'in the sky.' And the concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) [is established] through the relation of contemporaneity with the apprehension. Although the statement of the reason and example by 'because of quality-hood, like color' [may seem] inappropriate [77] — due to the contradiction with what was previously stated [that touch is the reason]; nevertheless, since 'inferred from touch' is a representative instance, the intention is that another inference with quality-hood and the like as the reason is also stated — this should be noted.

children.text:
atra
copalabhyamānasparśaviśiṣṭaḥ [yadi] pṛthivī syāt
tarhyudbhūtarūpavān syāt, yadi jalādikaṃ syāt
tarhyanuṣṇāśīyasparśavānna syāt, yadyayaṃ sparśaḥ
ākāśādicatuṣṭayānyatamasamavetaḥ syāt tarhi
deśāntarasthajanasamavetalaukikapratyakṣaviṣayaḥ syāt, yadi
manassamavetaḥ syāt tarhi laukikapratyakṣaviṣayo na syāt/
yadyayamudbhūtasparśaḥ pṛthivīsamavetaḥ syāt udbhūtarūpavadvṛttiḥ
syāt, yadi jalādisamavetaḥ syāt anuṣṇāśīto na syāt,
udbhūtasparśāśrayo yadi vibhuḥ syāt
deśāntarasthajanasamavetapratyakṣaviṣayasparśakaḥ syāt, yadi manaḥ syāt,
pratyakṣāviṣayasparśakaḥ syāt iti tarkaiḥ 'ayaṃ sparśaḥ
pṛthivyādibhinnakiñcitsamavetaḥ' ityākārakānumitirjāyata iti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Here, if the perceived touch were earth, it would possess manifest color; if it were water and the like, it would not have non-cold-non-hot touch; if this touch were inherent in one of the four [substances] beginning with space (<s>ākāśa</s>), it would be the object of ordinary perception of a person situated in another place; if it were inherent in mind (<s>manas</s>), it would not be the object of ordinary perception. If this manifest touch were inherent in earth, it would exist in what possesses manifest color; if it were inherent in water and the like, it would not be non-cold-non-hot; if the locus of manifest touch were all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>), it would produce touch that is the object of perception of a person in another place; if it were mind, it would produce touch that is not the object of perception — through such reasonings (<s>tarka</s>), the inference of the form 'this touch is inherent in something other than earth and the rest' arises — this is the purport.

children.text:
udbhūtasparśavadityādi/ atra ca ghrāṇendriye
vyabhicāravāraṇāya prathamamudbhūteti/ udbhūtatvasyābhāvakūṭātmakasya
dravyatve 'pi sattvāt taddoṣa ityataḥ sparśapadam/ vāyau tadvāraṇāya
pārthivatvaniveśaḥ/ vāyāvapyanudbhūtarūpasattvāt dravyatvasattvācca
udbhūtarūpaniveśaḥ/ atra copalabhyamānasparśāśrayasya pṛthivītvādikaṃ
prasaktaṃ na tu pṛthivyādestadāśrayatvam/
ato 'prasaktapratiṣedhaparihārāya yojanamāha- [82] asyetyādi/ dīpikāyāñ [83] na vibhucatuṣṭayamiti/
tadanyatamaṃ netyarthaḥ/ anyathā siddhasādhanaprasaṃgāt,
ekatrobhayādibhedasattvāditi dhyeyam/ navīnāstu vāyoḥ pratyakṣatāṃ
varṇayanti/ tanmatamākṣeptumanuvadati-- [83] nanu vāyuḥ pratyakṣa
ityādinā/ nanu pratyakṣatvaṃ pratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ, tathā ca vāyorapi
alaukikamānasapratyakṣaviṣayatvābhyupagamāt siddhasādhanamata
āha-prakāśikāyāñ [83] pratyakṣaḥ-bahirindrayajanyapratyakṣaviṣaya
iti/ yadyapyalaukikatādṛśapratyakṣaviṣayatvamapi vāyorastīti
taddoṣatādavasthyam, tathāpi mānasānirūpitalaukikaviṣayatvasya
sādhyatve tātparyānna doṣaḥ/ anirūpitāntaṃ ca
mānasaviṣayatāmādāyārthāntaravāraṇāya/ ata eva
vakṣyamāṇopādherātmani
children.translated_text: 'Possessing manifest touch' and so forth. Here, to prevent deviation in the olfactory organ (<s>ghrāṇendriya</s>), 'manifest' is first [specified]. Since the universal 'manifest-ness' (<s>udbhūtatva</s>), being of the nature of an absence-aggregate, exists even in substance — to address that defect, the word 'touch' [is added]. To prevent [deviation] in wind, the inclusion of earth-nature (<s>pārthivatva</s>) [is made]. Since even in wind non-manifest color exists, and since substance-hood exists [there too], manifest color (<s>udbhūtarūpa</s>) is included. Here, what is predicated of the locus of perceived touch is earth-nature and the like, not that earth and the like are its locus — hence, to resolve the [objection of] 'preventing what is not established,' he states the interpretation: [82] 'of this' and so forth. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: [83] 'Not the four all-pervading [substances].' The meaning is: not any one of them. Otherwise there would be the defect of proving what is already established — and one should note [the distinctions of] one, both, and so forth. The later logicians (<s>Navīnas</s>), however, describe the perceptibility of wind. He restates their view in order to refute it — [83] 'But wind is perceptible' and so on. Now, perceptibility means being the object of perception; and since even the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> accept that wind is the object of extraordinary mental (<s>mānasa</s>) perception, [the inference] would prove what is already established. Therefore he says — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [83] 'Perceptible — meaning the object of perception produced by external sense-organs.' Although even non-ordinary such perceptibility exists for wind, and hence the defect remains the same, nevertheless, since the intended <s>sādhya</s> is: perceptibility that is not determined by mental perception — there is no defect. And 'not determined by' extends up to mental objecthood, for the purpose of preventing the [objection of] proving something different (<s>arthāntara</s>). For this very reason, the forthcoming condition in the case of the self —

children.text:
sādhyavyāpakatābhaṅgasya nāvakāśaḥ/ [83] pratyakṣetīti/
laukikaviṣayatāśrayetyarthavivakṣaṇānnalaukikapratyakṣaviṣayasparśavati
tvagindriye vyabhicāratādavasthyam/ sparśapadaṃ tu
laukikaviṣayatāśrayadravyatvādikamādāya/
laukikaviṣayatāśrayaguṇetyuktāvapi śrāvaṇapratyakṣaviṣayaśabdamādāya
ākāśe vyabhicāravyudāsāya/ sparśasya samavāyena hetutvasūcanāya
āśrayatvakathanam/
children.translated_text: the breaking of the pervasion of the <s>sādhya</s> has no scope. [83] 'Perceptible' etc. Since the meaning-intention is 'locus of ordinary objecthood,' there is no remaining defect of deviation in the skin organ, which is the object of ordinary perception and possesses touch. The word 'touch,' however, [is used] taking substance-hood and the like that is the locus of ordinary objecthood. Even when stated as 'quality that is the locus of ordinary objecthood,' to prevent deviation in sound — which is the object of auditory perception — in space (<s>ākāśa</s>), [the word 'touch' is used]. The statement of 'locus-hood' serves to indicate that touch is the reason through the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>).

children.text:
dīpikāyām [83] udbhūtarūpasyeti/ atrodbhūtapadaṃ prācīnaikadeśibhiḥ
vāyāvapyanudbhūtarūpasvīkārāt upādheḥ
sādhanāvyāpakatvopapattyartham/ prakāśikāyāñ [83] sādhyavyabhicāronnayanasambhavāditi/ yadyapi
vyāpakatāvacchedakatvābhimatarūpāvacchinnānirūpitavyabhicārasya
vyāpyatāvacchedakatvābhimatarūpāvacchinnanirūpitavyabhicārasyānumāpakatayā
prakṛte ca dravyatvātmakapakṣadharmaviśiṣṭapratyakṣatvavyabhicāra eva
tadviśiṣṭasādhyavyāpakavyabhicāreṇānumātuṃ śakyate, na tu
śuddhasādhyavyabhicāro 'pi, vyāptigrahavirahāt/ tathāpi
tādṛśopādhivyabhicāreṇa viśiṣṭasādhyavyabhicārasiddhau
viśeṣaṇavaddhiśiṣṭābhāvavadvṛttitvena hetunā viśeṣyābhāvavadvṛttitvaṃ
paścādanumātuṃ śakyamiti bhāvaḥ/ atha vā pakṣadharmavati
sādhanāvyāpakatvena śuddhasādhyavyabhicāra evānumātuṃ śakyaḥ/
pakṣadharmavati sādhanāvyāpakatvaṃ ca
sādhanāśrayapakṣadharmavanniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitvam/ evaṃ
pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakatvaṃ ca
sādhyāśrayapakṣadharmavanniṣṭhābhāvāpratiyogitvamiti/ evamupādhyantare 'pi
draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> [§83], 'possessing manifest form' — here the word 'manifest' is used by some ancients because, since even in air a non-manifest form is accepted, the <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) would have the property of not pervading the probans — and [the word is used] to justify that. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [§83], 'because the raising of deviation of the probandum is possible' — even though the deviation delimited by the property accepted as the delimitor of pervasiveness, which does not determine the deviation delimited by the property accepted as the delimitor of pervaded-ness, can be inferred through [the <s>upādhi</s>], and in the present case, indeed only the deviation of perceptibility qualified by the thesis-property of substance-hood can be inferred through the deviation of the probandum-pervader — but not even the deviation of the pure probandum, due to the absence of the pervasion-cognition — nevertheless, when the deviation of the qualified probandum is established through the deviation of such an <s>upādhi</s>, the deviation with respect to the qualificand [alone] can be subsequently inferred through the probans 'occurring in what possesses the absence of the qualifier-qualified entity, just as the qualifier's absence obtains' — this is the purport. Alternatively, the deviation of the pure probandum can indeed be inferred as non-pervasiveness of the probans in what possesses the thesis-property. And the non-pervasiveness of the probans in what possesses the thesis-property is the counter-positiveness of an absolute absence residing in [what possesses] the thesis-property and is the locus of the probans. Similarly, the pervasiveness of the probandum delimited by the thesis-property is the non-counter-positiveness of an absence residing in [what possesses] the thesis-property and is the locus of the probandum. The same should be observed in other <s>upādhis</s>.

children.text:
vastutastu
1udbhūtarūpaśūnyatvadravyatva(dravyatva)ubhayābhāvaḥ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākasvābhāvīyadravyaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatāsaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasasaṃbandhena
udbhūtarūpaṃ vā upādhiḥ/ tasya rūpādāvapi sattvena sādhyavyāpakatvāt
pakṣabhūtavāyāvasattvena sādhanāvyāpakatvācca/ upadarśitadharmaviśeṣasya
upādhitvasūcanāyaiva pakṣadharmāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakatvakīrtanam/
children.translated_text: In reality, however, the joint absence of non-possession-of-manifest-form and substance-hood — or [alternatively] manifest form — is the <s>upādhi</s>, through the relation of [a complex technical specification involving inherence, substratum-hood, and difference]. Because of its existence even in form and the like, it has the property of pervading the probandum; and because of its absence in air, which is the thesis, it has the property of not pervading the probans. The mention of the probandum-pervading-ness delimited by the thesis-property is precisely for indicating the <s>upādhi</s>-hood of the specific property indicated.

children.text:
upādhicāturvindhyakathanamapi tatra tatra vivakṣitadharmaviśeṣasya
upādhitvalābhāya vivakṣitasambandhaviśeṣasya upādhitāvacchedakatvalābhāya
veti madekapariśīlitaḥ panthāḥ/
children.translated_text: The statement of the four types of <s>upādhi</s> is also for the purpose of establishing the <s>upādhi</s>-hood of the specific intended property in each case, or for establishing the intended specific relation as the delimitor of <s>upādhi</s>-hood — this is a path I have alone explored.

children.text:
kecittu
viśeṣaṇāvyabhicāritvaniścayasahakṛtaviśiṣṭavyabhicāritvavyāptigrahāt
viśeṣyavyabhicārasiddhiḥ iti vadanti/ tadasat/ yato
viśiṣṭavyabhicāraḥ viśiṣṭābhāvadvṛttitvameva/ na tu
viśeṣaṇavyabhicārāsahitaviśeṣyavyabhicāraḥ/ prattakṣasparśavattvādau
tadasaṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: Some, however, state that from the cognition of pervasion of the qualified-deviation, assisted by the ascertainment of the non-deviation of the qualifier, the deviation with respect to the qualificand is established. That is incorrect — because the qualified-deviation is precisely 'occurrence in what possesses the absence of the qualified entity,' not 'the deviation of the qualificand unaccompanied by the deviation of the qualifier.' Since that is impossible in perceptibility, touch-possession, and the like.

children.text:
1.
udbhūtarūpaśūnyatveti/ rūpādiguṇe dravyatvābhāvaprayuktobhayābhāvasya
sattvāt ghaṭādidravye udbhūtarūpaśūnyatvābhāprayuktobhayābhāvasattvācca
asya bahirindriyajanyapratyakṣaviṣayatvarūpasādhyavyāpakatvam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Non-possession of manifest form' — since in qualities like form and the like, the joint absence caused by the absence of substance-hood exists, and since in substances like pots and the like, the joint absence caused by the absence of non-possession-of-manifest-form exists, this has the property of pervading the probandum in the form of being an object of perception generated by external sense organs.

children.text:
samavāyasaṃbandhetyādi/
svābhāvīyetyasya svābhāvanirūpitetyarthaḥ/
dravyaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatāyāmanvayaḥ/ rūpādiniṣṭhādhikaraṇatāyāṃ
udbhūtarūpābhāvanirūpitatvasattve 'pi dravyaniṣṭhatvaṃ nāstīti
svābhāvanirūpitadravyaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatāsaṃbandhena svavattvaṃ
(udbhūtarūpavattvaṃ) rūpādau nāstīti tena saṃbandhena svavadbhinnatvasya
rūpādau sattvāt svavadbhinnatvasaṃbandhena udbhūtarūpaṃ tatrāstīti
sādhyavyāpakatvamiti bhāvaḥ/ ghaṭādiniṣṭhādhikaraṇatāyāṃ
dravyaniṣṭhatvasadbhāve 'pi udbhūtarūpābhāvanirūpitatvaṃ nāsti/ ataḥ
svābhāvanirūpitādhikaraṇatāsaṃbandhena svavadbhinnatvasattvāt
tatsaṃbandhena udbhūtarūpaṃ ghaṭādāvastīti sādhyavyāpakatā bodhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Through the relation of inherence' and so forth — the meaning of 'self-absence-determined' is 'determined by one's own absence.' The connection is with 'substratum-hood residing in a substance.' Even though in the substratum-hood residing in form and the like, the determination by absence-of-manifest-form exists, substance-hood does not — hence through the relation of substratum-hood residing in substance determined by one's own absence, the self-possession (i.e. possession of manifest form) does not exist in form and the like; hence the difference from what possesses self exists there through that relation, and through the relation of difference-from-what-possesses-self, manifest form exists there — thus there is probandum-pervading-ness. In the substratum-hood residing in pots and the like, even though substance-hood exists, the determination by absence-of-manifest-form does not exist. Therefore, through the relation of substratum-hood determined by one's own absence, the possession of difference-from-self exists, and through that relation, manifest form exists in pots and the like — thus the probandum-pervading-ness should be understood.

children.text:
tathā
copadarśitaparāmarśāt viśiṣṭavyabhicārasiddhau na kiñcidapi bādhakaṃ
paśyāma iti viśiṣṭasādhyavyāptikopādheḥ
śuddhasādhyavyabhicāronnāyakatvānirvāha eveti/
children.translated_text: And accordingly, from the indicated reflective judgment, when the qualified deviation is established, we see absolutely nothing that obstructs — hence the <s>upādhi</s> that disrupts the qualified-probandum-pervasion is indeed capable of raising the deviation of the pure probandum — and the matter is thus resolved.

children.text:
dīpikāyāñ [82] prāṇasya kutrāntarbhāva ityādi/ tathā ca daśamadravyatvaṃ prāṇasya,
vāyāvantarbhāve 'pi kāryavānucāturvidhyaṃ vā prasajyeteti bhāvaḥ/
śarīretyādiviśeṣaṇena
śarīrendriyabhinnatvarūpaviṣayalakṣaṇākrāntatvāt na caturvidhyam,
vāyvantarbhāvācca na daśamadravyatvamityāśaya iti bhāvaśca/"sa
caiko 'pyupādhibhedāt prāṇādisaṃjñābhedaṃ labhata"iti
saṃgrahavākye upādhibhedādityatra pañcamyāḥ prayojyatvamarthaḥ/ tasya
'labhata' ityatra dhātvarthasambandhe 'nvayaḥ/ sa ceha vācyatvarūpaḥ/
eko 'pītyatra ekatvaṃ prāṇatvanyūnavṛttidharmaśūnyatvam/ apiratra
virodhārthakaḥ/ virodhaśca
samabhivyāhṛtapadārthantāvacchedakaikatvādhikaraṇanirūpitopādhibhedānavacchi nnavṛttikatvābhāvaḥ/
tasya ca sambandhe anvayaḥ/ tathā ca
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> [§82], 'Where is <s>prāṇa</s> included?' and so forth. And accordingly, <s>prāṇa</s> would be a tenth substance, or if included in air, the fourfold division of its effects would be disrupted — this is the purport. By the qualifier 'body' and the like, since it falls under the definition of 'object' which is delimited by difference from body and sense organs, there is no disruption of the fourfold division; and because of inclusion in air, there is no tenth substance — this is the intent. In the summary statement 'And that one, though one, due to the difference of limiting conditions, acquires the different designations <s>prāṇa</s> and the like,' the fifth case ending in 'due to the difference of limiting conditions' has the meaning of instrumentality. Its connection is with the verbal meaning in 'acquires.' And here that [connection] is in the form of predicate-hood. In 'though one,' one-ness means the absence of a property that does not occur more narrowly than <s>prāṇa</s>-hood. The word 'api' (though) here means contradiction. And the contradiction is the absence of occurring without being delimited by the difference of limiting conditions determined by the locus of one-ness — which is the delimitor of the co-mentioned word-meanings. And its connection is with the relation. And accordingly,

children.text:
ekatvaviruddhopādhibhedaprayuktaprāṇāpānādisaṃjñānirūpitasaṃbadhāśrayaḥ
sa iti bodhaḥ/
children.translated_text: the cognition is: 'that (<s>saḥ</s>)' refers to the substratum of the relation of the designations <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the like, produced by the difference of limiting conditions that contradicts one-ness.

children.text:
kecittu apiśabdasya
virodhārthakatāmāhuḥ/ tadasat/ dharmiṇi
tādṛśasambandhāśrayatvabhānenaiva tādṛśasambandhāśrayatve
ekatvāvirodhalābhena pṛthakkathanavaiyarthyāt/ asmanmate tu
virodhatatsāmānādhikaraṇyayorekatra saṃbhavapradarśanaparatayā
tatsārthakyāt/ ke te upādhaya ityāśaṅkāyāmupādhiśabdārthamāha
dīpikāyām [82] sthāneti/ tatra pramāṇamāha prakāśikāyām
[82] hṛdi prāṇa ityādi iti/
children.translated_text: Some, however, state that the word 'api' means contradiction. That is incorrect — because since the appearance as substratum of such a relation in the property-bearer already yields the non-contradiction of one-ness with the status of being the substratum of such a relation, a separate statement would be purposeless. But on our view, since the purpose lies in demonstrating the possibility of both contradiction and co-location in one [entity], it is purposeful. Anticipating the question 'What are those limiting conditions?', he states the meaning of the word 'limiting condition' (<s>upādhi</s>) in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [§82] — 'location' etc. He states the authority for that in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [§82] — 'In the heart, <s>prāṇa</s>' and so forth.

children.text: sṛṣṭisaṃhāraprakriyā
children.translated_text: The Process of Creation and Dissolution (<s>Sṛṣṭisaṃhāraprakriyā</s>)

children.text:
dīpikāyām [85] cikīrṣāvaśāditi/ yadyapīśvarecchā nityaiva/ tathāpyetatkāle
paramāṇau kriyā bhūyāditi rītyā tasyāḥ kālaviśeṣāvagāhitayā
tatkāla eva tatra kriyātpattiḥ nānyadeti niyama upapadyate/ evaṃ
saṃjihīrṣāvaśādityatrāpi bodhyam/ cākṣuṣadravyatvādityatra cākṣuṣaṃ
yat dravyatvamityarthavivakṣāyāmātmani vyabhicāratādavasthyamabhisandhāya
dravyapadena karmadhārayaṃ 1karmadhārayopari' ityādinyāyaṃ
cābhipretyārthamāha- [85] cākṣuṣatve satītyādi/ [85] rūpādāviti/ idaṃ ca janyadravyatvasya sādhyatābhiprāyeṇa/
dravyasamevatatvarūpasāvayavatvasādhane tu ghaṭābhāvādau vyabhicāro
bodhyaḥ/ etatsaṃgrāhakamevādipadamiti dhyeyam/ [85] kāryatve 'navasthāprasaṅgāditi/
avayavatvavyāpakasāvayavatvakatvarūpāvyavasthitaparamparā
dhīnamerusarṣapagataparimāṇatāratamyānupapattirūpāniṣṭaprasajjanād ityarthaḥ/
tathā ca 'tryaṇukāvayavaḥ sāvayavaḥ mahādārambhakatvāt' ityatra
uktatarkabalāt nityāvayavasamaveta ityanumitirutpadyata iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> [§85], 'by the force of the desire to create' — even though <s>Īśvara</s>'s (God's) will is eternal, since it has the form 'let there be action in the atom at this time,' through its encompassing a specific time, the restriction is justified that action arises in that [atom] at that time alone and not at another — this is explained. The same should be understood in 'by the force of the desire to dissolve.' In 'because of possessing visual substance-hood' — if the intended meaning is 'substance-hood that is visual,' then considering that the deviation in the self would remain as before, and intending the maxim 'on top of a <s>karmadhāraya</s> [compound]' and so forth, he explains the meaning — [§85] 'when there is visual-ness,' etc. [§85] 'In form and the like' — this is said with the intent of produced-substance-hood being the probandum. But when the property of having parts (<s>sāvayavatva</s>) in the form of inhering in substance is the [alternative] probandum, deviation in the absence of a pot and the like should be noted. The word 'and the like' is intended to subsume this. [§85] 'Because of the unwanted consequence of infinite regress in effect-hood' — the meaning is: because there would arise an unregulated infinite series of the part-hood-pervading having-parts-hood, amounting to the impossibility of the gradation of magnitudes in <s>Dhīneru</s> (mount <s>Meru</s>) and a mustard seed. And accordingly, from the force of the <s>tarka</s> (counterfactual reasoning) 'a three-atom aggregate's part has parts, because of possessing great-origination-capacity,' the inference 'it inheres in an eternal part' arises — this is the purport.
In the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [§86]

children.text:
prakāśikāyāṃ saṃkṣepa iti/ ayamatra bhāvaḥ/
yadyapi truṭimahattvasya nityatvopagame avayavasaṃkhyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: , 'in brief' — the idea here is: even if the magnitude of a three-atom aggregate is accepted as eternal, the doubt that the number of parts

children.text:
nāpekṣeti
darśitānumānasyāprayojakatvaśaṅkā durvārā, tathāpi ---
children.translated_text: is not required — the objection regarding the purposelessness of the demonstrated inference is unavoidable. Nevertheless —

children.text:
'jālasūryamarīcisthaṃ
yatsūkṣmamupalabhyate/
children.translated_text: 'What is perceived as subtle, situated in the sunbeam coming through a lattice window —

children.text:
tasya ṣaṣṭhatamo bhāgaḥ
paramāṇuḥprakīrtitaḥ//'
children.translated_text: one-sixth of that is declared to be the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>).'

children.text:
iti
smṛtiprāmāṇyabalāt dvyaṇukaparamāṇvoḥ svīkāra āvaśyaka iti/
digiti/ atrāyamāśayaḥ-- sarvaśabdasya
svasamabhivyāhṛtapadārthatāvacchedakavyāpakatvārthakatayā
kāryadravyatvavyāpakatvamavāntarapralayasya, bhāvakāryatvavyāpakatvaṃ
mahāpralasya ca lakṣaṇam/ vyāpakatvaṃ ca
svaniṣṭhadhvaṃsapratiyogitāsaṃbandhena/ svananiṣṭhatvaṃ ca
kālikasaṃbandhena/ etena kāryāṇāṃ bhāvakāryāṇāṃ cānantānāṃ
viśiṣyāsarvajñadurjñeyatvena tāvaddhvaṃsasamudāyatvasya sutarāṃ
parijñānāsambhavāt etallakṣaṇakathanamasaṃgatamityapāstamiti/
children.translated_text: By the authority of this <s>smṛti</s> (traditional text), the acceptance of dyads and atoms is necessary — this is the indication. Here the intent is: since the word 'all' has the meaning of pervading the delimitor of the meaning of its co-mentioned words, partial dissolution (<s>avāntarapralaya</s>) pervades produced-substance-hood, and the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>) pervades positive-effect-hood — this is the definition. And pervasiveness means through the relation of counter-positiveness of destruction not residing in [the entity] itself. And not-residing-in-self means through temporal relation. By this, since effects and positive effects, being infinite, are impossible to enumerate individually even for a non-omniscient person, and since the aggregate of all their destructions is even more impossible to fully know — the objection that this definition-statement is incoherent is refuted.

children.text: ākāśanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of <s>Ākāśa</s> (Space/Ether)

children.text:
dyotanāyeti/ tathā ca śabdaguṇakamiti
saṃgrahavākye 'sarva vākya'miti nyāyena śabda eva guṇo viśeṣaguṇo
yasminniti bahuvrīṃhiriti bhāvaḥ/ nanu taccaikamiti saṃgrahavākye
ākāśasyaikatvamuktam, tanna yuktam,
children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of elucidation' — and accordingly, in the summary statement 'possessing sound as its quality,' by the maxim 'the complete statement,' [the compound is to be understood as] a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>: that in which sound alone is the specific quality — this is the purport. Now, in the summary statement 'and that is one,' the oneness of <s>ākāśa</s> was stated; that is not proper,

children.text:
1.
karmadhārayoparītyādinyāyamiti/ karmadhārayopari vidyamānaḥ
bhāvārthakapratyayaḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyabodhaka iti nyāyamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'The maxim "on top of a <s>karmadhāraya</s>"' — the meaning is: the maxim that a suffixed derivative occurring after a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound conveys co-location.

children.text:
ghaṭākāśo maṭhākāśa
ityādivyavahārasya ākāśānekatvasādhakasya sattvāt, vyavahārabhede
vyavahartavyabhedasyaiva niyāmakatvāt/ tathā ca 'ghaṭākāśavyavahāraḥ
maṭhākāśatvāvacchinnabhinnaniṣṭhavyavahartavyatākaḥ
maṭhākāśatvabhinnadharmāvacchinnavyavahartavyatākavyavahāratvāt, yo
yaddharmabhinnadharmāvacchinnavyavahartavyatākavyavahāraḥ sa
taddharmāvacchinnabhinnaniṣṭhavyavahartavyatākaḥ' iti
sāmānyavyāptyupaṣṭabhyamanumānamatra mānamityāśaṅkāyāṃ
'vyavahartavyatāvacchedakabheda eva vyavahārabhedaniyāmakaḥ, anyathā
prāṇāpānādivyavahārabhedānupapatteḥ/ evaṃ ca darśitānumāne
prāṇāpānādivyavahāramādāya vyabhicāraḥ/ tathā ca prakṛte
ghaṭamaṭhādirūpavyavahartavyatāvacchedakabhedena tādṛśavyavahāropapattau
na tasyākāśabhedasādhakatvam' iti samādhānamabhisandhāyāha- [88] ghaṭākāśo maṭhākāśa ityādīti/ [88] anekatve -
ākāśatvanyūnavṛttidharmavattve/ [88] pramāṇam - pramā, tasya
viśeṣyatāsambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvadityarthaḥ/ tathā ca
'ākāśaṃ ākāśatvanyūnavṛttidharmaśūnyaṃ,
tādṛśadharmavattvaprakārakapramāviśeṣyatvābhāvāt, yannaivaṃ tannaivam'
iti vyatirekyanumānamākāśasya ekatve pramāṇamupadarśitam/ [88] ekatvādeveti/ ākāśatvanyūnavṛttidharmaśūnyatvādevetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: because the usage 'pot-space,' 'hall-space,' and the like, which proves the multiplicity of <s>ākāśa</s>, exists, and because difference in usage necessarily determines difference in what is being spoken about. And accordingly, anticipating the inference — 'The usage "pot-space" has as its spoken-about-ness one that resides in what is different, delimited by hall-space-ness, because it is a usage whose spoken-about-ness is delimited by a property different from a property different from hall-space-ness; whatever usage has spoken-about-ness delimited by a property different from such-and-such a property has spoken-about-ness residing in what is different, delimited by such-and-such a property' — as a means of valid knowledge supported by such a general pervasion, he gives the resolution — intending that 'difference in the delimitor of spoken-about-ness alone is the determinant of difference in usage; otherwise the difference of usage in <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the like would be impossible. And accordingly, in the demonstrated inference, taking the usage of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the like, there is deviation. And thus, in the present case, since such usage is explained through the difference of delimitors of spoken-about-ness in the form of pot, hall, and the like, it does not prove the multiplicity of <s>ākāśa</s>' — he says [§88] 'pot-space, hall-space, and the like.' [§88] 'In multiplicity' — possessing a property occurring no more narrowly than <s>ākāśa</s>-hood. [§88] 'Means of valid knowledge' — valid cognition; the meaning is: the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of qualificand-hood. And accordingly, the negative-concomitance inference demonstrated for the oneness of <s>ākāśa</s> is: '<s>ākāśa</s> is devoid of a property occurring no more narrowly than <s>ākāśa</s>-hood, because of the absence of a valid cognition having such-a-property-possession as qualifier; what is not so is not so.' [§88] 'Because of oneness alone' — the meaning is: because of the very absence of a property occurring no more narrowly than <s>ākāśa</s>-hood.

children.text:
kecittu -
ākāśatvavyāpyadharmaviruddhadharmāvyāpakākāśatvakatvameva ākāśe
ekatvam/ atrāyamanugamaḥ-bhedaviśiṣṭākāśatvakatvaṃ tat/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasvāśrayatvobhayasambandhena/ avacchedakatā
svavyāpyadharmaviśiṣṭatvasambandhena/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaviruddhadharmaviśiṣṭatvasambandhena/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svasetyādibhedavattvasambandhena - ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: Some, however, [say]: oneness in <s>ākāśa</s> is precisely the possession of <s>ākāśa</s>-hood that does not pervade a property contrary to a property pervaded by <s>ākāśa</s>-hood. Here the analysis is: it is the possession of <s>ākāśa</s>-hood qualified by difference. And the qualification is through both relations of self-being-the-counter-positiveness-delimitor and self-being-the-substratum. The delimitor-hood is through the relation of being qualified by a property pervaded by self. And the qualification is through the relation of being qualified by a property contrary to self. And the qualification is through the relation of being-the-self-and-the-like-difference-possessing — thus they say.

children.text:
yattu
vibhājakadharmadvayaśūnyatvaṃ taditi/ tattuccham/ padārthavibhājakadravyatva
- dravyavibhājakākāśatvayoḥ sattvenāsambhavāpatteḥ/
ākāśavibhājakatvaniveśane ca siddhyasiddhibhyāṃ vyāghātāpatteriti
dhyeyam/ ākāśakāladigātmanāṃ sādhāraṇaṃ vibhutvaṃ na jātiḥ/
tatsādhikāyāḥ anugatapratyakṣadhiyo 'saṃbhavāt, teṣu rūpādyabhāvāt,
children.translated_text: As for the view that [<s>vibhutva</s> is] the absence of both dividing properties — that is worthless. For there would be the unwanted impossibility, since both substance-ness which divides the category of <s>padārtha</s> (object) and space-ness which divides substance exist [in space]. And if one specifies 'being a divider of space,' there would be a contradiction through both establishment and non-establishment — this should be noted. The all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>) common to space (<s>ākāśa</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), direction (<s>dik</s>), and self (<s>ātman</s>) is not a universal (<s>jāti</s>), since a recurring perceptual cognition that would establish it is impossible, because color and the like are absent in them,

children.text:
ananyathāsiddhaliṅgānupalambhenānumānāsambhavāt/ śabdasya
cāptoktatvāniścayena sandigdhaprāmāṇyakatvāt, anyathā
vaiparītyasyāpi suvacatvāt/ na ca vibhupadavācyatāvacchedakatayā
vibhutvajātisiddhiriti vācyam/ 1tulyayuktyā bhūtatvasyāpi
siddhyāpattyā prāguktatritayasambandhena tadviśiṣṭatvarūpajātisāṃkaryasya
jātitvābhāvavyāpyatayā gṛhītasya jātibādhakasya sattvena tasya
jātitvāsiddheḥ/
children.translated_text: and because inference is impossible due to the non-availability of a non-otherwise-established inferential mark; and because verbal testimony has doubtful authority due to uncertainty about it being spoken by a reliable person, and otherwise the opposite could equally well be stated. Nor should one say that the universal of <s>vibhutva</s> is established through being the limitor of the denotation-delimiting property of the word '<s>vibhu</s>' (all-pervading). By the same reasoning, there would be the unwanted consequence of establishing <s>bhūtatva</s> (element-ness) [as a <s>jāti</s>] too; and since the <s>jāti</s>-blocker — namely, the intermixture of classes in the form of being-qualified-by-that through the three relations stated earlier — has been accepted as pervaded by the absence of <s>jāti</s>-hood, the <s>jāti</s>-hood of that [<s>vibhutva</s>] is not established.

children.text:
yattu
paramamahatparimāṇavattvaṃ vibhutvamiti/ tanna/ 'vaibhavāt
mahānākāśastathā cātmā' iti sūtre kaṇādena
paramamahatvasādhakaliṅgātvena vibhutvasyoktatvāt
paramamahatparimāṇavattvasya tatsvarūpatāyāḥ sūtrakārānanumatatvāt
ityabhiprāyeṇa prakārāntareṇa vibhutvaṃ nirvakti- [88] sarvamūrteti/ atra ca paṭādisaṃyuktaghaṭādivāraṇāya sarvapadam/
children.translated_text: As for the view that <s>vibhutva</s> (all-pervasiveness) is the property of possessing the supremely great magnitude (<s>paramamahat-parimāṇa</s>) — that is incorrect. Because in the <s>sūtra</s> 'Due to all-pervasiveness, space is great, and similarly the self,' <s>Kaṇāda</s> has stated <s>vibhutva</s> as the inferential mark that establishes supreme greatness, and thus the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> does not accept that possessing supremely great magnitude is identical with <s>vibhutva</s> — with this intent, he defines <s>vibhutva</s> in another way: [<s>Tarkasaṅgraha</s> 88] 'that which is conjoined with every corporeal [substance],' etc. Here the word 'every' (<s>sarva</s>) is to exclude a pot and the like that is conjoined with a cloth and so forth.

children.text:
vibhūnāṃ
kriyāviraheṇa parasparasaṃyogābhāvāt asaṃbhavanirāsāya mūrtapadam/
mūrtatvasya kriyāsamavāyikāraṇatāvacchedakatayā
siddhajātiviśeṣarūpatvapakṣe
prācīnābhimatotpannavinaṣṭadravyamādāyāsambhavavāraṇāya dravyapadaṃ
saṃyogavadarthakam/ ata evoktadoṣavāraṇāya mūrtapadaṃ
nityamūrtaparamiti pralapitamanādeyam/ dravyapadavaiyarthyāpātācca/
'kriyāvattvaṃ mūrtatvam' iti mate utpannavinaṣṭadravyānupagantṛnaye
vā nopādeyameva tat/
children.translated_text: The word 'corporeal' (<s>mūrta</s>) is to remove the impossibility [that would arise] since all-pervading entities, lacking action (<s>kriyā</s>), do not have mutual conjunction. On the view that corporeality (<s>mūrtatva</s>) is an established particular universal that serves as the limitor of the causality of the inseparable cause of action, the word 'substance' (<s>dravya</s>), meaning 'possessing conjunction,' is to prevent the impossibility that would arise [even] by including produced-and-destroyed substances accepted by the earlier [logicians]. Therefore the claim that, to prevent the stated defect, the word 'corporeal' means 'eternally corporeal and supreme' is idle talk that should be rejected — since it would render the word 'substance' otiose. On the view that '<s>mūrtatva</s> is the property of possessing action,' or on the view that does not accept produced-and-destroyed substances, that [qualification] is simply not needed.

children.text:
atha
'sarvamūrtadravyasaṃyogitvam'ityasya sarvāṇi yāni mūrtadravyāṇi
tāvatpratiyogikasaṃyogavattvārthakatve
tāvatpratiyogikaikasaṃyogāprasiddhyā asambhavaḥ/ tāvatāṃ
pratyekapratyekapratiyogikasaṃyogasamudāyavattvārthakatve
ghaṭapaṭasaṃyogāderapi tādṛśasamudāyaghaṭakatayā
tadghaṭitasamudāyavattvasya ākāśādāvabhāvāt sa eva doṣaḥ/ yattu -
yāvanti mūrta dravyāṇi teṣāṃ
pratyekapratiyogikaikasaṃyogaghaṭitasamudāyavattvaṃ taditi - naiṣa
doṣaḥ/ na ca mūrtatvajātipakṣe
children.translated_text: Now, if 'being conjoined with every corporeal substance' (<s>sarvamūrtadravyasaṃyogitva</s>) means possessing a single conjunction whose counter-positive is all [corporeal substances together], there is impossibility since a single conjunction having all of them as counter-positives is not established. If it means possessing the aggregate of conjunctions each having each [corporeal substance] individually as counter-positive, then since a conjunction like pot-cloth conjunction too is a component of such an aggregate, the absence of that aggregate-possessing property in space and the like constitutes the same defect. As for the [alternative] interpretation — possessing the aggregate constituted by a single conjunction whose counter-positive is each individual among however many corporeal substances there are — this is not a defect. Nor [is there a problem] on the view that <s>mūrtatva</s> is a universal,

children.text:
1. tulyayuktyeti/

children.translated_text: since produced-and-destroyed earth and the like too, being substrata of that [conjunction], are not included within 'all corporeal [substances],' and hence the conjunction having them as counter-positive is not established, and therefore the aggregate of conjunctions constituted by that does not exist in space and the like — [one might say] this impossibility remains the same. [But] this is worthless, since the word 'substance' (<s>dravya</s>) has already been explained as meaning 'possessing conjunction,' and therefore such produced-and-destroyed earth and the like are not included [in the scope]; and if the word 'corporeal' means 'possessing action,' all the more so there is no defect. [The objection is] worthless because, [even granting the alternative], if one accepts as the definition of <s>vibhu</s> in general the property of possessing [a property] delimited by each individual aggregate-ness of the aggregate — which consists merely of the conjunctions each inhering in each of the four [all-pervading substances] space and so forth — this being the content of a particular relational cognition, and since such aggregate-nesses are mutually distinct, [the property of] possessing [something] delimited by each such aggregate-ness would suffer from under-extension, as it would not exist in anything else by the denotation-relation with the word '<s>vibhu</s>.' If the definition were possessing all four such aggregates, there would be impossibility, since that exists nowhere. If the definition were possessing any one of those, then since such 'any-one-ness' — being a distinct otherness delimited by the four aggregate-nesses of those respective aggregates — requires accepting absence whose correlate-hood is delimited by a property that occurs in a pervading manner, there would be impossibility [if this is not accepted]. And if it is accepted, then since even the conjunction of a pot with space and the like would be a substratum of such any-one-ness, there would be over-extension to pots and the like — how can this be reconciled?

children.translated_text: Also, from 'being conjoined with every corporeal substance,' what is obtained is that in corporeal substances there is no conjunction with space and the like [that is absent]. And thus what results as the definition is: possessing an absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the individual-ness of whatever corporeal substance is not conjoined with oneself. Here, since no corporeal substance unconnected with space and the like is established, by the word 'self' (<s>sva</s>), the inclusion of space and the like [in the scope] is impossible, and hence the definition is concordant with space and the like. To prevent the impossibility [that would arise] since space and the like are also not conjoined with qualities and so forth that are their own [properties], the word 'corporeal' [is used]. On the view that <s>mūrtatva</s> is a universal, to prevent the impossibility arising from produced-and-destroyed pots and the like — which are substrata of that [universal] — also being unconnected with themselves, the word 'substance' means 'possessing conjunction.' And for such pots and the like, even though they are not conjoined with space and the like, since they do not lack conjunction-ness [altogether], there is no impossibility. Nor should one say that the word 'corporeal' is then otiose, since qualities and the like are not of that nature [i.e., they lack conjunction]. Even so, since space and the like possess the property of being space-and-the-like that is not conjoined with themselves,

children.translated_text: and hence [the word 'corporeal'] is necessarily needed to prevent that defect — this too is incorrect. Since the particular instances of corporeal objects belonging to other times and other persons cannot be specifically known by us, the definition constituted by such a multitude of absences would be impracticable. Even though the definition could be the otherness qualified by knowability through both the relations of conjunction-of-what-is-conjoined-with-one's-own-corporeal [substance], identity, and both, as something that recurs [across all <s>vibhu</s>s], nevertheless, since [defining through] conjunction-relation and the property of being-different-delimited-by-self-delimitedness — when one's own conjunct is not established — would over-extend to color and the like; and since even when that is prevented by independently adding 'substance-ness,' there would be over-extension to produced-and-destroyed earth and the like; and since even preventing that by adding 'conjunction-ness' in place of 'substance-ness' would involve great cumbersomeness — and since, as will be stated, when an interpretation of the literal meaning of the words as they stand is possible, it is inappropriate to abandon that and fabricate a different meaning and then add further qualifications to ward off further defects — this follows the maxim of 'rather than washing [the mud off], it is better not to touch it from a distance.'

children.translated_text: By this [it is shown that]: through the expression 'not conjoined with oneself' (<s>svāsaṃyukta</s>), intending the absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the relation of being-conjoined-ness residing in oneself, there is no over-extension to produced-and-destroyed earth and the like. Thus, either being a substance-dividing-property that does not occur in [substances] possessing action, or being a property of possessing a substance-dividing-property that is not co-located with the universal of corporeality — this is what is intended by 'being conjoined with every corporeal substance.' And the possession of such a property is through either the relation of identity (<s>svarūpa</s>) or inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). Therefore, the [objection of] under-extension in time, self, and the like is also refuted. Since the flow of [unwanted consequences like] a leaking vessel is difficult to stop, and since, when there is no determinate basis for the qualifier-qualificand relation between the two absences that constitute the 'either-ness,'

children.translated_text: To this it is replied: The meaning of 'every corporeal' and so forth is pervasion of corporeal-substance-ness. Because the word 'every' (<s>sarva</s>) means 'pervading the delimiting property of the referent of the co-occurring word.' And the pervasion is through the relation of being the counter-positive of a conjunction whose correlate is oneself. It is precisely to obtain this that 'conjoined' (<s>saṃyogī</s>) was stated. Although pervasion of corporeal-substance-ness through the relation of being the counter-positive of a conjunction whose correlate is oneself amounts to not being devoid of counter-positive-hood delimited by that relation, of the absolute absence residing in corporeal substances — this is not established on the view that a non-occurrence-determining relation does not delimit the counter-positive-hood of absolute absence. Nevertheless, what is intended here is: not being devoid of limitor-hood delimited by the stated relation and determined by the counter-positive-hood of the absence residing in corporeal substances. Since even the relation that does not delimit the counter-positive-hood of absolute absence does delimit the limitor-hood-of-the-limitor of the counter-positive-hood of mutual absence —

children.translated_text: which is determined by the superstratum-hood-mode, which is determined by the [present-time] qualifier-mode — this is the meaning, with the ablative expressing the reason of identity. In reality, however, past-ness (<s>atītatva</s>) is: possessing the time that is the locus of the linguistic usage 'has passed' through the relation of being the counter-positive of the destruction residing in oneself. Future-ness (<s>bhaviṣyattva</s>) is: possessing the time that is the locus of the linguistic usage 'will be' through the relation of being the counter-positive of the prior absence residing in oneself. Present-ness (<s>vartamānatva</s>) is: possessing the time that is the locus of the linguistic usage 'exists' through the relation of superstratum-hood (<s>ādheyatā</s>). And thus, in linguistic usage, since the cognition having as qualifier-mode the delimiting property of what is to be expressed is causal, the causal role of time — being the possession of content-hood for that delimiting [property] — remains intact. The meaning of 'by being the pot-ness' is also: by being the locus of such content-hood. The ablative expresses identity. If prior absence is not accepted, then future-ness should be analyzed as: possessing the time — delimited by the destruction of the moment that is the locus of the linguistic usage 'will be' — through the relation of being-produced-at-the-time-delimited-by-one's-own-destruction, amounting to being qualified by such a moment. This should be noted. And the delimiting

By 'the western direction and so forth,' the northern and southern directions are included.

children.translated_text: 'Having knowledge through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence)' — this is the meaning. Otherwise, there would be over-extension to time and the like, which possess knowledge through temporal and other relations — this is the purport. [92] 'Contradiction' and so forth — the purport is that by that [scriptural statement], the nature of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) as knowledge itself is conveyed. In the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) '<s>nityaṃ vijñānam</s>' (eternal consciousness), regarding the word <s>vijñāna</s>, he states whether the affix is an <s>arśa-ādi</s> (indicating non-originated nature) or a <s>kartṛ-lyuṭ</s> (agent-noun suffix) due to belonging to the <s>nandyādi</s> class — [93] 'having the meaning of possessing knowledge' and so forth. Objection: since <s>Īśvara</s> lacks pleasure, how can the stated <s>śruti</s> have validity? Anticipating this, he says — [93] 'here' and so forth. [93] 'As in the expression "I have become happy"' means: like the word <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) in such a sentence. Here — in the stated <s>śruti</s> — the word <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) is used figuratively for the absence of suffering. The locative case has the meaning of locus. The figurative usage is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification). The meaning intended is: being the determinant. And accordingly, the result is that the word <s>ānanda</s> in the stated <s>śruti</s> determines the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> residing in the absence of suffering.

children.text:
1. teyati/ 'nityaṃ
vijñānamānandaṃ brahma' iti śrutyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. 'By that' and so forth — the meaning is: by the <s>śruti</s> '<s>nityaṃ vijñānam ānandaṃ brahma</s>' (Brahman is eternal consciousness and bliss).

children.text:
śrutivākyasthapadasyāsati bādhake lakṣaṇā na yuktetyānandaśabdasya
mukhyārthaparatvaṃ varṇayatāṃ navīnānāṃ matamāha [93] navīnāstviti/ nanvīśvare janyamukhābhāvāt kathamānandaśabdasya
mukhyārthakatvamata āha -- [93] nityasukhamiti/ darśitaśrutibalādityādiḥ/
[93] vijātīyeti/ anyathā parātmanaḥ pareṇa manasā pratyakṣāpatteriti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Since <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) of a word in a scriptural sentence is not appropriate when there is no sublating cognition, he presents the view of the moderns who hold that the word <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) has its primary meaning — [93] 'the moderns, however' and so forth. Objection: since <s>Īśvara</s> lacks originated pleasure, how can the word <s>ānanda</s> have its primary meaning? To this he says — [93] 'eternal pleasure' and so forth. 'By the force of the demonstrated <s>śruti</s>' and so forth. [93] 'Of a different kind' — otherwise, there would be the undesirable consequence that the supreme Self is perceptible through a mind other [than one's own] — this is the purport.

children.text:
idamatra bodhyam -
'ātmā bāhyapratyakṣīyalaukikaviṣayatāśūnyaḥ
udbhūtarūpaśūnyadravyatvāt', 'jīvagatasukhādyatiriktaṃ
mānasīyalaukikaviṣayatvābhāvavat
vijātīyamanoyogatadāśrayasamavetatvādiśūnyatvāt,
gaganādivat'ityanumānadvayaṃ vivakṣitam/ tena na cārvākamate
pakṣāprasiddhiḥ/ avacchedakāvacchedena sādhyasiddheruddeśyatvāt
nāṃśatassiddhasādhanam/ [92] nāpyanumānam liṅgābhāvādityatrāpi
prameyasāmānyaṃ
svavyatiriktātmasādhakatvasambandhāvacchinnajīvaniṣṭhapratiyogitākātyantābhāvavat
vastutvādityanumānamavaseyamiti/
children.translated_text: Here this should be noted: the two inferences intended are — 'the <s>ātman</s> (self) is devoid of ordinary perceptual object-hood in external perception, because of being a substance devoid of manifest form'; and 'what is distinct from pleasure and the like residing in the individual self is devoid of being an ordinary object of mental perception, because of being devoid of being a locus of contact with a mind of a different kind, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the like.' Hence there is no failure of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) being unestablished on the <s>Cārvāka</s> view. Since the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is intended to be established under a particular delimiting property, there is no fallacy of proving what is already established even partially. [92] In 'nor is inference [a means of knowing the self], due to the absence of a <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark)' as well, one should understand an inference of the form: '[the self] is real, because of being a thing (<s>vastu</s>) that possesses the universal absence of counterpositive-hood delimited by the relation of capacity to establish a self distinct from itself, residing in individual selves — like the class of <s>prameya</s> (knowable objects) in general.'

children.text:
digiti/ ayamatra bhāvaḥ - yadyapi
kulālakṛtitvādyavacchinnasattve ghaṭatvādyavacchinnasattvaṃ tadabhāve tadabhāva
ityanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ ghaṭatvādikulālādikṛtitvābhyāmeva
kāryakāraṇabhāvassidhyati, tathāpi yadviśeṣayoritivyāptibalāt
kāryatvāvacchinnaṃ prati kṛtitvena kāraṇatvamapyāvaśyakam/ evaṃ
kāryatvāvacchinna prati jñānatvecchātvābhyāmapi tathātvaṃ
tādṛśānvayavyatirekāviśeṣāt/ evaṃ ca 'kāryaṃ kṛtijanyaṃ
kāryatvāt' ityanumānamiva
children.translated_text: 'Direction' and so forth. Here the purport is as follows: although by <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) — when effort delimited by potter-effort-hood and so forth is present, existence delimited by pot-hood and so forth is present, and in its absence, the latter is absent — the causal relation is established through pot-hood, potter-effort-hood and so forth alone, nevertheless, by the force of the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) 'wherever there is a particular pair,' the causal relation through effort-hood with respect to what is delimited by effect-hood is also necessary. Similarly, by cognition-hood and desire-hood too, the same relation holds with respect to what is delimited by effect-hood, since there is no distinction in <s>anvaya-vyatireka</s> of that kind. And accordingly, just as the inference 'the effect is produced by effort, because of being an effect,'

children.text:
'kāryaṃ jñānajanyaṃ
icchājanyañca kāryatvāt' ityanumānadvayamapi vivakṣitāmiti,
[93] aparokṣajñānāderityādipadena cikirṣāparigrahaḥ/ [93] cikirṣādikamityādipadena kṛtiparigrahaḥ/ nanu 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ
sarvavit'iti śrutau sarvajñaśabdenaiva īśvarasya
sarvaviṣayakajñānatvalābhe punaḥ sarvavitpadaṃ vyarthamityāśaṅkyāha -
[93] sarvaviditīti/ vastutastu sarvavidityasya sarvaṃ vidantīti
vyutpattyā sarvavyāpta ityarthaḥ/ vida lābha iti dhātoḥ kvipi
tādṛśār thasambhavāditi dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: the two inferences 'the effect is produced by cognition' and 'the effect is produced by desire, because of being an effect' are also intended. [93] By the word 'and so forth' in 'direct cognition and so forth,' <s>cikirṣā</s> (desire to act) is included. [93] By the word 'and so forth' in '<s>cikirṣā</s> and so forth,' <s>kṛti</s> (effort) is included. Objection: in the <s>śruti</s> 'He who is omniscient, all-knowing,' since the property of having cognition of all objects is already obtained for <s>Īśvara</s> by the word <s>sarvajña</s> (omniscient) alone, the word <s>sarvavit</s> (all-knowing) would be redundant. Anticipating this, he says — [93] '<s>sarvavit</s>' and so forth. In truth, <s>sarvavit</s>, by the derivation 'one who obtains everything,' means 'all-pervading.' Since the root <s>vid</s> in the sense of 'obtaining' permits the suffix <s>kvip</s> and such meaning is possible, this should be noted.

children.text:
nanu [92] jīvasya lakṣaṇamāha - jīva itīti dīpikāyām [91] jīvastu pratiśarīraṃ bhinna iti saṃgrahavākyāvataraṇamayuktam/
pratiśarīraṃ bhinnatvasya indriyādisādhāraṇatayā
jīvalakṣaṇatvāsambhavāt, ato lakṣaṇapadasya bahulagrahaṇasāmarthyāt
lakṣyata idamiti vyutpattyā karmaṇi lyuḍantatvamāśritya
svarūpaparatvamabhisandhāya vyācaṣṭe - [93] svarūpamāhesyartha iti/
[93] mūle prati śarīraṃ bhinna iti/ atra ca
pratipadasamabhivyāhṛtadvitīyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Objection: [92] He states the definition of <s>jīva</s> (individual self) — 'the <s>jīva</s>' — thus in the <s>Dīpikā</s>. [91] The introduction of the root text statement 'the <s>jīva</s>, however, is distinct in each body' is inappropriate, since being distinct in each body, being common to the sense-organs and the like, cannot be the definition of <s>jīva</s>.
