Therefore, by the power of the liberal interpretation of the word <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (definition), relying on it being a passive <s>lyuṭ</s>-suffix by the derivation 'that which is defined is this,' with the intent that it refers to the nature itself, he glosses — [93] 'states the nature' — this is the meaning. [93] In the root text: 'distinct in each body.' And here, regarding the second case-ending co-occurring with the word <s>prati</s>,

children.text:
ādheyatāśrayabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvamabhāvaśca
khaṇḍaśor'thaḥ/ anyathā sāmānyato vyāpakatvasya vyāpyaviśeṣāghaṭitasya
durvacatvena dvitīyārthatānupapatteriti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: the meanings of the two components are: being the delimitor of the counterpositive-hood of the difference whose locus is the substratum. Otherwise, since universal pervasion, which is not constituted by a specific pervaded entity, would be difficult to state, the meaning of the second case-ending would not be established — this should be noted.

children.text:
nanu 'pratiśarīraṃ
bhinna' iti vākyāt pratidravyaṃ sattetyādiṣu dravyatvavyāpikā
sattetyādyarthavat pratipadasamabhivyāhṛtaśarīrapadasya
śarītatvavyāpakatvārthakatayā śarīratvavyāpakabhedapratiyogītyartho
labhyate/ tacca na ghaṭate/ jīvātmanyekatvopagame 'pi
īdṛśārthanirvāhāt ātmabhedasya śarīratvavyāpakatvākṣateḥ/
atrocyate - na hi bhedasya śarīratvavyāpakatvaṃ svarūpasaṃbandhena
vivakṣitam/ yenaivaṃ syāt/ api [tu] svasamānādhikaraṇabhogāvacchedakatvasvapratiyogitāvacchedakatvobhayasaṃbandhena
avacchedakatā
svaviśiṣṭayogajadharmādyajanyaśarīrāvacchinnabhogavattvasaṃbandhena/ śarīre
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca svabhinna
children.translated_text: Objection: from the statement 'distinct in each body,' just as in expressions like 'existence in each substance,' where the meaning is that existence is pervaded by substance-hood, by the same token the word 'body' co-occurring with <s>prati</s> would have the meaning that the body-word is a pervader of body-hood, yielding the meaning 'the counterpositive of a difference pervaded by body-hood.' But this does not work, because even if one accepts the unity of the individual self, such a meaning would still hold, since the pervasion of difference by body-hood would remain intact. To this it is replied: the pervasion of difference by body-hood is not intended through the <s>svarūpa</s> (intrinsic) relation, which would make it so. Rather, [the delimitation is] through the double relation of being the delimitor of the counterpositive-hood of one's own co-located enjoyment-delimitation and of being the delimitor of one's own counterpositive-hood; and the delimitation through the relation of enjoyment delimited by body, which is delimited by one's own distinguished <s>yogaja-dharma</s> (merit born of yogic practice) and the like. And the distinction of the body from oneself

children.text: tva
children.translated_text: is through the double relation of being different from oneself and being contemporaneous with oneself. Therefore there is no stated defect. Having intended this very point, he says — [93]

children.text:
svasamānakālīnatvobhayasaṃbandhena/ ato
noktadoṣaḥ/ etadevābhipretyāha - [93] samānākāliketyādi/ kiṃ
tarhi jīvalakṣaṇamityāśaṅkāyāmāha - dīpikāyām [92] sukhādikaṃ jīvalakṣaṇamiti/ atra sukhopādānaṃ
prācīnamatamanusṛtya/ anyathā navīnamate uktarītyā
īśvare 'tivyāpteḥ/ ādinā duḥkhadveṣayoḥ parigrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'of the same time' and so forth. Anticipating the question — what then is the definition of <s>jīva</s>? — he says, in the <s>Dīpikā</s>: [92] 'pleasure and so forth is the definition of <s>jīva</s>.' Here, pleasure is mentioned following the ancient view. Otherwise, on the modern view, there would be over-extension to <s>Īśvara</s> in the manner stated. By 'and so forth,' suffering and aversion are included.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām [93] anyathā-śarīrātiriktasyātmatve/ siddhānte manuṣyādiśabdasya
svavṛtticeṣṭāsādhāraṇakāraṇayatnavattvasaṃbandhena
manuṣyādiśarīrāvacchinnātmaparatayā
manuṣyo 'hamityādipratītyupapattirityabhisandhāyoktam [93] abhimāna iti/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [93] 'Otherwise' — if the self is something other than the body. On the established view, since the word '<s>manuṣya</s>' (human) and similar words refer to the self delimited by a human body and so forth through the relation of possessing effort that is the distinctive cause of one's own bodily activity, the cognitions 'I am a human' and the like are explained — with this intention it was stated: [93] 'self-identification' and so forth.

children.text:
yanmadhyamaparimāṇamityādi/ parimāṇe
madhyamatvaṃ ca paramāṇutvaparamahattvabhinnatvam/ tathā cātmanastathātve
children.translated_text: 'That which has medium magnitude' and so forth. Medium-ness in magnitude means being different from atomic size and maximal size. And accordingly, if the self were of such [medium] magnitude,

children.text:
yathādehaṃ tasyāpi
saṅkocavikāsaśālitvāpattyā anityatvaprasaṅga iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: since it would have the nature of contracting and expanding in accordance with each body, the undesirable consequence of impermanence would follow — this is the purport.

children.text:
digiti/ ayamatra bhāvaḥ- yadi ca
kāyavyūhasthale śarīrāntare 'pi sukhādisākṣātkāropapattaye
prabhāprasaraṇamaṅgīkriyate, tadā anyatrādṛṣṭasyeha kalpanamanupapannam;
dṛṣṭānurodhenaiva kalpanasya sarvasammatatvāt/
ekagrahavartidīpaprasaraṇasya grahāntare 'dṛṣṭeḥ/ evaṃ
vyāpitvapratipādakāgamo 'pi tatra pramāṇamiti/
children.translated_text: 'Direction' and so forth. Here the purport is as follows: if, in the case of the assemblage of bodies, the spreading of radiance is accepted in order to account for the direct perception of pleasure and the like even in another body, then the supposition here of what is unseen elsewhere is unjustified — because supposition must conform to what is observed, as is universally accepted. Since the spreading of a lamp situated in one vessel is not seen in another vessel. Similarly, scripture that establishes all-pervasiveness is also a valid means of knowledge in that regard.

children.text: manonirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Manas</s> (Mind)

children.text:
dīpikāyām [98] sparśarahitatve satīti/ vāyāvativyāptibhiyā
rūpādirahitatvopekṣaṇam/ saṅgrahe [98] pratyātmaniyatatvāditi/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: [98] 'Being devoid of touch' — the omission of 'being devoid of color and so forth' is due to the fear of over-extension to air. In the <s>Saṅgraha</s> (root text): [98] 'Because of being limited to each self' and so forth.

children.text:
atra kecit - yāvantaḥ
ātmānaḥ tāvatāṃ manasāṃ vācyatvāt manaso 'nantatvamiti
viśiṣṭārthaḥ/ tallābhaḥ kathamiti cet ittham -
pratipadasamabhivyāhṛtamātmapadaṃ prātisvikarūpeṇa tattadātmavyaktiparam/
tanniyatatvaṃ ca tadanyāsambandhitvam tacca
tadanyasamavetajñānājanakatvam/ tathā ca
svajanyajñānāśrayayatkiñcidātmabhinnasamevatajñānājanakatvādityarthaḥ/
ekaikasya manasa iti śeṣaḥ/ jñānajñāpyatvaṃ pañcamyarthaḥ anantatve
anvetīti - tattuccham/ ātmaśabdasyātmatvajātiviśiṣṭaśaktitayā
tattadvyaktitvāvacchinnaparatve tasya lakṣaṇāprasaṅgāt/
ātmanāmanantatvena viśiṣṭa durjñeyatvācca/
children.translated_text: Here some [commentators hold]: since as many minds as there are selves must be denoted, the infinity of minds is the qualified meaning. How is that obtained? Thus: the word <s>ātman</s> co-occurring with <s>prati</s> refers to each individual instance of <s>ātman</s> in its particularized form. Its being limited to that means not being related to anything other than that, which means not generating a cognition co-inhering in anything other than that self. And accordingly, the meaning is: of each individual mind, the property of not generating a cognition that co-inheres in any self whatsoever other than the self that is the locus of the cognition produced by it. 'Of each mind' is the remainder to be supplied. Knowledge being made known by knowledge is the meaning of the fifth case-ending. 'This connects with infinity' — that is worthless, because if the word <s>ātman</s> had the power qualified by the universal <s>ātmatva</s> (self-hood) and therefore referred to what is delimited by being a particular instance, it would lead to <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification). And because the particular meaning qualified by the infinity of selves is difficult to ascertain.

children.text:
vastutastu
niyatatvamatra bhedāśrayatvam; bhede cātmanaḥ
pratipadīsamabhivyāhārabalāt
1svasetyādibhedavattvarūpavyāpakatāsaṃbandhena anvayaḥ/ svādhikaraṇatā
tādātmyasaṃbandhena/
children.translated_text: In truth, 'being limited' here means being the locus of difference. And regarding the difference, by the force of the co-occurrence with <s>prati</s> and the word <s>ātman</s>, the connection is through the relation of pervasion-hood in the form of possessing a difference such as 'its own' and so forth. 'Being in one's own locus' is through the relation of identity.

children.text:
1.
svasetyādibhedavattveti/
svasamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvani ṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavatvasaṃbandhenatyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. 'Possessing a difference such as its own' and so forth — the meaning is: through the relation of possessing a difference whose counterpositive-hood is delimited by the delimitor of co-located difference from itself, which relation delimits the delimitor-hood of what resides in itself.

children.text:
bhedaḥ
svabhinnasamavetajñānajanakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasvāśrayamanojanyajñānasamavāyitva-
ubhayasaṃbandhena/ evaṃ cātmapadasya mukhyārthaparatāpi sutarāṃ
saṅgacchate/ ata eva saṅgrahaṭippaṇyāmuktamarthāntaramapi
dūrato 'pāstam/ nanu lāghavāt sarveṣāmapyātmanāṃ ekameva mana
āstāmityatrāha - [99] sarvātmanāmityādi/ nanu manaso 'ṇutva eva
uktadoṣaḥ syāt/ na hi vayaṃ tasyāṇutvaṃ svīkurmahe/ api tu
vibhutvameva/ tathā ca sarvātmanāṃ manasa ekatve 'pi sarvendriyairekadā
saṃyogasambhavāt naikasya puṃsaḥ jñānadaśāyāṃ aparasya
tadanupapattirityabhiprāyeṇa śaṅkate - dīpikāyām [99] nanu mana ityādinā/ [99]
sparśarahitatve satītyādi/
pṛthivyādau vyabhicāravāraṇāya satyantam/ guṇādau
vyabhicāranirāsāya viśeṣyam/ atra ca manaso 'ṇutve ānantyaṃ
kalpanīyam/ vibhutve tu na tatheti lāghavamiti tarkasattvāt
nāsyānumānasyāprayojakatvamiti
children.translated_text: Difference is through the double relation of being the delimitor of the counterpositive-hood of oneself delimited by the relation of capacity to generate cognition co-inhering in what is different from oneself, and being the locus of cognition produced by the mind that is one's own locus. And accordingly, the primary meaning of the word <s>ātman</s> is also entirely consistent. For this very reason, the alternative meaning stated in the commentary (<s>ṭippaṇī</s>) on the <s>Saṅgraha</s> is also firmly rejected. Objection: for the sake of parsimony, let there be just one mind for all selves. To this he says — [99] 'of all selves' and so forth. Objection: the stated defect would arise only if mind is atomic. But we do not accept its atomicity; rather, we accept its all-pervasiveness alone. And accordingly, even if there is one mind for all selves, since contact with all sense-organs at once would be possible, it would not be the case that when one person is in the state of cognition, another person cannot have cognition — with this intent, [the objector] raises the doubt: in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [99] 'objection: mind' and so forth. [99] 'Being devoid of touch' and so forth. The word 'being' is to exclude earth and the like from the over-extension. The qualificand is to exclude the over-extension to qualities and the like. And here, if mind is atomic, infinity must be postulated. But if it is all-pervasive, that is not so — parsimony being the consideration. Since this <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) is valid, this inference is not without purpose —

children.text:
bhāvaḥ/ samavāyena
saṃyogaṃ prati samavāyena kriyāyāḥ kāraṇatvāt vibhuṣu ca
kriyāviraheṇa noktasaṃyogopapattirityāśayenāha - prakāśikāyāṃ
[99] vibhudvayeti/ [99] kriyādītyādinā saṃyogaparigrahaḥ/
dīpikāyām [99] tadā suṣuptiriti/ idamatra bodhyam -
suṣuptiḥ svāpaḥ
purītannāḍīpradeśāvacchinnātmānuyogikaḥmanaḥpratiyogikasaṃyogaḥ na
tu tādṛśadeśānuyogikamanaḥpratiyogikasaṃyogaḥ/ tathā sati 'caitraḥ
svapiti', 'maitraḥ suṣuptaḥ' ityādivākyānāmaprāmāṇyāpātāt/ tatra
caitrādipadasya tattaccharīrāvacchinnātmaparatayā ātmani ca
tādṛśasaṃyogavirahāt/ kartṛpratyayasya cāśrayatvabodhakatvāt/ ata
evoktam
children.translated_text: this is the purport. Since contact [of mind with sense-organ] requires action through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), and since action through <s>samavāya</s> is the cause of contact, and since all-pervasive substances lack action, the stated contact cannot be accounted for — with this intent he says, in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [99] 'two all-pervasive entities' and so forth. [99] By 'action and so forth,' contact is included. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: [99] 'then there is deep sleep' and so forth. Here this should be noted: deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>) is the contact whose counterpositive is mind and whose locus is the self delimited by the region of the <s>purītat-nāḍī</s> (a particular channel), and not the contact whose counterpositive is mind and whose locus is such a region. For otherwise, the statements 'Caitra sleeps' and '<s>Maitra</s> is in deep sleep' would become invalid, since the word <s>Caitra</s> and the like refers to the self delimited by the respective body, and such contact is absent in the self. And because the agent-suffix conveys locus-hood. Therefore it was stated

children.text:
vyutpattivādaṭippaṇyām kṛṣṇambhaṭṭenāpi 'tatraikasmin
svāpe nidrānāḍyavacchinnamanoyogarūpe' daiti 'dhātvarthasvāpe
nidrānāḍyavacchinnātmamanoyorūpe' iti ca/
children.translated_text: by <s>Kṛṣṇambhaṭṭa</s> too in the commentary (<s>ṭippaṇī</s>) on the <s>Vyutpattivāda</s>: 'there, in the case of one [person's] sleep, being of the form of the contact of mind delimited by the sleep-channel' and also 'in the sense of the verbal root, sleep being of the form of the contact of the self and mind delimited by the sleep-channel.'

children.text:
yattu - svapitītyādau
purītatpradeśamanoyogānukūlakṛtimāniti bodhavarṇanam -
tadayuktam - svāpadaśāyāmātmani tādṛśakṛterabhāvāt
jīvanayonirūpayatnasya ca prāṇakriyāmātrahetutvena
tādṛśasaṃyogānukūlatvavirahāt
iṣṭasādhanatājñānajanyatāvacchedakapravṛttitvajāterevākhyātārthatāvacchedakatāyāḥ
gadādhareṇa uktatayā
jīvanayoniyatnasyākhyātārthatāprasakterevābhāvācca/ yadyapi
tādṛśamanoyogasya svāparūpatve manaḥ
svapitītyādadivākyaprāmāṇyāpattiḥ, tathāpyanuyogitāyā eva tatra
pratyayārthatvasvīkāreṇa tasyāśca pratiyoginyanabhyupagamāt
noktāpattiḥ/ yadyapyākhyātāderāśrayatvādyarthakatāyā apyanyatra kḷptatvāt
tattātparyeṇa manaḥ svapiti ityādiprayogāpattiḥ durvāraiva/ tathāpi
kṛtyādāvevākhyātasya śaktiḥ, āśrayatvādau tu nirūḍhalakṣaṇeti
sarvānumatam/ tatra svapidhātusamabhivyāhṛtapratyayasyānuyogitva
evānāditātparyaṃ kalpyate/ ato na doṣaḥ/
athānuyogitvādessaṃsargatayā bhānenaivopapattau
kimākhyātādestadarthakatāmupagamya prakāravidhayā tadbhānasvīkāreṇa?
anyathā tatsaṃsargasyāpi śābdabodhaviṣayatvakalpanāpattyā gauravāt/ na
caivaṃ caitro na svapitītyādau nañarthābhāvānvayānupapattiḥ/
pratiyogitāvadanuyogitāyāṃ api
vṛttyaniyāmakatvenābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakatvāditi vācyam/
vṛttyaniyāmakasyāpyabhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakatāghaṭakasambandhatvopagamenādoṣāt/
na ca vṛttyaniyāmakasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvasyātiriktasya
kalpane gauravamiti vācyam/
tādṛśasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatadabhāvasya
tadīyatādṛśasambandhābhāvasamaniyatatvena tadabhinnatayā
atiriktakalpanāvirahāt/ na caivamapi
vṛttyaniyāmakasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākalpane gauravamiti
vācyam/ bhavanmate 'pi prāguktagauravasattvena sāmyāt/ na ca
rājapuraṣavādoktayuktyānuyogitvasya śābdabodhe
prakāratvamāvaśyakamiti vācyam/ tādṛśayuktīnāṃ
vistareṇānyatrāsmābhirnirastatvāt/ svapitītyetāvanmātrasya
bodhakatvopapattaye ākhyātāderanuyogitārthakatāyā āvaśyakatvāt/
yadyapi caitraḥ svapitītyādau anuyogitāyāḥ padārthatve 'pi śābbodhe
saṃsargatayā bhāne na ko 'pi dāṣaḥ/ tathāpi
tātparyārthaviśeṣānurodhena tatsaṃsargako vā tatprakārako vā
bodho bhāvatviti na tatrāsmākamāgrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, the description of verbal cognition in cases like '<s>svapiti</s>' ('he sleeps') as 'one possessing effort conducive to the conjunction of the mind with the region of the excretory organ' — that is incorrect. Because in the state of deep sleep, such effort is absent in the <s>ātman</s> (self); and because the effort that is the cause of life merely causes vital activity and thus lacks conduciveness to such conjunction; and because <s>Gadādhara</s> has stated that the delimiting property of the meaning of the verbal suffix is precisely the universal of being-an-activity that delimits the productivity of cognition of being a means to a desired end, and hence the effort that is the cause of life simply has no connection to the meaning of the verbal suffix. Although, if such conjunction of mind were of the nature of one's own form, there would be the undesirable consequence of the invalidity of sentences like '<s>manaḥ svapiti</s>' ('the mind sleeps'), nevertheless, since the meaning of the suffix there is accepted to be precisely <s>anuyogitā</s> (the relation of being a subjunct), and since the counter-positive of that [relation] is not admitted, the stated undesirable consequence does not arise. Although the undesirable consequence of usages like '<s>manaḥ svapiti</s>' with the purport of substrate-hood and other meanings of verbal suffixes — since such meanings are established elsewhere — is indeed difficult to avoid, nevertheless, it is universally accepted that the <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) of the verbal suffix is in activity and such things, while in substrate-hood and so forth it operates through conventional <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification). There, the beginningless purport of the suffix co-occurring with the root '<s>svap</s>' is postulated to be precisely in <s>anuyogitā</s>. Hence there is no fault. Now, if the matter is accounted for by the appearance of <s>anuyogitā</s> and so forth merely as a connection, what is the point of accepting that as the meaning of the verbal suffix and accepting its appearance in the mode of a qualifier? Because otherwise, there would be the complexity of postulating that that connection too is an object of verbal cognition. Nor should it be said that in cases like '<s>Caitro na svapiti</s>' ('Caitra does not sleep'), the negation-meaning absence cannot be connected; because just as in the case of <s>pratiyogitā</s> (counter-positive-ness), <s>anuyogitā</s> too, by not being a restrictor of the <s>vṛtti</s> (occurrence relation), does not delimit the counter-positive-ness of the absence — so it should be said. But there is no fault, since even what is not a restrictor of <s>vṛtti</s> can be accepted as the relation constituting the delimiting of counter-positive-ness of absence. Nor should it be said that there is complexity in postulating the absence with counter-positive-ness delimited by a relation that does not restrict <s>vṛtti</s> as something additional; because the absence whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by such a relation, being co-extensive with the absence of such a relation in that entity, is non-different from it, and hence there is no postulation of anything additional. Nor should it be said that even so there is complexity in postulating counter-positive-ness delimited by a relation that does not restrict <s>vṛtti</s>; because in your view too, the previously stated complexity is equally present. Nor should it be said that by the reasoning stated in the <s>Rājapuruṣa</s> argument, the qualifier-hood of <s>anuyogitā</s> in verbal cognition is necessary; because such reasonings have been extensively refuted by us elsewhere. Since, for accounting for the capacity of just '<s>svapiti</s>' alone to produce cognition, the meaning of the verbal suffix as <s>anuyogitā</s> is necessary. Although in cases like '<s>Caitraḥ svapiti</s>', even if <s>anuyogitā</s> is a word-meaning, there is no fault in its appearing in verbal cognition as a connection; nevertheless, depending on the specific purport-meaning, the cognition may be either one having that as a connection or one having that as a mode — and we have no insistence on this matter.

children.text:
caitro
jānātītyādāvapyevameva bodhyam/ evaṃ bhavanmate purītat
svapitītyādiprayogasya prāmāṇyaṃ durvāram/ asmanmate tu neti
madekapariśīlitaḥ panthāḥ/
children.translated_text: In cases like '<s>Caitro jānāti</s>' ('Caitra knows') too, this should be understood in the same way. Thus, in your view, the validity of usages like '<s>purītat svapiti</s>' is difficult to avoid. But in our view it is not — this is the path examined by me alone.

children.text:
sukhādyupalabdhisādhanamindriyaṃ mana iti
saṅgrahaḥ/ atra ca ghaṭādyupalabdhisādhanībhūtacakṣurādinirāsāya
sukhādīti/ ātmanyativyāptivāraṇāya viśeṣyam/ yadi ca
tādṛśopalabdhisādhanatvaṃ
tādṛśopalabdhiniṣṭhānubhavatvavyāpyadharmāvacchinnajanyatānirūpitajanakatvam,
anyathā kālavidhayā tajjanake cakṣurādāvativyāpteḥ/ tathā ca
nātmanyativyāptiriti indriyatvaviśeṣeṇaṃ vyarthamiti vibhāvyate,
tadāpyāha - prakāśikāyām ātmamanoyogāditi/ ādipadena
sukhādiparigrahaḥ/ tathā ca sukhādimānasatvāvacchinnaṃ prati manasaḥ
karaṇatā nirvāharthaṃ ātmamanoyogasyātmasamevatayogyaviśeṣaṇatvena
sukhādervā vyāparatākalpanasyāvaśyakatayā tadvāraṇāya tatsārthakyamiti
bhāvaḥ/ [99] aṇutvasiddhiriti/ idamatra
pramāṇābhimatam 'manaḥ aṇutvatadabhāvānyataravat prameyatvāt'
ityanumānaṃ manaso 'naṇutve uktarītyā suṣuptyanupapattiriti
tarkasahakṛtamiti/
children.translated_text: The summary statement is: the sense organ that is the means of apprehending pleasure and so forth is <s>manas</s> (mind). Here, 'pleasure and so forth' is used to exclude the eye and other organs that serve as means for apprehending pots and so forth. It qualifies [mind] to prevent over-extension to the <s>ātman</s> (self). And if such means-of-apprehension-hood is the producer-hood that determines the productivity delimited by a property pervaded by experience-hood residing in such apprehension — since otherwise there would be over-extension to the eye and other organs in the mode of temporal relation — and accordingly, since there would be no over-extension to the <s>ātman</s>, the qualification by sense-organ-hood would be purposeless: considering this, he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'conjunction of the <s>ātman</s> with <s>manas</s>' and so forth. By the word 'and so forth,' pleasure and other [mental states] are included. And accordingly, the purposefulness of that [qualification] is for the sake of establishing the instrument-hood of <s>manas</s> with respect to the mental cognition delimited by pleasure and so forth — since it is necessary to postulate either the qualified-qualifier relation of <s>ātma-manas</s> conjunction as residing in the <s>ātman</s> by inherence, or the operation of pleasure and so forth [as an auxiliary] — and [the qualification serves] to prevent that — this is the purport. [99] 'Establishment of atomic-ness': the inference accepted as the proof here is 'the mind is either atomic or non-atomic, because of being knowable'; the impossibility of deep sleep in the manner stated if <s>manas</s> were non-atomic serves as <s>tarka</s> (counterfactual reasoning) assisting [the inference].

children.text: rūpanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Rūpa</s> (Color/Form)

children.text:
cakṣurmātragrāhyo guṇo rūpamiti
saṃgrahavākyam/ atra ca cakṣurmātragrāhya ityanane
cakṣurviśiṣṭadharmāśrayagrāhya iti bodhaḥ/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
laukikapratyāsattyā
svagrāhyarūpagrāhakendriyavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasaṃbandhāvacchinna
children.translated_text: The summary statement is: the quality apprehended by the eye alone is <s>rūpa</s> (color/form). Here, 'apprehended by the eye alone' produces the cognition: apprehended by the substrate of a property specific to the eye. And the qualification is through ordinary proximity, by the relation of both — being a locus of delimiting-property-hood of the counter-positive-ness of the difference from the particular occurrence of a sense organ that apprehends <s>rūpa</s> which is its own object, and eye-hood —

children.text:
svaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvacakṣuṣṭvaniṣṭhādheyatvobhayasambandhena/
adhikam anyatra prapañcitaṃ asmābhiḥ/ prakāśikāyām [101] na
rūpe sambhavatīti/ rūpasyātmamanogrāhyatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ [101] tathāpi tvagindriyeti/ yadyapi
cakṣuritaranirūpitajñānatvānavacchinnajanyatāśrayajñānīyalaukikaviṣayatāśūnya
children.translated_text: residing in the delimiting-property-hood of the counter-positive-ness of the difference possessing eye-hood, by the relation of superstratum-hood in both. The elaboration of this has been expounded by us elsewhere in detail. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [101] 'it is not possible in <s>rūpa</s>' — the purport is that <s>rūpa</s> is apprehended by the <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> [as well]. [101] 'Nevertheless, the organ of touch' — although there is no fault if what is intended is the non-apprehensibility by anything other than the eye, in the form of being devoid of ordinary objecthood residing in productivity not delimited by cognition-hood determined by anything other than the eye; nevertheless, for the organ of touch and so forth,

children.text:
tvarūpacakṣuritarāgrāhyatvavivakṣaṇe na doṣaḥ/ tathāpi tvagādeḥ
cākṣuṣapratyakṣaṃ prati kālādividhayā
children.translated_text: in order to prevent the impossibility [of the definition applying] by taking in the producer-hood with respect to visual perception in the mode of temporal relation,

children.text:
janakatāmādāyāsambhavavāraṇāya janakatāyāṃ
kālatvādyanavacchinnatvasya vā janyatāyāmevava vā
jñānatvavyāpyadharmāvacchinnatvasya vā vivakṣaṇīyatayā
cakṣussaṃyuktasamavāyamādāyāsambhavavāraṇāya cakṣuritarasya dravyatvena
viśeṣaṇīyatayā ca gauravamityālocya tatparityāgaḥ/ [101] tvagagrāhyatvetyādi/ tvācanirūpitalaukikaviṣayatāśūnyatvaṃ
cākṣuṣanirūpitalaukikaviṣayatāvatvaṃ ca jātiviśeṣaṇamatra vaktavyam/
tena tvācapratyakṣe yapatvasyopanayamaryādayā bhāne 'pi tvacaśca
kālavidhayā rūpacākṣuṣajñānajanakatve 'pi na kṣatiḥ/ evaṃ gurutvādeḥ
cākṣuṣe upanayamaryādayā bhāne 'pi nātivyāptiḥ/ atra rasādivāraṇāya
cākṣuṣeti/ prabhādivāraṇāya guṇavibhājaketi/ guṇatvavyāpyetyarthaḥ/
nanu prabhābhittisaṃyoge 'tivyāptivāraṇāya guṇapadameva
viśeṣaguṇaparaṃ kiṃ noktamityaśaṅkāyām āha- [101] ata
evetyādi/ tathā ca darśitātivyāptivāraṇā
cakṣurmātragrāhlayasāṃsiddhikadravatvaviśeṣe 'tivyāptinirāsāya ca
jātighaṭitapariṣkārasyāvaśyakatayā tvagagrāhyatvādeḥ/
tadviśeṣaṇatayaivopapattau lakṣaṇe viśeṣatvaniveśanaṃ gauravāvahamiti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: one must specify either that the producer-hood is not delimited by temporality and such [relations], or that in the productivity itself there is delimitation by a property pervaded by cognition-hood; and for preventing the impossibility by taking in the conjunction-with-what-is-conjoined-with-the-eye [relation], substance-hood must serve as a qualifier of what is other than the eye — and considering this complexity, that [approach] is abandoned. [101] 'Non-apprehensibility by touch' and so forth: what must be stated here as the qualification of the universal is the property of being devoid of ordinary objecthood determined by touch, and the property of possessing ordinary objecthood determined by vision. Thereby, even though in tactile perception, the quality of being wet appears within the bounds of subsumption, and even though touch is a producer of visual cognition of <s>rūpa</s> in the mode of temporal relation, there is no deficiency. Likewise, even though heaviness and such appear in visual cognition within the bounds of subsumption, there is no over-extension. Here, 'visual' is to exclude taste and so forth. 'Differentiating among qualities' is to exclude radiance and so forth. The meaning is: pervaded by quality-hood. Now, if one asks why the word 'quality' was not simply stated as referring to a specific quality, in order to prevent over-extension to the conjunction of radiance and a wall — he says [101] 'for this very reason' and so forth. And accordingly, for preventing the shown over-extension and for preventing over-extension in the specific natural fluidity apprehended by the eye alone, since a refinement involving the universal is necessary — [we use] non-apprehensibility-by-touch and so forth. Since the matter is accounted for by that alone serving as a qualifier, introducing specificity into the definition would incur complexity — this is the purport.

children.text:
dīpikāyām [100] avyāpyavṛttinīlādīti/ atrāvyāptivṛttitvaviśeṣaṇaṃ
parasparavaiyadhikaraṇyāśaṅkānirāsāya daiśikāvyāpyavṛttitvamiha
vivakṣitam/ tacca
1svapratiyogitvasvādhikaraṇanirūpitakiñciddeśāvacchinnādheyatvobhayasaṃbandhenābhāvaviśiṣṭatvam/
nanu [100] rūpasya vyāpyavṛttitvaniyamāditi dīpikoktirasaṅgatā/
utpannaṃ dravyamiti nyāyena rūpādīnāṃ
kālikāvyāpyavṛttitvasyāvaśyakatvādityata āha - prakāśikāyām [101] vyāpyavṛttitveti/ daiśikavyāpyavṛttitvetyartha
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [100] 'blue and so forth which have non-pervasive occurrence.' Here, the qualification of non-pervasive occurrence — what is intended is spatial non-pervasive occurrence, for the purpose of removing the suspicion of mutual exclusion of loci. And that is: being qualified by absence, by the relation of both — being the counter-positive of that very [absence] and being the superstratum-hood delimited by some spatial part, determined by one's own locus. Now, [100] 'because <s>rūpa</s> is necessarily of pervasive occurrence' — this statement in the <s>Dīpikā</s> is incongruous, since by the principle 'an originated substance,' temporal non-pervasive occurrence of <s>rūpa</s> and so forth is necessary. Therefore he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [101] 'non-pervasive occurrence' — meaning spatial non-pervasive occurrence.

children.text:
iti/
daiśikavyāpyavṛttitvaṃ ca pūrvoktobhayasambandhanābhāvaviśiṣṭānyatvam/
children.translated_text: Spatial non-pervasive occurrence is otherness qualified by absence through the two relations mentioned before.

children.text:
1.
svapratiyogitvetyādi/ svaṃ kapisaṃyogābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvaṃ
kapisaṃyoge, evaṃ svaṃ kapisaṃyogābhāvaḥ tadadhikaraṇaṃ vṛkṣaḥ
tannirūpitāgradeśāvacchinnavṛttitvaṃ kapisaṃyoge 'stīti samanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. 'Of one's own counter-positive-hood' and so forth: 'own' is the absence of monkey-conjunction; its counter-positive-hood is in monkey-conjunction. Similarly, 'own' is the absence of monkey-conjunction; its locus is the tree; the occurrence delimited by the top part determined by that — this exists in monkey-conjunction: such is the construal.

children.text:
1atra ca
nīlādisamudāyaḥ nitrarūpamiti pratītiviṣayatvatadabhāvānyataravān
prameyatvādityanumānaṃ nīlādisamudāyo yadi pratītiviṣayaḥ syāt
tarhyavyāpyavṛttiḥ syāditi tarkasahakṛtaṃ pramāṇaṃ vācyam/ tatra rūpasya
vyāpyavṛttitvaniyame vipratipannaṃ prati dūṣaṇāntaramāha - [101] idamupalakṣaṇamityādinā/ evaṃ ca
darśitagauravajñānasahakṛtamuktānumānameva citrarūpasyātiriktatve
pramāṇamiti bhāvaḥ/ prāgabhāvādītyādinā dhvaṃsaparigrahaḥ/ nanu
citrapaṭe rūpavattāpratīteḥ
2sāmānādhikaraṇsambandhenāvayavarūpamādāyopapatteḥ atiriktacitrarūpaṃ
nopeyate/ parasparavirodhena vyāpyavṛttinīlādisamudāyo 'pi na
tatrotpattumarhatīti āśaṅkate [100] nanu citretyādinā
dīpikāyām/ sāmānādhikaraṇyena tatra rūpasattvādāha - prakāśikāyām
[101] samavāyenetyādiriti/ 3samavetatvīyasambandhasya svarūpasya
kāraṇatāvacchedakatvākalpanayā lāghavamabhisandhāyāha - [101] svāśrayasamavetatvasambandhena rūpamiti/ jñānagatapratyakṣatvajātau
prayojakatvāsambhavādāha - [101]
pratyakṣaviṣayatveti/ nanu
dravyavṛttilaukikaviṣayatāsambandhena pratyakṣaṃ prati samavāyena rūpasya
kāraṇatve citrapaṭasthale 'tiriktarūpatatprāgabhāvataddhvaṃsānāṃ kalpanayā
mahāgauravamiti tadapekṣayā svaśrayasamavetatvasambandhenaiva rūpasya
kāraṇatvamucitamityato dūṣaṇāntaramāha - [101] citrāvayavāvayavaketyādinā/ dīpikāyām [101] tasmāt paṭasyetyādi/ ayamatra bhāvaḥ --- ayaṃ paṭaḥ
rūpatadabhāvānyataravān prameyatvādityanumānena yadyayaṃ rūpaśūnyaḥ
syāt tarhyapratyakṣaḥ syāditi tarkasahakṛtena siddhaṃ rūpaṃ
children.translated_text: 1. Here, the proof to be stated is the inference 'the aggregate of blue and so forth is either an object of cognition in the form of variegated color or it is not, because of being knowable'; if the aggregate of blue and so forth were an object of cognition, then it would have non-pervasive occurrence — this <s>tarka</s>-assisted inference is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. Regarding the restriction of <s>rūpa</s> to pervasive occurrence, he states another objection against the disputant by saying [101] 'this is illustrative' and so forth. And accordingly, the inference stated above, assisted by the cognition of the demonstrated complexity, is the proof for the additional existence of variegated color — this is the purport. By 'prior absence and so forth,' destruction is also included. Now, in a variegated cloth, since there is a cognition of possessing color, and since this is accounted for by taking the color of the parts through the relation of co-located-ness, additional variegated color need not be accepted. The aggregate of blue and so forth, being mutually contradictory and of non-pervasive occurrence, also cannot arise there — he raises this objection in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [100] by saying 'now, variegated' and so forth. Since color exists there through co-located-ness, he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [101] 'by inherence' and so forth. 3. Intending parsimony by not postulating the identity-relation of what-inheres-in-the-color-possessor as the delimiting relation of causality, he says [101] 'color through the relation of inhering-in-one's-own-substrate.' Since the universal of perceptuality in cognition cannot be a motivator, he says [101] 'being an object of perception.' Now, if color's causality with respect to perception is through the relation of inherence as an object of ordinary objecthood residing in substance — then in the case of variegated cloth, the postulation of additional color, prior absence of that, and its destruction would incur great complexity; and therefore it is more appropriate that color's causality is through the relation of inhering-in-one's-own-substrate alone. Hence he states another objection by saying [101] 'parts of variegated parts' and so forth. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [101] 'therefore, of the cloth' and so forth. The purport here is: by the inference 'this cloth is either possessing color or possessing the absence of that, because of being knowable,' and by the <s>tarka</s> that if it were devoid of color then it would be imperceptible, it is established that [the cloth possesses] color.

children.text:
1. atra ceti/
nīlīdisamudāyasya citrarūpatvābhāva ityarthaḥ/ yadvā rūpasya
vyāpyavṛttitva ityarthaḥ/ athavā citrarūpasyātiriktatva ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. 'Here' means: the absence of variegated-color-hood in the aggregate of blue and so forth. Or alternatively, the meaning is: the pervasive occurrence of <s>rūpa</s>. Or alternatively, the meaning is: the additional existence of variegated color.

children.text:
2.
sāmānādhikaraṇyasaṃbandheneti/ svādhikaraṇavṛttitvasaṃbandhenetyarthaḥ/
svaṃ avayavatanturūpaṃ tadadhikaraṇaṃ tantavaḥ tadvṛttitvaṃ paṭastheti tena
saṃbandhena paṭasya tanturūpavattvam/
children.translated_text: 2. 'Through the relation of co-located-ness' means: through the relation of residing in one's own locus. 'Own' is the color of the component thread; its locus is the threads; the residing-in-that is in the cloth — thus through that relation, the cloth possesses the thread's color.

children.text:
3. samavetatvīyeti/
rūpavatsamavetatvasya pratyakṣatvaprayojakatve tasya svarūpasaṃbandhenaiva
prayojakatvaṃ vācyamiti samavetatvapratiyogikasvarūpasaṃbandhasya
kāraṇatāvacchedakasaṃbandhatvaṃ vaktavyam/ svāśrayasamavetatvasaṃbandhena
rūpasya
children.translated_text: 3. 'Of what-inheres': if the inhering-in-what-possesses-color is the motivator of perceptuality, then its motivator-hood must be stated as being through the identity relation alone; hence, the identity-relation of the counter-positive of inhering-ness must be stated as the relation delimiting causality. But if color's causality is through the relation of inhering-in-one's-own-substrate,

children.text:
kāraṇatve tu
samavetatvameva kāraṇatāvacchedakasaṃbandhaḥ na tu tadīyasvarūpamiti
lāghavamiti/ kāraṇatāvacchedakadharmalāghavamapyatra bodhyam/
children.translated_text: then <s>samavetatva</s> (inherence-ness) itself is the relation delimiting causality, not its identity — hence the parsimony. The parsimony in the delimiting property of causality should also be understood here.

children.text:
pūrvoktayuktyā
atiriktatvasiddheḥ citrarūpamiti vyavahriyata iti/ citrarasāsiddhau
hetumāha - [101] dravyalaukiketyādi/ tathā cāyaṃ
rasatadabhāvānyataravān
prameyatvādityanumānamanukūlatarkavirahādaprayojakamiti bhāvaḥ/ atra
ca nānārasavadavayavadvayārabdhe vastuni atra rasa iti pratītyupapattaye
citrarasāṅgīkāra āvaśyaka iti tvanāśaṅkanīyam/
tatrāvayavarasasyaiva 1sāmānādhikaraṇyena bhānābhyupagamāt/ yatra ca
nānārasavatparamāṇudvayārabdhadvyaṇukādikrameṇa mahāvayaviparyantaṃ
utpannaṃ tatra rasapratītirnopeyata eva/ dharmiṇaḥ rāsanapratyakṣe
upanayamaryādayaiva bhānābhyupagamāt/ paramāṇurasasyāpi
viśeṣyavidhayālaukikapratyakṣāsambhavāt/ upanītaṃ viśeṣaṇatayaiveti
naiyāyikasiddhāntāditi/ vastutastu tasasya vyāpyavṛttitvaniyame
pramāṇābhāvāt deśabhedāvacchedena ekasminneva vastuni
nānārasotpattisambhavāt samavāyenātra rasa iti pratīteḥ
pramārūpāyā nānupapattiḥ/ sarvamidamabhisandhāyoktam [101] saṅkṣepa iti/
children.translated_text: Since the separateness [of variegated color] is established by the previously stated reasoning, it is designated as <s>citrarūpa</s> (variegated color). He states the reason for the non-establishment of <s>citrarasa</s> (variegated taste) — with '[101] substance, ordinary' and so on. And thus, the inference 'this possesses either taste or the absence of taste, because of being knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>)' etc. is ineffective due to the absence of a supportive <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) — this is the purport. And here it should not be objected that the acceptance of <s>citrarasa</s> is necessary to account for the cognition 'here is taste' with respect to a thing composed of two parts possessing different tastes — because it is accepted that only the taste of the parts appears through co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). And where something is produced through the sequence of dyads etc. composed of two atoms possessing different tastes, up to the great whole, there the cognition of taste need not be postulated at all — because it is accepted that [taste] appears only through the rule of application (<s>upanayamaryādā</s>) in the gustatory perception of the property-locus. Because even the extraordinary perception of the qualificand-mode with respect to atomic taste is impossible. Because according to the <s>Naiyāyika</s> doctrine, what is brought by application appears only as a qualifier. In reality, however, since there is no evidence for the rule that taste has only non-pervasive occurrence, and since the production of multiple tastes in a single thing delimited by spatial difference is possible, there is no impossibility in the cognition 'here is taste' through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) being a valid cognition. Having intended all this, it is said '[101] in brief.'

children.text: rasanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Rasa</s> (Taste)

children.text:
nanu [103] rasanagrāhyo guṇo rasa iti lakṣaṇavākye
paramāṇurase 'vyāptiḥ/ rasanagrāhyajātimattvavivakṣāyāmapi
children.translated_text: Now, in the definitional statement '[103] taste is the quality apprehensible by the gustatory organ,' there is non-pervasion with respect to atomic taste. Even if one intends the possession of a universal (<s>jāti</s>) apprehensible by the gustatory organ,

children.text:
sattādikamādāya
rūpādāvativyāptirata āha - [104]
rasanetyādi/ [104] guṇavibhājaketi/ 2guṇatvanyūnavṛttitvaṃ vivakṣitam/
children.translated_text: taking <s>sattā</s> (existence) and the like, there would be over-pervasion with respect to <s>rūpa</s> (color) and the like — therefore he says '[104] by the gustatory organ' and so on. '[104] Distinguishing among qualities' — the intention is: having occurrence no less extensive than <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood).

children.text: sparśanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Sparśa</s> (Touch)

children.text:
nanu tvagindrayamātragrāhya
ityādilakṣaṇe 'sambhavaḥ/ sparśasyatvagitarātmādigrāhyatvāt/ evaṃ
paramāṇusparśe 'vyāptiḥ/ tvagragrāhyatvāt ityata āha - [104] cakṣuragrāhyetyādi/
children.translated_text: Now, in a definition such as 'apprehensible only by the tactile organ,' there is impossibility — since touch is also apprehensible by the self (<s>ātman</s>) and other [faculties] beyond the tactile organ. Similarly, there is non-pervasion with respect to atomic touch, since [atomic touch] is not apprehensible by the tactile organ — therefore he says '[104] not apprehensible by the eye' and so on.

children.text:
1.
sāmānādhikaraṇyeneti/ svāśrayasamavetatvasaṃbandhenetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote] 1. 'Through co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>)' — the meaning is: through the relation of inhering in one's own substratum (<s>svāśrayasamavetatvasaṃbandha</s>).

children.text:
2. nanu
guṇavibhājakatvaṃ guṇatvavyāpyatvam, tacca guṇatvasyāpyakṣatamiti
tadādāya rūpādāvativyāptirityata āha - guṇatvanyūnavṛttitvaṃ
vivakṣitamiti/ guṇatvanyūnavṛttitvaṃ ca guṇatvasamānādhikaraṇatve
sati guṇatvasamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvam/ tacca
guṇatvasya nāstīti bhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: [Footnote] 2. Now, <s>guṇavibhājakatva</s> (being a distinguisher of qualities) is pervaded by <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood), and that is also unimpaired with respect to quality-hood itself — therefore, taking that, there would be over-pervasion with respect to <s>rūpa</s> (color) and the like — hence he says: 'the intention is having occurrence no less extensive than quality-hood.' And having occurrence no less extensive than quality-hood means: being a delimitor of the counter-positive-ness of a difference co-located with quality-hood, while itself being co-located with quality-hood. And that does not exist in quality-hood itself — this is the purport.

children.text:
cakṣuragrāhyatvaṃ ca
cākṣuṣanirūpitalaukikaviṣayatāśūnyatvam/ tvagindriyagrāhyatvaṃ ca
tvācanirūpitalaukikaviṣayatāvattvam/ nātaḥ 1pūrvavaddoṣaḥ/
guṇavibhājakatvaṃ ca vāyupratyakṣatāvādinavīnamate
vāyutvajātimādāya vāyāvativyāptivāraṇāya upāttam/
children.translated_text: 'Not being apprehensible by the eye' means the absence of ordinary object-hood as determined by visual [perception]. 'Being apprehensible by the tactile organ' means possessing ordinary object-hood as determined by the skin organ. Hence there is no defect as before. The [qualification] 'distinguishing among qualities' is employed to prevent over-pervasion with respect to <s>vāyu</s> (air), taking the universal <s>vāyutva</s> (air-ness), according to the new view that admits perceptibility of air.

children.text: pākaprakriyānirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of the <s>Pāka</s> Process (Transformation by Heat)

children.text:
parāvṛttyādītyādinā rūpāntaraparigrahaḥ/
nanu [105] āmanikṣipte ghaṭa iti dīpikāvākye
saptamyantaghaṭapadasyottaratrānvayāsambhavāt asaṅgatirityato
yojanāmāha -- [106] ghaṭe āmanikṣipte satīti/ tathā ca
ghaṭapadottarasaptamyā āmasaṃyogor'thaḥ/ tasya
cottarakālīnatvasaṃbandhena śyāmaghaṭanāśe anvaya iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: By transformation (<s>parāvṛtti</s>)' and so on — [this is] the inclusion of another color. Now, in the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement '[105] in a raw [substance] placed in [fire], the pot,' the locative-ending word 'pot' cannot be construed with what follows, hence there is incongruity — therefore he states the construal: '[106] when the pot is placed in a raw [state].' And thus, the locative case after the word 'pot' has the meaning of contact with the raw [state]. And its connection with the destruction of the dark-colored pot is through the relation of posteriority — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu paramāṇuṣu
rūpotpattau śyāmaghaṭanāśa iti dīpikāvākyāt śyāmaghaṭanāśe
paramāṇuniṣṭharūpotpattyuttarakālīnatvaṃ labhyate/ taccayuktam -
avayavināśānantarameva paramāṇuṣu rūpāntarotpatteḥ vaiśeṣikaiḥ
svīkārāt ato yojanayā anvayamāha -- [106] śyāmaghaṭanāśa ityādi/
jāti iti śeṣaḥ/ tathā ca nāśapadottarasaptamyāḥ utpattirarthaḥ/
tasyāścottarakālīnatvasambandhena rūpāntarotpattāvanvaya iti bhāvaḥ/
[106] svatantreṣviti/ viśakaliteṣvityarthaḥ/
ārambhakasaṃyogarahiteṣviti yāvat/ [106] aparāvayavīti/
pūrvavinaṣṭāvayavivyatiriktāvayavītyarthaḥ/ [106] ata
eveti/ avayavinyapi paramāṇuvat pākāṅgīkārādevetyarthaḥ/ nanu
children.translated_text: Now, from the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'the origination of color in the atoms upon the destruction of the dark-colored pot,' one obtains the posteriority of color-origination in the atoms to the destruction of the dark-colored pot. But that is not correct — since the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> accept that another color originates in the atoms immediately after the destruction of the whole. Therefore, he states the construal through a [different] interpretation: '[106] The destruction of the dark-colored pot' and so on. Supply: 'the universal (<s>jāti</s>).' And thus, the locative case after the word 'destruction' has the meaning of 'origination.' And its connection with the origination of another color is through the relation of posteriority — this is the purport. '[106] Independent' — the meaning is: separated; that is, devoid of the originating conjunction. '[106] Another whole' — the meaning is: a whole different from the previously destroyed whole. '[106] Therefore' — the meaning is: precisely because transformation is accepted even in the whole, just as in the atoms. Now,

children.text:
so 'yaṃ ghaṭa iti
pratyabhijñāsājātyamavalambate/ nirvāpitāropitadīpe seyaṃ
dīpajvāleti pratyabhijñāvat na tvekasyā eva vyakteḥ kāladvayasambandham/
ato na virodha ityato dūṣaṇāntaramāha - [105] anantāvayavītyādi/ nāśādītyādinā
children.translated_text: the recognition 'this is that same pot' is based on similarity [not identity]. Just as the recognition 'this is that same flame of the lamp' regarding an extinguished and re-lit lamp — it does not [require] the relation of a single individual to two times. Hence there is no contradiction — therefore he states another objection: '[105] having infinite parts' and so on. With 'from destruction' and so on,

children.text:
prāgabhāvaparigrahaḥ/
[107] vāraṇasambhavāditi/
vaijātyasyāvayavarūpājanyāvayavirūpavyāvṛttatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [there is] the inclusion of prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>). '[107] Because prevention is possible' — the purport is: because dissimilarity has the nature of being excluded from the color of a whole that is not produced from the color of its parts.

children.text:
1. pūrvavaddoṣa iti/
cākṣuṣe upanayamaryādayā sparśatvasya, tvāce
gurutvasyopanayamaryādayā bhāne 'pi nāsambhavaḥ ativyāptirvetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote] 1. 'The defect as before' — the meaning is: even though touch-hood (<s>sparśatva</s>) appears through the rule of application in visual [perception], and heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) appears through the rule of application in tactile [perception], there is neither impossibility nor over-pervasion.

children.text:
yathāyogyamiti/ tathā ca
rūpādicatuṣṭayapadaṃ tādṛśacatuṣṭayānyatamaparamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: As appropriate' — and thus, the word 'the four such as <s>rūpa</s> (color)' means any one of such a fourfold [set] — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu udbhūtatvasya
jātirūpatāyā indriyalakṣaṇāvasare nirastatvāt atra ca
jātirūpatvokteḥ pūrvottaragranthavirodha ityāśaṅkya
matabhedanobhayagranthasaṅgatiriti tasya jātirūpatvamevetyāha - [107] udbhūtatvaṃ jātirityādinā/ guṇagateti/ guṇaghaṭitetyarthaḥ/
[107] na doṣaḥ - na pūrvotataragranthavirodha ityarthaḥ/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ -
sāṅkaryasya jātibādhakatāyāṃ pramāṇabhūte dharmaśāstre
dravyagatasāṃkaryasyaiva jātibādhakatvokteḥ/
svādhikaraṇadravyavṛttitvasvābhāvādhikaraṇadravyavṛttitvasvādhikaraṇadravyavṛttyabhāvapratiyogitvatritayasaṃbandhena
jātiviśiṣṭatvarūpadravayaghaṭitajātisāṅkaryasyaiva
jātitvābhāvavyāpyatāyā upagamena jātibādhakatvaṃ svīkriyate/ na tu
guṇādisādhāraṇasvādhikaraṇaghaṭitajātisāṅkaryasyeti/
children.translated_text: Now, since the universal-nature of <s>udbhūtatva</s> (manifestness) was rejected in the context of the definition of the sense-organs, and here its universal-nature is asserted, there would be a contradiction between the earlier and later portions of the text — anticipating this [objection], since through a difference of viewpoints both portions are consistent, he says that its universal-nature is indeed [maintained]: '[107] <s>Udbhūtatva</s> is a <s>jāti</s> (universal)' and so on. 'Pertaining to quality' — the meaning is: constituted by quality. '[107] There is no defect' — the meaning is: there is no contradiction between the earlier and later portions of the text. The purport is as follows: regarding the capacity of admixture (<s>sāṅkarya</s>) to block universal-hood, since in the authoritative <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> it is stated that only admixture pertaining to substance blocks universal-hood — since it is accepted that only the substance-constituted <s>jāti</s>-admixture in the form of being qualified by a universal through the threefold relation of occurring in the substance that is one's own substratum, occurring in the substance that is the substratum of one's own absence, and being the counter-positive of the absence of occurrence in the substance that is one's own substratum, is pervaded by the absence of universal-hood — but not the <s>jāti</s>-admixture constituted by one's own substratum that is common to quality and the like.

children.text:
vastutastu
prāguktasambandhena dravyatvavyāpyajātiviśiṣṭatvameva
jātitvābhāvavyāpyamityupagamāt guṇatvavyāpyajātivaiśiṣṭyasya
cātathābhūtasya na jātibādhakatvamiti dhyeyam/
jātisāṅkaryasāmānyasyaiva jātibādhakatvamabhyupetya
prakṛtagranthamupapādayatāṃ matamāha - kecittviti/
āhurityanenāsvarasaḥ sūcitaḥ/ tadbījantūdbhūtatvasya
tattadanudbhūtatvābhāvakūṭarūpatve tasya gaganādisaṃyogasādhāraṇatayā
gaganādipratyakṣabhiyāpratyakṣaprayojakatvāsambhavāt udbhūtatvaṃ
pratyakṣaprayojakamitidīpikāgranthāsaṅgatiriti/
children.translated_text: In reality, however, since it is accepted that only being qualified by a universal pervaded by <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood) through the aforementioned relation is what is pervaded by the absence of universal-hood, the qualification by a universal pervaded by <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood), not being of that nature, does not block universal-hood — this should be noted. He states the view of those who justify the present text by accepting that <s>jāti</s>-admixture in general itself blocks universal-hood — with 'some, however.' The [expression] 'they say' indicates disagreement. But the seed [of the problem] is this: if <s>udbhūtatva</s> (manifestness) had the nature of an aggregate of absences of respective non-manifestnesses, then since it would be common to conjunction with the sky and the like, there would be an impossibility of its being the cause of perceptibility and the cause of the perception of sky and the like — and thus the <s>Dīpikā</s> text would be incongruent.

children.text: parimāṇanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Parimāṇa</s> (Magnitude)

children.text:
bhāvapradhāna iti/ bhāvaḥ pradhānaṃ
mukhyaviśeṣyaḥ yasminniti vyutpattyā dharmaniṣṭhamukhyatānirūpakatvaṃ
bhāvapradhānatvam, nirūpakatvaṃ ca jñānadvārakam, evaṃ
cāṇumahadādiśabdaḥ saṅgrahavākyasthaḥ aṇutvamahatvādikaṃ lakṣaṇayā
bodhayatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Having a real entity as principal' — through the derivation 'that in which a real entity (<s>bhāva</s>) is the principal, i.e., the chief qualificand,' <s>bhāvapradhānatva</s> (having a real entity as principal) means being the determiner of principality residing in a property; and the determination is through cognition. Thus, the words '<s>aṇu</s>' (atomic), '<s>mahat</s>' (great), etc. occurring in the compendium statement convey <s>aṇutva</s> (atomicity), <s>mahattva</s> (greatness), etc. through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — this is the purport.

children.text: saṃyoganirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Saṃyoga</s> (Conjunction)

children.text:
sādhāraṇakāraṇatvena -
kāryatvāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvena/ nanu
svātyantābhāvasamānādhikaraṇatvamavyāpyavṛttitvamiti dīpikāvākye
svapadasya yatrāvyāpyavṛttitvaṃ sthāpyam tadvyaktiparatāyā
āvaśyakatayā saṃyogādivyaktīnāmānantyāt
ekavyaktyupādāne 'paravyaktyasaṃgrahaḥ/ svātyantābhāvasamānādhikaraṇaṃ
yadyatsvaṃ tāvadanyatamatvaṃ tu sarvajñenaiva jñeyam, mahāgauravaṃ, ca ato
niṣkṛṣṭārthamāha -- [110] svapratiyogitvetyādi/ yadyapi
svātyantābhāvasamānādhikaraṇatvatādātmyobhayasaṃbandhena
prameyaviśiṣṭatvamanugatam, tathāpi
tādātmyādirūpādhikapadārthaniveśāt gauravamiti tadupekṣitam/
athātra
saṃyogādisambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāka-ghaṭatvādyabhāvādyadhikaraṇe
samavāyādinā ghaṭatvādessattvāt tatrātivyāptiḥ/ na ca
tatsambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatadabhāvādhikaraṇe
tatsambandhenādheyatvasya vivakṣayā na doṣa iti vācyam/
yattvatattvānanugamena lakṣaṇasya tattadvyaktiviśramāpātāt/
children.translated_text: As a common cause' — as a cause through cause-hood delimited by effect-hood. Now, in the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'being co-located with one's own absolute absence is <s>avyāpyavṛttitva</s> (non-pervasive occurrence),' since the word 'one's own' (<s>sva</s>), where non-pervasive occurrence is to be established, necessarily refers to a particular instance, and since the instances of conjunction and the like are infinite, if one particular instance is taken, the other instances are not included. And [the formulation] 'whatever is one's own that is co-located with one's own absolute absence' — [to determine] that particular 'one's own' can only be known by an omniscient being, and there is great complexity. Therefore he states the refined meaning: '[110] having one's own counter-positive-hood' and so on. Although [the property] 'being qualified by what is knowable through the identity relation in which there is co-location with one's own absolute absence' is common [to all cases], nevertheless, because it involves additional terms such as the identity relation and the like, there is complexity, and hence that [formulation] is set aside. Now, here, since <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-hood) and the like exist through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) and the like in a locus that is the substratum of the absence of <s>ghaṭatva</s> (pot-hood) and the like — whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by conjunction-and-other relations — there is over-pervasion there. Nor should one say that there is no defect because the intention is that the property of being contained through that relation in the substratum of the absence of that whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by that relation [resolves the issue] — because that [formulation] would not be common [to all cases], the definition would rest on particular instances only.

children.text:
na cābhāvaviśiṣṭatvaṃ
tat, vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca svapratiyogitvasvaviśiṣṭādheyatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
ādheyatāyāṃ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svapratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvasvādhikaraṇanirūpitatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
ato nānanugama iti vācyam, evamapi
saṃyogādisambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākaghaṭatvādyabhāvasyāvyāpyavṛttitāprasaṅgāt/
svasya saṃyogādinā yo 'bhāvaḥ tadīyapūrvakṣaṇādivṛttitvaviśiṣṭa
svābhāvaniṣṭhapratiyogitāvacchedakasvarūpasaṃbandhena paṭādau
tatsattvāt/
children.translated_text: Nor is that [avyāpyavṛttitva] being qualified by an absence, the qualification being through the twofold relation of one's own counter-positive-hood and one's own qualified-containedness. And in the containedness, one's own qualification is through the twofold relation of being delimited by the relation that is the delimitor of one's own counter-positive-hood and being determined by one's own substratum. Hence there is no lack of commonality — but this cannot be said, because even so, the absence of <s>ghaṭatva</s> (pot-hood) and the like — whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by conjunction-and-other relations — would have non-pervasive occurrence. Since there exists, in cloth and the like, [a relation] through the identity relation of the counter-positive-ness of the absence of one's own absence — which is qualified by occurrence at a prior moment and the like — residing in one's own self that is [related] through conjunction and the like.

children.text:
na ca svasmin
svābhāvīyaṃ yatpratiyogitvaṃ tadavacchedakasaṃbandhena
svābhāvādhikaraṇavṛttitvaniveśāt nāyaṃ doṣaḥ iti vācyam/
yattvatattvānanugamasya durvāratvāt/
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that there is no defect because the condition includes the occurrence of the absence's substratum through the relation that delimits one's own counter-positive-hood with respect to what is the counter-positive-hood in one's own self — because the lack of commonality of that [formulation] to all cases is unavoidable.

children.text:
na ca
adhikaraṇatāviśiṣṭatvaṃ tat, vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāśrayāśrayatvasvaviśiṣṭādheyatvobhayasaṃbandhena/ ādheyatāyāṃ
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svanirūpakābhāvādhikaraṇanirūpitatvasvāśrayāvacchedakasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
adhikaraṇatā ca
children.translated_text: Nor is that [avyāpyavṛttitva] being qualified by substratum-hood, the qualification being through the twofold relation of being-the-substratum-of-one's-own-substratum and one's own qualified-containedness. And in the containedness, one's own qualification is through the twofold relation of being determined by the substratum of the absence that is one's own determiner and being delimited by the relation that delimits one's own substratum. And the substratum-hood

children.text:
svanirūpitapratiyogitātvasambandhāvacchinnā/ ato na ko 'pi
doṣaḥ/ yadvā pratiyogitāviśiṣṭatvaṃ tat, vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāśrayatvasvaviśiṣṭādheyatvobhayasaṃbandhena/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvasvanirūpakābhāvādhikaraṇanirūpitatvobhayasambandheneti
vācyam/
children.translated_text: is delimited by the relation of being the counter-positive-hood-ness determined by one's own self. Hence there is no defect whatsoever. Alternatively, that [avyāpyavṛttitva] is being qualified by counter-positive-hood, the qualification being through the twofold relation of being-one's-own-substratum and one's own qualified-containedness. And one's own qualification is through the twofold relation of being delimited by the relation that delimits one's own [counter-positive-hood] and being determined by the substratum of the absence that is one's own determiner — thus it should be stated.

children.text:
evamapi
dravyānyatvaviśiṣṭasattābhāvādāvativyāpteḥ/
tadabhāvarūpaviśiṣṭasattāyāḥ śuddhasattānatiriktatayā tadadhikaraṇe
ghaṭādau tatsattvāt/ na cābhāvatvaviśiṣṭatvaṃ adhikaraṇatāviśiṣṭatvaṃ
vā tat/ prathame vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svanirūpitapratiyogitvasvaviśiṣṭādheyatvobhayasambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchinnādhikaraṇanirūpitatvasvanirūpitapratiyogitāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvobhayasambandhena/
dvitīye adhikaraṇatā svanirūpitapratiyogitātvasambandhena/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
ca svāśrayāśrayatvasvaviśiṣṭādheyatvobhayasambandhena/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svanirūpakābhāvatvāvacchinnādhikaraṇanirūpitatvasvāśrayāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvobhayasambandhena/
ato na doṣaḥ/ atra dravyānyatvaviśiṣṭasattābhāvo nāstītyapratyayāt
guṇādau tādṛśasattābhāvābhāvatvena vṛttyanupagamāditi vācyam/
evamapyabhāvatvasyānugatākhaṇḍopādhirūpatāyā anyatra vyavasthāpitatvena
tasya sarvatrābhinnatayā taddoṣatādavasthyāt/
children.translated_text: Even so, there is over-pervasion with respect to the absence of <s>sattā</s> (existence) qualified by otherness-from-substance and the like. Because the <s>sattā</s> qualified by the absence of that — [i.e.] pure <s>sattā</s> — being non-different [from sattā simpliciter], exists in its substratum, namely pot and the like. Nor is that [avyāpyavṛttitva] being qualified by absence-hood, or being qualified by substratum-hood. In the first case, the qualification is through the twofold relation of the counter-positive-hood determined by one's own self and one's own qualified-containedness. And one's own qualification is through the twofold relation of being determined by the substratum delimited by one's own self and being delimited by the relation that delimits the counter-positive-hood determined by one's own self. In the second case, the substratum-hood is through the relation of counter-positive-hood-ness determined by one's own self. The qualification is through the twofold relation of being-the-substratum-of-one's-own-substratum and one's own qualified-containedness. And one's own qualification is through the twofold relation of being determined by the substratum delimited by absence-hood that is one's own determiner and being delimited by the relation that delimits one's own substratum. Hence there is no defect. Here, from the cognition 'the absence of <s>sattā</s> qualified by otherness-from-substance does not exist,' since in quality and the like the absence of such <s>sattā</s>-absence is admitted as having occurrence [there], [the over-pervasion is avoided] — but this cannot be said, because even so, since <s>abhāvatva</s> (absence-hood) has the nature of a common undivided superimposed property established elsewhere, it being the same everywhere, the defect remains as before.

children.text:
atrocyate -
adhikaraṇatāviśiṣṭatvamavyāpyavṛttitvam/ adhikaraṇatā ca
svaviśiṣṭapratiyogitātvasambandhena/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaviśiṣṭābhāvanirūpitatvasvanirūpita -
kiñciddharmāvacchinnaprakāratānirūpitasaṃsargatvobhayasambandhena/ abhāve
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca svāśrayatva1svasetyādibhedavattvobhayasambandhena/
svādhikaraṇatā ca svāvacchedakatāsambandhena/
children.translated_text: Here it is stated: Non-pervasive occurrence (<s>avyāpyavṛttitva</s>) is the property of being qualified by <s>adhikaraṇatā</s> (substratum-hood). And <s>adhikaraṇatā</s> is [connected] by the relation of counter-positive-hood qualified by itself. And the self-qualification is by the dual relation of: being determined by an absence qualified by itself, and being a contact determined by a mode delimited by some property that is determined by itself. In the case of absence, the self-qualification is by the dual relation of: self-substratum-hood, and possessing difference [of the type] 'belonging to itself and so forth.' And its self-substratum-hood is by the relation of self-delimitor-hood.

children.text:
1.
svasetyādibhedavattveti/
svādhikaraṇavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 1:] 'Possessing difference belonging to itself and so forth' means: possessing difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the relation of being the delimitor of the counter-positive-hood of difference occurring in one's own substratum, and whose delimitor-hood is self-residing.

children.text:
bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā ca ādheyatāsambandhena/
adhikaraṇatāviśiṣṭatvaṃ
svāśrayāśrayatvasvaviśiṣṭādheyatvobhayasambandhena/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāśrayāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvaviśiṣṭādhikaraṇanirūpitatvībhayasambandhena/
adhikaraṇe svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca svasetyādibhedavattvasambandhena/
svādhikaraṇatvaṃ ca svanirūpakaviṣayatāvacchedakatāsambandhena/
bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā
svarūpasambandhāvacchinnādheyatāvacchedakatāsambandhena/ yadyapi
kālikasambandhena ghaṭatvābhāvādiviśiṣṭasya dhvaṃsasya ghaṭādau
sambhavāt atiprasaṅgaḥ, tathāpi svaviśiṣṭādhikaraṇanirūpitatvasthāne
svaviśiṣṭādhikaraṇatāvannirūpitatvaṃ niveśyam/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedanirūpitatvasvasetyādibhedavattvobhayasambandhena/
bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā svaviśiṣṭāvacchedakatāsambandhena/
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāśrayanirūpitasvarūpasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvanirūpitatvasvanirūpakaviṣayatāvacchedakatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvobhayasambandhena/
children.translated_text: And the delimitor-hood of counter-positive-hood of difference is by the relation of superimposed-ness (<s>ādheyatā</s>). The property of being qualified by <s>adhikaraṇatā</s> is by the dual relation of: being the substratum of one's own substratum, and being the superimposed-ness qualified by oneself. And the self-qualification is by the dual relation of: being delimited by the relation of one's own substratum-delimitor, and being determined by a qualified substratum. And the self-qualification in the substratum is by the relation of possessing difference 'belonging to itself and so forth.' And self-substratum-hood is by the relation of delimitor-hood of the content-hood of one's own determiner. And the delimitor-hood of counter-positive-hood of difference is by the relation of delimitor-hood of superimposed-ness delimited by the self-nature relation. Although there is over-extension because destruction qualified by the absence of pot-hood and so forth is possible in a pot by temporal relation, nevertheless, in place of 'being determined by a qualified substratum,' 'being determined by something possessing the qualified substratum-hood' should be inserted. And the self-qualification is by the dual relation of: being determined by the difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by itself, and possessing difference 'belonging to itself and so forth.' The delimitor-hood of counter-positive-hood of difference is by the relation of delimitor-hood qualified by itself. And the qualification is by the dual relation of: being delimited by the relation of delimitor-hood of the delimitor of content-hood of one's own determiner, and being determined by the superimposed-ness delimited by the self-nature relation determined by one's own substratum.

children.text:
vastutastu
1pratiyogitāviśiṣṭatvamavyāpyavṛttitvam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāśrayatvasvaviśiṣṭādheyatvobhayasambandhena/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvasvāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnatvasvanirūpakābhāvādhikaraṇanirūpitatvatritayasambandhena/
2tena viśiṣṭasattvasya nāvyāpyavṛttitvamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: But in reality, non-pervasive occurrence (<s>avyāpyavṛttitva</s>) is the property of being qualified by counter-positive-hood (<s>pratiyogitā</s>). And the qualification is by the dual relation of: self-substratum-hood and superimposed-ness qualified by oneself. And the self-qualification is by the triple relation of: being delimited by the relation of one's own delimitor, being delimited by the property that is one's own delimitor, and being determined by the substratum of the absence that is the determiner of oneself. It should be noted that thereby qualified existence (<s>viśiṣṭasattva</s>) does not have non-pervasive occurrence.

children.text:
1.
pratiyogitāviśiṣṭatvamityādi/ pratiyogitā kapisaṃyoganiṣṭhā
tadviśiṣṭatvaṃ kapisaṃyoge svāśrayatvasaṃbandhenāsti, kapisaṃyogasya
pratiyogitāśrayatvāt/ evaṃ
pratiyogitāvacchedakasamavāyasaṃbandhāvacchinnā
pratiyogitāvacchedakakapisaṃyogatvāvacchinnā
pratiyogitānirūpakakapisaṃyogābhāvādhikaraṇavṛkṣanirūpitā ca
kapisaṃyoganiṣṭhādheyatā bhavati iti tritayasaṃbandhena
pratiyogitāviśiṣṭamādheyatvaṃ ca kapisaṃyoge 'stīti
kapisaṃyogasyāvyāpyavṛttitvam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 1:] 'The property of being qualified by counter-positive-hood' and so forth: The counter-positive-hood resides in monkey-conjunction; the qualification by that exists in monkey-conjunction by the relation of self-substratum-hood, since monkey-conjunction is the substratum of counter-positive-hood. Similarly, there is superimposed-ness residing in monkey-conjunction that is: delimited by the relation of inherence which is the delimitor of counter-positive-hood, delimited by monkey-conjunction-hood which is the delimitor of counter-positive-hood, and determined by the tree which is the substratum of the absence of monkey-conjunction that is the determiner of counter-positive-hood. Thus by the triple relation, superimposed-ness qualified by counter-positive-hood exists in monkey-conjunction — hence monkey-conjunction has non-pervasive occurrence.

children.text:
2. tena
viśiṣṭasattvasyeti/ viśiṣṭasattāniṣṭhāyāḥ
viśiṣṭasattāniṣṭhapratiyogitānirūpakābhāvādhikaraṇaguṇanirūpitādheyatāyāḥ
pratiyogitāvacchedakaviśiṣṭasattātvāvacchinnatvavirahāt
uktatritayasambandhena pratiyogitāviśiṣṭatvābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: [Footnote 2:] 'Thereby, qualified existence' and so forth: Since the superimposed-ness residing in qualified existence that is determined by the substratum of the absence that determines qualified existence lacks being delimited by qualified-existence-hood which is the delimitor of counter-positive-hood, due to the absence of the property of being qualified by counter-positive-hood by the stated triple relation — this is the purport.

children.text: vibhāganirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of separation (<s>vibhāga</s>)
Passage 111:

children.text:
kecidityasvarasassūcitaḥ/ tadbījantu
janyamātrasya kālatvapakṣe janyarūpādāvativyāptiriti/ pare tvityādi/
atra cāvacchinnāntena janyatāviśeṣaṇena ghaṭitamekaṃ lakṣaṇam/
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvena kāraṇatāviśeṣaṇena ghaṭitamaparaṃ
lakṣaṇam iti vivekaḥ/ anyathā ekatra lakṣaṇe ubhayaniveśane
prayojanābhāvāt/ tattaddhvaṃsavyaktitvāvacchinnaṃ prati tādātmyena
tattatpratiyogivyakteḥ kāraṇatayaiva saṃyogā - [dya] (di)tivyāptivāraṇāditi bodhyam/
children.translated_text: The word 'some' indicates lack of consensus. The basis of that is: in the view that only what is produced is temporal, there is over-extension to produced color and such. 'Others, however' and so forth. And here the distinction is: one definition is constructed with the qualifier of produced-ness ending in 'delimited'; the other definition is constructed with the qualifier of causality ending in 'by the relation of inherence.' Otherwise, if both were introduced in a single definition, there would be no purpose. It should be understood that with respect to the individual instances delimited by the respective destruction-instance-hood, the instance of the respective counter-positive, by identity-relation, serves precisely as a cause — and thereby deviation from conjunction and so forth is blocked.

children.text:
nanu kāryasāmānyaṃ
prati tādātmyena hetubhūte kālādau ativyāptivirahāt
guṇapadavaiyarthyamityāśaṅkāṃ tasya
darśitārthatātparyagrāhakatvopagamena pariharati - [111] etattātparyeti/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since there is no over-extension in time and such, which are causes by identity-relation of effect-in-general, the word 'quality' is purposeless. Anticipating this doubt, he resolves it by accepting that [the word] serves as an indicator of the stated purport — [passage 111] 'this is the purport.'

children.text: paratvāparatvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of priority and posteriority (<s>paratva</s> and <s>aparatva</s>)

children.text:
nanu
parāparavyavahārāsādhāraṇakāraṇe paratvāparatve iti
saṅgrahavākyāt ubhayavyavahārāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvamubhayalakṣaṇamiti
labhyate/ taccāsambhavi, paratvādeḥ
pratyekamaparavyavahārādyasādhāraṇakāraṇatvavirahāt, ato vyācaṣṭe -
[112] dīpikāyāṃ paravyavahāretyādi/ asamavāyikāraṇatvamātrasya
gurutvalakṣaṇatve tantudvayasaṃyogādāvativyāptiḥ/ patanakāraṇatvasya
tathātve 'pi āśrayatayā patanasamavāyikāraṇe phalādāvativyāptiḥ
sphuṭaivetyālocyādyapadasya kṛtyamāha - [113] dvitīyādīti/
nanvādyatvamihādau bhavamiti vyutpattyā pūrvakālotpannatvaṃ, tacca
dvitīyādipatanasyāpi tṛtīyādipatanapūrvakālotpannatayā akṣatamiti
kathaṃ tadvāraṇasambhava ityata ādyatvamanyādṛśaṃ nirvakti - [111] prakāśikāyām ādyatvamiheti/ svasamānādhikaraṇetyādi/ athātra
svapadamanuyogiparam vā pratiyogiparam vā/ nādyaḥ,
ādyapatanavyaktīnāmānantyāt/ tenaikopādāne itarāsaṅgrahāt/
svasamānādhikaraṇapatanapratiyogikadhvaṃsāsamānakālīnaṃ yadyatsvaṃ
tāvadanyatamattvaṃ tu asarvajñadurjñeyam/ anyatamattvaghaṭakabhedānāṃ mitho
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāve vinigamanāvirahaśca/ nāpyuttaraḥ,
tādṛśayatkiñcidekapatanavyaktibhedasya dvitīyādipatanasādhāraṇatvāt/
tādṛśaṃ yadyatsvaṃ tattadvyaktitvāvacchinnabhedakūṭavattvasya
tāvadanyatamatvāvacchinnabhedavattvasya vā prāguktadoṣadūṣitatvāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: From the compendium statement 'priority and posteriority are the uncommon causes of the usages of prior and posterior,' the definition of both is obtained as being the uncommon cause of both usages. But that is impossible, since priority lacks being the uncommon cause of the usage of posteriority and so forth. Therefore he explains — [passage 112] 'In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, the usage of prior' and so forth. If mere non-inherent causality were the definition of heaviness, there would be over-extension to the conjunction of two threads and so forth. Even if causality of falling were [the definition], there would be clear over-extension to fruit and such which are the inherent cause of falling as a substratum. Considering this, he states the function of the word 'first' — [passage 113] 'the second and so forth.' Objection: First-ness here means being produced at a prior time, as derived from 'occurring in the first [moment],' and since the second and subsequent fallings too are produced prior to the third and subsequent fallings, that [prior-time-production] is unimpaired — so how is its exclusion possible? Therefore he explains first-ness differently — [passage 111] 'In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, first-ness here.' 'Co-located with itself' and so forth. Now, does the word 'self' here refer to the relatum or to the counter-positive? Not the first, because the instances of first falling are infinite; hence if one is selected, the others would not be included. Self-co-located-falling-counter-positive-destruction-not-contemporaneous: whatever is self in this way, that any-one-ness is unknowable by the non-omniscient. And among the differences constituting any-one-ness, there is absence of a deciding reason for their qualifier-qualificand relation. Nor the second, because the difference from any single instance of falling of that type is common to the second and subsequent fallings. And the possession of the aggregate of differences delimited by that-type-instance-hood, or the possession of difference delimited by that-type-any-one-ness, is vitiated by the previously stated fault.

children.text:
atrocyate -
1tādātmyasvasamānādhikaraṇapatanapratiyogikadhvaṃsasamānakālīnatvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacche-
children.translated_text: Here it is stated: By the dual relation of identity and possessing difference whose counter-positive-hood has delimitor-hood residing in itself, delimited by the relation of contemporaneity with the destruction whose counter-positive is a falling co-located with itself —

children.text:
dakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvobhayasambandhena
patanaviśiṣṭatvamādyatvamiti anuyogini svatvāntarbhāve
sthūlānugamaḥ/
2svasamānādhikaraṇapatanadhvaṃsasamānakālīnatvasambandhāvacchinnasvapratiyogitāvacchedakatvāśrayatvobhayasaṃbandhenabhedaviśiṣṭatvamiti
sūkṣmānugamaḥ/ 3pratiyogini svatvādare tu
svasamānādhikaraṇapatanadhvaṃsasamānakālikatvavādātmyobhayasaṃbandhena
patanaviśiṣṭānyatvamiti sthūlānugamaḥ/
4svasamānakālīkatvasvasamānādhikaraṇapatanapratiyogikatvasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvobhayasambandhena
children.translated_text: the property of being qualified by falling is first-ness — when self-hood is included in the relatum, this is the rough analysis. The property of being qualified by difference, by the dual relation of: being the substratum of the delimitor of one's own counter-positive-hood, delimited by the relation of contemporaneity with the destruction of the falling co-located with oneself, and [the delimitor of] one's own counter-positive-hood — this is the fine analysis. When self-hood is taken in the counter-positive, the rough analysis is: otherness qualified by falling, by the dual relation of: contemporaneity with the falling co-located with oneself, and identity. By the dual relation of: superimposed-ness delimited by the relation of counter-positive-hood of the falling co-located with oneself, and contemporaneity with oneself —

children.text:
1. tādātmyetyādi svaṃ
prathamapatanaṃ tatsamānādhikaraṇam yat dvitīyapatanaṃ
taddhvaṃsasamānakālikatvaṃ prathamapatane nāstīti
tādṛśasamānanakālikatvasambandhena svavadbhinnatvasya svatādātmyasya ca
prathamapatane sattvāt tasya ādyatvopapattiḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 1:] 'By identity' and so forth: Self is the first falling; what is co-located with it is the second falling; contemporaneity with the destruction of that [second falling] does not exist in the first falling. Thus, since by the relation of such contemporaneity, the difference from what possesses self and the identity with self both exist in the first falling, its first-ness is explained.

children.text:
2.
svasamānādhikaraṇetyādi/ prathamasvaśabdaḥ ādyapatanaparaḥ/ dvitīyasvaśabdaḥ
ādyapatanavadbhedaparaḥ/ ādyapatanasamānādhikaraṇaṃ yat dvitīyapatanaṃ
tatpratiyogikadhvaṃsasamānakālikatvasambandhena yaḥ ādyapatanavadbhedaḥ
tadāśrayatvaṃ tatpratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ cādyapatane 'stīti samanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 2:] 'Co-located with itself' and so forth: The first occurrence of the word 'self' refers to the first falling. The second occurrence of the word 'self' refers to the difference from what possesses the first falling. The correlation is: the second falling is co-located with the first falling; by the relation of contemporaneity with the destruction whose counter-positive is that [second falling], the difference from what possesses the first falling — its substratum-hood and its counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood exist in the first falling.

children.text:
3. pratiyoginītyādi/
svaṃ dvitīyapatanaṃ tatsamānādhikaraṇaṃ yat prathamapatanaṃ
taddhvaṃsasamānakālikatvaṃ tādātmyaṃ ca dvitīyapatane 'stīti
uktobhayasambandhena dvitīyapatanaviśiṣṭaṃ tadeva, tadanyatvaṃ
prathamapatane 'stīti samanvayo bodhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 3:] 'In the counter-positive' and so forth: Self is the second falling; what is co-located with it is the first falling; contemporaneity with the destruction of that [first falling] and identity both exist in the second falling. Thus by the stated dual relation, what is qualified by the second falling is that itself; the otherness from that exists in the first falling — this correlation should be understood.

children.text:
4.
svasamānakālikatvetyādi/ dhvaṃsapadena prathamapatanadhvaṃso grāhyaḥ/
tadviśiṣṭatvaṃ dvitīyapatane tadanyatvaṃ prathamapatana iti samanvayo
vācyaḥ/ tathāhi - prathamasvapadaṃ prathamapatanadhvaṃsaparam/
tādṛśadhvaṃsasamānakālikatvaṃ dvitīyapatane 'sita/ dvitīyasvapadaṃ
dvitīyapatanaparam/ dvitīyapatanaṃ hi
svasamānādhikaraṇapatanapratiyogikatvasambandhena prathamapatanadhvaṃse 'sti
iti dvitīyapatananiṣṭhā prathamapatanadhvaṃsanirūpitā ādheyatā
svasamānādhikaraṇapatanapratiyogikatvasambandhāvacchinnā bhavati/ tathā ca
