children.translated_text: [Footnote 4:] 'Contemporaneity with self' and so forth: By the word 'destruction,' the destruction of the first falling is to be understood. The qualification by that exists in the second falling; the otherness from that exists in the first falling — this correlation is to be stated. Namely: the first occurrence of the word 'self' refers to the destruction of the first falling. Such contemporaneity with that destruction exists in the second falling. The second occurrence of the word 'self' refers to the second falling. For the second falling exists in the destruction of the first falling by the relation of counter-positive-hood of the falling co-located with itself. Thus the superimposed-ness residing in the second falling that is determined by the destruction of the first falling is delimited by the relation of counter-positive-hood of the falling co-located with itself. And accordingly,

children.text:
tādṛśādheyatāsambandhena prathamapatanadhvaṃsaviśiṣṭaṃ dvitīyapatanaṃ
tadanyatvamādyapatane iti bodhyam/
children.translated_text: by the relation of such superimposed-ness, the second falling is qualified by the destruction of the first falling; the otherness from that is in the first falling — this should be understood.

children.text:
dhvaṃsaviśiṣṭānyatvamiti sūkṣmānugamaḥ/ tādṛśādheyatvasthāne
1svapratiyogipatanasamānādhikaraṇatvaṃ vā niveśyamiti na ko 'pi
doṣaḥ/ evamanyatrāpi/ yadyapi vṛkṣāt saudhe patitasya phalādeḥ
saudhātpatanadaśāyāṃ tatra niruktamādyatvamasambhavi/ tathāpi tatra
saudhāvadhikapatanaṃ tādṛśaphalādigatam na tāvat sāmānyata ādyam,
parantu saudhāvadhikapataneṣu prāthamikapatanasyādyatvaṃ sambhavati/ tacca
svasamānādhikaraṇasaudhāvadhikapatanadhvaṃsamānakālīnatvādirūpamityavadhiviśeṣaghaṭitamādyatvaṃ
vācyam/ evaṃ ca vṛkṣāvadhikapatanasya
svasamānādhikaraṇavṛkṣāvadhikapatanaprāgabhāvāsamānākālīnatvādirūpaṃ
avadhiviśeṣaghaṭitameva caramatvaṃ nirvācyam/
prakāśikoktamavadhiviśeṣāghaṭitamādyatvantu
sambhavasthalābhiproyaṇetyavadheyam/
children.translated_text: Otherness qualified by destruction — this is the fine analysis. In place of such superimposed-ness, the property of being co-located with the falling that is the counter-positive of oneself may also be inserted — there is no fault whatsoever. Similarly elsewhere. Although for a fruit that has fallen from a tree onto a terrace, in the state of falling from the terrace, the stated first-ness is impossible there, nevertheless the falling measured from the terrace belonging to such fruit and so forth is not first in general; rather, among fallings measured from the terrace, the first-ness of the initial falling is possible. And that has the form of contemporaneity with the destruction of the falling-measured-from-terrace co-located with itself — thus first-ness constructed with the specific limit-point (<s>avadhi</s>) is to be stated. And accordingly, the last-ness of the falling measured from the tree is to be explained as having the form of not being contemporaneous with the prior absence of the falling-measured-from-tree co-located with itself — thus constructed with the specific limit-point. The first-ness stated in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, not constructed with a specific limit-point, should be understood as intended for the case where [simple first-ness] is possible.

children.text: śabdanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of sound (<s>śabda</s>)

children.text:
dīpikāyām [113] guṇapadamiti/ na caivamadṛṣṭavāraṇāya
piṇḍībhāvāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvasya vivakṣaṇīyatayā guṇapadamiti
vyarthamiti vācyam/ asamavāyikāraṇabhūtacūrṇādivāraṇāya
tadāvaśyakatvāt/ prakāśikāyām [113] piṇḍībhāvassaṃyogaviśeṣa iti/ dhāraṇakarṣaṇādiyogya
ityarthaḥ/ śabdamātre ākāśasya samavāyikāraṇatāyāḥ spaṣṭatvādāha -
[113] ādye asamavāyikāraṇamityādi/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [passage 113] 'the word quality.' And one should not say that the word 'quality' is purposeless since, for blocking <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), the uncommon causality of compaction (<s>piṇḍībhāva</s>) needs to be specified — because [the word 'quality'] is necessary for blocking powder and such which are non-inherent causes. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [passage 113] 'compaction is a special conjunction' — the meaning is: fit for holding, pulling, and so forth. Since the inherent causality of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) for sound in general is obvious, he says — [passage 113] 'in the first case, the non-inherent cause' and so forth.

children.text: buddhinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of cognition (<s>buddhi</s>)

children.text:
nanu [114] sarvavyavahāraheturjñānaṃ buddhiriti saṃgrahavākye
sarvavyavahārahetutvaṃ buddhilakṣaṇaṃ phalitam/ tacca na ghaṭate/
śukādyuccaritavyavahārahetutvasya buddhāvabhāvāt/
bubodhayiṣādhīnavyavahāraṃ prati hetutvoktyā vyabhicāravirahe 'pi
yena jñānena pratibandhakavaśāt vyavahāro na janitaḥ tasya
vyavahāropadhāyakatvābhāvāt tatrāvyāptiḥ/
svarūpayogyatārūpahetutvasya niveśe 'pi ghaṭādijñāneṣu
paṭādivyavahārahetutvābhāvāt naikajñānasya
sarvavyavahārahetutvamityata āha - [114] jñānatvamātraṃ lakṣaṇamiti/
nanu tarhiṃ saṅgrahe sarvavyavahāraheturiti
children.translated_text: Now, in the compendium statement 'cognition, which is the cause of all practical activity, is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect),' the definition of <s>buddhi</s> amounts to being the cause of all practical activity. But that does not work, because <s>buddhi</s> does not have the property of being the cause of verbal activity uttered by parrots and the like. Even if one says it is the cause with respect to practical activity dependent on the desire to make known, and thereby deviation is absent — still, a cognition from which practical activity was not produced due to an obstruction, since it lacks the capacity to occasion practical activity, there is under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) to that case. Even if one includes causality in the form of intrinsic capacity, since a cognition of a pot and the like does not have the property of being the cause of practical activity regarding cloth and the like, no single cognition is the cause of all practical activity. Therefore he says — 'mere <s>jñānatva</s> (cognition-ness) is the definition.' Now then, [one asks about the purpose of] 'the cause of all practical activity' in the compendium.

children.text:
1. svapratiyogīti/ atra
svapadaṃ prathamapatanadhvaṃsaparam/ tatpratiyogi prathamapatanam,
tatsamānādhikaraṇatvaṃ dvitīyapatane/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Its own counter-positive...' Here the word 'own' (<s>sva</s>) refers to the destruction of the first occurrence. Its counter-positive is the first occurrence; co-substratum-ness with that [belongs to] the second occurrence.

children.text:
kimarthamuktamityatrāha -
idaṃ ceti/ [114] saṃskārasya trividhatvāditi/ tathā ca iha
saṃskārapadena vegasthitasthāpakayorvivakṣaṇe smṛtāvasambhava iti
bhāvaḥ/ [114] bhāvanākhya itīti/ tathā ca bhāvanāyāḥ
smṛtihetutvāt nāyaṃ doṣa iti bhāvaḥ/ [114] saṃskārajanyatvasya sattveneti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - jñānapratyāsatteḥ
anudbuddhasaṃskārānyasaviṣayakatvena hetutvamāvaśyakam, anyathā
icchādyanuvyavasāyena ghaṭādibhānānupapatteḥ/ evaṃ ca saṃskārasyāpi
upanayavidhayā hetutvamiti saṃskārajanayatvamiti tena
nānumityādāvativyāptiṃriti bhāvaḥ/ [114] tathāpi cakṣurādīti/ na
cātra manojanyatvābhāvāniveśe 'yo 'haṃ ghaṭamadrākṣam so 'haṃ
idānīṃ spṛśāmi' imi mānasapratyabhijñāyāmativyāptiḥ/ tanniveśe
tvasambhavaḥ/ jñānasāmānye manasaḥ karaṇatvāt/ evaṃ cakṣurādeḥ
kālādividhayā smṛtihetutvādasambhavaśceti vācyam/
cākṣuṣatvamānasatvādirūpajātyavacchinnapratiyogitākabhedakūṭavattvasya
pratyakṣatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedasya vā niveśyatvāt/
children.translated_text: To the question 'for what purpose is this stated?' he says — 'and this...' '<s>Saṃskāra</s> (dispositional impression) is of three kinds...' And thus, if by the word <s>saṃskāra</s> velocity and elasticity are intended, then memory (<s>smṛti</s>) would not be possible — this is the purport. 'Called <s>bhāvanā</s> (mental impression)...' And thus, since <s>bhāvanā</s> is the cause of memory, this is not a defect — this is the purport. 'Since the property of being produced by <s>saṃskāra</s> exists...' The purport is as follows: due to the proximity of cognition, causality in the form of having as its object something different from the unawakened <s>saṃskāra</s> is necessary — otherwise, the appearance of a pot and the like through the reflective cognition of desire and the like would be inexplicable. And thus, since <s>saṃskāra</s> too has causality in the manner of a subsidiary factor, the property of being produced by <s>saṃskāra</s> [is included]; thereby there is no over-extension to inference and the like — this is the purport. 'Even so, the eye and the like...' Nor should it be objected here that if the absence of being produced by <s>manas</s> (mind) is not included, there would be over-extension to mental recognition such as 'I who saw the pot earlier am now touching it,' while if it is included there would be impossibility, since <s>manas</s> is the instrument of cognition in general. Similarly, it should not be said that there is impossibility because the eye and the like are causes of memory in the manner of a temporal [relation] and so on — because what is to be included is a group of differences whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by a <s>jāti</s> (universal) of the form visual-ness, mental-ness, and the like, or a difference whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by perceptuality.

children.text:
idamatra cintyam -
mātrapadaghaṭitayathāśrutaśabdalabhyasya
saṃskāretaranirūpitajñānatvavyāpyadharmāvacchinnajanyatāśūnyatvasya
laghoḥ niveśenaivopapattau uktarītyā bhedaniveśe
udakṣaratāpattiriti/
children.translated_text: This should be reflected upon here: when the lighter [alternative of] including the absence of being-produced-by-something-delimited-by-a-property-pervaded-by-<s>jñānatva</s>-as-conditioned-by-something-other-than-<s>saṃskāra</s> — which is the meaning literally obtained from the word compounded with 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>) — suffices, including the [more complex] difference in the stated manner leads to the fault of unnecessary complexity.

children.text: yathārthānubhavalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of veridical experience (<s>yathārthānubhava</s>)

children.text:
jñānatvaniveśenāpīcchādivāraṇasambhavādāha - smṛtīti/ [116] etatphalamanubhavatvaniveśaprayojanam/ [116] yatretīt i/ atra ca 'ghaṭapaṭobhayaṃ ghaṭa' ityādijñānānāmapi
āṃśikapramātvasyeṣṭatvāt na tatrātivyāptiśaṅketi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Since blocking desire and the like is possible even by including <s>jñānatva</s> (cognition-ness), he says — 'memory (<s>smṛti</s>)...' 'This result [shows] the purpose of including <s>anubhavatva</s> (experience-ness).' 'In which...' And here, since even for cognitions such as 'both pot and cloth [constitute] a pot' partial veridicality is accepted, there is no apprehension of over-extension to those cases — this is the purport.

children.text:
kecittu-'ghaṭapaṭobhayaṃ
ghaṭa'ityādijñānasyālakṣyatve 'pi tatra nātiprasaṅgaḥ/
tatsambandhāvacchinnatadadhikaraṇatāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyatāniveśāt
tatpratiyogikatatsambandhānuyogitāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyatāniveśādvā
ghaṭapaṭobhayatvādeḥ niruktādhikaraṇatānavacchedakatvāt
niruktānuyogitānavacchedakatvācca tādṛśobhayatvādeḥ
tādṛśādhikaraṇatādinyūnavṛttitvāt/ na ca
nirdharmitāvacchedakakapramāyāmavyāptirita vācyam/
tādṛśādhikaraṇatādyata vacchedakadharmānavacchinnaviśeṣyatāniveśāt/ na
ca tathā
children.translated_text: Some [hold] however — even if cognitions like 'both pot and cloth [constitute] a pot' are not captured by the definition, there is no over-extension to them. This is because what is included is <s>viśeṣyatā</s> (qualificandness) delimited by a property that delimits the substratum-ness conditioned by that relation, or <s>viśeṣyatā</s> delimited by a property that delimits the relatum-ness of the counter-positive-ness and the adjunct-ness conditioned by that relation. Since 'both-pot-and-cloth-ness' and the like do not delimit the stated substratum-ness or the stated adjunct-ness, and since such 'both-ness' and the like have a narrower occurrence than the stated substratum-ness and the like — nor should it be said that there is under-extension in the case of valid cognition without a property delimiting the locus — because what is included is <s>viśeṣyatā</s> not delimited by a property delimiting such substratum-ness and the like. Nor should it be said that

children.text:
sati
nirdharmitāvacchedakakabhrame 'tivyāptiriti vācyam/
tādṛśabhramasyāprāmāṇikatvāt - ityāhuḥ/
children.translated_text: in the case of an erroneous cognition without a property delimiting the locus, there would be over-extension — because such an erroneous cognition is not authoritative. Thus they say.

children.text:
tadasat -
rajatatvādinā śuktyādyavagāhinaḥ rajatatvādyaṃśe
nirdharmitāvacchedakakasya iha rajatamastīdyākārakasya
bhrāntajanānāmanubhavasiddhatvāt uktapariṣkāre tatrātivyāpteḥ
durvāratvāt/
children.translated_text: That is wrong — because erroneous cognitions of people who apprehend nacre and the like through silver-ness and the like, being of the form 'there is silver here,' [cognitions] without a property delimiting the locus with respect to the silver-ness component, are established through experience; and with the stated refinement, over-extension to those [cases] is impossible to block.

children.text:
anye tu -
prasaktādhikaraṇatādyavacchedakadharmānavacchinnatvāvacchinnatvobhayābhāvasya
viśeṣyatāyāṃ niveśāt uktarītyā 'ghaṭapaṭobhayaṃ ghaṭa' ityādibhrame
nātiprasaṅgaḥ/ nāpi nirdharmitāvacchedakapramāyāmavyāptiḥ/ yattu -
vyāsajyavṛttidharmānavacchinnaviśeṣyatāniveśāt neyamativyāptiriti
- tattuccham/ 'etadghaṭatadghaṭobhayaṃ ghaṭa' iti
pramāyāmavyāpteriti vadanti/ tadapyasat/ uktāvyāpterevāvaraṇāt/
etadghaṭatadghaṭobhayatvādeḥ ghaṭatvādinyūnavṛttitayā
ghaṭatvādyadhikaraṇatānirūpitasvarūpasambandharūpāvacchedakatve
mānābhāvāt tadanyūnānatiprasaktasyaiva tadavacchedakatvopagamāt/
anthā anantānāṃ tādṛśobhayatvādīnāṃ tadavacchedakatve
mahāgauravaprasaṅgāt/ anitiriktavṛttitvarūpatadavacchedakatvaniveśe
dravyatvādisāmānādhikaraṇyamātreṇa ghaṭatvādyavagāhinyāṃ 'dravyaṃ ghaṭa'
ityādi pramāyāmavyāpteḥ/
children.translated_text: Others however [say] — since the absence of both being-delimited and not-being-delimited by a property that delimits the applicable substratum-ness and the like is included in the <s>viśeṣyatā</s>, there is no over-extension in the stated manner to erroneous cognitions like 'both pot and cloth [constitute] a pot.' Nor is there under-extension in the case of valid cognition without a property delimiting the locus. As for the [objection] that 'since <s>viśeṣyatā</s> not delimited by a disjunctively-occurring property is included, this over-extension does not arise' — that is empty. They say there is under-extension in valid cognitions like 'both this-pot and that-pot [constitute] a pot.' But that too is wrong — because it is blocked by the very under-extension stated [above]. Since 'both-this-pot-and-that-pot-ness' and the like have narrower occurrence than pot-ness and the like, and since there is no means of knowledge for its being the delimiter in substratum-ness conditioned by the self-nature relation conditioned by pot-ness and the like, only that which has neither narrower nor over-extended [occurrence] is accepted as the delimiter. Otherwise, infinitely many [delimiters would arise].
'Now, [the word]

children.text:
nanu tadvatītyasyetyādi/
nirūpakatāsambandhasya
vṛttyanavacchedakatvenābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakatayā
nañarthānvayānupapatteḥ viśeṣyatārthakatvāsambhavādāha- [115] saptamyartho viśeṣyitvamiti/ yadvā bhūtalaṃ vahnimāt, parvato
ghaṭavānityādi samūhālambanato vailakṣaṇyasiddhaye parvato
vahnimānityādijñāne viśeṣyatvaprakāratvayoḥ nirūpyanirūpakabhāvaḥ
svīkārya ityekaṃ matam/ tannirūpitaviṣayitārūpayoḥ
viśeṣyitvaprakāritvayoravacchedyāvacchedakabhāvastathetyaparaṃ matam/
tatra dvitīyamatamanusṛtyāha - viśeṣyitvamiti/ atra ca viśeṣyatāyāḥ
saptamyarthatve prakāratāviśiṣṭaviśeṣyatānirūpakānubhavatvaṃ
pramātvam/ viśeṣyitāyāstadarthatve tu
prakāritāviśiṣṭaviśeṣyitāvadanubhavatvaṃ tat/ prathame vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
1svāvacchedakasaṃbandhena svāśrayavanniṣṭhatvasvanirūpitatvobhayasambandhena/
dvitīye vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchinnatvasvanirūpitaprakāratāviśiṣṭaviśeṣyatānirūpitatvobhayasambandhena/
prakāratāvaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchedakasambandhenasvāśrayavanniṣṭhatvasambandheneti/ dhyeyam/ [116] tadvatīsyasya tatsaṃbandhinītyartha iti/ prathame
prakāratāviśiṣṭaviśeṣyatānirūpakānubhavatvam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
2svanirūpitatvasvaviśiṣṭapratiyogitānirūpitānuyogitāśrayaniṣṭhatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
children.translated_text: possessing that...' and so on. Since the relation of being-a-conditioner does not delimit the occurrence, and thereby does not delimit the counter-positive-ness of absence, the negative particle cannot be construed [with it], and hence the meaning of <s>viśeṣyatā</s> would be impossible — to address this he says — 'the meaning of the seventh case-ending is <s>viśeṣyitva</s> (being a qualificand).' Alternatively, to establish the distinction from a collective apprehension [as in] 'the ground possesses fire, the mountain possesses a pot,' one view holds that in cognitions like 'the mountain possesses fire,' the relation of qualifier and qualificand (<s>nirūpya-nirūpaka</s>) between <s>viśeṣyatva</s> (qualificandness) and <s>prakāratva</s> (qualifierness) must be accepted. Another view holds that the relation of delimited and delimiter obtains between <s>viśeṣyitva</s> and <s>prakāritva</s> (being-a-qualifier), which are of the nature of objecthood conditioned by those. Following the second view, he says — '<s>viśeṣyitva</s>...' And here, when <s>viśeṣyatā</s> has the meaning of the seventh case-ending, the <s>prakāratā</s>-qualified-<s>viśeṣyatā</s>-conditioned experience...

children.text:
1. svāvacchedaketyādi/
rajate idaṃ rajatamiti jñāne samanvayaḥ kriyate/ svaṃ
rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratā tadavacchedakasaṃbandhaḥ samavāyaḥ tena saṃbandhena
prakāratāśrayarajatatvavat rajataṃ tanniṣṭhatvaṃ viśeṣyatāyām, evaṃ svaṃ
rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratā tannirūpitattvaṃ ca viśeṣyatāyām iti
tādṛśaviśeṣyatānirūpakānubhavatvaṃ idaṃ rajatamiti jñāne 'stīti/
dvitīyānugame svaṃ prakāritā rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitā
jñānaniṣṭha tadavacchinnatvaṃ
ratajaniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitajñānaṣṭhiviśeṣyitāyāmasti, evaṃ svaṃ
prakāritā tannirūpitā yā rajatatvaniṣṭhā prakāratā
tadavacchedakasamavāyasambandhena
prakāratāśrayarajatatvanniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitatvaṃ ca
viśeṣyitāyāmasti,
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Its own delimiter...' and so on. The construal is made with respect to the cognition 'this is silver' in relation to silver. 'Own' is the <s>prakāratā</s> (qualifierness) residing in silver-ness; the relation that delimits it is inherence (<s>samavāya</s>); through that relation, the fact of residing in silver-ness which is the locus of <s>prakāratā</s> [is present] in <s>viśeṣyatā</s>. Similarly, 'own' is the <s>prakāratā</s> residing in silver-ness, and the property of being conditioned by that is [present] in <s>viśeṣyatā</s>. Thus the property of being an experience that conditions such <s>viśeṣyatā</s> exists in the cognition 'this is silver.' In the second construal, 'own' is <s>prakāritā</s> (being-a-qualifier) conditioned by the <s>prakāratā</s> residing in silver-ness, residing in the cognition; the property of being delimited by that [is present] in the <s>viśeṣyatā</s> residing in silver conditioned by the <s>viśeṣyitā</s> (being-a-qualificand) residing in the cognition. Similarly, 'own' is <s>prakāritā</s> conditioned by that, which is the <s>prakāratā</s> residing in silver-ness; through the inherence relation that delimits it,

children.text:

children.translated_text: in <s>pratiyogitā</s>, the qualification of itself [is established] through both the relation of possessing difference in the form of 'residing in its own locus, its own...' and so on. Its own substratum-ness is through the relation of being the delimiter of the delimiting-ness of its own delimiter. The delimiting-ness of the counter-positive-ness of difference is through the relation of being the conditioner distinct from the conditioner-ness of itself. Therefore, in the <s>Prācīna</s> (old) school's view that holds the unity of inherence, there is no over-extension in the erroneous cognition 'air possesses color through inherence.' Nor is there over-extension in erroneous cognitions like 'a quality possesses <s>sattā</s> (existence) qualified by otherness from quality and the like,' on the view that takes the <s>saṃsargatā</s> (relational property) to be inherence conditioned by what is qualified. Although on the view that conjunction, inherence, and the like have <s>saṃsargatā</s> intrinsically, impossibility [would result], nevertheless in that school what is to be included in <s>pratiyogitā</s> is precisely the property of being conditioned by the relation that delimits one's own delimiter. In the erroneous cognition 'possessing qualified <s>sattā</s>'...

children.translated_text: there is no over-extension. And if in such a case there is over-extension in a cognition whose <s>prakāratā</s> (qualifierness) is delimited by pot-ness and the like through both the relation of conjunction and inherence, [and if one says] that taking <s>prakāratā</s> delimited by both such relations makes it impossible to block — then [we respond:] the qualification of itself in <s>pratiyogitā</s> is through both the relation of possessing difference in the form of 'residing in its own locus, its own...' and so on. The substratum-ness of itself is through the relation of <s>saṃsargatā</s> (relational property) delimited by one's own delimiter. The delimiting-ness of the counter-positive-ness of difference is through the relation of being the conditioner of itself.

yattu -

svāvacchedakaparyāptāvacchedakatāvatvaṃ niveśyam/ tacca
svasetyādibhedavattvaparyavasitam/ svādhikaraṇāvacchedakatā ca
avacchedakatāsambandhena na

vyadhikaraṇatvāt/ tathā ca viśiṣṭasattāvā niti bhrame nātiprasaṅgaḥ/

pratiyogitāyāṃ tādṛśadharmāvacchinnatvasattvane taddoṣānirāsāditi/
children.translated_text: Now, [it is said that] in the counter-positiveness (<s>pratiyogitā</s>), since being qualified by itself is a component, the property of possessing delimitor-hood sufficient for its own delimitor should be introduced. And that amounts to the possession of difference from itself and the like. And the delimitor-hood of the locus of itself is [connected] by the relation of delimitor-hood. Nor should one say that in this way there is under-pervasion in the case of a valid cognition having an undelimited qualifier-hood such as pot-hood; because there is no fault in introducing the qualification by itself through the relation of possessing the constant absence of a counter-positive delimited by the delimitor-hood of the counter-positiveness of a difference co-located with itself, connected by the relation of delimitor-hood, rather than introducing the qualification by itself through the stated relation of itself and the like. Because the stated relation is located in a different locus with respect to undelimited qualifier-hood. And thus, in the erroneous cognition 'it possesses qualified existence,' there is no over-extension. Alternatively, the qualification by itself in counter-positiveness is [connected] by the triple relation of residing in the locus of itself, being determined by the relation that is one's own delimitor, and being the delimitor-hood of the counter-positiveness of the difference residing in itself. The delimitor-hood [is connected] by the relation of being delimited by a property qualifying itself. And the qualification by itself [is connected] by the relation of possessing a difference that is a counter-positive of a delimitor-hood residing in itself and delimited by the relation of delimitor-hood. However, the property of not being delimited by a property that is not one's own delimitor cannot be introduced — because if the property of not being one's own delimitor has the form of being different from one's own delimitor, then due to the non-establishment of one's own delimitor, there is under-pervasion in the previously stated valid cognition; and even if it has the form of being an absence of counter-positiveness residing in itself and delimited by the delimitor-relation, since the property of being delimited by such a property obtains in the counter-positiveness, that fault is not eliminated.

tadupapādanasyāsaṅgatatvāpātāt/
children.translated_text: That is wrong — because of over-extension in the erroneous cognition 'a quality possesses qualified existence' and the like. Since the validity of cognitions such as 'a quality possesses existence characterized by being different from qualities and the like' is universally accepted, the qualification by difference-from-qualities-and-the-like too does not depart from being the delimitor of superstratum-hood determined by qualities and the like. Because the qualifier of superstratum-hood and the like is itself the delimitor of superstratum-hood and the like. Precisely for this reason, <s>Gadādhara</s> accepted in his definitive definition that properties such as being the relation that delimits the counter-positiveness of a qualified absence apply to inherence delimited by the property of being determined by something qualified, while [the same properties] of an undelimited inherence [apply] to a characterized absence. Otherwise, since the distinction between qualified absence and characterized absence could be accomplished merely by the delimitor-hood of the qualifier with respect to counter-positiveness and the absence thereof, the demonstration in the manner shown would appear incongruous.

children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, 'that which possesses the absence of that' and so forth. And here, the property of being an experience that is qualified by qualifier-hood-qualified-qualificand-hood-determined-ness, or the property of being an experience that possesses qualificand-hood-qualified-by-qualifier-hood, is the property of being erroneous (<s>bhramatva</s>). In the first [alternative], the qualification is [connected] by the dual relation of residing in what possesses the constant absence of a counter-positive delimited by a property occurring in only what is qualified by itself, and being determined by itself. And the qualification by itself [is connected] by the dual relation of being delimited by the relation that is one's own delimitor and residing in one's own locus. In the second [alternative], the qualification should be inferred by oneself in the manner stated. Here, since the property of occurring only in the locus of itself should be introduced within the relational qualifier, there is no over-extension in a valid cognition having a qualifier with non-pervading occurrence. In truth, however,

children.translated_text: since the property of being an absence is introduced in the undelimited locus-hood, there is no fault at all — this is the essential point. Since one's own absence, being one's own delimitor, does not appear in erroneous cognition, [the commentator] says — in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [section 120] 'the absence of conjunction.' Now, [one might object that] the definition of error such as 'qualificand-hood delimited by the locus delimited by the delimitor of the absence of that' is under-pervaded in erroneous cognitions having a qualifier like silver-hood with non-pervading occurrence, as in 'this is silver' with respect to nacre — therefore [the commentator] says [section 120] 'this should be noted here' and so forth. This should be considered: since in the manner of 'the property of being an experience that determines qualificand-hood qualified by qualifier-hood,' a single definition is easily stated despite the difference between qualifiers with pervading and non-pervading occurrence, stating different definitions based on that distinction is most inappropriate. The qualification is [connected] by the dual relation of being determined by itself and residing in a locus of what is qualified by itself. The qualification by itself [is connected] by the relation of possessing what is qualified by itself as an absence. The qualification by itself in the absence [is connected] by the dual relation of being delimited by the relation that is one's own delimitor and not occurring in the locus of one's own locus, and having a counter-positiveness qualified by itself. The qualification by itself [is connected] by the dual relation of being delimited by the relation that is one's own delimitor and residing in one's own locus.

children.translated_text: Footnote 1: 'What is qualified by itself' — the phrase 'what is qualified by itself' construes with 'counter-positiveness delimited by a property occurring in only one [thing].' And thus, 'itself' is the qualifier-hood residing in silver-hood; the relation that is its delimitor is the relation of inherence; the counter-positiveness delimited by that and residing in silver-hood — such [counter-positiveness] resides in the locus of the qualifier-hood as well — hence it is counter-positiveness qualified by qualifier-hood. [That counter-positiveness is] delimited by a property occurring in only one [thing], namely silver-hood; the residing-in-what-possesses-the-absence-determined-by-that is [the property that qualifies] the qualificand-hood — the construal should be made in this manner.

The qualification is [connected] by the dual relation of being determined by itself and determining the qualifier-hood-qualified-qualificand-hood delimited by itself. The qualification of qualificand-hood by qualifier-hood is [connected] by the dual relation of residing in what possesses the constant absence of a counter-positive delimited by a property occurring in only what is qualified by itself, and being determined by itself. The qualification by itself in the counter-positiveness is [connected] by the dual relation of being delimited by the relation that is one's own delimitor and residing in one's own locus — this is what should be inferred, that is the meaning.

nirūpyanirūpakabhāvaṃ niveśyāpi samūhālambanavyāvṛttisambhavaḥ,
tathāpi śiṣyadhīvaiśadyāya prakārāntaramapyuktamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: Now, [the view] that the property of being an experience that determines qualifier-hood qualified by qualificand-hood that is determined by what is qualified in the manner shown, connected by the dual relation of shown-relation and identity with qualificand-hood qualified by what is qualified by itself — that is wrong, because of the unwanted consequence of great prolixity through the twofold introduction of qualifier-hood and the entry of the additional [relation of] identity. Nor should one say that the description is so stated in accordance with the natural import of the <s>Dīpikā</s> passage [section 120] 'by the delimitor of which'; because if such a <s>Dīpikā</s> passage is taken as referring to a different definition, there is over-extension in valid cognitions such as 'the tree characterized by the root text possesses monkey-contact.' Because the definition of error in the case of a qualifier with non-pervading occurrence is unavoidable. Because the desired result cannot be obtained without the absence of object-sublation. Therefore, the stated <s>Dīpikā</s> passage, with the intent of refining the definition of error in our stated manner, upon apprehending under-pervasion in the case of erroneous cognition with a qualifier having non-pervading occurrence, is aimed at showing that only a cognition apprehending conjunction and the like qualified by what is qualified by the root text and the like counts as erroneous. And thus, in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [section 120], the meaning of 'because it is intended' is 'because it counts as a definiendum' and the like. [Section 120] 'Qualificand-hood' — here, although it is possible to exclude collective apprehension by introducing the determiner-determined relation between qualificand-hood and qualifier-hood as well, nevertheless, another manner [of formulation] is also stated for the sake of clarity for students — this should be noted.

children.text: yathārthānubhavavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Classification of veridical experience

children.text:
dīpikāyām [123] prasaṅgāditi/ atra pañcamyartho jñānajanyajijñāsādhīnatvaṃ
vibhāgānvitam/ kaḥ prasaṅgaḥ ityākāṅkṣāyāmāha - prakāśikāyām
[123] smṛtasyopekṣānarhatvamityādi/ smṛtasya
pūrvāhitapadārthasambandhena smṛtigocarasyopekṣānarhatvaṃ
dveṣyajñānaviṣayatāvirodhirūpam/ tacca prakṛte pramitikaraṇatvam/
idaṃ
copodghātādipañcakabhinnatvamaniveśyānantarābhidhānaprayojanakajijñāsājanakajñānaprakāratvenopodghātādīnāmapi
prasaṅge evāntarbhāva ityabhimānena anyathā karaṇatvasya
kāraṇatāviśeṣarūpatayā kāraṇatāsāmānyabhedaghaṭitaprasaṅgalakṣaṇsya
prakṛte 'sambhavenāsaṅgateḥ/ vastutastu
anantarābhidhānaniyāmakajijñāsājanakanirūpyatāvacchedakaprakārakasmaraṇaprayojakaḥ
nirūpyaniṣṭhaupodghātādivyātiriktaḥ sambandhaḥ prasaṅgasaṅgatiḥ/
prakṛte ca caturvidhatvena pramitisādṛśyameva pramāṇasya tādṛśamiti/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [section 123] 'incidentally' — here, the fifth-case ending has the meaning of being dependent on the curiosity produced by cognition, construed with the classification. What is the incidental connection? In response to this expectation, [the commentator] says — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [section 123] 'that which has been recollected is not to be disregarded' and so forth. 'Not to be disregarded' of what has been recollected — that is, of what falls within the scope of recollection through the relation of word-meanings previously deposited — means not being in conflict with the content of a cognition of aversion. And that, in the present context, is the property of being the instrument of a resultant cognition. And this — without introducing the property of being different from the five, namely the introductory discussion and the like — since the introductory discussion and the like are also included within the incidental connection itself, as qualifiers of the cognition that produces the curiosity that occasions the sequential exposition — [this is stated] with the understanding [that otherwise], since the property of being an instrument, having the nature of a specific causal condition, the definition of incidental connection constituted by difference from the general causal condition would not be applicable in the present context, hence there would be incongruity. In truth, however, the incidental connection is a relation, other than introductory discussion and the like, that resides in the object of determination [and] that occasions the recollection having as its qualifier the delimitor of the determinability, which recollection produces the curiosity that governs the sequential exposition. And in the present context, the similarity among the resultant cognitions as being fourfold is precisely what constitutes such [incidental connection] for the <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text:
idamatrāvadheyam -
dharmaviśiṣṭadharmavatvaṃ saṅgatiḥ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svabhinnatvasvaviśiṣṭaśabdaviśiṣṭatvobhayasaṃbandhena/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaviśiṣṭaśabdottaratvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākaprati yogitākabhedavatvasvāvacchinnakarmanirūpaṇottaratvobhayasambandhena
children.translated_text: This should be noted here — the incidental connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) is the possession by a property-possessor of a property that is qualified. The qualification is [connected] by the dual relation of being different from itself and being qualified by a word qualified by itself. The qualification by itself is [connected] by the dual relation of possessing a difference that is a counter-positive of a delimitor-hood residing in itself and delimited by the relation of subsequence to a word qualified by itself, and being subsequent to the determination of the topic delimited by itself.

children.text:
/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāvacchinnakarmakanirūpaṇottaratvasvabhinnadharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyakalakṣaṇādiprakārakajñānajanakatvobhayasaṃbandhenaḥ/
śabdavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca ādheyatvasvaprayojakecchāviśiṣṭatvobhayasambandhena/
icchāvaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca ādheyatvasvajanakajñānaprakāratvobhayasambandhena/
ādheyatvaṃ
svaniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitavyāpyatvaprakāratānirūpitadharmaprakāratān irūpitaprakāratvaprakāratānirūpitanirūpakatvaprakāratānirūpitajñānatvāvacchinnaviśeṣyatākatvasaṃbandhena/
tathā cānumānaṃ pratyakṣasaṅgatamityādau dharmaviśiṣṭadharma eva
saṅgatipadārthaḥ/ tatra pratyakṣatvaniṣṭhādheyatāsambandhena pratyakṣasya
prathamadharme 'nvayaḥ/ dharmatvonānvayitāvacchedakadharmaviśeṣabodhakatvaṃ
saṅgatipadasya vyutpattisiddham/
evamanvayisamarpakapadapravṛttinimittatāghaṭakasambandhāvacchinnan iṣṭhanirūpitatvasambandhenapratyayārthaikadeśāśrayatāyāṃ
dvitīyadharmānvayabodhakatvamapi tathā/
children.translated_text: The qualification by itself is [connected] by the dual relation of being subsequent to the determination of a topic delimited by itself, and being a producer of cognition having as its qualifier a definition and the like that has as its qualificand a property delimited by a property different from itself. The qualification of the word is [connected] by the dual relation of superstratum-hood and being qualified by the will that occasions itself. The qualification of the will is [connected] by the dual relation of superstratum-hood and being a qualifier of the cognition that produces itself. Superstratum-hood [is connected] by the relation of being the qualificand-hood of a cognition delimited by the qualifier-hood of the determining relation determined by the qualifier-hood of the property determined by the qualifier-hood of the pervaded-ness determined by the qualifier-hood of the qualifier-hood determined by the qualifier-hood of the qualificand-hood residing in itself. And thus, in [the statement] 'inference has incidental connection with perception' and the like, the meaning of the word <s>saṅgati</s> is precisely a property-possessor's qualified property. Therein, the first property is connected to perception by the relation of superstratum-hood residing in perception-hood. The established derivational meaning of the word <s>saṅgati</s> is the capacity to convey the specific property that delimits the property of not being connected [to something unrelated]. Similarly, the capacity to convey the connection of the second property to the locus of a portion of the meaning of the suffix, through the relation of residing in what is determined by the relation that constitutes the ground of applicability of the word denoting the connected [item], is also [part of its meaning].

children.text:
vastutastu
dharmaviśiṣṭatvameva saṅgatiḥ/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaviśiṣṭādhikaraṇatāviśiṣṭatvasambandhena/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svabhinnadharmāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedanirūpitatvasvaviśiṣṭaśabdavi śiṣṭabobhayasambandhena/
śabde svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca prāgvat/ śabdavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
ādheyatvasvaprayojakecchāviśiṣṭatvobhayasambandhena/ ādheyatā
svanirūpakabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyakalakṣaṇādi prakārakajñānajanakatvasambandhena/
icchāvaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svanirūpakabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvopalakṣitadharmavyāpyadharmaprakārajñānatvāvacchinnaviśeṣyatākatvasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvaprayojakasamaraṇaviśiṣṭatvobhayasambandhena/
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaprayojakasaṃbandhaniṣṭhatvasvanirūpakabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakadharmaprakārakatvasambandhāvacchinnādheyatvobhayasambandhena/
adhikaraṇatāvaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca svāśrayāśrayatvasambandhena/ atra ca
saṅgatamityādau tatpratyayārthaikadeśabhūtāśrayatāyāmadhikaraṇatāyāḥ
yena sambandhena sambandhajñānasya smārakatvaṃ

svīkāryā/ anyat pūrvavadati/
karaṇalakṣaṇam

adṛṣṭāderityādinā īśvaraparigrahaḥ/ [124] anubhavatvavyāpyeti/ yadyapi
kāryatvātiriktadharmāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvaniveśādapi
kālādivāraṇasambhavaḥ, tathāpi
jñānasāmānyahetubhūtasyātmadāderavāraṇāt tadupekṣā/ [124] pramāvṛttīti/ idaṃ bhramajanakadoṣe 'tivyāptivāraṇāya/ nanu
niruktapramāṇalakṣaṇasya cakṣussaṃyogādāvativyāptiḥ/ na ca
dravyatvaniveśāt na doṣa iti vācyam/ tathā sati vyāptijñānādeḥ
pramāṇatvānupapatterityata āha -- [124] vyāpāravattve
satītyapīti/ vyāpāravattvaṃ ca
svajanakatvasvajanyajanakatvobhayasaṃbandhena kiñcidviśiṣṭatvam/

kāraṇavāraṇāya
satyantam/ phalavāraṇāya viśeṣyam/
svajanyatvasvajanyajanakatvobhayasambandhena prameyaviśiṣṭatvamanugatārthaḥ/

tadā janyatāviśiṣṭatvaṃ tadvācyam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca

svāśrayajanakatvasvanirūpakajanyatvobhayasambandhena/
janyatāviśiṣṭatvamityanugamo bodhyaḥ/

vastutastu
phalajanakatāprayojakajanakatānirūpakatvaṃ vyāpāratvam/ tena
kulālaputrādeḥ kulālādivyāpāratāprasaṅgasya nāvakāśaḥ/ yadvā
tajjanyajanakatvaṃ tādṛśajanakatāvacchedakasambandhatvarūpamiha bodhyam/
nanvevaṃ sati śrotrendriyasya pramāṇatānupapattiḥ/ tatra samavāyasyaiva

[124] śrotreti/ nanu kāraṇatvaṃ phalāvyavahitapūrvavṛttitvam/ tacca
kāraṇatāvacchedakasambandhena vācyam/ anyathā yāgādeḥ
svargādikāraṇatvānupapatteḥ/ tathoktau tu svajanyāpūrvasambandhena
yāgādestathātvāt nānupapattiḥ/ evaṃ ca
vyāpārasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatvameva karaṇatvam/ vyāpāravattve satīti
pṛthagviśeṣaṇasya vyarthatvāt cakṣussaṃyogāderuktarūpābhāvena
tatrānatiprasaṅgāt/ tathā ca śabdavṛttilaukikaviṣayatāsambandhena
śrāvaṇaṃ prati svavṛttimanassaṃyogasambandhena śrotrasya kāraṇatvaṃ na
sambhavatītyata āha [124] śabdo veti/ tathā ca
svavṛttiśabdatādātmyasambandhena śrotrasya kāraṇatvaṃ sambhavatīti bhāvaḥ/
[124] vadantīti/ prāñca iti śeṣaḥ/ navīnamatamāha [124] yadvilambāditi/
svetarayāvatprakṛtakāryakāraṇasamavadhānakālīnakāryotpattyabhāvaprayojakībhūtābhāvapratiyogitvaṃ

prameyaviśiṣṭatvaṃ tat,

1.
svasetyādyavacchedakatvasambandheneti/

- svaprayojaketyatra

svaśabdaḥ daṇḍādikāraṇaparaḥ/ svetaretyatrasvaśabdaḥ daṇḍādikāraṇaparaḥ/
tathā ca-

daṇḍavadbhedo

grāhyaḥ/

nanu

phalitam/

tantuviṣayakameveti/

bodhyā/ ata eva yatpadasya yaddharmāvacchinnaparatayā vyākhyānādeva
tantutvena tantoranyathāsiddhivāraṇasambhavaḥ/ tantuḥ
paṭaniyatapūrvavṛttiriti jñāne tantutvasya svarūpata eva bhānāt/ evaṃ
ca śūnyāntaviśeṣaṇaṃ vyarthathmati śaṅkā nirastā/
tantutvatvaviśiṣṭena
tadāśrayavṛttirūpatvāvacchinnasyānyathāsiddhivāraṇāya tatsārthakyāt/
svatantrānvayavyatirekaśālitvaṃ
svetaragatānvayavyatirekānadhīnānvayavyatirekavattvam/ anvayaśca
prakṛtakāryasattāprayojakasattāvattvam/ vyatirekaśca
prakṛtakāryavirahaprayojakavirahanirūpakatvam/ atra ca
1tādṛśasattāviśiṣṭatve sati tādṛśavyatirekaviśiṣṭatvamityanugamaḥ/
prathame vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāśrayatvasvavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
avacchedakatvaṃ svabhinnagatānvayādhīnatvasambandhena/ dvitīye vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svāśrayatvasvavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvobhayasambandhena/
bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā svabhinnagatavyatirekādhīnatvasambandhena/
atra ca satyantaṃ vā viśeṣyadalaṃ vā ekaikamevopādeyam/ ubhayaniveśe
children.translated_text: 'pertaining to thread alone' — because in the cognition produced by a word denoting a <s>jāti</s> (universal), the <s>jāti</s> appears in some form or other, and since <s>tantutvattva</s> (thread-universal-ness) is the qualificandum precisely as thread-universal-ness in the present context, and since <s>tantutvattva</s> has the nature of being co-inherent in all threads while being non-co-inherent in things other than threads — this is the purport. [127] 'In brief' — although since <s>tantutva</s> (thread-ness), which is necessarily a qualifier for preventing the <s>anyathāsiddhi</s> (otherwise-establishment) of thread-conjunction with thread, already prevents the otherwise-establishment of the thread, the qualifier 'possessing independent co-presence and co-absence' for the correlate of 'by which' is redundant; nevertheless, the necessity of that qualifier should be understood as being for the purpose of preventing the otherwise-establishment of thread-form by thread-ness. For this very reason, from the interpretation of the 'yat'-word as having reference delimited by a particular property, the prevention of otherwise-establishment of thread by <s>tantutva</s> is possible. In the cognition 'thread is an invariable antecedent of cloth,' <s>tantutva</s> appears in its own essential nature. And thus the objection that the qualifier with an empty remainder is purposeless is refuted — because it serves the purpose of preventing the otherwise-establishment of what is delimited by the nature of residing in the locus of that, as qualified by <s>tantutvatva</s>. 'Possessing independent co-presence and co-absence' means possessing co-presence and co-absence that do not depend on the co-presence and co-absence residing in things other than itself. Co-presence means possessing existence that is productive of the existence of the relevant effect. Co-absence means being the determinant of absence that is productive of the absence of the relevant effect. And here the <s>anugama</s> (formulation) is: being qualified by such co-absence while being qualified by such existence. The qualification in the first case is through both relations of being-the-locus-of and being-the-delimitor-of-the-counterpositive-ness-of-difference-from-what-resides-in-oneself. The delimitor-hood is through the relation of dependence-on-co-presence-residing-in-something-different-from-itself. The qualification in the second case is through both relations of being-the-locus-of and being-the-delimitor-of-the-counterpositive-ness-of-difference-from-what-resides-in-oneself. The delimitor-hood-of-counterpositive-ness is through the relation of dependence-on-co-absence-residing-in-something-different-from-itself. And here, either the portion ending in 'satya' or the qualificandum portion alone — only one of the two should be adopted. If both are included,

children.text:
prayojanavirahāt
tādṛśaviśiṣṭābhāva eva svatantrānvayavyatirekaśūnyatvam/
children.translated_text: there would be no purpose served. The absence of what is qualified in such a manner is itself the state of being devoid of independent co-presence and co-absence.

children.text:
1. tādṛśasattetyādi/
prakṛtakāryasattāprayojakasattāviśiṣṭatve sati
prakṛtakāryavyatirekaprayojakavyatirekaviśiṣṭatvamityarthaḥ/
prakṛtakārya paṭaḥ tatsattāprayojakasattāśrayatvaṃ tantoḥ/ evaṃ
tādṛśasattāniṣṭhaḥ yo bhedaḥ svabhinnagatānvayādhīnatvasaṃbandhena
tantumadbhedaḥ tatpratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ tantau/ evaṃ
pakṛkāryavyatirekaḥ paṭābhāvaḥ tatprayojako yo vyatirekaḥ
tantvabhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvarūpaṃ tadāśrayatvaṃ tantau/ evaṃ
tādṛśavyatirekaniṣṭhaḥ yaḥ svabhinnagatavyatirekādhīnatvasaṃbandhena
tantumadbhedaḥ tatpratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ tantāviti samanvayo
draṣṭavyaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. Regarding 'being qualified by such existence' etc. — the meaning is: being qualified by absence that is productive of the absence of the relevant effect, while being qualified by existence that is productive of the existence of the relevant effect. The relevant effect is cloth; the locus of existence that produces its existence is thread. Similarly, the difference that resides in such existence — through the relation of dependence-on-co-presence-residing-in-something-different-from-itself — is the difference from thread; the delimitor-hood of its counterpositive-ness resides in thread. Similarly, the co-absence of the relevant effect is the absence of cloth; its producer, the co-absence, is the absence of thread; the locus-hood in the form of counterpositive-ness resides in thread. Similarly, the difference that resides in such co-absence — through the relation of dependence-on-co-absence-residing-in-something-different-from-itself — is the difference from thread; the delimitor-hood of its counterpositive-ness resides in thread. This correlation should be understood thus.

children.text:
1vastutastu
svāśrayānvayavyatirekaprayuktatvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena
svaviśiṣṭānvayavyatirekavattvasvapratiyogitvobhayasambandhena vā
bhedaviśiṣṭatvamityanugamaḥ/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svapratiyogītarānvayavyatirekādhīnatvasambandhena
svāvacchinnabhedavattāsambandheneti/ tattu
tādātmyādirūpādhikapadārthaniveśanagauravādupekṣaṇīyamiti
dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: 1. In reality, the <s>anugama</s> (formulation) is: being qualified by difference through the relation of possessing-co-presence-and-co-absence-qualified-by-counterpositive-ness-whose-delimitor-hood-resides-in-itself-delimited-by-the-relation-of-being-productive-of-co-presence-and-co-absence-of-one's-own-locus, or through both relations of possessing-co-presence-and-co-absence-qualified-by-oneself and being-the-counterpositive-of-oneself. And the qualification of oneself is through the relation of dependence-on-co-presence-and-co-absence-of-things-other-than-one's-own-counterpositive, through the relation of possessing-difference-delimited-by-oneself. However, this should be noted as negligible due to the cumbersomeness of introducing additional entities in the form of <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) and so forth.

children.text:
yattu - 'yenaiva yasya
yaṃ prati pūrvavṛttitvamavagamyate' ityādyuktyaiva sāmañjasye
sahaśabdaveyarthyamiti - tanna - tathā sati sasyeti
ṣaṣṭyarthaviśeṣyatvānvayinaḥ avacchinnatvasya tṛtīyārthatyā
prakṛtakāryaniyatapūrvavṛttitvajñānīyayanniṣṭhaviśeṣyatāsāmānyaṃ
yadavacchinnamiti lakṣaṇaṃ sampadyate/ tatra
cāvacchedakakoṭipraviṣṭasyāvacchedakatvānādare daṇḍatvādāvavyāpteḥ/
sahaśabdopādāne cāsmaduktārthaparyavasānena doṣavirahāditi/ ata
eva tanatusamavetatvādiviśiṣṭarūpādestantutvādinānyathāsiddhiṃrapi
suvaceti dhyeyamiti bhāvaḥ/ tantutvasya tadvyaktitvena kāraṇatve 'pi
prathamānyathāsiddhimupapādayatāṃ matamāha - [127] itarānvayeti/
svānvayavyatirekavattvasvabhinnatvobhayasaṃbandhena
kiñcidviśiṣṭatvamanyathāsiddhatvamiti tu niṣkarṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: As for the objection that — 'the word <s>saha</s> (together) becomes purposeless since consistency is achieved merely by the reasoning beginning with "by which very thing, of which, with respect to which, antecedent-ness is cognized"' — that is not so — because in that case, the definition would amount to: the <s>viśeṣyatā-sāmānya</s> (general qualificandum-ness) residing in the correlate of 'yat' in the cognition of invariable-antecedent-ness-of-the-relevant-effect, delimited by the <s>avacchinnatva</s> (delimitedness) whose qualificandum-status is the meaning of the genitive 'of which' and whose third-case meaning is the delimitor. And there, if the delimitor-hood of what has entered the delimitor-position is disregarded, there would be under-extension in cases like <s>daṇḍatva</s> (staff-ness). But with the inclusion of the word <s>saha</s>, since the result is the meaning we have stated, there is no defect — this is the purport. Even though <s>tantutva</s> is a cause as an instance thereof, the view of those who establish the first type of otherwise-establishment is stated — [127] 'of-the-other co-presence' etc. The conclusion is that being qualified by something through both relations of possessing-one's-own-co-presence-and-co-absence and being-different-from-oneself constitutes <s>anyathāsiddhatva</s> (otherwise-established-ness).

children.text:
dīpikāyām anyaṃ pratītyādi/ anyaṃ prati
prakṛtakāryetarakāryaṃ prati/ 'pūrvavṛttitve' ityatra saptamyāḥ 'yasya ca
bhāvena'ityuktanyāyena jñānamarthaḥ/ tasya ca
janyatāsambandhenāvagame 'nvayaḥ/ tathā ca
prakṛtakāryetarakāryapūrvavṛttitvaprakārakajñānādhīnaprakṛtakāryapūvravṛttitvaprakārakajñānaviśeṣyatvaṃ
dvitīyānyathāsiddhasya lakṣaṇamiti phalitam/ tatra ca kāraṇatājñānaṃ
viśiṣṭānuyogikavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhitayā
viśeṣyatāvacchedakaprakārakanirṇayaṃ niyamato 'pekṣata iti
lakṣaṇagamanamityāśayenāha prakāśikāyām [127] tathā ceti/
anekadravyasamavetatveti/ aṇubhinnadravyatvetyarthaḥ/ [128] tadupasthiteḥ -- prāgabhāvopasthiteḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'with respect to another' etc. — 'with respect to another' means with respect to an effect other than the relevant effect. In 'in antecedent-ness,' the locative has the meaning of cognition, according to the maxim stated as 'and by the existence of which.' And its co-presence is through the relation of being-produced. Thus the result is that the definition of the second type of <s>anyathāsiddha</s> (otherwise-established) is: the qualificandum-ness in the cognition whose content is antecedent-ness-of-the-relevant-effect that depends on the cognition whose content is antecedent-ness-of-an-effect-other-than-the-relevant-effect. And therein, since the causal cognition, by virtue of apprehending qualification with a qualified correlate, necessarily requires the determination of the content that delimits the qualificandum-ness — with this intent, the <s>Prakāśikā</s> states [127] 'and thus' etc. 'Co-inherent in many substances' means: in substance-ness different from atoms — this is the meaning. [128] 'Of that presentation' — of the presentation of prior absence.

children.text:
1. vastutastu
svāśrayānvayetyādi/ sarvatra svaśabdaḥ tanvādibhedaparaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. Regarding 'in reality, of one's own locus, co-presence' etc. — everywhere the word 'sva' (self/own) refers to differences such as thread and so forth.

children.text: kāraṇavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of causes.

children.text:
saṃgrahe
yatsamavetamityādi/ kāryamityatra yadityādiḥ kāryaṃ yatsamavetaṃ
sadutpadyata iti yojanayā yatsamavetaṃ pratiyogitayā
yadanuyogikasamavāyavat utpadyata ityarthaḥ/ dhātvartha
ādyakṣaṇāvacchinnādheyatvam/ ākhyātārtha āśrayatvam/
udśyavidheyabhāvamahimnā tādṛśasamavāyāvacchinnatvamādheyatāyāṃ
bhāsate/ sadantaviśeṣaṇatāvacchedakasyoddeśyatāvacchedakatvaniyamāt/
uddeśyavidheyabhāvasthale
uddeśyatāvacchedakavidheyayoravacchedyāvacchedakabhāvabhānavyutpatteḥ/ tatha
ca yatkāryaṃ yadanuyogikasamavāyāvacchinnatādṛśādheyatāvat tatkāryaṃ
prati tatsamavāyikāraṇamiti vākyārthaḥ/ atra ca yattatpadayoḥ
kāryakāraṇavyaktiparatve kāryakāraṇabhāvāntyamityālocya tayoḥ
yattaddharmāvacchinnaparatāmabhisandhāyāha - prakāśikāyām [134] yaddharmāvacchinnamityādinā/ evaṃ ca
samavāyasambanadhāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitatādātmyasaṃbandhāvacchinnakāraṇatvaṃ
samavāyikāraṇasya lakṣaṇaṃ phalitam/ tatra ca ghaṭādipratyakṣe
ghaṭādirūpaviṣayasya tādātmyasambandhena kāraṇatvāt
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṃgraha</s>, 'that in which it is co-inherent' etc. — In the word 'effect,' supplying 'which' etc.: by construing as 'that which, being co-inherent, comes into existence,' the meaning is: that which comes into existence possessing <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) whose correlate is the counterpositive-ness of co-inherence. The meaning of the verbal root is being-the-superstratum delimited by the first moment. The meaning of the finite verb is being-the-locus. By the force of the topic-comment relation, the delimitation by such <s>samavāya</s> appears in the superstratum-ness. Because the delimitor of the topic-status is necessarily the delimitor of the predicate-status for the qualifier ending in 'sat.' In the context of the topic-comment relation, there is the convention that the topic-delimitor and the predicate have the relation of delimited and delimitor. Thus the sentence meaning is: that which has superstratum-ness delimited by <s>samavāya</s> whose correlate is the counterpositive of the effect — with respect to that effect, that is the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause). And here, considering that if the 'yat' and 'tat' words refer to particular instances of effect and cause, causal relation would be a last member — intending their reference as delimited by particular properties, the <s>Prakāśikā</s> states [134] 'delimited by which property' etc. Thus the resultant definition of <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> is: causal-ness delimited by <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) relation that determines the effect-ness delimited by <s>samavāya</s> relation. And therein, since in the perception of a pot etc., the content in the form of pot etc. possesses causal-ness through the <s>tādātmya</s> relation,

children.text:
ghaṭādiviṣayasya
svapratyakṣaṃ prati samavāyikāraṇatāvāraṇāya kāryatāyāṃ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvaniveśanam/
pratyakṣaniṣṭhaviṣayanirūpitakāryatāyāḥ viṣayatāsaṃbandhāvacchinnatvāt
na doṣaḥ/ asamavāyikāraṇe 'tivyāpitavāraṇāya kāraṇatāyāṃ
tādātmyasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvaniveśaḥ/
children.translated_text: to prevent the content of pot etc. from having <s>samavāyikāraṇatā</s> (inherent-cause-ness) with respect to its own perception, the delimitation by <s>samavāya</s> relation is included in the effect-ness. Since the effect-ness determined by the content residing in perception is delimited by the content-relation, there is no defect. To prevent over-extension to the <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause), the delimitation by <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) relation is included in the causal-ness.

children.text:
saṃgrahe [133] kāryeṇa kāraṇena vā sahetyādi/ atra ca kāryeṇa sahaikasminnarthe
samevataṃ sat yatkāraṇaṃ tadekaṃ asamavāyikāraṇam/ kāraṇena
sahaikasminnarthe samavetaṃ sat yatkāraṇaṃ tadapadaṃ asamavāyikāraṇamiti
vākyabhedena yojanā/ vākāraśca etaddyotaka eva/ sahaśabdārthaḥ
sahitatvam, tacca prakṛte adhikaraṇaniyapitatvarūpam
samavetapadārthatāvacchedakasamavetatve anvitam/ kāryeṇetyatra
tṛtīyāyāḥ adhikaraṇatānvayinirūpitatvamarthaḥ/ ekapadamatra
yatkiñcitparam/ arthapadottarasaptamyāḥ nirūpitatvamarthaḥ/ tathā ca
kāryādhikaraṇanirūpitayatkiñcidarthaniyapitasamavetatvavat
kāraṇamiti eko vākyārthaḥ/ evaṃ kāraṇenetyādivākye 'pi bodhyam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṃgraha</s> [133], 'together with the effect or the cause' etc. — here the construal is by dividing the sentence: that cause which, being co-inherent in one entity together with the effect, is one type of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause); and that cause which, being co-inherent in one entity together with the [inherent] cause, is the other type of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>. The particle 'vā' (or) is merely indicative of this distinction. The meaning of the word <s>saha</s> (together) is being-associated, and in the present context this has the nature of being-determined-by-the-substratum, construed with co-inherence that is the delimitor of the entity designated by the word 'co-inherent.' In 'with the effect,' the meaning of the instrumental case is being-determined-by-the-substratum-ness construed with the locus. The word 'one' here means 'some particular.' The locative following the word 'entity' has the meaning of being-determined. Thus one sentence-meaning is: a cause that possesses co-inherence determined by some-particular-entity determined by the substratum of the effect. The same should be understood in the sentence beginning with 'with the cause' as well.

children.text:
vastutaḥ saṃgrahe [133] kāryeṇa sahetyādi/ atra sahaśabdārthaṃḥ sāhityam/
taccaikakriyānvayitvarūpam/ prakṛte
samavetatvanirūpakatvaparyavasitam/ kāryeṇetyatra tṛtīyārtha
ādheyatvam, ekaśabdo 'dhikaraṇaparaḥ/ artha ityatra
samavetatvānvayinirūpitatvamarthaḥ/ tathā ca
kāryaniṣṭhasamevatatvanirūpakībhūtādhikaraṇārthanirūpitasamevatatvavadityartha
iti phalitam/ kāraṇenetyādāvapi evameva bodhyamiti tu sāram/
kāraṇenetyatra kasya kāraṇamityākāṅkṣāyāṃ āha - prakāśikāyām [134] svakāryeti/ svakāryasya samavāyikāraṇenetyarthaḥ/ atra ca
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitasamavāyasvāśrayasamavetatvānyatarasambandhāvacchinnakāraṇatvaṃ
asamavāyikāraṇasāmānyasya lakṣaṇam/ kāraṇatāyāṃ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvamātraniveśe prathamāsamavāyikāraṇasya
svāśrayasamavetatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvamātraniveśe
dvitīyāsamavāyikāraṇasya ca tadeva lakṣaṇaṃ bodhyam/
dravyavṛttilaukikaviṣayatāsaṃbandhena
dravyasamavetavṛttilaukikaviṣayatāsaṃbandhena ca pratyakṣaṃ prati
samavāyena svāśrayasamavetatvasaṃbandhena ca hetubhūte
udbhūtarūpādāvativyāptivāraṇāya lakṣaṇadvaye 'pi kāryatāyāṃ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvaniveśaḥ/ dvitīyāsamavāyikāraṇe
ativyāptivāraṇāya prathamāsamavāyikāraṇalakṣaṇe kāraṇatāyāṃ
samavāyasambandhāvacchinnatvaniveśaḥ/ prathamāsamavāyikāraṇe
ativyāptivāraṇāya dvitīyāsamavāyikāraṇalakṣaṇe tatra
children.translated_text: In reality, in the <s>Saṃgraha</s> [133], 'together with the effect' etc. — here the meaning of the word <s>saha</s> is association. And that has the nature of being-connected-with-a-single-action. In the present context, it amounts to being-the-determinant-of-co-inherence. In 'with the effect,' the instrumental meaning is superstratum-ness; the word 'one' refers to the substratum. In the word 'entity,' the meaning is being-determined construed with co-inherence. Thus the result is that the meaning is: possessing co-inherence that determines the substratum-entity that is the determinant of the co-inherence residing in the effect. The same should be understood in the passage beginning with 'with the cause' as well — this is the essence. In 'with the cause,' when the question arises 'cause of what?,' the <s>Prakāśikā</s> answers [134] 'of its own effect' etc. — meaning: with the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause) of its own effect. And here, the definition of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause) in general is: causal-ness delimited by either the relation of co-inherence-in-the-locus-of-samavāya or the <s>samavāya</s> relation, which determines the effect-ness delimited by <s>samavāya</s> relation. When only the delimitation by <s>samavāya</s> relation is included in the causal-ness, this should be understood as the definition of the first type of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>; when only the delimitation by the relation of co-inherence-in-one's-own-locus is included, it is the definition of the second type of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>. To prevent over-extension to manifested <s>rūpa</s> (color) etc., which serve as causes of perception through <s>samavāya</s> and co-inherence-in-one's-own-locus relations respectively — with respect to perception through the relation of content-ness-of-substance-residing and content-ness-of-what-resides-in-substance-co-inherent — the delimitation by <s>samavāya</s> relation is included in the effect-ness in both definitions. To prevent over-extension to the second type of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>, the delimitation by <s>samavāya</s> relation is included in the causal-ness of the definition of the first type of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>. To prevent over-extension to the first type of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>, in the definition of the second type of <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>, therein

children.text:
svāśrayasamavetatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvaniveśeḥ/ atra
coktānyatarasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvasthale
samavāyasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasvāśrayasamavetatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchidakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvobhayasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogi tākabhedavattvasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvaṃ
niveśanīyamityavadheyam/ tṛrītantusaṃyogāderapi
tṛrīpaṭasaṃyogādikaṃ pratyasamavāyikāraṇatvāt
asamavāyikāraṇasāmānyalakṣaṇe
tadbhinnatvaniveśanamavyāptisampādakamityālocya uktam
tattadasamavāyikāraṇalakṣaṇa iti/ [134] digiti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ --
samavāyena paṭaṃ prati saṃyogena turyā eva kāraṇatvasvīkārāt na
viśeṣaṇalakṣaṇe 'pi tadbhinnatvaṃ niveśanīyamiti tu na samyak/
niyatapūrvavṛttitvalakṣaṇasya kāraṇatvasya

iti/
children.translated_text: because of including the relation of being inherent in one's own substratum (<s>svāśrayasamavetatva</s>). And here, it should be noted that in the case where the stated 'either of the two relations' (<s>anyatarasaṃbandhāvacchinnatva</s>) applies, what should be included is: the delimitation by the relation that is either — the relation of difference from [something] whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the inherence-relation (<s>samavāya</s>) and whose counter-positive-hood is not delimited by [counter-positiveness] residing in itself, or the relation of being inherent in one's own substratum, [with counter-positiveness similarly specified], or both relations [jointly specified]. Since even the contact of the third thread and the like is a non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) of the contact of the third cloth and the like, the inclusion of 'being different from that' in the general definition of non-inherent cause would create under-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) — having considered this, [the author of the <s>Bālapriyā</s>] stated the definition of each respective non-inherent cause. [134] 'Direction' (<s>dik</s>) and so forth — the intent is as follows: since, through inherence, it is only the fourth [thread] that is accepted as a cause with respect to the cloth through contact, the inclusion of 'being different from that' is not required even in the qualified definition — but this is not correct, because the causal nature (<s>kāraṇatva</s>) defined as invariable prior occurrence is unimpaired even in the contact of the fourth thread. Although even so there would be over-pervasion of the qualified definition in the case of the contact of thread with space and the like, and although including 'being different from that' would involve great cumbersomeness, nevertheless, by including the qualifier 'being inherent in threads and the like alone' — which amounts to 'not being inherent in anything other than threads and the like' — there is no defect.

children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s> [133], 'different from both' (<s>tadubhayabhinna</s>) and so forth. In the definition of efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>), the word 'both' (<s>tadubhaya</s>) refers to the pair of inherent cause and non-inherent cause — this he says with: in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [133], 'inherent' (<s>samavāyī</s>) and so forth. And here, the definition should be stated as: an efficient cause is that which is a cause of an effect qualified by that [same] effect. And the qualification is through the three-fold relation of: being different from [something] whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of being an inherent cause as determined by itself, being different from [something] whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of being a non-inherent cause as determined by itself, and the three-fold causal relation as determined by itself. Although in the case of destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) and the like, the counter-positive and so forth would fail to be efficient causes — since for a negative effect, inherent cause and the like are not established — nevertheless, by including the qualification of the effect through the three-fold relation involving the absence of [something] whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of being an inherent cause as determined by itself, the absence of [something] whose counter-positiveness is delimited by the relation of being a non-inherent cause as determined by itself, and the three-fold causal relation, there is no defect. Destruction and the like

children.text:
prati
samavāyikāraṇatvādervyadhikaraṇasambandhatayā
tādṛśasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatadabhāvasaulabhyāt/ ata eva
turyādeḥ svagatarūpādau samavāyikāraṇatvādimattve 'pi
sāmānyatassamavāyyādibhinnatvāsambhavanibandhanā na kṣatiriti/
children.translated_text: with respect to [the effect], since the inherent-causal relation and the like operate as a relation in a different locus (<s>vyadhikaraṇasambandha</s>), and since the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by such a relation is easily available — for this very reason, even though the fourth [thread] and the like possess inherent causality and so forth with respect to their own internal qualities (<s>svagatarūpa</s>) and the like, since it is impossible in general for them to be different from the inherent cause and the like, there is no defect.

children.translated_text: 'Because of not being a determiner of the object-hood of the fourth' — otherwise, due to the absence of having an object, even cognition-hood (<s>jñānatva</s>) itself would be lost for indeterminate perception (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>). Because since cognition-hood is pervaded by having an object, when the pervader is negated, the negation of the pervaded necessarily follows — this is the intent. Because in indeterminate perception, just as the pot and the like appear through the sense-contact (<s>cakṣussaṃyoga</s>), so too pot-ness and inherence, through the sense-contacts of 'inherent in what is conjoined with the eye' and 'qualifier of what is conjoined with the eye,' their appearance too is unavoidable. children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s> [135], 'produced from the contact of sense-organ and object' and so forth — this is with the intention that only produced perception is the definiendum. Therefore, since <s>Īśvara</s>'s (God's) perception is eternal, the doubt of under-pervasion with respect to it is removed, because it is not a definiendum. Otherwise, by including [the property of] being produced that is not produced from the prior contact of sense-organ and object, through the relation of difference whose counter-positiveness is not delimited by [something] residing in itself and delimited by the absence-of-both relation residing in what is produced, the inclusion [of divine perception] through being qualified by being produced from the contact of sense-organ and object is to be understood. Here, although there is over-pervasion in inference and the like, because the contact of self and mind (<s>ātmamanaḥsaṃyoga</s>) is a general cause of cognition in general; the mind

children.translated_text: cognition-hood (<s>jñānatva</s>) is the definition. Since inference and the like have cognitions such as knowledge of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) and the like as their instruments, there is no over-pervasion there. Since <s>Īśvara</s>'s perception is unproduced [and eternal]. And since in produced perception, it is the sense-organ alone that has instrument-hood — thus the definition is consistent. Since indeterminate perception (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) is a cause of determinate perception (<s>savikalpaka</s>), instrument-hood is included [in the definition] — thus they say.

children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [137] 'perception of substance' and so forth. Here, it should be stated that the causality of eye-contact (<s>cakṣuḥ-saṃyoga</s>) with respect to visual perception (<s>cākṣuṣa</s>) is through inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), by the relation of ordinary objecthood (<s>laukika-viṣayatā</s>) residing in substance. To prevent deviation in cases of color and the like, the qualifier 'residing in substance' is introduced on the effect side. To prevent deviation by taking into account the extraordinary visual perception whose objects are past and future pots not connected with the eye, generated through <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa pratyāsatti</s> (extraordinary perceptual contact through universals) such as pot-ness, the qualifier 'ordinary' (<s>laukikatva</s>) is introduced. Similarly, in the case of a staff and the like, in the visual cognition generated through <s>jñāna-pratyāsatti</s> (perceptual contact through prior knowledge) of the form 'this formerly possessed a staff,' the same should be understood. Similarly, with respect to visual perception through the relation of ordinary objecthood residing in what inheres in a substance, the causality of contact-with-what-is-conjoined-by-inherence (<s>cakṣuḥ-saṃyukta-samavāya</s>) is through the intrinsic relation (<s>svarūpa-sambandha</s>). Here, on the view that the series of parts terminates at the triad (<s>tryaṇuka</s>), the qualifier 'residing in another [entity]' is [added] on the effect side to prevent deviation in the triad. Although, even with the introduction of 'residing in what inheres in substance,' the same difficulty arises on the view that accepts atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), nevertheless there is no fault because substance-otherness is accepted as a qualifier of the inherence-qualifier. And the qualifier 'residing in another' should be understood as preventing deviation in the perception of universals such as color-ness (<s>rūpatva</s>) and the like. To prevent deviation by taking into account the extraordinary visual perception whose objects are past colors and the like, generated through <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa pratyāsatti</s> of color-ness and the like, the qualifier 'ordinary' is introduced in the objecthood. Similarly in the case of blue and the like, even in the perception generated through <s>jñāna-pratyāsatti</s> of the form 'this formerly possessed blue color,' since the inherence determined by the qualification of eye-contact is absent, the same [qualification] also prevents deviation. Similarly, with respect to visual perception through the relation of ordinary objecthood residing in what inheres in what inheres in a substance, the causality of contact-with-what-is-conjoined-by-inherence-of-the-inherent (<s>cakṣuḥ-saṃyukta-samaveta-samavāya</s>) [obtains]. To prevent deviation from the yogic visual perception of all objects generated through <s>yoga-ja dharma pratyāsatti</s> (perceptual contact through yogic merit), and from the visual perception of all universals generated through <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa pratyāsatti</s> of universal-ness (<s>jātitva</s>), the qualifier 'ordinary' is introduced here. On the view of independent triads, the qualifier 'residing in another' prevents deviation in triads and their colors and the like. Even on other views, that [qualifier] must be introduced to prevent the accidentality of such objecthood. With respect to auditory perception (<s>śrāvaṇa pratyakṣa</s>) through the relation of ordinary objecthood residing in sound, the causality of inherence-in-the-ear (<s>śrotra-samavāya</s>) [obtains]; the qualifier 'residing in another' prevents deviation in sound-ness and the like. To prevent deviation from the perception of past sounds and the like generated through <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa pratyāsatti</s> of sound-ness, and from such perception generated through <s>yoga-ja pratyāsatti</s>, the qualifier 'ordinary' is introduced. With respect to auditory perception through the relation of ordinary objecthood residing in what inheres in sound, the causality of inherence-in-what-inheres-in-the-ear (<s>śrotra-samaveta-samavāya</s>) [obtains]. The qualifier 'residing [in another]' prevents deviation in the case of sound. To prevent deviation from the perception of universals such as the <s>ka</s>-class-ness and the like residing in past and future [sounds], generated through <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa pratyāsatti</s> of universal-ness, the qualifier 'ordinary' is introduced. The same should be understood elsewhere as well.

And if they are unified under the common concept of qualifier-relation, then why should not contact-by-inherence (<s>saṃyukta-samavāya</s>) and the rest also be unified under the concept of inherence? — He dispels this doubt with [138] 'here the following should be noted' and so forth.

children.translated_text: 'The sensory contact of qualifier-qualificand relation' — the meaning is: the sensory contact that is either qualificand-ness or qualifier-ness. [142] 'At the time of perceiving the pot' and so forth — since the determinate cognition of something's possessing [a pot] is an obstructor precisely with respect to the cognition of possessing the absence of that [pot], which is not generated by ordinary sensory contact, there is the undesirable consequence of perceptual cognition of the absence of the pot, generated through ordinary sensory contact, at the time of the determinate cognition of the pot's presence. And it cannot be said that there is no undesirable consequence of perceiving the absence of a pot in a place that has a pot, because of the very absence of the object in the form of pot-absence — nor can it be said: how can the determinate cognition of pot-possession arise when the pot is absent? — because even in a place devoid of a pot, the determinate cognition of pot-possession in the form of error is possible through a sensory contact constituted by a different substrate (<s>dharmin</s>), and hence the undesirable consequence of perception of pot-absence is possible there too; and even in a place that has a pot, the undesirable consequence of perception of pot-absence is possible through the force of a sensory contact constituted by a different substrate. [141] 'The status of being a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>' and so forth — although by the etymology 'another <s>pramāṇa</s> is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>,' what is obtained is instrumentality for valid cognition beyond perception and the rest, and the Naiyāyikas too accept non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) as functioning in the role of an auxiliary — because they accept that [non-apprehension], being of the nature of absence, is the instrument of knowledge of absence — nevertheless, accepting the transposition of the word 'other' (<s>antara</s>), what is intended is: instrumentality for valid cognition that is different in kind from perception and the rest, amounting to instrumentality for a valid cognition of a different species from perceptual and other valid cognitions — hence there is no defect, since the Naiyāyikas accept the valid cognition of absence as being of the nature of perception. Hence it is said later 'the postulation of instrumentality for a cognition of a different species.' Lest it be objected that since the fitness [condition] in non-apprehension is established by the [text] ending with 'it would be perceived,' the clause 'because of the absence of seeing, it does not exist' is redundant — he introduces [the next topic]

And thus, the contradiction with the expectation of existence is the capacity to obstruct the certainty of the exclusion of the reducible that is a component thereof. And since the capacity to obstruct belongs only to the non-defeasible (<s>anāhārya</s>), it is non-defeasibility alone that should be intended by the qualifier 'contradiction' — otherwise, at the time of apprehending a counter-positive that is defeasible, the consequence of non-apprehension of absence would not follow. Thus they say [142] 'the qualifier of contradiction.' Anticipating the objection that in darkness, the consequence of perceiving the absence of a pot would arise due to the absence of fit apprehension, he states the precise meaning with [142] 'when the counter-positive exists' and so forth — meaning: the object of the consequence generated by the <s>āpatti</s> whose object is the existence of the counter-positive. [142] 'In brief' — here the intent is: in every case of perception of absence, the <s>āpatti</s> (consequence) 'if the counter-positive were there, it would be apprehended' must arise, and there is no means of knowledge [for absence] without it. [142] With 'when the existence of the counter-positive is reduced' and so forth — what is intended is the pervader-ness determined by the pervaded-ness residing in the counter-positive. Further details should be seen in the <s>Muktāvalī-Prakāśa</s> and the like.
