children.translated_text: prevent [the consequence] by introducing that [refined fitness] — he states the view of certain [scholars] who explain the <s>Dīpikā</s> sentence beginning with 'reasoned' (<s>tarkita</s>) and so forth differently — with [142] 'some, however.' Hence, merely by giving the qualifier of being effected by such [reasoning] in the absence of apprehension [the problem is solved]. [142] 'They say' — this indicates that it is not in accord with the author's own intent. The basis for that [dissent] is: if the existence of the counter-positive [is already established], the qualifier 'being reasoned' (<s>tarkitatva</s>) would be redundant. On the former view, however, the word 'reasoned' (<s>tarkita</s>) is useful as indicating the purport of introducing the fitness [condition] in non-apprehension. On this [alternative] view, since the fitness itself takes the form of being effected by the absence of the cause in the form of the existence of the counter-positive, and since that is already obtained by the expression 'contradictory to the existence of the counter-positive,' the word 'reasoned' has no use anywhere. Furthermore, since there is no difference in absence based on difference in substratum (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), the consequence of perceiving the absence of a pot in darkness is not averted. To remedy the deficiency, he says [143] 'here the following.' [143] 'Among those' — among the three types of <s>pratyāsatti</s> (perceptual contacts) that have been shown. Objection: How is such a meaning obtained? — to this he says [143] 'universal' and so forth. [143] 'That' — meaning: the universal such as smoke-ness and the like. [143] 'That' — meaning: the universal (<s>jāti</s>). In '<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>' (characterized by a universal), to accommodate both the reading where the word 'universal' refers to knowledge thereof and the literal reading, he says [142] 'the object, or...' Objection: When the matter is accomplished by the stated sensory contacts in the form of eye-contact and the like, what is the need for accepting this [extraordinary] <s>pratyāsatti</s>? — to this he says [143] 'past' and so forth. Objection: Why should there not be perception of that without any sensory contact of the sense organ? — to this he says [143] 'of the sense organs.' 'Of those not in contact' is to be connected with 'perception,' and 'for the purpose of that' and so forth [should be supplied]. [143] 'Appearance' — 'is useful' should be connected. Objection: Why can the matter not be accomplished by contact-with-what-is-conjoined-by-inherence alone? — to this he says [143] 'by fragrance.' The sensory contact such as contact-with-what-is-conjoined-by-inherence is the cause of perception only for objects fit to be grasped by that sense organ, not for objects unfit to be grasped by that sense organ — because otherwise the distinction between qualities graspable and not graspable by a given sense organ could not be established — with this intent, 'fitness' is stated. Intending the delimitor of causality-relation and the like stated in the <s>Muktāvalī-Prakāśa</s>, he says 'in brief.'

children.translated_text: 'The relevance of being dependent on perception' — the meaning is: the effect of perception, that is, of the sense organ such as the eye which constitutes the means of perceptual knowledge, is dependence [of inference upon it]; and the relevance thereof is by way of a definition of its true nature. The meaning of the third [case-ending] is: being occasioned by the desire to know generated by cognition that connects with the object of inquiry. And in the cognition, the meaning of the verbal base connects in the mode of objecthood. The demonstration of relevance is to prevent inattention due to the suspicion that it is the babbling of a madman, arising from the knowledge that the subjects are unconnected. It should also be seen that another purpose of demonstrating relevance is the comprehension of syntactic unity (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) between the preceding and subsequent texts. And such comprehension is [established] by the inference: 'the text on inference possesses syntactic unity with the text on perception, because it expounds a subject connected with the subject expounded in the text on perception' — further elaboration is found elsewhere. From the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement [147] 'defines' (<s>lakṣayati</s>), the meaning obtained is: [the author] possesses effort favorable to producing a word that generates cognition having the definition as its qualifier. And since later, the essential nature, divisions, and the like are also expounded, lest there be a deficiency through not announcing those, it is said 'elucidates' (<s>nirūpayati</s>). And elucidation is a word favorable to cognition having as its qualifier any one of the definition, essential nature, validity, and the like — hence there is no deficiency. The same should be understood going forward. In the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, [147] 'the instrument of inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>) is inference (<s>anumāna</s>).' Since the word <s>anumāna</s> has a figurative usage delimited by <s>anumāna</s>-word-meaning-ness, on the view that there is no secondary meaning in the first member of the compound (<s>tatpuruṣa</s>),

children.translated_text: [Footnote 1:] Now, in the root text '<s>anumitikaraṇam anumānam</s>' ('inference is the instrument of inferential cognition'), since the word <s>anumāna</s> has the sense of 'instrument of <s>anumiti</s>,' the sentence-meaning culminates in '<s>anumitikaraṇam anumitikaraṇam</s>' (the instrument of inferential cognition is the instrument of inferential cognition). In a case of identity-predication, since the difference between the delimiter of subject-hood and the delimiter of predicate-hood must be accepted to prevent the invalidity of a sentence like '<s>ghaṭo ghaṭaḥ</s>' (a pot is a pot), and since <s>anumitikaraṇatva</s> (being the instrument of inferential cognition) itself would be both the delimiter of subject-hood and of predicate-hood — how can the stated sentence have validity? Addressing this, he says 'of the word <s>anumāna</s>.' Accordingly, <s>anumitikaraṇatva</s> is the delimiter of subject-hood, and <s>anumānapadārthatva</s> (being the referent of the word <s>anumāna</s>) is the delimiter of predicate-hood; since these two are different, the sentence-meaning 'the instrument of inferential cognition is non-different from the referent of the word <s>anumāna</s>' is not problematic — this is the purport.

vidheyatāvacchedakamiti tayorbhedāt
anumānapadasyānumitikaraṇārthakatve 'pi na nirākāṅkṣateti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 2:] 'On the alternative where secondary denotation of the first part is absent' — on the alternative where the first part [of the compound] has no secondary denotation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), the delimiter of subject-hood is 'being an instrument non-different from the relatum of <s>anumiti</s>,' and the delimiter of predicate-hood is <s>anumitikaraṇatva</s>; since these two are different, even when the word <s>anumāna</s> has the sense of 'instrument of <s>anumiti</s>,' there is no completeness of expectancy [that would make the sentence tautological] — this is the purport.

children.text:
1tena tātmādau
ativyāptiḥ/ nanu parāmarśajanyaṃ jñānamityanumiterlakṣaṇaṃ
kimarthamuktam? na ca ghaṭitajñāne ghaṭakajñānasya
kāraṇatvādanumitijñānamantarā tadghaṭitānumānalakṣaṇajñānaṃ na
sambhavatīti taduktisāphalyāmiti vācyam/
tathāpyanumitisvarūpapradarśanamātraṇaiva tannisaddheḥ
tallakṣaṇakathanānupayogāt ityāśaṅkya tallakṣaṇākathate 'numānasya
pramāṇāntaratvaṃ na sidhyati pratyakṣānumitipramityoḥ
vyāvṛttalakṣaṇābhyāṃ vailakṣaṇye ajñāte sati
pratyakṣādyatiriktapramāṇatvasādhyakānumitikaraṇatvahetukānumāne
vyabhicāraśaṅkāyā durvāratvāt/ ataḥ saṅgrahe
anumitilakṣaṇakathanamucitamityabhiprāyeṇa bhāvamāha - [147] tathā ceti/
children.translated_text: By that [definition], there is over-pervasion to the Self etc. Now, what is the purpose of stating the definition of <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition) as 'cognition born of <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection)'? Nor should one say that since knowledge of a constituent is a cause of the composite knowledge, the knowledge of the definition of <s>anumāna</s> — which involves [the concept of] <s>anumiti</s> — is not possible without the cognition of <s>anumiti</s>, and hence the statement [of the definition] has utility. Even so, anticipating the objection that merely demonstrating the nature of <s>anumiti</s> would suffice for that purpose, and stating its definition would be useless — [the commentator] states the intention: without stating the definition of <s>anumiti</s>, the distinctness of <s>anumāna</s> as a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) cannot be established; because when the definitional difference between perceptual cognition and inferential cognition is unknown, the suspicion of deviation in the inference having as its probandum 'being a means of valid cognition distinct from perception etc.' and as its probans 'being the instrument of <s>anumiti</s>' would be irremediable. Therefore, with the intention that stating the definition of <s>anumiti</s> in the <s>Saṅgraha</s> is appropriate, he states the purport — [with] 'and accordingly.'

children.text: anumitilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>anumiti</s> (inferential cognition)

children.text:
nanu saṃśayottarapratyakṣa iti
dīpikāvākyamasaṅgatam, 'nāyaṃ puruṣa' iti
viparītaniścayottarapratyakṣe 'pyativyāptisambhavena tadakathanena
nyūnatāpatterityāśaṅkya dīpikāvākyasthasaṃśayapadaṃ
virītajñānamātropalakṣaṇaparamityabhiprāyeṇāha - [188] viparītajñānottarapratyakṣaṃ pratīti/ [148] aṅgīkurvatāmiti/
miśrādīnāmiti śeṣaḥ/ etena prātyakṣikaniścaye
viśeṣapadarśanābhāvaviśiṣṭaviparītajñānasnaya pratibandhakatvaṃ
tadabhāvasya hetutvamiti vadatāṃ dīdhitikārādīnāṃ mate
nātivyāptiriti sūcitam/ nanu [147] sthāṇupuruṣasaṃśayānantaramiti dīpikāvākyamasaṅgatam/
saṃśayasya tattadabhāvakoṭikatvaniyamena
sthāṇupuruṣakoṭikatvāyogāt ityata āha - [148] idamiti/ [148] āhuḥ ityasvarasasūcanam/ tadbījantu
sthāṇutvatadabhāvakoṭikasaṃśayasya prathamaṃ vivakṣitatve puruṣa eveti
pratyakṣajananādityuttaragranthavirodhaḥ/ sthāṇureveti pratyakṣajananāditi
vaktavyatvāt/ ataḥ tādṛśagranthaparyālocanayā
sathāṇupuruṣasuśayānantaramiti vākye saṃśayadvayaṃ na vivakṣitam,
kintu eka eva saṃśaya iti/
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'perception following doubt' is inconsistent, because over-pervasion also arises in perception following erroneous determination such as 'this is not a person,' and since that case is not mentioned, there would be a deficiency. Anticipating this, with the intention that the word 'doubt' (<s>saṃśaya</s>) in the <s>Dīpikā</s> passage is meant as a secondary indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for erroneous cognition in general, he says: [188] 'perception following erroneous cognition as well.' [148] 'Of those who accept' — the rest is 'such as <s>Miśra</s> and others.' By this it is indicated that in the view of the <s>Dīdhiti</s> author and others, who hold that erroneous cognition — qualified by the absence of perceiving the distinguishing feature — has an obstructive role in determinate perceptual cognition, and that the absence of such [erroneous cognition] is a causal condition, there is no over-pervasion. Now, [147] the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'after the doubt regarding post and person' is inconsistent, because doubt necessarily has the form of [two] alternative limbs involving the absence of each, and hence cannot have the form 'post or person' as its [two] limbs. Addressing this, he says: [148] 'this.' [148] 'They say' — this indicates a lack of agreement [with that position]. The basis of that [objection] is: if the doubt having the limbs 'post-hood and the absence thereof' is what is initially intended, then since perception in the form 'it is indeed a person' would be generated, there would be contradiction with the subsequent text, because one would have to say 'since perception in the form it is indeed a post is generated.' Therefore, upon careful consideration of such passages, in the statement 'after the doubt regarding post and person,' two doubts are not intended, but rather a single doubt.

children.text:
1. teneti/ ātmādeḥ
anumitiniṣṭhajñānatvāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatāśrayatve 'pi
anumititvāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatāśrayatvābhāvannātivyāptiriti
bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 1:] 'By that' — the purport is: even though the Self etc. possess the substratum-hood of causality determined by the effect-hood delimited by cognition-hood residing in <s>anumiti</s>, since they lack the substratum-hood of causality determined by the effect-hood delimited by <s>anumititva</s> (inferential-cognition-hood), there is no over-pervasion.

children.text:
taccaitanmate na ghaṭata
iti/ nanu puruṣa iti pratyakṣajananāditi vaktavyam
kimevakāropādānenetyāśaṅyāha - [148] puruṣa evetīti/ nanu
'puruṣaṃ anuminomī'tyanuvyavasāyasattve anumititvamapi tatra
svīkāryaṃ syādityata āha - [148]
idamupalakṣaṇamiti/ [148] idaṃ bādhakayuktipradarśanam/ [148] upalakṣaṇam
bādhakayuktyantarasyāpi sūcakam/ nanu
saṃśayottarapratyakṣe 'tivyāptivāraṇātha
1parāmarśajanyatvaśarīrapraviṣṭajanakatāyāṃ
viśiṣṭaparāmarśatvāvacchinnatvameva kuto na niveśitam/
saṃśeyottarapratyakṣe ca puruṣatvavyāpyakarādimānayamiti parāmarśasya
2viśakalitajñānasādhāraṇyānurodhena 3jñānaviśiṣṭajñānatvenaiva
kāraṇatvopagamāt/ evaṃ viśeṣapadarśanasya
viparītajñānapratibanadhakatāyāṃ uttejakatāmate uktaviśeṣaṇaṃ viphalaṃ
syāt/ saṃśayottarapratyakṣe 4ativyāpteranavakāśādintyata āha - [148] eteneti/ janakatāyāṃ
children.translated_text: 'And that does not work in this system.' Now, one might object: it should simply be said 'since perception in the form person is generated' — why add the particle <s>eva</s>? Anticipating this, he says: [148] 'person indeed.' Now, if the subsequent reflective awareness (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) 'I infer a person' exists, then inferential-cognition-hood would also have to be accepted there. Addressing this, he says: [148] 'this is a secondary indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>).' [148] 'This is a demonstration of a defeating argument.' [148] '<s>Upalakṣaṇa</s>' also indicates other defeating arguments. Now, to prevent over-pervasion to perception following doubt, why not simply stipulate that the causality residing in <s>parāmarśa</s>-born-ness involves being delimited by qualified-<s>parāmarśa</s>-hood? In perception following doubt, since the <s>parāmarśa</s> of the form 'this possesses hands etc. which pervade person-hood' — in accordance with its being common to analytically decomposed cognitions — has causality only as cognition qualified by [another] cognition, [not as <s>parāmarśa</s> proper]. Similarly, in the view where perceiving the distinguishing feature has an exciting role in the obstructive capacity of erroneous cognition, the stated qualifier would be fruitless, since over-pervasion to perception following doubt has no scope. Addressing this, he says: [148] 'by this.' In the causality,

children.text:
tādṛśadharmāvacchinnatvamaniveśya
pakṣatāsahakṛtaparāmarśajanyatvasyaiva vivakṣaṇenetyarthaḥ/ [148] viśeṣaṇatāvacchedakaprakārakanirṇayavidhayetyanena
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhibuddheḥ
tādṛśaviśiṣṭaparāmarśatvāvacchinnajanakatākatvamastīti sūcitam/
saṅkṣepa iti/ atrāyamāśayaḥ --- pakṣatāsahakṛtasyaiva parāmarśasya
viśeṣadarśanatvena saṃśayottarapratyakṣe hetutvāt
taddoṣatādavasthyamiti pakṣatājanyatve sati parāmarśajanyatvamiti
tadartho vaktavyaḥ/ evaṃ pakṣatāpratyakṣe ativyāptivāraṇāya
parāmarśajanyatvopādānam/
children.translated_text: without stipulating delimitation by such a property, the intention is to state simply 'born of <s>parāmarśa</s> assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s>' (the thesis-condition). [148] By the statement 'a determinate cognition whose qualifier-mode is the delimiter of the qualifier-hood,' it is indicated that the cognition apprehending the qualified-qualification has causality delimited by such qualified-<s>parāmarśa</s>-hood. 'In brief' — the intention here is this: since only <s>parāmarśa</s> assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s> has causal status in perception following doubt, by virtue of being the perception of the distinguishing feature, the same difficulty remains. Hence what should be stated is: 'born of <s>parāmarśa</s>, when there is <s>pakṣatā</s>-born-ness.' Similarly, the inclusion of '<s>parāmarśa</s>-born-ness' is to prevent over-pervasion to <s>pakṣatā</s>-perception.

children.text:
1. parāmarśajanyatveti/
parāmarśaniṣṭhajanakatānirūpitajanyatvetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 1:] '<s>Parāmarśa</s>-born-ness' — meaning: being the counter-correlate of the generation-relation determined by the causality residing in <s>parāmarśa</s>.

children.text:
2. viśakalitajñāneti/
'puruṣatvavyāpyaṃ karādi', 'karādimāṃścāyam' iti
jñānadvayasādhāraṇyānurodhenetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 2:] 'Of analytically decomposed cognitions' — meaning in accordance with the commonality to the two cognitions: 'hands etc. are pervaded by person-hood' and 'this [thing] possesses hands etc.'

children.text:
3.
jñānaviśiṣṭajñānatveneti/
karādiviśeṣyakapuruṣatvavyāpyatvaprakārakajñānaviśiṣṭakaradiṃprakārakedantvāvacchinnaviśeṣyakajñānatvenetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 3:] 'As cognition qualified by cognition' — meaning: as cognition whose qualificand-hood is delimited by this-ness and whose qualifier-mode is 'possessing hands etc.,' qualified by cognition whose qualifier-mode is 'person-hood-pervasion' and whose qualificand is 'hands etc.'

children.text:
4.
ativyāpteranavakāśāditi/
jñānaviśiṣṭajñānatvāvacchinnakāraṇatānirūtipakāryatānirūpitakāryatāyāḥ
sattve 'pi parāmarśatvāvacchinnakāraṇatānirūpitakāryatāyāḥ
virahāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 4:] 'Since over-pervasion has no scope' — the purport is: although there is effect-hood determined by causality delimited by cognition-qualified-by-cognition-hood, there is an absence of effect-hood determined by causality delimited by <s>parāmarśa</s>-hood.

children.text:
yadyapi
pakṣatāparāmarśobhayaviṣayakasamūhālambanapratyakṣe 'tivyāptirevamapi
sambhavati, tathāpi
pakṣatājanyatāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnaparāmarśajanyatāvivakṣaṇāt 1na
doṣaḥ/ pakṣatāpratyakṣatvaparāmarśapratyakṣatvoḥ avacchedakayoḥ
bhedādityādikaṃ anumitigranthādau vistareṇoktaṃ draṣṭavyamiti/
children.translated_text: Even though over-pervasion is still possible in the case of collective-apprehension perception (<s>samūhālambana-pratyakṣa</s>) directed at both <s>pakṣatā</s> and <s>parāmarśa</s>, nevertheless, since what is intended is '<s>parāmarśa</s>-born-ness delimited by the property that delimits the <s>pakṣatā</s>-born-ness,' there is no defect — because the delimiters, namely <s>pakṣatā</s>-perception-hood and <s>parāmarśa</s>-perception-hood, are different. And so on — this should be seen in detail in the treatises on <s>anumiti</s>.

children.text: pakṣatālakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>pakṣatā</s> (the thesis-condition)

children.text:
nanu
sādhyasaṃśayarūpapakṣatāsahakṛtatvaṃ kuto nātra niveśayituṃ
śakyamityabhiprāyeṇa śaṅkate - [150] yadyapīti/ ghanagarjanena
suptotthitasya meghānumitau sādhyasaṃśayarūpakāraṇābhāvena
vyabhicārāpattyā sādhyasaṃśayasyānumitihetubhūtapakṣatārūpatvaṃ na
sambhavatīti nātṛ tadvivakṣaṇaṃ śakyamityabhiprāyeṇa samādhatte - [150] tathāpīti/ [150] sādhyānumitīcchāyā iti/ atra
cecchāmātraniveśe siddhisattve ghaṭo bhūyāt
itīcchādaśāyāmanumityāpattiḥ/ anumityasāniveśe 'pi
ghaṭānumitiḥ bhūyāt itīcchāyā vāraṇāsambhavaḥ/
sādhyānumitiviṣayakecchāniveśe 'pi ghaṭānumitiḥ
bhūyāditīcchāvāraṇaṃ na sambhavati/
2ghaṭasādhyobhayasamūhālambanānumiterviṣayatvasambhavāt/ ataḥ
prakṛtasādhyakatvaviśeṣitānumititvaprakārikecchāyā iti tadartho
bodhyaḥ/ abhāvapratiyogitāyāṃ ca tādṛśecchātvāvacchinnatvaṃ
niveśyam, tena tādṛśecchāghaṭobhayābhāvādikamādāya 3na doṣaḥ/
tādṛśecchātvāvacchinnatvaṃ ca tādṛśecchātvaparyāptāvacchedakatākatvam/
tacca 4tādaśecchātvetaradharmānavacchinnatvaparyavasitam/ tena caitrasya
siddhisiṣādhayiṣayoḥ sattve
children.translated_text: Now, with the intention of asking why the condition 'assisted by <s>pakṣatā</s> in the form of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum)' cannot be stipulated here, he raises the objection: [150] 'although.' When a person awakened by loud thunder infers clouds, since the cause in the form of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s> is absent, there would be a deviation; hence <s>sādhya</s>-doubt cannot be the form of <s>pakṣatā</s> that is a cause of <s>anumiti</s> — and thus that [condition] cannot be intended. With this understanding, he resolves: [150] 'nevertheless.' [150] 'The desire for <s>anumiti</s> of the <s>sādhya</s>' — here, if mere desire is stipulated, then in the state of desiring 'may a pot come into being,' there would be the unwanted consequence of <s>anumiti</s>. Even if one stipulates <s>anumiti</s>-desire, the desire 'may there be <s>anumiti</s> of a pot' cannot be excluded. Even if one stipulates the desire directed at <s>anumiti</s> of the <s>sādhya</s>, the desire 'may there be <s>anumiti</s> of a pot' cannot be excluded, because collective-apprehension <s>anumiti</s> directed at both the pot and the <s>sādhya</s> is possible. Therefore, the meaning should be understood as: the desire whose qualifier-mode is <s>anumiti</s>-hood qualified by the property of having the relevant <s>sādhya</s> as its content. And in the counter-correlate-hood of the absence [that constitutes <s>pakṣatā</s>], delimitation by such desire-hood must be stipulated; thereby, by taking the absence of both the desire and the pot etc., there is no defect. And 'delimitation by such desire-hood' means having a delimiting condition coextensive with such desire-hood, which amounts to not being delimited by any property other than such desire-hood. And thus, when both <s>siddhi</s> (established cognition) and <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> (desire to prove) exist for <s>Caitra</s>,

children.text:
1. na doṣa iti/
samūhālambanapratyakṣaniṣṭhāyāḥ parāmarśajanyatāyāḥ
parāmarśaviṣayakapratyakṣatvāvacchinnatve 'pi pakṣatāyāḥ janyatāvacchedakaṃ
yat pakṣatāpratyakṣatvaṃ tadavacchinnatvābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 1:] 'There is no defect' — the purport is: although the <s>parāmarśa</s>-born-ness residing in collective-apprehension perception has delimitation by perception-hood directed at <s>parāmarśa</s>, the <s>pakṣatā</s>-born-ness does not have delimitation by that <s>pakṣatā</s>-perception-hood [which would be the required delimiter].

children.text:
2. ghaṭasādhyeti/
'ghaṭavahnyubhayānumitirbhūyāt' iti icchā atra vivakṣitā/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 2:] 'Of the pot and the <s>sādhya</s>' — the desire intended here is: 'may there be <s>anumiti</s> of both the pot and fire.'

children.text:
3. na doṣa iti/
siddhisiṣādhayiṣobhayasattvakāle na pakṣatānupapattirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 3:] 'There is no defect' — meaning: when both <s>siddhi</s> and <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> are present, there is no impossibility of <s>pakṣatā</s>.

children.text:
4.
tādṛśecchātvetyādi/ tathā ca ghaṭavahnyubhayānumitirbhūyāditīcchāyāḥ
yo 'bhāvaḥ tadīyapratiyogitāyāḥ
tādṛśecchātvetaraghaṭasādhyakatvādyavacchinnatayā tadanavacchinnatvābhāvāt
tādṛśābhāvasya na uttejakābhāvarūpatetyāśaya/
children.translated_text: [Footnote 4:] 'Of such desire-hood' etc. — accordingly, the absence of the desire 'may there be <s>anumiti</s> of both the pot and fire' — the counter-correlate-hood of that absence, being delimited by 'having-the-pot-and-sādhya-as-content-hood' etc. which is other than such desire-hood, lacks non-delimitation by that [other property]; hence such absence does not have the status of being an absence of the exciting condition — this is the intention.

children.text:
maitravṛttitvaviśiṣṭasiṣādhayiṣayā abhāvamādāya
nānumityanupapattiḥ/ evamagre 'pi pratiyogitāyāṃ
viśiṣṭasiddhitvetaradharmāvacchinnatvaṃ niveśyam/ tena
viśiṣṭasiddhighaṭobhayādyabhāvasya

anyathā siṣādhayiṣāṃ vinā siddhisattve 'numityāpatteḥ/ yadyapi
tādṛśecchātvetaradharmaḥ tādṛśānumititvaprakārakatvarūpa iti
siṣādhayiṣāvirahasyaivāsaṃgrahaḥ/ evamagre 'pi/ tathāpi
1tādṛśaprakārakatvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatābhinna -
children.translated_text: Taking the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> qualified by <s>Maitra</s>'s-<s>vṛtti</s>-hood [as the pakṣatā], there is no impossibility of <s>anumiti</s>. Similarly, going forward too, in the counter-correlate-hood, 'non-delimitation by any property other than qualified-<s>siddhi</s>-hood' must be stipulated. By that, the absence of both qualified-<s>siddhi</s> and pot, and the absence of such <s>siddhi</s> qualified by residing-in-any-self-hood, are excluded. Otherwise, when <s>siddhi</s> exists without <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>, there would be the unwanted consequence of <s>anumiti</s>. Although the property other than such desire-hood is of the form 'having such <s>anumiti</s>-hood as qualifier-mode,' so that only the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> would fail to be included — and similarly going forward — nevertheless,

children.text:
icchātvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatābhinnāvacchedakatvānirūpakatvaṃ
vivakṣaṇīyam/ evaṃ
siṣādhayiṣāvirahavaiśiṣṭyaniṣṭhāvacchedakatābhinnasiddhitvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatābhinnāvacchedakatvānirūpakatvamagrimapratiyogitāyāṃ
niveśyamiti/ evamanyatrāpi bodhyam/ [151] samavāyenābhāva iti/
siṣādhayiṣāsiddhyoḥ sattvadaśāyāṃ
saṃyogasaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākasiṣādhayiṣāvirahasyātmani
sattvāt anumityanupapattiḥ ataḥ samavāyenetyuktam/
avacchinnapratiyogitākatvamabhāvānvayi tṛtīyārthaḥ/ nanu
siṣādhayiṣāvirahasya svarūpasaṃbandhena siddhiviśeṣaṇatve
siddhisiṣādhayiṣayoḥ sattve 'numittyanupapattitādavasthyam/
siṣādhayiṣāyāḥ samavāyenātmanyeva sattvāt ityata āha - [151] svarūpetyādi/ tathā ca siṣādhayiṣāvirahavaiśiṣṭyaṃ siddhau na
svarūpasambandhena, yenoktadoṣaḥ syāt/ api tu

The third-case-ending meaning is: having counter-correlate-hood delimited by [that relation] — this is what connects with the absence. Now, if the absence of <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> qualifies <s>siddhi</s> through the <s>svarūpa</s> relation (intrinsic relation), then when both <s>siddhi</s> and <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> are present, there would still be the same impossibility of <s>anumiti</s>, since <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s> exists in the self by <s>samavāya</s>. children.translated_text: Because of the same predicament of inference being impossible when [both <s>siddhi</s> and <s>siṣādhayiṣā</s>] are present. It should be noted that this is due to the absence of a qualificand in the form of absence of <s>siddhi</s> (establishment). [151] 'The absence of <s>siddhi</s> through inherence' — this is the meaning. Taking the absence of <s>siddhi</s> qualified by the absence of the desire-to-prove as being through conjunction, 'through inherence' is said in order to prevent inference at the stage of qualified <s>siddhi</s>. Here, in the first superstratum-relation in the co-located body, if being delimited by the self-linking relation is not included, then even when both <s>siddhi</s> and the desire-to-prove are present, since the absence of the desire-to-prove is present in the self through the relation of possessing its own counter-positive, inference would be impossible — hence its inclusion. Its purpose is: being delimited by the self-linking relation that is not delimited [by anything further]. By that, even when the absence of the desire-to-prove, delimited by pot and the like, is present in the self which also possesses the desire-to-prove, there is no difficulty. Since <s>siddhi</s> is present as a temporal qualifier at the time when the absence of desire-to-prove is present — the same defect [arises]; therefore causality through the self-linking relation that is not delimited by the second superstratum-relation must be stated. Otherwise, when <s>siddhi</s> is present, since the absence of that delimited by pot and the like would also be present, inference would undesirably follow at the stage of qualified <s>siddhi</s>. [151] 'The establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> is qualified by the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s>' and so forth. The meaning is: a cognition other than doubt, possessing a qualifier-mode delimited by the property-relation that delimits <s>sādhyatā</s> (probandum-hood) as determined by the <s>viśeṣyatā</s> (qualificand-ness) delimited by the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s> (subject-hood). Here, the inclusion of the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s> and the rest is to prevent the impossibility of inference even when determinate cognitions such as 'the stone possesses fire through conjunction,' 'the mountain possesses substance through conjunction,' 'the mountain possesses fire through temporal relation' and the like are present. The inclusion of the determinant-determined relationship between <s>viśeṣyatā</s> and <s>prakāratā</s> (qualifier-mode) should be understood as preventing the collective apprehension such as 'the mountain possesses pot and the lake possesses fire' from conflicting with the inference 'the mountain possesses fire.' The inclusion of 'other than doubt' is to prevent the doubt 'the mountain possesses fire or not' from being an obstruction. And that [otherness from doubt] is not difference from doubt in general, for if so, [the cognition] 'the mountain possesses fire through conjunction,'

children.translated_text: Objection: the purpose of including qualification by absence of desire-to-prove in [the definition of] <s>siddhi</s>, stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s> passage beginning with 'even when <s>siddhi</s> is present,' is possible only when the <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective consideration) of <s>siddhi</s> and the desire-to-prove are simultaneous. But that very [simultaneity] does not obtain, because — given the rule that eligible particular qualities are destroyed by the quality produced immediately after them — their simultaneous existence is impossible. Hence the statement of that purpose is irrelevant. Anticipating this objection, he reconciles it at the stage where <s>parāmarśa</s> is of the nature of <s>siddhi</s> — [151] with 'here <s>siddhi</s> also' and so forth. [151] 'Therefore, by tracing through to the collective apprehension.' 'The <s>parāmarśa</s>': otherwise, where first the <s>parāmarśa</s> [arises], then <s>siddhi</s>, then the desire-to-prove — then inference would simply not arise, since the <s>parāmarśa</s> has been destroyed previously. Hence there is no [need for] this purpose. The purport is thus. Accordingly, since the absence of the qualifier brings about the absence of the qualified, there is no deviation when <s>siddhi</s> and the desire-to-prove are both present. The purport is thus.

To prevent inference from the doubt 'the mountain possesses or does not possess smoke pervaded by fire,' [the qualification] 'determinate cognition' is stated. And the property of being determinate is not difference from doubt in general — since that would have the unwanted consequence that a partial doubt would not be a non-producer [of inference]. gaganādityādiviruddhavāraṇāya 1viśeṣyam/ dravyaṃ sattvāt
ityādivyabhicārivāraṇāya 2viśeṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s> statement 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire — this invariable co-presence is <s>vyāpti</s>,' the understanding is that <s>vyāpti</s> is identical with the invariable co-presence conveyed by such a statement. With this intention he says in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [157], 'wherever' and so forth. [157] 'Exemplification' means the statement of the illustrating word. [157] In the <s>Saṅgraha</s> statement '<s>sāhacaryaniyama</s>' (invariable co-presence): those that accompany each other are companions; the state of that is <s>sāhacarya</s> (co-presence). The meaning is co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). The 'invariability' (<s>niyama</s>) of that, according to the ancients, is qualification in the form of non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> and the like. According to the moderns, it is of the nature of the <s>sādhya</s> being determined by the pervader of the <s>hetu</s>; its residing in the <s>hetu</s> is to be stated only through the indirect relation of being the substrate of one's own substrate. Hence in [the expression] 'pervaded by' and the like, that alone is the meaning of the affix. [The objection that] 'own' introduces complexity is insurmountable if the invariability is the qualificand. But if it is the qualifier, then since the co-location qualified by invariability occurs in the <s>hetu</s> through the relation of substrate-hood alone, there is no occasion for complexity in the stated manner. Bearing this in mind, [157] it is said 'invariable co-location.' [157] 'In the form of non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> and the like': by 'and the like,' non-occurrence in what is other than what possesses the <s>sādhya</s> is also included. 'In the form of non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> and the like' means the qualifying constituent — that is to say, what is constituted by non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> and the like, as obtained by the derivation of 'wherever having such.' Here, to prevent the contradictory [reason] in 'the sky possesses fire' and the like, [there is] the qualificand. To prevent the deviating [reason] in 'a substance [possesses something], because of <s>sattva</s>' and the like, [there is] the qualifier.

children.text:
vṛttimātraniveśenoktaviruddhanirāse tu 'dhūmavān
vahne'rityādāvapi prayojanaṃ bodhyam/ kecittu - sāhacaryaniyama
ityatra kṛdabhihito bhāvo dravyavatprakāśata iti nyāyena
niyamaśabdo niyataparaḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaviśeṣaṇamityabhiprāyeṇāha
[157] niyatasāmānādhikaraṇyamiti - iti vyācakruḥ/ tadasat --
tathāsati sāhacaryaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyam, tasya niyama iti
ṣaṣṭhīsamāsena vyākhyānavirodhāt/ niyataparaniyamaśabdasya
'viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣye'tyādisūtreṇā pūrvanipātāpatteśca/ tasmāt
niyatasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃmiti phalitārthakathanama;
children.translated_text: If by including mere occurrence the stated contradictory [reason] is prevented, the purpose should also be understood in cases like 'that which possesses smoke from fire' and the like. Some, however, explain — in '<s>sāhacaryaniyama</s>,' by the principle 'a verbal noun denotes an entity possessing the abstract, like a substance,' the word <s>niyama</s> refers to what is invariable and qualifies <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> — and with this intention they explain [157] 'invariable co-location' thus. That is wrong — because in that case, <s>sāhacarya</s> would mean co-location and <s>niyama</s> of that [would require] a genitive compound, contradicting the interpretation. And because the word <s>niyama</s> meaning 'what is invariable' would have prior placement by the rule 'the qualifier [is placed before] the qualificand,' [which is undesirable]. Therefore, 'invariable co-location' is a statement of the resultant meaning.

children.text:
1. viśeṣyamiti/
sāmānādhikaraṇyarūpaṃ viśeṣyamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The qualificand': the meaning is that the qualificand is of the form of co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>).

children.text:
2. viśeṣaṇamiti/
niyamarūpaṃ viśeṣaṇamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The qualifier': the meaning is that the qualifier is of the form of invariability (<s>niyama</s>).

children.translated_text: Rather, the truth is that it is not a statement of word-meaning. And accordingly, in the body [of the definition] where co-location is restricted, the restriction in the form of the qualification of non-occurrence in the locus of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> and the like cannot be stated — this is the import. He states the defect in that case — [157] by 'this is to be stated' and so forth. Here, keeping in mind the alternative whether in the body [of the definition involving] non-occurrence in the locus of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, what is introduced is the absence whose counterpositive-hood resides in the <s>sādhya</s>, or whether [it extends] up to the absence whose counterpositive-hood is delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>-relation and not delimited by a property other than the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> — in the first alternative, taking the absence of both expressibility (<s>vācyatva</s>), pot-hood, and the like, and taking the absence of expressibility qualified by occurrence in pot and the like, and the absence of expressibility whose counterpositive-hood is delimited by the relation of conjunction and the like — since it is impossible to establish the non-deviation of a valid <s>hetu</s>, this being obvious, he states the refutation of the second [alternative] — [157] 'because there is no counter-establishment against the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>.' [157] The meaning is: 'delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> that is the non-delimitor of counterpositive-hood.' In cases like 'possessing smoke, because of fire,' to prevent over-pervasion by taking knowability (<s>prameyatva</s>), substance-hood (<s>dravyatva</s>), and the like, the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> is specifically introduced. Although the counterpositive-hood delimitor-hood of the absence of kitchen-fire and the like belongs to fire-hood and more — this is unimpaired by the principle. Nevertheless, by the expression 'non-delimitor of such counterpositive-hood' and the like, by intending the possession of content-hood delimited by the other <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> qualified by the absence co-located with the <s>hetu</s>, there is no defect. The qualification is through the relation of possessing-difference-of-the-type-beginning-with-'its-own.' Its-own-locus-hood is through the relation of its-own-counterpositive-hood-delimitor-hood; the difference-counterpositive-hood delimitor-hood is through the delimitor-hood relation. And accordingly, since kitchen-fire-hood and the like lack such content-hood delimitor-hood, the definition is consistent. The being-delimited-by-the-<s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s> in the content-hood — when a property occurring in only one [locus] is the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>, its possessing delimitor-hood-hood, and when there are two or more properties in that case,

children.translated_text: [Footnote:] The meaning is: the possession of content-hood delimited by the <s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>, which is other than [the content-hood] qualified by the absence co-located with the <s>hetu</s>. By the word 'its own' (<s>sva</s>), the absence of pot and the like co-located with the <s>hetu</s> is to be taken. The 'possessing-difference-of-the-type-beginning-with-its-own' means: possessing difference whose counterpositive-hood is delimited by the relation of the delimitor-hood-hood residing in itself and delimited by the relation of the difference-counterpositive-hood-delimitor-hood occurring in the locus of itself. 'Its own' is the absence of pot; through the relation of its-own-counterpositive-hood-delimitor-hood, the locus of the absence of pot is pot-hood; the difference therein, through the delimitor-hood relation, is the difference possessing content-hood delimited by fire-hood; the counterpositive-hood delimitor-hood of that is in the content-hood delimited by fire-hood — thus, through the relation of such difference-counterpositive-hood-delimitor-hood, the content-hood delimited by fire-hood possesses the absence of pot, and through that relation, what is different from that which possesses the absence of pot is the content-hood delimited by pot-hood. Thus, through the relation of possessing-difference-of-the-type-beginning-with-its-own, the content-hood delimited by pot-hood, qualified by the absence of pot, and other than that,

children.text: vahnitvāvacchinnaviṣayateti samanvayo bodhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: is the content-hood delimited by fire-hood — this syntactic connection should be understood.

children.translated_text: However, since two or more properties serve as delimitors of the qualifier-qualificandum-hood relation, the distinctive delimitor-hood that is of that kind has the nature of being-a-determinand — hence there is no deficiency. Nor

children.text:
caivamiti
saṃyogasamavāyobhayasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākavahnyādyabhāvamādāya
taddoṣatādavasthyamiti vācyam/
sādhyatāvacchedakasambandhamātrāvacchinnatvasya
taditarasambandhānavacchinnatvaparyavasitasya vivakṣitatvāt/ [158] hetutāvacchedakāvacchinnaparamiti/
1prakṛtahetutāvacchedakatāvyāpakatāvacchedakatākanirūpakatākaparami tyarthaḥ/
tādṛśanirūpakatākatvamadhikaraṇatānvayi/ tena viśiṣṭasattāhetuke
sattātvasyāpi hetutāvacchedakatāyā taddoṣatādavasthyamiti śaṅkā

children.translated_text: should it be said thus — that by taking the absence of fire and the like whose counterpositive-hood is delimited by both the relations of conjunction and inherence, the same defect persists — because what is intended is being-delimited-by-merely-the-<s>sādhyatāvacchedaka</s>-relation, which amounts to not-being-delimited-by-a-relation-other-than-that. [158] 'Delimited by the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>, the further [qualification]' — the meaning is: that which is further than the delimitor-hood-hood that pervades the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>-hood of the <s>hetu</s> under consideration, having the nature of being-a-determinand. Such being-a-determinand-hood connects with the locus-hood. By this, in the case where existence qualified [by genus and action-otherness] is the <s>hetu</s>, the doubt that there would be the same defect since existence-hood too has <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>-hood is dispelled.

children.text:
vastutastu ekadharmasya
hetutāvacchedakatve tanniṣṭhāvacchedakatākatvamevādhikaraṇatāyāṃ
niveśyam/ yatra
children.translated_text: In reality, however, when a single property is the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>, only the delimitor-hood-hood residing in it should be introduced into the locus-hood. Where

children.text:
dharmadvayādeḥ tathātvaṃ
tatra pūrvoktarītyā vilakṣaṇāvacchedakatākatvamiti na kiñcidavahīnam/
atraiva [158] hetutāvacchedakāvacchinnaparamityasyāpi
tātparyamiti dhyeyam/ [158] viśiṣṭeti/
2svarūpasamavāyobhayaghaṭitasāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena
guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭetyarthaḥ/ nanu viśiṣṭaśuddhayorbhendāt kathaṃ
hetvadhikaraṇatva guṇāderityata āha - [158] viśiṣṭasyeti/
dravyatvābhāvasya hetvadhikaraṇaguṇādiniṣṭhatve 'pīti yojanā/
guṇādītyādinā karmādisaṅgrahaḥ/ [158] nāvyāptiriti/
tanniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpakatāvacchedakaṃ yat
children.translated_text: two or more properties have that status, there the distinctive delimitor-hood-hood is of the previously stated kind — hence nothing is lacking. It should be noted that the purport of [158] 'delimited by the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>, the further' is precisely this. [158] 'Qualified' (<s>viśiṣṭā</s>) — the meaning is: qualified by the otherness from quality, action, and the like, through the relation of co-location constituted by both self-linking (<s>svarūpa</s>) and inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). Objection: Since the qualified and the pure [entity] are different, how can quality and the like be loci of the <s>hetu</s>? To this he responds — [158] 'Of the qualified.' The syntactic connection is: even though the absence of substance-hood resides in quality and the like, which are loci of the <s>hetu</s>. By 'quality and the like,' action and the like are also included. [158] 'There is no under-pervasion' — that which is the delimitor of the locus-hood determined by the [absence] residing therein,

1. nirūpakatāpadenātra
ādheyatā vivakṣitā/ tathā ca prakṛtahetutāvacchedakatāvyāpikā yā
ādheyatāvacchedakatā tannirūpakādheyatānirūpakatvamadhikaraṇatāyāṃ
vivakṣitam/ tena dravyaṃ viśiṣṭasattvāt ityatra hetutāvacchedakatā
viśiṣṭasattātve, tatra
guṇaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpitādheyatāvacchedakatā nāsti, 'guṇo
guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattāvān' iti pratītivirahāt/ api tu
dravyaniṣṭhābhikaraṇatānirūpitadheyatāvacchedakatā asti, 'dravyaṃ
guṇakarmānyatvaviśiṣṭasattāvat' iti pratīteḥ/ ataḥ
hetutāvacchedakatāvyāpakāvacchedakatākādheyatākādhikaraṇatāvat
dravyameva, tadvṛttyatyantābhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ dravyatve 'stīti
nāvyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] By the word 'determinand' (<s>nirūpakatā</s>), superstratum-hood (<s>ādheyatā</s>) is intended here. Accordingly, the superstratum-hood delimitor-hood that pervades the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>-hood of the <s>hetu</s> under consideration — the being-a-determinand-of-the-superstratum-hood-determined-by-that is what is intended in the locus-hood. Thus, in the [inference] 'substance possesses qualified existence,' the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>-hood is in qualified-existence-hood; therein, the superstratum-hood-delimitor-hood determined by the locus-hood residing in quality does not exist, because there is no cognition of the form 'quality possesses existence qualified by quality-action-otherness.' Rather, the superstratum-hood-delimitor-hood determined by locus-hood residing in substance exists, because of the cognition 'substance possesses existence qualified by quality-action-otherness.' Therefore, only substance possesses the locus-hood whose superstratum-hood has the delimitor-hood-hood that pervades the <s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>-hood; the non-counterpositive-hood of the constant absence residing therein is present in substance-hood — hence there is no under-pervasion. This is the import.

children.text:
2.
svarūpasamavāyobhayaghaṭitasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ nāma
svarūpasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhādheyatānirūpakādhikaraṇanirūpitasamavāyasaṃbandhāvacchinnavṛttitvam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] The co-location constituted by both self-linking and inherence (<s>svarūpa-samavāya-ubhaya-ghaṭita-sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) means: occurrence delimited by the inherence relation, whose locus is determined by the superstratum-hood residing in itself and delimited by the self-linking relation.

children.text:
tasyaiva
tadavacchinnanirūpitādhikaraṇatāvattvena guṇāderatathātvāditi bhāvaḥ/
yadyapi hetvadhikaraṇatāyāṃ hetutāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvāniveśe
kālikādinā dhūmādyabhikaraṇe hradādau
saṃyogādyavacchinnavahnyādyabhāvasattvāt apyavyāptisambhavaḥ/ tathāpi
janyamātrasya kālatvānupagame naiṣa doṣaḥ sambhavatīti tatra tanniveśasya
prakārāntareṇa phalamāha - [158] nāvyāptiriti/ ātmabhinnaṃ
jñānavadanyatvādityādau ātmanaḥ kenāpi sambandhena
hetvadhikaraṇatāviraheṇa lakṣaṇasamanvayasambhavāt nāsambhavo darśitaḥ/
saṃyogasāmānyābhāvasya vṛkṣe savivādatvādāha -- [158] kapīti/ [158] pratiyogivaiyadhikaraṇyasyeti/ yadyapi
sāmānyataḥ pratiyoginiveśe tādṛśaviśeṣaṇākrāntābhāvāprasiddhiḥ/
svapratiyoginiveśe svatvasya tattadvyaktiviśrāntatayā
vyāpterasarvajñadurjñeyatāpattiḥ/ tathāpi
1tādātmyasvapratiyogyadhikaraṇavṛttitvobhayasaṃbandhena
abhāvaviśiṣṭānyatvaṃ nirūpakatvasvāśrayādhikaraṇavṛttitvobhayasaṃbandhena
pratiyogitāviśiṣṭānyatvaṃ vā sthūlasūkṣmarītibhyāmanugatamabhāve
niveśyamiti na doṣaḥ/ atra ca svapratiyogyadhikaraṇāvṛttitvasya
pratiyogivaiyadhikaraṇyaśabdārthatve kapisaṃyogī sattvādityādau
vyabhicāriṇyatiprasaṅgaḥ/ adhikaraṇabhedenābhāvabhedaviraheṇa
sādhyābhāvasya vyāpakatāghaṭakatvāsambhavāt/
svapratiyogyanadhikaraṇavṛttitvasya niveśe ca kapisaṃyogī
etattvādityādau avyāpitatādavasthyamiti hetvadhikaraṇe
svapratiyogyanadhikaraṇatvaṃ niveśanīyamityādikaṃ manasi nidhāyāha -
[158] adhikamiti/
children.translated_text: The import is: of that [entity] alone, by virtue of possessing the locus-hood determined thereby, quality and the like do not have that status. Although, if being-delimited-by-the-<s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>-relation is not introduced into the <s>hetu</s>-locus-hood, there could be under-pervasion because the absence of fire and the like delimited by conjunction and the like exists in a lake and the like which are loci of smoke through temporal relation — nevertheless, since this defect does not arise when mere-product-hood is not accepted as time-hood, he states the result of introducing that by another method — [158] 'No under-pervasion.' In cases like 'what is different from the self possesses knowledge, because of otherness,' since it is possible to reconcile with the definition by the absence of the self's being a locus of the <s>hetu</s> through any relation — non-impossibility is shown. Since the general absence of conjunction is disputed as [being present] in a tree, he says — [158] 'monkey' (<s>kapi</s>). [158] 'Of the difference-from-the-counterpositive' — although, when the counterpositive is introduced generally, the relevant absence qualified by such a qualifier is not well-established; and when one's own counterpositive is introduced, since its 'own-ness' rests in each particular instance, <s>vyāpti</s> would become unknowable to non-omniscient beings — nevertheless, through the dual relation of identity and occurrence-in-the-locus-of-one's-own-counterpositive, the otherness qualified by absence; or through the dual relation of being-a-determinand and occurrence-in-the-locus-of-one's-own-substratum, the otherness qualified by counterpositive-hood — by both the broad and fine methods, this is what is to be introduced into the absence — hence there is no defect. And here, if non-occurrence-in-the-locus-of-one's-own-counterpositive is the meaning of the term 'difference from the counterpositive,' then in cases like '[this] has monkey-contact, because of existence,' there would be the unwanted extension to a deviating [probans], because in the absence of differentiation of absence by differentiation of locus, it is not possible for the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> to be a component of the pervader-hood. And if non-occurrence-in-the-non-locus-of-one's-own-counterpositive is introduced, then in cases like '[this] has monkey-contact, because of this-tree-hood,' the same situation of under-pervasion persists — hence non-locus-hood-of-one's-own-counterpositive must be introduced in the locus of the <s>hetu</s>. Keeping all this in mind, he says — [158] 'further.'

children.text:
1. abhāvapadena
saṃyogābhāvo grāhyaḥ tādātmyasaṃbandhena
svapratiyogyadhikaraṇavṛttitvasambandhena ca tadviśiṣṭaḥ sa eva, tadanyo
ghaṭādyabhāvaḥ/ evaṃ prayitogitā saṃyoganiṣṭhā, tannirūpakaḥ
saṃyogābhāvaḥ tathā svaṃ pratiyogitā tadāśrayaḥ saṃyogaḥ
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] By the word 'absence,' the absence of conjunction is to be taken. Through the relation of identity and the relation of occurrence-in-the-locus-of-one's-own-counterpositive, what is qualified thereby is that very [absence of conjunction]; what is other than that is the absence of pot and the like. Thus, the counterpositive-hood resides in conjunction; its determinand is the absence of conjunction; and 'its own' is the counterpositive-hood, whose substratum is conjunction,

children.text:
tadadhikaraṇavṛttiśca
saṃyogābhāva iti uktobhayasambandhena pratiyogitāviśiṣṭaḥ
saṃyogābhāvaḥ tadanyaḥ ghaṭādyabhāva iti samanvayo draṣṭavyaḥ/
children.translated_text: and what occurs in the locus of that [conjunction] is the absence of conjunction — thus, through the stated dual relation, the absence of conjunction is qualified by counterpositive-hood; what is other than that is the absence of pot and the like. This syntactic connection should be seen.

children.text: anumānavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of <s>anumāna</s> (inference)

children.text:
saṅgrahe [164] svayamevetyādi/ asya vākyasya
parānadhīnabhūyodarśanajanyamahānasādinirūpitasvāśrayāśrayatvarūpaparamparāsambandhāvacchinnādheyatāśrayaḥ
yatra dhūmastatrāgniriti
vyāptiviṣayakapratyakṣottarakālīnaparvatasamīpakarmakagamanāśrayaḥ
parvatavṛttivahniviṣayakasandehavān
parvatadharmikadhūmaprakārakacākṣuṣāśrayaḥ yatra
dhūmastatrāgnirityākārakavyāptiviṣayakasmaraṇāśraya ityakhaṇḍabodhaḥ/
tatra
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s> [164], 'by oneself alone' and so forth. The unitary cognition (<s>akhaṇḍabodha</s>) of this sentence is: [the person] who is the substratum of superstratum-hood delimited by the relation of indirect succession (<s>paramparā</s>) in the form of being-the-substratum-of-the-substratum determined by the kitchen and the like, produced by repeated observation not dependent on others; who is the substratum of going whose object is the vicinity of the mountain, [going which is] later than the perceptual cognition whose content is the <s>vyāpti</s> 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire'; who has doubt regarding fire occurring on the mountain; who is the substratum of visual cognition having smoke as qualifier with the mountain as qualificandum; who is the substratum of memory whose content is the <s>vyāpti</s> of the form 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire.' Therein,

children.text:
dhūmaṃ paśyan
smaratītyanena dhūmadarśanajanyatvaṃ vyāptismaraṇe labhyate/
uddeśyavidheyabhāvasthale
uddeśyatāvacchedakavidheyayorjanyajanakabhāvasambandhabhānasya dhanavān
sukhītayādau dṛṣṭatvāt/ tathā ca kathaṃ vyāptismaraṇahetutvaṃ
dhūmadarśanasyetyāśaṅkāyāṃ tadupapādayati prakāśikāyām [165] ekasaṃnbadhīti/
children.translated_text: by the expression 'seeing smoke, he remembers,' the property of being produced by the seeing of smoke is obtained for the memory of <s>vyāpti</s>. Because in the context of the subject-predicate relation, the appearance of the relation of cause-and-effect between the subject-delimitor and the predicate is observed in cases like 'the wealthy [person] is happy.' Accordingly, in response to the doubt 'how can the seeing of smoke be the cause of the memory of <s>vyāpti</s>?', the <s>Prakāśikā</s> establishes this — [165] 'of one relatum' (<s>ekasaṃbandhī</s>).

children.text: svārthānumānanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself)

children.text:
bhūyodarśanena
vyāptiṃ gṛhītveti saṅgrahavākyāt bhūyodarśanasya vyāptigrāhakatā
labhyate/ tacca nopapadyate/ anvayavyabhicārādityāśaṅkate -
dīpikāyāñ [164] nanviti/
children.translated_text: From the statement in the <s>Saṅgraha</s> 'having grasped <s>vyāpti</s> through repeated observation,' the capacity of repeated observation to grasp <s>vyāpti</s> is obtained. But this is untenable, due to the deviation from [actual] co-occurrence. He raises the objection — in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [164], 'objection' (<s>nanu</s>) and so forth.

children.text: vyāptigrahopāyanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of the means of grasping <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion)

children.text:
nanu
vyabhicārajñānadaśāyāmapi bhūyodarśanena vyāptiniścayaḥ svīkriyate
itīṣṭāpattiḥ kuto na sambhavati ityata āha - [165] vyabhicārajñānadaśāyāmityādi/ tathā cānubhavavirodha iti
bhāvaḥ/ yadi cānubhavavirodhamapyanādṛtya iṣṭāpattiḥ svīkriyate
tadāpyāha - [165] idamupalakṣaṇamiti/
idaṃ-vyabhicārajñānadaśāyāṃ
vyāptiniścayāpattirūpātiprasaṅgakathanam
upalakṣaṇam-vakṣyamāṇadūṣaṇāntarasūcakam/ [165] rasābhādisādhāraṇyād iti/ idamupalakṣaṇam
sāmānya-pratyāsattyanupagamapakṣe parvatīyavahnidhūmayoḥ
sāmānādhikaraṇyasyāsannikṛṣṭatayā mahānasādau vyāptipratyakṣe
bhānāsambhavāt parvatādau dhūmādidarśanānantaraṃ
vyāptismaraṇānupapattirityapi draṣṭavyam/ hetutāvacchedakaparyaṃntasya
vyāptitve dhūmatvādikamevāvacchedakaṃ avacchedyaṃ ca bhavatīti
avacchedyāvacchedakayoraikyaprasaṅgaḥ/ na ceṣṭāpattiḥ/
avacchedyaprakārakajñāne 'vacchedakaprakārakajñānasya kāraṇatayā
ātmāśrayaprasaṅgāt/ ātmāśrayaśca prakṛte
svajñānahetutvāpādanajanyasvajñānabhedāropātmakaḥ/ yadi svajñānaṃ
svajñānahetuḥ syāt tarhi svajñānavyatiriktaṃ syāditi tarka iti
yāvat/ yadvā yadi svaṃ svahetuḥ syāt tarhi svabhinnaṃ syādityādi
tarkarūpaḥ/ svajñānādihetutvasya svajñānādivyatiriktatvavyāpyatayā
āpādyāpādakayorvyāptisattvāt āha - [165] dhūmatvāderiti/ [165] na
kṣatiriti/ tathā ca tādṛśadhūmatvatvāvacchinnaprakāratāśālijñānaṃ
kāryam; dhūmatvādiniṣṭhānavacchinnaprakāratākajñānaṃ kāraṇamiti
kāryakāraṇayoḥ bhedāt nātmāśraya ityarthaḥ/ iṣṭāpattidoṣeṇa
tarkānutthānāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, [objection:] even in the state of cognizing deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>), the ascertainment of pervasion through repeated observation is accepted — why cannot the undesirable consequence of the desired (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>) occur? To this he says: [165] 'In the state of cognizing deviation' etc. Accordingly, there would be contradiction with experience — this is the purport. If, however, the undesirable consequence of the desired is accepted even disregarding the contradiction with experience, then too he says: [165] 'This is an indicator' (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). 'This' — the statement of the over-extension in the form of the consequence of ascertainment of pervasion in the state of cognizing deviation — is an indicator — suggesting another objection to be stated. [165] 'Because of commonality with taste etc.' — this is an indicator. It should also be seen that in the view that does not accept the extraordinary connection of universality (<s>sāmānyapratyāsatti</s>), since the co-location of fire and smoke on the mountain is not in contact [with the senses], and hence cannot appear in the perception of pervasion in the kitchen etc., the recollection of pervasion immediately after seeing smoke etc. on the mountain would be impossible. If the pervasion extends up to the delimitor of probans-hood (<s>hetutāvacchedaka</s>), then smoke-hood etc. would be both the delimitor and the delimited — and the undesirable consequence of identity of the delimited and the delimitor [would follow]. Nor is this an acceptable consequence (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>) — because, since the cognition having the delimitor as its qualifier-mode would be the cause of the cognition having the delimited as its qualifier-mode, there would be the defect of self-dependence (<s>ātmāśraya</s>). And self-dependence in the present context takes the form of superimposing a difference in self-cognition produced by establishing the causality of self-cognition. That is: the hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) is — if self-cognition were the cause of self-cognition, it would be different from self-cognition. Or alternatively, the hypothetical reasoning takes the form: if something were its own cause, it would be different from itself. Since the pervasion between what is to be established and what establishes it holds — because being the cause of self-cognition etc. is pervaded by being different from self-cognition etc. — he says: [165] 'Smoke-hood etc.' [165] 'There is no difficulty' — accordingly, the cognition possessing qualifier-mode-hood delimited by such smoke-hood-hood is the effect; the cognition not possessing qualifier-mode-hood delimited by smoke-hood etc. is the cause — since there is a difference between effect and cause, there is no self-dependence — this is the meaning. The purport is that the hypothetical reasoning does not arise due to the defect of the desired consequence (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>).

children.text:
nanu
vyabhicārajñānābhāvaḥ sahacāragrahaśca vyāptigrahaheturityuktam tatra
tādṛśaviśiṣṭavyāptigrahe kimaṃśe
vyabhicāragrahābhāvasyopayogaḥ-sāmānādhikaraṇyagrahasya ca
kutropayoga ityāśaṅkāyāṃ tadupapādayati [165] itthaṃ cetyādinā/ [165]
viśeṣaṇajñānavidhayeti/ hetuḥ
sādhyasamānādhikaraṇa iti jñānaṃ vinā hetutāvacchedake
sādhyasamānādhikaraṇavṛttitvasya durgrahatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyasya vyāptitve 'pi na doṣa ityāha - [165] vastutastviti/ [166] taddharmadharmitāvacchedakaketi/
taddharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyatāketyarthaḥ/ [166] ata eveti/
sāmānādhikaraṇyāntasyaiva vyāptitvavyavasthāpanādevetyarthaḥ/ [166] dhūmatvatveti/ dhūmatvatvasya
dhūmetarāsamavetatvasahitanikhiladhūmavṛttitvarūpatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, [question:] it was stated that the absence of cognition of deviation and the apprehension of co-occurrence are the causes of the apprehension of pervasion. In the apprehension of pervasion qualified by such [conditions], what role does the absence of apprehension of deviation play — and where does the apprehension of co-location play its role? In response to this doubt, he establishes it with [165] 'In this way' etc. [165] 'As a means of the cognition of the qualifier' — because without the cognition 'the probans occurs in what is co-located with the probandum,' it is difficult to grasp the occurrence-in-what-is-co-located-with-the-probandum of the delimitor of probans-hood — this is the purport. That there is no defect even if the co-location with the probandum is [included] in the pervasion, he says: [165] 'In reality, however.' [166] 'Having as delimitor the property-hood and locus-hood of that' — the meaning is: having qualificand-hood delimited by that property. [166] 'For this very reason' — the meaning is: because only the co-location-based [pervasion] is established as pervasion-hood. [166] 'Smoke-hood-hood' — because smoke-hood-hood has the nature of occurring in all smokes together with not being inherent in what is other than smoke — this is the purport.

children.text:
digiti/ ayamāśayaḥ -
hetutāvacchedakāvacchinnaprakāratānirūpitavyāpakatvaprakāratānirūpita
sādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnaprakāratānirūpitasāmānādhikaraṇyaprakāratāni rūpitahetutāvacchedakadharmasambandhāvacchinnaprakāratānirūpitapakṣatāvaccherakāvacchinnaviśeṣyatākaniścayatvena
hetutvopagamāt na viśiṣṭaparāmarśasya anumitihetutvānupapattiḥ/
evaṃ pūrvamate vahnimān jalāt ityādau
sādhyasamānādhikaraṇāvṛttihetutāvacchedakaṃ virodhaḥ/ etanmate ca
sādhyādhikaraṇāvṛttihetuḥ tathā/ evaṃ pūrvamate hetutāvacchedakasya
pakṣaviśeṣaṇatāvacchedakatayā svarūpato 'pi niveśasya
svarūpāsiddherhetvābhāsatopapattaye āvaśyakatayā
vyāptigrahaniṣṭhahetutāvacchedakagarbhe tredhā
hetutāvacchedakapraveśanamāvaśyakamiti gauravam etanmate tu dvidheti
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — the purport is: since probans-hood is accepted by virtue of being a determinate cognition whose qualificand-hood is delimited by the delimitor of locus-hood — [which is] delimited by the qualifier-mode-hood of the property bearing the relation to the delimitor of probans-hood — [which is] determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of co-location — [which is] determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of the probandum delimited by the delimitor of probandum-hood — [which is] determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of pervader-hood — [which is] determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of the probans delimited by the delimitor of probans-hood — there is no impossibility that the qualified subsumptive reflection (<s>viśiṣṭaparāmarśa</s>) be the cause of inference. Similarly, in the previous view, in cases like 'water possesses fire,' the delimitor of probans-hood that does not occur in what is co-located with the probandum is contradiction (<s>virodha</s>). In this view, however, a probans that does not occur in the locus of the probandum is such. Similarly, in the previous view, since the delimitor of probans-hood must necessarily be included even by its own nature as a delimitor of the qualifier of the thesis, and since this is necessary for accounting for the pseudo-reason of non-establishment of own-nature (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>), the delimitor of probans-hood must enter in three ways into the content of the apprehension of pervasion — which is cumbersome. In this view, however, [it enters] in only two ways —

children.text:
lāghavam/ evaṃ
hetuprakāratānirūpitavyāpakatvaprakāratānirūpitasādhyaprakāratānirūpi tasamānādhikaraṇaprakāratānirūpitavṛttitvaprakāratānirūpitahetutāvacchedakaprakāratānirūpitahetutāvacchedakāvacchinnaprakāratānirūpitapakṣatāvacchedakāvacchinnaviśeṣyatākaniścayatvena
pūrvamate hetutvaṃ vācyamiti gauravam/ etanmate tu na tatheti
lāghavamiti/ atra ca vyabhicāra saṃśayasya vyāptipratyakṣaṃ pratyeva
virodhitā na tu vyāptyanumityādau tatra tasyānukūlatvāt/ tathā ca
vyāptipratyakṣatvameva vyabhicārasaṃśayapratibadhyatāvacchedakam, na
tvanumityādisādhāraṇavyāptijñānatvam/ tathā sati
vyabhicārasaṃśayadaśāyāṃ
children.translated_text: hence the parsimony. Similarly, in the previous view, probans-hood must be stated as being a determinate cognition whose qualificand-hood is delimited by the delimitor of thesis-hood, delimited by the qualifier-mode-hood of the probans delimited by the delimitor of probans-hood, determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of occurrence-ness, determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of co-location, determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of the probandum, determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of pervader-hood, determined by the qualifier-mode-hood of the probans — which is cumbersome. In this view, however, it is not so — hence the parsimony. And here, the deviation-doubt acts as an obstruction only with respect to the perception of pervasion, not with respect to the inference of pervasion etc., because it is favorable to those. Accordingly, it is perception-of-pervasion-hood alone that is the delimitor of the obstructed-hood of the deviation-doubt, not the general property of pervasion-cognition-hood common [also] to inference etc. Otherwise, in the state of deviation-doubt,

children.text:
vyāptyanumityanupapatteḥ/ evaṃ caikadharmāvacchinnaṃ prati
saṃśayaniścayasādhāraṇavyabhicārajñānatvena naikaṃ pratibandhakatvaṃ
sambhavati/ evaṃ tadavacchinnābhāvasnaya hetutvamapi/ kiṃ ca
vyabhicārasaṃśayapratibandhakatāyāṃ tarka uttejakaḥ/
niścayapratibandhakatāyāṃ tu sa na tatheti
tarkābhāvaviśiṣṭavyabhicārasaṃśayatvena vyāptipratyakṣapratibandhakatvaṃ
tadaviśeṣitavyabhicāraniścayatvena ca vyāptigrahapratibandhakatvamiti na
pratibandhakataikyasambhava iti ekasyābhāvasya hetutvaṃ na
sambhavatītyabhisandhāya [166] hṛdayamityuktam/ [166] dhūmāgnyorityādivākye dīpikāsthe vyāptigrahe iti
saptamyantasya anvayānupapattimāśaṅkya śeṣaṃ pūrayati - [166] vyāptigrahe utpatsyamāna iti/ tathā ca 'yasya ca bhāvena
bhāvalakṣaṇam' iti sūtreṇa prāptā saptamī vyāptigrahapadottaraṃ
utpattiṃ bodhayati/ tasyāśca vyabhicāraśaṅkānivartaka ityatra
nivṛttau svaprākkālīnatvasaṃbandhena anvayaḥ/ ajñātasya vidheyatvāt
jñātasya coddeśyatvāt sāmānyato vyabhicāraśaṅkānivartakasya
kasyacit avagatatvena darśitadīpikāvākye yojanayā anvayamāha -
[166] vyabhicāraśaṅkānirvataka ityādi/ tarkākāraḥ
kathamityāśaṅkāyāmāha - [166]
sa ceti [166] asannikarṣeṇetyādi/
pratyakṣaviṣayatāyāḥ sannikarṣavyāpyatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: inference of pervasion would become impossible. And thus, with respect to what is delimited by a single property, it is impossible for one property of deviation-cognition-hood — common to both doubt and determinate cognition — to have a single obstructive role. Similarly, the causal role of its delimiting-absence [would also be impossible]. Moreover, in the obstructive role of deviation-doubt, hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) is the stimulant; but in the obstructive role of determinate [deviation-]cognition, it is not so. Therefore, the property of being deviation-doubt qualified by the absence of hypothetical reasoning is the obstructor with respect to perceptual pervasion, while the property of being determinate deviation-cognition not qualified by that is the obstructor with respect to the apprehension of pervasion — hence there is no possibility of unity of the obstructive roles, and so the causal role of a single absence is not possible. With this intention [165] he says 'the heart [of the matter].' [166] Anticipating the difficulty of syntactic connection of the locative ending in the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'of smoke and fire etc.' in the phrase 'in the apprehension of pervasion,' he completes the remainder: [166] 'About to arise in the apprehension of pervasion.' Accordingly, the locative obtained by the rule 'when the existence of one [entails] the existence [of another]' (<s>sūtra</s>) conveys that the arising is after the term 'apprehension of pervasion.' And the syntactic connection of 'remover of the doubt of deviation' is with the removal, through the relation of being prior to itself. Since what is unknown is the predicate and what is known is the subject — and since some remover of the doubt of deviation in general is already known — he states the syntactic connection in the demonstrated <s>Dīpikā</s> sentence through construal: [166] 'Remover of the doubt of deviation' etc. When the question arises as to what form the hypothetical reasoning takes, he says: [166] 'And that' [166] 'By the absence of contact' etc. The purport is that the object-hood of perception is pervaded by sense-contact.

children.text: parārthānumānanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of inference for the sake of others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>).

children.text:
parārthānumānaprayojaka ityādi/ ayaṃ
bhāvaḥ -- parārthaṃ anumānaṃ yasmāditi vyutpattyā
bahuvrīhāvuttaraparasyānyapadārthalākṣaṇikatayā parārthānumānaśabdena
parārthānumānaprayojakatvāvacchinnaṃ bodhyata iti
tasyaupacārikatvamiti/
children.translated_text: 'Productive of inference for the sake of others' etc. The purport is: by the etymological derivation 'that from which inference for the sake of another [arises]' — in the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, the latter member 'other' is used in the secondary sense of another word-meaning — hence the word <s>parārthānumāna</s> conveys what is delimited by the property of being productive of inference for the sake of another, and thus it is used figuratively (<s>aupacārika</s>).

children.text:
yattu -
parārthānumānaśabde karmadhārayamāśritya prayojakatārūpalakṣaṇayā
pañcāvayavavākyatvāvacchinnameva tena bodhyate/
parārthānumānaprayojaka ityuktistu śakyasaṃbandhapradarśanārtheti ---
tattuccham-parārthāna-mānaśabdasya vākyarūpatayā naiyāyikaiḥ
vākyalakṣaṇāyā anabhyupagamāt/ vākyaśakyāprasiddhyā
śakyasaṃbandharūpalakṣaṇāyā asambhavāt/ anyathā gabhīrāyāṃ nadyāṃ ghoṣa
ityādau nadyādipadasya granthakṛtāṃ
gabhīranadītīrādilakṣakatvakathanavirodhāpātāt/ ayamatra saṃgrahaḥ --
children.translated_text: As for [the view that] — relying on a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional) compound in the word <s>parārthānumāna</s>, through secondary signification in the form of causal relation, what is conveyed by it is precisely what is delimited by being a five-membered sentence. And the statement 'productive of inference for the sake of another' is for the purpose of showing the relation of denotation — that is trifling. Because the word <s>parārthānumāna</s>, being of the nature of a sentence, and since the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> do not accept the definition of a sentence, and since denotation of a sentence is not established, the secondary signification in the form of a denotation-relation is impossible. Otherwise, there would be the undesirable consequence of contradicting the statement by the authors of treatises that in expressions like 'there is a noise in the deep river,' the word 'river' etc. has the bank of the deep river etc. as its secondary referent. Here is the summary:

children.text:
"bahuvrīhiḥ padārthānumānaśabde 'tra
kīrtyate/
children.translated_text: The <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) is declared here regarding the word <s>parārthānumāna</s>.

children.text:
kecittu bruvate
karmadhārayaṃ tatra tanna sat//
children.translated_text: Some, however, say it is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional compound) — that is not correct.

children.text:
tathātve tasya
vākyatvāt lakṣaṇā nopapadyate/
children.translated_text: If so, since it would be a sentence, secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) would not be tenable.

children.text:
vākyaśakyasyāprasiddheḥ
vākyayogo hi lakṣaṇā//
children.translated_text: Because the denotatum of a sentence is not established — for secondary signification is [only] a connection with a sentence[-level denotatum].

children.text:
asmanmate bahuvrīhau
lakṣakaṃ padamuttaram/
children.translated_text: In our view, in the <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, the latter member is the denoting word.

children.text: tatprayojakatārūpaśakyayogena yujyate"//
children.translated_text: It is justified through its connection with a denotatum in the form of its causal role.

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the verse].

children.text:
atra cānumānaśabdaḥ
parārthānumānaprayojakaparaḥ/ parārthaṃpadaṃ tātparyagrāhakamiti
keṣāñcinmatam/ anumānaśabdaḥ anumānaprayojanakaparaḥ/

vivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: And here, the word <s>anumāna</s> (inference) refers to what is productive of inference for the sake of another. The word <s>parārtha</s> (for another's sake) serves as the indicator of the intended meaning — this is the view of some. [Alternatively,] the word <s>anumāna</s> refers to what is productive of inference, and the meaning of the word <s>parārtha</s> is syntactically connected with inference, which is a part of that [compound] — this is the view of others. This is the distinction.

children.translated_text: 'The definition of <s>nyāya</s> (syllogism) should be understood.' Accordingly, without knowing the definition of <s>nyāya</s>, the definition to be stated — which involves the component of being a member of a syllogism (<s>nyāyāvayavatva</s>) — would be difficult to understand; thus this apprehension is removed. Now, [172] from the summary statement beginning with 'by this one who has been made to understand, from the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>),' the meaning obtained is: another person also has the inference generated by the inferential mark, which is the object of the cognition produced by the collection of the five members beginning with the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>). But that does not work — because it is impossible for the inferential mark as a mere cognition to be the cause of inference; otherwise, inference would become impossible in the state of cognition of a past inferential mark etc. Anticipating this [objection] — the word <s>liṅga</s> here refers to the subsumptive reflection on the inferential mark (<s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s>); hence the meaning obtained is: another person also possesses the inference generated by the subsumptive reflection on the mark, which is produced by such a collection — thus there is no impossibility. Intending this resolution, he says: [172] 'By this' etc. [172] In the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'the expression of the thesis as possessing the probandum,' the word <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) refers to what is delimited by the delimitor of probandum-hood. The meaning of the instrumental case is qualifier-mode-hood. The word <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) refers to what is delimited by the delimitor of thesis-hood — with this intention, he states the meaning: [172]

Therefore, since the alternative interpretation is to be stated and it alone is supported by reasoning, with that intention — since the pure delimitor of probandum-hood must necessarily be included for the purpose of excluding the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) — if the word denoting the probandum in the example were to refer to the probandum qualified by being pervaded by the probans,

He states the purpose of including qualificand-hood and qualifier-mode-hood as determiner and determined, as well as the delimitor of probandum-hood: [163] with 'from the application' etc. Since the qualifier-mode-hood delimited by the delimitor of probandum-hood in the verbal cognition generated by the application (<s>upanaya</s>) 'the mountain possesses smoke pervaded by fire' lacks the property of being determined by the qualificand-hood delimited by the delimitor of thesis-hood — and since in cases where substance etc. is the probandum and smoke etc. is the probans, the qualificand-hood of the thesis determined by the verbal cognition generated by the application 'this possesses smoke pervaded by substance' lacks the property of being delimited by the delimitor of probandum-hood — there is no over-extension in the application. This is the purport. The delimitor of the probandum-relation is included to block the application in cases where fire etc. bears the probans-probandum relation through temporal or conjunctive relations. Now, let the definition simply be the property of generating such cognition — why

pakṣatāvacchedakāvacchinnaviśeṣaṇatāpannasādhyānvitaliṅgapratipādakatvasya

children.translated_text: Anticipating the objection 'by including sentence-hood,' he states its meaningfulness as excluding sentences outside the <s>nyāya</s> (syllogism) — with [172] 'of the word sentence.' The inclusion of member-hood is for the purpose of excluding the over-extension in the portion 'this possesses the probandum' within the <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion). [173] 'Hereafter too' — in the definitions of <s>hetu</s> (reason) and the like as well. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [172] 'ending in the fifth case' and so forth — by the derivation 'that in which the fifth case is internal,' the property of ending in the fifth case amounts to being constituted by a fifth-case ending that does not have a constituent word prior to it within its own [compound], and thus reduces to being qualified by the fifth case. The qualification is through both the relations of being-constituted-by and being-the-delimitor-of-the-counter-positiveness-of-difference-residing-in-itself. The delimitor-hood is through the relation of being-prior-as-a-constituent-word-of-itself. Since the purpose of that inclusion — namely, the exclusion of the <s>nigamana</s> 'therefore it possesses fire' — is obvious, he states the purpose of including 'conveying the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark)' — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [173] with 'this is not from a stick' and so forth. [173] 'Not produced from stick-conjunction' and so forth — the mention of both qualifier and qualificand is for preventing deviation in pot and the like and in stick-form and the like. Since the inclusion of being-constituted-by-the-fifth-case alone already excludes the <s>upanaya</s>, the purpose of including 'ending with' that is only the exclusion of the <s>nigamana</s>. Since the <s>pratijñā</s> such as 'the mountain possesses fire' lacks the property of ending in the fifth case, it is disregarded. Because 'this from a stick' and the like would conflict with tradition, 'not from a stick' was stated. To prevent confusion in the word <s>liṅga</s> with [grammatical] gender (<s>liṅga</s>) in the form of masculine and the like, he says [173] '<s>hetu</s>.' Although even in cases such as 'this is not from a stick, because of being a substance not produced from stick-conjunction' — where the co-located property is 'not produced from a stick' — there is still over-extension, nevertheless, since what is intended is 'conveying the <s>liṅga</s> as connected with the <s>sādhya</s> and qualified by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>' — which has the form of generating a cognition possessing content-hood of the <s>hetu</s> as determined by the content-hood of the <s>sādhya</s> as determined by the content-hood delimited by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s> — there is no defect.
