children.translated_text: no — because purity (<s>śuddha</s>) is included as a qualifier of the <s>liṅga</s> within the body of 'conveying the <s>liṅga</s>,' and since pure <s>liṅga</s>-conveying — which has the form of generating a cognition having content-hood of the <s>liṅga</s> not delimited by anything beyond the delimitor of the <s>liṅga</s>-hood under consideration — has no over-extension, because in the cognition generated by the <s>nigamana</s>, the additional element of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) appears in the <s>liṅga</s>. Since the property of conveying <s>vyāpti</s> also exists in the <s>upanaya</s> and the like, he says [173] 'possessing the <s>hetu</s> under consideration' and so forth. Since the natural interpretation alone in the proponent's sentence would cause over-extension, he says [173] 'established secondary signification' (<s>nirūḍha</s>). The meaning is: residing in the referent that has been the object of purport from beginningless time. With the intention that when meaningfulness is possible, purposelessness is inappropriate, he says [173] 'alternatively.' Since without the cognition of <s>vyāpti</s> from the <s>udāharaṇa</s>, its orientation toward <s>vyāpti</s> would not be maintained, hence he says [173] 'and thus.' And thus, taking the subsequent mental cognition having <s>vyāpti</s> as its content from the <s>udāharaṇa</s>, the orientation toward the apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> in the form of having been uttered with the desire for <s>vyāpti</s>-apprehension is what is intended by 'conveying <s>vyāpti</s>' — this is to be established. This is the purport. [173] 'The general direction' — the purport is: in 'whatever possesses the <s>hetu</s> is not from a stick' as the <s>udāharaṇa</s> sentence in cases like 'this is not from a stick, because of being a substance not produced from stick-conjunction,' when the subject is not intended, the word 'not' would have no capacity to generate cognition.

children.translated_text: 'Conveying the <s>liṅga</s> as qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>' — anticipating the over-extension of the definition of <s>upanaya</s> stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s> to the <s>nigamana</s>, he says [173] 'having a qualificand qualified by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>.' Since the relation of determinans-determinandum is included, there is no defect — this is the purport. [173] 'By supplying the complement "is employed"' — this is stated because, in the analysis that takes <s>pakṣadharmatājñānāya</s> as 'for the purpose of the cognition of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s>' with the fourth case as a case-ending requiring a verb, it depends on a verbal complement. But if the derivation 'that of which the meaning is the cognition of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s>' is accepted, then supplying a complement is not necessary. By supplying the word 'statement' (<s>vacana</s>), the neuter gender is obtained — this should be noted. [172] 'A statement of the <s>pakṣa</s> as possessing the <s>sādhya</s> by virtue of the <s>hetu</s>' — in the definition of <s>nigamana</s>, '<s>hetu</s>-<s>sādhya</s>' is a fifth-case compound. The fifth case should be justified by splitting the grammatical connection. Alternatively, 'of the <s>hetu</s>, the <s>sādhya</s>' — the sixth case is a secondary one conveying the property of being indicated (<s>jñāpyatva</s>). Now he states the meaning with the understanding that the compound should be understood by the rule '<s>sup sape</s>' — [173] 'by the cognition of the <s>hetu</s>.' [173] 'Having the possessor of the <s>sādhya</s> as content' — the meaning is: having a qualificand delimited by <s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s> and having the qualifier-mode of such <s>sādhya</s>. Now, since the relation of the <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>sādhya</s> is already obtained from the <s>pratijñā</s> and the rest, the <s>nigamana</s> is purposeless — anticipating this objection, and accepting that the word denoting the <s>hetu</s> in the <s>nigamana</s> has secondary signification referring to the <s>hetu</s> qualified by unsublated-ness and the like, and keeping in mind that the verbal nature of that apprehension is inappropriate because secondary signification is inferior, the mental apprehension of unsublated-ness and the like alone is the purpose of the <s>nigamana</s> — he says this in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [172] with 'unsublated-ness and the like.' By the word 'and the like,' the property of being free from counterbalancing reasons is included. 'Unsublated-ness and the like' — [means] the apprehension of unsublated-ness and the like. By that, the objection that, in the literal reading, the purpose constituted by the being-generated-of-the-content would be impossible, and hence there would be incoherence — that is refuted. The second case [accusative] in 'at a subsequent time' is in the sense of absolute conjunction. By that, it is obtained that the apprehension of unsublated-ness and the like in the <s>hetu</s> invariably arises after the verbal cognition generated by the <s>nigamana</s>. Since the verbal nature of that apprehension is impossible in the manner stated, in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [176] he says 'it should be understood as mental.'

bhāvaḥ/ [177] atra tvadabhimatetyādi/ etena
mīmāṃsakasyāpi jñānadvaye pūrvavṛttitvaṃ kalpanīyamiti sūcitam/
[177] śābdetīti/ tadbodhakapadamantareṇa tadbhānāsambhavāditi
bhāvaḥ/ etena pratyakṣasthale sannikarṣavaśāt kasyacit
hetutāvacchedakasya bhānaṃ durvāramiti na tatra vyabhicārasambhava iti
sūcitam/ dīpikāyām [177] parāmarśasyāvaśyakatayeti/
tvadabhimatajñānadvayaṃ vinaiva
viśiṣṭaparāmarśasyānumitipūrvamupeyatayetyarthaḥ/ nanaṃ kvacit
viśiṣṭaparāmarśādanumitirastu kiṃ sarvatra
viśiṣṭaparāmarśakalpanayetyata āha -- [177] lāghaveneti/ kasya
lāghavamityāśaṅgāyāmāha --- prakāśikāyām [177] kalpanālāghavenetyartha iti/ [177] jñānadvaye-vyāptijñānatvapakṣadharmatājñānatvāvacchinnadvaye/ [177] viśiṣṭaparāmarśe-vyāptiviśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhiparāmarśatvāvacchinne/
tathā caikadharmāvacchinne 'nanyathāsiddhatvādikalpanamapekṣya
pūrvoktadharmāvacchinnadvaye tatkalpanasya gurutvāditi bhāvaḥ/ nanu
vyāptigrahapakṣadharmatāgrahayoḥ prātisvikarūpābhyāṃ hetutvaṃ
nopeyate/ yenoktadoṣassyāt/ api tu
vyāptigrahaviśiṣṭapakṣadharmatājñānatvena tathātvamupeyate/ evaṃ
cāsmanmate 'pi ekadharmāvacchinna eva tatkalpanamiti lāghavaṃ
durapahnavam/ vinigamanāvirahastulya eva/
upadarśitaśābdaparāmarśasthanapale vyabhicārastu kāryatāvacchedakagarbhe
viśiṣṭaparāmarśāvyavahitottaratvaṃ niveśyaiva parihartavyaḥ/ anyathā
sādhyavyāpyahetutāvacchedakāvacchinnavāniti viśiṣṭaparāmarśaṃsya tatra
vyabhicāraprasaṅgāt ityatrāha -- [177] vastutastviti/
children.translated_text: 'Of what is already established' — by this it is indicated that invariable prior occurrence is accepted by both [parties]. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [176] 'for what purpose must it be accepted' — the purport is: by the principle that it is for that very reason. [177] 'But in your view' and so forth — by this it is indicated that even in the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>'s view, prior occurrence must be postulated in both cognitions. [177] 'Verbal' — the purport is: because the appearance of that is impossible without the word that conveys it. By this it is indicated that in the case of perception, since the appearance of some delimitor of reason-hood through the force of the sense-contact is irresistible, the possibility of deviation there does not arise. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [177] 'because of the necessity of the apprehension.' The meaning is: because the qualified apprehension must be accepted as prior to inference even without the two cognitions accepted by you. Now, let the inference arise from the qualified apprehension in some cases — why postulate the qualified apprehension everywhere? — hence he says [177] 'by parsimony.' Anticipating the question 'parsimony of what?', he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> [177] 'the meaning is: by the parsimony of postulation.' [177] 'In the two cognitions' — in the two [cognitions] delimited by <s>vyāpti</s>-cognition-hood and <s>pakṣadharmatā</s>-cognition-hood. [177] 'In the qualified apprehension' — delimited by the property of being an apprehension that grasps the qualificandness of [the <s>pakṣa</s>] as qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>. And thus, compared to postulating invariable-connection and the like in what is delimited by a single property, the postulation of the same in what is delimited by the aforementioned two properties involves cumbersomeness — this is the purport. Now, the reason-hood of the <s>vyāpti</s>-apprehension and the <s>pakṣadharmatā</s>-apprehension is not accepted through their individual forms, so that the stated defect would arise; rather, their reason-hood is accepted through the property of being the cognition of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>-apprehension. And thus, even in our view, the postulation is in what is delimited by a single property — so parsimony is undeniable. The absence of a decisive ground is exactly equal. As for the deviation in the case of the verbal apprehension that was illustrated, it must be resolved only by including the property of being immediately subsequent to the qualified apprehension within the body of the delimitor of the effect-hood. Otherwise, since the qualified apprehension of the form 'it possesses what is delimited by the delimitor of <s>hetu</s>-hood, which is pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s>' would be subject to deviation there — hence he says [177] 'in reality, however.'

children.text:
avadheyamiti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ -
mīmāṃsakamate 'numitikāraṇatāvacchedakakoṭau sāmānādhikaraṇyasya
dvidhā jñānatvasya ca praveśaḥ āvaśyakaḥ/ asmanmate tu na tathā/ evaṃ
vyāptigrahaviśiṣṭapakṣadharmatājñānatvena
pakṣadharmatājñānaviśiṣṭavyāptigrahatvena vā kāraṇateti
vinigamanāvirahāt kāraṇatādvayaṃ tanmate vaktavyam/ asmanmate tu
vinigamanāvirahasambhave 'pi samaniyatakāraṇatānāmabhedopagamāt na
kāraṇatādvayāvakāśaḥ/ evaṃ
vyāptyavacchinnapratiyogitākatvaviśiṣṭasamavāyādisambandhāvacchinnatādṛśadhūmādiprakāratāśālijñātvena
hetutve vyāptyaṃśe niścayatvamapi na niveśanīyam; asmanmate
viśeṣaṇatāvacchedakāṃśe saṃśayātmakajñānasya
viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhitvāyogāditi lāghavamiti/ [177] vinigamanāviraheṇeti/ liṅgaviśeṣitaparāmarśatvenaiva
kāraṇatvaṃ vaktavyamityatra niyāmakābhāvenetyarthaḥ/ uddeśyatāsaṃbandhena
anumitiṃ prati hetutāvacchedakasaṃbandhena saṃyogādinā
dhūmādihetoḥ kāraṇatvaṃ durghaṭamityāśayenāha - [177] tatrāpyanumiteriti/
children.translated_text: 'It should be noted' — the purport is: in the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view, the inclusion of co-location in two ways and of cognition-hood in the delimitor of the cause-hood of inference is necessary; but in our view, it is not so. Furthermore, since the causal relation [may be described] either through the property of being the cognition of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>-apprehension, or through the property of being the <s>vyāpti</s>-apprehension qualified by the cognition of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> — and since there is no decisive ground for distinguishing [between these two] — two causal relations must be stated in their view. But in our view, even when there is no decisive ground, since we accept that equi-extensive causal relations are identical, there is no room for two causal relations. Similarly, when the reason-hood is [stated] through the property of being a cognition possessing the qualifier-mode of smoke and the like delimited by the relation of inherence and the like, and possessing the counter-positive-hood delimited by <s>vyāpti</s>, the property of being determinate need not be included in the <s>vyāpti</s> portion; because in our view, a cognition that is doubtful in the qualifier-delimiting portion cannot grasp the qualificandness qualified by the qualifier — hence parsimony. [177] 'By the absence of a decisive ground' — the meaning is: because there is no determining factor for stating the causal relation only through the property of being an apprehension qualified by the <s>liṅga</s>. With the intention that the causal relation of smoke and the like as <s>hetu</s> to the inference through the relation of conjunction and the like, with the delimiting relation of <s>hetu</s>-hood and the relation of being-the-subject, is difficult to establish, he says [177] 'even there, of the inference' and so forth.

children.text: anvayavyatirekinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of the <s>Anvaya</s> (Positive) and <s>Vyatireka</s> (Negative) [Concomitance]

children.text:
anvayena
vyatirekeṇa ca vyāptimaditi saṃgrahe 'nvayaśabdaḥ
hetusādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyarūpānvayasahacāraparaḥ/ grahagrāhyatvaṃ
tṛtīyārthaḥ/ ata eva kevalavyatirekinirāsaḥ/ vyatirekeṇetyatrāpi
vyatireko vyatirekasahacāraḥ/ sādhyābhāvahetvabhāvayoḥ
sāmānādhikaraṇyarūpaḥ/ tṛtīyārthaḥ pūrvavat prakāśikāyām
anvayasahacāretyādi/ kevalavyatirekivāraṇāya satyantam/
kevalānvayivyudāsāya viśeṣyam/ anvayavyāptimattvamātraniveśe
'pṛthivī itarebhyo bhidyate ganadhavattvāt'
ityādivyatirekivāraṇāsambhavaḥ/ uktapariṣkāre
tvanvayavyāptigrāhakadṛṣṭāntavirahāt na hetusādhyayoḥ sahacāragraha
iti na doṣaḥ/ viśeṣyadale tu viśiṣṭayaiva vyāptirupādeyā/ na
tu tādṛśagrahagrāhyatvenāpīti bodhyam/ saṃgrahe [180] vahnau sādhya iti/ vahniniṣṭhasādhyatānirūpakaṃ
dhūmavattvamityarthaḥ/ dṛṣṭāntavākye mahānasādipadaṃ saptamyantam/
yatretyanurodhāt/
children.translated_text: 'Possessing <s>vyāpti</s> through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance)' — in the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, the word <s>anvaya</s> refers to <s>anvaya</s>-accompaniment in the form of the co-location of <s>hetu</s> and <s>sādhya</s>. The meaning of the third case [instrumental] is: apprehensibility of the apprehension. Hence the exclusion of the purely negative reason (<s>kevalavyatirekin</s>). In 'through <s>vyatireka</s>' as well, <s>vyatireka</s> means <s>vyatireka</s>-accompaniment — the co-location of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> and the absence of the <s>hetu</s>. The meaning of the third case is as before. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, '<s>anvaya</s>-accompaniment' and so forth — the portion ending with 'positive' is for excluding the purely negative reason. The qualificand [clause] is for excluding the purely positive reason (<s>kevalānvayin</s>). If merely the possession of <s>anvaya-vyāpti</s> were included, the exclusion of the <s>vyatireka</s> (negative-only) reason in 'earth differs from the others because of possessing smell' and the like would be impossible. But with the stated refinement, since there is no example that serves to apprehend the <s>anvaya-vyāpti</s>, the co-occurrence of <s>hetu</s> and <s>sādhya</s> cannot be apprehended — hence there is no defect. But in the qualificand clause, it is the qualified <s>vyāpti</s> itself that is to be taken up, not as apprehensible by such apprehension — this should be understood. In the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, [180] 'fire is the <s>sādhya</s>' — the meaning is: smoke-possession is what determines the <s>sādhya</s>-hood residing in fire. In the example-sentence, the word <s>mahānasa</s> (kitchen) and the like takes the seventh-case [locative] ending, in conformity with the word <s>yatra</s> (where).

children.text: kevalānvayinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of the Purely Positive Reason (<s>Kevalānvayin</s>)

children.text:
nanu
kevalānvayitvameva hetorlakṣaṇam kuto noktamityata āha - [182] kevalānvayisādhyaketi/ ghaṭo 'bhidheyaḥ pṛthivītvāt
ityādihetorityarthaḥ/ [182]
tadeva kevalānvayitvameva/ nanu
gaganābhāvavān meyatvāt ityādāvavyāptiḥ/ sādhyasya
gaganādyātmakābhāvapratiyogitvāt/ evaṃ saṃyogābhāvavān
prameyatvāt ityādāvapi sādhyasya
saṃyogādyātmakābhāvapratiyogitvādityatrāha - [182] niravacchinneti/ sapatamīnirdeśyaṃ yat vilakṣaṇamavacchedyatvaṃ
tadrahitetyarthaḥ/ tenādheyatāyāḥ kiñciddharmāvacchedyatvaniyame 'pi na
kṣatiḥ/ tathā ca gaganādeḥ vṛttimattvābhāvāt saṃyogādiniṣṭhavṛtteḥ
niravacchinnatvavirahācca noktadoṣadvayāvakāśa daiti bhāvaḥ/ kecittu
- svavirodhivṛttimadatyanatābhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ kevalānvayitvam/
yadyapyatra svapadenānuyogyupādāne tattadvyaktiviśrāmāpattiḥ
tāvadanyatamatvaṃ ca durgraham/ pratiyogyupādāne
vīpsāvirahe 'tiprasaṃgaḥ vīpsākaraṇe durjñeyatā; tathāpi
vṛttimadatyantābhāvaviśiṣṭānyatvaṃ tat/ 1vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svapratiyogitvasvaniṣṭhabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvobhāyasambandhena/
avacchedakatā svādhikaraṇavṛttitvasaṃbandhāvacchinnā/ ato na doṣa
ityāhuḥ/ taccintyam --
saṃyogādāvuktakevalānvayitvamativyāptamiti
svānadhikaraṇavṛttitvapraveśanasyāvaśyakatvena svātantryeṇa
vṛttimattvaviśeṣaṇaniveśavaiyarthyāpatteḥ/
svādhikaraṇanirūpitaniravacchinnādheyatāśūnyatvapraveśe ca
saṃyogābhāvasya kevalānvayitābhaṅgāpatteḥ/ saṃyogādirūpābhāvasya
tathātvāt/ vṛttāvapi niravacchinnatvaniveśane ca
prakṣālanāddhinyāyāpatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: Why is it not stated that exclusively-positive-ness (<s>kevalānvayitva</s>) alone is the definition of the probans? To this he says — [182] 'whose <s>sādhya</s> is exclusively positive' etc. The meaning is: of a probans such as 'a pot is name-able, because of earth-nature (<s>pṛthivītva</s>)' and the like. [182] 'That very' — exclusively-positive-ness alone. Objection: In cases like 'possessing the absence of sky, because of knowability (<s>meyatva</s>),' there is non-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>), since the <s>sādhya</s> has as its counter-positive an absence of the nature of sky and the like. Similarly, in 'possessing the absence of conjunction, because of knowability' and the like also, since the <s>sādhya</s> has as its counter-positive an absence of the nature of conjunction and the like — to address this he says — [182] 'unrestricted' etc. The meaning is: devoid of that distinctive delimitable-ness which is to be denoted by the seventh case-ending. Therefore, even though the superstratum-relation (<s>ādheyatā</s>) is restricted to being delimitable by some property, there is no difficulty. And thus, since sky and the like lack the property of having occurrence (<s>vṛttimattva</s>), and since the occurrence residing in conjunction and the like lacks unrestricted-ness, there is no scope for the two stated defects — this is the purport. Some, however, [define it as]: not being the counter-positive of an absolute absence residing in what possesses the occurrence of what is incompatible with itself — that is exclusively-positive-ness. Although here, when 'itself' is taken in the sense of the correlate, there is the undesirable consequence of resting upon each respective particular, and moreover, the both-ness is difficult to grasp; when the counter-positive is taken, there is over-extension in the absence of desiderative expression, and obscurity in the case of desiderative expression — nevertheless, that [exclusively-positive-ness] is otherness qualified by an absolute absence residing in what possesses occurrence. The qualification is through the dual relation of counter-positive-ness of itself, and delimitor-hood of the counter-positive-hood of the difference not residing in itself. The delimitor-hood is delimited by the relation of occurrence residing in one's own substrate. Therefore there is no defect — so they say. That is to be considered: because the stated exclusively-positive-ness in the case of conjunction and the like is over-extended, since the inclusion of not-occurring-in-one's-own-non-substrate is necessary, the independent inclusion of the qualifier 'possessing occurrence' (<s>vṛttimattva</s>) would be rendered purposeless; and because, upon the inclusion of the emptiness of unrestricted superstratum-relation determined by one's own substrate, there would result the breaking of the exclusively-positive-ness of the absence of conjunction, since the absence of the form of conjunction and the like is of that nature; and because, even upon the inclusion of unrestricted-ness in the occurrence, there would result the maxim of 'washing what was already clean' (<s>prakṣālanāddhinyāya</s>).

children.text: kevalavyatirekinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of the exclusively-negative (<s>kevalavyatirekin</s>)

children.text:
vyatirekamātravyāptikamiti saṃgrahapaṅktau
anvayavyāptiśūnyatve sati vyatirekavyāptimattvamartho labhyate/ atra
cānvayavyatirekivāraṇāya viśeṣaṇam, vyabhicārivāraṇāya
viśeṣyamiti bodhyam/ tacca na ghaṭate
hetuvyāpakasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyarūpāyāḥ
sādhyābhāvavadavṛttitvarūpāyā vā vyāpteḥ pṛthivī itarebhyo bhidyate
gandhavatvāt ityādau hetau sattvāt
anvayavyāpitaprakārakaniścayāviśeṣyatve sati
vyatirekavyāptiprakārakaniścayaviśeṣyatvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ
vācyamityabhiprāyeṇa vyācaṣṭe [184]
niściteti/
atrāpyanvayavyatirekivyabhicāriṇoḥ vāraṇāya viśeṣaṇaviśeṣye/
vyatirekavyāptimattvamevālam na lakṣaṇāsaṅgatiriti/
pṛthivīsāmānyasya pakṣatvena
tadatiriktadṛṣṭāntadaurlabhyenānvayavyāptiniścayāsambhavāditi bhāvaḥ/
itarapratiyogikabhedasya jalatvādyavacchinnabhedādyātmakasya prasiddhyā
vikalpāsaṅgaterāha - [184] pṛthivītaratvāvacchinneti/ nanu
pṛthivītaratvāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedarūpasya sādhyasya prasiddhipakṣe
ādye [183] yatretyādinā dīpikoktaṃ dūṣaṇamasaṅgatam/
children.translated_text: 'Whose pervasion is by negative concomitance alone' — in the text of the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, the meaning obtained is: possessing negative pervasion (<s>vyatirekavyāpti</s>) while being devoid of positive pervasion (<s>anvayavyāpti</s>). And here, the qualifier is for preventing the inclusion of the positive-and-negative (<s>anvayavyatirekin</s>), and the qualificand is for preventing the inclusion of the deviant (<s>vyabhicārin</s>) — this should be understood. But that does not work: whether pervasion takes the form of co-location of the pervader of the probans with the <s>sādhya</s>, or the form of not occurring in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> — since in 'earth is different from the others, because of smell (<s>gandhavatva</s>)' and the like the probans possesses [positive pervasion], the definition should be stated as: being the qualificand of a determinate cognition whose predicate is negative pervasion, while not being the qualificand of a determinate cognition whose predicate is positive pervasion. With this intent he explains — [184] 'ascertained' etc. Here too, the qualifier and qualificand serve to prevent the inclusion of the positive-and-negative and the deviant respectively. Possessing negative pervasion alone suffices — the definition is not incoherent. Since <s>pṛthivī</s>-universal being the thesis, due to the difficulty of finding an example other than that, the ascertainment of positive pervasion is impossible — this is the purport. Since the difference whose counter-positive is the other [i.e., non-earth] — being of the nature of difference delimited by water-hood and the like — is well-known through alternatives, to address the [potential] objection of inapplicability, he says — [184] 'delimited by other-than-earth-ness' etc. Objection: if the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of difference whose counter-positive is delimited by other-than-earth-ness is well-known, then in the first [exposition] the objection stated by the <s>Dīpikā</s> with [183] 'where' and so forth is incoherent.

children.text:
1. svaṃ vṛttimān
atyantābhāvaḥ ghaṭābhāvaḥ tadviśiṣṭaḥ ghaṭaḥ tadanyatvaṃ abhidheyatvādeḥ/
ghaṭasya uktobhayasaṃbandhena ghaṭābhāvaviśiṣṭatvaṃ cettham-svaṃ ghaṭābhāvaḥ
ghaṭābhāvaḥ tatpratiyogitvaṃ ghaṭasya, evaṃ svaṃ ghaṭābhāvaḥ tanniṣṭho yo
bhedaḥ svādhikaraṇavṛttitvasaṃbandhena ghaṭavadbhedaḥ, ghaṭābhāvasya
ghaṭādhikaraṇavṛttitvābhāvāt tādṛśabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ ca
ghaṭasyeti/
children.translated_text: 'Itself' means what possesses occurrence; the absolute absence is the absence of a pot; what is qualified by that is a pot; the otherness of that is [the otherness] of name-ability and the like. The qualification of a pot by both the stated relations is as follows: 'itself' is the absence of the pot; the absence of the pot — its counter-positive-ness belongs to the pot. Similarly, 'itself' is the absence of the pot; the difference residing in it — through the relation of occurrence in one's own substrate, is the difference possessing a pot; since the absence of the pot lacks occurrence in the substrate of the pot, such difference-counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood belongs to the pot.

children.text:
anvayitvasyānvayavyāptimattvarūpasya tatra sattvena
tadāpādanāsambhavāt āpattāvāpādya vyatirekanirṇayasya hetutayā
tadasambhavāt ityata āha - [184 ]
anvayasahacāreti/ iṣṭāpattiḥ kuto
na saṃbhavatītyāśṅkya bhāvamāha - [184] tathāceti/ [184] prasiddhānumānam vahnyādisādhyakadhūmādihetukānumānam/
[184] etadapi - pṛthivī itarebhyo bhidyate
gandhavatvādityādikamapi/
children.translated_text: Since the positivity — in the form of possessing positive pervasion (<s>anvayavyāptimattva</s>) — exists there, the postulation (<s>āpatti</s>) of that is impossible. Since in postulation, the negative determination is used as a reason, and since that [negative determination] is impossible — to address this he says: [184] 'positive co-occurrence' etc. Whence does the postulation (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>) not arise? Anticipating this doubt, he states the reason — [184] 'And thus' etc. [184] 'Well-known inference' — an inference having fire and the like as <s>sādhya</s> and smoke and the like as probans. [184] 'This too' — the inference 'earth is different from the others, because of smell' and the like too.

children.text:
sapakṣeti/ sapakṣatvamatra
sādhyaprakārakaniścayaviśeṣyatvam na tu sādhyavattvamātram asambhavāt/
tathā ca pṛthivītarabhede sādhye gandhavattvādirasādhāraṇahetvābhāsa
eva syāt na tu saddheturiti bhāvaḥ/ nanu viśeṣyajñānavirahe 'pi
sādhyaviśeśyakānumiteḥ sādhyāghaṭitavyatirekavyāptiviṣayakāt
pṛthivītaratvavyāpakībhūtābhāvapratiyogi gandhavatī pṛthivī
ityākārakāt parāmarśāt sambhave bādhakābhāva ityata āha - [184] aprasiddheti [184] abhiprāyeṇeti/ tathā cāprasiddhasādhyake 'pi
sādhyaprakārikaivānumitirityabhyupagamyaiva idaṃ dūṣaṇamuktamiti
bhāvaḥ/ evena sādhyaviśeṣyakānumitivyavacchedaḥ/ [184] jalādīnāmityādi/ trayodaśānyonyābhāvā iti karmadhāraya
etanmata iti dhyeyam/ kecittu mate tu jalāditrayodaśeti
punarbahuvrīhiḥ/ anyathā caturdaśātmakasamudāyālābhāt/
trayodaśānyonyābhāva iti ṣaṣṭhīsamāsaḥ/ [184] trayodaśatvāvacchinneti dīpikāvākye trayodaśatvaṃ
samudāyatvaviśeṣa iti sūcitam/ [184] apekṣetyādinā/
avacchinnatvaṃ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ bhedagatam/
children.translated_text: 'In the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>)' etc. Here, similar-instance-hood (<s>sapakṣatva</s>) is being the qualificand of a determinate cognition whose predicate is the <s>sādhya</s>, not merely possessing the <s>sādhya</s> — since [the latter] is impossible. And thus, when difference from other-than-earth is the <s>sādhya</s>, smell-ness and the like would be merely a non-common pseudo-reason (<s>asādhāraṇahetvābhāsa</s>), not a valid reason — this is the purport. Objection: even in the absence of cognition of the qualificand, since inference having the <s>sādhya</s> as qualificand is possible — from the inferential consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>) of the form 'earth possesses smell, which is the counter-positive of the absence that is the pervader of other-than-earth-ness,' which has as its content a negative pervasion not incompatible with the <s>sādhya</s> — since there is no sublation, to address this he says — [184] 'unestablished' etc. [184] 'with the intent' etc. And thus, even conceding that inference has the <s>sādhya</s> as predicate even in an unestablished <s>sādhya</s>, this objection is raised — this is the purport. By 'eva,' the exclusion of inference having the <s>sādhya</s> as qualificand [is indicated]. [184] 'Of water and the like' and so forth. 'Thirteen mutual absences' — this is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound, and one should note that 'in this view' [is implied]. Some, however, [take it as]: 'in the view of water and the like, thirteen' — a further <s>bahuvrīhi</s>. Otherwise, the aggregate of fourteen cannot be obtained. 'Thirteen mutual absences' — this is a sixth-case (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>) compound. [184] 'Delimited by thirteen-ness' — in the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement, thirteen-ness is indicated as a particular kind of aggregate-hood. [184] 'Expectation' and so forth. The delimitation-hood (<s>avacchinnatva</s>) is the qualification residing in the difference.

children.text:
nanu
jalāditrayodaśetyatroktarītyā caturdaśalābhe 'pi kevalaṃ
trayodaśetyādivākye kathaṃ tallābha ityata āha - [184] jalādītyādiriti/ tathā ca śeṣapūraṇena tādṛśārbhalābha iti
bhāvaḥ/ matāntarasādhāraṇyena
vyatirekavyāpteranumityaṅgatvasthāpanānupapattiśca/ evaṃ
jalāditrayodaśetyatra bahuvrīhyantarakalpanāprayāsaḥ pratyekamiti
padapūraṇena caturdaśātmakasamudāyasnaya pratyekaṃ ye 'nyonyābhāvā
iti vyākhyānakleśaḥ/ svāyatte śabdaprayoge īdṛśavakrābhidhānasya
granthakārarītiviruddhatvaṃ prathamaghaṭakārthasyādipadasya
prāthamyamātraparatve 'svārasyam ceti/ dīpikāyām [184] ekādhikaraṇavṛttitvābhāvāditi/ ekādhikaraṇavṛttitayā
anumiteḥ prāṅniścatatvābhāvādityarthaḥ/
sādhyāghaṭitavyatirekavyāptiviṣayakajñānasya
sādhyajñānanirapekṣatvādāha - [184]
sādhyābhāveti/ api tu
jalādibhedakūṭamiti/ etena dīpikāvākyasthaṃ melanamityantaṃ
vyākhyātam/ yadyapi kūṭatvasyaikaviśiṣṭāparatvarūpatve
taddoṣatādavasthyam, tāvadviṣayakadhīviṣayatvarūpatve viṣayatāyā
vyāsajyavṛttitve mānābhāvāt pratyekaviśrāntatvena
uktānumānasyānvayitvaprasaṅgaḥ,
tādṛśasādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnābhāvasyāprasiddhatvena
vyatirekavyāptigrahāsambhavaśca, tathāpi
jalabhinnānuyogikatvaviśiṣṭasvarūpasambandhena
vāyvādibhedaviśiṣṭatejobhedasya sādhyatvasvīkārāt na doṣaḥ/
apekṣābuddhiviśeṣetyādivakṣyamāṇagranthastu viṣayatāyā
vyāsajyavṛttitvābhyupagamena pravṛttaḥ/ anyathā punaruktarītireveti
dhyeyam/ [184] anumityaṅgatvam anumitiprayojakatvam/
[185] agre 'pi - jalāditrayodaśatvāvacchinnabhedātmakasādhyasyetyatrāpi/
asmaduktarītyā yathāśrutārthasyaiva upapatteḥ/ jalādīti
śeṣapūraṇasyāyuktatvamityasvarasaḥ āhurityanena sūcitaḥ/
idamatrāvadheyam -
tāvadviṣayakadhīviṣayatvasyādheyatāsambandhāvacchinnavyāpakatāsambandhena
sādhyatvamaṅgīkāryamiti viṣayatvasyāvyāsajyavṛttitve 'pi na
virodhaḥ/ evamanyatrāpi bodhyam/ tādṛśavyāpakatā ca
svasamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitvīyādheyatāsambandhāvacchinnāvacchedakatāsambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvamiti/
children.translated_text: Objection: In the expression 'thirteen of water and the like,' even though fourteen is obtained in the manner stated, how is it obtained in a statement that says merely 'thirteen'? To address this he says — [184] 'water and the like' etc. And thus, by supplying the remainder, such a meaning is obtained — this is the purport. And the inappropriateness of establishing the status of negative pervasion as a component of inference through what is common to another view [is also implied]. Similarly, in the expression 'thirteen of water and the like,' the effort of postulating an alternative <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, the difficulty of interpretation by supplying 'individually' to explain the aggregate of fourteen atoms as 'the mutual absences that individually [obtain],' the fact that such indirect expression in self-controlled word-usage is contrary to the author's style, and the lack of naturalness when the meaning of the first component-word 'ādi' is taken as mere priority — [all these are noted]. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [184] 'because of the absence of occurrence in a single substrate' etc. The meaning is: because of the absence of the inference [being established] as having occurrence in a single substrate prior [to this]. Since the cognition whose content is negative pervasion not incompatible with the <s>sādhya</s> is independent of the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>, he says — [184] 'the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>' etc. 'But rather, an aggregate of differences from water and the like.' By this, the passage in the <s>Dīpikā</s> up to 'merging' is explained. Although, if aggregate-hood (<s>kūṭatva</s>) has the nature of otherness qualified by a single [entity], the same difficulty [persists] regarding that defect; and if it has the nature of being the object of a cognition having that many objects, since there is no evidence for the disjunctive occurrence of objecthood, there would be the undesirable consequence of the stated inference being positive — through its resting upon each individual — and the impossibility of grasping the negative pervasion due to the non-establishment of the absence delimited by the delimitor of such <s>sādhya</s>-hood; nevertheless, by accepting the <s>sādhya</s> as the difference from fire qualified by the counter-positive-hood of the difference whose correlate is delimited by water-different-ness, through the self-linking relation, there is no defect. The forthcoming passage 'a particular expectation-cognition' and so forth is stated on the basis of accepting the disjunctive occurrence of objecthood. Otherwise, it would be merely a repetition of what was [already] stated — this should be noted. [184] 'Component-hood of inference' — being conducive to inference. [185] 'Further also' — in the passage 'delimited by thirteen-ness of difference of the nature of water and the like as <s>sādhya</s>' also. By our stated method, since the meaning as literally read is itself coherent, the supplying of the remainder in 'water and the like' is inappropriate — this lack of naturalness is indicated by the word 'he says.' Here the following should be noted: the <s>sādhya</s>-hood should be accepted through the relation of pervader-hood delimited by the relation of superstratum-relation delimited by the cognition having that many objects as objects — even when objecthood does not have disjunctive occurrence, there is no contradiction. Similarly in other cases too, this should be understood. Such pervader-hood is: possessing the difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the superstratum-relation delimited by the delimitor-hood of the delimitor of one's own co-located-difference-counter-positive-hood, delimited by the relation of delimitor-hood of one's own-residing delimitor-hood of delimitor-hood of the counter-positive-hood of the counter-positive-ness.

children.text: pakṣalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>)

children.text:
sandigdhasādhyavāniti
saṅgrahoktapakṣalakṣaṇavākyena sandehaprakārībhūtasādhyavattvaṃ
pakṣalakṣaṇamiti labhyate/ tacca hrado vahnimānityādau
hradādyavyāpakamityāśaṅkyāha [188]
viśeṣyatāsambandheneti/ [188] sapakṣalakṣaṇādikamityādi/ viśeṣyatāsaṃbandhena
sādhyaprakārakaniścayavattvaṃ sapakṣalakṣaṇam/ ādipadagrāhyaṃ vipakṣalakṣaṇamapi
tena saṃbandhena sādhyābhāvaprakārakaniścayavattvam/ anyathā hradādau
vahnyādibhramadaśāyāṃ tasya sapakṣatayā parvatādau
nirvahnitvādibhramadaśāyāṃ tasya vipakṣatayā
bhrāntapuruṣīyopanyāsānupapatteḥ/ dīpikāyām [188] niścitatveneti/ itaravilakṣaṇatvenetyādi/ dīpikāyāñ [188] uktetyādi/ yadyapi tādṛśasiddhyabhāvaḥ ghaṭādāvapyastīti
parvato vahnimānityādau tatrātiprasaṅgaḥ/ tathā ca
svapratiyogitāvacchedakakoṭipraviṣṭaviśeśyatāvacchedakadharmavattāsambandhena
tādṛśasiddhyābhāvasya
children.translated_text: 'Possessing the doubtful <s>sādhya</s>' — by the thesis-definition statement in the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, the definition of the thesis is obtained as: possessing the <s>sādhya</s>-hood that is the predicate-mode of doubt. And that, in cases like 'the lake possesses fire,' is non-pervading with respect to the lake and the like — anticipating this objection, he says: [188] 'through the relation of qualificand-hood (<s>viśeṣyatā</s>)' etc. [188] 'The definition of the similar instance and the like' and so forth. The definition of the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) is: possessing a determinate cognition whose predicate is the <s>sādhya</s>, through the relation of qualificand-hood. The word 'and the like' includes the definition of the dissimilar instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>) also — which is, through that same relation, possessing a determinate cognition whose predicate is the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>. Otherwise, in the lake and the like during the state of erroneous cognition of fire, it would be a similar instance; and in the mountain and the like during the state of erroneous cognition of absence-of-fire, it would be a dissimilar instance — [but then] the citation by an erring person would be incoherent. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [188] 'as ascertained' etc. 'Of a distinctive kind' etc. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [188] 'stated' etc. Although such absence of establishment exists even in pots and the like, there would be over-extension in 'the mountain possesses fire' and the like there. And thus, the absence of establishment whose counter-positive-ness is delimited by the qualificand-hood-delimitor-property included in the category of one's own counter-positive-ness,

children.text:
pakṣapadapravṛttinimittatopeyata iti na doṣaḥ/ 1tādṛśasya
iha parvatatvādeḥ ghaṭādāvabhāvāditi bodhyam/
children.translated_text: should be understood as the ground for the application of the word 'thesis.' Such [absence of establishment], in the present context, does not exist in pots and the like because of the absence of the property like mountain-ness and the like — this should be understood.

children.text: hetvābhāsanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>)

children.text:
dīpikāstha saddhetuṃ
nirūpye'tyantopādānasya prayojanamāha - [189] asaddhetunirūpaṇa iti/
kṛta iti śeṣaḥ/ tathā ca kṛtiḥ sapatamyarthaḥ/ tasyā
uttarakālīnatvasambandhena smaraṇe 'nvayaḥ/ [189] prasaṅgasaṅgatyeti/
asaddhetutvādirūpayeti śeṣaḥ/ [189]
taditi/ asaddhetvityarthaḥ/ (190)
hetuvadābhāsanta itīti/ idaṃ cārthapradarśanaparam, na tu
vigrahapradarśanaparam/ vigrahastu hetava ivābhāsā iti vaktavyam/
tādātmyena saddhetuprakārakabhramaviśeṣyatetyarthaḥ/ bhramahetudoṣaśca
children.translated_text: He states the purpose of the extensive treatment in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [saying:] 'having determined the valid reason' — [189] 'exposition of the invalid reason' etc. The word 'done' (<s>kṛta</s>) should be supplied. And thus the action [expressed by] 'done' is in the seventh-case meaning. Its syntactic connection is with recollection through the relation of being subsequent to that. [189] 'Relevance and connection (<s>prasaṅgasaṅgati</s>)' etc. The word 'of the nature of invalid reason-ness and the like' should be supplied. [189] 'That' — the meaning is: invalid reason (<s>asaddhetva</s>). [190] 'They appear like valid reasons' etc. This statement is for the purpose of indicating the meaning, not for the purpose of showing the grammatical analysis (<s>vigraha</s>). The grammatical analysis should rather be stated as: 'those that appear like valid reasons.' The meaning is: that which is the qualificand of an erroneous cognition having the predicate-mode of valid reason, through the relation of identity. The defect that is the cause of the error is

children.text:
pañcamyantapadapratipādyatvarūpaḥ/ dīnapikāyām [189] saddhentu nirūpyetyādi
saddhetuviśiṣyakalakṣaṇādaudiprakārakajñānajanakaśabdapratiyogikadhvaṃsaviśiṣṭaḥ
asaddhetuviśeṣyakalakṣaṇādiprakārakajñānajanakaśabdaviṣayakecchāviś iṣṭaśca
yaḥ asaddhetutvavyāpyadharmaprakārakajñānajanakaśabdaḥ
tadanukūlavartamānakālīnakṛtimānityakhaṇḍabodhaḥ/ atrāsaddhetumityasya
dehalīdīpanyāyenobhayatrānvayaḥ/ prathamavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svapratiyogisamānakartṛkatvasvāśrayakālavṛttitvobhayasambandhena/
dvitīyavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svaprayojyecchāviṣayatvasvaviṣayasamānakartṛkatvobhayasambandhena/
saddhetumityatra satpadasyārthamāha - prakāśikāyām [189] vyāptyādiviśiṣṭeti/ ādinā pakṣadharmatāparigrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: which is in the form of being denoted by a word ending in the ablative suffix. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [189] 'Having examined the valid reason' and so forth — the unitary understanding is: one who possesses a current effort favorable to a word that generates cognition having as its qualifier a property pervaded by the nature of being a fallacious reason, [that word] being qualified by the destruction of a word that generates cognition having as its qualifier the definition and so forth of a particular valid reason, and being qualified by the desire whose object is a word that generates cognition having as its qualifier the definition and so forth of a particular fallacious reason. Here, 'the fallacious reason' connects with both [qualifications] by the maxim of the lamp at the threshold (<s>dehalīdīpanyāya</s>). The first qualification is through both relations of being the same agent as its own counter-positive and residing in the time of its own substratum. The second qualification is through both relations of being the object of the desire prompted by itself and being the same agent as its own object. He states the meaning of the word 'valid' (<s>sat</s>) in 'the valid reason' — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [189] 'Qualified by pervasion and the like' — the word 'and the like' includes the property of being a property of the <s>pakṣa</s>.

children.text:
1. tādṛśasyeti/
svapratiyogitāvacchedakakoṭipraviṣṭaviśeṣyatāvacchedakadharmarūpasyetyarthaḥ
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Of that kind' — the meaning is: of the form of the property that is the delimitor of qualificand-hood included in the delimitor-side of one's own counter-positiveness.

children.text:
nanu syānnāma
sāmānyadharmakathanasyāvaśyakatā, tathāpi duṣṭalakṣaṇasya pratijñātatvāt
tasyaiva vaktavyatayā tadupekṣya doṣalakṣaṇābhidhānāsaṅgatirityata āha
- doṣalakṣaṇa ityādi/ [190] lābhaḥ bodhaḥ/
prāptyarthakadhātorjñānārthakatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ [190] atrānumitipadamityādi/ ayamāśayaḥ-anumitipadaṃ
prakṛtapakṣadharmiṅkaprakṛtasādhyaprakārakānumiti-prakṛtapakṣaviśeṣyakaprakṛtasādhyavyāpyahetuprakārakaparāmarśānyataraparam,
na tu parāmarśasyānumitikaraṇatvenātra praveśaḥ/ yadyapi parvato
vahnimān hradaśca tathetyanumitau parvato vahnivyāpyadhūmavān hradaśca
tathetyādiparāmarśeṃ ca samūhālambane hrado na vahnimān nāpi
vahnivyāpyadhūmavānityādiviparītaniścayayoḥ pratibandhakatvāt
tadviṣaye 'tivyāptiḥ/ bādhādyasaṅgrahabhiyā
tādṛśānyataratvavyāpakapratibadhyatāniveśāsambhavāt/ tathāpi
prakṛtānumititvavyāpakatvaprakṛtaparāmarśatvavyāpakatvānyataravatpratibadhyatānirūpitapratibandhakatāniveśāt
na doṣaḥ/ ata evānumitikaraṇatvena parāmarśaniveśopekṣā/
bhramabhinnetyarthaḥ iti/ bhamatvaṃ ca
1svāvacchinnatvasvānuyoginiṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitatvasvapratiyoginiṣṭhatvatritayasambandhena
saṃsargaviśiṣṭānyaprakāratānirūpakatvam/ tena parvato nirvahniriti
jñānasya kiñcidaṃśe pramātve 'pi na kṣatiḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: granted that stating the general property is necessary, nevertheless since the definition of the defective [reason] was promised, and since that alone is to be stated, it is incoherent to set that aside and state the definition of the defect. To this he says — 'The definition of defect' and so forth. [190] 'Obtaining' means understanding, since the verbal root meaning 'to obtain' also has the meaning of knowing — this is the purport. [190] 'Here the word inference' and so forth — the intent is this: the word 'inference' (<s>anumiti</s>) refers to either an inference having the <s>pakṣa</s> in question as qualificand and the probandum in question as qualifier, or a consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>) having the <s>pakṣa</s> in question as qualificand and the probans pervaded by the probandum in question as qualifier — but the consideration does not enter here in its capacity as the instrument of inference. Although in the inference 'the mountain possesses fire and the lake likewise,' and in the consideration 'the mountain possesses smoke pervaded by fire and the lake likewise,' since they obstruct the contrary determinations 'the lake does not possess fire' and 'the lake does not possess smoke pervaded by fire' in the case of collective apprehension, there would be over-pervasion in that domain — [this is addressed as follows:] since there is a fear of failing to include sublation and the like, it is impossible to include obstructed-ness that is a pervader of being either of such [types]; nevertheless, since what is included is obstructor-ness that determines obstructed-ness possessing either of [the properties of] being a pervader of being the inference in question or being a pervader of being the consideration in question, there is no defect. For this very reason, the inclusion of consideration as the instrument of inference is disregarded. 'Different from error' — the meaning. And error-ness is: through the three relations of being-delimited-by-itself, residing in the relatum of itself, and residing in the counter-positive of itself, the property of not determining a mode-ness qualified by a relational connection that is different. Therefore, even if the cognition 'the mountain lacks fire' is valid in some respect, there is no harm.

children.text:
yadrūpāvacchinnaviṣayaketi/
yadviṣayaketyuktau viśiṣṭaśuddhayoranatirekāt hrada
ityādyekadeśajñānamādāyāsambhavassyāditi tadupekṣā/ kastarhi
jñānaviśeṣa ityākāṅkṣāyāṃ tatpradarśanamukhena
niṣkṛṣṭahetvābhāsalakṣaṇaṃ pradarśayati - [190] evaṃ ceti/
atrāyamanumagamaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Having as its object what is delimited by a certain form' — if it were said 'having as its object [simply],' since there would be no distinction between qualified and pure [cognitions], there would be an impossibility by taking a partial cognition such as 'the lake' — hence that is disregarded. In response to the query 'what then is the specific cognition?', he demonstrates the refined definition of fallacious reason through presenting that [specific cognition] — [190] 'Thus' and so forth. Here the following is the analysis:

children.text:
1. svaśabdena rajate
idaṃ rajatamiti pramāyāṃ viṣayabhūtaḥ yaḥ samavāyākhyaḥ saṃbandhaḥ sa
grāhyaḥ, tadavacchinnatvaṃ rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratāyāmasti/ evaṃ svaṃ samavāyaḥ
tadanuyogi rajataṃ tanniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitatvaṃ ca
rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakaratāyāmasti/ eṃva svaṃ samavāyaḥ tatpratiyogi
rajatatvaṃ tanniṣṭhatvaṃ ca prakāratāyāmasti/ ataḥ uktatritayasaṃbandhena
saṃsargaviśiṣṭā pramīyaprakāratā tadanyā prakāratā bhramīyā
rajatatvaniṣṭhaprakāratā tannirūpakatvaṃ bhrama iti/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. By the word 'itself' — in the valid cognition 'this is silver' regarding silver, the relation called inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) which is the object should be grasped; being-delimited-by-that exists in the mode-ness residing in silver-ness. Thus, 'itself' is inherence; its relatum is silver; and being-determined-by-the-qualificand-ness-residing-in-that also exists in the mode-ness residing in silver-ness. Similarly, 'itself' is inherence; its counter-positive is silver-ness; and residing-in-that also exists in the mode-ness. Therefore, through the three stated relations, the mode-ness that is qualified by the relational connection and that belongs to valid cognition — a mode-ness different from that is erroneous; the mode-ness residing in silver-ness, and its determining-property, is error.

children.text:
pakṣatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭarūpasattvaṃ hetvābhāsatvam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaviśiṣṭapratibadhyatānirūpitapratibandhakatāviśiṣṭatvasambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
1svāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitasādhyatāvacchedakadharmasambandhāvacchinnaprakāratāśālyanumitivṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedaka
children.translated_text: The property of being a fallacious reason is the existence of a form qualified by the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s> (locus-of-inference-hood). And the qualification is through the relation of being qualified by the obstructor-ness that determines the obstructed-ness qualified by what is itself qualified. Its own qualification is through the relation of being delimited by the qualificand-ness delimited by itself, and [the relation of] the delimitor-hood of counter-positiveness of a difference residing in an inference possessing mode-ness with the qualifier of the property that is the delimitor of probandum-hood, delimited by the relation of the property

children.text:
tvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasvāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitasādhyavyāpyahetuprakāratāśāliparāmarśavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākaprat iyogitākabhedavattvobhayasambandhena/
pratibandhakatāvaiśiṣṭyaṃ ādheyatāsambandhena/ sā ca
2svasetyādibhedavattvasaṃbandhena/ svādhikaraṇatā
svāvacchinnaviṣayakānāhāryāprāmāṇyajñānānāskanditaniścayatvasambandhena/
bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā svarūpasambandhena/ tenātrāyaṃ doṣa
ityādau na vākyabhedaḥ/ atrāyaṃ pratibadhyapratibandhakabhāvaniṣkarṣaḥ/
hradatvādiniṣṭhānavacchinnāvacchedakatākaviśeṣyatānirūpitasaṃyogatvāvacchinnasaṃsargatākavahnitvādiniṣṭhānavacchinnavacchedakatākaprakāratākānāhāryabuddhitvāvacchinnaṃ
prati hradatvādiniṣṭhānavacchinnāvacchedakatākaviśeṣyatānirūpitā yā
children.translated_text: and [through] both relations: possessing a difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor-hood residing in itself delimited by the relation of the delimitor-hood of counter-positiveness of a difference residing in a consideration possessing mode-ness with the qualifier of a probans pervaded by the probandum, [and] the qualificand-ness delimited by itself. The qualification of obstructor-ness is through the relation of superstratum-hood. And that [relation] is through the relation of possessing a difference [as specified by] 'its own' and so forth. Its own substratum-hood is through the relation of being a determination that is not assailed by a non-erroneous cognition of invalidity having the same object as itself, and that is delimited by itself. The delimitor-hood of counter-positiveness of difference is through the intrinsic relation. Therefore, in [expressions like] 'here this is the defect,' there is no splitting of the sentence. Here is the extraction of the obstructed-obstructor relation: with respect to a non-erroneous cognition (<s>anāhārya</s>) whose qualifier-ness has the delimitor-hood not residing in lake-ness and the like, and whose qualificand-ness determines the relational-connection-hood delimited by conjunction-ness, and whose mode-ness has the delimitor-hood not residing in fire-ness and the like — with respect to the qualificand-ness that determines [that cognition], from the side of the <s>pakṣa</s> having lake-ness and the like,

children.text:
vahnitvādiniṣṭhānavacchinnāvacchedakatākasaṃyogasambandhāvacchinnaprati yogitāsambandhāvacchinnaprakāratānirūpitasvarūpasambandhāvacchinnābhāvatvāvacchinnaprakāratā
tacchālyanāhāryatvādiviśiṣṭajñānatvena virodhitvam/ atra jātimān
vahnimāniti jñānavyāvṛttaye pratibadhyadiśi jātimān
vahnyabhāvavānityādijñānavyāvṛttye pratibandhakadiśi
anavacchinnatvaniveśanam/ evaṃ pratibadhyadiśi kālikatvādinā
saṃyogāvagāhibhramasyāpratibadhyatvopapattaye saṃyogatvādinā
padārthāṃntarāvagāhi bhramasyāpratibadhyatvopapattaye saṃyogatvādinā
padārthāṃntarāvagāhibhramasya pratibadhyatvopapattaye ca
saṃyogatvāvacchinnasarṃsatāpraveśa iti dhyeyam/ jñānaviśeṣaniveśe
prayojanamāha - [190] taneti/ [190] aprāmāṇyajñānaviśiṣṭasyeti/
viṣayatvasāmānādhikaraṇyobhayasambandhenetyādiḥ/
children.translated_text: the mode-ness determined by the intrinsic relation, which determines the counter-positiveness delimited by the relation of conjunction and having the delimitor-hood not residing in fire-ness and the like, and which has the qualifier of absence-ness delimited by the intrinsic relation — a cognition possessing that [mode-ness] and qualified by non-erroneousness and the like has the status of being contradictory. Here, to exclude the cognition 'a universal-possessing entity possesses fire,' 'not-residing-in' is included on the obstructed side; and to exclude the cognition 'a universal-possessing entity possesses the absence of fire' and the like, 'not-residing-in' is included on the obstructor side. Similarly, on the obstructed side, the inclusion of relational-connection-hood delimited by conjunction-ness is for establishing the non-obstructed status of an error apprehending conjunction through temporality and the like, and for establishing the non-obstructed status of an error apprehending a different category through conjunction-ness and the like, and for establishing the obstructed status of an error apprehending a different category through conjunction-ness and the like — this should be noted. He states the purpose of including the specific cognition — [190] 'That.' [190] 'Qualified by the cognition of invalidity' — the supplement is: through both relations of objecthood and co-location, and so forth.

children.text:
1. svaṃ -
pakṣatāvacchedakam/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'Itself' means the delimitor of <s>pakṣatā</s>.

children.text:
atra sarvatra svaśabdaḥ
doṣatāvacchedakarūpaparaḥ/
children.translated_text: Here throughout, the word 'itself' refers to what is of the form of the delimitor of defect-ness.

children.text:
miśravyākhyāmupanyasyati - [191] paretvityādinā/ [191] duṣṭānāmityādi/ tathā ca na duṣṭanirūpaṇapratijñāvirodha
iti bhāvaḥ/ [191] idam -
anumitipratibandhakayathārthajñānaviṣayatvam/ [191] duṣṭānāmeveti/ evena doṣavyavacchedaḥ/ nanu parvato
vahnimān dhūmādityādau parvato vahnyabhāvavāniti
bādhabhramamādāyātiprasaṅgaḥ/ tasyāpyanumitipratibandhakatayā hetau
tatprakārakagrahasya yathārthatvasambhavādityata āha - [191] parantviti/ nanu jñāyamānavyabhicārādipratibandhakatāmatāśrayaṇe
pratibandhakayathārthajñānetyatra karmadhārayāsambhavāt
lakṣaṇavākyārthānupapattirityata āha - [191] tadarthastviti/
anumitītyādilakṣaṇavākyārthastvityarthaḥ/ [191] eketi/ svaviṣayaketyarthaḥ
jñānaviśeṣaṇam/ lakṣye lakṣaṇaṃ grāhayati - [191] dhūmavānityādinā/ [191] ukteti/
ekajñānaviṣayaprakṛtahetutāvacchedakadharmavattvarūpetyarthaḥ/ evamagre 'pi
[191] darśitetyasya/ [191] taditi/
dhūmābhāvavadvṛttitvaviśiṣṭavahnyādirūpavyabhicāretyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He presents the mixed interpretation — [191] 'Others however' and so forth. [191] 'Of the defective' and so forth — and thus there is no contradiction with the promise to examine the defective, this is the purport. [191] 'This' means being the object of a veridical cognition that obstructs inference. [191] 'Of the defective alone' — by 'alone,' the defect is delimited. Objection: in 'the mountain possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, by taking the sublation-error 'the mountain possesses the absence of fire,' there would be over-extension, since that too, having the capacity to obstruct inference, makes it possible for the apprehension of it as a qualifier of the probans to be veridical. To this he says — [191] 'However.' Objection: if one resorts to the obstructor-ness of known deviation and the like, since a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound would be impossible in 'veridical cognition that is an obstructor,' the meaning of the definitional sentence would be untenable. To this he says — [191] 'The meaning of that however.' The meaning is: the meaning of the definitional sentence beginning with 'inference' and so forth. [191] 'One' — the meaning is 'having its own object,' which qualifies the cognition. He makes the definition applicable to the definiendum — [191] 'Possessing smoke' and so forth. [191] 'Stated' — the meaning is: of the form of possessing the property that is the delimitor of the probans-hood in question, [the subject] of a single cognition. In what follows too, [191] the meaning of 'shown' [is similar]. [191] 'That' means: deviation of the form of fire and the like qualified by the property of occurring in what possesses the absence of smoke. [191] 'They say' — here is the difficulty: if 'inference' and so forth constitutes the definition of defect, the defectiveness — i.e. the definition of the defective — is clearly obtained. But if, in the manner stated, it constitutes the definition of the defective, the definition of defect is not obtained at all, and hence the clarity of understanding for students is not achieved. Although by 'that which obstructs inference,' the property of obstructing inference is obtained as the definition, nevertheless,

children.text:
nanu iha
lakṣaṇe 'numitisāmānyasya praveśāt parvato vahnimān
dhūmādityādāvativyāptiḥ/ hrado dhūmavānityādyanumitipratibandhako
yo vyabhicāraḥ dhūmābhāvavadvṛttitvaviśiṣṭavahnyādirūpaḥ
prāguktasaṃbandhena tatprakārakapramāviśeṣyatvasya dhūmādisaddhetau
sattvāt ityāśaṅkāṃ nirārakaroti [191] prakṛteti/
prakṛtapakṣakaprakṛtasādhyakaprakṛtahetuketyarthaḥ/ [191] saddhetāvit i/ nātivyāptirityanena sambandhaḥ/ [191] yathārthapadānupādāna ityādi/ yadyapyanupadameva parvato
vahnimān dhūmādityādisthale tādṛśavyabhicārādyaprasiddhyā
nātiprasaṅgaprasaktirityuktatvāt/ kathametatprayojanakathanasaṅgatiḥ/
tathāpi dhūmavān vahnerityatraiva
rāsabhādidharmikadarśitasaṃsargakatādṛśavyabhicārādirūpatatsthalapras iddhadoṣaprakārakabhramaviṣeṣyatāmādāya
rāsabhādāvatiprasaṅga ityāśayāt na doṣaḥ/ na caivaṃ
saddhetāvityuktirayukteti vācyam/ iha saddhetupadasya
prakṛtahetubhinnaparatvāt/ tathā ca saddhetāvapi pakṛtahetubhinne 'pi
rāsabhādāviti śeṣaḥ/ apinā prakṛtahetusaṃgrahaḥ/ dṛṣṭāntatayā
bhramapramāsādhāraṇyenaiva jñānasya lakṣaṇe niveśāditi bhāvaḥ/ [191] taditi/ yathārthapadetyarthaḥ/ [191] āhuriti/ atrāyamasvarasaḥ
--- anumitītyāderdeṣalakṣaṇatve doṣavattvaṃ duṣṭānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ
sphuṭatayā labhyate/ uktarītyā tasya duṣṭalakṣaṇatve tu doṣalakṣaṇaṃ naiva
