tanmate 'numitipratibandhakavattvamityuktimātreṇobhayasāmañjasye
children.translated_text: in that view, merely by the statement 'possessing what obstructs inference,' even though both are reconciled,

children.text: pratibandhakayathārthajñānetyādyukterasvārasyamiti/
children.translated_text: the statement 'veridical cognition that is an obstructor' and the like becomes dissonant.

children.text: savyabhicāranirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>savyabhicāra</s> (the deviating [fallacious reason])

children.text:
saṅgrahe [195] sādhyābhāvavadvṛttiriti/ atra kecit - vahnimān
dhūmādityādau ativyāptiḥ/ sādhyābhāvavatī yā dhūmādhikaraṇatā
tannirūpitādheyatvasya dhūmādau sattvāt/ na ca
sādhyābhāvavanniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpitādheyatvaṃ vivakṣitamiti na doṣa
iti vācyam/ evamapi dhūmādhikaraṇatā parvatānyā
dhūmādhikaraṇatātvādityādau ativyāpteḥ/ tatra sādhyābhāvavān
parvataḥ tanniṣchaṭhā yā dhūmādhikaraṇatā tannirūpitādheyatvasya
dhūmādhikaraṇatātve sattvāt/ na ca sādhyābhāvavannirūpitatve sati
sādhyābhāvavanniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpitā yā ādheyatā iti
vivakṣaṇāt 1na doṣa iti vācyam/ evamapi dhūmādhikaraṇatā
adhikaraṇatābhinnatvaparvatānyatvobhayavatī dhūmādhikaraṇatātvāt
2ityatrātivyāpteḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, [195] 'Occurring in what possesses the absence of the probandum.' Here some [say]: in 'it possesses fire, because of smoke' and the like, there would be over-pervasion, since the superstratum-hood residing in smoke, which is determined by the substratum-hood possessing the absence of the probandum, exists in smoke and the like. Nor should one say there is no defect because what is intended is superstratum-hood determined by the substratum-hood residing in what possesses the absence of the probandum — for even so, there would be over-pervasion in 'the substratum-hood of smoke is different from another substratum-hood of smoke' and the like, since the superstratum-hood determined by the substratum-hood residing in the mountain, which possesses the absence of the probandum, exists in the substratum-hood-of-smoke-hood, as the mountain possesses the absence of the probandum. Nor should one say there is no defect because what is intended is: the superstratum-hood that determines being-determined-by-what-possesses-the-absence-of-the-probandum while also residing in what possesses the absence of the probandum — for even so, there is over-pervasion in 'the substratum-hood of smoke possesses both being different from substratum-hood and being different from the mountain, because of being a substratum-hood of smoke.'

children.text:
1. na doṣa iti/
dhūmādhikaraṇatātvaniṣṭhāyāmādheyatāyāṃ
sādhyābhāvavatparvataniṣṭhadhūmādhikaraṇatānirūpitatve 'pi
sādhyabhāvavatparvatanirūpitatvābhāvādauditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'There is no defect' — [this is refuted] because in the superstratum-hood residing in the substratum-hood-of-smoke-hood, although there is being-determined-by the substratum-hood of smoke residing in the mountain which possesses the absence of the probandum, there is no being-determined-by the mountain which possesses the absence of the probandum — this is the purport.

children.text:
2.
ityatrātivyāpteriti/ tatra hi sādhyābhāvavān parvataḥ
dhūmādhikaraṇatā ca bhavati sādhyābhāvavatpadena parvatasyopādāne
tanniṣṭhā yā adhikaraṇatā dhūmādhikaraṇatā tannirūpitatvaṃ
dhūmādhikaraṇatātvaniṣṭhāyāṃ ādheyatāyāmasti,
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 2. 'Here there is over-pervasion' (<s>ativyāpti</s>) — for there, the mountain possesses the absence of the probandum, and the locus-hood of smoke also exists. When the mountain is taken by the expression 'that which possesses the absence of the probandum,' the locus-hood that resides in it, namely the locus-hood of smoke, and the property of being determined by that, exist in the superstratum-hood residing in the property of being the locus-hood of smoke.

children.text:
evaṃ
sādhyābhāvavatpadena dhūmādhikaraṇatārūpāyāḥ adhikaraṇatāyāḥ upādāne
tannirūpitatvaṃ ca dhūmādhikaraṇatātvaniṣṭhāyāmādheyatāyāmasti
ityativyāpterityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Similarly, when the locus-hood of the form of the locus-hood of smoke is taken by the expression 'that which possesses the absence of the probandum,' the property of being determined by that also exists in the superstratum-hood residing in the property of being the locus-hood of smoke — hence there is over-pervasion — this is the meaning.

children.text:
na ca
sādhyābhāvavadviśiṣṭādheyatvaṃ vivakṣitam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svanirūpitatvasvaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpitatvobhayasambandhena/ ato na
doṣa iti vācyam/ evamapi prameyatvādhikaraṇatā
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that what is intended is superstratum-hood qualified by 'that which possesses the absence of the probandum,' where the qualification is through both relations — being determined by itself and being determined by the locus-hood residing in itself — and hence there is no fault. Even so, the locus-hood of knowability (<s>prameyatva</s>)

children.text:
prameyatvādhikaraṇatātvaniṣṭhādheyatānirūpitādhikaraṇatābhinnā
prameyatvādhikaraṇatātvāt ityatrātivyāpteḥ/ sādhyābhāvavatī yā
sādhyabhūtabhedapratiyogyadhikaraṇatā tannirūpitatvasya sādhyābhāvavatī
yā tādṛśādhikaraṇatā tanniṣṭhā yā prameyatvādhikaraṇatā
tannirūpitatvasya ca
prameyatvādhikaraṇatātvaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpitādheyatāyāṃ sattvāt/
children.translated_text: is non-different from the locus-hood determined by the superstratum-hood residing in the property of being the locus-hood of knowability, because of being of the type 'locus-hood of knowability' — here too there is over-pervasion. Because the property of being determined by the locus-hood that possesses the absence of the probandum, which is the locus-hood of the counter-positive of the difference that is the probandum, and the property of being determined by the locus-hood of knowability residing in such locus-hood that possesses the absence of the probandum, both exist in the superstratum-hood determined by the locus-hood residing in the property of being the locus-hood of knowability.

children.text:
na ca
svaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpitatvasthale svaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpakatvaṃ
vācyam/ ādheyatāyā
adhikaraṇanirūpakatvābhāvenoktadoṣānavakāśāditi vācyam/ evamapi
ādheyatvādhikaraṇatā
ādheyatātvaniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpitādhikaraṇatābhinnā
ādheyatvādhikaraṇatātvādityatrātivyāpteḥ/
ādheyatāsāmānyanirūpitādhikaraṇatānirūpakatvasyādheyatāmātre
sattvāt/
children.translated_text: Nor should one say: in the place of 'being determined by the locus-hood residing in itself,' one should state 'being the determiner of the locus-hood residing in itself,' and since superstratum-hood lacks the property of being a determiner of the locus, the stated fault has no scope. Even so, there is over-pervasion in the case: 'the locus-hood of superstratum-hood is non-different from the locus-hood determined by the locus-hood residing in the property of being superstratum-hood, because of being of the type locus-hood of superstratum-hood' — because the property of being the determiner of the locus-hood determined by the generic superstratum-hood exists in superstratum-hood in general.

children.text:
na ca
svanirūpakatvasthale
svanirūpakatāvacchedakahetutāvacchedakadharmasambandhāvacchinnādheyatātvakatvaniveśāt
na doṣa iti vācyam/ tathā sati sādhyābhāvavadavṛttitvarūpavyāpteḥ
niruktavyabhicārābhāvarūpatve hetubhedena bhedāpattyā
kevalānvayigranthavirodhāpatteḥ/ tatra tādṛśavyāpterabhedasyoktatvāt/
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that there is no fault because in the place of 'being the determiner of itself,' the property of being superstratum-hood-type delimited by the relation of the property that is the delimitor of the reason-hood delimiting the delimitor of being the determiner of itself is included. If so, then since the pervasion of the form of non-occurrence in what possesses the absence of the probandum would, in its nature as the absence of the stated deviation, yield a difference due to the difference of the reason, this would conflict with the treatment of the purely positive case (<s>kevalānvayin</s>). Because in that [treatment], the non-difference of such pervasion has been stated.

children.text:
na ca
svanirūpakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhapratiyogitākātyantābhāvasvani rūpitatvobhayasambandhena/
sādhyābhāvavadviśiṣṭādheyatvaṃ vivakṣitamiti na doṣaḥ/ ādheyatāyā
adhikaraṇanirūpakatāvirahāt iti vācyam/
vṛttyaniyāmakasambandhasyātyanatābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakatāmate
uktapariṣkārāsambhavāt/
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that there is no fault because what is intended is superstratum-hood qualified by 'that which possesses the absence of the probandum,' through both relations — the counter-positiveness of the absolute absence residing in itself delimited by the relation of being determined by itself, and [the other] — and that superstratum-hood lacks the property of being a determiner of the locus. [This fails] because on the view that the relation that does not determine the word-function does not delimit the counter-positiveness of absolute absence, the stated refinement is impossible.

children.text:
na ca
svanirūpakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvameva
niveśyamiti na doṣaḥ/
vṛttyaniyāmakasambandhasyāpyanyonyābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakatāvacchedakatāyāḥ
sarvasaṃmatatvāt iti vācyam/ tathāsati dhūmavān
vahneritpayādāvasambhavāpatteḥ/ nirūpakatayā
ayogolakādimato 'prasiddheriti vadanti/
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that there is no fault because what should be included is merely the possession of a difference whose counter-positiveness-delimitor resides in itself, delimited by the relation of being determined by itself — and that even the relation that does not determine word-function is universally accepted as delimiting the counter-positiveness of mutual absence. If so, the inference 'that which possesses smoke possesses fire' etc. would become impossible in the case of lakes etc. They say this because the [required property] is not established in entities like iron balls etc. through the determiner relation.

children.text:
atrocyate-vilakṣaṇanirūpitatvasambandhena
sādhyābhāvavadviśiṣṭādheyatvaṃ vivakṣitam/ vailakṣaṇyaṃ cākhaṇḍopādhiḥ/
na ca tatra mānābhāva iti vācyam/ kāryatāyāḥ
kāraṇamityādyavyavahārāt kāryasya kāraṇamiti vyavahārācca
vilakṣaṇaniyapitatvasya ṣaṣṭhyarthatāyā gadādhareṇa bādhagranthe uktatayā
tattulyayuktyā adhikaraṇe vartate, adhikaraṇatāyāṃ vartata
ityādivyavahārāvyavahārābhyāṃ vilakṣaṇanirūpitatvasya
saptamyarthatāyā apyāvaśyakatvāt/ vailakṣaṇyasya
cākhaṇḍopādhirūpādanyasya nirvaktumaśakyatvāt iti bodhyay/
children.translated_text: Here it is said: what is intended is superstratum-hood qualified by 'that which possesses the absence of the probandum' through the relation of being determined by a distinct type (<s>vilakṣaṇa</s>). And the distinctness is an undivided imposed property (<s>akhaṇḍopādhi</s>). Nor should one say there is no valid means of knowledge for this, because from the usage '<s>kāryatāyāḥ kāraṇam</s>' (the cause of effect-hood) and '<s>kāryasya kāraṇam</s>' (the cause of the effect), <s>Gadādhara</s> has stated in his <s>Bādhagrantha</s> that the genitive case has as its meaning being-determined-by-a-distinct-type. By analogous reasoning, since from the usages and non-usages such as 'it exists in the locus' and 'it exists in the locus-hood,' the meaning of the locative case as being-determined-by-a-distinct-type is also necessarily required, and since the distinctness cannot be articulated as anything other than an undivided imposed property — this should be understood.

children.text:
anye tu
sādhyābhāvavanniṣṭhādhikaraṇatānirūpakatvaṃ vivakṣitamiti na doṣa
ityāhuḥ/ taccintyam -
children.translated_text: Others, however, say that what is intended is the property of being the determiner of the locus-hood residing in 'that which possesses the absence of the probandum,' and hence there is no fault. This is questionable —

children.text:
prameyādhikaraṇatā
parvatānyā prameyādhikaraṇatātvādityādāvavyāpteḥ/ prameyatvena
prakṛtahetorapi tādṛśādhikaraṇatānirūpakatvāt iti/
children.translated_text: because there is under-pervasion (<s>avyāpti</s>) in cases like 'the locus-hood of the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) is other than the mountain, because of being of the type locus-hood of the knowable,' since even the reason under discussion, namely knowability, has the property of being the determiner of such locus-hood.

children.text:
prakāśikāyām [196] sādhyatāvacchedakadharmasaṃbandhāvacchinneti/
sādhyatāvacchedakadharmasambandhaparyāptāvacchedakatāketyarthaḥ/ tena
dvitvādyavacchinnābhāvaviśiṣṭābhāvayoḥ
saṃyogasamavāyobhayasaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvasya ca
vyāvṛttiḥ/ tādṛśāvacchedakatākatvaṃ ca tādṛśadharmetaradharmānavacchinnatve
sati sādṛśasambandhetarasambandhānavacchinnatvam/
dharmasambandhayorniveśaprayojanamāha - [196] teneti
hetutāvacchedakasaṃbandhapraveśanaṃ ca vahnimān dhūmādityādau
vipakṣabhūte hradādau kālikādināṃ dhūmādessattvāt
ativyāptivāraṇāya/ [196] sādhyābhāvavattāyām
sādhyābhāvaniṣṭhādheyatāyām/ nanu kapisaṃyogī etatvādityādau
ativyāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [196] regarding 'delimited by the relation of the property that is the delimitor of the probandum-hood' — meaning: that whose delimitor-hood is exhausted by the relation of the property that is the delimitor of probandum-hood. By this, the following are excluded: the absence delimited by duality etc., the absence qualified by [another] absence, and the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by both the relations of contact and inherence. And the possession of such delimitor-hood means: while not being delimited by any property other than such property, not being delimited by any relation other than such relation. He states the purpose of including both the property and the relation — [196] 'by this.' And the inclusion of the relation delimiting the reason-hood is for the purpose of preventing over-pervasion, since in the counter-example (<s>vipakṣa</s>) such as the lake in the inference 'it possesses fire, because of smoke,' temporal entities like smoke etc. exist. [196] 'In the possession of the absence of the probandum' — in the superstratum-hood that is the absence of the probandum. Now, there is over-pervasion in cases like 'it has contact with a monkey, because of this-ness' etc.

children.text:
śuddhaviśeṣaṇatāyāstādṛśatvādityata āha - kapīti/ [196] digiti/
ākāśābhāvatvāvacchinnakālikaviśeṣaṇatāsaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvavān
ātmatvādityādau kālikaviśeṣaṇataiva
children.translated_text: Since the pure qualifier-hood is of that type, he says — 'monkey' etc. [196] 'Direction' etc. — In cases like 'it possesses the self, because of being space, in the absence delimited by temporal qualifier-hood not delimited by the relation of qualifier-hood delimited by the absence of space-hood,'

children.text:
tādṛśasambandhaḥ/ yadi ca
'adhikaṃ tu' ityādi nyāyena
niravacchinnaviśeṣaṇatāsaṃsargakakapisaṃyogābhāvaprakārakaniścayamādāya
taddoṣatādavasthyamityucyate/ tadā
yaddharmaparyāptāvacchedakatākasaṃsargatānirūpitasādhyābhāvaprakāratākaniściyaḥ
pratibandhakaḥ taddharmaparyāptādheyatāvacchedakatāniveśāt na doṣaḥ/ na
caivamapi tādṛśasamūhālambanajñānamādāya taddoṣatādavasthyamiti
vācyam/ tādṛśaniścayasāmānyaṃ pratibandhakamityarthavivakṣaṇāt/ tathā
ca jñānatvavṛttidharmaparyāptāvacchedakatākatvaṃ niveśyam/ vṛttiśca
svasetyādi bhedavattvasaṃbandhena/ svādhikaraṇatā
svaparyāptāvacchedakatākasaṃsargatākasādhyābhāvaprakāratānirūpitaviśeṣyatāvacchedakatānirūpakaniścayatvasaṃbandhena/
bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatāsvāśrayaviśiṣṭatvasaṃbandhena/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
tādātmyasvaviśiṣṭapratibadhyatānirūpitapratibandhakatvobhayasambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svaviśeṣyatāvacchedakadharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitasādhyatāvacchedakadharmasambandhāvacchinnaprakāratāśālyanāhāryajñānavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasaṃbandhena/
nāto vyabhicārasya viśiṣṭaikārtharūpatābhaṅga iti/
children.translated_text: temporal qualifier-hood itself is such a relation. And if, by the principle 'but the additional [qualifier]' etc., taking the determination having as its content the absence of monkey-contact with undelimited qualifier-relation, and saying that the fault remains the same — then, since what is included is: that property-exhaustive superstratum-hood-delimitor whose relation-determined probandum-absence-content determination is the obstructor, the property-exhaustive superstratum-hood-delimitor — there is no fault. Nor should one say that even so, taking a cognition grasping such a totality, the fault remains the same — because the intention is that it is the generic such determination that is the obstructor. And thus, what should be included is the possession of the property-exhaustive delimitor-hood residing in the property of cognition-hood. And the word-function is through the relation of possessing a difference, as 'residing in itself' etc. Its own locus-hood is through the relation of being the type of determination that is not the determiner of the qualificand-hood-delimitor determined by the content of probandum-absence having the relation of its own property-exhaustive delimitor-hood. The counter-positiveness-delimitor of difference is through the relation of being qualified by its own locus. The qualification is through both relations — identity and the obstructor-hood determined by the obstructed-hood qualified by itself. Its own qualification is through the relation of possessing a difference whose counter-positiveness-delimitor resides in itself, delimited by the relation of being the delimitor of the content-hood delimited by the relation of the property that is the probandum-hood-delimitor-property delimited by the qualificand-hood delimited by the property that is the qualificand-hood-delimitor of its own [cognition], being a non-suppressible cognition-function-difference of that probandum-hood-delimitor-property-relation-delimited-content-hood. Hence there is no breach of the unified meaning of the qualified deviation.

children.text:
sapakṣavṛttitvasāmānyābhāvaniveśasyāvaśyakatayā tata eva
kiñcitsapakṣamādāya doṣavirahāt sarvapadavaiyarthyathmatyāśaṅkyāha-
[196] sapakṣavṛttitveti/ nanu sapakṣatvaṃ yadi sādhyavattvamātraṃ tadā
asambhavaḥ/ śabdatvādāvanityatvādisāmānādhikaraṇyasattvādityata āha -
[196] sapakṣapadamiti/ nanu śabdādāvanityatvādisādhane
śabdatvādiḥsaddhetureveti kathaṃ
tasyāsādhāraṇahetvābhāsatetyāśaṅkyāha - [197] śabda ityādi/ [197] sampradāyavidaḥ prāñcaḥ/ navīnamatasya nirduṣṭatvāt
prāhurityuktam/ [195] anvayavyatirekadṛṣṭāntarahito 'nupasaṃhārī iti
saṃgrahoktayathāśrutalakṣaṇe siddhyasiddhibhyāṃ vyāghāta ityālocyāha -
[197] anvayavyatireketi/ yatkiñciddharmiṇi sādhyaniścayasya
sādhyābhāvaniścayasya vā sattve anupasaṃhāravyavahāravirahāt
daladvayopādānam/
children.translated_text: Since it is necessary to include the generic occurrence in the homologue (<s>sapakṣa</s>), anticipating the objection that by taking some homologue from that alone, the absence of fault [would follow and] the word 'all' would be rendered meaningless, he says — [196] 'occurrence in the homologue' etc. Now, if the homologue-hood (<s>sapakṣatva</s>) is merely the possession of the probandum, then there would be impossibility, since co-location with impermanence etc. exists in sound-hood etc. To this he says — [196] 'the word <s>sapakṣa</s>' etc. Now, in proving impermanence etc. of sound etc., since sound-hood etc. is indeed a genuine reason, how can it be a pseudo-reason of the <s>asādhāraṇa</s> type? Anticipating this, he says — [197] 'sound' etc. [197] 'The ancients who know the tradition' — it is said 'they state' because the modern view is faultless. [195] Having reflected that in the definition as literally stated in the <s>Saṅgraha</s> — 'that which lacks both positive and negative examples is <s>anupasaṃhārī</s>' — there would be a contradiction through both establishment and non-establishment, he says — [197] 'positive and negative' etc. Since in the case where either the determination of the probandum or the determination of the absence of the probandum exists in any property-bearer whatsoever, the usage of <s>anupasaṃhāra</s> is absent, both clauses are included.

children.text: viruddhanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory reason)

children.text:
nanu
virodhāsādhāraṇyayorabhedaprasaṅgaḥ ityata āha - [203] sādhyābhāveti/ sākṣāt - parāmarśamadvārīkṛtya/
tadabhāvavyāpyavattājñānavidhayeti yāvat/
children.translated_text: Now, since there would be the consequence of non-difference between contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) and uncommonness (<s>asādhāraṇya</s>), to this he says — [203] 'the absence of the probandum' etc. 'Directly' (<s>sākṣāt</s>) — without making the consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>) a medium. It amounts to saying: in the manner of the cognition of possessing what is pervaded by the absence of that [probandum].

children.text: satpratipakṣanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (the counter-balanced reason)

children.text:
yasya
sādhyābhāvasādhakamityādisaṅgrahavākye ṣaṣṭhyantayacchabdārthasya
sādhye 'nvayaḥ/ pakṣa ityadhyāhāryam/ prācīnamate
satpratipakṣasyānityadoṣatvena saddhetorapi tadvyavahārasyeṣṭatvena
vidyata ityasya jñāyata ityarthaḥ karmākhyātāśrayaṇāt/ navyamate tu
kartrākhyātāśrayaṇena vartata ityarthaḥ/ sādhakam - vyāpyatayā
gṛhyamāṇamityarthaḥ/ prācāṃmate/ navīnamate tu vyāpyamityartha
ityabhiprāyeṇa vyācaṣṭe - [203]
yatsambandhītyādi/ [203] navīnāḥ punariti/ sādhyābhāvavyāpyahetvantaravatpakṣaḥ
satpratipakṣaḥ/ vyāptiścānvayato vyatirekataśca bodhyā/ tadgrahaśca
tadabhāvavyāpyavattāgrahavidhayānumitivirodhīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s> sentence 'of which there is a prover of the absence of the probandum' etc. — the meaning of the relative pronoun in the genitive ending has its syntactic connection with the probandum. 'In the thesis' (<s>pakṣe</s>) is to be supplied. According to the older view, since <s>satpratipakṣa</s> is not a permanent defect, and since even for a genuine reason such usage is accepted, the meaning of 'exists' (<s>vidyate</s>) is 'is known,' because of the resort to the passive voice. According to the modern view, however, because of the resort to the active voice, the meaning is 'is present.' 'Prover' (<s>sādhaka</s>) — meaning: that which is apprehended as pervaded. [This is] according to the older view. According to the modern view, the meaning is 'that which is pervaded' — with this intention he comments — [203] 'that which is related to' etc. [203] 'The moderns, however' — the thesis that possesses another reason pervaded by the absence of the probandum is <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (counter-balanced). And the pervasion should be understood both through positive and negative concomitance. And the apprehension of that [counter-reason] is opposed to the inference in the manner of the apprehension of possession of what is pervaded by the absence of that — this is the purport.

children.text: asiddhanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished reason)

children.text:
pakṣe pakṣatāvacchedakaviraha iti/
tajjñānasya pakṣatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭapakṣagrahavirodhitvam/ [203] pakṣe hetvabhāva iti/ tadgrahasya ca
pakṣadharmatāvagāhiparāmarśavirodhitvaṃ bodhyam/ nanu
bādhāderivopādherapi doṣatvāt
tadviśiṣṭasyātiriktahetvābhāsatvamāvaśyakatvaṃ bādhitādivat
upadheyasaṅkare 'pīti nyāyāt/ ataḥ sopādhiko vyāpyatvāsiddha
ityasaṅgatamiti hetvābhāsapañcatvavyāghātāpattirityata āha - [204] upādheriti/ nanu
sādhyāprasiddhisādhanāprasiddhirūpayordeṣayoradhikayossattvāt kathaṃ
hetvābhāsānāṃ pāñcavidhyamityāśaṅkya
tayorvyāpyatvāsiddhāvantarbhāvāt na tadvirodha ityāha - [204] atredamavadheyamityādinā/
children.translated_text: 'The absence of the thesis-hood-delimitor in the thesis' — meaning: the cognition of that is opposed to the apprehension of the thesis qualified by the thesis-hood-delimitor. [203] 'The absence of the reason in the thesis' — the apprehension of that should be understood as opposed to the consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>) that comprehends the thesis-property-hood. Now, since just as obstruction (<s>bādha</s>) etc., the imposed condition (<s>upādhi</s>) too is a defect, the status of that qualified [reason] as a separate pseudo-reason is necessary, just as the obstructed etc. Even by the principle that 'even when there is a mixture of imposed conditions,' therefore 'the conditioned is established as lacking pervasion' is inappropriate — [this would lead to] a contradiction with the fivefold classification of pseudo-reasons. To this he says — [204] 'of the imposed condition' etc. Now, since there are additional defects of the form of non-establishment of the probandum and non-establishment of the means of proof, how can pseudo-reasons be fivefold? Anticipating this objection, he says that since those are subsumed under the non-establishment of pervasion, there is no contradiction — [204] with 'here this should be noted' etc.

children.text: upādhinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition)

children.text:
saṃgrahe [207] sādhyavyāpakatve satītyādi/ atra ca vahnimāndhūmādityādau
dravyatvāderghaṭādeśca vāraṇāya daladvayopādānam/ nanu
sādhyavyāpakatvaṃ sādhyavanniṣṭhābhāvāpratiyogitvarūpaṃ cet, tadā
asambhavaḥ; sarveṃṣāmeva
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s>: [207] 'while being pervaded by the probandum' etc. — here, both clauses are included in order to exclude entities like substance-hood (<s>dravyatva</s>) and objects like pots in inferences such as 'it possesses fire, because of smoke.' Now, if the pervasion by the probandum means being of the form of not being the counter-positive of the absence residing in what possesses the probandum, then there would be impossibility, since all [entities]

children.text:
dvitvādyavacchinnābhāvapratiyogitvāt/ kiṃ tu
sādhyavanniṣṭhābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakadharmavattvam/ tathā ca
vahnimān dhūmāditpayādau vahnitvādinā mahanasīyavahnyādeḥ
sādhyavyāpakatvāt upādhitāpattirityata āha - prakāśikāyām [207] sādhyavyāpakatvetyādi/ sādhyatāvacchedakasaṃbandhena
sādhyavanniṣṭhābhāvīyopādhitāghaṭakasaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitānavacchedakaḥ
sādhanatāvacchedakasaṃbandhena
sādhanavanniṣṭhābhāvīyopādhitāghaṭakasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāvacchedakaśca
ya 1upādhitāghaṭakadharmaḥ tadvattvamityarthaḥ/ ayamatrānugamaḥ --
bhedaviśiṣṭopādhitāvacchedakadharmavattvaṃ upādhilakṣaṇam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāśrayatvasvaviśiṣṭopādhitāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnasādhanavanniṣṭhābhāvīyapratiyogitāvacchedakatvobhayasambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ svapratiyogitāvacchedakatāsambandhena/ avacchedakatā
svāvacchinnasādhyavanniṣṭhābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasambandhāvacchinanā
iti/ upādhitāvacchedakasambandhapraveśaphalamāha --- teneti/
children.translated_text: Because of being the counter-positive of an absence delimited by duality and the like. Rather, [the definition is:] possessing the property that does not delimit the counter-positive-hood of the absence residing in what possesses the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). And thus, in the case of 'possessing fire, from smoke' applied to a lake, since the kitchen-fire and the like would be a pervader of the <s>sādhya</s> by virtue of fire-hood and the like, there would be the undesirable consequence of being an <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) — to address this, he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [207] "Being a pervader of the <s>sādhya</s>" etc. The meaning is: possessing that property which constitutes the <s>upādhi</s>-hood — which does not delimit the counter-positive-hood delimited by the relation constituting the <s>upādhi</s>-hood of the absence residing in what possesses the <s>sādhya</s> through the relation delimiting <s>sādhya</s>-hood, and which delimits the counter-positive-hood delimited by the relation constituting the <s>upādhi</s>-hood of the absence residing in what possesses the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) through the relation delimiting <s>sādhana</s>-hood. The universal here is this: the definition of <s>upādhi</s> is possessing the property that delimits the <s>upādhi</s>-hood qualified by difference. The qualification is through both relations — the delimitor-hood of the counter-positive-hood delimited by the relation that delimits the <s>upādhi</s>-hood qualified by itself and residing in what possesses the <s>sādhana</s>, and the self-locus-hood. The self-qualification is through the relation of counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood. The delimitor-hood is delimited by the relation of counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood of the absence residing in what possesses the <s>sādhya</s>, delimited by itself. He states the result of including the relation delimiting the <s>upādhi</s>-hood — with "therefore" etc.

children.text:
kecittu -
upādhitāghaṭakasambandhaviśiṣṭopādhitāghaṭakadharmavattvaṃ lakṣaṇam/
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ svāvacchinna
sādhyavannaṣṭhābhāvapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasvā
vacchinnasādhanavanniṣṭhābhāvīyapratiyogitāvacchedakatvobhayasambandhenet i
vadanti/ vastutastu avacchedakatāviśiṣṭadharmavattvam tat/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāśrayatvasvaviśiṣṭāvacchedakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvobhayasaṃbandhena/
children.translated_text: Some, however, [hold that] the definition is: possessing the property that constitutes the <s>upādhi</s>-hood, qualified by the relation constituting the <s>upādhi</s>-hood. The qualification is through both relations — the delimitor-hood of the counter-positive-hood of the absence residing in what possesses the <s>sādhana</s>, delimited by itself, and the possession of difference whose counter-positive-hood is the delimitor-hood residing in itself, delimited by the relation of delimitor-hood of the counter-positive-hood of the absence residing in what possesses the <s>sādhya</s>, delimited by itself. In reality, however, that [definition] is: possessing the property qualified by the delimitor-hood. The qualification is through both relations — the self-locus-hood, and the possession of difference whose counter-positive-hood is the delimitor-hood residing in itself, delimited by the relation of delimitor-hood qualified by itself.

children.text:
1. upādhitāghaṭakadharma
iti/ upādhitāvacchedakadharma ityarthaḥ/
upādhitāghaṭakasaṃbandhetyatrāpi upādhitāvacchedakasaṃbandhetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: "The property constituting the <s>upādhi</s>-hood" — the meaning is: the property delimiting the <s>upādhi</s>-hood. In "the relation constituting the <s>upādhi</s>-hood" also, the meaning is: the relation delimiting the <s>upādhi</s>-hood.

children.text:
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāvacchedakasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvasvaviśiṣṭapratiyogitānirūpitatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ svanirūpakapratiyogitāviśiṣṭatvasaṃbandhena/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnatvasvanirūpakābhāvaniṣṭhasādhanatāvacchedakasaṃbandhena
sādhanatāvacchedakāvacchinnavannirūpitādheyatāvacchedakasambandhāvacchinnasādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnavannirūpitādheyatāvadabhāvīyatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
ato na sambandhāntarāṇyādāya dūṣaṇāvakāśa iti/ [208] avyāptimiti/ vāyuḥ pratyakṣa ityādau udbhūtarūpādeḥ
guṇādisādhāraṇaśuddhasādhyavyāpakatvābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ/ [208] yaddharmaviśiṣṭasādhyetyādi/
pakṣadharmādiviśiṣṭopādhitāvacchedakadharmavattvamiti niṣkarṣaḥ/
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāvacchinnasādhyanirūpitatatsambandhāvacchinnavyāpakatāvacchedakatvasvāvacchinnasādhananirūpitatatsambandhāvacchinnāvyāpakatāvacchedakatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
children.translated_text: The self-qualification is through both relations — the delimitation by the delimitor-relation of itself, and being determined by the counter-positive-hood qualified by itself. The self-qualification is through the relation of the counter-positive-hood-qualification determined by itself. The qualification is through both relations — the delimitation by the delimitor-relation of itself, and being [an absence] of that which possesses the supervenience-hood determined by what possesses the <s>sādhya</s> qualified by itself, determined by the <s>sādhana</s>-hood-delimitor relation through the absence residing in [what is determined by] the delimitor-hood determined by itself. Therefore there is no occasion for objection by taking other relations. [208] "Non-pervasion" — the purport is that in cases like 'air is perceptible,' since manifest color and the like do not have the nature of being a pure pervader of the <s>sādhya</s> common to qualities and the like. [208] "The property qualified by the <s>sādhya</s>" etc. The conclusion is: possessing the property that delimits the <s>upādhi</s>-hood qualified by the thesis-property and the like. The qualification is through both relations — the delimitor-hood of the pervader-hood delimited by that relation, determined by the <s>sādhya</s> delimited by itself, and the delimitor-hood of the non-pervader-hood delimited by that relation, determined by the <s>sādhana</s> delimited by itself.

children.text:
vastutastu
adhikaraṇatāviśiṣṭarūpavatvaṃ vivakṣitam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāśrayāvacchedakatvasvaviśiṣṭapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasaṃbandhāvacchi nnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvābhaya
children.translated_text: In reality, however, what is intended is: possessing a form qualified by the locus-hood (<s>adhikaraṇatā</s>). The qualification is through both relations — the self-locus-delimitor-hood, and the possession of difference whose counter-positive-hood is the delimitor-hood residing in itself, delimited by the relation of counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood qualified by itself

children.text:
sambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svāśrayāvacchedakasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvasvanirūpakapakṣadharmādiviśiṣṭasādhyavanniṣṭhātyantābhāvīyatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
adhikaraṇatā ca svāvacchinnasādhanavanniṣṭhābhāvīyatvasambandhāvacchinnā/
tenātrāyamupādhirityatra na vākyabhedaḥ/ vastutastu
children.translated_text: — through both relations. The self-qualification is through both relations — the delimitation by the delimitor-relation of itself, and being [an absence] of the <s>atyantābhāva</s> (absolute absence) residing in what possesses the <s>sādhya</s> qualified by the thesis-property and the like, determined by itself. And the locus-hood is delimited by the relation of being [an absence] residing in what possesses the <s>sādhana</s>, delimited by itself. Therefore, in the statement 'this is the <s>upādhi</s> here,' there is no splitting of the sentence. In reality, however,

children.text:
adhikaraṇatāviśiṣṭadharmavattvamupādhilakṣaṇam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svanirūpakabhedapratiyogitākādhikaraṇatānirūpakabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvasvaviśiṣṭapratiyogitānirūpitatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svaviśiṣṭasādhyavannirūpitādheyatāvadabhāvīyatvasvanirūpakabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakādhikaraṇatāśrayasambandhāvacchinnatvobhayasambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ svāśrayasaṃmbandhāvacchinnatvasaṃbandhena/ dvitīye vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svanirūpakabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakādhikaraṇatānirūpakabhedapratiyogi tāvacchedakasaṃbandhāvacchinnatvasvaviśiṣṭapratiyogitānirūpitatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svanirūpakabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakādhikaraṇatāśrayasambandhāvacchinnatvasvaviśiṣṭasādhanavannirūpitādheyatāvadabhāvīyatvobhayasambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ svāśrayasambandhāvacchinnatvasambandhena/ atra sādhyavattvaṃ
sādhyatāvacchedakasambandhena sādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnavattvam, tena
saṃbandhāntareṇa sādhyādhikaraṇamādāya na doṣaḥ/ na vā
viśiṣṭasattāvān jāterityādau dravyatvāderūpādhitānupapattiḥ/ evaṃ
sādhanavattvamapi sādhanatāvacchedakasambandhena
sādhanatāvacchedakāvacchinnavattvam/ tena
children.translated_text: the definition of <s>upādhi</s> is: possessing a property qualified by the locus-hood. The qualification is through both relations — the delimitation by the relation of the counter-positive-hood-delimitor of difference that determines itself, delimited by the relation of the counter-positive-hood-delimitor of difference that determines the locus-hood, and being determined by the counter-positive-hood qualified by itself. The self-qualification is through both relations — being [an absence] of that which possesses the supervenience-hood determined by what possesses the <s>sādhya</s> qualified by itself, and the delimitation by the locus-relation of the locus-hood determined by the delimitor of the counter-positive-hood of difference that determines itself. The self-qualification is through the relation of delimitation by the self-locus-relation. In the second [alternative], the qualification is through both relations — the delimitation by the relation of the counter-positive-hood-delimitor of difference that determines the locus-hood, delimited by the relation of the counter-positive-hood-delimitor of difference that determines itself, and being determined by the counter-positive-hood qualified by itself. The self-qualification is through both relations — the delimitation by the locus-relation of the locus-hood determined by the delimitor of the counter-positive-hood of difference that determines itself, and being [an absence] of that which possesses the supervenience-hood determined by what possesses the <s>sādhana</s> qualified by itself. The self-qualification is through the relation of delimitation by the self-locus-relation. Here, 'possessing the <s>sādhya</s>' means possessing what is delimited by the <s>sādhya</s>-hood-delimitor through the relation delimiting <s>sādhya</s>-hood; therefore, by taking the locus of the <s>sādhya</s> through another relation, there is no fault. Nor is there the impossibility of <s>upādhi</s>-hood for substance-hood and the like in cases like 'a universal possesses qualified existence.' Similarly, 'possessing the <s>sādhana</s>' also means possessing what is delimited by the <s>sādhana</s>-hood-delimitor through the relation delimiting <s>sādhana</s>-hood. Therefore,

children.text:
saṃbandhāntareṇa
sādhanādhikaraṇamādāya na doṣaḥ/ na vā dravyaṃ viśiṣṭasattvādityādau
guṇāderupādhitāpattiḥ evaṃ vyāvṛttyantaramavaseyam/ kasyaciditi/
parvatīyadhūmādherityarthaḥ/ [208]
idaṃ-bahirdravyasya
pakṣadharmatākathanam/ tena bāhyapratyakṣaviṣayatvasya sādhyatāyāṃ
dravyatvamātrameva pakṣadharma iti sūcitam/ [208] anityatvavyāpakamiti/ dīpikāvākye 'nityatvapadasya
janyatvavināśitvasādhāraṇatvāt prakṛtānuguṇyārthamāha --- [208] vināśitveti/ anyathā tādṛśasādhyavyāpakatvopādanaparatvaṃ
tādṛśagranthasya na saṃbhavatīti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: by taking the locus of the <s>sādhana</s> through another relation, there is no fault. Nor is there the undesirable consequence of <s>upādhi</s>-hood for qualities and the like in cases like 'a substance possesses qualified existence' and so forth. Other exclusions should be understood similarly. "Of some" — the meaning is: of the smoke and the like on the mountain. [208] This is the statement of the thesis-property of external substance. By this it is indicated that for the <s>sādhya</s> of being the object of external perception, substance-hood alone is the thesis-property. [208] "The pervader of impermanence" — since in the <s>Dīpikā</s> sentence the word 'impermanent' (<s>anitya</s>) is common to both 'produced' (<s>janya</s>) and 'destructible' (<s>vināśitva</s>), in order to suit the present context he says: [208] "Destructibility" etc. The purport is that otherwise the text's reference to being a pervader of such a <s>sādhya</s> would not be possible.

children.text: bādhitanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Description of <s>bādha</s> (sublation).

children.text:
yasya sādhyābhāva iti saṃgrahapaṅktau pakṣa
ityadhyāhāryam/ tathā
cānumānātiriktapramāṇajanyapakṣadharmikaniścaprakārībhūtaḥ
yaddhetusaṃbandhi yat sādhyaṃ tadabhāva ityarthaḥ/ sambandhaśca
hetusādhyabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ/ atra bādhādiniścayānāṃ kutra kena rūpeṇa
pratibandhakatvamityāśaṅkāyāmāha - dīpikāyām bādhasyetyādinā/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saṅgraha</s> line "whose <s>sādhya</s>-absence," the word '<s>pakṣa</s>' (thesis) must be supplied. And thus the meaning is: the absence of that <s>sādhya</s> which is related to that <s>hetu</s> (reason), being a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) ascertained by a means of valid cognition other than inference. And the relation is characterized by the cause-effect relation between <s>hetu</s> and <s>sādhya</s>. When the doubt arises as to where and in what form the ascertainments of <s>bādha</s> and the like serve as obstructors, he says in the <s>Dīpikā</s>: "Of <s>bādha</s>" etc.

children.text: doṣāṇāmanumitipratibandhakatvaprakāraśodhanam
children.translated_text: Examination of the manner in which the defects (<s>doṣa</s>) obstruct inference.

children.text:
bādhaśabdasya
doṣaviśeṣe 'pi prayogādāha --- prakāśikāyām [212] bādhasya sādhyābhāvavattāniścayasyeti/ dīpikāyām [212] satpratipakṣasya virodhijñānajanakasāmagrītveneti/ satpratipakṣasya
satpratipakṣajñānasya/ virodhijñānajanakasāmagrītvena
tadabhāvavattājñānajanakasāmagrītvena/
children.translated_text: Since the word '<s>bādha</s>' is also used for a specific defect, he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [212] "Of <s>bādha</s>, the ascertainment that [the thesis-locus] possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>." In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: [212] "Of <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (the counter-argument), by being the aggregate of causes that generates the cognition of opposition" — of <s>satpratipakṣa</s> means: of the cognition of the counter-argument. "By being the aggregate of causes that generates the cognition of opposition" means: by being the aggregate of causes that generates the cognition that [the thesis-locus] possesses the absence of that.

children.text:
atra navīnāḥ ---
sāmagrītvamekakāraṇaviśiṣṭāparakāraṇatvamiti
pratibandhakatāvacchedakagarbhe kāraṇāntarapraveśo niṣphalaḥ
gauravasampādakaśceti viśeṣyabhūtajñānasya
tadabhāvavyāpyavattājñānatvenaiva pratibandhakatvamucitam, lāghavāt/
evaṃ pratihetuvyāpakaḥ sādhyābhāvaḥ pratihetumān pakṣa iti
viśakalitajñānadbayasādhāraṇatayā jñānaviśiṣṭajñānatvenaiva
virodhitvamāvaśyakam/ etena virodhijñānajanakatvena
virodhitvamityapi pratyuktamiti prāhuḥ/ tanmataṃ darśaṃyati ---
prakāśikāyām [212] vastutastviti/ nanu dīpikāyām
sādhāraṇasya ityādyasaṅgatam, duṣṭahetorevasādhāraṇaśabdārthatayā
tasyāvyabhicārābhāvarūpatvāsambhavāt ityata āha- [292] bhāvapradhānanirdeśatayeti/ vaiśiṣṭye tṛtīyā/ [212] evamagre 'pīti/ viruddhasyetyādāvityarthaḥ/ vastutastu
viruddhasyetyatra bhāvekta pratyayamaṅgīkṛtya virodhasyetyarthaḥ sulabha
iti dhyeyam/ nanu sādhyābhāvavadvṛttitvajñānasya hetudharmikasya
sattve 'pi hetusamānādhikaraṇetyādivyāptiḥ na hetau gṛhyata
ityanubhavasiddham, tacca nopapadyate/ sādhyābhāvavadvṛttitvajñānasya
grāhyābhāvānavagāhitvena tādṛśavyāptijñānavirodhitvāsambhavāt
ityāśaṅkyāha - [212] hetāviti/ vyāptīti/
hetusamānādhikaraṇetyādivyāptītyarthaḥ/ [212] maṇimantrādinyāyeneti/
tena grāhyābhāvānavagāhitvena
children.translated_text: Here the later [logicians maintain]: since the aggregate-hood is being another cause qualified by one cause, the inclusion of additional causes within the delimitor of the obstructor-hood is fruitless and produces unwanted complexity; therefore, it is proper that the obstruction-hood of the cognition that serves as the qualificand is [established] only through its being a cognition that [the thesis-locus] possesses what is pervaded by the absence of that — by parsimony. Similarly, since the <s>sādhya</s>-absence is a pervader of the counter-reason, and the thesis possesses the counter-reason — since this is common to the two analyzed cognitions, the opposition-hood must necessarily be only through the form of a cognition qualified by a cognition. By this, the [view] that opposition-hood is through being a generator of the cognition of opposition is also answered — thus they say. He presents their view in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [212] "In reality, however" etc. Objection: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, the passage beginning with 'of the common' is incongruous, since the word 'common' (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) refers to a defective reason and it cannot have the nature of absence of invariable concomitance — to this he says: [212] "Due to being expressed with the entity as primary" etc. The third case-ending is in the sense of qualification. [212] "Similarly later also" — the meaning is: in the passage beginning with 'of the contradictory' etc. In reality, however, in 'of the contradictory,' accepting the suffix in the sense of entity, the meaning 'of contradiction' is readily available — this should be noted. Objection: Even when the cognition that [something] occurs in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> exists, and the <s>hetu</s> is a property of the thesis-locus, still the invariable concomitance 'co-located with the <s>hetu</s>' etc. is not apprehended in the <s>hetu</s> — this is established by experience, and this cannot be explained, because the cognition that [something] occurs in what possesses the <s>sādhya</s>-absence, not comprehending the absence of what is to be apprehended, cannot oppose such a cognition of invariable concomitance — anticipating this objection, he says: [212] "In the <s>hetu</s>" etc. "Invariable concomitance" — the meaning is: the invariable concomitance beginning with 'co-located with the <s>hetu</s>.' [212] "By the maxim of the jewel and the spell" —

children.text:
tādṛśavyabhicāragrahasya
tādṛśavyāptigrahāvirodhitve 'pi na taddaśāyāṃ tadāpattiriti bhāvaḥ/
[212] viśiṣṭavyāptyabhāvatayetyādi/ athātra dhūmavān vahnerityādau
hetuvyāpakasādhyāprasiddhyā tadghaṭitaviśiṣṭavyāpateraprasiddhyā
tadabhāvasya sutarāmaprasiddhyā kathamābhāsatā/ na ca -
svavyāpakatāvacchedakasādhyatāvacchedakāvacchinnasāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhāvacchinnahetuniṣṭhapratiyogitākātyantābhāva
eva hetuniṣṭhaḥ vyāpyatvāsiddhiriti na doṣaḥ/
tādṛśasāmānādhikaraṇyasaṃbandhena hetuviśiṣṭahetumān pakṣa iti
jñānasyaiva cānumitihetutvam ato na tasyābhāsatānupapattiriti
vācyam/ tathā sati
prāguktavyabhicārādīnāmābhāsatānupapateraśakyaparihāratvāditi/
maivam/ yataḥ
svavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvasvāvacchinnasāmānādhikaraṇyobhayasambandhena
sādhyatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭahetumān pakṣa iti
jñānamevānumitiheturūpeyate bhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā
svasetyādyavacchedakatvasambandhena/
uktasvavṛttibhedapratiyogitvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasādhyatāvacchedakaniṣṭhapratiyogitākābhāvavaddhetureva
vyabhicāraḥ/
svāvacchinnasāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhāvacchinnasādhyatāvacchedakaniṣṭhapratiyogitākātyantābhāvavaddhetureva
vyāpyatvāsiddhiḥ/ uktagranthasyāpyatraiva tātparyam/ ato na dhūmavān
vahnerityādau uktarītyā tadaprasiddhiriti madekapariśīlitaḥ panthā/
children.translated_text: the purport is that even though the apprehension of such deviation does not oppose the apprehension of such invariable concomitance in the manner of [the jewel-spell maxim], at the stage [when the obstruction operates], that [apprehension of invariable concomitance] does not arise. [212] "Due to the absence of qualified invariable concomitance" etc. Now here, in cases like 'possessing smoke, from fire,' since the <s>sādhya</s> constituted by the pervader of the <s>hetu</s> is not established, the qualified invariable concomitance constituted by it is not established, and therefore the absence of that is even more not established — how then can it be a pseudo-reason? Nor should it be said: the non-establishment of pervaded-hood is just the <s>atyantābhāva</s> (absolute absence) residing in the <s>hetu</s> whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the co-location relation delimited by the <s>sādhya</s>-hood-delimitor delimited by the self-pervader-hood-delimitor — there is no fault, because the cognition 'the thesis possesses the <s>hetu</s> qualified by [the <s>sādhya</s>] through the relation of co-location delimited by the <s>sādhya</s>-hood-delimitor' is itself the basis of inference, and therefore the impossibility of its being a pseudo-reason does not arise — this should not be said, because if so, the impossibility of pseudo-reason-hood for the previously stated deviation and the like would be irremediable. This is not so. Because the cognition 'the thesis possesses the <s>hetu</s> qualified by the <s>sādhya</s>-hood-delimitor through both relations — the counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood of difference occurring in itself and the co-location delimited by itself' is what constitutes the basis of inference. The counter-positive-hood-delimitor-hood is through the relation of delimitor-hood as 'the self' etc. Deviation is just [the case where] the <s>hetu</s> possesses the absence whose counter-positive-hood resides in the <s>sādhya</s>-hood-delimitor, delimited by the stated relation of difference-counter-positive-hood occurring in itself. Non-establishment of pervaded-hood is just [the case where] the <s>hetu</s> possesses the <s>atyantābhāva</s> whose counter-positive-hood resides in the <s>sādhya</s>-hood-delimitor, delimited by the co-location relation delimited by itself. The purport of the stated text also lies here. Therefore, in cases like 'possessing smoke, from fire,' there is no non-establishment of those in the stated manner — this is the path explored by me alone.

children.text:
kecittu -
sādhyatāvacchedakaniṣṭha
hetuvyāpakatāvacchedakatvahetvadhikaraṇavṛttitāvacchendakatvobhayābhāvo
vivakṣita iti nāprasiddhiriti vadanti/ tattuccham --- dhūmavān
vahnerityādau hetuvyāpakasādhyasamānādhikaraṇahetumān pakṣa
u iti jñānasya sādadhyatāvacchedake
hetvadhikaraṇavṛttitāvacchedakatvānavagāhitayā darśitobhayābhāvasya
tadvirodhitayā hetvābhāsatāyā durvañcatvāt/ darśitajñāne
tulyavittivedyatānyāyena niyamatastadbhāne mānābhāvāt/ pratyakṣarūpe
tādṛśajñāne kathañcit tasya tathā bhāne 'pi
children.translated_text: Some, however, say that what is intended is the absence of both — the delimiter-of-pervasion-hood-of-the-probans residing in the delimiter of probandum-hood, and the delimiter-of-occurrence-in-the-locus-of-the-probans-hood — and therefore there is no unestablishedness. But that is frivolous. In cases like 'the mountain possesses smoke, because of fire' and the like, since the cognition 'the thesis possesses the probans that is co-located with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) pervading the probans' does not apprehend the delimiter-of-occurrence-in-the-locus-of-the-probans-hood in the delimiter of probandum-hood, the demonstrated absence-of-both, being contradictory to that, would make the pseudo-reason-hood (<s>hetvābhāsatā</s>) difficult to avoid. In the demonstrated cognition, by the principle of being knowable through cognitions of the same form, there is no authoritative basis for that necessarily appearing [therein]. Even if in a perception-like cognition of that kind, it somehow appears in that manner,

children.text:
anumitau śābde ca
tadbhāne niyāmakābhāvena tādṛśābhāvagrahadaśāyāṃ
tādṛśaparāmarśasambhavāt anumityutpādasambhavena tādṛśābhāvasya
hetvābhāsatāyā ayuktatvāt/ tādṛśaparāmarśasya
tulyarūpobhayānavagāhitvena
tādṛśobhayābhāvagrahapratibadhyatvāyogāt/ tādṛśaparāmarśe
dhūmatvādirūpasādhyatāvacchedakasya svarūpata eva bhānena
vyāpakatāvacchedakatvādyaṃśe tasya niyamato 'vacchedakakatvena sutarāṃ
viparītaniścayapratibadhyatvāsaṃbhavācca/
dhūmatvatvādirūpeṇadhūmatvādibhānopagame ca
dhūmatvatvādyanavacchinnavidheyatāvacchedakatākānumityanupapattiprasaṅgāt/
yadapi
hetuvyāpakatāvacchedakatvahetvadhikaraṇavṛttitāvacchedakatvobhayaviśi ṣṭasādhyatāvacchedakahetumān
pakṣa iti parāmarśasyānumitihetutvaṃ svīkriyate, nāto doṣa
iti --- tadapi na sat/ kāraṇatāvacchedakagarbhe
hetutāvacchedakāvacchinnaviṣayatāyāḥ tredhā niveśena
vyāpyatvāsiddheḥ/ [212] viśiṣṭavyāptyabhāvatayeti dīpikāvākyena
hetuniṣṭhābhāvasyaiva doṣatāpratīteḥ tāvatāpi tadanupapādanācca/
hetubhūtaparāmarśe bahuvrīhyarthasya sambandhasyādhikasya bhānena
mahāgauravācca iti sarvamanavadyam/
children.translated_text: in inference and in verbal testimony, due to the absence of a determining factor for its appearing [thus], at the stage of apprehending such an absence, since such a <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective consideration) is possible, and since the production of inference is [thereby] possible, it is improper that such an absence constitutes pseudo-reason-hood. [This is] because such a <s>parāmarśa</s>, being of the same form, does not apprehend both [factors], and hence cannot be obstructed by the apprehension of such absence-of-both. And because in such a <s>parāmarśa</s>, the delimiter of probandum-hood in the form of smoke-hood and the like appears in its own nature, and in the aspect of being a delimiter of pervasion-hood it necessarily functions as a delimiter — hence all the more so, being obstructed by a contrary determination is impossible. And if one were to accept that smoke-hood and the like appear in the form of smoke-hood-hood and the like, the consequence would be the impossibility of inference whose predicate-hood delimiter is not delimited by smoke-hood-hood and the like. As for [the view that] the causal status for inference of a <s>parāmarśa</s> [of the form] 'the thesis possesses the probans whose probandum-hood delimiter is qualified by both delimiter-of-pervasion-hood-of-the-probans and delimiter-of-occurrence-in-the-locus-of-the-probans-hood' is accepted, and hence there is no fault — that too is not correct. Because the pervasion-hood is unestablished, due to the threefold inclusion of content-hood delimited by the delimiter of reason-hood within the delimiter of causal status. [212] From the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'due to the absence of qualified pervasion,' since only the absence residing in the probans is understood as constituting the defect, even that much fails to establish [the position]. And due to the great cumbersomeness of an additional relation in the form of the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound meaning appearing in the <s>parāmarśa</s> that serves as the probans — all of this is beyond reproach.

children.text:
dīpikāyām [212] vyāptisaṃśayādhāyakatveneti/ ādhāyakatvaṃ prayojakatvam/ nanu
vyāptisaṃśayaprayojakatvaṃ kathaṃ tayorityataḥ tadupapādanayati ---
prakāśikāyām [213] hetāvasādhāraṇyādīti/ ādinā
anupasaṃhāritvasaṃgrahaḥ/ prācīneti/ navīnamataṃ tu prāgevoktamiti
bhāvaḥ/ [213] vyāptijñānapratibandhakaḥ --
vyāptijñānavirodhidhīviṣayaḥ/ paramukhanirīkṣakasyetyatra pratibandha
ityādiḥ/ [213] tathā cetyādi/ atrāyamāśayaḥ ---
hetvābhāsasāmānyalakṣaṇe
niviṣṭamanumititatkaraṇānyatarapratibandhakatvam na tāvat
tadanutpādaprayojakatvam/ vyabhicāritāsambandhena
upādhiviśiṣṭahetāvatiprasaṅgāt/ evaṃ ca
hetāvupādhiprakārakajñānābhāvasya parāmarśakāraṇatāvirahāt
nātivyāptiriti/ śithilam ayuktam/
pakṣatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭapakṣagrahāvirodhitvasyaivāśrayāsiddhilakṣaṇatayā
sādhyavatpakṣe tadabhāvāt uktalakṣaṇe ca sādhyasaṃśayāṃśaniveśasya
viphalatvena saṃśayasya pakṣatātvanirāsācca darśitasya śithilatvamiti
bhāvaḥ/ dīpikāyām/ [212] āśrayāsiddhāvantarbhavatīti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ -
āśrayasya pakṣatāviśiṣṭasyāsiddhiḥ ceneti vigrahaḥ/ tathā ca
sādhyaniścayadaśāyāṃ sādhyasaṃśayarūpapakṣatāviraheṇa tadviśiṣṭasya
pakṣatāvacchedakāvacchinnasya tadānīmasiddheḥ/ sādhyavatpakṣasya tatrāntarbhāva
ucita iti bhāvaḥ/ siddhasādhanasyāśrayāsiddhyantarbhāvaprayojakaṃ
pakṣatāvighaṭakatvamupapādayati --- [213] prakāśe tanamata iti/
prācīnamata ityarthaḥ/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ -- pakṣatāvighaṭakatvaṃ
āśrayāsiddhitvam/ vighaṭakatvaṃ ca virodhigrahaviṣayatvam/ pakṣatā ca
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [212] 'as being productive of doubt about pervasion': productivity means being the cause. Now, how is being the cause of doubt about pervasion [applicable] to both of those? To establish that, he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s> — [213] 'due to uncommonness and the like in the probans': by '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like), non-exhaustive enumeration (<s>anupasaṃhāritva</s>) is included. 'The earlier [logicians]': the newer view was already stated previously — this is the meaning. [213] 'An obstructor of the cognition of pervasion' means: the object of a cognition contrary to the cognition of pervasion. In 'of one who observes the face of another,' '<s>pratibandha</s>' (obstruction) and so forth is prefixed. [213] 'And thus' and so forth: here the intention is as follows — in the general definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (pseudo-reason), the included 'being an obstructor of either the inference or its instrument' is not [to be understood as] being the cause of its non-production, because of over-extension to a probans qualified by a <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) through the relation of deviating-ness. And thus, since the absence of a cognition having the <s>upādhi</s> as its mode regarding the probans is not a condition for the causal status of <s>parāmarśa</s>, there is no over-extension. [But this is] loose and untenable. Since only the non-opposition to the apprehension of the thesis qualified by the delimiter of thesis-hood constitutes the definition of <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s> (unestablished locus), and since that absence exists in a thesis that possesses the <s>sādhya</s>, and since the inclusion of the doubt-about-the-<s>sādhya</s> component in the stated definition is fruitless — and because doubt is thereby removed from thesis-hood — the looseness of what was demonstrated [follows]: this is the meaning. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [212] 'it is included in <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>': the meaning is as follows — the analysis is: 'if there is unestablishedness of the locus qualified by thesis-hood.' And thus, at the stage of determining the <s>sādhya</s>, due to the absence of thesis-hood in the form of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s>, what is qualified by it — what is delimited by the delimiter of thesis-hood — is unestablished at that time. Hence the inclusion of a thesis possessing the <s>sādhya</s> [in <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>] is proper: this is the meaning. He demonstrates that the incompatibility with thesis-hood is the cause of the inclusion of <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving the already established) within <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s> — [213] 'in the <s>Prakāśa</s>, this view': the meaning is 'the earlier view.' The meaning is as follows: incompatibility with thesis-hood is <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>-hood. And incompatibility means being the object of an apprehension of what is contradictory. And thesis-hood is

children.text:
pakṣatāvacchedakaviśiṣṭapakṣadharmakasādhyasaṃśayātmikā
prācīnamate/ tathā ca pakṣaniṣṭhapakṣatāvacchedakavirahasnya sādhyavatpakṣasya
ca niścayadaśāyāmuktapakṣatāyā asambhavāt/ ubhayorapi
tathātvamavyāhatamiti sādhyavatpakṣasya
siddhasādhanarūpasyāśrayāsiddhirūpatayā nādhikyāpattiriti na
vibhāgavyāghātaśaṅketi bhāvaḥ/ siddheḥ pūrvaṃ parato vā yatra
siṣādhayiṣā tatra siṣādhayiṣāvirahakālāvacchedena siddheḥ/
pratibandhakatāyā āvaśyakatvena sādhvatpakṣātiprasaṅgatādavasthyamiti
śaṅkānirāsāyoktañ [213] kevalamiti/ anena siddheḥ
siṣādhayiṣāsāhityābhāvavyavacchedaḥ/ tathā ca siddheḥ pūrvaṃ parataśca
yatra siṣādhayiṣā jātā tatra siddheratāthātvāt nātiprasaṅga
ityarthaḥ//
children.translated_text: of the nature of doubt about the <s>sādhya</s> which is a property of the thesis qualified by the delimiter of thesis-hood, according to the earlier view. And thus, since thesis-hood as described is impossible at the stage of determination — both due to the absence of the delimiter of thesis-hood residing in the thesis and due to the [already] established nature of a thesis possessing the <s>sādhya</s> — the fact that both are thus [instances of <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>] is uncontradicted. Hence there is no excess resulting from the thesis possessing the <s>sādhya</s> having the form of <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving the already established) being of the form of <s>āśrayāsiddhi</s> — and therefore there is no apprehension of a contradiction with the division [of fallacies]: this is the meaning. Wherever there is a desire to establish, whether before or after the establishment — in order to dispel the doubt that there would be an infinite regress of over-extension to a thesis possessing the <s>sādhya</s>, due to the necessity of obstruction-hood being delimited by the time of the absence of the desire to establish — [213] 'merely' is said. By this, the co-absence of the desire to establish with the establishment is excluded. And thus, wherever the desire to establish has arisen, whether before or after the establishment, since the establishment has not occurred there [at that time], there is no over-extension — this is the meaning.

children.text:
// iti
prasaraṇākhyāyāṃ dīpikāprakāśavyākhyāyāmanumānaparicchedaḥ//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on inference (<s>Anumānapariccheda</s>) in the commentary called <s>Prasaraṇa</s>, which is an exposition of the <s>Dīpikā</s> and <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text: samāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Concluded.

children.text: upamānaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Chapter on Comparison (<s>Upamānapariccheda</s>)

children.text:
kutaścidāraṇyakapuruṣādityādisaṅgrahavākye pañcamyāḥ
prayojyatvamarthaḥ/ tasya śrudhātvarthaśābdabodhe anvayaḥ/ iti śabdasya
śabdānvayītyākārakatvamarthaḥ/ sphuṭamanyat/ yattu itiśabdaḥ
tādṛśānupūrvyavacchinnavākyaparaḥ, śrudhātoḥ śrāvaṇapratyakṣamarthaḥ/ tatra
viṣayitayā vākyasyānvayaḥ iti - tattuccham -
smarannityuktasmṛtisāmagrīpraviṣṭāvaśyakaśābdarūpānubhavapratipādanaparatvasambhave
tatparityāgenānupayuktānyathāsiddhavākyasākṣātkārapratipādanaparatāyā
anyāyyatvāt/ prakāśe [218] avasarasaṅgatyeti/
pratibandhakībhūtaśiṣyajijñāsānivṛtyuttarakālīnāvaśyavaktavyatvamavasaraḥ/
tṛtīyārthādikaṃ sarvamapi pūrvavat/
children.translated_text: In the compendium statement 'from some forest-dwelling person' and the like, the fifth case ending has the meaning of being an instrumental cause. Its connection is with the verbal cognition of the meaning of the root '<s>śru</s>' (to hear). The meaning of the word '<s>iti</s>' is having the form 'connected with the word.' The rest is clear. As for [the view that] the word '<s>iti</s>' refers to a sentence delimited by such a word-sequence, and the root '<s>śru</s>' means auditory perception, and the sentence is connected [with the root] as its object — that is frivolous. Because when it is possible to have the purport of conveying the experience in the form of the verbal [cognition] which necessarily enters into the aggregate of the memory (<s>smṛti</s>) referred to by '<s>smaran</s>' (remembering), it is improper to abandon that and adopt the purport of conveying the direct apprehension of a sentence, which is an unnecessary alternative explanation. In the <s>Prakāśa</s>, [218] 'by the occasion and connection': the occasion is the necessary-to-be-stated-hood that comes after the removal of the obstructing student's curiosity. The meaning of the instrumental case and so forth is all as before.

children.text:
nanu [218] saṃjñāsaṃjñisaṃbandhajñānamupamitiriti saṅgrahavākyena upamiteḥ
padapadārthasambandhaviṣayakajñānatvaṃ lakṣaṇamuktam - tanna yujyate/
tādṛśānumityādāvativyāpteḥ/ atastādṛśasaṅgrahavākyaṃ
nopamiterlakṣaṇakathanaparam api tu tatsvarūpamātrapradarśanaparamityāha
- [218] upamitisvarūpamiti/ kiṃ tarhi tasyā lakṣaṇamityākāṅkṣāyām
āha - [218]
children.translated_text: Now, [218] by the compendium statement '<s>upamiti</s> (comparative cognition) is the cognition of the relation between a designation and its designatum,' a definition of <s>upamiti</s> as being a cognition having as its object the relation between word and word-referent has been stated — that is not proper, due to over-extension to inferences and the like of such a kind. Therefore, such a compendium statement is not intended to state the definition of <s>upamiti</s>, but merely to display its general nature — [thus] he says [218] 'the nature of <s>upamiti</s>.' Then what is its definition? — in response to this expectation, he says [218]:

children.text:
lakṣaṇaṃ tviti/
gamyetyantam upamititvasya jātirūpatāyāṃ pramāṇasūcanāya/ [218] etena smaranniti vartamānanirdeśena/ [218] āhuriti/ atra ca saṃgrahakārasya
kutaścidāraṇyakādityādyabhihitavataḥ
atideśavākyārthaviṣayakaśābdabodhaḥ karaṇam tadviṣayakaṃ smaraṇaṃ
vyāpāraḥ- upamitiḥ phalamiti matapradarśanamevābhimatam, na tu
sādṛśyādiviśiṣṭapiṇḍadarśanaṃ karaṇaṃ tādṛśasmaraṇaṃ vyāpāraḥ
upamitiḥ phalamiti matapradarśanam/ tathāsati śabdaprayogasya
svādhīnatvena smariṣyanniti piṇḍaṃ paśyatīti brūyāt, ataḥ
smarannityādyuktisvārasyaparyālocanayā pūrvamatamevābhimatam, na tu
dvitīyaṃ matamiti tatpradarśanaparatayā
tādṛśagranthavyākhyānānaucityamarucibījam/ saṃgrahe vākyeti/
gosadṛśo gavayapadavācya iti svarūpātideśetyādiḥ/ [218] udbodhakāntareti/
sādṛśyaviśiṣṭapiṇḍadarśanātiriktādṛṣṭādirūpodbodhaketyarthaḥ/
[219] sādṛśya(viśiṣṭapiṇḍa)darśanānantaramityādi/ atropamiteḥayaṃ
gavayapadavācya ityānakāratvopagame gavayavyaktyantaradarśanānantaraṃ
tatra padavācyatāyāḥ smaraṇānupapattiḥ, gosadṛśo gavayapadavācya
ityākārakatvasyopagame ca sādṛśyasya
tadbhedasamānādhikaraṇatadgatadharmavattvarūpasya gurutvena
padavācyatāvacchedakatvāsambhavāt tasyā bhramatvāpattirityālocya
gavayo gavayapadavācya ityākārikaiva
upamitirupagantavyetyabhiprāyeṇoktam [219] gavayatvādirūpalaghudharmet i/
tādṛśadharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyatāketyarthaḥ/ [219] idam-sādṛśyadarśanasya
upamitihetutāpradarśanaṃ, upalakṣaṇaṃ vakṣyamāṇārthasūcakam/ [218] sādṛśyādītyādinā vaidharmyasaṃgrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The definition is' — up to '<s>gamya</s>' (cognizable), [this is stated] as an indication of authoritative basis for the universal-nature of <s>upamititva</s> (comparative-cognition-hood). [218] 'By this, <s>smaran</s> (remembering)' — by the present-tense reference. [218] 'They say': and here what is intended is the display of the view that, for the author of the <s>Saṅgraha</s> who has stated 'from some forest-dweller' and the like, the verbal cognition having as its object the meaning of the analogical statement (<s>atideśavākya</s>) is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>); the memory having that as its object is the operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>); and <s>upamiti</s> is the result (<s>phala</s>) — and not the view that the perception of the individual qualified by similarity and the like is the instrument, such memory is the operation, and <s>upamiti</s> is the result. For if the latter were the case, since the use of the word [in the analogical statement] would be within one's own control, one should say 'intending to remember, he sees the individual' [rather than 'remembering']. Therefore, through careful consideration of the natural import of '<s>smaran</s>' and the like, the former view alone is intended, not the second — and presenting that [second view] as the purport would be an inappropriate exposition of such a text, and is the seed of dissatisfaction. In the <s>Saṅgraha</s>, 'by the sentence': '<s>gosadṛśo gavayapadavācya</s>' (what is similar to a cow is the referent of the word '<s>gavaya</s>') is a formal analogy (<s>svarūpātideśa</s>) and so forth. [218] 'By another awakener (<s>udbodhaka</s>)': the meaning is an awakener in the form of unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) and the like, distinct from the perception of an individual qualified by similarity. [219] 'After the perception (of an individual) qualified by similarity' and so forth: here, if one accepts that <s>upamiti</s> has the form 'this is the referent of the word <s>gavaya</s>,' then after seeing another individual of <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox), the memory of word-referent-hood regarding it would be untenable. And if one accepts the form '<s>gosadṛśo gavayapadavācya</s>' (what is similar to a cow is the referent of the word <s>gavaya</s>), then since similarity — being of the nature of possessing a property belonging to an entity co-located with its different instances — is too complex, it could not be the delimiter of word-referent-hood, and [the cognition] would turn out to be erroneous. Considering this, with the intention that <s>upamiti</s> should be understood as having precisely the form '<s>gavayo gavayapadavācya</s>' (the <s>gavaya</s> is the referent of the word <s>gavaya</s>), it was said [219] 'a simple property such as <s>gavayatva</s> (<s>gavaya</s>-hood) and the like.' The meaning is: having qualificand-hood delimited by such a property. [219] 'This' — the demonstration of the causal status of the perception of similarity for <s>upamiti</s> is a suggestive indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), pointing to a meaning to be stated later. [218] By '<s>sādṛśyādi</s>' (similarity and the like), with '<s>ādi</s>,' dissimilarity is also included.

children.text: // iti prasaraṇākhyāyāṃ dīpikāprakāśikāvyākhyāyāṃ upamānaparicchedaḥ//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on comparison (<s>Upamānapariccheda</s>) in the commentary called <s>Prasaraṇa</s>, which is an exposition of the <s>Dīpikā</s> and <s>Prakāśikā</s>.

children.text: śabdaparicchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Chapter on Verbal Testimony (<s>Śabdapariccheda</s>)

children.text: śabdalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of Verbal Testimony (<s>Śabdalakṣaṇa</s>)

children.text:
upajīvyopajīvakatvasaṅgatyeti/ atra
vaktavyaṃ sarvaṃ prāgeva prapañcitam/ [222] śābdabodhopajīvyatvena
children.translated_text: 'By the connection of dependence and being depended upon': all that needs to be said here has already been elaborated previously. [222] 'As being depended upon for verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>)' means:

children.text:
śābdabodhahetutvena/ [222] phalaniṣṭhatve 'pīti/
āśrayatārūpasākṣātsambandhenetyādiḥ/ [222] svarūpayorapi -
śabdapramāṇopamānapramāṇayorapi/ etena saṅgateḥ sākṣātsambandhena
karaṇaniṣṭhatvaṃ sūcitam/ [222]
karaṇayorityādi ṣaṣṭhyartho
viṣayatvam abhidhānaśabdārthaikadeśajñānānvitam/ anantaratvaṃ
cāvyavahitatvam/ tacca pūrvāparasādhāraṇam/
svanirūpaṇapūrvanirūpaṇapūrvatvaśūnyatvasvottaranirūpaṇānuttaratvānyataravattvarūpaṃ
bodhyam/
children.translated_text: as being the cause of verbal cognition. [222] 'Even though residing in the result': [this means] through the direct relation in the form of locus-hood, and so forth. [222] 'Of the two in their own nature also' — of verbal testimony as a means of knowledge (<s>śabdapramāṇa</s>) and comparison as a means of knowledge (<s>upamānapramāṇa</s>) as well. By this, it is indicated that the connection has instrument-hood (<s>karaṇaniṣṭhatva</s>) through a direct relation. [222] 'Of the two instruments' and so forth — the meaning of the sixth case is content-hood, conjoined with the cognition that is a part of the meaning of the word 'denotation.' And 'immediacy' (<s>anantaratva</s>) means being uninterrupted. And that is common to both prior and subsequent. It should be understood as having the form of being-any-one-of: the absence of priority to one's own description's prior description, and the absence of subsequence to one's own subsequent description.

children.text:
nanu [222] āptavākyaṃ śabda iti saṃgrahe śabdatvasya lakṣyatāvacchedakatve
vahninā siñcatītyādyapramāṇavākye 'vyāptiḥ;
āptoccaritatvavirahādityata āha - [222] pramāṇaśabda iti/ tathā
ca pramāṇaśabdatvaṃ lakṣyatāvacchedakam/ tacca vahninā
siñcatītyādivākyavyāvṛttamiti bhāvaḥ/ [222] lakṣaṇamiti/
jabagaḍadaśādau ativyāptivyudāsāya vākyatvamuktam/
āptoktavākyamityatra uktaśabdena samāsāntargataṣaṣṭhyāḥ uccaritatvamartha
iti sūcitam/ [222] yathārthavaktṛtvarūpeti/ etena āptatvaṃ
hīṣṭatvam/ tathā ca vahninā siñcatīti vākye 'tivyāptitādavasthyam/
tatprayoktuḥ kasyacit iṣṭatvasambhavāditiśaṅkā nirastā/ nanu
vahninā siñcatītyādiprayokturapi kadācit
bādhitārthakavākyaprayogahetubhūtayathārthajñānavattāyāḥ sambhavāt
kathamativyāptivāraṇamityata āha -- [222] prakṛtavākyārtheti/ [222] niṣkarṣa iti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ --
tādātmya1svapratipādyārthagocarayathārthajñānajanyatvobhayasambandhena
children.translated_text: Now, [222] by the compendium statement '<s>āptavākyaṃ śabdaḥ</s>' (verbal testimony is the statement of a reliable person), if <s>śabdatva</s> (verbal-testimony-hood) is the delimiter of the defined, then in non-authoritative statements like 'sprinkle with fire' there would be non-pervasion. Since this is due to the absence of being uttered by a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>), he says — [222] 'the word <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge).' And thus, <s>pramāṇaśabdatva</s> (being a valid-means-of-knowledge-type verbal testimony) is the delimiter of the defined. And that excludes statements like 'sprinkle with fire' — this is the meaning. [222] 'The definition': in order to exclude over-extension to <s>jabagaḍadaśa</s> and the like [meaningless syllable sequences], <s>vākyatva</s> (sentence-hood) is stated. In '<s>āptoktavākyam</s>' (a sentence stated by a reliable person), by the word '<s>ukta</s>' (stated), the meaning of the sixth case [genitive] included within the compound is indicated as 'having been uttered.' [222] 'In the form of being a speaker of truth': by this, <s>āptatva</s> (reliability) means desirability (<s>iṣṭatva</s>). And thus, the same situation of over-extension persists with respect to the statement 'sprinkle with fire' — the doubt that this is so because of the possibility that some utterer of it has desirability [as a speaker] — is dispelled. Now, since even the utterer of 'sprinkle with fire' and the like may sometimes possess truthful cognition that serves as the cause of uttering a statement with a contradicted meaning, how is over-extension prevented? — to this he says — [222] 'regarding the meaning of the relevant statement.' [222] 'The conclusion': the meaning is as follows — through both relations of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and being produced by truthful cognition concerning the meaning conveyed by one's own [statement],

children.text:
1. svapratipādyetyādi/
svaṃ jalena siñcatītyādivākyaṃ tatpratipādyo yo 'thaḥ
jalakaraṇakasekakartā tadviṣayakaṃ yat yathārthajñānaṃ
tādṛśavākyaprayoktṛniṣṭhaṃ tajjanyatvaṃ tādṛśavākye, 'artha buddhvā
śabdaracanā' iti nyāyāditi bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. '<s>Svapratipādya</s>' and so forth: 'self' refers to a statement like 'sprinkle with water'; 'the meaning conveyed by it' is the agent of sprinkling with water as instrument; 'truthful cognition having that as its object' is [such cognition] residing in the utterer of such a statement; 'being produced by that' pertains to such a statement — by the principle '<s>artha buddhvā śabdaracanā</s>' (verbal composition occurs after cognizing the meaning): this is the meaning.

children.text:
vākyaviśiṣṭavākyatvaṃ
1svajanyatvasvaviṣayībhūtārthapratipādakatvobhayasambandhena
yathārthajñānaviśiṣṭavākyatvaṃ vā śabdalakṣaṇamiti/ [222] etat vākyārthajñānasya śabdaprayogahetutvam/
children.translated_text: sentence-hood qualified by a sentence — through both relations of being-produced-by-it and conveying-the-meaning-that-has-become-its-object — or sentence-hood qualified by veridical cognition, is the definition of verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). [§222] This is the causality of verbal testimony for the cognition of sentence-meaning.

children.text: śaktinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Investigation of Denotative Power (<s>Śakti</s>)

children.text:
nanu [225] arthasmṛtyanukūletyādinā dīpikāyām
śaktipadārthaniruktirayuktā/ tannirukterihāprakṛtatvādityāśaṅkayāha -
[225] mīmāṃsaketyādi/ [225] nirāsakatveneti/ prayojanatayā
hetutvavivakṣayā tṛtīyā/ agra ityavatāraṇānvayi/ avatāraṇaṃ
pravṛttyanukūlo vyāpāraḥ/ sa ca śaṅkāgranthapravṛttiḥ/ [225] taditi/ mīmāṃsaketyarthaḥ/ [225] matam
children.translated_text: Now, the etymological analysis of the meaning of the word <s>śakti</s> in the <s>Dīpikā</s> with 'conducive to the recollection of the meaning' and the like is inappropriate — because such etymological analysis is not relevant here. Anticipating this objection, he says [§225] 'the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>' and so forth. [§225] 'By way of refutation' — the instrumental case is intended with the meaning of purposefulness. 'In advance' connects with the introductory passage. The introductory passage is the operation conducive to proceeding. And that is the proceeding of the objection-text. [§225] 'That' — means: of the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>. [§225] The view

children.translated_text: accepted as authoritative — this is the meaning. [§227] 'By commonality' — commonality means possessing a form that occurs in that. And the form is as stated in 'of the meaning' etc. The qualification connected with the meaning of the word <s>śakti</s> is the meaning of the instrumental case. The rest is clear. The statement 'the meaning of the word <s>śakti</s>' is made to indicate that the meaning of the word <s>śakti</s> in the <s>Dīpikā</s> is the referent of the word <s>śakti</s>. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, up to 'conducive' is the qualifier of the relation. Now, even with the inclusion of 'conduciveness to the recollection of the meaning' in the definition of the meaning of the word <s>śakti</s> in the <s>Dīpikā</s>, there would be the unwanted consequence of [including] the inherence between the word for <s>ākāśa</s> and <s>ākāśa</s>. Even with the inclusion of word-qualification through both relations of residing-in-self and residing-in-one's-own-meaning, the exclusion of the inherence between the word <s>ākāśa</s> and <s>ākāśa</s> is impossible, because that too possesses both those relations and is conducive to the recollection of the meaning. Therefore he says [§225] 'productive of verbal cognition.' This is a qualifier of the recollection. And accordingly, since the recollection of meaning such as <s>ākāśa</s> and the like, which depends on the cognition of inherence, lacks the property of being productive of verbal cognition, there is no unwanted consequence — this is the purport. Now, conduciveness means productive-ness, and that is contradicted with respect to the relation, because the cognition of the relation itself produces the recollection. Therefore he says [§225] 'conduciveness here [means].' [§225] 'The qualificand,' etc. — even though the word for <s>ātman</s> has the relation [of <s>śakti</s>] to <s>ātman</s> through the possession of the unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) that is the motivator [of <s>Īśvara</s>'s will], the final conclusion is that [the relation is]: being the substratum of the relation of having the delimitor delimited by the cognition-residing delimitor-hood that is delimited by the production-relation determined by the verbal-cognition-generating-ness of the recollection — hence there is no defect.
