children.translated_text: Objection: if <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) is accepted only in the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) that is the locus of the universal (<s>jāti</s>), then how is the appearance of the universal cow-hood and its relation possible in the verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>) generated by the word 'cow' and the like? — because there is a rule that what is not within the scope of <s>śakti</s> does not appear in verbal cognition. Nor should it be said that there is no valid ground for such a rule — because if so, there would be the unwanted consequence of cognizing a pot and the like from the verbal cognition generated by the word 'cow' and the like. As for [the objection] that in cases like 'the blue pot,' identity (<s>abheda</s>) would not appear in the verbal cognition on this account — that is not so — because of the qualification 'distinct from the aggregate of two word-meanings.' Anticipating this [objection], he states the resolution accepted by the earlier logicians — [231] with 'Here this should be understood' and so on. The later logicians (<s>Navīnas</s>), however, [say]: there is no valid ground for such a rule. Nor does the stated over-extension arise — because it is accepted that only <s>śakti</s>, its delimitor, and the relation that constitutes the delimitor of that delimitor determine what appears in verbal cognition. And thus, they say, <s>śakti</s> need not be accepted for both the universal and its qualification. He presents their view — with 'the later logicians, however.'

prayatnaḥ gavānayanadharmikeṣṭasādhanatājñānajanyaḥ pravṛttitvāt
svīyapravṛttivat ityanumānāntaramapīha bodhyam/ [235] gavānayanajñānasya - gavānayanadharmikeṣṭasādhanatājñānasya/
children.translated_text: Objection: in lexicons (<s>kośa</s>) beginning with 'one-tusked' (<s>ekadanta</s>) and so forth, the <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) of words like <s>ekadanta</s> and the like is unjustified — because the correctness of a <s>dvandva</s> obtains only when there is mutual difference among the word-meanings being compounded, and here that [difference] is absent. Therefore he says — [234] 'therein.' [235] 'From usage' — the meaning is: from practice (<s>pravṛtti</s>). [234] Even in the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'by the usage of the learned (<s>vṛddha</s>),' the meaning is: by the practice of one who is linguistically competent (<s>vyutpanna</s>). Now, in the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement [237] beginning with 'but,' since the genitive in 'having the purpose of the effect' cannot have a genitive-completion, and since the word 'of the usage' cannot construe with what follows, he says — [237] 'of the usage' and so forth. [237] 'Of the usage' — of the sentence-employment (<s>vākyaprayoga</s>). Now, from the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement [234] 'having observed the activity and having seen the bringing of a cow,' one obtains that the knowledge of cow-bringing comes after the inference of activity. And that is not correct — because since inference is not possible without the knowledge of the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), the knowledge of cow-bringing is first necessary. Therefore he says — [237] 'having seen the bringing of a cow' and so forth. Since the apprehension of the activity, being a different valid cognition, is not possible [in this way], he says — 'of the word upalabhya (having observed).' He states the form of the inference — [235] 'this is performed.' This inference too should be understood here: 'This effort, which has the subject cow-bringing, is produced by the cognition of its being the means to a desired end, because of being an activity — like one's own activity.' [235] 'Of the knowledge of cow-bringing' — of the cognition of its being the means to a desired end with respect to the subject cow-bringing.

children.text:
niścityeti/ ayamāśayaḥ - tādṛśajñānaṃ
tādṛśavākyajanyam
children.translated_text: 'Having ascertained' etc. The intent here is: such cognition is generated by such a sentence;

children.text:
tādṛśavākyaviśiṣṭatvādityānumāniko 'tra niścayaḥ/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
ca
children.translated_text: this ascertainment is inferential, since [the cognition] is qualified by such a sentence. And the qualification is

children.text: svasattādhīnasattākatvasvābhāvādhīnābhāvapratiyogitvobhayasambandheneti/
children.translated_text: through the dual relation of having-existence-dependent-on-one's-own-existence and having-one's-own-absence-as-the-counter-positive-of-an-absence-dependent-on-one's-own-absence.

children.text:
nanu gāmānaya
ityādiviśiṣṭavākyasyaiva tādṛśaviśiṣṭārthe śaktiḥ kuto na
svīkriyata ityata āha - [235] vākyasyeti/ nanu yavaśabdasya
dīrghaśūkaviśiṣṭa śaktisvīkāre mlecchānāṃ priyaṅgau prayogo na
syādityata āha - [235] priyaṅgau tviti/ [235] ākhyātasya yatnatvaviśiṣṭa ityādi/ ākhyātaṃ
yatnatvaviśiṣṭavācakaṃ 1tādṛśakarotivyākhyetatvāditi rītyā
vivaraṇasya śaktigrāhakatā bodhyā/ tatsamānārthakapadāntareṇa
tadarthakathanaṃ hi vyākhyānamiti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: why not accept <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) in the qualified meaning of the qualified sentence 'Bring a cow' and so forth itself? Therefore he says — [235] 'of the sentence' etc. Now, if <s>śakti</s> qualified by long-awned [grain] is accepted for the word <s>yava</s>, the usage by <s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians) for <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet) would not be possible. Therefore he says — [235] 'for <s>priyaṅgu</s>, however' etc. [235] 'The finite verb conveys what is qualified by effort-hood' and so forth. The finite verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>) denotes what is qualified by effort-hood; the capacity to apprehend <s>śakti</s> of an explanation (<s>vyākhyāna</s>) should be understood through the reasoning 'because it is an explanation of [the verb] <s>karoti</s> (does) having such a meaning.' For the explanation is the stating of the meaning by another word having the same meaning — this is the purport.

children.text:
śabdānāṃ
siddhaparatvamapīti nirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of whether words also convey accomplished entities (<s>siddha</s>)

children.text:
nanu siddhārtho 'pi
vākyaprayogī bhavatu kiṃ tāvatā vyutpatterityata āha - [237] tathāceti/ [237] anyathā-tatra śaktigrahāvaśyambhāvavirahe/
children.translated_text: Objection: let the user of sentences [convey] accomplished meanings too — what follows from that regarding linguistic competence (<s>vyutpatti</s>)? Therefore he says — [237] 'And thus' etc. [237] 'Otherwise' — in the absence of the necessity of apprehending <s>śakti</s> there.

children.text: lakṣaṇānirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (Secondary Signification)

children.text:
nanu [237] tīrepi śaktiḥ na kalpyata iti dīpikāvākyamanupapannam/
tīrādiśabdānāṃ tīre śaktisvīkārādityata āha - [238] gaṅgāpadasyeti/ [238] śeṣa iti/ [238] nānārthakatvānupapattiriti/ nānārthaśaktatvānupapattirityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement [237] 'The <s>śakti</s> is not postulated even in the bank' is unjustified — because <s>śakti</s> of words like 'bank' (<s>tīra</s>) and the like is accepted in the bank. Therefore he says — [238] 'Of the word <s>Gaṅgā</s>' etc. [238] 'The remainder' etc. [238] 'The impossibility of having multiple meanings' etc. — the meaning is: the impossibility of having <s>śakti</s> for multiple meanings.

children.text:
nanu lavaṇāśvayorapi
kathañcit saṃyogaḥ sambhavati, evamekakālīnatvādisambandho 'pīti
noktadoṣavistārasaṃbhava ityata āha - [238] idamupalakṣaṇamiti/
[237] idaṃ lavaṇāśvayoḥ parasparasambandhābhāvāt
nānāśaktikalpanam/ [238] prasiddhayoḥ
samānaprayogaprācuryayorityarthaḥ/ etena gaṅgādipadāt
viśeṣassūcitaḥ/ tatra tīrapravāhayoratathātvāt/ [238] mañcasthapuruṣa iti/ atra mañcapadaṃ puruṣamātraparam,
mañcasthetyuktistu tatra śakyasambandhalābhāya/ vācyārthasya mañcādestu na
śābdabodhe bhānamiti dhyeyam/ idamatrajahalallakṣaṇālakṣaṇam -
lakṣyatāvacchedakarūpeṇa lakṣyamātraviṣayakabodhajanikā lakṣaṇeti/ [238] apinā - apiśabdena/ [238]
ekasārthavāhitvena -
ekasamudāyaghaṭakatvena/ ajahallakṣaṇālakṣaṇam - lakṣyatāvacchedakarūpeṇa
śakyalakṣyobhayabodhikā
children.translated_text: Objection: even between salt and a horse, some conjunction is possible; similarly, a relation such as contemporaneity and the like is also [possible] — hence the scope for the stated proliferation of defects does not arise. Therefore he says — [238] 'This is a representative instance (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>)' etc. [237] 'This' — the postulation of multiple <s>śaktis</s> because of the absence of mutual relation between salt and horse. [238] 'Of two well-known [meanings]' — the meaning is: of two meanings having equal frequency of usage. By this, a distinction from the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and similar words is indicated — because in the case of 'bank' and 'stream,' the [equal frequency] does not obtain. [238] 'A man on the platform' etc. Here the word 'platform' (<s>mañca</s>) refers to a person alone; the expression 'on the platform' is for obtaining the connection with the denotable [meaning] there. But the literally expressed meaning of 'platform' and the like does not appear in the verbal cognition — this should be noted. The definition of <s>jahal-lakṣaṇā</s> (exclusive secondary signification) here is: that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> which generates a cognition having only the indicated meaning as its object, in the form of the delimitor of indicated-ness. [238] 'By the word api' — by the particle <s>api</s>. [238] 'By being a member of one caravan' — by being a constituent of a single aggregate. The definition of <s>ajahal-lakṣaṇā</s> (inclusive secondary signification) is: that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> which generates a cognition having both the denoted and the indicated meanings,

children.text:
lakṣaṇeti/
lakṣyatāvacchedakaṃ darśitam/ nanu chatripadamukhyārthasya chatriṇaḥ
gamanakartṛtvānvayānupapattivirahāt kimatra lakṣaṇāniyāmakamityata
āha [238] tātparyeti/ matubarthaketyanena inipratyayasya
śaktatvalakṣaṇapadatvaṃ sūcitam/ [238]
tacchaktyeti/ vākyaśaktyetyarthaḥ/
mīmāṃsakamatamabhiprayannāha - [238]
pratipādyeti/ svamatābhiprāyeṇāha -
[238] anyatheti/ [238] ekasārthe ekasamudāye lakṣaṇā
svāśrayapuruṣaghaṭitatvarūpaparamparāsambandhātmikā/ [238] āhurityasvarasasūcanam/ tadbījantu tathāsati
jahallakṣaṇodāharaṇamevedaṃ syāt/ tathā ca prakṛtānupayogaḥ
dīpikāyām tasyājahallakṣaṇodāharaṇatvakathanāditi/ [239] tasya tīvabrahmaṇoraikyasya/ [239] tattāṃśasyedānīmityādi/
ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - taddeśādisambandhaviśiṣṭe etaddeśādisambandho bādhitaḥ,
viśiṣṭe anvīyamānadharmasya viśeṣaṇe 'pyanvayāvaśyakatayā
viśeṣaṇībhūtataddeśādisambandhe tadbādhāt/ ataḥ tatpadaṃ
deśakālasambandhimātraparam na tu deśādau tattāṃśo 'pi vivakṣitaḥ/
tathā ca tacchabdalakṣaṇā jahadajahallakṣaṇā/ tallakṣaṇantu
vācyatāvacchedakāprakārakavācyaviṣayakabodhaprayojikā lakṣaṇetīti/
children.translated_text: in the form of the delimitor of indicated-ness. The delimitor of indicated-ness has been shown. Now, the primary meaning of the word <s>chatrī</s> (one with an umbrella) — since there is no incompatibility of the construal of the agent of going with the umbrella-possessor — what then is the ground for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> here? Therefore he says — [238] 'the speaker's intention (<s>tātparya</s>)' etc. By the word '<s>matubarthaka</s>' (conveying possession), the <s>ini</s> suffix's being a <s>śakta</s> (directly denoting) word is indicated. [238] 'By the <s>śakti</s> of that' — the meaning is: by the <s>śakti</s> of the sentence. Intending the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view, he says — [238] 'what is conveyed' etc. Intending his own view, he says — [238] 'otherwise' etc. [238] 'In the aggregate' — <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in a single aggregate is through the indirect relation (<s>paramparā-sambandha</s>) in the form of being-constituted-by-one's-own-persons. [238] 'He says' — this hints at reluctant acceptance. The ground for that is: if so, this would be just an example of <s>jahal-lakṣaṇā</s> (exclusive secondary signification), and accordingly it would be inapplicable to the present [discussion], since the <s>Dīpikā</s> states it as an example of <s>ajahal-lakṣaṇā</s>. [239] 'Of that' — of the identity of that (<s>tat</s>) and <s>Brahman</s>. [239] 'Of the tat-component now' and so forth. The purport is this: the spatio-temporal relation qualified by the 'that'-referent's locus and the like is sublated [when attributed to] the 'this'-referent's locus and the like, and since the property being construed with the qualified [entity] must necessarily also construe with the qualifier, the spatio-temporal relation that has become the qualifier is also sublated. Therefore the word 'tat' refers only to the possessor of spatio-temporal relation, not to the spatio-temporal component in the locus and the like. And thus the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the word 'tat' is <s>jahadajahal-lakṣaṇā</s> (exclusive-inclusive secondary signification). Its definition is: that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> which generates a cognition having the denoted meaning as object but not having the delimitor of denotedness as qualifier-mode.

children.text:
so 'yaṃ devadatta
ityādau yadi viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhiśābdabodhaḥ svīkriyate
tadaivaṃ syāt, na cāyaṃ svīkriyate, kiṃ tu
taddeśatatkālavṛttitvopalakṣitānuyogikavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhibodhaḥ/ tatra
ca na prāguktarītyā bādhāvakāśaḥ/ viśeṣaṇe vidheyānanvayāt/ ata eva
so 'yaṃ devadatta ityādivākyajanyaśābdabodhasamanantaraṃ
taddeśatatkālavṛttiḥ na vā devadatta
ityādisaṃśayānutpādo 'pyanubhavasiddha upapadyate/
atastattāṃśasyāhānāt nātralakṣaṇāvakāśa iti nopeyata eva
jahadajahallakṣaṇeti vadanti/ tanmatamāha - [239] pare tvityādinā/
children.translated_text: In cases like 'That same is this <s>Devadatta</s>' (<s>so'yaṃ Devadattaḥ</s>), if a verbal cognition grasping the qualification of the qualified is accepted, then it would be so. But such [a cognition] is not accepted; rather, what is accepted is a cognition grasping the qualification delimited by the property of existing at that place and time. And there, there is no scope for sublation in the manner previously stated — because the predicate does not construe with the qualifier. For this very reason, it is also established by experience that immediately after the verbal cognition generated by the sentence 'That same is this <s>Devadatta</s>' and the like, the doubt '<s>Devadatta</s> existed at that place and time or not' does not arise. Therefore, since the 'tat'-component is not abandoned, there is no scope for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> here — and thus <s>jahadajahal-lakṣaṇā</s> (exclusive-inclusive secondary signification) should not be accepted at all — so they say. He presents their view — [239] with 'Others, however' and so forth.

children.text: gauṇīvyañjanayorvṛttyantaratvakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of <s>gauṇī</s> (metaphorical usage) and <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) as distinct functions of words

children.text:
rājñāmapi śaktyaiveti/ bhuvaṃ dharati
rakṣatīti rītyā yogaśaktyaivetyarthaḥ/ nanu vyañjanāyāḥ kutra
lakṣaṇāyāmantarbhāva ityatrāha - [242] gaṅgāyāmityādi/ [242] lakṣaṇāsāmrājyāt - lakṣaṇābalāt/ cakārasya
samuccayaparatvāsambhavādāha - [242]
castvartha iti/ [242] vilakṣaṇaśabdaprayoktṛtvāditi/
children.translated_text: 'Even of kings, by <s>śakti</s> alone' — the meaning is: by <s>yoga-śakti</s> (compositional denotative power) alone, through the analysis 'he sustains the earth, he protects [it].' Now, where is <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) subsumed under <s>lakṣaṇā</s>? To this he says — [242] 'In <s>Gaṅgā</s>' and so forth. [242] 'By the sovereignty of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>' — by the force of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. Since the particle <s>ca</s> (and) cannot have the meaning of conjunction [here], he says — [242] 'The meaning of <s>ca</s> is <s>tu</s> (but).' [242] 'Because of being the user of a distinctive word' etc.

children.text:
vilakṣaṇaśabdaprayogaviśiṣṭatvādityarthaṃḥ/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svānukūlakṛtimattvādheyatvobhayasambandhena/ ādheyatā
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because of being qualified by the use of a distinctive word. The qualification is through the dual relation of possessing-an-agent-of-action-favorable-to-oneself and being-the-content-of. The being-the-content-of is

children.text:
svapativiśeṣyaka-evaṃvidhaśābdabodhaprakārakecchāprayojyatvobhayasambandhena/
tenāsmadādiṣvapi yathāśrutahetusattvena na
children.translated_text: through the dual relation of being-prompted-by-the-desire-having-as-qualifier-mode-such-a-verbal-cognition-having-one's-own-husband-as-qualificand. Thereby, even in us and the like, since the stated reason exists as literally understood, there is no

children.text: vyabhicāraḥ/ [242] sambhāvanādītyādinā mānasaparigrahaḥ/ [243] mantavyamiti/ tatha ca tathānuvyasāyo 'siddha iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: deviation. [242] 'Conjecture (<s>sambhāvanā</s>) and the like' — by this, the mental [perception] is included. [243] 'It should be considered' etc. And thus, the introspective cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) of that form is unestablished — this is the purport.

children.text: lakṣaṇābījanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of the ground for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification)

children.text:
lakṣaṇānupapattiriti/ śakyārthasya yaṣṭyādeḥ
kriyānvayasambhavāditi bhāvaḥ/ [245]
niyatakāle -
aśvādiniyataprayāṇādikāla ityarthaḥ/ [245] viśeṣaṇāderityādinā
sāhacaryādeḥ parigrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The impossibility of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>' — the purport is: because the construal of action with the primary meaning, namely a staff and the like, is possible. [245] 'At a fixed time' — the meaning is: at the time of the fixed departure of horses and the like. [245] 'By the qualifier and the like' — by this, association (<s>sāhacarya</s>) and the like are included.

children.text: arthāghyāhārakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of <s>arthādhyāhāra</s> (ellipsis / semantic supplementation)

children.text:
adhyāhāraḥ - upasthitiḥ/ [246] arthajñānārthatvādityatrārthajñānamupasthitiḥ/ yathākathañciditi/
mānāntareṇetyarthaḥ/ nanu padajanyatvaniveśasya ghaṭaḥ
karmatvamityādisthapalaviśeṣaprayojanakathanaṃ viphalaṃ,
pratyakṣādyupasthitapadārthasthale 'pi tatsambhavāt ityāśaṅkya na bodhe
padajanyatvaniveśasya idaṃ prayojanakathanam, api tu
viśeṣapadasyāpīti samādhānamāha - [247] viśeṣapadasyāpīti/
vṛttyeti vaiśiṣṭye tṛtīyā/ [247]
digiti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ --- yadyapi
ghaṭādipadaṃ vastugatyā vṛttiviśiṣṭameveti
tatsamavāyajñānajanyākāśopasthityā śābdabodhavāraṇāya
tattaddaṇḍavṛttiprakārakatattatpadadharmikajñānajanyatattadarthopasthiterhetutvaṃ
vaktavyam/ evaṃ
tattatpadavṛttiprakārakatattadarthadharmikajñānajanyatattadarthopasthiterapi/ evaṃ
ca samavāyasya vṛttirūpatvābhāvāt nātiprasaṅgaḥ/ śaktilakṣaṇayoreva
vṛttirūpatvāditi/
children.translated_text: '<s>Adhyāhāra</s>' (supplementation) — means presentation (<s>upasthiti</s>). [246] In 'because of being for the purpose of meaning-knowledge,' 'meaning-knowledge' means presentation (<s>upasthiti</s>). 'In whatever manner' — the meaning is: by another valid means of knowledge. Now, the statement of the specific purpose of including 'produced by a word' through the stale example 'the pot is an accusative' is fruitless — because [that purpose] obtains even in cases where the word-meaning is presented by perception and other [means]. Anticipating this [objection] and [noting that] this statement of purpose is not for the verbal cognition [proper] but for the specific word as well — he gives the resolution: [247] 'Of the specific word also' etc. 'By the function' — the instrumental case is in the sense of the qualification. [247] 'In a direction' etc. The purport is this: although the word 'pot' and the like, in reality, is qualified by its function (<s>vṛtti</s>) [i.e. denotative relation], and hence to prevent verbal cognition through the cognition of the inherence of that [function] in space, the causality of the presentation of each meaning generated by the cognition having each word as subject and having each word's function as qualifier-mode must be stated — similarly for the presentation of each meaning generated by the cognition having each meaning as subject and having each word's function as qualifier-mode — and thus, since inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) does not have the nature of a function (<s>vṛtti</s>), there is no over-extension. Because only <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) have the nature of a function — this is the purport.

children.text: padavibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Division of Words (<s>Padavibhāga</s>)

children.text:
avayavaśaktiḥ - svaghaṭakapadaśaktiḥ/ [248] tanmātreṇeti/ avayavaśaktimātreṇetyarthaḥ/ mātraśabdena
rūḍhiśaktivyavacchedaḥ/ tathā ca
rūḍhiśaktijñānajanyārthaviṣayakabodhajanakatvābhāve sati
avayavaśaktijñānajanyārthaviṣayakabodhajanakatvaṃ yaugikasya lakṣaṇamiti
paryavasitam/ yogarūḍhivāraṇāya satyantam/ [248] tanmātreṇetyādi/ rūḍhimātreṇetyarthaḥ/
mātrapadenāvayavaśaktivyayacchedaḥ/ tathā ca
yogaśaktijñānajanyārthaviṣayakabodhajanakatvābhāve sati
rūḍhiśaktijñānajanyārthaviṣayakabodhajanakatvaṃ rūḍhasvya lakṣaṇam/
yaugikavāraṇāya satyantam/ [248]
yogarūḍhibhyāmityādi
yogaśaktijñānajanyaḥ yaḥ rūḍhiśaktijñānajanyaśābdabodhaḥ
tajjanakatvamityarthaḥ/ rūḍhivāraṇāya prathamaṃ janyāntam/
yaugikavāraṇāya dvitīyam/ parasparasahakāreṇetyanudapādāne rūḍhyā
arthapratipādakatve sati yogenārthapratipādakatvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ syāt/ tatra
ca yaugikarūḍhāviśeṣaḥ, atastadupādānaṃ tenaikatra śābdabodhe
dvividhaśaktijñānajanyatvalābhaḥ/ sahakāre parasparatvaṃ ca
svāśrayanirūpitasahākarāśrayanirūpitatvaṃ
sahakāraviśiṣṭatvaparyavasitam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svanirūpakavṛttitvasvāśrayanirūpitatvobhayasambandhena/ [248] parasparāsahāyenetyagrimagranthasya niruktasahakārābhāvenetyarthaḥ/
tṛtīyārthaspaya vaiśiṣṭyasya śaktyādāvanvayaḥ/ tathā ca
rūḍhiśaktijñānajanyayogaśaktijñānājanyārthaviṣayakabodhajanakatve sati
rūḍhiśaktijñānājanyayogyaśaktijñānajanyārthaviṣayakabodhajanakatvaṃ
yaugikarūḍhasya lakṣaṇam paryavasitam/ kevalayaugikakevalarūḍhayoḥ
vāraṇāya daladvayam/ [249] yogarūḍhimiti/ yogasahitāṃ
rūḍhimityarthaḥ/ tena - yogaḥ ca rūḍhiśceti
itaretarayogadvandvāśrayaṇe yogarūḍhī iti dvivacanāntatvaprasaṅgaḥ/
yogarūḍhyossamāhāra iti samāhāradvandvāśrayaṇe yogarūḍhīti
napusaṃkatvaprasaṅga iti śaṅkāyāḥ nāvakāśaḥ/ śākapārthivādivat
madhyamapadalopisamāsāśrayaṇenāvirodhāt/
children.translated_text: '<s>Avayavaśakti</s>' (component-denotative-power) means the denotative power of one's own constituent words. [248] 'By that alone' — the meaning is: by the component-denotative-power alone. By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (alone), the conventional denotative power (<s>rūḍhiśakti</s>) is excluded. Accordingly, the definition of a derivative word (<s>yaugika</s>) amounts to: the capacity to generate cognition of the object produced by the knowledge of component-denotative-power, in the absence of the capacity to generate cognition of the object produced by the knowledge of conventional denotative power. The qualification 'in the absence of' is to exclude the derivative-conventional (<s>yogarūḍhi</s>). [248] 'By that alone,' and so forth — the meaning is: by conventional denotative power alone. By the word '<s>mātra</s>,' the component-denotative-power is excluded. Accordingly, the definition of a conventional word (<s>rūḍha</s>) amounts to: the capacity to generate cognition of the object produced by the knowledge of conventional denotative power, in the absence of the capacity to generate cognition of the object produced by the knowledge of derivative denotative power. The qualification 'in the absence of' is to exclude the derivative. [248] 'By both derivation and convention,' and so forth — the meaning is: the capacity to generate that verbal cognition which is produced by the knowledge of conventional denotative power and is also produced by the knowledge of derivative denotative power. The first [qualification] 'produced' is to exclude the merely conventional; the second is to exclude the merely derivative. Without the inclusion of 'through mutual assistance,' the definition would be: the capacity to convey meaning through derivation when there is the capacity to convey meaning through convention. In that case, there would be no distinction between the derivative-conventional and the merely conventional. Therefore, that inclusion is made, and thereby the verbal cognition in a single instance obtains the character of being produced by the knowledge of both kinds of denotative power. Mutuality in the assistance means being determined by the locus of assistance that determines one's own locus, which amounts to being qualified by assistance. The qualification is through the dual relation of occurring in one's own determiner and being determined by one's own locus. [248] 'Without mutual assistance' — the meaning of the subsequent text is: without the assistance as described. The qualification expressed by the instrumental case connects with the denotative power and so forth. Accordingly, the definition of the derivative-conventional (<s>yogarūḍha</s>) amounts to: the capacity to generate cognition of the object produced by the knowledge of derivative denotative power and not produced by the knowledge of conventional denotative power alone, together with the capacity to generate cognition of the object produced by the knowledge of conventional denotative power and not produced by the knowledge of derivative denotative power alone. The two clauses are to exclude the merely derivative and the merely conventional respectively. [249] '<s>Yogarūḍhi</s>' — means convention accompanied by derivation. Therefore, there is no occasion for the objection that adopting an iterative <s>dvandva</s> compound 'derivation and convention' would require the dual ending '<s>yogarūḍhī</s>,' or that adopting a collective <s>dvandva</s> would require the neuter gender '<s>yogarūḍhi</s>' — since there is no inconsistency by adopting a middle-word-elision compound, as in '<s>śākapārthiva</s>' and the like.

children.text:
etadabhiprāyeṇaivāgre
kumude kumudaprayogasattvāt iṣṭāpattirityata āha - [249] paṅkajādīti/
children.translated_text: With this very intention, [the author] says ahead — [249] '<s>paṅkaja</s> and the like' — because the usage of '<s>kumuda</s>' for the night-lotus establishes the desired conclusion (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>).

children.text: anvitaśaktikhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of <s>Anvitaśakti</s> (Sentential Denotation Theory)

children.text:
padārthadvayasyaiva parasparānvaya
ityetallābhāya itaretyuktam/ natvitaratvamapi
śakyatāvacchedakaghaṭakamityabhiprāyeṇāha - [251] anvita iti/
nanvanvayāṃśe 'pi śaktirāstām, kiṃ tata ityāha - [251] anvita ityādi/ uktarītyā kāryāṃśopekṣābījasambhavāt
itarapadasya kāryaparatve gauṇatvāpatteścāsvarasaṃ hṛdi nidhāya [251] āhurityuktam/ tattatkāraṇāvyavahitottaratvaṃ
children.translated_text: To obtain that the connection (<s>anvaya</s>) is precisely of two word-meanings with each other, [the author] said 'the other.' But the intention is not that otherness itself is a component of the delimitor of denotative-power-hood. [The author] says — [251] '<s>anvita</s>' (connected). Objection: let there be denotative power even for the connected portion; what of it? [The author] says — [251] '<s>anvita</s>,' and so forth. Keeping in mind that, in the manner described, there is the possibility of a basis for disregarding the effect-component, and that interpreting the other word as referring to the effect would result in secondary usage (<s>gauṇatva</s>), which is against the natural flow — [251] 'he says' was stated. The immediate-successiveness to that particular cause

children.text:
svasāmānādhikaraṇyāvacchinna-svāvyavahitottarakṣaṇotpattikatvasambandhena
tatkāraṇavaiśiṣṭyam/ tena vyadhikaraṇaśābdabodhavyudāsaḥ/
children.translated_text: is the qualification of that cause through the relation of having origination at the moment immediately successive to oneself, delimited by co-location with oneself. By this, verbal cognition relating to different loci is excluded.

ayogyodāharaṇatvādityādyāśaṅkyānākāṅkṣodāharaṇāntaramāha [255] ghaṭa ityādi/
children.translated_text: By 'fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) and the like,' words uttered without delay are included. Objection: the being-produced-by-the-absence-of-a-certain-word is being-generated-by-it, and that is not possible in the case of the capacity to generate verbal cognition, which has the nature of absence, since that [capacity] is eternal. Therefore [the author] says — [255] 'And the being-produced.' Objection: since verbal cognition arises even without the knowledge that [a certain word combination] does not generate the stated verbal cognition, how can expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) have that [knowledge] as a component? Therefore [the author] says — [255] 'Up to the non-generative capacity.' [255] '<s>Paricāyaka</s>' means illuminator (<s>bodhaka</s>). Since the sentence-meaning is novel and difficult to grasp prior to verbal cognition, in some cases verbal cognition arises even from a doubt about fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) — with this intention it was stated — [255] 'Doubt and ascertainment'

children.text: vedāpauruṣeyatvam
children.translated_text: The Unauthoredness (<s>Apauruṣeyatva</s>) of the <s>Veda</s>

children.text:
pratītidvayasyānyaviṣayakatvakalpanāmapekṣya ekasyāḥ
pratītestatkalpanaṃ yuktam/ tathā ca pratyabhijñā
sājātyāvagāhitvatadabhāvānyataravatī prameyatvādityanumānaṃ

kakārādyabhivyañjakakaṇṭhatālvādivyāpāraviṣayakatvarūpaṃ lāghavaṃ
syāditi tarkānunṛhītaṃ pramāṇamityāśayenāha - [259] utpattīti/ atra ca yadi pratyabhijñā sājātyāvagāhinī syāt tarhi
varṇānāmanityatayā dhvaṃsapratiyogitvaṃ prāgabhāvapratiyogitvaṃ ca
syāt iti gauravatarkasahakṛtanoktānumānena
pratyabhijñāyāssājātyāvagāhitvābhāvasiddhaṃ
utpattivināśapratyayoranyaviṣayakatvakalpanaṃ nirābādhameveti
uktayuktirevetyabhipretya [251] hṛdayam ityuktam/ etadasvarasenaiva
yuktyantaramāha - [259] varṇānāmiti/
children.translated_text: Rather than postulating that two cognitions have different objects, it is proper to postulate that for one cognition. Accordingly, the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) [of phonemes] either apprehends generic similarity or does not — the inference proceeds: '[the cognition] has the property of being an object of knowledge (<s>prameyatva</s>)' and so on. If the recognition apprehends generic similarity, then since the cognitions of origination and destruction would have as their objects the operations of the throat, palate, and the like that manifest [the phoneme] <s>ka</s> and so forth, there would be parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>). Thus the warrant, supported by the corroborative reasoning (<s>tarka</s>), is stated with this intention — [259] 'Origination,' and so forth. And here, if recognition were to apprehend generic similarity, then due to the non-eternality of phonemes, there would be counter-positive-hood of destruction and counter-positive-hood of prior absence — this is the corroborative reasoning based on the undesirable consequence of complexity,

children.text:
nanu varṇanityatve
kathaṃ vedasyānityatvamityāśaṅkya tadupapādayati - [259] prakāśikāyām agnīti/ [259] ucitamiti/
utpattivināśapratyayānuguṇyāditibhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: if phonemes are eternal, how is the non-eternality of the <s>Veda</s> [to be explained]? Anticipating this doubt, [the author] establishes it — [259] In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'fire (<s>agni</s>).' [259] 'Appropriate' — the purport is: in accordance with the cognitions of origination and destruction, and so forth.

children.translated_text: Objection: <s>ācāra</s> (practice) means performance; and that has the nature of activity. So if it were a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), it would conflict with the previously stated classification of <s>pramāṇas</s>. Therefore [the author] says — [260] 'Of the practices,' and so forth. [261] By this, the word '<s>ācāra</s>' is understood as referring to the stated sentence. [260] 'It is inferred' — here the manner of inference is as follows: this <s>smṛti</s> is rooted in some Vedic branch (<s>śākhā</s>), because it is a <s>smṛti</s> — and so on. By this inference, the Vedic branch that is the root of the <s>smṛtis</s> of <s>Vyāsa</s> and others is established. Such a branch has its recitation discontinued at present, because it is not currently available; whatever is not so is not so, like a branch that is being recited. [261] By '<s>nadī</s> and the like,' the inclusion of [etymological illustrations like] '<s>rāja</s>,' '<s>jarā</s>,' '<s>sara</s>,' '<s>rasa</s>,' and the like is [indicated]. [261] 'A specific meaning'

children.translated_text: 'Following the course of inference' — the specific meaning-intention here should be understood as: this [person] has a specific purpose, because of possessing distinctive behavior — and so on as the form of inference. [264] 'Distinctly,' and so forth. Since even the first speaker knows [the matter] in a general form, 'distinctly' was stated. 'First' qualifies the action. And priority in speech means not being co-temporal with the destruction of speech that conveys one's own intended meaning — which amounts to otherness qualified by destruction. The qualification is through the dual relation of co-temporality with oneself and the capacity of the counter-positive speech to convey the intended meaning.

children.translated_text: Thus concludes the chapter on <s>Śabda</s> (Verbal Testimony) in the <s>Prakāśa</s> commentary named <s>Dīpikāprasaraṇa</s>.

The word '<s>pramāṇa</s>'

children.translated_text: here is the <s>lyuḍ</s>-ending [nominal derivative] in the sense of instrument. Alternatively, the meaning is: on account of the relevance whose nature is the non-conflict with the content of disregard (<s>upekṣā</s>) residing in the remembered [validity], as determined by that [<s>pramāṇa</s>]. And that nature, in the present context, is extrinsic apprehensibility (<s>paratogrāhyatva</s>). And the <s>smṛti</s> (recollection) arises through the relation of residing in the occurrence produced by oneself. Alternatively, <s>pramāṇa</s> means <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition); the meaning is: on account of the relevance in the form of the connection whose nature is residing in one's own occurrence, as determined by that [<s>pramā</s>]. The meaning of the ablative case is dependence on the desire to know (<s>jijñāsā</s>) produced by the cognition. [This] connects with 'establishment.' Accordingly, the ascertainment favorable to the operation favorable to the uninterrupted determination whose content is the extrinsic-apprehensibility-qualifier qualifying the <s>pramātva</s>-substratum, dependent on the desire to know produced by the cognition whose content is the relevance determined by the <s>pramāṇa</s> in the form of connection —

children.text:
1.
pramāṇanirūpitetyādi/ pramāṇanirūpitetyasya saṃgatāvanvayaḥ/ svaṃ
pramāṇaṃ tajjanyā pramā tadvṛtti pramātvaṃ taninaṣṭhatvaṃ paratogrāhyatve '
tathā ca yannirūpaṇānantaraṃ yannirūpyate tayoreva saṃgatirūpaḥ saṃbandhaḥ/
pramāṇanirūpaṇānantaraṃ pramātvasya paratogrāhyatvaṃ nirūpyata iti
pramāṇanirūpitā saṃgatiḥ paratogrāhyatve vaktavyā/ sā ca
svajanyavṛttiniṣṭhatvātmakaprasaṅgarūpeti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote] 1. 'Determined by the <s>pramāṇa</s>,' and so forth — the connection of 'determined by the <s>pramāṇa</s>' is with 'relevance.' 'Oneself' is the <s>pramāṇa</s>; the <s>pramā</s> produced by it; the <s>pramātva</s> (validity) residing in it; the residing-in-that-ness pertains to extrinsic apprehensibility. Accordingly, the relation in the form of relevance is that between what is determined after the determination of [one thing] and what is [then] determined. Since extrinsic apprehensibility of <s>pramātva</s> is determined after the determination of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the relevance determined by the <s>pramāṇa</s> must be stated with respect to extrinsic apprehensibility. And that relevance has the nature of connection in the form of the occurrence produced by oneself residing in [it]. This is the purport.

children.text:
2. tannirūpitetyādi/
tannirūpitā pramāṇanirūpitā, smṛtaṃ pramātvaṃ tanniṣṭhaṃ
upekṣaviṣayatāvirodhirūpaṃ paratogrāhyatvaṃ tadātmikā saṃgatiḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote] 2. 'Determined by that,' and so forth — 'determined by that' means determined by the <s>pramāṇa</s>. The remembered [entity] is <s>pramātva</s>; the extrinsic apprehensibility, whose nature is non-conflict with the content of disregard, resides in that; the relevance has that as its nature.

children.text:
3. svajanyetyādi/ svaṃ
pramāṇam, tajjanyā pramā tadvṛtti pramātvaṃ tanniṣṭhatvaṃ paratogrāhyatve/
children.translated_text: [Footnote] 3. 'Produced by oneself,' and so forth — 'oneself' is the <s>pramāṇa</s>; the <s>pramā</s> produced by it; the <s>pramātva</s> residing in it; the residing-in-that-ness pertains to extrinsic apprehensibility.

children.text:
4. tannirūpitetyādi/
tannirūpitā pramānirūpitā, saṃgatirityanvayaḥ/ svaṃ pramātadvṛtti
pramātvaṃ tanniṣṭhatvaṃ paratogrāhyatve/
children.translated_text: [Footnote] 4. 'Determined by that,' and so forth — 'determined by that' means determined by the <s>pramā</s>; the connection is with 'relevance.' 'Oneself' is the <s>pramā</s>; the <s>pramātva</s> residing in it; the residing-in-that-ness pertains to extrinsic apprehensibility.

children.text:
5. svaśabda iti/
svaśabdo 'tra svīyavācī san jñānagrāhakasāmagrīpara iti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote] 5. 'The word "<s>sva</s>"' — the word '<s>sva</s>' here, meaning 'one's own,' refers to the aggregate of conditions that apprehend cognition. This is the purport.

children.text:
śaṅkate - [268] kathamiti/ [268] tasyāḥ - vipratipatteḥ/ [268] atra
- vipratipattiniṣṭhavicāraprayojakatvaviṣaye [268] akṣatamiti vadantītyanvayaḥ/ [268] hi - yataḥ/ upapādayati---
[268] viruddhetyādi/ [268] kabaliteti/
children.translated_text: [The commentator] raises the objection — [268] 'How?' [268] 'Of that' — of the conflicting position (<s>vipratipatti</s>). [268] 'Here' — in the subject matter of the investigative purpose residing in the conflicting position. [268] 'Intact' — the syntactic connection is with 'they say.' [268] 'For' — because. [The author] substantiates — [268] 'Contradictory,' and so forth. [268] 'Swallowed up.'

children.text:
viṣayībhūtetyarthaḥ/
bodhaviśeṣaṇam/ [268] vicāra iti/ pravartaka iti śeṣaḥ/ [268] evaṃ ca - uktarītyā vicārapravṛttau ca/ [268] vicāropayogitvamiti/ vipratipatterityādiḥ/ atra
jñānaprāmāṇyamiti pakṣanirdeśaḥ/ ghaṭakatvaṃ saptamyarthaḥ jñānapadānvitam/
[239] tādṛśeti/ aprāmāṇyāgrāhakajñānagrāhakayāvatsāmagrījanyetyarthaḥ/
[269] atrauktamatatraye/ ghaṭakatvaṃ saptamyarthaḥ gurumatānvayi/ [269] taditi/ gurvityarthaḥ/ [269]
evaṃ ca uktarītyā vyavasthāpane ca/ nanu
tatprakārakabuddhau tadjñānasya kāraṇatvāt uktavyavasāyāt prāk
prāmāṇyānupasthiteḥ kathaṃ darśitavyavasāye prāmāṇyabhānasambhava ityata
āha --- [239] viśiṣṭeti/ [239] viśeṣaṇeti/
tadrūpetyādiḥ/ yāvaditi sāmagrīviśeṣaṇam/ ata evāgre
jñānagrāhakayāvadityuktam/ pramitikaraṇatvarūpaprāmāṇyasya paraiḥ
svatogrāhyatvānupagamena tatra vicārāsambhavādāha [268] vastutastviti/
children.translated_text: — the meaning is: that has become the object. This is a qualifier of cognition. [268] 'Investigation' — the supplement is: 'that prompts [activity].' [268] 'And thus' — and in the occurrence of investigation in the stated manner. [268] 'Being useful for investigation' — the supplement is: 'because of conflicting views.' Here, 'the validity of cognition' is the statement of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). 'Being-a-cause' is the seventh-case meaning, connected with the word 'cognition.' [239] 'Of that sort' — the meaning is: produced from whatever aggregate of causes is apprehended by cognition that does not apprehend invalidity. [269] 'In the three stated views.' 'Being-a-cause' is the seventh-case meaning, connected with the teacher's view. [269] 'That' — the meaning is: the teacher's. [269] 'And thus' — and in the establishment in the stated manner. Now, since in the cognition having that as its mode, the cognition of that [mode] is causal, and since prior to the stated judgment the validity has not been presented [to awareness], how is the appearance of validity possible in the demonstrated judgment? To this he says — [239] 'qualified' etc. [239] 'The qualifier' — the supplement is: 'having that form' etc. The word 'whatever' (<s>yāvat</s>) is a qualifier of the aggregate of causes. It is precisely for this reason that later he stated 'whatever apprehends cognition.' Since the validity in the form of being the instrument of valid cognition (<s>pramitikaraṇatva</s>) is not accepted by others as self-apprehensible (<s>svataḥgrāhya</s>), and hence investigation is not possible regarding it, he says [268] 'In truth, however.'

yattu - jñānapadena
pramitikaraṇatvavyāvṛttiḥ na sambhavati/ parāmarśādeḥ
pramitikaraṇatvāt ata āha - vastutastviti iti vyākhyānam -
tadasat/ jñānasyaiva prāmāṇyamityavadhāraṇavivakṣā

yāvajjñānavyaktīnāṃ durgahatvāt tanniveśo na sambhavatītyata
children.translated_text: Now, the interpretation that 'by the word "cognition," the exclusion of being the instrument of valid cognition is not possible, since the reflective judgment (<s>parāmarśa</s>) and the like also have the status of being the instrument of valid cognition, and therefore he says "in truth, however"' — that is incorrect. Because the exclusion [of that meaning] is possible through the emphatic intention expressed by the restriction 'of cognition alone is validity,' since the being-the-instrument-of-valid-cognition that is common to the senses and the like [can be excluded thereby]. Because by the maxim 'every sentence,' such meaning is obtainable from the words alone. Now, since the particular instances of cognition qualified [in the stated manner] are difficult to apprehend, their inclusion [in the definition] is not possible — to this

children.text:
āha - [268] taddharmeti/ yāvatpadasya
samabhivyāhṛtapadārthatāvacchedakavyāpakatvaparatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ [274] phalataḥ-- tātparyataḥ/ [268]
samānyataḥ
children.translated_text: he says — [268] 'that property' etc. The purport is: the word 'whatever' (<s>yāvat</s>) has the sense of pervading the delimiting property of the referent of the co-occurring word. [274] 'In effect' — the meaning is: in purport. [268] 'In general'

children.text:
sāmānyarūpeṇa/
taddharmaprakārakatvarūpajñānaviśeṣaṇāviśeṣitena jñānatveneti yāvat/
jñānānvayini vaiśiṣṭye tasil/ anyathā ghaṭatvādighaṭitaprāmāṇyasya
ghaṭatvādiprakārakajñānagrāhakagrāhyatvābhāvena vidhau bādhāpatteḥ/ idaṃ
jñānaṃ prameti
children.translated_text: — in a general form. The meaning is: by cognition-hood (<s>jñānatva</s>) that is not particularized by the qualifier of cognition in the form of having-that-property-as-mode. Otherwise, since the validity constituted by pot-hood and the like is not apprehensible by a cognition that apprehends cognition having pot-hood and the like as its mode, there would be the reductio of sublation of the rule. 'This cognition is valid' —

children.text:
jñānena
svātmakānuvyavasāyaniṣṭhaprāmāṇyagrahāt prāmāṇyāgrahāditi
dīpikāvākyamasaṅgatam ata āha - [274] vyavasāyaniṣṭhetyādiḥ/
sāmagryā eva prāmāṇyagrāhakatayā anuvyavasāyaniṣṭhaprāmāṇyagrāhikāyā
iti strīliṅganirdeśa eva kārya ityata āha - [274] sāmānya iti/ tathā ca liṅgaviśeṣāvivakṣāyāṃ
napuṃsakasyaiva nirdeṣṭavyatayā noktadoṣa iti bhāvaḥ/
tasyāprāmāṇyamiti ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣabhramavāraṇāya [274] saptamīti/ [274] yādṛśaprāmāṇyami tyādi/ atrāyaṃ niṣkarṣaḥ
--- taddharmaghaṭitaprāmāṇyaṃ kiñcidviśiṣṭamiti/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
tādātmyasvavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatvobhayasambandhena/
avacchedakatā
1svasamānādhikaraṇabhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatāsambandhena/
svādhikaraṇatā
svaviśiṣṭataddharmaprakārakajñānagrāhakasāmagrījanyatānatvasambandhena/
svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ svaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena/
children.translated_text: since by [that] cognition, the validity residing in one's own self-directed re-cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) is apprehended, the <s>Dīpikā</s> statement 'from non-apprehension of validity, from non-apprehension' is incongruous — to this he says [274] 'residing in the judgment' etc. Since only the aggregate of causes has the property of apprehending validity, and since the aggregate that apprehends validity residing in the re-cognition is [its cause], the feminine gender should be used — to this he says [274] 'in general' etc. And thus, when there is no intention of gender-specificity, since only the neuter gender should be used for reference, there is no stated defect — this is the purport. To prevent the erroneous reading of 'its invalidity' as a genitive-<s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound, [he says] [274] 'seventh [case].' [274] 'Of whatever sort the validity' etc. Here the conclusion is: the validity constituted by that property is something qualified. And the qualification is through both the relations of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and the counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood of the difference occurring in one's own <s>vṛtti</s> (occurrence). The delimitor-hood is through the relation of being qualified by a property pervaded by oneself. And the qualification is through the relation of the co-located difference-counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood being co-located with one's own substratum. And the self-substratum-hood is through the relation of the non-plurality-of-the-causality-of-being-generated-by-the-aggregate-that-apprehends-cognition-qualified-by-oneself-having-that-property-as-mode. And the self-qualification is through the relation of possessing difference whose counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood resides in oneself.

children.text:
1. atra sarvatra svaśabdaḥ
taddharmaghaṭitaprāmāṇyaparaḥ/ svaviśiṣṭetyasya jñānagrāhakasāmagryāmanvayaḥ/
svāśrayaniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitāprāmāṇyaniṣṭhaprakāratāśālijñānajanakatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasaṃbandhena
svaviśiṣṭā yā taddharmaprakārakajñānagrāhakasāmagrī
tajjanyajñānaniṣṭhabhedapratiyogitānirūpitā yā
children.translated_text: 1. Here, in all instances, the word 'self' (<s>sva</s>) refers to the validity constituted by that property. The expression 'qualified by oneself' is to be connected with the aggregate that apprehends cognition. The [validity] that is qualified through the relation of difference-possessing-ness — the difference whose counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood is the causality-relation delimited by the cognition-generating-ness consisting of the cognition having as its mode the invalidity with respect to the qualificand-hood residing in one's own substratum — [that validity] is qualified [thus], and the aggregate that apprehends cognition having that property as mode and that is generated by it — the difference-counter-positiveness determined by the cognition generated by that

children.text:
svanirūpitaviṣayitāsaṃbandhāvacchinnāvacchedakatā
tatsaṃbandhāvacchinnā yā svavṛttibhedapratiyogitāvacchedakatā tena
saṃbandhena tādātmyasaṃbandhena ca kiñcidviśiṣṭaṃ
taddharmaghaṭitaprāmāṇyamiti phalitam/ etatsamanvayaprakāraḥ
ittham---svaṃ ghaṭatvavati ghaṭatvaprakārakatvarūpaṃ pramātvaṃ tadāśrayaḥ/
ayaṃ ghaṭa iti pramā; tadviśeṣyakāprāmāṇyaprakārakajñānajanakatvaṃ athaṃ
ghaṭa iti jñānagrāhakasāmagryāṃ nāstīti sā sāmagrī
svāśrayetyāditādṛśajanakatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnasva (pramātva)
niṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavatī bhavati/
atastādṛśabhedavacvasaṃbandhena svaviśiṣṭā yā uktasāmagrī tajjanyo yat
jñānaṃ ghaṭajñānaviṣayakaṃ jñānaṃ tanniṣṭho yo bhedaḥ
svanirūpitaviṣayitāsaṃbandhena ghaṭatvaghaṭitapramātvavadbhedo na
bhavati, tena saṃbandhena tādṛśapramātvavattvāt; api tvanyabhedaḥ
tatpratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ ghaṭatvaghaṭitapramātve nāstīti
tādṛśāvacchedakatāsaṃbandhena pramātvavadbhedaḥ tādṛśapramātvaniṣṭhaḥ
tatpratiyogitāvacchedakatvaṃ ghaṭatvaghaṭitapramātve, tattādātmyaṃ ca
tatreti saṃbandhadvayopapattiriti/ paścāttaneṣvanugameṣvapyevamūhyam/
children.translated_text: — the delimitor-hood delimited by the content-relation (<s>viṣayitā</s>) determined by oneself and the difference-counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood occurring in one's own <s>vṛtti</s> — through both that relation and the identity relation, what is somewhat qualified is the validity constituted by that property — this is the result. The manner of application of this is as follows: 'self' is the validity in the form of <s>pramātva</s> (being-a-valid-cognition) possessing pot-hood; its substratum is the valid cognition 'this is a pot'; the cognition-generating-ness consisting of [the cognition] having as its mode the invalidity with respect to the qualificand of that — 'this is not a pot' — does not exist in the aggregate that apprehends cognition; hence that aggregate is possessed of difference whose counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood is delimited by such generating-ness-relation and resides in the self (<s>pramātva</s>). Therefore, through the relation of such-difference-possessing-ness, [the aggregate] is qualified by self, and the cognition generated by that stated aggregate — the cognition about pot-cognition — has a difference that, through the content-relation determined by oneself, is not a difference possessing <s>pramātva</s> constituted by pot-hood, because of its possessing such <s>pramātva</s> by the stated relation; rather, it is some other difference — the delimitor-hood of whose counter-positiveness does not exist in <s>pramātva</s> constituted by pot-hood. Through the relation of such delimitor-hood and through identity, the <s>pramātva</s> constituted by pot-hood is [indeed] qualified — this is the conclusion. In subsequent applications too, the reasoning should be understood similarly.

svāśrayaviśeṣyakāprāmāṇyaprakārakajñānajanakatāvacchedakatvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasaṃbandhena/

deśāntarīyakālāntarīyatattatkāraṇānāmasarvajñādurjñeyatvena

niruktakiñcidviśiṣṭatvaṃ na susādhamiti/ śaṅkate -- [274] nanviti/ aprasiddhimupapādayati -- [274] na hīti/ [264] ekam - ekajātīyam/ [274]
na janyata ityanvayaḥ/ atra ca
yāvantastādṛśāḥ dharmāḥ tadavacchinnotpādyajñānaviṣayatve sati
tadavacchinnotpādyajñānaviṣayatvamiti rītyā svatastvaṃ sādhyamiti
noktāprasiddhiriti/ śaṅkate -- [274] na ceti/
children.translated_text: The delimitor-hood is through the relation of cognition-generating-ness consisting of the cognition having as its mode the invalidity with respect to the qualificand-hood residing in one's own substratum. The difference-counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood is through the content-relation determined by oneself. Alternatively: being qualified by the content-relation. And the qualification is through both the relations of: the determiner-hood of oneself and the difference-counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood occurring in one's own <s>vṛtti</s>. And the delimitor-hood is through the relation of the co-located difference-counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood. And the self-substratum-hood is through the relation of [being the locus of] 'such-and-such a qualifier of self's substratum' etc. — as before. And here, in the view of the 'whatever' (<s>yāvat</s>) qualification of the aggregate, the somewhat-qualified-ness is the rough application. The qualification is through both the relations of identity and being the object of cognition qualified by oneself. And the self-qualification is through the relation of difference-possessing-ness whose counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood is delimited by the co-located-difference-counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood-relation. And the self-substratum-hood is through the relation of the apprehension-delimiting-collectively-occurring property of the cognition qualified by oneself. And the self-qualification is through the relation of difference-possessing-ness whose counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood is delimited by the cognition-generating-ness consisting of the cognition having as its mode the invalidity with respect to the qualificand of one's own substratum. The difference-counter-positiveness-delimitor-hood is through the relation of the delimitor-hood of one's own production-delimiting-ness. Therefore, since the infinitely many particular causes belonging to other places and other times — each such cause — are unknowable by the non-omniscient, even though the inclusion of each such [cause] in the definition of self-validity is difficult to construct, there is no harm. And thus, in the teacher's (<s>gurūṇām</s>) view, the aggregate-causality of judgment and the like is: this cognition is mutually of a different kind — such stated somewhat-qualified-ness is not easy to establish — he raises the objection [274] 'now' etc. He establishes the non-establishment — [274] 'for indeed' etc. [264] 'One' — of one kind. [274] 'Is not produced' — this is the syntactic connection. And here, the self-validity is to be established in the manner of: 'the property of being the object of cognition delimited by however many such properties there are, while being the object of cognition produced [from them]' — hence the stated non-establishment [does not arise]. He raises the objection — [274] 'nor should it be said' etc.

children.translated_text: For the purpose is the prevention of the aggregate that grasps invalidity, and that cannot be accomplished without the entry of the 'as-many-as' (<s>yāvattva</s>) [qualifier] into the aggregate. Because the intrinsic nature of validity is easily established by taking the aggregate that grasps validity. But when that qualifier is present, since the aggregate grasping invalidity too would be included within such an 'as-many-as' [aggregate], validity would not be graspable by it, and hence there would be sublation — thus the existence of the qualifier of 'as-many-as-ness' serves to justify the 'up to non-grasper' [clause]. [273] 'First' — before the statement of the purpose of the 'up to non-grasper' [clause]. He establishes the proving-what-is-already-proved that is to be prevented by the qualifier of 'as-many-as-ness' entering the aggregate — [273] '<s>Naiyāyikas</s>' etc. Although on the positive side the qualifier of 'as-many-as-ness' could serve to prevent proving-what-is-already-proved, on the negative side that is not possible. Nevertheless, on the negative side the result of preventing sublation does obtain — so he says: [274] '<s>Naiyāyikas</s>' etc. [274] By 'through a sentence' and the like, the referent of the expression 'through inference and the like' is stated. [273] In 'since validity is not grasped by the cognition "this cognition is not a valid means,"' the meaning as literally obtained is: because of the absence of the grasping of validity occasioned by such a cognition. But that is not relevant to the matter at hand, since it is sublation that needs to be stated in the present context. Therefore, to give the meaning of 'because of not making validity its object,' he says: [274] 'of validity' and so forth. [274] 'Of that kind' — the meaning is: having the form 'this cognition is not a valid means.' [274] 'By that' — by the said aggregate of cognition. [274] 'Qualified' — the meaning is: delimited. Although in the cognition 'this cognition is not a valid means,' validity is an object through the relation of counter-positiveness, nevertheless, the being-intrinsically-graspable means the objecthood delimited by the relation of counter-positiveness belonging to the grasping generated by the aggregate that grasps cognition; alternatively, what is intended is the pervadedness through the relation of being the qualifier-hood residing in oneself, determined by the qualificand-hood residing in one's own locus — hence there is no incoherence. [280] 'Is grasped intrinsically indeed' — this should be considered here: the particle <s>eva</s> (indeed) here, by construal after 'is grasped,' means 'is grasped indeed.' And accordingly, this <s>eva</s> particle is associated with the verb, like 'a blue lotus exists indeed.' Hence the statement that it too has a purpose through [expressing] 'no contradiction' is unwarranted. This should be understood here: when the 'as-many-as' [qualifier] enters the aggregate, being qualified by cognition is the subtle tracking. The qualification is through both the relations of objecthood and being the delimitor of counter-positiveness of difference residing in oneself. The delimitor-hood is through the relation of the delimitor of counter-positiveness of difference co-located with oneself. The locus-hood of oneself and the like is as before. [274] 'Specifically' — through being the composite of the respective causes. Similarly later too. In 'of such a nature' — the subtle tracking is that when the 'as-many-as' [qualifier] enters cognition, it is qualified by difference. The qualification is through both the relations of the delimitor of counter-positiveness residing in oneself and being one's own locus. The delimitor-hood is delimited by the relation of being the delimitor of counter-positiveness of difference co-located with oneself. The locus-hood of oneself is through the relation of being the grasping generated by the aggregate that grasps the cognition qualified by oneself. The self-qualification is through the relation of possessing difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor-hood residing in oneself, delimited by the relation of being the cause of a cognition having invalidity as qualifier with respect to the qualificand residing in one's own locus. The delimitor of the counter-positiveness of difference is through the relation of the objecthood determined by oneself. [274] By 'in summary,' everything stated in the depth of the doctrine of validity is intended.

children.text:
nanu
tadvadviśeṣyakatvāvacchinnatatprakārakatvaṃ hi tatpramātvam/ tatkathaṃ
purovartinītyādidīpikāvākyasaṅgatirityata āha - [280] purovartinīti/ nanu purovartini
prakārasambandhabhānavyavasthāpanamātreṇa kathaṃ
viśiṣṭaprāmāṇyabhānasiddhiranuvyavasāyādāvityata āha - [280] naiyāyikā apīti/ nanu viśiṣṭabuddhau viśeṣaṇajñānasya
hetutvāt kathamanuvyavasāye prāganupasthitaviśeṣyatvādibhānamityata
āha - [281] anupasthitayorapīti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ -
viśeṣaṇajñānasya hetutvaṃ viśeṣaṇabhedena bhinnabhinnamiti
phalānurodhena prakṛte na tādṛśakāraṇatvakalpanamiti/
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>pramātva</s> (validity) of a cognition is the property of having that [object] as qualifier, delimited by having that as qualificand. Then how is the statement of the <s>Dīpikā</s> beginning with 'in what is present before one' coherent? To this he says: [280] 'In what is present before one' etc. But how is the cognition of qualified validity established merely by establishing the appearance of the relation of the qualifier in what is present before one, without the subsequent apperception (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) and the like? To this he says: [280] '<s>Naiyāyikas</s> too' etc. But since the cognition of the qualifier is a cause of the qualified cognition, how can the appearance of qualificand-hood and the like, which were not previously presented, occur in the apperception? To this he says: [281] 'Even of the non-presented' etc. The purport is: since the causality of the cognition of the qualifier differs with respect to different qualifiers, in conformity with the result, such causality need not be postulated in the present case.

children.text:
nanu
vyavasāyajñātatāliṅgakānumitibhyāṃ prāmāṇyagrahaṇasya
gurubhaṭṭābhyāmupapagamāt [242]
anuvyavasāyenetyuktiḥ dīpikāyāṃ
kathamityāśaṅkya tasya miśramatābhiprāyakatāmāha - (idaṃ ceti/)
tannirasanaprakāro bodhya iti/ na ca tathāsati ghaṭaṃ jānāmītayādau
ghaṭādeḥ jñānādikriyākarmatānupapattiḥ kriyājanyaphalaśālitāyā eva
karmatārūpatvāditi, tatra dvitīyānupapattiriti vācyam/
tādṛśaphalaśālitvasya mukhyakarmatārūpatayā grāmaṃ gacchatītyādāveva
grāmādau tadupagamāt/ ghaṭaṃ jānātītyādiṣu tadanabhyupagamāt
viṣayatālakṣaṇagauṇakarmatāyā eva tatra svīkaraṇāt/ anyathā
'ghaṭamicchati' ghaṭaṃ dveṣṭī'tyādau
iṣṭatvādirūpapadārthāntarakalpanāpātāt iti/
children.translated_text: But since it is conceded by both <s>Guru</s> [i.e. <s>Udayana</s>] and <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> that validity is grasped through inference based on the mark of what is known through the primary cognition (<s>vyavasāya</s>), how can the <s>Dīpikā</s>'s statement [242] 'through apperception' be [justified]? — anticipating this doubt, he states that it reflects the view of <s>Miśra</s> [i.e. <s>Vācaspati</s>] — 'And this' etc. The manner of its refutation should be understood. Nor should it be said that if so, in 'I know the pot' and the like, there would be the impossibility of the pot and the like having the grammatical object-hood of the action of knowing, because object-hood has the nature of possessing the result produced by the action — and hence there would be the impossibility of the accusative case. For such possession of the result is the primary object-hood, which is acknowledged only in 'goes to the village' and the like, with respect to the village; in 'knows the pot' and the like, it is not acknowledged — rather the secondary object-hood characterized by the relation of objecthood is alone accepted there. Otherwise, in 'desires the pot,' 'hates the pot,' and the like, there would be the unwanted consequence of having to postulate a separate category such as desiredness and so forth.

children.text:
saṅkṣepa iti/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ -
agṛhītāprāmāṇyakatvamaprāmāṇyajñānānāskanditatvam,
children.translated_text: 'In summary' etc. — the purport is: not having its invalidity grasped means not being assailed by the cognition of invalidity.

children.text:
taccāprāmāṇyaprakāratānirūpitaviśeṣyatvasāmānādhikaraṇyobhayasambandhāvacchinnajñānatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākābhāvaḥ/
evaṃ bhramatvajñānābhāvapramātvagrahābhāvāvapi niveśyau/
evamaprāmāṇyajñāne aprāmāṇyajñānaṃ yatrotpannam tatra pravṛttyupapattaye
children.translated_text: And that [not being assailed] is the absence whose counter-positiveness is delimited by cognition-hood, delimited by both the relations of co-location with the qualificand-hood determined by the qualifier-hood of invalidity. Similarly, the absence of the cognition of erroneousness and the absence of the grasping of validity should also be included. And thus, regarding the cognition of invalidity — for the justification of activity in the locus where the cognition of invalidity has arisen,

children.text:
aprāmāṇyajñānadharmikāprāmāṇyajñānatvena pṛthakkāraṇatvaṃ
kalpanīyam/ adhikaṃ prāmāṇyavādādau draṣṭavyamiti/ [283] prāmāṇyavyavasthāpakahetoḥ saphalapravṛttijanakatvarūpetyādiḥ/
prāmāṇye parato grāhyatvasya mīmāṃsakairapyupagamāt
siddhasādhanamāśaṅkya evakārapūraṇena vyācaṣṭe - [282] prāmāṇyasyānumānādita eveti/ [282] etena - anuvyavasāyādau
prāmāṇyabhānāsambhavasthāpanena/ [282]
vyabhicāra iti/ vyatireketyādiḥ/
children.translated_text: a separate causality through the property of being-a-cognition-of-invalidity belonging to the substratum of the cognition of invalidity must be postulated. More should be seen in the doctrine of validity and elsewhere. [283] The statement beginning with 'the cause that establishes validity has the nature of generating activity that produces results' and so forth. Anticipating the objection of proving-what-is-already-proved, since the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> too accept that validity is grasped extrinsically, he explains by completing the force of the particle <s>eva</s>: [282] 'the validity [is grasped] from inference and the like alone' etc. [282] 'By this' — by establishing the impossibility of the appearance of validity in the apperception and the like. [282] 'Deviation' etc. — [the fuller expression is:] 'in the negative concomitance' and so forth.

children.text:
evaṃ jñaptāvityādi
uktaprakārābhinnajñaptidharmikaparatastvavyavasthāpakadhvaṃsaviśiṣṭaḥ
utpattidharmikaparatastvaprakārakajñānānukūlaśabdaḥ tatkartetyanvayabodhaḥ/
[287] mātreti/ mātrapadamatrakārtsnyaparam/ [287] vyudāsa iti jñānatvādīnāmatathātvāditi bhāvaḥ/ nanu
pramāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvaṃ
pramāniṣṭhakāryatvātiriktadharmāvacchinnakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvam/
evaṃ ca kālādivāraṇe 'pi ātmādivāraṇamaśakyamata āha - [287] pramātvādhiketyādi/
pramātvaviśiṣṭakāryatānirūpitakāraṇatvamiti niṣkarṣaḥ/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
1svādhikaraṇavṛttitvasvaviśiṣṭadharmāvacchinnatvobhayasaṃbandhena/
children.translated_text: 'Thus in cognition' and so forth — the verbal understanding is: the word that is conducive to the cognition having extrinsic-ness as its qualifier, with the property of the locus of origination as its substratum, qualified by the destruction that establishes extrinsic-ness of cognition of the same kind as stated, [means] 'that is its maker' — this is the positive concomitance understood. [287] 'Only' (<s>mātra</s>) — the word <s>mātra</s> here means completeness. [287] 'Exclusion' — the purport is: because cognition-hood and the like are not of that nature. Now, the causality unique to valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) is the causality that determines effect-hood delimited by a property other than the effect-hood residing in valid cognition. And accordingly, even when time and the like are excluded, the self and the like cannot be excluded. To this he says: [287] 'In addition to validity' and so forth. The conclusion is: the causality that determines effect-hood qualified by validity. The qualification is through both the relations of occurring in one's own locus and being delimited by a property qualified by oneself.

children.text:
1. svādhikaraṇetyādi/
svādhikaraṇavṛttitva -
svādhikaraṇavṛttitvasvābhāvādhikaraṇavṛttitvobhayasaṃbandhāvacchinnasvan iṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavaddharmāvacchinnatvobhayasambandhena
pramātvaviśiṣṭā yā kāryatā tannirūpitakāraṇatvaṃ
pramāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvamityarthaḥ/ svaṃ pramātvaṃ tadadhikaraṇaṃ pramā
tanniṣṭhatvaṃ kāryatāyām, evaṃ svaṃ pramātvaṃ tadadhikaraṇaṃ
pramātadvṛttitvaṃ jñānatve svaṃ pramātvaṃ tadabhāvādhikaraṇabhramavṛttitvaṃ ca
jñānatve iti jñānatvaṃ
svādhikaraṇavṛttitvasvābhāvādhikaraṇavṛttitvobhayasambandhena
pramātvavat, pramātvaṃ tu na tathā tasya
pramātvābhāvādhikaraṇavṛttitvābhāvāt, ataḥ
tādṛśobhayasambandhāvacchinnapramātvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavat
pramātvaṃ tadavacchinnatvaṃ ca pramāniṣṭhakāryatāyāmiti ubhayasambandhena
pramātvaviśiṣṭā kāryatā bhavatīti samanvayo jñeyaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. 'One's own locus' and so forth — the meaning is: the causality that determines effect-hood qualified by <s>pramātva</s> (validity), which is qualified through both the relations of occurring in one's own locus, and being the property delimited by both the relations of occurring in one's own locus and occurring in the locus of one's own absence — [specifically,] possessing difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor-hood residing in oneself, delimited by the said double relation — this is the causality unique to valid cognition. 'Self' is <s>pramātva</s> (validity); its locus is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>); its residing-in [applies to] effect-hood. Similarly, 'self' is validity, its locus is valid cognition, and the occurring of that [validity] in cognition-hood; 'self' is validity, and the occurring of the absence-of-that in erroneous cognition — [this also applies] to cognition-hood. Thus cognition-hood possesses validity through both the relations of occurring-in-one's-locus and occurring-in-the-locus-of-one's-absence; but validity itself is not so, because of the absence of occurring-in-the-locus-of-the-absence-of-validity. Therefore, validity possesses difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor-hood residing in itself, delimited by the said double relation; and being delimited by that — [these] belong to the effect-hood residing in valid cognition. Thus, effect-hood qualified by validity through the double relation — this construction should be understood.

children.text:
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
svaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena/ avacchedakatā
svādhikaraṇavṛttitvasvābhāvādhikaraṇavṛttitvobhayasambandhena/
kāryatāyāṃ pramāniṣṭhaniveśaphalamāha - [287] bhrameti/ [287] ityādāvityādinā vaṃśoragabhramādisaṅgrahaḥ/ [287] pittādītyādinā maṇḍūkavasañjanādigrahaṇam/
children.translated_text: The qualification is through the relation of possessing difference whose counter-positiveness has the delimitor-hood residing in oneself. The delimitor-hood is through both the relations of occurring in one's own locus and occurring in the locus of one's own absence. He states the result of stipulating 'residing in valid cognition' in the effect-hood: [287] 'erroneous cognition' etc. [287] By the expression 'and the like in such cases,' the inclusion of erroneous cognitions such as [mistaking] a bamboo for a snake and so forth is made. [287] By 'bile and the like,' the inclusion of frog-born jaundice and the like is intended.

children.text:
visaṃvādoti/ tadabhāvavati
tatprakāraketyarthaḥ/ bodhyeti/ etena dharmiṇo 'prasiddhyā
niṣodho 'nupapanna iti śaṅkā nirastā/
children.translated_text: 'Discordance' — the meaning is: having that [object] as qualifier in what possesses the absence of that. 'Should be understood' — by this, the doubt that the refutation is impossible due to the non-establishment of the property-bearer is dispelled.

children.text:
kḷptaniyateti/ etena
kalpanāsāmyaśaṅkānirāsaḥ/ nanu iṣṭabhedāgrahamātrasya
kāraṇatvopapattau iṣṭe svatantropasthitatvaviśeṣaṇaṃ vyarthamityata
āha -- [289] etāvateti/ nanu
iṣṭabhedāgrahasyaivetyevakārāsaṅgatiḥ/
smṛterapyapekṣitatvenetaravyavacchedasya tenāśakyatvādityata āha ---
[289] evakāreṇeti/ [289] lāghavāditi/ anyathā tadvati
tatprakārakatvasyādhikasya niveśe kāryatāvacchedakagauravāditi bhāvaḥ/
[289] sāmānyaḥ-- sāmānyarūpeṇa/ abhedaḥ pratyayārthaḥ vṛttitvānvayī/
children.translated_text: 'Established and invariable' etc. — by this, the doubt of parity of postulation is dispelled. But if the mere non-grasping of the desired distinction suffices as a cause, then the qualifier 'independently presented' in what is desired would be otiose. To this he says: [289] 'This much alone' etc. But the particle <s>eva</s> (alone) in 'of the non-grasping of the desired distinction alone' would be incoherent, since recollection too is required, and the exclusion of the other cannot be achieved by it. To this he says: [289] 'By the particle <s>eva</s>' etc. [289] 'Because of economy' — otherwise, if the additional [condition of] having-that-as-qualifier-in-what-possesses-that were stipulated, there would be heaviness in the delimitor of effect-hood. This is the purport. [289] 'General' — in a general manner. 'Non-difference' is the meaning of the suffix; it is positively concomitant with occurrence.

children.text: ayathārthānubhavanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of erroneous experience (<s>ayathārthānubhava</s>)

children.text:
pradeśaviśeṣetyādi/ pradeśaviśeṣaḥ
nidrānāḍīviśeṣaḥ/ tatrāvasthitaṃ yanmanaḥ tena ātmanaḥ saṃyoga
ityarthaḥ/ [292] tadasamavāyikāraṇaketyādi/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ ---
svapnaśabdasya jñānaviśeṣa eva lakṣaṇā tadasaptavāyikāraṇaketyanena
śakyasambandhassūcita iti/ [292]
bhāktaḥ lākṣaṇikaḥ/ [292] tatbhāṣyaviru'miti/ ananubhūtārthaviṣayakasya svāpnajñānasya
darśanāt/ smṛteścātathātvāditi bhāvaḥ/ nanu paṭatvavāniti
jñānavāraṇamapi nānātvaniveśaprayojanaṃ saṃbhavatīti
ghaṭatvaviruddhapaṭatvāniti jñānaparyantānughāvanaṃ viphalamityāśaṅkyāha
- [292] koṭyoriti/ nanu ghaṭatvaviruddhapaṭatvavāniti jñāne 'pi
ghaṭatvapaṭatvarūpanānādharmaprakārakatvasattvāt kathaṃ tadvāraṇamiti,
tatrāha - [293] ekadharmiketi/ ayaṃ bhāvaḥ -
1prakāratāviśiṣṭajñānatvaṃ saṃśayatvam/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'In a particular region' and so forth — the particular region is a particular channel of sleep. The meaning is: the conjunction of the mind that is situated there with the self. [292] 'Having that as its non-inherence cause' and so forth — the purport is: the word <s>svapna</s> (dream) has <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) for a particular cognition, and by 'having that as its non-inherence cause,' the denotative relation is indicated. [292] 'Figurative' — meaning: by secondary signification. [292] 'Contradicted by that commentary' — because dream-cognition is observed to have as its content objects not [previously] experienced. And because recollection is not of that nature — this is the purport. Now, the prevention of cognitions like 'possessing cloth-ness' could also be a purpose for the stipulation of plurality — hence the pursuit up to the cognition 'possessing cloth-ness which is contradictory to pot-ness' would be fruitless. Anticipating this, he says: [292] 'Of the two alternatives' etc. But even in the cognition 'possessing cloth-ness contradictory to pot-ness,' since the property of having multiple properties — pot-ness and cloth-ness — as qualifiers obtains, how is that prevented? To this he says: [293] 'Having a single property-bearer' etc. The purport is: cognition-hood qualified by qualifier-hood is <s>saṃśayatva</s> (doubt-hood). The qualification is

children.text:
svanirūpakatvasvāvacchinnaviṣayatānirūpitavirodhaviṣayatānirūpitaviṣayatvāvacchinnatvasvanirūpitaviśeṣyatāsamānādhikaraṇaviśeṣyatānirūpitatvobhayasambandhena
svaviśiṣṭaprakāratānirūpakatvobhayasaṃbandhane/ evamapi parvato
vahnimān dravyaṃ
children.translated_text: through both the relations of the objecthood delimited by the determiner-hood of oneself, and the objecthood delimited by the opposition-objecthood determined by the objecthood delimited by oneself, [being] co-located with the qualificand-hood determined by the qualifier-hood qualified by the determiner-hood of oneself — and through both the relations of being the determiner of the qualifier-hood qualified by oneself. Even so, 'the mountain has fire, [and is] a substance'

children.text:
vahniviruddhajanavat/
iti jñāne ativyāptirdurvāraiveti śaṅkate -- [293] na
ceti/ [293] ekadharmāvacchinnetyādi/ ayamāśayaḥ --
svanirūpitaviśeṣyatāsamānādhikaraṇatvasthale
svanirūpitāviśeṣyatāvacchedakāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitatvaṃ
niveśya 2anyat pūrvavat bodhyamiti/ [293] digiti/
children.translated_text: like the generation of what is opposed to fire — he raises the objection that the over-pervasion in cognition is indeed unavoidable: [293] 'Not so.' [293] 'Delimited by one property' and so forth. The purport is this: by introducing, in the locus of co-location with the qualificand-ness determined by itself, the property of being determined by the qualificand-ness delimited by the delimitor of the qualificand-ness determined by itself, the rest is to be understood as before. [293] 'The direction' and so forth.

children.text:
1.
prakāratāviśiṣṭetyādi/ parvato vahnimān na veti saṃśaye vahniḥ
tadabhāvaśca prakāraḥ/ vahnitadabhāvayorvirodhaḥ saṃsargatayā bhāsate/
vahniniṣṭhaprakāratānirūpitā parvataniṣṭhā viśeṣyatā anyā,
vahnyabhāvaniṣṭhaprakāratanirūpitā pavataniṣṭhā viśeṣyatā anyā, iti
sthitiḥ/ etāṃ manasikṛtya anugamasya samanvayo jñeyaḥ/ tathā hi - svaṃ
vahniniṣṭhaprakāratā tannirūpakatvaṃ uktasaṃśayātmakajñāne, evaṃ svaṃ
vahniniṣṭhaprakāratā tadavacchinnā yā vahniniṣṭhā viṣayatā
(virodhaniṣṭhaviṣayatānirūpitaviṣayatā) tannirūpitāyā
virodhaniṣṭhā viṣayatā tannirūpitaviṣayatā vahnyabhāvaniṣṭhaviṣayatā
tadavacchinnatvaṃ vahnyabhāvaniṣṭhaprakāratāyāṃ svaṃ vahniniṣṭhaprakāratā
tannirūpitā yā parvataniṣṭhā viśeṣyatā tatsamānādhikaraṇā yā
viśeṣyatā parvataniṣṭhāṃ vahnyabhāvaprakāratā nirūpitā viśeṣyatā
tannirūpitatvaṃ ca vahnyabhāvaniṣṭhaprakāratāyāmiti ubhayasaṃbandhena
vahniniṣṭhaprakāratāviśiṣṭhā yā prakāratā vahnayabhāvaniṣṭhā
tannirūpakatvaṃ ca parvato vahnimānna veti saṃśaye 'stīti/ atra
vahniniṣṭhā virodhaniṣṭhasaṃsargatākhyaviṣayatānirūpitā viṣayatā
parvataniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirūpitayā vahniniṣṭhaprakāratā avacchidyate,
vahnyabhāvaniṣṭhā yā parvataniṣṭhaviśeṣyatānirupitaprakāratā sa
virodhaniṣḍaṭhaviṣayatānirupitavahnyabhāvaniṣṭhaviṣayatayā avacchidyate,
antarābhāsamānapadārthaniṣṭhaviṣayatayoravacchedyāvacchedakabhāva iti
iti siddhantādityapi dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: 1. 'Qualified by qualifier-ness (<s>prakāratā</s>)' and so forth. In the doubt 'does the mountain possess fire or not?' fire and its absence are the qualifiers (<s>prakāra</s>). The opposition (<s>virodha</s>) between fire and its absence appears as a relation (<s>saṃsarga</s>). The qualificand-ness (<s>viśeṣyatā</s>) residing in the mountain and determined by the qualifier-ness residing in fire is one thing; the qualificand-ness residing in the mountain and determined by the qualifier-ness residing in the absence of fire is another — this is the position. Keeping this in mind, the agreement of the definition should be understood. That is to say: 'itself' is the qualifier-ness residing in fire; its being a determiner is in the cognition that is the aforementioned doubt. Similarly, 'itself' is the qualifier-ness residing in fire; the object-ness (<s>viṣayatā</s>) residing in fire that is delimited by it (i.e. the object-ness determined by the object-ness residing in opposition) — the object-ness residing in opposition that is determined by it — the object-ness residing in the absence of fire — the property of being delimited by that belongs to the qualifier-ness residing in the absence of fire. 'Itself' being the qualifier-ness residing in fire, the qualificand-ness residing in the mountain that is determined by it, and the qualificand-ness that is co-located with it — namely the qualificand-ness residing in the mountain determined by the qualifier-ness of the absence of fire — the property of being determined by that also belongs to the qualifier-ness residing in the absence of fire. Thus, by both relations, the qualifier-ness residing in the absence of fire that is qualified by the qualifier-ness residing in fire, and the property of being its determiner, exist in the doubt 'does the mountain possess fire or not?' Here, the object-ness residing in fire, determined by the object-ness called relation-ness (<s>saṃsargatā</s>) residing in opposition, is delimited by the qualifier-ness residing in fire as determined by the qualificand-ness residing in the mountain; and the qualifier-ness residing in the absence of fire as determined by the qualificand-ness residing in the mountain is delimited by the object-ness residing in the absence of fire as determined by the object-ness residing in opposition. That the object-nesses residing in the entities appearing within [the cognition] stand in the relation of delimited and delimitor — this too should be noted from the established doctrine.

children.text:
2. anyat pūrvavaditi/

children.translated_text: 2. 'The rest as before.' And thus, <s>saṃśayatva</s> (doubt-ness) is the property of being a cognition qualified by qualifier-ness. The qualification is [constituted] by the triple relation of: being a determiner of itself, being delimited by the object-ness of opposition determined by the object-ness delimited by the delimitor of itself, [and] being determined by the qualificand-ness delimited by the delimitor of the qualificand-ness determined by itself — by both relations of being a determiner of the qualifier-ness qualified by itself. This is the purport.

children.text:
ayaṃ bhāvaḥ- yadyapi
pratyekaṃ dharmaṃyorekatvamasti tathāpi
1svāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitatanniṣṭhaprakāratākatvasvāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitatadabhāvaniṣṭhaprakāratākatvobhayasambandhena

saṃśayatvam/ dvitīye vaiśiṣṭyaṃ

ato na doṣa iti/ [293] tantrāntare - advaitaśāstre/ [293] tatprakārakatvetyādi ityādināṃ
tadabhāvavanniṣṭhaviśeṣyatāniyapitatanniṣṭhaprakāratākatvaparigrahaḥ/ [293] saṅkṣepa iti/ ayamāśayaḥ -- yadyapi idaṃ rajatam bhūtalaṃ
