saṃśayānyatvaniveśāt na doṣaḥ/ tadaṃśe saṃśayatvaṃ caikasmin
dharmiṇi tattadabhāvobhayaprakāratakatvamiti/ [293] śākhādāvityādi/
idamupalakṣaṇam - puruṣatvaniścayasyāhāryatvopapattaye
puruṣatvaniścayo jāyatāmitīcchāyā vācyatvāt/ anyathā
bādhakālīlanecchājanyajñānatvalakṣaṇasyāhāryatvasya tatrāsambhavāt/
jñānecchayoḥ yugapadutpādamate tādṛśabhramadaśāyāmeva
icchādisambhavāditi dhyeyam/ [293] upayogitvam
prayojakatvam/ [298] vedanīyamityādi ityādinā
pratikūlatayā vedanīyaṃ duḥkhamityasya saṅgrahaḥ/ [298] sukhādītyādinā duḥkhaparigrahaḥ/ [298] avyāpteriti/
idamupalakṣaṇam/ asādhūnāṃ paradravyopabhogādijanyanarakādidukhe
dveṣādarśanāt avyāpterityapi
children.translated_text: The purport is this: although there is unity with respect to each property individually, <s>saṃśayatva</s> (doubt-ness) is the property of being a cognition qualified by a property, by the double relation of: being a producer of qualifier-ness of that [entity] as determined by qualificand-ness delimited by itself, and being a producer of qualifier-ness of the absence of that as determined by qualificand-ness delimited by itself. Or alternatively, doubt-ness is the property of being a cognition possessing qualifier-ness qualified by qualifier-ness. In the second [formulation], the qualification is by the triple relation of: being determined by the qualificand-ness delimited by the delimitor of the qualificand-ness determined by itself, being determined by the object-ness of opposition determined by the object-ness delimited by the delimitor of itself, and being delimited by the non-delimitor of itself. Therefore there is no defect. [293] 'In another system' — in the <s>Advaita</s> school. [293] 'By being a qualifier of that' and so forth — by these words, the inclusion of the qualifier-ness of the absence of that, as determined by the qualificand-ness residing in the possessor of its absence, is accepted. [293] 'In brief' — the purport is this: although in partial doubt such as 'this is silver,' 'the ground possesses a pot or not,' there is over-pervasion, nevertheless, by introducing 'being other than doubt' with respect to that portion, there is no defect. Doubt-ness with respect to that portion is the property of having both the entity and its absence as qualifiers in one substratum. [293] 'In a branch and so forth.' This is illustrative — because it must be stated that the desire 'let the ascertainment of person-ness arise' is required for the possibility of the ascertainment of person-ness being <s>āhārya</s> (deliberately produced). Otherwise, <s>āhārya</s>-ness, defined as being a cognition produced by a desire not [arising from] sublating reasoning, would not be possible there. On the view that cognition and desire arise simultaneously, it should be noted that in such a state of erroneous cognition, desire and the like are possible. [293] 'Usefulness' means being an instrumental cause. [298] 'To be experienced' and so forth — by these words, 'pain is what is experienced as unfavorable' is included. [298] 'Pleasure and so forth' — by these words, pain is included. [298] 'Because of under-pervasion' — this is illustrative. Because aversion is not observed in the case of pain such as hell and the like produced by the enjoyment of others' wealth by the wicked, there is also under-pervasion.

'Itself' is mountain-ness; the property of being a determiner of the qualifier-ness residing in fire as determined by the qualificand-ness delimited by it is in the doubt 'does the mountain possess fire or not?' Similarly, 'itself' is mountain-ness; the property of being a determiner of the qualifier-ness residing in the absence of fire as determined by the qualificand-ness delimited by it is also in such a doubt — this is the agreement.

children.translated_text: 2. 'Determined by itself' and so forth. Similarly, 'itself' is the qualifier-ness residing in fire; the delimitor of it is fire-ness;

Similarly, 'itself' is the qualifier-ness residing in fire; what is not its delimitor is absence-of-fire-ness; the property of being delimited by it also belongs to the qualifier-ness residing in the absence of fire — the property of possessing that is the property of being a cognition that constitutes doubt. This is the agreement.

children.translated_text: He states the purpose of the word 'produced by experience (<s>anubhava</s>)' — in the <s>Dīpikā</s> [299] 'In the self and so forth.' Now, if merely the introduction of 'produced-ness' suffices to exclude the self and the like, then the component 'by experience' would be futile — in response to this doubt, it is stated: 'And so forth.' By the word 'and so forth,' the inclusion of the connection of self and mind is accepted. Experience-ness (<s>anubhavatva</s>) means being a cognition other than memory. And thus, since the introduction of 'being other than memory' in the body of the delimitor of causal-ness involves complexity, while causal-ness through mere cognition-ness involves simplicity — in response to the doubt [about which is preferable], he says in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [300] 'Of experience-ness also.' [300] 'As a universal (<s>jāti</s>).' The evidence for that is the reflective cognition 'I experience' itself; it should be noted that the reflective cognition 'I know' is [evidence] for cognition-ness. [300] 'Because of being a determiner of otherwise-establishment.' The meaning is: because of being the counter-positive of the respective property-differences. Otherwise, the acceptance of causal-ness of memories that are entirely non-causal would involve the defect of complexity. This is the purport. [300] 'Produced by itself' — 'itself' is the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). The same applies hereafter. To prevent the doubt that memory arises again through another experience: [300] 'Once' and so forth. [300] 'Final' — finality here, resolved through the triple relation of: not being simultaneous with the prior absence of a memory having the same object and produced by the impression that produced itself, being simultaneous with its own prior absence, being produced by the impression that produced itself, and having the same object as itself — amounts to being other than memory qualified [by these conditions]. [300] 'Not [yet] in the future, as an instance of that' — here this should be considered: if the property of being a final memory with respect to that object is accepted as a cause, through the relation of inherence, for the destruction of the impression having that object, through the relation of essential nature, there is no sublating cognition. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of indeterminacy by taking into account the conjunction with the life-force and the like that are simultaneous with it. [300] 'Of the impression, by being what destroys the result' — by this, the doubt that memory after memory is possible through the operation in the form of the impression produced by the earlier experience itself is refuted. Because the operation in the form of the impression is destroyed at that time, and hence the earlier experience cannot [cause] memory at the stage of memory after memory through that [destroyed] operation. And because it is universally accepted that the causal-ness of experience for memory is only through the operation characterized as impression. [300] 'Of one having no fewer objects' — the purport is this: causal-ness of memory should be accepted by the double relation of: co-location with the property of possessing a difference delimited by the relation of 'being the same as itself' and so forth as superstratum-ness, or by the double relation of: non-co-location with the counter-positive-delimiting property of the difference co-located with itself as delimiting the counter-positiveness of the difference residing in itself. Superstratum-ness of itself is through the relation of object-ness determined by itself. The delimitation of counter-positiveness of difference is also through that same relation. [300] 'Sudden memory' and so forth — this is for indicating the evidence for the particular universal; the meaning is: the delimitor of the productive capacity of sudden memory. The evidence should be understood as an inference supporting the thesis of productive capacity. [300] 'Excess of impression' — a particular universal residing in the impression. Now, regarding the under-pervasion of the definition of impression as 'produced by experience' and so forth with respect to impressions produced by memory, he says: [300] 'This is the view' — the meaning is: the view of the moderns.

children.translated_text: Definition of <s>viśeṣaguṇa</s> (specific quality)

children.text:

children.translated_text: 'Of earth-ness' and so forth. The outcome is: <s>viśeṣaguṇatva</s> (specific-quality-ness) is the property of being a quality possessing a universal that does not occur in [anything] qualified by a condition that differentiates substances, by the double relation of: occurring in one's own substratum and occurring in the substratum of a condition that differentiates substances [which is] different from oneself. Here, since both such conditions being substrata of a single [entity] is not established, 'individually' is stated. [303] 'Because of being of that kind' — because of not occurring in [anything] qualified by a condition that differentiates substances. [303] 'Subordinate' — the meaning is: pervaded. The same applies hereafter as well. [303] 'Of the pair of such conditions' and so forth — the otherness qualified by a condition that differentiates substances should be expressed with a zero-ending. The qualification is by the relation of possessing a universal with occurrence no less than that of a quality occurring in what is qualified by itself. The self-qualification is by the double relation of: occurring in one's own substratum and occurring in the substratum of a condition that differentiates substances [which is] different from oneself. [303] 'Of number-ness and the rest, because of existence and the rest' — the meaning is: because the occurrence of such duality and the like of number-ness and the rest is present. [303] 'Blue-ness and the like' and so forth — although at present, the definition can also be arrived at by taking color-ness (<s>rūpatva</s>) and the like, nevertheless, following the refinement to be stated, color-ness and the like are disregarded. Here,

children.translated_text: by the dual relation of: being the delimitor of the occurrence-hood residing in one's own substratum, and being the delimitor of the occurrence-hood residing in the substratum of the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) that differentiates the substance different from oneself. Thereby, there is no complexity arising from introducing an aggregate of differences. And through the delimitation by the duality of such limiting adjuncts, the introduction of 'some' which blocks the natural implication of co-location is also [explained, along with] the non-uniformity caused by it. If any single difference of such type were introduced, taking the difference of oneness-hood and such, there would be over-extension to duality and so forth. Similarly, since duality, which has the form of number, is impossible in a limiting adjunct of the form of substance-hood and such, because its subject-matter depends on the observer's expectation, due to the great complexity of having to state this, due to the lack of a distinct unified meaning of the definition upon the entry of whatever-ness and that-ness, and since there would be no scope for the absurd consequence of sentence-splitting in [expressions like] 'color is a specific quality' — [passage 303] 'constructed with the relation of inherence alone' — otherwise, taking co-location constructed with temporal and other relations, impossibility would follow. [Passage 304:]

na deyamiti/
sthitasthāpakatvasya yadrūpapadena dhartumaśakyatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
nanvanuṣṇāśītaḥ pṛthivīvāyvorityuktatvāt anuṣṇāśītatvasya
yadrūpapadena dhartuṃ śakyatayā anuṣṇāśītasparśe 'vyāptirityatrāha ---
[304] pārthiveti/ tathā ca tatrāpi vaijātyaviśeṣamādāya
lakṣaṇagamanamiti bhāvaḥ/ [304] tatra -- saṅkhyādiṣu/ evamagre 'pi/ [304] tādṛśeti/ uktobhāyasambandhena
dravyavibhājakopādhiviśiṣṭānyetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'should not be conceded' — the purport is: because the property of maintaining [something] in place cannot be captured by the word-form 'whichever.' Objection: Since it was stated 'neither hot nor cold [touch belongs] to earth and air,' and since the property of being neither-hot-nor-cold can be captured by the word-form 'whichever,' he says regarding the [alleged] non-pervasion in the case of neither-hot-nor-cold touch — [passage 304] 'of earth.' And accordingly, even there, taking the specific heterogeneity, the definition is arrived at — this is the purport. [Passage 304] 'there' — among number and such. 'Similarly further on as well.' [Passage 304] 'Of such type' — the meaning is: different from [those] qualified by the substance-differentiating limiting adjunct, by the aforementioned dual relation.

children.text:
yattu kenaciduktam -
tādṛśajātimattve sati guṇatvameva lakṣaṇamāstām, kiṃ
niṣedhadvayopādāneneti -- tanna - tathāsati rūpatvādijātimādāya
rūpādiviśeṣaguṇeṣvatiprasaṅgāt/ niṣedhadvayopādāne tu
tādṛśanīlatvādijātisattvenātivyāptyaprasakteḥ tasyāvaśyakatvaditi/
children.translated_text: As for what someone has said — let the definition simply be quality-hood when possessing such a universal, why introduce the two negations? — that is not so, because if that were so, taking the universal color-hood and such, there would be over-extension to the specific qualities of color and so forth. But when the two negations are introduced, since universals like blue-ness of such type exist, there is no occasion for over-extension — hence [the two negations] are necessary.

children.text: karmanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of action (<s>karma</s>)
Passage 309:

children.text:
mūloktamitpayādi/
patrādyākuñcanakriyāyāmavyāptiriti bhāvaḥ/ [309] ityāheti/
ityāśayenāhetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'As stated in the root text' and so forth. The purport is: there is non-pervasion in the action of contracting leaves and so forth. [Passage 309] 'Thus he says' — the meaning is: he says with this intent.

children.text: sāmānyanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of universal (<s>sāmānya</s>)

children.text:
nanu sāmānyānāṃ
lakṣaṇe ekatvaniveśanaṃ viphalamityata āha - [309] ekapadamiti/ nanu
sāmānyalakṣaṇe
ekatvāvacchinnapratiyogitākabhedarūpānekatvaśarīrapraviṣṭamekatvaṃ kiṃ
saṅkhyārūpam ata ekamātravṛttidharmaḥ/ nādyaḥ, guṇādau guṇādyanupagamena
guṇatvādau lakṣaṇagamena'pi dravyatvādāvavyāpteḥ/ nottaraḥ;
tādṛśadharmaspaya kevalānvayitayā
tadavacchinnapratiyogitākabhedāprasiddheḥ/ maivam --- yato 'tra
prameyaviśiṣṭatvaṃ bhedaviśiṣṭatvaṃ vā anekasamavetatvam/ prathame
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ svasamavetatvasvabhinnasamavetatvobhayasambandhena/ dvitīye
svapratiyogisamavetatvasvānuyogisamavetatvobhayasambandhena/ ato na
doṣa iti/
children.translated_text: Objection: The introduction of oneness in the definition of universals is fruitless. To this he says — [passage 309] 'the word one.' Objection: In the definition of universal, is the oneness that enters into the body of plurality — which is a difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by oneness — a number, or a property occurring in a single [entity] alone? Not the first, because even if the definition is arrived at for quality-hood and such through non-acceptance of quality in quality and such, there would be non-pervasion in substance-hood and the like. Not the second, because since such a property, being purely positive (<s>kevalānvayi</s>), the difference whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by it would not be well-established. Not so — because here, plurality is the property of being qualified by <s>prameya</s> (knowable), or the property of being qualified by difference, [i.e.,] being inhered in by many. In the first case, the qualification is by the dual relation of: inhering in itself and inhering in what is different from itself. In the second case, it is by the dual relation of: inhering in the counter-positive of itself and inhering in the relatum of itself. Therefore there is no fault.

children.text: viśeṣanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of particularity (<s>viśeṣa</s>)
Passage 309

children.text:
parasparamiti/ parasparatvaṃ ca
svāśrayanirūpitabhedāśrayanirūpitatvam
svanirūpakāśrayavṛttitvasvāśrayanirūpitatvobhayasaṃbandhena
bhedaviśiṣṭatvaparyavasitam/ [309]
bhedasādhakā iti/ etena vyāvartakā
ityatra vyāvṛttiśabdārthaḥ bhedaḥ sādhakaḥ pratyayārtha iti
sphuṭīkṛtam/ [309] na ca sugrahamityanvayaḥ/ atra ca prāguktarītyā
dharmigrāhakapramāṇasiddhamithobhedānāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ 'ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ
tadviśeṣāt bhidyate tādātmyena etadviśeṣā'dityanumānenāpi
dharmimānopajīvinā mithobhedasiddhiriti svato vyāvartakatā
teṣāmityāha - [309] sa eveti/ [309] atyantaṃ saṃkīrṇānāmiti/
atyantadurgrahabhedānāmityarthaḥ/ svasajātīyānāṃ viśeṣāntarāṇāṃ
parasparamityatrāpi pūrvavadeva bodhyam/ [309] tatrāpi - viśeṣe 'ti
nānavastheti/ atra vaktavyam prāgreva prapañcitam/
children.translated_text: 'Mutually' — and the mutual-ness is the property of being determined by the substratum of difference that is determined by one's own substratum, which amounts to the property of being qualified by difference, by the dual relation of: occurring in the substratum of one's own determiner, and being determined by one's own substratum. [Passage 309] 'Provers of difference' — thereby it is clarified that in 'differentiators,' the meaning of the word 'differentiation' is difference, and the meaning of 'prover' is cognition. [Passage 309] 'And it is not easy to grasp' — this is the syntactic connection. And here, in the previously stated manner, since the mutual differences of the <s>viśeṣas</s> (particularities) are established by the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) that grasps the property-bearer, and since mutual difference is also established by the inference 'this <s>viśeṣa</s> differs from that <s>viśeṣa</s> by identity, because it is a <s>viśeṣa</s> of this [entity]' — which depends on [grasping] the property-bearer — their self-differentiating capacity [follows]. He says this — [passage 309] 'that itself.' [Passage 309] 'Of those that are extremely intermixed' — meaning: whose differences are extremely difficult to grasp. Among the other <s>viśeṣas</s> of the same kind, in the word 'mutually' too, it should be understood as before. [Passage 309] 'There too — in <s>viśeṣa</s>, there is no infinite regress' — what is to be said here has already been elaborated previously.

children.text: samavāyanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>)
Passage 310

children.text:
nīlo ghaṭa iti viśaṣṭapratītirityādi/
ayamatrānumānapariṣkāraḥ ---
ghaṭādiviśeṣyatānirūpitanīlarūpādiprakāratā
kiñcinniṣṭhasaṃsargatānirūpikā prakāratātvāt
saṃyoganiṣṭhasaṃsargatānirūpakadaṇḍādiviśeṣyatānirūpitadaṇḍādiprakāratāvaditi
rītyā bodhyaḥ/ atra saṃyogādeḥ bādhaniścayasahāyabalāt
saṃyogādyatiriktakiñcinniṣṭhasaṃsargatānirūpakatvasiddhiriti sa eva
saṃbandhaḥ samavāyaśabdita iti dhyeyam/ nanu samavāyasadbhāve
nīlo ghaṭa ityādipratyakṣameva pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: 'The qualified cognition that the pot is blue' and so forth. Here is the refinement of the inference: The mode-hood (<s>prakāratā</s>) determined by the pot and such as qualificand (<s>viśeṣya</s>) and having blue color and such as the mode — it determines a contact-hood residing in something, because it is a mode-hood; just as the mode-hood having staff and such as its mode, determined by the qualificand-hood of staff and such, which determines the contact-hood residing in conjunction — it should be understood in this manner. Here, through the force of the sublating cognition regarding conjunction and so forth, the establishment of it determining a contact-hood residing in something other than conjunction and so forth [is achieved] — and that very relation is denoted by the word <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). This should be noted. Objection: If inherence exists, then perception itself in the form 'the pot is blue' will be the <s>pramāṇa</s>,

children.text:
anumānaparyanatānudhāvanavaiphalyamityata āha - [311] vaiśeṣiketyādi/ vaiśeṣikaiḥ samavāyapratayakṣatānugamāditi
bhāvaḥ/ saṃgrahe [310] tāvayutasiddhāviti/ athātra
kimidamayutasiddhatvam, na tāvat yutasiddhabhinnatvam/ yutasiddhasyaiva
children.translated_text: and the pursuit of inference would be fruitless. To this he says — [passage 311] 'the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>' and so forth. The purport is: because the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> accept the perceptibility of inherence. In the compendium, [passage 310] 'of those that are inseparably connected.' Now here, what is this inseparable connection (<s>ayutasiddhatva</s>)? It is not, to begin with, difference from what is separately established, because what is separately established itself

children.text:
durnirūpatvāt/ nāpi
saṃyuktatvam ghaṭakapālādau tadasambhavāt/ na ca yayordvayormandhye
ekamaparāśritamevāvatiṣṭhate tattvamayutasiddhatvamiti vācyam/
yattvatattvānanugamenāyutasiddhapadārthatāvacchedakasyānanugatatvādi ti -
atra kecit - dvitvaviśiṣṭadvitvamevāyutasiddham/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ
tādātmyasvāśrayavyaktiviśiṣṭatvobhayasambandhena/ vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaviśiṣṭavṛttitvasambandhena/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca
svaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena/ avacchedakatā
ca svaniṣṭhapratiyogitākātyantābhāvavattvasambandhena/ pratiyogitā
cādheyatāsambandhāvacchinnā ghaṭakapālādigatadvitvasya svapadenopādāne
tadāśrayībhūtakapālādivyaktīnāmādheyatāsambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhapratiyogitākātyantābhāvavattvasambandhāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhāvacchedakatākapratiyogitākabhedavattvasambandhena/
kapāladiviśiṣṭaghaṭādau vṛttitvasya tādātmyasya coktadvitve sattvāt
lakṣaṇasamanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: is difficult to define. Nor is it the property of being conjoined, because that is impossible in pot-potsherds and such. And one should not say that inseparable connection is the state where, of two things, one exists only as dependent on the other — because of the non-uniformity of the delimitor of the category of inseparably-connected entities, due to the non-uniformity of that state. Here some [say]: Duality qualified by duality itself is inseparably connected. The qualification is by the dual relation of: identity and the property of being qualified by the instance of one's own substratum. And the qualification is by the relation of occurring in what is qualified by oneself. And the self-qualification is by the relation of possessing difference whose counter-positive-hood has delimitor-hood residing in itself. And the delimitor-hood is by the relation of possessing absolute absence whose counter-positive-hood resides in itself. And the counter-positive-hood is delimited by the relation of superimposed-ness. When the duality residing in pot-potsherds and such is taken by the word 'self,' since the instances of potsherds and such that are its substratum possess difference whose counter-positive-hood has delimitor-hood delimited by the relation of possessing absolute absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the relation of superimposed-ness and resides in itself — by this relation, since occurring in [something] and identity both exist in the stated duality when the pot is qualified by potsherds and such, the definition is correlated.

children.text:
bhūtalādestu
ghaṭādiśūnyatādaśāyāṃ
ādheyatāsambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākātyantābhāvasattvāt
niruktasambandhena bhūtalādiviśiṣṭatvasya ghaṭādāvasattvāt
bhūtalaghaṭādīnāṃ dvitvaṃ na tādṛśamiti na bhūtalaghaṭādyoratiprasaṅgaḥ/
yadyapi saṃyogasaṃbandhāvacchinnānadheyatāsambandhena kapālādikaṃ ghaṭādau
nāsti, tathāpi ādheyatāsāmānyāvacchinnasvaniṣṭhapratiyogitākā
yantābhāvavattvapraveśāt na doṣaḥ/ na caivamapi kapālādināśakṣaṇe
kapālāderghaṭādau uktasambandhenābhāvādavyāptiriti vācyam/
svaviśiṣṭātyantābhāvavattvasya niveśyatvāt/ svavaiśiṣṭyaṃ
children.translated_text: But in the case of a ground-surface, in the state when it is devoid of pot and such, since absolute absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by the relation of superimposed-ness exists, the qualification by the ground-surface does not exist in the pot by the stated relation — hence the duality of the ground-surface and pot is not of such type, and there is no over-extension to the ground-surface-pot pair. Although by the relation of superimposed-ness delimited by the relation of conjunction, potsherds and such do not exist in the pot, nevertheless there is no fault because of the entry of possessing absolute absence whose counter-positive-hood is delimited by superimposed-ness-in-general residing in itself. And one should not say that at the moment of destruction of the potsherds, since the potsherds do not exist in the pot by the stated relation, there is non-pervasion — because possessing absolute absence qualified by oneself is what is to be introduced. And the self-qualification is

children.text:
ca
svāvacchinnādhikaraṇakālāvacchinnatvādheyatāsāmānyāvacchinnasvāśrayaprati yogitākatvobhayasambandhena/
yadyapi evamapi abhāvābhāvatvayorayutasiddhiprasaṅgaḥ, tathāpi
svāśrayātiriktasambandhāvacchinnādheyatāniveśāt na doṣa iti
vadanti/
children.translated_text: by the dual relation of: being delimited by the time of the substratum delimited by itself, and having superimposed-ness-in-general-delimited counter-positive-hood whose substratum is oneself. Although even so there would be the absurd consequence of inseparable connection between absence and the absence of absence, nevertheless, by introducing superimposed-ness delimited by a relation other than the substratum of oneself, there is no fault — so they say.

children.text:
tanna-kālikādisambandhamādāyātiprasaṅgavyudāsāya
samavāyasambandhena tasya pravṛttinimittatāyā vācyatvena prācīnamate
avayavāvayavināvayutasiddhāvityādivākyasya nirākāṅkṣatāpatteḥ/
svaviśiṣṭadvitvasambandhena dvitvasya tathātve 'pi dvitvasya
saṅkhyārūpatve guṇaguṇyādyoravyāpteḥ/
apekṣādhīviśeṣaviṣayatvarūpatve ca apekṣābuddheḥ
viṣayaviśeṣaniyantritatayā ananugamāpatteḥ/
svāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitaikatvaprakāratākatvasvabhinnadharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitaikatvaprakāratākatvobhayasambandhena
dharmaviśiṣṭabuddhitvenānugame ca
svāśrayadharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitaikatvaprakāratākatvasvapratiyogidharmāvacchinnaviśeṣyatānirūpitaikatvaprakāratākatvobhayasambandhena
bhedaviśiṣṭabuddhitvādinā anugamamādāya vinigamanāvirahāpattyā
ayutasiddhapadārthatāvacchedakanānātvāpatteḥ/ tanniṣkarṣastu
asmābhiranyatra prapañcitaḥ/
children.translated_text: That is not so — because to ward off the over-extension taking temporal and other relations, since its functioning as the occasion of [the term's] application must be stated through the relation of inherence, in the older view, the sentence 'parts and wholes are inseparably connected' would become self-sufficient [without needing inherence], which is absurd. Even if duality has such status through the relation of duality qualified by itself, since duality has the form of number, there would be non-pervasion in the case of quality and the thing possessing quality, and so forth. And if it has the form of depending on the observer's specific object-domain through expectation, since the expectation-cognition is governed by the specific objects, non-uniformity would follow. And even if uniformity is achieved through the property of being a cognition of a property-qualified [entity], by the dual relation of: having mode-hood of oneness determined by qualificand-hood delimited by oneself, and having mode-hood of oneness determined by qualificand-hood delimited by a property different from oneself — even then, taking uniformity through the property of being a cognition qualified by difference, by the dual relation of: having mode-hood of oneness determined by qualificand-hood delimited by one's own substratum-property, and having mode-hood of oneness determined by qualificand-hood delimited by one's own counter-positive-property — due to the absence of a deciding reason, the multiplicity of the delimitor of the category of inseparably-connected entities would follow. The determination of this, however, has been elaborated by us elsewhere.

children.text: abhāvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Exposition of absence (<s>abhāva</s>)

children.text:
nanu dhvaṃsādipratiyogitāyāḥ
sambandhāvacchinnatve mānābhāvāt saṃsargāṃbhāvatvaniveśādeva
dhvaṃsādivāraṇe nityatvaviśeṣaṇavaitharthyamityatrāha - [313] dhvaṃsetyādi/ siddhānṛte dhvaṃsādipratiyogitāyāḥ
saṃbandhāvacchinnatvānaṅgīkartṛnavyamate granthāntaroktaṃ manasi
nidhāyāha -- [314] saṅkṣepa iti/ [314] dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorityādi/
dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvayorekapratiyogikayorapi ekarūpatvameva/ tadvadiha
netyarthaḥ/ dīpikāyām [313] pratiyogitāvacchedakāropyetyādi/
pratiyogitāvacchedakaśca āropyasaṃsargaśca tayorbhedāt ityarthaḥ/
āropyaṃ ca pratiyogyāropaviṣayatvam/ abhāvabuddhau
pratiyogyāropahetutāyāḥ navīnairanabhyupagamādāha -
prakāśikāyām [314] āropyetīti/ nanvanyonyābhāvabhede
pratiyogitāvacchedakasaṃsargabhedo na niyāmakaḥ, anyonyābhāvasya
tādātmyasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākatvaniyamāt/ atra [314] yathāyogamiti [314] avacchedakabhedādatirikta ityanvayaḥ [322] prasaṅgāditi/ svavṛttyabhāvatvavattvamatra prasaṅgaḥ/ [322] tacchabdollikhiteti/ tacchabdajanyabodhasamānārthaketyarthaḥ/ [322] svātantryeṇa pratiyogini abhāsamānatayā/
children.translated_text: Objection: Since there is no evidence for the counter-positive-hood of destruction and such being delimited by a relation, the qualifier 'eternal' would be purposeless if the introduction of 'contact-absence-hood' alone suffices for blocking destruction and such. To this he says — [passage 313] 'of destruction' and so forth. In the established Navya view that does not accept the counter-positive-hood of destruction and such being delimited by a relation, having kept in mind what is stated in other texts, he says — [passage 314] 'in summary.' [Passage 314] 'Of destruction and prior absence' and so forth: Even though destruction and prior absence have the same counter-positive, they have only one form. The meaning is: it is not so here [with mutual absence]. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, [passage 313] 'the delimitor of counter-positive-hood is also what is superimposed' and so forth — the meaning is: because the delimitor of counter-positive-hood and the superimposed contact are different. And what is superimposed is the object of superimposition of the counter-positive. Since the newer logicians do not accept that the cause of superimposition of the counter-positive is the cognition of absence, he says — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, [passage 314] 'what is superimposed.' Objection: In the case of difference in mutual absence, the difference in the relation-contact of the delimitor of counter-positive-hood is not a determining factor, since mutual absence is necessarily such that its counter-positive-hood is delimited by the relation of identity. Here, [passage 314] 'as appropriate.' [Passage 314] 'Beyond the difference of delimitor' — this is the syntactic connection. [Passage 322] 'Incidentally' — the incidental point here is possessing the property of being an absence of one's own occurrence. [Passage 322] 'Indicated by that word' — meaning: having the same meaning as the cognition generated by that word. [Passage 322] 'Due to not appearing independently in the counter-positive.'

children.text:
ṣoḍaśapadārthānāṃ
saptapadārtheṣvantarbhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Subsumption of the sixteen categories under the seven categories

children.text:
pramāṇaprameyetyādisūtre prathamataḥ kathitasya
kḷpte yatra kutracidantarbhāvamanumuktvā dvitīyata uktasya prameyasya
dvādaśavidhasya yathāyathaṃ kḷptāntarbhāvakathanamanupapannamityatrāha- [331] pratyakṣeti/ cakṣurādīndriyarūpasyetpayādiḥ/
children.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s> 'valid cognition, knowable' and so forth, setting aside the subsumption of what is stated first [i.e., <s>pramāṇa</s>] in what is already established, the account of the subsumption of the twelve types of <s>prameya</s> (knowable) stated second, each in its proper place among the established [seven categories], is unjustified. To this he says — [passage 331] 'perception' and so forth. The meaning [of the preceding passage begins with]: 'that which has the form of sense-organs such as the eye' and so forth.
Passage 331

children.text:
anumānādīnāmiti ādinopamānaśabdayoḥ
saṅgrahaḥ/ [331] dravya iti antarbhāva ityanena sambandhaḥ/
[331] evamagre 'pīti/ pravṛttidoṣādirūpe prameye 'pītyarthaḥ/ nanu
prayatnaviśeṣaḥ pravṛttiriti tasyāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Of inference and so forth' — by the word 'and so forth,' <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) and <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) are included. [Passage 331] 'In substance' — the connection is with the word 'subsumption.' [Passage 331] 'Similarly further on as well' — the meaning is: in the <s>prameyas</s> having the form of effort, fault, and so forth. Objection: Since effort of a special kind is activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), its being stated as having the form of

children.text:
dharmādharmarūpatvakathanamanupapannamityata āha - [331] taditi/ dharmādharmetyarthaḥ/ svoktārthe pūrvagranthasammatimāha -
[331] etacceti/ dharmādharmāvityasya tajjaniketyarthakathanaṃ cetyarthaḥ/
[331] ākāre bhāṣye/
children.translated_text: <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) is unjustified. To this he says — [passage 331] 'that' — meaning: <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. He states the agreement of a prior text with his own stated meaning — [passage 331] 'and this.' The meaning is: and the statement that the meaning of 'born from that' applies to '<s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.' [Passage 331] 'In the <s>Ākāra Bhāṣya</s>.'

children.text:
nanu pretyabhāvo
maraṇamiti dīpikāvākyamasaṅgatam/ propasṛṣṭaiṇ dhātumātreṇa

To this he says: [331] 'after death,' etc. 'After-ness' means being at a later time. He shows the conformity of the stated meaning with the etymology of the word <s>pretyabhāva</s>: [331] 'and accordingly,' etc. The meaning is: when the word <s>pretyabhāva</s> has the stated meaning as its purport. He shows the meanings of the words 'death' and 'birth' in sequence: [331] 'final,' etc. 'Final' is a qualifier of the conjunction. Similarly in what follows. children.translated_text: then final-ness would be 'that particular-ness which is different from what is contemporaneous with the prior absence of a similar [conjunction] co-located with itself' — and since the instances of final conjunctions are infinite, there would be no recurrence. And if 'self' enters in the counter-positive, then [final-ness would be] 'that which is contemporaneous with the prior absence of a similar conjunction not co-located with itself' — but if the absence of a single such instance enters, then even the present conjunction would have the stated final-ness, and taking its destruction, there would be the unwanted consequence of death even now. And if the aggregate of absences of each and every such instance enters as 'that which is contemporaneous with the prior absence of such,' there would be a collapse of the unified meaning of the qualified, since final-ness would be constituted by the particular-ness of each instance. Moreover, even for an omniscient being, discerning each of those instances would be difficult. The rough recurrence is: final-ness is 'being qualified by knowability' — since aggregate-ness is of the nature of not being other than a single qualified [entity] — when 'self' enters. And the refined recurrence is: being qualified by an absence, through the dual relation of possessing an absence whose counter-positive-hood is of the nature of limitor-hood residing in oneself delimited by the relation of identity and contemporaneity with the prior absence of a similar conjunction co-located with itself. The qualification is through the dual relation of being-the-locus-of-self and being-the-limitor-of-one's-own-counter-positive-hood. The limitor-hood is through the relation of contemporaneity with the prior absence of a similar conjunction co-located with itself. And if 'self' enters in the counter-positive, then final-ness is 'otherness qualified by the prior absence of such a conjunction.' The qualification is through the dual relation of being-contemporaneous-with-self and co-location-with-self, or through the relation of co-location delimited by a single moment. And that [co-location] is of the form of superstratum-hood delimited by inherence, qualified by superstratum-hood delimited by the relation of identity residing in itself. And the qualification is through the dual relation of being-determined-by-self and being-delimited-by-the-moment-that-delimits-self. First-ness (<s>ādyatva</s>) is not being contemporaneous with the destruction of a similar conjunction co-located with itself. Here too, it should be analyzed as either 'being qualified by knowability' or 'being qualified by an absence' or 'otherness qualified by the destruction of such a conjunction' — substituting destruction for prior absence [in the formulas above]. The rest is as before. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: [331] 'and that is <s>mokṣa</s>.' Although elsewhere it has been established that the destruction of the final suffering is <s>mokṣa</s>, nevertheless the qualifier 'suffering' along with the temporal qualifier simply elaborates the very meaning of the word 'final' — hence there is no contradiction. The recurrence should be understood as before — of the form of otherness and so forth qualified by the prior absence of suffering through the previously stated relation of co-location. And here, when someone objects that specifying the suffering-component is otiose where <s>mokṣa</s> is defined as the destruction of any entity whatsoever that is not contemporaneous with the prior absence of suffering co-located with itself, he states the purpose of that specification in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>: [331] 'the conjunction of the liberated self,' etc. And here, without incorporating the prior-absence component, final-ness in the form of otherness qualified by suffering through the relation of co-location delimited by a single moment — as not being contemporaneous with suffering co-located with itself — is easily stated. Nor is there any problem of non-establishment when that [final-ness] qualifies suffering, since it is now accepted as qualifying destruction. Nor in that case would there be the unwanted consequence of us being liberated during deep sleep — since at that time there is absence of suffering in our selves, and the destruction of suffering at that time is pervaded by the stated qualifier. He raises the objection: [331] 'nor' etc. [331] 'subsequent' etc. [331] 'deep sleep' etc. The meaning is: subsequent. [331] 'In the arrangement as stated': in the stated manner involving prior absence. And here, if prior absence is not accepted, [the definition] should be considered as constituted by the stated manner of not-being-contemporaneous-with-such-suffering. Similarly, following the method stated in the <s>Pakṣatā</s> text, in the place of contemporaneity with the prior absence of suffering, one should substitute 'being the counter-positive of destruction residing in suffering' — with this intent it was said: [331] 'this is the direction.' Objection: Since in the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with '<s>pramāṇa</s>' etc., doubt is mentioned immediately after <s>prameya</s>, it is improper for the <s>Dīpikā</s> to state the nature of purpose and so forth without presenting the nature of doubt. To this he says: [331] 'of doubt' etc. He states the purpose of 'possessing the means for both [alternatives]': [335] 'and this' etc. The meaning is: the qualifier stated with 'both' and so forth is also [needed]. He gives the example of <s>sādharmyasamā</s>: 'for example,' etc. 'Possessing action' means having action. Here, the <s>hetu</s> (inferential mark) is of the form of possessing a quality that is a cause of action, applied to the body. The suffix <s>-tra</s> means 'pot-ness'; 'endowed with qualities.' 'Producer' is a qualifier [meaning] conjunction and the like. 'If it possesses action,'

children.translated_text: He defines <s>utkarṣasamā</s> (the futile rejoinder of excellence): [338] 'stated by the opponent,' etc. 'That' means the <s>sādhana</s> (proof) stated by the opponent — this is the meaning. He gives the example: 'for example,' etc. 'If it were' — this is the syntactic connection. Similarly in what follows. 'By that very [property]' — by producedness alone. Similarly in what follows. [338] 'Possessing parts (<s>sāvayava</s>)': having-parts-ness is being qualified by possessing an inseparable cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>). The qualification is through the relation of substance-ness that determines oneself — this is the precise formulation. And such having-parts-ness, being of the form of being-an-effect (<s>kāryatva</s>), is indeed not pervaded by producedness (<s>kṛtakatva</s>), since it is distinguished from color and the like that are effects — this should be noted. 'Thus' connects with 'someone says thus' stated earlier.

prakṛtānumānasādhyatayābhimatadharmātiriktadharmasya/ asyā udāharaṇamāha

children.translated_text: He defines <s>apakarṣasamā</s> (the futile rejoinder of degradation): [339] 'stated by the opponent,' etc. 'Of another property': of a property other than the property intended as the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) of the inference under discussion. He gives the example: 'for example,' etc. 'In that very [context]' — in the very form illustrated [in the inference] 'sound is eternal,' etc. 'Thus someone says' is to be supplied.

children.translated_text: Similarly in what follows.

He illustrates it: 'for example,' etc. 'As stated earlier': the meaning is the inference of the form 'the self possesses action because of possessing a quality that is a cause of action, like a clod of earth.' 'That' means action.

[350] sādhyeti/ tāmudāharati--- yatheti/ tataiva - ātmā sakriya
ityādirūpa eva/ sādhanam - sādhyāpattipratipādakamuttaram/

uktaguṇavattvasyātmanyasiddhatve ca/ tulyatayā

children.translated_text: He defines <s>avarṇyasamā</s> (the futile rejoinder of the inexplicable): [350] 'of the <s>sādhya</s>,' etc. He illustrates it: 'for example,' etc. 'In that very [context]' — of the very form 'the self possesses action' and so on. '<s>Sādhana</s>' (proof) means the reply that demonstrates the entailment of the <s>sādhya</s>. Similarly in what follows. 'Possessing motion' and 'possessing form' are qualifiers of the quality. And accordingly, when such possession-of-quality is not established in the self — 'due to the similarity of having a <s>sādhana</s> based on an unestablished <s>hetu</s> in the self, why should it not be proved?' — this is its connection with what follows. 'Of such a kind' — unestablished. 'That' means action.

yadī'ti sambandhaḥ/ tathā ca yathā ātmā tathā loṣṭa ityasyāpyāgamena/
sādhyate yaditi sambandhaḥ/ tat - kriyāvattvam/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>sādhyasamā</s> (the futile rejoinder of the unproved): [341] 'of the example,' etc. Objection: Since this [rejoinder] consists in asserting equality with the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis), the name '<s>pakṣasama</s>' (equal to the thesis) would be fitting, not '<s>sādhyasama</s>' (equal to the probandum). To resolve this doubt, [the commentator explains that] by the locative derivation 'that in which [something] is to be proved,' the word <s>sādhya</s> here itself conveys the <s>pakṣa</s>. Thus he says: '<s>sādhya</s>' etc. Here, in <s>sādhyasamā</s>, the suffix <s>-tra</s> means 'pot-ness,' connected with the word <s>sādhya</s>. He illustrates: 'for example,' etc. 'If it is said' — this is the connection. And accordingly, 'just as the self, so also the clod of earth' — by scripture [this is established]. 'That which is to be proved' — this is the connection. 'That' means the possession of action.

children.text:
prāptisamāyā
lakṣaṇamāha - [342] prāptyeti/ hetau tṛtīyā/ pratyavasthānam
-- pratyuttarakathanam/ evamagre 'pi/ tathā ca prāptiṃ hetūkṛtya
pratyuttaroktiriti yāvat/ atra prāptiśabdasyārthamāha - prāpitaśceti/
udāharati - yatheti/ tādṛśeti/ kriyāhetvityarthaḥ/ neti sādhyata
ityanuṣajyate/ ubhayoraviśeṣāt - ubhayoḥ
kriyāvattvakriyāhetuguṇavattvayoraviśeṣāt
sāmānādhikaraṇyasāmyāt/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>prāptisama</s> (the futile rejoinder of attainment): [342] 'through attainment (<s>prāpti</s>),' etc. The third case-ending is for the <s>hetu</s> (reason). '<s>Pratyavasthāna</s>' means counter-reply. Similarly in what follows. And accordingly, a counter-reply made on the basis of attainment — that much [is the definition]. He explains the meaning of the word <s>prāpti</s> here: 'and what is attained,' etc. He illustrates: 'for example,' etc. 'Of such a kind' means 'being a cause of action.' 'Is not proved' is to be supplied. 'Due to there being no distinction between the two': due to there being no distinction between the two — possession of action and possession of a quality that is a cause of action — that is, due to the equality of co-location.

children.text:
aprāptisamāṃ lakṣayati
--- [343] aprāptyeti/ pūrvavadeva hetau tṛtīyā/ aprāptiṃ hetūkṛtya
children.translated_text: He defines <s>aprāptisama</s> (the futile rejoinder of non-attainment): [343] 'through non-attainment (<s>aprāpti</s>),' etc. As before, the third case-ending is for the <s>hetu</s>. A counter-reply made on the basis of non-attainment,

children.text:
pratyuttarakathanamaprāptisameti yāvat/ udāharati - yatheti/
pūrvokteti/ loṣṭagatanodanādirūpetyādinā prāgupadarśitetyarthaḥ/
aprāptasyeti/ aprāptiriha sādhyavaiyadhikaraṇyam/ tathā ca -
tādṛśahetossādhyasādhakatvoktau ca/
children.translated_text: is <s>aprāptisama</s> — that much [is the definition]. He illustrates: 'for example,' etc. 'As stated earlier': the meaning is 'as previously illustrated by the form: activity in the nature of pushing and so forth present in the clod of earth.' 'Of what is not attained': non-attainment here means being in a different locus from the <s>sādhya</s>. And accordingly, when the stated <s>hetu</s> is said to prove the <s>sādhya</s>,

children.text:
ayameva -
kriyāhetuguṇavattvarūpa eva/
children.translated_text: 'this very [hetu]' means of the very form of possessing a quality that is a cause of action.

children.text:
prasaṅgasamāṃ lakṣayati
- [343] sādhaneti/ udāharati -- yatheti / tatra - kriyāhetuguṇavattve/
nanu sādhanāpekṣā kimarthamityatrāha -- na hīti/ nāsti hītyanvayaḥ/
tatrāpi - kriyāhetuguṇavattve 'pi/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>prasaṅgasamā</s> (the rejoinder by reductio) — 'the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>)...' He gives an example — 'for instance...' There — with respect to possessing the quality of being the cause of action. Now, to the question 'what is the purpose of the reference to the means of proof?' he says — 'for indeed not...' The construal is: 'for indeed there is not.' There too — even with respect to possessing the quality of being the cause of action.

children.text:
pratidṛṣṭāntasamāṃ
lakṣayati-- [344] dṛṣṭāntāntareṇeti/
paroktadṛṣṭāntātiriktadṛṣṭāntajanyetyarthaḥ/ sādhanam -
siddhyāpattipratipādakamuttaram/ udāharaṇamāha yatheti/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>pratidṛṣṭāntasamā</s> (the rejoinder by counter-example) — 'by means of another example...' The meaning is: produced by an example other than the example cited by the opponent. 'The means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>)' means the response that sets forth the establishment [of the thesis]. He states the illustration — 'for instance...'

children.text:
anutpattisamāṃ
lakṣayati--- [344] anutpatyeti/ atrāpi hetau tṛtīyā/
anutpattiṃ hetūkṛtya pratyuttarakathanamityarthaḥ/ udāharati - yatheti/
pramāṇaṃ yadīntyanvayaḥ/ taditi/ janyaikatvarūpapramāṇetyarthaḥ/ itīti/
iti kaścidāheti prāktanena sambandhaḥ/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>anutpattisamā</s> (the rejoinder by non-origination) — 'by non-origination...' Here too the instrumental case is used for the reason. The meaning is: stating a counter-reply by making non-origination the reason. He gives an example — 'for instance...' The construal is: 'if [there is] a means of valid knowledge...' 'That' means: the means of valid knowledge in the form of produced oneness. 'Thus' — the connection is with the preceding [statement]: 'thus someone says.'

children.text:
saṃśayasamāyā
lakṣaṇamāha --- [345] sādhāraṇeti/
sādhyatadabhāvasāmānādhikaraṇyetyarthaḥ/ udāharati -- yatheti/ ubhayeti/
nityānityobhayetyarthaḥ/ ekapariśeṣe ekasya
nityatvamātrasyānityatvamātrasya vā pariśeṣe niścaye/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>saṃśayasamā</s> (the rejoinder by doubt) — 'common [to both]...' The meaning is: co-location with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and its absence. He gives an example — 'for instance...' 'Both' means: both eternal and non-eternal. 'When one [alternative] remains by elimination' — when there is the ascertainment by elimination of only one [alternative], either eternality alone or non-eternality alone.

children.text: atra - prakaraṇasamāyām/
children.translated_text: Here — in [the context of] <s>prakaraṇasamā</s> (the rejoinder by the topic).

children.text:
ahetusamāyā
lakṣaṇamāha --- [346] kālatraye 'pīti/
bhūtabhaviṣyadvartamānakālatraye 'pītyarthaṃḥ/ udāharati - yatheti/ tadānīṃ
--- sādhyabhūtānityatvaprākkāle/ tasya - anityatvasya/ na sādhakam
kāryatvādirūpasādhanamiti sambandhaḥ/ paścāditi/
sādhyādanityatvāditi ādiranuṣajyate/ pūrveti/
kāryatvādiyapasādhanetyādiḥ/ sādhanābhāvāditi/ sādhanetyasya
kāryatvādirūpetyādiḥ/ tasya - kāryatvādirūpasādhanasya/ ubhayam -
kāryatvādirūpasādhanānityatvādirūpasādhyobhayam/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>ahetusamā</s> (the rejoinder by absence of reason) — 'even in all three times...' The meaning is: even in the three times of past, future, and present. He gives an example — 'for instance...' 'At that time' — at the time prior to non-eternality, which is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). 'Of that' — of non-eternality. 'Is not the prover' — the connection is: the means of proof in the form of being-an-effect and the like. 'Afterwards' — the word 'and the like' is carried over from: after the <s>sādhya</s>, i.e., after non-eternality. 'Before' — '[before] the means of proof in the form of being-an-effect,' and so on. 'Due to the absence of the means of proof' — the word 'means of proof' [here means] 'in the form of being-an-effect,' and so on. 'Of that' — of the means of proof in the form of being-an-effect. 'Both' — both the means of proof in the form of being-an-effect and the <s>sādhya</s> in the form of non-eternality.

children.text:
arthāpattisamāyā
lakṣaṇamāha - [346] arthāpattipuraskāreṇeti/
anyathānupapattirūpārthāpattiṃ hetūkṛtyetyarthaḥ/ pūrvokteti/ śabdo
nitya ityādirūpetyarthaḥ/ yadi sādhyamiti sambandhaḥ/ nityatvamapīti/
arthāpattyetyanuṣajyate/ siddhyediti śeṣaḥ/ ekatareti
ekatarasyānityatvaspanaya nityatvasya vā niścaya ityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: He states the definition of <s>arthāpattisamā</s> (the rejoinder by presumption) — 'by placing presumption first...' The meaning is: making <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — which has the form of impossibility-otherwise — the reason. 'The previously stated' — meaning: of the form 'sound is eternal' and the like. The connection is: 'if the <s>sādhya</s>...' 'Eternality too' — 'by presumption' is carried over. 'Would be established' is to be supplied. 'One of the two' — the meaning is: the ascertainment of one of the two, either non-eternality or eternality.

children.text:
aviśeṣasamāṃ lakṣayati
- [347] sarveti/ aviśeṣaḥ sāmyam/ udāharati -- tatraiveti/ anityatvaṃ
yadītyanvayaḥ/ evamagre 'ti/ taditi/ śabdetyarthaḥ/ tat - anityatvam/
upapattisamāṃ lakṣayati - [348] ubhayapakṣeti/
vādiprativādisammatapakṣadvayetyarthaḥ/ sādharmyeṇetyabhede tṛtīyā/
tādṛśasādharmyābhinnasādhanopapattiḥ upapattipratipādakamuttaramityarthaḥ/
udāharati -- yatheti/ evamagre 'pi avatārikā bodhyā/
children.translated_text: He defines <s>aviśeṣasamā</s> (the rejoinder by non-distinction) — 'all...' <s>Aviśeṣa</s> means equality. He gives an example — 'in that very [case]...' The construal is: 'if non-eternality...' 'Thus further...' 'That' means: sound. 'That' — non-eternality. He defines <s>upapattisamā</s> (the rejoinder by cogency) — 'in both positions...' The meaning is: in the two positions accepted by both the proponent and the opponent. 'By similarity' — the instrumental [case] is used in the sense of non-difference. The meaning is: a response that sets forth the cogency of the means of proof that is non-different from such similarity. He gives an example — 'for instance...' 'Thus further' — the introductory gloss should be understood [in the same way going forward].

children.text:
darśiteti
sādhanaviśeṣaṇam/ anuvidhāyitvaṃ - janyatvaṃ nāstīti sambandhaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Demonstrated' is a qualifier of the means of proof. <s>Anuvidhāyitva</s> (conformity) — the connection is: there is no produced-ness.
'The means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>)' means the response that sets forth the establishment [of the thesis]

children.text:
sādhanaṃ - siddhyāpattipratipādakamuttaram/
evamagre 'pi/ nopalabhyate yadītyanvayaḥ/ evaṃ nābhyupeyate
yadītyanvayaḥ/ anupalabdherapīti/ ṣaṣṭyarthaḥ pratiyogitvam
nirūpakatayā abhāvānvitam/ apiratrāvaraṇasamuccāyakaḥ dṛṣṭāntatvena/
taditi/ anupalabdhīyatyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: . 'Thus further' [applies going forward]. The construal is: 'if not perceived...' Similarly, the construal is: 'if not accepted...' 'Of non-perception too' — the meaning of the sixth case-ending is counter-positive-ness, conjoined with absence in the capacity of being a conditioner. The particle 'also' here functions as a cumulator, in the capacity of [serving as] an example. 'That' means: of the nature of non-perception.

children.text:
tasya - anityatvasya/
sadātanatvāt - nityatvāt/ [350]
tathātvam - sadātanatvam/ ubhayāthāpi
śabdavṛtteranityatve nityatve vā/
children.translated_text: 'Of that' — of non-eternality. 'Because of being perpetual' — because of being eternal. 'Such-ness' — perpetuality. 'In both ways' — whether the usage of the word 'sound' [points to] non-eternality or eternality.

children.text:
ucyate yadītyanvayaḥ/
taditi anityatvapadetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The construal is: 'if it is said...' 'That' means: by the word 'non-eternality.'

children.text:
tatraiva - śabdo 'nityaḥ
prayatnānuvidhāyitvāt ghaṭavadityanumāna eva/ ubhayathā--ubhābhyāmapi
prakārābhyām/ svarūpotpattyāvārakanivṛttirūpābhyām/ anuvidhānaṃ -
janyatā/ tathā ca - prayatnānuvidhāyitvasyobhayathā sambhave ca/ tasya -
prayatnānuvidhāyitvasya/ kāryāntareti/
svarūpotpattirūpakāryavyatiriktakāryetyarthaḥ niyatatvaṃ - vyāpyatvam
kvacit - keṣucit pusatakeṣu/ tasyāpi tādṛśāpāṭhasyāpi/ ukta
evārtha ityagrimeṇānvayaḥ/ atra - uktasamāviṣaye/
children.translated_text: In that very [context] — in the inference itself that 'sound is non-eternal, because of conformity to effort, like a pot.' 'In both ways' — by both modes: [namely] the cessation of something that obstructs the origination of the intrinsic nature, and [direct origination]. 'Conformity' — being produced. 'And thus' — when conformity to effort is possible in both ways. 'Of that' — of conformity to effort. 'By another effect' — the meaning is: by an effect other than the effect in the form of the origination of the intrinsic nature. 'Being invariably connected' — being pervaded. 'In some' — in some manuscripts. 'Even of that' — even of such a variant reading. 'The meaning is as already stated' — the construal is with what follows. 'Here' — in the subject matter of the stated type of rejoinder.

children.text: nigrahasthānanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat)

children.text:
dīpikāyāmam
[343] vādino 'pajayaheturnigrahasthānamiti/ tathā ca
nigrahasthānamityatra nigrahaśabdo vādyapajayaparaḥ/ sthānaśabdo hetupara
iti bhāvaḥ/ idaṃ ca vādyapajatahetutvarūpaṃ nigrahasthānalakṣaṇaṃ ca/
chalādāvityādinā prakaraṇasamārūpajātisaṅgrahaḥ/
arthāntarādītyādinā hetvābhāsasaṅgrahaḥ/ nanu tarhi
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s>: 'The point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) is the cause of the disputant's defeat.' And thus, in the expression '<s>nigrahasthāna</s>,' the word '<s>nigraha</s>' refers to the defeat of the disputant, and the word '<s>sthāna</s>' refers to the cause — this is the purport. And this definition of <s>nigrahasthāna</s> has the form of being the cause of the disputant's defeat. By 'sophistry (<s>chala</s>) and the like,' the collection of <s>jātis</s> (futile rejoinders) of the <s>prakaraṇasamā</s> type is included. By 'displacement of meaning and the like,' the collection of fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) is included. Now then,

children.text:
pramāṇetyādisūtre
nigrahasthānataḥ pṛthaktayā chalāderupādānamanarthakamityatrāha -
chalatvādināpīti/ ādinā prakaraṇasamātvasaṅgrahaḥ/
apirnigrahasthānatvasamuccāyakaḥ/ dṛṣṭāntavidhayā
jñānasyetayarayopādānamityasya ca
children.translated_text: in the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with '<s>pramāṇa</s>' (means of valid knowledge), the separate mention of sophistry and the like apart from points of defeat would be purposeless — to this he says — 'by the property of being sophistry and the like too...' By 'and the like,' the property of being <s>prakaraṇasamā</s> is included. The particle 'too' functions as a cumulator with the property of being a point of defeat. 'In the manner of an example, the mention of these [as part of] cognition' — and of this,

children.text:
chalāderityādiḥ/
upayogitvāt --- vādyapajayahetutvāt/ pṛthagiti/
nigrahasthānatvātiriktarūpeṇetyarthaḥ/ chalatvādinetyanuṣajyate/
upādānaṃ -- pratipādanam/ pramāṇetyādisūtreṇa kṛtamiti śeṣaḥ/
gobalīvardannayāyānusārāditi bhāvaḥ/ hetvābhāsavaditi
ṣaṣṭhīsamarthādvatiḥ, hetvābhāsasyevetyarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'sophistry and the like' and so on [serves as the beginning]. 'Because of being useful' — because of being the cause of the disputant's defeat. 'Separately' — the meaning is: in a form other than the property of being a point of defeat. 'By the property of being sophistry and the like' is carried over. 'Mention' — explication. 'Has been done by the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with <s>pramāṇa</s>' is to be supplied. The purport is: in accordance with the maxim of the cow and the bull. 'Like fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>)' — the suffix <s>vat</s> is from the sixth case-ending, meaning 'just as of fallacious reasons.'

children.text: pratijñāhānilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>pratijñāhāni</s> (abandonment of the thesis)

'Of that too' — of the point of defeat too. 'Sub-varieties' — specific instances of the pervaded. Here, the primary meaning of the word <s>pratijñāhāni</s> cannot be 'acceptance contrary to the thesis,' because what has the character of <s>pratijñāhāni</s> is precisely the abandonment of the thesis-content — since <s>pratijñā</s> means 'what is asserted' (from the root <s>pratijñā</s>), and the meaning of <s>pratijñā</s> is its content, and <s>hāni</s> is the abandonment thereof — this is derived through the analysis of the constituent parts. Such acceptance [of the contrary]

children.text:
tasyāpi-nigrahasthānasyāpi/
āvāntarabhedān-vyāpyaviśeṣān/ atra pratijñātārthavirūddhābhyupagamasya
pratijñāhāniśabdamukhyārthatā na sambhavati/ pratijñāyata iti pratijñā
pratijñātor'thaḥ tasya hānirityavayavavyutpattyā
pratijñātārthaparityāgasyaiva tādṛśatvāt
tādṛśābhyupagamasyātathātvādityataḥ tathaivāha -
pratijñātārthaparityāgo veti/
children.translated_text: does not have that character. Therefore he states it accordingly — 'or the abandonment of the thesis-content.'

children.text: pratijñāntaralakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>pratijñāntara</s> (shift of thesis)
'Previous...' [means:]

children.text:
pūrveti/ prāganuktaviśeṣaṇadānata
ityādiḥ/ dānamiha kathanam/
children.translated_text: 'by giving a qualifier not previously stated,' and so on. 'Giving' here means 'stating.'

children.text: avijñātārthalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>avijñātārtha</s> (unintelligible speech)
'And that' — and the point of defeat in the form of <s>avijñātārtha</s> (unintelligible speech). [It includes:]

children.text:
tacca/ avijñātārthakarūpanigrahasthānaṃ ca/
kliṣṭānvayam/ dūrānvayam/ aprasiddhārthakam - 1"bhūstanaṃ himabheṣajavat'ityādirūm/ ityādītyādinā
mṛdūccaritasaṅgrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: tortuous construal, far-fetched construal, [and speech] with an unestablished meaning — such as 'the earth-breast [has] snow-medicine,' and the like. By 'and the like,' softly uttered [speech] is included.

children.text: aprāptakālalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>aprāptakāla</s> (untimely statement)
'Out of order' — in an order other than the order established by the convention of the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise).

children.text:
vyutkrameṇa -
śāstrasaṅketasiddhakramātiriktakrameṇa/
adhikalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>adhika</s> (redundancy)

children.text:
hetvādītyādinā
dṛṣṭāntahetutāvacchedakasambandhavyāptidvayādisaṅgrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: By 'the reason and the like,' the collection [including] the example, the relation [delimiting] the reason, and the two pervasions is included.

children.text: apasiddhāntalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Definition of <s>apasiddhānta</s> (contradiction of accepted doctrine)

children.text:
dānamiha kathanam/
maṇyāderityataḥ paraṃ dāhādikaṃ pratīti śeṣaḥ--
children.translated_text: 'Giving' here means 'stating.' After 'of gems and the like,' 'burning and the like is cognized' is to be supplied.

children.text: śakteratiriktapadārthatvakhaṇḍanam
children.translated_text: Refutation of <s>śakti</s> (potency) as an independent category
'And that' — the obstructive capacity (<s>pratibandhakatā</s>) residing in gems and the like. To the question 'whence [is this known]

children.text:
sā ca -- maṇyādiniṣṭhā
dāhādipratibandhakatā ca/ kuta ityatrāha - pratibandhakatāyā iti/
anukūleti/ anukūlatvamiha janakatāvacchedakatvam/ vighaṭakatveti/
vighaṭakatvaṃ ca nāśajanakatvam/ taditi/
kāryānukūlaśaktivighaṭakatvarūpapratibandhakatetyarthaḥ/ arthāpattyeti/
arthāpattipramāṇātmikayeti śeṣaḥ/ siddhyanvitaṃ janyatvaṃ tṛtīyārthaḥ/
siddhiratrārthāpattipramitirūpā/ sā ca vahniḥ
dāhānukūlaśaktimānityākārikā bodhyā/
children.translated_text: ?' he says — 'of the obstructive capacity...' 'Favorable' — here 'favorability' means being the delimiter of the causality. 'Destructive capacity' — destructive capacity means being the producer of destruction. 'That' — the meaning is: the obstructive capacity in the form of being the destroyer of the potency favorable to the effect. 'By presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>)' — 'of the nature of the means of valid knowledge called presumption' is to be supplied. 'Being-produced conjoined with establishment' is the meaning of the instrumental case. 'Establishment' here is of the nature of the cognition through presumption. And that [presumption] should be understood as being of the form: fire possesses a potency favorable to burning.

children.text:
1. bhūstanamityasya
parvata ityarthaḥ/ himabheṣajavadityasya agnimānityarthaḥ/
'agninarhimasya bheṣajam' iti śrutiḥ/ pavataḥ bhūmisvanamiti
vadanti/
children.translated_text: [Footnote:] 1. The meaning of '<s>bhūstana</s>' is 'mountain.' The meaning of '<s>himabheṣajavat</s>' (possessing snow-medicine) is 'possessing fire.' children.translated_text: And the presumption in the form of a means of valid knowledge is of the following form: without fire possessing a potency favorable to burning, the capacity of gems and the like to produce burning — which is to be obstructed — would be inexplicable. And 'being-obstructable' means being occasioned by a destructible potency. Some, however, following the text as literally read, have stated the presumption to be of the following form: without fire possessing a potency favorable to burning, the obstructive capacity of gems — in the form of being the destroyer of the potency favorable to burning — would be inexplicable. But that is empty — because there is no co-location between the explanandum and the explanans. 'Thus he raises the objection' is the construal. 'Because of being additional...' children.translated_text: The meaning is: by a cause other than the cause in the form of fire and the like. The qualifier of this is: 'in the form of...' And thus — when the obstructive capacity is of a nature different from being the destroyer of the potency favorable to the effect, in the stated manner. 'By the impossibility of practical activity being otherwise' — by the impossibility of practical activity being [explained] otherwise, i.e., without accepting an additional category in the form of <s>śakti</s> (potency), [there being] the impossibility of it having a referent. Now, [if one asks:] even when both the fire and the gem are present, since fire lacks the potency favorable to burning, how on your view too is burning possible? To this he says — 'in my [view]...' This is from the <s>Prābhākara</s> standpoint. 'Thus further' [applies going forward]. 'Your [view] also...' 'By another potency' — the meaning is: a potency different from the potency present at the time of the removal of gems and the like.

children.translated_text: 'Even so' — even when the favorable potency is removed by the stated reasoning. 'Touch' — touch here everywhere means contact (<s>saṃyoga</s>), as is clear from the text itself. 'Form' is a qualifier of the effect. 'Is fit' — 'exists' is the remainder to be supplied; 'does not exist' is the syntactic connection. To the question 'why?' he says — 'possessing potency.' 'That' means: the effect in the form of dining and so forth. Similarly further ahead as well. 'And thus' — and in the establishment of the fitness for effects in the form of dining and so forth in bronze and the like, and of the absence thereof. 'In bronze and so forth' means: in the proximity residing in bronze and the like. And it should be noted that proximity is the substratum-hood that delimits the obstructed-ness, while <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) is the delimitor of the obstructing-ness. 'In the justification' — of the fitness for effects in the form of dining and so forth residing in bronze and the like, and of their absence, and so forth. 'That' means: in bronze and the like and so forth. The meaning is: the potency that is a superimposed property. Objection: since touch is a quality distinct from contact, how can it have the nature of contact? To this he says — 'in the present context.' The meaning is: in the context of stating the relation of obstructed and obstructor between the untouchable-touch and the effect such as dining pertaining to bronze and the like. 'That' means: the untouchable touch that has the nature of contact. Objection: if contact with ash and the like is possible, the desired conclusion would follow automatically. To this he says — 'without.' The meaning is: without. 'The fitness for dining and so forth would follow' — of bronze and the like, and so forth. 'Thus' means: in this manner. 'Again' means: in a manner different from what was stated before. 'By the first' means: by what is included in 'ash and so forth.' 'And by the second' — it connects with 'the word et cetera'; the meaning is: by what is included in 'bronze and so forth.' 'Established' means: accepted as included within the seven categories ending with substance and absence. 'By a particular destruction alone' — the particularity in destruction consists in being a counterpositive of contact with ash and so forth, accompanied by a constant absence whose counterpositive is the untouchable touch that is contemporaneous with the time of contact with ash and so forth. 'Even there' — connects with 'in bronze and the like.' 'Destruction' is to prevent the misconception of ash and the like being qualifiers. 'Here' means: in the body of the category of purification that has been shown. 'A particular relation' means: a particular qualifying relation pertaining to absence. 'Constrained' means: constructed. Otherwise, since in bronze and the like possessing untouchable touch, through the relation of possessing its own counterpositive, the possession of a constant absence whose counterpositive is such touch is possible, and since in bronze and the like possessing such constant absence, when not conjoined with ash and the like, the destruction of contact with ash and the like through temporal and other relations exists, the destruction of contact with ash and the like qualified by such constant absence would be common to the bronze and the like mentioned in the 'where' passage, leading to the undesirable consequence of infinite regress. 'Co-location' — and this is to be stipulated in the manner of a relation itself, since there is parsimony in not introducing the relation belonging to it. And accordingly, the conclusion is: the purifier is the destruction of contact with ash and the like, qualified by such constant absence, through the relation of co-location of such a kind, namely the superimposed-ness that determines the superimposed-ness delimited by the relation of spatial qualifying-ness residing in itself. Objection: if the matter is accomplished by merely stipulating the absence whose counterpositive is untouchable touch, what is the need for introducing the 'constant' qualification? Nor should one apprehend the infinite regress and over-extension in the case stated with 'where' and so forth by taking just any such absence, since by unifying such things under the heading of untouchable entities and stipulating an absence whose counterpositive-hood is delimited by untouchable-entity-touch-hood, there is no defect. To this he says — 'untouchable' and so forth. 'Whatsoever' is a qualifier of absence. 'Constant' — there, in the bronze and the like stated with 'where' and so forth. 'That' means: purification. Objection: in the bronze and the like stated with 'where' and so forth, the stated over-extension and infinite regress apply, because since such touch in the form of contact is of non-pervasive occurrence, the absence of it also exists in its own locus. To this he says — 'there' and so forth. The meaning is: in the bronze and the like stated with 'where' and so forth. 'Undelimited' — and accordingly, in the first superimposed-ness constituting the stated co-location,

children.translated_text: 'Ash and so forth' and so forth. There — in the locus of contact with ash and so forth. Although the superimposed-ness determined by the locus of contact with ash and so forth, delimited by the time of contact with ash and so forth, taken literally, is common to the relevant constant absence in the passage 'where there is untouchable touch and contact with ash and so forth,' and although at the time of the destruction of contact with ash and the like, the possibility of such constant absence exists there, nevertheless, since such absences exist in the locus of contact with ash and so forth of the earlier time — that is, in the locus of that contact, delimited by the moment of destruction of the earlier contact with ash and the like, which is qualified by contact with ash and the like occurring in another locus — the apprehension of the stated over-extension and infinite regress arises. Even so, there is no defect, because the meaning of 'contemporaneous' is: being qualified by contact with ash and the like. The qualification is through the relation of superimposed-ness delimited by the relation of undelimited qualifying-ness, which is itself qualified by superimposed-ness delimited by the relation of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) residing in itself. The qualification is through the double relation of being determined by what determines itself and being delimited by the moment that delimits itself. 'Absence is a qualifier' is to prevent the misconception of untouchable and such things being qualifiers. And accordingly, when a qualifier in the meaning of 'contemporaneous' with the stated sense is given — there, in the bronze and the like stated with 'where' and so forth. 'Constant' is a qualifier of absence. 'That' means: untouchable touch. 'Defect' means: in the form of the consequence of purification, and so forth.

Thus the establishment of the double relation.

children.translated_text: The absence-of-cognition-of-non-achievability-through-effort is relative to the cognition of achievability through effort — and so forth. 'That-that' means: the difference between the absence of achievability-through-effort and the achievable-through-effort — this is the meaning. By 'pervaded and so forth,' both the property delimiting those respective [states] and the property contradicting achievability-through-effort are included. 'The direction' — the intent is as follows: where there was no cognition either of achievability-through-effort or of non-achievability-through-effort, the prompting character of the cognition of achievability-through-effort is necessary to prevent activity [toward improper things]. Even there — even in the eating of poison and so forth. 'This' means the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and other [rituals]. 'Without my effort' and so forth — this is to prevent deviation in cases like cooking performed by another person. 'Inferential' means: produced by inference. 'In the form of' is a qualifier of the occasioning [condition]. After '<s>sandhyāvandana</s>' (twilight worship) the word 'and so forth' is to be supplied. By that, bathing is included. In 'purity of livelihood and so forth,' the meaning is 'possessing purity of livelihood and so forth.' By 'and so forth,' impurity at that time is included. Similarly in what follows. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'non-uniformity' means: the impossibility of a single causal relation of the cognitions of achievability-through-effort in the three cases of ritual mentioned with respect to activity-hood as the delimited [effect] — this is the meaning. In the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'he demonstrates — activity in general' means: of the nature of the delimiting property of causality determined by the effect-hood delimited by activity-hood — this is the meaning. 'Of a single one' means: common to the cognitions of achievability-through-effort in the three cases of ritual shown. In 'of that' and 'residing in that,' the word 'that' refers to the person. By 'desire and so forth,' both possessing purity-of-livelihood at the enjoined time and possessing impurity at that time are included. In 'of its possession,' the word 'that' refers to desire and so forth. Similarly in 'of the relation to that.' Likewise — 'of one's own object': the word 'own' here refers to desire. By 'means-hood and so forth,' substrate-hood is included. 'In the form of' qualifies the relation. The last occurrence of 'that' refers to cognition. 'Due to being pervasive' — now even so, since 'own-ness' rests on each individual person, there would be the undesirable consequence of infinite causal relations according to the difference of person-individuals. Otherwise, if activity-hood, which is pervasive, were the delimiting property of effect-hood, there would be the undesirable consequence of deviation. This should not be so — because there is no fault in accepting that with respect to activity-hood delimited by being directed toward Vedic rituals through the relation of inherence, the reason-hood consists in being cognition of achievability-through-effort through the relation of superstratum-hood and inherence.

children.translated_text: — since there is no fault in accepting reason-hood. 'Superstratum-hood' is through the relation of productivity born of the non-recollection of one's own qualification. After 'delimiting property of causality,' the word 'relation' should be supplied. 'Due to parsimony' is the meaning. Because of the extreme parsimony of that type of inherence — this is the purport. 'That' means complex — this is the meaning. 'Of the delimiting property of causality': 'of the relation' is to be supplied. 'Productivity' means: of the nature of necessarily subsequent occurrence — and so forth. By 'productivity and so forth,' delimitation-by-relation, superstratum-hood, and both are included. 'Here' means: in the body that is the object of cognition generating effort. 'Also not being followed by powerful undesirable [consequences]' means: not being followed by what is powerful and undesirable — this is the meaning. Powerful-ness here means non-difference from the time prior to the production of the desired [result]. The word 'also' serves as a conjunction to include both cognition of achievability-through-effort and cognition of being a means to the desired as examples.
