children.translated_text: 'by that.' The meaning is: by including the condition of not being followed by powerful undesirable [consequences] in the body that is the object of cognition generating effort. The syntactic connection is: there is no undesirable consequence of activity. 'In the form of the desired' is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional compound). 'Qualified' means: the desired means that is achievable through effort and not followed by powerful undesirable [consequences]. 'In activity' and so forth. 'Achievability through effort and so forth': by 'and so forth,' being a means to the desired and not being followed by powerful undesirable [consequences] are included. 'Separately alone' means: by the cognition of achievability-through-effort and so forth alone — this is the meaning. 'By the principle of the staff and the wheel' — otherwise, if reason-hood were accepted through the qualified cognition as stated, due to the absence of determination in the qualifier-qualificand relation, there would be the undesirable consequence of accepting multiple causal relations delimited by complex properties — this should be noted. 'Activity — is the meaning' means: otherwise, since effort is common to cessation [of activity] and life-sustaining [effort], if it were the delimiting property of the effect-hood of cognition of achievability-through-effort and so forth, there would be the undesirable consequence of deviation in negative concomitance — this is the purport. 'Of <s>pratyavāya</s> (sin of omission)' means: of sin — this is the meaning. 'Prior absence' means non-origination. Otherwise, for one who performs <s>sandhyāvandana</s> (twilight worship) and so forth throughout life, since the sin of omission is never generated, due to the impossibility of its prior absence, the <s>sandhyāvandana</s> and so forth of that person would be purposeless — this is the purport. Now, in the world, only pleasure, the cessation of pain, and the cessation of causes of pain are observed to be fruits in the sense of being desired — how then is the fruit-hood of the prior absence of the stated definition possible, since only what is desired has fruit-hood? To this he says 'of that.' 'By virtue of being the absence of a pain-producer' means: by virtue of being the absence of that which produces pain — this is the meaning. 'That' means the pain-producer. 'Fruit-hood' — this should be understood as constituted by being the aim of activity. And the desirability by virtue of being the absence of a pain-producer is being the object of a desire whose mode is such absence-hood. Now, how can there be fruit-hood of the prior absence of <s>pratyavāya</s> (sin of omission), which is of the nature of non-origination of that? For fruit-hood is being the aim of activity when there is productivity. But the stated prior absence is not produced — he raises this doubt by saying 'nor.' 'That' means <s>pratyavāya</s>. 'Of that' means of the prior absence of <s>pratyavāya</s>. 'Of the nature of the identity relation' means not different from the substrate's own nature. 'There' means in the prior absence of <s>pratyavāya</s>. 'From the objection to fruit-hood' — the purport is that in the place of productivity within the body of fruit-hood, being-an-effect-of should be introduced.

1svatādātmyasvotpattikṣaṇadhvaṃsotpattyadhikaraṇakṣaṇadhvaṃsotpattyadhikaraṇakṣaṇavṛttidhvaṃsapratiyogitvobhayasambandhena/
children.translated_text: indicates that the mode-ness is connected with the objecthood. The completion of '<s>bhāna</s>' is 'in verbal cognition' and so forth. [378] 'Due to unfitness' means: because of possessing the absence of means-hood for heaven. And since means-hood is of the nature of possessing a property that does not delimit the counter-positive-ness of the absence residing in the locus of the effect, as delimited by the moment immediately prior to the effect — therefore there is absence of sacrifice as delimited by the moment immediately prior to heaven — this is the purport. Now, 'more-rapid-destruction-hood' means extremely rapid destructibility; destructibility means being the counter-positive of destruction. And that is possible even in something that persists without a fruit, relative to something that persists longer — since it has that character relative to [something more enduring]. Therefore he glosses by saying 'third.' 'At the moment of one's own origination' and so forth. Otherwise, since third-ness relative to anything would be common to all moments without exception, that fault would follow. And third-ness from one's own origination moment means being the locus of the origination of the destruction of the locus of the origination of the destruction of the moment of one's own origination. Nor is there non-uniformity here through the involvement of 'own-ness.' For the gross uniformity is: being-qualified-by-knowability is more-rapid-destruction-hood. The qualification is through the relation of both — counter-positive-ness of the destruction occurring at the moment that is the locus of the origination of the destruction of the locus of the origination of the destruction of the moment of one's own origination, and identity with self.

children.translated_text: 1. It must be demonstrated that sacrifice and so forth have counter-positive-ness of a destruction occurring at the third moment from their own origination. There, by the word 'knowable,' only the sacrifice itself is to be taken; its being-qualified is in the sacrifice through the relation of both. That is: 'own' is the sacrifice; its identity is in the sacrifice. Similarly, 'own' is the sacrifice; the moment of its origination is the first moment; the locus of the origination of the destruction of that is the second moment; the locus of the origination of the destruction of that is the third moment; what occurs in that is the destruction of the sacrifice; the counter-positive-ness of that is in the sacrifice.

The persistence-until-the-fruit amounts to being the pervader of such moment-hood through superstratum-hood.

nanu [377] sthayikāryamapūrvameva iti dīpikāvākyamayuktam/
kṛtisādhyatārūpakāryatāyā yāga eva sambhavāt apūrve
tadasambhavādityatrāha - yāga iti/ sākṣāt - kiñcidadvārā/
āśrayatāsambandheneti yāvat/ yāgadvārā -
svāśrayayāgajanyatvarūpaparamparāsambandhena/ taditi/ janyetyarthaḥ/
ekadeśa iti/ kṛtāviti śeṣaḥ/ tatra - jyotiṣṭomena yajeteti
vākye/ sādhanāntaṃ yāgaviśeṣaṇam/ pūrvamiti/
jyotiṣṭomavākyajanyabodhādityādiḥ/ anupasthitatvāditi/
pramāṇāntareṇāpūrvasiddherasambhavāt tādṛśavākyenaiva
tatsiddhervaktavyatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ tatra - apūrve/
children.translated_text: Now, [377] the statement in the <s>Dīpikā</s> that 'the persistent effect is precisely <s>apūrva</s>' is incorrect — since the effect-hood in the form of achievability-through-effort is possible in the sacrifice itself, and is not possible in <s>apūrva</s>. To this he says 'sacrifice.' 'Directly' means without any intermediary. 'Through the relation of substrate-hood' is the completion. 'Through the sacrifice' means through the serial relation of being-produced-by-one's-own-substrate-the-sacrifice. 'That' means produced — this is the meaning. 'A part' — the completion is 'of effort.' 'There' means in the sentence '<s>jyotiṣṭomena yajeta</s>' ('one should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>'). 'Ending with the means' qualifies the sacrifice. 'Previously' means from the cognition produced by the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sentence — and so forth. 'Due to not being presented' means: since the establishment of <s>apūrva</s> through another <s>pramāṇa</s> is not possible, its establishment must be through such a sentence alone — this is the purport. 'There' means in <s>apūrva</s>.

children.text:
atra - uktākṣepe/
pravadantīti/ samādhānamiti śeṣaḥ/ taditi/ gurvityarthaḥ/ tādṛśeti/

tadviṣayakaśaktigrahasya

'Of such' means: having as its content what is delimited by that property — this is the meaning. Having-as-its-content-what-is-delimited-by-that-property means being the determinant of the objecthood delimited by that property. 'But not' means: the reason-hood of the apprehension having that as its content with respect to the verbal cognition having that as its content,

children.text:
1. prathamasvapadena
yāgotpattitṛtīyakṣaṇo grāhyaḥ/ tadvṛttidhvaṃsapratiyogitvaṃ yāge/
dvitīyasvapadaṃ tṛtīyakṣaṇaparam/ tṛtīyasvapadaṃ yāgaparam/
tṛtīyakṣaṇanirūpitā yāganiṣṭhā ādheyatā
svotpattikṣaṇadhvaṃsotpattyadhikaraṇakṣaṇadhvaṃsotpattyadhikaraṇakṣaṇatvasaṃbandhāvacchinnāḥ/
tena saṃbandhena yāgasya tṛtīyakṣaṇe sattvāditi
tādṛśādheyatvobhayasaṃbandhena tṛtīyakṣaṇaviśiṣṭatvaṃ yāgasyeti
samanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: 1. By the first word 'own,' the third moment from the origination of the sacrifice is to be taken. The counter-positive-ness of the destruction occurring in that is in the sacrifice. The second word 'own' refers to the third moment. The third word 'own' refers to the sacrifice. The superstratum-hood residing in the sacrifice, determined by the third moment, is delimited by the relation of being-the-moment-that-is-the-locus-of-the-origination-of-the-destruction-of-the-locus-of-the-origination-of-the-destruction-of-the-moment-of-one's-own-origination. Since the sacrifice exists at the third moment through that relation, the being-qualified-by-the-third-moment of the sacrifice is through the relation of both with such superstratum-hood — this is the construal.

children.text:
2. svaṃ yāgaḥ
tadutpattikṣaṇadhvaṃsādhikarakṣaṇamāramya
prakṛtaphalasyasvargāderutṣatikṣaṇadhvaṃsānadhikaraṇabhūtā/ yāvantaḥ kṣaṇāḥ
tāvadvṛttitvamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: 2. 'Own' is the sacrifice; beginning from the moment that is the locus of the destruction of the moment of its origination, [counting] up to the moments that are not the locus of the destruction of the moment of origination of the relevant fruit such as heaven. The meaning is: occurrence in as many moments [as there are between those limits].

children.text:
tadviṣayakopasthiteśca
hetutā na svīkriyata ityarthaḥ/ evaṃ coktarītyā
śaktigrahādiśābdabodhayoḥ samānaviṣayakatvena
kāryakāraṇabhāvamanupetya samānaprakārakatayā tayostadupagame
cetyarthaḥ/ yatra kutracit - ghaṭādau/ yogyateti/
children.translated_text: is not accepted as having reason-hood — this is the meaning. And accordingly, by the cognition of <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) and the verbal cognition stated having the same content, by accepting their cause-and-effect relation without requiring identity of content, but through having the same mode, and by accepting that [relation] between those two — this is the meaning. 'In whatever' means in a pot and so forth. 'Fitness' means:

children.text:
yāgaviṣayakatvānvayetyarthaḥ/ nanu śābdabodhe yogyatāvaśāt
ghaṭādirūpakāryasyaiva bhānaṃ kuto na sambhavatītyatrāha - na hīti/ na
sambhavati hītyanvayaḥ/ anyaditi/ apūrvarūpakāryādityādiḥ/ nitya
iti/ karmaṇīti śeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: the meaning is: the connection of having-sacrifice-as-content. Now, if due to fitness in verbal cognition the appearance of an effect in the form of a pot and so forth alone were possible, why not [accept that]? — to this he says 'for not.' The construal is: it is not possible indeed. 'Other' means from the effect in the form of <s>apūrva</s> — and so forth. 'Eternal' — the completion is 'in ritual.'

children.text:
phalābhāvāditi/
phalatvamiha janyatvaghaṭitam/ tatra - nityakarmavākye/ dīpikāyām
[377] nityavākye 'pīti apiḥ kāmyavākyasamuccāyakaḥ dṛṣṭāntatayā/
vācyamiti/ liṅāderityādiḥ/ nanvapūrvasya kenākāreṇa
nityavākyasthaliṅādivācyatetyāśaṅkāyāmāha - prakāśikāyām
kāryatvenetyādiriti/ paṇḍeti/ tanmate 'pūrvaṃ dvividham -
1kalikāpūrvam paṇḍāpūrvam ceti/ tatra
kāmyavākyasthaliṅādivācyamapūrvamādyam/ nityavākyasthaliṅādivācyaṃ
dvitīyam/ paṇḍatvaṃ napuṃsakatvam phalājanakatvamiti yāvat iti
dhyeyam/ dīpikāyām [377] kalpyata iti/ ayamatra
kalpanāprakāraḥ-nityavākyasthaliṅ kāryātvaprakāreṇāpūrvavācakaḥ
vaidikaliṅtvāt kāmyavākyasthaliṅvaditi/ kriyetyādivākye
kriyāyā dhātvarthasya yatkāryaṃ phalaṃ tatretyartha iti bhramavyudāsāyāha -
prakāśikāyām dhātvarthaniṣṭheti/ tathā cātra kāryaśabdaḥ kāryatvaparaḥ/
kriyākārya ityatra ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa eveti bhāvaḥ/ alaukiketi/
vaidiketyarthaḥ/ liṅādīti pūraṇīyam/ sādhāraṇyeneti/
sādhāraṇyamādheyatvam śaktyanvayini vaiśiṣṭye tṛtīyā/
kāryatvādāveveti/ evenāpūrvavyavacchedaḥ/ dīpikāyām [377] yāgasyāpīti/ apiratra dṛṣṭāntatvenāpūrvasamuccāyakaḥ/
ayogyeti/ svargasādhanatvābhāvavattetyarthaḥ/ sādhanatayeti/
svargādītyādiḥ/ taditi/
children.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of result' (<s>phalābhāva</s>) — here, result-hood (<s>phalatva</s>) is constituted by being produced. In that [context] — in the sentence prescribing obligatory rites (<s>nityakarmavākya</s>). In the <s>Dīpikā</s> [377], 'even in the sentence prescribing obligatory rites' — the word 'even' (<s>api</s>) serves to include the sentence prescribing desire-motivated rites by way of illustration. 'Is to be expressed' — 'by the optative and the like' is to be supplied. Now, to the doubt 'in what form is <s>apūrva</s> expressed by the optative and the like occurring in the sentence prescribing obligatory rites?', he replies — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'as effect-hood' and so forth. '<s>Paṇḍa</s>' — in that view, <s>apūrva</s> is of two kinds: (1) <s>kalikāpūrva</s> (result-producing <s>apūrva</s>) and (2) <s>paṇḍāpūrva</s> (barren <s>apūrva</s>). Of these, the <s>apūrva</s> expressed by the optative and the like in the sentence prescribing desire-motivated rites is the first; the <s>apūrva</s> expressed by the optative and the like in the sentence prescribing obligatory rites is the second. It should be noted that <s>paṇḍatva</s> means 'being neuter' — that is, 'incapacity to produce a result.' In the <s>Dīpikā</s> [377], 'is postulated' — the mode of postulation here is: the optative in the sentence prescribing obligatory rites denotes <s>apūrva</s> with effect-hood as its mode of presentation, because it is a Vedic optative, just like the optative in the sentence prescribing desire-motivated rites. In the sentence 'the effect of action' (<s>kriyākārya</s>) and so forth, to remove the confusion that 'the effect — i.e. the result — of the action that is the verb-meaning,' he says — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'residing in the verb-meaning.' And thus here the word 'effect' (<s>kārya</s>) refers to effect-hood (<s>kāryatva</s>). In 'effect of action' (<s>kriyākārya</s>), it is only a genitive compound — this is the intent. 'Non-ordinary' (<s>alaukika</s>) — means: Vedic. 'Optative and the like' is to be supplied. 'By commonality' (<s>sādhāraṇyena</s>) — commonality means superstratum-hood; the instrumental case is with respect to the qualification in which the denotative power (<s>śakti</s>) is connected. 'In effect-hood and the like alone' — by 'alone,' <s>apūrva</s> is excluded. In the <s>Dīpikā</s> [377], 'of sacrifice too' — 'too' (<s>api</s>) here serves to include <s>apūrva</s> by way of illustration. 'Unfit' (<s>ayogya</s>) — means: possessing the absence of being a means to heaven. 'As a means' — 'to heaven and the like' is to be supplied. 'That' (<s>tad</s>) —

children.text:
1. kalikāpūrvamiti/
kalayati utpādayati phalamiti vyutpattyā niṣpanno 'yaṃ śabdaḥ
savargādikāmyaphalasādhanamūparvamācaṣṭe/ napuṃsakavācī paṇḍaśabdaḥ
niṣphalatvārthakaḥ/ tathā ca niṣphalāpūrvamiti paṇḍāpūrvaśabdārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Footnote 1: '<s>Kalikāpūrva</s>' — this word is derived from the etymology '<s>kalayati</s>' (it produces) '<s>utpādayati phalam</s>' (it generates a result), and it denotes the <s>apūrva</s> that is a means to a desired result such as heaven and the like. The word '<s>paṇḍa</s>' denotes a neuter [entity] and means 'fruitlessness.' And thus '<s>paṇḍāpūrva</s>' means 'a fruitless <s>apūrva</s>.'

children.text:
sādhanatetyarthaḥ/ evaṃ
vyākhyāne 'pi tannirvāhāyetyatra avāntareti/
phalasādhanayormadhyadaśābhāvītyarthaḥ/ apūrvakalpanāditi/ ayamatra
kalpanāprakāraḥ--yāgaḥ svargajanakavyāpārajanakaḥ
svargāvyavahitaprākkālāvṛttitve sati svargajanakatvāt yo
yadavyavahitaprākkālāvṛttitve sati yajjanakaḥ sa
tajjanakavyāpārajanakaḥ/ yathā saṃskāradvārā smṛtijanakānubhava iti/
children.translated_text: 'means: as a means' — even in this interpretation, in 'for its accomplishment' (<s>tannirvāhāya</s>), 'intermediate' (<s>avāntara</s>) [is the sense] — means: occurring in the intermediate stage between result and means. 'From the postulation of <s>apūrva</s>' — the mode of postulation here is: sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) produces an operation that produces heaven; since it produces heaven while not occurring in the period immediately prior to heaven, whatever produces something while not occurring in the period immediately prior to that [thing] produces an operation that produces that — just like an experience that produces memory through the intermediary of an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>).

children.text:
nanu
yāgasyāyogyatāniścayo mā bhūt tatsaṃśayaḥ paraṃ jāyata eveti
niścayavatsaṃśayasyāpi tadvattādhīvirodhitvāt kathaṃ
svargādisādhanatayā yāgabodhasambhava ityatrāha --- prakāśikāyām
ayogyateti/ svargādisādhanatvābhāvavattetyarthaḥ/ tasya -
ayogyatāsaṃśayasya/ avighaṭakatvāditi/ avirodhitvādityarthaḥ/
tadabhāvavattāniṃścayasyaiva tadvattādhīvirodhitvāditi bhāvaḥ/
yāgadharmiṅkasvargādisādhanatvaprakārakabuddhāvityādiḥ/ bodha iti/
jyotiṣṭomādivākyataḥ svargādisādhanatāyā ityādiḥ/
vākyāditi/ jyotiṣṭomādītyādiḥ/ tasya-yāgasya/ nanvapūrvasya
yāgavyāpāratve yāgajanyatvaṃ yāgajanyasvargādirūphalajanakatvaṃ dvayamapi
kalpanīyam/ yāgadhvaṃsasya yāgavyāpāratāyāṃ tu pratiyogividhayā
yāgajanyatāyā yāgadhvaṃse kḷptatvāt svargādirūphalajanakatāmātraṃ
kalpanīyamityubhayakalpanayā pūrvapakṣe gauravamityāśaṅkate ---
nanviti/ dhvaṃsasyaivetyevenāpūrvavyavacchedaḥ/ vyāpāratvamiti/
yāgetyādiḥ/ sparśādītyādinā
karatoyātilaṅghanagaṇḍakībāhutaraṇayoḥ saṃgrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, the ascertainment that sacrifice is unfit [to produce heaven directly] may not arise, but doubt about it certainly does; and since doubt, like ascertainment, contradicts the cognition of [sacrifice] possessing that capacity, how is the cognition of sacrifice as a means to heaven and the like possible? To this he says — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'unfitness' — means: possessing the absence of being a means to heaven and the like. 'Of that' — of the doubt regarding unfitness. 'Because of not being an obstructor' (<s>avighaṭakatva</s>) — means: because of not being contradictory. Because only the ascertainment of [sacrifice] possessing the absence of that capacity contradicts the cognition of [sacrifice] possessing that capacity — this is the intent. 'In the cognition whose qualificand is sacrifice and whose mode of presentation is being a means to heaven and the like' and so forth. 'Cognition' — 'of being a means to heaven and the like, from the sentence concerning <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like' is to be supplied. 'From the sentence' — '<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like' is to be supplied. 'Of that' — of sacrifice. Now, if <s>apūrva</s> is the operation of sacrifice, two things must be postulated: (1) being produced by sacrifice, and (2) producing a result in the form of heaven and the like that is produced by sacrifice. But if the destruction of sacrifice is the operation of sacrifice, then since being produced by sacrifice is already established in the destruction of sacrifice by way of the counter-positive [relation], only the producing of a result in the form of heaven and the like needs to be postulated — and thus with both postulations, the prima facie view involves greater cumbersomeness — he raises this objection with 'but' (<s>nanu</s>). 'Of destruction alone' — by 'alone,' <s>apūrva</s> is excluded. 'As the operation' — 'of sacrifice' and so forth is to be supplied. By 'touch and the like,' the cases of crossing the river Karatoyā and the <s>Gaṇḍakī</s> and the like are included.

children.text:
dīpikāyām [377] na
yāgadhvaṃso vyāpāra iti/ na vyāpāra ityanvayaḥ/ vyāpāra
ityasya yāgetyādiḥ/ anyathā śrautasya kṣarateḥ naśyatītyarthaparatayā
dhvaṃsasya nāśaviraheṇa vyāpārasya
kīrtanādināśaśrutivirodhaprasaṅgāditi bhāvaḥ/ atra ca na kṣaratiḥ
nāśarūpamukhyakṣaraṇaparaḥ api tu phalāsamarthatvarūpagauṇakṣaraṇaparaḥ/ evaṃ
ca yāgadhvaṃsasya yāgavyāpāratāyāmapi na kṣatiḥ/ tasya phalāsamarthatvaṃ ca
bhavati/ dharmakīrtanādeḥ svargādiphalaṃ prati pratibandhakatvakalpanayā/
anyathā prāguktakalpanā -- apūrvarūpadharmasya nāśakalpanā tannāśaṃ prati
kīrtanādeḥ hetutvakalpanā ceti mahāgauravāpatteriti
dīpikoktadūṣaṇaṃ na vicārasahamiti ālocya dhvaṃsasya
vyāpāratāyāmabhedyaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ svayamāha - prakāśikāyām dhvaṃsasyeti/
dūṣaṇāntaram - prāgupāditadūṣaṇātiriktadūṣaṇam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dīpikā</s> [377], 'the destruction of sacrifice is not the operation' — the construction is: 'is not the operation.' 'Operation' — 'of sacrifice' and so forth is to be supplied. Otherwise, since the Vedic [root] '<s>kṣarati</s>' would mean 'perishes,' and destruction would then be described as an operation without destruction, there would be a contradiction with the Vedic text [that speaks of] destruction — this is the intent. And here, '<s>kṣarati</s>' does not refer to destruction in the primary sense, but rather to figurative deterioration in the form of incapacity to produce a result. And thus, even if the destruction of sacrifice is the operation of sacrifice, there is no defect — it [the sacrifice after destruction] does possess incapacity to produce a result, because of the postulation that the recitation of <s>dharma</s> and the like acts as an obstructor to the result of heaven and the like. Otherwise, the previously stated postulation — the postulation of the destruction of the <s>dharma</s> in the form of <s>apūrva</s>, and the postulation that recitation and the like are causes of that destruction — would involve great cumbersomeness. Having considered that the objection stated in the <s>Dīpikā</s> does not withstand scrutiny, he himself states an irrefutable objection against the destruction being the operation — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'of destruction.' A different objection — an objection beyond the one previously presented.

yatnārthakatvasthāpanam

āśrayatāsambandhenaivetyevakāraḥ anvayenetyuttaraṃ yojyaḥ/

abhedātiriktasambandhena nānvayaḥ/ tathehāpi nāmārthe

samabhivyāhāraviśeṣajñānaniyāmyatvavirahāt/ tatra-ratho
gacchatītyādau/ tathā - prathamāntārthe gamanāderāśrayatāsaṃbandhena/
saṃbandhe 'tiriktatvaviśeṣaṇapraveśaphalamāha - stokaṃ
pacatītyādāvapīti/ kartṛkarmaṇorākhyātārthatāsambhave dīpikākṛtā
children.translated_text: is synonymous with the word 'yat' ending in 'tra.' And thus the meaning is: one who possesses the cognition whose mode of presentation is being accomplishable by effort and being a means to a desired end. 'For that purpose' — the word 'that' here refers to 'on the strength of worldly usage.' 'There' — in the world. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, from 'by the optative' onward, 'and the like' is the remainder. 'Having the nature of injunction' (<s>vidhyarthatva</s>) — 'of the optative and the like' is to be supplied. This is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: 'that of which injunction is the meaning to be expressed.' And thus, since the word 'injunction' (<s>vidhi</s>) refers to the object of prompting cognition, it means 'having the capacity to denote such an object.' 'As a finite verb' (<s>ākhyātatvena</s>) and so forth — he unpacks the [property] delimited by finite-verb-hood — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'as a finite verb.' And that — finite-verb-hood. 'By convention' (<s>saṃketa</s>) — 'of <s>Pāṇini</s> and the like' is to be supplied. 'By the denotative power' (<s>śakte</s>) — 'determined by the effort residing in the optative and the like' and so forth is to be supplied. Means: being the determiner of the denotative power. 'In the delimited' — in the qualified. Similarly hereafter too. 'By the relation' (<s>saṃbandha</s>) — and the relation here is conduciveness (<s>anukūlatā</s>). Similarly hereafter too. 'That' — of the form 'what does [he] do?' 'That' — means: in the interrogative sentence of the form 'what does [he] do?' 'The capacity to remove' (<s>nivartakatva</s>) — 'is possible' is the remainder. Otherwise — in the absence of the capacity to convey the cooking-relation as delimited by effort-hood. 'The capacity to remove that' — the construction is: that capacity to remove is not possible, because of the connection with what follows. 'Because of the impossibility of conveying effort' — because in an insentient thing like a chariot, the conscious property of effort is impossible — this is the intent. 'That' — means: the finite verb in contexts such as 'the chariot goes.' 'In accordance with' (<s>anurodha</s>) — by this, the principle of uniformity of denotative power for all finite verbs is indicated. 'Operation alone' (<s>vyāpāra eva</s>) — by 'alone,' effort is excluded. Now, in 'the chariot goes' and the like, when consistency can be achieved simply by accepting a figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) delimited by the lighter property of having an operation, stating a figurative usage delimited by the heavier property of having a conducive operation is inappropriate on the part of the <s>Dīpikā</s> author. And furthermore, if conduciveness is accepted, since the connection of going and the like through the relation of being determined [by conduciveness] must be stated, postulating such an additional relation in verbal cognition (<s>śābdabuddhi</s>) involves great cumbersomeness — to this he says: 'operation.' 'By this' — by [the property of] conduciveness. 'Conventional' (<s>nirūḍha</s>) — means: residing in the object that has been the content of speaker's intention (<s>tātparya</s>) from beginningless time. Similarly hereafter too. 'By the substratum relation alone' — the word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>) should be connected with what follows, 'by the connection' (<s>anvaya</s>). By 'alone,' when substratum-hood is postulated as the meaning of the finite verb, the connection through the relation of being determined [by it] is excluded. 'Just as with the meanings of nouns' — just as the meaning of one noun does not connect with the meaning of another noun through any relation other than identity, so too here, the meaning of the verb-root does not connect with the meaning of the noun through any relation other than identity. Otherwise, in [expressions] like 'the king's man' (<s>rājapuruṣa</s>), the meaning of the noun 'king' would connect with the meaning of the noun 'man' through the relation of master-servant and the like; and in 'rice is cooked' (<s>pacyate taṇḍula</s>), the verb-meaning of cooking would connect with the noun-meaning 'rice' through the relation of action-object and the like — such unwanted connections would follow respectively — this is the intent. 'Because of not being derived' (<s>avyutpannatva</s>) — because of the absence of being determined by knowledge of a particular co-occurrence (<s>samabhivyāhāra</s>). 'There' — in 'the chariot goes' and the like. 'Thus' — the substratum relation connecting going and the like with the meaning of the nominative-ending [word]. The purpose of including the qualifier 'additional' in the relation, he states: 'even in "he cooks a little"' and so forth. When the finite verb cannot denote agent-hood or object-hood, the <s>Dīpikā</s> author

tatra tāmāha - ākhyātasyeti/ kartrādāviti/ ādinā

śeṣaḥ/ kṛtitvādītayādinā saṃyogatvādiparigrahaḥ/

lāghavamiti/ kṛtitvādijāterekatvenānantyavirahāt
jātyanullikhitapratītau jāteḥ svarūpata eva bhānopagamena

ādinetyasyādiśabdenetyarthaḥ/ evamanyatrāpi/ tarhi ākhyātasya
kṛtyādyarthakatve/ kartṛkarmaṇoriti/ devadattaḥ pacati pacyate taṇḍula
ityādāvitiśeṣaḥ/ lābhaḥ - pratitiḥ/ kartṛtvakarmantvābhyāṃ
devadattataṇḍulāderityādiḥ/
children.translated_text: does not state the reasoning [for this], so he himself states it — 'of the finite verb' (<s>ākhyātasya</s>). 'In the agent and the like' — by 'and the like,' the object is included, which consists of the respective results such as contact, separation, and the like that are considered to be the delimiters of verb-meaning-hood. 'And the like' in '<s>kṛti</s> and the like' is said to indicate great cumbersomeness. By 'and the like' in 'effort and the like,' results in the form of contact and the like are included. Similarly hereafter too. 'Must be accepted' — after this, the remainder is: 'the universals such as effort-hood and the like must also be accepted as delimiters of the delimitor of denotative-capacity-hood.' By 'and the like' in 'effort-hood and the like,' contact-hood and the like are included. Because any entity that is neither a universal nor an indivisible limiting property nor something additional [to these] appears merely as a particular (<s>yatkiñcidrūpa</s>) — this is the intent. 'Parsimony' (<s>lāghava</s>) — because universals such as effort-hood, being singular, lack the problem of infinity; and since, in a cognition that does not delineate the universal, the universal is accepted as appearing in its own essential form, there is no need to accept any additional property as a delimitor of the delimitor of denotative-capacity-hood — this is the intent. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'that' — refers to agent and object. 'Unity and the like' — he states the meaning of the 'and the like' — in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'by "and the like," effort and the like.' The meaning of 'by "and the like"' is 'by the word "and the like."' Similarly elsewhere too. 'Then, when the finite verb has the meaning of effort and the like' — 'of agent and object' — the remainder is: in [sentences like] '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks,' 'rice is cooked,' and the like. 'Obtaining' (<s>lābha</s>) — means: cognition. 'Of <s>Devadatta</s>, rice, and the like, through agent-hood and object-hood' and so forth is to be supplied.

children.text:
evamagre 'pi/
dīpikāyām tayoḥ - kartṛkarmaṇoḥ/ ākṣepādeveti/
ākṣepaścārthāpattiḥ/ devadattādeḥ kartṛtvādikamantarā
kṛtyādiparākhyātasamabhivyāhṛtadevadattādipadabodhyatvamanupapannami tyādirūpā/
nanu svamate uktarūpākṣepānupagamādākṣepādeveti
dīpikāvākyamasaṅgatamityatrāha - prakāśikāyām paramateneti/
svamate tviti/ svapadamatra naiyāyikaparam/ padenaiva ityevena
uktākṣepavyudāsaḥ/ taditi kartṛkarmetyarthaḥ/ devadattaḥ pacatītyādau
kañcanākṣepaṃ tatparihāraṃ ca vivakṣan tadupayo gitvena
śābdabodhaprakāraṃ yathāyogaṃ darśayati - devadattaḥ taṇḍulaṃ
pacatītyatreti/ tatra - tevadattaḥ pacati, taṇḍulaḥ pacyata
ityuktasthalayoḥ/ anabhidhānāditīti/ tṛtīyādvitīyāniyāmakayoḥ
sūtrayoranabhihitādhikārīyatvāditi bhāvaḥ/ anabhihvita iti/
lakārādibhirityādiḥ/ lakārādi janyaśābdabodhāviṣaya ityarthaḥ/
tādṛśe - lakārādibhiranabhihita - ityarthaḥ/ mūle 'pyevam/
children.translated_text: Similarly hereafter too. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, 'of those two' — of agent and object. 'By implication alone' (<s>ākṣepāt eva</s>) — and implication here is <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). It is of the form: without agent-hood and the like of <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, the cognizability by the noun '<s>Devadatta</s>' and the like co-occurring with the finite verb whose meaning is effort and the like would be inexplicable — and so forth. Now, since in our own view the above-described implication is not accepted, the <s>Dīpikā</s>'s statement 'by implication alone' is inconsistent — to this he says, in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>, 'according to the other view' (<s>paramatena</s>). 'But in our own view' — the word 'own' (<s>sva</s>) here refers to the <s>Naiyāyika</s>. 'By the word alone' (<s>padena eva</s>) — by 'alone,' the above-mentioned implication is set aside. 'That' — means: agent and object. Intending to state a certain objection and its resolution in [sentences like] '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks' and the like, he shows the manner of verbal cognition (<s>śābdabodha</s>) as preliminary to that — with 'in "<s>Devadatta</s> cooks rice"' and so forth. 'There' — in the two cases stated, namely '<s>Devadatta</s> cooks' and 'rice is cooked.' 'Because of non-denotation' and so forth — because the two <s>sūtras</s> that govern the third and second case-endings belong to the section on what is not denoted (<s>anabhihitādhikāra</s>) — this is the intent. 'Not denoted' (<s>anabhihita</s>) — 'by the verb-endings (<s>lakāra</s>) and the like' is to be supplied. What is not the object of verbal cognition produced by the verb-endings and the like — this is the meaning. 'Of such a kind' — means: not denoted by the verb-endings and the like. Similarly in the root text too.

children.text:
upasargāṇāṃ
dyotakatvam
children.translated_text: The indicative function (<s>dyotakatva</s>) of verbal prefixes (<s>upasarga</s>)
Section 385

children.text:
upasargāṇām - upasargāt kriyāyoga
iti vihitopasargasaṃjñakānām prādīnāmiti śeṣaḥ/ vacanatveti/
children.translated_text: 'Of verbal prefixes' — the completion is: of the <s>pra</s> and other [prefixes] designated as <s>upasarga</s> by the [Pāṇinian] rule '<s>upasargāt kriyāyoga</s>' (a verbal prefix [is so called when it is] in connection with an action). 'The property of being an expression' —

children.text:
prakarṣādirūpārthaviśeṣetyādiḥ/ tātparyeti/
samabhivyāhṛtadhātupratipādyārthaviśeṣetyādiḥ/ grāhakatvamiti/ anyathā

āseścādheyatvārthakatvena
samīpadeśādheyatvarūpaviśiṣṭārthaparasyopāserakarmakatvena 'laḥ
karmaṇi ca bhāve cākarmakebhyaḥ' (pā. sū 3.4.69) iti sūtroktarītyā
karmalakārānupapattiprasaṅgāt/ ataḥ upaśabdaḥ

upasargaṃsaṃjñārahitetyarthaḥ/ nipātanāditi evakārādīnāmiti śeṣaḥ/
'svarādinipātamavyayam' (pā. sū. 1.1.37) iti
sūtravihitanipātasaṃjñakānāmityarthaḥ/ evakārādīnāṃ
vācakatvaprakāramupapādayati - tathā hītyādinā/ ayogavyavacchedaḥ
uddeśyatāvacchedakībhūtaśaṅkhatvādivyāpakatvam/ anyayogeti
evakārasyetyādiranuṣajyate/ vyavacchedaśceti/ artha ityanuṣajyate/
anyayogavyavacchedaḥ uddeśyatāvacchedakapārthatvādivyāpyatvam/
ityādikamityādinā kriyāsaṅgataivakārasyātyantāyogavyavacchedaḥ
uddeśyatāvacchedakatvābhimatasarojatvādisāmānādhikaraṇyarūpaḥ/ artha
ityādikamityarthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the completion is: of a particular meaning in the form of excellence (<s>prakarṣa</s>) and the like. 'The purport' — the completion is: of a particular meaning conveyed by the co-occurring verbal root. 'The property of being an indicator' — otherwise, in [usages] such as '<s>upāsyate guruḥ</s>' (the teacher is worshipped), since the prefix <s>upa</s> would refer to a proximate location, and since the root <s>ās</s> would mean superstratum-hood, the compound <s>upās</s> referring to the qualified meaning of superstratum-hood-in-a-proximate-location would be intransitive, and there would be the unwanted consequence that the <s>lakāra</s> (verbal suffix) with an accusative object could not be accounted for, as per the rule '<s>laḥ karmaṇi ca bhāve cākarmakebhyaḥ</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 3.4.69) which states that the <s>lakāra</s> [in the passive] applies to the object and to the state [of being] from intransitive [roots]. Therefore, it must be said that the prefix <s>upa</s> indicates the purport of the root <s>ās</s> toward a particular meaning in the form of a specific cognition constituting worship (<s>upāsana</s>). The same should be understood elsewhere as well. In the <s>Dīpikā</s>, regarding 'in excellence' — [the commentator] clarifies what is excluded by the restrictive particle <s>eva</s> (only) in 'indicative function only in excellence and the like' — 'there is no denotative power (<s>śakti</s>) there.' 'There' means in excellence and the like. 'By that' — the connection is with 'is indicated,' through the establishment of the indicative function of verbal prefixes in the stated manner. 'The other' — the meaning is: lacking the designation of <s>upasarga</s>. 'By being listed as an indeclinable' — the completion is: of the particle <s>eva</s> and the like. The meaning is: of those designated as <s>nipāta</s> (particle) by the rule '<s>svarādinipātamavyayam</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 1.1.37). [The commentator] establishes the manner of denotative function of the particle <s>eva</s> and the like — with 'for indeed' and so forth. '<s>Ayogavyavaccheda</s>' (exclusion of non-connection) is the property of pervading [i.e., being superordinate to] conch-hood and the like that have become the delimitor of the property of being the subject. In 'exclusion of connection with another' — 'of the particle <s>eva</s>' and the like should be supplied. 'And exclusion' — 'meaning' should be supplied. '<s>Anyayogavyavaccheda</s>' (exclusion of connection with another) is the property of being pervaded by [i.e., being subordinate to] pot-hood and the like that is the delimitor of the property of being the subject. By 'and the like' and so forth, the <s>atyantāyogavyavaccheda</s> (exclusion of complete non-connection) of the particle <s>eva</s> related to an action is [defined as] the co-locationness of the form of lotus-hood and the like that are regarded as the delimitor of the property of being the subject. The meaning is: 'meaning' and the like [should be supplied].

children.text:
padārthatattvajñānasya
mokṣahetutvanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Determination that the knowledge of the true nature of the categories (<s>padārthatattvajñāna</s>) is the cause of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>)
Section 388

children.text:
prekṣāvaditi/ buddhimadityarthaḥ/ viṣayeti
muktiviśeṣaṇam/ pṛthivyādeḥ jalatvādinā jñānasyātattvajñānasya
muktiprayojakatvāsambhavādāha - padārthatattvajñānasyeti/
yathāvasthitākāreṇa padārthajñānasyetyarthaḥ/ anyeṣāmiti/
muktiyapaprayojanādityādiḥ/ avāntareti/ madhyavartītyarthaḥ/ parameti/
paramatvaṃ ca svānantarotpannatattvajñānasādhyaprayojanakānyatvam/
sādhyatvaṃ ca sākṣātparamparayā vā bodhyam/ anugamastu sphuṭaḥ/
śruteriti/ 'ātmā vāre'tyādiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'A discerning person (<s>prekṣāvat</s>)' — the meaning is: an intelligent person. 'Regarding the object' — this qualifies liberation (<s>mukti</s>). Since erroneous cognition of earth and the like through the properties of water and the like cannot be a cause of liberation, [the commentator] says 'of the knowledge of the true nature of the categories' — the meaning is: of the knowledge of the categories as they truly are. 'Of others' — the completion is: from the purpose of liberation and the like. 'Intermediate' — the meaning is: situated in between. 'Ultimate' — and the property of being ultimate is the property of being other than what has a purpose accomplishable by the knowledge of truth produced immediately after it. And 'accomplishable' should be understood either directly or indirectly. The applicability [of this definition] is clear. 'From scripture (<s>śruti</s>)' — [the reference is to texts] such as '<s>ātmā vāre</s>' (the Self indeed [is to be known]) and the like.

children.text:
nanūpāyasya
phalaprāgbhāvitvānurodhenopāyapratipādakasya bhāgasya
phalapratipādakabhāgaprāgbhāvitvamāvaśyakamiti kathaṃ draṣṭavya
ityādivākyasaṅgatirityatrāha ārtheti/ arthasambandhītyarthaḥ/
krameṇeti/ kramaśca paurvāparyam/ uktaśrutivākya ityādiḥ/
evamagre 'pi/ śabdeti/ śabdasambandhītyarthaḥ/ tyakto bhavatīti/
nididhyāsitavyo draṣṭavya iti yojaneti bhāvaḥ/ yuktibhiḥ
bahuyuktiviṣayakaparāmarśajanyānumitidhāretyarthaḥ/ ātmana iti/
ātmaviśeṣyaketarabhinnatvaprakārakānumitirityarthaḥ/ tacca -
uknarūpānumānaṃ ca/ pratiyogītareti samānādhikaraṇasamāsaḥ/ tacca
uktarūpānupānaṃ ca/ taditi/ ātmana
children.translated_text: Now, since a means must precede the result, the portion that teaches the means must necessarily precede the portion that teaches the result — how then is the textual connection to be understood with statements such as 'it is to be seen' and the like? In response to this, [the commentator] says 'pertaining to the meaning' — the meaning is: pertaining to the subject matter. 'In sequence' — and the sequence is the order of precedence. The completion is: the stated Vedic statement and the like. The same applies further on. 'Pertaining to the word (<s>śabda</s>)' — the meaning is: pertaining to the verbal [connection]. 'He becomes one who has renounced' — the purport is: the construal is '[the Self] is to be meditated upon, is to be seen.' 'By reasonings' — the meaning is: through the stream of inferences produced by deliberation whose object is many reasonings. 'Of the Self' — the meaning is: an inference having as its qualifier the property of being different from everything other [than the Self], with the Self as its qualificand. And that — is the inference of the stated form. 'Different from the counter-positive and the like' — this is a co-locative compound. And that — is the inference of the stated form. 'That' — of the Self,

children.text:
itararbhinnatvenānumānatyarthaḥ/ tadanantarami tyatra tacchabdo
mananapara ityāśayena vyācaṣṭe -- mananetyādi/ śrutasyetyādi/
nairantaryaṃ vijātīyapratyayāvyavahitatvam/ vaiśiṣṭye tṛtīyā/ pratyaye
vijātīyatvaṃ ca śrutārthātiriktārthaviṣayakatvam/ pratyāhṛtyeti/
pratyāharaṇaṃ sambandhanivṛttyanukūlavyāpāraḥ/ sambandhānvayini
anuyogitve pañcamī viṣayebhya ityatra/ evamagre 'pi tadanantaramityatra
tacchabdaḥ nididhyāsanapara ityabhisandhāyāha - [388] nididhyāsaneti/ nanu mithyājñānamātranāśe 'pi
tadadhīnavāsanāsattve doṣasambhavāt mithyājñānanāśena
doṣābhāvakathanamayuktamityato vyācaṣṭe --- [388] vāsanāsahiteti/ jñānaviśeṣaṇam/ vāsanā - saṃskāraḥ/
rāgādirityādinā doṣamohayoḥ parigrahaḥ/ [688] viśeṣeti/ rajatavyāvartakākāretyarthaḥ/
śuktitvādirūpetyādiḥ/ jñānenaivetyevena tādṛ
children.translated_text: the meaning is: the inference as being different from everything other. In 'after that,' with the intent that the word 'that' refers to deliberation (<s>manana</s>), [the commentator] glosses — 'deliberation' and so forth. 'Of what has been heard' and so forth. 'Continuity' means not being interrupted by a cognition of a different kind. The instrumental case [is used] in the sense of qualification. And the property of being of a different kind with respect to a cognition is the property of having as its object a meaning other than the meaning that has been heard. 'Having withdrawn' — withdrawal is an operation conducive to the cessation of connection. The ablative case in 'from the objects' [applies] when the substratum is [considered] in the relation of connection. The same applies further on — in 'after that,' with the intent that the word 'that' refers to meditation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>), [the commentator] says [section 388] 'meditation' and so forth. Now, since even upon the mere destruction of erroneous cognition, defects (<s>doṣa</s>) are possible due to the persistence of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) dependent on that [erroneous cognition], the statement that defects are absent through the destruction of erroneous cognition alone would be improper — therefore [the commentator] glosses [section 388] 'together with the latent impressions' — this qualifies knowledge. <s>Vāsanā</s> means dispositional impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). By 'attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the like,' the inclusion of defect (<s>doṣa</s>) and delusion (<s>moha</s>) [is indicated]. [Section 688] 'Specific' — the meaning is: having the form that excludes silver. The completion is: having the form of nacre-hood and the like. 'By knowledge alone' — by the [particle] <s>eva</s>, such [specific knowledge]
